Delhi College of Art: programmes and schemes
Delhi College of Art: BFA syllabus download page

title: B.F.Sc. (Bachelor of Fisheries Science)
description: An undergraduate degree program focused on the study of fish breeding, genetics, biotechnology, nutrition, farming, and diagnosis of diseases.

quick_facts.label: Credential
quick_facts.value: B.F.Sc. (Bachelor of Fisheries Science) is listed by ICAR as a four-year professional bachelor’s degree in agricultural and allied sciences.

quick_facts.label: Normal structure
quick_facts.value: The programme is ordinarily delivered across eight semesters (four academic years), with credit-based coursework and practical components.

quick_facts.label: ICAR-UG eligibility baseline
quick_facts.value: For CUET (ICAR-UG) 2026, B.F.Sc. applicants need Class 12 with at least three of Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture/Inter-Agriculture as core subjects; the bulletin specifies 50% aggregate for General/OBC-NCL/UPS/EWS and 40% for SC/ST/Third Gender/PwBD categories. Participating universities may impose additional programme-specific conditions.

quick_facts.label: Main postgraduate pathway
quick_facts.value: A B.F.Sc. in the 10+2+4 system is an accepted entry qualification for M.F.Sc. programmes; ICAR-CIFE lists specialisations including aquaculture, fisheries resource management, post-harvest technology, fish genetics and breeding, fish biotechnology, aquatic animal health management, fish nutrition and feed technology, fisheries economics and fisheries extension.

sections.heading: Eligibility for B.F.Sc.
paragraphs: For the ICAR all-India undergraduate route in the 2026–27 cycle, B.F.Sc. falls within the agriculture-and-allied-sciences group. The ICAR bulletin requires a recognised 10+2/equivalent qualification after 12 years of study and at least three relevant core subjects drawn from Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture/Inter-Agriculture.

The stated ICAR-UG aggregate-mark threshold is 50% for General, OBC (NCL), UPS and EWS candidates and 40% for SC, ST, Third Gender and PwBD candidates, without rounding off. This is an examination/counselling baseline rather than a guarantee of admission: universities can prescribe additional subject combinations, age limits or other statutory conditions.
bullets: Check the subject combination published for the particular university and B.F.Sc. seat before applying; requirements differ across participating institutions.
The ICAR bulletin states that the medium of instruction at admitting universities is English.

sections.heading: Duration and academic format
paragraphs: B.F.Sc. is normally a four-year, eight-semester undergraduate professional programme. A university academic regulation describes continuous evaluation under the semester system, while an ICAR-aligned fisheries college states that students complete eight semesters for the degree.

Programme rules are institution-specific. For example, one current regulation specifies 180 credits including Student READY components, while the Kamdhenu University college specifies a minimum OGPA of 5.5/10 for its own degree award.
bullets: Plan for a full-time four-year course rather than a three-year general bachelor’s programme.
Confirm the awarding university’s credit, attendance, OGPA and maximum-completion rules in its current prospectus or regulations.

sections.heading: What students study and practise
paragraphs: The curriculum combines fisheries science with laboratory, field and industry-oriented learning. ICAR’s minimum requirements identify core academic areas/departments covering aquaculture; fisheries resource management; aquatic animal health and environment; aquatic environment management; fish processing technology; fish engineering; and fisheries extension, economics and statistics.

The practical emphasis is substantial. An ICAR-aligned B.F.Sc. college describes Fisheries Rural Work Experience in the seventh semester and experiential learning in fish seed production and post-harvest technology in the final semester. A university regulation also includes in-plant training, experiential learning, skill development, rural fisheries work experience, project work, seminars and study tours within Student READY.
bullets: Typical academic coverage includes fish production and culture, aquatic environments, animal health, capture-fisheries/resource management, processing and engineering, and fisheries extension/economics.
Exact course titles, credits, field placements and assessment rules should be taken from the current curriculum of the admitting university, not assumed to be identical nationwide.

sections.heading: Admission routes: ICAR-UG and university rules
paragraphs: For the 2026–27 ICAR undergraduate cycle, B.F.Sc. admission under the ICAR-AU system is based on merit rank in CUET (ICAR-UG) 2026, not on the separately named AIEEA-PG examination. The ICAR bulletin identifies B.F.Sc. as programme code 03 and says actual university-wise seats, subject eligibility and special conditions are to be published in the UG online counselling brochure.

Applications for CUET (ICAR-UG) are online through the NTA process. Candidates must select examination subjects that match subjects passed at Class 12; attempting different subjects can lead to disqualification from ICAR counselling/admission. Universities also verify documents and final eligibility at admission.

The label “ICAR AIEEA” is therefore best treated carefully for this node: AIEEA-PG is the ICAR postgraduate entrance process, whereas the current undergraduate ICAR route is CUET (ICAR-UG). Universities may also have state, institutional or other quota procedures, so their current admission notice remains controlling for those seats.
bullets: Use the ICAR/NTA bulletin for the national ICAR quota route, then read the target university’s current seat matrix and special conditions.
Do not rely on a prior year’s cutoff, seat count, age condition or application date; ICAR says these may differ when the counselling brochure is issued.

sections.heading: After B.F.Sc.: postgraduate study and progression
paragraphs: A direct academic progression is M.F.Sc. ICAR-CIFE accepts B.F.Sc. holders under the 10+2+4 system and offers M.F.Sc. disciplines spanning aquaculture, fisheries resource management, post-harvest technology, fish genetics and breeding, fish biotechnology, aquatic animal health management, nutrition and feed technology, physiology and biochemistry, economics, extension and aquatic environmental management.

For the 2026–27 national postgraduate cycle, ICAR announced AIEEA (PG)-2026 registration from May 8, 2026 through June 7, 2026 at 5:00 pm. This is dated cycle-specific context rather than a recurring deadline; candidates should use the current ICAR/NTA notice for future application windows, eligibility, seats and scholarships.
bullets: Compare M.F.Sc. specialisations against intended work in aquaculture, hatchery/seed production, aquatic animal health, processing and quality systems, fisheries management, extension or research.
For a research pathway after postgraduate study, ICAR also runs the AICE-JRF/SRF (Ph.D.) process; eligibility and fellowship details must be verified in the relevant year’s bulletin.

useful_links.label: ICAR minimum requirements for fisheries education

title: B.F.Tech (Bachelor of Fashion Technology)
description: An undergraduate degree focusing on the technological and managerial aspects of apparel production and the fashion industry.

quick_facts.label: Official programme name
quick_facts.value: At the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), the degree is offered as Bachelor of Fashion Technology (Apparel Production), or B.F.Tech.

quick_facts.label: Duration
quick_facts.value: NIFT describes B.F.Tech (Apparel Production) as a four-year undergraduate programme.

quick_facts.label: Core eligibility
quick_facts.value: For regular entry, applicants need a recognised 10+2/equivalent qualification with Physics and Mathematics; the 2026 UG age limit was under 24 years on 1 August 2026, with a five-year relaxation for SC/ST/PwD candidates.

quick_facts.label: Entrance route
quick_facts.value: For NIFT Admissions 2026, B.F.Tech selection was based on the computer-based General Ability Test (GAT); there was no CAT, Situation Test, or interview for B.F.Tech regular admission.

quick_facts.label: Career orientation
quick_facts.value: The programme is oriented to apparel-manufacturing and techno-managerial work, including production planning, merchandising, quality control, supply chain, industrial engineering, product development, and entrepreneurship.

sections.heading: Eligibility for regular B.F.Tech entry
paragraphs: For NIFT’s 2026 regular B.F.Tech (Apparel Production) admission, candidates needed to have passed Class 12/10+2 or an accepted equivalent with both Physics and Mathematics. Accepted routes included a recognised central/state board, the National Open School senior-secondary examination with at least five subjects, an AIU-recognised equivalent, or GCE A-level/International Baccalaureate qualifications with Physics and Mathematics. Candidates taking their qualifying board examination in the admission year could apply provisionally, subject to meeting the requirements at seat allocation/admission.

For the 2026 admission cycle, the upper-age condition for UG programmes was that the candidate be under 24 on 1 August 2026; SC, ST and PwD candidates received a five-year relaxation. Eligibility policies can change by admission year, so applicants should use the current NIFT prospectus rather than relying on the 2026 conditions.
bullets: Physics and Mathematics are required for the regular B.F.Tech route; a general Class 12 qualification without those subjects does not meet this stated requirement.

NIFT also publishes a separate lateral-entry route. Its stated B.F.Tech lateral-entry criteria include a relevant 3- or 4-year diploma after Class 10, or qualifying Class 12 with Physics and Mathematics plus completion of NIFT’s two-year UG diploma programme.

sections.heading: Programme duration and academic character
paragraphs: B.F.Tech (Apparel Production) at NIFT is a four-year undergraduate programme. It is technology-oriented and multidisciplinary, built around the apparel business and the operational realities of apparel manufacturing rather than being solely a fashion-design degree.
The programme includes a final-year graduation project intended to address real-world problems in apparel design and development, manufacturing, or related areas.
bullets: Award: Bachelor of Fashion Technology (Apparel Production).
Study level: undergraduate.
Published duration: four years.

sections.heading: What students study
paragraphs: NIFT describes the B.F.Tech curriculum as combining apparel-production technology with managerial and business foundations. Its 2026 prospectus identifies mandatory study in apparel production technology, production planning, pattern making, fashion marketing, sourcing and costing; NIFT also states that specialised machinery and IT laboratories support hands-on learning.

The published programme description additionally identifies fabrics and trims, apparel machinery, quality management, information technology, artificial intelligence, work study, merchandising, production planning and quality control as important areas. Students may have opportunities for interdisciplinary minors across fields such as Fashion Management Studies, Fashion Design, Fashion Communication and Accessory Design, subject to NIFT’s academic offerings and rules.
bullets: Manufacturing and operations: apparel-production technology, machinery, production planning and control.
Commercial and supply functions: sourcing, costing, merchandising and fashion marketing.
Quality and process improvement: quality management/control, work study and industrial/operational practices.
Applied learning: laboratories and a final-year problem-oriented graduation project.

sections.heading: Admission through the NIFT Entrance Examination
paragraphs: For the 2026 cycle, NIFT used the General Ability Test (GAT) as the sole regular-entry test for B.F.Tech. The official FAQ states that GAT is computer based and assesses quantitative ability, analytical ability, logical reasoning, English comprehension, general knowledge and current affairs; final B.F.Tech merit was based 100% on the GAT score.

This differs from B.Des admission: B.F.Tech candidates do not take the Creative Ability Test (CAT), Situation Test or interview for the regular B.F.Tech route. A candidate with Mathematics who also applied to B.Des could take CAT together with GAT and receive separate merit ranks for B.Des and B.F.Tech.

The 2026 NIFTEE application window ran from 8 December 2025 to 6 January 2026, with a late-fee window through 10 January 2026; the entrance examination was scheduled for 8 February 2026. These are past, cycle-specific dates and should not be used as a forecast for the next intake.
bullets: Apply through NIFT/NTA’s admissions process for the applicable year.
Take GAT for B.F.Tech regular admission.
Use the official prospectus, admissions page and counselling notices for current dates, seat matrix, category rules and document requirements.

sections.heading: Fees: published 2026 context
paragraphs: Fees are institution-, category- and year-specific. In NIFT’s 2026 prospectus, the published non-NRI regular fee schedule lists tuition of ₹150,000 per semester for 2026–27, alongside annual library, mediclaim/student-development and examination charges. The prospectus shows grand totals of ₹191,700 for the applicable first listed semester and ₹150,000 for the following semester, including the relevant one-time charges in the first amount.

The same published schedule states that NIFT may revise fees for any academic year. These figures should therefore be treated as dated 2026 admission context, not as a guaranteed total programme cost; housing, meals, travel, materials and other personal expenses are separate planning considerations unless specifically included in a current campus notice.
bullets: Published 2026–27 non-NRI tuition: ₹150,000 per semester.
Published first listed semester grand total: ₹191,700; following semester grand total: ₹150,000.
Confirm the current prospectus and campus-specific notices before paying or budgeting.

sections.heading: Career and further-study options
paragraphs: NIFT identifies apparel-manufacturing career paths including sampling-room coordinator, fit analyst, product-development manager, shop-floor manager, production planner/controller, merchandiser, supply-chain manager, retail planner, quality controller/quality-assurance professional, industrial engineer/manager, consultant and entrepreneur. These describe possible role directions rather than guaranteed placement outcomes.

For further study at NIFT, a B.F.Tech is an eligible qualification for M.F.Tech. NIFT’s 2026 rules also state that an undergraduate degree in any discipline can meet the academic eligibility for M.F.M, subject to the programme’s entrance and admission process. Graduates interested in building a fashion label or consultancy can also use the production, sourcing, costing, quality and merchandising capabilities developed in the programme; NIFT notes that some B.F.Tech graduates establish clothing brands, technical-textile businesses, consultancy firms and apparel-technology ventures.
bullets: Employment directions: apparel production, quality assurance, sourcing/merchandising, product development, operations and supply chain.
Entrepreneurship direction: fashion label, manufacturing-linked venture, consultancy or apparel-technology business.
Further study direction: M.F.Tech; M.F.M is also academically open to holders of an undergraduate degree, subject to current NIFT requirements.

title: B.Pharm (Bachelor of Pharmacy)
description: Four-year undergraduate pharmacy degree; leads to pharmacist licensure, pharma industry roles, and M.Pharm.

quick_facts.label: Credential and standard duration
quick_facts.value: B.Pharm is a four-year pharmacy degree after 10+2 in the Pharmacy Council of India (PCI) framework.

quick_facts.label: Professional-registration relevance
quick_facts.value: For pharmacist registration, the B.Pharm qualification must be from an institution/course approved by PCI under section 12 of the Pharmacy Act, 1948; registration itself is administered by the relevant State Pharmacy Council, not PCI.

quick_facts.label: Typical school-subject preparation
quick_facts.value: Physics, Chemistry and Biology or Mathematics are a common prerequisite pattern. For example, BITS Pilani's 2026 B.Pharm admission eligibility requires Class 12 Physics, Chemistry and Biology/Mathematics, plus a language and one additional subject.

quick_facts.label: Admission routes vary by institution and state
quick_facts.value: B.Pharm admission is not governed by one all-India entrance route: BITS Pilani uses BITSAT for its B.Pharm intake, while WBJEE-2026 is an entrance examination for undergraduate pharmacy admissions in participating West Bengal institutions.

quick_facts.label: Fees are variable
quick_facts.value: PCI does not regulate student admission fees; fee setting is handled by the concerned Central or State Government. As a dated high-fee example, BITS Pilani listed ₹2,91,500 semester tuition for its first-degree programmes, including B.Pharm, for academic year 2026–27, before applicable hostel, mess and other charges.

sections.heading: Eligibility: build from Class 12 science, then check the target institute’s rules
paragraphs: PCI identifies the Bachelor of Pharmacy (B.Pharm) Course Regulations, 2014 as the governing regulation for B.Pharm admission qualifications. Applicants should treat the chosen college’s current prospectus and counselling rules as decisive, because entrance tests, marks thresholds, domicile rules and reservation requirements differ by institution and state.

A representative 2026 institutional rule is BITS Pilani’s: B.Pharm applicants need Class 12 under the 10+2 system with Physics, Chemistry and Biology or Mathematics, a language and an additional subject. BITS requires at least 75% aggregate in Physics, Chemistry and Biology/Mathematics and 60% in each of those subjects; applicants entering through PCB must have Class 10 mathematics proficiency. These are BITS-specific requirements, not a universal national cutoff.
bullets: Before applying, confirm that the programme is B.Pharm and that the institution has the PCI approval status needed for registration as a pharmacist.
Check the exact academic-year eligibility and counselling bulletin for every target college; do not assume that qualifying one entrance examination guarantees eligibility everywhere.

sections.heading: Duration and regulatory status
paragraphs: B.Pharm is structured as a four-year course after 10+2. It is one of the pharmacy qualifications PCI lists as approved for the purpose of pharmacist registration when completed at an institution approved under section 12 of the Pharmacy Act, 1948.

This approval distinction matters. PCI states that a B.Pharm course may be conducted only in institutions approved by it under section 12 for this purpose. A prospective student should verify the particular college and academic-session approval rather than relying only on advertising, university affiliation or the course title.
bullets: Study length: four years after Class 12.
Licensure pathway: apply to the State Pharmacy Council after completing an eligible, PCI-approved qualification and meeting the applicable statutory conditions.
State Pharmacy Councils handle registration, renewal and transfer of pharmacist registration.

sections.heading: Curriculum: PCI-prescribed syllabus delivered through the university or examining authority
paragraphs: The PCI approval scheme states that the syllabus for each B.Pharm subject is prescribed by PCI from time to time under regulation 8 of the Bachelor of Pharmacy (B.Pharm) Course Regulations, 2014. The detailed semester sequence, examination scheme, academic calendar and local implementation are set through the relevant university or examining authority within that regulatory framework.

When comparing colleges, ask for the current scheme of study, laboratory access, practical training arrangements, examination regulations and the exact PCI approval status for the intake year. These checks are more useful than assuming all programmes with a similar title provide the same delivery conditions.
bullets: Use the current university syllabus—not an old coaching syllabus or brochure—as the working academic reference.
Confirm PCI approval and university affiliation before paying fees or accepting a seat.

sections.heading: Admission: use the route required by the target college
paragraphs: Admissions are decentralised. For 2026–27, BITS Pilani offered B.Pharm admissions through BITSAT, while the West Bengal Joint Entrance Examinations Board conducted WBJEE-2026 for undergraduate pharmacy admissions in participating universities, government colleges and self-financing institutes in West Bengal. Other institutions and state counselling systems can use different entrance examinations, merit rules or processes.

Application windows and counselling dates are time-sensitive. For context, WBJEE-2026 registration ran from March 10 to April 8, 2026, and its examination was held on May 24, 2026. Those dates are historical as of July 19, 2026 and should not be reused for a later cycle.
bullets: Make a target-college list first, then identify the applicable examination or counselling authority for each institution.
Read the current information bulletin for eligibility, seat categories, document verification, choice filling and fee-refund rules.
For BITS, BITSAT is the stated admission test for B.Pharm; BITS also publishes separate eligibility and fee documents for its own cycle.

sections.heading: Costs: compare official fee schedules rather than relying on national averages
paragraphs: There is no single PCI-set B.Pharm tuition fee: PCI explicitly says that institutional admission fees are not regulated by PCI and are handled by the concerned Central or State Government. Fees therefore vary substantially by state, institution type, quota, residence/hostel status and annual revision policy.

As a dated example only, BITS Pilani’s 2026–27 first-degree fee schedule—covering B.Pharm—listed ₹64,100 admission fee and ₹2,91,500 semester tuition for the first and second semesters, plus separate annual, hostel, mess/electricity and other charges where applicable. BITS states that tuition and hostel fees are revised upward annually for that cohort. This is not a benchmark for government, state-counselling or other private colleges.
bullets: Request the official current-year fee circular and identify tuition, one-time admission charges, hostel, mess, examination, transport and refundable deposits separately.
Ask whether quoted fees cover all four years or only the first academic year, and whether scholarships or tuition-fee-waiver seats have separate eligibility rules.

sections.heading: What B.Pharm can lead to
paragraphs: A PCI-approved B.Pharm can support the pharmacist-registration route. The graduate applies to the appropriate State Pharmacy Council; PCI notes that State Pharmacy Councils, rather than PCI, carry out registration, renewal and transfers. The statutory framework also requires the applicant to meet applicable age, residence/business-or-profession-in-the-state, fee and approved-qualification conditions.

For postgraduate study, PCI lists M.Pharm as a two-year course after B.Pharm. NIPERs offer postgraduate M.Pharm, M.S. (Pharm.), M.Tech. (Pharm.) and MBA (Pharm.) programmes, with admissions through the NIPER JEE process. The 2026 NIPER JEE cycle covered master's programmes, so candidates should consult the current brochure and programme-specific eligibility rather than assume every B.Pharm degree fits every specialization.

B.Pharm is also relevant to drug-regulatory career paths, but it does not by itself guarantee appointment as a Drug Inspector. The Drugs Rules, 1945 include pharmacy/pharmaceutical-chemistry degree qualifications for specified inspector appointments, while the exact recruiting authority, experience conditions, examination and vacancies are determined by the applicable recruitment notification. Graduates may also pursue industry, sales and entrepreneurship roles, or use their bachelor's degree for broader examinations such as management and civil-services pathways, subject to the separate eligibility rules of those examinations.
bullets: Pharmacist: complete an eligible PCI-approved B.Pharm and apply through the relevant State Pharmacy Council.
M.Pharm and research-oriented postgraduate routes: consider GPAT where required or useful, and NIPER JEE for eligible NIPER master's programmes.
Drug Inspector: monitor official central or state recruitment notices and verify their current qualification and experience requirements.
Management, civil services and entrepreneurship: these are separate pathways; their selection rules are not part of B.Pharm licensure.

PCI: approved B.Pharm degree institutions under section 12

title: B.Plan (Bachelor of Planning)
description: A four-year undergraduate professional degree program focused on urban planning, regional planning, and resource management.

quick_facts.label: Credential and focus
quick_facts.value: B.Plan (Bachelor of Planning) is an undergraduate planning degree. At SPA New Delhi, it is designed around understanding and planning human settlements and includes physical, social, economic and political dimensions of cities and regions.

quick_facts.label: Typical duration
quick_facts.value: A representative B.Plan programme at SPA New Delhi is four years and eight semesters.

quick_facts.label: Main national entrance paper
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, JEE (Main) Paper 2B is the B.Planning paper; it tests Mathematics, Aptitude and Planning-Based Questions in computer-based mode.

quick_facts.label: NATA clarification
quick_facts.value: NATA 2026 is described by the Council of Architecture as an aptitude test for B.Arch admission, not as the national qualifying test for B.Plan. Applicants should therefore verify the entrance route specified by each B.Plan institute.

quick_facts.label: NIT+ eligibility context
quick_facts.value: For admission to NIT+ programmes through JEE (Main) Paper 2B in 2026, the qualifying examination requires Mathematics plus four other subjects. The JEE bulletin separately states that B.Plan candidates should have at least 50% in Mathematics and 50% aggregate in the qualifying examination; institute-specific conditions can still apply.

sections.heading: Eligibility: mathematics is central, but confirm the admitting institute's rules
paragraphs: For the 2026 NIT+ admission framework, a candidate using the JEE (Main) Paper 2B rank must have passed the Class XII/equivalent qualifying examination with Mathematics and four additional subjects. The NTA bulletin also records a B.Plan benchmark of at least 50% marks in Mathematics and 50% aggregate in the qualifying examination. These are admission-context requirements rather than a substitute for the conditions published by the individual institute or counselling authority.

JEE (Main) examination eligibility is not identical to final admission eligibility. NTA explicitly directs candidates to the JoSAA/CSAB rules for NIT+ admissions and notes that authorities may modify eligibility, allocation rules and procedures. Check the current institute prospectus, reservation rules and counselling instructions before applying.

Do not assume that NATA, JEE Advanced or a particular state examination is interchangeable with JEE (Main) Paper 2B for B.Plan. NATA's 2026 brochure is expressly for B.Arch; JoSAA identifies JEE (Main) Paper IIB as the qualifying examination for B.Planning in the NIT+ system.
bullets: For JEE (Main) 2026 Paper 2B: Class XII/equivalent passed in 2024 or 2025, or appearing in 2026, was the examination-eligibility window stated by NTA.
For final B.Plan admission: verify qualifying-subject requirements, marks, category documentation, domicile/reservation rules and any institute-level restrictions.
For non-JoSAA colleges: use the institution's own admission notice; state/private university processes may differ.

sections.heading: Duration and academic structure
paragraphs: B.Plan is commonly delivered as a four-year undergraduate programme. SPA New Delhi describes its B.Plan as eight semesters, combining studios, field-based exercises, theory courses, internships and independent research in the final semester. Actual credit totals, internship timing, exit options and assessment rules depend on the university's current curriculum and ordinances.
bullets: Four years / eight semesters at SPA New Delhi.
SPA New Delhi describes eight studios, field-based exercises, about forty theory subjects and two six-week internships as elements of its programme model.
Some institutions also offer an integrated B.Plan–M.Plan option; this is distinct from the standalone four-year B.Plan.

sections.heading: What students study and do
paragraphs: A planning degree is not simply an architecture degree without a drawing test. SPA New Delhi describes B.Plan learning as analysis of physical, social, economic and political aspects of settlements and their interrelationships. Its students prepare layout, zonal, master, regional and functional plans, supported by data collection, analysis, interpretation and mapping.

The curriculum is studio-led and multidisciplinary. In the SPA example, students develop planning principles and tools alongside fieldwork, communication, teamwork and problem-solving. Institutions can organise courses differently, so applicants should read the current semester-wise syllabus rather than rely on a generic subject list.
bullets: Planning studios and field-based work.
Settlement, regional and functional planning exercises.
Data collection, analysis, mapping and interpretation.
Theory drawn from multiple disciplines, internships and final independent research.

sections.heading: Admission route: JEE (Main) Paper 2B and counselling
paragraphs: For the national NIT+ route in 2026, take JEE (Main) Paper 2B (B.Planning), then participate in the relevant seat-allocation process if eligible. JoSAA lists JEE (Main) 2026 B.Planning among its qualifying examinations and manages admissions for the NIT+ system through a single platform; a qualifying score does not itself guarantee a seat.

JEE (Main) Paper 2B is a three-hour computer-based test. For 2026 it comprised Mathematics, an Aptitude Test and Planning-Based Questions, with 100 questions and 400 total marks. This is materially different from Paper 2A (B.Arch), which includes a drawing test.

SPA New Delhi states that its B.Plan admissions are made through JEE, subject to eligibility and reservation. Other providers may use JEE Main ranks, state counselling or their own published process. Treat application dates, seat matrices, opening/closing ranks and fees as cycle-specific information, not permanent thresholds.
bullets: Select Paper 2B specifically when the target programme is B.Planning.
Keep Class X/XII records, category/EWS/PwD documentation and other counselling documents current.
Use official NTA, JoSAA/CSAB and institute notices for the relevant admission year.

sections.heading: Costs: examples are dated and institution-specific
paragraphs: Fees vary substantially by institution, category, hostel choice, scholarship status and academic year. As a dated public-institution example only, SPA New Delhi's revised 2024–25 undergraduate fee notice for B.Arch and B.Plan students in the second, fourth, sixth and eighth semesters listed ₹47,600 for students other than SC/ST and ₹27,600 for SC/ST students. The listed components were tuition, academic support and student-activity fees.

That notice should not be treated as a four-year cost, a first-semester quote, a hostel/living-cost estimate or a current 2026–27 fee schedule. Obtain the current fee notice from each shortlisted institute and separately budget for accommodation, software/equipment, travel, studio materials and examination/counselling charges where applicable.
bullets: SPA New Delhi example, academic session 2024–25: ₹47,600 for all except SC/ST; ₹27,600 for SC/ST, for the semesters covered by the notice.
JEE (Main) 2026 Paper 2B application fees were separately prescribed by NTA and varied by candidate category, gender and test-centre location.
Always distinguish entrance-exam fees from tuition and living costs.

sections.heading: After B.Plan: postgraduate study and planning-related work
paragraphs: A common academic progression is M.Plan. SPA New Delhi offers M.Plan specialisations including Environmental Planning, Housing, Regional Planning, Transport Planning and Urban Planning, and it also gives B.Plan entrants an option to enter an integrated B.Plan–M.Plan programme under its own rules.

For postgraduate entrance preparation, GATE 2026 includes Architecture and Planning (AR). In the AR paper, candidates choose either the Architecture or Planning optional section; the Planning option is directly relevant for many planning-focused postgraduate pathways, but every admitting department sets its own eligibility and score requirements.

B.Plan graduates can pursue roles across public, private and third-sector organisations. SPA New Delhi identifies work areas including urban and regional planning, housing, transportation and design. Job titles such as Urban Planner, GIS Analyst or Assistant Town Planner are employer- and recruitment-rule-specific, so candidates should match their skills, software portfolio and any required experience to the particular vacancy.
bullets: M.Plan and, where offered, integrated B.Plan–M.Plan routes.
GATE Architecture and Planning (AR), with the Planning optional section.
Planning, housing, transport, urban/regional development, GIS/mapping and consultancy-oriented work.
MBA or public-service examinations are possible broader career choices, but their eligibility and selection requirements are governed independently by the relevant examination body or employer.

title: B.S.W. LL.B. (Hons.)
description: A five-year integrated undergraduate degree program combining Bachelor of Social Work and Bachelor of Laws with honours, focusing on social justice and human rights law.

quick_facts.label: Award and level
quick_facts.value: B.S.W. LL.B. (Hons.) is a five-year integrated undergraduate honours law degree that combines Bachelor of Social Work and Bachelor of Laws study. Gujarat National Law University (GNLU) lists it among its five-year integrated UG honours programmes for academic year 2026–27.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry qualification
quick_facts.value: For GNLU’s UG law programmes, applicants need 10+2/HSC or an equivalent qualification with at least 45% aggregate marks; the published threshold is 40% for SC/ST candidates. Candidates awaiting their qualifying result may be considered provisionally, subject to producing the required documents at admission.

quick_facts.label: Admission route
quick_facts.value: CLAT is the principal entrance route for the 2026–27 GNLU programme. The CLAT 2026 GNLU brochure specifically includes B.S.W. LL.B. (Hons.) in the university’s UG offerings and programme-wise seat allocation.

quick_facts.label: Practice pathway
quick_facts.value: To pursue practice as an advocate, graduates should confirm that their particular law course and institution hold the required Bar Council of India recognition/approval. BCI states that AIBE eligibility is limited to graduates or final-semester students of BCI-recognised universities or BCI-approved affiliated colleges; clearing AIBE leads to a certificate of practice.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: This is an entry-after-Class-12 integrated law programme, not a postgraduate law course. At GNLU, the published requirement for its five-year UG programmes is successful completion of HSC/Intermediate (10+2) or an equivalent examination with at least 45% aggregate marks, reduced to 40% for SC/ST candidates. Students appearing in the qualifying examination can be admitted provisionally, but must submit the requisite qualification documents before or at admission.

The relevant all-India entrance baseline for CLAT 2026 was also 45% in 10+2 or equivalent, or 40% for SC/ST/PwD applicants, with no upper age limit. Individual university, category, domicile, NRI/foreign-national and reservation rules can add conditions, so applicants should use the university’s current admission brochure rather than treating the general CLAT rule as a guaranteed offer of admission.
bullets: Check both the CLAT eligibility page and the target university’s programme-specific brochure.
For an advocate-practice plan, verify BCI recognition/approval for the specific institution and course before enrolling.

sections.heading: Duration and structure
paragraphs: The degree is structured as a five-year integrated honours programme, normally delivered across ten semesters. GNLU’s published undergraduate structure identifies the programme as part of its five-year BA/B.Com/BBA/B.Sc./BSW LL.B. (Hons.) suite and sets out courses from Semester 1 through Semester 10.

Because an integrated law degree is professionally consequential, prospective students should distinguish the programme title from professional eligibility: a degree alone does not remove the need to satisfy State Bar Council enrolment requirements and the applicable AIBE rules if the objective is court practice.
bullets: Academic duration: five years / ten semesters in the published GNLU structure.
Professional practice: separate enrolment and qualifying-examination requirements apply.

sections.heading: Curriculum: social work alongside core law
paragraphs: The defining feature is the integration of social-work learning with a full law curriculum. In GNLU’s published structure, early B.S.W.-specific papers include Nature and Development of Social Work, Social Work Methods and Interventions, Psychology for Social Work Practice, Sociology for Social Work Practice, Society and Sustainable Development, and Disaster Risk Management. Later components include Social Entrepreneurship, Livelihoods and Access to Justice, Social Work Research, Corporate Social Responsibility, Accountability and Audit, and Criminal Justice and Social Work.

The law component covers foundational and professional subjects including legal methods, torts, contract, constitutional law, jurisprudence, criminal law, family law, public international law, property, civil and criminal procedure, evidence, administrative law, corporate law, intellectual property, labour law, environmental law, human rights and international humanitarian law. The final year includes clinical papers in drafting, professional ethics, moot-court/advocacy skills, internship, litigation management and alternative dispute resolution, alongside electives.

Course names and sequencing are university-specific and may be revised. The list above describes GNLU’s published curriculum rather than a mandatory national syllabus for every programme using this degree title.
bullets: Social-work emphasis: development, livelihoods, access to justice, CSR, criminal justice and research.
Law emphasis: public law, private law, criminal justice, labour and environmental law, human rights, and clinical skills.
Practical components: drafting, professional ethics, mooting, advocacy and internship.

sections.heading: Admission through CLAT and university allocation
paragraphs: For the 2026–27 cycle, GNLU’s official CLAT brochure lists B.S.W. LL.B. (Hons.) at its Gandhinagar campus and shows programme-wise allocation. The brochure lists 26 total seats for the B.S.W. LL.B. (Hons.) programme: 23 All India, with additional seats shown for NRI/NRI-sponsored, foreign-national, Jammu and Kashmir resident, and North East India categories. Seat matrices, reservation rules and supernumerary categories are admissions-cycle-specific and can change.

CLAT is the relevant parent entrance examination for this node. The Consortium states that admissions offers and allotments are provisional and that participating universities may change intake and seat break-ups under their own policies. Applicants should therefore follow the live CLAT counselling instructions and the university’s admissions notices for the applicable year, rather than relying on prior cut-offs or dates.
bullets: Take the UG CLAT and complete the counselling/preference process for participating institutions.
Review the target university’s category, domicile and documentation requirements.
Treat seat numbers, counselling dates and fee notices as dated admissions-cycle information.

sections.heading: Next options after graduation
paragraphs: LL.M. is a direct academic progression. For CLAT 2026 PG, the Consortium’s baseline eligibility was an LL.B. or equivalent with 50% marks, or 45% for SC/ST/PwD candidates; particular universities may publish their own intake, specialisation and admission rules. The integrated B.S.W. LL.B. (Hons.) includes an LL.B. component, but applicants should still confirm that their degree meets the target institution’s stated LL.M. eligibility.

For litigation and advocacy, the relevant professional route is enrolment with a State Bar Council followed by the applicable AIBE process. BCI describes AIBE as a qualifying examination for advocates and states that candidates who clear it receive a certificate of practice. BCI’s current notices also stress that the underlying university/course must be BCI-recognised or BCI-approved, as applicable.

The degree can also support competitive and employment pathways such as judicial-services examinations, UPSC and state civil services, JAG recruitment, PSU legal-officer roles, corporate counsel, and management admissions such as CAT. These are not automatic outcomes of the degree: eligibility, age limits, enrolment status, experience, marks and selection stages are set separately by each state commission, employer, armed-forces recruitment notice, PSU or management institute. For example, UPSC’s Civil Services Examination is notified separately each year, and its 2026 preliminary notification was published on February 4, 2026.
bullets: LL.M.: check the relevant university’s LL.M. rules and, where used, CLAT PG requirements.
Advocacy: verify BCI recognition/approval, enrol with the appropriate State Bar Council, and meet AIBE requirements.
Judicial services and State PSC: use the notification of the relevant state; rules are state-specific.
UPSC, JAG, PSU/legal-employer, CAT and corporate-counsel routes: apply only against the current official notice or employer specification.

title: B.Sc (Bachelor of Science)
description: Three-to-four-year undergraduate science degree across physical, life, and applied sciences; leads to M.Sc, research, teaching and applied-sector roles.

quick_facts.label: Award and academic level
quick_facts.value: B.Sc. is an undergraduate science degree. Its precise award title, subject combination, duration, credit pattern and exit options are determined by the university or college; UGC’s current undergraduate framework supports flexible, multidisciplinary, choice-based study and multiple entry/exit arrangements.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry qualification
quick_facts.value: Entry is normally after Class 12/equivalent, but required subjects and minimum marks are programme-specific. For example, Physics-focused and physical-science B.Sc. routes may require Physics and Mathematics, while life-science routes may require Biology/PCB; applicants must verify the chosen programme’s rules.

quick_facts.label: Admissions
quick_facts.value: CUET-UG is a major admission route for B.Sc. programmes at participating institutions, but a CUET score alone does not establish eligibility or admission: universities set their own programme requirements, subject combinations, counselling and selection rules.

quick_facts.label: Further study route
quick_facts.value: A B.Sc. can lead to M.Sc., M.Sc.-Ph.D., joint M.Sc.-Ph.D. and integrated Ph.D. pathways. IIT JAM is one national route; its 2026 admissions brochure states that candidates need an undergraduate degree or final-year status and must meet programme-specific minimum educational qualifications.

sections.heading: Eligibility: Class 12 science background, with subject requirements tied to the B.Sc. discipline
paragraphs: There is no single India-wide eligibility rule for every B.Sc. programme. The baseline is generally a recognised Class 12/equivalent qualification, but the required subjects, marks, age conditions where applicable, category relaxations and accepted boards are set by the admitting institution and can differ sharply by discipline.

For example, CUET programme listings show that Mathematics is central to many physical-science, mathematics and electronics combinations, while Biology is expected for programmes such as microbiology and biotechnology. Some applied B.Sc. programmes accept either PCM or PCB, whereas regulated or health-linked programmes may prescribe additional subjects, English or age requirements.

Before applying, match all three items—not just the course title: (1) the university’s Class 12 subject prerequisites, (2) the entrance-test subject combination if an entrance test is used, and (3) the applicable category/document requirements.
bullets: PCM is commonly relevant for Physics, Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science and many physical-science programmes.
PCB is commonly relevant for Botany, Zoology, Microbiology, Biotechnology and other life-science programmes.
A science-stream background does not automatically make a candidate eligible for every B.Sc.; a university may require a particular subject studied and/or tested at Class 12 level.

sections.heading: Duration: distinguish a three-year bachelor’s degree from four-year honours pathways
paragraphs: In India, applicants should not treat “B.Sc.” as one uniform duration. Under the National Credit Framework, a three-year bachelor’s degree and a four-year bachelor’s degree with Honours/Honours with Research are distinct undergraduate outcomes. UGC’s Curriculum and Credit Framework for Undergraduate Programmes also provides for flexible credit-based, multidisciplinary study and multiple entry/exit arrangements.

Accordingly, confirm the exact award printed in the prospectus: B.Sc./B.Sc. Programme, B.Sc. (Hons.), or B.Sc. (Hons. with Research), as well as the number of semesters and the institution’s exit and re-entry rules. These details can affect later postgraduate eligibility and the depth of research preparation.
bullets: Three-year and four-year pathways should be compared by award title, major, credits, research component and the postgraduate programmes they support—not by the abbreviation “B.Sc.” alone.
Multiple entry/exit is a framework feature; its operational availability and conditions must be checked with the specific institution.

sections.heading: Curriculum: a science major plus practical, interdisciplinary and skill-oriented learning
paragraphs: The content of a B.Sc. is discipline-led rather than nationally identical. A Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Botany, Zoology, Computer Science, Statistics, Environmental Science or Biotechnology B.Sc. will have different core papers and laboratory/practical requirements. Under UGC’s CCFUP, undergraduate curricula are intended to use a flexible choice-based credit system and a multidisciplinary approach.

When comparing institutions, inspect the published semester-wise scheme for: core and elective papers, laboratory or fieldwork hours, mathematics/statistics/computing requirements, internship or research opportunities, assessment pattern and whether the final year includes a research project. These elements are more informative than a broad course label when planning for M.Sc. or technical roles.
bullets: Physical-science programmes commonly align their admission subject combinations around Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics.
Life-science programmes commonly align around Physics, Chemistry and Biology.
The exact syllabus, practical exposure and elective choices remain institution- and specialisation-specific.

sections.heading: Admission: use the institution’s route and choose entrance subjects strategically
paragraphs: B.Sc. admissions may be based on Class 12 merit, CUET-UG, or an institution-specific process. For CUET-UG participating institutions, the National Testing Agency conducts the examination, while participating universities retain responsibility for programme eligibility, subject mapping, counselling, merit preparation and final admission.

For the 2026 cycle, NTA published a CUET-UG information bulletin and application notices for undergraduate admission to participating central, state, deemed and private universities. Since admission calendars, seat matrices, subject requirements and counselling portals are institution-specific and change by cycle, applicants should treat the relevant university prospectus as the controlling document.

A practical application sequence is: shortlist the B.Sc. specialisation first; read its Class 12 prerequisites; identify the exact CUET subject combination or other test required; apply within the institution’s process; then complete counselling/document verification if selected.
bullets: Do not select CUET subjects solely from a generic science-stream list; select the combination required by each target B.Sc. programme.
A qualifying entrance score does not override a university’s subject or minimum-mark requirements.
Check official notices for the relevant admission year because dates, participating institutions and programme mappings vary.

sections.heading: After B.Sc.: postgraduate science, research-oriented study, teacher education and broader graduate pathways
paragraphs: For science specialisation and research preparation, common next steps include M.Sc., M.Sc. (Tech), joint M.Sc.-Ph.D., M.Sc.-Ph.D. dual-degree and integrated Ph.D. programmes. IIT JAM is a prominent route for several such programmes at IITs and associated institutions; however, each programme specifies minimum educational qualifications, including the undergraduate subjects that must have been studied.

A B.Sc. can also be used as the qualifying bachelor’s degree for professional or competitive pathways whose own eligibility rules are separately set—for example, teacher education, management admissions and public recruitment. Eligibility must be checked afresh for each destination; a B.Sc. title alone does not guarantee subject eligibility for a particular M.Sc., B.Ed., NET or recruitment post.

For B.Ed. planning, NCTE materials specify bachelor’s/master’s marks requirements under the applicable regulations, while states and institutions may administer admission through their own processes. Candidates should verify the currently applicable NCTE rules and the target institution’s notification before relying on an older regulation or draft proposal.
bullets: For M.Sc. or research pathways, preserve transcripts and verify prerequisite undergraduate subjects early.
For JAM-linked programmes, admission requires both a qualifying JAM result and satisfaction of the admitting institute’s programme-specific educational requirements.
For teaching, laboratory, clinical/paramedical and other applied roles, verify any additional professional-regulator, licensing, internship or employer requirements.

title: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture
description: A four-year undergraduate degree program focusing on agricultural science, research, and modern farming techniques.

quick_facts.label: Award and status
quick_facts.value: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture is listed by ICAR as a four-year bachelor’s programme in Agricultural Sciences and as a professional degree for the 2026–27 ICAR admission cycle.

quick_facts.label: Typical length
quick_facts.value: The programme is normally four years across eight semesters; an official Anand Agricultural University B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture offering follows this structure.

quick_facts.label: ICAR all-India admission route
quick_facts.value: For 2026–27, ICAR uses CUET (ICAR-UG) for its all-India bachelor-degree admission process in Agriculture and Allied Sciences. It covers 20% of participating agricultural-university seats, with 100% coverage at certain named ICAR/central institutions; it is not the sole admission route for every B.Sc. Agriculture seat in India.

quick_facts.label: CUET (ICAR-UG) subject baseline
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 ICAR route, candidates must have passed Class 12 with at least three core subjects from Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology, and Agriculture/Inter-Agriculture, while the final subject combination and other conditions can differ by admitting university.

quick_facts.label: Practical learning
quick_facts.value: A representative agricultural-university curriculum includes laboratory and field-oriented courses and a final-year Student READY/RAWE-style placement, village/KVK attachment, agro-industry attachment, and experiential-learning components; exact credits and modules vary by university.

quick_facts.label: Choosing a college
quick_facts.value: ICAR publishes updated lists of accredited agricultural universities, colleges, and programmes. Applicants should verify both institutional/programme accreditation and the university’s own admission rules before accepting an offer.

sections.heading: Eligibility: Class 12 science/agriculture preparation is central
paragraphs: For admission through CUET (ICAR-UG) 2026, ICAR requires a recognised 10+2/equivalent qualification and at least three Class 12 core subjects selected from Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology, and Agriculture/Inter-Agriculture. Candidates must take CUET subjects consistent with their Class 12 subjects; a mismatch can make them ineligible for ICAR counselling.

The ICAR 2026 bulletin sets a minimum aggregate of 50% for General, OBC-NCL, UPS, and EWS candidates and 40% for SC, ST, Third Gender, and PwBD candidates for this ICAR route. It also sets a minimum age of 16 years as of August 31, 2026. These are ICAR-route rules, not a substitute for programme-specific eligibility set by an individual university.

University-level conditions matter. ICAR expressly notes that institutions may impose additional subject combinations, age limits, or other statutory conditions. For example, an agricultural university may use a state entrance examination for its state-seat admissions rather than the ICAR all-India route.
bullets: Before applying, compare your Class 12 subject combination with the target programme’s published requirement.
Treat ICAR/CUET eligibility as one admissions channel; check the target university’s prospectus for state quota, domicile, category, age, language, and counselling requirements.
Verify the exact programme title on the offer letter: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture is distinct from horticulture, forestry, agribusiness management, and other allied degrees.

sections.heading: Duration and academic format
paragraphs: ICAR’s 2026–27 undergraduate admission bulletin places B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture among 13 bachelor’s programmes of four-year duration. A typical delivery model is eight semesters, as illustrated by Anand Agricultural University’s four-year, eight-semester residential programme.

The final year is often heavily experiential rather than purely classroom-based. In AAU’s published structure, Semester VII is Student READY for 20 weeks and Semester VIII is an Experiential Learning Programme for 24 weeks. The names, sequence, and credit weights are university-specific, so applicants should use the curriculum issued by the college that will award their degree.
bullets: Nominal duration: four academic years.
Common format: eight semesters.
Expect practical, field, village-extension, research-station, and agro-industry exposure in addition to lectures and laboratories.

sections.heading: What students study
paragraphs: The curriculum is interdisciplinary: it combines crop and soil sciences with biological sciences, farm engineering, economics, extension, and management. In AAU’s published B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture curriculum, early study includes soil science, agricultural microbiology, agro-meteorology and climate change, horticulture, plant pathology, agricultural informatics, mathematics, agronomy, genetics, and agricultural economics.

Later study broadens into crop-production technology, entomology and integrated pest management, agricultural finance and cooperation, farm machinery, agricultural extension, plant breeding, agricultural marketing, seed technology, sustainable agriculture, geoinformatics and precision farming, biotechnology, organic farming, watershed management, entrepreneurship, post-harvest management, and value addition.

This is a representative official curriculum rather than a nationally identical semester-by-semester prescription. Students should compare the current syllabus of each shortlisted university, especially the amount of fieldwork, elective choice, Student READY/RAWE, internship, and experiential-learning provision.
bullets: Crop, soil, plant-health, genetics, horticulture, and livestock foundations.
Farm systems, water/soil conservation, machinery, climate, and precision-agriculture exposure.
Agricultural economics, finance, marketing, extension, rural sociology, communication, and entrepreneurship.
Applied training through village/KVK, research-station, and agro-industry attachments in programmes that include Student READY/RAWE or equivalent.

sections.heading: Admission routes: CUET (ICAR-UG) and university/state processes
paragraphs: For the 2026–27 ICAR all-India quota process, the relevant examination is CUET (ICAR-UG). ICAR states that eligible candidates register and fill choices for online counselling; allocation of a programme, seat, and agricultural university follows merit rank, choices, and fulfilment of eligibility conditions. ICAR also says that direct nomination is not available for admission through its route without qualifying CUET (ICAR-UG).

The phrase “ICAR AIEEA” remains useful historical shorthand for ICAR entrance admissions, but the current undergraduate bulletin titles the route CUET (ICAR-UG). ICAR’s AIEEA-PG nomenclature continues for postgraduate admission. Applicants should therefore follow the current year’s official notices rather than rely on older AIEEA-UG instructions.

Not every B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture seat is allotted through ICAR counselling. State agricultural universities may separately use state-level entrance tests and merit formulas for their own admissions. AAU’s published example uses GUJCET plus Higher Secondary marks for its common Gujarat agricultural-university procedure. Check the target university’s prospectus and counselling portal for its active route, dates, fee, documents, and seat category.
bullets: For ICAR all-India seats: follow the current CUET (ICAR-UG) bulletin, take the permitted CUET subject combination, and participate in ICAR online counselling if eligible.
For state/university seats: check the university’s own admissions notice; entrance tests and merit rules can differ materially.
Do not assume a CUET score alone guarantees admission: eligibility is checked by the admitting university and programme-specific conditions apply.

sections.heading: After graduation: higher study, public recruitment, agribusiness, and entrepreneurship
paragraphs: For subject specialisation and research, graduates can pursue M.Sc. programmes in Agriculture and allied disciplines. ICAR’s 2026–27 notice identifies AIEEA-PG as the all-India examination route for postgraduate degree programmes in Agriculture and Allied Sciences; the applicable annual information bulletin governs discipline eligibility, seats, scholarships, and counselling.

For agribusiness management, a four-year B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture can meet the academic-background requirement for programmes such as MANAGE’s PGDM (Agri-Business Management). Its 2026 policy accepts agriculture-science/agriculture-related bachelor’s degrees of at least four years, subject to minimum marks and a valid CAT score. Comparable MBA/PGDM programmes have their own selection rules.

For entrepreneurship, NABARD’s Agri-Clinic and Agri-Business Centres framework lists agriculture graduates from SAUs, CAUs, and ICAR/UGC-recognised universities among eligible beneficiaries. The scheme describes ventures such as custom hiring of farm equipment, input and advisory services, post-harvest management, and market-linkage services; finance, training, and subsidy availability must be confirmed under the live scheme rules.

For public-sector examinations, a B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture is an eligible bachelor’s degree background for the Indian Forest Service because UPSC specifically accepts a bachelor’s degree in Agriculture. Civil Services requires a recognised graduate degree; eligibility alone does not replace the annual age, attempt, nationality, examination, and application conditions. Agriculture is also an accepted four-year degree for IBPS Agricultural Field Officer (Scale I) in the CRP SPL-XVI notification. NABARD Grade A is a recruitment process whose advertised disciplines, vacancies, age limits, and degree criteria vary by notification, so candidates should use the current NABARD advertisement rather than assume a permanent agriculture-specific vacancy.
bullets: M.Sc. Agriculture and allied specialisations through university processes and, for ICAR’s all-India route, AIEEA-PG.
MBA/PGDM in Agri-Business Management, with institution-specific entrance-test, marks, and interview requirements.
Agri-entrepreneurship and advisory/service enterprises, including possible ACABC support where the current scheme rules are met.
Competitive recruitment pathways: UPSC Civil Services, UPSC Indian Forest Service, IBPS Agricultural Field Officer, and notification-dependent NABARD Grade A opportunities.

Private-sector roles may include agri-inputs, seed, crop-protection, farm advisory, procurement, food/value-chain, plantation, sales, and operations roles; the employer’s job description determines whether a bachelor’s degree alone is sufficient.

title: B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science
description: An undergraduate degree focusing on family and community well-being through nutrition, resource management, and human development, formerly known as Home Science.

quick_facts.label: Award and former name
quick_facts.value: B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science is a four-year professional undergraduate programme; ANGRAU describes it as previously known as Home Science.

quick_facts.label: ICAR admission route
quick_facts.value: For the 2026–27 ICAR all-India route, B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science is one of 13 four-year bachelor programmes available on merit in CUET (ICAR-UG)-2026.

quick_facts.label: Indicative school-subject requirement
quick_facts.value: For CUET (ICAR-UG)-2026, candidates must have passed Class 12 with at least three core subjects from Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology, and Agriculture/Inter-Agriculture; the participating university can impose additional programme-specific conditions.

quick_facts.label: Academic focus
quick_facts.value: The programme commonly combines food and nutrition, human development and family studies, apparel/textiles, resource management and consumer science, and extension/communication management.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: Eligibility depends on the admission channel and university. Under the ICAR CUET (ICAR-UG)-2026 route, an Indian-national applicant must have completed a recognised 10+2/Senior Secondary qualification and studied at least three core subjects drawn from Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology, and Agriculture/Inter-Agriculture. The bulletin sets the examination minimum age at 16 years on August 31, 2026; it also makes clear that admitting universities’ statutes and programme conditions continue to apply.

The ICAR bulletin’s university-wise Community Science table shows that accepted Class 12 subject combinations and age conditions can vary by institution. Applicants should therefore treat the central test criteria as a baseline and check the current counselling brochure and the target university’s prospectus before applying.
bullets: A diploma or vocational course taken after matriculation does not meet the ICAR bulletin’s qualifying-examination requirement for this route.

ICAR’s minimum standards for Community Science identify PCB, PCM, or PCMB at Intermediate/10+2 level as the baseline eligibility framework; individual institutions may publish broader or additional combinations for a particular admission year.

sections.heading: Duration and award structure
paragraphs: The full B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science degree is a four-year undergraduate programme. ICAR’s 2026–27 admission bulletin describes the associated bachelor programmes as four years in duration, and ANGRAU lists Community Science as a four-year professional course.

Under the ICAR Sixth Deans’ Committee framework, a completed four-year programme leads to the B.Sc. (Hons.) award. The framework also describes institutionally implemented multiple-entry/exit arrangements and a maximum seven-year period to complete the programme; learners should confirm how their specific university has implemented these provisions.

sections.heading: What students study
paragraphs: Community Science applies scientific, social, design, and communication perspectives to individual, family, and community well-being. A representative official faculty description identifies core study areas as foods and nutrition; human development and family studies; apparel design and textiles; resource management and consumer science; and extension education and communication management.

The precise course titles, credit mix, practical work, electives, internship requirements, and assessment rules are university-specific. At the national level, ICAR’s Sixth Deans’ Committee includes Community Science among the agricultural-science disciplines for which the curriculum and credit framework were restructured, while ICAR’s minimum standards identify corresponding departmental domains such as food science and nutrition, textiles/apparel, family-resource management, human development, and extension/communication.
bullets: Nutrition and food-related learning
Human development, family studies, and community engagement
Textiles, apparel design, and consumer/resource management
Extension education and communication management

sections.heading: Admission through ICAR and universities
paragraphs: For academic year 2026–27, the ICAR all-India admission pathway is CUET (ICAR-UG)-2026. ICAR states that the examination is used for admission to agriculture and allied-science bachelor programmes at agricultural universities, generally for 20% of university seats, with specified institutions having different seat coverage. Candidates qualifying for ICAR registration and counselling are considered for programme and university allocation.

Application for CUET (ICAR-UG)-2026 is online through the NTA CUET portal. ICAR states that there is no direct nomination for admission through ICAR without qualifying CUET (ICAR-UG)-2026. The January 2026 bulletin says that final 2026–27 seat numbers, subject eligibility, and special conditions will be published in the online counselling brochure, so applicants should not rely on the prior-year university table as final availability.

Universities may also publish their own admission notices. For example, ANGRAU displayed a 2026–27 B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science application notice with an August 10, 2026 deadline; this is a university-specific date, not an all-India deadline, and should be rechecked on the university site.
bullets: Take CUET subjects that match the subjects passed in Class 12; ICAR says a candidate taking different subjects will not be considered for counselling/admission.
Read the final ICAR online counselling brochure for current seats and conditions.
Read the target university’s own prospectus for campus-specific eligibility, reservations, fees, documents, and deadlines.

sections.heading: Further study and career directions
paragraphs: A Community Science graduate can progress to postgraduate specialisation in the field. ANGRAU states that graduates may pursue PG and PhD study in its core Community Science subject areas, and lists an M.Sc. (Community Science) programme. Its published eligibility also includes a four-year B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science among qualifying degrees for its MBA (Agribusiness) and its PG Diploma in Post-Harvest Technology, Food Safety, and Quality.

Career outcomes depend on an employer’s recruitment rules, location, further credentials, and experience. As examples of relevant sectors rather than guaranteed jobs, ANGRAU identifies roles including Child Development Project Officer/departmental supervisory and instructional work in women-and-child development and social welfare, and quality-control work in food and textile sectors. A graduate seeking titles such as nutritionist should separately verify any employer, state, hospital, or professional-registration requirements.
bullets: M.Sc. Community Science or a discipline-specific master’s pathway
Food, nutrition, quality-control, textile, community-development, and extension-related work
MBA/agribusiness or relevant postgraduate diploma pathways where the admitting institution accepts the degree
Research progression through a relevant master’s degree and PhD

title: B.Sc. (Hons.) Forestry
description: An undergraduate degree focused on the science and practice of managing forests, tree plantations, and related natural resources.

quick_facts.label: Qualification
quick_facts.value: B.Sc. (Hons.) Forestry is one of the 13 four-year bachelor’s degree programmes covered by ICAR’s CUET (ICAR-UG) 2026 admission bulletin; it is listed as programme code 04.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry subjects
quick_facts.value: For the CUET (ICAR-UG) 2026 route, candidates must have passed Class 12 with at least three core subjects from Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture/Inter-Agriculture. Individual universities can impose additional subject combinations, age limits or other conditions.

quick_facts.label: Academic focus
quick_facts.value: ICAR’s minimum standards identify core forestry areas including silviculture and agroforestry, forest biology and tree improvement, natural-resource management, forest-products utilization, wildlife sciences, and basic and social sciences.

quick_facts.label: National forest-service pathway
quick_facts.value: A bachelor’s degree in Forestry is expressly accepted as an educational qualification for the UPSC Indian Forest Service Examination, subject to the full annual examination rules.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: For admission through the ICAR quota in the 2026–27 cycle, applicants needed a recognized 10+2/equivalent qualification and at least three Class 12 core subjects drawn from Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture/Inter-Agriculture. They also had to take CUET subjects corresponding to those passed at Class 12; taking different subjects could lead to rejection during counselling or admission.

ICAR’s published minimum standards for establishing a B.Sc. (Hons.) Forestry college describe the expected entry background as Intermediate/10+2 with PCM, PCMB or Agriculture. Actual eligibility is not identical across all institutions: the ICAR bulletin lists programme-specific combinations and sometimes university-specific age or other requirements. Applicants should therefore verify the target university’s current prospectus before applying.
bullets: Check that your Class 12 subjects match both the CUET (ICAR-UG) requirements and the specific university/programme entry listed in the current ICAR counselling bulletin.
Treat university-level conditions, including subject combinations and age rules, as controlling for that institution.

sections.heading: Duration and award
paragraphs: In the ICAR CUET (ICAR-UG) 2026 bulletin, B.Sc. (Hons.) Forestry is among the bachelor’s programmes stated to have a four-year duration. The same bulletin identifies undergraduate agricultural-science degrees in this admission framework as professional degrees.
bullets: Standard ICAR admission-framework duration: 4 years.
Confirm the academic calendar, credit rules, internship/fieldwork requirements and exit provisions in the admitting university’s regulations.

sections.heading: What the programme covers
paragraphs: The degree is designed around scientific and applied forest-resource management rather than only tree identification or plantation work. ICAR’s forestry standards organize provision around silviculture and agroforestry; forest biology and tree improvement; natural-resource management; forest-products utilization; wildlife sciences; and basic and social sciences. The precise paper titles, practicals, credits and electives remain university-specific.

A university curriculum can additionally include applied areas such as wood science and technology, forest hydrology and watershed management, forest economics and marketing, forest extension and community forestry, forest law and policy, geomatics, restoration ecology, plantation forestry, and non-timber forest products. These examples illustrate curriculum variation rather than a nationwide compulsory paper list.
bullets: Expect a blend of biological sciences, resource management, field-oriented forestry and social/economic dimensions of forest use.
Compare the semester-wise syllabus and practical/field facilities before choosing a college; ICAR’s accreditation listings are a useful starting point for checking institutions and programmes.

sections.heading: Admission through ICAR
paragraphs: For the 2026–27 ICAR quota process, undergraduate admission is based on merit rank in CUET (ICAR-UG) 2026. B.Sc. (Hons.) Forestry is specifically included in that process, and the bulletin publishes participating universities, ICAR-quota seats, accepted Class 12 subject combinations and any special conditions by programme.

This is a route for ICAR quota counselling, not a guarantee that every Forestry college uses the same selection process. Candidates should check the target university’s own admission notice alongside the current CUET and ICAR counselling notices.
bullets: Use the current CUET (ICAR-UG) information bulletin to select eligible test subjects.
After results, follow ICAR’s counselling instructions and validate the programme-specific requirements for each preferred university.
For quality due diligence, consult ICAR’s current accreditation-programme listings in addition to a university’s own recognition and admission information.

sections.heading: Further study and competitive-examination options
paragraphs: A common academic progression is M.Sc. Forestry. ICAR’s AIEEA (PG) is the national entrance route used for postgraduate agriculture and allied-sciences admissions in the ICAR-AU system; eligibility, participating seats, scholarships and other requirements must be checked in that year’s NTA/ICAR information bulletin. For the 2026–27 cycle, ICAR announced AIEEA (PG) registration from May 8 to June 7, 2026, so that application window is already past as of July 18, 2026.

For public-service careers, B.Sc. (Hons.) Forestry meets the named degree-field requirement for the UPSC Indian Forest Service Examination. The 2026 UPSC notice states that candidates must first take and qualify through the Civil Services Preliminary Examination for progression to the Indian Forest Service Main examination, and all age, nationality, medical and other conditions in the relevant annual notice still apply.
bullets: M.Sc. Forestry / allied postgraduate study: monitor the next ICAR AIEEA (PG) notice and the target university’s programme requirements.
UPSC Indian Forest Service: Forestry is an accepted qualifying degree, but eligibility and examination rules must be checked against the notification for the year of application.
State Forest Service recruitment: review the relevant State Public Service Commission notification, because eligibility, selection stages and vacancies vary by state and recruitment cycle.
