title: B.Sc. (Hons.) Horticulture
description: An undergraduate degree specializing in the science of plant cultivation, including fruits, vegetables, flowers, and ornamental plants.

quick_facts.label: Award and level
quick_facts.value: B.Sc. (Hons.) Horticulture is a four-year undergraduate horticulture degree under the ICAR Sixth Deans’ Committee curriculum framework.

quick_facts.label: Indicative entry subjects
quick_facts.value: The ICAR curriculum framework specifies 10+2 Science with PCM, PCB, Agriculture or Horticulture, subject to the applicable norms of the admitting State Agricultural University (SAU), ICAR or higher agricultural education institution.

quick_facts.label: ICAR-all-India admission route
quick_facts.value: For the 2025 cycle, B.Sc. (Hons.) Horticulture was included among programmes for CUET (ICAR-UG). The bulletin required 10+2 with at least three core subjects from Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture/Inter-Agriculture; university-specific conditions could still apply.

quick_facts.label: Curriculum scale
quick_facts.value: The Sixth Deans’ Committee model allocates 167 graded credits plus 10 MOOCs credits, for a stated total of 177 credit hours; universities may modify an individual course by up to 30% with competent approval.

quick_facts.label: Practical learning
quick_facts.value: The model curriculum includes practical and skill courses, a study tour, and a 20-credit final-semester Student READY component that can include RAWE, industrial attachment, experiential learning, hands-on training, project work and internship.

quick_facts.label: Multiple-exit design
quick_facts.value: Under the proposed ICAR framework, students who complete the relevant requirements and a 10-week internship may exit after year 1 with a UG Certificate in Horticulture or after year 2 with a UG Diploma in Horticulture; the B.Sc. (Hons.) award follows completion of the four-year requirements.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: The national ICAR curriculum model describes first-year entry as 10+2 Science with PCM, PCB, Agriculture or Horticulture, while expressly leaving room for the rules of the relevant SAU, ICAR or higher agricultural education institution. Applicants should therefore treat a particular university’s prospectus as controlling.

For CUET (ICAR-UG) 2025, the official eligibility bulletin listed B.Sc. (Hons.) Horticulture and required candidates to have passed Class 12 with at least three core subjects chosen from Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture/Inter-Agriculture. It also prescribed 50% aggregate marks for General, OBC (NCL), UPS and EWS candidates and 40% for SC, ST, Third Gender and PwBD candidates. These are dated 2025-cycle requirements, not a substitute for the admission-year bulletin.
bullets: Confirm the university’s subject combination, domicile, category, age and any programme-specific requirements before applying.

Candidates using the 2025 ICAR counselling route had to take CUET subjects aligned with the subjects passed at Class 12; different examination subjects could result in rejection at counselling/admission.

sections.heading: Duration and qualification structure
paragraphs: The standard ICAR Sixth Deans’ Committee design is a four-year B.Sc. (Hons.) Horticulture programme. It specifies award of the degree after successful completion of the four-year requirements.

The framework also proposes NEP-aligned exit awards: a UG Certificate in Horticulture after the first year plus a 10-week internship, and a UG Diploma in Horticulture after the second year plus a 10-week internship. Whether and how these exits are operationalised should be checked with the admitting university.
bullets: Four-year degree completion: B.Sc. (Hons.) Horticulture.
Year 1 exit: UG Certificate in Horticulture, with the prescribed internship.
Year 2 exit: UG Diploma in Horticulture, with the prescribed internship.

sections.heading: What students study
paragraphs: The ICAR model spans horticultural production and management across fruit, vegetables, flowers, spices, plantation crops and nursery systems, alongside agricultural sciences, business and technology. Early courses include Fundamentals of Horticulture; plant propagation and nursery management; commercial flower, spice and plantation-crop production; irrigation; and entrepreneurship and business management.

Later coursework covers commercial fruit and vegetable production, protected cultivation and precision farming, horticultural crop disease and pest management, urban and peri-urban horticulture, farm machinery, agricultural informatics and artificial intelligence, breeding, soil fertility, climate change, processing and value addition. In the seventh semester, the model provides 20-credit elective pathways in Fruit Science, Vegetable Science, or Floriculture and Landscaping.

This is a national model curriculum rather than an identical syllabus guarantee: the Committee permits universities and higher agricultural education institutions to adapt individual courses, within stated limits and approvals.
bullets: Skill-enhancement courses are concentrated in the first two years.
A 10–14-day study tour is scheduled in semester 5 in the model.
Semester 8 is dedicated to Student READY practical exposure, such as RAWE, industrial attachment, experiential learning or internship.

sections.heading: Admission routes
paragraphs: Admission is institution-specific. For the ICAR all-India counselling route in 2025, B.Sc. (Hons.) Horticulture was offered through CUET (ICAR-UG), with online application through the NTA CUET-UG process and seat allotment through online counselling based on merit rank and fulfilment of eligibility requirements.

Not every horticulture university necessarily follows the same route. For example, Dr Y.S. Parmar University of Horticulture and Forestry described entrance-test-based admission for normal undergraduate seats and Class 12 marks in English, Physics, Chemistry and Biology/Mathematics for self-financing seats. This illustrates why applicants must read the current prospectus for each target institution rather than rely solely on the ICAR route.
bullets: For an ICAR counselling route, check the current NTA/ICAR information bulletin, subject selection rules, participating universities and counselling schedule.
For direct or state-university routes, check that university’s current prospectus for its entrance examination, merit criteria, reservations and fee payment process.
Do not rely on the 2025 dates, cut-offs or application windows; admissions calendars and participating institutions can change each cycle.

sections.heading: Further study, examinations and career directions
paragraphs: A common academic progression is postgraduate study through ICAR AIEEA (PG). NTA’s 2025 notice states that ICAR AIEEA (PG) is conducted for admission to postgraduate degree programmes; the relevant year’s bulletin determines discipline mapping, qualifying-degree requirements and other eligibility conditions.

The degree’s applied curriculum supports horticulture-enterprise and farm-management pathways, including nursery, plantation, protected-cultivation, production, post-harvest and value-addition work. The National Career Service describes horticulture management work as involving crop and soil/climate selection, resource procurement, cultivation supervision, harvesting and post-harvest management, business planning and worker supervision; it identifies farm owners and agricultural cooperatives as probable employers. The listed senior management occupation is experience-dependent, so it should not be read as an entry-level salary or placement guarantee.

Recruitment examinations must be checked notification by notification. IBPS’s current CRP-SPL XVI notification includes Agricultural Field Officer (Scale I), and NABARD’s 2025 Grade A material included a specialist Plantation and Horticulture mains syllabus. A B.Sc. (Hons.) Horticulture holder should verify the exact degree wording, age, nationality, marks and other conditions in the active notification before applying. State Horticulture Officer recruitment is likewise conducted under individual state notifications rather than one uniform national examination.
bullets: Postgraduate route: ICAR AIEEA (PG), subject to that cycle’s eligibility and counselling rules.
Banking/rural-finance route: IBPS Agricultural Field Officer or NABARD Grade A only where the active notification accepts the candidate’s qualification.
Enterprise route: nursery, protected cultivation, plantation/farm operations, value addition and agribusiness; practical experience and local licences/compliance may be required.

National Career Service — General Manager Horticulture occupation profile

title: B.Sc. in Emergency Medical Technology
description: An undergraduate allied-health degree preparing students for advanced emergency, trauma, ambulance, and critical-care technical practice.

quick_facts.label: Award and naming
quick_facts.value: This undergraduate allied-health pathway is offered under closely related titles, including B.Sc. in Emergency Medical Technology, B.Sc. Emergency and Trauma Care Technology, and Bachelor of Emergency Medical Technologist (Paramedic); applicants should verify the exact award title and curriculum at the admitting institution.

quick_facts.label: Typical duration
quick_facts.value: Published institutional structures commonly specify four years, generally described as three academic years plus a one-year internship, though the exact design should be checked in the university’s current regulations.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry qualification
quick_facts.value: A common requirement is Class 12 / 10+2 science with Physics, Chemistry and Biology; institutions may additionally set a minimum percentage, English requirement, age threshold, medical-fitness requirement, or category-specific relaxation.

quick_facts.label: Training focus
quick_facts.value: Published course descriptions combine emergency and trauma care with pre-hospital/ambulance practice, clinical education, life-support and airway skills, emergency equipment and procedures, and supervised internship or externship.

sections.heading: Eligibility: science at Class 12 is the usual route
paragraphs: There is no single admission rule demonstrated by the sources reviewed; each university publishes its own conditions. ICFAI University Tripura lists 10+2 science with PCB and 45% marks, with a stated relaxation for SC/ST/OBC candidates. Apollo University requires 10+2/equivalent science subjects and specifies 45% marks (40% for reserved-category candidates) plus age 17 by 31 December of the calendar year. Dr. D. Y. Patil Vidyapeeth specifies Physics, Chemistry and Biology/Botany and Zoology, age 17 by admission or by 31 December, and a government-medical-officer-endorsed fitness certificate.

Applicants should treat the programme brochure and the university’s current admissions notice—not a generic course listing—as controlling. Required subject combinations, percentage thresholds, age cut-offs, equivalency treatment, category rules, and fitness documentation can differ by institution and admission cycle.
bullets: Prepare Class 10 and Class 12 certificates/marksheets, identity and category/domicile documents where applicable, and any medical-fitness documentation requested by the university.
If applying with a diploma or for lateral entry, confirm that the institution recognises the qualification and specifies the required prior instructional hours.

sections.heading: Duration and clinical training
paragraphs: A four-year structure is the clearest recurring model in the reviewed institutional sources. Dr. D. Y. Patil Vidyapeeth describes its undergraduate B.Sc. structure as three years plus one year of internship; ICFAI University Tripura describes a four-year full-time programme with internship/externship and project in the fourth year; Apollo University describes its related Emergency and Trauma Care Technology programme as four years.

Because the academic and internship calendars are institution-specific, candidates should check whether the internship is credit-bearing, whether it is arranged by the college, the clinical-site requirements, attendance rules, insurance/health requirements, and whether any additional fees apply.
bullets: Common published format: 3 academic years + 1 internship year.
A lateral-entry route may be available at some institutions, but it is not universal and is subject to diploma and curriculum-hour equivalence.

sections.heading: Curriculum: emergency-care science, technical procedures, and clinical education
paragraphs: The curriculum is clinically oriented rather than a general science degree. ICFAI University Tripura’s published structure starts with anatomy and physiology, hospital and health systems, medical terminology/records, computer applications, and introduction to emergency medical services. It then includes microbiology, pathology, biochemistry, pharmacology, medical law and ethics, research methods and biostatistics, airway management, emergency instruments and procedures, and progressively directed clinical education.

The same published structure culminates in medical-emergency modules, directed clinical education, and internship/externship plus project. Its programme description also identifies skills such as IV cannulation, oxygen therapy, physical examination, AED use, airway maintenance, CPR, spinal immobilisation, bleeding control and fracture management. Actual scope of practice in placements and employment remains subject to clinical supervision, employer protocols, and applicable law.
bullets: Foundational biomedical sciences: anatomy, physiology, microbiology, pathology, biochemistry and pharmacology.
Emergency-practice content: EMS systems, emergency procedures and instrumentation, airway management, medical emergencies, patient safety, law and ethics.
Applied learning: clinical education/rotations followed by internship or externship; simulation-based learning is also highlighted by Apollo University.

sections.heading: Admission: process varies by university
paragraphs: Admission methods are not standardised across the reviewed providers. ICFAI University Tripura states that selection is based on merit through an application and interview, with certificate verification at interview. In contrast, Dr. D. Y. Patil Vidyapeeth states that applicants for its undergraduate B.Sc. programme must appear for its entrance examination. Students should therefore confirm the exact selection route before applying rather than assuming that a national entrance examination, merit-only selection, or an interview will apply everywhere.

Timelines are especially variable. A course page can retain a prior-year calendar, so applicants should obtain the current-cycle prospectus or admission notice directly from the university before paying an application or seat-confirmation fee.
bullets: Check whether selection is merit-based, an institutional/state entrance test, interview-based, or a combination.
Verify document-verification steps, provisional-admission conditions for awaiting results, reservation/domicile rules, and refund terms before payment.

sections.heading: Costs: published examples are variable and date-sensitive
paragraphs: Fees differ substantially by institution and may exclude accommodation, transport, mess, uniforms, clinical requirements, examination charges, insurance, or refundable deposits. As a published example, ICFAI University Tripura lists a total programme fee of ₹2,30,000 for its B.Sc. Emergency Medical Technology programme, plus a ₹25,000 admission fee, ₹10,000 refundable caution deposit and separately listed activity/alumni/hostel charges. Apollo University lists a total course fee of ₹5,39,000 for its four-year B.Sc. Emergency Medical Technology programme, including the charges shown on its course page.

These figures are institutional website examples available at review, not a national fee benchmark or a quote for a particular applicant. Fees, scholarship criteria, instalments, deposits, and hostel charges can change by academic year; obtain a written fee schedule for the relevant intake.
bullets: Compare the total payable amount, not just annual tuition.
Ask whether the internship year has tuition/recurring fees and whether clinical consumables, certifications, transport, hostel and mess costs are additional.
Confirm scholarship eligibility and whether an offer is renewable each year.

sections.heading: After graduation: emergency, pre-hospital, and critical-care settings
paragraphs: The degree is designed for technical allied-health work around acute illness and injury. Institutional descriptions identify emergency medical services, ambulance/pre-hospital care, hospital emergency departments, ICUs/CCUs, nursing homes, community health centres, medical colleges and specialty hospitals as relevant practice settings. The precise job title, permitted duties, required registration/certification, and supervision arrangements depend on the employer, state rules, clinical protocols, and the graduate’s competencies.

A further study route may be possible through institution-specific postgraduate allied-health, public-health, healthcare-management, education, or research programmes, but eligibility is programme-specific. Graduates should check the receiving institution’s published entry rules rather than assume that every postgraduate degree accepts this qualification.
bullets: Assess vacancies by required competencies and clinical exposure, not title alone: some employers may use titles such as emergency medical technologist, emergency/trauma-care technician, or paramedic.
Maintain evidence of internship/clinical rotations, life-support training where applicable, and academic transcripts for employer or further-study applications.

Apollo University — B.Sc. Emergency Medical Technology: eligibility, duration and published fees

title: B.Sc. in Fashion Design
description: An undergraduate science degree focusing on the technical and aesthetic aspects of fashion design, textiles, and apparel manufacturing, often offered by various universities.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: B.Sc. in Fashion Design is a provider-specific undergraduate programme combining fashion and apparel design with textile, garment-production and portfolio skills; there is not one single nationally prescribed B.Sc. syllabus or admission route.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry qualification
quick_facts.value: Class 12/10+2 is the usual entry qualification. Published institutional rules differ: CSMU states 10+2 eligibility, while VIT requires a pass in any stream with a 60% overall aggregate (or a relevant 10+3 diploma with 60%).

quick_facts.label: Typical duration
quick_facts.value: A conventional B.Sc. Fashion Design route is three academic years across six semesters; some institutions also advertise four-year honours or honours-with-research variants under their undergraduate frameworks.

quick_facts.label: NIFT exam relationship
quick_facts.value: The NIFT entrance route is for NIFT’s bachelor programmes, including B.Des. Fashion Design; it is not a universal entry requirement for B.Sc. Fashion Design offered by other universities. For example, VIT publishes merit- and interview-based admission with no entrance examination for its B.Sc. Fashion Design.

quick_facts.label: Fee context
quick_facts.value: Fees are institution- and session-specific. As published by VIT for its 2024–25 B.Sc. Fashion Design admission information, tuition was ₹90,000 plus a refundable ₹2,000 caution deposit; applicants should obtain the current offer letter/fee notice before applying.

sections.heading: Eligibility: normally Class 12, but thresholds vary by university
paragraphs: B.Sc. Fashion Design does not have a single India-wide eligibility rule. A common baseline is completion of 10+2 from a recognised board in any stream. CSMU’s B.Sc. Fashion Design ordinance states that candidates qualified in the 10+2 examination may apply.

Institutions can impose their own minimum marks, stream, diploma and category-relaxation conditions. For example, VIT’s published rule for B.Sc. Fashion Design is a pass in any stream with at least 60% overall aggregate, or a 10+3 diploma in Fashion, Textile, Apparel or Garment with at least 60%. Applicants should use the eligibility notice for the exact campus and admission year rather than assuming a common cutoff.
bullets: Usual starting point: recognised 10+2/Class 12 qualification.
Possible additional conditions: minimum aggregate, accepted-board equivalence, relevant diploma pathway, category-specific relaxation and document verification.
A science stream is not universally required; published examples from CSMU and VIT allow entry from any stream, subject to their stated conditions.

sections.heading: Duration and award structure
paragraphs: The conventional format is a three-year undergraduate degree comprising six semesters. CSMU’s ordinance explicitly describes B.Sc. Fashion Designing as three academic years over six semesters, and VIT labels its B.Sc. Fashion Design as a three-year programme.

Programme structures can differ under institutional implementation of undergraduate curriculum frameworks. For example, Guru Nanak Dev University lists three-year B.Sc. Fashion Designing as well as four-year B.Sc. (Honours) and B.Sc. (Honours with Research) Fashion Designing options. Confirm the exact exit award, credit structure and availability of an honours year with the institution.
bullets: Common route: 3 years / 6 semesters.
Possible alternative at some universities: 4-year honours or honours-with-research structure.
The programme title may appear as Fashion Design, Fashion Designing, or Fashion & Apparel Design.

sections.heading: What students study
paragraphs: Course content is institution-specific, but the degree generally integrates creative design practice with textile and apparel-production knowledge. VIT’s published B.Sc. Fashion Design content includes textile science, wet processing and garment finishing, fashion illustration, patternmaking, computer-aided designing, surface ornamentation, fashion history, basics of design, and portfolio work.

Practical learning is a material part of the programme model rather than an optional add-on: VIT describes hands-on textile and design exploration, portfolio development, practical classes and industrial exposure. Students should inspect the semester-wise syllabus to check the balance of studio work, garment construction, software/CAD, manufacturing, merchandising and internships.
bullets: Design and visual communication: fashion illustration, design fundamentals, fashion history and portfolio development.
Technical and production subjects: textile science, wet processing, garment finishing and patternmaking.
Digital and surface practice: computer-aided design and surface ornamentation.
Professional exposure may include practical classes, industry exposure and portfolio-building, depending on the provider.

sections.heading: Admission routes: institution-specific, not automatically through NIFT
paragraphs: Admission procedures are set by the university or college. CSMU’s ordinance permits selection through qualifying-exam merit, an admission test and/or personal interview, subject to the university’s rules for that session. VIT’s published B.Sc. Fashion Design procedure instead states that there is no entrance examination; its ranking uses qualifying-exam marks and a personal interview.

The NIFT Entrance Examination should not be treated as a universal prerequisite for this node. NIFT’s own undergraduate page identifies Fashion Design as a B.Des. programme at NIFT. Therefore, use NIFT’s admission prospectus only when applying specifically to NIFT’s B.Des. Fashion Design; follow each B.Sc. provider’s separate application and selection instructions.
bullets: Check whether the provider uses Class 12 merit, a design/entrance test, a portfolio review, an interview, or a combination.
Check the admission-year notice for application dates, required documents, category rules and counselling/seat-allotment steps.
Do not infer that admission to a non-NIFT B.Sc. Fashion Design requires the NIFT entrance exam.

sections.heading: Costs: compare current institutional fee notices
paragraphs: There is no standard national fee for B.Sc. Fashion Design. Published amounts vary substantially by institution and may exclude or separately list examination, hostel, uniform, materials, registration, refundable deposits and other charges.

As dated fee context rather than a current nationwide benchmark, VIT’s 2024–25 B.Sc. Fashion Design page lists ₹90,000 tuition and a one-time refundable ₹2,000 caution deposit. DBUU’s fee page published for 2026 lists an All India first-semester academic fee of ₹40,000 before listed scholarships, plus separate one-time and recurring charges. These examples are not interchangeable quotations or guarantees; applicants should request the fee schedule and refund policy for the exact academic session.
bullets: Ask for a written fee breakup covering tuition, admission/registration, examinations, studio or laboratory charges, uniform/materials, hostel and refundable deposits.
Check whether scholarships are automatic, merit-based, domicile-based or conditional on payment dates.
Treat published fees as date- and campus-specific.

sections.heading: After the degree: fashion roles, entrepreneurship and further study
paragraphs: The degree can support entry-level work across design and apparel-related functions, with the actual role depending on a graduate’s portfolio, technical ability, internships and employer requirements. CSMU identifies potential paths including fashion designer and merchandiser, alongside work connected with apparel, e-commerce, retail, branding and marketing. VIT also describes the programme as preparing graduates for fashion-design work and higher studies.

Further study is a possible route for specialisation. For example, Guru Nanak Dev University lists M.Sc. Fashion Designing among the offerings of its apparel and textile technology department. Eligibility for postgraduate study is programme-specific, so graduates should check subject, marks and entrance requirements directly with the target university.

Fashion-label entrepreneurship is also a plausible progression, but a degree alone does not establish a label. CSMU frames entrepreneurship development, consumer behaviour and digital technologies as programme outcomes; prospective founders should additionally plan for portfolio development, production/sourcing capability, finance, branding, compliance and market validation.
bullets: Design-facing paths: fashion designer, stylist, costume-related work and portfolio-led creative roles.
Commercial and operations paths: fashion merchandising, apparel/retail functions, branding, e-commerce, sourcing and quality or production roles where the employer’s criteria are met.
Education pathway: relevant master’s programmes such as Fashion Designing/Fashion Technology/Textiles, subject to each university’s eligibility rules.
Entrepreneurship pathway: develop a distinct product proposition, portfolio, supplier/manufacturing network and commercial plan before launching a label.

title: B.Sc. in Hospitality and Hotel Administration
description: A three-year undergraduate degree focusing on the management and operational aspects of hotels and the hospitality industry.

quick_facts.label: Award and provider
quick_facts.value: NCHMCT offers this full-time B.Sc. programme through its affiliated Institutes of Hotel Management; NCHMCT states that successful graduates are awarded a JNU degree.

quick_facts.label: Standard duration
quick_facts.value: Six semesters (three years), with an optional fourth year under the NEP 2020 framework for an Honours degree, subject to completing the extended curriculum.

quick_facts.label: Entry qualification
quick_facts.value: Pass the 10+2 Senior Secondary examination or equivalent from a recognised board/institution, with English as a subject. There is no age bar stated for the programme.

quick_facts.label: Main admission route
quick_facts.value: For the NCHMCT affiliated route, admission is based on All India Rank in NCHM JEE, followed by centralised online counselling and institute/seat allotment on merit-cum-choice.

quick_facts.label: 2026 fee context
quick_facts.value: NCHMCT's 2026 brochure lists institute-variable tuition of approximately ₹3.00 lakh–₹5.00 lakh for the six-semester programme, in addition to listed common fees such as admission, enrolment, JNU, examination, and refundable academic caution-money charges. Fees should be confirmed with the allotted institute before payment.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: For the NCHMCT-affiliated B.Sc. in Hospitality and Hotel Administration, applicants must have passed the 10+2 Senior Secondary examination (or an equivalent recognised qualification) with English as one of the subjects. Candidates awaiting their qualifying result may apply provisionally, but must submit proof of passing by admission or by the deadline specified by NCHMCT; the current programme page states 30 September of the admission year. NCHMCT states that there is no age bar for this programme.
bullets: English may be studied as a core, elective, or functional subject in the qualifying examination.
Always check the applicable admission bulletin and counselling notice for the relevant academic session, as operational rules can change.

sections.heading: Duration and delivery
paragraphs: The standard programme is a full-time, six-semester B.Sc. spanning three years. NCHMCT also describes an optional fourth year aligned with NEP 2020 that can lead to an Honours degree on successful completion of the extended curriculum. The programme is delivered through NCHMCT's network of affiliated IHMs, which includes central-government, state-government, PSU-run, and private-sector institutes.
bullets: Standard pathway: 6 semesters / 3 years.
Extended option: an optional fourth year for an Honours degree, where offered and completed under the prescribed curriculum.

sections.heading: What students study
paragraphs: The curriculum combines operational laboratory training with hospitality-management learning. NCHMCT identifies the core operational areas as Food Production, Food and Beverage Service, Front Office Operations, and Housekeeping. It also lists management-oriented subjects including Hotel Accountancy, Food Safety and Quality, Human Resource Management, Facility Planning, Revenue/Financial Management, Strategic Management, Tourism Marketing, and Tourism Management.
bullets: Practical operational learning is a central part of the degree, rather than an add-on to classroom study.
The published academic structure includes a 17-week industrial-training block in Semester III or Semester IV, depending on the student group/calendar arrangement.
The degree is designed around preparation for supervisory responsibilities in hospitality, with progression toward managerial roles.

sections.heading: Admission process
paragraphs: The principal national admission route for NCHMCT-affiliated B.Sc. HHA seats is NCHM JEE, conducted by the National Testing Agency in computer-based-test mode. NCHMCT states that candidates are admitted according to their NCHM JEE All India Rank, then participate in centralised online counselling, register their preferences, and receive institute/seat allotment on a merit-cum-choice basis.
bullets: Prepare for the NCHM JEE subject areas published in the 2026 brochure: numerical ability and analytical aptitude, reasoning and logical deduction, general knowledge and current affairs, English language, and aptitude for the service sector.

Application dates, examination dates, participating institutes, seat availability, reservation procedures, and counselling rounds are session-specific. Verify them through the current NTA and NCHMCT notices rather than relying on a prior-year schedule.

sections.heading: Costs and financial planning
paragraphs: Costs vary materially by institute. In NCHMCT's 2026 admission brochure, the stated tuition range is approximately ₹3.00 lakh to ₹5.00 lakh for the whole six-semester programme. The same source separately lists common charges: ₹1,600 admission fee, ₹3,600 NCHMCT enrolment fee, ₹10,215 JNU fee, ₹3,000 examination fee per semester, and ₹8,000 refundable academic caution money. These figures are dated 2026 context, not a universal quote for every institute or later intake.
bullets: Request the institute's current fee notice and ask whether tuition covers uniforms, tools, laboratory charges, training-related expenses, accommodation, meals, and transport.
NCHMCT's 2026 brochure points students to national scholarship schemes and notes that state-level support may also be available, subject to each scheme's eligibility and current rules.

sections.heading: Progression and career options
paragraphs: Graduates can progress into hospitality operations and supervisory-track roles, including hotel management trainee, guest/customer-relations, sales and marketing, catering, railway hospitality, retail, cruise/shipping, and tourism-related work. Actual job title, employer requirements, placement outcomes, and pay vary by location, employer, prior practical experience, and the individual institute's placement process.
bullets: A direct academic progression is the two-year M.Sc. in Hospitality Administration, jointly offered by NCHMCT and IGNOU at select IHMs; its Semester III includes a choice between Human Resource Management and Sales and Marketing specialisation.
Another related postgraduate option is IGNOU's Master of Tourism and Travel Management, whose published eligibility includes B.Sc. Hospitality and Hotel Administration graduates.

Entrepreneurial routes can include restaurants, catering, bakery/patisserie, food-service ventures, and other hospitality services; business viability depends on licensing, capital, local demand, and operating capability.

title: B.Sc. in Interior Design
description: A three-year undergraduate degree focusing on the art and science of enhancing the interior of a building to achieve a healthier and more aesthetically pleasing environment for the people using the space.

quick_facts.label: Typical award and duration
quick_facts.value: B.Sc. in Interior Design is commonly offered as a six-semester, three-year undergraduate programme; however, programme structure is institution-specific, and some universities offer a four-year/honours format under their undergraduate framework.

quick_facts.label: Usual entry qualification
quick_facts.value: Examples of current university rules require Class 12 / 10+2 or an equivalent qualification. The required stream and minimum marks vary by institution: some accept any stream, while published thresholds in examples range from 45% for general-category applicants to institution-specific alternatives such as a relevant diploma.

quick_facts.label: Core learning areas
quick_facts.value: Published B.Sc. curricula combine design studios with spatial planning, interior materials and construction, furniture, lighting, building services, CAD/3D visualisation, drawings, costing, sustainability, project work and professional practice.

quick_facts.label: NATA relationship
quick_facts.value: NATA is the Council of Architecture’s aptitude test for admission to the first year of the five-year B.Arch. degree. It is therefore not a nationally prescribed admission test for a B.Sc. in Interior Design; a particular B.Sc. provider may set its own admissions process.

quick_facts.label: NIFT Entrance Exam relationship
quick_facts.value: NIFTEE is used for NIFT’s own B.Des., B.F.Tech. and postgraduate admissions. NIFT’s listed undergraduate design programmes include Fashion Interiors under B.Des., but this is distinct from a university B.Sc. in Interior Design.

quick_facts.label: Indicative published fee context
quick_facts.value: Fees are highly provider- and year-specific. For context, Sandip University publishes annual academic and special fees totalling ₹85,000 for its three-year B.Sc. Interior Design & Decoration, while AAFT College, Raipur publishes a total academic fee of ₹531,000 for its three-year B.Sc. Interior Design; applicants should verify the applicable intake-year fee notice and separate hostel, transport, application and refundable charges.

sections.heading: Eligibility: Class 12 is the usual entry point, but rules are set by the admitting university
paragraphs: A B.Sc. in Interior Design is not governed by one single national admission rule. Published institutional criteria show the usual baseline is a pass in 10+2 / Class 12 or an equivalent examination. Sandip University lists 10+2 in any discipline with at least 45% for general/open-category applicants and 40% for reserved-category applicants, with a Class 10 plus diploma route also listed. Thakur College of Science & Commerce similarly lists Class 12 or an equivalent qualification and states that it accepts applicants from any stream.

Applicants should treat the programme page, prospectus and admission notice for their chosen campus and intake year as controlling. They should check minimum marks, accepted boards, category concessions, portfolio or interview requirements, document requirements, and whether a diploma/lateral-entry route is available before applying.
bullets: Class 12 stream: may be open to Arts, Commerce and Science students, but confirm the provider’s rule.
Marks: thresholds differ; the examples cited publish 45% for general/open applicants, with a lower threshold for reserved categories at one provider.
Documents commonly needed in admissions workflows include Class 10 and 12 marksheets/certificates, identity and category certificates where applicable; exact requirements are institution-specific.

sections.heading: Duration: three years is a common B.Sc. format, alongside evolving four-year pathways
paragraphs: The canonical three-year framing matches programmes that are explicitly structured as six semesters: Sandip University lists six semesters and three years for its B.Sc. Interior Design & Decoration, and Bengaluru School of Design and Technology describes its B.Sc. Interior Design as a three-year, six-semester full-time course.

The degree title alone does not guarantee the same duration everywhere. Thakur College lists B.Sc./B.Sc. (Hons.) Interior Design as “3 Years / 4 Years,” and other providers advertise four-year B.Sc. pathways. This variation is consistent with the UGC’s undergraduate curriculum framework, which supports flexible, multidisciplinary undergraduate structures and multiple entry/exit options. Confirm the exit award, honours/research option, credits and total duration in the specific university regulations.
bullets: Common conventional route: 3 years / 6 semesters.
Possible alternative: 4-year honours or honours-with-research pathway.
Do not assume that a B.Sc. label has the same duration, credits or exit options across institutions.

sections.heading: Curriculum: studio design is supported by technical, visualisation and practice skills
paragraphs: Interior-design study is broader than decoration. Published programme content combines the creative work of conceiving spaces with technical knowledge needed to communicate and execute a project. AAFT’s B.Sc. outline includes basic design and visual arts, history of interiors, building materials and construction technology, residential and commercial space design, furniture design, execution drawings, estimating and costing, building services and sustainable interiors.

Digital visualisation and professional practice are recurring components. The same outline names AutoCAD, SketchUp, 3ds Max and Photoshop, while REVA describes design studios, core courses, electives, industry training and a final thesis/project, plus professional training under practising architects. Course names, software and the amount of internship/studio work differ by university, so candidates should obtain the current semester-wise syllabus rather than rely on a generic list.
bullets: Design foundation: visual arts, design thinking, interior history and space planning.
Technical development: materials, construction, furniture, lighting, building services, working/execution drawings and costing.
Digital and communication work: CAD, 3D visualisation, presentations and portfolio development.
Applied learning: studios, projects, industry exposure/training and, at some institutions, a final project or dissertation.

sections.heading: Admission: apply to the university; do not assume NATA or NIFTEE is required
paragraphs: For B.Sc. Interior Design, admission routes are set by the individual university or college. Some providers explicitly state that there is no entrance examination for their Bachelor of Interior Design route, while others may use merit, an institution-level assessment, an interview or other screening. The applicant should use the official admission notice for the particular campus and academic session to determine the process.

The two named parent examinations should be interpreted carefully. NATA is specifically a qualifying aptitude test for first-year admission to the five-year B.Arch. programme under the Council of Architecture framework, not a universal B.Sc. Interior Design test. Likewise, NIFTEE is the entrance examination for NIFT’s own programmes, including B.Des.; NIFT’s 2026 prospectus lists Fashion Interiors as a B.Des. specialisation, not a B.Sc. Interior Design degree. A NATA or NIFTEE score should only be submitted where the chosen institution expressly asks for it.
bullets: Start with the official programme page and current admission prospectus of the intended university.
Verify: eligibility, minimum marks, application form, entrance/portfolio/interview requirements, dates, reservation rules and fee schedule.
NATA: relevant to B.Arch. admission, not automatically to B.Sc. Interior Design.
NIFTEE: relevant to NIFT’s listed B.Des./B.F.Tech. and PG admissions, not automatically to a non-NIFT B.Sc. Interior Design course.

sections.heading: Costs: compare the complete, intake-year cost—not only tuition
paragraphs: There is no standard national fee for this degree. Published examples demonstrate substantial variation: Sandip University lists annual academic fees of ₹75,000 plus special fees of ₹10,000 for its three-year programme, whereas AAFT College, Raipur lists a total of ₹531,000 for its three-year B.Sc. Interior Design. These are provider-published figures available as of the review date, not a market average or a prediction of what another college will charge.

When comparing offers, separate tuition/academic fees from admission or prospectus fees, examination/library/lab charges, deposits, software or material costs, accommodation, transport and other living costs. Ask for the official itemised fee notice for the exact academic session and confirm refund, scholarship and instalment conditions in writing.
bullets: Published example 1: ₹85,000 per year in academic plus special fees at Sandip University for the cited programme.
Published example 2: ₹531,000 total academic fee at AAFT College, Raipur for the cited three-year programme.
These figures are dated provider examples and may change by session, campus, category, scholarship and payment plan.

sections.heading: Next options: employment, independent practice and postgraduate design or management study
paragraphs: A graduate can pursue design employment and build a portfolio through project, studio, retail, exhibition or site-execution work. Published B.Sc. career examples include interior/spatial designer, 3D visualiser, furniture designer, lighting designer and site supervisor. Related interior-architecture career material also identifies visual merchandising and set/scenography-oriented work as possible directions; suitability depends on the graduate’s portfolio, software skills, practical experience and the employer’s role requirements.

For postgraduate design study, CEED is one route to M.Des. admissions at participating design institutes. CEED 2026 permitted candidates with a degree, diploma or postgraduate programme of at least three years after 10+2, but qualifying CEED did not itself guarantee admission: institutes could impose their own eligibility checks, tests and interviews. Candidates considering an M.Des should check the precise discipline and eligibility at each target institute.

An MBA is another possible transition because management programmes admit graduates from different disciplines. For example, IIM Ahmedabad’s two-year MBA/PGP admission process uses CAT for domestic applicants and evaluates eligible applicants through its own selection process; its published pages describe students from arts, commerce, science and professional streams. CAT, CEED and postgraduate programme deadlines, eligibility and selection rules are revised by the relevant authorities and should be checked for the intended admission cycle.
bullets: Direct work and entrepreneurship: interior/spatial design, visualisation, furniture or lighting-related roles, site supervision, and eventually independent studio/firm work.
M.Des: CEED may be a relevant qualifying examination, but each institute separately decides final eligibility and selection.
M.Sc. in Interior Design/Interior Architecture: availability, title and eligibility are university-specific; verify the target programme directly.
MBA: a B.Sc. graduate may pursue management study; CAT-based selection requirements are set by individual IIMs and programmes.

title: B.Sc. in Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology
description: An undergraduate degree in medical radiography, imaging modalities, radiation physics, and diagnostic imaging patient care.

quick_facts.label: Recognised professional area
quick_facts.value: Medical radiology and imaging is listed under the Medical Radiology, Imaging and Therapeutic Technology Professional category in India’s National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP) framework; the NCAHP portal identifies Radiology and Imaging Technologist as a profession within that category.

quick_facts.label: Usual entry qualification
quick_facts.value: A common institutional requirement is Class 12 / 10+2 with Physics, Chemistry and Biology (PCB); minimum marks, English requirements, age criteria and accepted equivalents vary by university.

quick_facts.label: Usual duration
quick_facts.value: Many programmes are structured as three academic years plus a one-year internship (four years total), although titles and programme structures differ among institutions.

quick_facts.label: Scope of training
quick_facts.value: The degree prepares learners for technical diagnostic-imaging work involving modalities such as conventional and digital X-ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound, fluoroscopy and mammography, with attention to radiation safety, quality control and patient care.

quick_facts.label: Professional enrolment status
quick_facts.value: As of the NCAHP enrolment portal information reviewed, allied-health-professional enrolment is described as data collection rather than registration; the portal says registration regulations are under process.

sections.heading: Eligibility: science at Class 12 is the usual route
paragraphs: For direct entry, applicants should normally expect to need a recognised 10+2 / senior-secondary qualification with Physics, Chemistry and Biology. Some institutions additionally require English, a specified aggregate or individual passing marks, and minimum age requirements; applicants should therefore check the exact prospectus for the institution and admission year.

The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021 defines an allied health professional to include a technician or technologist supporting diagnosis and treatment, with a qualifying diploma or degree of at least 2,000 hours delivered across two to four years. This statutory definition is a framework for allied-health qualifications, not a substitute for an individual university’s admission rules.
bullets: Typical published requirement: 10+2 with PCB.
Potential additional conditions: English, minimum marks, age, medical fitness, category documentation and university-specific equivalence rules.

Lateral entry may be available at some institutions for holders of an appropriate post-10+2 medical-imaging diploma; for example, MAHE lists a lateral B.Sc. Medical Imaging Technology route based on a two-year diploma and specified marks.

sections.heading: Duration: generally four years when internship is included
paragraphs: The common full-time pattern is three years of coursework followed by a 12-month clinical internship, making four years in total. Institutions may describe this as B.Sc. Medical Imaging Technology, BMRIT, B.Sc. Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology, or a closely related title, so applicants should verify both the award title and whether internship is embedded or separately scheduled.

The statutory NCAHP Act describes allied-health diploma or degree qualifications as spanning two to four years and at least 2,000 hours, while individual BMRIT/MIT programmes commonly publish a four-year structure including internship.
bullets: A published example from JSS Academy: 6 semesters plus 12 months of internship.
A published example from Father Muller: 3 years plus 1 year of internship.
Confirm clinical-posting and internship arrangements before accepting an offer, especially where a course page lists only academic semesters.

sections.heading: Curriculum: imaging science, safe practice and supervised clinical learning
paragraphs: Published curricula combine health-science foundations with imaging-specific theory and practical work. Core foundations commonly include anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, pathology, microbiology and pharmacology; imaging content commonly covers radiographic physics, positioning and procedures, image processing, radiation biology and protection, quality control, and patient-care considerations.

Training normally extends across multiple diagnostic modalities rather than only conventional radiography. Published programme descriptions include X-ray and digital imaging, fluoroscopy, mammography, ultrasonography, CT, MRI, Doppler/DSA, PACS and department planning. The precise mix of modalities, clinical exposure and assessment is institution-specific.
bullets: Foundational sciences: anatomy, physiology, pathology and related biomedical subjects.
Professional imaging skills: positioning, radiographic techniques, image processing and equipment operation.
Safety and quality: radiation protection, radiobiology, quality assurance and quality control.
Advanced/modality exposure: CT, MRI, ultrasound, fluoroscopy, mammography and digital imaging/PACS, where offered.

sections.heading: Admission: process is determined by the university, state or Union Territory
paragraphs: There is no single admission route stated across all B.Sc. medical-radiology/imaging programmes. Universities may use qualifying-examination merit, their own entrance assessment and interview, or another process permitted by the relevant institution and jurisdiction. Applicants should rely on the current official prospectus rather than assuming that NEET-UG, CUET, or any one examination is universally required.

A 2026 BMRIT admission page from Symbiosis Institute of Health Sciences illustrates an institution-specific process: online registration, screening, entrance test and personal interview, document verification, and payment of the first fee instalment. Its published selection formula gives equal weight to senior-secondary performance and entrance examination/personal interaction; this is an example, not a national rule.
bullets: Check the programme’s current eligibility, selection method, document list, reservation policy and clinical-training arrangement.
Use the official university or state/UT admission notice for dates and deadlines, which can change during an admission cycle.
For foreign qualifications, check equivalence requirements and the applicable institution/state allied-health authority guidance.

sections.heading: Costs: compare the current institution-specific fee schedule
paragraphs: Fees are not standardised nationally and may exclude or separately charge for registration, examination, hostel, transport, uniforms, clinical materials, deposits and other charges. As dated examples for the 2026–27 academic year, Dayananda Sagar University lists ₹1,72,000 total annual fees for its B.Sc. Medical Radiology & Imaging Technology, while Symbiosis Institute of Health Sciences lists first-year academic fees of ₹1,74,000 in two instalments plus a ₹20,000 refundable institute deposit for BMRIT. These figures are contextual examples, not an India-wide fee benchmark.

Before applying, request the complete current fee sheet and determine whether it states tuition only or the full payable amount, whether internship fees are included, and which deposits or charges are refundable.
bullets: Dated fee example — Dayananda Sagar University, 2026–27: ₹1,72,000 annual total shown for B.Sc. Medical Radiology & Imaging Technology.
Dated fee example — Symbiosis Institute of Health Sciences, 2026–27: ₹1,74,000 first-year academic fee shown in two instalments, plus a ₹20,000 refundable deposit.
Fee schedules, scholarships, concessions and refund terms can change by institution and admission cycle.

sections.heading: Next options: postgraduate imaging study or employment-oriented specialisation
paragraphs: After the bachelor’s degree and required internship or experience under the relevant institution’s rules, graduates can pursue postgraduate study in medical radiology and imaging technology. MAHE’s 2026 postgraduate eligibility material lists Master of Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology pathways in CT Imaging Technology, MR Imaging Technology and Breast Imaging Technology, accepting BMRIT/BMRDIT/B.Sc. Medical Imaging Technology or specified equivalent backgrounds subject to its conditions.

Career pathways stated by universities include work in hospitals and diagnostic centres, imaging-industry roles, healthcare IT/PACS and research settings. The NCAHP framework categorises radiology and imaging technologists—including diagnostic medical radiographers, MRI and CT personnel, mammographers and diagnostic medical sonographers—within the medical-radiology, imaging and therapeutic-technology category.
bullets: Postgraduate option: M.MRIT/M.Sc.-level imaging programmes, subject to the receiving university’s eligibility rules.
Practice settings: hospital radiology departments, diagnostic centres, imaging-technology industry, PACS/healthcare IT and research environments.
Verify local employer requirements, state rules and any future NCAHP registration requirements before relying on a particular job pathway.

title: B.Sc. in Operation Theatre Technology
description: An undergraduate allied-health degree providing advanced training in operating theatre procedures, surgical assistance, anaesthesia support, and perioperative care.

quick_facts.label: Current national curriculum nomenclature
quick_facts.value: The NCAHP competency-based curriculum calls the baccalaureate programme “B.AOTT” (Baccalaureate in Anaesthesia & Operation Theatre Technology). Institutions may still use titles such as B.Sc. in Operation Theatre Technology; applicants should confirm the exact award title with the university.

quick_facts.label: Standard entry background
quick_facts.value: The NCAHP B.AOTT curriculum specifies 10+2/equivalent with at least 50% in Physics, Chemistry and Biology; Mathematics is optional in that curriculum. Institution-specific requirements can be more restrictive.

quick_facts.label: Standard programme pattern
quick_facts.value: The NCAHP baccalaureate curriculum lays out six academic semesters followed by a one-year internship in anaesthesia, surgery and specialty postings—normally a four-year pathway in total.

quick_facts.label: Professional scope
quick_facts.value: Training is directed toward supervised perioperative support: preparing and maintaining the operating theatre, assisting anaesthesia and surgical teams, monitoring infection-control procedures, supporting recovery care, and handling relevant equipment within assigned competence and institutional protocols.

quick_facts.label: National standards context
quick_facts.value: NCAHP’s competency-based curriculum for Anaesthesia and Operation Theatre Technology is among the allied-health curricula identified for mandatory implementation from academic year 2026–27.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: For the current NCAHP baccalaureate curriculum in Anaesthesia & Operation Theatre Technology, the baseline entry qualification is Higher Secondary/10+2 or equivalent from a recognised board with 50% marks in Physics, Chemistry and Biology; Mathematics is listed as optional. The curriculum also addresses equivalence for international qualifications through the Association of Indian Universities.

Individual universities can set additional conditions. For example, DIT University’s 2026–27 B.AOTT listing requires 10+2 with Physics, Chemistry and Biology/Mathematics, sets a minimum age of 17 by 31 December of the admission year, and requires a government medical officer-endorsed fitness certificate. Check the prospectus for the specific institution and admission cycle rather than treating one college’s rules as national rules.
bullets: Recommended preparation: strong Class 12 foundations in PCB, comfort with clinical learning, careful adherence to patient-safety and infection-control processes, and readiness for supervised hospital postings.
Verify whether the course accepts PCB only or PCB/Mathematics, its required percentage, age and medical-fitness conditions, domicile/category rules, and whether it offers any lateral-entry route.

sections.heading: Duration and clinical training
paragraphs: Under the NCAHP baccalaureate curriculum, the academic component spans the first six semesters, followed by a compulsory one-year internship labelled as seventh and eighth semesters. The internship is structured across anaesthesia, critical care and multiple surgical/OT settings; the curriculum describes it as 12 months, with six months in anaesthesia and six months in surgical disciplines.

Programme duration is not uniform across every legacy B.Sc. OTT offering. Older institutional syllabi may show three academic years plus internship, 3.5 years, or other structures. For admissions from 2026–27, confirm that the programme’s duration, internship and degree nomenclature align with the applicable NCAHP framework and the university’s approved regulations.
bullets: NCAHP internship examples include anaesthesia, critical care, general surgery/obstetrics and gynaecology, urology and paediatric surgery, CTVS/neurosurgery, emergency or trauma OT/orthopaedics, robotic surgery, and minor surgery.
Keep a clinical logbook: the national curriculum requires documented postings and faculty/senior review during internship.

sections.heading: What students study and learn
paragraphs: This is an allied-health, perioperative-care degree rather than a medical degree. The NCAHP curriculum aims to prepare graduates to assist anaesthesiologists during procedures and patient monitoring; work with operating-theatre technology and biomedical equipment; support pre-operative, intra-operative, recovery-room and post-operative care; and maintain infection-control standards while working under doctors’ guidance and supervision.

Coursework combines biomedical foundations with applied OT and anaesthesia practice. The NCAHP structure includes anatomy and physiology, biochemistry and haematology, pathology and microbiology, pharmacology, medical law and ethics, management, communication and computing. Professional modules cover basic and advanced anaesthesia techniques, surgical procedures, CSSD and manifold-area work, intensive care, specialised anaesthesia and surgery, disaster/environmental management, research methodology and biostatistics.

Practical and clinical learning are central. The curriculum specifies clinical/practical components alongside theory and then a full-year internship. Students should evaluate whether a prospective college has sufficient OT exposure, anaesthesia and critical-care postings, simulation/laboratory facilities, named hospital affiliations, and a transparent supervision and logbook process.
bullets: Core technical themes: anaesthesia support, surgical instruments and procedures, OT preparation and equipment, medical gases/manifold systems, sterilisation/CSSD, patient positioning and transfer, infection prevention, safety, documentation and biomedical-waste handling.

Professional boundary: graduates assist the clinical team within their training, assigned role and institutional protocols; diagnosis, prescribing and independent medical decision-making are not the purpose of this qualification.

sections.heading: Admission route
paragraphs: The NCAHP curriculum describes admission based on eligibility plus a university entrance test and interview, followed by merit-based counselling/seat allotment. In actual practice, selection mechanisms differ by institution: some use university entrance tests, while others publish 10+2-merit admissions. Therefore, applicants should treat the relevant university’s admission notice as controlling.

Prepare a document file early: Class 10 and 12 marksheets/certificates, photo ID, category or domicile documents where applicable, photographs, medical-fitness documentation if required, and equivalence documents for non-Indian qualifications. Confirm the 2026–27 application opening date, test/interview schedule, fee-payment deadline and hostel process directly with the institution.
bullets: Examples of variation: the NCAHP curriculum sets out an entrance-test-and-interview model, while DIT University states admission is on Senior Secondary merit for its B.AOTT course.

Before paying an application fee, verify the awarding university, exact degree title, programme duration including internship, clinical-training hospital, approved intake, refund rules and total compulsory charges.

sections.heading: Fees: dated examples, not a national benchmark
paragraphs: Fees vary materially by state, institution type, quota, scholarships, hostel choice and charges outside tuition. As dated 2026–27 examples, DIT University lists two instalments of ₹75,150 each for its All-India B.AOTT first year (₹150,300 before separately listed admission and caution-money charges). MGM School of Biomedical Sciences, Navi Mumbai lists a first-year total of ₹144,500 for its Anaesthesia and Operation Theatre Technology allied-health programme, followed by listed annual totals of ₹114,000, ₹114,000 and ₹114,500 for years two through four.

These examples are provider-specific published schedules, not an estimate of the cost of a B.Sc. OTT nationwide. Ask each college for a written fee sheet covering tuition, university/enrolment fees, examination/practical charges, refundable deposits, internship charges if any, transport, hostel/mess and annual increases. Check eligibility and continuation rules before relying on a scholarship.
bullets: DIT’s displayed 2026–27 first-year schedule separately lists a non-refundable ₹10,000 admission fee and a refundable ₹5,000 caution-money charge in addition to the displayed programme fee.

MGM’s displayed 2026–27 first-year total includes tuition, institute enrolment/eligibility fee, refundable deposit and semester examination fees; it should not be compared with tuition-only figures without adjustment.

sections.heading: After the degree
paragraphs: Typical entry employment is in hospital operating theatres, anaesthesia departments, recovery areas, critical-care units and trauma centres, as part of a multidisciplinary team. The NCAHP curriculum describes graduates as working under doctors’ guidance and supervision and identifies hospital and independent trauma-centre opportunities; the specific job title, duties and hiring requirements vary by employer and state.

For academic progression, the NCAHP curriculum includes a Master’s in Anaesthesia & Operation Theatre Technology (M.AOTT). Its stated focus is advanced knowledge in planning, setting up, maintaining and managing anaesthesia and surgical procedures, equipment handling, clinical supervision, research and training. Admission requirements must be checked with the university offering the master’s programme.

Build employability through a complete internship logbook, documented OT/anaesthesia/critical-care rotations, infection-control and patient-safety competence, equipment familiarity, communication skills and continuing professional education. Registration, recognition and recruitment rules can evolve as NCAHP standards are implemented, so verify the applicable state and employer requirements at the time of application.
bullets: Possible early-career titles may include operation theatre technologist, anaesthesia technologist or surgical/anaesthesia-related technology staff; nomenclature is employer-dependent.

A master’s degree and subsequent experience can support progression toward more senior clinical, teaching, supervision, management, research or industry-facing roles, subject to the employer’s criteria.
