title: BCA (Bachelor of Computer Applications)
description: Three-year undergraduate computing degree; leads to software roles or MCA.

quick_facts.label: Credential
quick_facts.value: BCA is an undergraduate computing qualification. A three-year full-time undergraduate programme leads to a bachelor's degree under UGC's undergraduate framework; IGNOU's BCA is an example with a 36-month minimum duration.

quick_facts.label: Illustrative entry requirement
quick_facts.value: Requirements are institution-specific. IGNOU currently lists 10+2 or equivalent, or a Diploma in Commercial Practice/equivalent, for its BCA programme.

quick_facts.label: Typical study areas
quick_facts.value: An official BCA curriculum example includes programming, data structures and algorithms, DBMS, computer organisation, operating systems, networks, web programming, software engineering, laboratories, and a software project.

quick_facts.label: Admission route
quick_facts.value: CUET-UG scores are used for undergraduate admissions at central and other participating universities, but applicants must confirm the specific BCA programme's eligibility and required test subjects with the chosen university.

quick_facts.label: Illustrative published fee
quick_facts.value: As listed by IGNOU when reviewed, its ODL BCA fee is ₹8,300 per semester (₹49,800 across all semesters). This is one provider's published fee, not an India-wide BCA fee benchmark, and may change.

quick_facts.label: MCA pathway
quick_facts.value: For NIMCET 2026, a three-year-or-longer undergraduate degree requires Mathematics or Statistics as a subject and the prescribed aggregate/CGPA; a BCA title alone does not establish NIMCET eligibility.

sections.heading: Eligibility: check the institution, not just the degree name
paragraphs: BCA entry rules differ by university, mode of study, and admission year. IGNOU's current ODL BCA listing accepts 10+2 or equivalent, or a Diploma in Commercial Practice/equivalent. Its listing does not make Mathematics at Class 12 a universal condition for that version of the programme.

Where a university uses CUET-UG, CUET is an admissions test route rather than a single nationwide BCA eligibility rule. NTA instructs candidates to review the target university's programme eligibility, qualifying marks, reservation rules, available seats, and required CUET subject choices before applying.
bullets: Students from Science, Commerce, or other Class 12 backgrounds should compare the exact BCA eligibility clause at each target institution; do not assume that PCM, Commerce, Computer Science, or Mathematics is universally required or universally waived.
For a later MCA plan, retain and document Mathematics or Statistics study where possible: some MCA admissions routes apply subject-specific conditions at the bachelor's-degree stage.

sections.heading: Duration and academic structure
paragraphs: BCA is commonly organised as a three-year undergraduate course. The UGC learning-outcomes framework states that students completing three years of full-time undergraduate study are awarded a bachelor's degree. Under UGC's newer undergraduate curriculum-and-credit framework, institutions may also implement flexible credit structures and multiple entry/exit arrangements, so the precise award structure should be verified with the admitting institution.

For a concrete current example, IGNOU describes its BCA as having a minimum duration of 36 months and a maximum duration of 72 months. That maximum-completion window is specific to IGNOU's programme and should not be treated as a rule for all colleges.
bullets: Confirm whether the programme is regular, online, or open/distance learning, as delivery, attendance, laboratory arrangements, assessment, and completion rules can differ.
Check the current prospectus for the number of semesters, credits, project requirements, and any exit options before paying an admission fee.

sections.heading: What students typically study
paragraphs: There is no single national BCA syllabus: universities set their own curriculum within applicable academic frameworks. IGNOU's current BCA curriculum is a useful official illustration rather than a universal syllabus. It covers computer fundamentals, mathematics, C and Python, computer organisation, operating systems, data structures and algorithms, database management systems, C++, Java, web programming, networks, statistics, software engineering, e-commerce, and practical laboratory work.

A substantial capstone component can matter for job readiness. IGNOU describes its BCA project as a sixth-semester software solution that applies requirements analysis, systems design, development, testing, and documentation; it encourages undertaking the project in a software industry or research organisation where feasible.
bullets: Look for hands-on programming and database labs, not only theory papers.
Compare whether the syllabus includes current practical exposure in web development, databases, networks, software engineering, algorithms, and a final project.
Review the current semester-wise scheme because course codes, programming languages, elective choices, and project rules can change.

sections.heading: Admissions: CUET may be relevant, but is not universal
paragraphs: BCA admission is administered by the university or college. CUET-UG provides a common score for undergraduate admissions at central universities and other participating state, deemed, private, and government institutions. Participation in CUET does not mean every participating institution offers BCA, nor that every BCA provider uses CUET.

For CUET-UG 2026, NTA stated that applicants could select up to five subjects, including languages and the General Aptitude Test, and specifically directed them to choose tests according to the eligibility requirements of their desired university programme. Therefore, select the target BCA programme first, then map its stated test-subject requirements before registration in a future cycle.
bullets: Use the university's programme page/prospectus to verify: whether BCA is offered; Class 12 subjects and minimum marks; entrance-test route; reservation and document rules; counselling process; and fee schedule.
Treat admission calendars and application deadlines as year-specific. The CUET-UG 2026 registration and examination dates published by NTA applied only to that cycle.

sections.heading: Costs: use provider-level figures, not a national average
paragraphs: BCA fees vary materially by institution type, location, delivery mode, facilities, and year. As a dated official reference point, IGNOU's current ODL BCA page lists ₹8,300 per semester and ₹49,800 for all semesters. It is not evidence of the fee at a regular college, private university, or another distance/online provider.

Applicants should separate tuition from one-time admission charges, examination fees, laboratory or technology charges, study materials, hostel and living costs, and entrance-test fees. The current official prospectus and payment page of the chosen institution are the appropriate sources for a final cost calculation.
bullets: Record the publication date and academic session attached to every fee quote.
Check refund, instalment, scholarship, and category-concession rules directly with the institution before enrolling.

sections.heading: After BCA: employment, MCA, and other postgraduate choices
paragraphs: A BCA can support entry-level IT or IT-enabled-services pathways when paired with demonstrable skills, projects, internships, and the employer's stated requirements. IGNOU identifies examples including assistant programmer, assistant software engineer, and data-processing assistant; these are illustrative roles rather than guaranteed outcomes or a salary promise.

MCA is a common academic progression. NIMCET 2026 is the national-level entrance route for MCA admissions at 11 participating NITs and two IIITs. Its 2026 eligibility required Indian nationals to have at least 60% aggregate or 6.5/10 CGPA (55% or 6.0/10 for SC/ST/PwD) in a minimum three-year undergraduate programme with Mathematics or Statistics as a subject, or a BE/BTech. Candidates should re-check the next cycle's brochure because eligibility, institutions, fees, and schedule can change.

A BCA graduate may also consider MBA or other master's programmes, government recruitment examinations, or specialised skill paths such as software development, web development, and digital marketing. Each route has independent degree, subject, age, test, work-experience, and selection conditions; the relevant official notification—not the BCA degree alone—determines eligibility.
bullets: For software and web roles, build a portfolio with source code, deployed work, documentation, and evidence of testing or collaboration.
For MCA planning, check Mathematics/Statistics eligibility early and preserve mark sheets/course records.
For MBA, public-sector examinations, or overseas study, verify the specific examination or university's current eligibility and selection rules.

useful_links.label: UGC Curriculum and Credit Framework for Undergraduate Programmes

title: BDS (Bachelor of Dental Surgery)
description: Five-year undergraduate dental degree (including internship); admission via NEET-UG; leads to clinical dentistry or MDS specialization.

quick_facts.label: Award and structure
quick_facts.value: BDS is the undergraduate dental qualification prescribed as four academic years plus one year of compulsory paid rotating internship; the degree is granted after internship completion.

quick_facts.label: Entrance route
quick_facts.value: Admission is based on NEET-UG merit. The National Testing Agency describes NEET (UG) 2026 as the common, uniform entrance test for undergraduate medical education, and the BDS regulations prescribe NEET-based merit for BDS admission.

quick_facts.label: School preparation
quick_facts.value: The standard qualifying route requires Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English; BDS regulations also set a minimum age of 17 by 31 December of the admission year.

quick_facts.label: Counselling
quick_facts.value: BDS seats are allotted through common counselling: DGHS/MCC handles 15% All India Quota seats and specified central/deemed-university seats, while States and Union Territories conduct counselling for their respective institutions and seats.

quick_facts.label: Clinical-practice pathway
quick_facts.value: Clinical dental practice is regulated: the Dentists Act restricts practice of dentistry to registered dentists, subject to statutory exceptions. Graduates should therefore complete the applicable State Dental Council registration process before practising independently.

sections.heading: Who can pursue BDS?
paragraphs: A typical entrant comes from the Class 12 science route with Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English, then qualifies NEET-UG and participates in counselling. The BDS regulations specify completion of age 17 on or before 31 December of the admission year. They prescribe 50% aggregate in Physics, Chemistry and Biology/Biotechnology for the general qualifying-examination standard, with 40% for SC/ST/OBC candidates and 45% for the disability category described in those regulations; applicants must also satisfy the NEET percentile and category rules applicable to the admission year.

The exact eligibility, disability provisions, category treatment, document requirements and cut-offs should always be checked in the current NEET-UG information bulletin and the relevant counselling authority’s notice, because these are admission-cycle-specific.
bullets: Complete an accepted 10+2/equivalent qualification with PCB/Biology-Biotechnology and English.
Meet the age requirement and the current year’s NEET-UG eligibility and qualifying criteria.
Use the current counselling rules for the quota, domicile and college category sought.

sections.heading: Duration and internship
paragraphs: The regulated BDS pathway is five years in total: four academic years, each with 240 teaching days, followed by a one-year paid rotating internship in a dental college. Internship is compulsory, and the BDS degree is granted only after it is completed.

The internship is designed as supervised clinical rotation rather than an optional placement. The regulations describe rotations across dental departments and community/rural-service exposure, with a stipend allowance during the internship period under the stated framework.
bullets: Four academic years of full-time dental education.
One compulsory paid rotating internship year.
Degree award follows successful internship completion.

sections.heading: What BDS studies and trains you to do
paragraphs: BDS progresses from biomedical foundations to oral sciences and clinical dentistry. The curriculum framework groups training into: medical and basic sciences such as anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, pharmacology, pathology, microbiology, medicine and surgery; oral and dental sciences such as oral biology and oral pathology; and the clinical and technical components required for general dental practice.

The programme includes laboratory, pre-clinical and patient-facing clinical learning. The official syllabus covers areas including human anatomy, embryology, histology and medical genetics, and the wider regulations identify clinical fields such as oral medicine and radiology, oral and maxillofacial surgery, prosthodontics, periodontics, conservative dentistry and endodontics, pedodontics, orthodontics, oral pathology and community dentistry.
bullets: Builds diagnostic, preventive, restorative and patient-management foundations for general dentistry.
Integrates basic medical sciences with oral-health science and clinical dental practice.
Includes compulsory rotating internship exposure after final BDS examinations.

sections.heading: How admission works
paragraphs: The practical sequence is: register for NEET-UG, meet that year’s qualifying requirements, obtain a score/rank, then register for the applicable counselling process and fill college choices. For the national counselling stream, MCC/DGHS conducts online allotment for 15% All India Quota seats of contributing States and for specified central and deemed-university BDS seats. State/UT authorities conduct counselling for their respective BDS institutions and seats.

Do not treat an exam result as an admission offer: allocation depends on the relevant merit list, choices, seat matrix, reservation and eligibility verification. Counselling calendars, rounds, security deposits and participating-institute lists vary by academic year; the MCC website currently identifies its UG services as including BDS seat allotment and publishes schedules and seat matrices.
bullets: NEET-UG is the entrance examination route.
Apply separately to the applicable MCC and/or State/UT counselling process.
Check current seat matrices, college recognition/approval status, fee notices and round schedules before locking choices.

sections.heading: What comes after BDS
paragraphs: After completing BDS and the required internship, graduates can pursue general clinical dentistry subject to registration requirements, seek dental-surgeon roles where they meet the recruiting employer’s conditions, or build toward independent practice/clinic entrepreneurship within the profession’s registration and other applicable legal requirements. The Dentists Act provides that unregistered persons may not practise dentistry, while the Indian Dentists Register is maintained from State Dental Council information.

For specialization, the principal postgraduate route is MDS. NEET-MDS is the national entrance examination for MDS admissions; NBEMS states that candidates who have passed BDS (or an eligible recognized foreign dental degree) and are completing the 12-month compulsory rotating internship by the prescribed cut-off may take NEET-MDS, subject to the information bulletin’s conditions. The BDS regulations also expressly recognize the 4+1 BDS structure for purposes including MDS admission, government jobs and State Dental Council registration.

BDS graduates may also move toward public-health education such as MPH, health administration, research, teaching after meeting institution-specific requirements, or non-clinical oral-health programme roles. These routes are not governed by one universal BDS admission rule, so applicants should verify the destination university’s current eligibility criteria.
bullets: Clinical dentist/dental surgeon pathway: complete internship and obtain applicable registration before practising.
MDS specialization: take NEET-MDS and meet its current bulletin, internship and counselling conditions.
Government dental-surgeon recruitment: monitor the relevant Union, State, public-health-service or institutional vacancy notice; eligibility, registration and experience requirements vary.
MPH and other public-health or management study: check each university’s current admissions policy.
Clinic entrepreneurship: requires professional registration plus compliance with applicable State/local establishment, taxation, biomedical-waste, labour and other operational rules.

title: BHMS (Bachelor of Homeopathic Medicine and Surgery)
description: An undergraduate degree program focused on the holistic system of homeopathic medicine, with admission based on NEET-UG scores.

quick_facts.label: Award and regulator
quick_facts.value: BHMS is the Bachelor of Homoeopathic Medicine and Surgery undergraduate qualification; its graduate-course standards are prescribed by the National Commission for Homoeopathy (NCH).

quick_facts.label: Standard duration
quick_facts.value: The regulated programme is 5 years and 6 months: 18 months in the first professional phase, three further 12-month professional phases, and a 12-month compulsory rotatory internship.

quick_facts.label: Entry examination
quick_facts.value: Admission is based on NEET-UG. The NCH regulations require a uniform NEET for undergraduate admission and prescribe NEET qualifying percentiles, subject to any academic-year-specific relaxation notified by the competent authorities.

quick_facts.label: Counselling route
quick_facts.value: AACCC conducts counselling for 15% All India Quota BHMS seats in government/government-aided institutions and for 100% of BHMS seats in Central Universities, National Institutes, and deemed universities; State/UT authorities handle the applicable state-side counselling.

quick_facts.label: Teaching language
quick_facts.value: The BHMS programme’s prescribed medium of instruction is English.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: Under the current NCH graduate-course framework, an applicant must have passed 10+2 (or an equivalent qualification) with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology or Biotechnology. The 2025 amendment replaced the earlier wording on Class 12 subject-score thresholds; applicants should therefore use the current NCH/AACCC admission directions and the counselling authority’s bulletin for the applicable academic year.

Applicants must be at least 17 years old on or before December 31 of the admission year. For NEET-UG eligibility, the baseline qualifying standard is the 50th percentile; it is 40th percentile for SC/ST/OBC candidates and 45th percentile for General-category candidates with specified disabilities (40th percentile for SC/ST/OBC candidates with specified disabilities). The NCH, in consultation with the Central Government, may lower the NEET threshold for a particular academic year if the regulatory condition is met.
bullets: Pass 10+2/equivalent with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology or Biotechnology.
Meet the minimum-age condition of 17 years by December 31 of the admission year.
Qualify NEET-UG at the percentile applicable to the candidate’s category and that academic year.

sections.heading: Duration and internship
paragraphs: BHMS is structured as a 5.5-year programme. The first professional period is 18 months, followed by second, third, and fourth professional periods of 12 months each, and then a 12-month compulsory rotatory internship. The degree is awarded after the candidate passes the prescribed examinations and completes both the course of study and internship.

The internship is not optional: a student may join it only after passing all subjects from the first through fourth professional examinations, including the required electives, and after receiving provisional degree and provisional registration certificates as specified in the regulations.
bullets: First professional: 18 months.
Second, third, and fourth professional phases: 12 months each.
Compulsory rotatory internship: 12 months.

sections.heading: Curriculum and learning format
paragraphs: The NCH framework combines homoeopathic subjects with biomedical, clinical, public-health, research, and professional-development components. Named subjects include Homoeopathic Materia Medica; Organon of Medicine with Homoeopathic Philosophy; Homoeopathic Pharmacy; Repertory and Case Taking; anatomy, histology and embryology; physiology and biochemistry; pathology and microbiology; forensic medicine and toxicology; community medicine and public health; surgery; gynaecology and obstetrics; practice of medicine; modern pharmacology; research methodology and biostatistics; psychology; and yoga.

The programme includes a foundation course of at least 15 working days and 90 hours after admission. Minimum prescribed teaching is 2,268 hours over 324 days in the first professional session and 1,512 hours over 216 days in each subsequent professional session. Clinical classes are built into every professional phase, with practical/clinical and demonstrative learning formats such as laboratory training, dissection, field visits, case-based learning, and early clinical exposure.
bullets: Four professional phases, with university examinations at the end of each phase.
At least two electives are listed in each professional year; six electives must be cleared before internship eligibility.
Clinical, community, and hospital-based exposure are integral to the regulated programme.

sections.heading: Admission through NEET-UG and counselling
paragraphs: Candidates first take and qualify NEET-UG, then participate in the counselling authority responsible for the seat category and institution. Direct admission outside the prescribed Central, State, or Union Territory counselling process is not approved under the BHMS regulations (other than the separately addressed foreign-national route).

For the central route, AACCC administers online counselling for 15% All India Quota undergraduate BHMS seats in government/government-aided AYUSH institutions, as well as 100% of eligible BHMS seats in Central Universities, National Institutes, and deemed universities. The relevant State or UT counselling authority administers state/UT quota admissions under its rules. Counselling schedules, seat matrices, registration charges, security deposits, and cut-off dates are academic-year-specific and should be checked on the official portal rather than assumed from a prior cycle.
bullets: Use only the official NEET-UG result and counselling portals.
Confirm that the college and its permitted intake are included in the current official seat matrix.
Read the current-year counselling information bulletin before locking choices; procedures and dates can change.

sections.heading: Options after BHMS
paragraphs: A principal regulated postgraduate route is MD (Homoeopathy). Entry requires a recognised BHMS (or specified equivalent) completed with the one-year compulsory rotatory internship, registration with the relevant State Board or Council, and performance in AIAPGET. The NCH’s MD (Homoeopathy) regulations describe a regular, full-time three-year programme and list specialties including Homoeopathic Materia Medica, Organon of Medicine and Homoeopathic Philosophy, Repertory and Case Taking, Homoeopathic Pharmacy, Practice of Medicine, Paediatrics, Psychiatry, Community Medicine, and Dermatology.

For professional practice, graduates should verify registration requirements with the relevant State Board/Council. The NCH National Register states that National Register enrolment remains valid while the practitioner’s State Register name/registration number remains live. This makes maintaining the applicable registration status important for a practitioner pathway; specific employment, clinic, public-health, research, or entrepreneurship opportunities can have additional employer, State, or programme requirements.
bullets: Postgraduate study: sit AIAPGET and pursue eligible MD (Homoeopathy) admission through the prescribed process.
Professional pathway: complete internship and maintain the relevant State registration; check National Register status where applicable.
Other academic pathways such as MPH or clinical-research training are institution-specific and require checking each programme’s current eligibility rules.

title: BPT (Bachelor of Physiotherapy)
description: An undergraduate program focused on physical therapy to treat disease, injury, or deformity by physical methods.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: BPT is the entry-level degree pathway described in the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare/NCAHP Physiotherapy Handbook for preparing physiotherapy graduates to assess, manage and help optimise movement, function and quality of life.

quick_facts.label: Standard duration
quick_facts.value: The handbook specifies four academic years (or eight semesters) followed by a compulsory one-year full-time rotatory clinical internship.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry baseline
quick_facts.value: The handbook specifies 10+2/equivalent with Physics, Chemistry and Biology and 50% aggregate, plus age 17 in the current year; institutions and applicable state rules can impose additional conditions.

quick_facts.label: Admission route
quick_facts.value: BPT admission is not uniformly NEET-only nationally: the handbook provides for an entrance test conducted by a university, government or other competent authority and states that admission can also occur through NEET. Applicants must follow the current prospectus and counselling rules of the specific institution or state.

quick_facts.label: Regulatory context
quick_facts.value: Physiotherapy Professional is a recognised category in the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021; the Act provides for standards, institutional recognition and Central/State registers.

quick_facts.label: Direct postgraduate progression
quick_facts.value: The handbook sets out MPT as a two-year/four-semester programme and lists specialities including musculoskeletal, neuroscience, cardio-pulmonary, sports, paediatrics and neonatal, community, and oncological physiotherapy.

sections.heading: Eligibility for BPT
paragraphs: Under the national Physiotherapy Handbook’s stated selection procedure, an applicant should have passed Higher Secondary (10+2) or an equivalent recognised qualification with Physics, Chemistry and Biology and at least 50% aggregate marks. It also specifies that the applicant must be 17 years old in the current year and submit a physical-fitness certificate. For overseas or open-school qualifications, the handbook gives additional subject/equivalence conditions. Because admission is administered by universities, states and competent authorities, candidates should treat the current institutional prospectus as controlling for reservations, category relaxations, domicile, subject combinations and document requirements.
bullets: Academic baseline: 10+2/equivalent with PCB and 50% aggregate under the handbook’s selection procedure.
Age baseline: 17 years in the current year under the handbook.
Check the relevant university/state notification for any current variations or additional requirements.

sections.heading: Duration and clinical internship
paragraphs: The handbook’s minimum framework describes BPT as four years of academic training—either an annual pattern or eight semesters—plus a one-year, full-time rotatory clinical internship. It separately specifies the internship as 12 months and at least 2,016 hours, with rotations through outpatient and inpatient clinical facilities. The handbook also places the entry-level physiotherapy degree at a minimum five-year pathway including internship.
bullets: Academic component: 4 years or 8 semesters.
Internship: compulsory 1-year full-time rotatory clinical internship after passing the required examinations.
Internship minimum stated in the handbook: 2,016 hours.

sections.heading: What the curriculum covers
paragraphs: The national handbook is competency-based rather than limited to classroom theory. Its stated BPT outcomes include examination, assessment, evaluation and physiotherapeutic management of disease, disorders and trauma; health promotion; ethical practice; communication; evidence-informed decision-making; teamwork; and service management. The published scheme includes foundational sciences such as anatomy, physiology and biochemistry, alongside exercise modalities, electro-physical agents, psychology and sociology, healthcare delivery, clinical orientation, pathology, pharmacology, public health and health promotion. Exact subject sequencing, examinations and credit structures can vary where a university implements its own approved scheme.
bullets: Foundations: anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, psychology and sociology.
Professional and clinical learning: exercise modalities, electro-physical agents, clinical orientation, pathology, pharmacology and emergency-care skills.
Population-health component: public health and health promotion.
Training model: competency-based learning with practical/clinical skill development and internship.

sections.heading: How admission works, including NEET-UG
paragraphs: The handbook states that BPT admission should be based on eligibility and an entrance test, with the test conducted by the university, government or another competent authority; it also states that a candidate can be admitted through NEET. Therefore, NEET-UG is an important possible route, but it should not be represented as a universal national requirement for every BPT seat. Selection, counselling, merit rules, deadlines, seat categories and whether NEET is accepted or required are determined by the current notification of the relevant university, state authority or college. For context, the National Testing Agency’s 2026 notice archive records NEET-UG 2026 activity, but candidates must rely on the applicable admission authority rather than assume one examination route fits all BPT programmes.
bullets: Read the current BPT prospectus before applying; do not rely solely on general course listings.
Where an institution uses NEET, follow its stated score, counselling and document rules.
Where an institution conducts its own or a state/competent-authority test, follow that route and timetable instead.

sections.heading: Post-BPT study and career directions
paragraphs: A direct specialist progression is Master of Physiotherapy (MPT). The handbook describes MPT admission as requiring a recognised BPT/BSc Physiotherapy qualification with 50% pass marks and specifies a two-year/four-semester duration; it lists specialities such as musculoskeletal, neuroscience, cardio-pulmonary, sports, paediatrics and neonatal, obstetrics and gynaecology, community, and oncological physiotherapy. Graduates may also pursue physiotherapist roles in settings identified by the handbook, including hospitals, outpatient clinics, rehabilitation centres, community-health settings, schools, occupational-health centres, sports centres/clubs and physiotherapist private offices or clinics. Before choosing employment or entrepreneurship, verify the institution’s recognised status and the applicable Central/State registration requirements, because the NCAHP Act provides for standards, recognition and professional registers.
bullets: Specialise through MPT, subject to the university’s current admission criteria and entrance process.
Work across clinical rehabilitation, hospitals, outpatient care, community health, occupational health, education/research and sports settings.
Private clinic/practice is a possible work setting identified in the handbook; compliance obligations and local registration requirements should be checked before practice.

title: BS in Medical Sciences and Engineering
description: A four-year undergraduate program focusing on the intersection of medical sciences and engineering disciplines, offered by institutions like IIT Madras.

quick_facts.label: Award and provider
quick_facts.value: IIT Madras offers this as a four-year B.S. (Medical Sciences & Engineering) leading to a Bachelor of Science on completion of the programme’s credit requirements.

quick_facts.label: Admission route
quick_facts.value: For the regular 2026 intake, admission is through IAT 2026 qualification/rank and registration on the IIT Madras B.S. admissions portal; JEE or NEET is not the regular entrance requirement for this programme.

quick_facts.label: Class XII subject requirement
quick_facts.value: Applicants need Mathematics plus at least two of Biology, Chemistry and Physics in Class XII (or equivalent).

quick_facts.label: Learning format
quick_facts.value: The programme is campus-based and includes a hospital internship/clinical exposure component; IIT Madras states that it is fully offline, with campus presence required.

quick_facts.label: Professional limitation
quick_facts.value: This B.S. does not qualify a graduate to practise medicine as a doctor.

quick_facts.label: 2026 intake context
quick_facts.value: The published 2026 seat matrix lists 36 regular seats for Medical Sciences & Engineering, with category and gender-pool distribution shown by IIT Madras; seat availability and allocation are admission-year specific.

sections.heading: Eligibility for the IIT Madras B.S. (Medical Sciences & Engineering), 2026 intake
paragraphs: Applicants had to satisfy all three published conditions: qualify IAT 2026; be an Indian national or an OCI/PIO card holder whose card was issued before 4 March 2021; and meet the Class XII/equivalent requirements.
paragraphs

For the medical-sciences programme specifically, Class XII/equivalent must have been passed in 2024, 2025 or 2026 from a COBSE-recognised board, with Mathematics and at least two subjects among Biology, Chemistry and Physics. The minimum aggregate was 55% for SC/ST/PwD candidates and 60% for other categories. IIT Madras allowed applicants awaiting Class XII results to apply provisionally, subject to subsequently meeting the criteria.
bullets: Do not treat JEE Advanced or NEET as substitutes for IAT in the ordinary admission route: IIT Madras states that IAT is required and that NEET/JEE are not required for this B.S. programme.

Equivalent examinations and board-recognition rules are detailed in the IIT Madras 2026 information brochure; applicants with non-standard qualifications should use that brochure rather than assuming equivalence.

sections.heading: Duration and mode
paragraphs: This is a four-year, English-medium, credit-based undergraduate B.S. programme at IIT Madras. The institute describes it as a fully offline programme requiring presence on campus, rather than an online B.S. course.
The academic design includes hospital internship/visits intended to connect classroom learning with clinical practice.

sections.heading: What students study
paragraphs: The programme deliberately combines medical science with engineering. IIT Madras identifies basic engineering, fundamental sciences, mathematical methods, machine learning, medical imaging and physiological systems as broad curricular strands, taught by medical and engineering faculty.

Its published curriculum includes anatomy, physiology, mechanics and fluid mechanics for physiological systems, electrical circuits/bioelectricity, medical biochemistry, microbiology/immunology/pathology, medical genetics, medical imaging, biomedical signal processing, clinical-research statistics, pharmacology, surgery and surgical devices, AI in medicine, healthcare economics, medical image analysis, cardiovascular/respiratory mechanics, orthopaedic biomechanics, professional electives and a final project.

IIT Madras lists possible elective-led specialisation areas as organ-specific device development, AI applied to health, medical image analysis, quantitative pharmacology, drug design and deployment, translational medicine/regulatory processes, and fundamental physiological sciences. The detailed downloadable curriculum is labelled as effective from July 2023, so course titles and sequencing should be checked with IIT Madras for a future cohort.
bullets: Clinical and research orientation: hospital visits/internship, laboratory-oriented courses and a final-year project are built into the published structure.
Computational orientation: mathematical modelling, software skills, biomedical signal processing, AI in medicine and medical-image analysis feature in the published course plan.

sections.heading: Admission process and 2026 status
paragraphs: The regular IIT Madras route requires first taking IAT and then applying through the IIT Madras B.S. admissions portal. Offers are based on seat availability, the candidate’s IAT rank and category; a seat remains provisional until document verification and the institute’s joining formalities are completed.

For 2026, IIT Madras published a ₹1,000 non-refundable application processing fee for General/GEN-EWS/OBC-NCL candidates and ₹500 for SC/ST/PwD/third-gender/female candidates. A seat-acceptance fee applied only after an offer: ₹30,000 for General/EWS/OBC-NCL and ₹15,000 for SC/ST/PwD, including a ₹5,000 non-refundable processing charge. These are 2026-cycle figures and may change in later cycles.

As of 18 July 2026, the IIT Madras portal says new registration is closed. Applicants who received an allotment must follow the live, round-specific portal timeline rather than relying on an older brochure: deadlines and number of rounds can be revised during counselling.
bullets: 2026 regular-seat matrix: 36 Medical Sciences & Engineering seats, distributed across OPEN, GEN-EWS, OBC-NCL, SC, ST and PwD/female pools under the published matrix.

Other 2026 admission modes identified by IIT Madras included Sports Excellence, Fine Arts and Culture Excellence, and Science Olympiad Excellence; their rules and portals are separate from the IAT route.

sections.heading: Costs and fees
paragraphs: For the 2026 admission cycle, the application and seat-acceptance charges were as stated in the admission section. IIT Madras specifies that tuition and hostel charges for this B.S. use the institute’s B.Tech fee structure rather than a separately fixed programme fee schedule.

Costs should be treated as dated context, not a four-year price guarantee: institute fees, hostel/mess charges, category concessions, scholarships and refundable deposits may be revised by the institute. Applicants should consult the current IIT Madras fee circular and their offer letter before paying.

sections.heading: Career and further-study options
paragraphs: IIT Madras says graduates are eligible to use the IIT Madras placement cell in the same way as B.Tech students. Given the programme’s published focus on devices, AI in health, medical imaging, pharmacology, translational/regulatory processes and physiological science, plausible role directions include biomedical/medical-device R&D, device quality or regulatory work, clinical-research support and research-assistant roles. These are career directions rather than guaranteed designations; employers determine the precise degree, skills and experience required.

For postgraduate study, GATE is one relevant route: GATE 2026 permits students in the third year or later of a four-year B.S./B.Sc. (Research) programme, and a valid GATE score can be used to seek admission to relevant master’s, direct-doctoral and doctoral programmes subject to each admitting institution’s criteria. Other listed pathways such as CAT or CSIR-UGC NET have their own, separately published eligibility rules and should be checked for the year of application.

A critical distinction is that this undergraduate degree is not an MBBS-equivalent qualification and does not authorise medical practice. Students interested in clinical medicine should not select it on the assumption that it leads to doctor licensure.
bullets: Placement route: IIT Madras placement-cell eligibility after graduation.
Research and technical postgraduate route: GATE, subject to the chosen paper and the receiving programme’s eligibility rules.
Management route: CAT/MBA options may be considered after a bachelor’s degree, but the current CAT eligibility and each business school’s selection criteria must be verified separately.
Role directions aligned with the curriculum: biomedical engineer; medical-device R&D, quality-assurance or regulatory-affairs work; clinical-research support; and research-assistant positions.

title: BS-MS Dual Degree
description: A five-year integrated program in science, culminating in both a Bachelor of Science and a Master of Science degree, primarily offered by IISERs.

quick_facts.label: Credential and format
quick_facts.value: The IISER BS-MS is a five-year integrated science programme that awards BS and MS degrees; the central IISER admissions portal lists the regular 5-Year BS-MS at all seven IISERs.

quick_facts.label: Current admission route
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 admission cycle, entry to the regular IISER BS-MS programme is through the IISER Aptitude Test (IAT). IISER Pune states that the earlier JEE Advanced, KVPY and board channels were replaced from 2024 onward by the IAT-based channel.

quick_facts.label: 2026 qualifying-exam eligibility
quick_facts.value: For IAT 2026, applicants may have passed Class XII/equivalent or a qualifying three-year diploma in 2024, 2025 or 2026, or be appearing in 2026. For the regular five-year BS-MS, they must have taken at least three of Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics and Physics in the qualifying examination.

quick_facts.label: Research component
quick_facts.value: At IISER Pune, eight semesters of coursework, laboratories and semester projects are followed by two semesters devoted to a Master's research project. Programme structures and major options differ by IISER.

sections.heading: Who the programme is for
paragraphs: The regular IISER BS-MS pathway is designed for students entering after school-level science education and seeking an integrated, research-oriented science degree. In the 2026 IAT rules, eligible applicants include Indian nationals, OCI/PIO applicants and foreign nationals, subject to the stated qualifying-examination and documentation conditions.

For the 2026 cycle, a candidate must have passed Class XII/equivalent or an eligible three-year diploma in 2024–2026, or be appearing in 2026. A candidate who first passed the qualifying examination in 2023 or earlier is not eligible for IAT 2026. For admission to the five-year science BS-MS, at least three subjects from Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics and Physics must have been studied in the qualifying examination. Applicants should use the current-year brochure because these rules can change by cycle.
bullets: The programme is science-focused rather than a conventional single-discipline BSc from day one.
The subject combination requirement is specific to the regular 5-Year BS-MS; specialised IISER programmes can impose additional requirements.
Meeting eligibility permits an IAT application; admission still depends on the central counselling/allocation process and applicable seat availability.

sections.heading: Duration and award
paragraphs: The standard IISER BS-MS is a five-year integrated programme. It combines undergraduate and master's-level study in one continuous course and culminates in BS and MS degrees, rather than requiring a separate master's admission after a three-year bachelor's degree.

The central 2026 IISER portal identifies the regular five-year BS-MS as being offered across IISER Berhampur, Bhopal, Kolkata, Mohali, Pune, Thiruvananthapuram and Tirupati. Individual institutes may additionally offer distinct four-year BS, B.Tech. or specialised programmes, which should not be treated as interchangeable with the regular BS-MS.
bullets: Nominal duration: 5 years / 10 semesters.
Award: BS and MS degrees.
Primary setting: the IISER system of science education and research.

sections.heading: How the curriculum typically works
paragraphs: The programme is built to provide breadth before deeper specialisation. IISER Pune describes its BS-MS curriculum as integrating biological, chemical, mathematical, physical and earth sciences. Its structure includes three semesters of study across core science areas, alongside selected earth-science, humanities, trans-disciplinary and foundational courses.

At IISER Pune, students then identify pre-major disciplines around the third and fourth semesters and may proceed to a major, subject to completing its prescribed courses. The final two semesters are dedicated to a Master's research project, which may be completed at IISER Pune or another research laboratory in India or abroad. This is an institute-specific example, not a guarantee of the identical curriculum at every IISER.
bullets: Early phase: broad science coursework, lectures and laboratories.
Middle phase: pre-major/major exploration or credit-based interdisciplinary study, depending on institute rules.
Final phase: substantial supervised research and an MS project/thesis component.

sections.heading: Admission: IAT is the operative route
paragraphs: For the 2026 cycle, applicants apply through the central IISER admissions process and take the IISER Aptitude Test (IAT); the central portal coordinates admissions for the IISERs. The IAT information brochure covers eligibility, application procedures, syllabus, test arrangements, counselling and institute/programme allocation.

The node's historical JEE Advanced parent should be read with care: IISER Pune records that JEE Advanced, KVPY and the earlier board channel were used in previous years, but states that from 2024 candidates have been admitted only through the board channel with IAT. Thus, JEE Advanced is not the current regular admission channel for the IISER BS-MS as of the 2026 cycle.

Applicants should rely on the current central portal rather than past cut-offs, dates or admission-channel advice. The 2026 portal was already publishing the provisional IAT answer key and response/objection information by June 2026, illustrating why cycle-specific deadlines must be checked directly.
bullets: 1. Confirm that the qualifying-exam year and science-subject combination meet the current brochure rules.
2. Register for IAT and submit the required application and category/nationality documentation through the central portal.
3. Take IAT and participate in the central admission/counselling process if eligible by the published results and rules.
4. Review the programme/institute allocation, fee notice and joining instructions issued for the allotted IISER.

sections.heading: Fees: institute-specific and subject to revision
paragraphs: Fees are set by the admitting IISER and can change by batch, category, accommodation choice and policy. As a dated illustration only, IISER Pune's fee notice for the August 2025 BS-MS batch listed a first-semester total with hostel accommodation of ₹80,948 for General/OBC/KM/EWS students and ₹32,047 for SC/ST/PwBD students. The notice included one-time charges, a refundable caution deposit, insurance, semester charges and hostel fees; it is not a 2026 all-IISER fee quote.

Before accepting an offer, use the fee schedule issued by the allotted institute and distinguish refundable deposits, tuition/studentship charges, hostel/mess costs, insurance and one-time fees. IISER Pune maintains a BS-MS fee-structure page and PDF for its entering batch.
bullets: Do not extrapolate one IISER's fee notice to another institute or academic year.
Check whether accommodation is included and whether a listed deposit is refundable.
Use the current allotment and institute fee notice for the payable amount and due date.

sections.heading: What graduates can do next
paragraphs: A common progression is a PhD in a science or interdisciplinary research area. IISER Pune's doctoral programme accepts applicants with a master's degree in science, engineering or mathematics, and notes that national examinations such as CSIR-UGC NET, GATE, JEST, NBHM or JGEEBILS may be expected depending on the research area. Its stated policy also provides a test-eligibility exemption for BS-MS/master's graduates from Institutes of National Importance with CGPA 8.0 or above on a 10-point scale; departmental advertisements remain controlling.

The degree's research training can also support applications to research assistant, project staff and private-sector R&D roles, subject to the employer's requirements. IISER Pune describes its BS-MS students as receiving laboratory training and research-project exposure, and invites industry employers to recruit through campus interviews. Eligibility for BARC OCES/DGFS, DBT-JRF (BET), GATE, ISRO ICRB, CSIR-UGC NET and JEST must always be verified in the relevant examination or employer notification, because requirements, disciplines and age/category rules vary by cycle.
bullets: Doctoral study in India or abroad, usually through institute- and department-specific admissions.
National eligibility/entrance examinations where the current notification accepts the candidate's discipline and qualification.
Research assistant, project, laboratory and private R&D roles where a five-year science degree and research experience fit the job requirements.

title: Executive MBA
description: A one-year MBA program designed for working professionals with significant prior work experience.

quick_facts.label: What this node represents
quick_facts.value: In India, “Executive MBA” is not a single nationally standardised programme title. This node covers the intensive, full-time, one-year MBA format for experienced professionals, exemplified by IIM Ahmedabad’s MBA-PGPX and IIM Bangalore’s EPGP.

quick_facts.label: Typical duration and format
quick_facts.value: A leading example, IIM Bangalore EPGP, is a one-year, full-time residential MBA; IIM Ahmedabad likewise describes MBA-PGPX as a one-year full-time MBA.

quick_facts.label: Experience threshold
quick_facts.value: Experience requirements are programme-specific: IIM Ahmedabad MBA-PGPX requires at least four years of full-time post-graduation experience, while IIM Bangalore EPGP requires at least five years.

quick_facts.label: Common entrance tests
quick_facts.value: GMAT or GRE is required by the cited IIM Ahmedabad and IIM Bangalore one-year MBA admissions processes; applicants should check the current programme rules because accepted tests and score conditions can change by intake.

quick_facts.label: Fees: dated example
quick_facts.value: For context only, IIM Calcutta listed a programme fee of ₹33.50 lakh for its MBAEx 2025–26 batch, with some personal expenses excluded. Fees, inclusions, instalments, and financing terms vary by school and intake.

sections.heading: Who an Executive MBA is for
paragraphs: The one-year Executive MBA route is generally aimed at professionals who already have meaningful full-time experience and now want broad general-management preparation, rather than an entry-level management qualification. At IIM Ahmedabad, MBA-PGPX applicants need a bachelor’s degree or equivalent, a minimum age of 25 by the stated cut-off, at least four years of full-time experience after graduation, and a valid GMAT or GRE score. IIM Bangalore’s EPGP requires a bachelor’s degree with stipulated marks, at least five years of post-degree experience, and a valid GMAT or GRE score.

These examples illustrate the format rather than a universal India-wide rule: exact work-experience calculations, age cut-offs, academic thresholds, category provisions, and test-score policies belong to each school’s current admissions notice.
bullets: Suitable profile: an employed professional or entrepreneur seeking a management/leadership transition after building work experience.
Academic background: programmes can accept bachelor’s degrees across disciplines; professional qualifications may be treated separately under each school’s rules.
Work experience: count only the type and period the school explicitly recognises—do not assume internships, part-time work, or pre-graduation work will qualify.

sections.heading: Duration and study commitment
paragraphs: The canonical format is an intensive one-year, full-time residential programme. IIM Bangalore calls EPGP a one-year full-time residential MBA, and IIM Ahmedabad positions MBA-PGPX as a one-year MBA for experienced professionals. This is materially different from part-time, weekend, online, blended, or longer executive-management programmes that may also be marketed using “executive MBA” language.

Because the learning is compressed into roughly a year, applicants should plan for the opportunity cost of stepping away from full-time employment, as well as relocation and living arrangements where relevant.
bullets: Verify whether a programme is full-time residential or work-compatible before applying.
Check the academic calendar, attendance expectations, immersion travel, and whether internships are part of the format.
Do not infer that every programme labelled “Executive MBA” grants the same credential or follows the same duration.

sections.heading: What students study
paragraphs: Curricula combine management fundamentals with leadership and strategic decision-making. IIM Ahmedabad’s published MBA-PGPX structure begins with core “Building Blocks” courses and then moves into top-management preparation, electives, an international immersion, and a capstone. Its listed core subjects include customer value, data analysis, operations, finance and accounting, economics, organisational behaviour, corporate finance, communication, strategy, human resources, and legal aspects of business.

Electives allow participants to tailor study toward functions or sectors such as marketing, finance, supply chain, and strategy. At IIM Ahmedabad, participants may also pursue an individual research project, such as a business plan, industry note, case analysis, or paper addressing a socio-economic divide. Course lists and international components are school- and intake-specific.
bullets: Core management foundation: finance, economics, strategy, operations, marketing, organisational behaviour, and communication.
Experienced-professional focus: leadership, corporate governance, change, complex decision-making, and capstone integration.
Customisation: electives and, at some schools, research projects or international immersion.

sections.heading: How admission usually works
paragraphs: Admission is selective and holistic, not simply a test-score cut-off. IIM Bangalore requires applicants to submit academic records, a GMAT/GRE scorecard, statement of purpose, work-experience evidence, and two references; shortlisted applicants proceed to an interview. Its final composite assessment includes academic record, GMAT/GRE, quality of work experience, a writing-ability test, and interview performance.

At IIM Ahmedabad, the published MBA-PGPX requirements similarly combine eligibility screening with a valid GMAT/GRE and an admissions process involving shortlisting, essays, and faculty interviews. Current deadlines are intake-specific: for example, IIM Ahmedabad’s 2027–28 page lists application rounds in 2026, but expressly notes that dates may change. Applicants should rely on the relevant school’s live admissions page rather than old brochures or third-party deadline lists.
bullets: Prepare: degree transcripts/certificates, test score report, detailed résumé, employment proof, essays or statement of purpose, and references where required.
Take the required test in the accepted mode; the cited IIM Ahmedabad and IIM Bangalore policies exclude at-home GMAT/GRE scores for their stated cycles.
Apply early enough to accommodate test reporting, document verification, interview scheduling, loan processing, notice periods, and relocation.

sections.heading: Costs and financial planning
paragraphs: Cost should be assessed as total cost of attendance, not tuition alone. As a dated reference point, IIM Calcutta’s MBAEx fee page for the 2025–26 batch lists ₹33.50 lakh, payable in instalments, and states that tuition, course material, books, accommodation, economy airfare, and some immersion expenses were included; electricity, food, and personal expenses were excluded. This is an example from one school and one intake, not a market-wide price benchmark.

In IIM Ahmedabad’s MBA-PGPX guidance, the packaged fee is described as covering tuition, books/course materials, accommodation, and services such as library and computing, while international-immersion costs and certain utilities may be additional. Before accepting an offer, obtain the current fee schedule and identify refundable deposits, travel, visas, insurance, food, foregone salary, and financing costs.
bullets: Ask for the current batch’s official fee schedule and payment dates.
Confirm what is included: housing, meals, course materials, immersion travel, insurance, utilities, and deposits.
Treat scholarships and bank-loan availability as programme-specific; terms and eligibility can change.

sections.heading: Career and further-study options
paragraphs: Graduates commonly use the degree to pursue larger management responsibilities, change function or industry, return to an employer in a more strategic role, or explore entrepreneurship. IIM Ahmedabad describes MBA-PGPX as general-management preparation that can be shaped through electives around post-programme employment aims, and says its alumni move into senior leadership and entrepreneurial paths.

Career support should not be mistaken for a guaranteed outcome. IIM Ahmedabad states that its placement office supports the student placement committee but that placements are neither guaranteed nor an entitlement. The same programme says successful graduates are eligible to apply for higher studies, including PhD programmes; admission to any doctoral programme remains subject to that institution’s selection rules.
bullets: Career progression: leadership, strategy, product, consulting, transformation, and general-management roles, depending on prior experience and recruiting conditions.
Career change: use electives, projects, peer network, and career services to build evidence for a function or sector pivot.
Further study: an MBA may support applications to doctoral study, but it does not guarantee admission.

title: FPM (Fellow Programme in Management)
description: A doctoral-level program in management offered by premier institutions like IIMs, equivalent to a Ph.D., for those aspiring to careers in academia or research.

quick_facts.label: Level and nomenclature
quick_facts.value: FPM (Fellow Programme in Management) is the traditional name used for doctoral management education at Indian Institutes of Management. At IIM Ahmedabad, the historical FPM evolved into the PhD Programme in Management after IIMs gained degree-granting authority; IIMA first conferred the PhD title in 2019.

quick_facts.label: Typical purpose
quick_facts.value: It is designed for candidates seeking advanced research and academic careers rather than a master’s-level MBA outcome. IIM Bangalore describes its doctoral programme as a full-time PhD intended to develop internationally publishable research.

quick_facts.label: Award
quick_facts.value: The credential name now varies by institution and admission cycle: for example, IIM Bangalore states that successful doctoral candidates receive a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in their specialization.

quick_facts.label: Study mode and length
quick_facts.value: A conventional IIM management doctorate is generally full-time and residential. Published expectations differ by institute: IIM Bangalore lists a four-year full-time residential programme, while its doctoral FAQ says students are expected to finish within five years.

quick_facts.label: Entrance tests
quick_facts.value: CAT can be an accepted route for some management-doctoral applicants, but it is not universally mandatory. IIM Calcutta’s doctoral process, for example, permits specialization-specific alternatives such as GMAT, GRE, GATE, or UGC-JRF/NET for various areas.

sections.heading: Eligibility: postgraduate preparation is common, but institute rules control
paragraphs: Eligibility is institution- and specialization-specific. A representative official policy from IIM Calcutta accepts applicants with a first-class master’s degree or two-year postgraduate diploma plus a three-year bachelor’s degree; it also recognizes specified professional qualifications and four-year B.Tech/equivalent degrees. Its rules additionally state that non-engineering applicants with 10+2+5 years of education may apply.

Applicants should treat the relevant institute’s current admission notice as authoritative, including category-specific marks, degree-recognition, and specialization requirements. An MBA is useful preparation but is not inherently required: IIM Bangalore’s doctoral FAQ explicitly says candidates do not need to be MBA graduates.
bullets: Academic background normally needs to demonstrate strong prior performance; exact minimum marks, CGPA conversions, and qualifying degrees vary.
Check the selected research area’s requirements before applying, especially where quantitative, economics, behavioural-science, or domain-specific preparation is expected.
Meeting published minimum eligibility does not itself ensure shortlisting or admission.

sections.heading: Duration: coursework followed by independent doctoral research
paragraphs: The standard structure is multi-year: initial doctoral coursework, a comprehensive examination, and supervised dissertation research. IIM Bangalore says doctoral students are expected to complete coursework, pass a comprehensive examination, and then undertake publication-quality research; its FAQ gives an expected completion period of five years.

Time to completion is variable. IIM Ahmedabad’s archival account describes its doctoral programme as typically involving two years of coursework followed by several years of research under a thesis advisory committee, while IIM Bangalore’s programme listing characterizes its PhD as a four-year full-time residential programme. Candidates should therefore plan around the specific institute’s registration and completion rules rather than assume a single national duration.
bullets: Full-time participation is typical for the regular doctoral route.
The research stage culminates in a dissertation/thesis; progression is normally conditional on coursework and comprehensive-exam milestones.
Executive doctoral variants are separate programmes and may have different residency, work-experience, fee, and duration rules.

sections.heading: Curriculum: research methods, specialization depth, comprehensive examination, thesis
paragraphs: FPM/PhD curricula combine advanced training in a management specialization with research training. IIM Ahmedabad’s published FPM overview describes doctoral-level area courses, selected management courses for a broader overview, and skills for analysing managerial problems; after coursework, students must clear an area comprehensive examination before working on the dissertation.

The detailed credit structure and available areas change by institute. IIM Indore’s doctoral curriculum, for example, lists compulsory work in philosophy in management research alongside area courses, electives, research components, and workshops. Prospective scholars should compare faculty supervision capacity and current specialization offerings—not only the programme label—when deciding where to apply.
bullets: Early stage: common and area-specific doctoral coursework.
Milestone stage: comprehensive or area-comprehensive examination.
Research stage: proposal development, supervised original research, thesis submission, and defence.

sections.heading: Admission: test score plus research-focused selection
paragraphs: Admission is competitive and typically evaluates more than an entrance score. IIM Bangalore says area-level selection can draw on qualifying-test performance, prior academics, work experience, area-specific written tests, and interview performance. Its current doctoral FAQ lists CAT, GMAT, GRE, GATE, JRF/NET, and an IIMB test among acceptable options depending on the area.

CAT should therefore be understood as one possible pathway to this node, not as the universal or exclusive doctoral entrance examination. At IIM Calcutta, candidates may use CAT or, depending on specialization, specified alternative tests; score-validity and test-centre requirements are set in the applicable admissions notice.
bullets: Choose one or more research areas only after reviewing the faculty and area-wise test matrix.
Prepare for research-fit questions in the written assessment and interview, not only aptitude-test performance.
Confirm the application deadline, accepted test year, application fee, and document requirements from the live admission page for the intended batch; these are cycle-specific.

sections.heading: Costs and funding: often fellowship-supported, but verify the institute and cohort
paragraphs: Regular full-time management doctorates at IIMs may be funded rather than charged like an MBA, but support is not standardized nationally. IIM Bangalore’s published financial-support page lists a tuition-fee waiver and a monthly fellowship of ₹52,000, with additional grants and certain accommodation support subject to its stated terms. This is institution-specific published context, not a guaranteed package for every FPM/PhD applicant.

Before accepting an offer, verify the current fee waiver, fellowship duration, service obligations, hostel availability, continuation rules, medical coverage, and support available after programme milestones. IIM Bangalore states that fellowship recipients are expected to provide research-assistant and teaching-assistant service at stages of the programme, and that its stated support is available for up to five years from registration.
bullets: Do not extrapolate one IIM’s stipend or waiver to another institution.
Separate regular residential doctoral funding from executive/part-time doctoral fees.
Treat all funding figures as variable and confirm them in the admission offer and current financial-aid notice.

sections.heading: After FPM/PhD: academic and research-oriented careers
paragraphs: The primary pathway is academic or research work. IIM Bangalore identifies advanced research and academia, including teaching, as the suitable career direction for doctoral students, and frames the programme around high-quality research capable of international-standard publication. IIM Ahmedabad likewise describes its doctoral programme as preparation for careers in academia or research positions in industry.

Common next steps can include faculty positions in management schools or universities, research roles in industry and policy/knowledge institutions, and postdoctoral research. The competitiveness of each option depends on the candidate’s dissertation, publications, teaching experience, research methods, area of specialization, and hiring conditions at the time of application.
bullets: Academic-track candidates should build a publication record and teaching/research-assistant experience during the doctorate.
Research-track candidates can translate specialization and methods expertise into corporate, consulting, policy, or research-institute roles.
A postdoctoral fellowship can be a relevant bridge for candidates seeking further research output before faculty recruitment.

title: Integrated M.Sc. (BITS)
description: A five-year dual degree program offered by BITS Pilani, combining a Master of Science in a fundamental science with a Bachelor of Engineering.

quick_facts.label: Award structure
quick_facts.value: Students enter an integrated first-degree M.Sc. programme after Class 12; an intermediate B.Sc. is not awarded. M.Sc. students may be allotted a second B.E. degree under BITS Pilani’s dual-degree scheme.

quick_facts.label: M.Sc. disciplines covered by the dual-degree scheme
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 admission framework, the scheme covers M.Sc. Biological Sciences, Chemistry, Economics, Mathematics, Physics, and Semiconductor and Nanoscience, with a second B.E. programme allotted after the first year.

quick_facts.label: Normal time to complete both degrees
quick_facts.value: The requirements for the M.Sc. and B.E. degrees are structured for normal completion in five years; BITS also notes that dual-degree students may take about 5 to 5½ years depending on academic pace and programme requirements.

quick_facts.label: 2026 academic eligibility
quick_facts.value: For M.Sc. admission through BITSAT-2026, applicants need Class 12/equivalent with Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, a language, and one additional subject; minimum 75% aggregate in PCM and at least 60% in each PCM subject are required.

quick_facts.label: 2026–27 domestic fee context
quick_facts.value: For students admitted in 2026–27 at Pilani, Goa, or Hyderabad, the listed first-degree admission fee is ₹64,100 and semester fee is ₹291,500 per semester, before hostel, mess/electricity advances, other advances, and applicable additional charges. BITS states that tuition, summer-term, and hostel fees are revised upward annually; a student admitted to the second B.E. degree also pays that programme’s admission fee when admitted.

sections.heading: Eligibility for entry through BITSAT
paragraphs: For the 2026–27 first-degree admission cycle, the relevant entry route is BITSAT. An applicant to an M.Sc. programme must have completed Class 12 under the 10+2 system from a recognised Central or State board, or an equivalent qualification, with at least five subjects including Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, one language, and one further subject. The stated academic threshold is 75% aggregate in Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics (PCM), with at least 60% in each of those three subjects; theory and practical marks are both considered.

The 2026 eligibility page limits BITSAT-2026 eligibility to candidates appearing in Class 12 in 2026 or who passed in 2025, subject to its rules on first attempt, improvement examinations, result availability, and pass status. These cycle-specific rules should be rechecked for later BITSAT years.
bullets: PCM—not PCB alone—is the relevant subject combination for M.Sc. entry and for the later B.E. dual-degree pathway.
Meeting the academic eligibility minimum does not itself secure admission: allocation is merit-based through the applicable BITS admission process.

sections.heading: What “Integrated M.Sc. (BITS)” means—and when it becomes a five-year dual degree
paragraphs: BITS describes its M.Sc. programmes as integrated first degrees: they are entered after Class 12 and do not confer an intermediate B.Sc. The standard standalone integrated M.Sc. structure is designed for eight semesters, although BITS’s modular system permits variation in an individual student’s pace.

The canonical five-year route is created when an M.Sc. student receives and accepts a second B.E. degree under the dual-degree scheme. BITS states that the academic requirements for the two degrees are structured for normal completion in five years. Its broader education-process document gives an approximate range of 5 to 5½ years (10–11 semesters), so “five years” is a normal planning duration, not an unconditional guarantee.
bullets: Standalone M.Sc. integrated first degree: normally planned around eight semesters.
M.Sc. plus B.E. dual degree: normally planned around five years, potentially longer depending on registration pace and academic circumstances.

sections.heading: Curriculum and experiential learning
paragraphs: The programme combines an M.Sc. discipline with the requirements of the later-allotted B.E. discipline. BITS’s curriculum materials show composite, semester-wise patterns that retain the science first-degree coursework while adding engineering requirements; the exact course sequence depends on the selected M.Sc., the allotted B.E. branch, campus, and the student’s cohort. BITS therefore publishes programme-specific academic patterns rather than one identical syllabus for every dual-degree combination.

The broader integrated-first-degree education model includes common foundational study and electives. BITS states that students complete at least 12 electives across humanities, discipline, and open-elective categories. Integrated first-degree students can also choose the Practice School option: PS-I is two months after the second year and PS-II is five and a half months in the final year; BITS describes these as faculty-supervised, credit-bearing work at professional locations. A thesis may be an alternative to Practice School in relevant cases.
bullets: Science component: M.Sc. Biological Sciences, Chemistry, Economics, Mathematics, Physics, or Semiconductor and Nanoscience, as applicable.
Engineering component: a B.E. programme allotted through the internal dual-degree process.
Applied component: optional Practice School pathway, with PS-I and PS-II, or a permitted thesis alternative.
Course plans and degree requirements can change by cohort; students should use the academic bulletin and their registration advice as the controlling sources.

sections.heading: Admission and B.E. branch allotment
paragraphs: For domestic applicants, BITS identifies BITSAT—a computer-based online examination—as the primary merit route into integrated first-degree programmes, alongside a Board Topper scheme. Applicants submit one set of programme and campus preferences for the Pilani, K. K. Birla Goa, and Hyderabad campuses; offers are processed on merit, stated preferences, available facilities, and seats.

Admission to an M.Sc. programme does not mean that a particular B.E. branch is locked at entry. BITS states that every admitted M.Sc. student is accommodated in the dual-degree scheme for a second B.E. degree, with allocation made separately by campus after first-year performance using the Progressive Branching Index (PBI). Thus, the M.Sc. is the initial admission choice, while the engineering branch is competitively allotted after the first year and depends on first-year performance and branch-seat availability.

The 2026 BITSAT admissions cycle is time-sensitive. As of the official BITS admissions updates posted in July 2026, first-degree admission iterations were in progress; applicants should treat dates, cut-offs, fees, and iteration instructions as live information and check the official admissions portal rather than relying on prior-year schedules.
bullets: Choose and rank M.Sc. programmes/campuses in the BITS admissions preference process.
Complete the first year at the allotted campus.
Compete for the B.E. branch through campus-specific PBI-based dual-degree allocation.
Pay the additional second-programme admission fee when admitted to the B.E. degree.

sections.heading: Fees and budgeting considerations
paragraphs: For domestic students entering first-degree programmes in academic year 2026–27, BITS lists the same base charges across Pilani, Goa, and Hyderabad: ₹64,100 admission fee, ₹291,500 semester fee in each of the first two semesters, ₹36,000 hostel fee per semester for on-campus students, ₹10,000 mess and electricity advance per semester, ₹12,000 other advances per semester, ₹3,000 institute caution deposit, and annual Students’ Union and Student Aid Fund charges. Mess/electricity and other advances are described as adjustable, so they should not be treated as final consumption costs.

This is dated fee context, not a five-year fee quote. BITS expressly states that semester tuition, summer-term, and hostel fees for the 2026–27 entrant cohort will rise each year. A dual-degree student also pays the admission fee for the second B.E. programme at the time it is allotted. Costs can further vary with summer-term registration, Practice School, campus living arrangements, taxes or new levies, and personal expenses.
bullets: Use the official 2026–27 fee schedule for current components and payment timing.
Budget for annual fee revisions rather than multiplying first-year charges by five.
Include the second-programme admission fee if a B.E. dual-degree allotment is accepted.

sections.heading: Further study, examinations, and career directions
paragraphs: The combined science-and-engineering curriculum can support several directions represented by this node’s children: postgraduate engineering or science study (including an M.S. abroad or Ph.D.), software and data roles, graduate-engineer and technical consulting roles, research-organisation roles, entrepreneurship, and management or public-service examinations. These are pathways to investigate rather than automatic outcomes; selection depends on academic record, skills, projects, experience, entrance tests, recruitment criteria, and the requirements of each destination institution or employer.

For research progression, BITS Pilani’s 2026–27 Ph.D. brochure lists M.Sc., B.E., and equivalent qualifications with at least 60% aggregate among the minimum entry qualifications, while noting that departments may apply additional shortlisting criteria and that minimum eligibility does not guarantee admission. For government-research careers, current CSIR Scientist Recruitment and Assessment Promotion Rules show that Scientist-B requirements vary by stream: science posts may require an M.Sc. or equivalent, engineering posts a B.E./B.Tech. or equivalent, and some streams have distinct requirements. This illustrates why graduates should read the recruitment notice for the exact discipline and post.

For examination-led transitions, graduates should verify the relevant annual notification. UPSC ran the Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination 2026 under its published schedule; CAT and management-school requirements, as well as civil-services rules, are set by their respective current notifications and institutes. The degree itself does not replace exam-specific eligibility, performance, or selection requirements.
bullets: MS in Engineering abroad or Ph.D. in Science: build research exposure, strong grades, recommendations, and meet the destination university’s stated admissions requirements.

Software Developer, Data Scientist, Graduate Engineer Trainee, Management Consultant, or Scientist roles: use the M.Sc.–B.E. combination alongside internships/Practice School, projects, technical preparation, and each employer’s recruitment criteria.

Tech Startup Founder: pursue through independent venture-building; BITS identifies entrepreneurship and innovation support as part of its student ecosystem, but startup outcomes are inherently individual and uncertain.
CAT and UPSC Civil Services Examination: track the official yearly eligibility rules, registration dates, syllabus, and selection process.
