PCI final M.Pharm scheme and syllabus

title: M.Plan (Master of Planning)
description: A postgraduate degree focusing on the design and management of urban and regional environments, including land use, transportation, and infrastructure.

quick_facts.label: Credential and typical format
quick_facts.value: M.Plan (Master of Planning) is a postgraduate planning degree. At the School of Planning and Architecture (SPA), New Delhi, its Urban Planning, Housing, and Transport Planning M.Plan programmes are listed as two-year programmes.

quick_facts.label: Common specialisations
quick_facts.value: Specialisations differ by institution. SPA New Delhi publishes M.Plan pathways in Environmental Planning, Housing, Regional Planning, Transport Planning, and Urban Planning.

quick_facts.label: Entry background
quick_facts.value: B.Plan and B.Arch are directly relevant feeder qualifications, but eligibility is institution- and specialisation-specific. SPA New Delhi’s published M.Plan criteria also accept selected engineering and social-science degrees for particular specialisations, subject to minimum marks.

quick_facts.label: Admission basis
quick_facts.value: At SPA New Delhi, the published postgraduate selection process considers qualifying-examination performance, a valid GATE/CEED/UGC-NET score where applicable, portfolio/thesis/project, interview, statement of purpose, and work experience. Applicants should treat this as an institution-specific example and check the current admission notice.

quick_facts.label: Illustrative public-institution cost
quick_facts.value: For SPA New Delhi’s 2024–25 fee schedule for Indian postgraduate students, general-category tuition was listed as ₹45,000 per semester and SC/ST tuition as ₹22,500 per semester, with additional institutional and optional hostel charges. This is dated 2024–25 information, not a national fee benchmark.

sections.heading: Eligibility: B.Plan and B.Arch are strong routes, but not the only ones
paragraphs: An M.Plan is commonly a next step after B.Plan or B.Arch, particularly for applicants seeking advanced work in urban, regional, housing, environmental, or transport planning. However, the exact qualifying degree, marks threshold, and accepted disciplines are set by each institution and can vary by specialisation.

SPA New Delhi’s published criteria require at least 55% aggregate or equivalent credits for general applicants and 50% for SC/ST/OBC applicants. For example, its Urban and Regional Planning routes accept planning, architecture, civil/architectural engineering and, for some routes, relevant master’s degrees in geography, economics, or sociology. Its Environmental Planning route additionally lists environmental engineering and selected environmental/social-science master’s qualifications. Applicants should verify the live notice for the target institution rather than assume that every M.Plan accepts the same background.
bullets: For an applicant with B.Plan or B.Arch: identify the intended planning specialisation, then compare its current eligibility rule and required documents.

For applicants from engineering or social-science backgrounds: check whether the specific specialisation explicitly lists the degree; eligibility can be narrower than the generic title “M.Plan” suggests.
Confirm the applicable marks rule, category provisions, score requirements, portfolio expectations, and whether final-year applicants may apply.

sections.heading: Duration
paragraphs: A full-time M.Plan is commonly structured as a two-year postgraduate programme. SPA New Delhi explicitly identifies its M.Plan programmes in Urban Planning, Housing, and Transport Planning as two-year programmes. The academic structure, internship requirements, and maximum time to complete the degree should nevertheless be checked in the rules of the admitting university.
bullets: Typical study pattern: two academic years.
Named specialisation and programme rules matter: M.Plan (Urban Planning), M.Plan (Housing), and M.Plan (Transport Planning) can have different course and studio emphases.

sections.heading: Curriculum: applied planning, analysis, studios, and thesis work
paragraphs: M.Plan curricula are specialisation-led and combine planning theory with applied analysis and studio-based work. SPA New Delhi’s Urban Planning syllabus, for example, includes city and metropolitan planning, infrastructure planning, sustainable planning and development, project planning and management, quantitative methods and GIS applications, land-use and transport planning, governance, development finance, planning legislation, studios, research seminar, and a final thesis.

The applied focus is visible across specialisations. SPA New Delhi describes its Urban Planning programme as using GIS, project planning, information technology, and studios based on real-world urban-development cases. Its Housing programme combines lectures, field assignments, and practical studios addressing housing policy, finance, infrastructure, informal settlements, GIS, real-estate project formulation, and governance. Its Transport Planning programme covers urban transport, public transport, traffic engineering, highway planning and design, transport economics, freight, road safety, intelligent transport systems, and policy.
bullets: Common capabilities developed: spatial and policy analysis, data and GIS use, plan preparation, infrastructure assessment, project formulation, research, professional communication, and implementation thinking.
Likely learning modes: taught courses, studios, fieldwork or case studies, electives, research seminar, and thesis.

Choose the specialisation based on the problem domain you want to work in—such as urban development, housing, regional development, environment, mobility, or transport systems—not only on the generic M.Plan title.

sections.heading: Admission: monitor institution-specific notices and prepare a planning portfolio
paragraphs: There is no single all-India M.Plan admission route. Institutions prescribe their own application calendars, eligibility conditions, entrance-score treatment, interviews, and documents. SPA New Delhi’s published process illustrates a multi-factor assessment: shortlisted candidates attend an in-person interview, and selection considers qualifying performance, valid GATE/CEED/UGC-NET score, portfolio/thesis/project, statement of purpose, and relevant work experience.

For the published SPA process, an applicant can apply to only one programme, and the page lists a non-refundable application fee of ₹2,500 for Indian nationals. These details are from SPA’s published postgraduate admissions information and may change in a later admission cycle; do not rely on historical dates, fees, or seat numbers without checking the current notification.
bullets: Build an application file early: marksheets, degree/provisional certificate, category documents if relevant, scorecard if required, CV, portfolio or thesis/project material, and statement of purpose.
Match the portfolio to the specialisation: show planning analysis, maps/GIS, studio outputs, research, policy work, fieldwork, design or infrastructure projects as relevant.
Use only the current notice of the chosen institution for deadlines, intake, score validity, interview format, and reservation rules.

sections.heading: Costs: use current institutional schedules, not a national average
paragraphs: M.Plan fees vary substantially by institution, applicant category, domicile or sponsorship status, hostel choice, and the academic session. As a dated public-institution example, SPA New Delhi’s fee notice dated June 21, 2024 for the 2024–25 session lists postgraduate tuition for Indian students at ₹45,000 per semester for the general category and ₹22,500 per semester for the SC/ST category. It separately lists enrolment, registration, academic-support, student-activity, refundable security-deposit, and hostel charges.

This example should not be projected to 2026–27 or treated as a typical private-college fee. Compare the latest fee notice and hostel/mess charges for every shortlisted institution, and separately budget for software, printing, fieldwork, travel, laptop/GIS needs, accommodation, and living expenses.
bullets: Dated SPA New Delhi 2024–25 illustration: general-category postgraduate tuition ₹45,000 per semester; SC/ST postgraduate tuition ₹22,500 per semester.

SPA’s same notice lists a refundable postgraduate school-and-library security deposit of ₹20,000 at admission and annual hostel room rent/electricity totalling ₹28,000 before the listed refundable hostel security; these figures are historical and may have changed.

SPA’s published postgraduate admissions page also states that limited merit scholarships may be available to non-sponsored postgraduate students with a valid GATE score, subject to government and school terms.

sections.heading: Next options after M.Plan
paragraphs: An M.Plan can lead to planning and related roles in public agencies, development authorities, urban local bodies, consulting, research, NGOs, real-estate and infrastructure organisations, and international-development settings. SPA New Delhi’s Urban Planning department reports alumni working with central and state town-and-country-planning organisations, development authorities, urban local bodies, international agencies, developers, consultants, research institutes, and NGOs; this is an institutional example rather than a placement guarantee.

For further study, relevant next steps can include a PhD in planning or an allied field, subject to each university’s doctoral eligibility and selection process. SPA New Delhi lists PhD programmes alongside its M.Plan offerings. Specialised professional development can also build depth in GIS and spatial analysis, urban policy, transport modelling, housing and real estate, climate resilience, infrastructure, or public finance.
bullets: Public-sector and statutory planning work: town and country planning organisations, development authorities, and urban local bodies.
Private and third-sector work: planning and urban-design consultancies, developers, infrastructure and mobility organisations, NGOs, and research bodies.
Academic/research route: pursue a PhD where eligible, or combine planning practice with research, teaching, policy, and technical specialisation.

title: M.S. (Pharm.) Master of Science in Pharmacy
description: A postgraduate pharmacy degree at NIPER focused on advanced pharmaceutical science research and specialisations.

quick_facts.label: Credential and setting
quick_facts.value: M.S. (Pharm.) is a postgraduate pharmacy-sciences degree offered across the NIPER system. NIPER is an autonomous institution under India’s Department of Pharmaceuticals and is designated an Institute of National Importance.

quick_facts.label: Standard duration
quick_facts.value: The M.S. (Pharm.) programme is ordinarily a two-year postgraduate programme; the precise academic structure and available specialisations depend on the admitting NIPER campus.

quick_facts.label: Entry route
quick_facts.value: Admission to the master’s programmes is through NIPER JEE and subsequent merit-based counselling. The 2026 NIPER JEE portal covers the seven participating NIPERs and publishes master’s counselling notices and seat-matrix updates.

quick_facts.label: Specialisation-led degree
quick_facts.value: Rather than one uniform subject syllabus, M.S. (Pharm.) admissions are made to named specialisations. Recent NIPER admission material lists examples including Medicinal Chemistry, Natural Products, Pharmaceutical Analysis, Pharmacology and Toxicology, Pharmaceutics, Pharmacoinformatics, Regulatory Toxicology, Traditional Medicine, and Regulatory Affairs; not every specialisation is offered at every campus or in every admission cycle.

sections.heading: Eligibility is specialisation-specific
paragraphs: Applicants must first match the qualifying-degree requirement for the particular M.S. (Pharm.) specialisation they select. In the published NIPER master’s brochure, examples include B.Pharm. or M.Sc. Organic Chemistry for Medicinal Chemistry and Natural Products; B.Pharm. or M.Sc. Organic/Analytical Chemistry for Pharmaceutical Analysis; B.Pharm., B.V.Sc., MBBS, or M.Sc. Pharmacology for Pharmacology and Toxicology; and B.Pharm. for Pharmaceutics.

The same published brochure states a general minimum of 60% aggregate marks or a 6.75/10 CGPA in the qualifying degree, and ordinarily requires GPAT, GATE, NET, or another national fellowship qualification. It specifies exceptions for holders of MD, MVSc, MDS, or Pharm.D degrees, foreign nationals, and certain sponsored candidates. These requirements are admission-cycle rules, so applicants should treat the revised 2026 brochure and notices as controlling before applying.
bullets: Pharmacoinformatics has a wider listed entry base, including B.Pharm., B.Tech. Bioinformatics, and specified M.Sc. science subjects.
Regulatory Affairs has a wider listed entry base that includes B.Pharm., certain engineering degrees, selected clinical degrees, and specified M.Sc. subjects.
Eligibility is not interchangeable across specialisations: select the discipline first, then verify the matching degree and examination requirements in the live NIPER JEE material.

sections.heading: Two-year, research-oriented postgraduate study
paragraphs: NIPER Hyderabad describes M.S. (Pharm.) as a two-year postgraduate degree and identifies a range of departmental pathways. Its course page also notes an opportunity to spend the second year in industry or at NIPER Hyderabad; this is a campus-specific feature rather than a guarantee applicable to every NIPER or specialisation.

The degree is research-oriented in practice: NIPER Hyderabad states that research leading to M.S. (Pharm.) degrees is undertaken by scholars under faculty guidance, using departmental laboratory resources and covering theoretical as well as experimental work.

sections.heading: Curriculum: advanced pharmaceutical science through a chosen discipline
paragraphs: The curriculum is anchored in the selected department rather than a single all-NIPER M.S. (Pharm.) syllabus. At NIPER Hyderabad, listed M.S. (Pharm.) disciplines include Medicinal Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Analysis, Pharmacology and Toxicology, Pharmaceutics, Regulatory Toxicology, Regulatory Affairs, Natural Products, Pharmacoinformatics, Biopharmaceuticals, and Medical Devices.

Teaching combines advanced subject modules, laboratory work, and supervised research. Illustrative official course listings at NIPER Hyderabad include Experimental Pharmacology, Clinical Pharmacology and Regulatory Toxicology, Principles and Methods in Toxicology, General Pharmacology, Drug Metabolism, Molecular Toxicology, Quality Control and Quality Assurance, and Pharmacopeial Methods of Analysis. Actual course codes, electives, research topics, and dissertation arrangements vary by department and campus.

Prospective students should compare the current seat matrix, departmental research areas, laboratory capabilities, and course/syllabus pages before ranking preferences in counselling. A discipline available at one NIPER may be absent at another.
bullets: Medicinal-chemistry and natural-products pathways emphasise chemical and drug-discovery research.
Pharmaceutical-analysis pathways address analytical, quality-control, quality-assurance, and pharmacopeial methods.
Pharmacology, toxicology, pharmaceutics, and pharmacoinformatics pathways align the degree with different experimental, formulation, safety, or computational research approaches.

sections.heading: Admission through NIPER JEE and counselling
paragraphs: For master’s programmes, the NIPER Ordinance provides that admission is based on merit in the entrance test. The NIPER JEE 2026 portal identifies NIPER Mohali as the organising institute and records master’s-programme notices for document submission, merit lists, seat matrices, web-option registration, and online counselling.

For the 2026 cycle, the official schedule recorded online applications from April 16, 2026, through May 23, 2026 (11:50 PM IST), with the computer-based NIPER JEE on June 13, 2026. The portal subsequently announced web-option registration and online counselling for M.S. (Pharm.), M.Pharm., and M.Tech. beginning July 10, 2026. These dates are historical as of July 19, 2026 and should not be used to predict the next cycle’s dates.

Applicants should use the current NIPER JEE portal to register, upload the required qualifying-degree and entrance-examination evidence, participate in merit/counselling steps if eligible, and verify documents when instructed. Programme availability and the seat matrix can be updated during a cycle.
bullets: Check the current revised master’s information brochure before submitting an application.
Rank only specialisations and campuses for which the applicant meets the published discipline-specific eligibility.
Keep original qualifying-degree, marks, entrance-score, category/PwBD where applicable, and sponsorship documents ready for verification when required.

sections.heading: Progression after the M.S. (Pharm.)
paragraphs: A direct academic progression is a Ph.D. in pharmaceutical, chemical, biological, or allied research. NIPER’s published Ph.D. eligibility material explicitly recognises relevant M.S. (Pharm.) specialisations for doctoral routes such as Medicinal Chemistry/Pharmaceutical Technology, Natural Products, Pharmacoinformatics, and Pharmacology and Toxicology, subject to the discipline-specific eligibility published for that cycle.

The degree also develops a research profile through faculty-guided theoretical and experimental work. Graduates should map their dissertation topic, laboratory methods, and specialisation to the entry requirements of the particular doctoral programme or research opportunity they pursue, rather than assuming that every M.S. (Pharm.) specialisation qualifies for every Ph.D. discipline.
bullets: Consider NIPER JEE Ph.D. admissions or other doctoral programmes whose discipline-specific eligibility explicitly accepts the completed M.S. (Pharm.) specialisation.
Build a portfolio of research outputs permitted by the programme, such as dissertation work, technical methods, presentations, and publications where available.
For research roles or further study, use the department’s research areas and facilities to identify a coherent specialisation-to-opportunity fit.

title: M.Sc. Forestry
description: A postgraduate degree covering advanced forest management, silviculture, forest ecology, conservation and forest-resource research.

quick_facts.label: Award and level
quick_facts.value: M.Sc. Forestry is a postgraduate forestry degree; the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE) curriculum report specifies the award title as “M.Sc Forestry,” with institutions also offering closely named variants such as M.Sc. Forestry & Environmental Sciences.

quick_facts.label: Usual duration
quick_facts.value: The standard model is two academic years / four semesters. This is stated in ICFRE’s model curriculum and is reflected in current programme listings at Guru Ghasidas Vishwavidyalaya and NERIST.

quick_facts.label: Entry qualification
quick_facts.value: B.Sc. (Hons.) Forestry is the most directly aligned feeder degree. However, eligibility is institution-specific: ICFRE’s model recommended a four-year B.Sc. Forestry with stated minimum marks, while FRI and Guru Ghasidas Vishwavidyalaya also publish routes for graduates with specified science, agriculture, biology, mathematics or environmental-science backgrounds.

quick_facts.label: Academic emphasis
quick_facts.value: Model and institutional curricula combine advanced forest management, silviculture, ecology, biodiversity conservation, forest protection, resource economics, geospatial methods, research methods, specialization coursework, and dissertation/project training.

sections.heading: Eligibility: Forestry graduates are the canonical entrants, but accepted backgrounds vary
paragraphs: For the canonical pathway, a B.Sc. (Hons.) Forestry provides the directly relevant foundation. ICFRE’s model M.Sc. Forestry framework recommended eligibility of a four-year B.Sc. Forestry with 50% aggregate marks for the general category and 45% for SC/ST candidates; this is a curriculum recommendation rather than a universal, current admission rule.

Actual university rules can be broader. FRI’s published 2022–24 bulletin accepted a B.Sc. with at least one of Botany, Chemistry, Geology, Mathematics, Physics or Zoology, or a B.Sc. in Agriculture or Forestry. Guru Ghasidas Vishwavidyalaya lists B.Sc. Forestry, B.Sc. (Hons.), or a 10+2+3 B.Sc. with Forestry, Biology, Mathematics, Agriculture or Environmental Sciences among the accepted subject backgrounds, with a 50% aggregate threshold. Applicants should treat the target institution’s current prospectus as controlling, including category relaxations, subject prerequisites and document requirements.

Because programme titles and prerequisites differ across institutions, graduates from non-forestry science or agriculture degrees should verify subject-level eligibility before applying rather than assuming that every M.Sc. Forestry programme accepts all science graduates.
bullets: Canonical preparation: B.Sc. (Hons.) Forestry / four-year B.Sc. Forestry.
Possible alternative feeder disciplines at particular institutions: agriculture and specified basic-science, biology, mathematics or environmental-science backgrounds.
Published minimum-mark rules and reservation provisions are institution- and admission-cycle-specific.

sections.heading: Duration and programme structure
paragraphs: M.Sc. Forestry is ordinarily structured as a two-year, four-semester postgraduate programme. ICFRE’s model framework specifies four semesters across two academic years, and official programme pages at Guru Ghasidas Vishwavidyalaya and NERIST likewise state a two-year duration.

In ICFRE’s model, the first year concentrates on core and supporting coursework; the early second year covers specialization coursework, followed by a dissertation and an attachment with an industry, organisation or institute. Universities may adapt this framework under their academic regulations, so the exact credit total, fieldwork and thesis/attachment requirements must be checked in the adopted syllabus.
bullets: Typical duration: 2 academic years.
Typical structure: 4 semesters.
Common culminating components in the ICFRE model: dissertation and institutional/industry attachment.

sections.heading: What students study
paragraphs: The degree develops advanced capability in planning, managing, conserving and researching forest resources. ICFRE’s model core includes Advanced Silviculture, Forest Biometric, Advanced Forest Management, Remote Sensing & GIS, Forest Resource Management and Economics, Wood-based Industries, Chemistry of Forest Products, Forest Policy and Utilization, Advanced Forest Ecology, Forest Biodiversity Conservation, and Forest Protection.

Research and analytical preparation is built into the model through computer applications/information technology, research methodology and statistical methods, plus a seminar. The prescribed framework also includes a dissertation and attachment, making research design, data analysis, technical communication and applied exposure integral rather than optional add-ons in that model.

Specialisation availability depends on the university. ICFRE’s framework identifies options including wood science and technology, medicinal and aromatic plants, plantation technology, watershed management, eco-tourism, agroforestry, bio-energy, forest biotechnology, environmental management and forest business management. NERIST describes complementary faculty expertise spanning forest ecology, wood science, taxonomy, ethnobotany, silviculture, biodiversity conservation, wildlife management, genetics, forest economics and environmental restoration.
bullets: Core themes: silviculture, forest management, ecology, biodiversity, protection, policy, economics and forest products.
Methods and tools: biometrics, statistics, research methodology, remote sensing and GIS.
Applied/research elements: seminar, dissertation/project work, and—under the ICFRE model—an institutional or industry attachment.
Specialisation options differ by campus and may reflect regional forestry needs.

sections.heading: Admission: verify the current institution-level notice
paragraphs: There is no single current all-India admission route evidenced by the sources for every M.Sc. Forestry provider. Admission is set by the admitting university. ICFRE’s model report proposed a national entrance test for a portion of seats and allowed universities to determine the mode for other seats; this should be read as a policy-model recommendation, not as a standing nationwide rule.

As an example of institution-specific practice, FRI’s 2022–24 M.Sc. Forestry bulletin used an online remote-proctored admission test and required applicants to meet its published B.Sc.-level eligibility and qualifying-mark conditions. That bulletin is historical: its application deadline and test date must not be reused for a later cycle.

A sound application process is to identify the exact degree title and specialisation, read the university’s current admission notice, confirm eligibility against the marksheet, and follow its stated examination, merit, counselling, reservation and document-verification procedures.
bullets: Do not rely on an old entrance-test date, fee or seat count.
Check the current prospectus/admission portal of each target university.
Confirm whether selection is through an entrance test, academic merit, counselling, or a combination specified by that institution.

sections.heading: Next options after the degree
paragraphs: A principal academic progression is doctoral research in forestry or a closely related environmental/forest-science field. NERIST states that its forestry department offers degree, postgraduate and Ph.D. programmes and that its faculty guide doctoral students; Guru Ghasidas Vishwavidyalaya also lists a Ph.D. alongside its M.Sc. Forestry & Environmental Sciences programme.

The M.Sc. curriculum’s dissertation, research-methodology and specialisation components can provide preparation for research-focused doctoral applications. The appropriate Ph.D. discipline and admission route will depend on the target university’s research areas and current doctoral regulations.
bullets: Ph.D. in Forestry or Forestry & Environmental Sciences.

Research-oriented pathways aligned with the student’s M.Sc. specialisation, such as forest ecology, biodiversity, silviculture, forest products, geospatial analysis, agroforestry or environmental management.
Applicants should review the target university’s current doctoral entrance and supervisor-availability requirements.

title: M.Sc. in Agriculture
description: A postgraduate degree focusing on advanced topics in agricultural science, research, and specialized farming practices.

quick_facts.label: Award and specialization
quick_facts.value: ICAR’s minimum standards recognise the postgraduate award as “M.Sc. (Agriculture)” with a disciplinary suffix, rather than a single undifferentiated programme. Listed suffixes include Agronomy, Agricultural Economics, Agricultural Extension & Communication, Entomology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Soil Science and Agricultural Chemistry, Plant Pathology, Seed Science and Technology, Plant Biotechnology, and others.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry qualification
quick_facts.value: For M.Sc. (Agriculture), ICAR’s published minimum educational requirement is a B.Sc. (Agriculture). Individual universities and entrance bulletins can add subject-specific, marks, domicile, or document requirements.

quick_facts.label: Standard duration
quick_facts.value: ICAR’s common academic regulations specify a minimum residential requirement of two academic years (four semesters) for a master’s degree; the stated maximum is five academic years (ten semesters).

quick_facts.label: National admission route
quick_facts.value: NTA administers ICAR AIEEA (PG) for admission to master’s programmes in agriculture and allied sciences and for ICAR-PG Scholarships. University-specific admissions may use additional or different routes.

quick_facts.label: Fee context
quick_facts.value: Fees vary materially by university and specialization. As one dated institutional example, Punjab Agricultural University lists ₹63,375 for the first semester of its M.Sc. Agricultural Extension Education programme; this should not be treated as a national fee benchmark.

sections.heading: Eligibility after B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture
paragraphs: The direct academic pathway from the parent node is well aligned: ICAR’s published minimum standard for M.Sc. (Agriculture) admission is a B.Sc. (Agriculture). A B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture graduate should nevertheless check the chosen university’s current prospectus, because admission rules can specify an eligible undergraduate subject combination, minimum marks, category provisions, and required certificates.
source_urls
bullets: ICAR minimum qualification: B.Sc. (Agriculture).
The intended M.Sc. discipline matters: applicants should match their undergraduate preparation to the selected specialization and the current university/entrance bulletin.
Final eligibility is determined by the admitting university and the applicable entrance authority for that admission cycle.

sections.heading: Duration and academic structure
paragraphs: Under ICAR’s common academic regulations for postgraduate programmes, the master’s residential requirement is normally two academic years across four semesters. The same regulations set a maximum completion window of five academic years (ten semesters), subject to the institution’s rules. They also contemplate course-work evaluation and submission of a master’s thesis during the prescribed residency period.
source_urls
bullets: Minimum duration: 2 academic years / 4 semesters.
Published maximum duration under the common regulations: 5 academic years / 10 semesters.
The programme combines taught course work, assessment, and supervised research/thesis work.

sections.heading: What the degree covers
paragraphs: M.Sc. (Agriculture) is normally a specialization-led research degree. ICAR’s approved nomenclature spans crop-production and resource fields such as Agronomy, Soil Science and Agricultural Chemistry, and Agro-meteorology and Environmental Sciences; crop-improvement and protection fields such as Genetics and Plant Breeding, Entomology, Plant Pathology, Plant Nematology, Plant Virology, and Seed Science and Technology; and social, technology, and enterprise-facing fields such as Agricultural Economics, Agricultural Extension & Communication, Food Science and Technology, and Agricultural Engineering.

The detailed syllabus depends on the discipline and university. For example, ICAR’s published Agronomy curriculum includes modern crop production, soil fertility and nutrient management, weed and water management, conservation agriculture, organic production systems, research methodology, and biostatistics. A university’s programme may further prescribe core courses, electives/minors, seminars, practical work, and a thesis.
source_urls
bullets: Choose the specialization first; the same M.Sc. (Agriculture) title can represent substantially different coursework and research.
Expect advanced discipline coursework plus research methods/statistics and a dissertation or thesis component.
Compare the department-level syllabus, facilities, field/laboratory access, and supervisor research areas before applying.

sections.heading: Admission routes and 2026-cycle context
paragraphs: A major national route is ICAR AIEEA (PG), conducted by the National Testing Agency for admission to master’s programmes in agriculture and allied sciences and for the award of ICAR-PG Scholarships. For the 2026–27 cycle, ICAR’s May 11, 2026 notice stated that registration had opened on May 8, 2026 and was scheduled to close on June 7, 2026; these dates are historical context, not future deadlines. Candidates should use the active NTA/ICAR notices and their target university’s prospectus for current schedules, seats, qualifying requirements, counselling procedures, and scholarship terms.

Some institutions also run discipline-specific admissions. For example, PAU’s 2026 notice for M.Sc. (Agri.) Molecular Biology and Biotechnology states that admission is based on GAT-B score plus fulfilment of the university’s prospectus requirements. This illustrates why a candidate should not assume that every M.Sc. (Agriculture) specialization uses exactly the same entrance route.
source_urls
bullets: Check whether the selected programme admits through ICAR AIEEA (PG), another national test, or its own institutional process.
Read the current information bulletin and the university prospectus before applying; they control eligibility, documents, reservation, fees, counselling, and dates.
Treat any published deadline, seat matrix, or test requirement as cycle-specific.

sections.heading: Costs and funding
paragraphs: There is no single India-wide tuition figure for M.Sc. (Agriculture): charges depend on the university, specialization, category, hostel and mess choices, and yearly revisions. As a dated example available on PAU’s website, the first-semester fee listed for M.Sc. Agricultural Extension Education is ₹63,375. Applicants should obtain the current programme fee table directly from the admitting institution before budgeting.

For eligible entrants through the ICAR route, NTA identifies AIEEA (PG) as the examination used both for master’s admission and for ICAR-PG Scholarships. The applicable bulletin governs scholarship eligibility, award conditions, number of awards, and any updates for a given academic year.
source_urls
bullets: Budget separately for tuition/academic charges, hostel and mess, field or laboratory charges, deposits, travel, and thesis-related expenses where applicable.
Use an institution’s current prospectus or fee notification rather than third-party fee estimates.
Review the applicable ICAR/NTA information bulletin for scholarship conditions.

sections.heading: Next academic and professional options
paragraphs: A common academic progression is a Ph.D. in an agriculture or allied-science specialization. ICAR’s common academic regulations present master’s and doctoral programmes within the same postgraduate framework, with a separate doctoral residential requirement of at least three academic years; the admitting institution’s current Ph.D. rules determine subject eligibility and selection.

For agricultural-research career tracks, the Agricultural Scientists Recruitment Board has published discipline-wise eligibility qualifications for its NET/ARS-related examinations. Its official combined notification shows that acceptable master’s qualifications are specialization-specific—for example, a master’s degree in Agriculture may be eligible only where paired with the required specialization for the relevant discipline. Candidates should therefore select and document their M.Sc. specialization carefully, and verify the current ASRB notification when an examination is announced.
source_urls
bullets: Ph.D. study in the chosen agricultural specialization.
Research-oriented competitive examinations and posts where the current notification accepts the candidate’s exact master’s discipline/specialization.

Specialist roles in agricultural research, extension, crop/soil advisory, seed and plant-health fields, agribusiness, and higher education depend on the specialization, experience, employer criteria, and applicable recruitment rules.

title: M.Sc. in Biotechnology
description: A two-year postgraduate program focusing on the application of biological systems for technological and industrial purposes, offered by IITs and NITs.

quick_facts.label: Named IIT offerings in the 2026 JAM matrix
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 admission cycle, the JAM Biotechnology (BT) matrix lists M.Sc. in Biotechnology at IIT Bombay (35 total seats) and IIT Indore (15 total seats). Seat matrices and programme availability can change by cycle.

quick_facts.label: Duration
quick_facts.value: At IIT Bombay, M.Sc. programmes are two-year programmes spread over four semesters; the Biotechnology M.Sc. curriculum is structured across four semesters.

quick_facts.label: 2026 entry eligibility at IIT Bombay and IIT Indore
quick_facts.value: The JAM 2026 matrix states “Any Branch/Subject” as the bachelor’s-level essential-subject requirement for the named M.Sc. in Biotechnology programmes at IIT Bombay and IIT Indore. The admitting institute performs final eligibility verification.

quick_facts.label: Primary admission route
quick_facts.value: For Indian-national admissions at IIT Bombay, M.Sc. Biotechnology admission is through JAM; JAM 2026 admissions are considered using All India Rank, subject to eligibility and institute requirements.

quick_facts.label: Illustrative academic fee context
quick_facts.value: For IIT Bombay’s 2026 Autumn intake, the published first-semester academic-fee total is ₹42,400 for GEN/EWS/OBC-NCL and ₹34,150 for SC/ST/PwD students. This includes one-time admission charges and refundable deposits, excludes hostel charges, and is subject to revision.

sections.heading: Eligibility: programme-specific, with broad bachelor’s access at the listed IITs
paragraphs: For the 2026 JAM cycle, the named M.Sc. in Biotechnology programmes at IIT Bombay and IIT Indore specify “Any Branch/Subject” in the bachelor’s degree as their minimum educational qualification. This means a B.Tech in Biotechnology is an eligible background, but it is not the only listed academic background for these two programmes.

Final eligibility is not determined by the JAM organising institute alone: the admitting IIT verifies the Eligibility Requirements and Minimum Educational Qualifications. Applicants should therefore re-check the current cycle’s brochure and the institute’s own admission notice before applying, because the JAM brochure explicitly says that the MEQs and seat matrix are subject to change.
bullets: For IIT Bombay and IIT Indore in the JAM 2026 matrix: bachelor’s degree in any branch/subject.
A qualifying JAM result alone does not guarantee admission; the candidate must meet the applicable requirements and be verified by the admitting institute.
Eligibility should not be generalised to every biotechnology-, bioscience-, or life-science-titled master’s programme, because programme names and subject requirements differ by institute.

sections.heading: Duration and academic structure
paragraphs: The M.Sc. in Biotechnology is commonly structured as a two-year, four-semester postgraduate programme at IIT Bombay. IIT Bombay describes its M.Sc. programmes as core and elective coursework across four semesters, often including a research-project component.

The IIT Bombay Biosciences and Bioengineering M.Sc. page describes the Biotechnology programme as a four-semester course. Its 2026-batch curriculum assigns 30 credits in Semester I and 40 credits of intensive laboratory work in Semester II, followed by project and/or elective pathways in Semesters III and IV.
bullets: Typical duration at IIT Bombay: 2 years / 4 semesters.
Later semesters can be organised around academic or industry projects and advanced electives.
Exact credit requirements, assessment, and project rules are institute- and cohort-specific.

sections.heading: Curriculum: molecular biosciences, quantitative tools, laboratories, and research
paragraphs: IIT Bombay’s 2026-batch M.Sc. Biotechnology curriculum illustrates the academic emphasis: Semester I includes Cell and Molecular Biology, Microbiology, Biochemistry and Analytical Biochemistry, Mathematics and Statistics, and Molecular Immunology. Semester II is laboratory-intensive, including Bioinformatics and Programming for Biologists and an integrated laboratory covering biochemistry, microbiology, genetic engineering, and biophysics.

In the final year, students may take a two-semester academic or industry project, combine electives with an industry project, or take electives in both semesters. Listed advanced options include molecular biology, molecular diagnostics, programming for bioinformatics, plant/animal/environmental biotechnology, bionanotechnology, proteomics, drug discovery, and drug delivery. This is an IIT Bombay example rather than a universal curriculum for every institution.
bullets: Core foundations: cell and molecular biology, microbiology, biochemistry, immunology, and quantitative methods.
Technical preparation: bioinformatics, programming for biologists, integrated wet-lab work, and analytical/biophysical methods.
Advanced study: electives and substantial academic or industry project options in the later semesters.

sections.heading: Admission through IIT JAM, with institute-level confirmation
paragraphs: For the 2026 cycle, IIT Bombay’s Academic Office states that its M.Sc. admissions are based on a JAM score followed by counselling. The JAM 2026 admission brochure places the named M.Sc. in Biotechnology programmes at IIT Bombay and IIT Indore under the Biotechnology (BT) paper’s programme matrix.

Candidates satisfying the relevant eligibility requirements and programme-specific qualifications are considered on the basis of JAM All India Rank. JAM 2026 states that admissions are made from the JAM merit list without additional written tests or interviews unless an admitting institute explicitly states otherwise. For 2026, the listed intake is 35 total seats at IIT Bombay and 15 at IIT Indore; these figures are cycle-specific rather than permanent capacity.

The phrase “M.Sc. in Biotechnology” should not be assumed to be a uniform offering across the NIT system. For example, NIT Rourkela says that its M.Sc. admissions use CCMN based on IIT-JAM scores and directs candidates to the CCMN brochure for programme-wise eligibility; applicants should check whether the relevant NIT actually offers the named specialisation in that year.
bullets: Take the JAM Biotechnology (BT) paper when targeting the named IIT Bombay or IIT Indore programmes in the 2026 matrix.
Apply and participate in the applicable centralised admission/counselling process after receiving a qualifying rank.
Treat programme availability, seat count, eligibility, and admission dates as annual-cycle information.

sections.heading: Costs: use published institute schedules, not a single nationwide estimate
paragraphs: Costs vary substantially by institute, category, semester, hostel arrangement, and revision year. As a dated official example, IIT Bombay’s schedule for new entrants to the 2026–27 Autumn Semester lists total academic fees of ₹42,400 for GEN/EWS/OBC-NCL students and ₹34,150 for SC/ST/PwD students. The totals include ₹16,000 in one-time admission charges and ₹10,000 in refundable security deposits.

The same IIT Bombay schedule lists per-semester charges of ₹16,400 for GEN/EWS/OBC-NCL and ₹8,150 for SC/ST/PwD in the first semester, and separately directs students to the hostel coordination unit for hostel-fee matters. It also says IIT Bombay may revise fees in subsequent semesters, so this is useful only as 2026-entry context, not as a guaranteed full-programme cost.
bullets: IIT Bombay, Autumn 2026 first-semester academic total: ₹42,400 (GEN/EWS/OBC-NCL); ₹34,150 (SC/ST/PwD).
Published figure excludes hostel charges.
SC/ST/PwD students are exempt from tuition fees in this IIT Bombay schedule, though other listed academic charges remain.

sections.heading: Next options: research projects, industry exposure, and a possible doctoral pathway
paragraphs: At IIT Bombay, later-semester pathways can include an internal academic project, an external academic project, or an industry project; students may also combine electives with an industry project. These routes can help a student build evidence of laboratory, computational, research, or applied-development work, but they do not constitute a placement guarantee.

IIT Bombay also publishes an internal progression option: students in M.Sc. Biotechnology with a CGPA of at least 8.5 after three semesters may convert to the M.Sc.-Ph.D. programme, subject to the institute’s stated rules. The M.Sc. degree is awarded after four semesters upon completion of master’s requirements, including for students who convert.
bullets: Academic or industry project work in Semesters III–IV at IIT Bombay.
Advanced electives in areas such as bioinformatics, diagnostics, biotechnology, proteomics, and drug discovery at IIT Bombay.
Potential M.Sc.-to-Ph.D. conversion at IIT Bombay for students meeting the published CGPA threshold; policies may change.

title: M.Sc. in Community Science
description: A postgraduate degree advancing expertise in community nutrition, human development, family resource management, textiles, and extension education.

quick_facts.label: Award and academic field
quick_facts.value: M.Sc. in Community Science is a postgraduate programme in the Community Science/Home Science domain. In ICAR’s postgraduate curriculum, it is organised around Apparel and Textile Science, Extension Education and Communication Management, Food and Nutrition, Human Development and Family Studies, and Resource Management and Consumer Science.

quick_facts.label: Usual duration
quick_facts.value: Two years is the common full-time duration reflected in university programme and admission information; applicants should confirm the structure for their target university and academic session.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry background
quick_facts.value: A four-year B.Sc. in Community Science/Home Science is a common qualifying background. Minimum marks/OGPA, accepted allied degrees, domicile rules, and specialisation prerequisites vary by university.

quick_facts.label: Admissions route
quick_facts.value: For participating agricultural universities, postgraduate admission may be routed through ICAR’s AIEEA (PG); some universities additionally use their own entrance test and merit/document-verification process.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: For a learner progressing from B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science, this degree is a direct and commonly accepted next step, but it is not a nationwide single-rule admission category. Assam Agricultural University’s published master’s eligibility includes B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science among qualifying four-year degrees and applies stated CGPA thresholds; its prospectus also specifies that eligibility for individual Community Science specialisations can differ.

Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University’s published master’s admission criteria illustrate another institutional pattern: a four-year B.Sc. in Home Science or Community Science with at least 60% marks or 7.0 OGPA was required in that notice. Therefore, candidates should check the current prospectus for the exact accepted bachelor’s discipline, minimum score/OGPA, reservation and domicile provisions, and the specialisation they select.
bullets: A B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science is an aligned feeder qualification.
Do not assume that all universities accept every allied bachelor’s degree for every specialisation.
Meet both the general PG eligibility rule and any specialisation-specific rule in the current university prospectus.

sections.heading: Duration
paragraphs: The programme is ordinarily structured as a two-year postgraduate degree. This is shown both on MGM University’s current M.Sc. Community Science programme page and in Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University’s published M.Sc. (Home Science) admission information. Semester pattern, dissertation/project requirements, and attendance rules remain university-specific.
bullets: Typical full-time length: 2 years.
Confirm the academic calendar, credit load, and dissertation/project rules with the admitting institution.

sections.heading: Curriculum and specialisations
paragraphs: There is no single identical syllabus across all Indian universities. ICAR’s revised PG Community Science curricula provide a useful sector-level reference and set out five major disciplinary streams: Apparel and Textile Science; Extension Education and Communication Management; Food and Nutrition; Human Development and Family Studies; and Resource Management and Consumer Science.

Depending on the stream and university, coursework can cover subjects such as public-health and clinical nutrition, food analysis and diet therapy; development communication and participatory programme management; textile chemistry, apparel quality and product development; human-development assessment and early-childhood interventions; or ergonomics, consumer economics, interior-space planning and environmental resource management. The ICAR material includes both theory and practical components, so candidates should compare the current course catalogue and research/dissertation requirements before choosing an institution.
bullets: Food and Nutrition
Extension Education and Communication Management
Human Development and Family Studies
Resource Management and Consumer Science
Apparel and Textile Science

sections.heading: Admission process
paragraphs: Admission routes differ by institution. ICAR has published a 2026–27 notice for PG and Ph.D. degree-programme admissions, while Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University states that Community Science postgraduate admissions are through ICAR-AIEEA (PG). By contrast, MGM University describes an institution-level route involving registration, its MGMU-CET, merit-list publication, document verification, and fee payment.

Applicants should treat each year’s prospectus and examination notice as controlling. Entrance-exam dates, application windows, counselling procedures, seat matrices, category rules, and document requirements can change from one admission cycle to the next.
bullets: Identify whether the target programme uses ICAR-AIEEA (PG), a university entrance test, merit selection, or a combination.
Keep qualifying-degree marksheets, identity/category/domicile documents where applicable, and specialisation eligibility evidence ready.
Use the current-year university prospectus and official examination notice rather than prior-year timelines.

sections.heading: Costs and fees
paragraphs: Fees are highly institution- and category-dependent and should be verified for the specific admission year. As an illustrative published university fee schedule, MGM University lists annual tuition of ₹30,000 for its M.Sc. Community Science programme, alongside separate annual examination and student-activity charges and one-time application, insurance/UMIS, refundable caution-deposit, eligibility, and alumni charges. This example is not a national fee benchmark and may change before admission.
bullets: Check whether quoted tuition excludes examination, hostel, mess, insurance, caution-deposit, and one-time charges.
Confirm scholarship, fee-waiver, and category-specific provisions directly with the university for the applicable session.

sections.heading: Next options
paragraphs: Graduates may continue into doctoral study in the relevant Community Science specialisation. ICAR’s accredited-programme listing includes Community Science M.Sc. specialisations and corresponding Ph.D. offerings in fields such as Apparel and Textile Science, Food and Nutrition, Extension Education and Communication Management, Human Development and Family Studies, and Resource Management and Consumer Science. ICAR also maintains a national AICE-JRF/SRF route for doctoral admissions in agriculture and allied sciences.

A suitable next step should follow the master’s specialisation and intended work: nutrition and food research, child and family studies, consumer/resource management, textiles and apparel, development communication, teaching, extension, or doctoral research. Specific job eligibility is employer- and role-dependent.
bullets: Ph.D. in a relevant Community Science/Home Science specialisation.
Research, teaching, extension, development-programme, nutrition, textile/apparel, child-development, or consumer/resource-management pathways aligned with the selected specialisation.
Track current ICAR and university doctoral admission notices for eligibility and examination requirements.

title: M.Sc. in Earth Sciences
description: A postgraduate degree program covering geology, geophysics, and other related fields concerning the Earth, with admission through the JAM Geology paper.

quick_facts.label: Degree route
quick_facts.value: In the JAM 2026 Geology (GG) admission matrix, relevant postgraduate routes include M.Sc. Applied Geology, M.Sc. (Tech.) Applied Geology, Joint M.Sc.-Ph.D. Geology, and Joint M.Sc.-Ph.D. Geophysics; programme titles and eligibility differ by institute.

quick_facts.label: Entrance examination
quick_facts.value: JAM 2026 included Geology (GG) as one of its seven computer-based test papers. Admission is based on All India Rank, applicable Government of India reservation policy, and seat availability, subject to institute requirements.

quick_facts.label: Typical duration
quick_facts.value: A standalone M.Sc. example at IIT Bombay is a two-year programme over four semesters; Earth Sciences specializations listed there are Applied Geology and Applied Geophysics.

quick_facts.label: Subject eligibility is programme-specific
quick_facts.value: For example, JAM 2026 lists IIT Bombay M.Sc. Applied Geology as requiring Geology for three years/six semesters plus any two of Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, and Biological Science; applicants must check the current programme-level MEQ rather than assume one common Earth Sciences rule.

quick_facts.label: Illustrative fee context
quick_facts.value: For IIT Bombay's 2026-27 Autumn Semester, the published academic-fee total for new Indian-national entrants to the two-year M.Sc./M.Sc.-Ph.D. programmes was ₹42,400 for GEN/EWS/OBC-NCL and ₹34,150 for SC/ST/PwD, including one-time admission fees and refundable deposits but excluding hostel charges. IIT Bombay states that fees may be revised in later semesters.

sections.heading: Eligibility: verify the exact institute and specialization
paragraphs: There is no single subject-combination rule for every JAM Geology pathway. The JAM 2026 brochure specifies minimum educational qualifications separately for each institute and programme. For IIT Bombay's M.Sc. Applied Geology, the listed requirement is Geology for three years/six semesters and any two of Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, and Biological Science. IIT Roorkee lists the same subject pattern for its M.Sc. Applied Geology and states that engineering degrees have no restrictions; IIT Kharagpur's Joint M.Sc.-Ph.D. Geology requires six semesters/three years of Geology plus specified Physics–Mathematics, Physics–Chemistry, or Chemistry–Mathematics combinations.
bullets=[
source_urls
bullets: For JAM 2026, candidates who had completed, or were appearing in the final examination of, their qualifying degree in 2026 could sit the examination. Before admission, they had to complete the undergraduate programme and submit proof of the qualifying degree meeting the admitting institute's requirements.

Eligibility requirements, seat matrices, and programme availability are explicitly subject to change under admitting-institute policy. Use the admission-year JAM brochure and the target institute's notice as the controlling sources.

sections.heading: Duration and programme formats
paragraphs: A conventional M.Sc. in this area is commonly a two-year programme. IIT Bombay describes its M.Sc. programmes as two years, with core and elective courses distributed across four semesters and often a research-project component. Its Earth Sciences department lists Applied Geology and Applied Geophysics as M.Sc. specializations.

The JAM Geology paper can also lead to longer research-oriented formats rather than only a standalone M.Sc. The JAM 2026 matrix includes Joint M.Sc.-Ph.D. programmes in Geology and Geophysics at IIT Kharagpur, and IIT Kharagpur confirms that its Joint M.Sc.-Ph.D. entries in Geology and Geophysics use JAM for admission.

sections.heading: What the Earth Sciences curriculum can cover
paragraphs: Curriculum is specialization- and institute-dependent. IIT Bombay says its two-year Applied Geology and Applied Geophysics M.Sc. programmes build theoretical and practical foundations for industry work and research. Its Applied Geology description names economic geology; geological and geochemical exploration; geochemistry; engineering, environmental and petroleum geology; mineralogy; mining geology; petrology; palaeontology; remote sensing; sedimentology; and structural geology, with practical field-based and laboratory training.

At IIT Bombay, the broader M.Sc. structure combines core and elective courses. The first two semesters generally address fundamental and applied aspects, while later semesters place more weight on electives and advanced study; a research project is often included. Applicants should obtain the current departmental course catalogue before treating a topic as compulsory.

sections.heading: Admission through JAM Geology
paragraphs: For the 2026 cycle, JAM was a computer-based test, and Geology (GG) was one of the available test papers. JAM states that admission uses the candidate's All India Rank in the relevant paper, Government of India reservation policies, and seat availability. A qualifying JAM result does not override each admitting institute's programme-specific minimum educational qualification.

JAM distinguishes between Admitting Institutes, whose process is coordinated through the JAM organizing institute, and Result Sharing Institutes, which candidates approach directly after qualifying. The current admission-year brochure should be used to identify the exact programme code, seats, eligibility requirements, application process, and deadlines.

sections.heading: Costs: use institute-specific, dated fee schedules
paragraphs: Fees vary materially by institute, category, residence/hostel choice, and academic year. As a dated illustration, IIT Bombay's fee schedule dated June 12, 2026 lists Autumn Semester 2026-27 academic fees for new Indian-national entrants to its two-year M.Sc. and M.Sc.-Ph.D. programmes as ₹42,400 for GEN/EWS/OBC-NCL students and ₹34,150 for SC/ST/PwD students. These totals include one-time admission charges and refundable security deposits, while hostel charges are handled separately.

The same IIT Bombay notice says SC/ST/PwD students are exempt from tuition fees and reserves IIT Bombay's right to revise the fee structure in subsequent semesters. Therefore, applicants should budget using the fee notice published by the specific admitting institute for their entry year, not a generic M.Sc. estimate.

sections.heading: Progression after the M.Sc.
paragraphs: A research pathway is available at some institutions. IIT Bombay states that students in its M.Sc. programme may convert to a Ph.D. programme when they meet Senate-approved eligibility criteria in force at the time. Separately, JAM Geology also offers direct entry routes into Joint M.Sc.-Ph.D. programmes at participating institutes, including Geology and Geophysics at IIT Kharagpur.

Whether to choose a two-year M.Sc. followed by a separate Ph.D. application or a Joint M.Sc.-Ph.D. route depends on the institute, specialization, academic performance, and the current rules. Confirm the applicable regulations with the target department and admission office.

title: M.Sc. in Economics
description: A two-year postgraduate degree program in Economics offered by select IITs through the JAM Economics paper.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: A full-time postgraduate M.Sc. in Economics offered at select IITs. In the JAM 2026 admission matrix, IIT Delhi, IIT Kanpur and IIT Roorkee list this programme under the Economics (EN) paper.

quick_facts.label: Typical duration
quick_facts.value: Two years (four semesters/24 months), as explicitly stated by IIT Kanpur, IIT Delhi and IIT Roorkee for their M.Sc. Economics programmes.

quick_facts.label: 2026–27 listed intake
quick_facts.value: For the 2026–27 JAM cycle, the EN-paper seat matrix lists 15 seats at IIT Delhi, 24 at IIT Kanpur and 13 at IIT Roorkee, including indicated PwD-reserved seats. IIT Kanpur and IIT Roorkee also list additional M.Sc. Economics seats under the Mathematical Statistics (MS) paper, so accepted JAM papers are institute-specific.

quick_facts.label: Admissions basis
quick_facts.value: Admission is centralized through the JAM admission portal for candidates on the JAM merit list, subject to each admitting institute's eligibility requirements and minimum educational qualifications; allocation is based on JAM All India Rank and programme preferences unless an institute explicitly specifies otherwise.

sections.heading: Eligibility depends on the IIT and JAM paper
paragraphs: A completed undergraduate degree, or final-year undergraduate status, makes a candidate eligible to sit the JAM examination. Admission to a particular M.Sc. Economics programme is separate: the candidate must also meet that institute's minimum educational qualification (MEQ), which is verified by the admitting IIT.

For the 2026–27 cycle, IIT Delhi accepted specified three-year-or-longer bachelor's qualifications including B.A., B.Sc., B.Com., B.Stat., B.Math., B.Tech. and B.E. (or equivalent). IIT Kanpur required a bachelor's degree following at least three years of education after 10+2. IIT Roorkee required Economics, Statistics, BCA, or a B.Sc./B.A./B.Com. with Mathematics, while placing no subject restriction on engineering degrees. These are programme-specific rules and can change in a future JAM brochure.

Applicants should not infer that qualifying JAM alone guarantees a seat: the JAM authority states that both the relevant eligibility requirements and MEQs must be satisfied, and final verification is conducted by the admitting institute.
bullets: Check the applicable year's JAM brochure for the programme code, accepted paper(s), MEQ and seat matrix.
For 2026–27, EN was the principal Economics-paper route; IIT Kanpur and IIT Roorkee also showed M.Sc. Economics options under MS.
Final-year candidates should confirm the qualifying-degree completion and document deadlines in the applicable admission cycle.

sections.heading: Duration and study format
paragraphs: This is normally a two-year, full-time master's degree. IIT Delhi describes its M.Sc. as four semesters (24 months); IIT Roorkee describes admission to a two-year M.Sc. Economics programme; and IIT Kanpur describes its programme as a two-year M.Sc. launched in 2023–24.
The degree title is shared, but detailed academic regulations, credit requirements, electives and assessment are set by the individual IIT rather than by JAM.

sections.heading: Curriculum: economics theory with quantitative and computational training
paragraphs: The exact curriculum varies by institute. IIT Kanpur's published M.Sc. Economics structure comprises 20 courses and approximately 180 credits: 11 compulsory courses and 9 electives. Its compulsory coverage includes microeconomics, macroeconomics, mathematical methods, applied probability and statistics, econometrics, game theory, and computational methods in economics.

This published structure illustrates the programme's expected quantitative orientation. Prospective students should compare the current course template and department offerings of each IIT before ranking preferences, since an M.Sc. Economics at one IIT need not have the same elective menu or credit structure as another.
bullets: Core areas commonly represented in IIT Kanpur's published structure: microeconomics, macroeconomics, mathematics, probability/statistics and econometrics.
Examples of specialised or interdisciplinary study at IIT Kanpur include computational methods and department/open electives.

sections.heading: Admission through JAM and JOAPS
paragraphs: For the 2026–27 cycle, candidates first took JAM, then candidates appearing in the JAM merit list applied through the Joint Admission Test for Masters Online Application Processing System (JOAPS), selected eligible programmes in preference order, and participated in centralized seat-allocation rounds. The JAM brochure states that admission consideration requires the relevant JAM qualification, the programme's MEQ and the institute's eligibility requirements.

The 2026–27 timetable is historical context rather than a future deadline: JAM 2026 was held on February 15, 2026, and the official site states that the final additional allocation round occurred on July 6–7, 2026, after which that admission process closed. A future applicant must use the next cycle's official JAM site and brochure, because dates, fees, seats and rules can change.

An offer is provisional until the admitting IIT completes document, eligibility and payment verification. In the 2026 cycle, the admission application fee was ₹750, while the seat-booking fee was ₹15,000 for General/OBC-NCL/EWS candidates and ₹7,500 for SC/ST/PwD candidates; the booking fee was to be adjusted against institute admission fees. These are cycle-specific administrative amounts, not the total cost of the degree.
bullets: Take the JAM paper(s) accepted by the intended programme.
After appearing on the merit list, apply in JOAPS and rank only programmes for which the MEQ is met.
Act within the offer letter's deadline; the available actions are accept-and-freeze, accept-and-upgrade, or reject-and-quit.

sections.heading: Costs: compare institute-level fee schedules, not a single national price
paragraphs: There is no single JAM-wide tuition price for this degree: JAM seat-booking and application payments are separate from the admitting IIT's tuition, hostel, mess and other institute charges. Costs should therefore be checked against the fee notice and admission offer of the allotted IIT.

As dated context, IIT Delhi's 2026–27 prospectus lists M.Sc./M.A. tuition for entry-year 2026 students at ₹7,500 per semester. That figure is tuition only; it should not be treated as the full two-year cost, and exemptions or additional institute, accommodation and living charges may apply. IIT Roorkee separately publishes an M.Sc. fee structure for 2026–27, illustrating that fees are institute-specific.
bullets: Separate JAM application/seat-booking payments from institute tuition and joining charges.
Confirm tuition waivers, hostel availability, mess advances and refund rules directly with the allotted IIT before accepting an offer.

sections.heading: Next options after the degree
paragraphs: A research-oriented next step is a Ph.D. in Economics or Economic Sciences. For example, IIT Kanpur's doctoral programme covers advanced microeconomics, macroeconomics, quantitative methods and econometrics, followed by supervised research; it is designed principally for teaching and research careers and can also support roles in government, research organisations and private businesses.

The precise progression route is not automatic: doctoral admission has its own eligibility, selection and funding rules. Graduates should evaluate Ph.D. admissions independently and use the research methods, econometrics and quantitative training developed during the master's programme to prepare for research-oriented applications.
bullets: Ph.D. study in economics/economic sciences or related quantitative social-science fields.
Research, policy-analysis and quantitative roles in government, research organisations or private businesses, subject to each employer's requirements.
Further specialised study where an applicant's research or career goals require it.

title: M.Sc. in Food and Nutrition
description: A postgraduate degree focused on nutrition science, diet planning, food service management, public nutrition, and food product development.

quick_facts.label: Degree naming
quick_facts.value: The degree is offered under closely related titles. ICAR’s accredited-programme listings include “M.Sc. (Community Science) Food & Nutrition,” while Delhi University uses “M.Sc. Food and Nutrition.”

quick_facts.label: Relevant prior study
quick_facts.value: A B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science background is closely aligned with this pathway: ICAR lists institutions offering both B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science and M.Sc. (Community Science) Food & Nutrition. Exact admission eligibility remains university-specific.

quick_facts.label: Duration is not uniform
quick_facts.value: Programme length depends on the institution and the applicable NEP pathway. Delhi University approved a one-year coursework-and-research M.Sc. track for eligible four-year graduates in 2026, while the Institute of Home Economics describes its M.Sc. Food and Nutrition as a two-year postgraduate programme.

quick_facts.label: Core areas
quick_facts.value: Official programme material covers nutrition assessment and diet planning, clinical and public-health applications, food science and processing, food-service management, practical work, and research/project activity.

sections.heading: Eligibility after B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science
paragraphs: Eligibility is determined programme by programme rather than solely by the degree title. For example, Delhi University’s 2026 one-year M.Sc. Food and Nutrition route required a four-year Home Science honours degree with 28 credits of Food and Nutrition discipline-specific electives, plus category-specific minimum marks. Its published requirement is therefore an example of a specific institutional rule, not a nationwide rule for every Community Science graduate.

For a Community Science graduate, the practical check is whether the transcript contains the required Food and Nutrition coursework and credits. This is a natural academic progression at some agricultural universities: ICAR’s accredited-programme list records B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science and M.Sc. (Community Science) Food & Nutrition at the same institutions. Applicants should obtain the target university’s current equivalence decision before assuming that their degree or individual papers qualify.
bullets: Keep semester-wise marksheets and the detailed syllabus/credit record available for verification.

Compare prior papers with the target programme’s requirements, especially nutrition, food science, biochemistry, physiology, microbiology, therapeutic/clinical nutrition, and public nutrition where specified.
Treat published percentage thresholds, category provisions, and accepted degree titles as admission-cycle-specific.

sections.heading: Duration and programme format
paragraphs: There is no single national duration for this canonical degree title. Delhi University’s Academic Council-approved NEP 2025 curriculum specifies a one-year, two-semester “Coursework + Research Track” for four-year B.Sc. Home Science graduates with the Food and Nutrition specialisation. In contrast, the Institute of Home Economics course page describes a two-year M.Sc. Food and Nutrition programme. Students should therefore verify both the master’s duration and the entry pathway—one-year versus two-year—before applying.

The one-year Delhi University coursework-and-research example carries 44 credits across two semesters and includes a six-credit dissertation, academic project, or entrepreneurship component in each semester. These details illustrate a current institutional design rather than a mandatory national template.
bullets: Confirm whether a university is admitting to a one-year or two-year master’s route for the relevant academic session.
Check whether the programme is a coursework-only route, coursework plus research, or requires a dissertation/project.
Do not infer duration from the M.Sc. title alone.

sections.heading: What students study
paragraphs: The curriculum normally integrates nutrition science with applied food systems and population health. Delhi University’s current one-year curriculum lists analytical techniques and instrumentation, nutritional epidemiology, food product development and quality evaluation, nutrition communication and health promotion, and dissertation/project/entrepreneurship work. Its elective pool includes medical nutrition therapy, institutional food-service management, public-health nutrition, maternal/infant/young-child/adolescent nutrition, food processing, exercise nutrition, and sport-specific nutrition.

Applied learning is material rather than incidental in the available official examples. The food-service management syllabus includes menu planning, quantity cooking, sanitation and hygiene work, and food-service surveys; the public-health nutrition material includes needs assessment, programme planning, monitoring, evaluation, nutrition surveillance, and field exposure. Course names, credits, electives, placements, and laboratory requirements can vary substantially across universities.
bullets: Nutrition assessment, epidemiology, therapeutic or clinical nutrition, and diet planning.
Public-health nutrition, communication, programme planning, monitoring, and evaluation.
Food product development, processing, quality evaluation, and food-service operations.
Laboratory/practical work plus a research, dissertation, project, or entrepreneurship component where prescribed.

sections.heading: Admission routes and application planning
paragraphs: Admission mechanisms vary. Delhi University’s two-year PG admissions for 2026–27 used CUET (PG) 2026 scores and its Common Seat Allocation System (CSAS), with applicants required to satisfy programme-specific eligibility. The Institute of Home Economics also states that applicants for its M.Sc. Food and Nutrition must meet programme-specific eligibility and take the relevant CUET paper. Other universities, especially agricultural universities, may use their own notified procedures or other entrance routes.

For a time-sensitive application, use the target university’s current admission bulletin as the controlling document. In Delhi University’s 2026 cycle, the university explicitly stated that allocation for two-year PG programmes would be based on CUET (PG) scores through CSAS; schedules, seats, test-paper requirements, and cut-offs should not be carried forward from a previous year.
bullets: Read the current programme-specific eligibility table before selecting an entrance test paper.
Apply through the university’s specified counselling/allocation portal after the required test, where applicable.
Verify seats, fee schedule, document-verification rules, and dates directly from the current institutional bulletin.

sections.heading: Further study and career directions
paragraphs: A research progression is available at institutions that offer doctoral study in the field. ICAR’s accredited-university listing includes examples where M.Sc. (Community Science) Food and Nutrition and Ph.D. Food and Nutrition are both offered. Doctoral admission requirements, entrance tests, research proposals, and fellowship conditions must be checked separately at each university.

The degree can support work in clinical/public-health nutrition, food science, food-service operations, quality assurance, research, and teaching-oriented pathways, depending on the electives, practical exposure, employer criteria, and any additional credentials required for a particular role. Delhi University’s curriculum identifies food scientist, quality-assurance manager/analyst, and food-service management as intended competency directions, while the Institute of Home Economics highlights public-health nutrition, dietetics, food science, academic, and research preparation. These are programme outcomes and directions, not guarantees of employment or authority to practise in a regulated role.
bullets: Ph.D. in Food and Nutrition or a related Community Science/Home Science discipline, subject to university-specific rules.
Research, academic, food-product-development, quality, food-service, and public-health-nutrition oriented roles.
Build role-specific competence through internships, supervised practical work, research projects, and any credentials required by the intended employer or professional setting.
