title: Master of Business Administration (Abroad)
description: A Master of Business Administration degree from a business school outside India that accepts GRE scores for admission.

quick_facts.label: What this node covers
quick_facts.value: A full-time MBA pursued at a business school outside India where the programme accepts the GRE General Test. GRE acceptance is not universal: applicants must confirm the policy for the exact MBA, intake and application round.

quick_facts.label: GRE acceptance
quick_facts.value: ETS states that more than 1,300 business schools accept GRE General Test scores for some or all MBA programmes. Stanford GSB, for example, requires either a GMAT or GRE score and states that it has no preference between them.

quick_facts.label: English testing
quick_facts.value: IELTS is programme-specific rather than automatic for every Indian applicant. Stanford requires an English-proficiency test for applicants whose undergraduate instruction included a language other than English, subject to its stated graduate-study exception; it accepts IELTS. INSEAD accepts IELTS, TOEFL or PTE Academic where English proof is needed, and also describes English-taught-degree/exchange alternatives.

quick_facts.label: Typical format
quick_facts.value: MBA duration varies substantially by school and country. INSEAD describes its MBA as a one-year, full-time programme, while Stanford describes a two-year MBA.

quick_facts.label: Illustrative tuition context
quick_facts.value: Fees are institution- and intake-specific. As published for INSEAD's August 2026 and January 2027 intakes, its MBA tuition was €109,860, payable in instalments; applicants should use each target school's current fee page before budgeting.

sections.heading: Eligibility: assess the target school's rules, not a single “abroad MBA” standard
paragraphs: There is no universal eligibility rule for an MBA abroad. Schools can differ on prior education, work experience, aptitude tests and English-language evidence. For example, Stanford GSB says work experience is not required for entry, whereas INSEAD reports that participants in its current class have an average of six years of post-graduate experience, with a two-to-ten-year range.

For a GRE-led application, first check that the precise full-time MBA accepts the GRE for the intended intake and whether it is required, optional or waivable. Stanford requires a valid GMAT or GRE and says neither test is preferred. INSEAD requires GMAT or GRE scores for its MBA application and says scores must be sent directly and remain valid for five years.

Applicants educated in India should also review the individual school's English-language policy rather than assume IELTS is always necessary. Stanford accepts IELTS, TOEFL and PTE Academic for applicants who must demonstrate English proficiency. INSEAD requires fluency in English and, where applicable, accepts IELTS Academic, TOEFL or PTE Academic; it also recognises specified evidence of degree or exchange study taught fully in English.
bullets: Prepare official academic transcripts and diploma/degree evidence where required; INSEAD requests scanned transcripts and diploma during application, with official documents required if admitted.
Plan professional references early. INSEAD requires two recommendations and recommends referees who can evaluate professional performance.

Do not treat an MBA as restricted to business graduates: INSEAD states that applicants from academic and professional backgrounds including arts, law, medicine, military and non-profit are welcome, with leadership potential and prior performance considered.

sections.heading: Duration and study model
paragraphs: An overseas MBA is not a fixed-length qualification. One-year accelerated programmes and two-year programmes both exist. INSEAD structures its full-time MBA over one year in five eight-week periods; Stanford structures its MBA over two years, with foundations in year one and electives in year two.

This difference affects more than calendar time: it can change the timing available for electives, internships, recruiting and relocation. Compare the academic calendar and career timetable of each target programme rather than assuming that all overseas MBAs operate alike.
bullets: INSEAD: one year, full time; two intakes; five periods of eight weeks each.
Stanford: two years; first-year foundations followed by an elective-focused second year.

sections.heading: What students study
paragraphs: MBA curricula generally combine core management disciplines with electives and applied learning, but the required course mix differs by school. INSEAD's published curriculum requires 14 core courses, 10.5 elective courses and one capstone project. Its core subjects include accounting, finance, markets, strategy, organisational behaviour, operations, marketing, macroeconomics, ethics and public policy.

At Stanford, the first year is organised around analytical, leadership and management foundations, alongside a global-experience requirement. The second year consists of electives, and students may also pursue seminars, courses elsewhere at Stanford, or a joint/dual degree subject to programme rules.

For applicants, curriculum fit should be tested against a target role—for example, whether the school provides sufficient depth in finance, strategy, operations, entrepreneurship, technology, sustainability or leadership—rather than chosen solely because it accepts the GRE.
bullets: Core learning commonly covers accounting, finance, economics, marketing, operations, strategy, data/decision-making and organisational behaviour.
Electives allow specialisation, but the number, format and availability of electives are school-specific.
Experiential components can include capstone work, simulations, global experiences, case discussion and team-based learning.

sections.heading: Admissions roadmap for a GRE-based MBA application
paragraphs: Start by building a school-by-school admissions sheet: MBA format and location, GRE policy, test-score validity, English-language policy, required documents, recommendation requirements, rounds, fees and interview format. This is essential because even schools accepting the same test can apply different rules.

For GRE timing, allow enough time for the score to be available and valid by the relevant deadline. ETS says GRE scores are valid for five years; Stanford requires the exam to be taken before application submission and says the test must be taken before the deadline of the round applied to. INSEAD similarly says GMAT/GRE scores are valid for five years and may be taken up to the selected application deadline.

A complete application is broader than a test score. INSEAD's current process includes an online application, test scores, a video and written assessment, career and motivation responses, two recommendations, CV, transcripts/diploma, supporting documents and application fee. Candidates pre-selected by INSEAD are invited to interviews with alumni before committee review.

Deadlines are variable and can change by intake. For example, INSEAD publishes separate rounds for its January 2027 and August 2027 intakes; use the school's live admissions page, not an older coaching-site calendar, when selecting a round.
bullets: Choose GRE or GMAT based on the policies of every target programme and your strongest credible score; do not assume that submitting a GRE is a disadvantage where a school states no test preference.
Request official score transmission using the institution's current reporting instructions.
Where IELTS is required, check whether the school requires IELTS Academic, its accepted test-delivery format, minimum sub-scores and the score-validity period.
Submit well before a final round if you need time for scholarship decisions, visas, financing or relocation; the appropriate timing is school- and country-specific.

sections.heading: Costs and budgeting
paragraphs: Published MBA tuition is only comparable when the intake, currency, programme length and what the fee covers are clear. As one dated example, INSEAD lists €109,860 tuition for its August 2026 and January 2027 MBA intakes, payable in instalments. Its page says this amount covers specified items including printed course materials, library and campus IT access, language tuition and testing, student council fees, gym access, printing and health insurance.

Applicants should create a school-specific budget that separates the official tuition figure from application and test fees, deposits, housing, travel, visa/immigration expenses, local living costs and foregone earnings. The amounts, currency exposure and funding arrangements vary by destination, school and personal circumstances; verify each item through the university and relevant government sources before committing.

Funding availability also varies. INSEAD's admissions materials note that applying in earlier rounds may be preferable where scholarships or relocation time are priorities, but this should not be read as a universal rule across MBA programmes.
bullets: Record the fee's stated intake and currency; tuition can change between cohorts.
Check the payment schedule and whether any initial instalment or deposit is non-refundable.
Use the school's official tuition, scholarship and cost-of-living information as the primary budget source.

title: Master of Finance (Abroad)
description: A specialised overseas postgraduate finance degree for which many business schools accept GMAT scores.

quick_facts.label: Degree type
quick_facts.value: A Master of Finance (MFin)—also offered under related names such as Master in International Finance—is a specialised postgraduate degree centred on finance. Exact programme design, entry profile and award title differ by school.

quick_facts.label: GMAT relevance
quick_facts.value: GMAT policies are school-specific: MIT Sloan lists GMAT/GRE submission as optional for its 2026 MFin application, whereas HEC Paris requires an approved management test (GMAT, GRE or TAGE MAGE) for its Master in International Finance. Applicants should verify the policy for the intended intake and programme rather than assume that GMAT is universally required.

quick_facts.label: Typical study length
quick_facts.value: Full-time formats can be approximately one year, but vary: MIT Sloan offers 12- and 18-month MFin routes, while Cambridge Judge lists its MFin as a one-year, full-time programme.

quick_facts.label: Work-experience profile
quick_facts.value: Some programmes target recent graduates, while others are post-experience. HEC Paris accepts applicants holding a bachelor’s or master’s degree with a strong quantitative background; Cambridge’s 2026-entry MFin guidance calls for at least two years of post-graduation finance or finance-related work experience by programme start.

sections.heading: Eligibility and academic preparation
paragraphs: There is no single overseas-MFin eligibility rule. A common baseline is a completed undergraduate degree, but schools may evaluate the academic record, quantitative preparation, English proficiency and professional experience differently. For example, HEC Paris asks applicants to hold a bachelor’s or master’s degree from an international institution, be fluent in English and have a strong quantitative background; its Business Track additionally expects introductory knowledge of accounting, corporate finance, investments, derivatives, business statistics and calculus.

Cambridge Judge illustrates the post-experience variant: its MFin application guidance states that applicants should have a strong bachelor’s record and at least two years of graduate work experience in a core finance or finance-related role by the programme start. Thus, an Indian applicant should distinguish between pre-experience MFin/MSc Finance courses and programmes designed for working finance professionals before investing in GMAT preparation or applications.
bullets: Check whether the programme accepts a three-year Indian bachelor’s degree and how it assesses its equivalence; the school’s country-specific admissions guidance is controlling.
Build evidence of quantitative readiness through transcripts and relevant coursework in mathematics, statistics, economics, accounting, programming or finance where required.
Plan for English-language evidence when it is not waived; HEC lists TOEFL, TOEIC, IELTS or Cambridge tests, while Cambridge lists accepted English-proficiency routes separately.
Treat work experience as a programme-specific condition, not a universal MFin requirement.

sections.heading: Duration and mode of study
paragraphs: MFin study abroad is commonly full-time, but the calendar and opportunities for internships differ. MIT Sloan states that its degree requirements can be completed in 18 months or accelerated to 12 months; the 18-month route may allow an internship or research assistantship in the second summer. Cambridge Judge describes its MFin as full-time for one year, beginning in September 2026.

Applicants should compare the published academic calendar, internship window, visa implications and whether a programme permits part-time work. HEC Paris states that attendance is mandatory throughout its Master in International Finance and that the programme is not compatible with part-time work.
bullets: 12 months: a compressed format may suit applicants seeking a faster return to work.
18 months or longer: may create additional space for a summer internship, research, electives or career transition activities.
Confirm the specific intake start date and completion date directly with the university before arranging funding or visa documentation.

sections.heading: What students study
paragraphs: The curriculum is typically quantitative and applied rather than a general-management MBA curriculum. MIT Sloan describes required core courses, restricted electives and an action-learning course. Its stated foundations include modern finance, financial mathematics and financial accounting, alongside electives that can cover areas such as fintech, quantitative methods, fixed income, mergers and acquisitions, asset management and healthcare finance.

Specialisation pathways vary. HEC Paris structures its Master in International Finance around Accelerated or Business tracks, then Capital Markets or Corporate Finance specialisations, followed by advanced core courses and electives. Its published structure also includes a research paper and four to six months of professional experience through an internship and/or full-time employment.
bullets: Core concepts commonly include corporate finance, capital markets, valuation, accounting, investments, risk and financial economics.
Quantitative preparation can include probability, statistics, optimisation, programming and financial mathematics.
Applied components may include a finance lab, industry project, research paper, career workshops or internship; these are not identical across schools.
Compare required modules—not only programme titles—if choosing between MFin, MSc Finance, financial engineering and international-finance degrees.

sections.heading: GMAT and the admissions process
paragraphs: A GMAT score can be relevant for this node, but it is not a universal admission requirement. MIT Sloan says GMAT (Focus Edition or 10th Edition) or GRE submission is optional for its 2026 MFin application, while encouraging candidates with a score to submit it as an additional data point. By contrast, HEC Paris lists an official GMAT, GRE or TAGE MAGE score report among its Master in International Finance application documents and says no minimum score is required to apply.

A typical application also includes academic transcripts, degree documentation, CV/resumé, English-language evidence where applicable, references, essays or statements, and sometimes an interview. HEC Paris describes a two-stage process comprising application review followed by a face-to-face or Zoom interview for pre-selected candidates. Cambridge asks for transcripts, evidence of professional development/work experience, English evidence where required, and two references.

Deadlines and test policies change by intake. For context, MIT states that its 2026-entry deadline has passed, and Cambridge says applications for September 2027 entry will open on 1 September 2026. These dates should not be extrapolated to other universities or later cycles.
bullets: First shortlist programmes by career stage, quantitative prerequisites, location, cost and work-authorisation considerations.
Read each school’s current test policy before booking the GMAT; a strong GMAT may be useful even where optional, but it does not replace required academic or language evidence.
Request transcripts and references early, and allow time for test-score reporting and visa documentation.
Use only the intake year published by the university when planning application rounds and deposits.

sections.heading: Fees, living costs and funding
paragraphs: Costs are highly school-, country- and intake-specific, and tuition is only one part of the budget. As published for the 2026–27 academic year, MIT Sloan lists MFin tuition of US$96,884 for its 12-month format and US$133,007 for its 18-month format. Cambridge Judge lists £60,000 tuition for its 2026/27 MFin. HEC Paris lists total tuition fees of €47,500 for 2026/27 for its Master in International Finance, with a stated additional €2,000 charge applicable to international students; its page labels the fees as indicative and subject to change.

Students should separately budget for accommodation, food, health insurance, travel, visa-related charges, books or equipment, local transport and currency movement. HEC Paris estimates remaining living costs at approximately €1,500 per month, but this is programme-specific context rather than a universal European budget. Scholarships, bursaries, institutional aid and external funding may be available, but eligibility, amounts and timing vary.
bullets: Use the university’s official cost-of-attendance or fees page for the intended year; do not rely on rankings pages, coaching estimates or old tuition figures.
Identify whether fees cover student services, insurance, course materials, residence, travel or internship-related costs.
Review deposit deadlines and refund terms before accepting an offer; HEC Paris states that admitted students confirm their place with a non-refundable deposit that is deducted from total tuition.
Plan the budget in the fee currency and retain contingency for exchange-rate changes.

sections.heading: Possible next steps after the degree
paragraphs: Graduates may use an MFin to pursue finance roles or further academic study, but outcomes depend on prior experience, visa/work-authorisation rules, local hiring conditions and individual performance. HEC Paris frames its programme around capital-markets and corporate-finance career paths, and its curriculum requires a research paper plus professional experience. MIT’s curriculum includes action learning with corporate partners and allows a thesis or independent study with faculty approval.

For applicants considering doctoral study, confirm whether the intended degree carries sufficient research training and credential recognition. HEC Paris explains that its 120-ECTS programme can bring the cumulative total to 300 ECTS for students with 180 ECTS from a bachelor’s degree, enabling progression to doctoral study in that system; this is a programme- and jurisdiction-specific example, not a guarantee of PhD admission.
bullets: Career route: use electives, projects, internships and the career office to target a finance specialism aligned with prior preparation.
Academic route: prioritise programmes offering research methods, a supervised research paper, thesis options and faculty fit if a PhD is a serious goal.
Professional route: compare whether the degree complements—not substitutes for—relevant work experience and any professional credentials sought in the target market.

title: Master of Public Health at a Foreign University
description: An overseas postgraduate public-health degree for graduates seeking population health, policy, or health-management careers.

quick_facts.label: What this degree is
quick_facts.value: An overseas MPH/MSc Public Health is a postgraduate, population-health degree; exact title, entry profile, delivery mode and professional outcomes vary substantially by university and country.

quick_facts.label: Entry profile
quick_facts.value: A prior bachelor’s degree is common, but experience requirements differ: LSHTM considers an appropriate first degree (and may consider a 2:2 with typically at least two years’ relevant experience), while Johns Hopkins’ MPH generally requires two years of post-baccalaureate health-related experience or an accepted alternative.

quick_facts.label: English language evidence
quick_facts.value: For applicants whose first language is not English, universities may require an approved English-language qualification. LSHTM lists Band B English requirements and permits an application without results, with a test result potentially made a condition of an offer; IELTS is therefore a common pathway but not a universal or automatically sufficient requirement.

quick_facts.label: Typical academic content
quick_facts.value: MPH curricula commonly combine epidemiology, biostatistics/quantitative methods, health policy and management, social and behavioural determinants, electives, and applied work. For example, Johns Hopkins requires 80 credits, a practicum of at least 100 hours and a capstone.

quick_facts.label: Cost context
quick_facts.value: Fees and total living costs are location- and institution-specific and change by intake. For 2026/27, LSHTM lists overseas full-time MSc Public Health tuition of £31,450; this is an example rather than a market-wide benchmark and excludes personal living and travel costs.

sections.heading: Eligibility and fit
paragraphs: An overseas public-health master’s can suit graduates from health, life sciences, social sciences, management and related disciplines, but there is no single international eligibility rule. Applicants should compare the specific programme’s academic-equivalence standard, quantitative preparation, work-experience expectation and English-language policy rather than assuming that any Indian bachelor’s degree automatically meets entry requirements.

LSHTM’s 2026/27 MSc Public Health, for example, accepts a relevant first degree at UK upper-second-class (2:1) standard or an overseas equivalent; it may consider a 2:2 with sufficient relevant training or experience, typically at least two years in a field allied to public health. It also asks applicants to demonstrate post-16 mathematics ability, such as statistics, quantitative methods or epidemiology. In contrast, Johns Hopkins’ MPH normally expects two years of full-time, post-baccalaureate health-related experience (or specified alternatives) and has course prerequisites that include mathematics and health-related science for June 2027 entry onward.

For IELTS-linked planning, treat English testing as an admission-document requirement, not as the degree’s only prerequisite. At LSHTM, applicants who do not have English as a first language must meet its Band B requirement unless exempt; an application may be submitted before results are available, but an offer can be conditional on them. Confirm accepted tests, minimum component scores, validity period and exemption rules directly with each university before booking a test.
bullets: Build evidence of quantitative readiness: transcript modules in statistics, mathematics, research methods, epidemiology or a recognised preparatory course where the programme permits it.

Document public-health relevance clearly in the CV and statement: clinical service, research, NGO work, government programmes, hospital quality work, analytics, internships and volunteering may be relevant depending on the university.
Obtain a formal assessment only where the university asks for one; universities make their own decisions on whether an Indian qualification is equivalent.

sections.heading: Duration and study format
paragraphs: Programme length is not standardised. Intensive, campus-based programmes can be completed in about one academic year, while part-time, hybrid and online routes can take longer. Johns Hopkins states that its full-time MPH runs July to May and can be completed in 11 months; its broader MPH options allow completion from as little as 11 months to up to four years. Students should distinguish an on-campus degree, a blended degree and a fully online degree before assessing visa needs or post-study work options.

The degree title also varies. UK institutions may use MSc Public Health rather than MPH, while both can be postgraduate public-health qualifications. LSHTM lists its MSc Public Health as an intensive in-person master’s programme and separately lists a distance-learning MSc Public Health option.
bullets: Check whether placements, orientation sessions, examinations and capstone presentations require in-country attendance.
Plan for an intake-specific academic calendar; duration can change with credit load, leave, placement timing and approved part-time study.
Do not assume a distance-learning programme supports a student-visa or post-study-work pathway; confirm this with the destination-country immigration authority and university.

sections.heading: What you study
paragraphs: A strong public-health master’s is interdisciplinary rather than confined to clinical medicine. At Johns Hopkins, the MPH core is designed around public-health knowledge and competencies spanning biostatistics, epidemiology, social and behavioural determinants, management sciences, public-health problem-solving, demography, environmental health, biological sciences and public-health policy. The remaining coursework can be tailored to career interests through electives and concentrations.

Applied learning is material when comparing programmes. The Johns Hopkins MPH requires 80 credits in total, approximately 45–50 core credits, at least 100 practicum hours, and a capstone project with written and oral components. Its listed concentrations include health leadership and management, health systems and policy, infectious diseases, epidemiologic and biostatistical methods, humanitarian health, nutrition and reproductive health.
bullets: Prioritise modules and practicum partners that match the intended pathway: epidemiology/data, health policy, programme management, global health, hospital quality, environmental health or behavioural health.
Assess whether the programme includes a supervised practicum, a client-based project, a dissertation/capstone and opportunities to use quantitative software.
Review each programme’s current module catalogue rather than relying solely on the degree name; course availability and concentration offerings can change.

sections.heading: Application approach for Indian applicants
paragraphs: Apply to each university’s stated system and submit the full evidence package early enough for academic review, scholarship decisions and immigration processing. LSHTM says applications are made online and are considered only after required information and supporting documentation have been provided. Its personal-statement guidance asks applicants to explain why they want to study the programme, how it fits career objectives and what they will contribute as a student.

A practical application file normally needs the items the university specifies: academic transcripts and degree certificate, CV/resumé, statement of purpose, references where requested, English-language evidence or an approved exemption, and any programme-specific quantitative or work-experience evidence. Requirements are programme-specific: Johns Hopkins, for example, treats GRE/GMAT/LSAT/MCAT scores as optional for its MPH but still expects evidence of quantitative/analytical ability through other components.

After receiving an offer, separately meet the destination country’s student-immigration rules. For Canada, the federal government says a letter of acceptance from a designated learning institution is required for a study-permit application; from January 1, 2026, master’s and doctoral students attending a public degree-granting institution do not need a provincial or territorial attestation letter, although Quebec requirements still apply.
bullets: Shortlist programmes by entry requirements, curriculum, applied-learning model, total cost, location and post-study immigration rules—not by rankings alone.
Use the university’s own country-equivalency and English-language pages to validate eligibility before paying application or test fees.
Keep scanned documents, certified translations where required, and referee details ready; application portals may close while references or verification are pending.

sections.heading: Fees, funding and budget planning
paragraphs: Budget for tuition plus housing, food, health insurance, local transport, books, visa charges, travel and emergency funds. Published tuition is only one component, and both fees and living-cost estimates can change each academic year. As dated examples for 2026/27, LSHTM lists overseas full-time tuition of £31,450 for its MSc Public Health. Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health lists annual tuition of US$77,400 for its one-year, 45-credit MPH and estimates total annual cost including indirect costs at US$114,534; these figures illustrate the scale at one US institution, not a typical global MPH price.

Seek funding through the university and external scholarship schemes, but do not assume an award is automatic. Johns Hopkins says MPH applicants admitted to the programme are automatically considered for certain scholarship support, while some named funding opportunities have additional application requirements. Read award eligibility carefully, particularly citizenship/residency rules, minimum credit loads and whether funding covers tuition only or living costs too.
bullets: Create a country- and university-specific budget in the currency in which fees are charged; include exchange-rate and remittance contingency.
Compare refundable versus non-refundable deposits, health-insurance requirements, payment schedules and the financial evidence required for a visa.
Use official university cost-of-attendance pages for the intended intake; do not extrapolate last year’s fee or a consultant’s estimate.

sections.heading: Career and further-study options
paragraphs: An MPH can support work in population health, health systems, policy, programme design and evaluation, research, health management and global health, but job eligibility depends on the employer, country, prior experience and any profession-specific licence. Johns Hopkins lists example MPH-related titles including health policy analyst, consultant, hospital quality manager, evaluation associate, grants officer, medical officer and programme manager; these are examples rather than guaranteed outcomes or salary promises.

Possible next steps include public-health roles in government, hospitals, NGOs, multilaterals, research organisations and consulting; specialised postgraduate study such as a PhD or DrPH; or a return to India with applied skills in epidemiology, policy, programme monitoring and health management. For overseas employment, make immigration planning programme-specific. In Canada, a graduate of an eligible designated learning institution may qualify for a post-graduation work permit if all conditions are met; for graduates of master’s degrees, current rules require language evidence at CLB/NCLC 7 and do not impose a field-of-study requirement, but the rules can change.
Where a role is regulated—such as clinical practice—an MPH does not substitute for the country-specific professional registration, licensing or recognition requirements for that regulated occupation.
bullets: Match electives, capstone and practicum to the target job family before enrolment; this creates a more credible portfolio than the degree title alone.
For country-specific work rights, verify the rules immediately before applying for a visa and again before graduation.
For doctoral study, prioritise research methods, biostatistics, faculty fit, research output and a substantial capstone or dissertation experience.

title: Master of Public Health (MPH)
description: A postgraduate degree focusing on the science and art of preventing disease, prolonging life, and promoting health through organized community efforts.

quick_facts.label: Typical format
quick_facts.value: The MPH is offered in India as a full-time postgraduate programme; current official examples at IIPHG and Manipal describe it as a two-year programme.

quick_facts.label: Eligibility pattern
quick_facts.value: Entry requirements are institution-specific, but current examples accept a recognised bachelor's degree in any discipline, with stated minimum marks of 50% at IIPHG's 2024 MPH intake brochure and 55% at Manipal for 2026 admission.

quick_facts.label: Core learning areas
quick_facts.value: Official curricula commonly include epidemiology, biostatistics, research methods, disease prevention and management, health systems/management, health policy, social and behavioural sciences, environmental health, and programme monitoring or evaluation.

quick_facts.label: Applied component
quick_facts.value: MPH programmes may include field placements or internships and a dissertation, thesis, or capstone; the precise requirement depends on the institution and specialisation.

quick_facts.label: Indicative private-university fee context
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 intake at Manipal's PSPH, the published total MPH fee is ₹4,06,000 plus a one-time refundable ₹10,000 caution deposit. Fees, inclusions, scholarships, and revision dates vary substantially by institution and intake.

sections.heading: Eligibility: broad-entry degree, but check the institution's exact rules
paragraphs: An MPH is multidisciplinary rather than restricted to one clinical profession. This makes it a plausible postgraduate option after many of the listed parent pathways—including nursing, medicine, dentistry, physiotherapy, AYUSH, community science, and other recognised bachelor's degrees—provided that the target institution accepts the applicant's qualification.

Current official examples differ in their thresholds. IIPHG's MPH brochure states that applicants need a bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognised university, in India or abroad, with at least 50% marks; it lists medical and paramedical sciences, biological and veterinary sciences, management, social work, engineering, law, commerce, accounting, and communication among eligible backgrounds. Manipal's 2026 MPH page requires a bachelor's degree in any discipline, preferably health sciences, from a UGC-recognised university or equivalent recognised by the Government of India, with at least 55% aggregate marks.

Applicants with an MBBS earned outside India should not assume that the degree automatically meets every MPH provider's documentation or equivalence rules. They should obtain written confirmation from the admitting university and follow its requirements for recognition, transcripts, completion certificates, and any applicable immigration or nationality documentation.
bullets: A prior health qualification can be relevant for public-health experience and context, but it is not universally required.
Minimum marks, recognised-university wording, final-year eligibility, category provisions, and work-experience preferences vary by provider.

Do not treat a job title such as Community Health Officer, Staff Nurse, Nursing Officer, Government Physiotherapist, or Military Nursing Officer as a substitute for the required qualifying bachelor's degree unless the institution explicitly says so.

sections.heading: Duration and study mode
paragraphs: A two-year, full-time format is a common current model. IIPHG describes its MPH as a comprehensive two-year full-time programme, while Manipal describes a two-year, four-semester, full-time programme. However, an MPH title does not by itself guarantee identical duration, delivery mode, internship rules, or academic calendar across India.

Applicants should distinguish a degree-granting MPH from shorter public-health certificates, diplomas, and e-learning programmes, which can have different outcomes and may not satisfy an employer's or doctoral programme's requirement for a master's degree.
bullets: Confirm whether fieldwork, internship, dissertation, or capstone is compulsory and whether it extends the calendar duration.
Check the specific academic year's prospectus for start date, attendance rules, assessment, and maximum time allowed to complete the programme.

sections.heading: What an MPH teaches
paragraphs: The MPH develops population-health and health-system skills rather than training students for independent clinical practice. IIPHG groups its MPH curriculum across research and analytics; disease management; health systems; environmental health; communication; and social sciences. Its listed subjects include epidemiology, biostatistics, research methodology, advanced analytics, communicable and non-communicable diseases, reproductive and child health, public-health nutrition, health management, economics, financing, insurance, policy and law, national health programmes, environmental and occupational health, climate and urban health, health communication, programme management, social and behavioural sciences, and gender and health.

At Manipal, the learning-outcomes curriculum describes competency-based learning, fieldwork, assignments, and problem-based learning, with basic and advanced epidemiology and biostatistics, social and behavioural sciences, One Health, maternal health, global health policy, and non-communicable diseases and occupational health. Its programme page also describes internships or field placements, community projects, and a capstone project or thesis.

Course titles and elective tracks are not nationally standardised. Compare the actual semester-wise curriculum with the intended role: for example, candidates targeting epidemiology or monitoring and evaluation should look closely at quantitative methods, data analysis, surveillance, evaluation design, and practical placement opportunities.
bullets: Quantitative and research foundation: epidemiology, biostatistics, research methods, and analytics.
Population-health content: infectious and non-communicable diseases, maternal and child health, nutrition, environment, and occupational health.
Systems and implementation content: health management, economics and financing, policy and law, national programmes, communication, and programme management.
Applied learning may include internships, field placements, community projects, and dissertation/capstone work.

sections.heading: Admissions: institution-led selection, sometimes with an entrance route
paragraphs: There is no single admission mechanism that applies to every MPH in India. Institutions set their own eligibility, application process, selection method, seat availability, reservation implementation where applicable, and deadlines. Therefore, CUET-PG should be treated as a possible route only where a particular university names it, not as an automatic eligibility credential for every MPH.

For 2026, Manipal states that eligible MPH applicants submit documents and attend a personal interview for merit-list preparation, or may submit a PGCUET 2026 scorecard. IIPHG describes a multi-stage process for its full-time MPH admissions: online application with academic documents and a statement of purpose, an online MCQ screening test for shortlisted candidates, and subsequent evaluation stages. Its official site also reported MPH admission merit-list activity in 2026.

Deadlines and status can change during an admission cycle. For example, Manipal's MPH page displayed a July 25, 2026 application date and a tentative July 2026 course start when reviewed, but applicants should rely on the live admissions page and the current prospectus before paying an application fee or making travel plans.
bullets: Prepare official marksheets/degree or provisional certificate, identity and category documents where applicable, and any documents specified by the university.
Expect some providers to request a statement of purpose, screening test, interview, or proof of relevant work experience.
Verify whether a score from CUET-PG/PGCUET or another test is accepted for the exact campus and intake year.

sections.heading: Costs: use current, institution-specific fee documents
paragraphs: MPH costs vary widely by provider, campus, category, specialisation, accommodation choice, and academic year. Published tuition should not be treated as a national benchmark, and applicants should separately budget for application charges, refundable deposits, hostel or rent, food, travel, devices, insurance where applicable, and fieldwork-related expenses.

As a dated example, Manipal's 2026 MPH page lists total course fees of ₹4,06,000 and a one-time refundable caution deposit of ₹10,000. IIPHG's 2024 MPH brochure listed tuition of ₹2,75,000 per annum for Indian nationals, excluding accommodation, food, and other welfare activities; that brochure is useful historical context, not confirmation of the fee for a future intake.

Scholarship availability is also provider-specific. IIPHG publishes scholarship and fellowship information for public-health students, while Manipal lists merit and eligibility-linked scholarships. Applicants should confirm eligibility, number of awards, timelines, and whether an award offsets tuition only or total living costs.
bullets: Obtain the latest official fee circular and refund policy for the exact intake before accepting an offer.
Ask whether the quoted figure includes examination, registration, internship, hostel, and caution-deposit charges.
Treat all published fees as dated figures that may be revised by the institution.

sections.heading: Progression and career directions after MPH
paragraphs: The degree can support progression to research training and public-health roles, but it is not a professional licence and does not guarantee a particular designation or salary. IIPHG lists employment contexts for MPH graduates including government departments, NGOs, international organisations, foundations, academic institutions, hospitals, and research organisations. Manipal lists example career directions including epidemiology, public-health education, environmental science, biosecurity, and healthcare administration.

The immediate child roles in this node—Epidemiologist, Monitoring and Evaluation Officer, Policy Analyst, Public Health Nurse, Public Health Programme Manager, and Research Assistant—should be viewed as role targets rather than automatic outcomes. Employers commonly set their own requirements for subject expertise, analytics, software, field experience, clinical registration where relevant, language capability, and years of experience.

A Ph.D. in Public Health is a possible academic progression after an MPH. IIPHG's current doctoral page publishes 2026-27 PhD admissions materials, and its PhD admission notification states a master's-degree route with at least 55% marks as one eligibility pathway; entrance, interview, research proposal, and other rules must be checked in the current institution-specific notification. UGC-NET eligibility and subject mapping likewise must be verified against the current NTA information bulletin rather than inferred solely from holding an MPH.
bullets: Research and analytics: epidemiology, research assistant roles, surveillance, data analysis, and monitoring and evaluation.
Programme implementation: public-health programme management, health promotion, community and NGO implementation, and health-system strengthening.
Policy and management: policy analysis, health financing or management, and government or development-sector roles.
Further study: Ph.D. in Public Health or a related field, subject to the university's current doctoral eligibility and selection rules.

title: Master of Public Policy (Abroad)
description: A graduate degree program focusing on public policy analysis and implementation from a university outside India.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: An MPP is a postgraduate, practice-oriented public-policy degree. Program design differs by university: Harvard describes a social-science-based toolkit for action, while Oxford describes an intensive taught degree for current and future public-service leaders.

quick_facts.label: Typical study length
quick_facts.value: Duration is institution-specific rather than uniform: Oxford lists its full-time MPP as 12 months, while Harvard Kennedy School lists its MPP as two years.

quick_facts.label: Academic background
quick_facts.value: A strong bachelor's degree is a common baseline. For example, Harvard requires a bachelor's degree and evidence of quantitative proficiency; Oxford accepts applicants from any discipline but expects a first-class or strong upper-second-class equivalent academic record.

quick_facts.label: Work experience
quick_facts.value: Professional experience can strengthen an application but is not universally compulsory. Harvard says it is not strictly required and notes that incoming students typically have 2–3 years of experience; Oxford says applicants are not required to have prior experience, although many successful candidates bring at least one or two years.

quick_facts.label: GRE relevance
quick_facts.value: GRE requirements are program-specific. Harvard's published MPP requirements state that the GRE or GMAT is required, with a possible waiver for applicants who have completed specified quantitative coursework; ETS states GRE scores are reportable for five years.

quick_facts.label: Cost context
quick_facts.value: Fees and living costs vary sharply by country and school and change by intake. For 2026–27, Oxford lists an annual MPP course fee of £54,450 for overseas students, excluding living and possible placement-related costs; Harvard lists $72,106 in MPP tuition and mandatory fees before indirect living costs.

sections.heading: Eligibility and academic fit
paragraphs: Applicants from India ordinarily apply after completing a recognised bachelor's degree, but the exact equivalency, grade threshold, quantitative preparation and English-language evidence are set by each university. Harvard's MPP requires a strong bachelor's record plus quantitative proficiency demonstrated through undergraduate economics, statistics or calculus; Oxford's MPP accepts applicants from any discipline and specifies a first-class or strong upper-second-class equivalent as its minimum academic benchmark for the 2026–27 entry cycle.

Professional experience is valuable for many policy degrees because programmes emphasise applied problem-solving and leadership. It should not, however, be assumed to be mandatory: Harvard calls work experience an admissions advantage rather than a strict requirement, and Oxford says prior experience is not required even though many successful candidates have it.

English testing must be checked course by course. Oxford's 2026–27 MPP page, for example, specifies its higher English-language level and gives test-specific minimums; applicants should rely on the target university's current admissions page rather than applying a generic IELTS or TOEFL threshold.
bullets: Build evidence of quantitative readiness where required: transcripts and relevant coursework are important even for applicants whose undergraduate major was not economics or mathematics.
Treat GRE/GMAT policy as university- and intake-specific. A GRE parent node is useful for planning, but it does not establish that every overseas MPP requires the GRE.
Prepare official transcripts and, where applicable, certified translations or the university's stated credential documentation.

sections.heading: Duration and study format
paragraphs: There is no single standard duration for an overseas MPP. Oxford presents a full-time, 12-month MPP; Harvard Kennedy School presents a two-year MPP. This difference affects total tuition exposure, opportunity cost, visa planning and the sequencing of internships or capstones.

Most campus-based MPPs combine intensive taught work with applied assignments. Oxford states that its course is full-time and requires attendance in Oxford, while Harvard's published degree requirements include full-time, in-residence enrolment.
bullets: Compare the programme's stated length, residency requirement and full-time credit load before applying.
For one-year programmes, confirm whether a summer policy placement, project or report is mandatory and budget time and funds accordingly.
For two-year programmes, check the timing of internships, capstone work and any joint-degree options.

sections.heading: What students study
paragraphs: MPP curricula typically combine policy analysis with the institutional and practical dimensions of implementation. Harvard's first-year core develops competence in policy analysis, empirical methods, negotiation, economics and politics/ethics, and its second-year work includes a policy-area concentration and Policy Analysis Exercise capstone.

Oxford's current published core includes economics for public policy, politics of policymaking, law and public policy, evidence in public policy and policy challenges. It also requires a policy-report placement, intended to apply course learning in a public-policy context.

Electives allow specialisation, but offerings change. Oxford notes that its option and applied-policy modules vary by year; examples from prior years include climate change, cybersecurity, education policy, migration, public budgeting, communications and negotiations.
bullets: Look for analytical training: economics, statistics or empirical methods, evidence use and policy evaluation.
Look for implementation training: politics, law, public management, negotiation, communication and stakeholder decision-making.
Compare the final applied requirement: policy memo, client project, practicum, placement, capstone or thesis. An MPP need not be a research-master's degree.

sections.heading: Application components and planning
paragraphs: Application packages are holistic and should connect prior academic or professional work to a credible public-policy goal. Harvard lists an online application, essays, résumé/CV, three recommendations, transcripts, standardised-test scores where required or not waived, English-language results where applicable, and an application fee or waiver. Oxford's MPP process requires a personal statement, CV, transcripts, three references and two written essays, among other course-specific requirements.

Deadlines are intake-specific and can close many months before the programme begins. For example, Oxford's page for 2026–27 reports that applications are closed and identifies a December-cycle application process for that intake; Harvard's programme page lists December 2026 as its displayed MPP admission deadline. These dates are dated examples, not deadlines to reuse for a later cycle.

Applicants should request references and official academic documents early, complete language testing in time for conditional-offer requirements, and verify whether the target school expects scores to be sent directly by ETS or another testing body.
bullets: Start with a shortlist whose curriculum, work-experience profile, location and budget fit your policy interests.
Use the statement of purpose and policy essays to demonstrate problem definition, evidence-based reasoning, leadership or public-service commitment, and realistic career intent.
Check each course's current application portal for document formats, word limits, referee submission rules, fee-waiver rules and test-reporting codes.
Do not use a previous cycle's deadline, fee or test rule without reconfirming it on the official course page.

sections.heading: Costs, funding and financial planning
paragraphs: The financial commitment includes more than tuition: applicants should budget for university fees, accommodation and food, health insurance where applicable, travel, visa and immigration-health charges where applicable, books/materials, application and test fees, and any practicum or fieldwork costs. Oxford explicitly states that its course fee excludes accommodation and other living costs, and notes that a policy-report placement can create additional expenses.

As dated 2026–27 examples, Oxford lists an overseas annual MPP fee of £54,450, a £8,200 deposit, and estimated Oxford living costs of £1,405–£2,105 per month for a single full-time student. Harvard lists 2026–27 MPP tuition and mandatory fees of $72,106, and separately notes that its full cost of attendance includes indirect costs such as living expenses. These figures are not estimates for all overseas MPPs and may change before a future intake.

Funding is competitive and varies by citizenship, university, college, external sponsor and admission cycle. Oxford and Harvard both direct admitted or prospective students toward programme/university funding opportunities; applicants should examine whether awards cover tuition only or also living costs, insurance and travel.
bullets: Create a currency-aware budget for the full programme length, not only the first term's tuition.
Separate guaranteed funding from scholarships still under consideration before making an enrolment decision.
Review deposit deadlines and refund conditions before accepting an offer.
Check official student-visa financial-evidence requirements for the destination country separately from the university's admission financial declaration.

sections.heading: Possible next options after the degree
paragraphs: An MPP is commonly positioned for applied policy work rather than automatically as research preparation. Oxford explicitly describes its MPP as a professional degree focused on policy-making and analysis and says it is not designed to prepare students for research-based study such as its DPhil in Public Policy.

Next steps can therefore include policy, government, multilateral, nonprofit, consulting or private-sector roles that use policy-analysis and implementation skills, subject to an individual's prior experience, work authorisation and employer requirements. Oxford reports alumni in public-sector roles, multilaterals and the third sector, while Harvard publishes an employment-sector snapshot spanning public/international-governmental, nonprofit and private sectors.

Students seeking a research-focused route should assess research-methods preparation carefully. Oxford offers a Public Policy 1+1 pathway in which applicants submit separate applications for the MPP and MSc in Public Policy Research in the same cycle; Harvard also describes joint and concurrent degree options with disciplines such as business, law, medicine and design.
bullets: For professional policy careers, use electives, client projects, internships and the capstone to create a portfolio of policy writing and evidence-based recommendations.
For doctoral ambitions, verify that the intended MPP has sufficient research methods, quantitative training and dissertation or thesis opportunities—or plan a separate research master's route.
For employment abroad after graduation, investigate post-study work rules and employer sponsorship conditions in the destination country at the time of application; these rules can change.

title: MBA (Master of Business Administration)
description: Two-year postgraduate management degree; admission via CAT/XAT/GMAT and others; the standard credential for management, consulting and finance careers.

quick_facts.label: Credential
quick_facts.value: MBA (Master of Business Administration) is a specified master’s-degree title in India.

quick_facts.label: Typical format
quick_facts.value: The canonical full-time MBA is commonly a two-year postgraduate programme; for example, IIM Bangalore’s PGP leads to an MBA degree and is a two-year, full-time residential programme.

quick_facts.label: Entry qualification
quick_facts.value: Requirements are institution-specific, but a bachelor’s degree is the standard entry base. For its 2026–28 MBA, IIM Bangalore requires a bachelor’s degree in any discipline with at least 50% marks/equivalent CGPA (45% for SC, ST and PwD applicants).

quick_facts.label: Admissions
quick_facts.value: Admission-test routes vary by institution: IIM Ahmedabad uses CAT for domestic applicants and GMAT for overseas Indian applicants/foreign nationals; XLRI’s management admission route uses XAT for its PGDM programmes.

quick_facts.label: Fees are highly variable
quick_facts.value: As dated institutional context, IIM Ahmedabad listed a programme fee of INR 27,50,000 for its 2025–27 PGP batch, while stating that fees for future batches would be announced later; this is not a nationwide MBA fee benchmark.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: An MBA is a postgraduate route open to graduates from varied academic backgrounds, rather than only commerce or business graduates. IIM Bangalore’s 2026–28 MBA admission criteria illustrate the common pattern: a bachelor’s degree in any discipline, at least 50% marks or equivalent CGPA, with a 45% threshold for SC, ST and PwD applicants, plus a valid CAT score. Each institution sets its own exact minimum marks, category rules, accepted qualifications and work-experience expectations.

The broader UGC master’s-degree framework historically requires completion of an undergraduate degree for admission to a master’s programme. Applicants should therefore check the current prospectus of every target institution instead of treating one school’s percentage threshold as universal.
bullets: A prior degree may be from arts, commerce, science, engineering, medicine, design, law or another recognized discipline, subject to the admitting institution’s rules.
Final-year applicants may be permitted by particular schools, but completion-document and minimum-mark conditions are institution-specific.
Work experience is not universally required for the standard two-year MBA; it is often more important or mandatory for executive/one-year MBA formats.

sections.heading: Duration and study mode
paragraphs: For the canonical Indian MBA node, the usual format is a two-year postgraduate management degree. IIM Bangalore describes its PGP MBA as two-year, full-time and residential; IIM Ahmedabad likewise describes its flagship MBA/PGP as a two-year programme.

This should not be confused with every programme carrying the MBA name. IIM Ahmedabad, for example, separately offers a one-year MBA-PGPX for experienced professionals and a two-year blended postgraduate management degree. Prospective students should compare the award, mode, work-experience requirement, placement access and total fee rather than assuming that all MBAs are interchangeable.
bullets: Typical canonical route: two academic years after a bachelor’s degree.
Common structure: classroom terms in year one, a summer internship between years, and electives/specialisation choices in year two.
Variants may be one-year, executive, online or blended and can have materially different admissions criteria.

sections.heading: Curriculum and learning experience
paragraphs: MBA curricula normally establish a common management foundation before allowing greater choice. IIM Ahmedabad’s MBA curriculum, for example, makes the first year compulsory across accounting and finance, behavioural science, communication, economics, information technology, marketing, personnel management and industrial relations, operations management, law, strategy and quantitative methods. It requires an eight-to-ten-week organisational internship after the first year, while the second year enables study in areas of special interest alongside compulsory context courses.

The exact mix of cases, lectures, projects, live industry work, exchange opportunities, specialisations and assessment differs by school. At IIM Ahmedabad, the programme describes a first-year core and second-year electives; it reports approximately 173 elective courses as an example of how broad second-year choice can be at a large business school.
bullets: Core managerial domains commonly include finance/accounting, marketing, operations, economics, strategy, organisational behaviour, communication, law and quantitative analysis.
A summer internship commonly links the first and second years, but duration and assessment rules vary.
Second-year electives can support general management or functional depth such as finance, marketing, operations, strategy, analytics or entrepreneurship.

sections.heading: Admission routes and selection
paragraphs: There is no single all-India MBA admission process. At IIM Ahmedabad, domestic applicants are assessed through CAT followed by an analytical writing test and personal interview for shortlisted candidates; selection also considers academic record and other achievements. IIM Bangalore’s 2026–28 MBA process likewise requires a valid CAT score in addition to its academic eligibility criteria.

Other established routes exist. XLRI uses XAT for admission to its management PGDM programmes. Some university postgraduate admission systems use CUET-PG: for the University of Delhi’s 2026–27 two-year postgraduate admissions, allocation is through its CSAS(PG) process using CUET-PG 2026 scores and the programme-specific eligibility rules. GMAT is also used by some Indian MBA routes, including IIM Ahmedabad’s overseas Indian/foreign-national admission category. Test acceptance, score validity, cut-offs, interview stages, reservation rules and deadlines must be verified in the relevant year’s official admission notice.
bullets: CAT: central route for many IIM two-year MBA/PGP programmes, but each IIM applies its own shortlist and final-selection policy.
XAT: key route for XLRI’s management PGDM programmes and accepted by some other management schools.
GMAT: commonly relevant for international, overseas Indian, executive or school-specific routes; acceptance is institution-dependent.
CUET-PG: used by some university postgraduate systems; it is not a universal MBA entrance test.

sections.heading: Costs and financial planning
paragraphs: MBA costs vary sharply by institution, city, programme format and whether accommodation and course materials are bundled. As a dated example rather than a market-wide estimate, IIM Ahmedabad listed INR 27,50,000 for its 2025–27 PGP batch, including tuition of INR 20,10,000; it explicitly excluded several personal expenses and stated that fees for future batches would be announced later.

Applicants should budget beyond headline tuition: application and test fees, deposits, hostel/board where not bundled, laptop and living costs, travel, insurance and the opportunity cost of leaving employment. Check the school’s current fee schedule, payment calendar, refund rules and scholarship/loan information before accepting an offer.
bullets: Use only the current batch’s official fee page or admission offer for decision-making.
Compare what is included: tuition, academic materials, board/hostel, international module, placement services and refundable deposits may be treated differently.
Scholarships and financial assistance can be school-specific; IIM Ahmedabad publishes financial-assistance information alongside its MBA admissions material.

sections.heading: What an MBA can lead to
paragraphs: An MBA can support management and business career transitions, but it is not a guaranteed job outcome. As dated placement context, IIM Bangalore reported that in its 2026 final and lateral placement cycle, management consulting accounted for 45% of offers, technology/product management 15%, and investment banking 11%. This is evidence from one highly selective institution and one placement cycle—not a salary or placement forecast for all MBA programmes or students.

Common post-MBA directions therefore include management consulting, investment banking and other finance roles, product management, general-management/management-trainee roles, marketing, operations, entrepreneurship and further study. Candidates targeting investment work may also consider the CFA Program: CFA Institute states that the credential involves three exam levels, with bachelor’s degree/work-experience entry routes and additional work-experience requirements for the charter. Management research is another route; IIM Bangalore maintains a doctoral programme with its own admissions process and requirements.
bullets: Employment: role availability depends on prior experience, school, internship performance, market conditions and employer selection—not only the MBA title.
Finance specialisation: the CFA Program can complement, rather than replace, an MBA for candidates pursuing investment-oriented work.
Research: doctoral/FPM/PhD routes have separate test, academic-record, interview and research-fit requirements.
Entrepreneurship: an MBA may build management and network capabilities, but starting a venture does not require the degree.

title: MBA in Agri-Business Management
description: A specialized MBA program focusing on the business aspects of agriculture production, processing, and its international trade.

quick_facts.label: What this node covers
quick_facts.value: MBA in Agri-Business Management is a specialised, management-focused postgraduate route for food, agriculture, rural and allied-sector value chains. The title is not fully standardised across institutions: for example, IIM Ahmedabad awards an MBA in Food and Agri-business Management, while MANAGE offers an AICTE-recognised PGDM (ABM).

quick_facts.label: Typical duration
quick_facts.value: A common full-time format is two years. IIM Ahmedabad describes its MBA-FABM as a two-year, full-time residential programme, and MANAGE describes its PGDM(ABM) as a two-year programme.

quick_facts.label: Relevant undergraduate foundation
quick_facts.value: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture is a directly relevant feeder qualification. In its 2026 policy, MANAGE lists Agriculture among eligible agriculture-related disciplines; IIM Ahmedabad accepts agricultural sciences and agriculture-related degrees.

quick_facts.label: CAT relationship
quick_facts.value: CAT is commonly used for admissions but requirements are institute-specific. For the 2026–28 cycles, IIM Ahmedabad required a valid CAT 2025 score for domestic MBA-FABM applicants, and MANAGE required CAT 2025 for PGDM(ABM).

quick_facts.label: Credential availability
quick_facts.value: MBA (Agri Business Management) is listed among programmes at accredited agricultural universities in ICAR's December 2025 accreditation list, alongside related MBA/agribusiness variants.

sections.heading: Eligibility: agriculture graduates are well aligned, but rules differ by institute
paragraphs: A B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture graduate is strongly aligned with this pathway, but applicants should read each institute's current admission policy rather than assume a single national rule. For its 2026–28 PGDM(ABM), MANAGE required a bachelor’s degree in agricultural sciences or an agriculture-related discipline with at least 50% marks/equivalent CGPA (45% for SC/ST/PwD), and specified a four-year degree after Class XII. Its eligible list explicitly includes Agriculture, agricultural engineering, food technology, horticulture, fisheries, forestry and veterinary science, among other allied areas.

IIM Ahmedabad's 2026–28 MBA-FABM policy illustrates a broader alternative: it accepts agricultural science/agriculture-related bachelor’s or master’s degrees with 50% marks/equivalent CGPA (45% for SC/ST/PwD), and also permits graduates from non-agricultural disciplines who can demonstrate a strong interest in agriculture, food, rural and allied sectors through the required special form. Final-year students may be eligible provisionally, subject to the institute's documentation and completion conditions.
bullets: Check the required degree length: a four-year agriculture degree was required by MANAGE for its 2026 policy, whereas IIM Ahmedabad specified a minimum of three years after 10+2.
Check category-specific mark thresholds, recognised-university requirements, final-year conditions and any discipline/interest form before applying.
Treat B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture as a relevant academic parent, not as a guarantee of admission.

sections.heading: Duration and study format
paragraphs: The mainstream campus-based programme format is two years. IIM Ahmedabad describes MBA-FABM as a two-year, full-time residential MBA-level programme. MANAGE likewise states that its PGDM(ABM) is a two-year programme; its award is a postgraduate diploma rather than an MBA degree.

Because programme names and awards differ, applicants should verify whether an institution awards an MBA, a PGDM, or another postgraduate qualification, as well as whether residence, internships and campus attendance are compulsory.
bullets: MBA-FABM at IIM Ahmedabad: two-year, full-time residential programme.
PGDM(ABM) at MANAGE: two-year, AICTE-recognised PGDM programme.

sections.heading: Curriculum: management core plus food and agribusiness context
paragraphs: A specialised agri-business MBA combines general management preparation with sector-specific learning. IIM Ahmedabad states that its first year includes orientation, compulsory courses, a rural immersion module and summer placement; the second year includes sector-specific compulsory and elective courses. It describes the sector component as covering the socio-economic, political, policy and market environment for agribusiness, with decision-making shaped by uncertainty, perishability and seasonality.

The same programme reports three curriculum components: core management courses, compulsory food- and agribusiness-related courses, and electives. Its rural immersion module is mandatory and is intended to give students exposure to rural life, rural markets and links with socio-economic institutions. These are an example of curriculum design rather than a universal syllabus; course lists and credits vary by school.
bullets: Management foundation: functional and analytical management learning.
Sector focus: food, agriculture, agribusiness, rural and allied-sector markets and policy.
Applied components may include rural immersion, case work, group work, industrial exposure and a summer internship.

sections.heading: Admission: CAT-based shortlisting is common, followed by institute selection
paragraphs: CAT is a meaningful immediate parent for CAT-based MBA/PGDM agri-business routes, but candidates must apply separately to the relevant programme and meet its own policy. For IIM Ahmedabad’s 2026–28 MBA-FABM cycle, applicants needed a valid CAT 2025 score, an application to the programme and the stated eligibility conditions to be considered for Analytical Writing Test (AWT) and Personal Interview (PI). Its published process uses CAT and an application-rating score for shortlisting, then AWT, PI and a composite score for final selection.

For MANAGE’s 2026–28 PGDM(ABM), a valid CAT 2025 score was required and CAT percentile was identified as the primary shortlisting category; MANAGE also states that the IIMs have no role in MANAGE’s selection process or programme delivery. Dates, score cut-offs, interview procedures, reservation implementation and document deadlines change by admission cycle, so candidates should use the live admission notice for the intended batch.
bullets: Register for CAT in the relevant examination year where the target institute requires it.
Submit the institute-specific application; a CAT score alone does not create an application.
Prepare for subsequent evaluation such as written assessment, group discussion and/or interview where prescribed.
Verify the policy for the exact batch before relying on any cutoff or deadline.

sections.heading: Costs: compare batch-specific total charges, not just tuition
paragraphs: Fees are highly institution- and batch-dependent. As a dated example only, IIM Ahmedabad published a total programme fee of INR 27,50,000 for its 2025–27 PGP-FABM batch, including INR 20,10,000 tuition; it stated that the fee excluded personal costs such as boarding-related personal expenses, laptop, travel, clothing, stationery and laundry, and that future-batch fees would be announced later.

Applicants should obtain the current batch fee schedule directly from each institution and account for tuition, accommodation/mess where applicable, laptop, travel, insurance, deposits and other personal expenses. Do not treat a prior-batch fee as a quote for a future intake.
bullets: Dated fee reference: INR 27.50 lakh total for IIM Ahmedabad PGP-FABM 2025–27, not a forecast for later batches.
Ask for the current official fee schedule and refund/withdrawal rules before paying.
Compare scholarship, need-based aid and education-loan options only using the institution's current information.

sections.heading: Next options after graduation
paragraphs: Graduates can pursue management roles across agribusiness-linked industries and functions. IIM Ahmedabad identifies sectors including FMCG, agricultural inputs, agri-banking, agri-consulting, renewable energy, and food and agribusiness advisory; it identifies functions such as strategy, marketing, commodity trading, sales and distribution, supply-chain management, procurement, and research and advisory.

Entrepreneurship is another possible direction. IIM Ahmedabad states that it supports students interested in entrepreneurship through second-year electives and an in-house incubation centre. Actual job titles, hiring volumes, compensation and placement outcomes vary by institute, prior experience, location and market conditions; they should be checked in current official placement reports rather than inferred from programme branding.
bullets: Private-sector and cooperative value-chain roles: inputs, food/FMCG, procurement, trading, supply chain and distribution.
Financial and advisory roles: agri-banking, consulting, research and advisory.
Entrepreneurship: food, farm, rural-market or agriculture-service ventures, subject to individual opportunity and execution.
