title: MSW (Master of Social Work)
description: A two-year postgraduate degree program focused on social work, community development, and public welfare administration.

quick_facts.label: Typical format
quick_facts.value: MSW is commonly offered as a two-year, four-semester postgraduate programme. For example, SNDT Women’s University describes its on-campus MSW as two years/four semesters, while the Central University of Tamil Nadu describes its MSW as a regular two-year full-time programme.

quick_facts.label: Entry qualification
quick_facts.value: Entry requirements are institution-specific, but official examples admit graduates from any discipline. SNDT requires graduation from a recognised university plus its entrance test; the Central University of Tamil Nadu specifies a bachelor’s degree in any discipline and category-specific minimum marks.

quick_facts.label: Practice orientation
quick_facts.value: MSW curricula commonly combine social-work theory, methods of work with individuals, groups and communities, policy and research with supervised fieldwork or placement. SNDT lists fieldwork practicum in every semester and a summer block placement.

quick_facts.label: Admission routes
quick_facts.value: Admission is not uniform across India: universities may use CUET-PG, a university entrance process, or a combination of tests and merit. The Central University of Tamil Nadu lists CUET score as its MSW selection mode, whereas SNDT lists a written test, group discussion and personal interview.

quick_facts.label: Fee context
quick_facts.value: Fees vary sharply by university and mode. As published on their programme pages, SNDT lists approximate on-campus MSW fees of ₹41,765 for Year I and ₹40,940 for Year II, while IGNOU lists ₹36,000 for its full MSW (ODL) programme, excluding examination fees. Applicants should verify the applicable session’s prospectus before applying.

quick_facts.label: Further-study and examination options
quick_facts.value: An MSW can support applications to PhD programmes, UGC-NET in Social Work, and general-degree competitive examinations such as UPSC Civil Services, subject to each examination or university’s current rules. NTA’s UGC-NET materials identify Social Work as subject code 010.

sections.heading: Eligibility: graduation is the usual starting point, but cut-offs differ
paragraphs: For a conventional MSW, applicants should treat a recognised bachelor’s degree as the baseline rather than assume that a BA is the only accepted parent qualification. SNDT Women’s University accepts graduates in any discipline from a recognised university and requires its entrance test. The Central University of Tamil Nadu similarly accepts a bachelor’s degree of at least three years, or an equivalent qualification, in any discipline.

Minimum marks, reservation treatment, final-year candidature and document rules are set by the admitting institution. For example, the Central University of Tamil Nadu publishes minimum qualifying marks of 55% for general-category applicants, 50% for OBC-NCL applicants and 45% for SC/ST applicants; those figures should not be generalised to other universities.
Distance-learning MSW rules can differ from regular programmes. IGNOU’s MSW (ODL) page lists eligibility as 10+2+3 and describes a 24- to 48-month completion window.
bullets: Check that the degree-awarding university and the specific MSW programme meet the recognition and mode requirements relevant to the applicant’s intended employer or next step.

Use the institution’s current admission bulletin—not a generic course listing—to confirm marks, category certificates, entrance-test requirements and whether final-year applicants may apply provisionally.

sections.heading: Duration and study mode
paragraphs: A regular on-campus MSW is generally structured as two academic years across four semesters. SNDT explicitly describes a two-year, four-semester, full-time on-campus degree and a 64-credit structure. The Central University of Tamil Nadu also describes its MSW as a regular two-year full-time postgraduate programme.

Do not assume every MSW has identical attendance, credit, placement or completion rules. An open-and-distance-learning example is IGNOU’s MSW, which has a minimum duration of 24 months and a maximum duration of 48 months.
bullets: Regular example: two years/four semesters, full-time and on campus.
ODL example: minimum 24 months and maximum 48 months at IGNOU.

sections.heading: What students study: professional methods, welfare systems, research and field learning
paragraphs: There is no single institution-by-institution identical MSW syllabus, but official curricula show a consistent professional-practice core. SNDT’s 64-credit MSW includes history and ideology of social work; work with individuals and families, groups and communities; integrated practice; gender and society; social policy and planning; social-work research; management of developmental and welfare services; child rights; health; law; and counselling.

Field education is a substantive component rather than merely an optional internship in the SNDT example: the curriculum includes fieldwork practicum in each semester and a summer block placement after Semester II. Goa University’s published MSW syllabus likewise includes mandatory fieldwork practicum, rural camp, study tour, block placement and a research project across its two-year, four-semester programme.

Students should compare specialisations and practice settings before applying. Universities may organise electives or placements around areas such as community development, health, counselling, livelihoods, human-resource management or social entrepreneurship; availability depends on the institution and cohort.
bullets: Core knowledge: social-work theory, social policy, welfare/development management, rights and law.
Core methods: case/individual work, group work, community practice, communication and counselling.
Evidence skills: social-work research and, in some programmes, a supervised dissertation or research project.
Applied learning: recurring fieldwork, placement and community exposure.

sections.heading: Admission: confirm the university’s route for the relevant session
paragraphs: Admission mechanisms vary by university. The Central University of Tamil Nadu lists CUET score as the selection mode for its MSW. TISS states that admission to its postgraduate master’s programmes for the 2026 cycle is based on CUET-PG scores except for the programmes specifically excluded on its admissions page. By contrast, SNDT describes an institutional process comprising a written test, group discussion and personal interview, followed by a merit list.

Because entrance-paper mapping, participating universities, application windows, category documentation and counselling rules can change by academic year, CUET-PG should be understood as a possible admission pathway—not an automatic requirement for every Indian MSW. Check both the NTA CUET-PG notices and the target university’s programme-level eligibility and selection page.
bullets: For CUET-PG route: verify the current NTA bulletin and the university’s accepted test-paper code and score-use policy.
For institution-run admission: verify whether selection includes a written test, interview, group discussion, qualifying-degree merit, work experience or any combination.
Keep marksheets, degree/provisional certificate, category/EWS/PwBD documents and other specified certificates ready in the prescribed format.

sections.heading: Costs: use published fees only as dated examples
paragraphs: MSW fees are set by the provider and may differ by public/private status, campus, resident category, scholarship eligibility, hostel use and delivery mode. As displayed on SNDT’s programme page when reviewed, its approximate on-campus fees are ₹41,765 for Year I and ₹40,940 for Year II. These are programme-page figures, not a national benchmark.

For a lower-fee distance-learning comparison, IGNOU lists ₹36,000 for the complete MSW (ODL) programme and states that examination fees are not included. The applicable amounts, payment schedule and any additional charges should be checked in the current admission prospectus before committing.
bullets: Compare tuition with application, examination, fieldwork/travel, hostel, insurance, library and other mandatory charges.
Check scholarship and fee-waiver eligibility directly with the university or the National Scholarship Portal where applicable.
Treat all fee figures as time-sensitive and programme-specific.

sections.heading: Next options after MSW
paragraphs: For research progression, MSW holders can apply to relevant PhD programmes subject to the university’s current rules. TISS’s Social Work PhD admissions page, for example, accepts a two-year/four-semester master’s after a three-year bachelor’s degree, or a one-year/two-semester master’s after a four-year bachelor’s degree, with at least 55% aggregate or equivalent grade; it also states that applicable reserved-category relaxations may apply.

For an academic route, UGC-NET includes Social Work as subject code 010. NTA advises candidates to appear in their postgraduate subject, or a related subject where the postgraduate subject is not included in the NET subject list. UGC’s published teacher-qualification regulations identify a relevant master’s degree with 55% marks plus NET/SLET/SET—subject to listed exemptions—as one route for Assistant Professor eligibility in social-science disciplines.

An MSW may also be useful for public-sector and social-sector roles, but a degree alone does not guarantee eligibility for a named post. For example, an AIIMS recruitment notice for Medical Social Service Officer Grade II required a master’s degree in social work plus relevant welfare/health-agency experience. UPSC Civil Services eligibility is based on a qualifying graduate degree rather than an MSW-specific requirement; the current notification for each cycle governs.

State PSC civil-services and welfare-development posts should be checked state by state: post title, domicile/language conditions, age limits, reservation rules, degree requirements and syllabus are set by the relevant state commission or employing department.
bullets: Research and teaching: PhD in Social Work or allied social-science areas; UGC-NET in Social Work.
Competitive examinations: UPSC Civil Services and relevant State PSC examinations, where the candidate meets the current notification’s general and post-specific requirements.

Practice and programme roles: social-work, welfare, health, development, research, monitoring/evaluation and CSR-related roles; employers may require domain experience, field exposure or specialised skills in addition to MSW.

title: Ph.D. in Arts and Humanities
description: A doctoral research degree in a humanities discipline such as English, History, Philosophy, Languages, or Cultural Studies.

quick_facts.label: Award
quick_facts.value: Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.), a research degree pursued in a humanities subject or an interdisciplinary humanities area at an eligible Indian higher-education institution.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry route from this node's parent
quick_facts.value: An MA holder is eligible under the UGC route where the master's qualification has at least 55% aggregate marks (or equivalent grade), subject to the institution’s notified criteria; applicable reserved-category relaxations are provided in the regulations.

quick_facts.label: Minimum and normal regulatory duration
quick_facts.value: The UGC minimum is 3 years including coursework, with a standard maximum of 6 years from admission; institutional re-registration can permit up to 8 years in total, subject to the regulations and institution’s ordinance.

quick_facts.label: Mandatory doctoral coursework
quick_facts.value: UGC regulations require at least 12 coursework credits, including research methodology and Research and Publication Ethics; scholars must earn at least 55% (or equivalent) in coursework to continue and submit the thesis.

quick_facts.label: Common admission routes
quick_facts.value: An institution may admit candidates with qualifying national fellowships/tests through interview and/or through its own entrance test followed by interview; for an institutional entrance test, the UGC specifies a 50% research-methodology and 50% subject-specific syllabus and 70:30 entrance-test/interview weighting.

quick_facts.label: Fee context
quick_facts.value: Fees are institution-specific. As an illustrative official listing, IGNOU’s regular Ph.D. (Hindi) page lists ₹17,850 per year and states that examination fees are additional as decided by the university; applicants should confirm the current department prospectus before applying.

sections.heading: Eligibility after an MA
paragraphs: For the usual MA-to-Ph.D. route, the UGC’s 2022 Ph.D. Regulations allow applicants with a qualifying master’s degree and at least 55% aggregate marks or equivalent grade. A 5-percentage-point relaxation (or equivalent grade relaxation) may apply to SC, ST, OBC non-creamy layer, Persons with Disabilities, EWS, and other categories as decided by the Commission from time to time.

Eligibility is not limited to an MA: the regulations also provide routes from a qualifying four-year bachelor’s degree and from an M.Phil. However, a humanities MA in, or demonstrably related to, the proposed research field is the direct pathway represented by this node. Individual universities can set discipline-specific conditions, minimum marks above the UGC floor, language requirements, and supervisor/seat availability.

For example, IISER Pune’s Humanities and Social Sciences Ph.D. admission page for the August 2026 session required a relevant master’s degree with stated minimum marks and a qualifying national test, while also using a research-plan-based shortlist and interview. This illustrates why candidates must read the current departmental notice rather than rely on a single national threshold.
bullets: Prepare an academic record/transcripts and category certificate where applicable.
Match the proposed topic with faculty research areas and advertised seats.
Check whether the department requires NET/JRF, NET-PhD eligibility, another national test, or an institutional entrance examination.

sections.heading: Duration and completion window
paragraphs: Under the UGC Ph.D. Regulations, the programme has a minimum duration of three years, inclusive of coursework, and a maximum duration of six years from the admission date. The higher-education institution may permit up to two further years through re-registration under its own statute or ordinance, but the ordinary overall cap is eight years.

Female scholars and Persons with Disabilities with more than 40% disability may receive up to two additional years of relaxation, subject to an overall cap of ten years. Female Ph.D. scholars may also be provided maternity/child-care leave of up to 240 days during the programme. Exact implementation is governed by the university’s regulations.
bullets: Treat three years as the regulatory minimum, not a guaranteed completion date.
Confirm registration, progress-review, extension, and re-registration rules in the university’s current Ph.D. ordinance.

sections.heading: What the doctorate involves
paragraphs: A Ph.D. in Arts and Humanities is primarily supervised original research culminating in a thesis. The humanities subject, theoretical framework, languages, archives or field materials, and methods depend on the department and approved research proposal. A Research Advisory Committee reviews and finalises the topic, guides the study design and methodology, identifies required courses, and reviews progress.

National minimum standards require at least 12 credits of coursework, including research methodology and Research and Publication Ethics. All doctoral scholars must also receive training in teaching, education, pedagogy, or writing connected to their Ph.D. subject; institutions may assign teaching or research-assistant work.

Before thesis submission, the scholar presents the work before the Research Advisory Committee. The institution must use plagiarism-detection mechanisms; the thesis is submitted with originality declarations and is evaluated by the supervisor and at least two external experts.
bullets: Core elements: approved proposal, coursework, supervised research, periodic progress presentations, thesis, external evaluation, and final examination procedures set by the institution.
Humanities-specific content varies: one department may emphasise textual criticism, languages, archives, history of ideas, theory, cultural analysis, or interdisciplinary methods.

sections.heading: Admission process
paragraphs: Admissions are competitive and institution-led. UGC regulations permit two broad routes: admission of candidates who qualify for fellowships/scholarships through UGC-NET, UGC-CSIR NET, GATE, CEED, or similar national tests, based on interview; and/or admission through an institution’s own entrance test. For the latter, the prescribed syllabus is 50% research methodology and 50% subject-specific, candidates scoring 50% may be called for interview, and selection uses 70% entrance-test and 30% interview weightage.

The university must publish its prospectus in advance with seat numbers, discipline-wise distribution, eligibility, and procedure, while following the applicable national or state reservation policy. In practice, applicants should expect a topic- or supervisor-fit assessment in addition to formal eligibility.

For a current humanities example, NLSIU requires a research proposal addressing a tentative title, research problem and questions, relevant literature, and methodology for its Ph.D. in Social Sciences, Humanities and Public Policy. Its published process then evaluates the written proposal and oral presentation. Requirements differ by institution and admission cycle.
bullets: Shortlist current departments, supervisors, and advertised research areas.
Write a focused proposal that states the question, sources/materials, literature context, method, and feasibility.
Track the institution’s official admissions page for cycle-specific dates, fees, tests, and interview arrangements.

sections.heading: Costs and funding
paragraphs: There is no single national Ph.D. fee for Arts and Humanities. Tuition, registration, examination, hostel, thesis-evaluation, and other charges are set by the university and may differ by full-time or part-time mode, category, and year of entry. Applicants should use the current official prospectus and fee notice—not older aggregators—to budget.

As an illustrative official listing rather than a sector-wide benchmark, IGNOU’s regular Ph.D. (Hindi) programme page lists ₹17,850 per year and notes that examination fees are not included. Some institutions also offer competitive doctoral fellowships: NLSIU’s published Ph.D. page states that selected candidates may receive a doctoral fellowship, subject to its stated conditions and continuation requirements. Funding availability, amount, and eligibility are time-sensitive and must be verified for the intended intake.
bullets: Budget separately for application fees, tuition/registration, living costs, travel or archival research, and thesis examination/submission charges where applicable.
Check national fellowships and the university’s current fellowship notice before accepting an offer.
Do not assume that admission automatically includes a stipend.

title: Ph.D. in Commerce
description: A doctoral research degree focused on advanced scholarship in commerce, accounting, finance, taxation, or related business disciplines.

quick_facts.label: Regulatory basis
quick_facts.value: In India, Ph.D. programmes are governed by the UGC (Minimum Standards and Procedure for Award of Ph.D. Degree) Regulations, 2022, which apply to universities, colleges and institutions deemed to be universities covered by the UGC Act.

quick_facts.label: Usual entry qualification
quick_facts.value: An M.Com is a directly relevant route: the UGC baseline permits a qualifying master's degree with at least 55% aggregate marks or equivalent grade, subject to the institution’s notified requirements; AMU’s Commerce department specifically lists M.Com or equivalent with 55%.

quick_facts.label: Minimum and maximum duration
quick_facts.value: The UGC baseline is 3 years including coursework and 6 years from admission. An HEI may allow up to 2 additional years through re-registration under its ordinance; specified additional relaxations apply to female scholars and persons with disabilities.

quick_facts.label: Admission route
quick_facts.value: HEIs may admit through an eligible national fellowship/scholarship test followed by interview and/or through their own entrance test. For an HEI entrance test, the UGC framework specifies 50% research methodology and 50% subject-specific content, with 70% entrance-test and 30% interview/viva weightage for that selection route.

quick_facts.label: Coursework and thesis
quick_facts.value: Ph.D. coursework has a UGC minimum of 12 credits, including research methodology and Research and Publication Ethics; scholars need at least 55% or equivalent in coursework to proceed to thesis submission.

quick_facts.label: Mode of study
quick_facts.value: Part-time Ph.D. study is permitted when UGC conditions are met, including an employer NOC where applicable. Ph.D. programmes may not be conducted through distance or online mode.

sections.heading: Eligibility after M.Com
paragraphs: For the canonical M.Com-to-Ph.D. pathway, the national baseline is a qualifying master's degree with at least 55% marks in aggregate, or an equivalent grade. The UGC permits a 5% relaxation, or equivalent grade relaxation, for SC, ST, OBC non-creamy-layer, Differently-Abled, EWS and other categories as decided by the Commission from time to time. Each university can apply additional discipline, equivalence, seat and document requirements in its admission notice.

A Commerce-specific example is Aligarh Muslim University’s Department of Commerce, which states M.Com or equivalent with a minimum of 55% aggregate or equivalent UGC grade as its course requirement. Applicants should therefore check both the UGC baseline and the exact prospectus of the department to which they apply.
bullets: M.Com is an appropriate immediate predecessor, but it does not itself guarantee admission.
A four-year bachelor’s degree route and an M.Phil route also exist under the UGC framework; they are alternatives rather than requirements for an M.Com graduate.
Confirm subject equivalence, category documentation, supervisor availability and the university’s current seat notification before applying.

sections.heading: Duration and study mode
paragraphs: Under the UGC 2022 Regulations, a Ph.D. has a minimum duration of three years, including coursework, and a normal maximum duration of six years from admission. Subject to the university’s statute or ordinance, re-registration can add up to two years; the overall ceiling is ordinarily eight years. The regulations provide additional time provisions for female scholars and persons with disabilities, and up to 240 days of maternity/child-care leave for female Ph.D. scholars during the programme.

A Commerce Ph.D. may be undertaken full time or part time where the university offers that mode. For employed part-time candidates, the institution must obtain an employer NOC confirming permission to study, adequate time for research and, if needed, release for coursework. A doctoral degree cannot be delivered through distance or online mode under these regulations.
bullets: Plan on a multi-year research commitment rather than a fixed taught-course timetable.
The actual registration, coursework, thesis-submission and extension rules are university-specific within the UGC framework.
Verify part-time availability directly with the admitting university; it is not automatic at every Commerce department.

sections.heading: What the programme involves
paragraphs: A Ph.D. in Commerce is primarily a supervised original-research programme rather than a sequence of broad M.Com-style papers. The UGC requires at least 12 coursework credits, including research methodology and Research and Publication Ethics. The Research Advisory Committee reviews and finalizes the proposal, helps shape study design and methodology, identifies any additional courses, and reviews progress each semester.

Commerce departments determine their own subject-specific preparation and research areas. For example, Devi Ahilya Vishwavidyalaya’s Ph.D. Commerce coursework lists research methodology, review of published research, computer application, an advanced course in the research subject, research and publication ethics, and a comprehensive viva. The final degree process includes coursework completion, original thesis preparation, plagiarism checks, external evaluation and a thesis-defense viva voce.
bullets: Typical research domains can include accounting, finance, taxation, banking, corporate regulation, marketing, international business, entrepreneurship and related commerce questions, depending on departmental faculty and approved supervision.
Scholars must obtain at least 55% or the equivalent grade in coursework before continuing to thesis submission.
The UGC framework also requires training in teaching, education, pedagogy or writing related to the chosen doctoral subject; scholars may be assigned teaching or research assistantship work.

sections.heading: Admissions: tests, interviews and choosing a department
paragraphs: Admission is competitive and seat-bound. An HEI may admit candidates holding qualifying fellowships or scholarships from UGC-NET, UGC-CSIR NET, GATE, CEED or similar national-level tests through interview, and/or through its own entrance examination. Where an HEI entrance test is used, its syllabus must be split equally between research methodology and the subject; candidates scoring 50% are eligible to be called for interview, with a 5% entrance-mark relaxation for specified reserved categories. For selection through the HEI test, the prescribed weighting is 70% test and 30% interview/viva voce.

The university must publish a prospectus in advance stating available seats, discipline-wise distribution, admission criteria and procedures, and it must follow the applicable national or state reservation policy. Current department practice can differ: Kurukshetra University’s Commerce department, for example, lists admission based on valid NET/GATE/GPAT and specifies an order of preference among qualifying categories. Always use the relevant university’s current doctoral notice rather than relying on an old prospectus or a general admissions website.
bullets: Shortlist departments by faculty supervision fit, active research areas, library/data access, part-time policy and available seats.
Prepare a focused research proposal, academic records, category certificates where applicable, and test/fellowship evidence required by the university.
Check whether the department requires a separate research proposal presentation, departmental test, interview, employer NOC or other documents.

sections.heading: After the Ph.D.
paragraphs: The principal outcome is the capability to undertake and defend original Commerce research. The UGC requires thesis evaluation by the supervisor and at least two external subject experts, followed—when the required recommendations are obtained—by an open viva voce defense. This makes the degree a foundation for research-intensive academic and institutional roles, but employment eligibility and selection remain subject to the recruiting institution’s current rules.

A Commerce department’s own stated prospects illustrate the common academic direction: AMU identifies academic positions in institutions and universities and roles in research-and-development organisations. A graduate can also pursue postdoctoral research, research projects, scholarly publication, research administration or specialized analytical work aligned with the thesis area; the fit depends on the person’s research record, skills and the particular employer rather than the degree title alone.
bullets: For academic careers, check the recruiting institution’s current qualification, publication, experience and selection requirements.
Keep research outputs, methods skills, datasets, software capability and teaching experience documented alongside the Ph.D. credential.
Consider postdoctoral or project-based research where it strengthens the intended specialty—such as accounting, taxation, finance or business policy.

title: Ph.D. in Computer Science
description: A doctoral research degree focused on advancing knowledge in the field of computer science through original research, culminating in a dissertation.

quick_facts.label: National baseline
quick_facts.value: The UGC (Minimum Standards and Procedure for Award of Ph.D. Degree) Regulations, 2022 set minimum standards for Ph.D. programmes at Indian universities, colleges, and deemed-to-be universities covered by the regulations.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry route
quick_facts.value: UGC permits entry after a qualifying master’s degree with at least 55% aggregate marks (with specified category relaxations); a four-year bachelor’s route requires at least 75%. For example, IIT Delhi CSE specifically lists MCA applicants with a valid accepted GATE score among its Ph.D. eligibility routes.

quick_facts.label: Regulatory duration
quick_facts.value: The UGC minimum duration is three years including coursework; the normal maximum is six years from admission, with re-registration and specified additional-relaxation provisions potentially extending the permitted completion period.

quick_facts.label: Core doctoral requirements
quick_facts.value: UGC requires at least 12 coursework credits, including research methodology and Research and Publication Ethics, followed by supervised original research, thesis submission, plagiarism checks, and evaluation involving the supervisor and at least two external examiners.

quick_facts.label: Fees and funding context
quick_facts.value: Fees are institution- and admission-category-specific. IIT Bombay’s published Autumn 2026–27 schedule distinguishes concessional and non-concessional Ph.D. categories, identifies assistantship and government-fellowship categories, and states that its fee structure may be revised in later semesters.

sections.heading: Eligibility for a Ph.D. in Computer Science
paragraphs: At the UGC minimum-standard level, applicants may enter after a one-year master’s following a four-year bachelor’s degree, a two-year master’s following a three-year bachelor’s degree, or an equivalent qualification, normally with at least 55% aggregate marks or an equivalent grade. The regulations provide a 5-percentage-point relaxation for specified categories; applicants using the four-year/8-semester bachelor’s route require at least 75%, subject to the stated relaxation provisions.

For this node’s MCA pathway, department-level rules matter. As a concrete Computer Science example, IIT Delhi CSE lists an MCA with a valid GATE score in accepted papers as an eligibility route. Applicants should therefore check the target department’s current qualifying-degree, score-validity, discipline, category, and seat requirements rather than assuming that an MCA alone guarantees eligibility.
bullets: A master’s degree route is the standard regulatory pathway; marks/grade thresholds and applicable category relaxations must be checked against the current institutional notice.
Computer Science departments can require a relevant national test score, specify acceptable GATE papers, and impose additional shortlisting criteria.
A four-year bachelor’s degree can also be a UGC-recognized entry route, but its regulatory minimum is 75% aggregate or equivalent rather than the master’s-route threshold.

sections.heading: Duration
paragraphs: Under the UGC Ph.D. Regulations, 2022, the programme has a minimum duration of three years, including coursework, and a normal maximum duration of six years from admission. An HEI may allow up to two additional years through re-registration under its own statute or ordinance, subject to the UGC’s overall limits. Female scholars and persons with disabilities above the stated threshold may receive further regulatory relaxation, with a maximum completion period of up to ten years in those cases.

Actual time to completion in Computer Science depends on the research problem, coursework and qualifying requirements, progress reviews, publications or other institution-specific milestones, thesis preparation, and examination timelines.
bullets: Minimum: 3 years, including coursework.
Normal maximum: 6 years from admission.
Potential extensions are governed by UGC limits and the institution’s own rules.

sections.heading: Curriculum and research work
paragraphs: A Ph.D. in Computer Science is principally a supervised research programme rather than a fixed taught-degree syllabus. UGC requires at least 12 credits of coursework, including research methodology and Research and Publication Ethics. The Research Advisory Committee may identify additional courses and may recommend UGC-recognized online courses as part of the credit requirement.

After coursework, the scholar develops and executes an original research project under a supervisor and Research Advisory Committee. UGC requires periodic semester-wise progress presentations and reports. Before award, the scholar produces a thesis, completes institutional plagiarism and research-integrity processes, and undergoes evaluation by the supervisor and at least two external subject experts.

Computer Science-specific topics—such as algorithms, artificial intelligence, systems, security, theory, programming languages, data science, networks, graphics, or human-computer interaction—are determined by the department, available supervisors, and approved research proposal rather than prescribed nationally as a single uniform specialisation list.
bullets: Minimum 12 coursework credits, including research methodology and Research and Publication Ethics.
Teaching, education, pedagogy, or writing training is required during the doctoral period; institutions may assign 4–6 weekly hours of teaching or research assistance.
Research progress is reviewed by a Research Advisory Committee, and the completed thesis is externally evaluated.

sections.heading: Admission process
paragraphs: UGC permits HEIs to admit candidates who qualify for fellowships or scholarships through UGC-NET, UGC-CSIR NET, GATE, CEED, or similar national-level tests on the basis of an interview. Alternatively, an HEI may conduct its own entrance test: its syllabus must be 50% research methodology and 50% subject-specific, candidates need 50% to be eligible for interview subject to listed relaxations, and selection through that test must weight the entrance test at 70% and the interview/viva voce at 30%.

The institution must publish its prospectus or admission notice in advance with available seats, discipline-wise distribution, eligibility, and procedures, and it must follow the applicable Central or State reservation policy. IIT Delhi CSE illustrates how this national framework is implemented locally: it states that admissions are held twice yearly and gives its own degree and GATE-based eligibility conditions. Dates, accepted test papers, shortlisting cut-offs, and interview formats should always be taken from the current departmental notification.
bullets: Identify prospective supervisors and research fit before applying.
Read the current institute and department notice for eligible degrees, accepted examination papers, score validity, seat categories, documents, and deadlines.
Prepare for an interview or for the institution’s entrance test, where applicable.

sections.heading: Costs, assistantships, and fee variability
paragraphs: There is no single all-India Ph.D. in Computer Science fee. Costs vary by HEI, residency status, admission category, semester, hostel choice, and whether the scholar receives a teaching assistantship, research assistantship, government fellowship, sponsorship, or self-financing placement. Applicants should use the fee notice for the exact admission cycle and budget separately for academic, refundable-deposit, hostel, and living costs where applicable.

As dated context, IIT Bombay’s Autumn 2026–27 official fee circular separates concessional and non-concessional Ph.D. fee groups and lists teaching assistantships, research assistantships, and several government fellowship categories in its concessional group. It also explicitly reserves the right to revise fees in subsequent semesters, so this is an institutional example rather than a national price benchmark.
bullets: Verify the current cycle’s institute fee circular before accepting an offer.
Check whether the offer is tied to TA, RA, project, fellowship, sponsored, external, or self-financed status.
Confirm whether tuition concessions or exemptions apply to the relevant category and whether hostel charges are separate.

title: Ph.D. in Design
description: A doctoral research degree focused on advancing knowledge in a specialized area of design.

quick_facts.label: National minimum duration
quick_facts.value: Under the UGC Ph.D. Regulations, 2022, a Ph.D. has a minimum duration of 3 years (including coursework) and a normal maximum of 6 years from admission; institutional re-registration provisions can extend the overall limit to 8 years, with specified additional relaxations for women scholars and persons with disabilities.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry qualification
quick_facts.value: UGC permits entry after a qualifying master’s degree with at least 55% aggregate (subject to the stated category relaxation), or directly after a 4-year bachelor’s degree with at least 75% aggregate (also subject to relaxation). Individual Design schools can set discipline-specific evidence requirements.

quick_facts.label: Admission routes
quick_facts.value: UGC regulations allow admission through national fellowship/scholarship examinations such as UGC-NET, CSIR-NET, GATE and CEED, based on interview, and/or through an institution’s Ph.D. entrance test followed by interview. CEED qualification alone does not guarantee admission.

quick_facts.label: Coursework requirement
quick_facts.value: UGC requires at least 12 coursework credits, including research methodology and Research and Publication Ethics. The exact design coursework and credit load are determined by the admitting institution and entry background.

quick_facts.label: Mode of study
quick_facts.value: Part-time Ph.D. study is permitted if UGC conditions are met, including an employer no-objection certificate where applicable; Ph.D. programmes may not be offered through distance or online mode.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: In India, the baseline eligibility is set by the UGC Ph.D. Regulations, 2022. Applicants may qualify with a 1-year master’s after a 4-year bachelor’s degree, a 2-year master’s after a 3-year bachelor’s degree, or an equivalent recognised qualification, normally with at least 55% aggregate marks. A candidate with a 4-year bachelor’s degree may also seek direct Ph.D. admission with at least 75% aggregate marks. UGC provides a 5-percentage-point relaxation for specified reserved and disability categories, subject to the regulations and institutional implementation.

At the programme level, Design schools may assess disciplinary preparation, research capability, portfolio or substantial design-related work. For example, IIT Bombay IDC lists M.Des, M.Tech, MFA, M.Arch, MA (Design), specified design diplomas and other master’s degrees as possible entry routes; it also allows selected applicants with B.Des, B.Tech, B.Arch, BFA or an undergraduate design diploma when they demonstrate design competence. These are an institutional example, not a universal rule for every Indian Ph.D. in Design.
bullets: Check the target institute’s current prospectus for accepted qualifying degrees, marks/CGPA conversion, category rules, full-time or part-time categories, portfolio/research-proposal requirements, and supervisor availability.
An M.Des is a strong and common preparation route, but it is not the only possible qualifying background under national rules or at all Design schools.

sections.heading: Duration and study mode
paragraphs: The UGC minimum is 3 years, including coursework, and the standard maximum is 6 years from the date of admission. An institution may allow up to 2 additional years through re-registration under its own statutes, making 8 years the general outer limit. Women scholars and persons with disabilities of more than 40% disability may receive up to 2 further years of relaxation, subject to an overall limit of 10 years; the regulations also provide women scholars up to 240 days of maternity/child-care leave over the programme.

The practical time to completion depends on the research problem, fieldwork or prototyping, ethics approvals, publications, review milestones and thesis examination. IIT Bombay IDC describes its Design Ph.D. as a long-term commitment requiring a minimum of 3–4 years, which is illustrative rather than a national duration rule.

A part-time Ph.D. is possible where the institution permits it and all UGC requirements are met. Employed applicants need an employer no-objection certificate confirming permission, sufficient research time and release for coursework if required. A distance/online Ph.D. is not permitted.

sections.heading: Curriculum and research work
paragraphs: A Ph.D. in Design is research-led rather than a fixed taught degree. Nationally, the UGC requires a minimum of 12 coursework credits that include research methodology and Research and Publication Ethics; scholars must secure at least 55% or the equivalent grade in coursework before they can continue and submit a thesis. The Research Advisory Committee reviews the proposal, helps finalise the topic and methodology, and reviews progress each semester.

Design-specific coursework varies by school and prior qualification. At IIT Bombay IDC, postgraduate entrants in design-related fields have a 20-credit minimum, while undergraduate entrants in design-related fields have a 44-credit minimum. Its first-year structure includes Quantitative Design Research Methods, Qualitative Design Research Methods, two research-oriented mini-projects, communication skills and teaching-assistant training; additional electives may be required based on entry background.

Possible research domains are broad and may combine design with engineering, social sciences, media or education. IIT Bombay IDC identifies Industrial Design, Communication Design, Interaction Design, Animation and Film, Mobility and Vehicle Design, and Human Factors and Ergonomics as core domains, while encouraging interdisciplinary work.
bullets: Expect to develop and defend a research proposal, undertake supervised original research, complete periodic progress reviews, write a thesis, undergo plagiarism checks, obtain external evaluation and defend the thesis in an open viva voce.
Choose a programme based on the fit between the proposed question and available supervisors, laboratories, field access and research expertise—not only on the degree title.

sections.heading: Admission process
paragraphs: Admission is institute-specific but must follow the institution’s notified criteria and applicable reservation policy. Under UGC rules, an institution may select candidates holding a qualifying national fellowship or scholarship—examples named in the regulations include UGC-NET, CSIR-NET, GATE and CEED—through interview. Alternatively, it may conduct its own entrance test, with 50% research methodology and 50% subject-specific content; candidates scoring 50% may be called for interview, and selection through that route gives 70% weight to the test and 30% to interview/viva voce.

CEED can be relevant to this node: the official CEED site states that qualified candidates may apply to Ph.D. programmes at various institutes, but the result is valid for one year and does not itself ensure a place. Applicants must separately meet each institute’s eligibility and selection requirements.

A representative Design-school process is IIT Bombay IDC’s Ph.D. admission model: applicants are advised to identify faculty research areas and suggested topics, apply through IIT Bombay’s portal, and shortlisted candidates complete a presentation and interview. IDC states that it admits twice each year, in Spring and Autumn semesters. Dates, seats, research areas and funding categories should always be checked in the current intake notice.
bullets: Prepare a focused research proposal or statement of purpose aligned to a prospective supervisor’s active research area.

Keep degree records, marksheets, category/disability documents where applicable, portfolio or evidence of design work where requested, test/fellowship documentation, and employer permissions for part-time study ready.
Do not rely on CEED alone: institute-level application, shortlisting and interview requirements remain decisive.

sections.heading: Fees, funding and cost planning
paragraphs: Fees are highly institution-, category-, residency- and semester-dependent, so there is no reliable single all-India price for a Ph.D. in Design. As dated context, IIT Bombay’s Academic Office has published a 2026–27 fee circular for new and on-roll Ph.D. students, distinguishes concessional and non-concessional categories, and explicitly reserves the right to revise fees in later semesters. Hostel, living, materials, travel, fieldwork and prototype costs may be separate from academic fees.

Funding can materially change the out-of-pocket cost. IIT Bombay lists Teaching Assistantship, Research Assistantship, project-linked assistantships, government fellowships and PMRF among Ph.D.-relevant support routes. Its posted Teaching Assistantship schedule, revised effective January 1, 2023, lists ₹37,000 per month for the first two years and ₹42,000 per month thereafter for eligible Ph.D. recipients, subject to its stated conditions and satisfactory progress; this is an IIT Bombay example, not a guaranteed or universal Design Ph.D. stipend.
bullets: For each target institute, compare the current fee circular, hostel circular, assistantship eligibility, fellowship terms, duration of support, teaching/research duties and expected research expenses.
Treat published fee and fellowship figures as dated information: verify them immediately before applying or accepting an offer.

sections.heading: Next options after the Ph.D.
paragraphs: A Ph.D. in Design can support research-intensive careers in higher education, design research, research-and-development organisations, public-interest or social innovation work, and specialised industry research. It can also lead to postdoctoral research or to applying research methods and intellectual property in a venture or consultancy. IIT Bombay IDC specifically describes its Ph.D. alumni pathways as teaching and mentoring, academic and design-research careers, developing business ideas or design methods, and postdoctoral research.

The best next step should follow the scholar’s thesis area and output: for example, an interaction-design researcher may target HCI or product-research roles, while a scholar working on design pedagogy, healthcare, mobility, inclusive design or visualisation may pursue corresponding faculty, lab, policy, R&D or research-practice opportunities.
bullets: Academic route: postdoctoral research, faculty positions and design education.
Research route: research scientist, design researcher, human-factors or UX research roles, depending on disciplinary expertise.
Practice route: research-led design consultancy, innovation labs, product/service strategy or an entrepreneurship pathway.

title: Ph.D. in Engineering
description: A doctoral research degree in an engineering discipline, pursued through GATE-supported admission at eligible institutions.

quick_facts.label: Credential and route
quick_facts.value: A Ph.D. in Engineering is a research doctorate. GATE is one recognised national-test/fellowship route that higher-education institutions (HEIs) may use for Ph.D. admission and interview-based selection; it does not by itself guarantee admission or make GATE mandatory at every institution.

quick_facts.label: National duration standard
quick_facts.value: Under the UGC Ph.D. Regulations, 2022, the minimum duration is 3 years including coursework and the normal maximum is 6 years from admission. An HEI may permit up to 2 further years through re-registration, subject to the regulation’s overall limits.

quick_facts.label: Coursework baseline
quick_facts.value: UGC requires at least 12 Ph.D. coursework credits, including research methodology and Research and Publication Ethics. Scholars must earn at least 55% or an equivalent grade in coursework to continue and submit the thesis.

quick_facts.label: Typical direct-entry pattern
quick_facts.value: Direct doctoral entry after a B.E./B.Tech. is available at some engineering institutions for candidates with a valid GATE score, subject to discipline-specific academic eligibility and selection. For example, IISc’s 2026 Computer Science and Automation Ph.D. information lists a valid GATE score as one qualifying route for eligible B.Tech.-level applicants.

quick_facts.label: Funding and fees are institution-specific
quick_facts.value: For 2026 entry, IIT Delhi lists ₹7,500 tuition per semester for full-time Ph.D. students, while IISc’s AY 2026–27 circular lists annual Ph.D. tuition and other annual fees totalling ₹25,800 for General/EWS/OBC students before refundable deposits; hostel and living costs are separate where applicable.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: At the national minimum-standard level, a candidate can seek Ph.D. admission after a qualifying master’s degree with at least 55% aggregate marks (or equivalent grade), or after a four-year/eight-semester bachelor’s degree with at least 75% aggregate marks (or equivalent). The UGC Regulations allow a 5-percentage-point/equivalent-grade relaxation for specified categories, including SC/ST/OBC (non-creamy layer), Persons with Disabilities and EWS, as decided by the Commission.

For a GATE-supported engineering route, the admitting department’s rules are decisive. IISc’s research-programme admissions information illustrates one common model: candidates with a bachelor’s degree in engineering/technology require a valid GATE score or NET-JRF for that entry category, while a master’s degree in engineering/technology is listed with GATE/NET-JRF/GPAT as desirable. Departmental subject prerequisites, score validity, category rules and shortlisting thresholds can differ by institution and admission cycle.
bullets: Check the qualifying degree, minimum marks/CGPA, accepted GATE paper and score-validity rule in the target department’s current admission notice.
Treat a GATE qualification as an admission/funding pathway rather than an automatic offer of admission.

Applicants from a four-year engineering degree may be eligible for direct Ph.D. entry at institutions that offer it; some institutions also provide exemptions or alternate national-test routes for specified high-CGPA graduates.

sections.heading: Duration
paragraphs: The UGC’s nationwide minimum standard is three years, inclusive of coursework, and the normal maximum is six years from the date of admission. Re-registration can allow up to two additional years under the HEI’s rules; the regulations also provide additional time provisions for women scholars and scholars with more than 40% disability.

Actual completion time in engineering is often longer than the minimum because it depends on prior preparation, coursework, comprehensive examinations, research complexity, publication/thesis requirements and evaluation. As a dated institutional example, IISc’s Computer Science and Automation department describes a typical Ph.D. duration of five to six years.
bullets: Use the statutory 3–6 year range for baseline planning.
Confirm the department’s milestones and maximum-registration rule before accepting an offer.
Do not assume that direct entry after B.Tech. has the same timeline or coursework load as entry after M.Tech.

sections.heading: Curriculum and research milestones
paragraphs: This degree is principally a supervised original-research programme, not a taught engineering course. UGC requires a minimum of 12 coursework credits, including research methodology and Research and Publication Ethics; the Research Advisory Committee may recommend additional relevant courses, including UGC-recognised online courses. Scholars must also receive training in teaching, education, pedagogy or writing related to their doctoral subject.

After coursework, the Research Advisory Committee reviews and finalises the research topic, advises on study design and methodology, and reviews progress. The scholar presents progress each semester. Before thesis submission, the scholar makes a pre-submission presentation; the thesis is subject to plagiarism checking and is evaluated by the supervisor and at least two external experts.

Coursework and qualifying milestones vary materially by department and entry qualification. For example, IISc CSA’s 2026 programme overview expects at least 12 credits for M.Tech.-background entrants and at least 24 credits for B.Tech.-background entrants, followed by a comprehensive examination and research proposal before the main thesis research phase.
bullets: Core requirements: research methodology, research/publication ethics, discipline-relevant advanced study and thesis research.

Typical milestones: supervisor/RAC oversight, coursework completion, comprehensive or qualifying examination where prescribed, research proposal, recurring progress reviews, thesis, external evaluation and viva/defence.
Teaching or research assistance may be assigned; UGC says scholars may be assigned 4–6 hours per week for tutorials, laboratory work or evaluation.

sections.heading: Admission through GATE-supported pathways
paragraphs: The usual process is to identify a department and research area, submit the institute’s online Ph.D. application during its notified cycle, meet its academic and national-test requirements, and clear its selection process. Under the UGC Regulations, an HEI may admit candidates who qualify for fellowships/scholarships in GATE and similar national-level tests through an interview. An HEI may alternatively or additionally use its own entrance test; where it does, the UGC specifies a 70% entrance-test and 30% interview/viva-voce weighting for that route.

Institutions must publish the number of seats, discipline-wise distribution, admission criteria and procedure in their prospectus, and follow the applicable national or state reservation policy. Thus, a candidate should use the current notice rather than relying on a prior year’s cut-off, deadline or score expectation.

A concrete engineering example is IISc: its research admissions information states that B.E./B.Tech. holders with a GATE score who satisfy the relevant engineering department’s basic qualifications can be considered for both Ph.D. and M.Tech. (Research), with the choice communicated to the department at interview.
bullets: Shortlist departments by faculty research fit, laboratories and currently advertised research areas.
Apply to the institution directly; GATE is not a single common-counselling admission offer for all engineering Ph.D. seats.
Prepare for a technical/research interview and, where requested, a research proposal, statement of purpose, transcripts, GATE record and references.
Verify whether the offer is full-time, part-time, sponsored or externally registered, because eligibility, employer approvals, fees and financial support differ.

sections.heading: Costs and financial support
paragraphs: Fees and funding are highly variable by institution, student category, registration mode, scholarship status and accommodation choice. For dated 2026-entry context, IIT Delhi’s 2026–27 prospectus lists full-time Ph.D. tuition of ₹7,500 per semester and part-time/sponsored Ph.D. tuition of ₹17,500 per semester; other charges and living costs may apply.

For another dated 2026–27 example, IISc’s fee circular effective 1 August 2026 lists annual Ph.D. tuition of ₹20,000 plus gymkhana, other academic and student-emergency charges, for an annual total of ₹25,800 excluding refundable deposits for General/EWS/OBC students. The same circular lists Ph.D. tuition as fully waived for SC/ST/PwD students, with the listed annual non-tuition charges bringing the total to ₹5,800 before refundable deposits.

Financial assistance should be checked in the individual admission notice and offer terms. IIT Delhi states that its full-time Institute Assistantship includes teaching/research assistance and, on its current admissions page, lists ₹37,000 per month plus applicable HRA for the first two years and ₹42,000 per month plus applicable HRA thereafter, up to five years. These are institutional figures, not a nationwide guaranteed stipend.
bullets: Budget separately for tuition/academic fees, refundable deposits, hostel or rent, mess/food, health insurance where required, research travel and personal expenses.
Confirm whether a GATE-linked or institute assistantship is attached to the admission category and whether it requires teaching/research duties.
Use fee and stipend figures only as dated planning context; verify the final amount in the current prospectus and admission offer.

title: Ph.D. in Nursing
description: A doctoral research degree in nursing that prepares graduates for academic, research, and advanced leadership careers.

quick_facts.label: Award and focus
quick_facts.value: A Ph.D. in Nursing is a doctoral research degree. Indian Nursing Council (INC) guidelines describe its purpose as preparing nurse scholars to develop and apply nursing knowledge, improve nursing education, research and practice, and disseminate nursing knowledge.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry qualification
quick_facts.value: Under INC’s revised guidelines for part-time Ph.D. Nursing enrolment, applicants need an INC-recognised M.Phil. Nursing, M.Sc. Nursing, or postgraduate nursing degree; an M.Sc. Nursing score of at least 60%; and three years of teaching or clinical experience after M.Sc. Nursing, while working within the university’s jurisdiction. Institution-specific rules can differ.

quick_facts.label: Duration
quick_facts.value: INC lists Ph.D. Nursing as 3–5 years. Its 2025 revised guidelines specify three years with a five-year maximum for full-time scholars, and five years with a seven-year maximum for part-time scholars; the 2026–27 INC–RGUHS National Consortium prospectus is part-time and requires thesis submission within five years, with a possible maximum of seven years subject to approval.

quick_facts.label: Assessment and completion
quick_facts.value: The INC framework includes a Pre-Ph.D. examination after one year, covering Research Methodology & Applied Statistics and Nursing Science & Theory Development, plus a seminar/term paper and proposal defence. Award follows thesis evaluation and successful viva voce.

quick_facts.label: 2026–27 National Consortium fee context
quick_facts.value: For the INC–RGUHS National Consortium’s 2026–27 prospectus, listed charges include ₹3,000 application fee, ₹4,000 registration fee, ₹15,000 Pre-Ph.D. examination fee, and ₹25,000 thesis examination fee. The annexure also lists a ₹75,000 non-refundable nodal-officer fee and ₹25,000 caution fee; fees are explicitly subject to change, so applicants should confirm the current notice before paying.

sections.heading: Eligibility after M.Sc. Nursing
paragraphs: For the INC’s 2025 Ph.D. Nursing framework, the relevant pathway for a working, part-time scholar is an INC-recognised M.Phil. Nursing, M.Sc. Nursing, or other postgraduate nursing degree, with at least 60% in M.Sc. Nursing. The framework also specifies three years of teaching or clinical experience after M.Sc. Nursing and employment in a teaching institution, hospital, community centre, or nursing department within the university’s jurisdiction.

The entry standard is not identical across every university. For example, the 2026–27 INC–RGUHS National Consortium documentation requires successful entrance-exam selection before registration and asks selected candidates for B.Sc. and M.Sc. Nursing credentials, a guide’s consent, a research proposal, an employer NOC where applicable, and State Nursing Registration Council authentication of RN&RM registration.
bullets: Confirm that the university and nursing programme are recognised/approved for Ph.D. Nursing before applying.
For a part-time route, confirm both experience and employer/NOC requirements early.
Check the current university or consortium prospectus, because its operational admission rules may be more specific than the INC baseline.

sections.heading: Duration and research timeline
paragraphs: The national regulator’s nursing-programme overview gives a broad Ph.D. duration of 3–5 years. INC’s 2025 revised guidelines distinguish full-time study (three years, maximum five) from part-time study (five years, maximum seven).

The INC–RGUHS National Consortium’s 2026–27 route is expressly part-time: it expects completion and thesis submission within five years of provisional registration, with a possible maximum of seven years subject to the required approvals. Scholars submit half-yearly progress reports; two consecutive late or unsatisfactory reports can lead to cancellation of provisional registration.
bullets: Full-time: 3 years; maximum 5 years under the INC 2025 guideline.
Part-time: 5 years; maximum 7 years under the INC 2025 guideline.
National Consortium route: part-time, ordinarily submit within 5 years; extension to a 7-year maximum is conditional.

sections.heading: Research-based curriculum and milestones
paragraphs: This is principally a supervised research degree rather than a taught clinical-specialisation programme. The required academic work combines research design, applied statistics, nursing science, theory development, literature review, ethics/permissions, a research proposal, data collection and analysis, thesis writing, external evaluation, and viva voce.

In the INC framework, confirmation of registration follows successful completion of the Pre-Ph.D. examination after one year. The specified components are two three-hour, 100-mark papers—Research Methodology & Applied Statistics and Nursing Science & Theory Development—plus a research-area seminar/term paper and proposal defence. The National Consortium prospectus requires at least 60% in each paper and 70% attendance for contact hours.
bullets: Pre-Ph.D. Paper I: Research Methodology & Applied Statistics.
Pre-Ph.D. Paper II: Nursing Science & Theory Development.
Internal assessment: seminar or term paper in the research area.
Proposal defence and final thesis viva voce.

sections.heading: Admission route
paragraphs: Admission is university- or consortium-administered. INC’s revised guidelines allow selection either on entrance-test merit or M.Sc. Nursing merit (with a minimum 60% in M.Sc. Nursing). Where a university uses an entrance test, the guideline specifies 90 entrance-test marks, with 54/90 as the minimum qualifying weightage, plus possible weightage for M.Phil. Nursing and publications.

The INC National Consortium page currently publishes a 2026–27 part-time Ph.D. Nursing application and prospectus. Its selected-candidate registration process requires a recognised guide, a proposed research title and synopsis, and—in-service candidates—guide consent and an NOC from the employing department/institution. Applicants should use the live notice rather than relying on a previous intake’s dates or seat availability.
bullets: Identify a recognised guide and an INC/consortium-approved study centre or a university-approved Ph.D. Nursing setting.
Prepare qualification records, registration authentication, proposal/synopsis, guide consent, and employer NOC if employed.
Follow the current entrance, merit-list, document-verification, and fee-payment notice for the intended university or consortium.

sections.heading: Fees: dated and provider-specific
paragraphs: There is no single India-wide Ph.D. Nursing tuition price. Charges depend on the university, study mode, location, hostel arrangements, research expenses, and whether the scholar is funded or employed. The 2026–27 INC–RGUHS National Consortium prospectus is useful as dated context rather than a universal price list.

That prospectus lists ₹3,000 for application, ₹4,000 for registration, ₹15,000 for the Pre-Ph.D. examination, and ₹25,000 for the Ph.D. examination submitted with the thesis. It additionally lists a ₹75,000 non-refundable nodal-officer fee, a ₹25,000 caution fee, and ₹30,000 per year for the sixth and seventh years. The prospectus states that RGUHS fees are subject to change.
bullets: Treat published fees as intake-specific, not as a nationwide benchmark.
Ask whether the quoted amount includes guide/study-centre, institutional, ethics-review, travel, statistical-software, fieldwork, thesis-printing, hostel, and extension costs.
Confirm payment method and refundability before submitting fees.

sections.heading: What the degree prepares graduates to do
paragraphs: INC describes doctoral nursing education as preparation for nurse-scholar roles that conduct relevant research, develop nursing theories and nursing science, synthesize nursing and allied-science knowledge, lead in nursing practice, education and research, and disseminate research findings. These outcomes align the degree with research-intensive academic, nursing-education, clinical-research, evidence-based-practice, and health-system leadership pathways.

The immediate next step after successful thesis evaluation and viva voce is award of the degree by the university. Career outcomes and hiring requirements remain employer- and institution-specific; candidates should therefore compare doctoral research areas, supervisor expertise, publications, and approved study-centre status against their intended academic or research path.
bullets: Academic nursing and postgraduate teaching/research roles.
Nursing and health-services research, including evidence-generation and dissemination.
Leadership roles involving nursing education, research, practice improvement, and policy-relevant research.

title: Ph.D. in Physiotherapy
description: A doctoral research degree focused on generating advanced evidence in physiotherapy, rehabilitation science, and clinical practice.

quick_facts.label: Degree level and purpose
quick_facts.value: A Ph.D. in Physiotherapy is a research doctorate undertaken under an approved research supervisor and culminating in original scholarly work; it is distinct from the practice-oriented MPT that normally precedes it.

quick_facts.label: Usual entry qualification
quick_facts.value: For this physiotherapy pathway, an MPT or equivalent relevant postgraduate qualification is ordinarily expected. The UGC baseline permits a qualifying master’s degree with at least 55% aggregate/equivalent grade, subject to applicable relaxations; individual universities may set discipline-specific requirements and higher thresholds.

quick_facts.label: Minimum duration
quick_facts.value: The UGC Ph.D. framework sets a minimum of 3 years, including coursework, and a normal maximum of 6 years from admission. Individual institutions can publish mode-specific minimums; for example, Integral University lists 3 years minimum full-time and 4 years minimum part-time for its Physiotherapy Ph.D.

quick_facts.label: Required doctoral coursework
quick_facts.value: UGC regulations require at least 12 coursework credits, including research methodology and Research and Publication Ethics; scholars also receive training related to teaching, education, pedagogy or writing in their Ph.D. subject.

quick_facts.label: Admission route
quick_facts.value: Admission is institution-specific but may use an HEI entrance test and interview/viva voce, or an interview route for candidates qualifying relevant national fellowship/scholarship tests. For an HEI test, UGC specifies 50% research methodology and 50% subject-specific content, with 70% test and 30% interview weightage for that selection route.

sections.heading: Eligibility after MPT
paragraphs: The usual progression is MPT to Ph.D. in Physiotherapy. At the national level, the UGC permits admission to a Ph.D. for candidates holding an eligible master’s degree with at least 55% aggregate marks or equivalent grade; it allows a 5-percentage-point relaxation for SC/ST/OBC (non-creamy layer)/Differently-Abled/EWS and other categories as decided by the Commission. The university offering the Physiotherapy Ph.D. determines the exact subject match, recognition/equivalence rules, and any higher cutoff.

A concrete programme example illustrates this institutional variation: Integral University lists an MPT from a recognised institute/university with 60% aggregate for both its full-time and part-time Ph.D. in Physiotherapy options. Applicants should therefore treat the UGC threshold as a baseline and check the current doctoral prospectus of each target university.
bullets: Prepare MPT marksheets and degree/provisional certificate, and confirm that the awarding institution and qualification are accepted by the target university.
Check category-relaxation, equivalence, employment/no-objection requirements for part-time registration, and supervisor/seat availability in the intended physiotherapy research area.
Match the proposed topic to available research supervision—for example, programmes may organise physiotherapy research around musculoskeletal/sports, neurological, or paediatric areas.

sections.heading: Duration and registration limits
paragraphs: Under the UGC Ph.D. Regulations, 2022, the doctorate has a minimum duration of 3 years, including coursework, and a maximum duration of 6 years from admission. An HEI may allow up to 2 additional years through re-registration under its own statute or ordinance, taking the usual absolute limit to 8 years.

Female scholars and persons with disabilities of more than 40% may receive up to a further 2 years’ relaxation, subject to a total limit of 10 years; the regulations also provide for up to 240 days of maternity/child-care leave during the programme. Delivery and registration mode are university-specific: Integral University, for example, publishes a 3-year minimum for full-time Physiotherapy Ph.D. registration and a 4-year minimum for part-time registration.
bullets: Plan for a multi-year sequence of coursework, proposal development, ethics and data-collection approvals where relevant, research execution, thesis writing, and examination.
Do not assume a part-time option, duration, or extension policy is identical across universities; verify the current research ordinance and department notice before applying.

sections.heading: What the doctoral work covers
paragraphs: This is a research-led degree rather than a fixed taught specialisation. The national minimum requires at least 12 Ph.D. coursework credits, specifically including research methodology and Research and Publication Ethics. The Research Advisory Committee may also recommend UGC-recognised online courses as part of the credit requirement.

Beyond coursework, the programme centres on supervised original research and a dissertation/thesis. The specific clinical or rehabilitation focus is set by the approved proposal, departmental expertise and supervisor availability. Published Physiotherapy Ph.D. offerings demonstrate possible focus areas such as musculoskeletal and sports disorders, neurophysiotherapy, and paediatric physiotherapy, but these should not be read as a universal syllabus.
bullets: Core doctoral preparation: research methodology, research and publication ethics, and discipline-relevant scholarly training.
Scholars must also train in teaching, education, pedagogy or writing related to their chosen Ph.D. subject; they may be assigned 4–6 hours per week of teaching or research assistantship.

Choose a department based on supervisor publications, ethical/clinical research infrastructure, access to participants or rehabilitation settings, and fit with the proposed question—not solely on the degree title.

sections.heading: Admission process
paragraphs: The UGC requires institutions to notify a doctoral prospectus in advance with seat numbers, subject-wise availability, criteria and procedure, and to follow the applicable national or state reservation policy. In practice, first identify departments offering Physiotherapy Ph.D. seats and supervisors whose areas match the proposed research question.

UGC permits HEIs to admit candidates qualifying relevant national-level fellowship/scholarship examinations—such as UGC-NET, UGC-CSIR NET, GATE or CEED—through an interview route. Alternatively, an HEI may conduct its own entrance test: its syllabus must be 50% research methodology and 50% subject-specific, candidates scoring 50% are eligible to be called for interview, and selection through this route uses 70% entrance-test and 30% interview/viva-voce weightage. Applicable category relaxation in entrance-test marks is 5 percentage points.

University implementation varies. For example, Sharda University’s published Allied Health Sciences page lists Physiotherapy among its Ph.D. specialisations and describes an application, entrance examination where required, and interview sequence; its displayed fees and application details are tied to the page’s stated 2025–26 context and should be reconfirmed for the intended admission cycle.
bullets: Shortlist current university notifications rather than relying on generic course listings.
Prepare a concise research proposal, academic records, identity/category documents where applicable, and evidence of national test/fellowship qualification if claimed.

Before paying an application fee, verify the current cycle’s seat matrix, supervisor availability, full-time/part-time rules, entrance-test exemption policy, fee schedule and refund conditions directly with the university.

useful_links.label: UGC Ph.D. Regulations, 2022 — duration and institutional admission criteria
