title: Agniveer Recruitment (Army/Navy/Air Force)
description: Agniveer Recruitment (Army/Navy/Air Force) — govt recruitment exam (defence), conducted by Indian Armed Forces.

quick_facts.label: What this node covers
quick_facts.value: Agniveer is an umbrella recruitment route under the Agnipath scheme, not one identical examination: the Army uses category-based Online CEE followed by a recruitment rally; Navy SSR uses INET and subsequent selection stages; and the Air Force publishes intake-specific Agniveervayu selection notices.

quick_facts.label: Education routes represented
quick_facts.value: Eligibility is category-specific. For example, the 2026 Army notice permits Class 10 entry for Agniveer General Duty and sets PCM/English or specified ITI/vocational routes for Technical; the Navy SSR notice specifies 10+2 Mathematics and Physics, or listed engineering-diploma/vocational alternatives.

quick_facts.label: Engagement term
quick_facts.value: The Army and Navy notices describe Agniveer enrolment as a four-year engagement. Further regular-cadre enrolment is not guaranteed; the cited notices state that up to 25% of a specific batch may be enrolled, subject to service requirements, policy, and performance.

quick_facts.label: Current intake example
quick_facts.value: A Government of Odisha posting for IAF Agniveervayu Intake 02/2027 lists online registration from June 23, 2026 through July 26, 2026. Dates and availability are intake-specific and must be confirmed on the service recruitment portal before applying.

quick_facts.label: Army fee context
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 Army recruitment notice, the stated online-examination fee was ₹250 per application category, plus applicable bank charges. This is dated recruitment-notice context, not a promise for future intakes.

sections.heading: Purpose and route structure
paragraphs: Agniveer recruitment is the entry route for eligible youth to serve below commissioned-officer level in the Indian Army, Indian Navy, or Indian Air Force under the Agnipath framework. It should be treated as a family of service- and category-specific recruitments rather than as a single national examination with one common syllabus, qualification threshold, or calendar.

For the Army, the 2026 notice describes a two-phase process: an Online Common Entrance Examination (CEE) at allotted computer-based centres, followed by an Army Recruiting Office recruitment rally. The Navy SSR notice uses Stage I INET followed by Stage II selection; IAF Agniveervayu recruitment is published by intake, with its own registration and selection notice.
bullets: Choose the service and entry category first; only then compare education, age, physical, medical, domicile, and document requirements.
Use only the official recruitment portal and the notification for the relevant intake or recruiting year; older notices are useful for orientation but do not replace the current one.

sections.heading: Eligibility: match the exact service and category
paragraphs: Do not infer eligibility from the umbrella term “Agniveer.” The Army’s 2026 notification, for example, lists Class 10 with specified marks for Agniveer General Duty, while Agniveer Technical requires a science/PCM-and-English pathway or certain alternative ITI/vocational qualifications. The Navy SSR notice requires 10+2 with Mathematics and Physics and 50% aggregate marks, or specified engineering-diploma or vocational-course alternatives with 50% aggregate marks.

Age bands, marital-status conditions, sex/category availability, physical standards, medical standards, permitted relaxations, and required certificates are all notification-specific. The cited Army and Navy notices require unmarried candidates for the relevant entries and require an undertaking not to marry during the four-year engagement; candidates should not generalize a regional or one-intake notice to another service or intake.
bullets: Class 10 is relevant to some Army categories, especially General Duty; it is not a universal qualification for every Agniveer role.
PCM, ITI, diploma, and vocational pathways can be relevant to technical entries, but the acceptable subjects, marks, NSQF level, and trades must be checked against the current notification.
Check date-of-birth cut-offs rather than relying only on a stated age range, because notices commonly publish exact eligible birth-date windows.
Verify physical measurements, fitness standards, medical requirements, and documentary proofs before applying.

sections.heading: Selection format
paragraphs: Army Agniveer selection in the cited 2026 notice has two phases. Phase I is a computer-based, objective multiple-choice CEE. Depending on category, it has either 50 questions in one hour or 100 questions in two hours; the notice also specifies a typing test during CEE for Agniveer Clerk/Store Keeper Technical candidates. Candidates are shortlisted from the CEE result for Phase II, the recruitment rally.

The cited Army recruitment-rally update identifies the subsequent procedures for shortlisted candidates as Physical Fitness Test, Physical Measurement Test, physical-efficiency events, medical examination, and other rally procedures. For Navy SSR, the official notice identifies Stage I INET and Stage II physical-fitness, written-examination, and recruitment-medical components; the final list is subject to the required qualifying stages and merit.

The IAF should be read separately through the applicable Agniveervayu intake notice. The Government of Odisha posting confirms a distinct Intake 02/2027 registration notice, illustrating why an applicant must not assume that Army CEE or Navy INET rules apply to IAF recruitment.
bullets: Expect both academic testing and physical/medical selection; clearing a written or online test alone does not establish final selection.
Download and follow the service-issued admit card for the precise reporting time, venue, identity-document, and original-certificate instructions.

sections.heading: Application process
paragraphs: Start on the official service portal, create or log into the candidate profile, select only categories for which the current notification confirms eligibility, complete the online form accurately, upload the required current photograph and documents, and pay a fee only through the official workflow where applicable. The Army’s 2026 notice says candidates must provide an active email address and mobile number, enter Aadhaar details, and use the Join Indian Army portal to check eligibility and apply.

Keep original educational, identity, domicile, caste/category, character, and other certificates specified by the admit card ready for later stages. A Ministry of Defence recruitment update for the Army specifically advises shortlisted candidates to monitor the official website, registered email, and mobile number for results and call letters, and to bring the requisite original documents to the rally.

Deadlines are volatile. As a dated illustration, the cited IAF Intake 02/2027 government posting lists June 23–July 26, 2026, while the cited Army notice used February 13–April 1, 2026. Always treat the live portal and current notice as authoritative.
bullets: Apply personally; recruitment is merit-based and official notices warn applicants not to use agents or pay bribes.
Save the application confirmation and payment record, and download the admit card only from the official portal.
Recheck the entered name, date of birth, education details, category, height, and uploaded photo before final submission; discrepancies can lead to cancellation.

sections.heading: Preparation strategy
paragraphs: Prepare in parallel for the online/written component and for physical and medical screening. For Army CEE, begin with the sample/practice material associated with the exact category: the cited notification says category-wise online CEE practice links and explanatory registration/exam videos are available through Join Indian Army. Study to the category’s notified pattern rather than a generic “Agniveer syllabus.”

Build fitness progressively and safely because the selection path can include a Physical Fitness Test, physical measurements, physical-efficiency events, and recruitment medical examination. Before reporting, reconcile every qualification and certificate with the wording of the current notice and admit card; keep originals and the required copies ready.

Use a fraud-aware approach. The Army notification and Ministry of Defence update both state that selection is fair, transparent, and merit-based and caution candidates against recruiters, intermediaries, or anyone claiming they can influence selection.
bullets: Create a timetable covering category-specific CEE/INET subjects, timed objective-question practice, and weak topics.
Practise running and prescribed fitness activities only after checking the current service/category standard and, where appropriate, seeking medical advice.
Conduct a document audit early: marksheets, identity documents, Aadhaar, domicile, certificates for any claimed category/relaxation, photographs, and other notification-specific forms.
Track only official portal notices, dashboard messages, registered email, and SMS updates.

sections.heading: Service outcome, pay context, and next steps
paragraphs: Selection leads to enrolment as an Agniveer for a four-year engagement and military training according to service requirements. It is not an automatic permanent appointment. The cited 2026 Army notice states that, after four years, Agniveers may be offered the opportunity to apply for permanent enrolment; selection is centralized and performance-based, and up to 25% of a specific batch may be enrolled in the regular cadre. The Navy SSR notice describes the same maximum-up-to-25% framework for its regular sailor cadre.

Pay and terminal-benefit figures should be read as dated policy/notice context. The cited 2026 Army notice lists a customised monthly package progressing from ₹30,000 in year one to ₹40,000 in year four, with 70% shown as in-hand pay and 30% contributed to the corpus, matched by the Government. It lists an approximate ₹10.04 lakh Seva Nidhi package after four years, excluding interest, and says there is no gratuity or pensionary benefit for the engagement period.

The cited Army notice also states that an Agniveer receives a detailed skill-set certificate at the end of engagement and is not eligible for ex-servicemen status. Candidates should plan for both possible pathways: performance-based consideration for regular enrolment and a civilian education, skill, or employment transition after the four-year term.
bullets: Do not treat retention as assured: it depends on service requirements, policy, eligibility, and performance.
Treat all salary, allowance, insurance, compensation, and Seva Nidhi figures as subject to the applicable current service notice and policy.
Retain official training, skill, and service records for later education or employment applications.

title: AIAPGET
description: AIAPGET — pg entrance exam (medical), conducted by NTA. AYUSH PG.

quick_facts.label: Exam authority
quick_facts.value: NTA conducts AIAPGET on behalf of NCISM and NCH, in consultation with the Ministry of Ayush; NTA’s role covers the test and results rather than seat counselling.

quick_facts.label: Counselling route
quick_facts.value: AACCC conducts counselling for specified All India Quota, central/national-institute and deemed-university PG seats; State/UT counselling authorities handle State/UT quota seats under their applicable rules.

sections.heading: Purpose and place in the AYUSH education pathway
paragraphs: AIAPGET is the national postgraduate entrance test used for admission to MD/MS AYUSH programmes in Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy. For the 2025–26 session, NTA described it as one examination covering both All India and State quota seats across AYUSH colleges, institutions, universities and deemed universities; it also stated that separate AYUSH MD/MS entrance tests were not to be conducted for that session.

For candidates progressing from BAMS, AIAPGET is the gateway to regulated postgraduate Ayurveda study. NCISM’s postgraduate Ayurveda regulations specify AIAPGET as the uniform entrance examination for MD/MS Ayurveda programmes, while the NCH’s Homoeopathy PG regulations similarly provide for AIAPGET as the uniform entrance test for Homoeopathic graduates seeking M.D. (Homoeopathy) admission.
bullets: The examination rank supports admission counselling; it is not itself a college allotment or admission offer.
Eligibility, subject choice, domicile, reservation and institute-specific conditions are checked during the relevant counselling/admission process, not conclusively by NTA at application stage.

sections.heading: Who should apply
paragraphs: The 2025 NTA bulletin allowed applicants holding a recognised BAMS, BUMS, BSMS, BHMS or Graded BHMS degree, provisional certificate or pass certificate, with permanent or provisional registration issued by the relevant former council, commission or State/UT board. It also required completion of the one-year internship, or completion by the year-specific deadline. The 2025 internship cut-off was June 30, 2025, so that date must not be reused for a future cycle.

For BAMS candidates seeking MD/MS Ayurveda, NCISM regulations require a recognised Ayurvedacharya/BAMS qualification and prescribe qualifying at the 50th percentile, with 40th-percentile provisions for SC/ST/OBC candidates and 45th percentile for general-category candidates with benchmark disabilities, subject to the regulations’ provisions. For BHMS candidates, NCH’s 2024 regulations likewise set a 50th-percentile threshold, with 40th-percentile provisions for SC/ST/OBC and 45th percentile for general-category candidates with specified disabilities; regulators may lower marks for an academic year when the stated conditions are met.
bullets: Meeting the examination eligibility criteria does not by itself guarantee eligibility for every seat: universities and counselling authorities can apply their own valid admission, domicile, reservation and document-verification rules.

Foreign-national treatment is regulated separately; applicants should use the current NTA bulletin and the relevant NCISM/NCH and counselling instructions rather than relying on domestic-candidate guidance.

sections.heading: Application, test and counselling sequence
paragraphs: In the 2025 cycle, NTA used an online-only application process: create registration using the candidate’s own email address and mobile number, complete the application, upload the required scanned image files, pay online, and retain the confirmation page. The bulletin instructed candidates to submit only one application and said that the confirmation page is generated after successful payment. These mechanics and document specifications are cycle-specific, so applicants should wait for and follow the current-year bulletin.

After NTA declares the result and All India Rank, counselling is separate. AACCC handles its notified PG seats, including AIQ seats in government/government-aided institutions and 100% PG seats in specified central/national and deemed-university categories; State/UT authorities handle their respective quota seats. Candidates need to register separately for the relevant counselling and follow its choice filling, fee, reporting and document-verification rules.
bullets: For context only, the 2025 NTA application fee was ₹2,700 for General (UR), ₹2,450 for General-EWS/OBC-NCL, and ₹1,800 for SC/ST/PwD and Third Gender, plus applicable processing charges/GST. Do not treat these past fees as a current fee schedule.

At counselling, keep original degree/provisional documents, registration evidence, internship-completion documentation, category/PwD documentation where applicable, and any documents specified in the current counselling bulletin.

sections.heading: Practical preparation approach
paragraphs: Build revision around the official graduate-level regulations for your own discipline, because NTA ties the syllabus to NCISM/NCH graduate education regulations. Pair subject revision with timed CBT practice that reflects the latest confirmed structure; the 2025 structure allowed roughly one minute per question and included negative marking, making accuracy and question selection important as well as recall.

Use official notices after the exam as part of the process: in 2025, NTA displayed provisional answer keys and recorded responses and allowed challenges through its stated online process. Retain the admit-card, application and result records, then shift attention promptly to the appropriate AACCC and/or State/UT counselling notices rather than assuming the NTA result creates a seat automatically.
bullets: Prioritise the prescribed undergraduate knowledge areas before using commercial question banks or coaching material.
Take full-length CBT simulations only against the latest official format; replace assumptions when a new bulletin is issued.
Check the official NTA AIAPGET page, AACCC PG portal, and the relevant State/UT counselling authority regularly for dated notices.

sections.heading: What qualifying AIAPGET can lead to
paragraphs: A qualifying AIAPGET performance makes a candidate eligible to compete in the applicable counselling process for postgraduate AYUSH seats; allotment depends on merit/rank, choices, seat availability and the relevant eligibility, domicile, reservation and institutional conditions. In the 2025 result release, NTA explicitly stated that AACCC and State/UT authorities use AIAPGET merit alongside these conditions for counselling.

For BAMS graduates, the intended postgraduate outcome is entry to a three-year regulated MD/MS Ayurveda programme. NCISM regulations describe postgraduate Ayurveda education as preparation for specialists, teachers and researchers. For BHMS graduates, the NCH regulations provide for a regular, full-time three-year M.D. (Homoeopathy) programme and list specialisations including Materia Medica, Organon and Philosophy, Repertory and Case Taking, Pharmacy, Practice of Medicine, Pediatrics, Psychiatry, Community Medicine and Dermatology.
bullets: An AIAPGET score is an admissions credential, not a professional licence or a guarantee of admission.

The 2025 official result release recorded 42,075 test-takers across the four disciplines; competition and qualifying marks vary by discipline and year, so historic cut-offs should be used only as dated context, not targets or promises.

title: AIIMS NORCET
description: The Nursing Officer Recruitment Common Eligibility Test used by AIIMS and participating institutions to recruit Nursing Officers.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: AIIMS NORCET is the Nursing Officer Recruitment Common Eligibility Test: a common AIIMS New Delhi–conducted recruitment examination for Nursing Officer posts in participating AIIMS and other participating institutions/hospitals.

quick_facts.label: Latest referenced cycle
quick_facts.value: The latest official notice located is NORCET-10 (Notice No. 17/2026, dated February 24, 2026). Its Stage I CBT was scheduled for April 11, 2026 and Stage II for April 30, 2026; dates and future cycles are variable.

quick_facts.label: Eligibility snapshot
quick_facts.value: For NORCET-10, applicants needed either an INC/State Nursing Council-recognized B.Sc. Nursing route plus nurse-and-midwife registration, or a GNM diploma plus registration and two years’ experience in a minimum 50-bedded hospital. Institute-specific recruitment rules can also apply.

quick_facts.label: Exam structure
quick_facts.value: NORCET-10 used two computer-based stages: a qualifying preliminary test and a Main examination used for merit. Both stages used multiple-choice questions and one-third negative marking for each wrong answer.

quick_facts.label: Selection outcome
quick_facts.value: A NORCET score does not itself guarantee appointment. Final allocation is based on NORCET Main merit, eligibility, vacancies reported by participating institutions, and the candidate’s submitted preferences, followed by document verification and institute processes.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
paragraphs: NORCET is a centralized recruitment route for Nursing Officer positions. AIIMS New Delhi conducts the examination, while participating AIIMS, hospitals, and institutions report vacancies and apply their applicable recruitment rules. The NORCET-10 notice included AIIMS institutions and provided for participation by other named health institutions; the exact participating employers and vacancy numbers can change by cycle.
source_urls
bullets: Use NORCET to compete for Nursing Officer vacancies rather than for admission to a nursing course.
AIIMS New Delhi acts as the examination-conducting body; the receiving institution remains responsible for its recruitment rules, verification, joining, and posting decisions.
Candidates should treat each cycle’s notification as controlling because vacancies may be added, changed, or withdrawn.

sections.heading: Eligibility: qualifications, registration, and age
paragraphs: In NORCET-10, the principal degree route was B.Sc. (Hons.) Nursing, B.Sc. Nursing, B.Sc. (Post-Certificate), or Post-Basic B.Sc. Nursing from an Indian Nursing Council or State Nursing Council-recognized institution/university, together with registration as a nurse and midwife with a State Nursing Council or the Indian Nursing Council. The alternative GNM route required a recognized diploma, nurse-and-midwife registration, and two years’ post-qualification experience in a hospital with at least 50 beds.

The NORCET-10 general age band for AIIMS was 18–30 years, with specified relaxations. Eligibility is assessed against the relevant cycle’s closing date, and participating institutions’ recruitment rules may impose applicable institution-specific conditions. Candidates are provisionally permitted to take the examination based on their online declarations, but can be disqualified later if records or eligibility do not withstand scrutiny.
bullets: Confirm that the nursing qualification and institution are recognized by the appropriate nursing council.
Ensure required nurse-and-midwife registration is valid and available for verification.
If applying through the GNM route, retain experience certificates that state the hospital, period of employment, duties, and other details required in the notice.
Read the participating employer’s rules as well as the NORCET notice before applying.

sections.heading: Exam format and scoring
paragraphs: NORCET-10 had two successive CBT stages. Stage I, NORCET Preliminary, was a qualifying screen rather than the source of final rank: it comprised 100 MCQs in 90 minutes, including 20 General Knowledge and Aptitude questions and 80 nursing questions. It was divided into five timed 18-minute sections, with one-third mark deducted for each incorrect answer.

Stage II, NORCET Main, comprised 160 nursing MCQs in 180 minutes. It was divided into four 45-minute sections, emphasized case-scenario questions testing nursing skills and competency, and also applied one-third negative marking. The Main score is the basis for the merit list and seat allocation process. For NORCET-10, stated qualifying standards were 50% for UR/EWS, 45% for OBC, and 40% for SC/ST, with the stated PwBD relaxation; those thresholds are cycle-specific and may change.
bullets: Stage I: qualifying only; it does not determine final merit rank.
Stage II: determines merit, subject to qualifying criteria and applicable normalization where multiple shifts are used.
Because timed sections close and cannot be revisited, candidates need a section-by-section attempt strategy.

sections.heading: How the application process works
paragraphs: NORCET applications are submitted online through the AIIMS examinations portal during the dates published for the relevant cycle. In NORCET-10, AIIMS required candidates to use an existing One Time Registration/previous-examination ID where applicable, complete the form online, and retain the application and payment record rather than sending a physical application. The NORCET-10 registration window was February 24 through March 16, 2026, so it is closed; prospective applicants should wait for and follow the next official notice.

After the Main result and eligibility screening, qualified candidates are invited to submit institutional choices/preferences. Allocation is made in merit order from the choices submitted. A candidate who does not exercise choices in the allotted window is not considered for selection, and a candidate should select only positions they are prepared to join.
bullets: Create or use the required AIIMS examination registration profile and apply only through the official portal.
Check the application-status and correction window, city intimation, and admit-card dates stated in the current notice.
Upload a No Objection Certificate by the specified deadline if employed by a government, semi-government, PSU, autonomous, or government-funded organization, where required.
Keep original education, registration, category, identity, and experience records ready for later verification.

sections.heading: Preparation aligned to the official scheme
paragraphs: Preparation should be anchored to the qualification-level nursing curriculum because the official NORCET-10 scheme states that the Preliminary nursing questions are drawn from nursing courses taught at the essential-qualification level, while the Main covers the nursing-course syllabus with a focus on case-scenario questions and competency. Stage I also requires General Knowledge and Aptitude preparation.

The published structure makes timed CBT practice especially important: Preliminary candidates must work through five 18-minute sections, and Main candidates through four 45-minute sections without returning to earlier sections. Because each wrong answer carries one-third negative marking, practice should include disciplined question selection and error review rather than indiscriminate guessing.
bullets: Revise core nursing subjects at B.Sc./GNM qualification level and connect concepts to clinical case scenarios.
Prepare General Knowledge and Aptitude for Stage I.
Use timed practice sets that mirror the fixed section durations and train yourself to finish review within the active section.
Track accuracy as well as speed to account for negative marking.

sections.heading: Results, allocation, and appointment
paragraphs: Candidates who meet the Stage I criteria are screened for Stage II; in NORCET-10, up to five times the total seats in each category were to be called for Stage II, subject to stated provisions for PwBD candidates and ties. The final merit list is prepared from Stage II performance only, after applying the notice’s qualifying criteria and, where relevant, AIIMS normalization procedures.

Selection and appointment remain conditional. AIIMS allocates seats in order of Main merit against eligible candidates’ choices, but the relevant AIIMS or hospital carries out verification and applies its own recruitment rules. The official notice expressly states that examination success does not confer a right to appointment, and candidatures may be cancelled for ineligibility, unsupported claims, or failed document/identity verification.
bullets: A Stage I qualification is not a final selection.
A Stage II qualification may still not yield allocation if no eligible preferred vacancy is available.
An allocated candidate must satisfy the receiving institution’s verification and joining requirements.
Posting is determined under the applicable rules of the institution to which the candidate is allocated.

title: AILET
description: AILET — ug entrance exam (law), conducted by NLU Delhi.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: National Law University Delhi (NLU Delhi) conducts AILET, a national-level entrance test for its B.A. LL.B. (Hons.) and one-year LL.M. programmes.

quick_facts.label: UG purpose
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 admission cycle, AILET was the entrance route for NLU Delhi’s five-year B.A. LL.B. (Hons.) programme; NLU Delhi states that admission cannot be secured through CLAT or LSAT instead.

quick_facts.label: UG eligibility — 2026 cycle
quick_facts.value: The 2026 notice required Senior Secondary (10+2) or an equivalent qualification with at least 45% marks, reduced to 42% for OBC and 40% for SC/ST applicants. Candidates taking the qualifying Class 12 examination in 2025 could apply for that cycle.

quick_facts.label: UG test format — 2026 cycle
quick_facts.value: The UG paper had 150 multiple-choice questions worth 150 marks in 120 minutes: English Language (50), Current Affairs and General Knowledge (30), and Logical Reasoning (70). Each wrong answer attracted a deduction of 0.25 mark.

quick_facts.label: Mode — 2026 cycle
quick_facts.value: AILET 2026 was conducted offline as a pen-and-paper, OMR-sheet-based test.

quick_facts.label: UG seats — 2026 cycle
quick_facts.value: The 2026 notice listed 110 B.A. LL.B. (Hons.) seats to be filled on AILET merit, plus 10 direct-admission-on-merit seats for Foreign Nationals and OCI/PIO applicants; the latter categories were exempt from AILET subject to the stated conditions.

quick_facts.label: Application fee — 2026 cycle
quick_facts.value: The published online application fee was ₹3,000 for general applicants and ₹1,000 for SC/ST and PwD applicants; SC/ST and women applicants who were below the poverty line were exempt. Fees and concessions should be rechecked in the applicable year’s official notice.

sections.heading: What AILET is for
paragraphs: AILET (All India Law Entrance Test) is NLU Delhi’s own national-level entrance examination. For undergraduate applicants, it is used for admission to the University’s five-year B.A. LL.B. (Hons.) programme rather than CLAT or LSAT. The test also has a separate postgraduate LL.M. route, but the undergraduate route is the relevant pathway for Class 12-level law aspirants.
bullets: The successful AILET route leads to National Law University Delhi, Sector 14, Dwarka, New Delhi.
For the 2026 cycle, the University listed 110 B.A. LL.B. (Hons.) seats on AILET merit; this figure is cycle-specific and may change in a later admission notification.

sections.heading: UG eligibility
paragraphs: For AILET 2026, NLU Delhi required applicants to have passed the Senior Secondary School Examination (10+2 system) or an equivalent examination with at least 45% marks. The stated thresholds were 42% for OBC applicants and 40% for SC/ST applicants. The same notice allowed candidates appearing in the relevant Class 12 annual examination to apply. NLU Delhi’s FAQ for that cycle also stated that there was no minimum or maximum age limit.
bullets: Foreign Nationals and OCI/PIO applicants applying in those categories were exempt from AILET in the 2026 notice, but had separate qualifying-mark requirements and a direct-admission-on-merit route.
Eligibility, reservation documentation, and category rules should be checked against the official notification for the particular admission year.

sections.heading: UG examination pattern
paragraphs: In the completed AILET 2026 cycle, the UG examination was a two-hour, offline OMR-based paper containing 150 multiple-choice questions for 150 marks. Its sections were English Language (50 questions), Current Affairs and General Knowledge (30), and Logical Reasoning (70). NLU Delhi stated that logical-reasoning questions may use legal principles to test aptitude, but that no legal knowledge or technical legal understanding was required.
bullets: Negative marking in 2026 was 0.25 mark for each wrong answer.
For a marks tie in 2026, higher Logical Reasoning marks were considered first, followed by seniority in age and then a computerized draw of lots if necessary.
The structure, marking, mode, and tie-break rules are admission-cycle-specific; confirm them in the current official scheme.

sections.heading: How the process worked in the 2026 cycle
paragraphs: NLU Delhi required online application through its AILET portal. For AILET 2026, applications opened on August 7, 2025 and the stated closing date was November 10, 2025; the examination was held on December 14, 2025. These are historical dates for the 2026 cycle, not a forecast of future deadlines.
bullets: Applicants could make up to three test-city preferences; NLU Delhi said that allocation was subject to administrative and technical constraints and that a city with fewer than 100 candidates might not receive a test centre.

The 2026 FAQ said hard copies of the application or documents did not need to be sent at the application stage, except that eligible BPL applicants had to provide the specified BPL certificate; original category and admission documents were to be produced during provisional admission and verification.
Applicants should rely on the official NLU Delhi AILET portal and notification for the live application window, document list, payment methods, and counselling timetable.

sections.heading: Preparing for the UG paper
paragraphs: A sound preparation plan should be built directly around NLU Delhi’s published UG scheme: English Language, Current Affairs and General Knowledge, and Logical Reasoning. Because the 2026 scheme assigned 70 of 150 questions to Logical Reasoning and applied negative marking, candidates should practise both section-specific accuracy and timed decision-making rather than treating all attempted questions as equally valuable.
bullets: Use NLU Delhi’s official syllabus and the University-linked prior-year B.A. LL.B. (Hons.) question papers to become familiar with the stated test design.

Do not assume prior-year patterns are permanent: legal principles may appear within Logical Reasoning, but NLU Delhi said that the 2026 examination did not require legal knowledge or technical understanding.
Practise completing 150 MCQs within the official two-hour benchmark while accounting for the published negative-marking rule.

sections.heading: After the test
paragraphs: AILET performance is used to create merit for NLU Delhi admission. In the 2026 cycle, NLU Delhi announced results on December 18, 2025 and invited candidates for online counselling based on AILET merit, at approximately three invitees per available seat in each category. Being invited to counselling did not itself guarantee admission; candidates had to complete the prescribed registration and payment steps.
bullets: For AILET 2026, NLU Delhi made official scorecards available through the candidate’s AILET account.
Admission, seat allocation, merit lists, refunds, and document verification remain subject to the notification and counselling instructions for the applicable cycle.

title: All India Bar Examination (AIBE)
description: A mandatory qualifying examination for law graduates in India to be eligible to practice law, conducted by the Bar Council of India (BCI).

quick_facts.label: Conducting authority
quick_facts.value: The All India Bar Examination (AIBE) is conducted under the Bar Council of India framework; the official AIBE portal is operated by the Bar Council of India Trust—PEARL FIRST.

quick_facts.label: Purpose
quick_facts.value: AIBE is a qualifying examination for advocates. The BCI states that practising advocates enrolled after 2010 must pass it in order to practise before courts.

quick_facts.label: Current published cycle
quick_facts.value: AIBE-XXI was held on June 7, 2026. Its result was declared on July 18, 2026.

quick_facts.label: Who may register
quick_facts.value: The published AIBE eligibility framework covers final-semester 3-year or 5-year LL.B. students without prior-semester backlogs, and specified graduates of BCI-recognised/approved institutions, including some who have not yet obtained a degree or State Bar Council enrolment certificate.

quick_facts.label: AIBE-XXI assessment and qualifying standard
quick_facts.value: The AIBE-XXI syllabus allocated 100 questions across 19 legal subjects. Although the announced thresholds were 45% for General/OBC and 40% for SC/ST and specially abled candidates, the BCI's July 18, 2026 release says the qualifying marks for that cycle were moderated downward by three marks.

quick_facts.label: Qualification outcome
quick_facts.value: BCI states that a candidate who clears AIBE is awarded a Certificate of Practice. Candidates qualifying under the undertaking-based framework may also need to submit their State Bar Council enrolment certificate within the applicable BCI timeline for processing.

sections.heading: What AIBE is for
paragraphs: AIBE is a professional qualifying examination in the pathway to legal practice in India, rather than an admission test for an LL.B. programme or an academic degree examination. The BCI describes it as a qualifying exam that advocates enrolled after 2010 must successfully pass in order to practise before courts.

The BCI says the examination was designed to establish a minimum benchmark for entry into legal practice and that, after clearing it, a candidate is awarded a Certificate of Practice. Its official AIBE information also distinguishes this purpose from non-practice career paths: the examination is directed at those intending to enter the legal profession.
bullets: For a law graduate planning litigation or advocate practice, AIBE is an important professional-regulation milestone after or alongside the relevant State Bar Council enrolment process.

It should not be treated as a substitute for an LL.B.; the official eligibility notices are specifically framed around 3-year and 5-year LL.B. candidates from BCI-recognised or BCI-approved institutions.

sections.heading: Eligibility: LL.B. status and institutional recognition matter
paragraphs: The current published AIBE portal clarification limits eligibility to candidates connected with a 3-year or 5-year LL.B. from a BCI-recognised university or BCI-approved college. It includes final-year/final-semester students with no earlier-semester backlogs, as well as eligible LL.B. pass-outs who may still be awaiting their degree, may not yet have enrolled with a State Bar Council, or may have surrendered an enrolment certificate.

The BCI eligibility notice expressly excludes candidates studying at or graduating from institutions that are not recognised or approved by the BCI. Candidates should therefore verify the status of their law institution and preserve the documentation required for their particular category before registering.
bullets: Final-semester students: no backlogs from previous semesters; the notice calls for self-attested semester marksheets.
Graduates awaiting degree conferral: eligible under the stated framework if they completed a qualifying 3-year or 5-year LL.B. at a recognised/approved institution.

Graduates without current State Bar Council enrolment, including certain candidates who surrendered enrolment because of employment: included in the published undertaking framework, subject to its conditions.

sections.heading: AIBE-XXI format and qualifying marks
paragraphs: For AIBE-XXI, the official syllabus specified 100 questions distributed across 19 subject areas. The largest allocations were Constitutional Law, Criminal Procedure Code/Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, and Civil Procedure Code at 10 questions each; the syllabus also expressly paired several legacy statutes with the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam.

The published AIBE-XXI schedule initially fixed the qualifying percentage at 45% for General and OBC candidates and 40% for SC/ST and specially abled candidates. However, the BCI's result release dated July 18, 2026 reports that the monitoring committee moderated the AIBE-XXI result by reducing the qualifying marks by three. Candidates should use the final result notice for their own cycle rather than assuming a prior cycle's cut-off will apply unchanged.
bullets: Core syllabus areas include constitutional law; criminal law and procedure; civil procedure; evidence; family law; professional ethics; contract, property and negotiable instruments; labour law; tax; torts; intellectual property; and cyber law.
AIBE-XXI was evaluated on a 100-mark basis, according to the BCI result release.

Exam rules and accommodations are cycle-specific. For AIBE-XXI, the official guidelines provided compensatory time for eligible candidates with more than 40% disability and set conditions for use of a scribe.

sections.heading: Application process: use the live official AIBE portal
paragraphs: Registration is conducted online through the official AIBE registration portal linked from the AIBE website. The AIBE-XXI cycle illustrates the typical sequence: online registration, online fee payment, a limited correction window, admit-card release, and the examination. Those dates are historical for AIBE-XXI and should not be reused for a future cycle without checking a new BCI notice.

For the AIBE-XXI cycle, registration opened February 11, 2026, closed April 30, 2026, online payment was due by May 1, corrections closed May 3, admit cards were scheduled from May 22, and the examination took place June 7, 2026. The official portal also warns that some application fields could not be edited after payment during the correction window.
bullets: Check the active notification before beginning: eligibility and documentation rules may be revised.
Prepare category-specific academic records and, where applicable, the undertaking and enrolment-related documents described in the official notice.
Download the admit card from the candidate portal and follow the examination-day requirements; AIBE-XXI required the admit card and government-issued photo identification at the centre.
Do not rely on historic registration dates or fees. AIBE-XXI registration and examination dates are already past as of July 2026.

sections.heading: Preparation strategy based on the official syllabus
paragraphs: Start with the official syllabus for the specific AIBE cycle, because subject labels and statutory references can change. For AIBE-XXI, the BCI allocated 100 questions across 19 areas, making a subject-weighted revision plan more defensible than studying only a handful of favourite law-school subjects.

Prioritise the high-weight areas first: constitutional law; criminal procedure and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita; civil procedure; criminal law and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita; evidence and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam; family law; and contract/property/negotiable instruments. Reserve dedicated revision time for professional ethics and cases of misconduct under BCI Rules, because this is a separately listed area of the official syllabus.
bullets: Create a checklist using the 19 official subject headings and their stated question weights.
Revise both the legacy and new criminal-law references where the official syllabus names both.

Practise accurate OMR completion and exam-day compliance: the AIBE-XXI instructions required blue or black ball-point pen markings and warned that incorrect question-booklet-set or roll-number details could lead to rejection of the answer sheet.
Read the current cycle's examination guidelines shortly before the test; authorised materials, timings, accessibility arrangements and centre procedures must be verified from that cycle's notice.

sections.heading: After qualifying: Certificate of Practice and enrolment follow-through
paragraphs: The BCI states that clearing AIBE leads to a Certificate of Practice and enables the qualified advocate to practise before courts, tribunals and administrative bodies in India. In practical career terms, this is the regulatory credential most directly relevant to entering litigation and advocate roles; it is separate from an employer's recruitment process for corporate, law-firm, PSU or other legal positions.

Candidates who qualified in AIBE-XIX or later under the undertaking-based eligibility framework must pay attention to the post-result enrolment-certificate process. The official AIBE portal stated on July 7, 2026 that the revised framework applied to those candidates and set January 6, 2027 as the then-published deadline to submit the enrolment certificate. This is a dated operational deadline, not a permanent rule, and candidates should confirm the latest BCI instruction before acting.
bullets: Check the result through the official AIBE candidate login rather than relying on third-party result pages.
Where a result is marked 'Pass (Undertaking)' or 'Withheld,' follow the official portal instructions for submitting the enrolment certificate.

Keep copies of the final result, enrolment documentation and Certificate of Practice records; official notices have clarified that provisional or draft online COP views are not themselves valid printable certificates.

title: AP EAPCET
description: AP EAPCET — ug entrance exam (engineering), conducted by JNTU Kakinada / APSCHE.

quick_facts.label: Conducting authority
quick_facts.value: AP EAPCET 2026 was conducted by Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University Kakinada (JNTUK) on behalf of the Andhra Pradesh State Council for Higher Education (APSCHE).

quick_facts.label: Purpose
quick_facts.value: It is an Andhra Pradesh entrance test for first-year professional courses, including engineering and technology programmes, agriculture-related programmes, pharmacy, and Pharm.D; the applicable stream and course eligibility differ.

quick_facts.label: Engineering test format (2026)
quick_facts.value: The 2026 Engineering stream was a three-hour computer-based multiple-choice test: 160 questions—80 Mathematics, 40 Physics, and 40 Chemistry—with one mark per question and no negative marking.

quick_facts.label: Baseline eligibility (2026)
quick_facts.value: The 2026 booklet required Indian nationality, PIO status, or OCI-cardholder status; Andhra Pradesh local/non-local requirements; and at least 45% in the specified qualifying subjects (40% for reserved-category candidates), alongside course-specific academic requirements.

quick_facts.label: Registration fee (2026; variable by cycle)
quick_facts.value: For 2026, the stated registration fee was ₹800 for the open category, ₹750 for BC candidates, and ₹700 for SC/ST candidates, before any applicable late fee. Applicants should verify the next cycle's notification because fees can change.

quick_facts.label: Ranking and validity (2026)
quick_facts.value: For 2026, ranking used 75% AP EAPCET normalized marks and 25% relevant 10+2 group-subject marks; the resulting rank was valid only for admissions to the applied courses in academic year 2026–27.

sections.heading: What AP EAPCET is for
paragraphs: AP EAPCET is Andhra Pradesh’s Engineering, Agriculture and Pharmacy Common Entrance Test. In the 2026 cycle, JNTUK conducted it for admission to first-year professional programmes for academic year 2026–27. The Engineering booklet covers Engineering, Biotechnology, B.Tech Dairy Technology, B.Tech Agricultural Engineering, B.Tech Food Science and Technology, B.Sc Agriculture, B.Sc Horticulture, B.V.Sc. & A.H., B.F.Sc., B.Pharmacy and Pharm.D; applicants must select the stream appropriate to their intended course and qualifications.

Qualifying in the examination is not, by itself, an admission offer. The official booklet states that candidates must also meet the applicable government-order and admission eligibility requirements, while the counselling process publishes participating institutions, intake, disciplines and categories separately.
bullets: Use the Engineering (E) category for the Mathematics–Physics–Chemistry route and the Agriculture & Pharmacy (AP) category for the Biology–Physics–Chemistry route, where applicable.
Candidates eligible for both categories could select E & AP together in the 2026 application, subject to the official instructions for that cycle.

sections.heading: Eligibility: check the course-specific rules
paragraphs: The 2026 Engineering-stream rules required candidates to be Indian nationals, PIOs or OCI card holders; to satisfy Andhra Pradesh local/non-local requirements; and to have at least 45% aggregate in the specified qualifying subjects, or 40% for candidates in reserved categories. For Engineering and the MPC pharmacy/technology routes, the usual qualifying route was Intermediate (10+2) with Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, relevant engineering/technology vocational study with the required bridge course, or a recognised equivalent; specified engineering-diploma candidates could also apply. Candidates awaiting their qualifying result could apply, but the rank was valid only if they passed.

Requirements vary materially by programme. For example, the 2026 Agriculture & Pharmacy booklet sets subject combinations for agriculture, horticulture, veterinary and fisheries courses, and specifies separate requirements for BiPC pharmacy, biotechnology and Pharm.D routes. Some programmes also carry age rules. Applicants should therefore rely on the instruction booklet and counselling notification for their exact course rather than treating the general rule as sufficient.
bullets: For the 2026 Engineering/technology route, final-year Intermediate or diploma candidates awaiting results were permitted to apply, subject to passing the qualifying examination.

For the 2026 cycle, some courses—including B.Tech Dairy Technology, B.Tech Agricultural Engineering, B.Tech Food Science & Technology and B.Sc Agricultural Engineering—had a minimum age of 17 by December 31, 2026 and stated upper-age limits.
Eligibility and local-status rules are cycle-specific; confirm the current booklet before applying.

sections.heading: Exam pattern and test-day format
paragraphs: For the 2026 Engineering stream, AP EAPCET was online only and lasted three hours. It had 160 objective questions: Mathematics (80), Physics (40), and Chemistry (40). Each question had four response options and one correct answer; every question carried one mark, and unanswered or incorrect responses did not attract negative marking.

For the 2026 Agriculture & Pharmacy stream, the same three-hour computer-based format and 160-question total applied, but the subject distribution was Biology (80: Botany 40 and Zoology 40), Physics (40), and Chemistry (40). The official booklets state that question papers were available in English and Telugu; Urdu-medium qualifying-exam candidates requesting translation assistance were assigned a Kurnool test centre under the 2026 rules.
bullets: Use only the current official syllabus and stream-specific instruction booklet when planning study.
The 2026 booklets required candidates to report early, bring the hall ticket and prescribed identification/documents, and prohibited calculators, phones and other unauthorised materials.

sections.heading: How the online application worked in 2026
paragraphs: Applications for AP EAPCET 2026 were submitted online through the APSCHE CET portal. The official instructions listed information to prepare before applying, including qualifying-exam and SSC/equivalent hall-ticket numbers, date of birth, Aadhaar number, and—where relevant—caste, income, local-status, disability, NCC or sports documentation. After fee payment and form submission, candidates were instructed to verify the information, save the registration number and retain a printed application form.

The 2026 schedule is past context, not a forecast: regular applications opened on February 4, 2026 and closed without late fee on March 24, 2026; late-fee windows ran through April 10, 2026. Engineering testing took place May 12–15 and May 18, 2026, while Agriculture & Pharmacy testing took place May 19–20, 2026. Future dates, fees, document rules and correction windows must be checked in the next official notification.
bullets: Submit one application for the relevant category—E, AP, or E & AP—following the current booklet’s rules.
Check the official portal for application status, hall-ticket download, results, rank card and counselling notices.

sections.heading: Preparation using official materials
paragraphs: Start by choosing the correct stream, then map study to the official syllabus: Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry for Engineering; Biology, Physics and Chemistry for Agriculture & Pharmacy. Because the 2026 test was computer-based, candidates should also practise navigation and timed answering in the official sample/mock test environment rather than preparing only on paper.

A practical plan is to complete the official syllabus topic by topic, regularly take three-hour mixed-subject practice tests, and use the results to revisit weak units. The official booklet’s no-negative-marking rule means candidates can use remaining time to make considered attempts on unanswered questions, while prioritising accuracy and speed throughout.
bullets: Use the official stream-specific syllabus and model questions as the scope of study.
Take the official mock test to experience the computer-based format.
Practise full-length papers with the stream’s actual question distribution: 80 questions in Mathematics or Biology, plus 40 each in Physics and Chemistry.

sections.heading: Results, rank and next steps
paragraphs: In the 2026 rules, the general qualifying threshold was 25% of the maximum marks considered for ranking; SC/ST candidates had no prescribed minimum qualifying mark, with admission limited to the reserved seats available. Candidates were ranked on a combined score using 75% EAPCET normalized marks and 25% marks in relevant 10+2 group subjects. The rank was valid only for academic year 2026–27 admissions to courses named in the application.

After results, candidates download their rank card and participate in the separate admissions/counselling process if eligible. The AP EAPCET Convener conducts the examination but is not responsible for seat allotment; the 2026 booklet identifies the Andhra Pradesh Commissioner of Technical Education as Convener for admissions. Institution lists, intake and reservation details are released with the counselling information.
bullets: Preserve the filled application form, hall ticket and rank card for verification.
A qualifying score or rank does not guarantee a seat; final admission depends on course eligibility, counselling rules, available seats, reservations and document verification.

title: Army Cadet College Entry Examination
description: An internal competitive selection examination and assessment route through which eligible serving Indian Army personnel can seek commissioned-officer training at the Army Cadet College.

quick_facts.label: Entry type
quick_facts.value: Army Cadet College (ACC) is listed by the Ministry of Defence’s parliamentary material as a service entry to commissioned-officer training, rather than a UPSC civilian examination.

quick_facts.label: Published baseline eligibility
quick_facts.value: A Ministry of Defence parliamentary reference lists ACC as requiring 10+2 qualification and an age range of 20–27 years. These are published reference criteria, not a substitute for the current Army order or course notification.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: The published service-entry process specifies Army personality-development training and a written entrance examination before a five-day Service Selection Board (SSB) assessment; recommended candidates then proceed under the applicable medical and merit processes.

quick_facts.label: How applications move
quick_facts.value: Applications for service entries are processed through the candidate’s unit or Formation Headquarters, Records office, and personnel/line directorates—not through the ordinary civilian UPSC application route.

quick_facts.label: Training pathway
quick_facts.value: The Ministry of Defence parliamentary table describes the ACC course as 3+1 years and identifies selection as an Army Headquarters written examination plus SSB; course design, vacancies, dates, and detailed conditions can change by Army instructions.

sections.heading: Purpose and place in the officer-selection system
paragraphs: ACC is an in-service route intended to develop eligible serving personnel into commissioned officers. Ministry of Defence material groups it with other service entries, distinct from UPSC entries such as NDA and CDS and from non-UPSC civilian entries. The examination is therefore only one gate in an internal Army selection-and-training pathway, not a stand-alone public university entrance test.

The official parliamentary record identifies the deciding elements as an Army Headquarters written examination and SSB assessment. This makes ACC relevant to serving personnel who seek a permanent-commission officer-training route through Army channels.
bullets: Treat ACC as an internal service-entry selection route, not as a UPSC examination.

Confirm the current course instruction through the unit chain of command, because published historical tables do not establish current vacancies, dates, medical standards, number of attempts, or branch-specific conditions.

sections.heading: Eligibility: use the current Army order as controlling
paragraphs: The published Ministry of Defence table gives a useful baseline: ACC is shown as a service entry with 10+2 qualification and an age band of 20–27 years. A later Lok Sabha reply separately lists ACC (from Other Ranks) with the same 20–27 age band. These sources support the broad profile but are not a current notification for a particular course.

Eligibility must also be established within the service system. The published process says that ACC applications are processed through units/Formations, Records, and personnel or line directorates, and that processing follows successful Army personality-development training and qualification in the written entrance examination. Serving personnel should obtain the current eligibility certificate, documentation requirements, medical-category rules, service requirements, and timing from their unit/Record office.
bullets: Published reference qualification: 10+2.
Published reference age: 20–27 years.
Do not assume that historic eligibility tables settle current eligibility; verify the course-specific Army instruction before applying.

sections.heading: Assessment format
paragraphs: The official parliamentary account describes ACC selection as sequential: eligible personnel must successfully attend Army-run Personality Development Training and qualify the written entrance examination; SSB interviews are then conducted over five days. The SSB team comprises an Interviewing Officer, Psychologist, and Group Testing Officer.

The same source describes the SSB sequence as Stage I screening through Officer Intelligence Rating and Picture Perception and Description Tests, followed for recommended candidates by interview, group testing, and psychological tests. Candidates should rely on their current call-up instructions for exact reporting arrangements and medical procedures.
bullets: Written entrance examination administered under Army Headquarters arrangements.
Army Personality Development Training before ACC application processing, as described in the published process.
Five-day SSB assessment after the qualifying stages.

sections.heading: Application process
paragraphs: ACC is administered through the service chain. The Ministry of Defence’s published procedure states that service-entry applications move from the concerned unit or Formation Headquarters through the relevant Records office and personnel/line directorate. This is materially different from applying directly to UPSC for CDS or NDA.

A practical sequence is to monitor unit/Record-office instructions; confirm current eligibility and documentation; complete the Army-directed preparatory requirement; sit the written entrance examination; and follow official instructions for SSB call-up, medical examination, and final selection. The National Portal of India also directs users seeking Indian Army recruitment forms and instructions—including ACC material—to the official Join Indian Army site.
bullets: Start with the unit administration/personnel channel rather than an external coaching or third-party website.
Keep educational, service, identity, and other documents in the form specified by the current Army instruction.
Use Join Indian Army only as an official information/form source; the controlling process for a serving candidate remains the service chain.

sections.heading: Preparation priorities
paragraphs: Preparation should address both gates of selection. First, prepare for the Army’s written entrance examination in accordance with the current syllabus or unit-issued instructions. Second, prepare for the multi-assessor SSB process: the published SSB structure includes intelligence and perception screening, followed by interview, group testing, and psychological assessment for those who clear Stage I.

The Army has institutional support for prospective service-entry candidates: a Lok Sabha reply states that the Young Leaders Training Wing at Officers’ Training Academy, Chennai was established in September 2019 to groom prospective candidates for in-service entries including ACC. Candidates should use officially allotted Army training and unit guidance rather than treating private coaching claims as authoritative.
bullets: Obtain the current written-exam syllabus from official/unit channels before choosing study material.
Practise clear communication, group participation, reasoning, and self-reflection for the SSB assessment stages described in the Ministry of Defence record.
Follow the conduct, fitness, and administrative directions issued by the unit and current call-up documentation.

sections.heading: Outcome after selection
paragraphs: The intended outcome is entry to pre-commission officer training and, on successful completion of the prescribed selection, medical, training, and merit requirements, commissioning in the Indian Army. The published Ministry of Defence table records ACC as a 3+1-year course and identifies selection through an Army Headquarters written examination and SSB.

That duration is historical published context rather than a current guarantee. Serving applicants should verify the current course structure, commissioning terms, seniority, pay and allowances during training, service liability, and vacancies in the applicable Army order; these matters may be revised by policy or course instructions.
bullets: Successful written-exam performance alone does not confer a commission.
SSB, medical fitness, merit, and completion of prescribed training remain consequential stages.
Do not infer a fixed intake or timetable from older published material.
