title: BARC OCES/DGFS
description: BARC OCES/DGFS — govt recruitment exam (research), conducted by BARC.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: BARC OCES/DGFS is a Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) recruitment route for Scientific Officer posts through BARC Training Schools, rather than a stand-alone academic entrance examination.

quick_facts.label: Programmes
quick_facts.value: OCES is a one-year Orientation Course for engineering graduates and science postgraduates; DGFS is a two-year DAE Graduate Fellowship Scheme for eligible engineering graduates who secure applicable M.Tech. admission.

quick_facts.label: 2026 screening routes
quick_facts.value: The 2026 cycle allowed shortlisting through the BARC computer-based online examination and/or a valid applicable GATE 2024, 2025, or 2026 score; final selection was based solely on the selection interview, subject to medical fitness.

quick_facts.label: Core academic threshold for 2026
quick_facts.value: For the eight engineering screening disciplines, the 2026 brochure required an eligible B.E., B.Tech., B.Sc. (Engineering), or five-year integrated M.Tech. with at least 60% aggregate marks or 6.0/10 CGPA (or equivalent); science disciplines have separate, subject-specific M.Sc./integrated-M.Sc. requirements.

quick_facts.label: 2026 application status
quick_facts.value: The OCES/DGFS-2026 portal listed January 31, 2026 as the last date for online registration, with no further extension; applicants should treat each future cycle's portal notice and brochure as controlling.

quick_facts.label: Training support and service obligation
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, the brochure stated a ₹74,000 monthly training stipend for OCES and DGFS, plus programme-specific support; selected OCES and DGFS candidates were required to execute a personal indemnity bond to serve DAE for at least three years after training.

sections.heading: Purpose and position in the DAE career pathway
paragraphs: OCES/DGFS is BARC Training Schools’ recruitment-and-training pathway for early-career scientists and engineers in the Department of Atomic Energy. The 2026 information brochure describes recruitment to Group-A Scientific Officer positions through two linked schemes: OCES for engineering graduates and science postgraduates, and DGFS for eligible engineering graduates pursuing selected M.Tech. programmes.

Successful completion of the relevant training scheme leads to appointment as Scientific Officer “C” in DAE units or, where applicable, the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board. It is therefore best understood as a selective government scientific-officer recruitment programme whose screening examination is only the first stage—not as an admission test alone.
bullets: OCES: one-year orientation and professional training route.
DGFS: two-year M.Tech.-linked fellowship route for selected engineering candidates who also independently obtain admission in listed institutes and specialisations.

The 2026 brochure identifies work areas spanning nuclear science and technology, reactors, accelerators, fuel-cycle technologies, and research in engineering, physics, chemistry, biosciences, geology, and geophysics.

sections.heading: Eligibility: match the notified discipline, degree, and personal criteria
paragraphs: Eligibility is discipline-specific. In the 2026 cycle, engineering applicants were screened in Mechanical, Chemical, Metallurgical, Electrical, Electronics, Computer Science, Instrumentation, or Civil Engineering. The core qualifying credentials were an eligible B.E., B.Tech., B.Sc. (Engineering), or five-year integrated M.Tech. in the applicable discipline, with at least 60% aggregate marks or 6.0/10 CGPA (or equivalent).

Science applicants were not covered by a generic “science degree” rule: Physics, Chemistry, Biosciences, Geology, and Geophysics each had their own required subjects, degree combinations, and prior-study conditions. The brochure also names many related-looking qualifications that are not eligible. A candidate should therefore verify the exact degree title, subject history, and screening discipline against the current cycle’s eligibility tables before applying.

For 2026, applicants had to be Indian citizens and at least 18 on August 1, 2026. The stated maximum ages were 26 for General, 29 for OBC non-creamy-layer, and 31 for SC/ST candidates, with specified additional provisions for other categories and persons with disabilities. These are cycle-specific criteria, not assumptions for a later recruitment year.
bullets: A valid applicable GATE 2024, 2025, or 2026 score was needed only for candidates seeking GATE-score screening in the 2026 cycle; it did not replace the underlying degree eligibility.
Candidates could apply in only one OCES screening discipline even if their qualifications could fit more than one.
Candidates awaiting 2025–26 final results could apply in 2026, subject to completing academic requirements and later submitting qualifying proof under the brochure’s conditions.
DGFS required selection for OCES plus independent admission to a listed M.Tech. programme; that admission alone did not guarantee a DGFS fellowship.

sections.heading: Selection and online-test format
paragraphs: The 2026 selection process had two stages: screening to shortlist candidates, followed by a selection interview. Screening could be through the BARC online computer-based test, an applicable GATE score, or both; BARC specifically advised eligible applicants to use both avenues to improve their chance of being shortlisted. Final selection was based solely on selection-interview performance, subject to medical fitness.

For the 2026 CBT, the test comprised 100 single-correct-answer objective questions in 120 minutes. Each correct response earned three marks, each incorrect response carried a one-mark penalty, and unattempted questions earned zero. The brochure stated that questions and instructions were in English.

The test syllabus was tied to the selected discipline: B.E./B.Tech./B.Sc. (Engineering) level for engineering disciplines and M.Sc. level for science disciplines. BARC stated that the questions emphasize basic understanding and problem-solving rather than memory, and that General English, general knowledge, and aptitude are not assessed.
bullets: 2026 CBT screening disciplines: eight engineering and five science disciplines.
2026 interview locations: Mumbai for all disciplines except Geology and Geophysics; Hyderabad for Geology and Geophysics.
Use the notification for the relevant year to confirm whether test structure, screening routes, locations, and schedules have changed.

sections.heading: Application process and 2026-cycle timing
paragraphs: The application is completed online through the BARC OCES/DGFS portal. The 2026 instructions required preliminary registration and verification of email and mobile number, followed by personal, academic, screening, and document-upload stages; candidates then reviewed and finally submitted the form. A valid email address and mobile number were mandatory, and no modifications were permitted after final submission.

Applicants choosing CBT in 2026 had to select three preferred examination cities. Applicants could select CBT and/or GATE-based screening and had to provide the relevant GATE details and scorecard as directed. The official instructions also required uploading a recent photograph and signature and entering academic marks; incomplete information could invalidate an application.

Dates and fees are annual, variable notice items. In the 2026 cycle, online registration opened on December 22, 2025 and the live portal reported January 31, 2026 as the final registration date. The 2026 brochure charged ₹500 plus bank charges to specified male General/OBC and certain other listed categories, while women, transgender applicants, SC/ST applicants, eligible defence-dependant applicants, and qualifying persons with disabilities were exempt. Future applicants must use the then-current portal and brochure rather than these historical figures.
bullets: Retain the registration number and monitor the portal and registered email/mobile for venue, admit-card, shortlist, and interview notices.
For 2026, no paper copies of application documents were to be sent to BARC at application stage.
Government/PSU/aided-institute employees needed a no-objection certificate at interview under the 2026 rules.

sections.heading: Preparation approach grounded in the official test design
paragraphs: Start by choosing the one screening discipline for which the degree title and subject record are explicitly eligible. Then map preparation to that discipline’s undergraduate engineering level or postgraduate science level, as applicable. Because the official description stresses conceptual understanding and problem-solving, preparation should prioritize derivations, numerical applications, core theory, and timed single-correct MCQ practice over general-aptitude preparation.

If eligible, consider both the CBT and GATE screening channels. The 2026 brochure expressly advised applicants to use both because GATE cut-offs for interview shortlisting were finalized only after the online examination. This does not mean a GATE score guarantees an interview; it is one screening route.

Practise the disclosed 2026 CBT conditions: 100 questions in 120 minutes, +3 for correct answers and −1 for incorrect answers. Build an attempt strategy that accounts for negative marking, and practise on-screen calculation because personal calculators and logarithmic tables were prohibited, while an on-screen calculator was enabled.
bullets: Study only the selected discipline’s notified level: engineering at B.E./B.Tech./B.Sc. (Engineering) level; science at M.Sc. level.
Do not allocate primary preparation time to General English, general knowledge, or generic aptitude for the 2026 CBT, because the brochure said these were not assessed.
Prepare separately for the technical selection interview; it is the stage on which final selection was based in the 2026 programme.

sections.heading: Training, appointment, compensation, and obligations
paragraphs: OCES trainees undertake one year of orientation training. In the 2026 scheme, a trainee needed at least 35% in each subject and 50% aggregate to pass; successful trainees were posted as Scientific Officer “C” according to DAE requirements and performance. OCES placement could be in BARC, IGCAR, RRCAT, VECC, HWB, NFC, BRIT, NPCIL, BHAVINI, UCIL, AMD, DCSEM, or AERB, including facilities elsewhere in India.

DGFS fellows complete a two-year M.Tech.-linked programme with a DAE-assigned, jointly supervised project, followed by a four-month orientation course after joining. For the 2026 offering, successful fellows from IIT Bombay were to be placed at BARC and those from IIT Madras at IGCAR, subject to the stated placement conditions.

Compensation figures should be read as dated 2026 context. The 2026 brochure stated a ₹74,000 monthly stipend during OCES training plus a ₹30,000 one-time book allowance. DGFS fellows were stated to receive ₹74,000 per month for two years, M.Tech. tuition reimbursement, and specified project support. After absorption, the stated base appointment was Scientific Officer “C” at Level 10, ₹56,100 in the 7th Central Pay Commission pay matrix; the brochure’s illustrative joining emoluments at the then-current Mumbai rate were approximately ₹1.34 lakh with three increments and applicable allowances. Actual pay and allowances can change with government orders, posting, and performance-based increments.

Both routes carried a service obligation in the 2026 brochure: selected candidates had to execute a personal indemnity bond to serve DAE for at least three years after training. The bond basis differed by scheme and included the specified programme support actually paid; the brochure stated that no third-party surety was required.
bullets: OCES performance above the relevant threshold may support HBNI postgraduate diploma or M.Tech. enrolment pathways, subject to the programme’s stated conditions.
DGFS is not merely financial aid: it combines M.Tech. study, DAE-linked project work, and subsequent Scientific Officer appointment.
Posting is needs- and merit-based; candidates should not assume a preferred city or DAE unit.

title: BITSAT
description: BITSAT — ug entrance exam (engineering), conducted by BITS Pilani.

quick_facts.label: Conducting institution
quick_facts.value: BITSAT is conducted by Birla Institute of Technology and Science (BITS) Pilani for admission to its Integrated First Degree programmes.

quick_facts.label: Primary purpose
quick_facts.value: For the 2026–27 cycle, BITSAT was the computer-based entrance test for B.E., M.Sc. and B.Pharm. first-degree programmes at BITS Pilani’s Pilani, K K Birla Goa and Hyderabad campuses.

quick_facts.label: Academic eligibility baseline
quick_facts.value: For most B.E. and M.Sc. programmes, applicants need Class 12/10+2 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, at least 75% aggregate in PCM and at least 60% in each of those subjects; B.Pharm., B.E. Environmental and Sustainability Engineering and M.Sc. Biological Sciences use PCB or PCM under the published rules.

quick_facts.label: Test structure (2026)
quick_facts.value: The published 2026 format was a three-hour computer-based multiple-choice test: Physics (30), Chemistry (30), English Proficiency (10), Logical Reasoning (20), and Mathematics or Biology (40), for 130 questions. Correct answers earned +3, incorrect answers −1, and unattempted questions earned 0.

quick_facts.label: Attempts (2026)
quick_facts.value: The 2026 cycle allowed up to two attempts, in Session 1 and Session 2; for a candidate who took both, BITS Pilani considered the higher score for admission.

quick_facts.label: Admission step beyond the test
quick_facts.value: Writing BITSAT alone does not complete the admission process: eligible candidates seeking a seat must also submit the separate admission/preference form with Class 12 marks, programme preferences and the required fee within the cycle’s published timetable.

sections.heading: What BITSAT is for
paragraphs: BITSAT is BITS Pilani’s entrance examination for its Integrated First Degree admissions. In the 2026–27 brochure, BITS Pilani states that admissions at its Pilani, K K Birla Goa and Hyderabad campuses are made through this computer-based online test, subject to the published eligibility and admission rules.

The programmes reachable through the BITSAT route include B.E. programmes, B.Pharm. and integrated M.Sc. programmes. Although this node uses “B.Tech” as a child label, BITS Pilani’s official programme nomenclature is generally “B.E.” rather than “B.Tech.”
bullets: Applicants should treat the BITS admissions website—not unofficial counselling or coaching sites—as the authoritative source for the active cycle.

The 2026 brochure also describes opportunities to apply to certain international 2+2 collaborative programmes using a BITSAT score; those pathways have separate programme-specific conditions and should not be assumed to be available unchanged in later cycles.

sections.heading: Who can take BITSAT
paragraphs: Eligibility is programme- and cycle-specific. Under the published BITSAT-2026 rules, candidates for most B.E. programmes and M.Sc. programmes needed a recognized 10+2 qualification with Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, a language and one additional subject; they needed 75% aggregate in PCM and 60% in each PCM subject, counting theory and practical components.

For B.Pharm., B.E. Environmental and Sustainability Engineering, and M.Sc. Biological Sciences, the 2026 rules allowed Biology or Mathematics alongside Physics and Chemistry, with the same 75% aggregate and 60%-per-subject thresholds in the relevant three subjects. PCB entrants were required to have mathematics proficiency at Class 10 level.

For the 2026 examination, students appearing for Class 12 in 2026 or who passed it in 2025 were eligible, subject to the other rules. Students who passed Class 12 in 2024 or earlier, and students already enrolled in a BITS campus programme, were not eligible for BITSAT-2026. These year-of-passing rules should be checked afresh for a future cycle.
bullets: CAIE candidates must satisfy the required subjects at A Level; IB candidates must have them at Higher Level under the 2026 brochure.
Meeting the Class 12 marks threshold is required for admission even where a candidate has taken BITSAT; admission merit is based on the BITSAT score among eligible applicants.

sections.heading: Exam format and scoring
paragraphs: BITSAT-2026 was a three-hour, no-break computer-based test. It used four-option objective questions, with 130 regular questions across Physics, Chemistry, English Proficiency, Logical Reasoning, and Mathematics or Biology. Candidates could move among sections and revise answers during the test.

The 2026 marking scheme awarded three marks for each correct response, deducted one mark for each incorrect response, and gave no marks for an unattempted question. A candidate who answered all 130 regular questions without skipping any could choose to attempt 12 extra questions if time remained.

The test is delivered in English. BITS Pilani states that different candidates receive questions selected from a large question bank and that question sets are designed to be comparable in difficulty and content.
bullets: Physics: 30 questions; Chemistry: 30 questions.
English Proficiency: 10 questions; Logical Reasoning: 20 questions.
Mathematics or Biology: 40 questions. Biology is available for the eligible B.Pharm., B.E. Environmental and Sustainability Engineering and M.Sc. Biological Sciences routes under the 2026 rules.
A calculator, mobile phone and other unauthorized electronic material are prohibited; the brochure states that a scratch pad is supplied at the test centre.

sections.heading: Application and admission workflow
paragraphs: The process has two distinct stages: register and apply to write BITSAT, then—if seeking admission—submit the separate BITS admission application with Class 12 marks and ordered programme preferences. The second step is essential; a BITSAT score by itself is not a completed seat application.

For the 2026 cycle, BITS Pilani offered Session 1 and Session 2, permitted an eligible candidate to take the test up to twice, and used the higher of the two scores for admission. Applicants selected test-city preferences, received a city allotment, booked a date and slot when available, and downloaded a hall ticket.

Dates, application charges, operating test cities, available programmes and preference-form deadlines are cycle-specific. The 2026 brochure labelled several schedule items tentative and directed candidates to the official admissions site for changes; future applicants should rely on the next cycle’s brochure and live notices rather than reuse 2026 dates or fees.
bullets: Register online through BITS Pilani’s official admissions process and complete the BITSAT application and payment.
Use the published edit window, if applicable, to correct permitted fields; the 2026 rules excluded some fields, including test-city preference, from later changes.
Book the test slot if the cycle requires booking, download the hall ticket, and appear at the allotted centre.
After the test, submit Class 12 marks, documents and programme/campus preferences through the First Degree admission form, then follow iteration, offer-acceptance and fee-payment notices.

sections.heading: Preparation approach grounded in the official syllabus
paragraphs: Start with the official BITSAT syllabus and build Class 11–12 command in the tested science and mathematics/biology subjects. BITS Pilani explicitly directs candidates to the detailed syllabus in its brochure and says that candidates may refer to NCERT textbooks for the content.

Preparation should also include English Proficiency and Logical Reasoning rather than treating BITSAT as only a PCM examination. The published syllabus includes grammar, vocabulary, reading comprehension and composition-related skills in English, plus verbal and non-verbal reasoning topics.

Because the 2026 paper required 130 questions in three hours and used negative marking, timed computer-based practice and disciplined question selection are practical priorities. Candidates should use full-length practice to learn pacing, review weaker syllabus areas after each attempt, and avoid blind guessing when the expected benefit is poor under the +3/−1 scheme.
bullets: Study from the official topic list first; use NCERT-aligned revision to cover the stated content base.
Practise with a keyboard and mouse before test day: BITS Pilani says basic computer familiarity is assumed.
Include mixed-section, three-hour mock sessions so that Physics, Chemistry, English, reasoning and Mathematics/Biology pacing is rehearsed together.
Review accuracy as well as attempt count, since wrong answers carry a one-mark penalty in the published 2026 scheme.

sections.heading: Programmes and what the score leads to
paragraphs: A qualifying BITSAT score is used in a merit-based admission process for BITS Pilani’s First Degree programmes at its Indian Pilani, Goa and Hyderabad campuses. The precise programme list varies by campus and cycle, but the 2026 brochure lists B.E. programmes, B.Pharm. at Pilani and Hyderabad, and integrated M.Sc. options including Biological Sciences, Chemistry, Economics, Mathematics, Physics, and Semiconductor and Nanoscience.

Students entering an integrated M.Sc. programme may apply for a dual degree in engineering after their first year; the 2026 brochure says this is competitive and based on performance at BITS. It is not an automatic engineering-seat guarantee. For M.Sc. Biological Sciences entrants with PCB input, the published options are restricted to B.E. Environmental and Sustainability Engineering and B.Pharm.

Published cut-offs are historical outcomes rather than guaranteed future targets. For context, BITS Pilani’s official page reports final programme- and campus-specific BITSAT cut-offs for the 2025–26 admission year on a 390-mark scale; selection thresholds can change with programme, campus, applicant performance and seat availability.
bullets: Main immediate academic outcomes: B.E. (the official BITS designation corresponding broadly to the engineering pathway), B.Pharm. and four-year integrated M.Sc. programmes.
Admission rankings are prepared from BITSAT scores for applicants who also meet the Class 12 eligibility requirements and submit the prescribed admission application.
Applicants should use official historical cut-offs only to understand past competition, not as a promise of an admission score for a later cycle.

title: CA Final
description: CA Final — professional exam (finance), conducted by ICAI.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: The CA Final examination is conducted by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) as the Final Course examination under ICAI’s New Scheme of Education and Training.

quick_facts.label: Current exam frequency
quick_facts.value: As of the 2026 change effective from the May 2026 examination, ICAI conducts CA Final twice yearly, in May and November. This superseded the earlier January/May/September schedule.

quick_facts.label: Papers and groups
quick_facts.value: CA Final has six 100-mark papers across two groups: Group I—Financial Reporting, Advanced Financial Management, and Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics; Group II—Direct Tax Laws & International Taxation, Indirect Tax Laws, and Integrated Business Solutions.

quick_facts.label: Examination eligibility
quick_facts.value: Under the current FAQ guidance, a student must be registered for Final, have completed practical training six months before the first day of the examination month, have completed Advanced ICITSS, and have qualified all four Self-Paced Online Modules (SPOM) to appear.

quick_facts.label: Assessment and pass rule
quick_facts.value: All six papers use 30% case-scenario/case-study MCQs and 70% descriptive questions; Paper 6 is an open-book, entirely case-study-based paper, while the other five are closed book. A candidate ordinarily needs at least 40% in each paper and 50% aggregate in each group, or 50% aggregate across both groups when appearing together.

quick_facts.label: Indicative Final registration fee
quick_facts.value: ICAI’s student FAQ states a ₹22,000 registration fee for both groups of the Final Course. This is dated fee guidance (FAQ last updated September 27, 2024) and applicants should verify the current amount in ICAI’s registration materials before payment.

sections.heading: What CA Final is for
paragraphs: CA Final is the final examination stage in ICAI’s Chartered Accountancy education pathway. ICAI’s New Scheme retains the three-tier Foundation–Intermediate–Final structure, with Final comprising six examination papers and four SPOM sets. Passing Final is a key requirement on the route to becoming an ICAI member; practical training and the Institute’s membership process remain separate requirements.
source_urls
bullets: It tests advanced financial reporting, finance, audit and professional ethics, direct and indirect tax, and multidisciplinary business problem-solving.
The New Scheme also requires SPOMs in corporate and economic laws, strategic cost and performance management, one elective, and one multidisciplinary subject.

sections.heading: Who can take CA Final
paragraphs: Students may register for the Final Course after passing both groups of the Intermediate Examination. For examination admission under ICAI’s New Scheme, ICAI’s FAQ specifies Final registration, completion of practical training six months before the first day of the examination month, successful completion of Advanced ICITSS, and qualification in all four SPOMs. Requirements can differ for transitional/earlier-scheme candidates, so candidates should use the session-specific ICAI notice and their own scheme status.
source_urls
bullets: Final Course registration follows passing both Intermediate groups.
Advanced ICITSS must be completed after practical training and before appearing in Final, according to ICAI’s FAQ guidance.
SPOM comprises Sets A, B, C, and D; Sets A and B are mandatory, while the student selects one paper each from Sets C and D.

sections.heading: Exam structure and scoring
paragraphs: The current Final syllabus has two groups of three papers each. Each listed paper carries 100 marks. ICAI states that all six papers contain 30% case-scenario/case-study MCQs and 70% descriptive questions, with no negative marking for the MCQ component. Paper 6, Integrated Business Solutions, is fully case-study based and assessed as an open-book examination; the other five papers are closed book.
source_urls
bullets: Group I: Financial Reporting; Advanced Financial Management; Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics.
Group II: Direct Tax Laws & International Taxation; Indirect Tax Laws; Integrated Business Solutions (Multidisciplinary Case Study with Strategic Management).

Candidates may take one group or both together. Ordinarily, passing a group requires at least 40% in every paper and 50% aggregate in that group; the regulations also allow a both-groups aggregate route when both groups are taken together.

sections.heading: Registration and examination application
paragraphs: The process has two distinct stages: register in ICAI’s Final Course after passing both Intermediate groups, then apply for a particular examination session once all applicable eligibility conditions are met. Final registration also registers the student for SPOM. Because application windows, examination dates, centres, fees, and document instructions are session-specific and can change, candidates should rely on the current ICAI Examination announcements rather than a past deadline.
source_urls
bullets: Register for the Final Course and order/use the applicable ICAI study material.
Complete practical training, Advanced ICITSS, and all four SPOM qualifications by ICAI’s applicable eligibility cut-offs.
Monitor ICAI’s Examination Students page for the current May or November Final examination form and instructions.

sections.heading: Preparation using ICAI materials
paragraphs: Use ICAI’s official Final Course study material as the primary syllabus reference and check the material, statutory updates, corrigenda, model test papers, and applicable pronouncements for the intended attempt. This matters particularly in tax and law papers, where ICAI publishes attempt-specific updates. ICAI also provides digital SPOM learning and has offered official live/revision learning resources through its Board of Studies.
source_urls
bullets: Plan paper-wise preparation around the six-paper syllabus and practise the required mix of case-based MCQs and descriptive answers.
Prepare Paper 6 with case-study and open-book exam practice rather than treating it like a conventional closed-book theory paper.
Complete SPOM learning and assessments early enough to avoid an eligibility bottleneck.

sections.heading: What passing leads to
paragraphs: A candidate passes CA Final by passing both groups under ICAI’s prescribed marks rules. Passing Final is not by itself the same as ICAI membership: the Chartered Accountancy pathway also requires completion of prescribed practical training and enrolment as an ICAI member. ICAI publishes results and marks through its examination systems after each session; pass rates vary substantially by attempt and should be treated as historical context, not a forecast.
source_urls
bullets: The January 2026 Final result illustrates variability: ICAI reported pass rates of 21.03% in Group I, 9.76% in Group II, and 10.97% for candidates appearing in both groups.
After meeting all professional requirements, eligible candidates can pursue ICAI membership and use the Chartered Accountant designation in accordance with ICAI rules.

title: CA Foundation
description: CA Foundation — professional exam (finance), conducted by ICAI.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), a statutory body set up by an Act of Parliament, conducts CA Foundation as part of the Chartered Accountancy course.

quick_facts.label: Role in the CA pathway
quick_facts.value: CA Foundation is the entry-level examination and gateway to the Chartered Accountancy profession under ICAI’s three-level education and training scheme: Foundation, Intermediate and Final.

quick_facts.label: Examination frequency
quick_facts.value: Foundation examinations are held three times a year, in January, May and September.

quick_facts.label: Eligibility baseline
quick_facts.value: A student may register for the Foundation Course after passing Class 10. To sit the Foundation examination, the student must have registered for the required minimum period and have appeared in the Class 12/Senior Secondary examination or an accepted equivalent.

quick_facts.label: Papers and marks
quick_facts.value: The exam has four 100-mark papers—Accounting, Business Laws, Quantitative Aptitude, and Business Economics—for a total of 400 marks.

quick_facts.label: Passing standard
quick_facts.value: To pass in one sitting, a candidate needs at least 40% in each paper and at least 50% aggregate across all four papers.

quick_facts.label: September 2026 application context
quick_facts.value: For the September 2026 Foundation examination, ICAI scheduled online applications from 6 July 2026; the deadline was 19 July 2026 without late fee and 22 July 2026 with late fee. These session-specific dates should be checked against ICAI’s latest notice before applying.

quick_facts.label: Fees—dated context
quick_facts.value: For September 2026, the Foundation Course registration fee is listed as ₹9,000, inclusive of the prospectus and Foundation study material; the India-centre examination fee is ₹1,500. Fees can change by ICAI decision and examination session.

sections.heading: What CA Foundation is for
paragraphs: CA Foundation is ICAI’s entry-level professional examination for students beginning the Chartered Accountancy route. It tests foundational knowledge in accounting, business law, quantitative aptitude and business economics before a student progresses to ICAI’s Intermediate level. It is a professional-qualification examination, not a replacement for an undergraduate degree such as B.Com or BBA; students may pursue those degrees separately alongside the CA pathway.
source_urls
bullets: ICAI’s New Scheme comprises Foundation, Intermediate and Final levels, with self-paced online modules included in the broader CA structure.
Candidates who pass Foundation and Class 12 are eligible to register for Intermediate through the Foundation route.

sections.heading: Eligibility and timing
paragraphs: Students can register for the Foundation Course after passing Class 10. ICAI requires a minimum four-month registration period ending on or before the first day of the examination month, and candidates must have appeared in the Class 12/Senior Secondary examination conducted by a legally constituted examining body or a recognised equivalent.

For the September 2026 sitting specifically, ICAI required Foundation registration on or before 1 May 2026. Applicants who had appeared in Class 12 could apply provisionally, but had to upload their Class 12 admit card or marksheet in the Self Service Portal (SSP) by 10 August 2026 for an admit card to be issued.
source_urls
bullets: A recognised Class 12 equivalent can meet the academic-examination condition.
Foundation registration is ordinarily valid for four years from the first eligible Foundation attempt; ICAI’s FAQ states that revalidation is not permitted at Foundation level.

Certain graduates/postgraduates and candidates who have passed the intermediate examination of ICMAI or ICSI may be exempt from passing Foundation and may use ICAI’s Direct Entry route to Intermediate, subject to ICAI’s stated criteria.

sections.heading: Exam structure, marking and medium
paragraphs: CA Foundation is a 400-mark, four-paper descriptive-cum-objective examination. Papers 1 and 2 are subjective/descriptive, while Papers 3 and 4 are objective. ICAI applies negative marking of 0.25 mark for each wrong answer in the objective papers.

The four papers are Accounting; Business Laws; Quantitative Aptitude, covering Business Mathematics, Logical Reasoning and Statistics; and Business Economics. ICAI permits candidates to choose English or Hindi medium when submitting the examination form, although it specifies particular bilingual and OMR arrangements for some papers.
source_urls
bullets: Paper 1: Accounting — 100 marks.
Paper 2: Business Laws — 100 marks.
Paper 3: Quantitative Aptitude — 100 marks.
Paper 4: Business Economics — 100 marks.
Pass requirement: at least 40% in every paper and 50% aggregate in the same sitting.
No paper-wise exemption is available at Foundation level.

sections.heading: How to register and apply
paragraphs: First, create or access an ICAI Self Service Portal account and register for the Foundation Course with the Board of Studies. After the required study period and Class 12 condition are met, submit a separate online examination application through SSP for the intended session; course registration alone does not enter a student for the examination.

ICAI’s September 2026 guidance states that applicants should verify their course-registration status, uploaded photograph and signature, Class 12 documentation, selected examination centre and medium before making online payment. After successful payment, retain the generated bar-coded examination-form PDF. ICAI states that a hard copy does not need to be sent to the Examination Department.
source_urls
bullets: For September 2026, ICAI opened the exam form on 6 July 2026, set 19 July 2026 as the no-late-fee deadline, and allowed submissions with late fee through 22 July 2026.
For that session, ICAI scheduled a correction window from 23 to 25 July 2026; centre and medium changes were not entertained after the correction window closed.
For September 2026, the India-centre exam fee was ₹1,500; Kathmandu was ₹2,200; Bahrain and Dubai were US$325. These are session-specific charges, so applicants should consult the current fee notice.

sections.heading: Preparation using ICAI resources
paragraphs: Start with ICAI’s prescribed Foundation study material and syllabus, then plan study across all four papers because the pass rule requires both a paper-wise minimum and an aggregate minimum. For the objective papers, include timed MCQ practice and account for the 0.25-mark penalty for wrong answers; for Accounting and Business Laws, practise descriptive answers under examination timing.

ICAI’s Board of Studies publishes Foundation study material, mock-test information and academic-support announcements. For the September 2026 session, ICAI announced mock-test-paper series and ‘Success at CA Exam’ sessions for Foundation candidates; these official resources are useful supplements to the prescribed material rather than substitutes for it.
source_urls
bullets: Use the latest ICAI material and session-specific applicability announcements, particularly where business-law provisions or other examinable content may be updated.
Practise the full four-paper sequence and preserve time for revision before the scheduled session.
Use official mock tests and Board of Studies classes where available; availability and schedules vary by session.

sections.heading: What happens after CA Foundation
paragraphs: Passing CA Foundation, together with passing Class 12 or its recognised equivalent, enables registration for ICAI’s Intermediate Course through the Foundation route. It is the first professional milestone in the CA pathway, rather than a qualification that by itself confers Chartered Accountant status.

As a dated indication of examination outcomes, ICAI reported that 18,124 of 90,217 candidates who appeared in the May 2026 Foundation examination passed, a pass percentage of 20.09%. This result is historical session data, not a prediction of difficulty or pass rates for later sessions.
source_urls
bullets: Next CA step: register for ICAI Intermediate through the Foundation route after satisfying the stated Foundation and Class 12 conditions.
B.Com, BBA and integrated law-commerce degrees can be pursued as separate academic programmes; admission rules are set by the relevant university or institution, not by CA Foundation alone.

title: CA Intermediate
description: CA Intermediate — professional exam (finance), conducted by ICAI.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: CA Intermediate is administered by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), the statutory body established under the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 and supervised administratively by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

quick_facts.label: Place in the CA pathway
quick_facts.value: Intermediate is the first stage of the CA course’s theoretical education, positioned after Foundation or eligible direct entry and before CA Final.

quick_facts.label: Entry routes
quick_facts.value: Candidates may enter after passing CA Foundation, or through Direct Entry when they meet ICAI’s prescribed graduate/postgraduate or ICSI/ICMAI Intermediate-level eligibility conditions.

quick_facts.label: Current paper structure
quick_facts.value: Under ICAI’s New Scheme, CA Intermediate has six 100-mark papers in two groups: Group I covers Advanced Accounting, Corporate and Other Laws, and Taxation; Group II covers Cost and Management Accounting, Auditing and Ethics, and Financial Management and Strategic Management.

quick_facts.label: Exam frequency
quick_facts.value: ICAI announced that Intermediate examinations are held three times yearly—May/June, September, and January. Exact timetables, eligibility cut-offs, examination-form windows, and fees are cycle-specific and should be checked in the current ICAI announcement.

quick_facts.label: Passing standard
quick_facts.value: For a group, ICAI states that a candidate needs at least 40% in every paper and 50% aggregate in that group; the examination FAQ also describes the conditions for passing both groups together.

sections.heading: Purpose and role in the CA pathway
paragraphs: CA Intermediate develops the working knowledge of core and allied accountancy subjects that precedes the advanced application focus of CA Final. ICAI frames the CA curriculum as a combination of theoretical education, professional ethics and practical training, so Intermediate is an academic gateway rather than a licence to practise as a Chartered Accountant.

Passing both Intermediate groups is a key progression point: ICAI’s course FAQ states that a student may register for CA Final after passing both groups. The full CA qualification additionally requires the later components of the CA pathway, including practical training, CA Final and membership requirements.
bullets: The syllabus spans financial accounting, company and other laws, direct and indirect taxation, costing, audit and ethics, financial management, and strategic management.
It is relevant preparation for supervised accounting, audit, tax and finance work, but passing Intermediate alone does not make a person an ICAI member or Chartered Accountant.

sections.heading: Eligibility and routes of entry
paragraphs: The Foundation route requires a candidate to pass the CA Foundation examination and register for Intermediate. ICAI’s published eligibility material specifies an eight-month study course before the first Intermediate examination for Foundation-route candidates.

The Direct Entry route is available to commerce graduates or postgraduates with at least 55% aggregate marks and specified commerce-related paper coverage, and to non-commerce graduates or postgraduates with at least 60% aggregate marks. ICAI also recognises candidates who have passed the Intermediate-level examination of the Institute of Cost Accountants of India or the Institute of Company Secretaries of India for Direct Entry. Final-year graduation students may provisionally register, subject to ICAI’s conditions for later confirmation.
bullets: Registration is for both Intermediate groups, even though a student may choose to sit one group at a time.
Eligibility and transitional provisions can differ for students converting from earlier ICAI schemes; such candidates should use ICAI’s current examination and SSP guidance.

sections.heading: Examination format and assessment
paragraphs: The New Scheme divides the examination into two groups of three papers. Group I comprises Advanced Accounting; Corporate and Other Laws; and Taxation, split between Income-tax Law and Goods and Services Tax. Group II comprises Cost and Management Accounting; Auditing and Ethics; and Financial Management and Strategic Management, with the last paper split between Financial Management and Strategic Management.

Each paper is worth 100 marks. ICAI permits candidates to appear group-wise or for both groups, while registration remains for both groups. The published pass rule is 40% in each paper plus a 50% aggregate in the relevant group; candidates appearing for both groups may also meet the alternative combined-aggregate condition described by ICAI.
bullets: Group I: Papers 1–3 — Advanced Accounting; Corporate and Other Laws; Taxation.
Group II: Papers 4–6 — Cost and Management Accounting; Auditing and Ethics; Financial Management and Strategic Management.
Refer to the examination-cycle-specific ICAI material for applicable statutory updates, study guidelines, question-paper pattern and any transitional unit scheme.

sections.heading: Registration and examination application
paragraphs: First, select the appropriate entry route and register for the Intermediate Course through ICAI’s Self Service Portal (SSP). ICAI’s guidance distinguishes course registration from an application to sit a particular examination; after registration, students must also submit the examination form and pay the applicable examination fee during the window announced for their intended attempt.

After successful registration, ICAI provides credentials for ordering study material through its Centralized Distribution System portal. Candidates should track ICAI notices for the applicable exam-form dates, centre options, deadlines, late-fee rules, eligibility cut-off and examination fee because these are revised by examination cycle.
bullets: Register for both groups on SSP, even if planning to appear group-wise.
Complete the required study period before the first eligible attempt.
Use only the current ICAI examination announcement and SSP for a specific attempt’s deadline or fee.

sections.heading: Preparation using ICAI resources
paragraphs: Begin with ICAI’s current Board of Studies study material and the applicable revision test papers, mock tests, revision materials and study guidelines. This is particularly important for law and tax papers, where ICAI may prescribe statutory updates, inclusions and exclusions for a named examination cycle.

ICAI also provides live virtual classes for Intermediate students. Its 2026 programme lists classes across all six papers and offers interactive doubt resolution, notes, assignments, MCQs, examination-preparation guidance and access to recorded lectures. These resources can support a structured plan of syllabus coverage, question practice and revision, but students should verify that the material is marked applicable to their specific attempt.
bullets: Map preparation to the six-paper, two-group structure and practise both objective/application-oriented and written problem-solving work as prescribed by ICAI materials.
Use current RTPs, mock tests and model test papers after completing each subject’s base study material.
For Taxation and Corporate and Other Laws, cross-check the attempt-specific statutory update and study guidelines before final revision.

sections.heading: What passing CA Intermediate leads to
paragraphs: Passing both CA Intermediate groups enables registration for the CA Final Course under ICAI’s stated progression rules. It also marks completion of the Intermediate academic stage in the CA route, whose subsequent requirements include practical training and Final-level assessment before a candidate can seek ICAI membership.

Practical training is intended to complement the theoretical curriculum by building on-the-job professional experience and the ability to apply knowledge in real situations. ICAI’s current training administration includes a mandatory E-Diary for students commencing practical training from 1 January 2026, which records attendance and tasks performed. The availability, title and pay of roles such as accounts executive, audit assistant or tax associate depend on employers and are not guaranteed by Intermediate examination results.
bullets: Progression: pass both Intermediate groups → register for CA Final and complete the remaining ICAI training and examination requirements.
Professional exposure: practical training supports work involving audit, taxation, accounting, compliance and related finance functions.
Membership and the right to describe oneself as a Chartered Accountant arise only after completing ICAI’s full qualification and membership process.

title: CAT
description: CAT — pg entrance exam (management), conducted by IIMs (rotating).

quick_facts.label: What CAT is
quick_facts.value: CAT (Common Admission Test) is a computer-based management entrance test conducted by the Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs). It is used as a prerequisite for specified postgraduate management and fellow/doctoral programmes at IIMs; listed non-IIM institutions may also use CAT scores.

quick_facts.label: Conducting arrangement
quick_facts.value: CAT is nationally administered by the IIMs. The convening IIM changes on a rotational basis; IIM Ahmedabad describes the rotation as once every six years.

quick_facts.label: Baseline eligibility (CAT 2025 reference)
quick_facts.value: The CAT 2025 bulletin required a bachelor’s degree/equivalent with at least 50% marks or equivalent CGPA for General, EWS and NC-OBC candidates, and 45% for SC, ST and PwD candidates. Final-year students and candidates awaiting results could apply subject to later documentary requirements.

quick_facts.label: Test areas (CAT 2025 reference)
quick_facts.value: CAT 2025 used three sections: Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension (VARC), Data Interpretation and Logical Reasoning (DILR), and Quantitative Ability (QA). Test structure can change by cycle, so applicants should rely on the current official bulletin.

quick_facts.label: Admission is not automatic
quick_facts.value: A CAT score is an important input, but each IIM sets its own eligibility rules, cut-offs, weights and selection process; institutes may also consider prior academics, work experience and other inputs.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
paragraphs: CAT is the principal common entrance examination route for many IIM postgraduate management programmes and fellow/doctoral programmes. The CAT 2025 official bulletin listed programmes such as PGP/MBA variants across the IIM system, while also allowing listed non-IIM member institutions to use CAT scores.

A CAT score alone does not constitute an admission offer. The receiving institute controls programme eligibility, shortlisting, interviews and final selection. For example, IIM Ahmedabad’s domestic MBA process for its 2026–28 batch used a valid CAT 2025 score for shortlisting, followed by an Analytical Writing Test (AWT) and Personal Interview (PI) for shortlisted applicants.
bullets: Use CAT to establish eligibility for participating programmes, then apply and satisfy the separate rules of every target institute.
Confirm whether a non-IIM school accepts the relevant CAT cycle; IIMs state that they do not run the selection processes of non-IIM institutions.

sections.heading: Who can take CAT
paragraphs: The CAT 2025 baseline rule was a recognised bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification with at least 50% marks/equivalent CGPA for General, EWS and NC-OBC candidates, or 45% for SC, ST and PwD candidates. The bulletin also recognised certain completed professional qualifications—CA, CS, ICWA/CMA and Fellow of the Institute of Actuaries of India—subject to the required percentage.

Final-year bachelor’s students and candidates who had completed degree requirements but were awaiting results could apply in CAT 2025. If selected, they had to meet the respective IIM’s documentary and completion requirements. Meeting CAT’s minimum eligibility did not guarantee an IIM shortlist.
bullets: Use the university’s prescribed CGPA-to-percentage conversion where available; CAT 2025 specified a fallback calculation where no conversion scheme existed.
Check programme-specific rules in addition to CAT eligibility: an IIM or a particular MBA/PGP programme can apply additional academic, category, work-experience or other requirements.

sections.heading: Test format
paragraphs: CAT 2025 was a computer-based examination conducted in three sessions on one test day. Its three assessed areas were VARC, DILR and QA. These details are useful as the latest fully published official-cycle reference available in the cited material, not as a promise of the next cycle’s exact pattern.

Candidates should treat the current CAT information bulletin, official mock/test instructions and admit-card notices as controlling for the number of questions, time limits, accessibility arrangements, session timing, permitted items and test-centre procedures for their own cycle.
bullets: Prepare for all three areas; individual IIM selection policies can require sectional as well as overall CAT performance.

CAT percentile expectations are institute- and programme-specific. For example, IIM Ahmedabad published separate overall and sectional preliminary thresholds for its CAT 2025-based MBA selection process.

sections.heading: Application process and cycle timing
paragraphs: Apply only through the official CAT portal when registration for the relevant cycle is open, using a unique email address and mobile number that remain available throughout the selection process. The official CAT material warns applicants to verify that they are using the official website.

CAT 2025 is historical reference only: registration opened on August 1, 2025, the advertised closing date was later extended to September 20, 2025, the test was held on November 30, 2025, and results were published on December 24, 2025. Its registration fee was ₹1,300 for SC/ST/PwD candidates and ₹2,600 for other candidates. Dates, fees, test cities, documents and payment rules are variable by cycle and must be checked in the new official notice before applying.
bullets: Complete the CAT registration accurately, including category and academic information; CAT 2025 did not permit category changes after registration.
In the CAT 2025 process, applicants selected up to five test-city preferences and received a city/centre subject to availability.
After CAT, follow each chosen institute’s application and admission instructions separately; some institutes require additional forms or steps.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Build preparation around VARC, DILR and QA, and practise working across all three rather than relying on a single strong area. This follows from CAT’s three-section structure and from institute policies that can apply sectional as well as overall CAT thresholds.

Plan beyond the test score. Keep academic records and applicable category documentation ready, research each target programme’s selection policy early, and prepare for post-CAT assessment components where required. At IIM Ahmedabad, for example, shortlisting and final selection for the CAT 2025-based MBA process used CAT performance alongside academic records, AWT/PI performance, and other achievements and work experience.
bullets: Use official CAT notices and any official practice/test instructions for the applicable cycle as the primary source for rules and interface expectations.

Create a target-institute list before results: compare programme eligibility, sectional requirements, application steps and interview/assessment methods rather than assuming one percentile ensures admission everywhere.

sections.heading: What a CAT score can lead to
paragraphs: A valid CAT score can support applications to a range of IIM management programmes and, where a school is listed for the relevant cycle, to participating non-IIM institutions. Programme names and availability vary across institutes and admission years.

For IIM admissions, the outcome is normally a multi-stage decision rather than a score-only allocation. The CAT 2025 bulletin states that IIMs independently determine their own relative weights and may use prior academic performance, relevant work experience and similar inputs. IIM Ahmedabad’s MBA process additionally used AWT and PI after shortlisting; its graduates receive the Master of Business Administration degree.
bullets: Possible downstream study paths include MBA/PGP and specialised management programmes; research-oriented routes such as FPM/PhD may also accept CAT subject to their own policies.
Do not treat one institute’s published cut-off or selection formula as universal: it is dated, programme-specific and subject to change.

useful_links.label: IIM Ahmedabad MBA admissions and CAT-linked selection policy

title: CEED
description: CEED — pg entrance exam (design), conducted by IIT Bombay.

quick_facts.label: Full name and conducting body
quick_facts.value: Common Entrance Examination for Design (CEED), conducted by the UCEED-CEED Office at IIT Bombay.

quick_facts.label: Purpose
quick_facts.value: CEED is a qualifying design-aptitude examination used for applications to M.Des programmes at specified institutes and to Ph.D. programmes at several IITs and design schools; a CEED qualification alone does not secure admission.

quick_facts.label: Baseline examination eligibility (CEED 2026 cycle)
quick_facts.value: Applicants needed a minimum three-year graduate degree, diploma, or postgraduate programme after 10+2; final-year candidates due by July 2026 and holders of the GD Arts diploma after 10+5 were also eligible. There was no age limit or attempt limit for CEED 2026.

quick_facts.label: 2026 exam structure
quick_facts.value: The 2026 paper had Part A (one-hour, computer-based NAT, MSQ and MCQ questions; 150 marks) and Part B (two hours, five drawing/design/writing questions answered in an invigilator-provided booklet; 100 marks). The final score used 25% of Part A and 75% of Part B.

quick_facts.label: Score validity
quick_facts.value: The CEED 2026 score card is valid for one year from the result-declaration date. For that cycle, results were declared on March 4, 2026 and score-card download is available through July 31, 2026.

sections.heading: What CEED is for
paragraphs: CEED assesses aptitude for design, including visual perception, drawing, logical reasoning, creativity, communication and problem-solving. It is an entrance/qualifying examination rather than an admission offer: candidates who qualify must separately apply to each institute and satisfy that institute’s programme-specific eligibility and selection process.

For the 2026 cycle, IIT Bombay identified M.Des routes at IISc Bengaluru, IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, IIT Guwahati, IIT Hyderabad, IIT Jodhpur, IIT Kanpur, IIT Roorkee, IIITDM Jabalpur and IIITDM Kancheepuram, alongside Ph.D. opportunities at several IITs and design schools. The official site also distinguishes participating institutes from result-sharing institutes, so applicants should confirm whether their target programme accepts CEED in the relevant admission year.
bullets: Treat CEED as one component of postgraduate design admissions, not as a common counselling/allotment process.
Check the target institute’s own eligibility, application deadline, test/interview requirements, fees and scholarship rules before applying; these can differ from CEED examination eligibility.

sections.heading: Who can take CEED
paragraphs: For CEED 2026, a candidate needed to have completed—or be due to complete by July 2026—a graduate degree, diploma or postgraduate degree programme of at least three years’ duration after the 10+2 level. Candidates who had completed the GD Arts diploma programme after 10+5 by July 2026 were also eligible. IIT Bombay stated that CEED 2026 had neither an age limit nor a limit on the number of attempts.

This is only the eligibility to sit CEED. Admission requirements at individual M.Des and Ph.D. programmes may be narrower or otherwise different, and institutes verify documents, category status and programme eligibility during their own admission process.
bullets: Applicants from design and non-design academic backgrounds may meet the examination-level qualification rule if their credential meets the stated duration requirement.
Final-year applicants should check both the CEED cycle’s completion deadline and the target programme’s separate completion/document rules.

sections.heading: Exam format and evaluation
paragraphs: In the 2026 format, CEED ran for three hours in two compulsory parts. Part A was a one-hour computer-based test comprising Numerical Answer Type (NAT), Multiple Select Question (MSQ) and Multiple Choice Question (MCQ) items. It assessed areas such as visualization and spatial reasoning, practical/scientific knowledge, observation and design sensitivity, environment and society, analytical reasoning, English comprehension, creativity, art/design knowledge, and design methods and practices.

Part B lasted two hours. Questions appeared on a computer screen, but candidates wrote/drew their responses in the answer booklet supplied at the centre. Its five questions covered sketching, creativity, form sensitivity, visual sensitivity and problem identification. Part-A performance was used to shortlist answer books for Part-B evaluation; the final score weighted Part A at 25% and Part B at 75%.
bullets: Part B is subjective and is evaluated holistically against criteria in the questions; no model solution is provided for it.
The 2026 rules provided no re-evaluation or re-totaling of either part.
The exact paper structure and rules can change by cycle; use the current year’s official brochure rather than relying on the 2026 pattern alone.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: For CEED 2026, registration was online only through the official CEED website/application portal. The application required a recent colour photograph, signature, and academic-status evidence such as a degree/diploma certificate, final-year marks/provisional certificate, or an institutional certificate for candidates whose programme was unfinished. Applicants claiming EWS, SC, ST or OBC-NCL status also had to upload the applicable valid certificate; PwD applicants had additional document requirements where relevant.

Fees and dates are cycle-specific. In the 2026 brochure, the regular registration fee was ₹2,000 for women and SC/ST/PwD candidates and ₹4,000 for other candidates, plus applicable banking/service charges; the fee was non-refundable and non-transferable. Those figures and the 2025 registration dates should be treated as past-cycle context, not as a quote for a future CEED cycle.
bullets: Read the current official information brochure before submitting the form, then retain the confirmation and download the admit card when released.

If applying with a disability accommodation request, use the current cycle’s prescribed forms and submit the request with the application. For 2026, a scribe could be available for Part A but not Part B.
After the result, submit separate applications to each desired M.Des or Ph.D. programme; CEED does not itself complete programme admission.

sections.heading: Preparation priorities
paragraphs: IIT Bombay characterises CEED as an aptitude test and does not recommend a specific textbook or guide. Its official advice is to practise drawing, rendering and visualization skills and to use previous CEED question papers available from the official website.

A practical preparation plan should map practice to both modes of the paper: timed computer-based work for Part A’s objective design-aptitude questions, plus timed hand-drawn and written responses for Part B. For Part B, practise clear visual communication, proportion, perspective, composition, shading, user/context understanding and generating varied solutions—not only polished rendering.
bullets: Use official past papers and answer keys to become familiar with question styles and time pressure.

Practise the listed syllabus areas: spatial visualization, observation, logical reasoning, design awareness, materials/processes and ergonomics for Part A; drawing, creativity, communication and problem identification for Part B.

Verify current exam-day materials and prohibited-item rules in the current brochure. In 2026, candidates brought their own drawing materials, while sheets were supplied and electronic devices were prohibited.

sections.heading: What happens after CEED
paragraphs: A CEED result enables a candidate to apply to relevant M.Des and Ph.D. programmes, but it is not a seat allocation or guaranteed admission. Admitting institutes may conduct their own tests and/or interviews and independently verify academic eligibility, category certificates and other documents.

For CEED 2026, all successful test-takers could view Part-A marks, while Part-B marks and ranks were provided only to candidates shortlisted from Part A. The CEED 2026 score card remains valid for one year from the March 4, 2026 result declaration. As of the review date, the official site lists July 31, 2026 as the final date to download the 2026 score card.
bullets: Apply directly to each target institute after qualifying, and track that institute’s separate admissions notice.
Use the result within its one-year validity period; a score card is not proof of date of birth, category or disability status.
Keep a local copy of the score card before the official download window closes.

useful_links.label: CEED 2026 official website, announcements, programmes and previous papers

title: CFA Program (Levels I–III)
description: CFA Program (Levels I–III) — professional exam (finance), conducted by CFA Institute.

quick_facts.label: Provider and structure
quick_facts.value: The CFA Program is administered by CFA Institute and comprises three sequential exams: Level I, Level II, and Level III.

quick_facts.label: Level I entry routes
quick_facts.value: For Level I registration, a candidate must have a completed bachelor’s degree, be an undergraduate within 23 months of graduation, or meet CFA Institute’s combined higher-education/professional-work-experience route; an international travel passport is also required.

quick_facts.label: Exam delivery and sequence
quick_facts.value: Exams are computer-based. Candidates must pass Level I before Level II and Level II before Level III; CFA Institute permits no more than two attempts in a calendar year, not in consecutive windows or within six months, with a maximum of six attempts per level.

quick_facts.label: Study expectation
quick_facts.value: CFA Institute states that successful candidates report spending more than 300 hours preparing for each exam level; this is an indicative preparation benchmark, not a guarantee of success.

quick_facts.label: 2026 fee context
quick_facts.value: For exams from 2026, CFA Institute lists total registration fees across all three levels at USD 3,520–4,600 depending on early versus standard registration; local taxes may be added and individual exam-window prices and deadlines vary.

quick_facts.label: What is required for the charter
quick_facts.value: Passing all three exams alone does not award the CFA designation. The candidate must also complete required Practical Skills Modules, obtain at least 4,000 hours of qualifying experience over at least 36 months, and become a CFA Institute Charterholder member.

sections.heading: Purpose and place in a finance career
paragraphs: The CFA Program is a professional investment credential pathway rather than an Indian university degree. CFA Institute describes its three progressively more complex levels as building knowledge and skills for investment analysis and portfolio management. It is therefore commonly relevant to learners moving from commerce, economics, finance, or management education toward analytical investment roles, but enrolment and examination success do not themselves guarantee a particular job or salary.

The curriculum covers foundational and advanced investment topics, with Level I focused on learning and describing concepts, Level II on analyzing and evaluating vignette-based situations, and Level III on integrating and applying concepts in portfolio-management-oriented scenarios.
bullets: The program assesses investment-industry knowledge and application across three exam levels.
It is international in administration; Indian candidates should use CFA Institute’s current exam calendar to check available local appointments, fees, taxes, and deadlines for their selected window.

sections.heading: Eligibility for Level I and progression through the program
paragraphs: A candidate registering for Level I must satisfy one of CFA Institute’s education or work-experience entry routes. The degree route requires a completed bachelor’s or equivalent degree. A current undergraduate may select a Level I window that is no more than 23 months before the graduation month. Alternatively, the candidate may qualify through a combination of at least 4,000 hours of professional work experience and/or higher education obtained over at least three sequential years; the education and work periods cannot overlap for this calculation.

An international travel passport is required for registration. To sit Level II, candidates must have passed Level I and meet the program’s continuing requirements; to sit Level III, they must have passed Level II and, if entering as a student, completed the bachelor’s degree or accrued 4,000 hours of professional work experience.
bullets: Paid internships/articleships may be accepted in the professional-work-experience entry route; CFA Institute states that the work does not need to be investment related for Level I enrolment.
Applicants should confirm their own graduation timing, degree equivalence, identification, and exam-window rules directly with CFA Institute before paying, as policies can change.

sections.heading: Three-level exam format
paragraphs: Each CFA exam has two timed content sessions and approximately 4.5 hours of testing time. Level I consists of stand-alone multiple-choice questions. Level II uses vignettes followed by multiple-choice questions. Level III combines vignette-supported constructed-response (essay) and multiple-choice questions, assessing integration and application of the curriculum.

For the currently published format, Level I has 180 multiple-choice questions in two 135-minute sessions. CFA Institute states that Level II and Level III also total 4.5 hours, with 132 minutes allotted to each of their two content sessions; candidates should rely on the current level-specific guide for their chosen exam window.
bullets: Level I: learn and describe.
Level II: analyze and evaluate.
Level III: integrate and apply.

sections.heading: Registration, scheduling, and exam-day administration
paragraphs: CFA Institute describes registration as a two-step process: create or access a CFA Institute account and register for the relevant exam; after payment is processed, use the candidate account to schedule the appointment. Registration windows include early and standard deadlines as well as scheduling, rescheduling, and accommodation deadlines, so candidates in India should select their intended level and window in the official calendar rather than rely on third-party dates.

CFA exams are offered at test centres in multiple global locations. CFA Institute says candidates should arrive about 30 minutes before the appointment and bring a valid international travel passport and an approved calculator. Before the result is released, candidates must complete at least one required Practical Skills Module.
bullets: Check the registration deadline and then separately schedule the test-centre appointment.
Verify the passport name against the CFA Institute account well before the appointment.
Review the current personal-belongings, identification, calculator, conduct, and rescheduling rules before travel.

sections.heading: Preparing effectively
paragraphs: CFA Institute provides a Learning Ecosystem and identifies practice questions, mock exams, its mobile app, candidate discussion resources, Practical Skills Modules, and an approved-prep-provider list among available study supports. Its reported benchmark is more than 300 hours of preparation per exam level among successful candidates, but an appropriate plan depends on a candidate’s prior finance knowledge, work commitments, and selected exam date.

Preparation should match the level’s question style: foundational concepts and formulas for Level I, vignette analysis for Level II, and both constructed responses and item sets for Level III. Candidates should also use the official exam tutorial and become familiar with the test software before their appointment.
bullets: Begin with the current official curriculum and topic outlines for the registered exam year.
Build timed practice around the actual level-specific question format.
Complete the required Practical Skills Module in time for exam results to be issued.

sections.heading: From exam candidate to CFA charterholder
paragraphs: Completion of the three exams is an important milestone but is distinct from being awarded the CFA charter. To become a Charterholder member and use the CFA designation, CFA Institute requires completion of the CFA Program and Practical Skills Modules, at least 4,000 hours of eligible work experience accumulated over a minimum of 36 months, professional references, and successful membership application.

Qualifying experience must be directly involved in investment decision-making or produce work that informs or adds value to that process. CFA Institute states that relevant experience can be earned before, during, or after program participation and may be full-time, part-time, or remote. This makes the program compatible with gaining relevant finance experience while progressing through the exams, subject to CFA Institute’s review of the membership application.
bullets: Passing Levels I–III does not by itself confer the right to use “CFA.”

Relevant experience may include work such as investment research, portfolio-related analysis, financial modelling, investment advice, or work products supporting investment decisions, subject to CFA Institute review.

The direct next credential outcome is Charterholder membership; career outcomes such as research, credit, investment, portfolio, banking, or wealth roles depend on the candidate’s experience, employer requirements, and labour market conditions.
