title: CLAT
description: CLAT — ug entrance exam (law), conducted by Consortium of NLUs. also LLM (PG) paper.

quick_facts.label: What CLAT is for
quick_facts.value: CLAT is the Consortium of National Law Universities’ entrance test for admissions to participating universities’ five-year integrated LL.B. programmes and LL.M. programmes for the 2026–27 academic year.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: The examination and central admissions counselling are administered by the Consortium of National Law Universities; final admission remains subject to verification by the allotted NLU.

quick_facts.label: UG eligibility — CLAT 2026 cycle
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 UG cycle, candidates needed 10+2 or an equivalent qualification with at least 45% marks; the threshold was 40% for SC, ST and PwD candidates. There was no upper age limit.

quick_facts.label: PG eligibility — CLAT 2026 cycle
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 PG cycle, candidates needed an LL.B. degree or equivalent with at least 50% marks; the threshold was 45% for SC, ST and PwD candidates. There was no upper age limit.

quick_facts.label: UG paper pattern — CLAT 2026 cycle
quick_facts.value: UG CLAT 2026 was a two-hour, 120-question multiple-choice test worth 120 marks, with a deduction of 0.25 mark for each wrong answer. Its five areas were English Language, Current Affairs including General Knowledge, Legal Reasoning, Logical Reasoning and Quantitative Techniques.

quick_facts.label: 2026 cycle timing and mode
quick_facts.value: CLAT 2026 was scheduled as an offline examination on December 7, 2025. This is historical cycle information, not a deadline for a future CLAT cycle.

sections.heading: Purpose and place in the law-admissions pathway
paragraphs: CLAT is principally an admissions examination, not a law qualification or a professional licence. In the CLAT 2026 cycle, the Consortium described it as the route for admissions to five-year integrated LL.B. and LL.M. programmes at participating universities for the 2026–27 academic year. Accordingly, students from Arts, Commerce, PCM and PCMB backgrounds may use the UG route after Class 12; the subject stream itself is not listed as an eligibility condition in the Consortium’s UG criteria.

Admission offers and seat allotments are provisional. The allotted National Law University verifies documents and applies its own course, intake, reservation and fee rules. Applicants should therefore treat CLAT rank as one part of the admissions process rather than a guarantee of enrolment.
bullets: UG route: leads toward integrated law degrees such as B.A. LL.B. (Hons.), B.B.A. LL.B. (Hons.), B.Com. LL.B. (Hons.) and other programme combinations offered by individual participating NLUs.
PG route: leads toward LL.M. admission for applicants who already hold the required LL.B. qualification.

Career note: CLAT itself does not award a degree or appoint a candidate to a legal job; later outcomes depend on completing the relevant programme and meeting the rules of the particular employer, regulator or recruitment process.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: For CLAT 2026 UG, the Consortium required a passed 10+2 or equivalent examination with at least 45% marks or equivalent grade, reduced to 40% for SC, ST and PwD candidates. Candidates taking the qualifying examination in March or April 2026 could apply provisionally, but had to provide proof of passing at admission. The Consortium stated that there was no upper age limit.

For CLAT 2026 PG, the qualifying credential was an LL.B. degree or equivalent with at least 50% marks or equivalent grade, reduced to 45% for SC, ST and PwD candidates. Final-year candidates could apply provisionally subject to producing passing evidence at admission; there was no upper age limit.
bullets: Use the official eligibility page for the relevant cycle: qualifying marks, permitted provisional applications and category treatment can change.
For CLAT 2026, Indian nationals and NRIs could appear; the Consortium instructed foreign nationals to approach individual NLUs directly rather than use CLAT.
Reservation claims require the certificates prescribed by the relevant government and NLU, and university-level eligibility verification remains decisive.

sections.heading: Test format and what it assesses
paragraphs: The CLAT 2026 UG paper was an offline, two-hour paper with 120 objective questions carrying one mark each and negative marking of 0.25 for a wrong response. The Consortium framed the UG test as an assessment of comprehension and reasoning skills needed for legal education, rather than a test requiring prior legal study.

The five UG areas were English Language; Current Affairs including General Knowledge; Legal Reasoning; Logical Reasoning; and Quantitative Techniques. The official syllabus says Legal Reasoning does not require prior knowledge of law, although awareness of contemporary legal and moral issues may help; quantitative questions use skills including ratios, basic algebra, mensuration and statistical estimation at approximately Class 10 level.

The CLAT 2026 PG paper was also 120 minutes, with 120 objective questions worth one mark each and a 0.25-mark deduction for wrong answers. It used extracts from primary legal materials and covered compulsory undergraduate-law subjects including Constitutional Law, Jurisprudence, Contract, Torts, Criminal Law and Public International Law.
bullets: Check the official syllabus for the target cycle before relying on any prior-year pattern: the Consortium appointed an expert committee to consider UG and PG reforms for CLAT 2027.
For future applications, confirm mode, duration, accessibility arrangements and question pattern from that cycle’s official information page.

sections.heading: Application, counselling and admission process
paragraphs: In the 2026 cycle, applicants registered online through the Consortium website using their own mobile number and email address, validated the mobile number by OTP, completed the form, uploaded the required files, and paid online. The official UG instructions listed a photograph, signature and applicable category, PwD and BPL certificates; uploads had to be PDFs. The 2026 online-registration period was August 1 through October 31, 2025, so those dates are past and should not be reused for a future cycle.

After the result, the Consortium’s central counselling process required selected candidates to register for counselling, provide NLU preferences and pay the applicable counselling-registration fee. In the 2026 process there were five rounds; candidates allotted a seat could generally use Freeze, Float or Exit options. The Consortium also stated that final seat allotment was provisional and subject to the concerned NLU’s validation.
bullets: For a future cycle, start only from the official Consortium portal and read that cycle’s instructions and participating-NLU brochures before choosing preferences.
Enter names and category information exactly as supported by official records. The 2026 instructions warned that false information or a material mismatch could cancel provisional admission.

Fees, participating institutions, seats, reservation rules, test centres and deadlines are cycle- and university-specific. Verify them in the live official notice rather than relying on the 2026 figures.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Build preparation around the official syllabus and passage-based testing method. For UG CLAT 2026, this means sustained reading comprehension, argument analysis and inference, current-affairs awareness, applying stated legal principles to facts, and accurate interpretation of numerical information. The official syllabus specifically recommends developing the ability to read and understand substantial text, following quality newspapers and periodicals, and practising quantitative speed with material such as Class 10 mathematics textbooks.

Use official practice material where available. For CLAT 2026, the Consortium said it planned guides, sample questions, model papers, subject exercises, a learning platform for successfully registered candidates, and online expert sessions. These materials are preferable for understanding the intended question style; commercial resources should be checked against the official syllabus rather than treated as authoritative.
bullets: Begin with a diagnostic timed paper, then maintain an error log separating comprehension, reasoning, current-affairs and calculation errors.
Practise full-length papers under the applicable official time limit and account for negative marking when deciding whether to attempt uncertain questions.
For PG, revise the listed compulsory LL.B. subjects and practise reading judgments, statutes and other primary legal extracts closely.

sections.heading: What a CLAT result can lead to
paragraphs: A qualifying CLAT result can be used in the Consortium’s admissions process for participating NLUs’ integrated five-year LL.B. programmes or LL.M. programmes, depending on whether the applicant takes the UG or PG route and meets programme-specific conditions. The precise degree combinations, seats, fees and reservation arrangements vary by participating NLU and can change before final allotment.

A result does not itself secure admission. In the 2026 process, counselling registration did not guarantee a seat, and the Consortium specified that an allotment remained provisional until document and eligibility verification by the concerned NLU. After central counselling closes, member NLUs may separately fill remaining vacancies according to their own norms.
bullets: For integrated-law applicants, compare each NLU’s programme title, curriculum, location, total cost and reservation policy directly from its official brochure or website before preference submission.
For LL.M. applicants, confirm the NLU’s specialisation, eligibility and admission requirements in addition to the CLAT PG requirement.

Do not infer eligibility for PSU legal-officer employment from a CLAT result alone: such roles are governed by the recruiting organisation’s separate notice and typically require the specified law qualification and other stated conditions.

title: CMA Final
description: CMA Final — professional exam (finance), conducted by ICMAI.

quick_facts.label: Awarding body
quick_facts.value: CMA Final is the Final Course examination stage administered by The Institute of Cost Accountants of India (ICMAI) under its CMA Syllabus 2022 framework.

quick_facts.label: Papers and groups
quick_facts.value: Under Syllabus 2022, CMA Final has Group III (Papers 13–16) and Group IV (Papers 17–19 plus one chosen elective from Papers 20A, 20B, or 20C), for eight papers in total.

quick_facts.label: Training before Final examination
quick_facts.value: The published Syllabus 2022 pathway requires Final-level skills training (80 hours), a 10-day Industry Oriented Training Programme (IOTP), and 15 months of practical training before appearing in both or remaining Final group(s).

sections.heading: What CMA Final is for
paragraphs: CMA Final is the capstone examination stage in ICMAI’s professional Cost and Management Accountancy pathway. Its Syllabus 2022 curriculum advances from corporate and economic law, strategic finance, direct and indirect taxation, strategic cost management, audit, and corporate financial reporting to an elective in performance management and valuation, banking and insurance risk, or entrepreneurship and start-up.

Passing Final is an examination milestone rather than automatic professional membership. ICMAI’s published Associate Membership conditions state that a Final passer may seek Associate Membership after obtaining at least three years of the specified practical experience and satisfying the Council with evidence of that experience.
bullets: Use this node for the professional examination stage, not for ICMAI membership itself.
The elective is selected at the time of Final Course enrollment.

sections.heading: Eligibility to enroll and sit for CMA Final
paragraphs: ICMAI’s published Final Course enrollment rule is that only candidates who have passed the Institute’s Intermediate examination are eligible; the prospectus expresses this as qualifying Intermediate in both groups. A copy of the Intermediate pass marksheet is to be provided with the Final admission form.

For admission to a Final examination, the prospectus lists further conditions: a valid registration number, completion of prescribed Final training, no debarment from the Institute’s Final examination, and submission of the examination form with the required fee. It additionally says that a student who passes Intermediate in the December examination cannot sit for the immediately following June Final examination.
bullets: Complete Final enrollment at least four months before the examination under the published prospectus rule.
Treat eligibility and training requirements as term-sensitive: ICMAI says syllabus, examination scheme, and patterns may be modified through its notifications.

sections.heading: Groups, papers, and assessment structure
paragraphs: The Syllabus 2022 Final is organized into two groups. Group III comprises Corporate and Economic Laws; Strategic Financial Management; Direct Tax Laws and International Taxation; and Strategic Cost Management. Group IV comprises Cost and Management Audit; Corporate Financial Reporting; Indirect Tax Laws and Practice; and one elective paper selected from Strategic Performance Management and Business Valuation, Risk Management in Banking and Insurance, or Entrepreneurship and Start-up.

The Institute’s prospectus states that each Final paper carries 100 marks. The published standard of pass is at least 40% in every paper and 50% aggregate in the non-exempted papers of a group; passing all groups is required to pass the examination. A score of 60% or more in a paper can create an exemption or carry-forward benefit subject to ICMAI’s stated conditions and validity period.
bullets: ICMAI says Final examinations are held twice a year, on dates decided by its Council.
Intermediate and Final candidates may elect to write answers in Hindi; mixing Hindi and English in an answer script may lead to cancellation under the published rule.

sections.heading: Enrollment and examination application process
paragraphs: First, an Intermediate-qualified student enrolls in the Final Course, submits the Intermediate pass marksheet, chooses one Final elective, and completes the applicable coaching and training pathway. ICMAI directs students to its online student portal for online enrollment.

Separately, candidates apply for a specific Final examination term. The 2025 ICMAI prospectus says Final examination forms are completed online through the Institute website and paid through the online payment gateway; it also describes a bank-challan route. The same prospectus listed ordinary online application cut-offs of April 10 for the June term and October 10 for the December term, but these are dated published guidance rather than a confirmation of a current-term deadline. Candidates should use the relevant examination notification for the term they intend to take.
bullets: Published 2025 fee context for an Indian centre: ₹1,800 for a single Final group and ₹3,200 for both groups; verify the current notification because fees may change.
ICMAI’s published Final enrollment cut-offs were January 31 for a June term and July 31 for a December term; confirm current applicability before relying on them.

sections.heading: Preparation using ICMAI materials
paragraphs: Start with ICMAI’s official Syllabus 2022 Final curriculum and paper-wise study materials, then map preparation across both groups and the chosen elective. The official syllabus gives topic-level weightages, which the prospectus describes as a guide to study time and the approximate proportional allocation of marks in an examination.

Use ICMAI’s official Final model question papers and answer keys to practise under examination conditions. The Institute has published Final model-question-paper resources for the June 2026 term, alongside official study materials for Papers 13 through 19 and the three elective options.

Build training completion into the study plan. ICMAI’s Final skills-training page lists an 80-hour-plus-10-day requirement, comprising ERP-focused training, business/data analytics, and IOTP; the prospectus also specifies the related practical-training requirement for Final examination eligibility.
bullets: Prioritize current ICMAI supplementary material and term notifications, especially for law and tax papers that may be amended.
Practise both paper-level performance and group aggregate: the pass rule requires both the per-paper minimum and group aggregate.

useful_links.label: ICMAI Final Model Question Papers — June 2026

title: CMA Foundation
description: CMA Foundation — professional exam (finance), conducted by ICMAI.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: CMA Foundation is the entry-level examination in ICMAI’s CMA course. ICMAI is a statutory professional body constituted under the Cost and Works Accountants Act, 1959 for regulation of the cost and management accountancy profession.

quick_facts.label: Syllabus structure
quick_facts.value: Under CMA Syllabus 2022, Foundation has four 100-mark papers: Business Laws and Business Communication; Financial and Cost Accounting; Business Mathematics and Statistics; and Business Economics and Management.

sections.heading: What CMA Foundation is for
paragraphs: CMA Foundation is ICMAI’s entry route into the professional CMA curriculum. It introduces the legal, accounting, quantitative, economic and management foundations used in later cost and management accountancy study. ICMAI describes its statutory role as regulating the cost and management accountancy profession in India under the Cost and Works Accountants Act, 1959.
source_urls
bullets: It is a professional-course examination, rather than a university degree.
It is particularly relevant for learners seeking a structured route toward cost accounting, management accounting and related finance responsibilities.
Passing it is one route to registration at the CMA Intermediate level.

sections.heading: Subjects, assessment and passing rule
paragraphs: The current published Syllabus 2022 sets four Foundation papers, each carrying 100 marks. The published paper areas are business laws and communication; financial and cost accounting; business mathematics and statistics; and business economics and management. ICMAI states that Foundation, Intermediate and Final examinations are held twice a year on dates decided by its Council; exact dates and programme are announced term by term.
source_urls
bullets: Paper 1: Fundamentals of Business Laws and Business Communication.
Paper 2: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting.
Paper 3: Fundamentals of Business Mathematics and Statistics.
Paper 4: Fundamentals of Business Economics and Management.
Pass standard: minimum 40% in every paper and 50% aggregate. The prospectus states that paper-wise exemption/carry-forward benefits are not available at Foundation level.

sections.heading: How to apply and plan around a term
paragraphs: Admission may be completed online through ICMAI’s student portal. The prospectus says applicants must provide qualification and age proof, and that admission should be completed at least four months before the examination. Examination applications are submitted online through ICMAI, with the examination fee and operational deadlines set or notified for the relevant term.
source_urls
bullets: Confirm that you meet the Class 10 admission requirement and will meet the Class 12 requirement before sitting the examination.
Apply for Foundation admission through the official ICMAI student portal and retain the issued identification number.
After enrolment, submit the separate examination form by the deadline in the term-specific notification.
Treat dates and fees as variable: for example, ICMAI extended the June 2026 admission/registration cut-off to February 10, 2026; future terms require checking the latest notification.

sections.heading: Preparing with ICMAI materials
paragraphs: ICMAI states that a student admitted to Foundation has to undergo its Foundation coaching scheme. Its Syllabus 2022 page also publishes Foundation study resources, including the curriculum, study materials, practice test papers, model question papers and an MCQ bank. These official materials are the best starting point because the Institute notes that syllabus content and examination patterns can be modified through notifications.
source_urls
bullets: Start with the official Syllabus 2022 curriculum and study materials for all four papers.
Use the official model and practice papers to practise full-paper timing and identify weak areas.
Give repeated practice to calculation-heavy accounting, mathematics and statistics topics, while scheduling separate revision cycles for law, economics, management and communication.
Check ICMAI notifications before the term for any syllabus, schedule or examination-process changes.

sections.heading: What passing Foundation leads to
paragraphs: A Foundation pass qualifies the student to register for CMA Intermediate, subject to ICMAI’s then-applicable registration rules. It is therefore an entry-stage milestone in the CMA pathway, not a standalone licence to practise as a Cost Accountant. ICMAI’s membership requirements are tied to passing the Final examination and meeting the specified practical-experience conditions.
source_urls
bullets: Immediate academic/professional outcome: eligibility to register for CMA Intermediate.
Longer CMA route: Intermediate, Final, prescribed training and applicable membership requirements.
Foundation knowledge can complement commerce and business undergraduate study, but the Foundation pass does not replace a B.Com, BBA or another university degree.

useful_links.label: ICMAI CMA Syllabus 2022 and official study resources
ICMAI student portal for online admission

title: CMA Intermediate
description: CMA Intermediate — professional exam (finance), conducted by ICMAI.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: CMA Intermediate is administered by The Institute of Cost Accountants of India (ICMAI), a statutory professional body established under the Cost and Works Accountants Act, 1959 for regulation of the cost and management accountancy profession.

quick_facts.label: Entry routes
quick_facts.value: A candidate may register after 10+2 plus ICMAI Foundation/CAT Foundation Part I, or through direct-entry qualifications such as a recognized university degree (with specified exclusions), qualifying engineering status, or other listed qualifying examinations. Degree-result-awaiting candidates may seek provisional registration.

quick_facts.label: Current syllabus structure
quick_facts.value: Under ICMAI Syllabus 2022, Intermediate has two groups and eight papers: four papers in Group I and four in Group II.

sections.heading: What CMA Intermediate is for
paragraphs: CMA Intermediate is ICMAI’s second academic examination level in the CMA pathway. It builds technical capability in financial accounting, taxation, cost accounting, management accounting, corporate accounting and auditing, financial management, business data analytics, business laws, operations management and strategy. ICMAI is the statutory body responsible for examining candidates and regulating student training in this profession.
source_urls
bullets: The course is designed as preparation for progression to CMA Final after qualifying both Intermediate groups.
It combines examination papers with required skills training and access to practical-training pathways.
It is particularly aligned with cost and management accounting work: cost analysis, financial and management accounting, compliance, audit-related work, reporting and business decision support.

sections.heading: Who can register
paragraphs: ICMAI lists multiple entry routes to Intermediate. The standard route is Senior Secondary/Higher Secondary (10+2) together with ICMAI Foundation. Direct registration is available to candidates with a degree from a recognized university, subject to ICMAI’s exclusions for certain fine-arts/performance disciplines, and to certain other specified categories such as qualified engineers and eligible engineering students. ICMAI also permits provisional registration for candidates awaiting degree results, who must convert to regular status within the period specified by the Institute.
source_urls
bullets: 10+2 plus ICMAI Foundation is an entry route.
A recognized degree can provide direct entry, subject to ICMAI’s stated conditions and exclusions.
Candidates should check ICMAI’s current qualifying-examination annexure and provisional-registration conditions before applying, because admission rules can be revised.

sections.heading: Exam format and subjects
paragraphs: Syllabus 2022 divides CMA Intermediate into two groups of four papers. Group I covers Business Laws and Ethics, Financial Accounting, Direct and Indirect Taxation, and Cost Accounting. Group II covers Operations Management and Strategic Management, Corporate Accounting and Auditing, Financial Management and Business Data Analytics, and Management Accounting.

For the June 2026 term, ICMAI scheduled the eight Intermediate papers on June 11–18, 2026, in a 2:00 p.m.–5:00 p.m. IST slot, and specified an offline, centre-based examination mode. This is a dated timetable, not a guarantee of the mode, timings, centres, or dates for future terms.
source_urls
bullets: Group I: Papers 5–8.
Group II: Papers 9–12.
For a candidate taking both groups, ICMAI’s published Syllabus 2022 rule requires at least 40% in every paper appeared and at least 50% aggregate across both groups to qualify the course.

sections.heading: Registration and examination application
paragraphs: The process has two distinct stages: register for the Intermediate course, then submit an examination application for a particular term when eligible. ICMAI’s prospectus says registration should be completed at least four months before an examination starts. To be admitted to the Intermediate examination, a student needs a valid registration number, completion of prescribed Intermediate training, no debarment, and a timely examination form with the fee set by the Council.

The 2025 ICMAI prospectus listed Intermediate course fees of ₹23,100, or an instalment option of ₹12,000 at registration plus ₹11,100 later. Separately, the June 2026 exam notice listed ₹1,500 for one group and ₹2,800 for both groups at inland centres. These are published historical/term-specific amounts; applicants should treat fees, cut-offs, payment modes, and late fees as variable and confirm them in the current ICMAI notification.
source_urls
bullets: Create or use the ICMAI student-portal account and submit the course-registration documents required for the applicable entry route.
Complete the prescribed training and pay any required course instalment before filing the exam form.
Use the official Examination and Student Circulars pages to confirm the next term’s registration cut-off, exam-form window, centre availability, fee, and instructions.

sections.heading: How to prepare using ICMAI resources
paragraphs: Begin with the Syllabus 2022 study material and make a separate plan for each group and paper. ICMAI publishes Intermediate study materials, workbooks, MCQ banks, postal test papers, practice test papers, model question papers, and past examination question papers. These official resources are particularly useful for matching preparation to the Institute’s current paper names and syllabus.

Training is part of readiness, not merely an add-on. The published Intermediate Skills Training programme totals 120 hours and includes ERP exposure, communication and soft skills, office/productivity tools, and e-filing. ICMAI states that the Skills Training assessment must be completed before a student can appear for either/both groups or a remaining group.
source_urls
bullets: Study paper-by-paper, then use full-group revision to practise integrating related accounting, tax, costing and management-accounting concepts.
Attempt official model, practice, and prior-term question papers under timed conditions.
Track ICMAI supplementary material and term-specific clarifications, especially for law, taxation, cost-accounting standards, and other update-sensitive content.

sections.heading: What it can lead to
paragraphs: The direct academic outcome of qualifying both CMA Intermediate groups is eligibility to enrol in ICMAI Final. ICMAI’s training scheme also allows practical training to start from Intermediate level; the published scheme describes 15 months of practical training in recognized accounting, finance, audit, compliance and related areas, with the full training requirement linked to Final-examination eligibility.

Before full CMA qualification, Intermediate students and pass-outs may be considered for trainee and entry-level finance/accounting opportunities. ICMAI’s placement updates in 2026 included invitations directed at CMA Intermediate candidates or CMA Intermediate-qualified candidates. Actual job title, employer requirements, location, work experience, compensation, and selection outcome vary; ICMAI Intermediate alone does not confer CMA membership.
source_urls
bullets: Immediate next educational step: qualify both groups and enrol for CMA Final.

Practical exposure can begin through ICMAI-recognized practical training in areas such as management accounting, cost accounting, financial accounting, financial management, auditing and regulatory compliance.
Possible early-career directions include accounting, accounts operations, audit support, tax support and cost-accounting trainee work, subject to each employer’s requirements.

title: CMAT
description: CMAT — pg entrance exam (management), conducted by NTA.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: The National Testing Agency (NTA), an autonomous organization under India’s Ministry of Education, has conducted CMAT since 2019.

quick_facts.label: Purpose
quick_facts.value: CMAT is a national-level entrance examination for management programmes. It enables AICTE-affiliated/participating institutions to select graduate candidates; the 2026 bulletin states that CMAT scores are accepted by AICTE-approved institutions, university departments, constituent colleges and affiliated colleges.

quick_facts.label: Exam format (CMAT 2026)
quick_facts.value: The 2026 test was a 180-minute, English-only computer-based test with 100 questions and 400 maximum marks across five 20-question sections: Quantitative Techniques & Data Interpretation, Logical Reasoning, Language Comprehension, General Awareness, and Innovation & Entrepreneurship.

quick_facts.label: Marking (CMAT 2026)
quick_facts.value: Each correct answer carried 4 marks; each incorrect answer incurred a 1-mark deduction; unattempted questions received 0 marks.

sections.heading: What CMAT is for
paragraphs: CMAT is an entrance test for postgraduate management admissions rather than an admission offer itself. NTA conducts the examination, processes answer-key challenges, declares scores and provides score data; it does not conduct counselling or allocate seats.

A CMAT score can be used to apply to participating institutions, but candidates must separately meet each institution’s admission requirements. Institutions set their own score cut-offs and may use further selection stages such as group discussion and personal interview. Merely taking CMAT does not create an automatic right to a postgraduate seat.
bullets: Useful for graduates from diverse undergraduate backgrounds—including BBE, BTTM and hotel-management programmes—who intend to pursue eligible management courses.
Always verify programme-specific eligibility, accepted test scores, selection components, fee and application dates on the target institution’s own admissions page.

sections.heading: Eligibility: the CMAT 2026 reference point
paragraphs: For CMAT 2026, NTA required Indian citizenship and a bachelor’s degree in any discipline. Final-year bachelor’s students could apply if their result would be declared before the start of academic-year 2026–27 admissions. NTA specified no age restriction.

Applicants should not treat test eligibility as identical to admission eligibility. The bulletin directs candidates to verify the requirements of the institutions to which they apply, and notes that the degree should be recognized under AICTE provisions.
bullets: A completed bachelor’s degree in any discipline was acceptable for the 2026 examination.
Final-year candidates were permitted subject to the stated result-timing condition.
No age limit applied for CMAT 2026.

sections.heading: Test structure and scoring
paragraphs: The CMAT 2026 structure was a three-hour CBT in English. It contained five equally weighted areas: Quantitative Techniques & Data Interpretation, Logical Reasoning, Language Comprehension, General Awareness, and Innovation & Entrepreneurship. Each area had 20 questions, for 100 questions and 400 marks overall.

The 2026 marking rule was +4 for a correct answer, −1 for an incorrect answer and 0 for an unattempted question. The 2026 bulletin also stated that, if a question were dropped because of a technical error, full marks would be awarded to all candidates irrespective of attempt status. Future-cycle format and rules should be checked in that cycle’s official bulletin.
bullets: Mode: Computer Based Test (CBT).
Duration: 180 minutes.
Language: English only.
Question count and maximum score in 2026: 100 questions and 400 marks.

sections.heading: How the application process works
paragraphs: In the 2026 cycle, applications were accepted online only through the official CMAT portal. The stated workflow was: register to obtain an application number; complete personal, education, programme and examination-city details; upload required images/documents; pay the fee online; and save the confirmation page after successful payment.

The CMAT 2026 registration window, including its extensions, is over. The original 2026 bulletin listed application fees of ₹2,500 for General (UR) male candidates and ₹1,250 for General (UR) female candidates and the listed reserved-category/third-gender candidates, plus applicable processing charges and GST. These were 2026-cycle figures, not a prediction of future fees. Candidates seeking a later CMAT cycle should rely only on a new NTA notice and information bulletin for dates, categories, fees and correction rules.
bullets: Use only the official CMAT portal for registration; NTA said applications submitted by other modes would not be accepted.
Use an active personal or parent/guardian mobile number and email address, as NTA sends examination communications through the registered details.
Save the confirmation page after payment; the 2026 bulletin treated successful fee receipt as necessary for confirmed candidature.

sections.heading: Preparation approach aligned to the official pattern
paragraphs: Build preparation around the five official CMAT domains and the three-hour CBT constraint. A practical plan is to diagnose performance separately in Quantitative Techniques & Data Interpretation, Logical Reasoning, Language Comprehension, General Awareness, and Innovation & Entrepreneurship; then practise mixed, timed sets that reproduce the 100-question, 180-minute format.

Because the 2026 scoring rule penalized incorrect answers by one mark, use mock-review data to distinguish questions worth attempting from questions better left unanswered. This is a preparation inference from the official marking scheme, not an NTA-prescribed strategy. Before the exam, review the official CBT procedure and the current cycle’s bulletin for interface, identification, permitted-items and centre instructions.
bullets: Practise completing 100 questions in 180 minutes under CBT-like conditions.
Track accuracy as well as speed because incorrect answers carried negative marking in 2026.
Revise each section deliberately; the 2026 blueprint assigned equal question counts and marks to all five sections.
Use the official information bulletin as the definitive source if a coaching resource conflicts with it.

sections.heading: After the test: scores and admissions
paragraphs: For the most recent completed cycle, NTA declared CMAT 2026 scores on February 17, 2026. Since that examination was conducted in a single shift, NTA stated that the scorecard contained candidates’ marks and corresponding percentile scores.

A CMAT result is an input to institutional admissions, not a centralized seat allocation. Candidates must apply to desired participating institutions separately, meet their respective cut-offs and complete any additional selection procedure. The relevant institution—not NTA—determines final admission.
bullets: CMAT 2026: test held January 25, 2026; results declared February 17, 2026.
NTA’s 2026 result notice reported 53,453 registered candidates and 41,872 candidates who appeared.
Retain the scorecard and monitor each target institution’s admissions process, cut-off and selection requirements.

title: COMEDK UGET
description: COMEDK UGET — ug entrance exam (engineering), conducted by COMEDK.

quick_facts.label: Purpose
quick_facts.value: COMEDK UGET is a common undergraduate entrance test used for merit determination and B.E./B.Tech seat selection at participating COMEDK engineering institutions in Karnataka.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: The exam is conducted by COMEDK (Consortium of Medical, Engineering and Dental Colleges of Karnataka) for the Karnataka Unaided Private Engineering Colleges Association (KUPECA) member-institution admission process.

quick_facts.label: 2026 examination status
quick_facts.value: For the 2026–27 admission cycle, COMEDK UGET was held on 9 May 2026; rank/score cards were scheduled to go live on 29 May 2026. The 2026 entrance-exam application window is closed.

quick_facts.label: Eligibility baseline
quick_facts.value: For 2026 B.E./B.Tech admission, candidates needed a recognized 10+2/2nd PUC or equivalent qualification with Physics, Mathematics and English, plus Chemistry, Biotechnology, Biology, Computer Science or Electronics; the stated aggregate minimum in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics was 45% for General Merit and 40% for Karnataka-state SC/ST/OBC candidates.

quick_facts.label: Test pattern (2026)
quick_facts.value: The 2026 test was an English-medium computer-based test with 180 multiple-choice questions: 60 each in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics. Each correct answer carried one mark and there was no negative marking.

quick_facts.label: Counselling route
quick_facts.value: COMEDK uses centralized online counselling. For 2026, eligible rank holders had to register, pay the stated non-refundable counselling registration fee, upload documents, obtain document approval, and then participate in choice filling and online allotment.

sections.heading: What COMEDK UGET is for
paragraphs: COMEDK UGET is the engineering entrance route for participating COMEDK institutions, rather than a general national engineering admission examination. For 2026–27, COMEDK stated that KUPECA—comprising more than 150 engineering colleges in Karnataka—had entrusted it with conducting the common test and centralized seat-selection process. The 2026 brochure says that the score is valid only for admissions in the 2026–27 academic year and for participating COMEDK institutions or other expressly permitted institutions.
source_urls
bullets: The result is used to generate a merit/rank card for the COMEDK seat-selection process.
A COMEDK UGET rank is not, by itself, an offer of admission: candidates must meet course eligibility requirements and complete the applicable counselling steps.
The official site described the 2026 process as an examination followed by centralized online counselling.

sections.heading: Eligibility: how to assess it
paragraphs: For the 2026 B.E./B.Tech cycle, COMEDK permitted Indian citizens, OCI candidates and PIO candidates to sit the entrance test, subject to the stated documentation requirements. The qualifying examination was 2nd PUC/10+2 or an equivalent State- or Central-Government-recognized examination. The final two years of study had to include Physics, Mathematics, English, and one of Chemistry, Biotechnology, Biology, Computer Science or Electronics.

The stated 2026 academic threshold was a pass with at least 45% aggregate in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics for General Merit candidates, or 40% for SC, ST and OBC candidates of Karnataka state; the relevant subjects also had to be passed individually. COMEDK additionally stated that subjects must be passed from one board, and that diploma candidates were not eligible because the process has no lateral-entry admissions.

Eligibility rules can be revised if AICTE or Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU) requirements change. Applicants should therefore treat these as the 2026-cycle rules and confirm the future-cycle brochure before applying or registering for counselling.
bullets: Check both exam eligibility and the counselling/admission eligibility for the intended B.E./B.Tech seat.
Do not assume a reserved-category qualifying-mark concession applies outside Karnataka: COMEDK specified that the 40% threshold was for Karnataka-state SC/ST/OBC candidates.
A candidate scoring zero in the entrance test is not assigned a rank in the 2026 rules.

sections.heading: Exam format and ranking
paragraphs: In 2026, COMEDK UGET was conducted only as a computer-based test (CBT). It comprised 180 MCQs—60 each in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics—in English only, for 180 total marks. A correct response earned one mark, and a wrong response had no negative marking.

The 2026 syllabus was based on the CBSE syllabus, with approximately 33% attributed to Class 11 and 67% to Class 12. COMEDK noted that, where the exam ran in multiple sessions with different question sets, it would use normalization and announce rank using normalized percentile. Its published tie-break order considered percentile in Physics and Mathematics together, then Mathematics, then Chemistry, then age (older candidate ranked higher).
bullets: Practice for a screen-based MCQ environment: candidates could navigate between questions, mark questions for review, and revise answers during the test.
The 2026 rank was generated from entrance-test performance only; the rank card was the basis for entering seat-selection counselling.
The 9 May 2026 examination was also administered as one combined exam for candidates opting for both COMEDK UGET and Uni-GAUGE E, but COMEDK and Uni-GAUGE outcomes/counselling were distinct.

sections.heading: Application and counselling process
paragraphs: The 2026 entrance-test application period ran from 3 February 2026 until 23 March 2026 after extensions, and that application window is now closed. In the 2026 instructions, COMEDK required candidates to register on its website, use the resulting login credentials to complete the online application and payment, and download the Test Admission Ticket (TAT) from candidate login when made available. Future-cycle dates, fields, documents and fees should be checked only in the corresponding official notice and information brochure.

After results, the 2026 central counselling process was online. Rank holders who wished to participate had to register in applicant login, pay the stated ₹2,000 non-refundable counselling registration fee, upload readable supporting documents, and receive an approved document-verification status before choice filling. COMEDK stated that online counselling could run for four rounds, subject to the schedule of statutory authorities; dates and seat availability were explicitly subject to change.

As of the latest official 2026 page reviewed, Round 1 choice filling had been extended from 17 July 2026 at 3 PM to 24 July 2026 at 2 PM. This is time-sensitive, 2026-specific information rather than a recurring deadline.
bullets: Preserve the TAT and download the rank card from applicant login; COMEDK stated that it would not send hard copies by post or email.
For counselling uploads, COMEDK required clear scans; unclear or mobile-photographed documents could be rejected.
Check the official counselling page for current seat availability, course options, round dates, fee structure and refund conditions before making choices.

sections.heading: Preparation approach grounded in the official scheme
paragraphs: Build preparation around Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics at the published 11th- and 12th-standard CBSE-syllabus balance for the applicable cycle. For the 2026 paper, that meant approximately one-third Class 11 and two-thirds Class 12 content. Because all three subjects carried the same 60-question weight, a balanced plan is more defensible than neglecting one subject.

Use the official CBT mock test when it is made available for the relevant cycle. COMEDK said its mock test was intended to familiarize candidates with the computer-based environment; candidates should use it to rehearse navigation, reviewing answers and handling a 180-question English-medium MCQ paper. For 2026, mock-test availability was restricted to candidates with successful payment.

Since there was no negative marking in the 2026 scheme, candidates could plan their final review around attempting every question while still prioritizing accuracy and time management. This is a 2026-specific strategy: verify the marking scheme in the next information brochure before relying on it.
bullets: Convert the official syllabus into a chapter checklist and schedule mixed-subject practice sets.
Use timed CBT-style practice, then review incorrect and skipped questions by topic.
Read the current official brochure and TAT instructions before test day; the centre, session and reporting instructions are candidate-specific.

sections.heading: What happens after the test
paragraphs: COMEDK publishes results and makes the online rank card available in applicant login. Under the 2026 rules, rank/merit derives from entrance-test performance; candidates with a rank card who also meet the qualification requirements may register for centralized online counselling. The rank card is needed for participation, but admission depends on document verification, choices submitted, seat availability, eligibility and allotment outcomes.

For the 2026 counselling cycle, COMEDK described choice filling followed by online seat allotment and up to four rounds, subject to the statutory timetable. College/course availability and fee structures are variable: COMEDK stated that they would be notified before counselling and later published revised and final availability/fee notices. Applicants should evaluate the specific allotment-round documents rather than rely on a static fee or cut-off figure.

The 2026 score was valid only for the 2026–27 admission year. A future applicant should expect to take the examination again for a later admission cycle unless a future official notification says otherwise.
bullets: Download and retain the rank card; COMEDK does not dispatch it as a hard copy.
Track each counselling-round deadline, because a missed registration, document-verification or choice-filling action can end participation.
Treat previous-year cut-offs, seats and fees as historical context only, not as admission guarantees.

title: CS Executive
description: CS Executive — professional exam (finance), conducted by ICSI.

quick_facts.label: Administering body
quick_facts.value: The CS Executive Programme is administered by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI), the professional body for the Company Secretaryship course.

quick_facts.label: Current syllabus structure
quick_facts.value: Under ICSI Syllabus 2022, CS Executive has seven papers arranged in two groups: four papers in Group 1 and three papers in Group 2.

quick_facts.label: Main entry routes
quick_facts.value: Eligible routes include passing CSEET after Class 12 (10+2), passing CS Foundation, or direct/provisional admission through specified higher-education and accountancy qualifications, including graduates/postgraduates, ICAI Intermediate pass, ICMAI Final pass, and qualifying integrated-programme students.

quick_facts.label: Examination prerequisites
quick_facts.value: For Syllabus 2022 students, ICSI requires successful completion of the Pre-Examination Test before enrolment and appearance in the Executive examination. Students registered in the Executive Programme from 1 February 2025 are also subject to the mandatory Three Days Orientation Programme (TDOP) before filing an examination form.

quick_facts.label: Fees (variable; schedule effective 15 April 2026)
quick_facts.value: The published Executive registration total is ₹18,900 for CSEET/CS Foundation entrants and ₹23,900 for specified direct-entry categories; the Executive examination fee is ₹1,500 per group. Optional journal subscription and applicable concessions can affect amounts, so applicants should confirm the live ICSI schedule before payment.

sections.heading: What CS Executive is for
paragraphs: CS Executive is the intermediate professional stage in ICSI’s Company Secretaryship pathway, positioned after entry through CSEET or another permitted admission route and before the CS Professional Programme. Its syllabus combines company law, securities regulation, business and labour law, corporate accounting and financial management, economic/commercial/IP law, and tax—areas central to corporate compliance and governance work.

Passing CS Executive is not itself ICSI membership or the Company Secretary qualification. It is the academic progression point for registration to the CS Professional Programme and can also support the separate ICSI Secretarial Executive Certificate route when the additional development-programme, practical-training and application conditions are met.
bullets: Group 1: Jurisprudence, Interpretation & General Laws; Company Law & Practice; Setting Up of Business, Industrial & Labour Laws; Corporate Accounting & Financial Management.
Group 2: Capital Market & Securities Laws; Economic, Commercial & Intellectual Property Laws; Tax Laws & Practice.

sections.heading: Who can register
paragraphs: As reflected in ICSI’s April 2026 student-services FAQ and March 2026 Council decision, an applicant may register after passing CSEET and the Senior Secondary (10+2) examination, after passing CS Foundation, or through listed direct-entry routes. The direct-entry categories include graduates and postgraduates, ICAI Intermediate pass candidates, ICMAI Final pass candidates, and students who have passed the sixth semester of a recognised five-year integrated programme.

ICSI also permits provisional registration for students appearing in the final year/final semester of a three-year undergraduate programme and for students appearing in the sixth semester of a recognised five-year integrated programme, subject to ICSI’s documentary and completion requirements. CSEET-qualified students should check the stated validity condition of their CSEET result when registering.
bullets: CSEET route: passed 10+2 or equivalent and passed CSEET.
CS Foundation route: passed ICSI CS Foundation.
Direct-entry routes: graduate/postgraduate; ICAI Intermediate pass; ICMAI Final pass; or eligible five-year integrated-programme entrants.
Provisional route: eligible final-year/final-semester undergraduate or sixth-semester integrated-programme students.

sections.heading: Programme and examination format
paragraphs: The active Executive curriculum is ICSI Syllabus 2022, introduced for Executive registration from 1 February 2023 and first examined in December 2023. It has two groups and seven papers. ICSI’s current academic portal publishes the applicable study material and session-specific supplements, including updated material for the 2026 examination cycle.

Before enrolling for an Executive examination, Syllabus 2022 students must pass the ICSI Pre-Examination Test. In addition, ICSI identifies TDOP as mandatory for students registered in the Executive Programme on or after 1 February 2025, with completion required before examination-form filing. Examination timetables, mode instructions, centres, form windows and session-specific requirements should be checked on ICSI’s examinations page because they can change by session.
bullets: Group 1 has four papers; Group 2 has three papers.
Pre-Examination Test: required for eligibility to enrol and appear under Syllabus 2022.
TDOP: an examination-form prerequisite for the specified post-1-February-2025 Executive registrations.
Use ICSI’s published timetable and exam notices for the current session rather than relying on prior cut-off dates.

sections.heading: How to register and enrol
paragraphs: Registration is completed online through ICSI; the Institute’s FAQ states that a downloaded registration form is not accepted. Applicants should select the appropriate route—CSEET/CS Foundation or direct admission—submit the requested qualification and identity documents in their ICSI account, and pay the applicable fee. ICSI says physical copies are not normally required unless it specifically requests them for verification.

Fee context is time-sensitive. The schedule effective 15 April 2026 lists ₹18,900 for CSEET/CS Foundation entrants and ₹23,900 for the listed direct-entry categories, comprising registration, education, pre-examination-test and TDOP fees; an optional journal subscription is additional. The same schedule lists the Executive examination fee as ₹1,500 per group. Concessions are separately published for eligible categories, so the final amount may differ.
bullets: Create or access the ICSI student account and choose the relevant Executive registration route.
Upload required documents and await/document completion as directed by ICSI.
Complete TDOP and the Pre-Examination Test where applicable.
Submit the separate examination enrolment/form and examination fee for the intended session.

sections.heading: Preparing effectively
paragraphs: Start with ICSI’s own Executive Syllabus 2022 study materials and use only the edition and session supplements that ICSI identifies as applicable to the target examination. The academic portal lists the seven Executive papers, while ICSI’s e-cart/study-material page identifies revised 2026 material for most Executive papers and the currently listed Tax Laws & Practice edition.

Build practice around the official question papers and current legal/tax updates. ICSI’s syllabus notes that candidates are expected to track relevant developments up to the prescribed cut-off dates for each examination session; therefore, preparation should include the official supplements and amendments rather than relying solely on older notes. Complete the mandatory Pre-Examination Test and TDOP early enough to avoid an administrative barrier to exam enrolment.
bullets: Map a study plan separately to Group 1 and Group 2, then decide examination-group enrolment based on ICSI’s current session rules.
Use ICSI study material, supplements and official past question papers for paper-specific practice.
Maintain a session-specific amendments register for company, securities, tax, labour and commercial-law changes.
Finish TDOP and the Pre-Examination Test before the examination-form window closes.

sections.heading: What follows after passing
paragraphs: Passing CS Executive makes a student eligible to register for ICSI’s CS Professional Programme, which is the next examination stage in the Company Secretaryship route. It can also be the point at which a student begins the ICSI long-term practical-training pathway after meeting the relevant training and development-programme requirements; ICSI’s long-term-training agreement specifies commencement after passing Executive and completing one month of EDP.

For a separate interim credential, an Executive pass holder who also completes the prescribed Executive Development Programme/equivalent and practical training may apply for ICSI’s Secretarial Executive Certificate. ICSI describes this as recognition for Executive-qualified, semi-qualified professionals; it does not confer ICSI membership or the rights of a member. Job titles such as compliance executive, corporate governance associate, or secretarial executive are possible employment directions rather than automatic outcomes of passing the examination.
bullets: Next academic stage: CS Professional Programme registration.
Training direction: long-term practical training after Executive pass and the stipulated development-programme requirement.
Optional recognition route: Secretarial Executive Certificate, subject to additional conditions.
Professional membership requires completing the full ICSI pathway and membership requirements; CS Executive alone is insufficient.

title: CS Professional
description: CS Professional — professional exam (finance), conducted by ICSI.

quick_facts.label: Administering body
quick_facts.value: The CS Professional Programme is the Professional stage of the Company Secretaryship course administered by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI).

quick_facts.label: Entry requirement
quick_facts.value: Applicants must have passed both groups of the CS Executive Programme under the same syllabus to register for the Professional Programme.

quick_facts.label: Current syllabus structure
quick_facts.value: Under ICSI Syllabus 2022, the Professional Programme has seven papers across two groups, including one selected paper from each of two elective sets.

quick_facts.label: Exam cadence
quick_facts.value: ICSI states that Executive and Professional examinations are conducted twice yearly, in June and December.

quick_facts.label: Pre-examination condition
quick_facts.value: Students registered under ICSI Syllabus 2022 must successfully complete the online Pre-Examination Test before enrolling for and appearing in the Professional examination.

quick_facts.label: Fees — dated context
quick_facts.value: ICSI's fee schedule effective 15 April 2026 lists ₹19,000 education fee plus ₹1,000 Pre-Examination Test fee for Professional registration after Executive; it lists examination fee of ₹1,800 per group, effective from the December 2024 examination session. Fees, concessions and session rules can change.

sections.heading: Purpose and place in the CS pathway
paragraphs: CS Professional is the advanced academic examination stage that follows the CS Executive Programme. Under ICSI Syllabus 2022, its compulsory coverage includes ESG and governance, drafting and appearances, compliance management/audit/due diligence, strategic management and corporate finance, and corporate restructuring, valuation and insolvency, alongside two chosen electives.

The syllabus describes practical professional aims: for example, the drafting paper is intended to build capability in agreements, documents, applications to quasi-judicial bodies, pleadings and appearances. This makes the stage relevant to corporate-governance, compliance, secretarial, transaction, audit and regulatory-practice work.
bullets: It is not an entry-level test: registration follows passing the complete CS Executive Programme.

Passing the examination is an important milestone toward ICSI membership, but ICSI also requires completion of applicable training requirements before a person becomes entitled to be enrolled as a member.

sections.heading: Eligibility and timing
paragraphs: ICSI's student-services FAQ, updated 10 April 2026, says a student who has passed both Executive groups under the same syllabus is eligible to register for the Professional Programme. Passing Executive groups under different syllabi does not qualify the student for admission under that FAQ.

For eligibility to the Professional examination itself, ICSI states that at least nine calendar months must have elapsed after passing the Executive examination. Under Syllabus 2022, successful completion of the Pre-Examination Test is also required before examination enrolment.
bullets: For a June session, ICSI's April 2026 FAQ gives Professional-registration cut-offs of 30 November of the preceding year for both groups and 31 January of the examination year for one group.
For a December session, the stated cut-offs are 31 May for both groups and 31 July for one group.
These are published cut-offs and may be revised; applicants should verify the applicable session notice in ICSI's SMASH portal before acting.

sections.heading: Syllabus and examination format
paragraphs: The current ICSI Syllabus 2022 places the seven Professional papers in two groups. Group 1 comprises ESG – Principles & Practice, Drafting, Pleadings & Appearances, Compliance Management, Audit & Due Diligence, and one Elective 1 paper. Group 2 comprises Strategic Management & Corporate Finance, Corporate Restructuring, Valuation & Insolvency, and one Elective 2 paper.

Each elective slot requires a selection from ICSI's prescribed choices. The currently published study-material portal lists Elective 1 choices including CSR & Social Governance, Internal & Forensic Audit, Intellectual Property Rights, AI/Data Analytics/Cyber Security laws, Advanced Direct Tax, and IFSCA regulations; it lists Elective 2 choices including Arbitration/Mediation, GST & Corporate Tax Planning, Labour Laws, Banking & Insurance, and Insolvency and Bankruptcy.

ICSI conducts the Professional examinations in June and December. The Institute publishes session-specific timetables, study-material updates and supplements, so candidates should use the session applicable to their attempt rather than relying on older paper lists or amendments.
bullets: Group 1: three compulsory papers plus one Elective 1.
Group 2: two compulsory papers plus one Elective 2.
The official syllabus assigns 100 marks across the stated components of individual Professional papers.

sections.heading: Registration and examination enrolment
paragraphs: After passing both Executive groups under the same syllabus, candidates submit the Professional-registration request exclusively through ICSI's SMASH portal. ICSI's April 2026 FAQ says physical or downloaded application forms are not accepted. The portal workflow includes selecting the mandatory optional subjects, proceeding to payment, then downloading the Professional Registration Letter and student identity card after successful payment.

Professional registration and examination enrolment are separate steps. For each examination session, ICSI requires an online examination-enrolment request through SMASH. Its April 2026 FAQ lists recurring form windows of 26 February–25 March without late fee and 26 March–9 April with late fee for June examinations; for December, it lists 26 August–25 September without late fee and 26 September–10 October with late fee.

As dated fee context, ICSI's schedule effective 15 April 2026 states Professional registration charges of ₹20,000 in total (₹19,000 education fee and ₹1,000 Pre-Examination Test fee). The stated general examination fee is ₹1,800 per group, and ICSI lists concessions for SC/ST and physically handicapped students. Candidates should confirm the fees and deadlines shown in their live SMASH request because they are subject to change.
bullets: 1. Pass both CS Executive groups under the same syllabus.
2. Submit Professional registration online in SMASH and select the required electives.
3. Complete the online Pre-Examination Test.
4. Submit the separate online examination-enrolment request and pay the applicable session fee.
5. Download the admit card from ICSI when it is made available; ICSI's FAQ says it can be accessed 10 days before examinations commence.

sections.heading: Preparation approach using official materials
paragraphs: Begin with ICSI's current Professional Programme study-material page and select materials for the two electives actually chosen at registration. ICSI publishes updated materials and, where relevant, session-specific supplements; for example, the portal flags GST & Corporate Tax Planning material for the June 2026 examination onwards.

Build preparation around the applied outcomes in the syllabus rather than only memorisation. The prescribed papers combine governance and sustainability reporting, drafting and appearances before regulatory or quasi-judicial bodies, compliance/audit/due diligence, corporate-finance decisions, restructuring and insolvency. Use the official syllabus to make a topic-by-topic plan, then practise with ICSI guideline answers from the applicable syllabus and session.

Complete the required online Pre-Examination Test early enough to avoid blocking examination enrolment. ICSI's June 2026 instructions required it no later than one working day before the relevant enrolment cut-off at 5:30 PM; candidates should check their own session's instruction because operational deadlines can change.
bullets: Use the official Syllabus 2022 as the master checklist of outcomes and subtopics.
Use current ICSI study materials and session supplements, particularly for tax, regulatory and other amendable subjects.
Use ICSI guideline answers to practise answer structure and application of law to facts.
Treat the Pre-Examination Test and examination-enrolment deadline as separate compliance tasks.

sections.heading: What passing leads to
paragraphs: A successful Professional Programme candidate receives ICSI's Professional Programme pass credential: ICSI's current student-services FAQ says a hard-copy mark sheet and pass certificate are issued to candidates who pass the Professional Programme.

Passing Professional alone should not be treated as automatic ICSI membership. ICSI states that a Professional-pass student's registration may need continuation until all training requirements are completed so that the student becomes entitled to enrol as a member. The exact training pathway depends on the applicable Company Secretaries Regulations and ICSI training rules.

For those planning independent practice, membership is also not itself a Certificate of Practice. ICSI states that a member seeking to enter practice must meet Certificate-of-Practice conditions; members intending to enter practice on or after 1 April 2023 are generally required to complete the PCS Orientation Programme before applying, subject to specified exemptions.
bullets: Professional pass certificate and hard-copy marks documentation are issued by ICSI to successful Professional candidates.
Complete all applicable training and membership formalities to become entitled to ICSI membership.
A Certificate of Practice is a separate post-membership step for those wishing to practise.
