title: CSEET
description: CSEET — professional exam (finance), conducted by ICSI.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: CSEET is the Company Secretary Executive Entrance Test, the entrance examination in ICSI’s Company Secretary course pathway before the CS Executive Programme.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: It is conducted by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI), a professional body constituted under the Company Secretaries Act, 1980 and functioning under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

quick_facts.label: Current structure
quick_facts.value: The restructured, centre-based CSEET took effect from the June 2026 session; it is held three times yearly, in the first weeks of February, June and October.

quick_facts.label: Basic eligibility
quick_facts.value: Only Indian nationals who have passed or are appearing in the Senior Secondary (10+2) examination or an equivalent examination may register for CSEET.

quick_facts.label: Papers and marks
quick_facts.value: There are four 100-mark papers: Business Communication; Fundamentals of Accounting; Economic and Business Environment; and Business Laws and Management. The first three are subjective papers; Business Laws and Management is OMR-based.

quick_facts.label: Passing standard
quick_facts.value: To pass in one sitting, a candidate must score at least 40% in each paper and 50% in aggregate; ICSI provides no paper exemption or carry-forward of marks in CSEET.

quick_facts.label: Fees and validity
quick_facts.value: Under ICSI’s restructured-CSEET FAQ published for the 2026 structure, registration is ₹7,500 (including SIP and free online classes) and each exam-session enrolment is ₹1,500. Registration remains valid for three years; a passing result is valid for one year. Fees and policies can change, so candidates should confirm them for their intended session.

sections.heading: Purpose and position in the CS pathway
paragraphs: CSEET is not a general finance entrance test; it is ICSI’s entry examination for the Company Secretary qualification route. ICSI presents the sequence as CSEET, CS Executive Programme, CS Professional Programme, pre-membership training and then CS membership. Its stated restructured assessment focus includes conceptual understanding, analytical ability, communication skills and professional aptitude intended to prepare entrants for the Executive and Professional stages.
source_urls
bullets: Passing CSEET, together with meeting the Senior Secondary requirement, enables a student to register for the CS Executive Programme.
Graduates/postgraduates and certain specified ICSI, CA and CMA candidates may be exempt from CSEET and use the direct-entry route to CS Executive instead.

sections.heading: Who can take CSEET—and who may not need to
paragraphs: For the restructured CSEET, ICSI states that applicants must be Indian nationals and must have passed or be appearing in Senior Secondary (10+2) or an equivalent examination. This means Commerce in Classes 11–12 is a useful academic background but is not stated as an exclusive eligibility condition.

ICSI lists several categories that can register directly for CS Executive rather than taking CSEET: CS Foundation pass candidates; graduates and postgraduates; CA Intermediate-pass students; CMA Final-pass students; eligible final-year/final-semester three-year undergraduate students on a provisional basis; and eligible students in recognised five-year integrated programmes, including certain sixth-semester students on a provisional basis.
bullets: CSEET registration is valid for three years from the month of registration.
A CSEET result is valid for one year from its declaration date; a successful candidate should complete CS Executive registration within that period.

Students registered under the restructured system must complete the one-day Student Induction Programme (SIP) within one month of CSEET registration, and SIP completion is required before CSEET exam enrolment.

sections.heading: Exam format, subjects and assessment
paragraphs: From the June 2026 session onward, CSEET is conducted at designated examination centres rather than through the previous remote-proctored format. It is spread across four examination days: three subjective papers of three hours each—Business Communication, Fundamentals of Accounting, and Economic and Business Environment—and one two-hour OMR-based paper, Business Laws and Management.

Each paper carries 100 marks. Economic and Business Environment is divided into Economics (50 marks) and Business Environment (50 marks); Business Laws and Management is divided into Business Laws (60 marks) and Business Management (40 marks). ICSI’s FAQ says there is no negative marking for wrong answers in OMR-based papers.
bullets: Business Communication covers English usage, communication, business correspondence and business terminology.
Fundamentals of Accounting covers accounting principles and process, bank reconciliation, depreciation, final accounts, partnership/LLP accounts, company accounts and not-for-profit accounts.
Economic and Business Environment covers economics, the Indian economy and financial markets, entrepreneurship, regulators, global environment, sustainability, AI and corporate governance.
Business Laws and Management covers introductory law, company law, contracts, partnership/LLP, sale of goods, negotiable instruments and management principles/functions.

sections.heading: Registration and examination enrolment
paragraphs: The process has two practical stages: first register for CSEET through ICSI’s online student-registration system; then separately enrol for the selected examination session after completing SIP. ICSI says offline applications are not accepted for exam enrolment, and its registration portal provides the CSEET registration route.

For the standard restructured calendar, CSEET registration windows are November 1–February 28/29 for the June session, March 1–June 30 for the October session, and July 1–October 31 for the February session. ICSI’s published schedule sets separate examination-enrolment windows, including late-fee windows, so a candidate should verify the live notice for the specific session before paying.
bullets: As published for the 2026 restructured scheme, registration fee is ₹7,500, including SIP and online classes; examination fee is ₹1,500 per session.
Published fee concessions apply to specified categories, including SC/ST and persons with disabilities; further category and regional concessions are listed by ICSI.

For the standard schedule, exam enrolment with normal fee is March 16–April 15 for June, July 16–August 15 for October, and November 16–December 15 for February; late-fee windows follow. These dates are schedule-dependent and should be treated as variable.

sections.heading: How to prepare using ICSI materials
paragraphs: Start with the restructured syllabus applicable from June 2026, because the revised CSEET changed both the delivery mode and paper pattern. Build a subject-wise plan around the four papers, reserving written-answer practice for the three subjective papers and timed OMR practice for Business Laws and Management.

ICSI states that study material is made available at registration and on its website, and that free online classes are conducted for registered CSEET students for each session. ICSI also publishes sample question papers and question papers; these are particularly useful for learning the expected scope and for timed practice.
bullets: Use the official syllabus as the checklist rather than relying solely on coaching notes.
Practise accounting problems and written presentation for the subjective papers.
Practise reading and answering OMR questions within the two-hour limit for Business Laws and Management.
Complete SIP early: it is a prerequisite for exam enrolment, not merely an orientation activity.

sections.heading: What passing CSEET leads to
paragraphs: A CSEET pass is the normal entry point from the 10+2 route into ICSI’s CS Executive Programme. The candidate must use the result within one year to register for CS Executive. Passing CSEET does not itself confer Company Secretary membership or authorise professional practice; it is an entrance-stage milestone in the longer CS qualification pathway.

The broader Company Secretary pathway includes CS Executive and CS Professional examinations followed by prescribed pre-membership training and ICSI membership. ICSI describes Company Secretary roles in areas such as board advisory, compliance, corporate governance, risk management and secretarial/compliance audit; these are professional-pathway outcomes rather than guaranteed jobs or salary outcomes from passing CSEET alone.
bullets: Next immediate academic/professional step: register for the CS Executive Programme within the one-year result-validity period.
Longer route: pass CS Executive, pass CS Professional, complete applicable training requirements, then seek ICSI membership.

Students who later complete undergraduate programmes such as B.Com, BBA, BCA, BA LL.B. or B.Com LL.B. may also have degree-based direct-entry options for CS Executive, but CSEET eligibility itself remains available from the 10+2 stage.

title: CSIR-UGC NET
description: CSIR-UGC NET — eligibility exam (science), conducted by NTA / CSIR HRDG.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: A national eligibility examination in Science & Technology conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) on behalf of CSIR, for Junior Research Fellowship (JRF), Assistant Professor eligibility, and/or Ph.D. admission in Indian universities and colleges.

quick_facts.label: June 2026 exam subjects
quick_facts.value: The June 2026 cycle covered Chemical Sciences; Earth, Atmospheric, Ocean and Planetary Sciences; Life Sciences; Mathematical Sciences; and Physical Sciences.

quick_facts.label: Exam mode and duration
quick_facts.value: For the June 2026 cycle, the examination was a three-hour, objective-type multiple-choice Computer Based Test (CBT).

quick_facts.label: Primary postgraduate eligibility
quick_facts.value: For June 2026, General/Unreserved/General-EWS candidates needed at least 55% in a recognised master's degree or equivalent; OBC-NCL, SC, ST, PwD/PwBD and third-gender candidates needed at least 50%. Final-year/result-awaited master's candidates could apply provisionally, subject to later completion requirements.

quick_facts.label: Four-year bachelor's route
quick_facts.value: For June 2026, candidates with a four-year/eight-semester bachelor's degree required at least 75% aggregate marks (with a stated 5-percentage-point relaxation for specified categories). Qualification through this route could lead to JRF and Ph.D. admission, but not Assistant Professor appointment eligibility.

quick_facts.label: Age rules in June 2026
quick_facts.value: The JRF upper age limit was 30 years as of July 2026, with specified relaxations. There was no upper age limit for Assistant Professor eligibility or Ph.D. admission.

quick_facts.label: June 2026 application fee context
quick_facts.value: The June 2026 bulletin listed application fees of ₹1,150 for General, ₹600 for General-EWS/OBC-NCL, and ₹325 for SC/ST/PwD/PwBD/third-gender applicants, plus applicable payment-gateway charges. Fees can change by cycle.

sections.heading: Purpose and what qualifying means
paragraphs: CSIR-UGC NET is an eligibility examination rather than a degree programme or a direct recruitment examination. In the June 2026 framework, NTA conducted it on CSIR’s behalf for three result categories: (1) JRF plus Assistant Professor eligibility plus Ph.D. admission, (2) Assistant Professor eligibility plus Ph.D. admission, and (3) Ph.D. admission only.

A Category-1 JRF qualification supports research training under eligible supervisors and institutions. The bulletin states that the fellowships are accepted in universities, IITs, postgraduate colleges, government research establishments—including CSIR establishments—and recognised public- or private-sector industrial R&D organisations in India. Qualification does not itself guarantee employment.

For Category-2 and Category-3 candidates using NET for Ph.D. admission, the June 2026 bulletin states that the NET result is valid for one year for that purpose; the concerned university or higher-education institution uses a 70% written-test and 30% interview/viva-voce weighting. JRF-qualified candidates enter Ph.D. programmes through an interview under the applicable UGC Ph.D. regulations.
bullets: A qualifying certificate for Assistant Professor eligibility has no stated end-period of validity in the June 2026 bulletin.

A NET qualification may strengthen routes into doctoral research, academic teaching eligibility, and research roles, but an employer, laboratory, or university retains its own selection and appointment processes.

sections.heading: Eligibility: degree, marks, age, and nationality
paragraphs: For the June 2026 cycle, the examination was for bona fide Indian citizens. The usual route was a recognised master's degree or equivalent with at least 55% marks for General/Unreserved/General-EWS candidates, or 50% for OBC-NCL, SC, ST, PwD/PwBD and third-gender candidates. Candidates pursuing the qualifying master's degree, awaiting final results, or delayed by their qualifying examination could apply provisionally, subject to the bulletin’s completion deadlines and minimum marks.

A four-year/eight-semester bachelor's degree route was also available. Applicants needed at least 75% aggregate marks or the equivalent grade, with a 5% relaxation stated for SC, ST, OBC-NCL, differently abled, EWS and other categories as decided by the Commission. Candidates qualifying on this bachelor's-degree basis could receive JRF and pursue Ph.D. admission, but were not eligible for Assistant Professor appointment through that route.

For JRF in June 2026, applicants had to be no more than 30 years old as of July 2026. The bulletin provided up to five years’ relaxation for women and OBC-NCL, SC, ST, PwD/PwBD and third-gender candidates, as well as specified provisions for research experience and armed-forces service. It set no upper age limit for the Assistant Professor or Ph.D.-admission routes. Applicants should always check the information bulletin for their own cycle because eligibility rules and dates may be updated.
bullets: A four-year bachelor's student in the final semester/year could apply provisionally for JRF/Ph.D. routes, subject to completing the prescribed requirements after the result.
A foreign qualification should be assessed for equivalence through UGC; the bulletin also advises holders of Indian-institute postgraduate diplomas to establish master's equivalence where needed.

sections.heading: Test format and subjects
paragraphs: The June 2026 CSIR-UGC NET was delivered in CBT mode, in Hindi and English, with a three-hour duration and objective multiple-choice questions. It had three parts with no break between them. Part A is common across subjects and tests general aptitude; Part B covers conventional subject-related MCQs; and Part C asks higher-order analytical questions that require application of scientific concepts.

The five test papers were Chemical Sciences (701), Earth, Atmospheric, Ocean and Planetary Sciences (702), Life Sciences (703), Mathematical Sciences (704), and Physical Sciences (705). Each paper had a maximum score of 200, but question counts, permitted attempts, marks per question, and negative-marking rules differed by subject. Candidates should use the scheme for their own subject rather than assuming a common attempt limit.
CSIR HRDG publishes the subject syllabi and model question papers. These official materials are the appropriate base for mapping a preparation plan to Parts A, B, and C.
bullets: Part A: logical reasoning, graphical analysis, analytical and numerical ability, quantitative comparison, series formation, and puzzles.
Part B: syllabus-linked subject MCQs.
Part C: analytical, application-oriented scientific questions.
Negative marking applies according to the subject-specific scheme; for example, Mathematical Sciences had no negative marking in Part C in the June 2026 bulletin.

sections.heading: Application process and June 2026 cycle status
paragraphs: NTA’s June 2026 process was online-only through the Joint CSIR-UGC NET portal. The process required candidates to register using their own email address and mobile number, complete the application, upload the required photograph and signature files, pay the fee, and retain the confirmation page. The bulletin also required candidates to select four examination-city preferences.

For the June 2026 cycle, online applications were open from May 27 through June 19, 2026, fee payment closed on June 20, and the correction window ran June 22–23. The examination was scheduled for July 17–18, 2026. These are historical, cycle-specific dates and not a timetable for a future cycle; candidates should monitor the official NTA portal and bulletin for the next application notice.

For this cycle, the NTA issued the city-intimation notice on July 8 and the admit-card notice on July 13. The city-intimation slip was not an admit card; candidates needed to download the separate admit card using their application number and password.
bullets: Use a personal email address and mobile number; the bulletin says these cannot later be changed.
Keep the application number, confirmation page, admit card, and score card for future reference.
Check the correction-window rules carefully: some information can only be corrected during that limited period.

sections.heading: Preparation approach using official materials
paragraphs: Start by selecting the applicable subject paper and downloading its official CSIR HRDG syllabus. Turn each syllabus unit into a checklist, then distinguish between factual/revision-heavy Part B topics and the concept-application work expected in Part C. Maintain a separate aptitude practice track for the common Part A areas listed in the information bulletin.

Use CSIR HRDG’s official model papers to become familiar with the three-part structure, subject-specific attempt caps, and marking rules. In timed practice, stop attempting questions once the subject-specific permitted number has been reached; the bulletin notes that, where candidates answer more than the permitted number, only the first permitted responses are evaluated.

Review each mock or past-question attempt by error type: missing subject knowledge, a faulty calculation, misreading, excessive time spent, or an avoidable negative-marking risk. This creates a targeted revision plan while keeping practice aligned to the official syllabus and format.
bullets: Build conceptual fluency for Part C rather than relying solely on recall.
Practice Part A regularly because it is common to all five science papers.
Before the exam, re-check the current-cycle bulletin because question counts, permitted attempts, and negative marking are subject-specific and may be revised.

sections.heading: Outcomes: Ph.D., teaching eligibility, and research pathways
paragraphs: The result category matters. Category 1 confers eligibility for JRF, Assistant Professor appointment, and Ph.D. admission; Category 2 is for Assistant Professor appointment and Ph.D. admission but not JRF; Category 3 is for Ph.D. admission only. A score alone is not an appointment letter or Ph.D. offer, so candidates must still meet the recruiting institution’s or university’s programme-specific requirements.

As dated June 2026 fellowship context, a JRF selected through CSIR-NET was listed at ₹37,000 per month for the first two years, plus a ₹20,000 annual contingent grant reimbursed directly to the fellow. After two years, a fellow registered for a Ph.D. could be upgraded to SRF at ₹42,000 per month following assessment of research progress. These terms, fellowship numbers, and amounts are policy-dependent and can change.

The fellowship can be held at eligible academic, government-research, and recognised industrial R&D settings in India. This supports the node’s links to doctoral study and research-oriented careers, while actual research-scientist and government-scientist jobs require separate recruitment processes and eligibility criteria.
bullets: Assistant Professor certificate validity: no end-period is stated in the June 2026 bulletin.
Category-2 and Category-3 NET marks were valid for Ph.D. admission for one year from result declaration in the June 2026 framework.
The bulletin explicitly states that a JRF award is for a fixed tenure and does not guarantee subsequent employment.

title: CTET
description: CTET — eligibility exam (teaching), conducted by CBSE.

quick_facts.label: Conducting authority
quick_facts.value: The Ministry of Education entrusts CBSE, Delhi with conducting the Central Teacher Eligibility Test (CTET).

quick_facts.label: Teaching stages covered
quick_facts.value: CTET Paper I is for candidates intending to teach Classes I–V; Paper II is for Classes VI–VIII. Candidates intending both levels must take both papers.

quick_facts.label: Current September 2026 cycle
quick_facts.value: The September 2026 bulletin scheduled Paper II and Paper I for 6 September 2026, with 5 September available if candidate numbers require it. The published online-application and fee deadline was 10 June 2026; dates are cycle-specific and should be checked on CTET’s official site.

quick_facts.label: Certificate validity
quick_facts.value: The CTET qualifying certificate is stated to be valid for appointment for life for all categories; there is no limit on attempts, and qualified candidates may retake CTET to improve their score.

quick_facts.label: Appointment status
quick_facts.value: Passing CTET is an eligibility condition, not an offer of recruitment or employment. The relevant recruiting or appointing authority verifies final eligibility.

sections.heading: What CTET is for
paragraphs: CTET is the Central Teacher Eligibility Test: a teacher-eligibility examination connected to the minimum qualifications framework for appointment to teach Classes I–VIII under the Right to Education framework. CBSE describes the test as a national benchmark intended to support teacher quality in recruitment, and conducts it on behalf of the Ministry of Education.

A CTET result should be understood as a qualifying credential rather than a teaching job. A candidate must still meet the applicable professional qualifications and the recruiting organisation’s rules, then succeed in that organisation’s separate selection process where applicable.
bullets: Paper I aligns with the primary stage, Classes I–V.
Paper II aligns with the elementary/upper-primary stage, Classes VI–VIII.
For both stages, candidates must appear in both papers.

sections.heading: Eligibility: confirm qualifications against the applicable rules
paragraphs: CTET does not treat merely being allowed to sit the examination as final confirmation of appointment eligibility. CBSE directs candidates to the NCTE’s minimum-qualification regulations as amended from time to time, as well as the recruitment rules of the appropriate government, Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS), or Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS), as relevant.

Accordingly, a B.Ed. or D.El.Ed. pathway may be relevant to a prospective teacher’s qualification profile, but the candidate should match their exact academic and teacher-education credentials with the paper/stage sought and the rules of the prospective employer. The recruiting agency or appointing authority makes the final verification. The September 2026 bulletin also records that NCTE-notified relaxation of up to 5% in minimum educational-qualification marks may apply to specified reserved categories.
bullets: Check the current NCTE rules before applying.
Check the recruitment rules of the school system or employer targeted.
Keep evidence of educational and teacher-training qualifications ready for later employer verification.

sections.heading: Exam format and qualifying standard
paragraphs: For the September 2026 cycle, CTET uses multiple-choice questions with four options, one mark per question, and no negative marking. Each paper is 2 hours 30 minutes, has 150 questions, and carries 150 marks. The main question paper is bilingual in Hindi and English; candidates select two different languages for Language I and Language II from the listed options.

Paper I contains 30 questions each in Child Development and Pedagogy, Mathematics, Environmental Studies, Language I, and Language II. Paper II contains 30 questions each in Child Development and Pedagogy, Language I, and Language II, plus 60 questions in either Mathematics & Science or Social Studies/Social Science, depending on the teaching subject choice.

The bulletin states that a score of 60% or more is a TET pass. It also says that school managements may consider concessions for SC/ST, OBC, and differently abled candidates under their applicable reservation policies; candidates should therefore verify the particular recruitment notification rather than assume a universal relaxed cut-off.
bullets: Paper I: Classes I–V.
Paper II: Classes VI–VIII.
Both papers: 150 MCQs, 150 marks, 2 hours 30 minutes, and no negative marking for the September 2026 cycle.

sections.heading: Applying through the official portal
paragraphs: For the September 2026 cycle, CBSE required online application through the CTET or CBSE website. The published workflow was to complete the online form, note the registration/application number, upload a current photograph and signature, pay online, and retain the confirmation page. Candidates were not required to send a hard copy of the confirmation page to the CTET Unit.

Fees and deadlines vary by cycle. In the September 2026 bulletin, the stated examination fees were ₹1,000 for one paper or ₹1,200 for both papers for General/OBC (NCL) candidates, and ₹500 or ₹600 respectively for SC/ST/differently abled candidates, plus applicable bank GST. Those figures and the 10 June 2026 deadline are historical, cycle-specific context—not a fee or deadline for a future cycle.
bullets: Use only the official CTET/CBSE application route.
Read the current information bulletin before submitting the form.
Retain the confirmation page and monitor the official site for admit-card and correction-window notices.

sections.heading: Preparing effectively
paragraphs: Build preparation around the current official information bulletin and its syllabus, not only coaching material. CBSE advises candidates to use authentic textbooks and the syllabus suggested by NCTE. For Paper I, questions are based on NCERT Classes I–V topics, with difficulty and linkages potentially extending to the secondary stage. For Paper II, they are based on NCERT Classes VI–VIII topics, with difficulty and linkages potentially extending to senior-secondary level.

Give substantial study time to pedagogy as well as subject content: Child Development and Pedagogy is compulsory in both papers, and the official syllabus emphasizes diverse learners, inclusive education, learning processes, assessment, and subject-specific pedagogy. Use the official archive’s previous question papers to practise the question style and pacing.
bullets: Select the intended paper(s) first, then map study topics to the official syllabus.
Practise all compulsory components, including both language papers and pedagogy.
Use official past question papers as timed practice; they are not a substitute for checking the current bulletin for syllabus changes.

sections.heading: Where CTET can be used
paragraphs: CTET applies to Central Government schools, including KVS, NVS and Central Tibetan Schools, and to schools under the listed Union Territory administrations. The bulletin says unaided private schools may choose to consider CTET. State-government, local-body, and aided schools ordinarily consider their State TET, although a State Government may consider CTET if it decides not to conduct a State TET.

For CBSE-affiliated schools, the bulletin notes the amended affiliation bye-laws position that teachers appointed from 6 March 2012 to teach Classes I–VIII must qualify CTET or the appropriate Central/State TET. This does not override an employer’s separate academic, professional, subject, vacancy, reservation, interview, document-verification, and recruitment requirements.
Successful candidates receive digital CTET eligibility certificates and all candidates receive digital mark sheets through DigiLocker, according to the September 2026 bulletin.
bullets: Potential pathway: primary teaching roles for Classes I–V after Paper I, subject to employer rules.
Potential pathway: upper-primary teaching roles for Classes VI–VIII after Paper II, subject to employer rules.
CTET can strengthen eligibility for some private-school roles, but private schools may decide whether to consider it.

useful_links.label: CTET archive and previous question papers

title: CUET-PG
description: CUET-PG — pg entrance exam (general), conducted by NTA.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: CUET (PG) is the Common University Entrance Test for postgraduate admissions, conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) for central and other participating universities/institutions.

quick_facts.label: 2026 eligibility baseline
quick_facts.value: Applicants who have passed a bachelor’s degree/equivalent, or who were appearing in the final year of a bachelor’s/equivalent examination in 2026, could appear. Programme-level eligibility remains university-specific.

quick_facts.label: Age rule
quick_facts.value: There was no NTA age limit for CUET (PG) 2026, but a university could apply its own age requirements for admission.

quick_facts.label: Test format (2026 cycle)
quick_facts.value: The 2026 examination was computer-based. Each question paper ran for 90 minutes and contained 75 multiple-choice questions; candidates could select up to four question-paper codes.

quick_facts.label: Scoring (2026 cycle)
quick_facts.value: Each correct response carried +4 marks, each incorrect response incurred −1 mark, and unattempted questions received no marks.

quick_facts.label: Who handles admission
quick_facts.value: NTA conducts the test and issues scores; participating universities prepare merit lists and run their own counselling and admissions.

quick_facts.label: 2026 score validity
quick_facts.value: The CUET (PG) 2026 NTA score is valid only for the 2026–27 academic year.

sections.heading: Purpose and place in postgraduate admissions
paragraphs: CUET (PG) is a common entrance examination used for admissions to postgraduate programmes at participating universities. NTA states that it was introduced in 2022 to provide a common platform and wider access to postgraduate admissions; for the 2026 cycle, its scores were intended for participating universities’ 2026–27 admissions.

Taking CUET (PG) is not itself an admission offer. NTA’s role ends with registration, testing, answer-key processes, results and scorecards; each participating university applies its own programme eligibility, reservation rules, merit process and counselling arrangements.
bullets: Use the participating-university listings to identify whether a target institution accepts CUET (PG).
Then check that university’s programme page for the required CUET question-paper code, qualifying degree/subject requirements, category rules, seats and its separate admission/counselling process.

sections.heading: Eligibility: examination access versus admission eligibility
paragraphs: For CUET (PG) 2026, candidates who had completed a bachelor’s degree or equivalent, or who were taking the final-year bachelor’s/equivalent examination in 2026, were eligible to sit the test. NTA set no examination age limit for that cycle.

This is only the baseline to take the exam. Admission eligibility can differ by university and programme—for example, a university may prescribe a particular undergraduate discipline, minimum marks, subject combination, age condition or reservation documentation. NTA expressly says that appearing in CUET (PG) does not by itself entitle a candidate to admission.
bullets: Match your intended programme to its accepted question-paper code before applying.
Read the target university’s current postgraduate admission bulletin before relying on general CUET eligibility.
Keep qualifying-degree and category/disability documents ready for the university’s verification stage.

sections.heading: Examination format and language
paragraphs: In the 2026 cycle, CUET (PG) was conducted only as a computer-based test (CBT). Each selected question paper lasted 90 minutes and had 75 MCQs. Candidates could choose up to four question-paper codes, subject to the courses and codes accepted by their prospective universities.

The 2026 marking scheme awarded four marks for a correct response and deducted one mark for a wrong response; no marks were awarded for unanswered questions. Humanities, science and common-subject papers were generally bilingual in English and Hindi. The bulletin specified exceptions for language, M.Tech/higher-science and Acharya papers, and stated that the English version is final in a discrepancy except for language and Acharya papers.
bullets: Plan paper choices from university programme mappings rather than selecting papers only because they appear related to an undergraduate degree.
Practice on a computer and time 75-question sets to a 90-minute limit.
Use the official syllabus for the exact question-paper code; preparation content is code-specific.

sections.heading: Application process and 2026 fee context
paragraphs: CUET (PG) applications are submitted online through the NTA CUET (PG) portal. The 2026 bulletin required one application form per candidate, registration with a unique mobile number and email address, completion of personal and academic details, paper and city choices, uploads, online fee payment, and saving the confirmation page after successful payment.

For context only, the 2026 application window ran from December 14, 2025 to January 14, 2026, with a correction window from January 18 to January 20, 2026; these dates are past and should not be treated as a schedule for a later cycle. The 2026 base fee for up to two papers was ₹1,400 for General candidates, ₹1,200 for Gen-EWS/OBC-NCL, ₹1,100 for SC/ST/Third Gender, and ₹1,000 for PwD/PwBD, plus applicable payment-processing charges/GST. Later cycles may change dates and fees.
bullets: Apply only through the official NTA portal when registration opens.
Complete fee payment and download the confirmation page; an application is not complete without successful payment.
Use your own accessible email and mobile number, and monitor the NTA portal for city-intimation, admit-card, answer-key and result notices.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Start with the official syllabus for the exact CUET (PG) question-paper code required by each target programme. NTA publishes the paper-code list and directs candidates to the official syllabus; because similar programme titles may be mapped to different codes by different universities, confirming each university’s mapping should come before building a study plan.

Prepare for the actual CBT format: 75 MCQs in 90 minutes with negative marking. In practice, this means combining subject revision with timed computer-based question practice, an attempt strategy that accounts for the −1 penalty, and review of mistakes by syllabus topic.
bullets: Create a target-university and programme list, then record the accepted question-paper codes beside each programme.
Download the official syllabus and divide it into revision units.
Take timed 90-minute mock tests; review incorrect and skipped questions separately.
Practise only with the medium and paper-specific conventions applicable to your chosen code.

sections.heading: After the examination: scorecards, merit and counselling
paragraphs: After the examination, NTA hosts provisional answer keys and recorded responses for challenge, finalises answer keys, declares results and hosts scorecards. NTA does not conduct counselling or create the final admission merit list; participating universities receive score data and conduct their own admissions.

For the 2026 cycle, the NTA FAQ says the score was valid only for academic year 2026–27. Candidates therefore needed to follow each target university’s separate admission portal and timetable after receiving a CUET (PG) score. The NTA participating-university list is dynamic, so it should be checked alongside the relevant university’s own admissions notices.
bullets: Download and preserve the NTA scorecard.
Register separately wherever a participating university requires a post-result application or counselling registration.
Check each university’s eligibility verification, merit/allotment notices, fee deadlines and document-verification requirements.
Do not assume that a score, a particular rank expectation or inclusion in NTA’s university list guarantees a seat.

title: CUET-UG
description: CUET-UG — ug entrance exam (general), conducted by NTA.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: The National Testing Agency (NTA), an autonomous organization under India’s Ministry of Education, conducts CUET-UG.

quick_facts.label: What it is for
quick_facts.value: CUET-UG is a common entrance test whose scores are used by Central Universities and other participating universities/institutions for undergraduate admissions.

quick_facts.label: Eligibility baseline for CUET-UG 2026
quick_facts.value: There was no age limit; candidates who had passed Class 12/equivalent or were appearing in 2026 could sit the test, subject to the admission conditions of their target university and programme.

quick_facts.label: 2026 test structure
quick_facts.value: CUET-UG 2026 offered 37 tests—13 languages, 23 domain subjects, and one General Aptitude Test. A candidate could choose up to five tests.

quick_facts.label: 2026 delivery and marking
quick_facts.value: The 2026 examination used computer-based testing. Each test paper had 50 compulsory multiple-choice questions in 60 minutes, with +5 for a correct answer and −1 for an incorrect answer.

quick_facts.label: Score use
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, the NTA score was valid only for admission to the 2026–27 academic year; individual universities conducted their own merit-list and admission processes.

sections.heading: Purpose and place in undergraduate admissions
paragraphs: CUET-UG is a national common entrance examination for undergraduate programmes. NTA’s role is to register candidates, conduct the test, host answer-key challenges, declare NTA scores, and provide scorecards. The participating university—not NTA—sets the programme-level eligibility, prepares the merit list, and manages counselling or admission.

For students coming from arts, commerce, PCM, PCB, or PCMB in Classes 11–12, CUET-UG can support applications to a broad range of participating-university programmes. It is not itself an admission offer: a candidate must meet the specific university’s required Class 12 subjects, marks, category rules, documentation requirements, and any other admission conditions.
bullets: Use CUET-UG to seek admission to programmes at Central Universities and other participating state, deemed, private, autonomous, or other institutions.
Check the intended university’s programme mapping before selecting CUET papers; the participating-university list and programme offerings can change.
Do not assume that a CUET score alone guarantees a seat.

sections.heading: Eligibility: exam eligibility versus course eligibility
paragraphs: For CUET-UG 2026, NTA imposed no age limit. Candidates who had passed Class 12 (or an equivalent qualifying examination), or who were appearing in Class 12/equivalent in 2026, could take the examination. Recognized qualifying routes included 10+2 examinations of recognized boards, certain pre-university examinations, NIOS senior secondary examinations, specified diplomas, and recognized international qualifications.

This exam-level permission does not replace course eligibility. A university may impose its own age limit, minimum marks, required Class 12 subjects, accepted qualifying-examination year, reservation requirements, or additional criteria. Students should therefore first choose target programmes and then select only the CUET tests required by those programmes.
bullets: There was no CUET-UG 2026 age limit, but a target university could apply one.
Candidates could choose CUET tests irrespective of their Class 12 subjects for the exam; however, university programme requirements still governed admission eligibility.
Candidates with overseas or otherwise unlisted Class 12-equivalent qualifications may need an equivalence certificate as specified by NTA and the admitting university.

sections.heading: CUET-UG 2026 format
paragraphs: CUET-UG 2026 was conducted only as a computer-based test (CBT), in multiple shifts as required by candidate volume and subject choices. Question papers were available in 13 Indian languages: Assamese, Bengali, English, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, and Urdu. Where a bilingual paper was used, the English version prevailed in case of a discrepancy.

The 2026 catalogue comprised 13 language tests, 23 domain-specific tests, and the General Aptitude Test. Candidates could select a maximum of five tests, including languages and the General Aptitude Test. Each selected test paper had 50 compulsory objective MCQs and a 60-minute duration. The published marking rule was +5 for a correct response, −1 for an incorrect response, and 0 for an unanswered question.
bullets: Language tests assess reading comprehension, literary aptitude, and vocabulary.
Domain-subject syllabi are based on NCERT syllabi.
The General Aptitude Test covers general knowledge and current affairs, mental ability, numerical/quantitative reasoning, and logical and analytical reasoning.
PwBD candidates eligible for compensatory time were provided 20 minutes for each hour of examination.

sections.heading: Application process and 2026 fee context
paragraphs: The CUET-UG 2026 process was online through the NTA CUET portal. Applicants registered to obtain an application number, completed personal and education details, selected universities/programmes and test papers, chose examination-city preferences, uploaded the required photograph, signature, and applicable disability/identity documents, paid the fee online, and saved the confirmation page. NTA instructed candidates to submit only one application form.

For context only, the original 2026 bulletin scheduled applications for January 3–30, 2026, followed by a January 31 fee-payment deadline and a February 2–4 correction window; NTA subsequently issued separate notices about registration and deadline extensions. These dates are past and should not be reused for a later cycle. Prospective applicants should rely on the live CUET-UG notice board and the relevant year’s information bulletin.

The 2026 fee was variable by category and number of selected subjects. For up to three subjects, it was ₹1,000 for General candidates, ₹900 for OBC-NCL/EWS candidates, ₹800 for SC/ST/PwD/PwBD/third-gender candidates, and ₹4,500 at centres outside India; additional-subject charges applied. Bank/payment-gateway charges and GST could be additional. These are dated 2026 figures, not a forecast for future cycles.
bullets: Read the target university prospectus before submitting the form; confirm required CUET subjects, Class 12 prerequisites, minimum marks, and admission procedures.
Use an email address and mobile number that remain accessible, retain the application number, and download the confirmation page after successful payment.
Monitor official notices for any correction window, city-intimation slip, admit card, answer-key challenge, and scorecard updates.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Begin with reverse planning from the intended degree and university. Identify each programme’s prescribed CUET subjects, then download the official syllabus for every selected language, domain subject, and/or General Aptitude Test. This matters especially for applicants whose school stream is broad: for example, a commerce, humanities, science, or vocational student should select papers based on the receiving programme’s stated requirements rather than on assumptions about the stream alone.

Prepare domain papers from the applicable NCERT-aligned syllabus, build language-test skill through timed comprehension, vocabulary, and literary-aptitude practice, and prepare General Aptitude through current-affairs awareness plus numerical, logical, and analytical-reasoning practice. Since every paper is a 60-minute CBT with all 50 questions compulsory and negative marking, use full-length computer-based practice to refine pacing, accuracy, and question-selection discipline.
bullets: Make a paper-selection sheet: target university, programme, mandatory Class 12 subjects, required CUET tests, and admission portal/counselling steps.
Use the official subject syllabus rather than relying solely on coaching-material topic lists.
Review mistakes by category—concept gap, careless error, time-management issue, or incorrect guess—to reduce the impact of −1 marking.
Keep university admissions separate from exam preparation: after results, monitor every target university’s merit-list and counselling notices.

sections.heading: Results, counselling, and next steps
paragraphs: NTA calculates results from the final answer key. For papers held in multiple shifts, raw marks are converted into an NTA Score using the published multi-shift procedure. In the 2026 cycle, NTA stated that the resulting score was valid only for the 2026–27 academic year, and that there would be no re-evaluation or re-checking after the result.

A CUET score enables participation in admissions at universities that accept the relevant score, but it does not grant admission automatically. Each institution applies its own programme eligibility, merit/rank rules, document verification, medical-fitness requirements where applicable, reservation rules, and counselling schedule. The student must therefore complete the separate university admission/counselling process and act on that university’s deadlines.

The range of possible academic outcomes includes undergraduate routes such as BA, B.Com, B.Sc, BBA, BCA, B.Voc, agriculture-related degrees, and integrated law or other programmes where a participating university lists CUET-UG for that course. Availability, required papers, seat counts, and admission cut-offs are university- and year-specific.
bullets: Download and retain the scorecard, confirmation page, and admit card.
Follow each target university’s admissions portal after NTA results; NTA does not conduct university counselling or publish the final institutional merit list.
Treat participating-university and programme lists as dynamic, and verify the current mapping directly with the university before making decisions.

title: DBT-JRF (BET)
description: DBT-JRF (BET) — doctoral or fellowship exam (science), conducted by DBT.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: The Biotechnology Eligibility Test (BET) is the national qualifying examination used for award of doctoral research fellowships under the Department of Biotechnology (DBT) Junior Research Fellowship (DBT-JRF) programme.

quick_facts.label: Administering arrangement
quick_facts.value: For BET 2026, DBT conducted the programme through its nodal agency, the Regional Centre for Biotechnology (RCB), Faridabad; the examination bulletin identifies the National Testing Agency (NTA) as the testing agency for the CBT process.

quick_facts.label: Who can apply
quick_facts.value: The 2026 notice permits bona fide Indian citizens residing in India who hold specified four-year UG, B.Tech/B.E., or relevant master's/equivalent qualifications in biotechnology, life sciences, or allied disciplines, subject to marks and age requirements.

quick_facts.label: Exam mode and duration
quick_facts.value: BET 2026 was an English-language, computer-based, multiple-choice examination of 180 minutes; it was scheduled for 17 May 2026, 3:00 PM–6:00 PM.

quick_facts.label: Merit categories
quick_facts.value: BET produces Category-I and Category-II merit lists. Category-I supports activation of the DBT-JRF after PhD enrolment and registration; Category-II does not itself confer a DBT-JRF fellowship, but may support appointment to a DBT-sponsored project subject to the project/institutional selection process.

quick_facts.label: 2026 fee context
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, the non-refundable examination fee was ₹1,300 for General/OBC-NCL/EWS candidates and ₹650 for SC/ST/PwD candidates, plus applicable payment processing charges and GST. Fees are cycle-specific and should be checked in the current notice.

sections.heading: Purpose and place in the doctoral-research pathway
paragraphs: DBT-JRF (BET) is not a college-admission examination. It is an all-India qualifying examination for a DBT doctoral research fellowship in biotechnology and life sciences. A candidate who earns Category-I status still needs to secure admission and PhD registration at a recognized university or institution; DBT/RCB do not place candidates into PhD programmes.
paragraphs_placeholder
bullets: The DBT-JRF programme was initiated in 2004 to develop skilled research human resources and support doctoral research in frontier biotechnology.
The fellowship is tenable at a recognized university or institution in India where the selected candidate registers for a PhD.
BET is ordinarily held once each year, but applicants should rely on the current official notification rather than assume a date or schedule.

sections.heading: Eligibility: qualifications, marks, age and nationality
paragraphs: Under the BET 2026 rules, eligible academic routes included: a four-year/eight-semester UG degree in biotechnology, life sciences or listed allied disciplines; a B.Tech/B.E.; or a relevant master's/equivalent degree such as M.Sc., M.Tech., M.V.Sc., M.Pharm., integrated M.Sc./M.Tech. or MBBS. Relevant allied areas expressly included biomedical science, bioinformatics, biochemistry, biophysics, botany, chemistry, computational biology, genetics, microbiology and zoology, among other biology/life-sciences areas.

Final-year and result-awaited candidates could apply in the result-awaited category, but had to submit the prescribed attestation/undertaking certified by the head of their institution. Eligibility is verified for shortlisted candidates, so meeting the application condition does not remove the need to supply valid documents later.
bullets: For a four-year research bachelor's degree, the 2026 notice specified at least 75% aggregate marks or equivalent grade, with a 5% relaxation/equivalent grade as applicable under the referenced UGC PhD regulations.
For B.Tech/B.E. and relevant master's/equivalent qualifications, the 2026 threshold was 60% for General, EWS and OBC candidates and 55% for SC/ST/differently abled candidates.

The 2026 age limit was 28 years on the application closing date for General/EWS candidates, with up to five years' relaxation for SC/ST/differently abled/women candidates and up to three years for OBC-NCL candidates.
The 2026 notice required the applicant to be a bona fide citizen and resident of India. Because eligibility rules can change, prospective applicants should use the notice for their own cycle.

sections.heading: Exam format and scoring approach
paragraphs: BET 2026 used a 300-mark multiple-choice format. Section A had 50 compulsory questions worth three marks each, while Section B offered 150 biotechnology-specialism questions, of which a candidate had to attempt 50, also worth three marks each. Both sections applied negative marking: one mark was deducted for each incorrect answer, while unattempted questions received zero.

Section A covered general science, mathematics, chemistry, general aptitude, analytical and quantitative ability, and general biotechnology. Section B covered specific biotechnology areas according to the official syllabus. The official 2026 bulletin continued to point candidates to the DBT-JRF BET syllabus document hosted by RCB.
bullets: Section A: 50 questions; all 50 compulsory; 150 marks.
Section B: 150 questions offered; answer 50; 150 marks.
Total: 200 questions offered, 100 answered, 300 marks.
Medium: English; mode: computer-based test; duration: three hours.

sections.heading: Application process and 2026 cycle context
paragraphs: BET applications are submitted online through the NTA GAT-B/BET portal. In the 2026 process, candidates registered with their own email address and mobile number, completed the form, uploaded the required scanned records, paid online, and retained the confirmation page. The bulletin lists photo, signature, identity proof, date-of-birth proof, category certificate where applicable, PwD certificate where applicable, and the result-awaited certificate where applicable among the uploads.

For date context, the published BET 2026 application window ran from 19 March 2026 to 9 April 2026 (5:00 PM), with fee payment allowed until 11:50 PM on 9 April and a correction period from 11 to 13 April 2026. Those dates have passed; they are useful only as the 2026 record, not as a prediction of a future cycle's deadline.
bullets: Use one application only; the 2026 bulletin stated that multiple applications would not be accepted.
Download and retain the confirmation page after successful payment.
Check official RCB, NTA and DBT notices for the next application window, correction window, admit-card instructions and result updates.

sections.heading: Preparation strategy anchored to the official blueprint
paragraphs: Build preparation around the two-part design rather than treating BET as only a subject-recall test. Section A is compulsory and mixes 10+2-level general science, mathematics and chemistry with aptitude, analytical/quantitative ability and general biotechnology. Section B requires selective answering: candidates should develop sufficient breadth to identify their strongest 50 questions among the 150 specialised biotechnology questions offered.

Use timed computer-based practice and an error-review log. This is particularly important because every wrong answer carries a one-mark penalty against a three-mark correct answer; therefore, question selection and accuracy matter alongside coverage. Read the RCB-hosted syllabus named in the current bulletin before making a topic plan.
bullets: First, map the official syllabus into Section A foundations and the Section B biotechnology areas in which you are strongest.
Practise answering a 100-question, three-hour paper, including decisions about which 50 Section B questions to attempt.
Revise quantitative/analytical methods as well as biology and biotechnology content; all are explicitly included in Section A.
Use official notifications and the official syllabus as the authoritative reference if coaching materials conflict with them.

sections.heading: What qualifying can lead to
paragraphs: Category-I is the direct DBT-JRF outcome. It can be activated after the candidate joins and subsequently registers for a PhD at a recognized Indian university or institution, within two years of the award-letter date under the 2026 terms. Obtaining a BET Category-I result therefore does not by itself create a PhD seat: the candidate must independently meet the host institution's PhD admission and selection requirements.

Category-II is a distinct merit-list outcome. It can make a candidate eligible for appointment to a DBT-sponsored project with fellowship equivalent to NET/GATE qualification under current DST guidelines, and/or for PhD enrolment subject to institutional selection. However, the 2026 rules explicitly state that Category-II does not entitle the candidate to a DBT-JRF fellowship and does not oblige a principal investigator to hire from that list.
bullets: Dated 2026 fellowship context: activated Category-I fellows were to receive ₹37,000 per month as JRF for two years, then ₹42,000 per month as SRF for the remaining three years after the required assessment; HRA where applicable and ₹30,000 annual contingency on a pro-rata basis were also stated. These amounts and terms can be revised, so applicants should confirm the current award notice.
Document verification applies to shortlisted candidates; an award letter is not issued if eligibility is not established or required records are incorrect or missing.
The programme's broader outcome is funded doctoral training and research in biotechnology/life sciences, rather than a standalone professional licence or guaranteed employment.

title: Departmental Promotion Exams
description: Internal competitive exams for promoting employees from LDC/JSA to higher posts like Upper Division Clerk (UDC) or Assistant Section Officer (ASO).

quick_facts.label: What this node covers
quick_facts.value: “Departmental Promotion Exams” is an umbrella term, not one all-India examination. Government departments and public employers run their own Limited Departmental Competitive Examinations (LDCEs), limited departmental examinations, or qualifying examinations under the relevant cadre’s recruitment rules and departmental instructions.

quick_facts.label: Who can apply
quick_facts.value: These examinations are ordinarily for existing employees in the feeder cadre, rather than outside applicants. The qualifying service, cadre, number of attempts, vacancy year, reservation treatment, and any integrity/APAR or disciplinary-clearance requirements must be checked in the employer’s current notification and recruitment rules.

quick_facts.label: Illustrative pathways
quick_facts.value: Documented departmental pathways include MTS to LDC, LDC to UDC, UDC to Assistant through LDCE, Senior Secretariat Assistant (SSA) to ASO, and LDC to Junior Accountant. These are examples, not a universal hierarchy applicable to every employer or parent occupation.

quick_facts.label: Test design
quick_facts.value: There is no single syllabus or mode. For example, a 2025–26 NACIN departmental examination notice for promotion to LDC listed General English, Numerical Aptitude and General Knowledge, and Hindi papers, while other departments publish their own post-specific papers and schemes.

quick_facts.label: How selection works
quick_facts.value: Passing an examination does not itself guarantee immediate posting: appointment or promotion is tied to available promotion/test-quota vacancies and the department’s subsequent panel, verification, and order process.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
paragraphs: Departmental promotion examinations are internal selection mechanisms used by an employer to fill specified promotion or test-quota vacancies from serving staff. They should not be confused with open recruitment examinations such as SSC examinations: eligibility is tied to the employee’s present cadre and the employer’s recruitment rules.

For clerical and secretariat-oriented cadres, a departmental route may support movement such as MTS to LDC, LDC to UDC, UDC to Assistant, or SSA to ASO. However, these labels and routes are not interchangeable across the Union Government, state governments, railways, defence establishments, CAPFs, postal services, PSUs, or autonomous bodies. An employee should treat the notification issued by their own cadre-controlling authority as controlling.
bullets: Use this node as a career-progression category rather than as a single exam calendar.
A post is available through an examination only where its recruitment rules provide an examination/test-quota or other competitive-promotion channel.
The same department can use different methods for different posts: regular seniority/selection promotion, departmental qualifying tests, and LDCEs may coexist.

sections.heading: Eligibility: verify the feeder cadre and service conditions
paragraphs: The essential eligibility question is not simply whether an employee holds an LDC/JSA-equivalent post. It is whether the current recruitment rules and notification name that cadre as a feeder grade and whether the employee meets the prescribed regular-service and other conditions on the stated crucial date.

Conditions vary materially by organization and post. India Post’s rules for one LDCE example prescribe specified eligible grades, eight years of regular service, and limits on examination chances; this illustrates why an employee must not import eligibility rules from another department. In a separate departmental context, Puducherry’s promotion records show pre-selection requests for service particulars, APARs, integrity/no-disciplinary-proceedings certificates, and category certificates in connection with UDC-to-Assistant appointments through LDCE.
bullets: Read the current recruitment rules, examination notice, corrigenda, and vacancy circular together.
Confirm the feeder designation, regular-service calculation date, probation/confirmation position, and whether any APAR, vigilance, integrity, medical, trade, or category documentation is required.

Do not assume that every job listed as a parent of this node has an LDC/JSA-to-UDC/ASO exam route; technical, uniformed, railway, defence, police, PSU, and state cadres may have entirely different promotional rules.

sections.heading: Exam format and syllabus
paragraphs: There is no standard national pattern. The conducting authority defines the papers, subjects, marking, medium, qualifying standard, duration, computer/practical component where applicable, and merit method. A NACIN notice for its 2025–26 LDC promotion examination, for instance, identifies separate papers in General English, Numerical Aptitude and General Knowledge, and Hindi; that is an example of a departmental scheme, not a universal LDC/UDC syllabus.

Departments may publish previous question papers, model papers, training instructions, schedules, admit-card directions, and results separately. The Controller General of Communication Accounts examination page, for example, lists MTS-to-LDC LDQE material and prior LDC-to-Junior Accountant papers, while DDA maintains separate LDCE circulars for SSA-to-ASO and other cadres.
bullets: Build preparation around the exact notification, not a generic “departmental exam” course outline.
Check whether the exam tests office procedure, service/recruitment rules, departmental manuals, language, numerical ability, computer skills, or technical work relevant to the target post.
Treat previous papers only as practice material: pattern and syllabus may be revised through a fresh notice or corrigendum.

sections.heading: Application and selection process
paragraphs: Application is usually internal. The employee should watch the establishment/personnel branch, official departmental website, intranet, or cadre-controlling office for the notification. The department may obtain nominations and service details through the controlling office rather than through an open public application portal; the NACIN LDC notice includes nomination and centre/candidate-detail formats for authorized officers.

A practical sequence is: identify the applicable notification; verify eligibility and supporting records with the establishment branch; submit the prescribed application or nomination before the notified deadline; obtain the admit-card or examination instructions; take the examination; then monitor the result, merit/panel, document or vigilance verification, and final promotion/appointment order. Dates, fees if any, and application method are notification-specific and should be treated as variable.
bullets: Keep copies of the notification, application/nominated-candidate acknowledgement, service certificate, category certificate where applicable, and admit card.
Check corrections and postponement notices; departmental schedules can change.
If selected, complete all post-selection formalities promptly, since departments may request integrity, disciplinary-status, service, or category verification before issuing orders.

sections.heading: Preparation strategy
paragraphs: Start by creating a notification-specific checklist: eligibility conditions, scheme of examination, syllabus, departmental reference material, language options, dates, and documents. Then obtain official previous papers or practice material where the department provides them. This is especially useful for identifying the level and style of questions, but the current notification remains the authoritative syllabus.

For an office/ministerial promotion examination, devote time to the rules, manuals, procedures, and drafting or computer requirements expressly named in the notice, alongside any language, numerical, general-knowledge, or technical papers. Use timed practice for each paper and retain an error log; departmental exams are often closely tied to the work of the destination cadre.
bullets: Download the latest notice and corrigenda first; do not rely on old coaching notes alone.
Use official previous papers where available, such as the CGCA LDC-to-Junior Accountant paper links.
Ask the establishment/cadre branch which edition of a departmental manual, rule book, or office-procedure material is prescribed for the current cycle.

sections.heading: Outcomes and career progression
paragraphs: A successful departmental examination can place an eligible employee in the selection process for a higher post, subject to the recruitment rules, the number of notified vacancies, merit or qualifying criteria, applicable reservation rules, and completion of administrative checks. Official promotion pages demonstrate outcomes such as MTS promoted to LDC, LDC promoted to UDC, and UDC appointed as Assistant through LDCE; DDA also publishes SSA-to-ASO LDCE-related circulars.

The outcome should therefore be described as a route to consideration or selection for promotion, not an automatic salary or post guarantee. Pay level, pay fixation, seniority, probation, posting location, and joining date depend on the receiving cadre’s rules and the final order in the relevant vacancy year.
bullets: Possible destination titles include UDC, Senior Secretariat Assistant, Assistant, ASO, Junior Accountant, or post-specific technical/supervisory grades, depending on the employer.
Read the final appointment/promotion order for effective date, place of posting, pay-fixation instructions, probation, and seniority treatment.
For current salary or vacancy information, consult the specific employer’s latest recruitment rules, vacancy circular, and promotion order; neither is uniform across this node.

title: DRDO CEPTAM
description: DRDO CEPTAM — govt recruitment exam (research), conducted by DRDO.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: CEPTAM (Centre for Personnel Talent Management) conducts DRDO recruitment processes. The current CEPTAM-11 notice is issued by CEPTAM under DRDO, Ministry of Defence, Government of India.

quick_facts.label: What the current cycle recruits for
quick_facts.value: CEPTAM-11 advertised direct recruitment to the Defence Research & Development Organisation Technical Cadre (DRTC): 561 Senior Technical Assistant-B (STA-B) vacancies and 203 Technician-A vacancies. Vacancy counts and post mix can change in later advertisements.

quick_facts.label: ITI/NAC relevance
quick_facts.value: For the CEPTAM-11 Technician-A trades, the standard requirement was Class 10/equivalent plus the specified recognised ITI trade certificate. Where an ITI does not award a certificate in a required trade, a recognised one-year certificate, National Trade Certificate, or National Apprenticeship Certificate in that trade could be accepted.

quick_facts.label: Selection route in CEPTAM-11
quick_facts.value: STA-B selection uses Tier-I and Tier-II computer-based tests. Technician-A selection adds a qualifying, ITI-level trade test after Tier-II, except where the advertisement provides an exemption for eligible recent DRDO apprentices.

quick_facts.label: Latest official cycle status
quick_facts.value: In CEPTAM-11, Tier-I CBT was scheduled for March 23, 2026; DRDO’s CEPTAM-11 page subsequently listed the Tier-I result dated May 25, 2026 and the Tier-II question-challenge portal dated June 18, 2026. Candidates should rely on the DRDO vacancy page for subsequent notices rather than assume an annual fixed schedule.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
paragraphs: DRDO CEPTAM is not a single permanent examination syllabus for every DRDO job; it is the recruitment framework used by the Centre for Personnel Talent Management for the posts specified in each advertisement. CEPTAM-11, for example, recruited Senior Technical Assistant-B and Technician-A into the Defence Research & Development Organisation Technical Cadre (DRTC), for work across DRDO laboratories, establishments and units.

The appropriate target post depends on the candidate’s qualification. In the CEPTAM-11 cycle, STA-B was a Group B, non-gazetted, non-ministerial technical post, while Technician-A was a Group C, non-gazetted, non-ministerial technical post. Older or future CEPTAM advertisements may cover different DRDO roles, so eligibility and selection should always be read from the advertisement for the particular post code.
bullets: Use the CEPTAM/DRDO advertisement—not coaching-site summaries—to identify the posts, disciplines or trades, number of vacancies, locations and rules for the cycle in which you apply.
For an ITI or NAC holder, Technician-A is the directly relevant CEPTAM-11 pathway; an STA-B application instead requires the prescribed relevant diploma or B.Sc. qualification for its post code.

sections.heading: Eligibility: read it post-code by post-code
paragraphs: In CEPTAM-11, applicants had to be Indian nationals and be 18–28 years old on the cycle’s crucial eligibility date, January 1, 2026. The notice provided category-specific age relaxations under extant Government of India rules. These dates and limits are advertisement-specific and should not be treated as a guarantee for a future CEPTAM cycle.

For STA-B, CEPTAM-11 required the qualification stated against the chosen discipline—typically a relevant AICTE-recognised diploma in engineering/technology or a B.Sc. from a recognised university or institute. For Technician-A, the normal requirement was Class 10/equivalent plus the specified recognised ITI trade certificate. The detailed advertisement also set restrictions concerning certain higher qualifications, so candidates should not assume that a higher degree automatically qualifies them.
bullets: Match the exact post code and trade/discipline before applying; similar-sounding credentials may not be accepted.

For Technician-A, an NAC/NTC or a recognised minimum one-year certificate was an alternative only in the circumstance specified by the CEPTAM-11 notice: where ITIs do not award a certificate in the required trade.
Keep qualification, date-of-birth and category/relaxation documents ready. CEPTAM-11 required uploaded documents and later verification of originals.

sections.heading: Exam format and selection stages
paragraphs: For CEPTAM-11, both Tier-I and Tier-II were bilingual (Hindi and English) computer-based tests using objective multiple-choice questions. Tier-I was a 120-minute, 150-question screening test: General Science (40), General English (30), Quantitative Aptitude/General Mathematics (40), and General Intelligence and Reasoning (40).

For STA-B, Tier-II included a personality test and a 120-question, 120-minute post-code-specific subject test; merit for Tier-II was based on the subject-specific Part II rather than the personality test. For Technician-A, Tier-II included a personality test and a 120-question, 90-minute trade-specific Part II. Technician-A candidates then faced a qualifying practical trade test at ITI level; the CEPTAM-11 notice stated minimum trade-test qualifying marks of 50% for UR/OBC/EWS and 45% for SC/ST/PwBD candidates.

The CEPTAM-11 advertisement described Tier-I as screening and Tier-II Part II as the basis for provisional selection or, for Technician-A, for shortlisting toward the trade test. It also stated that shortlisting ratios, normalization and selection mode could vary with organisational requirements and government policy.
bullets: Tier-I preparation is common across post codes; Tier-II preparation must be tailored to the applied STA-B discipline or Technician-A trade.
For Technician-A, practical trade competence matters in addition to CBT performance because the trade test is mandatory and qualifying in nature, subject to stated exemptions.
Official CEPTAM-11 notices scheduled Tier-I on March 23, 2026 and directed applicants to DRDO for city information and admit-card updates.

sections.heading: Application process and fees
paragraphs: CEPTAM-11 used an online-only application through the DRDO website’s Offerings/Vacancies area and its linked application portal. Applicants were told to review the form before final submission, pay online, and upload the required documents. The official FAQ advised using a desktop or laptop because some application-module features might not work properly on mobile devices.

Fee rules are cycle- and category-specific. In CEPTAM-11, the total paid at application was ₹750 for STA-B General/OBC/EWS/MSP applicants and ₹600 for Technician-A General/OBC/EWS/MSP applicants; the amount included a ₹500 refundable component for candidates who appeared in Tier-I. Women, SC, ST, PwBD and eligible ex-servicemen had a nil non-refundable application fee but still paid the refundable ₹500 component. Bank charges could apply. These are historical CEPTAM-11 amounts, not a promise of future fees.

The CEPTAM-11 application window ran from December 11, 2025 to January 1, 2026, with fee payment through January 3, 2026. Those dates are past. Future dates, correction windows, documentation rules and exam-city choices must be taken from the live official advertisement.
bullets: Read the complete advertisement, FAQs and portal instructions before beginning the form.
Use qualification and category documents whose details support every claim made in the application; CEPTAM may reject unsupported claims during document scrutiny or verification.
Monitor the official DRDO vacancy page for admit cards, answer keys, result notices and any corrigenda.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Start with the official pattern: prepare the four Tier-I areas—General Science, English, quantitative aptitude/general mathematics, and intelligence/reasoning—under the 150-question, 120-minute format. Because CEPTAM-11 specified time-bound sections that lock when their allocated time expires, practice section-wise pacing rather than only untimed question solving.

Make Tier-II preparation post-code-specific. DRDO publishes detailed Tier-II syllabus material for STA-B disciplines and Technician-A trades. The published Technician-A topics cover trade knowledge and, depending on the trade, occupational safety, tools, workshop calculations, engineering drawing, computer or equipment fundamentals and other relevant trade content. Technician-A candidates should also practise the applied ITI-level skills needed for the qualifying trade test.

Use the official advertisement, syllabus and answer-key notices as the primary preparation source. The CEPTAM-11 advertisement says that answer keys for both CBT tiers are published on DRDO’s website and allows online representations within the stated period after publication.
bullets: Build a Tier-I timed practice routine, then reserve substantial time for the exact Tier-II discipline/trade in your post code.
For Technician-A, revise ITI practical procedures, safety and measurement alongside theory; a CBT-only strategy is incomplete.
Check the official syllabus file for the exact trade or subject rather than relying on a generic ‘DRDO CEPTAM syllabus’.

sections.heading: What selection leads to
paragraphs: Candidates provisionally selected through CEPTAM-11 are nominated to the relevant DRDO laboratory, establishment or unit based on merit, vacancy availability and submitted posting preferences, while DRDO retains the right to post candidates anywhere in India. Appointment follows document verification and satisfaction of eligibility, antecedent and character requirements.

As dated CEPTAM-11 pay context, STA-B carried Pay Matrix Level 6 (₹35,400–₹1,12,400) and Technician-A carried Pay Matrix Level 2 (₹19,900–₹63,200), under the 7th CPC matrix. The advertisement also referred to allowances and benefits under prevailing Government of India rules. Actual take-home pay, allowances and future pay rules vary by posting, policy and time.

The CEPTAM-11 service conditions stated a two-year initial probation, all-India service liability, and a minimum five-year period at the first posting station without transfer on request, subject to DRDO’s organisational needs and applicable rules.
bullets: A CEPTAM result is not by itself an appointment letter: document verification and the concerned DRDO unit’s appointment process follow nomination.
Be prepared for postings across India, including field or remote locations, rather than treating a preferred station as guaranteed.
Treat salary figures and conditions as CEPTAM-11 context; verify the current advertisement and applicable government rules before making career or financial decisions.
