title: IBPS Clerk
description: IBPS Clerk — govt recruitment exam (finance), conducted by IBPS.

quick_facts.label: Current official naming
quick_facts.value: The exam commonly called “IBPS Clerk” was titled the Common Recruitment Process for Customer Service Associates (CRP-CSA-XV) in the most recent official clerical-cadre notification; it recruited for clerical-cadre Customer Service Associate posts in participating public-sector banks.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body and purpose
quick_facts.value: IBPS is an autonomous selection body. Its CRP programme conducts recruitment processes for participating public-sector banks, including Customer Service Associates (the current clerical-cadre designation).

quick_facts.label: Latest process status
quick_facts.value: As reviewed on 2026-07-18, the official Clerical Cadre XV page listed provisional-allotment and main-examination-result updates dated 2026-07-17. A fresh CSA/clerical notification and its dates should be treated as unannounced unless published by IBPS.

quick_facts.label: Most recent baseline eligibility
quick_facts.value: For CRP-CSA-XV, candidates needed a graduation degree in any discipline, computer working knowledge, and proficiency in the official language of the applied-for State/UT. The age band was 20–28 years as on 2025-08-01, with notified relaxations for eligible categories.

quick_facts.label: Selection format
quick_facts.value: CRP-CSA-XV used two online objective-test stages: Preliminary and Main. The preliminary test had English Language, Numerical Ability, and Reasoning Ability; the main test had General/Financial Awareness, General English, Reasoning Ability & Computer Aptitude, and Quantitative Aptitude. Wrong answers attracted a one-fourth-mark penalty in the cited cycle.

quick_facts.label: Outcome
quick_facts.value: IBPS conducts the process and makes provisional allotments; appointment is made by the allotted participating bank, which remains responsible for final employment decisions and eligibility verification.

sections.heading: What IBPS Clerk is now called and what it is for
paragraphs: “IBPS Clerk” is the widely used legacy name for IBPS’s clerical-cadre bank recruitment process. In the latest official cycle, IBPS used the title “Customer Service Associate” (CSA): CRP-CSA-XV invited candidates seeking clerical-cadre roles in participating public-sector banks for 2026–27 vacancies. The process is a common recruitment route rather than a job with IBPS itself.

IBPS describes itself as an autonomous body that supports organisations’ personnel selection. Under its flagship CRP programme, it runs selection processes for participating public-sector banks; candidates should rely on the specific cycle’s notification because participating banks, vacancy totals, State/UT vacancies, conditions, and schedule can change.
bullets: Use the official IBPS CRP-CSA/clerical-cadre page—not coaching-site calendars—as the authoritative source for a new application window.
The node title “IBPS Clerk” remains useful for search and recognition, but applicants should also search for “CRP-CSA” and “Customer Service Associate.”

sections.heading: Eligibility: use the next notification as the controlling document
paragraphs: Eligibility is cycle-specific. IBPS explicitly directs candidates to the relevant notification for age and educational requirements. The following is therefore a dated baseline from CRP-CSA-XV, not a guarantee for the next cycle.

For CRP-CSA-XV, the stated age requirement was 20 to 28 years as on 2025-08-01 (birth dates from 1997-08-02 through 2005-08-01, inclusive). The notice provided upper-age relaxations for eligible categories, including SC/ST, OBC (non-creamy layer), persons with benchmark disabilities, ex-servicemen/disabled ex-servicemen, and specified women candidates.

The same cycle required a graduation degree in any discipline from a Government-recognised university or an equivalent qualification. It also required operating and working knowledge of computer systems and proficiency—reading, writing, speaking, and understanding—in the official language of the State/UT applied for. Applicants should confirm documentary requirements, category rules, nationality/citizenship conditions, and local-language requirements in the live notice before paying any fee.
bullets: Check the notification’s cut-off dates; an otherwise valid qualification or age may not count if it is obtained after the specified date.
Apply for only the State/UT and vacancy options permitted in that cycle, and retain original documents for bank-stage verification.
Do not treat passing the examinations or receiving provisional allotment as automatic confirmation of final employment.

sections.heading: Exam format and scoring
paragraphs: In CRP-CSA-XV, selection began with an online Preliminary Examination followed by an online Main Examination for candidates who qualified and were shortlisted. The Preliminary Examination was 100 questions/100 marks in 60 minutes: English Language (30 questions, 30 marks, 20 minutes), Numerical Ability (35 questions, 35 marks, 20 minutes), and Reasoning Ability (35 questions, 35 marks, 20 minutes).

The CRP-CSA-XV Main Examination was 155 questions/200 marks in 120 minutes: General/Financial Awareness (40 questions, 50 marks, 20 minutes), General English (40 questions, 40 marks, 35 minutes), Reasoning Ability and Computer Aptitude (40 questions, 60 marks, 35 minutes), and Quantitative Aptitude (35 questions, 50 marks, 30 minutes). The notice stated that one-fourth of the marks assigned to a question would be deducted for each wrong answer.

The cited cycle also set out a Local Language Proficiency Test framework. Candidates should read the new notification carefully because test structure, sectional timing, scoring rules, accommodations, language provisions, and local-language requirements may be revised.
bullets: Prepare for sectional timers, not only an overall two-hour target.
Use accuracy discipline: the cited cycle’s 0.25 negative marking makes indiscriminate guessing costly.
Verify the current cycle’s cut-off, normalization, and language-test rules directly in its notification.

sections.heading: How to apply when a new CRP-CSA/clerical window opens
paragraphs: Applications are online only. In CRP-CSA-XV, applicants used the IBPS website’s CRP-CSA link, chose new registration, entered basic details, received a provisional registration number and password, completed the form, uploaded the prescribed files, paid online, and retained the application and e-receipt. IBPS’s candidate guidance says an online submission remains subject to later scrutiny and may be rejected if eligibility is not met.

Fees and dates are variable. For historical context only, the original CRP-CSA-XV notice set online registration and fee payment for 2025-08-01 to 2025-08-21 and listed ₹175 inclusive of GST for SC/ST/PwBD/ESM/DESM candidates and ₹850 inclusive of GST for all others, with bank transaction charges borne by the applicant. Those figures and dates must not be carried forward to a new cycle without confirmation.

As reviewed on 2026-07-18, the official Clerical Cadre XV page was carrying result/provisional-allotment updates rather than an advertised new CSA/clerical application window. Monitor IBPS’s CRP updates and the relevant clerical-cadre page for the next notification, then follow its exact dates and upload specifications.
bullets: Before final submission, check name, category, State/UT choice, education details, bank preferences, email address, and mobile number against documents.
Download and preserve the submitted application and fee receipt; IBPS advises candidates to retain registration communications and records.
Use only IBPS’s official website or the application portal linked from it; IBPS has published warnings concerning fraudulent websites resembling IBPS.

sections.heading: Preparation approach aligned to the official test design
paragraphs: Build preparation around the official section list and sectional time limits. For prelims, practise English, numerical ability, and reasoning in separate 20-minute blocks before combining them into full 60-minute tests. For mains, add general/financial awareness, computer-oriented reasoning, and longer quantitative and English practice under the notified sectional timers.

Use timed objective practice with an error log. Review missed questions by cause—concept gap, calculation speed, interpretation, or rushed reading—and repeat weak areas. Because CRP-CSA-XV applied a one-fourth-mark deduction for an incorrect answer, set an attempt rule that prioritises questions you can solve accurately rather than maximising raw attempts.

Treat the current official notification as the syllabus and operations checklist. Before the exam, review call-letter instructions, permitted identification, centre rules, accessibility provisions where applicable, and any official mock-test or candidate-information links published by IBPS for that cycle.
bullets: Prelims priority: speed plus accuracy in three short sections.
Mains priority: retain reasoning and quantitative accuracy while systematically covering financial awareness and English.
Take full mocks only after practising individual timed sections; then review every incorrect and skipped question.

sections.heading: What qualifying leads to—and what it does not guarantee
paragraphs: Candidates who qualify and are shortlisted after the preliminary examination take the main examination. In the latest official cycle, IBPS’s process culminated in provisional allotment to a participating bank, based on the applicable merit, preferences, vacancies, reservation guidelines, and administrative conditions described in the notification.

A provisional allotment is not the same as an appointment letter. IBPS states that its role ends after provisional allotment; the allotted bank/organisation makes the employment offer. The relevant bank may verify originals and other eligibility conditions and can reject a provisionally allotted candidate under the terms of the recruitment process.

Pay and benefits should be checked with the allotted bank rather than inferred from the IBPS exam. IBPS’s FAQ specifically directs candidates seeking pay-scale information to the bank, and the CRP-CSA-XV notification stated that allowances and perquisites are governed by the participating bank’s rules in force from time to time.
bullets: Track both the IBPS result/provisional-allotment notice and communications from the allotted bank.
Keep original degree, identity, category, disability, local-language, and other supporting documents ready for bank verification.
Compare role location, local-language conditions, compensation, joining instructions, and probation/service rules in the allotted bank’s offer documents.

title: IBPS PO (CRP-PO/MT)
description: IBPS PO (CRP-PO/MT) — govt recruitment exam (finance), conducted by IBPS.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS), which conducts the Common Recruitment Process (CRP) for Probationary Officer/Management Trainee posts in participating public-sector banks.

quick_facts.label: Current recruitment cycle
quick_facts.value: CRP PO/MT-XVI is the 2026 notification cycle, for participating-bank vacancies of 2027–28.

quick_facts.label: Application window (dated context)
quick_facts.value: For CRP PO/MT-XVI, online registration and online fee payment run from 1 July 2026 through 21 July 2026. As of 19 July 2026, the window is still open; applicants should use the official portal and not rely on third-party deadlines.

quick_facts.label: Baseline qualification
quick_facts.value: The XVI notification requires a graduation degree in any discipline from a Government of India-recognised university, or an equivalent qualification recognised by the Central Government; the required result/document deadline is specified in the cycle notification.

quick_facts.label: Age rule (XVI dated context)
quick_facts.value: For CRP PO/MT-XVI, the standard age range is 20–30 years as on 1 July 2026, with upper-age relaxations for eligible categories under the notification.

quick_facts.label: Selection route
quick_facts.value: The current cycle uses an online preliminary examination, online main examination, mandatory personality test, interview, and then provisional allotment subject to merit, preferences, vacancies, and verification.

quick_facts.label: Application fee (XVI dated context)
quick_facts.value: For CRP PO/MT-XVI, the stated online fee/intimation charge is ₹175 inclusive of GST for SC/ST/PwBD candidates and ₹850 inclusive of GST for all other candidates; bank transaction charges are additional where applicable.

sections.heading: What IBPS PO (CRP-PO/MT) is for
paragraphs: IBPS PO/MT is a common recruitment process rather than a university qualification. IBPS conducts it on behalf of participating public-sector banks to identify candidates for entry officer roles titled Probationary Officer (PO) or Management Trainee (MT). A candidate applies once for the notified CRP cycle and, if successful, may be provisionally allotted to a participating bank according to the applicable merit, preferences, vacancies, and eligibility checks.

The cycle number and participating banks can change. For the current XVI cycle, IBPS describes the recruitment as being for vacancies of 2027–28, so candidates should treat the detailed notification for their specific cycle—not older coaching material or prior-year notices—as the controlling document.
bullets: This exam is a route into participating public-sector banks; it is not a guarantee of appointment merely by registering or taking the examination.
The official IBPS FAQ states that eligibility criteria must be checked in the notification for the relevant CRP examination.

sections.heading: Eligibility: who can apply
paragraphs: For CRP PO/MT-XVI, the educational requirement is a degree (graduation) in any discipline from a university recognised by the Government of India, or an equivalent qualification recognised by the Central Government. This means commerce, science, arts, management, computer applications, vocational degrees, and distance-learning degrees can be relevant pathways only where the individual award and institution meet the notification’s recognition and documentation requirements.

The XVI notification’s standard age band is 20 to 30 years as on 1 July 2026. It also sets category-specific upper-age relaxations and documentary requirements. Applicants should verify nationality, category certificate, disability accommodation, ex-serviceman, and other special-case rules directly against the current detailed notice before paying the fee.

Candidates must have the required graduation result and supporting mark-sheet/degree documentation by the notification’s stated cutoff. For XVI, the notification specifies 21 July 2026 for the final result to have been declared.
bullets: Do not assume that enrolment in a final year is enough: check the result-declaration cutoff for the cycle.
Where a university awards CGPA/OGPA, retain the university’s conversion evidence if the notification requires percentage reporting.
Use the current notification to confirm age-relaxation eligibility and the prescribed certificate format.

sections.heading: Selection and examination format
paragraphs: CRP PO/MT-XVI is scheduled as a staged process: preliminary examination in August 2026, main examination in October 2026, personality test in November 2026, interview in November/December 2026, and provisional allotment in January 2027. These dates are stated as tentative and can be revised by IBPS.

The preliminary examination tests English Language, Quantitative Aptitude, and Reasoning Ability. The main examination tests Reasoning & Computer Aptitude, Data Analysis & Interpretation, General/Economy/Banking Awareness, and English Language, with a descriptive English component. The notification specifies the authoritative question counts, marks, timings, cut-offs, and negative-marking rules for the current cycle.

Candidates shortlisted from the main examination must take the personality test to be eligible for interview. For the final score in XVI, the notification assigns relative weightage of 80:20 to the online main examination and interview; candidates must qualify both as required to be considered for provisional allotment.
bullets: Preliminary examination: qualifying screening stage for shortlisting to the main examination.
Main examination: the score-bearing written stage used with interview performance for final merit.
Personality test: mandatory for interview eligibility in the XVI process; interview remains a separate assessed stage.
Always download the call letter and examination information handout when issued, because centre, reporting, and test-day instructions are cycle-specific.

sections.heading: How to apply in the current cycle
paragraphs: Apply online through the official IBPS CRP PO/MT-XVI registration portal. The portal lists 1 July 2026 to 21 July 2026 for registration and online fee payment, and it warns that submission of an application does not itself establish eligibility; IBPS may scrutinise and reject candidature later if requirements are not met.

Before submitting, read the detailed notification and portal instructions, complete registration, upload the required image/documents in the prescribed form, provide the requested academic and category details, state bank preferences where the form requests them, pay online, and preserve the application printout and e-receipt. Keep the registered mobile number and email accessible throughout the process.

The XVI schedule provides for an edit window after registration closes, with timing to be notified on the official IBPS website. This is not a reason to submit incomplete or inaccurate information: applicants should review every field and uploaded document before final submission.
bullets: Official registration/fee deadline for XVI: 21 July 2026.
The portal currently lists 5 August 2026 as the last date to print the submitted application.
Use only the IBPS portal and official IBPS notices for application, call-letter, result, and correction-window updates.

sections.heading: Preparation approach aligned to the official process
paragraphs: Build preparation around the notified test domains rather than a generic “banking exam” syllabus: English, reasoning, quantitative/data analysis, computer aptitude, and general economy/banking awareness. For the main examination, include regular descriptive-English practice because it is a separately specified component.

Use timed online practice that reflects the sectional and overall time limits in the current information handout/notification. After each attempt, diagnose errors by topic and by question-selection decisions, then revise fundamentals before increasing mock-test volume. This is particularly important because the preliminary and main stages have different purposes and content depth.

Maintain a current-affairs and banking-awareness revision system using reliable primary sources such as RBI, Government of India, and bank/regulator publications, while treating the IBPS notification as the source of truth for the test structure and selection rules. Recheck the official website for revised dates, call letters, accessibility instructions, and any corrigendum.
bullets: First establish speed and accuracy for preliminary English, quantitative aptitude, and reasoning.
Then devote substantial study time to main-level data interpretation, reasoning/computer aptitude, banking/economy awareness, and descriptive writing.
Practise writing clear, time-bounded English responses for the descriptive component rather than preparing objective questions alone.

sections.heading: What success leads to
paragraphs: Candidates who clear the required stages may be provisionally allotted as PO/MT to a participating public-sector bank. Provisional allotment is not the same as a final appointment: it remains subject to merit position, the candidate’s bank preferences, available vacancies, document/eligibility verification, medical fitness or other bank requirements, and the participating bank’s final decision.

For XVI, the notification states that interview carries 100 marks, sets minimum interview qualifying marks, and combines the online main examination and interview in an 80:20 weightage for the final score. This makes main-exam performance and interview readiness both material to the outcome; preliminary-exam performance is used for shortlisting rather than final-score weightage.

After appointment, a PO/MT enters a bank officer career path and may later pursue professional banking qualifications such as JAIIB/CAIIB, subject to the rules of the employing bank and the certifying body. Those qualifications are separate from the IBPS recruitment process.
bullets: A high score alone does not create an appointment right; allotment and joining depend on the notification and bank verification.
Vacancy numbers and participating-bank requirements are cycle-specific and may be updated by IBPS.

Do not treat a coaching-provider salary estimate as a guaranteed outcome: pay, allowances, location, probation terms, and posting are determined by the allotted employer and applicable rules at appointment.

title: IBPS RRB
description: IBPS RRB — govt recruitment exam (finance), conducted by IBPS.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: IBPS RRB is the Institute of Banking Personnel Selection’s Common Recruitment Process (CRP) for participating Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), covering Group B Office Assistants (Multipurpose) and Group A Officers in Scale I, II and III.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: IBPS is an autonomous employment-testing and selection body; it conducts the RRB CRP on behalf of participating banks.

quick_facts.label: Selection routes
quick_facts.value: In CRP-RRBs XIV, Office Assistant and Officer Scale I used preliminary and main online examinations; Officer Scale II and III used a single online examination. Officer posts also involved an interview, while Office Assistant provisional allotment was based on main-exam marks and reported vacancies.

quick_facts.label: Eligibility baseline
quick_facts.value: Eligibility is post-specific. The XIV notice required a bachelor’s degree for Office Assistant and Officer Scale I, with local-language proficiency for those posts; Scale II and III required the qualifications and experience specified for the relevant generalist or specialist post.

quick_facts.label: Latest cycle context
quick_facts.value: As of the review date, the official CRP-RRBs XIV page records reserve-list provisional-allotment notices dated June 30, 2026. This is a past-cycle status, not an announcement of a new application window; candidates should rely on the next official RRB notification for fresh dates and eligibility.

sections.heading: Purpose and posts covered
paragraphs: IBPS RRB is a common recruitment route into participating Regional Rural Banks rather than a single-bank recruitment examination. The process recruits Office Assistants (Multipurpose) and Officers at Scale I, Scale II—including generalist and specialist roles—and Scale III. Participating RRBs, vacancies, state/UT coverage and post requirements are specified in the notification for each cycle.
paragraphs_placeholder
bullets: Office Assistant (Multipurpose): Group B role.
Officer Scale I (Assistant Manager): entry officer role.
Officer Scale II (Manager): general banking and specialist officer roles, subject to the advertised streams and requirements.
Officer Scale III (Senior Manager): senior officer role.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: Treat each cycle’s notification as controlling: IBPS explicitly directs candidates to the relevant notification for educational, age and other eligibility conditions. For CRP-RRBs XIV, the general-category/EWS age bands as of September 1, 2025 were 18–28 for Office Assistant, above 18 and below 30 for Scale I, above 21 and below 32 for Scale II, and above 21 and below 40 for Scale III. Statutory/category relaxations applied under that notice; these dates and limits can change in a later cycle.

For XIV, Office Assistant required a bachelor’s degree in any discipline and local-language proficiency prescribed by the participating RRB. Scale I also required a bachelor’s degree, with specified degree subjects receiving preference. Scale II and III candidates needed the post-specific degree, aggregate-mark and experience conditions in the detailed notification; specialist applicants should verify the exact stream rather than assume a general graduation degree is sufficient.
bullets: For Scale I and Office Assistant, XIV treated study of the state language at Standard VIII or above through a government-recognised board, or an equivalent certificate, as evidence of local-language proficiency. Candidates otherwise selected could be allowed time after joining to acquire it, subject to the notice’s conditions.
The XIV notice also stated that applicants should maintain a healthy credit history by joining, according to the policy of the participating RRB; it said this was not a precondition to apply.
Nationality/citizenship, reservation, disability/scribe provisions, document requirements and cut-off dates must be checked against the applicable notification.

sections.heading: Exam format and selection
paragraphs: The XIV process used online objective tests. Office Assistant and Officer Scale I candidates first took a preliminary examination and, if shortlisted, a main examination. Scale II and Scale III candidates took a single online examination and, if shortlisted, proceeded to interview. The detailed notice set the examination structure, cut-offs, negative-marking rules, language options and centre arrangements, so candidates should use the notification for their own cycle rather than an older pattern.

For example, the XIV preliminary examination for Office Assistant had 40 Reasoning and 40 Numerical Ability questions, for 80 marks in 45 minutes. The notice also set a one-fourth-of-the-marks-assigned penalty for each wrong answer in objective tests. Exact section timings, marks and qualifying rules vary by post and cycle.
bullets: Office Assistant: preliminary examination → main examination → provisional allotment.
Officer Scale I: preliminary examination → main examination → common interview → provisional allotment.
Officer Scale II and III: single online examination → common interview → provisional allotment.

IBPS’s published highlights state that RRB Office Assistant and Scale I examinations have been offered in English, Hindi and 13 regional languages; candidates should confirm language availability in the current notice.

sections.heading: Application process
paragraphs: Applications are made through the official IBPS registration portal during the window stated in the relevant notification. For XIV, candidates could apply for Office Assistant and also for an officer post, but could apply for only one officer-cadre post; separate applications and fees were required where applicable. Online submission does not itself establish eligibility: IBPS states that applications remain subject to scrutiny and can be rejected if eligibility is not met.

Fee and deadline information is cycle-specific. In XIV, the stated online fee was ₹175 inclusive of GST for SC/ST/PwBD candidates for officer posts and ₹850 inclusive of GST for other officer applicants; Office Assistant fee categories differed, including ₹175 for SC/ST/PwBD/ESM/DESM candidates. These 2025 figures should not be used as a forecast for a future cycle.
bullets: Read the detailed notification before registration and select the correct post, state/UT and RRB preferences where required.
Prepare the photograph, signature, thumb impression, handwritten declaration and any live-photograph or identity details in the specifications published for that cycle.
Keep the registration number, password, e-receipt and submitted application. IBPS advises re-login after payment and printing the e-receipt/application when registration succeeds.
Use the edit/correction facility only if and when the notification provides one; IBPS says already submitted registered data generally cannot simply be changed outside the applicable edit window.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Build preparation around the post-specific official test structure: practise the objective sections under the published time limit, then use timed mixed sets and full-length computer-based simulations. For Office Assistant and Scale I, preparation should separately account for the preliminary screening stage and the main examination; for Scale II/III, it should cover the single examination and the advertised specialist or professional content where relevant.

Use official materials for process familiarity. IBPS says a mock-test link is made available when call letters are issued so candidates can view the system interface, and its RRB programme has provided online pre-examination training for eligible candidates under government-guideline categories. PET is familiarisation support, not a substitute for study.
bullets: Read the current notification and information handout first; make a section-and-time plan from that document.
Practise the on-screen actions IBPS describes: selecting, clearing, saving and marking answers for review.
For officer interviews, organise originals and valid eligibility/category documents early; the interview call letter and notification specify the required documents.
Do not depend on coaching-site syllabus summaries where they conflict with the current IBPS notice.

sections.heading: Results, allotment and employment outcome
paragraphs: A successful IBPS RRB result leads to provisional allotment, not automatically to an appointment letter. Allotment is based on the relevant selection outcome, reported vacancies, merit, reservation-policy considerations, preferences where applicable and administrative requirements. For Scale I and Office Assistant, XIV tied allotment to the state/UT applied for; Scale II and III allotment was to an RRB according to merit-cum-preference and the published process.

IBPS states that its role ends after provisional allotment and that the allotted bank/organisation makes the appointment offer. The bank can therefore conduct appointment-stage checks and apply its own joining requirements. Pay, posting, probation and service conditions are employer matters and should be confirmed from the allotted RRB rather than inferred from the IBPS exam notice.
bullets: Check results, score information, cut-offs and allotment notices only through official IBPS channels.
Preserve credentials and documents through joining; document or eligibility failures can affect candidature.

The XIV CRP validity was stated to expire one year after provisional allotment or when a fresh provisional allotment was made, whichever occurred earlier; validity terms may differ in later notifications.

title: IBPS Specialist Officer Agricultural Field Officer Examination
description: A national IBPS recruitment examination for Agricultural Field Officer posts in participating public-sector banks, open to eligible agricultural engineering graduates.

quick_facts.label: Conducting process and post
quick_facts.value: IBPS CRP-SPL-XVI recruits Agricultural Field Officers (Scale I) for participating banks for the 2027–28 vacancy cycle.

quick_facts.label: 2026 application window
quick_facts.value: For CRP-SPL-XVI, online registration and online fee payment are scheduled from 1 July 2026 through 21 July 2026, inclusive; IBPS describes the schedule as tentative where applicable.

quick_facts.label: Core qualification
quick_facts.value: The current AFO eligibility route is a four-year degree in one of the notified agriculture or allied disciplines, including Horticulture and Agricultural Engineering; IBPS does not accept an unspecified “equivalent” qualification.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: The process comprises an online preliminary examination, an online main examination, and a common interview, followed by provisional allotment to a participating bank for eligible candidates high enough in merit.

quick_facts.label: 2026 fee context
quick_facts.value: For CRP-SPL-XVI, the dated application fee/intimation charge is ₹175 inclusive of GST for SC/ST/PwBD candidates and ₹850 inclusive of GST for all other candidates, plus any applicable bank transaction charges.

sections.heading: What the IBPS AFO examination is for
paragraphs: The IBPS Specialist Officer Agricultural Field Officer examination is the Agricultural Field Officer (Scale I) stream within IBPS’s Common Recruitment Process for Specialist Officers (CRP-SPL). IBPS conducts the online examination stages and coordinates the process, while participating banks conduct the common interview through nodal-bank arrangements.

For the CRP-SPL-XVI cycle, the process is intended for participating-bank vacancies in financial year 2027–28. IBPS states that notified vacancies are indicative and that eventual provisional allotment depends on actual vacancies reported by participating banks.
bullets: This is a specialist-officer banking recruitment route, not an agricultural university entrance examination.
A successful candidate is provisionally allotted to a participating bank; the bank subsequently controls appointment, document verification, joining terms, and posting decisions.

sections.heading: Eligibility for Agricultural Field Officer (Scale I)
paragraphs: For CRP-SPL-XVI, applicants must be at least 20 and not more than 30 years old as of 1 July 2026, subject to the notification’s category-specific age relaxations and other conditions.

The required qualification is a four-year graduation degree from a Government of India-recognised or regulator-approved institution in a specifically listed discipline: Agriculture, Horticulture, Animal Husbandry, Veterinary Science, Dairy Science, Fishery Science, Pisciculture, Agricultural Marketing and Cooperation, Co-operation and Banking, Agro-Forestry, Forestry, Agricultural Biotechnology, B.Tech Biotechnology, Food Science, Agriculture Business Management, Food Technology, Dairy Technology, Agricultural Engineering, Sericulture, or Fisheries Engineering. The final result must have been declared by 21 July 2026.

For posts other than IT Officer, including AFO, the notification also requires a certificate, diploma, or degree in computer operations/language, or study of Computer or Information Technology at high-school, college, or institute level. Applicants should treat the published degree list as exhaustive because IBPS says it will not consider equivalent qualifications.
bullets: A B.Sc. (Hons.) Horticulture pathway may qualify when it is a four-year Horticulture graduation degree meeting the notification’s recognition and result-date requirements.
A B.Tech in Agricultural Engineering pathway is explicitly listed, provided it is a four-year degree and the candidate meets the other conditions.
Eligibility is checked later as well: an online application or examination result does not itself establish appointment eligibility.

sections.heading: Current CRP-SPL-XVI assessment format
paragraphs: The AFO preliminary examination is online and has four separately timed tests: English Language (25 questions, 25 marks, 20 minutes); Reasoning (25 questions, 25 marks, 20 minutes); Quantitative Aptitude (25 questions, 25 marks, 20 minutes); and Professional Knowledge (25 questions, 50 marks, 20 minutes). The total is 100 questions, 125 marks, and 80 minutes. Candidates must meet IBPS cut-offs in each test to be considered for main-examination shortlisting.

The AFO main examination is online and has English Language (30 questions, 30 marks, 25 minutes), Reasoning (40 questions, 40 marks, 35 minutes), Quantitative Aptitude (30 questions, 30 marks, 25 minutes), and Professional Knowledge objective questions (50 questions, 100 marks, 40 minutes): 150 questions, 200 marks, and 125 minutes in total. For this group of posts, the non-professional tests are qualifying and merit listing is based on Professional Knowledge.
In both objective examination stages, an incorrect answer carries a penalty of one-fourth (0.25) of the marks assigned to that question; an unanswered question has no penalty.
bullets: Preliminary stage: screening/shortlisting stage, with four sectional tests.
Main stage: professional knowledge is decisive for merit listing and interview shortlisting.
Interview: 100 marks; the minimum qualifying mark is 40%, or 35% for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD candidates.

sections.heading: How to apply in the current cycle
paragraphs: IBPS accepts applications only online. For CRP-SPL-XVI, candidates use the IBPS website’s CRP-SPL route, choose the online application link, complete new registration, enter the required details, upload the prescribed materials, pay online, and submit the application.

The currently notified registration and payment period is 1 July 2026 to 21 July 2026, inclusive. This is dated information: applicants should verify the live IBPS notice and application portal for any corrigendum, edit-window instructions, or schedule change before submitting.

Applicants may apply for only one post in the process. They should preserve the evidence needed for interview/document verification, including proof that the qualifying result was declared by the stated eligibility date and, where applicable, official CGPA/OGPA-to-percentage conversion documentation.
bullets: Read the detailed notification before registration; the submitted form remains subject to later scrutiny.
Use a name that exactly matches the required identity and educational documents.
Do not rely on a submitted application as confirmation of eligibility; IBPS and the participating bank verify eligibility later.

sections.heading: Preparation priorities from the official format
paragraphs: A practical preparation plan should be built around the sections IBPS actually tests. For the preliminary stage, allocate timed practice across English, Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, and agriculture-related Professional Knowledge, because every test has its own 20-minute limit and requires a minimum cut-off.

For the main examination, prioritize Professional Knowledge in the eligible agriculture and allied-domain curriculum: it carries 100 of 200 marks and is the test used for AFO merit listing. Continue timed practice in English, Reasoning, and Quantitative Aptitude because they remain qualifying tests.
Use accuracy-aware practice rather than blind guessing. The official one-fourth-mark negative penalty applies to wrong answers in both preliminary and main objective tests.
bullets: Simulate the preliminary examination as four 20-minute sections.
Simulate the main examination as four separately timed sections totaling 125 minutes.
Review the official notification again before the exam because IBPS reserves the right to communicate examination-structure changes on its website.

sections.heading: From main examination to bank appointment
paragraphs: Only candidates shortlisted from the main examination are called to the common interview. The final combined score uses an 80:20 weightage for the online main examination and interview respectively; candidates must qualify both and rank sufficiently high for the provisional-allotment process.

Provisional allotment is made on merit-cum-preference, reservation-related government guidelines, administrative requirements, and actual vacancies reported by participating banks. It is not itself an employment offer: the allotted bank separately verifies eligibility and determines appointment formalities and terms.

This is an all-India cadre process. Subject to meeting all requirements, provisionally allotted candidates may be posted anywhere in India or outside India at the participating bank’s discretion. The CRP-SPL-XVI schedule lists provisional allotment as January 2027, but IBPS marks recruitment timing and vacancies as subject to change.
bullets: The main-examination score—not the preliminary score—is used for interview shortlisting and final merit listing.
An interview score below the applicable minimum does not qualify a candidate for allotment.
A reserve list may be maintained, but IBPS says it does not guarantee subsequent allotment or recruitment.

title: ICAR AIEEA
description: ICAR AIEEA — ug entrance exam (agriculture), conducted by NTA.

quick_facts.label: Current UG admission route
quick_facts.value: For academic year 2026-27, the former ICAR UG entrance route is administered as CUET (ICAR-UG) through CUET (UG)-2026, rather than as a separately scheduled ICAR AIEEA-UG examination.

quick_facts.label: Conducting bodies
quick_facts.value: NTA conducts the examination and declares the result/merit list; ICAR administers the agriculture-and-allied-sciences admission pathway and online counselling.

quick_facts.label: Scope
quick_facts.value: CUET (ICAR-UG)-2026 is for ICAR quota admission to bachelor’s programmes in agriculture and allied sciences, explicitly excluding Veterinary Sciences.

quick_facts.label: Programmes covered in 2026-27
quick_facts.value: The 2026 bulletin lists 13 four-year bachelor’s programmes, including Agriculture, Horticulture, Fisheries, Forestry, Community Science, Agricultural Engineering, Dairy Technology, Food Technology and Biotechnology.

quick_facts.label: Baseline academic eligibility
quick_facts.value: Applicants must have passed Class 12/equivalent with at least three core subjects drawn from Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture/Inter-Agriculture; the candidate’s CUET subject choices must match subjects passed in Class 12.

quick_facts.label: Minimum marks and age for 2026
quick_facts.value: The 2026 bulletin specifies 50% aggregate in the qualifying examination for General/OBC-NCL/UPS/EWS applicants and 40% for SC/ST/Third Gender/PwBD applicants; applicants must be at least 16 on August 31, 2026. Universities may impose additional programme-specific conditions.

quick_facts.label: 2026 registration status
quick_facts.value: ICAR’s January 15, 2026 notice stated that CUET (UG)-2026 registration for this route ran from January 3 through January 30, 2026, 11:50 PM. This was a cycle-specific deadline and is past as of July 2026.

sections.heading: What ICAR AIEEA means for UG applicants now
paragraphs: “ICAR AIEEA” remains a useful legacy label in career guidance, but applicants to undergraduate agriculture and allied-sciences programmes should use the current official name: CUET (ICAR-UG). For the 2026-27 session, ICAR states that admission to its All India Quota (AIQ) seats in 13 UG programmes is through CUET (UG)-2026. NTA has conducted ICAR’s competitive examinations since 2019, while ICAR sets the agriculture-specific admission framework and conducts counselling.

The route is designed for bachelor’s admission in agriculture and allied sciences in the ICAR-AU system. In 2026-27 it applies to 20% of university seats, with specified institutions having 100% ICAR-quota coverage. It does not cover Veterinary Sciences; students targeting B.V.Sc. & A.H. should confirm the distinct admission route applicable to their intended institution rather than treating CUET (ICAR-UG) as a veterinary entrance examination.
bullets: The 13 listed programmes are four-year degrees and include B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture, Horticulture, Forestry and Community Science; B.F.Sc.; and B.Tech programmes in Agricultural Engineering, Dairy Technology, Food Technology and Biotechnology.

The bulletin also lists Food Nutrition and Dietetics, Sericulture, Natural Farming and Agribusiness Management; programme and university availability must be checked in the counselling material for the relevant year.

sections.heading: Eligibility: match Class 12 subjects to the intended programme
paragraphs: For CUET (ICAR-UG)-2026, an Indian-national applicant must have passed a recognized 10+2/equivalent examination after 12 years of study. The baseline subject rule is at least three core subjects selected from Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture/Inter-Agriculture. A diploma or vocational course taken after matriculation is not accepted as the qualifying route under this bulletin.

Subject selection is consequential: candidates must take at least three relevant CUET subjects and may not use subjects different from those passed in Class 12. ICAR says that a mismatch can lead to disqualification from counselling or admission. The bulletin also gives baseline aggregate-mark and minimum-age requirements, but the admitting university can set additional conditions, including a specific Class 12 combination, an upper age limit, or other programme rules.
bullets: 2026 baseline qualifying marks: 50% aggregate for General, OBC-NCL, UPS and EWS; 40% for SC, ST, Third Gender and PwBD. No rounding up is permitted.
2026 minimum age: 16 years as of August 31, 2026; no relaxation is provided for the minimum age.

Check the university-wise conditions in the year’s counselling brochure before applying. For example, engineering or dairy technology programmes may require a more specific subject combination than the general ICAR baseline.

sections.heading: Examination format and score use
paragraphs: The current ICAR-UG bulletin does not prescribe a standalone AIEEA-UG paper pattern. It states that the CUET (ICAR-UG)-2026 test, its schedule and its syllabus are defined and notified by NTA through the CUET portal. Therefore, candidates should treat the current NTA CUET (UG) information bulletin—not old AIEEA-UG question-count or marking-scheme pages—as the controlling source for the test format of their cycle.

ICAR uses the CUET route to generate merit ranks for agriculture-and-allied-sciences admissions. Qualifying or taking the test alone does not guarantee a seat: allocation depends on merit rank, programme/university subject eligibility, available seats and fulfilment of all admission requirements through ICAR counselling.
bullets: The 2026 bulletin says NTA determines the examination date, duration, timing, city, centre and shift through its schedule and the candidate’s admit card.

ICAR noted that the 2025-26 seat figures in its bulletin were guidance only; the actual 2026-27 seats and special conditions were to be published in the Online Counselling Brochure. Seat counts therefore vary by admission year and university.

sections.heading: Application and counselling process
paragraphs: Apply online through the NTA CUET portal during the applicable registration window, selecting only the subjects that correspond to the applicant’s Class 12 subjects and intended ICAR-UG options. The 2026 ICAR notice announced a January 3–30, 2026 registration period; that window has passed, so a future applicant should wait for and follow the next official NTA/ICAR notice rather than rely on that date.

After completing the form and paying the required NTA fee, retain the confirmation page, payment proof and uploaded-photo record. NTA issues the e-admit card through its portal. After results, only candidates declared eligible by ICAR for counselling registration and choice filling are considered for programme, seat and agricultural-university allocation. Admission and any scholarship linked to this route require participation in ICAR counselling.
bullets: Use an active personal email address and mobile number; the bulletin says these cannot later be changed.
The candidate does not select an agricultural university in the initial application form; university and programme choices are handled through the subsequent counselling process.
Verify the counselling brochure for the specific cycle because university-specific eligibility, seat numbers and other conditions can change.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Start by mapping the intended degree to its university-level Class 12 subject requirements, then register for the corresponding CUET subjects already studied in Class 12. This is more important than preparing from legacy AIEEA-UG materials, because ICAR’s current bulletin directs candidates to NTA’s CUET (UG) bulletin and syllabus for examination instructions and content.

Build preparation around the official NTA syllabus for the selected subjects, with systematic revision of the Class 12 curriculum, timed practice in the current CUET interface/pattern when NTA publishes it, and careful review of the final NTA and ICAR notices. Do not add subjects merely because they seem useful for a course: ICAR warns that attempting subjects different from those passed in Class 12 can invalidate counselling eligibility.
bullets: Read the current NTA CUET (UG) information bulletin and syllabus before finalising subjects.
Keep copies of Class 12 marksheets, category/PwBD documents where applicable, identity records and application confirmation materials ready for later verification.
Before counselling, compare each target university’s programme-specific subject rule, age rule and other special conditions.

sections.heading: What this route can lead to
paragraphs: A successful CUET (ICAR-UG) merit rank and ICAR counselling allocation can lead to a four-year undergraduate programme in agriculture or allied sciences at participating institutions in the ICAR-AU system. The current route provides pathways aligned with this node’s child degrees—B.F.Sc., B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture, Community Science, Forestry and Horticulture, plus B.Tech in Agricultural Engineering, Biotechnology, Dairy Technology and Food Technology—subject to programme availability and the chosen university’s eligibility conditions.

This is an admission pathway, not a degree or an employment guarantee. Course outcomes, internships, fees, seat availability and placement opportunities vary substantially by university and programme. Candidates should evaluate the individual institution and its current accreditation/programme status separately before accepting a seat.
bullets: The 2026 bulletin identifies 13 agriculture-and-allied bachelor’s programmes for the route and notes that these undergraduate agricultural-science degrees have been declared professional degrees.
ICAR publishes an updated list of accredited agricultural universities, colleges and programmes; use it alongside the cycle’s counselling brochure when comparing institutions.

title: ICAR AIEEA PG
description: National entrance examination for postgraduate admission to ICAR-affiliated agricultural and fisheries science programmes, including M.F.Sc. courses.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: ICAR AIEEA (PG) is the All India Entrance Examination for Admission to postgraduate/master’s programmes in agriculture and allied sciences; NTA conducts the test and ICAR uses the process for PG admissions and ICAR-PG scholarships.

quick_facts.label: 2026–27 test format
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, the examination was a single English-language computer-based test: 120 multiple-choice questions in 120 minutes, with +4 for a correct answer, −1 for an incorrect answer, and 0 for an unattempted question.

quick_facts.label: Eligibility baseline
quick_facts.value: For ICAR-AU-system PG admission in 2026, applicants generally needed an eligible four-/six-year bachelor’s degree or a five-/five-and-a-half-year B.V.Sc. & A.H. degree, plus the prescribed OGPA or percentage; subject-specific eligibility and the admitting university’s rules also apply.

quick_facts.label: Subject choice
quick_facts.value: The 2026 bulletin lists 20 major subject groups and 81 sub-subjects. Candidates select one major subject group compatible with their undergraduate subject; sub-subject choices are made during online counselling.

quick_facts.label: Fisheries route
quick_facts.value: Fisheries Science is a major subject group in AIEEA (PG), with listed areas including aquaculture, fish processing technology, aquatic animal health management, fisheries extension, fish genetics and breeding, and fisheries economics. Exact master’s degree nomenclature can vary by university.

quick_facts.label: 2026 timing and fee context
quick_facts.value: The 2026 application window ran from May 8 to June 7, 2026, and the exam was scheduled for July 4, 2026. The published examination fee was ₹1,300 for General/Unreserved, ₹1,255 for OBC-NCL/UPS/EWS, and ₹675 for SC/ST/PwBD/Third Gender, excluding applicable payment-processing charges. These dates and fees are cycle-specific.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
paragraphs: ICAR AIEEA (PG) is the national entrance route used for postgraduate admissions under the ICAR–Agricultural University system. For the 2026–27 cycle, the official bulletin describes admission through ICAR All India Quota seats at participating agricultural universities and institutes; the final university- and subject-wise seat availability is published for counselling.

The examination covers agricultural and allied disciplines rather than a single degree title. Its 2026 subject structure included groups such as horticulture, forestry, agricultural engineering and technology, community science, fisheries science, dairy science, dairy technology, food science technology, agri-business management, and water science and technology. For a fisheries graduate, the Fisheries Science group is the relevant route for participating universities’ fisheries master’s offerings, whose award title may differ by institution.
bullets: NTA’s role includes candidate registration, test conduct, answer-key challenges, result declaration, and transfer of the resulting data to ICAR.
Candidates take one major subject-group test aligned with their undergraduate discipline; qualifying sub-subject preferences are made later in ICAR online counselling.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: Eligibility has two layers: a candidate must meet the examination rules and must also satisfy the specific programme and admitting university’s requirements. In the 2026 bulletin, Indian nationals were required to meet both; merely applying, appearing, or qualifying did not itself establish admission eligibility.

The normal degree-duration rule for the ICAR-AU system was a four-/six-year bachelor’s programme after 10+2 or a five-/five-and-a-half-year B.V.Sc. & A.H. programme. Three-year bachelor’s graduates were generally not eligible in ICAR agricultural universities, with limited course-specific exceptions at ICAR deemed universities named in the bulletin. The relevant subject table must be checked before applying: for example, fisheries, dairy technology, food technology, forestry, horticulture, and community science graduates have different eligible subject pathways.

For 2026, the general minimum OGPA was 6.60/10 for General, OBC, UPS, and EWS candidates, or 5.60/10 for SC/ST/PwBD/Third Gender candidates, with equivalent cut-offs listed for other grading scales. Where grades were not awarded, the bulletin also specifies percentage-based standards. University-specific equivalence, additional conditions, and document verification remain decisive at admission.
bullets: Choose a major subject group only after matching the undergraduate degree against the subject-specific eligibility table.
Confirm that the undergraduate institution and degree will be accepted by the admitting university; the bulletin states that degree equivalence is decided by that university.
Treat all eligibility, age, seat, and programme exceptions shown in the current year’s bulletin and counselling material as controlling.

sections.heading: Examination format
paragraphs: In 2026, AIEEA (PG) used one computer-based, objective multiple-choice paper in English. It contained 120 questions to be completed in two hours. The scoring scheme was +4 for each correct answer, −1 for each incorrect answer, and no marks for a question left unattempted.

ICAR prepares an overall merit/rank list separately for each major subject. In a tied score, the 2026 rules placed the candidate with fewer negative marks higher; further tie-breaks used age and then Class XII percentage/CGPA.
bullets: Mode: computer-based test (CBT).
Questions: 120 MCQs; four options are shown for each question in the CBT interface.
Medium: English only.
Merit is subject-group-specific, so candidates should select their examination group carefully.

sections.heading: Application and counselling process
paragraphs: The application is online through the NTA ICAR examination portal. The 2026 process required candidates to register and receive an application number, complete personal, educational, programme and examination-city details, upload the required images/documents, pay the fee online, and save the confirmation page. NTA stated that applications submitted in another mode would not be accepted.

For the 2026 cycle, online applications were accepted from May 8 through June 7, 2026; the correction window was June 9–10, and the examination was held on July 4, 2026. These dates have passed and should not be used as a future-cycle deadline. The next cycle’s bulletin and notices on the NTA/ICAR portals are the authoritative source for new dates, fees, document specifications, and correction rules.

After the result, only candidates declared eligible for registration and choice filling by ICAR can participate in online counselling. Allocation of the subject and agricultural university follows that counselling process, and the bulletin states that admission and scholarships are granted through the ICAR counselling route.
bullets: Use one application only, a personal active email address and mobile number, and retain the application number and confirmation page.
Upload the candidate’s own live photograph, scanned photograph, signature, and applicable PwD/PwBD documentation in the prescribed format.
Read the current bulletin before payment: application fees, bank/payment-gateway charges, deadlines, and allowed correction fields may change by cycle.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Start by selecting the correct major subject group from the official eligibility table, then prepare against ICAR’s prescribed syllabus for that group. This avoids a common strategic error: studying broadly for a desired master’s specialisation while choosing an examination group that is not compatible with the undergraduate qualification.

Use timed CBT practice that reproduces the official constraints: 120 questions in 120 minutes and negative marking. Because an incorrect response carries a one-mark deduction, build an attempt strategy that distinguishes high-confidence answers from guesses. This is preparation advice inferred from the published scoring scheme, not an official cut-off or attempt target.

Before the examination, use the NTA bulletin’s CBT instructions to familiarise yourself with the on-screen question palette, review marking, and submission flow. Monitor the official NTA portal for admit-card, city-intimation, answer-key, and result notices.
bullets: Download and map every syllabus topic to undergraduate notes, standard texts, and topic-wise question practice.
Run full-length two-hour mocks and review errors by topic as well as by avoidable negative marks.
Keep official eligibility, syllabus, and counselling notices separate from coaching or social-media guidance; the official bulletin governs admission.

sections.heading: Results, admission and scholarship outcomes
paragraphs: AIEEA (PG) results are issued as an overall merit rank in the candidate’s major subject for candidates declared eligible for counselling choice filling. A rank does not by itself allocate a seat: candidates must complete ICAR online counselling, where eligible candidates are considered for subject and university allocation.

For 2026, the bulletin stated that the prior academic year had 4,883 ICAR All India Quota PG seats across relevant programmes, while also making clear that the final current-cycle seat count would be displayed at counselling. Seat availability is therefore variable by cycle, university, and sub-subject.

Meritorious candidates admitted to eligible course-and-research master’s programmes may be awarded an ICAR-PG Scholarship, subject to the applicable rules and counselling outcome. The 2026 published rate was ₹12,640 per month plus a ₹6,000 annual contingent grant, normally for up to two years; the number of scholarships and governing rules can change, and the bulletin says final scholarship availability is known at counselling. Eligible candidates may also receive National Talent Scholarship support under the applicable guidelines.
bullets: Check the NTA result portal and ICAR counselling notices rather than relying on individual communications.
Complete counselling and admissions verification promptly; documents are verified by the admitting university.
For a fisheries pathway, verify the specific university’s programme title, prerequisite degree, seats, and any special conditions before locking counselling choices.

title: ICMR-JRF
description: ICMR-JRF — doctoral or fellowship exam (medical), conducted by ICMR / NTA.

quick_facts.label: Current identity and status
quick_facts.value: “ICMR-JRF” is the legacy name for ICMR’s non-medical doctoral-fellowship eligibility examination. ICMR labels its JRF page “until 2023 batch” and states that the programme was revised as the Biomedical Research Eligibility Test (BRET) from 2024 onward.

quick_facts.label: Purpose
quick_facts.value: The successor DHR-BRET determines eligibility of Indian nationals for a Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) to pursue Ph.D. research in biomedical/health-research subjects; qualification alone does not confer a fellowship without placement at an eligible host institution.

quick_facts.label: Exam administration
quick_facts.value: For the DHR-BRET 2025 cycle, AIIMS New Delhi’s Examination Section handled the online application, computer-based test, and declaration of eligible candidates; DHR retained responsibility for fellowship award, placement, disbursal, and tenure.

quick_facts.label: Latest published eligibility context
quick_facts.value: The DHR-BRET 2025 notice accepted specified M.Sc./equivalent PG qualifications, including M.Tech and M.Pharm in listed biomedical and health-related disciplines, with 55% for General/EWS/OBC and 50% for SC/ST/PwBD applicants. Its stated base upper-age limit was 35 years as of the application closing date, with category-based relaxations.

quick_facts.label: Latest published test pattern
quick_facts.value: The DHR-BRET 2025 notice specified an English-medium CBT: 150 MCQs in 180 minutes, with +1 for a correct answer and −0.25 for an incorrect answer.

quick_facts.label: Fellowship support context
quick_facts.value: Under the current DHR HRD guidelines, BRET-selected fellows are listed for ₹37,000 per month plus HRA during JRF years 1–2 and ₹42,000 plus HRA after approved SRF upgradation for years 3–5, plus a ₹20,000 annual contingency. These are scheme guidelines, not a permanent salary guarantee, and should be rechecked against the applicable call and award letter.

sections.heading: What ICMR-JRF means now
paragraphs: ICMR-JRF was a national eligibility examination for an ICMR-supported Ph.D./research fellowship. For new cycles, applicants should treat DHR-BRET—not the legacy ICMR-JRF examination—as the relevant examination route: ICMR explicitly says the JRF programme was revised as BRET from 2024 onward.

DHR describes BRET as part of its biomedical-research fellowships for scholars with non-medical backgrounds. The route is intended to support postgraduate science applicants pursuing a Ph.D. in biomedical sciences, with the research topic falling within the DHR–ICMR mandate.
bullets: Passing the examination establishes eligibility; it does not by itself secure admission, a supervisor, a host institution, or fellowship activation.

The 2025 BRET notice described two placement routes: a Ph.D. at a UGC-recognized university/research institution or Institute of National Importance, or a Ph.D. at an ICMR institute/centre under the AcSIR–ICMR Faculty of Medical Research.
Because notices, administering agencies, and allocations can change by session, applicants should use the current DHR/AIIMS notice rather than historic ICMR-JRF schedules.

sections.heading: Eligibility: use the current BRET notice
paragraphs: The latest detailed official examination notice located, DHR-BRET 2025, required an M.Sc. or equivalent postgraduate qualification (including M.Tech/M.Pharm) in listed life-science, biomedical, health, and related disciplines. It specified minimum PG marks of 55% for General/EWS/OBC candidates and 50% for SC/ST/PwBD candidates.

That notice also permitted final-year postgraduate candidates to apply as result-awaited applicants, but made JRF eligibility conditional on later producing proof of the qualifying Master’s degree with the required marks. It set a base age limit of 35 years as on the application deadline, with non-cumulative relaxation provisions listed for SC/ST, PwBD, female, and OBC applicants.

Eligibility to sit the test is distinct from eligibility to activate the fellowship. DHR’s scheme guidelines require the proposed Ph.D. work to be biomedical/health-research related and require host-institution, guide, doctoral-registration, synopsis, and other joining documentation.
bullets: Verify the discipline list in the notice for the particular cycle; do not infer eligibility solely from the older ICMR-JRF rules.
Check both the examination notice and the fellowship/HRD guidelines before applying, especially if you are result-awaited, near the age limit, already employed, or receiving another stipend.
Reservation and relaxation are governed by the applicable Government of India policy and the cycle-specific notice.

sections.heading: Exam format and syllabus
paragraphs: In the DHR-BRET 2025 notification, the examination was an English-only computer-based test of 150 objective MCQs in 180 minutes. The published marking rule was one mark for a correct response, minus 0.25 for an incorrect response, and zero for an unanswered question.

The paper was divided into three roughly equal components: Section A, aptitude and analytical skills; Section B, general/interdisciplinary biomedical and life-science knowledge; and Section C, a chosen discipline-specific domain. The 2025 notice stated that candidates choose one Section C discipline during application, including options such as microbiology, biochemistry, biostatistics, public health, nursing, biotechnology, social and behavioural sciences, nutrition, pharmacology, and biological sciences.

The stated standard was the qualifying-degree level, appropriate for higher study and research. The official notice, not older ICMR-JRF papers, should be the primary specification for the active BRET cycle.
bullets: Section A: reading comprehension, reasoning, data interpretation, analytical and quantitative skills.
Section B: cross-disciplinary foundations such as cell biology, physiology, genetics/genomics, biotechnology, biosafety/bioethics, immunology, and infectious diseases.
Section C: approximately 50 questions from the selected subject domain.

sections.heading: How to apply and what happens after qualification
paragraphs: For the 2025 BRET session, applications were online through the AIIMS examinations website; physical application documents were not to be sent. The official notice instructed applicants to retain their registration slip and payment proof and to monitor the portal for notices, corrections, city/centre information, admit card, and results. The actual portal, dates, document specifications, and correction window must be taken from the next live notice.

As dated 2025 fee context only, the notice listed ₹2,000 for General/OBC, ₹1,600 for SC/ST/EWS, and an exemption for PwBD applicants; online payment processing charges could also apply. Fees and categories may change, so this is not a current fee quote.

After selection, the fellowship has further steps beyond the exam: the DHR guidelines require a willingness letter, ePMS registration, a research synopsis routed through the guide and host institution, joining documents, Ph.D. registration/enrolment evidence, and relevant ethics approvals for human or animal research.
bullets: Before the application opens: confirm degree/marks/age eligibility and select the most appropriate Section C subject domain.
During application: follow the live notice precisely for photograph/signature, category certificates, payment, state/centre preferences, and correction dates.
After qualification: secure an eligible host institution and guide, then meet the fellowship activation and research-proposal requirements within the timelines in the award letter and guidelines.

sections.heading: Preparation approach aligned to the official blueprint
paragraphs: Build preparation from the current BRET notice’s three components rather than relying only on the old ICMR-JRF pattern. Allocate study time across aptitude/analytical work, common biomedical foundations, and the selected domain because the 2025 format assigned approximately 50 questions to each.

For Section A, practise reading comprehension, verbal and non-verbal reasoning, data interpretation, logical/deductive reasoning, numerical analysis, and graphical interpretation. For Section B, revise the published cross-disciplinary topics at postgraduate depth. For Section C, map your postgraduate coursework to the selected domain’s official syllabus topics.

Use timed CBT-style practice to accommodate the 150-question, 180-minute format and the published negative marking. Before finalising a study plan, download the current notice because the syllabus, domain choices, scoring, and examination agency may be revised for a later session.
bullets: Prioritise accuracy as well as speed: the latest published pattern imposed a −0.25 deduction for an incorrect response.
Choose the Section C domain that best matches both your qualifying discipline and intended biomedical Ph.D. research direction.
Maintain a separate checklist for exam eligibility and fellowship placement requirements; a strong test score does not replace the need for an eligible host, guide, and research proposal.

sections.heading: What qualification can lead to
paragraphs: A successful BRET candidate may pursue doctoral research in a biomedical or health-research subject through an eligible UGC/Institute of National Importance route or, for the designated ICMR–AcSIR route, at one of the ICMR institutes/centres. Placement remains a condition of award, and the precise number and allocation of fellowships is subject to the notified cycle and budget.

DHR’s guidelines describe a five-year overall tenure or completion of the Ph.D., whichever is earlier. JRF is generally for the first two years; after a satisfactory progress assessment and institutional recommendation, the fellow may be upgraded to SRF after 22 months. The rules provide for exceptional no-cost extension only within the stated outer limit.

Financial support is variable policy context, not an employment salary. The current guideline lists ₹37,000/month plus HRA for JRF years one and two, ₹42,000/month plus HRA after approved SRF upgradation in years three to five, and ₹20,000 annual contingency; applicants should verify the award letter and active scheme rules before relying on these figures.
bullets: The 2025 notice described selection on BRET performance and a tentative 250 selected candidates, subject to budgetary provisions and DHR guidelines.
DHR guidelines describe a combined merit threshold of 50% for General-UR/OBC/PwBD/EWS and 45% for SC/ST; the final merit and fellowship offer remain governed by the applicable notification.
Fellowship activation entails compliance duties, including a defined research plan, institutional support, progress review, and ethics clearance where applicable.
