title: IELTS
description: IELTS — abroad exam (general), conducted by British Council / IDP.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: IELTS is an English-language proficiency test used for study, work, professional registration and migration pathways abroad.

quick_facts.label: Test types
quick_facts.value: The principal options are IELTS Academic, generally for undergraduate/postgraduate study and some professional registration, and IELTS General Training, generally for migration, work, training or study below degree level.

quick_facts.label: Skills tested
quick_facts.value: Both Academic and General Training assess Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking; Listening and Speaking are the same across the two tests, while Reading and Writing differ.

quick_facts.label: Scoring
quick_facts.value: Candidates receive four component scores and an overall band score. The overall band is the average of the four component scores, rounded to the nearest whole or half band.

quick_facts.label: India booking context
quick_facts.value: For candidates booking through IDP IELTS India, the official registration guidance requires a passport for registration and the original passport on test day; available test dates and seats vary by city and format.

sections.heading: Purpose and choosing the right IELTS test
paragraphs: IELTS is relevant to this node because it can provide the English-language evidence requested for overseas undergraduate or postgraduate admissions after programmes such as B.Sc. Nursing or BPT, including the foreign-university degree pathways listed as children of this node. IELTS Academic is the normal option for degree-level study and may also be used for professional registration; IELTS General Training is aimed at migration, work, training and study below degree level.

Applicants should not select a test solely from a general rule: the intended university, professional regulator, employer, or immigration authority determines the accepted test type and the required overall and component bands. For UK visa routes, candidates may specifically need an IELTS for UKVI product, so the relevant UKVI and visa requirement should be checked before booking.
bullets: For bachelor's, master's and other higher-education applications abroad, first check whether the institution specifies IELTS Academic and whether it imposes minimum scores in each skill.

For nursing and other regulated healthcare careers abroad, verify the requirement directly with the destination-country professional registration body; required bands and accepted test types vary by profession and jurisdiction.
For immigration or employment-led pathways, confirm whether General Training, Academic, or a UKVI-specific test is required before paying the test fee.

sections.heading: Test format and scoring
paragraphs: IELTS Academic and General Training contain Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking. In the Academic format, the stated total test time is 2 hours 45 minutes: Listening is about 30 minutes, Reading 60 minutes, Writing 60 minutes and Speaking 11–14 minutes. The Reading and Writing content changes by test type, whereas Listening and Speaking do not.

Scores are reported for each skill and as an overall result. IELTS calculates the overall band by averaging the four component bands and rounding to the nearest whole or half band. There is no universal passing band: the receiving institution, regulator or immigration authority sets the score it will accept.
bullets: Academic Writing has two tasks; Task 2 counts twice as much as Task 1 in the Writing score.
The Speaking test is a three-part interview with an examiner and is recorded.
Academic Listening has 40 questions in four parts; recordings are heard once.

sections.heading: Booking from India
paragraphs: A practical booking sequence is: identify the receiving organisation's required IELTS product and score; choose Academic, General Training or, where applicable, a UKVI option; select a delivery format, city and date; complete registration using passport details; pay the displayed fee; and retain the confirmation. IDP IELTS India's official guidance says candidates need their passport for registration and must carry the original passport on test day.

Test dates, city availability, delivery formats and fees are variable rather than national fixed deadlines. The official India booking guidance lists online, in-person and courier registration routes, but candidates should use the live booking flow to confirm current availability and charges before committing.
bullets: Match your booking name and passport details exactly.
Book only after checking the target university's programme-level language requirement, including any minimum band in Listening, Reading, Writing or Speaking.
Keep the booking confirmation and follow the test-centre instructions for identity documents and arrival.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Preparation should begin with the official format and sample tasks for the exact module booked. Official IELTS Academic materials provide sample Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking tasks, while the General Training materials provide module-specific Reading and Writing practice. These materials can be used to become familiar with task types, practise under timed conditions and compare responses with available model answers.

For Academic applicants, build preparation around the tasks actually assessed: academic reading passages, visual-information description and argumentative writing, together with the interactive three-part Speaking test. Use full timed practice, then diagnose weaknesses by skill because receiving organisations may set component-band minima as well as an overall requirement.
bullets: Use official samples rather than assuming Academic and General Training Reading/Writing are interchangeable.
Practise Writing Task 1 and Task 2 to their required minimum lengths; Academic Task 1 is at least 150 words and Task 2 at least 250 words.
Practise Speaking aloud in the three-part format, not only vocabulary memorisation.

sections.heading: Using results for overseas study and professional pathways
paragraphs: An IELTS Test Report Form is the official confirmation of the result and can be shared with organisations that need evidence of English proficiency. IELTS states that results for IELTS on Computer are available in 1–5 days and IELTS on Paper results in up to 13 days; timelines can vary by test product and operational circumstances.

IELTS recommends treating a result as valid for two years after the test date, although a university, employer, regulator or immigration authority can set its own acceptance policy. Applicants should therefore work backwards from application and visa deadlines, obtain the exact score target from the recipient, and avoid relying on a result that may be outside the recipient's permitted validity period.
bullets: A score itself does not guarantee university admission, professional registration, a job offer or a visa; it is one requirement assessed by the receiving organisation.
IELTS reports that Academic scores are recognised by more than 12,500 colleges, universities and professional bodies, but applicants must still verify acceptance for their exact programme and intake.
For overseas nursing and allied-health routes, confirm both the admissions requirement and any later professional-registration English requirement.

title: IIFT MBA(IB) Entrance
description: IIFT MBA(IB) Entrance — pg entrance exam (management), conducted by NTA.

quick_facts.label: Current admissions gateway
quick_facts.value: For IIFT’s full-time MBA (International Business) 2026–28 intake, the institute used CAT 2025 scores for shortlisting/selection, followed by Group Discussion and Personal Interview. This is not a separately administered NTA IIFT entrance test for that intake.

quick_facts.label: MBA (IB) eligibility for 2026–28
quick_facts.value: A recognised bachelor’s degree of at least three years in any discipline with at least 50% marks is required; the minimum is 45% for SC, ST and PwD candidates. Final-year candidates could apply subject to providing qualifying proof by October 31, 2026. IIFT states that there is no age limit.

quick_facts.label: Programme offered
quick_facts.value: The resulting programme is a two-year, full-time MBA (International Business), structured across six trimesters, and offered for the 2026–28 cycle at Delhi, Kolkata, Kakinada and GIFT City.

quick_facts.label: 2026–28 application fee context
quick_facts.value: For the 2026–28 MBA (IB) application, IIFT listed ₹3,000 for General/OBC-NCL/EWS applicants and ₹1,500 for SC/ST/PwD/Transgender applicants. These are intake-specific, non-refundable application fees and may change in a future admission cycle.

sections.heading: What this node represents now
paragraphs: “IIFT MBA(IB) Entrance” is best understood as the admissions route to the Indian Institute of Foreign Trade’s full-time MBA (International Business), rather than as a current standalone IIFT examination. For the 2026–28 intake, IIFT specified CAT 2025 as the score used for shortlisting and selection, with later Group Discussion (GD) and Personal Interview (PI) stages. Therefore, the node’s older description that labels it an NTA-conducted examination is not current for this intake.

The destination programme is a two-year, six-trimester general-management MBA with an international-business focus. IIFT describes it as preparing candidates for international-business operations and covering areas relevant to international business activity.
bullets: Use the official IIFT MBA(IB) admission notice and prospectus for the applicable intake; do not rely on legacy IIFT/NTA exam notices for current admissions.
CAT is an input to IIFT’s selection process; IIFT states that the IIMs have no role in IIFT’s selection process or in conducting the IIFT programme.

sections.heading: Eligibility for the 2026–28 MBA (IB) intake
paragraphs: IIFT’s 2026–28 prospectus requires a recognised bachelor’s degree of minimum three years’ duration in any discipline. The stated minimum is 50% marks, reduced to 45% for SC, ST and PwD candidates. There is no stated age limit.

Candidates appearing in the qualifying examination could apply provisionally, but had to submit evidence of the required qualification by October 31, 2026. A candidate who ultimately did not meet the minimum bachelor’s-degree percentage would have admission cancelled.
bullets: Academic stream: any discipline, subject to the degree and marks requirements.
Final-year status: permitted for the 2026–28 intake subject to the stated documentation deadline.
Category documentation: applicants claiming SC/ST/PwD/OBC-NCL/EWS/Kashmiri Migrant status were required to upload the relevant certificate with the application.

sections.heading: Selection format
paragraphs: For MBA (IB) 2026–28, IIFT’s selection pathway had two broad stages: shortlisting using CAT 2025 score and other defined parameters, then a second round comprising GD and PI for shortlisted candidates. IIFT’s separate selection-criteria notice says the shortlisting assessment included CAT score/percentile including sectional cut-offs, work experience and gender diversity.

For that cycle, IIFT published physical GD/PI locations at Delhi, Kolkata, Kakinada, GIFT City, Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, Indore, Lucknow and Mumbai, while reserving the right to change centres for administrative reasons. Future cycles can alter the test year accepted, cut-offs, weights, interview format and locations.
bullets: Stage 1: CAT-based shortlisting plus IIFT-defined parameters.
Stage 2: Group Discussion and Personal Interview for shortlisted applicants.
Check the intake-specific selection criteria rather than assuming that prior IIFT-exam patterns, NTA procedures, or CAT cut-offs remain applicable.

sections.heading: How the 2026–28 application process worked
paragraphs: IIFT directed applicants to apply online through its designated admissions portal. The published workflow was: create a login with a valid email address; complete personal and education details; upload photograph, signature and supporting documents; make online payment; submit; and retain a printed application for records. IIFT required a separate application for MBA (IB) and MBA (BA) where an applicant sought both programmes.

The published document list included Class 10 and 12 marksheets, graduation degree/provisional certificate/consolidated marksheet, work-experience documents where applicable, and category certificates where applicable. The application guidance says applicants did not need to post a printout or documents to IIFT, but documents would be scrutinised during verification.
bullets: Keep the CAT registration number available: IIFT instructed applicants to quote it, along with the IIFT application number and registered email, in admission-related communications.
For the 2026–28 MBA (IB) intake, payment options listed were debit card, credit card, net banking and UPI.
The published application fee was non-refundable; confirm fee, required documents and dates from the live official intake page before applying.

sections.heading: Preparation priorities
paragraphs: Because IIFT used CAT performance as the primary shortlisting input for the 2026–28 MBA (IB) intake, preparation should first prioritise the applicable CAT attempt and both overall and sectional performance. This follows from IIFT’s published selection criteria, which explicitly refer to CAT score, percentile and sectional cut-offs; applicants should wait for the next intake’s official criteria before treating any particular weight or cut-off as binding.

Applicants who expect to be shortlisted should also prepare for the later GD and PI. A sensible evidence-based approach is to organise accurate academics and work-experience records early, be ready to explain professional experience and career goals, and ensure that all claims in the application can be documented. IIFT’s guidance warns that ineligibility, incorrect information or suppression of material facts can result in cancellation of candidature or admission.
bullets: Build the application file early: academic records, identity/contact details, work-experience evidence and category certificate if applicable.
Prepare a clear account of interest in international business, because the MBA (IB) is specifically focused on international business and IIFT’s second stage includes GD/PI.
Use only the official IIFT notice for the relevant intake to determine the accepted CAT year, shortlist methodology and GD/PI requirements.

sections.heading: What successful admission leads to
paragraphs: Successful candidates enter IIFT’s full-time MBA (IB), a two-year programme with six trimesters and a focus on international business. The current programme page lists a summer internship project, a port visit, a social-awareness assignment and a final research project among programme components, alongside core and elective coursework.

For the 2026–28 prospectus, IIFT listed MBA (IB) seats as 240 each at Delhi and Kolkata and 120 each at GIFT City and Kakinada, with reservations under Government of India norms. Seat counts, campuses and programme arrangements are admission-cycle-specific and should be verified against the prospectus for the cycle being pursued.
bullets: Academic outcome: an MBA (International Business) from IIFT on completion of programme requirements.
Experiential components listed by IIFT include summer internship, port visit and research project.
The full-time MBA (IB) is described by IIFT as residential; the prospectus states that students are required to stay in the hostel.

title: IISER Aptitude Test (IAT)
description: IISER Aptitude Test (IAT) — ug entrance exam (science), conducted by IISERs.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: The IISER Aptitude Test (IAT) is the national undergraduate entrance test used for admissions to participating Indian Institutes of Science Education and Research (IISERs). For 2026, the IISER brochure covers 5-year BS-MS dual degrees and specified 4-year BS and B.Tech. programmes.

quick_facts.label: 2026 test date
quick_facts.value: IAT 2026 was scheduled for Sunday, June 7, 2026, from 9:00 AM to 12:00 noon IST. This is past as of July 18, 2026; candidates should treat later-cycle dates as variable and consult the next official admission portal.

quick_facts.label: Test structure
quick_facts.value: For 2026, IAT was a 3-hour computer-based test with 60 single-correct multiple-choice questions: 15 each in Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics, and Physics.

quick_facts.label: Baseline academic eligibility
quick_facts.value: For IAT 2026, applicants could be Indian nationals, OCI/PIO candidates, or foreign nationals, and needed a qualifying Class XII/equivalent credential or an eligible diploma within the stated 2024–2026 window. Candidates also needed at least three of Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics, and Physics in the qualifying examination. Programme-specific requirements can be stricter.

quick_facts.label: Core IISER destinations in 2026
quick_facts.value: The 2026 IISER admission portal listed 5-year BS-MS programmes at all IISERs, a BS-MS in Computational and Data Sciences at IISER Kolkata, 4-year BS programmes at IISER Bhopal and IISER Tirupati, and 4-year B.Tech. programmes at IISER Bhopal.

sections.heading: Purpose and role in the Indian science-education pathway
paragraphs: IAT is an entrance examination rather than a degree or professional licence. It is designed for entry to participating undergraduate science, interdisciplinary science, and selected engineering programmes; a test score is followed by the relevant institution’s admission, rank, seat-allocation, document-verification, and programme-eligibility processes.

The IISER system comprises autonomous institutions established under the Ministry of Education, Government of India, to promote interdisciplinary science education and research. For the 2026 cycle, admission to the IISER programmes described on the central portal was through IAT.

An IAT score may also be accepted by institutions that run their own admissions process. For example, IISc Bengaluru’s 2026 four-year BS (Research) admissions accepted IAT as one eligible national-examination route, while IIT Guwahati required a qualified IAT 2026 result for its four-year BS in Biomedical Science and Engineering. These are separate applications with separate eligibility rules, not automatic IISER seat allotments.
bullets: Use IAT primarily if the intended path is foundational science, research-oriented undergraduate study, or one of the specifically advertised BS/B.Tech. options.
Do not infer that every generic child degree in a career map is available through IAT: availability, subjects required, and admissions workflow depend on the particular institution and academic year.
IAT is not the entrance route for MBBS admission; medical undergraduate admission is governed separately by the applicable NEET-UG framework.

sections.heading: Eligibility: check both IAT and programme conditions
paragraphs: For the 2026 IAT cycle, the central brochure allowed Indian nationals, OCI/PIO candidates, and foreign nationals. The educational route was Class XII/equivalent completed in 2024, 2025, or 2026, or appearing in 2026, from a recognized board; it also recognized specified three-year-or-longer diploma routes within the same time period. Foreign-national equivalence documentation could be required.

Applicants had to have studied at least three subjects among Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics, and Physics in the qualifying examination. This makes IAT accessible to many PCB, PCMB, and PCM-oriented students, but it does not mean every programme is available to every subject combination.

Always apply the programme-level rule after the IAT rule. For example, IISc’s 2026 BS (Research) pathway required Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics as main qualifying subjects, and IIT Guwahati’s 2026 BS in Biomedical Science and Engineering required all four: Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, and Biology. The institution’s own notice controls for that destination.
bullets: Confirm qualifying-exam year, nationality category, board/diploma recognition, and the required subject combination.
Read the current information brochure and the destination institute’s admission notice before paying an application fee or making preference choices.
Reservation, category certificates, aggregate/performance criteria, and foreign-national documentation are cycle-specific and should be checked in the applicable official notice.

sections.heading: Examination format and syllabus focus
paragraphs: In 2026, IAT was conducted as a computer-based test of three hours. It contained 60 single-correct MCQs, divided evenly across Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics, and Physics: 15 questions per subject. Consequently, candidates from PCB or PCMB backgrounds should not assume that they can ignore Mathematics, and candidates from PCM backgrounds should not assume that they can ignore Biology.

The official admissions portal publishes the cycle-specific syllabus, mock-test access, answer-key material, and previous-year question papers. Because syllabus wording and test arrangements can change from one admission year to the next, use the official material for the cycle being attempted rather than relying on coaching summaries or old patterns.
bullets: Plan preparation across all four IAT subjects, not only the subjects required by a preferred degree.
Practise in computer-based, timed conditions for the full three-hour duration.
Use the official syllabus as the scope document and official previous papers/mock test as pattern evidence.

sections.heading: Application and admission process
paragraphs: For the 2026 cycle, candidates applied only through the IISER admission portal. The official brochure recorded an application window from March 5, 2026 to April 13, 2026, and the test took place on June 7, 2026. Those dates are historical, not a forecast for the next cycle.

A practical sequence is: create an account on the official portal; complete personal, academic, category, and examination details; upload the requested documents; pay the published application fee through the official portal; correct details if a correction window is provided; download the hall ticket; take IAT; then follow result, rank, preference, and seat-allocation instructions. Admission remains conditional on document verification and meeting all programme requirements.

For an institution outside the central IISER allotment process, submit that institution’s separate application as well. IISc and IIT Guwahati both operated separate 2026 admissions workflows even where IAT was an accepted or required score.
bullets: Never use a third-party payment page or unofficial application intermediary.
Save the submitted application, payment confirmation, hall ticket, score/rank record, and all required certificates.
Do not treat an IAT score alone as an offer of admission; monitor each relevant portal for counselling or institute-specific instructions.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Build preparation around the official, current-cycle syllabus for Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, and Biology, then use the official mock test and previous-year papers to calibrate difficulty, interface familiarity, pacing, and error patterns. The equal subject split means a balanced plan is usually more robust than studying only a preferred discipline.

A useful workflow is to first establish Class XI–XII-level conceptual coverage in all four subjects; next, practise mixed-subject MCQs under time limits; then review mistakes by concept, calculation, interpretation, and avoidable error. In the final stage, take full-length computer-based simulations and revise the official syllabus checklist.

Candidates should avoid relying on claims about a fixed cutoff, rank, fee, or admission chance from prior years. Seat matrices, programme offerings, reservation implementation, applicant performance, and the current cycle’s rules all affect outcomes.
bullets: Download the official syllabus before selecting books or a coaching plan.
Use official past papers to identify recurring gaps, but do not assume questions will repeat.
Schedule Biology and Mathematics practice even if only one is central to the intended academic programme.

sections.heading: Academic outcomes after IAT
paragraphs: At IISERs in 2026, the principal outcomes included five-year BS-MS dual degrees, including the Computational and Data Sciences BS-MS at IISER Kolkata; selected four-year BS programmes in economic sciences/statistical sciences; and specified four-year B.Tech. programmes at IISER Bhopal. The exact campus, programme, major options, seat matrix, and fee structure are annual and must be verified in the applicable admission notice.

IAT can also support particular external-institute opportunities when that institute announces it. In 2026, IISc Bengaluru used IAT rank as one route into its four-year BS (Research), and IIT Guwahati used IAT 2026 qualification for its four-year BS in Biomedical Science and Engineering. Such pathways have their own subject requirements, application windows, and selection rules.

The long-term outcome is therefore determined by the programme actually joined—not by the test name. A BS-MS pathway is research-intensive undergraduate education; four-year BS/B.Tech./BS (Research) routes differ in curriculum and progression options. Students should compare programme curricula, majors, research exposure, fees, location, and progression rules directly on the destination institute’s website before choosing preferences.
bullets: BS-MS Dual Degree: core IISER route; 2026 offerings varied by IISER and included specified interdisciplinary options.
Four-year BS and B.Tech.: available only for the particular programmes and campuses listed for that cycle.
BS (Research) and biomedical-science pathways outside IISERs: require separate institutional applications and compliance with separate eligibility criteria.

useful_links.label: IISc BS (Research) admissions and IAT selection route
IIT Guwahati BS in Biomedical Science and Engineering admissions

title: IIT JAM
description: IIT JAM — pg entrance exam (science), conducted by IITs (rotating).

quick_facts.label: What IIT JAM is
quick_facts.value: The Joint Admission Test for Masters (JAM) is an IIT-administered entrance examination for postgraduate study in science, mathematics, technology and related fields. In the 2026 cycle, IIT Bombay was the organising institute.

quick_facts.label: 2026 test papers
quick_facts.value: JAM 2026 had seven papers: Biotechnology (BT), Chemistry (CY), Economics (EN), Geology (GG), Mathematics (MA), Mathematical Statistics (MS), and Physics (PH).

quick_facts.label: Exam mode and length
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, every paper was an English-language, three-hour computer-based test with 60 compulsory questions for 100 marks.

quick_facts.label: Who could sit the exam
quick_facts.value: For JAM 2026, candidates of any nationality who had completed an undergraduate degree or were taking their qualifying degree's final examination in 2026 could appear; there was no age limit.

quick_facts.label: Admission is programme-specific
quick_facts.value: A JAM score alone did not guarantee admission. Candidates needed to meet the relevant institute's Eligibility Requirements and Minimum Educational Qualifications, and admissions were based on AIR, applicable reservation policy and seat availability.

quick_facts.label: 2026 IIT admission scale
quick_facts.value: For academic year 2026–27, the JAM admission brochure stated that IIT Bombay would coordinate admissions to more than 3,000 seats in 105 postgraduate programmes across 23 IITs. These figures are cycle-specific and can change in later years.

sections.heading: Purpose and the academic routes it opens
paragraphs: IIT JAM is primarily a gateway from an undergraduate science or quantitative degree into postgraduate study. The official 2026 materials list routes including M.Sc., M.Sc. (Tech.), MS (Research), M.Sc.–M.Tech. dual degree, Joint M.Sc.–Ph.D., M.Sc.–Ph.D. dual degree and Integrated Ph.D. programmes. The exact programmes available through a particular paper and the academic background required vary by institute and programme.

For the 2026–27 cycle, IIT admissions were centrally coordinated by IIT Bombay. JAM results could also be used by result-sharing institutions; for example, the official admission brochure identifies CCMN-linked institutions and other institutes where candidates had to follow the respective institution's own admission process rather than assume an IIT-JAM allotment process applied automatically.
bullets: Treat JAM as an entrance score and rank, not as an admission offer or a scholarship guarantee.
Match three things before choosing a test paper: the programme you want, that programme's accepted JAM paper(s), and its institute-specific Minimum Educational Qualifications (MEQs).

sections.heading: Eligibility: separate the examination from admission
paragraphs: For taking JAM 2026, the baseline was broad: an applicant could have completed an undergraduate degree or be appearing in the final examination of the qualifying degree in 2026. The official FAQ also states that the examination had no age limit and was open to foreign nationals. This exam-appearance eligibility did not impose a minimum percentage requirement for appearing in the test.

Admission had additional conditions. A qualifying candidate had to complete the undergraduate programme before the admitting institute's admission date and submit proof of passing with the required programme-specific eligibility within that institute's timeline. Each admitting institute verifies its own MEQs, so a B.Sc. or B.Sc. (Research) holder should check the precise subject/course requirements for every programme preference rather than infer eligibility from the programme title alone.
bullets: You may be eligible to write JAM but ineligible for a particular M.Sc., integrated Ph.D. or other programme if its MEQ is not met.
Qualifying the paper and appearing in the merit list do not create an automatic entitlement to a seat.

sections.heading: Exam format and paper choice
paragraphs: In JAM 2026, each paper was a three-hour CBT in English. It contained 60 questions worth 100 marks, split into three compulsory sections: 30 MCQs in Section A, 10 multiple-select questions (MSQs) in Section B, and 20 numerical-answer-type questions (NATs) in Section C. Negative marking applied only to incorrect Section A MCQs: one-third mark for a wrong one-mark MCQ and two-thirds mark for a wrong two-mark MCQ. MSQ and NAT questions had no negative marking under the 2026 pattern.

Candidates could take one or two papers, provided the two papers were not scheduled in the same session. The 2026 subjects were BT, CY, EN, GG, MA, MS and PH. The organising institute also provided an on-screen virtual calculator, while personal calculators and electronic devices were prohibited in the examination hall.
bullets: Practise MCQ accuracy because only MCQs carried negative marking in the 2026 pattern.
Practise MSQs as all-or-nothing questions: full credit required selecting every correct option and no incorrect option.
Practise entering signed numerical answers with the virtual keypad used for NAT questions.

sections.heading: Application and admission workflow
paragraphs: The process has two distinct stages: first, registration and application for the examination through the JAM Online Application Processing System (JOAPS); second, after qualifying and subject to that year's rules, a separate admission application and programme-preference process. In the 2026 examination application, JOAPS was used to register with an email address and mobile number, upload the photograph, signature, proof of date of birth and applicable category/PwD documents, pay online, and track scrutiny status.

For the 2026 admission stage, candidates could apply to programmes linked to the paper(s) they had qualified, provided they met each programme's MEQ and ER. Applicants listed programmes in preference order, and the admission brochure states that no changes, additions or rearrangement of those choices were permitted after form submission. The 2026 admission dates and fees were specific to that completed cycle; future candidates should rely on the next organising IIT's official brochure and JOAPS notices rather than reuse them.
bullets: Create and retain one JOAPS account; the 2026 instructions warned that multiple applications from the same candidate could be rejected.

Keep academic marksheets/degree or provisional certificate, valid category or EWS certificate where applicable, PwD certificate where applicable, photo ID, photograph and signature ready for the applicable stage.
Before submitting preferences, verify the programme's eligible JAM paper and MEQ in the current admission brochure and on the admitting institute's website.

sections.heading: Preparation approach using official materials
paragraphs: Start from the official syllabus for the selected paper, then map each topic into a revision plan that includes concept study, worked problems and timed retrieval practice. Because the 2026 structure mixed MCQs, MSQs and NATs, preparation should include the different response behaviours—not merely solving conventional single-answer questions.

Use the official JAM mock test to rehearse the computer interface and the virtual-calculator workflow. Then use official previous-year papers to identify recurring topic areas, calibrate timing and make an error log. When analysing a paper, distinguish conceptual gaps from calculation mistakes and negative-marking errors; that lets later practice target the decision to attempt, skip or revisit a question.
bullets: Complete at least some full-length practice under the three-hour limit.
Use the official paper-specific syllabus rather than a generic B.Sc. syllabus as the scope boundary.
After every timed paper, review unattempted and incorrect questions as carefully as correct ones.

sections.heading: What a qualifying JAM result can lead to
paragraphs: A qualifying JAM result can support applications to advanced postgraduate programmes such as M.Sc., Joint M.Sc.–Ph.D., M.Sc.–Ph.D. dual degree and Integrated Ph.D. options at IITs, with the particular options determined by the qualifying paper, AIR and programme-specific requirements. It can therefore be a relevant next step after a B.Sc. or Bachelor of Science (Research) for students aiming for disciplinary specialisation, research training or later doctoral study.

The outcome is competitive and conditional: the official admission materials specify AIR-based consideration, institute MEQs and seat availability, and state that qualifying does not guarantee admission, scholarship or employment. In the 2026 cycle, JAM results were additionally accepted by various result-sharing institutions, but candidates needed to approach those institutes or their admission body directly.
bullets: Use opening/closing-rank data only as historical context, not as a future admission guarantee.
Compare curriculum, MEQ, research areas, location, fees and financial-support rules directly on each admitting institute's official site before finalising preferences.

title: IMU CET
description: IMU CET — ug entrance exam (maritime), conducted by Indian Maritime University.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: Indian Maritime University (IMU), which conducts IMU-CET on an all-India basis for admissions to its campuses and affiliated institutes.

quick_facts.label: UG scope
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, the technical UG CET covered B.Tech (Marine Engineering), B.Sc. (Nautical Science), Diploma in Nautical Science (DNS), B.Tech (Naval Architecture & Ocean Engineering), and B.Tech (Naval Architecture & Ship Building); BBA had a separate admission route.

quick_facts.label: 2026 exam status
quick_facts.value: IMU scheduled IMU-CET 2026 for May 24, 2026. Its 2026 admissions page subsequently published the CET result, qualified-candidate lists, rank-certificate access, counselling notices, and admission lists; these dates and processes are cycle-specific rather than standing deadlines.

quick_facts.label: UG test content
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 UG technical test, IMU specified 200 multiple-choice questions from English, General Aptitude, Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics at Class 12/Plus Two/Intermediate/equivalent level. IMU stated that each wrong answer attracts a 0.25-mark deduction.

quick_facts.label: Rank and use
quick_facts.value: IMU says it issues a rank certificate to qualified CET candidates. The certificate is essential for admission to IMU courses and affiliated institutes, and for the specified DG Shipping-approved B.Tech (Marine Engineering), B.Sc. (Nautical Science), and DNS programmes at non-affiliated maritime training institutes.

quick_facts.label: 2026 registration fee context
quick_facts.value: For 2026, the published registration fee for UG and PG programmes other than BBA was ₹1,200 for General/General-EWS/OBC(NCL) applicants and ₹800 for SC/ST applicants. Fees can change in later admission cycles.

sections.heading: What IMU CET is for
paragraphs: IMU-CET is Indian Maritime University’s all-India common entrance test. In the 2026 admission cycle, its UG technical route was used for the principal maritime programmes: B.Tech (Marine Engineering), B.Sc. (Nautical Science), DNS, B.Tech (Naval Architecture & Ocean Engineering), and B.Tech (Naval Architecture & Ship Building). Applicants should not treat the test as a universal route to every IMU undergraduate programme: IMU’s 2026 prospectus describes a separate BBA admission mechanism.

For maritime pre-sea training, the CET rank has importance beyond IMU campuses. IMU states that DG Shipping-regulated maritime training institutes are required to admit candidates on the basis of IMU-CET rank, and that the rank certificate is needed for the named DG Shipping-approved Marine Engineering, Nautical Science, and DNS programmes, including at relevant non-affiliated institutes.
bullets: The exam is a selection and ranking step; passing the test alone does not replace programme-specific academic, medical, document-verification, counselling, or seat-allotment requirements.
The precise programme list, admission rules, and schedule should be checked against the prospectus and admissions page for the target academic year.

sections.heading: Eligibility: check the programme, not only the exam
paragraphs: Eligibility is programme-specific. For example, IMU’s published B.Sc. Nautical Science criteria require 10+2 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, at least 60% aggregate in PCM, and at least 50% in English; the page also sets medical-fitness requirements. The 2026 prospectus lists recognized 10+2/equivalent qualifications for UG applicants and says a candidate whose qualifying examination is scheduled after the CET date is not eligible to register for IMU-CET 2026.

Marine programmes can impose additional professional fitness conditions. IMU’s FAQ says applicants to B.Tech (Marine Engineering), B.Sc. (Nautical Science), DNS, and PGDME must meet the physical-fitness standards and eyesight conditions prescribed by the Directorate General of Shipping, and selected candidates submit the required medical certificate at admission.
bullets: Review the exact course page and current prospectus for PCM/English marks, age limits, category relaxations, marital-status conditions where applicable, and lateral-entry rules.
For sea-going courses, obtain an eligibility view from a DG Shipping-approved medical practitioner early; do not assume that an academic score or CET rank overrides medical standards.
DNS at an IMU affiliated institute has an additional sponsorship condition: IMU says sponsorship is required there, although not for courses in IMU campuses.

sections.heading: UG technical test format
paragraphs: For IMU-CET 2026, IMU specified 200 multiple-choice questions for UG technical programmes. The stated syllabus areas were English, General Aptitude, Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics at the Class 12/Plus Two/Intermediate/equivalent level. IMU also specified negative marking: 0.25 mark is deducted for each incorrect answer.

IMU reserves the right to change the distribution, type, or difficulty of questions and to conduct the CET through a centre-based or proctored mode or another suitable alternative arrangement. Candidates should therefore rely on the current-year information bulletin, admit-card instructions, and IMU announcements rather than older coaching-site patterns.
bullets: Prioritize accuracy as well as coverage because wrong answers carried a penalty in the 2026 rule set.
Use IMU’s official model-question-paper sets; the 2026 admissions page provided UG materials overall and separate practice papers for English, Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, and Aptitude.

sections.heading: Application through admission and counselling
paragraphs: The 2026 process was online and followed the sequence of registration, city selection, admit-card download, IMU-CET, result/rank certificate, counselling, seat allotment/confirmation, and certificate verification. IMU’s admissions page records these stages for the 2026 cycle, including a city-selection portal, admit-card notice, result, counselling, qualified-candidate lists, rank-certificate download, admission lists, confirmation portal, and document-verification schedule.

As dated context only, IMU’s February 2026 prospectus initially listed February 5, 2026 as the tentative registration opening, April 24, 2026 as the tentative closing date, May 24, 2026 as the CET date, and August 1, 2026 as programme commencement. IMU explicitly noted that dates could change, so these are not deadlines for a future cycle.
bullets: Create the application with personal and academic details that match supporting records; retain payment and application acknowledgements.

Select examination-city preferences when IMU opens that facility. In 2026, IMU stated that city selection was available for a limited window and used a first-come, first-served process within preference levels.
After qualifying, download the rank certificate and complete counselling and document verification within the dates IMU publishes for that cycle.

sections.heading: Preparation approach grounded in the official syllabus
paragraphs: Build preparation around the official UG subject list: Class 12/equivalent Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, plus English and General Aptitude. Start with syllabus mapping and core concepts, then practise timed multiple-choice questions across all five areas. Because IMU applied a 0.25-mark penalty to wrong answers in 2026, full-length practice should include an attempt-selection strategy rather than indiscriminate guessing.

IMU published official model question papers for the 2026 CET, including an overall UG (except BBA) set and separate sets for English, Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, and Aptitude. These are the most appropriate starting point for familiarising yourself with IMU’s own question style; use the current-cycle materials whenever they are released.
bullets: Make a topic checklist from the current prospectus, then diagnose weak areas with short timed tests.
Practise calculations and reading accuracy under timed conditions; review every error by cause—concept gap, formula recall, interpretation, or rushed guessing.
For sea-going programme choices, prepare application documentation and assess medical eligibility in parallel with exam study.

sections.heading: What a qualifying rank can lead to
paragraphs: A qualifying IMU-CET rank produces a rank certificate that can be used in IMU’s counselling and, subject to each institute’s admission conditions, for the relevant affiliated and DG Shipping-approved maritime training pathways. It is not an employment guarantee and does not by itself secure a berth, course seat, medical clearance, or admission.

The undergraduate pathways reached through the CET lead to distinct maritime education routes. IMU describes B.Tech (Marine Engineering) as a four-year residential programme focused on the design, construction, operation, and maintenance of ships and marine vessels. It describes B.Sc. Nautical Science as preparation for deck-officer and broader maritime-industry careers, while DNS is a one-year residential programme in navigation, seamanship, and safety management that leads toward the examinations required for a Deck Officer Certificate of Competency.
bullets: Use counselling preferences to distinguish sea-going technical programmes from naval-architecture and shipbuilding-oriented programmes.

Evaluate each target institute’s approval status, residential requirements, medical standards, sponsorship rules where relevant, fees for that specific cycle, and published placement/career support separately from the CET rank.

title: INI-CET
description: INI-CET — pg entrance exam (medical), conducted by AIIMS New Delhi.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: INI-CET (Institute of National Importance Combined Entrance Test) is the common postgraduate entrance examination for specified MD, MS, six-year DM, six-year MCh, MDS, and MD (Hospital Administration) seats at participating Institutes of National Importance (INIs).

quick_facts.label: Conducting authority
quick_facts.value: AIIMS New Delhi’s Examination Section administers the examination process in consultation with participating INIs; institute-specific admission rules remain governed by the relevant institute’s prospectus and regulations.

quick_facts.label: Eligible qualifying degrees
quick_facts.value: For the medical postgraduate streams, the qualifying degree is MBBS; for MDS, it is BDS. The degree must meet the recognition requirements stated in the session prospectus.

quick_facts.label: July 2026 exam format
quick_facts.value: The July 2026 prospectus specified a computer-based test of 200 objective questions in 180 minutes, with +1 for a correct answer, −1/3 for an incorrect answer, and 0 for unanswered or marked-for-review questions.

quick_facts.label: Admission threshold
quick_facts.value: For the July 2026 session, the prospectus used INI-CET percentile eligibility thresholds of 50th percentile for UR/OCI, EWS, sponsored, and foreign-national seats, and 45th percentile for OBC, SC, ST, PwBD, and the specified Bhutanese-national category at PGIMER Chandigarh.

sections.heading: Purpose and place after MBBS
paragraphs: INI-CET is a postgraduate medical and dental entrance route after MBBS or BDS, rather than an undergraduate entrance examination. It is used for admissions to the session-specific MD, MS, six-year DM, six-year MCh, MDS, and MD (Hospital Administration) seats announced by participating INIs.

AIIMS New Delhi manages the common examination, results, and seat-allocation process. However, the final admission conditions, course availability, fees, stipends, reporting requirements, and other institute-level rules are not uniform: applicants must read the Part B prospectus and admission instructions for every institute they may prefer.
bullets: Treat the session’s Part A prospectus as the source for examination-wide rules.
Treat each participating institute’s Part B prospectus as the source for institute- and course-specific admission conditions.
Do not assume that a qualifying rank alone guarantees admission; seat availability, eligibility verification, preference order, and allocation rules also matter.

sections.heading: Eligibility: core checks before applying
paragraphs: For the July 2026 cycle, applicants for MD/MS/DM (six years)/MCh (six years)/MD (Hospital Administration) needed an MBBS qualification, while MDS applicants needed BDS. The prospectus also requires completion of the prescribed compulsory rotating internship by the session’s stated cut-off and applies recognition requirements to the qualifying degree.

The published minimum aggregate requirement for Indian nationals was 50% for SC/ST candidates and 55% for other categories including OBC/EWS; PwBD applicants follow the threshold applicable to their underlying category. Eligibility to take the examination is not identical to eligibility for every institute or seat, so institute-specific conditions must be checked separately.
bullets: Confirm the qualifying degree, internship completion date, registration/document requirements, and category documentation against the current session prospectus.
Check the Part B prospectus of each preferred INI, because an applicant may be eligible for some participating institutes but not others.
Foreign-national, sponsored, OCI, and institute-specific categories have separate conditions and should be verified directly from the applicable prospectus.

sections.heading: Exam format and scoring
paragraphs: For July 2026, INI-CET was a computer-based examination with 200 objective questions over three hours. Questions could include single-correct-choice and multiple-correct-choice formats. Scoring was +1 for a correct response, −1/3 for an incorrect response, and 0 for an unanswered or marked-for-review response.

The July 2026 paper was divided into four sequential 50-question parts, each available for 45 minutes. Once a part’s time expired, it was submitted automatically and the next part opened; candidates could not return to an earlier part. This makes paced decision-making and block-by-block practice important.
bullets: Plan for four 45-minute blocks rather than treating the paper as a freely navigable three-hour test.
Use the applicable percentile threshold only as an eligibility threshold, not as a prediction of a particular specialty or institute allocation.
Re-check the next session’s prospectus because question delivery, scoring, and cut-offs can be revised.

sections.heading: Application and allocation process
paragraphs: The common process is online and proceeds through application, examination, and seat allocation. For the July 2026 cycle, AIIMS’s revised registration process used One-Time Registration (OTR), followed by submission of qualification and internship details, online fee payment, image uploads, and final submission. The notice states that information placed in OTR is intended for future examinations and may not be changeable later, so applicants should enter it carefully.

After the examination and result, eligible candidates participate in online seat allocation. The prospectus describes at least two allocation rounds followed by an open round, with additional rounds possible. Original-document verification and final joining occur under the rules of the allotted INI.
bullets: Use only the AIIMS examinations portal and official notices for the active session’s dates, uploads, correction window, admit card, result, seat matrix, and allocation schedule.
Save the submitted application/registration record and verify the admit-card details when it becomes available.
Rank preferences only after reviewing the current seat matrix and every preferred institute’s Part B prospectus; seats and rules can change by session.

sections.heading: Preparation approach aligned to the official format
paragraphs: Build preparation around the official format first: timed, computer-based practice in four 45-minute blocks; deliberate handling of negative marking; and a strategy for completing and reviewing questions within the currently active block. Because an earlier block cannot be revisited after time expires in the July 2026 scheme, leaving all uncertain questions for a final-paper review is not workable.

Use the current session’s prospectus and notices as the authority for administrative preparation as well: eligibility cut-off, document formats, registration steps, admit-card instructions, and allocation procedure. These rules can change between sessions, so older coaching material or past prospectuses should not override current official instructions.
bullets: Practise 50-question, 45-minute sets to mirror the block structure.
Track incorrect answers separately from unattempted questions so that revision also addresses the −1/3 negative-marking trade-off.
Before submitting the application, audit degree, internship, identity, category, and other required documents against the active prospectus.

sections.heading: What a result can lead to
paragraphs: A qualifying INI-CET result permits participation in the applicable online seat-allocation process; it does not itself constitute admission. Allocation depends on the applicant’s merit/rank, eligibility, submitted preferences, category and roster rules where applicable, and the session’s available seats.

Successful allocation can lead to postgraduate training in a participating INI in the allotted specialty. Applicants should evaluate the institute-specific Part B prospectus before choosing preferences because programme eligibility, fees, stipends, hostel arrangements, resignation rules, and reporting requirements are set at institute level and may vary by session.
bullets: Use the official seat matrix and allocation notices, not unofficial rank-versus-branch estimates, to make final choices.
Complete reporting and original-document verification by the allotted institute’s deadline.
If no seat is allotted, follow the official notices for any later allocation or open-round opportunities rather than assuming they will occur.

title: ISRO ICRB (Scientist/Engineer)
description: ISRO ICRB (Scientist/Engineer) — govt recruitment exam (research), conducted by ISRO.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: ISRO ICRB is the Indian Space Research Organisation’s Centralised Recruitment Board process for recruiting Scientist/Engineer ‘SC’ posts; ‘SC’ is a job designation, not a reference to Scheduled Caste status.

quick_facts.label: Qualification baseline
quick_facts.value: The 2025 discipline-specific notices required a relevant B.E./B.Tech or equivalent degree with at least 65% aggregate marks or CGPA 6.84/10. Exact eligible disciplines and equivalencies are advertisement-specific.

quick_facts.label: Selection routes vary
quick_facts.value: ICRB used both written-test-plus-interview recruitment and, in a separate 2025 Scientist/Engineer ‘SC’ advertisement, GATE-score-based interview shortlisting without a written test. Applicants must follow the method stated in the particular notification.

quick_facts.label: 2025 written-test pattern example
quick_facts.value: For ICRB:02(EMC):2025, the written paper was objective, 120 minutes, with 80 discipline MCQs in Part A (+1, −1/3) and an aptitude/ability Part B of up to 15 MCQs worth 20 marks without negative marking.

quick_facts.label: Age example
quick_facts.value: The upper-age limit in ICRB:02(EMC):2025 was 28 years as on June 16, 2025, with relaxation for specified groups under Government of India orders. This date and limit should not be treated as a standing rule for future notices.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: The 2025 written-test advertisement stated appointment at Pay Matrix Level 10 with minimum basic pay of ₹56,100 per month, plus applicable allowances. Pay, allowances and pension terms are dated policy context and can change.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
paragraphs: ISRO ICRB is a centralized employer recruitment route, rather than a university entrance examination or a credential. It is used by ISRO to fill Scientist/Engineer ‘SC’ vacancies in notified technical disciplines. For example, the 2025 ICRB notices covered Electronics, Mechanical and Computer Science, and separately Civil, Electrical, Refrigeration & Air-Conditioning and Architecture. The disciplines, number of posts, employer units and selection method are determined separately in each advertisement.
source_urls
bullets: A successful candidate proceeds to appointment as Scientist/Engineer ‘SC’ at ISRO or, where the notice specifies it, an associated unit such as the Physical Research Laboratory (PRL).
The designation ‘SC’ does not itself restrict the post to a caste category; reservation and eligibility conditions are stated separately in each notice.

sections.heading: Eligibility: read the vacancy-specific notice
paragraphs: In the 2025 ICRB Scientist/Engineer ‘SC’ recruitment examples, the core academic requirement was a relevant B.E./B.Tech or equivalent degree with an aggregate minimum of 65% marks or CGPA 6.84/10. The qualifying discipline must match the specific post: an engineering degree alone does not make a candidate eligible for every stream. ISRO’s FAQ also states that there was no relaxation in the educational-marks requirement for reserved categories in that recruitment.

AMIE can be relevant to this node, but only subject to conditions. ISRO’s 2025 FAQ recognized AMIE as an equivalent route in the relevant discipline, while stating that AMIE eligibility was regulated by the cited MHRD order: candidates registered for AMIE after May 31, 2013 were not considered under that advertisement, and AMIE/Grad IETE applicants needed 65% marks or CGPA 6.84 in Section B alone. This is notification-specific guidance, so AMIE candidates should verify the latest ISRO notice before applying.

Age limits, relaxations, disability suitability, nationality, completion status and document requirements can change by notification. As one dated example only, ICRB:02(EMC):2025 set an upper age of 28 years on June 16, 2025 and applied Government of India relaxation rules to specified categories.
bullets: Relevant B.Tech/B.E. and BS-MS/dual-degree holders should compare their exact branch, transcript, marks/CGPA and completion status with the advertised eligibility table.
Applicants employed by a government department, PSU or autonomous body may need prior permission and an original no-objection certificate at interview, when required by the advertisement.
Do not assume a postgraduate degree compensates for an ineligible or below-threshold qualifying engineering degree; ISRO’s 2025 FAQ required the prescribed B.E./B.Tech baseline.

sections.heading: Assessment format and selection
paragraphs: There is no single permanent ‘ISRO ICRB exam pattern.’ In the written-test route used in ICRB:02(EMC):2025, ISRO specified a 120-minute, single objective paper. Part A had 80 discipline-specific MCQs, one mark each, with +1/−1/3 marking; Part B had up to 15 aptitude/ability MCQs totaling 20 marks, with no negative marking. ISRO stated that candidates would be shortlisted for interview from written-test performance, generally in a 1:5 ratio, and that final-panel generation would give 50% weight to the written test and 50% to the interview.

The interview rubric in that 2025 notice allocated 100 marks across technical knowledge, technical awareness related to the specialization, presentation/communication, comprehension and academic achievements. In contrast, the separate ICRB:01(EMC):2025 GATE-based recruitment had no written test and shortlisted candidates for interview using GATE scores in a 1:7 ratio. Therefore, a candidate should not prepare from an older pattern without first confirming the new advertisement’s selection route.
bullets: For written-test notices, call letters are issued to the registered email address and ISRO may set or change centres according to the notice.
ISRO’s 2025 written-test process published answer keys and provided a time-limited online objection mechanism; this was a feature of that notice, not a guarantee for every future campaign.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Apply only through the ISRO Careers/Current Opportunities page when an ICRB advertisement is live. ISRO’s 2025 FAQs describe an online application flow and state that candidates ordinarily need not send application printouts or supporting documents to ISRO Headquarters at the application stage; originals are produced when called for. Applicants should retain their registration number, verify the submitted information before final submission, and monitor the official advertisement page and registered email.

Fees and deadlines are variable. In the ICRB:02(EMC):2025 written-test notice, all applicants initially paid ₹750 as processing fee per application; for candidates who appeared in the written test, the notice provided a full ₹750 refund to women, SC/ST, PwBD and ex-servicemen, and a ₹500 refund to other candidates after the ₹250 application fee. Payment was online through the designated BharatKosh flow. Future notices may use different charges, refund terms, or no written-test route, so candidates must use the current notice rather than this 2025 example.
bullets: Open the applicable ICRB vacancy from ISRO Careers, then read the detailed advertisement and FAQ before submitting the form.
Use the exact qualification option and discipline specified in the application portal; ISRO’s FAQ says only qualifications listed in the drop-down menu are eligible.
Where a written test is used, check the official payment-status page after payment and save the receipt/confirmation.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Start with the notified engineering discipline and the current selection route. For the 2025 CEPO written-test recruitment, ISRO stated that the syllabus consisted of topics in the B.E./B.Tech curriculum. For a written-test notice, prepare the full undergraduate core curriculum for the exact branch, then practise timed objective questions and the aptitude/ability component. For a GATE-score route, prioritize the GATE paper and score requirements specified by the notification rather than expecting an ICRB written test.

Use official materials first. ISRO has published previous recruitment question papers on relevant recruitment pages, including Electronics, Mechanical and Computer Science papers for the 2023 recruitment linked from the 2025 EMC page. Review the notification’s interview criteria as well: technical fundamentals, awareness in the specialization, communication and document verification all matter after shortlisting.
bullets: Build a branch-by-branch revision map from the B.E./B.Tech curriculum and the vacancy’s stated specialization.
Complete official previous papers under the advertised time limit where a comparable written-test pattern applies.
Prepare concise explanations of projects, core subjects and technical developments relevant to the advertised discipline for interview.

sections.heading: Outcome after selection
paragraphs: The direct outcome is eligibility for appointment to the notified Scientist/Engineer ‘SC’ post, subject to final panel placement, document verification and other appointment conditions. ISRO’s 2025 FAQ described these posts as permanent, while remaining temporary until the incumbent completed the prescribed probation period. A selection panel or interview result is not by itself a substitute for satisfying appointment formalities.

As dated 2025 pay context, the written-test advertisement said selected candidates would be appointed at Pay Matrix Level 10 with minimum basic pay of ₹56,100 per month, with DA, HRA and transport allowance under extant rules, and coverage under the New Pension Scheme/Unified Pension Scheme. Actual take-home pay, allowances, posting location and applicable pension rules depend on the appointment date, place of posting and prevailing government rules.
bullets: This node is a recruitment pathway to the child outcome: Scientist/Engineer ‘SC’ at ISRO.
Final appointment can require original proof of qualification, age, category and other claims; government/PSU/autonomous-body employees may also need an NOC when called for.
