title: JEE Advanced
description: JEE Advanced — ug entrance exam (engineering), conducted by IITs (rotating).

quick_facts.label: Purpose
quick_facts.value: JEE (Advanced) is the entrance examination whose performance forms the basis for admission at the 10+2 entry level to bachelor’s, integrated master’s and dual-degree programmes at the IITs.

quick_facts.label: Conduct and organising institute
quick_facts.value: The 2026 examination was conducted by the seven Zonal Coordinating IITs under the Joint Admission Board; IIT Roorkee was the organising institute for the 2026 cycle. The organising IIT and annual rules may change by cycle.

quick_facts.label: 2026 eligibility gateway for Indian nationals
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, an Indian national or OCI/PIO (I) candidate had to be among the top 250,000 successful candidates in the JEE Main 2026 B.E./B.Tech. paper, as well as satisfy the other published age, attempt, Class XII and prior-IIT-admission criteria.

quick_facts.label: Exam format
quick_facts.value: In 2026, JEE (Advanced) was a computer-based test with two compulsory three-hour papers. Each paper covered Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics; the marking scheme could include negative marks for some questions.

quick_facts.label: 2026 examination date
quick_facts.value: The 2026 exam was held on Sunday, May 17, 2026, with Paper 1 from 09:00–12:00 IST and Paper 2 from 14:30–17:30 IST. These dates are cycle-specific and already past as of this review.

quick_facts.label: Seat allocation
quick_facts.value: A JEE (Advanced) rank does not itself guarantee an IIT seat: candidates must participate in JoSAA’s online joint seat-allocation process, and allotment depends on merit, choices, eligibility and seats available in each round.

sections.heading: What JEE Advanced is for
paragraphs: JEE (Advanced) is the IIT undergraduate entrance examination following the JEE Main screening route for most Indian applicants. In the 2026 information brochure, the Joint Admission Board states that a candidate’s performance is the basis for admission to IIT bachelor’s, integrated-master’s and dual-degree programmes for the 2026–27 academic year.

It is not a universal engineering-admission examination. The IIT programme types shown in the 2026 brochure include B.Tech., B.S., B.Arch., B.Tech.–M.Tech. dual degrees, B.S.–M.S. dual degrees and selected integrated or dual-degree variants; the exact programme and seat matrix are published by JoSAA for the relevant admission year.

One important pathway distinction: B.Arch. at the listed IITs requires both qualification in JEE (Advanced) and a pass in the Architecture Aptitude Test (AAT). By contrast, JoSAA identifies JEE Main B.Planning—not JEE Advanced—as the qualifying examination for B.Planning admissions in its 2026 system.
bullets: Use JEE Main B.E./B.Tech. performance to become eligible for JEE (Advanced), if applying as an Indian national or OCI/PIO (I).
Use the resulting JEE (Advanced) rank in the applicable JoSAA process for IIT choices and allotment.
Treat programme availability, seat counts and admission business rules as annual, not permanent.

sections.heading: Eligibility: the 2026 rules in practical terms
paragraphs: Eligibility is cycle-specific. For Indian nationals and OCI/PIO (I) candidates in 2026, all five criteria applied together: top-250,000 performance in the JEE Main B.E./B.Tech. paper; the stated age limit; no more than two attempts in two consecutive years; first appearance in Class XII/equivalent in the permitted years with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics compulsory; and compliance with restrictions relating to earlier IIT admission.

For 2026 specifically, the normal age threshold was birth on or after October 1, 2001, with a five-year relaxation for SC, ST and PwD candidates. A candidate could attempt JEE (Advanced) at most twice in two consecutive years. The Class XII first-appearance rule was normally 2025 or 2026, subject to a narrowly specified board-result-date exception for certain 2024 candidates.

Being permitted to sit the exam is different from meeting the Class XII condition for IIT admission. For 2026 admission, candidates needed Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics and had to meet either at least 75% aggregate marks in a minimum of five Class XII subjects (65% for SC, ST and PwD candidates) or be within their category-wise top 20 percentile in the relevant board examination. Applicants should read the current year’s brochure rather than rely on these 2026 thresholds.
bullets: Foreign nationals and OCI/PIO (F) candidates follow separate eligibility and direct-registration provisions; they were not required to write JEE Main in the 2026 rules.
Earlier admission to an IIT can make a candidate ineligible, although the brochure specifies limited exceptions, such as certain withdrawals before the final allocation round.
Reservation, disability accommodations and documentation are governed by the current brochure and applicable Government of India rules.

sections.heading: Exam structure and what it tests
paragraphs: The 2026 test used computer-based testing only. It comprised Paper 1 and Paper 2, each lasting three hours, and a candidate had to appear in both for responses to be evaluated. Each paper had separate Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics sections.

The papers are designed to assess comprehension, reasoning and analytical ability. They were offered in English and Hindi, with the candidate able to switch languages during the examination; the English version prevailed if an interpretation differed. Some questions could carry negative marks, and the detailed question-type and marking instructions were provided at the time of the examination.

For candidates eligible for compensatory time under the published disability provisions, the 2026 rules allowed one additional hour per paper. The official site also provided practice tests for Paper 1 and Paper 2, useful for becoming familiar with the CBT interface.
bullets: Plan for the full two-paper day rather than treating Paper 2 as optional.
Practise the official CBT workflow as well as PCM problem solving.
Read the marking instructions on the live test carefully; they can vary by question type.

sections.heading: Application and admission process
paragraphs: For the 2026 cycle, eligible candidates registered online through the JEE (Advanced) portal. Registration for JEE Main-qualified candidates ran from April 23, 2026 to May 2, 2026, and the fee-payment deadline was May 4, 2026. These dates are historical 2026 dates, not a forecast for a future cycle.

The 2026 India-centre registration fee was ₹1,600 for female candidates of all categories and for SC, ST and PwD candidates, and ₹3,200 for other Indian-national candidates; payment-gateway and bank charges were excluded. Fees, categories, centres and deadlines can change, so applicants should use the current official registration notice before paying.

After the examination, qualifying candidates receive category-wise All India Ranks through the JEE (Advanced) portal and then use JoSAA’s online process to submit choices and participate in seat allocation. A rank, choice filling or participation does not guarantee admission because allotment depends on merit and available seats. For B.Arch. at IIT (BHU) Varanasi, IIT Kharagpur and IIT Roorkee in 2026, a qualified candidate also needed to pass AAT.
bullets: Check eligibility before beginning registration; registration can later be cancelled if criteria are not met.
Keep the current brochure’s document, category-certificate and payment instructions alongside the portal checklist.
After results, follow JoSAA’s current-year business rules, schedule, seat matrix and institute-specific restrictions.

sections.heading: Preparation approach grounded in the official exam design
paragraphs: Build preparation around the official syllabus and the three subject areas in both papers: Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics. Because the papers are intended to assess comprehension, reasoning and analytical ability—not merely recall—use timed multi-step problem practice and review the reasoning behind errors.

Take the official Paper 1 and Paper 2 practice tests before exam day. This reduces avoidable friction with the CBT interface, including moving among questions, selecting answers and working under the on-screen timer. Also use official previous-year question papers and the current syllabus available from the JEE (Advanced) website.

Include a two-paper simulation in the study plan. In the 2026 format, both three-hour papers were compulsory and negative marking could apply to some questions, so accuracy, question selection and time management are as important as attempting a high volume of questions.
bullets: Map every topic to the official syllabus before adding external study material.
Use full-length, two-session mocks and analyse incorrect, guessed and unattempted questions separately.
Recheck the current brochure for changes to format, language, accessibility arrangements or marking instructions.

sections.heading: What a JEE Advanced result can lead to
paragraphs: A qualifying JEE (Advanced) result produces rank-list eligibility, not automatic enrolment. In 2026, rank lists were prepared from aggregate marks across Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, and JoSAA used the common online allocation process for seats across participating institutions. Candidates should judge options using the current year’s published opening/closing ranks, seat matrix, programme restrictions and business rules rather than assume a past closing rank will repeat.

The principal outcome is access to IIT undergraduate programmes, subject to Class XII performance requirements and allocation. The JEE (Advanced) brochure also notes that some other institutions have used JEE (Advanced) ranks for admissions, including IISc, IISERs, IIST, RGIPT and IIPE, but applicants must consult those institutions directly because their participation and rules may differ by year.

For the 2026 JoSAA session, the Ministry of Education’s joint allocation system covered IITs and IISc alongside other institute groups, but different qualifying examinations apply to different programmes. That distinction matters when comparing engineering, architecture and planning routes.
bullets: For IIT B.Arch., plan for AAT in addition to JEE (Advanced) qualification.
For B.Planning, verify the JEE Main B.Planning route rather than assuming JEE (Advanced) applies.
Compare programme curriculum, location, duration and institute-specific admission conditions after the current seat matrix is released.

title: JEE Main
description: JEE Main — ug entrance exam (engineering), conducted by NTA. Paper 2 covers B.Arch/B.Plan.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: The National Testing Agency (NTA) conducts JEE (Main); the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education has entrusted NTA with conducting it since 2019.

quick_facts.label: Papers and academic purpose
quick_facts.value: Paper 1 is for B.E./B.Tech undergraduate engineering admissions and is also the eligibility test for JEE (Advanced); Paper 2A is for B.Arch and Paper 2B is for B.Planning.

quick_facts.label: 2026 examination cycle
quick_facts.value: For academic session 2026–27, NTA conducted JEE (Main) in two sessions: January 2026 and April 2026. The official portal lists final scores/scorecards for Paper 1 and Paper 2.

quick_facts.label: Paper 1 format in 2026
quick_facts.value: Paper 1 (B.E./B.Tech) was a three-hour computer-based test covering Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, with MCQs and numerical-value questions.

quick_facts.label: Paper 2 format in 2026
quick_facts.value: Paper 2A combined CBT Mathematics and Aptitude with an offline pen-and-paper Drawing Test; Paper 2B used CBT for Mathematics, Aptitude and Planning-based questions.

quick_facts.label: 2026 exam eligibility
quick_facts.value: There was no age limit for appearing in JEE (Main) 2026. Candidates who passed Class XII/equivalent in 2024 or 2025, or were appearing in 2026, could take the examination; admission eligibility is separately determined by the admitting system or institution.

sections.heading: What JEE Main is for
paragraphs: JEE (Main) is India’s national undergraduate entrance examination administered by NTA for engineering, architecture and planning pathways. In the 2026 bulletin, NTA specifies that Paper 1 serves undergraduate engineering admissions at NITs, IIITs, other centrally funded technical institutions, and participating state-funded/recognised institutions; it also functions as the qualifying examination for JEE (Advanced), the route to IIT admissions. Paper 2 is used for B.Arch and B.Planning admissions.

A JEE (Main) score is therefore an entrance-test result rather than an offer of admission. The institute, programme, counselling authority and applicable admission rules determine whether and how a score can be used.
bullets: Paper 1: B.E./B.Tech.
Paper 2A: B.Arch.
Paper 2B: B.Planning.
JEE (Advanced): a separate examination for which JEE (Main) is an eligibility test, subject to that examination’s rules.

sections.heading: Eligibility: distinguish taking the test from getting a seat
paragraphs: For the 2026 examination, NTA set no age limit. The examination-level Class XII/equivalent window covered candidates who had passed in 2024 or 2025 and those appearing in 2026; candidates who had passed in 2023 or earlier were not eligible for JEE (Main) 2026. These dates are cycle-specific and should not be assumed for a later JEE Main cycle.

Admission requirements can be more restrictive than examination eligibility. For the NIT+ system through JoSAA/CSAB in 2026, the bulletin required Class XII/equivalent with at least five subjects and either 75% aggregate marks (65% for SC/ST/PwD candidates) or a place in the category-wise top 20 percentile. It also specifies subject combinations: Paper 2A requires Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics and two additional subjects; Paper 2B requires Mathematics plus four other subjects. JoSAA/CSAB may modify its criteria and procedures.
bullets: Check the NTA bulletin for the applicable examination year before applying.
Check JoSAA/CSAB and the target institution separately before ranking colleges or relying on a score.
PCM fits Paper 1’s tested subjects; PCMB students may also take Paper 1, but programme-level subject requirements still govern admission.

sections.heading: Examination format
paragraphs: In 2026, Paper 1 was delivered entirely in computer-based test (CBT) mode. Its three equally weighted subject areas were Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, and its question types included multiple-choice and numerical-value questions. A single Paper 1, Paper 2A, or Paper 2B attempt had a three-hour duration; candidates taking both architecture and planning components had three hours and 30 minutes.

Paper 2 was not a single uniform format. Paper 2A (B.Arch) used CBT for Mathematics and Aptitude, but the Drawing Test was completed offline on an A4 drawing sheet. Paper 2B (B.Planning) used CBT for Mathematics, Aptitude and Planning-based questions. NTA’s 2026 result process used NTA Scores, and where a candidate appeared in both sessions, the best total NTA Score—not separate best subject scores—was considered for further ranking processing.
bullets: Paper 1: Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry; CBT only.
Paper 2A: Mathematics, Aptitude and Drawing; mixed CBT plus offline drawing.
Paper 2B: Mathematics, Aptitude and Planning-based questions; CBT only.
In 2026, question papers were offered in 13 languages for Paper 2 Session 2; language and delivery arrangements can change by cycle.

sections.heading: Application process and status of the 2026 cycle
paragraphs: The 2026 process required online registration, creation of an application number and password, completion of personal, educational, paper and exam-city details, upload of prescribed images/documents, online fee payment, and retention of the confirmation page. NTA stated that one application number was used for both sessions, while Session 2 registration/payment was handled during its own application period.

As of the review date, the 2026 examination and results cycle has concluded: the official portal displays 2026 Paper 1 and Paper 2 scorecard services and final-result notices. A candidate targeting a future cycle should not use the 2026 dates, documents or fees as deadlines; monitor the NTA JEE Main portal for the next information bulletin and public notices.
bullets: Use only the official JEE Main portal for notices, application access, city/admit-card instructions and scorecards.
Keep the application number, password and confirmation page securely.
Fees, correction windows, permitted edits, document specifications and dates are cycle-specific and variable.

sections.heading: Preparation approach grounded in the official scheme
paragraphs: Begin with the official NTA syllabus and match preparation to the selected paper. For Paper 1, build coverage and timed practice across Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, remembering that the 2026 scheme assigned equal weight to the three subjects and included both MCQ and numerical-value questions. For Paper 2A, add drawing practice; for Paper 2B, prepare Planning-based questions rather than assuming the B.Arch drawing component applies.

Use official question papers and the CBT familiarisation material linked by the JEE Main site to practise the interface and timing. For an attempt in a later year, re-check the new bulletin before finalising a plan because the syllabus, paper pattern, language options and operational instructions may be revised.
bullets: Download the current official syllabus before making a topic checklist.
Practise full-length, paper-specific tests under the applicable time limit.
Review mistakes by topic and question type, then reattempt weak areas.
For Paper 2A, practise drawing under the stated offline format; for Paper 2B, practise planning-based CBT questions.

sections.heading: What follows a JEE Main result
paragraphs: A JEE Main result can support different next steps depending on the paper: Paper 1 ranking is used for engineering admissions and for eligibility toward JEE (Advanced); Paper 2A and Paper 2B rankings support B.Arch and B.Planning routes respectively. Candidates who took both 2026 sessions had their best total NTA Score considered in the overall ranking process.

For NITs, IIEST, IIITs and other government-funded technical institutions in the NIT+ system, seat allocation is handled through JoSAA/CSAB rather than by NTA’s result alone. Candidates should use their score/rank alongside the current counselling business rules, category and home-state conditions, programme prerequisites, seat matrix and institute-specific requirements. Other institutions and states may use JEE Main results under their own admissions policies.
bullets: Engineering outcome: pursue eligible B.E./B.Tech admissions through the relevant counselling or institutional process.
Architecture/planning outcome: use the relevant Paper 2A/Paper 2B result where accepted, subject to programme rules.
IIT outcome: if otherwise eligible, apply separately for JEE (Advanced).
Do not treat an NTA scorecard as a counselling registration or a confirmed seat.

title: JEST
description: JEST — doctoral or fellowship exam (science), conducted by Science academies consortium.

quick_facts.label: What JEST is
quick_facts.value: The Joint Entrance Screening Test (JEST) is a national-level screening examination conducted annually in Physics and Theoretical Computer Science for research-oriented admissions at participating institutes.

quick_facts.label: Programs supported
quick_facts.value: Participating institutes use JEST scores, together with their own requirements, to shortlist applicants for Physics PhD, Integrated PhD and MSc programmes; Theoretical Computer Science PhD and Integrated PhD programmes; and a Computational Biology PhD route.

quick_facts.label: Recognition
quick_facts.value: The official JEST site states that ANRF (formerly SERB) recognizes JEST as a National Eligibility Test (NET) under OM No. SB/S9/Z-01/2015.

quick_facts.label: 2026 status and score validity
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, the examination was held on 12 April 2026 and results were declared on 30 April 2026; the official FAQ says the 2026 score remains valid until declaration of JEST 2028 results.

quick_facts.label: Subjects and attempt rule
quick_facts.value: A candidate may take JEST in either Physics or Theoretical Computer Science in a given year, not both.

quick_facts.label: 2026 application fee
quick_facts.value: For JEST 2026, the non-refundable application fee was ₹600 for SC/ST and PwD applicants and ₹1,200 for other applicants. This is cycle-specific and may change in a future notification.

sections.heading: Purpose and place in the research-admissions pathway
paragraphs: JEST is not itself a degree programme, job examination, or automatic fellowship award. It is a common screening examination whose score is used by participating institutes alongside their own admission eligibility rules to shortlist applicants for science research programmes. The official 2026 site identifies Physics and Theoretical Computer Science as its two examination subjects, with admissions pathways also including Computational Biology through the Physics test.

ANRF recognition of JEST as a NET can matter for fellowship eligibility in relevant ANRF/SERB programmes, but candidates should distinguish that recognition from an admission offer or a guaranteed fellowship: the receiving institute and the relevant fellowship scheme apply their own conditions.
bullets: For a BS-MS or BSc (Research) student, JEST can be relevant when planning a transition into MSc, Integrated PhD, or PhD study in the participating-institute ecosystem.
A JEST score is used for screening and shortlisting; applicants must separately check the programme, discipline, degree, marks, and application requirements of each target institute.

sections.heading: Eligibility: exam access versus admission eligibility
paragraphs: The official JEST eligibility page says there are no specific criteria merely to sit the examination. However, a useful score requires meeting the additional eligibility criteria set by the institute and programme to which the candidate applies. The official site characterizes its consolidated institute criteria as tentative and directs candidates to confirm the current rules on each institute’s website.

There is no age limit and no limit on the number of JEST attempts according to the official FAQ. Students from engineering backgrounds may appear, but that does not establish eligibility for a particular programme; programme-level requirements differ by institute.

For Theoretical Computer Science, IMSc states that candidates with a bachelor’s degree in CS or related disciplines, or a relevant MSc/ME/MTech/MCA, including final-year students, may appear for JEST. Its own PhD and Integrated PhD admissions have separate degree requirements.
bullets: Physics PhD eligibility commonly involves an MSc in Physics or a related qualification, but the exact accepted degrees vary by institute.
Candidates considering an MSc or Integrated PhD should verify whether their current year of study and degree background meet the target institute’s requirements before relying on the score.
For 2026, JEST stated that its score would remain usable until the declaration of JEST 2028 results; this validity statement is specific to that cycle.

sections.heading: Test format and level
paragraphs: JEST 2026 was delivered as a computer-based test at assigned examination-centre workstations; the official FAQ distinguishes this from an internet-based test. The examination is held at a level corresponding to MSc or advanced BSc study in Physics and Computer Science, and the official FAQ says questions draw on general graduation- and postgraduate-level syllabi.

The 2026 Physics paper was 180 minutes and 100 marks: Part A had 10 MCQs worth +1 each with −1/3 for an incorrect response; Part B had 20 MCQs worth +3 each with −1 for an incorrect response; and Part C had 10 numerical-answer questions worth +3 each without negative marking.

The 2026 Theoretical Computer Science paper was 180 minutes. Part A comprised 25 computer-entered MCQs carrying +3 for correct and −1 for incorrect answers. Part B had nine questions; candidates could attempt more than required, with evaluation based on the best three answers among the eight-mark questions and best two among the thirteen-mark questions. Part B closed after 105 minutes. Formats can change by cycle, so applicants should use the current official notice.
bullets: Candidates cannot take both subjects in the same JEST year.
Calculators, phones, books, charts, and other listed electronic or reference materials are not permitted in the examination hall.

sections.heading: Application process and 2026 timeline
paragraphs: The official application flow begins with registration and declaration/verification using a valid, unique email address and mobile number. After verification, the candidate completes personal details, educational details, exam-city selection, and online payment. The site says the application can be saved and resumed, but recommends completing it without interruption.

For the completed 2026 cycle, applications opened on 26 February 2026 and closed on 25 March 2026; admit cards became available on 7 April 2026, the exam was held on 12 April 2026, and results were declared on 30 April 2026. These dates and the 2026 fee are historical, variable information—not a schedule for a future cycle.
Admit cards are downloaded from the portal rather than sent by post or email. The official FAQ instructs candidates to bring a printout of the admit card and photo identification to the centre.
bullets: Use a personal email address that will remain accessible through the admission process.
Review personal details before confirmation: the 2026 FAQ says certain registration details could not be edited after confirmation.
Check the official JEST site for the next cycle’s notification, portal dates, fee, test cities, and documentation rules.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Start with the official subject-specific materials rather than relying on unofficial past-paper compilations. The JEST site provides a Physics syllabus, a Physics sample paper, Theoretical Computer Science preparation material, and a TCS sample paper. The FAQ cautions that official full question papers are not made available, though some earlier questions are available through the official site.

For Physics, build preparation around the published syllabus and timed practice. The syllabus includes mathematical methods and major core-physics areas; candidates should match their study depth to the stated advanced-BSc/MSc level and practise numerical-response work as well as negatively marked MCQs.

For TCS, prepare for both the multiple-choice component and concise written/entered problem-solving under the time split used in the current pattern. IMSc describes JEST TCS as aimed at candidates interested in the mathematical aspects of computer science; its programme page is useful context, but the annual JEST notice governs the live exam pattern.
bullets: Download the current official syllabus and samples before making a study plan, because the 2026 official site explicitly notes a pattern change.
Practise question selection and accuracy: both 2026 subjects used negative marking in their objective portions.
Use timed, full-length simulations that reflect the relevant year’s official duration and section rules.

sections.heading: What a qualifying score can lead to
paragraphs: A JEST result can support institute-specific shortlisting for interviews or subsequent selection stages; it does not by itself confer admission. For example, TIFR’s 2026 JEST score-based admissions page states that interview shortlists were published for its Integrated PhD and PhD routes in Physics, while IMSc explains that it uses JEST as one means of screening students for interview in Theoretical Computer Science.

The destination programme depends on subject, academic background, institute eligibility, score, and selection process. The official JEST site lists participating institutions spanning research areas such as physics, astronomy/astrophysics, and related theoretical and computational fields, so applicants should select programmes based on disciplinary fit—not solely on the existence of JEST acceptance.

An Integrated PhD may be particularly relevant after a BS-MS or BSc (Research): the JEST FAQ explains that the TCS Integrated PhD route awards an MSc after completion of the first two years’ course requirements and a PhD after graduate-school completion. Degree structure and funding terms remain institute-specific.
bullets: After results, check each intended institute’s separate admission page and shortlist/interview instructions.
Keep score-validity rules in view: the official FAQ gives JEST 2026 validity through the declaration of JEST 2028 results.
Do not infer a uniform stipend, fellowship, seat count, or cutoff from JEST alone; those are determined by the programme, institute, and cycle.

title: Judicial Services Examination (PCS-J, state-wise)
description: Judicial Services Examination (PCS-J, state-wise) — govt recruitment exam (law), conducted by State High Courts / PSCs.

quick_facts.label: What this examination is
quick_facts.value: “Judicial Services”/PCS-J is not one single India-wide examination. It is a family of state judicial-service recruitment processes for entry-level judicial posts, administered under the applicable state rules by the relevant High Court, Public Service Commission, or other recruiting authority.

quick_facts.label: Primary entry qualification
quick_facts.value: A professional LL.B. is the core qualification in the official Rajasthan Civil Judge rules; the relevant current state notification/rules must be checked for age, domicile/language, character, medical-fitness, reservation, and any experience conditions.

quick_facts.label: Typical selection structure
quick_facts.value: The structure is state-specific. For example, the Haryana Civil Judge rules prescribe preliminary examination, main examination, and viva voce; Rajasthan’s rules provide preliminary and main examinations, with candidates shortlisted from the main examination for interview.

quick_facts.label: Result of selection
quick_facts.value: Successful candidates are recommended and appointed to the state Civil Judge cadre, subject to the appointing authority’s process. In Rajasthan, directly recruited Civil Judges are placed on two years’ probation under the published rules.

quick_facts.label: Vacancies, dates and fees
quick_facts.value: There is no common annual calendar, vacancy count, deadline, or fee nationwide. These are fixed in each state recruitment notice; for context, Rajasthan High Court determined 44 Civil Judge vacancies for its 2025 cycle, while its rules leave the application fee to the recruiting authority to specify from time to time.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
paragraphs: The Judicial Services Examination is the entry route for state-level subordinate judiciary recruitment, commonly described as PCS-J, Civil Judge, or Judicial Magistrate recruitment. It should be treated as a state-wise recruitment pathway rather than as a centrally standardised exam: the recruiting institution, eligibility, syllabus, stages, language requirements, vacancies, reservations, and result procedure follow the particular state’s rules and advertisement.

A concrete official example is Rajasthan, where recruitment to the Civil Judge cadre is by direct recruitment on the result of a competitive examination conducted by the recruiting authority. Haryana’s published Civil Judge rules likewise allocate recruitment operations such as inviting and screening applications and issuing roll numbers/admit cards to the Haryana Public Service Commission, while the selection committee handles examination-related functions.
bullets: Use the official recruitment page of the relevant State High Court and/or State PSC as the authoritative source for a particular cycle.
Do not rely on another state’s eligibility, calendar, fee, age band, or syllabus as if it automatically applies to your target state.

sections.heading: Eligibility: verify the target state’s current notice
paragraphs: A professional law degree is the principal academic gateway for entry-level judicial-service recruitment. Rajasthan’s published Judicial Service Rules require a Bachelor of Laws (Professional) degree from a university established by law in India and recognised under the Advocates Act, 1961; they also specify knowledge of written Hindi in Devanagari and Rajasthan’s dialects and social customs. A Rajasthan Civil Judge recruitment notice published for the 2025 cycle similarly states the LL.B. requirement, Indian citizenship, and its cycle-specific age provisions.

Eligibility is not safely reducible to one national checklist. State rules and recruitment notices can prescribe different age cut-offs and relaxations, local-language requirements, documentation, category reservations, and fitness/character conditions. Candidates should read the detailed advertisement and amendments applicable to the exact recruitment year before applying.
bullets: Check that the LL.B. degree and institution meet the wording in the target state’s notification.
Check the notification’s specified cut-off date for age and qualification, rather than assuming eligibility based on the examination date.
Prepare the language/local-law requirements where the state rules or syllabus prescribe them.

sections.heading: Selection format and assessed subjects
paragraphs: The usual pattern is a screening preliminary examination followed by a written main examination and, in many states, an interview/viva voce, but exact design varies. Haryana’s rules expressly provide three stages—preliminary, main, and viva voce—and limit main-examination shortlisting to no more than ten times advertised posts. Rajasthan’s rules describe preliminary and main examinations, state that preliminary marks do not count towards final merit, and provide for candidates up to three times the vacancies to be called for interview on the basis of main-examination marks.

The written syllabus is jurisdiction-specific. Haryana’s published main-examination scheme illustrates the breadth: civil-law papers include procedural and commercial statutes; criminal law; English; Hindi; and viva voce. It also specifies three-hour written papers. This is an example of a state scheme—not a substitute for the current syllabus of another jurisdiction.
bullets: Download the current notification, syllabus, exam scheme, and any corrigenda from the target recruiting authority.
Build a subject list from the notified syllabus, including state-specific laws and language papers where prescribed.
Treat preliminary-exam marks and interview rules as state-specific; their role in final merit may differ.

sections.heading: Application process
paragraphs: Apply only through the method in the applicable recruitment notice. The Rajasthan High Court’s 2025 Civil Judge application instructions required online submission, advised applicants to read the detailed advertisement, and asked them to have educational documents, scanned photograph, and scanned signature ready. Those instructions also caution that details cannot be changed after submission and payment of the prescribed fee.

Procedural mechanics can differ by state. Haryana’s rules, for example, say candidates apply to the Haryana Public Service Commission in its prescribed form with required information and documents, and that the Commission undertakes application screening and issues roll numbers and admit cards. Application fees and deadlines are variable, cycle-specific items and should be taken only from the live official notice.
bullets: Read the advertisement and application instructions before starting the form.
Prepare degree/marks documents, identity/category certificates where applicable, photograph, signature, and any state-prescribed certificates.

Save the submitted application and payment confirmation; monitor the official recruitment page for correction windows, admit cards, answer keys, objections, results, and interview/document-verification notices.

sections.heading: Preparation strategy grounded in the notified syllabus
paragraphs: Start with the target state’s current scheme and syllabus, then prepare statute-by-statute rather than relying solely on generic coaching material. The Haryana rules’ published scheme, for example, names civil procedure, contract and commercial law, specific relief, evidence, family/personal-law topics, registration and limitation, criminal law, English, and Hindi. It also provides that only bare copies of legislative enactments are supplied in that state’s written examination; this reinforces the need to practise statutory navigation and answer-writing under the rules applicable to the target state.

For mains preparation, practise timed, structured legal answers that identify issues, state the governing provision/principle, apply facts, and reach a reasoned conclusion. Include language-paper preparation where notified and use previous official question papers, answer keys, and syllabus updates where the recruiting authority publishes them. Keep a separate update log for amendments or changes to criminal-law and procedural statutes reflected in the current notification.
bullets: Map every topic in the official syllabus to primary statutes, leading principles, and revision notes.
Practise preliminary-style objective questions separately from mains-style descriptive answers.
Simulate the official paper duration and language requirements.
Prepare for viva voce only after confirming that the target state’s scheme includes it and understanding its notified assessment criteria.

sections.heading: Career outcome after selection
paragraphs: Selection leads to appointment in the entry-level state judicial-service cadre under the applicable state rules, commonly bearing titles such as Civil Judge (Junior Division), Civil Judge-cum-Judicial Magistrate, Judicial Magistrate First Class, or Munsiff Magistrate depending on the state’s nomenclature and allocation of judicial/magisterial work. In Rajasthan, the rules provide for appointment to the Civil Judge cadre in merit order from the recommended list, after the appointing authority is satisfied as to suitability.

The post is the start of a judicial-service career, not an immediate appointment as a District Judge. Rajasthan’s rules provide that Senior Civil Judge appointments are made by promotion from Civil Judges on merit-cum-seniority, and specify a two-year probation period for directly recruited Civil Judges. Actual progression, pay, posting, training, and service conditions are governed by the relevant state service rules and orders and can change over time.
bullets: Expect appointment, probation/training, posting, and service conditions to be controlled by the state judiciary/government framework.
Use the final appointment order and current service rules—not coaching estimates—for pay, posting, probation, and promotion information.

title: KCET
description: KCET — ug entrance exam (engineering), conducted by Karnataka Examinations Authority.

quick_facts.label: Conducting authority
quick_facts.value: KCET is the Karnataka Common Entrance Test (also described in KEA materials as UGCET/CET), conducted by the Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA).

quick_facts.label: Engineering purpose
quick_facts.value: For the 2026–27 cycle, KCET was used to determine eligibility and merit for first-year/first-semester Government-share seats in Engineering and Technology, among other professional courses, in Karnataka institutions.

quick_facts.label: Engineering subjects
quick_facts.value: Engineering/Technology applicants take Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics (PCM) in CET; the 2026 timetable scheduled Physics and Chemistry on April 23, 2026, and Mathematics on April 24, 2026.

quick_facts.label: Test structure
quick_facts.value: In the 2026 bulletin, each subject paper was an 80-minute, 60-mark objective multiple-choice paper with four answer options per question; incorrect answers did not attract negative marking.

quick_facts.label: Engineering rank basis
quick_facts.value: For Engineering/Technology, the 2026 merit/rank rule used Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics marks in KCET and in the qualifying examination in equal proportions.

sections.heading: What KCET is for
paragraphs: KCET is Karnataka’s state professional-course entrance and admissions process administered by KEA. In the 2026–27 bulletin, KEA described its role as determining eligibility and merit for Government-share seats in first-year or first-semester Engineering, Technology, Architecture, BNYS, Nursing, Veterinary, Farm Science, Pharmacy and related courses in Government, University, aided and unaided professional institutions in Karnataka.

For the engineering pathway, KCET is not simply an examination score: the rank is used in KEA’s online seat-allotment process, alongside the Government-issued seat matrix and the candidate’s ordered college/course options. A verification slip is required before a candidate can enter options.
bullets: For B.E./B.Tech, take the PCM CET papers.
Architecture uses NATA rather than the CET written paper for its entrance score, although candidates must register with KEA to participate in KEA counselling.
Medical, dental and AYUSH admissions use NEET; they are not admissions based on the KCET PCM paper.

sections.heading: Engineering eligibility
paragraphs: Under the 2026 KCET bulletin, an Engineering/Technology candidate needed to pass the qualifying examination (2nd PUC/12th standard or equivalent) with Physics and Mathematics as compulsory subjects, plus Chemistry, Biotechnology, Biology, Electronics or Computer Science as an optional subject, and English as a language of study. The stated minimum aggregate was 45% in the relevant optional subjects, reduced to 40% for the listed Karnataka SC, ST, Category-I and OBC categories.

Candidates awaiting their 2026 qualifying-examination result could apply and sit CET, but could not be admitted unless they subsequently passed the qualifying examination with the required percentage. Eligibility for Government seats is also subject to the CET-2006 Admission Rules, the applicable eligibility clause, document verification, and approvals or rules issued by competent bodies and the Government.
bullets: The 2026 bulletin states that there was no separate minimum CET mark prescribed for Engineering/Technology eligibility.
For Engineering rank preparation, KEA uses PCM marks; the flexibility to substitute an optional subject for Chemistry applies to eligibility, not rank calculation.

Category concessions and Government-seat eligibility are rule-bound and can depend on the candidate’s applicable Karnataka eligibility clause; read the current bulletin rather than relying on a prior year’s category rule.

sections.heading: Exam format for the engineering route
paragraphs: The 2026 KCET written test ran across two days and four sessions: Physics and Chemistry on the first day, then Mathematics and Biology on the second. Engineering/Technology candidates were required to appear in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics.

Each subject paper was 80 minutes and worth 60 marks. Papers were objective multiple-choice questions, each with four options and one mark. KEA stated that there was no negative evaluation for wrong answers, but no marks would be awarded if more than one answer was marked for a question.

KCET uses OMR answer sheets. KEA instructs candidates to use blue or black ballpoint pen, fill the identifying details and version code correctly, and shade one response per question; an incorrect CET number or version code can prevent scanning and rank assignment.
bullets: Engineering paper set: Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics.
2026 per-paper format: 60 marks, 80 minutes, MCQ.
Marking: one mark per question; no negative marking; multiple marked responses receive no mark.

sections.heading: Application, verification and counselling
paragraphs: The process is conducted through KEA’s online portal. In the 2026 cycle, KEA required online registration, application completion and payment, followed by verification of original documents according to the claim certificates. After verification, candidates holding a verification slip could log in, enter and prioritise course/college options, and participate in online seat allotment.

Deadlines are annual and variable. As dated historical context only, the 2026 bulletin opened registration on January 17, 2026, set February 16, 2026 as the online-application deadline and February 18, 2026 as the online-fee deadline; those dates have passed. Candidates for a subsequent cycle should use KEA’s current portal and current information bulletin rather than these dates.

Information entered in the online application is treated by KEA as the candidate’s responsibility. The bulletin also warns that applying, taking the exam or qualifying does not itself create an admission right: eligibility, supporting certificates and document verification remain necessary.
bullets: Register and pay through the KEA portal for the applicable cycle.
Keep qualifying-exam, study/reservation and other claim documents ready for verification, where applicable.
Obtain the verification slip before entering seat-allotment options.
Enter options in genuine preference order and follow the round-specific allotment instructions published by KEA.

sections.heading: Preparation priorities
paragraphs: Base academic preparation on the Karnataka first- and second-PUC syllabus. KEA states that the CET question papers are based on the First and Second PUC syllabi prescribed by Karnataka’s Department of Pre-University Education, with the CET syllabus published on the KEA website.

For B.E./B.Tech, prepare PCM together with 12th-standard performance: the engineering rank uses CET PCM and qualifying-examination PCM marks in equal proportions. This makes board/PUC preparation material to the final rank, not merely a separate eligibility step.

Practise the OMR workflow as well as questions. KEA specifically advises candidates to download and familiarise themselves with the specimen OMR sheet, including correct entry of the name, CET number and question-booklet version code.
bullets: Study the notified first- and second-PUC Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics syllabus.
Use timed 80-minute, 60-question practice sets for each subject.
Practise OMR marking carefully with a blue or black ballpoint pen and one selected bubble per question.
Check the current KEA noticeboard for the current-cycle syllabus, hall-ticket instructions and permitted-item rules.

sections.heading: Results, rank and seat allotment
paragraphs: For Engineering/Technology, KEA prepares rank using PCM marks from both KCET and the qualifying examination in equal proportions. If candidates are tied, the 2026 rule resolves engineering ties first using CET Mathematics marks, then CET Physics, then the relevant qualifying-examination marks, then age; a draw of lots applies if the specified criteria remain tied.

After the test, KEA publishes a provisional answer key and accepts online objections with supporting justification on the notified schedule. KEA then applies the expert-approved answer key for merit determination and publishes separate eligible-candidate rank/result sheets, including an Engineering rank list.

A rank supports participation in KEA allotment but is not a guarantee of a seat. Allotment depends on eligibility, verification, rank/merit, the published seat matrix, the candidate’s entered options and the applicable rules. KEA’s 2026 bulletin described online allotment in up to three rounds or as directed by apex bodies or Government.
bullets: Check the provisional key and submit any objection only by KEA’s notified method and time.
Check qualifying-exam marks displayed with the result; report discrepancies under KEA’s notified process.
Use the verification slip and ranked option list to participate in allotment.
Treat an allotment as provisional until all applicable institutional, university, regulatory and Government requirements are satisfied.

title: Lateral Entry Entrance Test (LEET)
description: A state-level entrance examination for diploma holders and B.Sc. graduates for direct admission into the second year of B.E./B.Tech programs.

quick_facts.label: What this node refers to
quick_facts.value: LEET is the label used in Haryana’s 2026 B.E./B.Tech. lateral-entry prospectus for the route into the second year (third semester) of B.E./B.Tech. This is a state-administered admission route, not a single all-India examination.

quick_facts.label: Current 2026 admission basis
quick_facts.value: HSTES’s current B.Tech lateral-entry instructions state that 2026–27 admissions are to use inter-se merit based on the percentage in the qualifying examination through centralized online counselling. Applicants should not assume that an entrance test is required without checking the latest HSTES notice.

quick_facts.label: Core eligibility
quick_facts.value: For Haryana 2026–27, the listed routes include a 3-year or 2-year lateral-entry engineering/technology diploma with at least 45% marks (40% for reserved-category candidates), or a recognized B.Sc. with the same marks threshold plus Mathematics at 10+2; B.Voc/3-year D.Voc in the same or allied sector and an NCVT-approved diploma are also listed.

quick_facts.label: Study duration and entry point
quick_facts.value: Successful lateral-entry applicants enter the second year/third semester, making the B.Tech lateral-entry course a three-year route rather than the standard four-year first-year entry route.

quick_facts.label: Seat availability
quick_facts.value: The prospectus states that lateral-entry seats may be taken up to a maximum of 10% of sanctioned intake, but institute-wise and branch-wise availability is tentative and can change before or during counselling.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
paragraphs: This node should be understood principally as Haryana’s B.E./B.Tech. lateral-entry pathway, because the Haryana State Technical Education Society (HSTES) explicitly uses the term “LEET” in its 2026 prospectus. Its purpose is to allow eligible diploma holders and certain B.Sc./vocational candidates to join B.E./B.Tech. directly in the second year (third semester), rather than begin again in first year.

“LEET” is not a uniform national exam brand. States and institutions use their own lateral-entry admission arrangements—for example, West Bengal uses JELET—so applicants outside Haryana should identify the relevant state authority, examination, admission brochure, and counselling rules rather than rely on Haryana LEET information.
bullets: The route is for progression into an undergraduate engineering degree after an eligible prior technical or science qualification.
Admission, branch allotment, domicile/reservation rules, and the selection method are controlled by the applicable state authority and can change by admission year.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: For Haryana’s 2026–27 B.Tech lateral-entry admission, HSTES lists an engineering/technology diploma of at least three years—or a two-year lateral-entry diploma—with at least 45% marks; the threshold is 40% for candidates in listed reserved categories. The diploma can be in any engineering and technology branch under the stated HSTES rule.

HSTES also lists a recognized B.Sc. degree with at least 45% marks (40% for listed reserved categories), provided the candidate passed 10+2 with Mathematics. It further lists B.Voc/three-year D.Voc in the same or allied sector and NCVT-approved diplomas. Universities may provide bridge courses such as Mathematics, Physics, and Engineering Drawing for entrants from varied backgrounds.

An applicant should verify that the exact awarding body, qualification, marks, category documentation, domicile status, and branch/institute choices meet the current prospectus. Holding a related credential alone does not guarantee eligibility or a seat.
bullets: Entry is to second year/third semester, not to first year.
For the 2026–27 Haryana cycle, HSTES says qualifying-examination eligibility must be established during online application/document verification.
The current HSTES eligibility page notes that its criteria remain subject to AICTE and State Government directions.

sections.heading: Selection format: verify the current notice
paragraphs: The 2026 HSTES materials contain an important inconsistency. The current HSTES lateral-entry instructions, updated in July 2026, say admissions will be made using inter-se merit of qualifying-examination percentage through online centralized counselling. That is the operational basis applicants should treat as current unless HSTES issues a later change.

However, the 2026 prospectus also contains a full Online Common Entrance Test (OCET)/LEET scheme: 90 objective questions for 90 marks in 90 minutes, in English, with no negative marking. Its listed coverage includes basic sciences, electronics, mechanical, civil and other engineering-stream topics. This material may be relevant if HSTES activates or restores the test process, but it should not be treated as confirmation that a test remains required for the 2026–27 intake.

Because the selection basis, dates, and testing arrangements can be amended, check the HSTES B.Tech lateral-entry instructions and the Haryana technical admissions portal before registering, booking travel, or paying for preparation.
bullets: Current instruction page: merit from qualifying-examination percentage plus online counselling.
Prospectus test model: 90 single-correct-answer MCQs; 90 minutes; no negative marking.
Do not infer an OCET date, admit-card release, or test centre from the prospectus alone when the later instruction page specifies merit-based admission.

sections.heading: Application and counselling process
paragraphs: For the 2026–27 Haryana cycle, applicants apply online through the Haryana technical-admissions portal. HSTES instructs candidates to choose B.E./B.Tech. (Lateral Entry), enter information exactly as in the qualifying examination, upload a photograph and signature, and upload the Class 10 detailed marks certificate, qualifying-examination marks certificate, and applicable category documents for verification.

After fee payment and verification by a designated centre, HSTES says it prepares and displays the inter-se merit. Candidates then log in to fill institute and branch choices for centralized online counselling. After an allotment, the allotted institute verifies credentials and issues a provisional admission slip; failure to report by the notified schedule or submission of incorrect documents can result in cancellation of the seat.

Fees and dates are admission-cycle-specific. As a dated example only, HSTES’s 2026–27 instruction page lists a non-refundable registration-cum-application fee of ₹1,000 for the General Category and ₹700 for listed reserved categories, payable online. Applicants should confirm the fee and deadline shown in the live portal and current prospectus before payment.
bullets: Create and retain the unique application number and password.
Upload legible, correct documents and ensure names, date of birth, marks, and category details match official records.
Fill and, where available, lock choices carefully; allotment depends on merit, choices, seat availability, and applicable rules.
Report to the allotted institute as instructed and retain the provisional admission slip.

sections.heading: Preparation strategy
paragraphs: For the currently stated 2026–27 merit-based Haryana process, the highest-priority preparation is administrative: obtain final, accurate marks documents; calculate and verify qualifying-examination marks; scan required certificates; confirm category/domicile evidence where applicable; and prepare a realistic ranked list of branches and institutes before choice filling.

If HSTES later confirms that OCET/LEET will be conducted, use only the official syllabus and mock-test information. The 2026 prospectus’s test scheme emphasizes Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, communication skills, general awareness, and foundational topics across electronics, mechanical, civil, and other engineering streams; it also says the syllabus aligns with the AICTE/HSBTE diploma curriculum and advises broad study of important topics.
bullets: Monitor HSTES and the Haryana admissions portal for superseding notices.
Review the official branch- and institute-wise intake when it is published; availability is not fixed until counselling.
If an entrance test is officially activated, practise timed computer-based MCQs and use the official mock test rather than relying solely on third-party material.

sections.heading: Outcome after selection
paragraphs: A successful applicant receives admission to the second year (third semester) of an allotted B.E./B.Tech. programme and follows the three-year lateral-entry degree route. The eventual branch depends on the preferences submitted, merit position, and seats available during counselling; HSTES’s prospectus notes that eligible diploma holders may seek branches beyond their original diploma discipline, subject to rank, choice, and availability.

A seat is not final merely because it appears in allotment results. HSTES requires institute-level verification of uploaded credentials and reporting under the notified schedule; incorrect documentation or non-reporting can lead to forfeiture or cancellation. Intake and vacancies are variable by institute and branch, so applicants should use the live counselling information rather than assume a particular engineering branch will be available.
bullets: Direct entry point: second year/third semester.
Programme duration: three years under the Haryana lateral-entry route.
Final admission requires verification and reporting to the allotted institute.

title: LIC AAO
description: LIC AAO — govt recruitment exam (finance), conducted by LIC.

quick_facts.label: Conducting organisation
quick_facts.value: LIC AAO is a recruitment process conducted by the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) for Assistant Administrative Officer posts; the official 2025 recruitment covered Generalist and Specialist AAO streams.

quick_facts.label: Most recent official reference cycle
quick_facts.value: LIC’s Careers page records the 2025 AAO recruitment, including examination results and lists of candidates shortlisted after pre-recruitment medical examination. Candidates should not assume an annual 2026 cycle or reuse 2025 dates, vacancies, eligibility, fees, or pattern unless LIC issues a new notice.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: For AAO Generalist in the 2025 notice, selection comprised preliminary examination, main examination, interview, and subsequent pre-recruitment medical examination. Preliminary marks were not used in final merit; main-exam and interview marks were used for final merit.

quick_facts.label: Generalist eligibility snapshot
quick_facts.value: In the 2025 Generalist notification, applicants needed to be 21–30 years old as of August 1, 2025 and hold a bachelor’s degree in any discipline from a recognised Indian university or institution. The notice provided category-specific upper-age relaxations.

quick_facts.label: Application fee context
quick_facts.value: For the 2025 Generalist cycle, the non-refundable online charge was ₹85 plus transaction charges and GST for SC/ST/PwBD candidates, and ₹700 plus transaction charges and GST for other candidates. This was cycle-specific and may change in a future notification.

quick_facts.label: 2025 Generalist pay context
quick_facts.value: The 2025 notice stated starting basic pay of ₹88,635 per month and approximate minimum-scale total emoluments of ₹1,26,000 per month in an A-class city, inclusive of applicable allowances. These figures were explicitly subject to LIC rules and city classification and should be treated as dated context rather than a current guarantee.

sections.heading: What LIC AAO is
paragraphs: LIC AAO is LIC’s officer-level recruitment route for Assistant Administrative Officers. It is not a permanent admission test or a reliably annual examination: LIC publishes recruitment-specific notices through its Careers portal, which define the available streams, vacancies, eligibility, schedule, assessment structure, and service conditions for that cycle. The official 2025 page covered AAO Generalists and several Specialist categories, alongside Assistant Engineer recruitment.

For applicants, the practical implication is to identify the exact post named in the live notice. “AAO Generalist” and AAO specialist posts can have materially different educational and assessment requirements; specialist roles in the 2025 cycle included Chartered Accountant, Company Secretary, Actuarial, Legal, Insurance Specialist, and engineering-related recruitment streams.
bullets: Use LIC’s Careers page as the controlling source for whether an application window is open and for all cycle-specific instructions.
Do not treat third-party “expected” dates, cut-offs, vacancies, or syllabi as official until they appear in LIC’s notice or candidate handout.

sections.heading: Eligibility: use the post-specific notification
paragraphs: For the 2025 AAO Generalist recruitment, the baseline requirement was a bachelor’s degree in any discipline from a recognised Indian university or institution. The age band was 21 to 30 years as of August 1, 2025. LIC also listed upper-age relaxations, including 5 years for SC/ST, 3 years for OBC, and specified relaxations for PwBD, eligible ex-servicemen/commissioned officers, and confirmed LIC employees. These dates and limits belong to the 2025 cycle and must be rechecked for any later recruitment.

Specialist AAO eligibility was not interchangeable with Generalist eligibility. For example, the 2025 Chartered Accountant post required a bachelor’s degree, ICAI Final qualification, completed articleship, and ICAI associate membership; other specialist posts had their own qualifications and, in some cases, different maximum ages. LIC stated that equivalent qualifications would not be accepted unless specifically prescribed, and that supporting evidence is verified during the process.
bullets: First choose the notified post/discipline; then read its age, qualification, experience, category, and disability provisions in full.
Ensure the qualifying result date and documents meet the notice’s stated cut-off; eligibility is provisional at application and subject to document verification.
Applicants seeking a reserved category or age relaxation should preserve the prescribed, valid supporting certificates required by LIC.

sections.heading: Exam and selection format
paragraphs: The 2025 AAO Generalist process had three competitive stages—online preliminary examination, online main examination, and interview—followed by pre-recruitment medical examination for candidates reaching final merit. Preliminary marks did not count towards final merit. LIC used main-examination marks to shortlist candidates for interview, and used main-examination plus interview marks for final merit.

In the 2025 Generalist preliminary exam, the online objective test was one hour with separate 20-minute sections: Reasoning Ability (35 questions/35 marks), Quantitative Aptitude (35/35), and English Language (30 questions/30 marks). The notice described English as qualifying, with its marks not counted for ranking; it also stated that there was no negative marking in the Generalist preliminary examination.

The 2025 Generalist main exam comprised objective tests totalling 300 marks—Reasoning Ability, General Knowledge/Current Affairs, Data Analysis & Interpretation, and Insurance and Financial Market Awareness—plus a 25-mark English descriptive paper. The descriptive component assessed communication tasks such as emails, reports, situation analysis, and precis writing; it was qualifying and its marks were not counted for ranking. LIC reserved the right to modify examination structure in a future cycle.
bullets: Prepare from the current notification and official handout for the specific AAO stream, not from a generic AAO pattern.
Treat sectional qualifying standards and shortlisting ratios as notice-specific: LIC can set or revise them for a recruitment cycle.
Specialist and Legal streams in the 2025 recruitment used different preliminary subjects and main-exam professional-knowledge components.

sections.heading: How to apply when LIC opens a cycle
paragraphs: In the 2025 Generalist cycle, applications were online only through LIC’s website and Careers recruitment link. Candidates created a new registration using their name, contact details, and email address, received a provisional registration number and password, completed the application, uploaded required files, paid the online charge, and were advised to retain the system-generated application printout. A future cycle may use a different portal, dates, document specifications, or payment amount.

The 2025 notice required candidates to have a valid personal email address and mobile number active through the recruitment process, and to upload a photograph, signature, left-thumb impression, and handwritten declaration in the specified format. For examination entry, the notice required the call letter, original valid photo identity proof, and a photocopy of that identification. LIC directed candidates to download call letters through its Careers site, generally from seven days before the online examination.
bullets: Apply only through the official LIC Careers recruitment link published for the live cycle.
Read the live notice before payment: fees are non-refundable and the eligibility conditions are enforced even after registration.
Check the uploaded images, name consistency, contact information, category selection, and final preview before submission; preserve the completed application and payment proof.

sections.heading: Preparation aligned to the official scheme
paragraphs: Build preparation around the post-specific official scheme. For the 2025 AAO Generalist notice, that means timed practice for preliminary Reasoning Ability, Quantitative Aptitude, and English Language; then deeper main-exam practice in Reasoning, General Knowledge and Current Affairs, Data Analysis & Interpretation, and Insurance and Financial Market Awareness. Include typed English communication practice because the main descriptive component covered emails, reports, situation analysis, and precis writing.

Because the official notification gives separate timing for sections and requires candidates to qualify section-wise, use timed sectional practice as well as full-length simulations. For specialist AAO posts, replace a generic Generalist plan with the professional-knowledge and descriptive requirements stated for the relevant discipline. Before the examination, download and follow LIC’s official handout and call-letter instructions, since LIC may modify the structure and issues detailed candidate instructions through its website.
bullets: Create a syllabus checklist directly from the current LIC notice and official handout.
Practise computer-based descriptive responses, rather than only handwritten essays, where the notification requires typed answers.
Track insurance and financial-market awareness for the notified Generalist main exam, but avoid assuming that prior-cycle topics or marks will recur unchanged.

sections.heading: What selection leads to
paragraphs: Successful candidates in the 2025 AAO Generalist process were considered for regular LIC posts, subject to final merit, document checks, and medical fitness. The notice said selected candidates could be posted or transferred anywhere in India according to LIC requirements, noted that many vacancies were in mofussil branches, and stated that candidates would be posted for at least five years in mofussil branches outside their home zones after selection and successful training. These are 2025 service conditions and can change in a later recruitment.

For the 2025 Generalist appointment, LIC specified one year of probation, extendable up to two years, and a minimum four-year service undertaking including probation. Leaving before that period could trigger ₹5 lakh liquidated damages under the guarantee bond described in the notice. The official Careers page subsequently published lists of candidates shortlisted after pre-recruitment medical examination, illustrating that an examination result alone was not the final appointment step.
bullets: Final selection requires more than clearing an online exam: candidates must satisfy interview, merit, document, and medical requirements.
Review posting, probation, bond, pay, and benefits terms in the exact notice before deciding whether to accept an offer.
Treat all compensation and service-condition figures as dated notice-specific context.

title: LSAT—India
description: LSAT—India — ug entrance exam (law), conducted by LSAC / Pearson VUE.

quick_facts.label: Current status
quick_facts.value: LSAT—India appears to be discontinued rather than an active Indian law-admissions examination. A 2024 update states that Pearson VUE scrapped the examination, and current Jindal Global Law School (JGLS) five-year law admissions specify LNAT-UK and state that no other law-school admissions test is accepted.

quick_facts.label: Historical operator
quick_facts.value: For the 2024 cycle, LSAT—India was described as designed by the Law School Admission Council (LSAC) and delivered by Pearson VUE.

quick_facts.label: Last documented cycle
quick_facts.value: The last clearly documented LSAT—India cycle is 2024. Reporting on that cycle records a May 2024 registration window and acceptance by 18 law schools; these are historical facts, not a current admissions schedule or participating-college list.

quick_facts.label: Applicant action
quick_facts.value: Applicants seeking Indian undergraduate law admission should verify the entrance test directly with each target institution. For example, JGLS currently requires LNAT-UK for its five-year integrated B.A. LL.B., B.B.A. LL.B., and B.Com. LL.B. programmes, rather than LSAT—India.

sections.heading: What LSAT—India was—and its present status
paragraphs: LSAT—India was a law-school admissions test used by a group of Indian institutions. In its 2024 cycle, it was described as an LSAC-designed assessment delivered by Pearson VUE and accepted by 18 law schools. It was therefore not the common entrance test for all Indian law schools or National Law Universities; acceptance depended on the individual institution.

For current planning, treat LSAT—India as a legacy examination, not an open application route. A 2024 exam update says Pearson VUE scrapped it, while a current JGLS page for five-year integrated law programmes names LNAT-UK as the required test and expressly says JGLS does not accept another law-school admissions test. Prospective students should use each university's current admissions page rather than historical LSAT—India college lists.
bullets: Historical context: LSAT—India was used for admissions at participating institutions during the 2024 cycle.
Current implication: do not pay for preparation or assume a registration pathway exists for LSAT—India without an institution-specific, current official notice.
The international LSAT administered by LSAC is a separate test and should not be assumed to substitute for LSAT—India at an Indian university; follow the target university's stated test requirements.

sections.heading: Application guidance for Indian law aspirants
paragraphs: There is no current LSAT—India application process presented here because the available evidence identifies the examination as discontinued. Historical registration dates, fees, formats, and participating-college lists from 2024 should not be relied on for a future admission cycle.

Instead, begin with the admissions page of each target law school, identify its accepted examination(s), and apply through the school's official route. JGLS, for example, currently states that its five-year integrated law programmes use LNAT-UK, while its current postgraduate legal-studies requirements list JSAT–LAW 2026 or CLAT–PG 2026 for the LL.M. pathway. Requirements are programme-specific.
bullets: Check the exact programme, degree level, academic year, eligibility rules, test requirement, application deadline, and fee on the university's official page.

If you hold a historical LSAT—India score, ask the intended institution in writing whether it remains acceptable for the specific programme and intake; do not infer acceptance from an old participating-college list.
Use only official university admissions channels for applications and payments.

sections.heading: Admissions outcome and alternatives
paragraphs: Historically, an LSAT—India score could support an application only at schools that chose to accept it; it did not itself confer admission. The documented 2024 cohort included 18 accepting institutions, but that list was cycle-specific and has no demonstrated continuing validity after the examination's discontinuation.

The practical outcome for a present-day applicant is to select the test required by the desired institution. JGLS's current five-year integrated law admissions page identifies LNAT-UK as its route, whereas its current LL.M. admissions requirements identify JSAT–LAW 2026 and CLAT–PG 2026. This illustrates why applicants should decide at programme level rather than treating LSAT—India as a general Indian-law entrance option.
bullets: A historical LSAT—India result is an admissions credential only if a receiving institution currently confirms it will consider that result.
Current alternatives differ by university and degree programme; they are not interchangeable by default.
Any deadline, fee, score threshold, scholarship, or seat claim must be checked against the target institution's current official notice because such terms can change by intake.
