Historical LSAT—India 2024 overview and discontinuation notice

title: MAT
description: MAT — pg entrance exam (management), conducted by AIMA.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body and purpose
quick_facts.value: The Management Aptitude Test (MAT) is a standardized national-level management entrance test conducted by the All India Management Association (AIMA) for screening applicants to MBA, PGDM, and allied management programmes.

quick_facts.label: Eligibility
quick_facts.value: AIMA states that graduates in any discipline and final-year students in graduate courses may apply. AIMA’s MAT FAQ also says there is no age bar and no work-experience requirement.

quick_facts.label: Test modes
quick_facts.value: For the September 2026 administration, AIMA lists Paper-Based Test (PBT), Computer-Based Test (CBT), and the combined PBT+CBT option.

quick_facts.label: Exam structure
quick_facts.value: AIMA specifies 150 multiple-choice questions across five 30-question sections, to be completed in 120 minutes, with a deduction of 0.25 marks for each incorrect answer.

quick_facts.label: Score validity
quick_facts.value: AIMA states that a MAT score is valid for one year; individual institutions may nevertheless set their own admission rules and score requirements.

quick_facts.label: September 2026 timing and fee context
quick_facts.value: As listed by AIMA on July 18, 2026, September 2026 PBT registration closes September 7 and the test is September 13; CBT registration closes September 14 and the test is September 20. Listed registration fees are ₹2,300 for one mode and ₹4,000 for PBT+CBT; schedules and fees can change by administration.

sections.heading: What MAT is for
paragraphs: MAT is AIMA’s management-admissions aptitude test. AIMA describes it as a standardized test administered since 1988 to help business schools screen candidates for MBA and allied programmes; its official information page also describes it as a national-level test for MBA/PGDM admissions.

MAT is an entrance-test score, not an admission offer. Candidates should identify programmes that accept the relevant MAT administration and then satisfy each institution’s separate application, eligibility, cutoff, interview, and other selection requirements.
bullets: The Ministry of Education approved MAT as a national-level test in 2003, according to AIMA.

AIMA’s current information describes MAT as being administered four times yearly—February, May, September, and December—though candidates should rely on the live schedule for the administration they intend to take.

sections.heading: Who can take MAT
paragraphs: AIMA’s published baseline eligibility is broad: graduates in any discipline may apply, and students in the final year of a graduate course may also apply. Its FAQ says there is no age bar and that job experience is not required.

This examination-level eligibility does not replace a target school’s programme eligibility. AIMA specifically advises candidates to confirm approval or recognition status and score acceptance directly with the concerned institute or university before applying.
bullets: Base qualification: graduation in any discipline.
Final-year graduate-course students: eligible to apply under AIMA’s stated rule.
No stated MAT age limit or work-experience prerequisite.
Check the chosen MBA/PGDM programme’s own minimum marks, degree-completion, category, work-experience, and selection requirements.

sections.heading: Test pattern and delivery modes
paragraphs: AIMA’s September 2026 MAT information specifies an objective, multiple-choice test with five sections: Language Comprehension; Intelligence and Critical Reasoning; Mathematical Skills; Data Analysis and Sufficiency; and Economic and Business Environment. Each section has 30 questions, for 150 questions total in 120 minutes.

AIMA lists PBT and CBT as the available modes, with an option to register for both. Its published pattern applies negative marking of 0.25 marks for every incorrect answer. Candidates should verify the current bulletin before preparing because test arrangements and administration details may change.
bullets: 150 questions in 120 minutes.
Five sections, 30 questions each.
Negative marking: −0.25 per incorrect answer.
Modes listed for September 2026: PBT, CBT, or PBT+CBT.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: MAT registration is online through AIMA’s MAT portal. AIMA’s registration guidance directs a new candidate to create an account using a valid email address and mobile number, verify them by OTP, choose one or two test modes, upload the required images, select management institutes, enter personal and qualification details, pay, and submit the application.

AIMA lists a valid email ID, scanned photograph, scanned signature, personal and educational-qualification information, and an electronic payment method as registration prerequisites. Provisionally registered candidates download their admit card from the applicant dashboard; AIMA says it is not sent by post or email.

For the September 2026 administration, the listed fee is ₹2,300 for PBT or CBT and ₹4,000 for PBT+CBT. AIMA’s published dates and charges are administration-specific and should be rechecked on the official portal before payment.
bullets: Select PBT, CBT, or the available combined option.
Choose score-recipient management institutes during registration; AIMA states that the standard choice is five institutes, while a two-mode registration includes two additional choices.
Pay using the methods AIMA currently lists, such as debit/credit card, UPI, net banking, or wallet, where offered.
Download the admit card from the MAT applicant dashboard according to the published schedule.

sections.heading: Using a MAT score for admissions
paragraphs: After the result is released, candidates can download their score card from the MAT applicant dashboard using the account credentials created during registration. AIMA states that the overall MAT score is based on all five sections and that the score is valid for one year.

A MAT score can be used only where the receiving institution accepts it for the relevant programme and intake. AIMA notes that participating-institute lists and admission criteria vary by test administration, and warns candidates to reconfirm acceptance and approval or recognition status directly with the institute or university. Institutions determine their own cutoff scores and further selection process.
bullets: Download the score card from the official MAT dashboard.
Apply separately to target schools where required; a score transmission or institute selection is not itself admission.
Confirm score acceptance for the specific programme, year, and mode of study before relying on MAT.
Compare each school’s current eligibility, cutoff, fee, recognition, and selection criteria directly from that school or university.

useful_links.label: Official MAT information and September 2026 bulletin

title: MCAT
description: MCAT — abroad exam (medical), conducted by AAMC.

quick_facts.label: Administrator
quick_facts.value: The Medical College Admission Test (MCAT) is administered by the Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC).

quick_facts.label: Purpose
quick_facts.value: It assesses natural- and social-science knowledge, critical thinking, and scientific problem-solving for entry to the study of medicine.

quick_facts.label: Eligibility
quick_facts.value: An examinee may register when intending to apply to an eligible health-professions school; international examinees have no additional eligibility requirements, and current or degree-holding MBBS/equivalent students may register without special permission.

quick_facts.label: Score scale
quick_facts.value: The four section scores are each scaled from 118 to 132; their sum is a total MCAT score from 472 to 528. There is no penalty for guessing.

quick_facts.label: 2026 testing and India context
quick_facts.value: The AAMC’s published 2026 international calendar lists test locations by country but does not list India. Applicants based in India should verify currently available international locations, dates, and seats in the MCAT Registration System before making travel plans.

quick_facts.label: 2026 fee context
quick_facts.value: For 2026, the standard registration fee is US$355; testing outside the United States, Canada, and U.S. territories adds a non-refundable US$130 international fee. Fees and policies can change by testing year.

sections.heading: What the MCAT is for
paragraphs: The MCAT is an admissions examination used by health-professions schools that accept MCAT results. AAMC identifies eligible intended destinations as MD, DO, podiatric medicine, veterinary medicine, and other health-related programs that use the MCAT to meet an admissions-test requirement.

For an Indian applicant, the practical role of the MCAT is therefore determined by the admission policy of each overseas program—not merely by taking the examination. Before registering, confirm that each target university accepts the MCAT, its required score-reporting route, and its own academic, English-language, visa, and application requirements.
bullets: The exam tests the use of science concepts to think critically and solve problems, rather than functioning as a standalone medical-school admission decision.
The AAMC advises applicants to choose a test date based on intended medical-school entry, readiness with tested content, and whether they may need time for a retake.

sections.heading: Who can take it
paragraphs: Registration is tied to a genuine intention to apply to a health-professions school. During registration, the candidate must attest to that intention. There are no extra eligibility conditions solely because an examinee is international.

There are no mandatory courses required merely to register. However, AAMC says the tested material is generally covered in introductory biology, general and organic chemistry, physics, psychology, sociology, and first-semester biochemistry; research methods and statistics also appear in introductory science, psychology, and sociology coursework.

A currently enrolled medical student normally needs special permission to register, except for a student in an MBBS or equivalent program. AAMC sets testing limits of three attempts in one testing year, four over two consecutive testing years, and seven in a lifetime; voids and no-shows count toward the lifetime limit.
bullets: Apply for testing accommodations early if a disability or medical condition requires an adjustment to standard testing conditions; AAMC requires an electronic application and supporting documentation.
Use the target medical school’s published eligibility rules as the final authority for admission, because MCAT eligibility does not itself establish eligibility for a degree program.

sections.heading: Exam structure and scoring
paragraphs: The MCAT has four multiple-choice sections: Chemical and Physical Foundations of Biological Systems; Critical Analysis and Reasoning Skills (CARS); Biological and Biochemical Foundations of Living Systems; and Psychological, Social, and Biological Foundations of Behavior. Its content framework covers scientific knowledge alongside reasoning, research, data-analysis, and critical-analysis skills.

AAMC reports one scaled score for each section and a combined total. Each section is scaled 118–132 and the total is 472–528. Scores are equated across test forms so that small form-difficulty differences are accounted for; wrong and unanswered answers are treated the same, so there is no guessing penalty.
bullets: AAMC’s 2026 testing-year materials govern test-day procedures, identification, scheduling, conduct, and score policies; candidates should read them before registration and again before travel.
The official content outline is the best starting point for identifying the foundational concepts, content categories, and skills assessed.

sections.heading: Registration, location, and fees
paragraphs: Create or use an existing AAMC account, complete the registration questions, agree to the Examinee Agreement and associated policies, then select an available test date and location in the MCAT Registration System. Seats have limited capacity and are reserved first-come, first-served.

As dated 2026 context, the AAMC calendar covers January through September testing. The published international-location schedule does not include India, so an India-based candidate should use the live registration system to identify an available country, confirm the test-centre address, and allow for travel and visa planning.

The 2026 standard registration fee is US$355, plus a US$130 international fee for locations outside the United States, Canada, and U.S. territories. The final scheduling deadline is 10 days before test day, and all scheduling deadlines are at 11:59 p.m. local test-centre time. These costs, deadlines, locations, and availability are variable and should be rechecked when booking.
bullets: Register using an MCAT-accepted ID and make sure the registration name exactly matches that ID.
After scheduling, retain the confirmation email and check the current address of the assigned test centre; AAMC notes that locations can occasionally change.

Applicants who qualify for the AAMC Fee Assistance Program may receive reduced MCAT fees and free AAMC Official Prep products; assess eligibility before registering because benefits are not retroactive.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Start by mapping preparation to the official MCAT content outline and the four sections, then select a test date only after the required content and reasoning skills are sufficiently developed. AAMC notes that students may self-study, take a commercial course, or use an institution-provided course; a commercial course is not required.

The AAMC MCAT Official Prep Hub provides free planning materials. As of the 2026 testing year, official free resources include a full-length Practice Exam 1, a free sample test, the content-outline course with 120 free practice questions, a study-plan resource, sample questions, and a tool for practicing exam features. AAMC also points candidates to the Khan Academy MCAT collection.
bullets: Use official full-length practice material to rehearse the computer-based format and to identify section-specific weaknesses.
Build practice around content review, passage-based scientific reasoning, CARS reading and analysis, and review of mistakes—not only around memorisation.
Where available, seek advice from a pre-health adviser or faculty member on sequencing preparation with prerequisite coursework and target-school plans.

sections.heading: Using MCAT results in applications
paragraphs: An MCAT score is one element of a medical-school application, and acceptance rules are set by individual schools. AAMC notes that schools commonly accept scores from tests taken two to three years earlier, but this varies by institution; applicants should verify each target school’s current deadline and score-validity policy.

For AMCAS-participating medical schools, AAMC sends MCAT scores to the schools designated in the AMCAS application. For a non-AMCAS institution or application service, an applicant can use the MCAT score-reporting system when scores are released, or provide a printed score report where the receiving school is not listed.

AAMC’s full-disclosure policy means MCAT tests taken from April 2003 onward are included in MCAT score reports and made available through AMCAS. Plan retakes carefully and confirm how each target institution reviews multiple scores.
bullets: Do not use a total score alone to judge admission prospects; target programs set their own academic and non-academic selection criteria.

For US and Canadian MD programs, the AAMC MSAR service is a source for school-specific admissions information, including reported MCAT data and policies; always compare it with each school’s own current admissions page.

title: MHT CET
description: MHT CET — ug entrance exam (engineering), conducted by Maharashtra State CET Cell.

quick_facts.label: Conducting authority
quick_facts.value: MHT-CET is conducted by the Government of Maharashtra’s State Common Entrance Test Cell; the Commissioner of State CET Cell is the competent authority for the 2026 examination and related candidate selection process.

quick_facts.label: Primary purpose
quick_facts.value: For academic year 2026–27, the technical-education MHT-CET brochure covers first-year undergraduate admissions in Engineering and Technology, Pharmacy, B.Planning, integrated M.E./M.Tech and M.Planning, and Pharm.D.

quick_facts.label: Exam delivery
quick_facts.value: MHT-CET 2026 is an online computer-based test (CBT) with separate PCM and PCB groups; a candidate may choose either group or both, subject to the options made in the application.

quick_facts.label: Basic examination eligibility
quick_facts.value: For MHT-CET 2026, Indian-national candidates who have passed or are appearing in HSC/Class 12 or an equivalent qualifying examination may appear; the brochure states that there is no age limit for appearing or admission.

quick_facts.label: Question format and duration
quick_facts.value: The 2026 test uses four-option multiple-choice questions. PCM is 150 questions in 180 minutes, with Physics and Chemistry worth 1 mark each and Mathematics worth 2 marks; PCB is 200 questions in 180 minutes, with 1 mark per question. The brochure specifies no negative marking.

quick_facts.label: Admission route after the exam
quick_facts.value: MHT-CET scores feed into Maharashtra’s Centralized Admission Process (CAP) for applicable courses. The 2026–27 CAP portal separately lists undergraduate B.E./B.Tech, B.Pharmacy/Pharm.D, B.Planning, and Agriculture & Allied course admission routes.

sections.heading: What MHT-CET is for
paragraphs: MHT-CET is Maharashtra’s state entrance examination for professional undergraduate pathways. For the 2026–27 technical-education cycle, it is used in the selection process for first-year Engineering and Technology, Pharmacy, B.Planning, integrated M.E./M.Tech and M.Planning, and Pharm.D programmes. Although it is commonly associated with engineering admissions, the applicable programme and admission rules depend on the course-specific CAP process.
source: State CET Cell’s 2026 information brochure.
bullets: Choose PCM for the Physics–Chemistry–Mathematics examination group and PCB for the Physics–Chemistry–Biology group; the 2026 rules allow candidates to choose one group or both.

MHT-CET is an examination and score route, not by itself a college seat: candidates seeking admission must also follow the relevant CAP portal, notices, eligibility rules, verification steps and merit/allotment process.

sections.heading: Who can appear—and why course eligibility must be checked separately
paragraphs: The MHT-CET 2026 brochure states that candidates with Indian nationality who have passed or are appearing for HSC/Class 12 or an equivalent qualifying examination can appear for the test, with no age limit. It distinguishes Maharashtra State, All India and Minority candidature, among other categories; eligibility for a specific course and CAP seat remains subject to the applicable admission rules and documentation.

For B.E./B.Tech in 2026, MHT-CET is mandatory for Maharashtra State and Minority candidates under the brochure’s stated rule. All India candidates may appear, but JEE Main 2026 score is preferred over MHT-CET for B.E./B.Tech admissions. For B.Pharm/Pharm.D, the brochure similarly states that NEET 2026 is preferred for All India candidates. These are cycle-specific policies and applicants should verify the current CAP brochure before relying on them.
bullets: Maharashtra State candidature types are defined through factors such as qualifying-exam location, domicile/birth, or a parent’s eligible government employment; candidates can claim only one Maharashtra State candidature type.

Children of NRIs, children of Indian workers in Gulf countries, OCI/PIO candidates and foreign nationals are listed as exempt from appearing for MHT-CET 2026; their admission route should be confirmed through the relevant official admission portal.

sections.heading: Test structure
paragraphs: MHT-CET 2026 is delivered online as a CBT at centres in Maharashtra. The paper is made up of four-option MCQs. PCM and PCB are separate groups, and marks from one group are not transferred to the other. Physics, Chemistry and Biology questions may be offered in English, Marathi or Urdu; the language choice made in the application is irrevocable, and the English version controls in a question dispute.

The total test duration is 180 minutes. In PCM, candidates solve 150 questions: Physics and Chemistry carry one mark per question and Mathematics carries two marks per question. In PCB, candidates solve 200 questions, with one mark per question in Physics, Chemistry and Biology. The 2026 brochure says there is no negative marking.
bullets: PCM timing: first 90 minutes for Physics and Chemistry, followed by 90 minutes for Mathematics.
PCB timing: first 90 minutes for Physics and Chemistry, followed by 90 minutes for Biology.
The State CET Cell uses a percentile/normalization method; a percentile score is not the same as percentage marks.

sections.heading: Application and exam-day workflow
paragraphs: For the 2026 cycle, MHT-CET registration was online only through the State CET Cell website. The brochure directs candidates to read the official user manual, retain their application number and login credentials, and keep their registration details accurate. It also says that Aadhaar authentication and APAAR ID verification are carried out through DigiLocker, so candidates should ensure that those details are current and consistent before registration.

Candidates select the examination group and preferred examination city/district while applying. The CET Cell attempts to allot a centre in the candidate’s district or a nearby district, but the final centre allotment is binding and is shown on the admit card. A candidate taking both groups or multiple attempts can be allotted different centres.
bullets: For the 2026 cycle, the brochure listed general-category examination fees of ₹1,300 for a single PCM or PCB first attempt and ₹2,600 for both attempts; Maharashtra reserved-category fees were ₹1,000 and ₹2,000 respectively. These fees are dated 2026-cycle context and may change in later notifications.
After successful online fee payment, the candidate should save the receipt and print or retain the completed application form.
At the test centre, candidates must follow the admit-card schedule. The 2026 brochure prohibits phones, calculators, smart watches and other electronic gadgets in the examination hall.

sections.heading: A practical preparation approach
paragraphs: Start with the official State CET Cell syllabus and marking scheme for the relevant academic cycle, then prepare specifically for the selected group: PCM or PCB. Because MHT-CET is a timed on-screen MCQ exam, preparation should include computer-based practice under the actual 180-minute constraint, not only untimed textbook study.

Use the official pattern to allocate practice time. In both groups, Physics and Chemistry occupy the first 90-minute block; the final 90 minutes are Mathematics for PCM or Biology for PCB. For PCM, prioritize accuracy as well as pace in Mathematics because its questions carry two marks each. The Cell also indicates that an official CBT mock link is made available on its website in due course.
bullets: Build topic coverage from the official syllabus before increasing mock-test volume.
Practise four-option MCQs without relying on negative-marking strategies, since the 2026 brochure specifies no negative marking.
Review incorrect answers by subject and simulate the group-specific two-block timing in full-length CBT practice.
Before the exam, rehearse the official candidate instructions and confirm the allotted centre and reporting time from the admit card.

sections.heading: What the score can lead to
paragraphs: A qualifying MHT-CET score can be used in the Maharashtra CAP for applicable professional programmes, but admission is not automatic: course eligibility, candidature category, document verification, merit rules, seat availability and CAP allotment all matter. For 2026–27, the State CET Cell’s CAP page directs candidates to dedicated portals for B.E./B.Tech, B.Pharmacy/Pharm.D, B.Planning and Agriculture & Allied undergraduate admissions.

Applicants should treat cutoff expectations, seat availability and admission schedules as year-specific rather than fixed. The State CET Cell publishes CAP notices, brochures and course portals separately, so the correct next step after receiving a score is to use the official portal for the intended course and academic year.
bullets: For Maharashtra State and Minority candidates seeking B.E./B.Tech in the 2026 cycle, the CET brochure identifies MHT-CET as mandatory.
For All India B.E./B.Tech candidates in the 2026 cycle, the brochure says JEE Main 2026 score is preferred over MHT-CET score.

The State CET Cell’s 2026–27 CAP page also lists Agriculture & Allied programmes that may use MHT-CET PCM/PCB scores alongside other specified score routes; candidates should use that course portal for definitive eligibility and admission instructions.

State CET Cell: CAP 2026–27 course portals

title: NABARD Grade A
description: NABARD Grade A — govt recruitment exam (finance), conducted by NABARD.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: NABARD Grade A is NABARD’s recruitment process for Assistant Manager posts, including Rural Development Banking Service (RDBS) posts and, in the 2025 cycle, Legal and Protocol & Security Service posts.

quick_facts.label: Latest official cycle located
quick_facts.value: The latest Grade A advertisement located was Advertisement No. 05/Grade A/2025-26. Its online-application window was 08–30 November 2025; these dates are past and schedules, vacancies, eligibility, and fees must be checked in the next official notification.

quick_facts.label: Agriculture-related routes
quick_facts.value: In the 2025 RDBS notice, General accepted a bachelor’s degree in any subject with the stated minimum marks; dedicated specialist eligibility was listed for Agriculture Engineering and Plantation & Horticulture. Therefore, B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture holders could use the General route if they met its conditions, B.Sc. (Hons.) Horticulture holders could also match the Plantation & Horticulture route, and Agricultural Engineering degree holders could match the Agriculture Engineering route, subject to the wording of the particular cycle’s notice.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: For RDBS/Legal in the 2025 notice, the process comprised Phase I preliminary examination, Phase II mains examination, a mandatory psychometric test, and interview; final selection was based on Phase II mains and interview performance together.

quick_facts.label: 2025 fee context
quick_facts.value: For the 2025 Grade A cycle, the advertised non-refundable total was ₹150 plus applicable GST for SC/ST/PwBD applicants and ₹850 plus applicable GST for other applicants; a future cycle may set different charges.

sections.heading: Purpose and roles
paragraphs: NABARD Grade A is an entry route to Assistant Manager roles at the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development. The 2025 Grade A advertisement describes NABARD as an all-India apex organisation wholly owned by the Government of India and recruited for RDBS, Legal, and Protocol & Security Service posts.

For agriculture-linked technical disciplines, the 2025 notice describes work such as mapping rural-sector resource potential, credit-linked planning, preparation of sectoral and State Focus Papers, techno-financial advice, liaison with government departments and research institutions, and support for development schemes. Actual assignments can vary: NABARD states that specialist officers may be assigned other work for administrative reasons.
bullets: The relevant post/discipline must be chosen carefully: the 2025 notice permitted only one post or discipline application.
Selected candidates in the 2025 terms were liable to posting and transfer anywhere in India.

sections.heading: Eligibility: how the listed feeder degrees relate
paragraphs: Eligibility is notification-specific. In the 2025 RDBS notice, the General discipline accepted a bachelor’s degree in any subject from a recognised university/institution with at least 60% aggregate marks (55% for SC/ST/PwBD applicants), or specified postgraduate/professional alternatives. The same notice required the qualifying result to have been declared by 01 November 2025.

For a dedicated route, the 2025 notice required a bachelor’s degree in Agriculture Engineering with at least 60% aggregate marks (55% for PwBD applicants), or a postgraduate Agriculture Engineering degree with at least 55% (50% for PwBD applicants). For Plantation & Horticulture, it required a bachelor’s Horticulture degree with at least 60% aggregate marks (55% for PwBD applicants), or a postgraduate Horticulture degree with at least 55% (50% for PwBD applicants). Applicants should compare the precise degree title on their certificate with the next notification; NABARD says that where a certificate does not state a specialisation, a university/college certificate specifying it is required.
For the 2025 RDBS/Legal recruitment, the base age band was 21–30 years as of 01 November 2025, with specified upper-age relaxations. That dated cut-off is not a standing rule for future cycles.
bullets: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture: review the General discipline criteria in the next notice; the 2025 specialist list did not show a separate Agriculture discipline.
B.Sc. (Hons.) Horticulture: review both General and Plantation & Horticulture, where offered.
B.Tech in Agricultural Engineering: review both General and Agriculture Engineering, where offered.
Check nationality, reservation, disability accommodation, age relaxation, marks calculation, and document requirements in the cycle-specific official advertisement.

sections.heading: Examination format
paragraphs: The 2025 RDBS/Legal process used a preliminary examination, mains examination, mandatory 90-minute MCQ-based psychometric test, and 50-mark interview. Candidates clearing the applicable Phase I cut-offs were shortlisted for mains; candidates meeting the mains cut-offs and appearing in the psychometric test could be shortlisted for interview. NABARD stated that final RDBS/Legal ranking used mains and interview marks together.

For the 2025 General RDBS mains, Paper I was a 90-minute, 100-mark descriptive General English paper. Paper II covered Economic & Social Issues (ESI) and Agriculture & Rural Development (ARD): 30 objective questions for 50 marks in 30 minutes, followed by a 50-mark descriptive component in which four of six questions were attempted in 90 minutes. Specialist mains used the same Paper I structure but a stream-specific Paper II.

The 2025 notice applied a penalty of one-fourth of the marks assigned to each wrong objective answer in Phase I and Phase II. Formats and weightings may change, so use the information handout and advertisement published for the cycle you enter.
bullets: For General RDBS, Phase I shortlisting was based on the merit section: General Awareness, ESI with rural-India focus, and ARD with rural-India emphasis.
The 2025 notice allowed Hindi or English where applicable; the General English descriptive paper remained in English.

sections.heading: Application process
paragraphs: Apply only when NABARD publishes an active Grade A notice. In the 2025 cycle, applications were accepted online through the NABARD website only; the form was to be completed in English. The dated 2025 registration period has closed, so applicants should monitor NABARD’s Career Notices page rather than rely on old registration links.

The 2025 instructions required applicants to prepare a photograph, signature, left-thumb impression, handwritten declaration, online payment details, and an active personal email address and mobile number. Eligibility was verified at interview/joining, so an application did not itself establish eligibility.
bullets: Read the complete advertisement before selecting a post or discipline.
Confirm the education-result cut-off date and all category certificates before applying.
Retain the completed application and fee details after payment; do not send a printout unless the current notice specifically asks for it.
Treat fees, deadlines, documents, examination centres, and vacancy totals as cycle-specific.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Start with the official syllabus for the discipline you plan to enter and map preparation to the examination phase. NABARD’s ESI/ARD syllabus expressly says it is illustrative rather than exhaustive and instructs candidates to prepare for relevant current developments and Acts, even if a topic is not named in the syllabus.

For General RDBS, build working coverage of Indian economic and social issues, rural banking and financial institutions, agriculture, soil and water conservation, irrigation, farm and agri-engineering, storage and processing, and plantation/horticulture. The official syllabus also includes current economic and social issues, so revise contemporary policy and sector developments from authoritative sources alongside core concepts.

Practise typed descriptive writing for the mains format: English essay/précis/comprehension/official or business correspondence, plus structured ESI/ARD responses. For a specialist route, devote equivalent attention to the notification’s stream-specific Paper II syllabus and terminology.
bullets: Use timed objective practice and account for the one-fourth negative marking stated in the 2025 notice.
Practise keyboard-based descriptive answers, including Hindi input layouts if you intend to answer Paper II in Hindi and the current notice permits it.
Use official NABARD notices, syllabus documents, government publications, and primary regulatory sources for current-affairs revision.

sections.heading: Outcome after selection
paragraphs: Successful candidates are appointed as Assistant Managers in the discipline/service advertised for that cycle. Under the 2025 Grade A terms, initial appointment carried a two-year probation period that NABARD could extend by up to one additional year; selected candidates were liable to be posted and transferred anywhere in India.

For agriculture, horticulture, and agricultural-engineering backgrounds, the 2025 indicative role description connects technical knowledge with rural credit planning, techno-financial appraisal and advisory work, government-scheme implementation, research-institution liaison, and agri-business areas such as value chains, processing, value addition, and organic farming. These are indicative duties rather than a guarantee of a particular first posting.
bullets: For RDBS/Legal in 2025, the final merit ranking was based on Phase II mains and interview, not preliminary marks.
Vacancies and available specialisations vary by notification; the 2025 advertisement allowed NABARD to increase, decrease, leave unfilled, or cancel vacancies/processes as required.

title: NATA
description: NATA — ug entrance exam (design), conducted by Council of Architecture.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: NATA (National Aptitude Test in Architecture) is the Council of Architecture’s aptitude test for admission to the Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch.) programme.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: The Council of Architecture (CoA)—a statutory body under the Architects Act, 1972—conducts NATA.

quick_facts.label: 2026 test structure
quick_facts.value: NATA 2026 totals 200 marks: Part A is a 90-minute offline Drawing and Composition test worth 80 marks; Part B is a 90-minute online adaptive test worth 120 marks, with 42 MCQs and 8 NCQs.

quick_facts.label: B.Arch admission baseline
quick_facts.value: For first-year B.Arch admission, CoA specifies 10+2/equivalent with Physics and Mathematics plus one permitted subject and at least 45% aggregate, or a 10+3 diploma with Mathematics and at least 45% aggregate; the institution and admission authority may also impose applicable requirements.

quick_facts.label: 2026 score validity
quick_facts.value: The NATA 2026 score is valid for the 2026–27 academic session. A valid NATA score does not by itself guarantee a B.Arch seat.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
paragraphs: NATA is a national aptitude assessment for aspirants to the five-year B.Arch. degree. CoA describes it as measuring architecture-oriented aptitude through cognitive skills, visual perception and aesthetic sensitivity, logical reasoning, critical thinking, and prior learning. The CoA brochure states that the architecture-admission aptitude-test requirement may be met through NATA or the NTA-conducted JEE route, subject to the applicable admission rules.

NATA should not be treated as a general entrance examination for every design-related programme. Its stated role is qualification for B.Arch admission; B.Des, B.Plan, interior-design and diploma programmes can use separate institutional or state admission processes. Applicants should therefore verify the specific programme’s current prospectus and counselling rules before relying on a NATA score.
bullets: CoA conducts the test, but state/UT competent authorities and institutions conduct the actual admissions.
Reservation, merit-list construction, counselling procedures and seat allocation are governed by the relevant state/UT or institutional authority rather than by NATA alone.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: For taking NATA 2026, candidates may have passed or be appearing in the relevant 10+2 examination, or may have passed or be appearing in a 10+3 diploma examination with Mathematics. This permission to sit the test is distinct from final B.Arch admission eligibility.

For admission to the first year of B.Arch, CoA’s stated baseline is: 10+2 or equivalent with Physics and Mathematics as compulsory subjects and one of Chemistry, Biology, Technical Vocational subject, Computer Science, Information Technology, Informatics Practices, Engineering Graphics or Business Studies, with at least 45% aggregate; alternatively, a 10+3 diploma with Mathematics as compulsory subject and at least 45% aggregate. Candidates must also satisfy the requirements applied by the relevant admission/counselling authority and institution.
bullets: PCM and PCMB students normally meet the subject-combination direction because both include Physics and Mathematics, but admission depends on the full rule set and marks requirement.
NATA qualification does not create a right to admission; document verification and all authority/institutional conditions still apply.

sections.heading: Exam format and scoring: 2026 context
paragraphs: NATA 2026 uses a two-part, 200-mark format in English and Hindi. Part A is an offline, 90-minute Drawing and Composition test worth 80 marks: Composition and Colour (25), Sketching and Composition in black and white (25), and 3D Composition (30). Part B is a 90-minute online adaptive test worth 120 marks: 42 multiple-choice questions and 8 no-choice questions.

Part B covers visual reasoning, logical derivation, general knowledge related to architecture and design, language interpretation, design sensitivity and thinking, and numerical ability/geometry. For Phase 1, the final percentile is based on the candidate’s best permitted performance; Phase 2 produces raw scores for vacant-seat admissions after centralised counselling.
bullets: Phase 1 ran from April 4 through June 13, 2026; the official NATA site lists Phase 2 on August 7–8, 2026 for candidates who did not appear in Phase 1 and who seek vacant-seat opportunities.

There is no minimum raw score prescribed for qualifying in NATA 2026; CoA states that the final scorecard’s non-zero percentile score is the valid qualifying score. Admission authorities may apply their own merit procedures.

sections.heading: Application and admission process
paragraphs: For NATA 2026, applications are made online through the NATA portal. The official process is: create login credentials, complete personal details, upload required documents/images, pay the application fee, and save the confirmation page. The brochure says no documents need be posted. Candidates select a preferred city/region and date, but CoA makes the final test-centre and session allocation.

After the test, candidates download their statement(s) of marks and final scorecard from their login. They must then separately follow the applicable state, centralised or institutional B.Arch counselling/admission process; NATA does not itself allot a college seat. The appointment card and original photo identification are required at the test centre.
bullets: The 2026 brochure lists application fees per test as ₹1,750 for General/OBC (NCL), ₹1,250 for SC/ST/EWS/PwD, ₹1,000 for transgender candidates, and ₹15,000 outside India. Fees and policies are annual and should be checked in the live official notice before payment.
A candidate may take up to two Phase 1 attempts or one Phase 2 attempt in 2026, but may appear in only one phase.

sections.heading: Preparation approach aligned to the official syllabus
paragraphs: Preparation should mirror the two parts rather than focus only on drawing. For Part A, practise timed composition and colour work, freehand sketching of built environments and people, proportion, scale, texture, shading and shadows, plus physical 3D composition. For Part B, work on 2D/3D visualisation, logical inference, basic geometry and numerical reasoning, reading and grammar, architecture/design awareness, and analysing people, products, spaces and environments.

Use full 180-minute practice simulations: complete a 90-minute paper-based drawing/composition segment followed by a 90-minute computer-based question segment. Review errors by skill category and practise working within the prescribed time, because the official Part B format allocates 108 seconds per question.
bullets: Read the current official brochure before preparing because the pattern, scoring, schedule and permitted attempts can change by year.
For the drawing component, prioritise clarity of idea, proportion, spatial understanding and effective use of the medium—not only decorative detail.

sections.heading: What a NATA score leads to
paragraphs: A valid NATA score can be used in B.Arch admission processes for the 2026–27 session, subject to CoA eligibility and the applicable counselling or institutional rules. Phase 1 final scorecards carry the best raw score and percentile for centralised admission counselling; Phase 2 scorecards carry raw scores for admissions against vacant seats after centralised counselling.

The immediate academic outcome is eligibility to compete for B.Arch seats rather than automatic enrolment. A B.Arch degree from an appropriately recognised programme is relevant to the regulated pathway for using the title ‘Architect’: CoA states that registration requires education compliant with its minimum standards and a recognised qualification under the Architects Act.
bullets: Check whether a target college accepts NATA, JEE (Paper 2), or both, and whether it uses raw score, percentile and qualifying-examination marks in its merit rule.
Verify that a prospective B.Arch programme is recognised/approved as applicable before accepting a seat.

useful_links.label: Council of Architecture — NATA notices and documents

title: NCHM JEE
description: NCHM JEE — ug entrance exam (hospitality), conducted by NTA.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: NCHM JEE is conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) for NCHMCT, an autonomous body under India’s Ministry of Tourism; NTA has conducted the examination on NCHMCT’s behalf since 2019.

quick_facts.label: Primary admission purpose
quick_facts.value: The examination is the entry route for the three-year B.Sc. in Hospitality & Hotel Administration (B.Sc. HHA) at NCHMCT-affiliated Institutes of Hotel Management; the bulletin states that its score is accepted by all affiliated institutes for this course.

quick_facts.label: 2026 cycle status
quick_facts.value: The 2026 CBT was scheduled for April 25, 2026. NTA published the NCHM JEE 2026 score-card notice on May 22, 2026, so the 2026 entrance-test application window is no longer current as of July 2026.

quick_facts.label: Basic eligibility
quick_facts.value: For 2026, candidates needed 10+2 or an equivalent recognised qualification with English as a subject; students awaiting their qualifying result could apply provisionally. There was no age restriction.

quick_facts.label: Test structure
quick_facts.value: For 2026, NCHM JEE was a 120-minute computer-based, objective/MCQ test with 120 questions: Numerical Ability and Analytical Aptitude (15), Reasoning and Logical Deduction (15), General Knowledge and Current Affairs (15), English Language (45), and Aptitude for Service Sector (30).

quick_facts.label: Admission method after the test
quick_facts.value: Admission is based on All India Rank (AIR), followed by centralised online counselling in which eligible candidates register and submit institute/course choices; allotment is merit-cum-choice.

sections.heading: What NCHM JEE is—and what it is not
paragraphs: NCHM JEE is the national entrance examination for admission to the NCHMCT-affiliated B.Sc. in Hospitality & Hotel Administration programme. NCHMCT describes this as a three-year, six-semester programme recognised by Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), combining practical training in food production, food and beverage service, front office/rooms operations and housekeeping with management subjects.

The examination should not be treated as a universal entrance test for every hospitality, tourism, BBA or diploma programme. The official 2026 NTA bulletin specifically identifies the B.Sc. HHA at affiliated Institutes of Hotel Management as the programme for which NCHM JEE scores are accepted. Applicants considering BTTM, BBA, BBA Hotel Management, or diploma courses should verify the individual institution’s stated admission route rather than assume that NCHM JEE is required.
bullets: NTA conducts the test; NCHMCT is the hospitality-education body that uses it for B.Sc. HHA admissions.
The B.Sc. HHA route leads to centralised counselling and institute allocation based on rank and the candidate’s submitted choices.

sections.heading: Eligibility for the 2026 examination
paragraphs: The 2026 bulletin required candidates to have passed 10+2 Senior Secondary or an equivalent examination from a recognised board, with English studied as a core, elective or functional subject. Candidates appearing in the qualifying examination could take NCHM JEE provisionally, but had to provide proof of passing by counselling/admission or, at the latest, September 30, 2026.

There was no age restriction for NCHM JEE 2026. Candidates who qualify also have to provide a physical-fitness certificate for practical classes at admission, in the prescribed format. Original qualification, category and PwD documents are verified during admission.
bullets: Relevant streams are not restricted to Commerce: the published requirement is 10+2/equivalent with English, rather than a specified school stream.

Equivalent qualifications listed in the 2026 bulletin include recognised Central/State-board senior secondary examinations, certain pre-university qualifications, NIOS/state open-school senior secondary with at least five subjects including English, and other recognised equivalents.

sections.heading: Exam format and marking
paragraphs: In 2026, NCHM JEE was delivered as a computer-based test (CBT) in English and Hindi. It ran for 120 minutes and used objective multiple-choice questions. Candidates chose the question-paper medium in the online form; the bulletin says that selection could not later be changed, and that the English version governs where a translation ambiguity arises.

The 120-question paper gave the greatest weight to English Language (45 questions), followed by Aptitude for Service Sector (30). Numerical Ability and Analytical Aptitude, Reasoning and Logical Deduction, and General Knowledge and Current Affairs each carried 15 questions. Each correct response earned four marks, each incorrect response incurred a one-mark deduction, and unanswered questions received zero marks.
bullets: Total questions: 120.
Scoring: +4 correct; −1 incorrect; 0 unattempted.
2026 subjects: English Language 45; Service-Sector Aptitude 30; Numerical Ability/Analytical Aptitude 15; Reasoning/Logical Deduction 15; GK/Current Affairs 15.

sections.heading: Application and admission process
paragraphs: The 2026 application was online only. The registration period was December 26, 2025 through January 25, 2026, with fee payment due by 11:50 PM on January 25, 2026. These dates are historical, not a forecast for a future cycle; applicants should use NTA’s NCHM JEE portal and the next year’s information bulletin for any newly announced schedule.

For the 2026 process, applicants registered using their own email address and mobile number, completed the application, uploaded a photograph and signature (and a PwD certificate where applicable), paid through the integrated payment gateway, and retained the confirmation page. The stated 2026 examination fee was ₹1,000 for General/OBC-NCL, ₹700 for Gen-EWS, and ₹450 for SC/ST/PwD/Third Gender, plus applicable processing charges and GST. Fees, documents, correction windows and deadlines can change by cycle.

After receiving an AIR, eligible candidates participate in centralised web-based counselling, register on the counselling portal and submit choices. Seat and institute allocation is made on merit-cum-choice; meeting the examination eligibility alone does not replace document verification at admission.
bullets: 2026 application status: closed; the score-card notice was published on May 22, 2026.
Keep the confirmation page and monitor the registered email/mobile number and NTA portal for admit-card, result and counselling notices.
Check NCHMCT’s counselling portal for the applicable counselling procedures and seat-allotment notices.

sections.heading: Preparation approach aligned to the official blueprint
paragraphs: Build preparation around the published distribution rather than treating all sections equally. English Language accounts for 45 of 120 questions and Aptitude for Service Sector accounts for 30, so together they make up 75 questions; retain regular practice in numerical ability, reasoning, and current affairs as well. This weighting-based study allocation is an inference from NTA’s published scheme, not an official recommendation.

Use timed CBT-style practice: the 2026 format allowed 120 minutes for 120 MCQs and applied negative marking. Review errors and practice selective answering, because an incorrect response loses one mark while an unattempted question gains or loses nothing. Candidates should also read the current-cycle information bulletin before applying, since the pattern and operational instructions may be revised.
bullets: Practise English comprehension, grammar and vocabulary alongside service-orientation judgement/aptitude questions.
Practise core arithmetic and analytical questions, logical reasoning, and a routine for current-affairs revision.
Simulate the official 2026 pace: approximately one minute per question, while preserving time for review.

sections.heading: What admission can lead to
paragraphs: A successful NCHM JEE rank can lead to admission to the B.Sc. HHA at an NCHMCT-affiliated Institute of Hotel Management through counselling. The programme is three years/six semesters, with an optional fourth year under the NEP 2020 framework for an honours degree, according to NCHMCT’s published course information.

NCHMCT identifies career pathways for B.Sc. HHA graduates in hotel and allied hospitality management training, guest/customer relations, food and catering services, sales and marketing, railway hospitality and catering, state tourism organisations, retail, flight kitchens/on-board services, cruise and shipping lines, amusement parks, teaching roles and self-employment. These are examples of potential pathways rather than guaranteed placements, job titles or earnings.
bullets: Degree outcome: B.Sc. in Hospitality & Hotel Administration, recognised by JNU according to NCHMCT.

Fees vary by institute. NCHMCT’s July 2026 course page lists tuition as typically ₹3 lakh–₹5 lakh for the six-semester programme, in addition to stated common fees; applicants should confirm the current fee notice of each institute before budgeting.

useful_links.label: NCHMCT B.Sc. Hospitality & Hotel Administration course and admission page

title: NEET-MDS
description: NEET-MDS — pg entrance exam (medical), conducted by NBEMS.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: NEET-MDS is the national eligibility-cum-ranking examination and single entrance examination for admission to MDS courses in India; it is conducted by NBEMS.

quick_facts.label: 2026 examination date
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 admission session, NBEMS conducted NEET-MDS on May 2, 2026, as a computer-based examination at centres across India.

quick_facts.label: Core eligibility
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, candidates needed a recognised BDS degree, State Dental Council registration (provisional or permanent), and a one-year compulsory rotatory internship at an approved/recognised dental college. The internship completion cut-off was May 31, 2026.

quick_facts.label: 2026 exam format
quick_facts.value: The 2026 paper had 240 English-language multiple-choice questions, four response options per question, and three hours of testing time. It was divided into time-bound Part A (100 questions, 75 minutes) and Part B (140 questions, 105 minutes).

quick_facts.label: 2026 qualifying benchmark
quick_facts.value: For NEET-MDS 2026, NBEMS reported qualifying cut-offs of 308 for General/EWS at the 50th percentile, 289 for General PwBD at the 45th percentile, and 271 for SC/ST/OBC including PwBD at the 40th percentile, out of 960. These are dated, session-specific thresholds and may change in later cycles.

quick_facts.label: Counselling responsibility
quick_facts.value: NBEMS conducts the exam, declares results, and supplies results to the designated counselling authority; it does not conduct MDS seat counselling or allotment. MCC/DGHS conducts counselling for the categories of seats within its remit, while States/UTs apply their own rules for state-quota admissions.

sections.heading: Purpose and place in the dental education pathway
paragraphs: NEET-MDS is the postgraduate entrance examination following BDS for admission to Master of Dental Surgery (MDS) programmes. For the 2026 session, the bulletin described it as the single eligibility-cum-ranking examination for MDS admissions under the Dentists Act, 1948; state- or institution-level entrance tests were not valid for MDS admission.

Its 2026 scope included 50% All India Quota MDS seats, state-quota seats, private dental colleges and universities, and Armed Forces Medical Services MDS courses. AIIMS New Delhi was listed as outside NEET-MDS coverage for that session.

Passing or appearing in NEET-MDS does not itself guarantee a seat. Admission remains subject to applicable institutional, university, counselling, medical-fitness, reservation, and documentary requirements.
bullets: Use NEET-MDS to establish eligibility and merit for MDS admission after BDS.
Treat the examination rank as one part of admission: counselling registration, choices, allotment, and document verification are separate stages.
Check the relevant counselling authority and institute rules for the seat category you intend to pursue.

sections.heading: Eligibility after BDS
paragraphs: For NEET-MDS 2026, the baseline requirement was a recognised BDS degree from an Indian university or institution, registration with a State Dental Council, and provisional or permanent registration plus one year of compulsory rotatory internship in an approved or recognised dental college.

A candidate who was still completing the 12-month internship could take the 2026 examination if likely to complete it by May 31, 2026. However, admission required completion of the internship and registration by that cut-off, or the specified certification from the head of institution.

Eligibility is provisional at examination stage and is checked again by the counselling or admitting authority. State quota, domicile, institutional, reservation, and other admission conditions can differ by State or institution.
bullets: Confirm that the BDS qualification is recognised for the applicable admission cycle.
Track the internship-completion cut-off in the current information bulletin; the May 31, 2026 date applied only to the 2026 cycle.
Keep original registration and internship-completion evidence available for counselling and admission verification.

sections.heading: Examination format and scoring
paragraphs: In 2026, NEET-MDS was a single-day, single-session computer-based test. The syllabus was at BDS standard and covered subjects taught in the BDS curriculum under the DCI Revised BDS Course Regulations, 2007, as amended.

The 2026 paper contained 240 English-language MCQs with four options each. Part A contained 100 questions in 75 minutes and Part B contained 140 questions in 105 minutes. Candidates could not move to the next part early; when a part closed, they could not revisit or change its responses.

The 2026 marking scheme awarded four marks for a correct answer, deducted one mark for an incorrect answer, and awarded zero for an unattempted question. These operational details should be checked again against the bulletin for the intended exam year.
bullets: Plan preparation around BDS subjects rather than assuming a narrow specialty-only syllabus.
Practise under sectional time limits, not only under a three-hour full-test limit.
Account for negative marking when developing an attempt strategy.

sections.heading: Application and examination process
paragraphs: For the 2026 cycle, NBEMS made the information bulletin available on March 13, 2026, opened online applications from March 14, 2026 at 3:00 PM, and closed them on March 30, 2026 at 11:55 PM. These dates are historical and should not be used as a schedule for a future cycle.

The 2026 application fee was ₹3,500 for General, OBC, and EWS candidates and ₹2,500 for SC, ST, and PwD candidates, excluding applicable payment-gateway charges. Fees and categories are session-specific and may change. NBEMS required online payment through the application payment gateway.

After the examination, candidates use their score and rank in the applicable counselling system. For 2026, NBEMS said that counselling registration would use details supplied in the NEET-MDS application, so candidates were advised to retain the same mobile number and email address.
bullets: Use only the NBEMS NEET-MDS examination page and current information bulletin when an application window is announced.
Submit accurate academic, internship, registration, identity, category, and contact details; eligibility and documents are verified later.
Preserve the admit card, scorecard, payment confirmation, BDS records, registration documents, and internship-completion certificate for counselling.

sections.heading: Preparation approach grounded in the official scheme
paragraphs: Start from the official BDS-standard syllabus statement and build a subject-wise revision plan covering the full BDS curriculum. Because the 2026 examination used 240 MCQs in three hours, preparation should combine content revision with sustained question practice.

Make timed mocks reflect the actual two-part structure: 75 minutes for 100 questions, then 105 minutes for 140 questions. The 2026 rules prevented revisiting a completed part, so practising a strict section-close routine is useful.

Use error review to improve both knowledge and decision-making. With +4 for a correct answer and −1 for an incorrect answer in 2026, review why answers were wrong, whether the error was factual or interpretive, and whether an uncertain attempt was justified.
bullets: Create a BDS-subject checklist from the current bulletin and track first-pass revision, question practice, and error revision.
Take computer-based, timed practice tests using the current year's section timing where available.
Re-read the current official bulletin before the exam for test-day documents, reporting time, prohibited items, and identity-verification rules.

sections.heading: Results, rank, and progression to MDS admission
paragraphs: NEET-MDS produces an examination score and national rank used in the MDS admission process. For 2026, NBEMS declared results on June 2, 2026 and made individual scorecards available from June 10, 2026; scorecards were available for download for six months. These dates and access periods are specific to that cycle.

The NEET-MDS 2026 result was valid only for the 2026 admission session. NBEMS stated that the final merit/category lists for state-quota seats would be generated by the respective States and UTs under their own eligibility criteria, regulations, and reservation policies.

For central counselling categories, MCC/DGHS is responsible for the online counselling process for 50% All India Quota postgraduate dental seats and other listed institutional categories. Candidates should therefore follow both NBEMS for examination notices and the relevant counselling authority for counselling schedules, seat matrices, choices, allotment, and joining requirements.
bullets: Download and retain the scorecard promptly when released.
Use the applicable counselling portal rather than assuming NBEMS will allot a seat.
Verify state-specific eligibility, domicile, reservation, and institutional rules before relying on a NEET-MDS rank for a particular seat pool.

title: NEET-PG
description: NEET-PG — pg entrance exam (medical), conducted by NBEMS.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS), an autonomous body under India’s Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, conducts NEET-PG.

quick_facts.label: Purpose
quick_facts.value: NEET-PG is the national eligibility-cum-ranking/entrance examination for admission to postgraduate medical pathways including MD/MS/PG Diploma, Post-MBBS DNB, Direct 6-year DrNB, and NBEMS Diploma courses.

quick_facts.label: 2026 examination date
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 session, NBEMS scheduled NEET-PG as a computer-based examination in a single shift on August 30, 2026; NBEMS stated that results would be declared by September 30, 2026.

quick_facts.label: Core Indian-graduate eligibility for 2026
quick_facts.value: Applicants need an MBBS degree or provisional MBBS pass certificate recognized under the NMC Act/PG Medical Education Regulations, permanent or provisional MBBS registration from NMC/MCI/State Medical Council, and completion of the one-year internship by September 30, 2026.

quick_facts.label: 2026 test format
quick_facts.value: The 2026 bulletin specifies 180 English-language MCQs, each with four options, in 3 hours 30 minutes. Marks are +4 correct, −1 incorrect, and 0 unattempted; the test has five time-restricted sections of 36 questions and 42 minutes each.

quick_facts.label: 2026 application fee
quick_facts.value: For 2026, the published examination fee is ₹3,500 for General/OBC/EWS candidates and ₹2,500 for SC/ST/PwBD candidates, excluding applicable payment-gateway charges. Fees and policies are session-specific and should be rechecked in the live bulletin.

sections.heading: What NEET-PG is for
paragraphs: NEET-PG is the single national eligibility-cum-ranking examination prescribed for admission to postgraduate medical education. For the 2026–27 admission session, its stated scope includes MD/MS/PG Diploma programmes, Post-MBBS DNB programmes, Direct 6-year DrNB programmes, and NBEMS Diploma programmes.

The NEET-PG score is used in admission processes, but NBEMS’s role ends with conducting the test, declaring results, and transmitting results to the designated counselling authority. Taking or qualifying the examination does not itself create a right to a seat; the relevant counselling/admitting authority verifies documents and applies its own applicable eligibility, reservation, and institutional rules.
bullets: For All India Quota, deemed/central university and all-India open DNB seats, counselling information is handled through the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) of DGHS.
State quota and in-service-seat counselling are handled by the relevant state authority. Candidates should independently check domicile, reservation, and institution-specific conditions.

sections.heading: Who can apply
paragraphs: For an Indian medical graduate in NEET-PG 2026, the central requirements are a recognized MBBS degree or provisional pass certificate, permanent or provisional registration for the MBBS qualification issued by NMC/the former MCI/a State Medical Council, and completion of the compulsory one-year internship on or before September 30, 2026. Candidates whose internship finishes after that date, or whose qualification is not recognized as prescribed, are not eligible for the 2026 process.

Indian citizens and Overseas Citizens of India whose primary medical qualification was obtained outside India must, in addition, have qualified FMGE under the Screening Test Regulations, be registered with NMC/MCI/State Medical Council, and satisfy the applicable internship deadline. Foreign-national rules are more specific, including NMC recognition of the basic qualification and, where applicable, Ministry of Home Affairs security clearance and documentation for temporary registration.
bullets: Eligibility shown at the admit-card stage is provisional; verification occurs in counselling/admission.

For 2026, the published qualifying thresholds are the 50th percentile for General/EWS, 45th percentile for UR-PwBD, and 40th percentile for SC/ST/OBC including PwBD in those categories. These are qualifying standards, not a guarantee of admission.

sections.heading: Exam structure and scoring
paragraphs: NEET-PG 2026 is scheduled as a computer-based test on August 30, 2026 in one shift. The paper contains 180 multiple-choice questions in English, with four response options per question; candidates select the correct/best/most appropriate response. Total testing time is 3 hours 30 minutes.

The 2026 scoring rule is +4 for a correct response, −1 for an incorrect response, and 0 for an unanswered question. NBEMS describes five time-restricted sections—Groups A through E—with 36 questions and 42 minutes per section; once a section’s allotted time ends, a candidate cannot revisit or modify its responses.
bullets: The syllabus is based on the MBBS curriculum issued by NMC/the former Medical Council of India.
NBEMS has indicated that a computer-based-test demo will be made available on its website, tentatively from August 15, 2026.

sections.heading: Applying for the 2026 session
paragraphs: NBEMS published the 2026 application window as July 1, 2026 at 5:00 PM through July 21, 2026 at 11:55 PM. The only valid submission route is the online application through the NBEMS process; applications submitted by another mode or after the window closes are not accepted. The 2026 notice also says that early submission does not confer priority for a particular test state, city, or centre.

Applicants should enter their information carefully, upload the required images/documents, choose the required test-state preferences, pay online, and confirm that payment status is successful. NBEMS says an application is completed only after successful payment and advises candidates to retain the submitted application PDF. The 2026 admit card is scheduled to go live on August 27, 2026.
bullets: Published 2026 fee context: ₹3,500 for General/OBC/EWS and ₹2,500 for SC/ST/PwBD, plus any applicable payment-gateway charges.
For 2026, candidates must select three preferred test states; the first must be the state of the correspondence address supplied in the form.
The fee is generally non-refundable and cannot be carried forward after a submitted application; applicants should consult the current bulletin before paying.

sections.heading: Preparation approach grounded in the official scheme
paragraphs: Build revision around the NMC/erstwhile MCI MBBS curriculum, because that is the syllabus base stated in the 2026 bulletin. Use timed practice that reflects the current 2026 format: 36 questions in 42 minutes across five locked sections. This is especially important because a completed section cannot be revisited or edited.

Plan response decisions around the scoring rule rather than treating every unanswered item as equivalent to a wrong answer: correct answers earn four marks, wrong answers lose one mark, and unattempted items receive zero. Before test day, use the NBEMS computer-based-test demo when it becomes available to practise navigation and time-restricted sections.
bullets: Prioritize retrieval practice and error review across the MBBS knowledge areas rather than relying only on passive reading.
During timed mocks, rehearse a section-level workflow: answer high-confidence items, mark review candidates while time remains, and complete all revision before that section locks.

sections.heading: What follows the result
paragraphs: NBEMS scheduled declaration of the NEET-PG 2026 result by September 30, 2026. Candidates can download scorecards using their login credentials; the bulletin states that scorecards will be available for six months from result declaration. NBEMS also states that it will publish the answer key and each candidate’s recorded responses in accordance with the cited Supreme Court order.

A qualifying result enables participation in the applicable counselling pathway only if all additional rules are met. For All India Quota, deemed/central university, and all-India open DNB seats, MCC/DGHS publishes counselling procedures; state quota eligibility, ranks, reservation benefits, and admission rules remain subject to the relevant state/UT or institution.
bullets: NEET-PG 2026 qualifying cut-offs published in the bulletin are percentile-based; competitive rank, seat availability, category rules, preferences, and counselling choices determine actual allotment.
A candidate who merely appears in or passes NEET-PG is not automatically eligible for every state quota, private university, or institute.

title: NEET-SS
description: NEET-SS — pg entrance exam (medical), conducted by NBEMS. super-speciality (DM/M.Ch).

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: NEET-SS (National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test—Super Specialty) is NBEMS’s single eligibility-cum-ranking entrance examination for admission to DM, MCh and DrNB Super Specialty courses.

quick_facts.label: Exam authority
quick_facts.value: The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) conducts NEET-SS.

quick_facts.label: Who can apply
quick_facts.value: Applicants need a recognised MD/MS/DNB qualification (or equivalent) or must obtain it by the session-specific cut-off date, and their prior qualification must be an eligible feeder specialty for the chosen super-specialty course/group.

quick_facts.label: 2026 timing
quick_facts.value: NBEMS’s April 29, 2026 notice lists NEET-SS 2026 tentatively for December 11–12, 2026, with January 31, 2027 as the tentative prior-entry-qualification cut-off. NBEMS states that exact dates will be set out in the later Information Bulletin.

quick_facts.label: Recent exam pattern reference
quick_facts.value: In NEET-SS 2025, the computer-based, group-based paper had 150 MCQs over 150 minutes, arranged as three time-bound 50-question/50-minute sections; correct answers received +4 and incorrect answers incurred −1.

quick_facts.label: Counselling route
quick_facts.value: For the 2025 admission session, qualified candidates participated in national-level common counselling for DM, MCh and DrNB Super Specialty seats conducted by MCC under DGHS. Counselling rules and seat availability are session-specific.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
paragraphs: NEET-SS is the national gateway examination for postgraduate doctors seeking entry to super-specialty training. NBEMS describes it as the prescribed single entrance examination for DM, MCh and DrNB Super Specialty programmes under section 61(2) of the National Medical Commission Act, 2019.

The scope stated by NBEMS includes DM/MCh courses across the country—including private, deemed-university and Armed Forces Medical Services institutions—and DrNB Super Specialty courses other than direct six-year DrNB programmes. NBEMS’s overview separately identifies AIIMS, PGIMER, JIPMER and NIMHANS as outside NEET-SS centralised admissions for DM/MCh seats; candidates should therefore confirm the applicable admission route for a particular institution and programme.
bullets: A qualifying NEET-SS score is used for admission to the applicable DM/MCh/DrNB Super Specialty pathway; it is not itself an admission offer.

The current public schedule notice describes the December 11–12, 2026 examination dates as tentative. Watch for the 2026 Information Bulletin before treating any date, eligibility cut-off, fee or procedure as final.

sections.heading: Eligibility: postgraduate qualification and feeder specialty
paragraphs: The core eligibility model is qualification-based: candidates must hold a recognised MD, MS, DNB or equivalent postgraduate qualification—or be likely to hold it by the notified cut-off—and must meet the feeder-specialty requirement for the super-specialty they want to pursue. The exact feeder mappings are published in the session Information Bulletin and can differ by course/group.

The 2025 bulletin required NMC or State Medical Council registration for Indian candidates, with documentary proof at the test centre. It also stated that foreign nationals and OCI cardholders could take the examination without NMC registration, subject to the provisions described for temporary registration if admitted. These details should be reconfirmed against the 2026 bulletin.

A candidate who is already pursuing or has joined a DM, MCh or DrNB doctoral course through NEET-SS was not eligible in the 2025 rules to seek a DrNB Super Specialty seat through that session for the prescribed duration of the earlier course, irrespective of resignation or discontinuation.
bullets: Check the course-specific feeder list rather than assuming that every MD/MS/DNB specialty qualifies for every group.
For planning only: the April 29, 2026 NBEMS notice gives January 31, 2027 as the tentative cut-off for completing the prior-entry qualification for NEET-SS 2026.

sections.heading: Exam format and scoring
paragraphs: NEET-SS 2025 was delivered as a computer-based examination and organised by question-paper group. Candidates could choose one or more groups only where their broad-specialty qualification was an eligible feeder qualification. NBEMS used 15 groups in 2025, with a common question paper for the super-specialty courses covered by each group.

The 2025 paper contained 150 multiple-choice questions to be attempted in 150 minutes. It was split into Sections A, B and C, each allowing 50 minutes for 50 questions. A candidate could not move forward early, or revisit and change answers from a completed section. The scoring rule was +4 for a correct response, −1 for an incorrect response, and 0 for an unattempted question.

For most 2025 groups, questions were drawn from the general/basic and subspecialty components of the primary feeder broad specialty at postgraduate-exit level. Critical Care Medicine and Medical Oncology were separately examined on their respective super-specialty topics. Pattern, groups and syllabus coverage must be verified from the 2026 bulletin when released.
bullets: The 2025 qualifying standard was the 50th percentile or above within each question-paper group-specific merit list.
NBEMS stated that group-wise merit lists were prepared from marks, without equating, scaling or normalisation; its published tie-break sequence began with fewer negative responses.

sections.heading: Application and admissions process
paragraphs: When NBEMS opens the session window, candidates apply online through the NEET-SS area of the NBEMS website and Applicant Login. In the 2025 process, applicants selected eligible question-paper group(s), supplied the requested personal and qualification details, uploaded a recent photograph, signature and thumb impression, selected an available test city, and completed online payment. The application was complete only after the payment status showed successful.

The 2025 fee was ₹3,500 per selected question-paper group, excluding any applicable payment-gateway charges; this is historical, session-specific context rather than a quote for NEET-SS 2026. The 2025 bulletin allowed certain edits only within a notified edit window and excluded key fields such as name, nationality, test city, mobile number and email from correction.

After result and qualification, the 2025 system used group-specific merit and MCC/DGHS common national counselling. Candidates could exercise choices only for the courses in their qualified group for which their own broad-specialty qualification was an eligible feeder. A score was valid only for that admission session and could not be carried forward.
bullets: Do not rely on the 2025 application dates: they were November 5–25, 2025 and are already past.
For NEET-SS 2026, NBEMS advises candidates to monitor its website for the Information Bulletin and online application form; the current December 2026 examination dates remain tentative.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Build preparation around the specific question-paper group and feeder mapping, not simply the title of a desired DM/MCh/DrNB course. In the 2025 scheme, primary-feeder groups tested the postgraduate-exit curriculum of the relevant broad specialty, including general/basic and subspecialty components; Medical Oncology and Critical Care Medicine had specialty-topic papers. Start by reading the current bulletin’s group table and feeder annexures when the 2026 version becomes available.

Practise in the computer-based format and rehearse time management in three 50-minute blocks. This is especially important because the 2025 format prevented candidates from returning to a prior section after its allotted time elapsed. NBEMS also made a CBT demo test available to 2025 applicants; candidates should look for any comparable official familiarisation resource for the 2026 session.
bullets: Use the official Information Bulletin as the primary checklist for syllabus boundaries, eligible groups, image specifications, test-day requirements and deadline changes.
Apply only after checking that qualification, registration and documentary requirements will be met by the session’s notified cut-off date.

sections.heading: What qualifying leads to
paragraphs: A qualifying result makes a candidate eligible to enter the applicable counselling process; it does not automatically confer admission.
