For NEET-SS 2025, NBEMS declared candidates at or above the 50th percentile in their respective question-paper group qualified, and MCC/DGHS conducted the common national counselling for the covered DM, MCh and DrNB Super Specialty seats.

The practical outcome is a group-specific merit position and the ability to state preferences for seats that both fall within the qualified group and accept the candidate’s feeder qualification. Final allotment, reservation rules, seat matrix, reporting and admission verification are handled through the counselling/admitting process and vary by session.
bullets: The 2025 NEET-SS result was declared on January 23, 2026 for the 2025–26 admission session.
Candidates should use MCC’s official portal for the live counselling schedule, scheme, seat matrix and allotment notices once the relevant session opens.

useful_links.label: NEET-SS 2025 Information Bulletin (reference for prior cycle rules and format)

title: NEET-UG
description: NEET-UG — ug entrance exam (medical), conducted by NTA.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: NEET (UG) is conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA).

quick_facts.label: What it is for
quick_facts.value: It is the common national eligibility-cum-entrance test used for undergraduate medical education and, under the applicable laws and regulations, for MBBS, BDS, BAMS, BUMS, BSMS and BHMS admissions.

quick_facts.label: 2026 test format
quick_facts.value: The 2026 bulletin specified a single-shift pen-and-paper test of 180 compulsory MCQs in 180 minutes: Physics 45 questions, Chemistry 45, and Biology 90, for 720 marks.

quick_facts.label: Eligibility baseline
quick_facts.value: For NEET (UG)-2026, candidates had to complete age 17 by December 31, 2026. The qualifying-study requirements include Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English; Class 12 candidates awaiting results could sit the test but needed to pass the qualifying examination for admission.

quick_facts.label: 2026 cycle status
quick_facts.value: The originally scheduled examination was held on May 3, 2026; NTA’s official NEET site lists score cards and a subsequent re-examination-related result/answer-key process. Candidates should rely on the official portal for their own score and counselling notices.

quick_facts.label: Counselling routes
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 framework, MCC/DGHS handles specified All India Quota, central, AIIMS, JIPMER and deemed-university medical/dental seats; state/UT authorities handle seats under their control. AACCC handles AYUSH All India Quota counselling.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
paragraphs: NEET (UG) is the national entrance examination administered by NTA for undergraduate medical education. The 2026 NTA bulletin identifies it as the uniform test for MBBS and BDS, and as the uniform entrance test for BAMS, BUMS, BSMS and BHMS under their respective statutory frameworks. NEET has also been the qualifying entrance examination for MBBS at AIIMS and JIPMER since 2020.

A NEET score is not by itself an admission offer. NTA conducts the examination, declares results and provides the All India Rank; the relevant regulator, counselling authority, state authority and college apply their own seat, category, domicile, document-verification and admission rules.
bullets: Use the official NTA bulletin for examination rules and the official websites of counselling authorities and institutions for seat-level admission conditions.
Do not assume that every health-science programme uses NEET nationally: institutions may use a NEET score for additional programmes under their own rules.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: For the NEET (UG)-2026 cycle, the age rule stated that a candidate must have completed 17 years on or before December 31 of the examination year. Indian nationals, NRIs, OCI cardholders and foreign nationals could appear, subject to the applicable admission rules and documentation requirements.

The qualifying-study baseline is Class 12 or an equivalent qualification with Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English. A student whose Class 12 result was pending could apply and take the test, but could not be admitted until the qualifying examination was passed. The bulletin also permits candidates who studied the required subjects, including English, as additional subjects after Class 12 from a government-recognised board to appear in NEET (UG).

Meeting NEET examination eligibility and qualifying the test do not eliminate course-specific conditions. For undergraduate medical courses, the 2026 bulletin stated minimum qualifying percentiles of 50th for General/General-EWS, 40th for SC/ST/OBC, and 45th for PwBD candidates in General/General-EWS; the applicable authority may set or modify rules for a given admission year.
bullets: Check the current-year NTA bulletin before applying: dates, age cut-offs, nationality documentation and correction windows can change.
Check the target course and college separately for academic marks, category certificates, domicile, disability certification, language requirements and other admission conditions.

sections.heading: Exam format and scoring
paragraphs: The 2026 scheme used a single-day, single-shift, pen-and-paper examination. It contained 180 compulsory multiple-choice questions to be completed in 180 minutes: 45 each in Physics and Chemistry and 90 in Biology (Botany and Zoology), for a maximum of 720 marks.

The 2026 marking rule was +4 for a correct or most-appropriate answer, −1 for an incorrect marked option, and 0 for an unanswered question. The question paper was offered in 13 media, including English and Hindi; the selected medium could not be changed later in the application process.
NMC notifies the syllabus. Preparation should therefore be anchored to the current official syllabus rather than to coaching-provider topic lists or prior-year assumptions.
bullets: Build test strategy around accuracy as well as speed because of negative marking.
Practise full-length paper-based mock tests under the official three-hour constraint.
Verify the current-year subject distribution, duration, mode, languages and marking scheme from the official bulletin before finalising a study plan.

sections.heading: Application process
paragraphs: The NTA process is online through the NEET portal. For 2026, applicants were instructed to keep identity, date-of-birth, Class X and XII, address, contact and supporting-document details ready; Indian applicants could use Aadhaar, an Indian passport, DigiLocker, PAN or another valid government-issued photo ID. Mobile number and email verification by OTP were required.

The core online workflow is: register and record the system-generated application number; complete the form and upload the required images/documents; pay the applicable fee; and save the confirmation page. NTA permitted only one application per candidate and warned that duplicate or false applications can lead to disqualification and further action.

The 2026 application window ran from February 8 through March 8, with a correction window from March 10 through March 12. These dates are historical context only, not a forecast: prospective candidates should wait for and follow the next official NTA notice.
bullets: Use personal email and mobile access that will remain active through results and counselling.
Enter names, dates of birth, category and identification details exactly as supported by documents.
Download and retain the confirmation page, admit card and score card; then monitor the NTA portal and applicable counselling authority until counselling closes.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Start from the NMC-notified NEET syllabus and organise revision across Physics, Chemistry and Biology. Since Biology accounts for half of the 720 marks in the 2026 format, it merits proportionate study time, while Physics and Chemistry remain jointly worth the other half.

Use a cycle of content review, topic-level questions, error analysis and timed full-length practice. For every mock, review incorrect answers, guessed answers and unanswered questions separately; this directly reflects the official +4/−1/0 scoring framework.

Use only official notices for operational rules such as the admit card, centre instructions, permitted items, dress code, OMR challenge process and answer-key challenge windows. Such rules can change between cycles.
bullets: Create a syllabus checklist and mark each unit as unstarted, learning, practising or revision-ready.
Practise filling answers carefully in OMR-style conditions.
Plan exam-day logistics from the official admit card rather than map pins or unofficial social-media messages.

sections.heading: Results, counselling and academic pathways
paragraphs: After the exam, NTA publishes the score card and All India Rank. The bulletin provides for display of scanned OMR responses and provisional answer keys, with time-limited paid challenge mechanisms; answer sheets are not ordinarily rechecked or re-evaluated after that process.

For the 2026 admission framework, NEET feeds MBBS, BDS, BAMS, BUMS, BSMS and BHMS admissions. MCC/DGHS conducts counselling for specified 15% All India Quota and central-institution pathways, while state/UT counselling authorities manage seats under their control. AACCC is the All India Quota counselling authority for BAMS, BUMS, BSMS and BHMS.

NEET data may also be used under specific rules for other pathways. The 2026 bulletin says it may be used for B.Sc. (Hons.) Nursing under the relevant eligibility rules and for B.V.Sc. & A.H. under the Veterinary Council of India’s 15% quota in recognised veterinary colleges. The VCI’s 2025-26 bulletin likewise used qualified NEET-UG merit for that 15% All India quota. For B.Pharm, BPT and other programmes, confirm the individual institution’s current admission notification rather than assuming a nationwide NEET requirement.

Indian citizens and OCI applicants planning an MBBS-equivalent programme abroad should note NMC’s stated NEET qualification requirement for primary medical education outside India, alongside all foreign-medical-graduate and destination-country requirements. A NEET score alone does not establish that a foreign degree will meet later Indian registration or licensing requirements.
bullets: A qualifying percentile is not a guaranteed seat: admission depends on rank, choices, category, quota, seat availability, verification and the applicable counselling rules.
Register separately with the appropriate counselling authority after results; taking NEET does not automatically enter a candidate into counselling.
For foreign MBBS plans, obtain written, current confirmation from NMC and the proposed foreign institution before paying fees or enrolling.

useful_links.label: NMC NEET-UG page and syllabus resources

title: NEST
description: NEST — ug entrance exam (science), conducted by NISER / UM-DAE CEBS.

quick_facts.label: What NEST is for
quick_facts.value: NEST (National Entrance Screening Test) is the compulsory computer-based entrance test for the five-year Integrated MSc programmes at NISER Bhubaneswar and UM-DAE CEBS Mumbai.

quick_facts.label: 2026 eligibility baseline
quick_facts.value: For 2026 admission, applicants needed at least three of Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics and Physics in Classes XI–XII; Class XII passed in 2024 or 2025, or appearing in 2026; and 60% aggregate (55% for SC/ST/Divyangjan), as well as a NEST merit rank. There was no age limit.

quick_facts.label: 2026 exam structure
quick_facts.value: NEST 2026 was a three-hour CBT with four 60-mark subject sections—Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics and Physics—each containing 20 single-correct MCQs. Marking was +3 for correct, −1 for incorrect and 0 for unattempted.

quick_facts.label: Merit method
quick_facts.value: A candidate had to clear the section-wise minimum admissible score (SMAS) in at least three sections; when all four qualified, the total used the best three section scores. A category-specific minimum admissible percentile (MAP) was also required for a merit rank.

quick_facts.label: 2026 cycle status
quick_facts.value: The official 2026 portal lists the examination on June 6, 2026 and result announcement on June 24, 2026; its application process is closed. Dates, fees, intake and rules are cycle-specific and should be rechecked for a later NEST cycle.

sections.heading: Purpose and programmes accessed through NEST
paragraphs: NEST is the common admission examination for the five-year Integrated MSc programmes at NISER, Bhubaneswar, and UM-DAE CEBS, Mumbai. The official 2026 brochure describes the programmes as research-oriented basic-science education in Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics and Physics, with residential study, semester-and-credit curriculum, and early research exposure.

NISER is an off-campus centre of the Department of Atomic Energy’s Homi Bhabha National Institute, while UM-DAE CEBS was established jointly by the Department of Atomic Energy and the University of Mumbai; the programme affiliations differ accordingly. NEST is therefore an undergraduate-entry route aimed principally at research-oriented education in the basic sciences rather than a general engineering or medical entrance exam.
bullets: For the 2026–31 intake, the brochure listed 202 seats at NISER and 59 at UM-DAE CEBS, including supernumerary seats for eligible candidates from Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. Intake is expressly proposed/cycle-specific and may change in subsequent years.

The 2026 brochure states that admitted students were eligible for a Department of Atomic Energy DISHA annual scholarship of ₹60,000 plus a ₹20,000 annual summer-internship grant. This financial support is dated 2026 information and applicants should verify the policy for their admission year.

sections.heading: Eligibility for the 2026 admission cycle
paragraphs: The published rules required a student to have studied at least three of the four basic-science subjects—Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics and Physics—in both Classes XI and XII. Candidates had to have passed Class XII from a recognised board in India in 2024 or 2025, or be appearing in 2026; candidates taking Class XII in 2026 had to meet the conditions when admitted.

The aggregate Class XII threshold was 60% or an equivalent grade for the unreserved category and 55% for SC, ST and Divyangjan candidates. The aggregate certificate had to be issued by a single board; where only letter grades were issued, the brochure required board documentation of their percentage equivalence. Admission also depended on securing a NEST 2026 merit-list rank and later original-document verification.
bullets: No upper age limit applied in the 2026 rules, provided the other admission conditions were met.

Reservation and certificate requirements followed Government of India rules; for example, OBC reservation required OBC-NCL status in the Central List, and category documentation was checked at admission.
These are 2026-cycle conditions, not a guarantee of eligibility in a future cycle.

sections.heading: Exam format and ranking
paragraphs: NEST 2026 was held as a computer-based test in one three-hour session. It had four subject sections—Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics and Physics—with 20 four-option, single-correct MCQs per section. Each section carried 60 marks, making 240 marks available across all four sections; the paper was offered in Hindi and English, with English prevailing if there was a discrepancy.

Candidates could attempt all four sections, but had to attempt at least three to enter the scoring process. For merit, they needed scores at or above the subject-specific SMAS in at least three sections and also had to meet the announced MAP. When a candidate qualified in all four subjects, the total was calculated from the best three eligible section scores; final rank was based on percentile.
bullets: Marking in 2026: +3 correct, −1 incorrect, 0 unattempted.
NEST 2026 used a single-correct MCQ format; it is not safe to assume that question types or ranking mechanics will remain identical in a future brochure.
The official site maintains a question archive and, for the 2026 cycle, offered a CBT mock test for registered applicants.

sections.heading: How the 2026 application worked
paragraphs: The 2026 application was online only through the official NEST website. Applicants first registered with core personal and school details, then used the issued login credentials to complete the form, upload the required photograph and signature, select test-city preferences, and pay online. The official instructions stated that candidates did not need to send documents to the NEST office during the application process.

As dated 2026 context, the portal lists applications opening January 5, 2026 and closing April 8, 2026 after an extension; the examination took place June 6 and results were announced June 24. The portal now states that the application process is closed. Future applicants should use the next cycle’s official notice rather than reuse these deadlines.
bullets: The 2026 application fee was ₹1,400 for male/other UR and OBC applicants, and ₹700 for female applicants of any category and for UR-EWS, SC, ST and Divyangjan applicants. These fees are historical, cycle-specific context.
The official portal describes three phases: registration, logged-in form completion/submission, and helpdesk escalation for technical problems.
The 2026 brochure required a recent JPG/JPEG photograph and signature, each no larger than 80 KB; future upload specifications may differ.

sections.heading: Preparation approach grounded in the official syllabus
paragraphs: Start with the official syllabus rather than assuming that another science entrance syllabus is identical. For NEST 2026, the exam authority said the syllabus primarily followed the CBSE 2025–26 curriculum and NCERT Classes XI–XII books in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Biology; some science knowledge up to Class X could also be needed.

A practical approach is to build subject coverage from the detailed official syllabus, then practise under the CBT constraints using the official mock test when available and the official previous-question archive. Since merit required qualifying in at least three subject sections, preparation should include at least three sciences and should not rely only on a single preferred subject.
bullets: Practise the 2026-style single-correct MCQ decision rule carefully because an incorrect response incurred −1 while an unattempted question incurred no deduction.
Use timed mixed-subject practice: the 2026 test allotted three hours for all four sections, and each section carried equal marks.
For a future attempt, confirm the then-current syllabus, mock-test availability, language rules, and pattern in that year’s official brochure.

sections.heading: What follows a NEST merit rank
paragraphs: A NEST merit rank does not itself complete admission: the 2026 rules made admission subject to the institutes’ merit-based process, satisfaction of academic eligibility, reservation rules where applicable, and verification of original documents at counselling/admission. The NEST portal directs candidates to the respective NISER and UM-DAE CEBS sites for institute merit-list and admission information.

The official brochure characterises the Integrated MSc pathway as research-focused and says that many graduates proceed to doctoral research in India or abroad, including at NISER or CEBS, and enter academia or industry primarily in research roles. That describes an institutional outcome profile, not a guaranteed job, placement, doctoral admission or salary result for an individual student.
bullets: For the 2026 cycle, only candidates who met both SMAS and MAP requirements received a merit rank.
The two institutes run the five-year Integrated MSc programmes in the four basic-science disciplines listed in the brochure.
No salary or placement figure is stated here because outcomes vary materially by discipline, further study, employer and year.

title: NID DAT
description: NID DAT — ug entrance exam (design), conducted by NID. also M.Des.

quick_facts.label: Conducting institution
quick_facts.value: NID DAT is the National Institute of Design’s Design Aptitude Test admission process. NID Ahmedabad is an autonomous Institute of National Importance under DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Government of India.

quick_facts.label: Programmes reached through DAT
quick_facts.value: For the 2026–27 cycle, DAT was used for B.Des admission at NID Ahmedabad, Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh and Assam, and for M.Des admission at NID Ahmedabad, Bengaluru and Gandhinagar.

quick_facts.label: Selection structure
quick_facts.value: The process has two stages: DAT Prelims followed by DAT Mains. Prelims is used to shortlist candidates; it does not itself confer admission.

quick_facts.label: Latest published-cycle dates
quick_facts.value: In the published 2026–27 handbooks, the online-application deadline was 1 December 2025 at 11:59 pm IST and DAT Prelims was scheduled for 21 December 2025. These dates are cycle-specific and should not be treated as dates for a future admission cycle.

quick_facts.label: Official application channel
quick_facts.value: NID states that applications are invited online through its official admissions portal; candidates should rely on the current handbook and notices on that portal for changes.

sections.heading: What NID DAT is for
paragraphs: NID DAT is the entrance and selection process for designated undergraduate and postgraduate design programmes at National Institute of Design campuses. NID describes the test objective as assessing candidates’ knowledge, skills and behavioural abilities for design education. Qualifying or appearing in a stage does not create an automatic right to admission; final admission depends on the applicable merit list, seat availability, eligibility verification and the rules of that admission cycle.

For B.Des, the 2026–27 handbook covered a four-year programme across NID Ahmedabad and four other NIDs. For M.Des, it covered NID Ahmedabad, Bengaluru and Gandhinagar; the handbook describes that programme as a two-and-a-half-year full-time degree. Programme locations, disciplines, capacities and rules can change by cycle, so applicants should use the handbook released for their own year.
bullets: Use the B.Des route after senior secondary education (10+2 or an accepted equivalent).
Use the M.Des route after a qualifying bachelor’s degree or equivalent, subject to the cycle’s detailed eligibility rules.
Treat DAT as an admission examination, not as a standalone degree or professional credential.

sections.heading: Eligibility: B.Des and M.Des differ
paragraphs: For the 2026–27 B.Des cycle, candidates needed to meet both age and educational requirements. The educational requirement was passing, or appearing in 2025–26 for, a recognised higher-secondary (10+2) examination in any stream; NID listed examples including CBSE, IB and ICSE/equivalent. The cycle’s age cut-offs differed by category—for example, General and General-EWS Indian applicants had to be born on or after 1 July 2005. These are historical, cycle-specific thresholds rather than a prediction of future cut-offs.

For the 2026–27 M.Des cycle, applicants needed a bachelor’s degree or equivalent in any discipline from an eligible Indian institution, or an appropriately recognised equivalent qualification. Final-year candidates could apply provisionally subject to passing and submitting their result by the stipulated date. The published age cut-off for General and General-EWS Indian applicants was birth on or after 1 July 1994; reserved-category and PwD cut-offs differed. International qualifications required the specified equivalence documentation.
bullets: B.Des: 10+2 in any stream is the central academic route in the cited 2026–27 rules.
M.Des: a bachelor’s degree or equivalent in any discipline is the baseline academic route in the cited 2026–27 rules.
Always check nationality, category, age, equivalence, final-result and document requirements in the current official handbook before applying.

sections.heading: Exam format and merit calculation
paragraphs: Both B.Des and M.Des use DAT Prelims and DAT Mains. In the 2026–27 rules, Prelims was a common paper-and-pencil/pen examination held across test centres, with text and visual questions, in English. Its score was used for shortlisting to Mains and was not carried into the final Mains-stage calculation.

The Mains components differed by programme in 2026–27. B.Des Mains comprised a Studio Sensitivity Test and an In-Person Sensitivity Test; final B.Des marks were weighted 60% and 40% respectively. M.Des Mains comprised a Studio Test and Interviews, weighted 40% and 60% respectively. NID reserves the right to change the schedule, mode or structure in exceptional circumstances, so applicants should confirm the current-cycle admit-card instructions and handbook.
bullets: B.Des DAT Prelims: common paper-and-pencil/pen test; Prelims is only a shortlist stage.
B.Des DAT Mains: Studio Sensitivity Test plus In-Person Sensitivity Test.
M.Des DAT Prelims: one common paper for all faculty streams; applicants select a faculty stream and may apply to up to two disciplines within that stream under the cited rules.
M.Des DAT Mains: Studio Test plus Interviews.

sections.heading: How to apply through the official portal
paragraphs: NID’s published process begins at the official admissions portal. Applicants first read the applicable handbook and register online by selecting the programme, nationality and category. They then complete personal and educational details, upload the required documents, pay the application fee online and retain the completed application form. M.Des applicants also provide work-experience information where requested by the portal.

Use an active personal email address and mobile number, because NID uses these for OTP validation, login credentials, admit-card and admissions communications. The published handbooks make applicants responsible for the accuracy of their submitted information; incorrect information or invalid supporting documents can lead to cancellation of candidature or admission. The application portal may offer a limited edit window, but key registration details and rules on editable fields are cycle-specific.
bullets: Start only from NID’s official admissions portal, not from a coaching, intermediary or look-alike website.
Upload the photo, signature and category/PwD documents that apply to your application; check the current handbook for file and certificate requirements.
Pay and complete the final submission step, then save or print the completed form.
Download DAT admit cards from the portal when announced; NID’s handbooks say separate physical admit cards are not issued.

sections.heading: Preparation using official materials
paragraphs: Begin with the current B.Des or M.Des admissions handbook, because it defines the applicable eligibility rules, test stages, admissions workflow and any cycle-specific changes. NID also publishes DAT Prelims sample test papers for B.Des and M.Des on its admissions portal. These are the most reliable starting point for understanding the official style of practice material, although they are not a guarantee that future questions will match past samples.

For preparation, practise working with both written and visual prompts, communicate ideas clearly within time limits, and develop a disciplined approach to studio-style problem solving and in-person discussion. For M.Des, align preparation with the selected faculty stream and discipline preferences. NID explicitly says it does not encourage coaching for the admission test and has not authorised or franchised anyone to conduct such classes.
bullets: Download and attempt the official DAT Prelims sample paper relevant to your programme.
Review your response for clarity of observation, visual communication, reasoning and idea development—not only for a final answer.
For M.Des, decide the faculty stream and up to two discipline preferences carefully, because the cited rules make those applications discipline-specific and non-transferable.
Do not rely on claims that a private coaching provider is NID-authorised.

sections.heading: What a successful DAT result can lead to
paragraphs: A successful final result can lead to a seat offer in the programme and campus for which the candidate is eligible and ranked, subject to the candidate’s submitted preferences, category rules, document verification and seat availability. It does not guarantee a particular specialisation unless the applicable programme structure and allocation process say so.

The immediate academic outcomes are a B.Des or M.Des admission. At NID Ahmedabad, the official B.Des page describes a four-year degree with a Foundation Programme and specialisations across communication, industrial, textile/apparel/lifestyle and ceramic-and-glass design areas. The 2026–27 M.Des handbook lists faculty streams including Industrial Design, Communication Design, Textile/Apparel/Lifestyle Accessory Design, IT Integrated Design and Interdisciplinary Design Studies. Specific disciplines, seats and allotment arrangements are variable by campus and cycle.
bullets: B.Des outcome: entry to a full-time undergraduate design degree, subject to final admissions conditions.
M.Des outcome: entry to a full-time postgraduate design degree, subject to final admissions conditions.
A rank or test appearance alone is not an offer of admission; follow the official result, preference, document-upload and seat-allotment instructions for the relevant cycle.

title: NIFT Entrance Exam
description: NIFT Entrance Exam — ug entrance exam (design), conducted by NIFT / NTA.

quick_facts.label: Conducting arrangement
quick_facts.value: For NIFTEE 2026, the National Testing Agency (NTA) handled online registration, examination conduct, answer-key challenges and results; NIFT handled the admission framework and later-stage processes.

quick_facts.label: Primary UG routes
quick_facts.value: The regular undergraduate entrance routes covered are B.Des and B.F.Tech (Apparel Production). B.Des covers NIFT design specialisations; B.F.Tech is the technology/apparel-production route.

quick_facts.label: UG age rule for 2026
quick_facts.value: For 2026 admission, applicants to B.Des and B.F.Tech had to be under 24 years old on 1 August 2026. SC, ST and PwD candidates received a five-year upper-age relaxation.

quick_facts.label: 2026 written-test structure
quick_facts.value: B.Des used GAT and CAT, followed for shortlisted candidates by a Situation Test. B.F.Tech used GAT only. GAT was computer-based and CAT was pen-and-paper based.

quick_facts.label: 2026 B.Des merit weights
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, B.Des final merit used GAT (30%), CAT (50%) and the Situation Test (20%). B.F.Tech merit used GAT Section A (30%) and Section B (70%). These weights can change in a future admissions cycle.

quick_facts.label: 2026 application timing
quick_facts.value: The regular 2026 application window opened on 8 December 2025, closed on 6 January 2026 at the applicable fee, and allowed late-fee registration from 7 to 10 January 2026. These dates are historical and should not be used for a future cycle.

sections.heading: What the NIFT Entrance Exam is for
paragraphs: The NIFT Entrance Examination (NIFTEE) is the selection route for regular admission to NIFT’s undergraduate B.Des and B.F.Tech programmes. For the 2026 cycle, the NIFT admissions guidelines list B.Des specialisations in Accessory Design, Fashion Communication, Fashion Design, Fashion Interiors, Knitwear Design, Leather Design and Textile Design, plus B.F.Tech in Apparel Production.

The exam’s practical scope is narrower than the broader set of design and fashion qualifications sometimes associated with it. The official NIFT material supports NIFTEE as an admission route to the NIFT programmes listed above; it should not automatically be assumed to be an entrance examination for B.F.A., B.Sc., B.Voc or diploma programmes at other institutions.
bullets: For B.Des, the selection process measures both general aptitude and creative/design ability, then assesses shortlisted candidates through a hands-on Situation Test.
For B.F.Tech, selection is based on the General Ability Test (GAT), with the programme intended for the apparel-production technology pathway.

sections.heading: Eligibility for the regular UG routes
paragraphs: For B.Des in 2026, a candidate could qualify through recognised 10+2/senior-secondary study, the National Open School senior-secondary examination with at least five subjects, an AICTE or State Board-recognised three- or four-year diploma after Class 10, or specified equivalent international qualifications. A candidate appearing in the qualifying examination could apply provisionally, but had to meet the stated eligibility conditions by admission/seat allocation.

For B.F.Tech in 2026, the corresponding school-level routes required Mathematics. A recognised three- or four-year engineering diploma after Class 10 was also an accepted route. The 2026 guideline sets the bachelor-programme age ceiling at under 24 on 1 August 2026, with a five-year relaxation for SC, ST and PwD categories.
bullets: B.Des: Mathematics is not stated as a general compulsory subject in the 2026 eligibility list.
B.F.Tech: Mathematics is required for the senior-secondary/equivalent routes.
Always check the next cycle’s prospectus and admission guidelines: equivalence, documentation, category rules and age cut-offs are cycle-specific.

sections.heading: Exam format and how merit is made
paragraphs: For B.Des, Stage 1 comprises GAT and CAT. GAT is a computer-based test and CAT is a pen-and-paper test; candidates shortlisted from Stage 1 take NIFT’s Situation Test. The 2026 information bulletin describes CAT as assessing intuitive ability, observation, concept development, design ability, and creative use of colour and illustration.

For B.F.Tech, admission is based on GAT without CAT, a Situation Test or interview in the regular UG process. In the 2026 structure, GAT for B.F.Tech had Section A and Section B, and merit weights were 30% and 70% respectively. The bulletin cautions that the number and difficulty of questions may vary by course and year.
bullets: B.Des 2026: GAT 120 minutes; CAT 180 minutes; the stated structure was 100 GAT questions plus three CAT questions/tasks.
B.F.Tech 2026: GAT Section A 120 minutes and 100 questions; Section B 60 minutes and 50 questions.
The written papers were bilingual in Hindi and English; where versions differed, the English version governed.
For objective questions in the 2026 GAT framework, the stated marking was +1 for a correct response and −0.25 for an incorrect response; unattempted questions received zero.

sections.heading: How to apply and track admission
paragraphs: NIFTEE applications are submitted online through the NTA portal announced by NIFT/NTA. The 2026 process required candidates to register with their own email address and mobile number, complete programme and personal details, upload the prescribed images/documents, pay online, and retain the generated confirmation page and payment proof. NTA stated that applications submitted in another mode would not be accepted.

For the historical 2026 cycle, initial registration ran from 8 December 2025 to 6 January 2026, with a late-fee period through 10 January and an online correction window from 12 to 14 January. The written entrance exam was scheduled for 8 February 2026. NIFT explicitly described calendar dates marked with an asterisk as tentative and directed candidates to its website for final notices; a future applicant should use the current cycle’s official bulletin, not these dates.

After the exam, candidates should follow official notices for results, B.Des Stage 2/Situation Test, final merit and e-counselling or seat allocation. NIFT’s admissions page publishes the current cycle’s notices, including final-result and counselling updates.
bullets: Use an email address and mobile number controlled by the applicant; official communication is sent there.
Upload requirements for 2026 included a photograph, signature and, where applicable, PwD/UDID documentation; check the current bulletin for file formats and sizes.
The 2026 form asked candidates to select four exam-city preferences. Centre allocation remained subject to availability and administration.
Keep the confirmation page and fee-payment proof; do not send a hard copy to NTA unless a current official notice specifically requires it.

sections.heading: Preparation strategy aligned to the official tests
paragraphs: Prepare to the route you are actually applying for. A B.Des candidate needs both aptitude-test preparation and a timed creative-practice routine because CAT and the Situation Test materially affect final merit. A B.F.Tech candidate should concentrate on GAT, especially its quantitative, analytical, logical-reasoning, English-comprehension and general-knowledge dimensions.

For B.Des CAT, practise visual observation, translating a prompt into a coherent concept, drawing and illustration, and inventive use of colour under the allotted time. For the Situation Test, practise quickly constructing a clear three-dimensional model from limited supplied materials and writing a concise explanation of the concept. Official NIFT materials state that personal identification details or coaching-centre marks on CAT work can lead to disqualification.

Use NIFT’s official sample-question-paper resource alongside the current information bulletin and admission guidelines. Treat commercial mock-test patterns or coaching claims as supplementary only, because the bulletin says question counts and difficulty can vary from year to year.
bullets: B.Des: time GAT and CAT practice separately, then review concept clarity, proportion, composition and written explanation.
B.F.Tech: build speed and accuracy for GAT; use the official negative-marking rule applicable to the current cycle when planning attempt strategy.
Read the current cycle’s syllabus, instructions, permitted materials and admit-card directions before test day rather than relying on past-year social-media advice.

sections.heading: What happens after the exam
paragraphs: For regular B.Des applicants, the final rank is based on the combined weighted scores from GAT, CAT and the Situation Test. For regular B.F.Tech applicants, the final merit is based on GAT. Candidates who obtain the relevant rank then participate in NIFT’s seat-allocation process; rank alone is not the same as a confirmed campus or programme seat.

For 2026, NIFT listed regular B.Des seats across its design specialisations and B.F.Tech seats in Apparel Production, while noting that it could increase or decrease the courses or seats offered. Therefore, programme availability, campus preferences, category eligibility, rank and the live seat-allocation rules all matter to the eventual outcome. NIFT’s admissions page should be treated as the authoritative tracker for notices, results and counselling.
bullets: B.Des outcomes: Common Merit Rank and participation in admission/seat allocation after all required assessment stages.
B.F.Tech outcomes: Common Merit Rank based on GAT and participation in admission/seat allocation.
A prior-year cut-off is context, not a guarantee: NIFT publishes historical cut-off merit-rank resources, but actual availability and competition vary by year.

useful_links.label: NIFT admissions hub: current notices, prospectus, guidelines, seat matrix and sample papers

title: NIMCET (NIT MCA Common Entrance Test)
description: A national-level entrance test for admission to Master of Computer Applications (MCA) programs offered by National Institutes of Technology (NITs).

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: NIMCET is the national-level common entrance test used for MCA admission at participating NITs and IIITs; for the 2026–27 cycle, admission at 11 NITs and 2 IIITs is based on NIMCET-2026 rank.

quick_facts.label: 2026 eligibility
quick_facts.value: Indian nationals need either a minimum three-year undergraduate degree with Mathematics or Statistics as a subject, or a B.E./B.Tech.; the required aggregate is 60% or 6.5/10 CGPA, reduced to 55% or 6.0/10 for SC/ST/PwD candidates.

quick_facts.label: Test format (2026)
quick_facts.value: The computer-based test is a single, two-hour paper with 120 English-language MCQs: Mathematics (50), Analytical Ability and Logical Reasoning (40), Computer Awareness (20), and General English (10).

quick_facts.label: Scoring (2026)
quick_facts.value: The paper carries 1,000 weighted marks. Each wrong answer attracts a 25% negative mark for that question, while unanswered questions have no deduction.

quick_facts.label: 2026 application-fee context
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 test, the non-refundable application processing fee was ₹2,500 for OPEN/OPEN-EWS/OBC candidates and ₹1,250 for SC/ST and PwD candidates. Fees and future-cycle dates can change, so applicants should use the current official brochure.

sections.heading: Purpose and participating institutions
paragraphs: NIMCET is the common national entrance route for MCA programmes at the participating institutes. In the 2026–27 admission cycle, the official portal identifies 11 NITs—Agartala, Allahabad, Bhopal, Delhi, Jamshedpur, Kurukshetra, Meghalaya, Patna, Raipur, Tiruchirappalli and Warangal—and IIIT Bhopal and IIIT Vadodara. Admission is determined through the NIMCET rank and the candidate’s online institute choices, rather than through a separate state quota.
bullets: The 2026 brochure states that there is no separate state-wise quota.
Reservation for SC, ST, OBC, EWS and PwD is governed by Government of India rules.
The MCA curricula are described by the coordinating authority as being designed with IT-sector needs in mind; this describes programme intent, not a guarantee of placement or salary.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: For NIMCET 2026, eligibility to sit the test required Indian nationality and either: (1) a minimum three-year undergraduate programme in which Mathematics or Statistics was a subject, or (2) a B.E./B.Tech. from a recognised university or institution. Candidates needed at least 60% aggregate marks or 6.5 CGPA on a 10-point scale; the threshold was 55% or 6.0 CGPA for SC/ST/PwD candidates.
bullets: Candidates appearing in their qualifying undergraduate examination could apply, but had to submit proof of meeting the requirements by September 30, 2026 for that cycle.
A minimum three-year bachelor’s programme completed through an open university could qualify when the programme had the approvals specified in the brochure.
Eligibility to take the test does not itself secure MCA admission: only candidates who receive a NIMCET rank are eligible for admission in the participating institutes.

sections.heading: Exam pattern and ranking
paragraphs: In the 2026 cycle, NIMCET was a computer-based, single-paper examination lasting two hours. The sections were time-locked: Mathematics had 50 questions in 70 minutes; Analytical Ability and Logical Reasoning had 40 questions in 30 minutes; and Computer Awareness plus General English had 20 and 10 questions respectively in the final 20 minutes. Candidates could not move back to a prior section after its time expired.
bullets: Mathematics: 12 marks for a correct answer and 3 marks deducted for a wrong answer.
Analytical Ability and Logical Reasoning, and Computer Awareness: 6 marks for a correct answer and 1.5 marks deducted for a wrong answer.
General English: 4 marks for a correct answer and 1 mark deducted for a wrong answer.

A candidate with zero or negative marks in Mathematics or in the total score is disqualified from ranking. Rankings use total weighted marks; ties are first resolved using Mathematics marks, then Analytical Ability and Logical Reasoning, then Computer Awareness, followed by age and computerised random sampling if necessary.

sections.heading: Application and counselling process
paragraphs: The 2026 process was online. Applicants registered with a personal email address and mobile number, completed personal and academic details, selected three test-centre preferences, uploaded required documents, paid the application-processing fee, and downloaded the final submitted application form carrying its registration number. The 2026 application window ran from March 3, 2026 to May 1, 2026 at 5:00 PM IST, so those dates are historical rather than a timetable for a future cycle.
bullets: For 2026, required uploads included a photograph, signature, academic marksheets/grade cards and certificates, identity proof, and applicable category certificates.
After qualifying, candidates applied separately for online counselling, filled and locked institute choices, and could be allotted a seat based on NIMCET rank, preferences and seat availability.
For the 2026 counselling process, the brochure specified a ₹1,000 counselling registration fee and a ₹10,000 seat-acceptance fee after allotment. These are cycle-specific amounts and may be revised.
Candidates should rely on the official NIMCET portal and current information brochure for future deadlines, document rules, fees, test centres and counselling instructions.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: A practical preparation plan should mirror the official blueprint: devote the largest share of study and timed practice to Mathematics because it has 50 questions, the longest section, the largest marks allocation, and priority in the rank tie-break rules. This is a preparation recommendation inferred from the official 2026 pattern, not an official prescribed study plan.
bullets: Build Mathematics coverage around set theory and logic, probability and statistics, algebra, coordinate geometry, calculus and trigonometry.
Practise timed reasoning sets covering verbal and non-verbal reasoning, puzzles, seating arrangements, syllogisms, data interpretation, numerical reasoning and data sufficiency.

Review computer fundamentals, data representation, hardware, operating systems, internet/email and basic online security; also practise reading comprehension, vocabulary, grammar and technical-expression questions.

Use full-length computer-based mocks with the official 70/30/20-minute section timing. Include accuracy review because wrong answers carry 25% negative marking and unanswered questions do not attract a deduction.

sections.heading: What a NIMCET result enables
paragraphs: A qualifying NIMCET result produces a rank, which enables the candidate to participate in the MCA counselling and choice-filling process for the participating institutes. Final allotment depends on the NIMCET rank, the institutes selected by the candidate and seat availability; it is not automatic merely because a candidate took the test.
bullets: The immediate education outcome is admission consideration for a participating MCA programme.

The 2026 brochure describes MCA graduates as having potential for IT-sector jobs, while the official site says the participating MCA curricula are designed with the needs of IT firms in India and abroad in view. Specific job outcomes, employers and compensation vary by institute, skills, experience and labour-market conditions.

Programme fees vary materially by institute and scheme. The 2026 brochure directs candidates to each institute’s official website for complete fee details, particularly where listed figures are tuition-only or subject to revision.

title: NIPER JEE
description: NIPER JEE — pg entrance exam (medical), conducted by NIPER.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: NIPER JEE is the National Institutes of Pharmaceutical Education and Research joint entrance examination used for admissions to postgraduate programmes across the participating NIPERs; the 2026 portal lists Ahmedabad, Guwahati, Hajipur, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mohali and Raebareli.

quick_facts.label: 2026 organising institute
quick_facts.value: NIPER Mohali (S.A.S. Nagar, Punjab) is the organising institute for NIPER JEE 2026.

quick_facts.label: Programmes reached through the master's route
quick_facts.value: The 2026 admission process covers M.S. (Pharm.), M.Pharm., M.Tech. and MBA (Pharm.) programmes; offerings, disciplines and seats vary by NIPER and the annual seat matrix.

quick_facts.label: 2026 examination status
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 master's cycle, the official schedule listed the computer-based test (CBT) on June 13, 2026. The portal subsequently published counselling and MBA merit-list/GD-PI notices in June and July 2026.

quick_facts.label: Core eligibility benchmark
quick_facts.value: NIPER's published master’s regulations specify programme-specific qualifying degrees, a minimum 60% aggregate or 6.75/10 CGPA, and generally require GPAT/GATE/NET qualification, subject to stated exceptions and relaxations. Applicants must confirm the current annual brochure for the programme they select.

sections.heading: Purpose and place in the pharmacy education pathway
paragraphs: NIPER JEE is a national postgraduate admissions route for the participating National Institutes of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPERs). It is principally a pharmaceutical-sciences and pharmaceutical-management entrance process—not a general undergraduate engineering JEE or a clinical medical-licensure examination.

For a B.Pharm graduate, it can be a route into M.Pharm, M.S. (Pharm.), M.Tech. (Pharm.) or MBA (Pharm.) study, provided the candidate meets the specific degree eligibility for the selected discipline. The available disciplines and seats are not identical at every NIPER, so the annual brochure and seat matrix—not the exam name alone—determine the actual choices in a cycle.
bullets: The 2026 portal identifies seven participating NIPERs: Ahmedabad, Guwahati, Hajipur, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mohali and Raebareli.
NIPER Hyderabad’s admissions page illustrates the type of postgraduate offerings accessible through the process, including M.S. (Pharm.), M.Tech. (Pharm.) and MBA (Pharm.) programmes.

sections.heading: Eligibility: check the programme, not only the exam
paragraphs: Eligibility is discipline-specific. The current NIPER master’s ordinance lists B.Pharm as an eligible qualification for several pathways, including M.Pharm specialisations and M.S. (Pharm.) Pharmaceutics; other disciplines also accept defined science, medicine, veterinary-science or engineering qualifications. For example, M.Tech. (Pharm.) Pharmaceutical Technology (Process Chemistry) can accept B.Pharm, M.Sc. Organic Chemistry or B.Tech. Chemical Engineering/equivalent, while MBA (Pharm.) can accept B.Pharm, specified chemical-engineering qualifications, or M.Sc. Chemical/Life Sciences.

The published general academic threshold is 60% aggregate marks or a 6.75/10 CGPA (or equivalent) in the qualifying degree. Published NIPER guidance gives lower thresholds for SC/ST candidates (55% or 6.25/10) and PwBD candidates (50% or 5.75/10). These rules should be rechecked against the current-cycle brochure because annual admission notices control the operative requirements.

NIPER’s published guidance also states that a valid GPAT, GATE or NET score is generally essential, with listed exceptions including certain medical/veterinary degree holders, foreign nationals and specified sponsored/NRI cases. Do not assume that a B.Pharm degree alone establishes eligibility for every programme or category.
bullets: Match your qualifying degree to the exact discipline before registering.
Keep degree marks/CGPA records and, where applicable, GPAT/GATE/NET documentation ready for counselling verification.
Treat eligibility as provisional until documentary verification during the admission process.

sections.heading: Examination and selection format
paragraphs: For the 2026 master’s cycle, NIPER scheduled NIPER JEE as a computer-based test (CBT) on June 13, 2026. The 2026 portal shows that candidates for M.S. (Pharm.), M.Pharm. and M.Tech. proceeded through merit-list and online-counselling steps, while MBA (Pharm.) selection additionally involved group discussion and personal interview (GD/PI) notices and merit lists based on CBT plus GD/PI scores.

The detailed paper pattern should always be taken from the cycle-specific master’s brochure. As a useful historical planning reference rather than a promise for a future cycle, the official 2025 master’s brochure described application procedure, test venues and an “About the Entrance Test” section; NIPER may revise the structure, syllabus, centres, scoring or selection stages in a later notification.
bullets: 2026 master’s CBT date: June 13, 2026.
MBA (Pharm.) has an additional selection component beyond the CBT in the 2026 process: GD/PI.
Counselling and seat allocation are separate stages after the examination/shortlisting process.

sections.heading: Application process and 2026 timing context
paragraphs: Use the official NIPER JEE portal for registration, the revised information brochure, the schedule, notices, document formats and counselling instructions. For the 2026 master’s cycle, online applications opened on April 16, 2026 and the extended closing date shown on the official schedule was May 23, 2026 at 11:50 PM IST; those dates are historical context for the 2026 cycle, not a prediction of the next cycle’s dates.

After CBT results, the 2026 portal published merit and counselling-related notices. Candidates seeking M.S. (Pharm.), M.Pharm. or M.Tech. were directed to online counselling and web-option registration, whereas MBA (Pharm.) candidates were notified separately for GD/PI and MBA merit lists. Follow only the notices for the programme category for which you applied.

Before paying or submitting an application in a future cycle, verify the selected programme group, eligibility, category certificates, payment instructions and document-upload rules in that cycle’s revised brochure. The 2025 official brochure, for example, required applicants to choose the appropriate programme group and warned that a wrong selection could require a fresh application and a non-refundable fee; fees and procedures are variable by year.
bullets: Monitor the official portal for revised dates and notices rather than relying on third-party calendars.
Download the admit card/hall ticket only when the official portal opens that step.
For counselling, submit the required certificates and programme choices by the published deadline; missed uploads or options can affect consideration.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Start with the programme-specific eligibility and the current information brochure, then build a preparation plan around the relevant qualifying-degree curriculum. This matters because NIPER’s master’s pathways span pharmacy, chemical sciences, biological sciences, medical-device and management-oriented options; a B.Pharm candidate should not assume that every programme tests or admits on exactly the same basis.

Use only official current-cycle material to finalise the test plan. The 2026 portal made a master’s mock test available, and its revised brochure and notices are the authoritative place to confirm the current CBT instructions, programme grouping and any updates before the examination.

For MBA (Pharm.) applicants, prepare separately for the post-CBT selection stage as well: the 2026 process included group discussion and personal interview, so preparation should include communicating pharmaceutical-management interests and explaining one’s academic background in addition to CBT preparation.
bullets: Read the current brochure before choosing subjects, centres or programme groups.
Revise foundational B.Pharm topics most relevant to the target discipline, then practise within the official CBT instructions.
Use the official mock test to check computer-based-test readiness.
If applying to MBA (Pharm.), plan for GD/PI after the CBT rather than treating the written test as the only stage.

sections.heading: Academic outcomes after admission
paragraphs: A successful NIPER JEE application can lead to postgraduate study in the degree families named in the annual admission process: M.S. (Pharm.), M.Pharm., M.Tech. and MBA (Pharm.). The NIPER master’s ordinance describes these master’s programmes as four-semester programmes, while the specialisations and participating campuses differ by discipline and annual availability.

At NIPER Hyderabad, for example, published academic information lists two-year M.S. (Pharm.), M.Tech. (Pharm.) and MBA (Pharm.) offerings, including Pharmaceutical Technology (Process Chemistry) and Pharmaceutical Management. This is an example of institutional offerings rather than a guarantee that every discipline will be offered in each admission year.

The degree is a postgraduate academic and research-oriented outcome. NIPER Hyderabad describes master’s degree requirements as including both coursework and project work, underscoring that admission leads to a structured programme rather than an exam credential by itself.
bullets: Possible degree outcomes include M.Pharm, M.S. (Pharm.), M.Tech. (Pharm.) and MBA (Pharm.).
Confirm campus, discipline, seats and curriculum in the annual seat matrix and institute-specific academic pages.
Expect programme completion requirements to include credits, coursework and project work.

title: NMAT by GMAC
description: NMAT by GMAC — pg entrance exam (management), conducted by GMAC.

quick_facts.label: Purpose
quick_facts.value: NMAT by GMAC is a computer-based graduate-management entrance examination used by participating business schools for admissions to MBA and other graduate business programmes.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: The examination is administered under the NMAT by GMAC brand by Graduate Management Global Connection (India) Private Limited, a GMAC entity.

quick_facts.label: Test structure
quick_facts.value: The current official structure states 108 questions in 120 minutes: 36 Language Skills questions (28 minutes), 36 Quantitative Skills questions (52 minutes), and 36 Logical Reasoning questions (40 minutes).

quick_facts.label: Scoring
quick_facts.value: Section scores range from 12–120 and the total score ranges from 36–360. The exam uses computer-adaptive question delivery and reports scaled scores.

quick_facts.label: Attempts
quick_facts.value: A candidate may take the exam up to three times in a testing cycle, comprising the initial attempt and up to two retakes; applicable dates and retake rules should be checked for the relevant cycle.

quick_facts.label: Fee context
quick_facts.value: The official important-dates page listed an examination registration fee of INR 3,000 plus applicable taxes for the January 2026 delivery window. Fees, taxes, availability, and deadlines are cycle-specific and should be verified before applying.

sections.heading: What NMAT by GMAC is for
paragraphs: NMAT by GMAC is an admissions test intended to help applicants demonstrate language, quantitative, and logical-reasoning skills for graduate management education. GMAC states that participating schools use it for graduate business programmes in India and in several other countries; it is therefore an exam score, not by itself an admission offer or a common counselling process.

Applicants should separately confirm whether each target programme accepts NMAT scores, which testing cycle and score it accepts, and what additional selection stages it requires. GMAC explicitly distinguishes NMAT registration from a school’s own programme application process.
bullets: The three assessed domains are Language Skills, Quantitative Skills, and Logical Reasoning.
The official NMAT website describes the test as computer adaptive: question difficulty is tailored according to prior responses.
A score report supplies scaled section scores and a total score for use in participating schools’ admissions processes.

sections.heading: Eligibility: distinguish exam registration from programme admission
paragraphs: GMAC’s NMAT materials direct candidates to review the eligibility and admissions requirements of each university or business school. Consequently, there is no single exam-score threshold or academic eligibility rule that guarantees admission across NMAT-accepting programmes.

For example, NMIMS’s published 2026–28 admission handout required a recognised bachelor’s degree with at least 50% aggregate marks for several MBA and MBA HR programmes, while certain specialised programmes specified relevant undergraduate disciplines. This is an institution- and programme-specific example, rather than a universal NMAT rule.
bullets: Before registering, check the target programme’s academic qualification requirements, minimum marks, work-experience rules if any, accepted NMAT cycle, and its separate application deadline.
If requesting testing accommodation, GMAC says candidates must provide the requested information and upload a disability certificate during online registration; requests are reviewed case by case.

sections.heading: Exam format and score reporting
paragraphs: The official format has three separately timed sections. Candidates choose the section order at the start of the exam, but must complete each section within its own time allocation; unused time from one section cannot be transferred to another. Questions are delivered one at a time from a question pool.

The test has no negative marking. Official materials describe a total of 108 questions over 120 minutes, with equal numbers of questions in the three sections. The published topic list includes reading comprehension and grammar-related tasks in Language Skills; arithmetic, algebra, probability, data interpretation and data sufficiency in Quantitative Skills; and critical reasoning, puzzles and deductions in Logical Reasoning.

GMAC states that the downloadable scorecard is normally available within 48 hours after the test, although results from exams with a test-security incident may be audited and published later. Score ranges are 12–120 per section and 36–360 overall.
bullets: Language Skills: 36 questions; 28 minutes.
Quantitative Skills: 36 questions; 52 minutes.
Logical Reasoning: 36 questions; 40 minutes.
Total: 108 questions; 120 minutes; total scaled-score range 36–360.

sections.heading: Registration, scheduling, and school applications
paragraphs: Registration for NMAT and applying to a business school are separate actions. In GMAC’s stated workflow, a candidate creates an NMAT account, completes the profile and application details, verifies the email address, selects score-recipient schools, uploads a recent photograph, and pays the test fee. The selected schools’ own applications and admission requirements must be completed separately.

After payment, candidates use the dashboard to book an available date, time, and location. GMAC states that slots are subject to availability and are allocated first come, first served. The support guidance says that an admit card becomes available seven days before the scheduled examination date.

Details entered in the form should be checked carefully before submission. GMAC’s support guidance says personal details and address changes are not entertained after submission, while its current form guidance identifies only limited editable fields during the published edit period.
bullets: Use a valid email address and complete account verification.
Ensure the name and date of birth exactly match the photo identification used for the test.
Select score-recipient schools during registration; GMAC’s published process says five score reports are included, with charges for additional reports.
Book promptly after registration if a particular test-centre city, date, or time is important.
Treat all dates, test modes, centres, fees, edit windows, and document instructions as cycle-specific; verify them in the current official candidate dashboard and dates page.

sections.heading: Preparation approach using official materials
paragraphs: Begin by learning the fixed section timing and taking an official practice exam under realistic time conditions. Because the exam is computer adaptive and each section has its own time limit, preparation should include both concept review and timed decision-making rather than relying only on untimed question practice.

GMAC offers an official guide, a free practice examination with two attempts, and paid practice examinations. The official guide is presented as a source for exam format, topic coverage, past questions, explanations, and a six-week study plan. Practice results can be used to identify whether Language Skills, Quantitative Skills, or Logical Reasoning needs more focused work.

A practical plan is to allocate routine practice to the three official topic groups, record accuracy and time by question type, and complete full-length simulations before the scheduled test. Use the results to decide section order in advance, since the chosen order is set at the beginning of the test.
bullets: Language Skills: practise reading comprehension, paragraph formation, error identification, prepositions, sentence completion, and analogies.
Quantitative Skills: revise number properties, arithmetic, algebra and probability, data integration, and data sufficiency.
Logical Reasoning: practise critical reasoning, analytical puzzles, deductions, and related reasoning tasks.
Use official practice products to become familiar with the 108-question, 120-minute structure.

sections.heading: Using results in admissions
paragraphs: The NMAT scorecard reports scaled scores for the three sections and a total score. GMAC also publishes percentile information, but percentile tables are tied to a specified test-taker sample and data period, so they should be read as descriptive context rather than as an admission cut-off.

Whether a score leads to the next selection stage depends on the receiving school and programme. Applicants should submit the programme application separately and follow that school’s rules on accepted score attempts, section requirements, interviews, written assessments, and final selection. GMAC specifically notes, for example, that NMIMS accepts the first valid score, illustrating why school-specific score-use policies matter.

As dated context, GMAC’s published percentile page reports that its displayed table used a sample of 53,271 test takers from November 5, 2025 through January 17, 2026. It should not be assumed to predict future percentiles or a particular school’s admission threshold.
bullets: Download the scorecard when notified by GMAC and retain it for programme applications.
Check the programme’s own NMAT score policy before deciding whether to use a retake.
Do not treat percentile information or previous admission thresholds as a guaranteed current cut-off.

title: Patent Agent Examination
description: A qualifying examination conducted by the Indian Patent Office for eligible science and technology graduates to register as patent agents.

quick_facts.label: Conducting authority
quick_facts.value: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), Government of India.

quick_facts.label: Statutory gateway
quick_facts.value: Passing the qualifying examination is one route toward entry in the Register of Patent Agents under section 126 of the Patents Act, 1970; registration also requires the statutory qualifications and prescribed fee.

quick_facts.label: Core eligibility
quick_facts.value: For the usual examination-and-registration route, section 126 requires Indian citizenship, age 21 or over, and a degree in science, engineering or technology from a university established by law in India (or another Central Government-specified equivalent qualification), in addition to passing the qualifying examination.

quick_facts.label: 2027 application window
quick_facts.value: For Patent Agent Examination 2027, IP India announced online-only registration from July 1, 2026, 10:00 AM to September 30, 2026, 11:59 PM. This is a dated examination-cycle deadline and should be checked against the live official portal before applying.

quick_facts.label: Assessment and pass standard
quick_facts.value: The qualifying examination comprises Paper I, Paper II and viva voce. Rule 110 specifies 100 marks each for Papers I and II and 50 for viva voce; candidates need at least 50 marks in each written paper and 60% aggregate overall.

quick_facts.label: 2027 examination fee
quick_facts.value: The notified application fee for Patent Agent Examination 2027 is INR 1,600, payable online. Fees are dated, rule-based and subject to change in later notifications.

sections.heading: What the Patent Agent Examination is for
paragraphs: The Patent Agent Examination is the CGPDTM qualifying examination used in the statutory pathway to become a registered Indian patent agent. A registered patent agent is authorized to practise before the Patent Office and may assist inventors, companies, startups and research institutions with patent specifications, applications, examination responses and hearings.
Passing the examination does not by itself complete registration: the candidate must apply for entry in the Register of Patent Agents and satisfy the remaining statutory and documentary requirements.
bullets: The professional role is grounded in the Patents Act, 1970 and the Register of Patent Agents.
It is a professional qualifying examination, not an academic degree or a general law-licensing examination.

sections.heading: Who should check eligibility
paragraphs: Section 126 of the Patents Act, 1970 sets the baseline for registration: the person must be an Indian citizen, have completed 21 years of age, and hold a degree in science, engineering or technology from a university established by law in India, or another equivalent qualification specified by the Central Government. The standard route also requires passing the prescribed qualifying examination and payment of the prescribed fee.

For the 2027 cycle, IP India states that eligibility is assessed under section 126 and notes that a candidate who qualifies must submit the required science, engineering or technology degree within six months of declaration of the final result to complete registration. Applicants remain responsible for ensuring that they meet the statutory criteria.
bullets: Citizenship, age and degree evidence are material to registration.
The 2027 notice requires candidates to keep proof of age, citizenship and degree certificate ready for the online application.
A qualifying degree should not be assumed from a law degree alone; the statutory provision specifically names science, engineering or technology.

sections.heading: Exam format, syllabus and qualifying marks
paragraphs: Under Rule 110, the examination has two written papers and a viva voce: Paper I is 100 marks on the Patents Act and Rules; Paper II is 100 marks on drafting and interpretation of patent specifications and other documents; and viva voce is 50 marks. The official patent-agent page also identifies the Designs Act and Designs Rules within Paper I coverage and design specifications within Paper II.

For the notified 2027 cycle, Paper I is an objective, two-hour paper worth 100 marks, and Paper II is a descriptive, three-hour paper worth 100 marks. Candidates with at least 50% in each written paper may appear for viva voce. The published syllabus includes the Patents Act, 1970, Patents Rules, 2003, Designs Act, 2000, Designs Rules, 2001 and matters relating to IP jurisprudence. Candidates select English or Hindi for the question paper when applying.

To pass under Rule 110(3), a candidate must score at least 50 marks in each of Paper I and Paper II and achieve 60% aggregate across the examination. Candidates should rely on the notification for their own cycle, as operational details can change.
bullets: Paper I: patent and design legislation/rules; objective format in the 2027 notice.
Paper II: drafting and interpretation; descriptive format in the 2027 notice.
Viva voce: 50 marks, scheduled after the written examination for eligible candidates.

sections.heading: Applying and registering after qualification
paragraphs: For the 2027 examination, IP India has specified an online-only application process. Candidates register on the official portal, complete the application, upload a colour photograph, signature, proof of age, proof of citizenship and degree documentation, and make payment online. The stated registration period is July 1, 2026, 10:00 AM to September 30, 2026, 11:59 PM; the notice says the deadline will not be extended.

The 2027 application fee is INR 1,600. This is dated fee context from the 2027 notice, not a permanent fee quotation; applicants should verify the applicable amount in the live official notification and portal.

After passing, the next step is a separate registration application in Form 22. In instructions issued to PAE 2026 qualifiers, CGPDTM required Form 22, supporting age, degree, citizenship, character and admit-card documents, and the prescribed registration-related payments. Those instructions listed INR 3,200 for registration and INR 800 continuation fee for one financial year; future cohorts should confirm fees and documents in their own post-result notice.
bullets: Apply online; the 2027 notice does not provide an alternative application mode.
Retain the application/payment record and monitor IP India for admit-card, result and viva updates.
Qualifying the examination should be followed promptly by the Form 22 registration process and the cycle-specific document requirements.

sections.heading: Preparation priorities
paragraphs: Preparation should be built around the official legal syllabus and the separate demands of the two written papers: statutory and procedural knowledge for Paper I, and practical drafting and interpretation for Paper II. Candidates should also prepare for oral questioning after clearing the written-paper threshold.

IP India publishes prior Patent Agent Examination papers and answer keys, including 2026 materials. These are particularly useful for understanding question wording, subject coverage and Paper I’s objective-question style; they should complement study of the currently amended Acts, Rules and the current examination notice rather than replace them.
bullets: Read the currently applicable Patents Act and Patents Rules alongside the Designs Act and Designs Rules.
Practise drafting complete specifications and interpreting patent-related documents under timed conditions.
Use official previous papers and answer keys, then check each new notification for changes to format, dates or instructions.

sections.heading: What qualification can lead to
paragraphs: A successful candidate who completes registration is entered in the Register of Patent Agents and receives a registration certificate. Registration enables professional practice before the Patent Office within the Patents Act framework, including work such as preparing specifications, filing patent applications, responding to examination reports and representing applicants in hearings.

This credential is therefore most directly relevant to patent-prosecution and patent-drafting work for inventors, companies, research organizations and IP practices. It does not eliminate the need to comply with registration, continuation and professional-conduct requirements administered by the Patent Office.
bullets: Immediate administrative outcome: eligibility to seek registration through Form 22 after passing.
Professional outcome after registration: authority to practise before the Patent Office as a patent agent.

Patent Agent Examination 2027 official notice and instructions
