title: Ph.D. in Law Entrance Test
description: A university-specific doctoral entrance examination for admission to a Ph.D. programme in Law, typically followed by an interview.

quick_facts.label: What this exam is
quick_facts.value: “Ph.D. in Law Entrance Test” is a generic label for an institution-level doctoral admissions test, not one single all-India examination. Under the UGC Ph.D. Regulations, an HEI may admit through its own entrance test and/or through national-test fellowship/scholarship routes followed by interview.

quick_facts.label: Typical qualifying background
quick_facts.value: For Ph.D. admission, UGC regulations provide for a qualifying master’s degree with at least 55% aggregate marks or an equivalent grade, subject to specified category relaxations; universities may publish discipline-specific eligibility. NALSAR’s Law doctoral programme, for example, lists a relevant master’s degree in Law or cognate disciplines and 55% marks, with stated relaxations.

quick_facts.label: Test and interview rule
quick_facts.value: For an HEI-run entrance test, the UGC framework specifies 50% research methodology and 50% subject-specific syllabus. Candidates securing 50% in the test may be called for interview, with a 5% entrance-mark relaxation for specified categories; selection weightage is 70% test and 30% interview/viva voce.

quick_facts.label: Illustrative Law-school format
quick_facts.value: NALSAR’s published Ph.D. Law process illustrates the variation institutions can set: a 100-mark, 3.5-hour online examination with research aptitude/writing and disciplinary knowledge components, followed by a preliminary research proposal and interview stage. Its official page also states that UGC-NET/UGC-CSIR NET-qualified applicants or JRF holders are exempt from its written test.

quick_facts.label: Dates and fees vary by university
quick_facts.value: Applicants should use the particular university’s current notification rather than assume a common schedule or fee. For context only, NALSAR’s 2026–27 Ph.D. notice listed registration from June 12 to July 10, 2026 and an entrance examination on August 2, 2026; these dates are not a national schedule.

sections.heading: Purpose and place in legal education
paragraphs: This entrance test is a selection mechanism for admission to a university’s Ph.D. programme in Law after an LL.M. or another qualifying route accepted by that institution. It is not a nationally uniform examination: the UGC permits eligible higher-education institutions to use their own Ph.D. entrance test, while also permitting admission through qualifying national fellowship/scholarship tests followed by interview.

The test is designed to assess readiness for doctoral research rather than professional legal practice. The UGC framework requires an institution-run test to divide its syllabus equally between research methodology and subject-specific knowledge, which explains why Law Ph.D. admissions commonly assess both legal-domain understanding and research capability.
bullets: Read the university’s Ph.D. prospectus or admission notice as the controlling document for seats, discipline coverage, reservation, eligibility, test mode, exemptions, selection method, deadlines and fees.
Treat the test as one stage of doctoral selection: a research proposal, supervisor availability and interview can affect whether an applicant is ultimately admitted.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: At the UGC baseline, eligible applicants include candidates with a prescribed master’s-degree pathway and at least 55% aggregate marks or its equivalent grade. The regulations also provide a 5% marks/grade relaxation for SC, ST, OBC non-creamy-layer, Differently-Abled and EWS candidates, as determined by the Commission; they additionally recognize the specified four-year bachelor’s route and M.Phil. route. A university may impose relevant-subject or faculty-fit requirements in its own notification.

For Law-focused programmes, the immediate parent pathway is commonly an LL.M. NALSAR’s current doctoral programme page, for example, accepts a master’s degree or equivalent in Law, Humanities, Social Sciences or cognate disciplines with the stated minimum marks, and identifies certain professional qualifications as additional accepted routes. This is an example of institutional eligibility, not a rule that every university must copy.
bullets: Check whether your LL.M. specialization, marks, category certificate, NET/JRF status and proposed topic meet the specific institution’s published conditions.
Do not assume a national-test qualification automatically produces the same exemption everywhere: confirm the relevant university’s current notice.

sections.heading: Exam and selection format
paragraphs: Under the UGC Ph.D. Regulations, an HEI-administered entrance test has a 50:50 syllabus split between research methodology and subject-specific content. Applicants scoring 50% in that test are eligible to be called for interview, subject to the institution’s available seats and its published process. For selection based on that entrance test, the regulations prescribe 70% weightage for the test and 30% for interview/viva voce.

The exact question style, duration and delivery mode are institution-specific. NALSAR provides one Law-school example: its online test is stated to be 3.5 hours and 100 marks, split between research aptitude/writing skills and disciplinary knowledge. Its 2025–26 notification described the first component as including MCQs, essay, comprehension and précis writing, and the second as testing scholarly writing, referencing and domain knowledge.
bullets: Prepare for legal research methodology as well as substantive legal knowledge; neither component should be treated as optional.
Expect the interview to examine the proposed research problem, literature engagement, originality, feasibility and fit with available supervision, where those criteria are set by the institution.

sections.heading: Application process
paragraphs: The institution must publish its Ph.D. prospectus or notification in advance, including the available seats, subject/discipline-wise distribution, eligibility, admission procedure and other candidate information. Start by locating that official notice, then apply through the specified channel and retain proof of submission and payment.

A typical university-specific sequence is: verify eligibility and exemption status; submit the application and supporting academic/category documents; take the written test if required; submit a preliminary research proposal; and attend the interview if shortlisted. NALSAR’s Law notification is an official example: it required online application, provided a written-test exemption for specified UGC-NET/UGC-CSIR NET/JRF applicants, and required qualified or exempt applicants to submit a 1,500–2,000-word preliminary proposal for scrutiny before interview.
bullets: Use only the institution’s active admission portal and notification for deadlines. Dates, seats, application fees and test logistics change by university and admission cycle.
Before submitting a proposal, check faculty research areas, supervisor availability and already registered topics where the university makes these available.

Keep copies of degree/marks documents, identity documents, applicable category certificates, national-test certificates and the final submitted proposal; exact document requirements are university-specific.

sections.heading: Preparation strategy
paragraphs: Build preparation around the two UGC-prescribed content areas: research methodology and subject-specific knowledge. For a Law Ph.D. test, practise converting a broad legal interest into a researchable question, identifying relevant primary and secondary sources, explaining a defensible method, and using accurate legal citation and referencing.

Prepare the proposal and interview in parallel with the written test. NALSAR’s published process requires a preliminary proposal that states the research problem and literature survey and demonstrates an unexplored topic capable of an original scholarly contribution. Its notice also states that proposals are screened for duplication and plagiarism, and that internal supervisory expertise is a factor in consideration.
bullets: Review research design, doctrinal and empirical approaches, research ethics, literature-review methods, legal citation and academic writing.
Revise the legal field closest to your proposal and practise timed analytical writing, not only objective questions.
Draft a concise proposal early; be ready to explain its question, gap, sources, method, feasibility and likely contribution in an interview.
Independently check citations, quotations and paraphrasing before submission; do not reuse another person’s work or submit a topic already registered at the institution.

sections.heading: What follows after the test
paragraphs: Passing an entrance test does not by itself guarantee Ph.D. admission. Under the UGC framework, test performance determines eligibility to be called for interview, and the number called may depend on seats. At NALSAR, applicants whose proposal clears the institution’s scrutiny and who qualify in interview are provisionally admitted, illustrating that written performance, proposal quality and interview are distinct stages.

Admission begins the doctoral programme rather than ending the selection process. UGC regulations set a minimum Ph.D. duration of three years including coursework, with a normal maximum of six years from admission, subject to the regulations’ re-registration and category-related provisions. NALSAR’s Law notice also states that admitted candidates undertake foundational research-methodology coursework and further coursework before defending a modified proposal.
bullets: The immediate outcome of a successful process is admission to a supervised Ph.D. in Law programme, subject to the institution’s conditions and seat/supervisor capacity.
Confirm the university’s current coursework, residency, fee and thesis requirements after admission; these are programme-specific and can change between academic years.

title: PLAB (UKMLA)
description: PLAB (UKMLA) — abroad exam (medical), conducted by GMC (UK).

quick_facts.label: Regulator and purpose
quick_facts.value: PLAB (Professional and Linguistic Assessments Board) is the GMC assessment route used to help establish that doctors who qualified abroad have the knowledge and skills to practise medicine in the UK.

quick_facts.label: Relationship to UKMLA
quick_facts.value: PLAB remains its current name, but is compliant with the UK Medical Licensing Assessment (MLA) requirements: PLAB 1 meets the MLA Applied Knowledge Test requirements and PLAB 2 meets the Clinical and Professional Skills Assessment requirements.

quick_facts.label: Parts and format
quick_facts.value: PLAB has two parts: PLAB 1 is a 180-question, single-best-answer written exam completed in three hours; PLAB 2 is a practical OSCE comprising 16 eight-minute scenarios.

quick_facts.label: Core entry checks
quick_facts.value: Before booking PLAB 1, applicants must create a GMC Online account and have an acceptable overseas primary medical qualification and acceptable English-language evidence verified by the GMC.

quick_facts.label: 2026 GMC exam fees
quick_facts.value: From 1 April 2026, GMC lists the PLAB 1 fee as £283 and the PLAB 2 fee as £1,036. These are exam fees only; registration, travel, visa, accommodation and preparation costs may also apply, and fees can change.

quick_facts.label: Post-exam pathway
quick_facts.value: Passing PLAB alone is not GMC registration or a job offer. A candidate who has passed both parts may apply for registration with a licence to practise; the GMC’s IMG full-registration route also requires an internship and specifies that both PLAB parts must have been passed within the previous two years.

sections.heading: What PLAB (UKMLA-compliant) is for
paragraphs: PLAB is the GMC’s assessment route for many international medical graduates (IMGs), including doctors with an Indian MBBS, who seek to join the UK medical register. It assesses the knowledge, clinical skills and professional behaviours expected of a doctor beginning UK Foundation Programme Year 2 (F2) practice.

PLAB is not currently renamed “UKMLA.” Rather, the GMC states that PLAB is compliant with MLA requirements and continues to be the assessment taken by international doctors who need this route to UK registration. The common MLA content map underpins the assessments.
bullets: For applicants with a medical degree outside the UK, EEA or Switzerland, the GMC says PLAB will probably be required, subject to the applicant’s individual route and qualification.

Other GMC registration routes can exist, such as routes based on sponsorship or certain postgraduate qualifications; applicants should use the GMC registration guidance rather than assume PLAB is mandatory in every case.

sections.heading: Eligibility for an Indian MBBS graduate
paragraphs: An Indian MBBS is an overseas primary medical qualification for GMC purposes. Before PLAB 1, the GMC must find the applicant’s primary medical qualification acceptable and must accept the applicant’s evidence of English-language knowledge. The GMC evaluates overseas qualifications individually against its published criteria and lists institutions or qualifications it does not accept or may accept only in some circumstances.

For PLAB 2, the GMC requires an acceptable overseas primary medical qualification and a valid PLAB 1 pass. PLAB 2 must be passed within two years of the PLAB 1 pass date; the pass date is the examination date, not the results-release date.
bullets: English evidence requirements for PLAB can differ from the evidence required later for registration. The GMC publishes routes using IELTS, OET, a primary medical qualification, employer reference, a UK job offer, or other evidence, depending on the applicant’s circumstances.
Candidates normally have up to four attempts at each examination. After a fourth failed attempt, an additional attempt must be requested; a fifth failed attempt is final.

Passing both PLAB parts does not by itself meet every requirement for full registration. For the GMC IMG full-registration route, the applicant must also have completed an internship and satisfy documentary, identity, fitness-to-practise and other registration requirements.

sections.heading: Exam structure, delivery and scope
paragraphs: PLAB 1 is the applied knowledge test. It is a written examination of 180 single-best-answer multiple-choice questions in three hours. Its scenarios concern current UK best practice and routinely available UK hospital resources; it tests application of knowledge for patient care rather than recall alone.

PLAB 2 is the clinical and professional skills assessment, delivered as an OSCE. It has 16 scenarios of eight minutes each, designed to resemble settings such as consultations and acute wards. The GMC holds PLAB 2 at its clinical assessment centres in Manchester, UK.
Both parts are based on the MLA content map. This framework includes the core knowledge, skills and behaviours expected for safe UK practice, including professional values and behaviours.
bullets: PLAB 1 is offered in the UK and selected international locations; availability, dates and locations must be checked in GMC Online.

The GMC announced on 20 May 2026 that some international PLAB 1 locations and the number of non-UK/EEA sittings will change from February 2027. Candidates should therefore rely on the live GMC booking service, not historic location lists.
PLAB 2 dates run through the year, but availability can be constrained by demand; booking is available after PLAB 1 results are available.

sections.heading: Application and booking sequence
paragraphs: Start by opening a personal GMC Online account, then submit the evidence requested for the overseas primary medical qualification and English-language knowledge. Once the GMC has verified that the information meets its requirements, the candidate can book PLAB 1 through GMC Online.

After passing PLAB 1, book PLAB 2 only through the candidate’s own GMC Online account. The GMC explicitly warns that third parties cannot book on a candidate’s behalf and that sharing account access can constitute misconduct.

After passing both parts, apply separately for GMC registration with a licence to practise. The GMC says the registration application should be approved within two years of passing PLAB 2. For the IMG full-registration route, evidence includes the primary medical qualification, internship, English knowledge, identity and other required declarations or documents.
bullets: As of 1 April 2026, the GMC lists PLAB 1 at £283 and PLAB 2 at £1,036; cancellation charges can apply. Confirm fees, booking dates and cancellation terms directly with the GMC before payment.

For PLAB 2, applicants should plan independently for UK entry permission, travel, accommodation and lead time. The GMC notes that the number of PLAB places is not linked to the number of NHS or other employer vacancies.
The GMC recommends reviewing its guidance on working as a doctor in the UK before booking, because job opportunities differ by specialty and location and change over time.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Use the GMC’s MLA content map as the primary syllabus framework: the GMC states that it sets out the knowledge, skills and behaviours required in PLAB and beyond. For PLAB 1, focus on applying evidence-based UK practice to common, important and acute F2-level presentations, alongside longer-term conditions encountered in primary care.

Prepare professional judgement and communication as well as clinical knowledge. The GMC identifies Good medical practice and its interactive professional-standards resources as relevant preparation, because candidates are expected to demonstrate those professional values both in the examination and in UK practice.

The GMC provides official PLAB 1 sample questions and PLAB 2 preparation material. It does not provide, endorse or quality-assure commercial coaching courses. Candidates should avoid any provider that claims access to GMC examination content or asks them to share recalled live-exam content, because this may breach the GMC misconduct policy.
bullets: For PLAB 1: practise timed single-best-answer questions and apply answers to UK guidance and UK care settings rather than local protocols.
For PLAB 2: rehearse structured consultations, clinical examination, explanation, consent, prioritisation, safety-netting and professional communication within the eight-minute station format.
Use only legitimate materials and preserve exam confidentiality.

sections.heading: What passing PLAB enables—and what it does not
paragraphs: Passing PLAB 1 and PLAB 2 allows an eligible IMG to apply for GMC registration with a licence to practise. It does not automatically grant registration, a UK visa, an NHS training place, or employment; those outcomes require separate processes and decisions.

For the GMC’s full-registration route for IMGs, both PLAB parts must have been passed within the past two years and the applicant must have completed an internship. The GMC also states that the application for registration should be approved within two years of passing PLAB 2; applicants outside that period may need to provide additional evidence of knowledge and skills.

Candidates should treat employment prospects as variable rather than guaranteed. The GMC says PLAB-place numbers are not directly linked to the number of vacancies offered by employers, and that vacancies vary by specialty, geography and time.
bullets: Successful registration permits a doctor to work only within the scope of their GMC registration and licence, subject to the role’s employer checks, immigration status where applicable, and any other legal or contractual requirements.
PLAB is one route into UK practice, not a postgraduate specialty qualification or a guarantee of specialty training.

title: RBI Assistant
description: RBI Assistant — govt recruitment exam (finance), conducted by RBI.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body and role
quick_facts.value: RBI Assistant is a Reserve Bank of India recruitment examination for appointment to the Assistant post in RBI offices.

quick_facts.label: Most recent notified cycle
quick_facts.value: The Assistant – Panel Year 2025 notification, dated February 16, 2026, advertised 650 vacancies; RBI stated that vacancies could be increased, decreased, or left unfilled according to requirements.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: Under the 2026 notification, selection is through an online Preliminary Examination, online Main Examination, and a Language Proficiency Test (LPT).

quick_facts.label: Baseline eligibility in the latest cycle
quick_facts.value: As of February 1, 2026, candidates generally needed to be 20–28 years old, hold a bachelor’s degree in any discipline with at least 50% aggregate marks (pass class for SC/ST/PwBD candidates), know PC word processing, and be proficient in the relevant recruiting-office state language.

quick_facts.label: Latest-cycle fee context
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, the non-refundable charge was ₹50 plus 18% GST for SC/ST/PwBD/EXS candidates and ₹450 plus 18% GST for GEN/OBC/EWS candidates; bank transaction charges were extra. These amounts can change in a later notification.

sections.heading: What RBI Assistant is
paragraphs: RBI Assistant is a nationwide competitive recruitment route to the Assistant post at the Reserve Bank of India. The latest official notification describes recruitment across RBI offices and makes selection conditional on clearing preliminary and main online examinations followed by the LPT.

The examination is office-specific: applicants select one recruiting office, and the vacancy distribution, local-language requirement, and examination-centre options are linked to that choice. The notification also states that an applicant may apply for a vacancy in only one office.
bullets: The 2026 Panel Year 2025 notice advertised 650 posts across 17 recruiting offices.
RBI may revise the number of vacancies or decide not to fill vacancies, so a notification’s vacancy total is not a permanent annual intake figure.

sections.heading: Eligibility: use the notification for the cycle you apply to
paragraphs: Eligibility is cycle-specific. In the Assistant – Panel Year 2025 notice, the general age band was 20–28 years as on February 1, 2026; the notice also set category-specific upper-age relaxations, including five years for SC/ST and three years for OBC candidates. Applicants should not assume these cut-offs or relaxations will be identical in a future cycle.

For education, the latest notice required a bachelor’s degree in any discipline with at least 50% aggregate marks, while SC/ST/PwBD candidates could use a pass class where the relevant reservation was available. It also required knowledge of word processing on PC. Candidates for a recruiting office had to be able to read, write, speak, and understand the official/local language of the applicable state or states.

Nationality was not limited only to Indian citizens in the notice: it also listed certain specified Nepalese, Bhutanese, Tibetan-refugee, and persons-of-Indian-origin categories, subject where applicable to a Government of India eligibility certificate. Ex-servicemen had a separate education/service route set out in the notification.
bullets: Check the notification’s stated eligibility date; qualifications must be completed by that date.
Check the office-wise vacancy table before choosing an office.
Treat local-language proficiency as a compulsory selection condition, not merely a preference.

sections.heading: Exam format and selection rules
paragraphs: The latest notified preliminary examination was an objective online test of 100 questions and 100 marks in 60 minutes: English Language (30 questions/20 minutes), Numerical Ability (35/20 minutes), and Reasoning Ability (35/20 minutes). Candidates must qualify in the preliminary examination to proceed to the main examination.

The Main Examination was an objective online test of 200 questions and 200 marks in 135 minutes: Reasoning, English Language, Numerical Ability, General Awareness, and Computer Knowledge, with 40 questions in each test. The notice specifies sectional timing: 30, 30, 30, 25, and 20 minutes respectively.

Wrong answers attract a penalty of one-fourth of the marks assigned to the question in both objective tests. Candidates provisionally shortlisted from Main must take the LPT in the official/local language for the relevant state; a candidate who is not proficient in that language is disqualified.
bullets: Prelims: 100 questions, 100 marks, 60 minutes.
Mains: 200 questions, 200 marks, 135 minutes.
The English-language test is excluded from the multilingual availability provision; the notice says other online tests are offered in English, Hindi, and specified additional languages.
RBI states that candidates must qualify in each objective-test part separately.

sections.heading: How to apply and what to watch for
paragraphs: RBI requires online-only applications through its official recruitment site; it does not accept another submission mode. In the latest cycle, candidates registered online, supplied basic details, uploaded the prescribed images/documents, reviewed the form, completed registration, and paid through the integrated payment gateway.

The 2026 application window was initially February 16–March 8, 2026, and RBI later extended the closing time to 23:59 on March 10, 2026 because candidates had faced technical difficulties. Those dates are historical and must not be used as a deadline forecast for a future RBI Assistant cycle.

The notification required a recent photograph, signature, left-thumb impression, and handwritten declaration, as well as a personal email address kept active through results. It also instructed candidates to retain the registration credentials, e-receipt, and application printout. Eligibility is ultimately checked at document verification, so submitting an application does not establish eligibility.
bullets: Apply only via RBI’s official recruitment/vacancy pages and the linked registration portal.
Read corrigenda and notices on RBI’s site: RBI says corrigenda for the advertisement are published there.
Match the name in the form exactly to the photo identification document used at the examination.
Choose the recruiting office and associated examination-centre state carefully; the latest notice allowed only one office application.

sections.heading: Preparation aligned to the notified scheme
paragraphs: A practical preparation plan should mirror the official stage and section structure: prepare English, numerical ability, and reasoning for the timed Preliminary Examination; then add general awareness and computer knowledge for Main. Because every test is separately timed, practice should include sectional time limits rather than only full-length untimed question sets.

Accuracy should be trained alongside speed: RBI’s latest scheme deducts one-fourth of the marks for each incorrect objective answer. Candidates should also prepare for the local-language LPT early, especially if applying outside their primary language area, because failure to demonstrate proficiency is disqualifying.

Use the information handout and instructions made available with the official call letter for the applicable cycle as the controlling source for operational examination details, accommodations, and venue procedures.
bullets: Run 20-minute practice sets for each Preliminary section.
Run Main-section practice at the notification’s 20-, 25-, and 30-minute limits.
Use error logs to reduce avoidable guesses under the 0.25-mark negative marking rule.
Confirm the official/local language required for the selected recruiting office before applying.

sections.heading: Appointment and compensation context
paragraphs: Candidates who clear the relevant stages are considered for appointment as RBI Assistants, subject to document verification and being declared medically fit under Bank rules. RBI’s general recruitment process also says that, after selection and acceptance of the offer, candidates must complete formalities that can include medical testing, police verification, referee reporting, and employer reporting before receiving an appointment letter.

Compensation is variable and should be treated as dated notification context. The February 2026 Assistant notice stated a starting basic pay of ₹29,000 per month on the specified pay scale and approximate initial gross monthly emoluments of ₹58,514 without HRA; it also stated that 15% of pay as HRA would be paid additionally where the employee was not staying in Bank accommodation. Allowances and service benefits are governed by rules in force from time to time.
bullets: Appointment is not final merely on exam performance: eligibility documents and medical fitness remain conditions.

The latest notice listed benefits such as Bank accommodation subject to availability and eligibility, medical facilities/reimbursements, leave fare concession, and certain advances/loans subject to service requirements.
Do not rely on the 2026 salary or benefit figures for a future recruitment notification without checking the new notice.

title: RBI Grade B
description: RBI Grade B — govt recruitment exam (finance), conducted by RBI.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: Reserve Bank of India Services Board conducts direct recruitment for Officers in Grade ‘B’ in the RBI’s General, DEPR (Department of Economic and Policy Research), and DSIM (Department of Statistics and Information Management) cadres.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: The 2026 notice specifies Phase-I and Phase-II online/written examinations followed by an interview.

quick_facts.label: General-cadre education requirement (2026 notice)
quick_facts.value: For Grade B (DR)–General, eligibility was graduation with at least 60% aggregate marks, or post-graduation with at least 55%; the notice provides lower thresholds for eligible SC/ST/PwBD applicants where posts are reserved.

quick_facts.label: Age requirement (2026 notice)
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 recruitment, the base age band was 21 to 30 years as on April 1, 2026, with specified upper-age relaxations for eligible categories and circumstances.

quick_facts.label: 2026 application window
quick_facts.value: For panel year 2026, online registration and fee payment opened on April 29, 2026 and closed at 6:00 PM on May 20, 2026. These dates are recruitment-cycle-specific and may change in future notices.

quick_facts.label: 2026 General-cadre fees
quick_facts.value: The 2026 notice listed ₹850 plus 18% GST for GEN/OBC/EWS applicants and ₹100 plus 18% GST as intimation charges for SC/ST/PwBD applicants; RBI staff candidates were listed as nil. Bank/transaction charges were additional, and future fees may differ.

sections.heading: What RBI Grade B is for
paragraphs: RBI Grade B is a direct-recruitment route into officer roles at the Reserve Bank of India. The 2026 recruitment notice covered General, DEPR, and DSIM cadres. RBI describes Grade B work as spanning an array of roles within a full-service central bank, with the precise work depending on posting and cadre.
source_urls
bullets: The General cadre is the broad officer stream.
DEPR is the economics and policy-research stream.
DSIM is the statistics and information-management stream.

sections.heading: Eligibility: choose the cadre that matches your qualification
paragraphs: Eligibility is set separately for each recruitment cycle and cadre. In the 2026 notice, candidates needed to meet nationality, age, education, and other conditions as of the notice’s specified cutoff date. Applicants should use the current RBI notice rather than relying on an earlier year’s thresholds.

For Grade B (DR)–General in 2026, RBI accepted a recognised graduation/equivalent technical or professional qualification with at least 60% aggregate marks, or a recognised post-graduation/equivalent qualification with at least 55%. Eligible SC/ST/PwBD candidates had the relaxations stated in the notice where posts were reserved. DEPR required specified economics or finance master’s qualifications; DSIM required specified statistics, mathematics, econometrics, informatics, data-science, AI, or related qualifications at the master’s level, or an eligible four-year bachelor’s degree in listed fields.
source_urls
bullets: 2026 base age band: 21–30 years as of April 1, 2026; the notice listed category-, qualification-, and experience-based upper-age relaxations.
For General/EWS candidates, the 2026 notice barred applying after six prior Phase-I appearances; it stated that this restriction did not apply to SC/ST/OBC/PwBD candidates where posts were reserved.
Candidates could apply for either DEPR or DSIM, according to the 2026 notice; applicants should confirm the choices available in the relevant year’s advertisement.

sections.heading: Selection format
paragraphs: RBI’s 2026 scheme provides for Phase-I and Phase-II examinations, conducted online and/or in written mode depending on cadre, followed by an interview. Progression is sequential: candidates must be shortlisted at the earlier stage to advance.

For the General cadre, RBI’s official 2024 Phase-II result notice identifies the three Phase-II papers as Economic and Social Issues, English (Writing Skills), and General Finance and Management. Candidates should treat the current recruitment advertisement and its appendices as controlling, because scheduling, modality, and other details may be revised from one panel year to another.
source_urls
bullets: Panel year 2026 scheduled General Phase-I for June 13, 2026 and General Phase-II for July 25, 2026.
For panel year 2026, DEPR Phase-I and DSIM Phase-I were scheduled for June 14, 2026; their Phase-II examinations were scheduled for July 26, 2026.
RBI states that candidates must appear in all required Phase-II papers and shifts.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Applications are submitted online only through RBI’s website; the 2026 notice states that no other submission mode is available. Applicants should first verify their cadre-specific eligibility, complete the online application, upload/provide the required information and documents as directed, pay the applicable fee or intimation charge, and preserve the registration details and application record.

Eligibility is finally checked by the RBI Services Board at the interview stage. The notice warns that incorrect information or failure to meet the conditions can result in cancellation of candidature, including after provisional admission to examinations. RBI also says corrigenda, if issued, will be published on its website.
source_urls
bullets: For the 2026 cycle, the application window was April 29–May 20, 2026, and is now closed as of July 19, 2026.
The 2026 notice provided a two-day post-closing edit window for limited fields; future edit-window availability and fields are not guaranteed.
Candidates employed in government, public-sector, or similar organisations must follow the employer-intimation requirements set out in the applicable notice.

sections.heading: Appointment and career context
paragraphs: Successful candidates are appointed as Officers in Grade B in the cadre for which they are selected. The 2026 notice states that General-stream selectees join the General Cadre, while DEPR and DSIM selectees join their respective cadres. Initial appointment is on probation for two years, which RBI may extend up to four years, and selected candidates are liable to be posted and transferred anywhere in India.

Compensation is variable and should be read as dated context rather than a guaranteed future figure. The April 2026 notice listed starting basic pay of ₹78,450 per month in the stated Grade B scale and approximately ₹154,936 initial monthly gross emoluments without HRA, alongside allowances and benefits subject to rules in force. It also stated that defined-contribution NPS applies to employees joining RBI on or after January 1, 2012, in addition to gratuity.
source_urls
bullets: RBI lists prospects for promotion to higher grades.
Accommodation is subject to availability; the 2026 notice stated that HRA at 15% of pay would be paid if accommodation was not provided.
Benefits, allowances, posting conditions, vacancies, and pay can change under RBI rules and future recruitment notices.

title: RRB ALP
description: RRB ALP — govt recruitment exam (engineering), conducted by Railway Recruitment Boards.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: RRB ALP is the Railway Recruitment Boards’ centralised recruitment process for the Indian Railways Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) post, rather than a standalone academic qualification.

quick_facts.label: Current recruitment context
quick_facts.value: The most recent detailed notification located is CEN 01/2026. It notified 11,127 provisional ALP vacancies across participating RRBs; the notification states that vacancies may increase or decrease according to Railway Administration requirements.

quick_facts.label: Entry qualification
quick_facts.value: For CEN 01/2026, applicants needed Matriculation/SSLC plus a recognised NCVT/SCVT ITI in specified trades, or a Course Completed Act Apprenticeship in those trades, or a three-year diploma/engineering degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Electronics, Automobile Engineering, or permitted combinations of those disciplines.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: The notified process comprises CBT-1, CBT-2, Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT), document verification, and medical examination.

quick_facts.label: Medical standard
quick_facts.value: ALP is an A-1 medical-standard post. The 2026 notice requires 6/6 distant vision in each eye without glasses, specified near vision without glasses, and passing colour, binocular, field, night, and mesopic vision tests; candidates who have undergone LASIK or other refractive-error corrective surgery are ineligible for this post.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: In CEN 01/2026, ALP was listed at Level 2 of the 7th CPC pay matrix with initial pay of ₹19,900. This is notification-specific pay context and can change under future government pay rules or recruitment notices.

sections.heading: Purpose and role in the career pathway
paragraphs: RRB ALP is the entry route used by Railway Recruitment Boards to select Assistant Loco Pilots for Indian Railways. It is especially relevant to candidates coming from ITI, NCVT/SCVT trade training, Course Completed Act Apprenticeship, National Apprenticeship Certificate-related pathways, or eligible engineering diploma/degree routes.

A candidate does not receive an ALP job merely by taking the CBTs. The RRB first recommends empanelled candidates; the concerned Railway Zone issues the appointment offer after document verification, medical fitness, and other required checks. Zone or production-unit allocation is subject to merit, the candidate’s preferences, medical standard, and vacancies.
bullets: The latest detailed notice found, CEN 01/2026, listed the post as Assistant Loco Pilot, Pay Level 2, with medical standard A-1.
Vacancy totals are provisional: candidates should treat the individual CEN and its corrigenda as controlling for a specific cycle.

sections.heading: Eligibility: technical qualification, age, and medical fitness
paragraphs: For CEN 01/2026, the core technical routes were: Matriculation/SSLC plus ITI from an NCVT/SCVT-recognised institution in one of the listed trades; Matriculation/SSLC plus Course Completed Act Apprenticeship in those trades; or Matriculation/SSLC plus a three-year diploma in Mechanical, Electrical, Electronics, Automobile Engineering, or combinations of those disciplines. A degree in the same engineering disciplines was acceptable in lieu of the diploma. Applicants awaiting final results were not eligible.

The base age band in that cycle was 18–30 years as on July 1, 2026. The notice provided category-specific upper-age relaxations, including five years for SC/ST and three years for OBC-NCL candidates, subject to the notification’s conditions and required evidence. Age rules must be checked afresh for each CEN.

Medical eligibility is central, not a formality. The ALP post carries A-1 standards. The 2026 notice calls for vision without glasses at the stated thresholds and passing several functional vision tests. It also says that LASIK or another surgical refractive-error correction makes a candidate ineligible for ALP; final fitness is determined by Railway medical authorities.
bullets: Listed ITI/apprenticeship trades include Fitter, Electrician, Instrument Mechanic, Millwright/Maintenance Mechanic, Electronics Mechanic, Mechanic (Motor Vehicle), Wireman, Tractor Mechanic, Mechanic (Diesel), Turner, Machinist, and Refrigeration & Air-Conditioning Mechanic, among others specified in Annexure A.
PwBD candidates were marked “Not Suitable” for the ALP post in the 2026 post-wise parameters.
Candidates should preserve original qualification, category, identity, and other supporting documents: RRB verifies eligibility against originals at document verification.

sections.heading: Selection format and scoring
paragraphs: CBT-1 is a screening test: 75 objective questions in 60 minutes for 75 marks. Its syllabus covers mathematics, mental ability, and general science at roughly Class 10 level. CBT-1 marks are used to shortlist candidates for CBT-2 and do not count in the final panel.

CBT-2 has 175 questions over 2 hours 30 minutes: Part A has 100 questions in 90 minutes, while Part B has 75 questions in 60 minutes. Part A covers mathematics, general intelligence and reasoning, and basic science and engineering. Part B is a qualifying trade test based on Directorate General of Training trade syllabi; every candidate must obtain 35% in Part B. For ITI/trade-apprenticeship candidates, Part B is in the candidate’s own trade.

Candidates who qualify CBT-2 may be shortlisted for CBAT. Every CBAT test battery must be cleared separately with a minimum T-score of 42, irrespective of community. CBAT is offered only in English and Hindi and has no negative marking. Final merit for document verification uses a 50:50 weighting of CBT-2 Part A marks and CBAT scores; appointment remains conditional on document and medical clearance.
bullets: CBT-1 and CBT-2 each apply negative marking of one-third of a mark for every wrong answer.
CBT question papers are available in English, Hindi, and the regional languages listed in the notification; the CBAT is only in English and Hindi.

The 2026 notice states that CBT-2 shortlisting is ordinarily RRB-wise at up to 15 times vacancies, and CBAT shortlisting is ordinarily up to eight times vacancies, subject to the notice’s conditions and RRB discretion.

sections.heading: How to apply and what to monitor
paragraphs: Applications are online-only through the official RRB application route. Candidates may submit only one application to one RRB for a CEN; multiple applications to the same or different RRBs can result in rejection and debarment. The application requires account creation using a personal mobile number and email address; those account details and the chosen RRB cannot later be changed.

For the 2026 cycle, the application window ran from May 15, 2026 through June 14, 2026, with online fee payment due by June 16, 2026 and a paid modification window from June 17 through June 26, 2026. Those dates are past and were specific to CEN 01/2026, not a prediction of future cycles.

The 2026 examination fee was ₹500 for most applicants, with ₹400 refundable after appearing in CBT-1, less bank charges. The fee was ₹250 for SC, ST, ex-servicemen, female, transgender, minority, and EBC candidates, refundable after appearing in CBT-1, less bank charges. Fees, refunds, application requirements, and dates can change in a future CEN.

Candidates should use official RRB sites for city intimation, e-call letters, result notices, and corrigenda. The notification advises Aadhaar or DigiLocker authentication to make identity checking smoother, while stating that alternate-ID applicants may face stricter scrutiny.
bullets: Before submission, check that names and date of birth match the Matriculation/SSLC certificate.
The 2026 process used a live photo capture and required an uploaded signature; SC/ST candidates seeking the applicable travel facility also had to upload the required certificate.

The 2026 online form included a self-screening medical declaration. Candidates reaching CBAT had to bring the resulting report signed by a general physician and eye specialist from a Central/State Government hospital or medical college.

sections.heading: Preparation priorities
paragraphs: Build preparation around the notified stages, not a generic railway-exam syllabus. For CBT-1, practise timed objective questions in arithmetic, mental ability, and Class 10-level physics, chemistry, and life sciences. For CBT-2 Part A, add basic science and engineering topics such as engineering drawing, units and measurements, work and energy, basic electricity, safety, environment education, and IT literacy.

Treat CBT-2 Part B as trade-specific qualifying preparation. ITI and trade-apprenticeship candidates are tested in their respective trade; diploma and degree candidates choose an eligible mapped trade. Use the Directorate General of Training’s official trade syllabus as the syllabus reference identified in the CEN.

Use the official RRB mock tests when released to become familiar with the computer-based interface. For CBAT, use the Railway Design and Standards Organisation’s candidate guidance and practise working accurately under the allotted time. Because candidates must clear every CBAT battery separately, preparation should address each battery rather than relying on an aggregate score.
bullets: Practise accuracy as well as speed: CBT-1 and CBT-2 have one-third negative marking for an incorrect answer.
Confirm A-1 medical eligibility before committing substantial preparation time, particularly vision requirements and the LASIK exclusion.
Keep the current CEN open while studying: question counts, cut-offs, trade lists, language options, and selection rules can be revised by a later notification.

sections.heading: Outcome after selection
paragraphs: A successful candidate can be recommended for appointment as an Assistant Loco Pilot in Indian Railways. In the CEN 01/2026 context, this was a Level 2 post with initial pay of ₹19,900 under the 7th CPC pay matrix. Actual appointment follows the Railway Zone’s offer and remains conditional on final document verification, antecedent/character verification, and passing the Railway medical examination.

This recruitment can also create a useful signalling outcome for candidates who consent in the application: the RRB notice says scores may be shared with other ministries, departments, PSUs, and private organisations for their own recruitment. That optional score-sharing provision is not an offer of employment and does not replace the ALP selection process.
bullets: An RRB’s empanelment recommendation is not itself the appointment letter; the relevant Railway Zone issues the offer.
Failing the prescribed ALP medical standard prevents empanelment for the post, and the 2026 notice says no alternative appointment is provided on that basis.

title: RRB Group D (Level 1) Exam
description: A recruitment exam by Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs) for entry-level posts like Track Maintainer and Helper in Indian Railways.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: RRB Group D is the common name used for Railway Recruitment Board recruitment to various Level 1 posts in the 7th CPC Pay Matrix; it is a recruitment process rather than an academic qualification.

quick_facts.label: Recent Level 1 notification
quick_facts.value: CEN 09/2025 notified 22,195 Level 1 vacancies, with an initial pay of ₹18,000 and an age band of 18–33 years as on January 1, 2026. Those vacancy, pay, and age figures are specific to that notification and can change in later CENs.

quick_facts.label: Typical qualifying routes
quick_facts.value: For the Level 1 posts listed in CEN 09/2025, the stated qualification was 10th pass, ITI/equivalent, or an NCVT-granted National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC), subject to the post parameters in the notification.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: The notified process is CBT, followed by a qualifying Physical Efficiency Test (PET), document verification, and a railway medical examination; RRBs may conduct the CBT in single- or multi-stage mode.

quick_facts.label: CEN 08/2024 status
quick_facts.value: For the preceding CEN 08/2024 cycle, RRB Bhubaneswar published the CBT result and PET-shortlist notice on July 1, 2026; subsequent PET, document verification, medical examination, and panel activities are handled by the relevant Railway Recruitment Cells.

sections.heading: Purpose and posts
paragraphs: RRB Group D/Level 1 recruitment is used by the Railway Recruitment Boards to recruit for operational, engineering, electrical, mechanical, traffic, and related entry-level railway roles. The CEN 09/2025 post-parameter and vacancy tables include examples such as Trackmaintainer-IV, Pointsman B, Assistant Track Machine, Assistant Bridge, Assistant Carriage and Wagon, Assistant Loco Shed (Electrical), and Assistant TRD. The precise posts, railway zones, medical classifications, and vacancies must be checked in the particular CEN because they vary by recruitment cycle.
source_urls
bullets: The notification is issued by RRBs on behalf of Railway Recruitment Cells (RRCs), while the relevant Railway Administration makes appointment offers after selection.

The 2026 CEN 09/2025 notice stated an initial pay of ₹18,000 for Level 1 posts; this is a dated notification figure, not a guarantee of current take-home pay, which depends on applicable allowances and rules.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: Eligibility is post-specific. In CEN 09/2025, the general Level 1 age range was 18–33 years as on January 1, 2026, with specified relaxations for eligible categories. The notification required candidates to hold the prescribed qualification from a recognized board, institute, or university by the application closing date; candidates awaiting final results were not eligible for that cycle.

For the listed Level 1 posts in CEN 09/2025, the qualification shown in the post parameters was 10th pass, ITI or equivalent, or an NCVT-granted NAC. The notification also states that an engineering diploma or degree is not accepted in place of a required ITI or Course Completed Act Apprenticeship qualification unless a post specifically provides otherwise.
source_urls
bullets: Read the current CEN's Annexure A before choosing posts: it specifies the qualification, age, medical standard, and disability suitability for each post.
Candidates must meet the prescribed medical standard for the post selected. A candidate found medically unsuitable is not entitled to an alternative appointment under the cited CEN.

sections.heading: Exam and selection format
paragraphs: Under CEN 09/2025, the CBT was specified as 90 minutes with 100 one-mark multiple-choice questions: General Science 25, Mathematics 25, General Intelligence and Reasoning 30, and General Awareness and Current Affairs 20. Eligible scribe users receive 120 minutes. The section split is indicative, and one-third of a mark is deducted for each wrong answer.

Candidates shortlisted on CBT merit are called to the qualifying PET, ordinarily at three times the community-wise vacancies, subject to the Railways' stated discretion to vary the ratio. PET standards in CEN 09/2025 require male candidates to carry 35 kg for 100 m within two minutes and run 1,000 m in 4 minutes 15 seconds; female candidates must carry 20 kg for 100 m within two minutes and run 1,000 m in 5 minutes 40 seconds. PwBD, Course Completed Act Apprentices, and ex-servicemen have the exemptions described in the CEN.
source_urls
bullets: The CBT syllabus includes secondary-school-level Physics, Chemistry, and Life Sciences, along with mathematics, reasoning, and current-affairs/general-awareness topics.

After PET qualification, document-verification shortlisting is normally at a 1:1 vacancy ratio; appointment remains subject to original-document checks, medical fitness, character/antecedent verification, and the Railway Administration's offer.

sections.heading: Application process
paragraphs: The CEN 09/2025 application period ran from January 31, 2026 through March 2, 2026, so it is closed. Future Level 1 applications should be made only when a new official CEN opens, using the application link published on official RRB websites. CEN 09/2025 allowed an applicant to choose only one RRB/Railway Zone; multiple applications could result in rejection and debarment.

For the cited cycle, candidates first created or used an RRB account with a personal mobile number and email address, selected eligible posts and preferences in the chosen railway, completed the online form, supplied the required live photograph and signature, and paid the fee online. The notification advised Aadhaar or DigiLocker identity authentication, while noting that alternate-photo-ID applicants would face stricter scrutiny.
source_urls
bullets: CEN 09/2025 charged ₹500 for most applicants, with ₹400 refundable after appearing in CBT, less applicable bank charges. It charged ₹250 for listed concession categories, refundable after CBT appearance, less bank charges. These were cycle-specific fee rules.
Keep original educational, category, and other claimed-eligibility documents ready for document verification; failure to produce originals on the scheduled day can forfeit candidature.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Prepare directly against the official CBT distribution: build timed practice across mathematics, reasoning, general science, and general awareness/current affairs, and account for the one-third negative mark for wrong answers. The official syllabus identifies 10th-standard CBSE-level Physics, Chemistry, and Life Sciences for General Science, and lists core mathematics and reasoning topics such as number systems, percentages, time and work, coding-decoding, syllogisms, directions, and data interpretation.

Do not postpone physical preparation until after the CBT. Candidates targeting posts requiring PET should progressively train for the applicable load-carry and 1,000-metre standard, while considering personal health and medical fitness. RRB notices state that official mock/practice tests are made available to help candidates become familiar with the online examination process.
source_urls
bullets: Use official RRB/RRC notices, e-call-letter instructions, and mock-test links rather than unofficial timetable or answer-key claims.
Practise accuracy as well as speed: unanswered questions do not attract a deduction, but wrong CBT answers do under the cited CEN.

sections.heading: Outcomes after qualifying
paragraphs: A successful candidate may be empanelled for a Level 1 railway post in the selected RRB/Railway Zone and post preferences, but passing CBT, PET, or document verification alone does not create an entitlement to appointment. RRBs/RRCs recommend empanelled candidates; the relevant Railway Administration issues the appointment offer after final checks.

For candidates in the CEN 08/2024 cycle, the July 1, 2026 CBT-result notices short-listed candidates for PET. The notices state that PET, document verification, medical examination, and publication of panels are to be conducted by the respective RRCs, so candidates should follow the RRC for their railway zone after RRB CBT results.
source_urls
bullets: Employment outcomes depend on merit, notified vacancies, post preferences, qualifying PET where applicable, document verification, medical fitness, and antecedent/character verification.

A bachelor's degree, distance-learning course, diploma, or further technical study can be pursued separately, but it does not replace the notification's specific entry qualification where ITI/NAC or another stated credential is required.

title: RRB JE
description: RRB JE — govt recruitment exam (engineering), conducted by Railway Recruitment Boards.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: RRB JE is a Railway Recruitment Board (RRB) competitive recruitment process for Junior Engineer posts in Indian Railways; the latest detailed JE notification also included Depot Material Superintendent (DMS) and Chemical & Metallurgical Assistant (CMA) posts.

quick_facts.label: Latest notified cycle
quick_facts.value: The latest detailed notice located is CEN 05/2025. Its online application window ran from 31 October 2025 to 30 November 2025; this is a past window, not an open application deadline.

quick_facts.label: Age context
quick_facts.value: For CEN 05/2025, the advertised age range for the JE/DMS/CMA group was 18–33 years as on 1 January 2026, with specified category-based upper-age relaxations. Age criteria can change in a future CEN.

quick_facts.label: Qualification context
quick_facts.value: Eligibility is post-specific and must be checked against the notification’s Annexure A. The 2025 technical exam-group mapping covered a three-year engineering diploma or a bachelor’s degree in Engineering/Technology in listed disciplines, including mechanical, electrical, electronics/computer-related, and civil/allied streams.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: The notified process consists of CBT-I, CBT-II, document verification, and medical examination. CBT-I is a screening test; shortlisting for document verification is based on CBT-II merit and options.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: For CEN 05/2025, JE/DMS/CMA posts were advertised at 7th CPC Pay Level 6 with initial pay of ₹35,400. This is an advertised basic-pay figure for that CEN, not a guarantee of take-home pay; allowances and future terms may vary.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope of RRB JE
paragraphs: RRB JE is not an academic entrance examination or engineering qualification. It is a centralised recruitment route through the Railway Recruitment Boards for technical railway roles, principally Junior Engineer positions. Individual notifications can combine JE hiring with related technical posts, so applicants should read the specific Centralised Employment Notice (CEN), including its post parameters, vacancy table, medical standard, and discipline mapping.

In the latest located cycle, CEN 05/2025 advertised 2,569 combined vacancies for JE, DMS and CMA across RRBs. Vacancy figures are expressly provisional and may change according to Railway Administration requirements.
bullets: Choose the RRB carefully: the CEN permits one RRB and one common application; multiple applications can result in rejection.
Post, railway zone/production unit, and eventual allocation are governed by eligibility, preferences, merit, medical fitness, and vacancies rather than by the examination score alone.

sections.heading: Eligibility: check the exact post, discipline, age and medical standard
paragraphs: Eligibility is determined by the particular CEN rather than by the exam name alone. Under CEN 05/2025, candidates had to possess the prescribed educational, technical or professional qualification from a recognised institute or university by the application closing date; candidates awaiting final results were not eligible. The post-wise requirements appear in Annexure A, so a diploma or degree should not be assumed eligible unless its discipline is mapped to the intended post.

For the 2025 cycle, the standard age band for the JE/DMS/CMA group was 18–33 years on 1 January 2026. The notice provided upper-age relaxations for specified categories, including SC/ST, OBC-NCL, PwBD, ex-servicemen and certain railway employees. Candidates also need to meet the applicable nationality/citizenship conditions and the medical standard of the posts for which they opt.
bullets: Use the Annexure A post parameters—not coaching-site summaries—to match the diploma/degree branch to the post.

Review the required medical category before applying. Medical fitness, including vision standards for relevant categories, is assessed by Railway Administration; failing the prescribed standard does not lead to an alternative appointment.

Candidates already employed by a Central/State Government department, Railways or a PSU may apply after informing their employer, but shortlisted candidates must produce the required NOC at document verification.

sections.heading: Exam pattern and selection format
paragraphs: CEN 05/2025 specifies two objective, multiple-choice computer-based tests, followed by document verification and a medical examination. CBT-I is common to the notified posts and functions as a screening stage; its normalised score is used to shortlist candidates for CBT-II. CBT-II performance is used for shortlisting to document verification, subject to merit and the candidate’s options.

CBT-I was specified as 100 questions in 90 minutes: Mathematics (30), General Intelligence and Reasoning (25), General Awareness (15), and General Science (30). CBT-II was specified as 150 questions in 120 minutes, covering General Awareness, Physics and Chemistry, computer basics, environment/pollution control, and post-relevant technical abilities. The notice allows indicative section splits to vary in the actual paper.
bullets: Negative marking in CBT is one-third of the marks allotted to a question for each incorrect answer.
For CEN 05/2025, questions were offered in English, Hindi, and 13 listed regional Indian languages; candidates selected their medium in the application.

The latest RRB Chandigarh notice page records that CBT-I for CEN 05/2025 was held on 19, 20 and 25 February 2026, and that CBT-II had been tentatively scheduled for 2 July 2026. Always verify subsequent notices on the relevant official RRB site.

sections.heading: Application process and fee context
paragraphs: RRB applications are made online through the application link published on official RRB websites. The CEN 05/2025 procedure required candidates to create or use an RRB account, select only one RRB, complete the application accurately, upload the required live photograph/signature and documents, pay the applicable fee, and retain the submitted application details. A personal active mobile number and email address are required for OTPs and recruitment communications.

The CEN 05/2025 window is closed: applications were accepted from 31 October through 30 November 2025, with a correction window from 3 to 12 December 2025. Future recruitment dates, fees, correction rules and document requirements must be taken only from the next official CEN.
bullets: CEN 05/2025 charged ₹500 for most candidates, with ₹400 refundable after appearing in CBT-I, less applicable bank charges. It charged ₹250 for SC, ST, ex-servicemen, PwBD, female, transgender, minority and EBC candidates, refundable after appearing in CBT-I, less applicable bank charges. These were cycle-specific fees.
In the 2025 notice, Aadhaar or DigiLocker authentication was strongly advised to facilitate verification; alternative photo-ID verification could involve stricter scrutiny.
Download city intimation, e-call letters and any travel authority only from official RRB links. RRBs warn applicants against fake sites and job touts.

sections.heading: Preparation approach aligned to the official syllabus
paragraphs: Prepare in two layers. First, build speed and accuracy for the CBT-I screening syllabus: mathematics, reasoning, general awareness, and Class 10-level science. Second, devote substantial time to the CBT-II technical syllabus that matches the exam group selected through the eligible engineering discipline; CBT-II also includes general awareness, Class 10-level physics and chemistry, computer basics, and environment/pollution control.

Because incorrect answers attract one-third negative marking, preparation should include timed practice, disciplined question selection, and review of errors—not merely maximising attempts. Use the official CEN’s Annexure VII technical syllabus for the relevant civil, electrical, electronics, mechanical or CMA exam group, and use the RRB-provided practice test when available to become familiar with the CBT interface.
bullets: Create a post-specific checklist from the CEN: eligible qualification, exam group, technical syllabus, medical standard and preferred posts/zones.
Practise CBT-I as a 90-minute, 100-question screening test and CBT-II as a 120-minute, 150-question technical test.
Treat current-affairs material as time-sensitive and update it near the examination date; the official syllabus identifies General Awareness but does not prescribe a fixed current-affairs cutoff.

sections.heading: What selection can lead to
paragraphs: Candidates who clear the applicable CBT stages, document verification and medical examination may be empanelled according to merit, options and vacancy availability. The RRB recommends empanelled candidates, while the concerned Railway Administration issues the offer of appointment. Therefore, passing a CBT or appearing on a shortlist is not itself an appointment guarantee.

For the 2025 CEN, the combined JE/DMS/CMA group was advertised in Pay Level 6 with initial basic pay of ₹35,400. Actual appointment, posting, allowances, training and service conditions depend on the post, railway administration and terms prevailing at appointment. The notice states that selected candidates may undergo prescribed training and receive a stipend during that training period.
bullets: Potential JE workstreams in the notification included civil works, permanent way/bridges, track machines, electrical services, workshops, mechanical carriage-and-wagon work, diesel, and signalling/telecommunication, subject to the vacancies and post parameters notified.
Railway-zone or production-unit allocation follows candidate options, merit, medical fitness and vacancies; an initial posting does not create an automatic right to transfer to another railway.
Document verification compares original supporting documents with application claims. A mismatch or failure to meet qualification, age, category or medical requirements can cancel candidature.
