CEN 05/2025 detailed Centralised Employment Notice (official PDF)

title: RRB NTPC
description: RRB NTPC — govt recruitment exam (general), conducted by Railway Recruitment Boards.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: RRB NTPC is the Railway Recruitment Boards’ (RRBs) recruitment stream for Non-Technical Popular Categories in Indian Railways. Recruitment is issued through Centralised Employment Notices (CENs), with separate Graduate and Undergraduate notices when vacancies are notified.

quick_facts.label: Current recruitment references
quick_facts.value: The latest NTPC notices listed by RRB Chandigarh are CEN 06/2025 for Graduate posts and CEN 07/2025 for Undergraduate posts. The application windows stated on those official notice pages were 21 October–20 November 2025 and 28 October–27 November 2025, respectively; those dates are past as of 19 July 2026.

quick_facts.label: Qualification route
quick_facts.value: In the 2025 NTPC cycle, the Graduate notice is for Graduate NTPC posts and the Undergraduate notice is for Undergraduate NTPC posts. The exact educational, age, medical and typing requirements are post-specific and must be checked in the applicable CEN.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: The NTPC recruitment model uses computer-based testing and, where the notified post requires it, a computer-based aptitude test or typing skill test, followed by document verification and medical examination. The applicable stages vary by post.

quick_facts.label: Official information
quick_facts.value: Candidates should rely on official RRB websites and the relevant CEN rather than social-media notices or third-party application links.

sections.heading: Purpose and jobs covered
paragraphs: RRB NTPC is a large, centralised hiring route for non-technical operational, commercial, clerical and accounts roles in Indian Railways. It is not one permanently open examination: RRBs publish a CEN for a particular recruitment cycle, identify the posts and railway units, and run selection for those notified vacancies.

The node’s child roles align with the usual NTPC split. Undergraduate notices cover roles such as Commercial cum Ticket Clerk, Accounts Clerk cum Typist, Junior Clerk cum Typist and Trains Clerk. Graduate notices cover roles such as Chief Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor, Goods Train Manager, Junior Account Assistant cum Typist, Senior Clerk cum Typist and Station Master. A candidate should treat the specific CEN—not an old syllabus page or salary article—as the controlling document for the posts actually available in a cycle.
bullets: The official RRB recruitment-notice index lists CEN 06/2025 as “NTPC-Graduate Posts” and CEN 07/2025 as “NTPC-Undergraduate Posts.”
Vacancies, railway/zone allocation, category reservation, medical standards and post parameters are recruitment-cycle-specific and may be amended through corrigenda.

sections.heading: Eligibility: choose the correct NTPC level and post
paragraphs: The primary academic distinction is between the Undergraduate and Graduate NTPC notices. The detailed CEN must be read post by post because it specifies the required qualification, age cut-off date, permitted age relaxations, nationality/citizenship conditions, medical standard, and whether computer typing proficiency is required.

For example, the official CEN 06/2024 Undergraduate notice required candidates to use the post-parameter and vacancy tables to determine eligibility; it listed the undergraduate NTPC posts as Commercial cum Ticket Clerk, Accounts Clerk cum Typist, Trains Clerk and Junior Clerk cum Typist. Its structure illustrates why applicants should not assume that a qualification alone makes them eligible for every NTPC post.
bullets: Use the Graduate CEN only for the Graduate posts stated in that notice; use the Undergraduate CEN only for the Undergraduate posts stated in that notice.
For typist-designated posts, confirm the notified computer typing requirement and the applicable typing-skill-test rules.
Check the medical standard for the exact post before ranking preferences; medical suitability is assessed for the post offered.
Do not apply while awaiting a required result where the relevant CEN says the qualification must already be held by its closing date.

sections.heading: Selection format
paragraphs: The standard NTPC pathway is staged. Candidates first sit Computer Based Test (CBT) stages. After CBT-2, candidates for some posts are shortlisted for a post-specific qualifying stage: Station Master-type selections can require a Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT), while typist posts can require a Computer Based Typing Skill Test (CBTST). Shortlisted candidates then proceed to document verification and the required medical examination.

Stages are not interchangeable and not every applicant takes every test. The official result notice for CEN 05/2024 states that CBT-2 shortlisting was for CBAT and TST, demonstrating that the next stage depends on the post and CBT-2 merit. The exact question counts, durations, qualifying thresholds, normalisation and shortlisting ratios must be taken from the CEN for the candidate’s own cycle.
bullets: CBT-1: screening/shortlisting stage under the relevant CEN.
CBT-2: further merit-based stage for shortlisted candidates.
CBAT: applicable only to notified aptitude-test posts.
CBTST: applicable to notified typing posts.
Document verification and medical examination: later selection stages; candidature remains provisional until requirements are met.

sections.heading: Application process and status checking
paragraphs: Apply only when an NTPC CEN is open, using the application route named on official RRB pages. The 2025 Graduate and Undergraduate application windows are already past as of 19 July 2026, so a new applicant should monitor the official RRB employment-notice index for a future NTPC CEN rather than attempt to use an expired link.

When applications are open, the usual process is to create or use the required RRB application account, select one RRB as instructed, complete personal and educational details exactly as supported by records, upload the prescribed materials, pay any applicable fee, submit, and retain the acknowledgement. The CEN controls correction windows, permitted edits, fee/refund terms and deadlines.

For candidates already in CEN 07/2025, the official RRB Chandigarh page reported a revised CBT-1 schedule in June 2026 and stated that exam-city/date information and e-call letters are released through official RRB channels. This is a reminder to check the board’s notice page, registered email and SMS rather than relying on forwarded messages.
bullets: Before applying: download the detailed CEN and verify post parameters, eligibility, medical standard and preferred RRB/railway options.
During the application: use a personal active mobile number and email address and preserve the submitted application/acknowledgement.
After submission: track application status, exam-city information, e-call letter, answer-key/result notices and document-verification instructions on the official RRB website.
Fees, correction charges, dates and refund conditions are variable and should always be read from the active CEN.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Prepare against the syllabus and test instructions in the CEN for the specific recruitment cycle, because the notification defines the actual subjects, scoring rules, negative-marking provisions, qualifying requirements and post-specific tests. Build CBT familiarity by practising timed computer-based multiple-choice questions, then add targeted preparation for CBAT or computer typing only if the selected post requires it.

Use official notices to plan logistics as well as study. RRBs issue the exam-city/date information and e-call letter close to the examination, and may reschedule individual centres or shifts. Candidates should keep identification and eligibility documents consistent with their application data and review official updates before travelling.
bullets: Read the CEN first; make it the master checklist for syllabus, test stages and eligibility evidence.
Practise in CBT conditions: timed sections, on-screen navigation and accuracy under negative-marking rules where notified.
For typist posts, practise computer typing in the language and format prescribed by the applicable CEN.
For aptitude-test posts, use only the official instructions and the CEN to determine whether CBAT applies and how it is evaluated.

sections.heading: Outcomes after selection
paragraphs: A successful NTPC candidate is considered for appointment to the post and railway/production unit for which they are selected under the applicable CEN, subject to merit, vacancy, document verification and medical fitness. Selection is therefore not simply a CBT score: post preferences, eligibility, the required qualifying test where applicable, documents and medical suitability can affect the final outcome.

Pay level and initial pay should be treated as dated notification context, not a guarantee of take-home salary. The 2025 notices and their detailed post tables are the proper sources for the pay level, basic pay and vacancy count for a particular post; allowances, deductions, location and later pay-policy changes affect actual earnings.
bullets: Possible outcomes include appointment to a commercial/ticketing, clerical/accounts, train-operations or station-management role, depending on the notified post and final selection.
Appointment remains conditional on the CEN’s document-verification and medical requirements.
Do not infer a post, railway allocation, pay or joining date from an exam qualification alone; wait for the RRB’s official result/panel and appointment process.

title: RRB Paramedical Staff Recruitment
description: A competitive examination conducted by the Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs) for various paramedical posts in Indian Railways.

quick_facts.label: Recruiting authority
quick_facts.value: Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs) under the Ministry of Railways conduct centralized recruitment for notified Indian Railways paramedical categories.

quick_facts.label: Latest cited recruitment cycle
quick_facts.value: CEN 03/2025 notified seven paramedical categories: Nursing Superintendent, Dialysis Technician, Health & Malaria Inspector Grade II, Pharmacist (Entry Grade), Radiographer X-Ray Technician, ECG Technician, and Laboratory Assistant Grade II.

quick_facts.label: Vacancies in CEN 03/2025
quick_facts.value: The CEN 03/2025 notice listed 434 vacancies across all RRBs. Vacancies are notification-specific and may be increased, decreased, or cancelled by the Railway Administration.

quick_facts.label: Selection method
quick_facts.value: The cited cycle used a single-stage Computer Based Test (CBT), followed by document verification and the prescribed Railway medical examination; empanelment is merit-based subject to completing those requirements.

quick_facts.label: Latest cited cycle status
quick_facts.value: For CEN 03/2025, the CBT was scheduled for March 11–13, 2026, and the RRB Chandigarh CEN page posted CBT result, cut-off, and score-card information on June 5, 2026. Candidates should treat the concerned RRB website and the applicable CEN as authoritative for subsequent stages and new recruitment cycles.

sections.heading: What RRB Paramedical Staff Recruitment is
paragraphs: RRB Paramedical Staff Recruitment is the centralized Railway Recruitment Board route for filling paramedical positions in Indian Railways. It is not a single permanent course examination: the posts, number of vacancies, zones, age bands, medical standards, qualifications, dates, and terms are set separately in each Centralised Employment Notice (CEN). In the cited CEN 03/2025 cycle, the notified posts ranged from Laboratory Assistant Grade II (Level 3) to Nursing Superintendent (Level 7).
bullets: A candidate selects one RRB and gives preferences only for eligible notified posts and railway zones within that chosen RRB.
The RRB’s role is to recommend suitable candidates; the concerned Zonal Railway issues appointment offers, subject to vacancy availability and final eligibility conditions.
A CBT e-call letter or provisional acceptance of an application is not final confirmation of eligibility.

sections.heading: Eligibility: qualification, age, and medical fitness
paragraphs: Eligibility is post-specific. Applicants must possess the stated educational, technical, and professional qualifications from a recognized institution by the notification’s closing date; candidates awaiting final results are not eligible in the cited cycle. They must also meet the nationality, age, disability-suitability, and Railway medical-standard requirements in the applicable CEN.
bullets: Nursing Superintendent: registered nurse and midwife certificate after a three-year General Nursing and Midwifery course recognized by the Indian Nursing Council, or B.Sc. Nursing; CEN 03/2025 specified age 20–40.
Dialysis Technician: B.Sc. plus a diploma in haemodialysis, or two years of satisfactory in-house haemodialysis training/experience; age 20–33 in CEN 03/2025.
Radiographer X-Ray Technician: 10+2 with Physics and Chemistry plus a two-year diploma in Radiography, X-Ray Technician, or Radio-diagnosis Technology; age 19–33 in CEN 03/2025.
ECG Technician: 10+2 or graduation in Science plus a certificate, diploma, or degree in ECG/cardiology technology; the certificate route must be at least one year; age 18–33 in CEN 03/2025.
Laboratory Assistant Grade II: 10+2 Science plus DMLT or an eligible, full-time Medical Laboratory Technology certificate course of at least one year; age 18–33 in CEN 03/2025.

The CEN 03/2025 age cut-off was January 1, 2026. It provided upper-age relaxations, including 5 years for SC/ST candidates and 3 years for OBC-NCL candidates, subject to the notification’s conditions and certificates.
Medical fitness is compulsory. The post’s B1, C1, or C2 standard may include visual-acuity and other requirements; failure to meet the prescribed standard prevents empanelment for that post.

sections.heading: Examination and selection format
paragraphs: The cited CEN 03/2025 format was a single-stage objective multiple-choice CBT of 90 minutes for 100 questions. Eligible PwBD candidates using the scribe facility received 120 minutes. The question standard is generally aligned to the minimum professional or technical qualification for the relevant post.
bullets: Professional ability: 70 questions / 70 marks.
General Awareness: 10 questions / 10 marks.
General Arithmetic, General Intelligence and Reasoning: 10 questions / 10 marks.
General Science: 10 questions / 10 marks.
Negative marking: one-third of the mark assigned to a question is deducted for each wrong answer.
Minimum qualifying marks in the cited notice were 40% for UR/EWS, 30% for OBC and SC, and 25% for ST, with the stated PwBD provision if sufficient candidates were unavailable.
The recruitment sequence is CBT, document verification, and the prescribed medical examination; final empanelment depends on merit, successful verification, and medical fitness.

sections.heading: How to apply when a new CEN opens
paragraphs: Apply only through the link published on an official RRB website for the relevant CEN. In CEN 03/2025, applicants created or reused an RRB account, used a valid personal mobile number and active email address for OTPs, selected one RRB, chose eligible posts/zones in preference order, completed the live-photo and signature requirements, and paid the fee before the notified deadline. Multiple applications to the same or different RRBs could lead to rejection and debarment.
bullets: Read Annexure A for post parameters and Annexure B for RRB- and zone-wise vacancies before submitting preferences.

Recheck entries before submission: the cited notice stated that no correction could be made after submission, while account-creation details and the chosen RRB could not be changed in the modification window.

For dated fee context only: CEN 03/2025 charged ₹500 for most applicants, with ₹400 refundable after appearing in CBT less applicable bank charges; SC, ST, Ex-Servicemen, PwBD, female, transgender, minority, and EBC candidates paid ₹250, refundable after appearing in CBT less applicable bank charges. Future CENs may differ.

Download city/date information and the CBT e-call letter from the official RRB site; in the cited cycle, city information was to be available about 10 days before the CBT and the e-call letter about 4 days before.
The original CEN 03/2025 closing date of September 8, 2025 was extended by corrigendum to September 18, 2025. Those dates are past and do not establish a deadline for a future cycle.

sections.heading: Preparation strategy tied to the official syllabus
paragraphs: Preparation should prioritize professional ability because it carried 70 of 100 marks in CEN 03/2025. Start by matching your study plan to the syllabus for the exact post, then add daily practice for arithmetic, reasoning, general awareness, and secondary-school-level general science. Use timed objective-question practice because wrong answers attracted one-third negative marking in the cited cycle.
bullets: For nursing posts, revise anatomy, physiology, nutrition, microbiology, pharmacology, pathology, medical-surgical nursing, community health nursing, child health nursing, mental health nursing, midwifery, research/statistics, and nursing management.

For radiography, emphasize radiology and radiation physics, X-ray equipment and image processing, positioning, modern imaging, contrast/special procedures, patient care, quality control, and radiation safety.
For laboratory posts, cover medical laboratory technology fundamentals, microbiology, clinical biochemistry, pathology and histopathology, haematology, and blood-bank topics.

For the common portions, practice arithmetic topics such as percentage, ratio, time and work, algebra and mensuration; reasoning topics such as series, coding-decoding, syllogisms and data interpretation; and general science up to the CBSE Class 10 level.

Use the official RRB mock/practice test when made available, and prepare to take the test in the language option selected in the application; CEN 03/2025 offered English, Hindi, and 13 listed regional Indian languages.

sections.heading: What selection can lead to
paragraphs: Successful candidates can be empanelled for the paramedical post, Railway zone, and production unit allotted according to CBT merit, stated preferences, medical fitness, and vacancies at panel preparation. The RRB does not guarantee a particular post or location merely because it was preferred; appointment follows final verification and an offer from the relevant Zonal Railway.
bullets: For CEN 03/2025, initial basic pay was ₹44,900 for Nursing Superintendent (Level 7); ₹35,400 for Dialysis Technician and Health & Malaria Inspector Grade II (Level 6); ₹29,200 for Pharmacist and Radiographer X-Ray Technician (Level 5); ₹25,500 for ECG Technician (Level 4); and ₹21,700 for Laboratory Assistant Grade II (Level 3). These are dated notification figures, not a promise for future CENs or an estimate of take-home pay.
Shortlisting for document verification and empanelment is based on CBT merit, subject to minimum qualifying marks and the notification’s rules.

Original qualification, identity, category, and other supporting documents are checked at document verification. A candidate who cannot produce required originals on the date of verification can forfeit candidature.

Passing the Railway medical test is essential. The notification states that a candidate who fails the prescribed medical standard will not be empanelled for that post and will not receive an alternate Railway appointment on that basis.

CEN 03/2025 detailed notification and post parameters

title: SAT
description: SAT — abroad exam (general), conducted by College Board.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: College Board administers the SAT, a standardized admissions test used by colleges and other educational institutions.

quick_facts.label: Primary use
quick_facts.value: For an Indian student applying abroad for undergraduate study, the SAT can be submitted where a university accepts or requires it; each institution sets its own admissions and testing policy, and some institutions are test-optional.

quick_facts.label: Delivery mode
quick_facts.value: The SAT is delivered digitally in College Board’s Bluebook application at a test center. Approved devices include Windows laptops/tablets, Mac laptops, iPads, and school-managed Chromebooks; personal Chromebooks and phones are not supported.

quick_facts.label: Test structure
quick_facts.value: The test has Reading and Writing (54 questions, 64 minutes) and Math (44 questions, 70 minutes): 98 questions/tasks and 2 hours 14 minutes of testing time, plus a 10-minute break.

quick_facts.label: Scoring
quick_facts.value: The total SAT score is 400–1600, comprising Reading and Writing and Math section scores of 200–800 each. The digital SAT uses a multistage adaptive design with two modules in each section.

quick_facts.label: India-specific note
quick_facts.value: Students testing in India register online for international testing. College Board’s international policy states that Sunday testing is not available in India.

quick_facts.label: International fee context
quick_facts.value: As listed by College Board for the 2026–27 cycle, the SAT registration fee is US$68 plus a US$43 international fee. Fees, exchange-rate costs, test-center charges, and refund/change charges can change, so applicants should confirm the live fee page before paying.

quick_facts.label: Score timing
quick_facts.value: Weekend SAT scores are typically available online 2–4 weeks after the test date; applicants should plan around the score-reporting and university-application timelines for their own intake.

sections.heading: What the SAT is for in an abroad-undergraduate pathway
paragraphs: The SAT is an admissions assessment that can support applications to bachelor’s-level programmes abroad, including arts, business, computer science, engineering, and broader undergraduate degrees. It is not itself an admission offer, a degree qualification, or a substitute for school-leaving results, English-language requirements, essays, recommendations, portfolios, visas, or other documents that a particular university may require.

For applicants from Indian curricula such as CBSE, CISCE, state boards, IB, or A Levels, the relevant decision is not whether the SAT is tied to a PCM stream, but whether each target university and programme accepts, recommends, requires, or does not consider SAT scores for the intended entry year. EducationUSA notes that there is no single U.S. national college entrance examination that every applicant must pass; individual institutions set their own requirements, and test-optional institutions may allow applicants to submit scores if they think the scores strengthen the application.
bullets: Check the admissions page for every university and course—not just the university-wide homepage—for its current testing policy and application deadline.
Treat an SAT score as one component of a holistic application where the institution considers it; do not infer a guaranteed admission outcome from any particular score.
Use the SAT mainly where it is accepted and strategically useful for the chosen overseas destination and intake.

sections.heading: Who should consider taking it
paragraphs: College Board’s weekend-registration instructions are built around choosing a test date and centre, creating or signing in to a College Board account, entering registration information, and uploading a compliant photo. The published process does not make PCM, a particular Indian school board, or a completed Class 12 qualification a general registration prerequisite. In practice, students commonly plan their test around university application timing rather than a fixed academic-eligibility threshold.

A student should take the SAT only after confirming that it is relevant to the target institutions. Test-optional does not mean test-blind: a university may permit score submission without requiring it. Conversely, a university may change its policy by admission cycle, programme, applicant category, or campus.
bullets: Choose an intended application cycle and verify each target programme’s policy before registering.
Ensure the legal name in the College Board account, registration, admission ticket, and acceptable photo ID matches exactly; a mismatch can prevent admission to the test centre.

Students needing disability-related accommodations should start the College Board accommodation process early; the official practice guidance says requests should be submitted at least seven weeks before test day.

sections.heading: Digital format, content, timing, and scores
paragraphs: The digital SAT has two sections. Reading and Writing contains 54 questions in two 32-minute modules; Math contains 44 questions in two 35-minute modules. The testing time is 134 minutes (2 hours 14 minutes), with a 10-minute break between sections. Most questions are multiple choice; some Math questions require a student-produced answer.

The assessment is multistage adaptive. All students begin with a mixed-difficulty first module in each section. Performance in that module helps determine the difficulty mix in the second module; College Board calculates the section score using performance across both modules. Once a student leaves a module, they cannot return to it.

Scores are reported as a 400–1600 total, made from two 200–800 section scores. A “good” or competitive score is not universal: applicants should compare their results with the score information and admissions policy published by each specific university, while recognising that the institution evaluates other application evidence as well.
bullets: Reading and Writing: 64 minutes; 54 questions.
Math: 70 minutes; 44 questions.
Total: 98 questions/tasks; 134 minutes of testing time.
The test runs in Bluebook; an embedded calculator is available for Math, alongside permitted personal calculators.

sections.heading: Registration and test-day process for students in India
paragraphs: Start by mapping university application deadlines backwards from the expected score-release date. College Board publishes test dates and registration deadlines for U.S. and international students, with deadlines expressed in U.S. Eastern Time. As of the published 2026–27 schedule, dates and deadlines may be revised, so the live College Board schedule and test-centre availability—not a coaching-centre calendar—should be the source of record.

Register through the student’s own College Board account. The online process includes choosing a date and centre, entering identifying information, and uploading a compliant photo. College Board advises considering multiple test centres because a preferred centre may not have seats available. International test takers, including those in India, register online.

Before test day, install Bluebook on an approved device and complete exam setup 1–5 days before the test. Bring the fully charged device, up-to-date admission ticket, an acceptable physical photo ID, College Board credentials, and permitted writing materials. If a student needs to borrow a College Board device, the request must be made at least 30 days before test day. Internet supplied by the test centre is needed to start the test and submit answers.

International cost is variable. College Board lists a US$68 base registration fee and a US$43 international fee for the 2026–27 period, with possible extra charges for late registration, changes, cancellation, particular centres, and later score reports. Verify current fees and whether a chosen centre has an additional centre fee immediately before payment.
bullets: 1. Confirm test policy and application deadlines for each target university and intake.
2. Select a SAT date that leaves time for score release and, if needed, a retake.
3. Create/sign in to a College Board account and register personally for a centre with available seating.
4. Install Bluebook and complete exam setup before test day; arrange a compliant device or request lending early.
5. Check the exact name and photo-ID requirements, then take the admission ticket and physical ID to the centre.
6. After scores are released, send scores only to the institutions or scholarship organisations selected by the student, following their required timelines.

sections.heading: A practical official-preparation plan
paragraphs: Begin with College Board’s Bluebook test preview and a timed full-length digital practice test. This is important because the SAT’s digital tools, timing, two-module sections, and adaptive structure differ from a paper test. After a Bluebook practice test, students can review their results and questions in My Practice, then use the identified weak skills to plan targeted study.

College Board links official SAT preparation on Khan Academy, which provides skill practice, lessons, videos, diagnostics, quizzes, and tests. Its Student Question Bank also provides official questions that can be filtered by section, domain, skill, and difficulty. These first-party resources are especially useful for avoiding outdated material designed for earlier paper SAT formats.

Preparation should include both content and operations: practise the current test format, learn the Bluebook tools and calculator, solve timed modules, analyse recurring errors, and complete exam setup on the actual device planned for test day. A practice score is diagnostic rather than a guarantee of a particular official result.
bullets: Take an initial full-length Bluebook practice test under timed conditions.
Turn the score report into a short list of Reading and Writing and Math skills to improve.
Use official Khan Academy and Student Question Bank practice for focused drills, then retest under timed conditions.
Complete at least one full practice session using the same type of approved device intended for test day.

Do not rely solely on old paper-SAT books: College Board says paper practice materials are not identical to the digital test and are mainly relevant for approved paper-format accommodations or extra sample questions.

sections.heading: Using results in overseas applications
paragraphs: College Board states that weekend SAT scores are typically available online two to four weeks after testing. The student can then send scores to colleges, scholarship organisations, and other educational institutions. College Board delivers scores electronically to colleges on a rolling basis, but an institution’s own processing time may vary; applicants should not wait until a university deadline to investigate score-reporting rules.

Students can select score recipients during registration or the test process and can later send scores to additional institutions. College Board’s current international-fee page states that the first four score reports are free if ordered by nine days after the test date, while later additional reports have a listed fee; this is a time-sensitive policy and should be checked at the time of testing.

The practical outcome is an application credential, not an automatic route to a foreign bachelor’s degree. The applicant still needs to meet the target university’s complete entry requirements, including academic records and any programme-specific, English-language, financial-aid, immigration, or portfolio requirements. Where a university is test-optional, decide whether to submit based on that institution’s current policy and the overall strength of the application.
bullets: Download and review the official score report when released.
Match score-reporting timing to every university’s deadline and policy.
Send only to institutions or scholarship programmes the student has chosen.
Keep SAT planning separate from visa, financial documentation, English-proficiency testing, and final school-exam planning, which are governed by different organisations and requirements.

EducationUSA guidance on U.S. undergraduate standardized tests

title: SBI Clerk (Junior Associate)
description: SBI Clerk (Junior Associate) — govt recruitment exam (finance), conducted by SBI.

quick_facts.label: Conducting employer and post
quick_facts.value: State Bank of India (SBI) recruits Junior Associates (Customer Support & Sales) in its clerical cadre through this recruitment process.

quick_facts.label: Latest verified reference cycle
quick_facts.value: The latest detailed SBI Junior Associate notice located was Advertisement No. CRPD/CR/2025-26/06, dated August 6, 2025. Its online-registration window was August 6–26, 2025; applicants should treat those dates as historical, not as a current application deadline.

quick_facts.label: Core eligibility in the 2025–26 notice
quick_facts.value: Indian citizens with a graduation degree in any discipline from a recognised university (or a Central Government-recognised equivalent) were eligible; final-year/semester students could apply provisionally if they could prove graduation by December 31, 2025. The stated age band was 20–28 years as of April 1, 2025, with category-specific upper-age relaxations.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: The 2025–26 process comprised online Preliminary and Main examinations plus a specified local-language test where applicable. Preliminary marks did not count toward the final merit list; Main-exam aggregate marks were used for selection, subject to eligibility verification and local-language requirements.

quick_facts.label: State/UT and local-language rule
quick_facts.value: For the 2025–26 recruitment, a candidate could apply for vacancies in only one State/UT and needed proficiency in that State/UT's specified local language. A Class 10 or 12 record showing study of that language exempted the candidate from the language test; otherwise the test was required after provisional selection and before joining.

quick_facts.label: Fee context
quick_facts.value: In the 2025–26 notice, the non-refundable application fee/intimation charge was nil for SC/ST/PwBD/XS/DXS candidates and ₹750 for General/OBC/EWS candidates. Fees can change in a future notification.

quick_facts.label: Compensation context
quick_facts.value: The August 2025 notice stated a starting basic pay of ₹26,730 for graduate Junior Associates and approximate starting monthly emoluments of ₹46,000 in a metro such as Mumbai, inclusive of then-current allowances. SBI stated that allowances vary by posting location, so this is dated context rather than a current salary guarantee.

sections.heading: What the SBI Clerk / Junior Associate exam is for
paragraphs: “SBI Clerk” is the commonly used name for SBI’s recruitment of Junior Associates (Customer Support & Sales) in the clerical cadre. SBI describes Junior Associates as a clerical-cadre entry route for young graduates. The role is customer-facing: the 2025–26 notice says recruits are expected to make customer calls, provide banking and advisory services, cross-sell products, and may have outdoor travel, flexible hours, or shift work depending on requirements.

The examination is therefore a recruitment selection process rather than an academic entrance examination. SBI publishes recruitment notices, application links, results, and later announcements through its official Careers pages; a fresh notice is the controlling source for a future cycle.
bullets: The recruitment is State/UT-specific: candidates in the 2025–26 cycle could choose only one State/UT.
There was no inter-circle/inter-state transfer provision for Junior Associates recruited under that notice, subject to limited intra-state exceptions specified by SBI.
SBI identifies Junior Associate as a clerical-cadre role and says eligible employees can seek promotion to the officer cadre after three years of service.

sections.heading: Eligibility: use the next notification as the final authority
paragraphs: The 2025–26 notice required Indian citizenship and graduation in any discipline from a recognised university or an equivalent qualification recognised by the Central Government. Integrated dual-degree candidates needed to have passed by the notice’s stipulated date; final-year/semester candidates were allowed to apply provisionally but had to produce proof of passing by December 31, 2025 if selected. The notice also recognised specified education certificates held by matriculate ex-servicemen with at least 15 years of Union Armed Forces service.

For that cycle, the age requirement was 20 to 28 years on April 1, 2025 (birth dates April 2, 1997 through April 1, 2005, inclusive). Upper-age relaxation was stated for OBC, SC/ST, PwBD, ex-servicemen/disabled ex-servicemen, eligible widowed/divorced/judicially separated women, and specified SBI trained apprentices. Exact cut-off dates and relaxation rules must be rechecked against the next advertisement.

Applicants for a State/UT vacancy had to be able to read, write, speak, and understand the specified local language. Those who could show a Class 10 or 12 marksheet/certificate evidencing study of the language did not have to take the local-language test; other provisionally selected candidates had to qualify it before appointment.
bullets: The 2025–26 notice provided 4% horizontal reservation for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities, subject to the notice’s post-suitability and documentation conditions.
Candidates already working in SBI’s clerical cadre, and people previously employed in SBI’s clerical cadre who resigned, were ineligible under that specific recruitment project.
Selection and appointment remained subject to document/eligibility verification, medical fitness, and SBI’s Know Your Employee formalities.

sections.heading: Exam format and how merit was determined in the 2025–26 notice
paragraphs: The verified 2025–26 pattern had two online objective-test stages. Preliminary examination was 100 questions for 100 marks in one hour: English Language (30 questions, 30 marks, 20 minutes), Numerical Ability (35, 35, 20 minutes), and Reasoning Ability (35, 35, 20 minutes). SBI applied a one-fourth-mark penalty for each wrong objective-test answer and stated that it did not maintain sectional marks or prescribe a preliminary minimum qualifying score.

The Main examination was 190 questions for 200 marks in two hours 40 minutes: General/Financial Awareness (50 questions, 50 marks, 35 minutes), General English (40, 40, 35 minutes), Quantitative Aptitude (50, 50, 45 minutes), and Reasoning Ability & Computer Aptitude (50, 60, 45 minutes). It also carried a one-fourth-mark wrong-answer penalty. SBI could set an aggregate qualifying standard, with the stated 5% relaxation for listed reserved categories; no individual-subject qualifying mark was prescribed.

SBI shortlisted candidates for Main examination from the preliminary aggregate ranking, approximately 10 times vacancies subject to availability. Preliminary marks were not added to the final merit list. State- and category-wise merit was based on Main-exam aggregate marks, then remained subject to eligibility checks and, where needed, the local-language test.
bullets: The question-paper medium depended on the State/UT applied for; English was used for English sections, while other tests were offered in the listed State/UT languages as applicable.
The 2025–26 local-language assessment for applicable candidates included non-verbal objective and subjective components plus a verbal test.
Exam structure, duration, languages, score rules, and shortlisting ratios may be revised by SBI in a future recruitment.

sections.heading: Application process and practical checklist
paragraphs: When SBI opens a Junior Associate recruitment, application is online only through the SBI Careers current-openings page. In the 2025–26 process, candidates registered online, uploaded a photograph, signature, left-thumb impression, and handwritten declaration, checked the form, paid online through debit card, credit card, or internet banking where a fee applied, and retained the e-receipt and completed form. SBI stated that no printout of the application form had to be sent to the bank.

The 2025–26 form allowed a saved application to be reopened and edited up to three times before final submission. After submission, changes were not allowed. Candidates needed an active email address and mobile number through results, because SBI used those channels for call-letter and related communications.

For the examinations, the notice required the downloadable call letter, appropriate photographs, and an original photo identity proof plus self-attested copy. For the Main examination, shortlisted candidates also had to bring their authenticated Preliminary call letter and authenticated identity-proof copy. SBI advised candidates to rely on its Careers site for announcements rather than assuming a yearly schedule.
bullets: Before submitting, confirm the chosen State/UT, local language, category, personal details, graduation status, and document uploads; the notice says corrections are not entertained after final submission.
The 2025–26 fee was nil for SC/ST/PwBD/XS/DXS and ₹750 for General/OBC/EWS; it was non-refundable. Do not assume the same fee in a later cycle.
Avoid third-party application portals: SBI identifies its authorised Careers website as the channel for announcements and applications.

sections.heading: Preparation aligned to the official pattern
paragraphs: Build preparation around the two timed online objective tests in the latest verified notice. For Preliminary examination, practise English Language, Numerical Ability, and Reasoning Ability in separate 20-minute blocks. For Main examination, add General/Financial Awareness, General English, Quantitative Aptitude, and Reasoning Ability & Computer Aptitude under the specified sectional time limits. Timed practice is particularly important because both stages used separately timed sections.

Use accuracy as well as speed: the 2025–26 notice imposed a one-fourth-mark deduction for each wrong answer in objective tests. Candidates should therefore practise deciding when to attempt, skip, and return within the permitted section time, rather than treating the exam solely as a question-volume test.

Prepare the specified State/UT local language early. Candidates without Class 10 or 12 evidence of studying that language could be required to take the local-language test after provisional selection and before joining. SBI also offered online pre-examination training for eligible SC/ST/OBC/ex-servicemen/PwBD candidates who opted for it in the application.
bullets: Use the official “Acquaint Yourself” booklet issued with the call letter for the live cycle’s operational instructions and test details.
Practise with the language medium applicable to the State/UT selected in the notice.
Do not bring prohibited devices: the 2025–26 notice barred mobile phones, smart watches, pagers, calculators, and similar communication devices at the venue.

sections.heading: What selection leads to
paragraphs: A successful candidate is provisionally selected as a Junior Associate (Customer Support & Sales) in SBI’s clerical cadre for the State/UT applied for, subject to document verification, local-language qualification where applicable, medical fitness, and other joining formalities. The 2025–26 notice provided for a minimum six-month probation period, required prescribed e-learning during probation for confirmation, and allowed SBI to extend probation where completion or performance requirements were not met.

As dated compensation context only, the August 2025 notice stated a pay scale beginning at ₹24,050 and a graduate entrant’s starting basic pay of ₹26,730 after two advance increments. It estimated starting emoluments at about ₹46,000 per month in a metro such as Mumbai, inclusive of allowances at the then-current rates; SBI expressly noted that allowances vary by place of posting.

SBI’s Careers site describes a longer-term pathway: Junior Associates may be eligible for promotion to the officer cadre after three years of service. This is an employer-stated opportunity, not a guarantee of promotion, which remains governed by applicable service and promotion rules.
bullets: The 2025–26 notice described customer service, banking/advisory services, marketing and cross-selling responsibilities, and possible outdoor travel, flexible hours, or shifts.
The notice stated that final merit used Main-exam performance, not Preliminary marks.
The 2025–26 process could maintain a State/category-wise waitlist of up to 50% of vacancies for one year from final-result declaration; this should not be assumed for a future cycle.

title: SBI PO
description: SBI PO — govt recruitment exam (finance), conducted by SBI.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: SBI PO is State Bank of India’s recruitment process for appointment as Probationary Officers; the 2025–26 notification invited online applications from eligible Indian citizens.

quick_facts.label: Qualification benchmark
quick_facts.value: In the 2025–26 cycle, SBI required a graduation degree in any discipline from a recognised university (or a Central Government-recognised equivalent); final-year/semester students could apply provisionally, subject to passing by the stipulated date.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: The 2025–26 process had three phases: online Preliminary Examination, online Main Examination, and Phase III comprising a psychometric test, group exercise, and personal interview.

quick_facts.label: 2025–26 application window
quick_facts.value: For the 2025–26 notification, online registration and fee payment ran from 24 June 2025 through 14 July 2025. This is historic, cycle-specific information—not a future deadline.

quick_facts.label: Where to verify notices
quick_facts.value: SBI states that recruitment notices, schedules, results, and related information are published through its official careers sites; candidates should rely on those sites rather than purported selection letters or lists from other sources.

sections.heading: Purpose and role
paragraphs: SBI PO is a competitive hiring route into State Bank of India’s officer cadre. SBI’s 2025–26 advertisement describes recruitment for appointment as Probationary Officers and says selected candidates may be posted anywhere in India. On joining, selected candidates are designated Probationary Officers and may be placed on probation under the bank’s policy.
source_urls
bullets: The role is an entry route to Junior Management Grade Scale-I after successful completion of the recruitment, joining, and probation requirements.
The notification-specific terms matter: SBI can alter vacancies or the process, and appointment remains subject to document, antecedent, and medical verification.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: Eligibility must be checked against the advertisement for the particular cycle. In the 2025–26 cycle, applicants had to be Indian citizens, be 21–30 years old as of 1 April 2025, and hold a graduate degree in any discipline from a recognised university or an equivalent qualification recognised by the Central Government. Final-year students could apply provisionally if they met the notification’s proof-of-passing deadline.
source_urls
bullets: For 2025–26, the upper-age relaxation stated was 3 years for OBC (Non-Creamy Layer), 5 years for SC/ST, and 10/13/15 years for PwBD candidates in UR/EWS, OBC, and SC/ST categories respectively; other specified categories also had provisions. These details can change by notification.
The 2025–26 notice capped attempts at 4 for UR/EWS, 7 for UR/EWS PwBD/OBC/OBC PwBD, and imposed no restriction for SC/ST categories; appearing only in prelims did not count as an attempt.
Candidates seeking reserved-category benefits or age relaxation had to provide prescribed valid certificates at verification; the current cycle’s notice controls.

sections.heading: Exam and selection format
paragraphs: The 2025–26 SBI PO selection process used a three-phase design. Phase I was a one-hour online preliminary objective test: English Language (40 questions), Quantitative Aptitude (30), and Reasoning Ability (30), each with a separate 20-minute time limit. SBI shortlisted approximately ten times the category-wise vacancies to the main examination based on preliminary merit, without a sectional cut-off at prelim level.

The online Main Examination comprised a 200-mark objective test over three hours and a 50-mark, 30-minute descriptive communication-skills test typed on the computer. Phase III included a psychometric test, group exercise, and personal interview. In the 2025–26 scheme, final merit used Main Examination and Phase III marks—not Preliminary Examination marks—and objective-test wrong answers attracted a one-quarter-mark penalty.
source_urls
bullets: 2025–26 Main objective subjects: Reasoning & Computer Aptitude; Data Analysis & Interpretation; General Awareness/Economy/Banking Knowledge; and English Language.
The 2025–26 descriptive component covered emails, reports, situation analysis, and précis writing, subject to the detailed instructions and corrigenda for that cycle.

SBI provides scribe and compensatory-time provisions for eligible candidates under the applicable rules; candidates needing them should declare this in the online application and follow the notification’s documentation requirements.

sections.heading: Application process
paragraphs: Apply only through the SBI careers portal when a relevant PO application link is live. For the 2025–26 cycle, SBI accepted online applications only; applicants registered online, uploaded the prescribed photograph, signature, thumb impression, and handwritten declaration, checked the form before final submission, and paid online through the integrated payment gateway. SBI stated that changes were not allowed after final submission.

The 2025–26 fee was ₹750 for UR/EWS/OBC applicants and nil for SC/ST/PwBD applicants; this was non-refundable. It is dated, cycle-specific fee context and must be rechecked in the next notification. SBI required an active email address and mobile number through declaration of results for communications and call letters.
source_urls
bullets: Read the detailed advertisement before applying; preserve the registration number, password, e-receipt, and submitted application printout.
Use only official SBI careers domains to check application links, corrigenda, call letters, schedules, and results.
The 2025–26 application dates—24 June to 14 July 2025—have passed and should not be treated as an upcoming window.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Build preparation around the official, notification-specific test structure rather than assuming an older syllabus or pattern remains unchanged. For the 2025–26 pattern, this means practising timed prelims across English, quantitative aptitude, and reasoning; then preparing for the longer main objective sections, banking/economy awareness, and computer-typed descriptive communication tasks. Because the official scheme used separate section timings and negative marking in objective tests, timed practice and accuracy control are directly relevant.

Before each exam, read SBI’s official “Acquaint Yourself” booklet and the call letter carefully. The booklets describe the online assessment and venue requirements, including identity documentation and restrictions on items such as calculators, phones, notes, and smart watches.
source_urls
bullets: Use the official preliminary and main booklets to familiarise yourself with online-test instructions and document requirements.
Practise the main descriptive formats specified in the current notice; in 2025–26 these included email, report, situation-analysis, and précis tasks.
Track SBI’s official current-openings and recruitment-results pages for amendments, as SBI says changes and updates are hosted on its website.

sections.heading: Selection outcomes and employment context
paragraphs: Candidates who qualify through the process and complete appointment formalities may join SBI as Probationary Officers. Under the 2025–26 notice, selected candidates had to complete an online basic-banking course before joining, execute a ₹2 lakh service bond for a minimum three-year period, and could be on probation for two years with continuous assessment before confirmation in Junior Management Grade Scale-I. These are notification-specific employment terms and should be checked again for any subsequent recruitment.

As dated salary context only, the 2025–26 notice listed starting basic pay of ₹48,480 plus four advance increments, and an approximate initial Mumbai-centre CTC of ₹20.43 lakh, with allowances and benefits governed by rules in force. Pay, location-based CTC, benefits, bond terms, and probation terms are variable and should not be assumed for a later cycle.
source_urls
bullets: Final selection in 2025–26 required qualifying separately in Main Examination and Phase III; SBI formed final merit from normalized Main and Phase III marks.
Appointment remained conditional on verification of credentials and other formalities, including medical examination and antecedent verification.
SBI stated that officers may be posted anywhere in India.

title: SEBI Grade A
description: SEBI Grade A — govt recruitment exam (finance), conducted by SEBI.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body and post
quick_facts.value: SEBI (the Securities and Exchange Board of India) recruits Indian citizens as Officer Grade A (Assistant Manager) through stream-specific recruitment exercises.

quick_facts.label: Latest documented cycle status
quick_facts.value: The 2025 Grade A cycle is no longer accepting applications: its application window was October 30–November 28, 2025; SEBI published the selected-candidates list on June 23, 2026 and final Phase II/cut-off and selected-candidate information in July 2026. A future notification should be treated as a new cycle with its own dates and rules.

quick_facts.label: Recruitment streams
quick_facts.value: The 2025 exercise covered General, Legal, Information Technology, Research, Official Language, Engineering (Electrical), and Engineering (Civil) streams. Vacancies and streams can change in a later notification.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: The 2025 process had three stages: Phase I online screening (two papers), Phase II online examination (two papers), and an interview.

quick_facts.label: Age context
quick_facts.value: For the 2025 notification, candidates could not be older than 30 on September 30, 2025 (born on or after October 1, 1995), with category-based relaxations under the stated rules. The applicable cut-off date and relaxations must be checked in the next notification.

quick_facts.label: Application fee context
quick_facts.value: In the 2025 cycle, the non-refundable charge was ₹1,000 plus 18% GST for Unreserved/OBC/EWS candidates and ₹100 plus 18% GST for SC/ST/PwBD candidates. Fees are cycle-specific and may change.

sections.heading: What SEBI Grade A is for
paragraphs: SEBI Grade A is a competitive recruitment route into SEBI at the Officer Grade A (Assistant Manager) level. SEBI describes itself as the statutory body created to protect investors, promote the development of the securities market, and regulate that market; Grade A recruitment therefore supports work in a financial-market regulator rather than admission to an academic programme.

Work assignments can range across policy formulation, intermediary registration, inspection, supervision, investigation, and adjudication. SEBI states that the work profile also depends on the recruited stream, and that officers may be posted or transferred anywhere in India where SEBI has offices.
bullets: Choose the stream that matches the qualification requirements in the specific advertisement; the General stream and specialist streams have different Paper 2 content and eligibility rules.
Do not assume that a vacancy is annual. Follow SEBI's official Careers/Vacancies pages for a new notice.

sections.heading: Eligibility: check the notification and stream
paragraphs: Eligibility is stream-specific. In the 2025 notification, the General stream accepted a master's degree or two-year postgraduate diploma in any discipline, a law or engineering bachelor's degree, or qualifications such as CA, CFA, CS, or Cost Accountant. Legal required a law bachelor's degree; IT accepted an engineering bachelor's degree in any branch or a bachelor's degree plus a qualifying two-year postgraduate computer science/computer application/IT qualification.

The 2025 notice also set distinct specialist qualifications for Research, Official Language, Electrical Engineering, and Civil Engineering streams. Candidates in final examinations could sit Phases I and II, but candidates who reached the interview had to produce evidence that they had obtained the required qualification. Requirements, age cut-off dates, experience treatment, reservations, and PwBD provisions must be verified against the live advertisement.

For the 2025 cycle, the upper age limit was 30 years as of September 30, 2025, with stated relaxations including up to five years for SC/ST candidates and up to three years for eligible OBC candidates where posts were reserved. This is dated policy context, not a standing guarantee for later cycles.
bullets: Read the table for the exact stream before applying; a relevant-looking degree alone may not meet the notified wording.
Ensure category, disability, and experience documents meet the notification's dates and formats before applying.
Use SEBI's official opportunity page only as a high-level guide; the advertisement for the open cycle controls.

sections.heading: Exam format: 2025 cycle reference
paragraphs: In the 2025 notification, Phase I was an online screening examination with two 100-mark multiple-choice papers. Paper 1, common to all streams, covered General Awareness including the financial sector, English Language, Quantitative Aptitude, and Reasoning. Paper 2 tested General-stream subjects—Commerce, Accountancy, Management, Finance, Costing, Companies Act, and Economics—or the relevant specialist subject for the other streams.

The 2025 Phase I timing was 60 minutes for Paper 1 and 40 minutes for Paper 2. It prescribed a 30% Paper 1 minimum, a 40% Paper 2 minimum, and a 40% aggregate threshold; one-quarter negative marking applied to both papers. Phase I marks were used for shortlisting rather than final selection.

For Phase II in 2025, Paper 1 was a 100-mark, 60-minute descriptive English test for drafting skills, weighted one-third; Paper 2 was 100 marks and generally weighted two-thirds, with a 40% minimum. The Phase II aggregate threshold was 50%, and the notice provided that up to three times the vacancies would be shortlisted by merit for interview. In final selection, Phase II carried 85% and the interview 15%; the notice also specified limited experience weightage for certain streams. SEBI may modify procedures, so this should be used as a preparation baseline rather than a promise of the next format.
bullets: All question papers except the English test were set bilingually in Hindi and English in the 2025 notice.
Download the current Phase I and Phase II information handouts when SEBI publishes them; they provide candidate-facing test instructions in addition to the advertisement.

sections.heading: How to apply when the next notification opens
paragraphs: For the 2025 exercise, SEBI directed applicants to its website, then Careers, then the Grade A recruitment notification, and then the “Apply Online” option. Registration generated a provisional registration number and password, after which candidates completed, checked, submitted, and paid for the application online. The 2025 application period has passed, so prospective applicants should wait for an official future notice rather than use third-party application links.

The 2025 notice required a valid personal email address and mobile number to remain active through the recruitment process. It also required specified uploads, including photograph, signature, left-thumb impression, and handwriting declaration; unclear or incorrectly uploaded images could lead to rejection. Candidates were advised to print the system-generated application after registration.
bullets: Begin from SEBI's official Careers page and confirm the notice title, dates, stream, and application link.
Keep the registration credentials, submitted application, payment proof, and call-letter notices securely available.
Check fee, document dimensions, identity-proof rules, examination-centre choices, and accommodation provisions in the live notice, because these can change.

sections.heading: Preparation plan aligned to the notified structure
paragraphs: Start with the official advertisement's annexure and the relevant stream syllabus. For the 2025 General stream, this means preparing the Phase I/II Paper 2 domains of Commerce, Accountancy, Management, Finance, Costing, Companies Act, and Economics; for specialist streams, prioritize the notified technical syllabus. Pair this with timed practice for Phase I Paper 1's financial-sector awareness, English, quantitative aptitude, and reasoning.

Treat Phase II English as a separate skill: the 2025 notice made it a descriptive test of drafting skills, with one-third Phase II weight. Practise concise, structured English answers under the prescribed time limit while also practising stream Paper 2 in the specified format. Because wrong answers incurred one-quarter negative marking on Phase I papers and Phase II Paper 2 MCQs in 2025, incorporate accuracy review rather than relying only on attempt volume.

Use the official information handouts for the cycle to understand online-test procedures and accessibility arrangements. Recheck the next recruitment notice before locking a study plan because SEBI reserves the right to modify the selection procedure.
bullets: Build two tracks: common aptitude/financial awareness and stream Paper 2.
Schedule full timed sets matching the 2025 reference durations: 60 plus 40 minutes in Phase I; 60 minutes plus the notified Paper 2 duration in Phase II.
After each mock, classify errors as concept, calculation, interpretation, time management, or avoidable negative-marking errors.

sections.heading: What selection leads to
paragraphs: Successful candidates are recruited as Officer Grade A (Assistant Manager) and, under the 2025 notice, undergo a two-year probation subject to satisfactory performance. SEBI stated that selected officers could be posted and transferred to any location in India where it has offices and could be assigned to any department irrespective of recruitment stream.

Career progression at SEBI runs from Grade A (Assistant Manager) through Grade F (Chief General Manager), according to SEBI's careers information. Promotion eligibility is linked to stipulated service in grade, but progression rules and vacancies remain subject to SEBI policy.

Pay is variable and should be read as dated context only. The 2025 notice stated a Grade A pay scale of ₹62,500–₹126,100 over 17 years and estimated gross monthly emoluments at Mumbai at approximately ₹1.84 lakh without accommodation or ₹1.43 lakh with accommodation at the minimum of the scale, inclusive of listed allowances and SEBI's NPS contribution. A later notice or appointment terms may differ.
bullets: The 2025 selection list was published on June 23, 2026; SEBI subsequently published Phase II/cut-off and selected-candidate data in July 2026.
Selection remains subject to meeting the notified eligibility and verification requirements.

title: SET / SLET (state-level)
description: SET / SLET (state-level) — eligibility exam (general), conducted by State agencies.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: SET/SLET denotes a State Eligibility Test or State Level Eligibility Test: an accredited, state-level eligibility examination used in the higher-education faculty-recruitment framework.

quick_facts.label: Primary purpose
quick_facts.value: It establishes eligibility for Assistant Professor appointments; it is not itself a recruitment examination or a job offer.

quick_facts.label: Geographic scope
quick_facts.value: A SLET/SET qualification is valid as the minimum eligibility for direct recruitment in the respective state; candidates should check the recruiting institution’s notification and applicable regulations.

quick_facts.label: Conducting bodies
quick_facts.value: The examination is administered by state-designated agencies rather than through one single national SET authority. For example, Savitribai Phule Pune University conducts M-SET for Maharashtra and Goa, while the West Bengal College Service Commission conducts WB SET.

sections.heading: Purpose and position in the higher-education system
paragraphs: SET/SLET is a state-level route within India’s Assistant Professor eligibility framework. UGC’s 2023 amendment states that NET/SET/SLET is the minimum criterion for direct recruitment to Assistant Professor posts in higher-education institutions. A state SET is therefore an eligibility credential, not a selection process: the relevant university, college, state government, or other employer still advertises vacancies and applies its own recruitment rules.

A critical practical distinction is territorial scope. UGC’s regulations state that SLET/SET is valid as minimum eligibility for direct recruitment in universities, colleges, and institutions in the respective state only. Applicants considering jobs outside the state for which they hold SET/SLET should read the specific recruitment notification and consider whether UGC-NET or another accepted qualification is required.
bullets: SET/SLET qualification does not create a right to appointment or guarantee a teaching post.
The examination is state-administered; the conducting agency, subjects, schedule, language, reservation implementation, and procedures can differ by state.
Faculty recruitment additionally depends on the vacancy advertisement and applicable institutional, state, and UGC rules.

sections.heading: Eligibility: check the current state bulletin and the eventual job advertisement
paragraphs: Eligibility is not perfectly uniform across all SET/SLET agencies, so the current prospectus for the chosen state and subject is authoritative. In the M-SET 2025 official prospectus, applicants needed a UGC-recognised Master’s degree in a SET subject; candidates awaiting their final qualifying result could apply provisionally but needed to complete the Master’s degree within the prescribed period and achieve the required marks. That bulletin specified 55% for the general benchmark and 50% for listed eligible categories.

The same M-SET bulletin required candidates normally to take the subject corresponding to their postgraduate study; where a postgraduate subject was absent from the SET subject list, it allowed a related/equivalent subject in accordance with its stated guidance. It also stated that there was no upper age limit for applying. These are useful examples, not a substitute for another state agency’s current rules.

For an actual Assistant Professor application, qualifying SET/SLET is only one element. UGC’s regulatory framework and the recruiting employer’s notification determine the full qualification requirements, including the relevant subject, degree, category documentation, and any applicable exemptions or additional criteria.
bullets: Before applying, verify: eligible postgraduate subject, minimum marks, category and domicile rules, provisional-result conditions, accepted documents, and whether the state permits the selected subject.
Use the category and reservation rules in the notification of the state conducting the examination; they can be state-specific.
Read the eventual employer’s faculty-vacancy notice separately from the SET/SLET bulletin.

sections.heading: Examination format
paragraphs: There is no single nationwide SET/SLET paper pattern. The applicable state notification sets the mode, papers, timing, subjects, syllabus, question-paper medium, marking, and result methodology. As a concrete recent official illustration, M-SET 2025 used an OMR-based two-paper format: a general Paper I on teaching and research aptitude, followed by subject-specific Paper II. Both papers consisted of compulsory objective questions, and the bulletin stated that no negative marking applied.

Candidates should not assume that an older pattern or another state’s format will apply. West Bengal’s official SET page, for example, separately publishes state SET notices, syllabus material, and prior question papers, illustrating that state agencies maintain their own examination resources and cycles.
bullets: Paper I commonly tests general teaching/research aptitude; confirm the actual syllabus and structure in the selected state’s bulletin.
Paper II is normally tied to the candidate’s selected academic subject; verify the available subject list.
Download and retain the official information bulletin, syllabus, and admit-card instructions for the particular examination cycle.

sections.heading: Application process
paragraphs: The process is cycle-specific and usually begins with the state agency’s online notification. An official M-SET example instructs candidates to read the information bulletin before submitting the online application, select their correct category and subject, and ensure that they satisfy eligibility themselves; candidature remains provisional and may be cancelled if ineligibility is found later.

A sound workflow is to use only the relevant official state SET/SLET portal: read the live notification; confirm eligibility and the correct subject; submit the online form and fee through the methods specified for that cycle; keep the confirmation and payment records; obtain the admit card when released; and monitor the official portal for answer-key, result, scorecard, or certificate notices. Do not treat dates, fees, centres, or correction windows from a past bulletin as current.
bullets: Use the official portal rather than coaching or aggregator sites for the application link and deadlines.
Enter category, domicile, and subject carefully; state bulletins may limit later corrections.
Keep copies of the submitted form, payment receipt, admit card, results, and certificate/scorecard for future recruitment applications.

sections.heading: Preparation strategy
paragraphs: Start with the official syllabus for the exact state SET/SLET cycle and subject, then map study time separately for the general aptitude paper and the subject paper. M-SET’s official bulletin describes Paper I as assessing teaching/research aptitude, reasoning, comprehension, divergent thinking, and general awareness, while Paper II covers the candidate’s chosen subject. The bulletin also directs candidates to the official SET and UGC syllabus resources.

Practice with authentic material wherever the state agency makes it available. The West Bengal College Service Commission’s SET portal links to SET syllabus and question papers, and its notices include answer-key and result-related publications. Use such agency material to understand the expected subject coverage and examination administration rather than relying solely on unofficial mock tests.
bullets: Download the official syllabus first and turn it into a topic checklist.
Prepare Paper I and Paper II in parallel; do not treat the general paper as an afterthought.
Use official previous question papers, answer-key notices, and the current bulletin to practise timing and identify weak topics.
Recheck the live bulletin shortly before the exam for any changes to reporting, materials, or examination instructions.

sections.heading: What qualifying SET/SLET does—and does not—do
paragraphs: A qualifying SET/SLET result can meet the examination-eligibility component for direct Assistant Professor recruitment within the relevant state, subject to the applicable UGC rules and the individual employer’s requirements. It does not itself appoint the candidate. The M-SET agency explicitly states that its test determines eligibility and that the state/nodal agency is not liable to provide jobs to qualified candidates.

Qualification is also not a replacement for reading each faculty recruitment notice. The M-SET prospectus states that candidates who qualify are governed by the recruitment rules of the concerned universities, colleges, or state governments. Candidates should preserve the issued certificate or scorecard and use it when an eligible vacancy is advertised, while confirming that the post, subject, state scope, and all other qualifications match.
bullets: Outcome: eligibility credential for the relevant state’s Assistant Professor recruitment framework.
Not an outcome: automatic placement, salary entitlement, or a guaranteed vacancy.
Next step: apply separately to eligible faculty vacancies and satisfy the recruitment advertisement in full.
