title: SNAP
description: SNAP — pg entrance exam (management), conducted by Symbiosis International University.

quick_facts.label: Exam owner and purpose
quick_facts.value: SNAP (Symbiosis National Aptitude Test) is the common entrance test used for admission to specified postgraduate MBA programmes at Symbiosis International (Deemed University) (SIU).

quick_facts.label: 2026-cycle status
quick_facts.value: As reviewed on July 19, 2026, the official SNAP homepage displayed “SNAP 2026 Enquiries Open.” Applicants should rely on the official portal for the eventual 2026 bulletin, dates, fees, participating programmes, and rules rather than treating prior-cycle details as current.

quick_facts.label: Baseline academic eligibility
quick_facts.value: For many listed MBA programmes in the published eligibility table, the baseline is a degree from a recognised university or Institution of National Importance with at least 50% marks/equivalent grade; the published SC/ST threshold is 45%. Programme-specific requirements can differ.

quick_facts.label: Published 2025 test format
quick_facts.value: The 2025 official structure was a 60-minute computer-based objective test with 60 questions and 60 marks across General English (15), Analytical & Logical Reasoning (25), and Quantitative, Data Interpretation & Data Sufficiency (20).

quick_facts.label: Scoring and attempts in the published 2025 cycle
quick_facts.value: For SNAP 2025, each incorrect answer carried 25% negative marking. Candidates could take up to three tests, with the higher score used for final percentile calculation if more than one attempt was taken.

quick_facts.label: 2025 fee context, not a 2026 quote
quick_facts.value: In the 2025 cycle, the test registration fee was INR 2,250 per test plus applicable government taxes, and programme registration was INR 1,000 per selected programme plus applicable taxes; the fees were stated to be non-refundable and non-transferable. These amounts may change for a later cycle.

sections.heading: What SNAP is for
paragraphs: SNAP is SIU’s common admissions test for the MBA programmes designated by the university. The published 2025 overview states that an applicant seeking an MBA at an SIU institute had to take the common SNAP computer-based test at a test centre, then apply to the desired programme or programmes separately through the integrated portal.

A SNAP score is an entry point, not an admission offer. Under the published process, an applicant shortlisted by a chosen programme proceeded to that programme’s further selection process, identified by SIU as GE-PI. Admission is based on the university’s prescribed criteria and assessment process.
bullets: Use SNAP only for the SIU MBA programmes listed for the applicable admission cycle; the participating programme list can change.
Confirm the precise programme, campus, specialization, eligibility conditions, and follow-up selection process before paying fees.

sections.heading: Eligibility: start with the programme, not only the test
paragraphs: The published SIU eligibility table shows a common baseline for many MBA options: graduation from a recognised university or Institution of National Importance with at least 50% marks or equivalent grade, reduced to 45% for SC/ST candidates. Final-year candidates were permitted in the published 2025 FAQ, subject to meeting the required marks at admission; applicants with a qualifying degree from a foreign university were directed to obtain an Association of Indian Universities equivalence certificate.

Eligibility is programme-specific. For example, the published table gave additional academic or work-experience requirements for some programmes, including MBA (Infrastructure Development and Management), MBA (Business Analytics), MBA (Operations Management), and certain dual-degree offerings. SIU explicitly advises candidates to check the criteria for each programme they select.
bullets: Match your degree, marks, category documentation, work experience, and any subject-specific requirements to the exact programme page.
Do not infer eligibility for a specialized or dual-degree MBA from the general 50%/45% baseline.
Re-check the 2026 eligibility table once SIU publishes the active admission-cycle details.

sections.heading: Test format and how to interpret it
paragraphs: The latest fully specified official test structure available in the reviewed material is for SNAP 2025. It used computer-based testing (CBT), ran for 60 minutes, and contained 60 objective questions worth 60 marks: 15 General English questions, 25 Analytical & Logical Reasoning questions, and 20 Quantitative, Data Interpretation & Data Sufficiency questions. Each question had four responses.

For that 2025 cycle, wrong answers attracted a 25% deduction. Candidates could attempt sections in any order. SIU also allowed up to three test attempts and stated that, where a candidate took more than one, the higher score would be considered for final percentile calculation. SIU reserved the right to alter schedules or test structure in unavoidable circumstances, so these rules should be verified against the 2026 notice.
bullets: Treat the 2025 60-question, 60-minute structure as a preparation reference—not a guarantee for SNAP 2026.
Practice selecting questions and moving between sections, because the published 2025 instructions allowed any section order.
Account for negative marking in attempt decisions rather than guessing indiscriminately.

sections.heading: Application process
paragraphs: In the published 2025 process, registration was online through snaptest.org. Candidates registered for SNAP test attempt(s), paid the test registration fee, selected the SIU programme(s) they wished to pursue, and paid a separate registration fee for each programme. SIU stated that paying only the SNAP test fee did not make an applicant eligible for shortlisting to a programme.

The 2025 registration guide instructed candidates to create an account, verify with an OTP, retain their SNAP ID, upload a recent colour passport-size photograph, provide accurate details, and maintain a valid unique email address and mobile number throughout admissions. The published 2025 payment options included BillDesk, Easebuzz, and demand draft.

Fees and deadlines are cycle-specific. For context only, SNAP 2025 registration/payment closed on November 20, 2025, with the three tests held on December 6, 14, and 20, 2025; results were announced on January 9, 2026. Those dates have passed and must not be used as 2026 deadlines.
bullets: Register for both the SNAP attempt(s) and every target programme; they are distinct payments in the published process.
Save payment confirmations, the SNAP ID, admit card, and scorecard.
Before payment, check the live 2026 portal for active dates, test-city availability, programme deadlines, document rules, taxes, and refund policy.

sections.heading: Preparation approach aligned to the published structure
paragraphs: Build preparation around the published sections: General English (reading comprehension, verbal reasoning, and verbal ability); Analytical & Logical Reasoning; and Quantitative, Data Interpretation & Data Sufficiency. Because the published 2025 structure allocated 60 questions to 60 minutes and used negative marking, preparation should include timed mixed-section practice as well as accuracy review.

Use mock attempts to establish a personal section order, time budget, and skip rule. After each attempt, classify errors as concept gaps, question-selection mistakes, calculation or reading errors, and rushed guesses; then revise by section. This is a practical strategy derived from the published one-hour format, free section order, and 25% penalty for incorrect responses—not an official cutoff or score guarantee.
bullets: Practice all three published sections, then prioritize the error types that recur in timed work.
Simulate the full 60-minute CBT-style attempt rather than preparing only through untimed drills.
Attempt questions when you can eliminate options or solve confidently; review whether negative-marked guesses helped or hurt in mocks.
Check the active 2026 information bulletin before finalizing preparation, since SIU may change the structure.

sections.heading: What happens after the test
paragraphs: In the published 2025 admissions flow, a candidate’s SNAP score was used for shortlisting to the SIU programme(s) for which the candidate had separately registered. A shortlisted applicant then participated in that programme’s subsequent admission process (GE-PI). The relevant institute, rather than a single universal SNAP cutoff, published category-wise merit-list and wait-list cutoffs after results.

The official portal listed 17 Symbiosis institutes and 29 MBA programmes for the 2025 cycle. Available outcomes therefore depended on the programme selected and on meeting its distinct eligibility and selection requirements; a test score alone did not complete admission. SIU states that admissions are strictly merit-based under the university’s prescribed criteria and processes.
bullets: Keep the scorecard until the programme’s admission process is complete; SIU identified it as necessary for further institute selection processes in the published 2025 guidance.
Follow the selected institute’s own shortlist, GE-PI, merit-list, and wait-list announcements.
Do not rely on third-party “guaranteed admission” claims; SIU’s official caution notice says it has not appointed individuals or agencies to make such assurances.

title: SRMJEEE
description: SRMJEEE — ug entrance exam (engineering), conducted by SRM IST.

quick_facts.label: Conducting institution
quick_facts.value: SRMJEEE (UG) is the engineering entrance examination administered through SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST)'s admissions process for B.Tech and integrated engineering study routes.

quick_facts.label: 2026 examination mode
quick_facts.value: For 2026, SRMIST specified an online, remote-proctored examination taken from home on a desktop or laptop; mobile phones were not permitted.

quick_facts.label: 2026 structure
quick_facts.value: The published 2026 pattern was 130 questions and 130 marks in 2 hours 30 minutes: Physics 35, Chemistry 35, Mathematics or Biology 40, and English plus Aptitude 20. SRMIST stated there was no negative marking.

quick_facts.label: Core B.Tech eligibility
quick_facts.value: SRMIST's current B.Tech eligibility page specifies 10+2 passed or appearing status and at least 60% aggregate across Physics, Mathematics, and one listed third subject; Physics and Mathematics are mandatory for the regular B.Tech route.

quick_facts.label: 2026 application context
quick_facts.value: SRMIST listed three SRMJEEE 2026 phases. The published application fee was ₹1,400 per phase and was non-refundable; phase-specific applications were required. This is dated 2026 context, and future-cycle fees and procedures may change.

sections.heading: What SRMJEEE is for
paragraphs: SRMJEEE (UG) is SRMIST's entrance-exam route associated with admission to B.Tech and B.Tech/M.Tech Integrated programmes. It is not itself a degree or job credential: candidates use their examination result/rank in SRMIST's admission and counselling process, where programme and campus choices are considered alongside eligibility and seat availability.

For the 2026 cycle, SRMIST described three phases: Phase I from April 24–29, Phase II from June 10–15, and Phase III from July 4–5. These dates are historical as of July 19, 2026; applicants should not treat them as dates for a later admission cycle.
bullets: The exam is relevant primarily to applicants seeking SRMIST engineering admissions through the regular Indian admissions route.
International-admission handling is separate: SRMIST's FAQ says JEE Main/SAT scores are considered for B.Tech International admission.

sections.heading: Who should check eligibility
paragraphs: For the regular-stream B.Tech/M.Tech Integrated route, SRMIST's published eligibility page identifies Resident Indian applicants and directs NRI, PIO, and OCI applicants to the international application route. It requires a candidate to have passed, or be appearing in, the Higher Secondary (10+2) examination with a minimum 60% aggregate in three subjects: Physics, Mathematics, and at least one approved third subject. The approved third-subject list includes Chemistry, Biotechnology, Biology, Computer Science, Information Technology, Informatics Practices, Engineering Graphics, Botany, and Zoology.

SRMIST separately states that Biotechnology, Genetic Engineering, and Biomedical Engineering programmes can use a 60% aggregate in specified PCM/PMB/PCB combinations; students admitted without Mathematics in 10+2 to those programmes must take an additional four-credit Mathematics course in first year. The institution also publishes qualification rules for GCE A-level and IB applicants, and a NIOS-related schooling condition.
bullets: Treat programme-specific rules as controlling: the subject combination can differ for biotechnology-related programmes.

The SRMJEEE 2026 FAQ also stated an age threshold of 16 years and 6 months by July 31 of the year in which the candidate takes the Class 12 board examination, and stated that a gap exceeding three years after Class 12 is not permitted. Confirm this and all eligibility criteria against the prospectus for the intended cycle before applying.

sections.heading: Exam format and remote-testing requirements
paragraphs: The official 2026 examination-pattern document set the paper at 130 questions for 130 marks over 2 hours 30 minutes. The subject split was Physics (35), Chemistry (35), Mathematics or Biology (40), and English & Aptitude (20), with no negative marks.

SRMIST described the 2026 delivery as remote-proctored online testing from home. Candidates were to use a desktop or laptop rather than a mobile phone; the institution said monitoring would involve AI, proctors, and super-proctors. Its FAQ listed a functional webcam, a Chrome or Firefox browser, stable internet of at least 2 Mbps, and a microphone/headphones where needed among the technical requirements.
bullets: SRMIST stated that there were two test slots per examination day and that slot booking enabled hall-ticket download.
A mock examination was provided before the main examination; use it to test both the interface and home setup.

sections.heading: Application, phase selection, and counselling
paragraphs: In the 2026 process, SRMIST required a separate application for each phase. The official FAQ listed online payment by debit card, credit card, UPI, or net banking; it required photo and signature images for upload, and stated that the per-phase application fee was non-refundable. The fee was ₹1,400 per phase in 2026, but applicants should regard that amount as cycle-specific rather than a standing fee.

SRMIST stated that the course/campus preferences entered with the application were only for statistical purposes; the actual choices were made during counselling. After results, candidates check their rank in the admissions portal. Counselling was held online separately for each phase, and the admission committee allocates campus, programme, and specialisation using factors including SRMJEEE rank, qualifying examination, and availability. A candidate who is allotted a seat must pay within the stipulated period for the provisional allotment letter to be issued.
bullets: As of July 19, 2026, the official 2026 deadlines—April 16, June 4, and June 30 for Phases I, II, and III—had passed.
Do not rely on an old application form or deadline: use SRMIST's current admissions portal and the cycle-specific FAQ/important-dates notice.
Keep application credentials safe; SRMIST says results and rank are accessed through the admissions portal using the application number and date of birth.

sections.heading: Practical preparation plan
paragraphs: Build the study plan from the official syllabus and the published weightage. For the Mathematics route, Physics and Chemistry account for 70 questions, Mathematics for 40, and English plus Aptitude for 20; Biology replaces Mathematics for the Biology route. The official syllabus covers 10+2-level subject areas, including mechanics, electricity, optics and modern physics; physical, inorganic and organic chemistry; and mathematics topics such as algebra, calculus, coordinate geometry, vectors, probability, and trigonometry.

Practise in timed 2-hour-30-minute blocks using the actual 130-question distribution. Because SRMIST published no negative marking for 2026, candidates can plan a final review pass for unanswered questions, while still prioritising accuracy and time management. Before the test, complete the official mock test and verify webcam, browser, laptop, and internet readiness in the same space intended for the remote-proctored exam.
bullets: Use the official syllabus as the scope checklist, rather than assuming another engineering entrance examination has identical coverage.
Reserve explicit practice time for English and Aptitude; together they comprised 20 questions in the 2026 pattern.
For a future cycle, re-check both syllabus and pattern, since the linked detailed syllabus document is labelled 2025 even though SRMIST's 2026 FAQ directed candidates to it.

sections.heading: What happens after the examination
paragraphs: SRMIST states that SRMJEEE results are made available online and that candidates can check their rank in the admissions portal. Qualifying candidates proceed to online counselling, select their preferred course and campus, and may receive an allocation based on rank and seat availability. Payment within the specified timeline is needed to confirm the allotted seat; SRMIST says the provisional allotment letter and fee receipt are then issued.

An SRMJEEE rank can also be relevant to SRMIST scholarship consideration. Its scholarship policy, updated March 5, 2026, lists provisions for top SRMJEEE ranks and a merit-scholarship category for ranks 101–500 across phases/campuses, subject to admission, counselling, annual application, academic-performance, and committee conditions. Scholarship availability, amount, and renewal terms are variable and should be checked against the policy in force at the time of admission.
bullets: An examination rank does not by itself guarantee a particular branch or campus: allocation depends on the institution's admission criteria and available seats.
SRMIST's FAQ says fee structures vary by campus and course; applicants should use the current programme-level fee information before accepting an allotment.

title: SSC CGL
description: SSC CGL — govt recruitment exam (general), conducted by SSC.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: Staff Selection Commission (SSC), Government of India.

quick_facts.label: Purpose
quick_facts.value: SSC CGL is an open competitive recruitment examination for various Group B and Group C posts in Union Government ministries, departments, organisations, and constitutional, statutory and tribunal bodies.

quick_facts.label: 2026 application status
quick_facts.value: For CGLE 2026, SSC originally accepted applications from 21 May to 22 June 2026, then reopened the application window until 25 June 2026; the associated fee-payment deadline was 26 June 2026 and correction window was 1–3 July 2026. These dates have passed as of 19 July 2026.

quick_facts.label: Minimum education
quick_facts.value: For most listed posts in CGLE 2026, SSC requires a bachelor's degree from a recognised university or equivalent. JSO and Statistical Investigator Grade-II have subject-specific qualifications.

quick_facts.label: Exam structure
quick_facts.value: The 2026 notice specifies two computer-based tiers: Tier-I and Tier-II. Tier-I has four 25-question sections; Tier-II Paper-I is compulsory for all posts, with additional papers only for specified post groups.

quick_facts.label: 2026 examination timetable
quick_facts.value: SSC listed Tier-I for August–September 2026 and Tier-II for December 2026, both as tentative schedules that SSC may change through its website.

quick_facts.label: Application fee context
quick_facts.value: In the CGLE 2026 notice, the fee was ₹100. Women candidates and eligible SC, ST, PwBD and ex-servicemen candidates were exempt; fee rules can change in a later notice.

sections.heading: What SSC CGL is for
paragraphs: SSC CGL is a central-government recruitment route rather than an academic entrance examination. The 2026 notice says it is used to fill likely Group B and Group C posts across Government of India ministries, departments and organisations, as well as constitutional bodies, statutory bodies and tribunals.

Examples in the 2026 post list include Assistant Section Officer in the Central Secretariat Service, Inspector of Income Tax in CBDT, Sub-Inspector in CBI, Junior Statistical Officer in the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Auditor under C&AG, and Tax Assistant in CBDT. The exact posts, vacancies, age bands, eligibility conditions and physical standards are post-specific and must be checked against the applicable cycle's notice.
bullets: The examination is administered by SSC; the user departments report vacancies and handle aspects such as appointment formalities after allocation.
The 2026 notice lists posts at Pay Levels 4 through 8. The pay ranges printed in that notice are recruitment-cycle context, not a guarantee of an individual candidate's final compensation.

sections.heading: Eligibility: degree, age, nationality and post-specific rules
paragraphs: For CGLE 2026, the baseline qualification for all other posts was a bachelor's degree from a recognised university or equivalent, to be possessed by 1 August 2026. Candidates in the final year of graduation could apply, but had to acquire the essential qualification by that date. SSC also states that eligible open-and-distance-learning qualifications must have the relevant Distance Education Bureau/UGC approval for the period in which the qualification was earned.

Some posts require more than a general degree. For Junior Statistical Officer (JSO), the 2026 notice requires either a degree in any subject with at least 60% in Mathematics at Class 12 level, or a degree with Statistics as a subject. Statistical Investigator Grade-II requires a degree in one of the specified statistics, mathematics, economics, population, computing, data-science or related subjects.

Nationality rules in the 2026 notice include Indian citizens, subjects of Nepal or Bhutan, and specified persons of Indian origin intending to settle permanently in India; the latter eligible categories require a Government of India eligibility certificate before appointment. Age requirements depend on the post: the 2026 list uses 18–27, 20–30, 18–30 and 18–32 bands, with category-based upper-age relaxations set out in the notice.
bullets: Do not infer eligibility from holding a degree alone: confirm the age limit, degree subject, medical or physical requirements, disability suitability and any departmental conditions for each post selected.
For 2026, SSC set 1 August 2026 as the educational-qualification and age reference date; a future cycle can use a different date.
Candidates must substantiate application claims with original documents during document verification; unsupported claims can lead to cancellation.

sections.heading: Examination format and scoring
paragraphs: The CGLE 2026 scheme has two computer-based tiers. Tier-I is an objective multiple-choice test with 100 questions and 200 marks: 25 questions each in General Intelligence and Reasoning, General Awareness, Quantitative Aptitude, and English Comprehension. It has a one-hour duration with a 15-minute sectional timer for each subject, and a 0.50-mark deduction for each wrong answer.

Tier-II Paper-I is compulsory for every post. Its Session-I covers Mathematical Abilities, Reasoning and General Intelligence, English Language and Comprehension, General Awareness, and a Computer Knowledge Test; Session-II contains the Data Entry Speed Test (DEST). Paper-II (Statistics) is only for candidates applying and shortlisted for JSO or Statistical Investigator Grade-II. Paper-III, General Studies (Finance and Economics), is only for candidates shortlisted for Assistant Audit Officer or Assistant Accounts Officer posts.

In Tier-II, all sections of Paper-I must be qualified separately. The Computer Knowledge Test and DEST are qualifying in nature, but SSC may prescribe higher qualifying standards for particular computer-proficiency or DEST-linked posts. Tier-II objective sections use negative marking: one mark per wrong answer in Paper-I Sections I–III, and 0.50 marks per wrong answer in Papers II and III.
bullets: Tier-I questions are bilingual in English and Hindi except English Comprehension.
Tier-II Paper-I uses two sessions on the same day: Session-I is 2 hours 15 minutes, followed by a 15-minute DEST session.
SSC states that scores from examinations conducted in multiple shifts are normalised and used for merit and cut-offs.

sections.heading: How the application process works
paragraphs: SSC requires online application through its current website or the mySSC Android application. A candidate who has not created a One-Time Registration (OTR) on the new SSC website must first do so; an OTR from SSC's former website is not usable on the new website. The new-site OTR remains valid for future SSC applications on that website.

For the 2026 cycle, SSC later reopened applications from 23 June 2026 at 23:00 to 25 June 2026 at 23:00. It moved the eligibility closing date to 25 June, set 26 June as the fee-payment deadline, and set 1–3 July as the correction period. Those windows are closed as of the review date, so prospective candidates should monitor SSC for a later notice rather than rely on the 2026 dates.

Candidates should preserve their application form and relevant examination records. SSC says admission certificates are issued online, and original documents are checked by the allocated user department or Commission during document verification.
bullets: Create and carefully verify OTR details before applying; SSC warns that incorrect non-editable registration information can result in cancellation.
Use only SSC's official portal or official app for registration, application, notices, admit cards, answer keys and results.
The 2026 fee was ₹100 for non-exempt candidates, payable online through the methods stated in the notice; treat this as cycle-specific.

sections.heading: Preparation aligned to the official scheme
paragraphs: Prepare against the current SSC notice rather than an older coaching outline, because SSC can revise dates, post lists, qualifying standards and procedures. For Tier-I, build timed practice across reasoning, general awareness, quantitative aptitude and English, since the official 2026 structure allocates 15 minutes to each of the four sections and applies a wrong-answer penalty.

For Tier-II, plan for the compulsory Paper-I sections as well as Computer Knowledge Test and DEST. Candidates targeting JSO, Statistical Investigator Grade-II, Assistant Audit Officer or Assistant Accounts Officer should add the applicable specialist paper early: Statistics for the first two post groups, and Finance and Economics for the audit/accounts officer group.

Use the official indicative syllabus to turn preparation into a topic checklist. For example, SSC describes Tier-I general awareness as including current events, India and neighbouring countries, history, culture, geography, economic scene, general policy and scientific research. DEST practice should reflect the prescribed 15-minute data-entry task.
bullets: Practise full mock sessions with the official sectional timing and negative-marking rules, not only untimed topic questions.
Select post preferences only after checking each post's eligibility, age band, physical standards where applicable, and Tier-II paper implications.
Recheck SSC notices before the exam because the 2026 notice explicitly describes its examination schedule as tentative.

sections.heading: Selection and career outcomes
paragraphs: A successful SSC CGL candidate is considered for allocation to a specific post and department according to merit and the post preferences submitted online, subject to eligibility and vacancies. The 2026 notice identifies a broad range of potential outcomes, including Group B roles such as Assistant Section Officer, Inspector of Income Tax, Sub-Inspector in CBI and JSO, alongside Group C roles such as Auditor, Accountant/Junior Accountant and Tax Assistant.

Selection is not the same as final appointment. In the CGLE 2025 final-result process, SSC stated that the allocated department would undertake document verification and appointment formalities after the final result. It also stated that it does not prepare a reserve or waiting list; unfilled and non-joining vacancies are carried forward by the concerned departments to later year(s).

As a recent scale indicator—not a prediction for later cycles—SSC's final CGLE 2025 result reported 15,118 vacancies and 15,118 provisionally shortlisted candidates. Vacancy totals, post mix and cut-offs vary by recruitment cycle and should not be used as a target or assurance for CGLE 2026.
bullets: Final outcome depends on the candidate's merit, valid post preferences, applicable eligibility and the vacancies reported by user departments.
For CGLE 2026, SSC lists Tier-I for August–September 2026 and Tier-II for December 2026 as tentative; candidates should treat SSC updates as controlling.
Departmental document verification and appointment communications follow allocation; SSC's CGLE 2025 final result directs candidates to the allocated user department for those later formalities.

title: SSC CHSL
description: SSC CHSL — govt recruitment exam (general), conducted by SSC.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: Staff Selection Commission (SSC), Government of India.

quick_facts.label: What SSC CHSL is for
quick_facts.value: SSC CHSL (Combined Higher Secondary (10+2) Level Examination) is an SSC recruitment examination for clerical and data-entry roles in Central Government ministries, departments and organisations.

quick_facts.label: Examination structure
quick_facts.value: SSC’s published CHSL scheme has two computer-based tiers: Tier-I and Tier-II. The annual notice is the controlling document for that cycle.

quick_facts.label: Tier-I pattern
quick_facts.value: In SSC’s published scheme, Tier-I has 100 objective questions for 200 marks across English Language, General Intelligence, Quantitative Aptitude and General Awareness; it is 60 minutes long, and each wrong answer carries a 0.50-mark deduction.

quick_facts.label: 2026 cycle timing
quick_facts.value: SSC’s 2026–27 tentative calendar listed CHSL 2026 advertisement in April 2026, closing in May 2026, and Tier-I in July–September 2026. These were tentative calendar dates, not a substitute for the detailed notice.

sections.heading: Purpose and roles
paragraphs: SSC CHSL is the Staff Selection Commission’s higher-secondary-level recruitment route for clerical and lower-division work in Central Government establishments. SSC describes the examination as recruiting candidates for clerical and lower-division-clerk positions in government ministries, departments and organisations.

The exact vacancies, departments, post codes, pay levels, reservation roster, functional requirements and eligibility conditions are cycle-specific. Candidates should treat the detailed notice and subsequent corrigenda for the particular CHSL year as authoritative rather than relying on a prior cycle’s vacancy mix.
bullets: Common role families associated with the examination include Lower Division Clerk (LDC), Junior Secretariat Assistant (JSA), and Data Entry Operator (DEO).

Post and department preference matters: for CHSL 2025, SSC required Tier-II candidates to submit an option-cum-preference for posts and departments before allocation; allocation was to be based on merit-cum-preference under the notice and corrigendum.

sections.heading: Exam format
paragraphs: SSC’s published CHSL scheme sets out two computer-based tiers. Tier-I is a multiple-choice screening examination. It covers English Language (Basic Knowledge), General Intelligence, Quantitative Aptitude (Basic Arithmetic Skill), and General Awareness, with 25 questions and 50 marks assigned to each part.

The published scheme also provides for Tier-II components including Mathematical Abilities, Reasoning and General Intelligence, English Language and Comprehension, General Awareness, Computer Knowledge, and a skill or typing test as applicable to the post. Candidates should confirm the exact timing, qualifying requirements, marking, and post-specific skill-test standard in the notice for their own recruitment year.

The 2025 cycle illustrates the multi-stage process: SSC conducted Tier-I in computer-based mode from November 12 through November 30, 2025, declared Tier-I results to shortlist candidates for Tier-II, and then held Tier-II in April 2026.
bullets: Tier-I: 100 questions, 200 marks, 60 minutes; 0.50 marks are deducted per incorrect answer under the published scheme.
Tier-II: includes post-linked skill/typing assessment in addition to computer-based modules.

A 2026 corrigendum confirms that a qualifying PwD candidate who is permanently unable to type because of a physical disability may seek typing-test exemption subject to the prescribed medical documentation and conditions.

sections.heading: Application process
paragraphs: Apply only through SSC’s official portal when the relevant CHSL application window is live. SSC states that One-Time Registration (OTR) is mandatory before applying for its examinations. The detailed CHSL notice then specifies the cycle’s closing date, fee rules, eligibility cut-off date, documents, examination-city choices and correction arrangements.

Do not assume that dates from an older notice remain open. For example, the 2025 CHSL correction window was changed by SSC from July 23–24, 2025 to July 25–26, 2025, showing why applicants should watch SSC notices and corrigenda rather than third-party deadline listings.
bullets: Create or verify SSC One-Time Registration before starting the application.
Read the current detailed notice before selecting posts, claiming reservation or age relaxation, or paying any fee.
Save the submitted application and monitor the SSC candidate login for examination-city, admission-certificate, answer-key, result and preference-window notices.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Prepare directly against the SSC-published scheme. For Tier-I, build coverage and timed accuracy across English, reasoning, quantitative aptitude and general awareness. Because Tier-I uses objective questions and has negative marking, practice should include question selection, error reduction and full-length timed computer-based mocks—not only untimed topic drills.

For Tier-II, add regular practice in mathematical abilities, reasoning, English comprehension, general awareness and computer knowledge. Candidates targeting DEO or LDC/JSA-type posts should also begin computer typing or data-entry practice early, because the Tier-II scheme includes a post-linked skill or typing component.
bullets: Use SSC’s published syllabus/scheme as the primary checklist; compare it with the year-specific notice before finalising a study plan.
Track accuracy as well as attempts because the published Tier-I scheme deducts 0.50 marks for each incorrect response.
Practise on a computer and simulate the applicable time limit, including the four Tier-I sections within a single 60-minute session.

sections.heading: Selection outcomes and next steps
paragraphs: Progression is competitive and post-specific. In CHSL 2025, SSC used normalized Tier-I scores from a multi-shift computer-based examination to shortlist candidates for Tier-II and set separate category-wise cut-offs for different post groups, including LDC/JSA/Clerk-Cum-Typist and DEO groupings.

Clearing an examination stage alone does not guarantee appointment. SSC’s CHSL 2025 preference notice states that candidates who appeared in Tier-II had to submit post/department preferences to be considered for first-round tentative allocation or final selection, and that allocation would be made under the examination notice on a merit-cum-preference basis.
bullets: Possible outcomes include consideration for LDC/JSA and DEO-type appointments, subject to the notified vacancy, eligibility, merit, post suitability, document checks and preference rules.
Watch SSC notices after Tier-II for preference submission, tentative allocation, document-verification instructions and final-result updates.
Cut-offs and vacancy numbers change by cycle and post; they should not be treated as fixed targets or guarantees.

title: SSC GD Constable
description: SSC GD Constable — govt recruitment exam (defence), conducted by SSC.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body and posts
quick_facts.value: SSC conducts this open competitive recruitment examination under the Ministry of Home Affairs scheme for Constable (GD) posts in BSF, CISF, CRPF, ITBP, SSB and SSF, plus Rifleman (GD) in Assam Rifles.

quick_facts.label: Minimum education
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 notice, applicants had to have passed Matriculation/Class 10 from a recognised board or university by 1 January 2026.

quick_facts.label: Age and citizenship
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, candidates had to be Indian citizens aged 18–23 on 1 January 2026, with prescribed category-based upper-age relaxations. CAPF and Assam Rifles vacancies are generally tied to the candidate’s domicile State/UT or specified area.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: The recruitment pathway comprises a Computer-Based Examination (CBE), Physical Efficiency Test (PET), Physical Standard Test (PST), Detailed/Review Medical Examination, and document verification.

quick_facts.label: 2026 pay and vacancies context
quick_facts.value: The 2026 notice listed Pay Level 3, ₹21,700–₹69,100, and 25,487 tentative vacancies. Pay, allowances, vacancy totals and force-wise distribution can change in future notices.

sections.heading: What SSC GD Constable is for
paragraphs: SSC GD Constable is a central-government recruitment examination rather than an academic entrance test. Under the 2026 recruitment notice, it was used to select Constables (General Duty) for the CAPFs and SSF, and Riflemen (General Duty) for Assam Rifles.

The examination is administered by the Staff Selection Commission, while CAPFs conduct later physical, medical and document-verification stages. Final force allocation depends on CBE merit, the applicant’s force preferences and successful completion of the required physical and medical stages.
bullets: Recruiting organisations in the 2026 notice: BSF, CISF, CRPF, ITBP, SSB, SSF and Assam Rifles.
CAPF vacancies are generally State/UT and area based; SSF vacancies are filled on an all-India basis.

sections.heading: Eligibility: baseline requirements
paragraphs: The exact eligibility rules change by notification, so applicants should use the notice for their own cycle. In the 2026 notice, the essential educational qualification was a pass in Matriculation/Class 10 from a recognised Board or University by 1 January 2026.

For that cycle, the normal age range was 18–23 years as on 1 January 2026, and Indian citizenship was required. The notice provided upper-age relaxations for specified categories, including SC/ST, OBC and eligible ex-servicemen.

Candidates must also meet the notice’s physical and medical requirements. The 2026 standard height was 170 cm for men and 157 cm for women, subject to specified relaxations for eligible categories and regions; PST also includes prescribed weight and, where applicable, chest measurements.
bullets: Check the notification’s cut-off dates for Class 10 completion and age; dates are cycle-specific.
Use the correct domicile State/UT and district details. The 2026 notice required the relevant domicile/PRC at medical examination/document verification for State/UT-based vacancies.
Read the complete PET, PST and medical-standard annexures before applying; a CBE score alone does not establish eligibility.

sections.heading: Exam and selection format
paragraphs: In the 2026 scheme, the CBE was a 60-minute objective multiple-choice paper with 80 questions worth 160 marks: 20 questions each in General Intelligence and Reasoning, General Knowledge and General Awareness, Elementary Mathematics, and English/Hindi. Each incorrect answer carried a 0.25-mark deduction.

The CBE was offered in English, Hindi and 13 listed regional languages. Its questions were at Matriculation level. SSC shortlists candidates for PET/PST on CBE merit; candidates who qualify the physical stages proceed to medical examination and document verification according to the recruitment process.

For the 2026 PET, candidates outside the Ladakh Region had to complete 5 km in 24 minutes (men) or 1.6 km in 8½ minutes (women). Ladakh-region standards differed. These are notification-specific standards, not a guarantee for future cycles.
bullets: CBE: 80 questions, 160 marks, 60 minutes; 0.25 negative marking per wrong answer in the 2026 notice.
CBE syllabus areas: reasoning, general knowledge/awareness, elementary mathematics and English/Hindi.
Physical stages: biometric verification, PET race and PST measurements; then medical examination and document verification for shortlisted candidates.

sections.heading: How the application process works
paragraphs: SSC accepts applications online. The 2026 notice described a two-part process: completing One-Time Registration (OTR) and then submitting the examination-specific online application through the SSC system. Applicants were required to give examination-centre choices, select the CBE medium, provide domicile information and rank all listed force preferences.

For dated context, the 2026 application window ran from 1 December to 31 December 2025; online fee payment was allowed until 1 January 2026, and the correction window ran from 8 to 10 January 2026. The notice set the fee at ₹100, with exemptions for women candidates, SC/ST candidates and eligible ex-servicemen. These dates and charges are historical 2026-cycle details and may differ in a later notification.

Applicants should retain the submitted application record and regularly check SSC and CRPF channels for admission certificates and later-stage updates. Admission certificates are issued online, not by post.
bullets: Create or update SSC OTR, then apply only through the live examination module when a new notice is open.
Enter domicile and force preferences carefully: the 2026 notice said changes to force preference would not be accepted after application submission.
Check the payment status and submit before the deadline; an application for which the applicable fee is not received is treated as incomplete.

sections.heading: Preparation approach aligned to the official scheme
paragraphs: Prepare to the official four-part CBE structure rather than treating the examination as only a physical recruitment test. A balanced plan should practise Matriculation-level arithmetic, non-verbal and analytical reasoning, basic English or Hindi comprehension, and broad general awareness including current events and India-focused topics identified in the notice.

Use timed objective-question practice because the 2026 CBE allowed 60 minutes for 80 questions and used negative marking. SSC also stated that a CBE mock test was available in its Candidate’s Corner; candidates should use official practice material and the latest notice for their cycle.

Start PET conditioning well before the physical stage. Build running volume gradually, practise the applicable distance and target time, and confirm the current cycle’s standards before training to a specific benchmark. Candidates should also verify physical standards and medical eligibility early, because qualifying the written stage does not override later PST/PET or medical requirements.
bullets: Practise all four CBE subjects weekly and review errors, especially where guessing could trigger negative marking.
Take full 60-minute mocks and practise selecting only answers you can support confidently.
Train for the relevant PET race progressively; use the current notification to confirm region- and category-specific standards.

sections.heading: What selection can lead to
paragraphs: A successful candidate can be recommended for appointment as a Constable (GD) in BSF, CISF, CRPF, ITBP, SSB or SSF, or as a Rifleman (GD) in Assam Rifles, subject to force allocation, medical fitness, document verification and other notified conditions.

For the 2026 cycle, SSC stated that allocation would be based on normalized CBE merit, applicable NCC bonus marks and the force preferences submitted in the application, after qualifying PST, PET and medical requirements. Recommended candidates may be required to serve anywhere in India, and appointment can occur in phases depending on training capacity.

The 2026 notice placed all listed posts at Pay Level 3, ₹21,700–₹69,100. This is a dated basic-pay context from that notice; actual take-home pay and allowances vary by posting, applicable rules and future pay revisions.
bullets: Primary employment outcomes: GD roles in CAPFs/SSF or Rifleman (GD) in Assam Rifles.
Final allocation is not determined by a candidate’s preferred force alone; it is merit-and-preference based and contingent on all qualifying stages.
The 2026 notice said SSC would not maintain a waiting/reserve list after final results.

title: SSC JE
description: SSC JE — govt recruitment exam (engineering), conducted by SSC.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: Staff Selection Commission (SSC), Government of India.

quick_facts.label: What SSC JE recruits for
quick_facts.value: An open competitive examination for Junior Engineer posts in Civil, Mechanical and Electrical disciplines in Government of India organisations/offices.

quick_facts.label: Qualification route
quick_facts.value: Eligibility is post-specific. In the 2025 notice, the listed routes generally used a relevant engineering degree or three-year diploma; some posts additionally required relevant post-qualification experience.

quick_facts.label: Examination structure
quick_facts.value: The official SSC scheme specifies two computer-based papers: Paper I has General Intelligence and Reasoning, General Awareness, and a chosen General Engineering discipline; Paper II is the chosen General Engineering discipline.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: For the 2025 recruitment notice, SSC described the advertised JE posts as Group B (Non-Gazetted), Non-Ministerial, Pay Level 6: ₹35,400–₹1,12,400 in the 7th CPC Pay Matrix. This is a dated notice-level pay context, not a guarantee for later cycles or every employer-specific posting.

quick_facts.label: Most recent confirmed 2025-cycle milestone
quick_facts.value: SSC published the First Round of Tentative Allocation on July 9, 2026. SSC states that marks from both papers were used for that allocation process.

sections.heading: What SSC JE is for
paragraphs: SSC JE is the Staff Selection Commission’s competitive recruitment examination for Junior Engineer roles in central-government organisations and offices. The examination covers Civil, Mechanical and Electrical engineering streams; the exact organisations, posts, vacancies, physical/medical requirements where applicable, and qualifications are set out in each cycle’s SSC notice.

For example, SSC’s 2025 notice described the recruitment as being for Group B (Non-Gazetted), Non-Ministerial Junior Engineer posts. Candidates should treat the notice for the cycle they apply to—not a prior-year list of posts or vacancies—as authoritative.
bullets: Use SSC JE when seeking entry into eligible central-government Junior Engineer recruitment in the notified engineering discipline.
Do not assume that every listed department accepts the same diploma, degree, age range, experience record, or disability category: these are post-specific in the notification.

sections.heading: Eligibility: check the post, discipline and cut-off date
paragraphs: SSC JE eligibility is not a single universal rule. The 2025 notice lists essential qualifications separately by organisation and post. Relevant Civil, Electrical or Mechanical engineering degrees and three-year diplomas are common routes, but certain notified posts require work experience in addition to a diploma. The notice states that required experience must be obtained after completing the specified educational qualification; internship, training and research experience undertaken while acquiring the qualification do not count as the required experience.

Age limits also vary by post. The 2025 notice included posts with maximum ages such as 30 or 32 years, subject to the notice’s applicable cut-off date and relaxation provisions. Applicants should match their exact qualification, engineering branch, experience and age against the table for each post before submitting preferences.

The 2025 notice also explains that engineering programmes are generally not permitted through open and distance learning under the cited UGC regulations, subject to the stated historical IGNOU exception. Qualification recognition and documentary proof are checked by the user department during document verification.
bullets: Read the post table rather than relying only on the exam’s broad title.
Keep original degree/diploma mark sheets, certificates and, where required, post-qualification experience evidence ready for document verification.
For Border Roads Organisation or any other post with additional standards, review the specific physical and medical conditions before choosing that post.

sections.heading: Exam format and scoring stages
paragraphs: SSC’s published JE scheme uses two computer-based examination papers. Paper I is a two-hour test comprising 50 questions/50 marks in General Intelligence and Reasoning, 50 questions/50 marks in General Awareness, and 100 questions/100 marks in one General Engineering option: Civil & Structural, Electrical, or Mechanical. Paper II is a two-hour computer-based test with 100 questions for 300 marks in the selected General Engineering option. Eligible scribe candidates receive the extended duration stated by SSC.

The 2025 cycle illustrates the sequence: SSC conducted Paper I in computer-based mode, declared its result to shortlist candidates for Paper II, and later used marks from both papers for the First Round of Tentative Allocation. SSC reported normalization for Paper I because it was held in multiple shifts and described additional normalization between Mechanical and Electrical Paper II scores for common posts.
bullets: Choose and prepare the General Engineering option that corresponds to the discipline and posts for which you are eligible.
Treat current cut-offs, negative-marking rules, normalization procedures and qualifying thresholds as notification-specific; verify them in the active SSC JE notice and its later updates.

sections.heading: How to apply and track a cycle
paragraphs: Apply only through SSC’s official platform when an SSC JE notice is open. SSC’s candidate guidance states that One-Time Registration (OTR) is mandatory before applying for Commission examinations. The 2025 JE notice required online application through SSC’s new website and set a separate application window, payment deadline and correction window; those dates are historical and must not be reused for a future cycle.

SSC’s 2026–27 tentative calendar listed SSC JE 2026 with a tentative March 2026 advertisement period, April 2026 closing period, and May–June 2026 Paper I window. Because the calendar is explicitly tentative, candidates must rely on the actual advertisement, corrigenda and notice-board updates for operative dates, fees, vacancies, eligibility cut-offs, examination dates and admit-card instructions.

After Paper II, SSC may require candidates to submit an option-cum-preference for posts/organisations through Candidate Login. In the 2025 cycle, SSC made this a required step for candidates who appeared in Paper II and stated that candidates who did not submit preferences within the specified window would not be considered for the final merit list/final selection.
bullets: Create or verify SSC OTR before the deadline; do not wait until the last day of an application window.
Download and save the cycle notice, submitted application, payment confirmation, correction confirmation, admit-card notices and answer-key/scorecard records.
Submit post and organisation preferences only after checking qualification, age, experience and any job-specific physical or medical requirements.

sections.heading: Preparation approach aligned to the official scheme
paragraphs: Build preparation around the two-paper structure. Paper I requires three parallel areas—reasoning, general awareness and the selected engineering discipline—while Paper II concentrates entirely on the selected Civil & Structural, Electrical or Mechanical engineering syllabus. This makes discipline-specific technical revision central to performance across both papers.

Use SSC’s official scheme and the current cycle’s detailed notice as the primary checklist. Practise computer-based questions under the two-hour time limit, separately track accuracy in Paper I’s non-technical portions, and devote substantial revision time to the General Engineering branch chosen for both papers. Review official answer-key and result notices after the examination, because SSC has published final answer keys, response sheets and marks for completed cycles for limited access periods.
bullets: Make a topic tracker for the three Paper I components and the Paper II technical syllabus.
Use timed mock sessions matching the paper durations stated by SSC.
Prioritise official notices, scheme documents, answer-key notices and prior SSC materials over unofficial claims about pattern changes or cut-offs.

sections.heading: What happens after the examination
paragraphs: Qualifying SSC JE can lead to consideration for notified central-government Junior Engineer posts, but selection is not simply a pass result. SSC’s 2025 process shortlisted candidates from Paper I for Paper II, collected post/organisation preferences from Paper II candidates, and made tentative allocation using merit and the applicable preference process. The relevant user department subsequently handles required document verification and appointment-related checks.

For the 2025 cycle, SSC’s July 9, 2026 First Round of Tentative Allocation notice states that 15,607 candidates had been shortlisted for Paper II, 14,062 appeared in Paper II, and 11,052 candidates who submitted online preferences were considered further. These figures describe that particular cycle only and should not be used to estimate future competition or vacancies.

The pay level, employer, work location and post conditions can differ by the actual vacancy. The 2025 notice’s Level 6 pay matrix reference is useful context, but applicants should verify the current notice and the eventual appointing organisation’s conditions.
bullets: A good Paper I score alone does not complete the process; Paper II, merit treatment and required preference submission matter.
Keep eligibility evidence available through document verification; a qualification or experience mismatch can cancel candidature.
Review allocation, identity-verification and user-department communications after SSC publishes results.

title: SSC MTS Exam
description: An SSC-conducted national-level exam for non-technical Group C posts in central government ministries and departments.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body and purpose
quick_facts.value: The Staff Selection Commission (SSC) conducts this competitive recruitment examination for Multi-Tasking (Non-Technical) Staff, a General Central Service Group C, non-gazetted, non-ministerial post in central-government ministries, departments, offices, and specified statutory or constitutional bodies.

quick_facts.label: Minimum qualification
quick_facts.value: In the 2025 notice, applicants had to have passed Matriculation (Class 10) or an equivalent qualification from a recognized board by the stated cut-off date. Requirements must be checked again in the notice for the cycle being applied to.

quick_facts.label: Age context
quick_facts.value: For the 2025 cycle, the age band was 18–25 years for MTS, while an 18–27 band applied to Havaldar and to some MTS posts; category-based upper-age relaxations were listed in that notice. These dates and limits are cycle- and post-specific.

quick_facts.label: Exam structure
quick_facts.value: The 2025 scheme used a computer-based objective test in two mandatory 45-minute sessions: Numerical and Mathematical Ability; Reasoning Ability and Problem Solving; General Awareness; and English Language and Comprehension. Session I had no negative marking; Session II deducted one mark for each wrong answer.

quick_facts.label: 2026 schedule context
quick_facts.value: SSC’s 2026–27 tentative calendar listed the MTS and Havaldar 2026 advertisement for June 2026, closing in July 2026, and CBE in September–November 2026. A calendar is tentative; applicants should rely on the live SSC notice and application portal for final dates.

sections.heading: What the SSC MTS examination is for
paragraphs: SSC MTS is a national competitive recruitment route into Multi-Tasking (Non-Technical) Staff posts at Pay Level 1 under the 7th Central Pay Commission matrix. The 2025 SSC notice describes MTS as a General Central Service Group C, non-gazetted and non-ministerial post across central-government ministries, departments, offices, constitutional bodies, statutory bodies, and tribunals in States and Union Territories.

The same examination notice also included Havaldar recruitment in CBIC and CBN under the Department of Revenue. Havaldar is a separate post choice with additional physical testing, so candidates seeking only MTS should read the post-specific provisions in the applicable notice carefully.
bullets: The examination is a recruitment process, not a diploma or academic qualification.
The number, location, and category of vacancies are reported by user departments and may differ by recruitment cycle.
Pay and service conditions should be verified from the specific recruitment notice and appointing department; Pay Level 1 is the classification stated in the 2025 notice.

sections.heading: Eligibility: Class 10 is the educational entry point
paragraphs: The latest full official notice used here—the SSC MTS and Havaldar Examination, 2025 notice—required a pass in Matriculation or an equivalent examination from a recognized board by August 1, 2025. At document verification, candidates were required to produce original proof of completing Matriculation or its equivalent; an equivalence certificate is required where an equivalent qualification is claimed.

That notice set the MTS age range at 18–25 years as of August 1, 2025. It separately specified 18–27 years for Havaldar and for a few MTS posts in various departments, and it provided prescribed upper-age relaxations for eligible categories. Treat these as 2025-cycle examples rather than permanent limits: the next notification controls the applicable cut-off date, age bands, relaxations, nationality rules, disability suitability, and documents.
bullets: Confirm that the Class 10 result was declared by the notice’s cut-off date; merely having a result under processing did not meet the 2025 rule.
Keep the Class 10/secondary certificate, mark sheet or provisional certificate, and any equivalence or category documents ready for later verification.
Review the post-specific disability suitability and accommodation provisions in the live notification if applicable.

sections.heading: Test format and the Havaldar distinction
paragraphs: For MTS, the 2025 scheme consisted of a Computer Based Examination (CBE). It had two mandatory sessions on the same day, each lasting 45 minutes: Session I covered Numerical and Mathematical Ability and Reasoning Ability and Problem Solving, while Session II covered General Awareness and English Language and Comprehension. The paper used objective multiple-choice questions.

The 2025 CBE allocated 20 questions/60 marks to each Session I subject and 25 questions/75 marks to each Session II subject. There was no negative marking in Session I, but one mark was deducted for each incorrect Session II answer. SSC stated that Session I and the General Awareness component could be offered in English, Hindi, and 13 regional languages, while English Language and Comprehension necessarily assesses English.

Candidates applying for Havaldar faced an additional Physical Efficiency Test and Physical Standard Test after the CBE. In the 2025 notice, the PET walking standard was 1,600 metres in 15 minutes for men and 1 kilometre in 20 minutes for women; physical standards were also specified. Those additional requirements do not apply to ordinary MTS recruitment, but the current notice should always be checked.
bullets: Base preparation on the official four-subject syllabus, rather than assuming the pattern will remain identical every year.
Answer carefully in Session II because wrong answers carried a penalty under the 2025 rules.
If choosing Havaldar, begin physical preparation early and review the precise PET/PST and medical requirements in the applicable notice.

sections.heading: How to apply and track the recruitment cycle
paragraphs: Applications are made through SSC’s online system. SSC states that One-Time Registration (OTR) is a mandatory prerequisite before a candidate can apply for an examination. In the 2025 MTS process, candidates logged in with their registration credentials, selected the live MTS/Havaldar examination, supplied qualification and preference information, captured a photograph through the module, uploaded a signature, reviewed the form, submitted it, and made payment where applicable.

Application dates and fees vary by cycle. As dated context only, the 2025 notice prescribed a ₹100 application fee and exempted women candidates and eligible SC, ST, PwBD, and ex-servicemen candidates. SSC’s 2026–27 tentative calendar listed June 2026 for the MTS/Havaldar advertisement, July 2026 for closing, and September–November 2026 for the CBE; final dates must be taken from the current live notice, not from the calendar alone.

After applying, retain the submitted application and payment record, monitor the SSC site for city/admission-certificate information and notices, and bring the prescribed original identification and documents to examination or verification stages. SSC’s 2025 notice stated that application details are verified against original documents and that unsubstantiated claims can lead to cancellation of candidature.
bullets: Create or update SSC OTR before the application window closes.
Read the live notice before choosing post-cum-State/UT preferences and examination-centre preferences.
Check the final fee, exemptions, correction window, photograph/signature rules, and document checklist in the applicable cycle’s notice.
Use only SSC’s official website for notices, application access, answer keys, and results.

sections.heading: Preparation approach aligned to the official syllabus
paragraphs: Build a study plan around the CBE’s four areas. The 2025 syllabus identifies arithmetic topics such as integers, fractions, percentage, ratio and proportion, work and time, interest, profit and loss, geometry basics, distance and time, and simple graphs/data for Numerical and Mathematical Ability. Reasoning includes alpha-numeric series, coding-decoding, analogy, directions, similarities and differences, problem solving, diagrams, age calculations, calendars, and clocks.

For General Awareness, SSC’s 2025 indicative syllabus covered social studies—history, geography, art and culture, civics and economics—along with general science and environmental studies up to Class 10 level. English preparation should cover vocabulary, grammar, sentence structure, synonyms, antonyms, correct usage, and comprehension.

Practise the two-session structure under timed conditions. Since the 2025 pattern assigned different marking rules to the sessions, use a deliberate attempt strategy: prioritise accurate, well-practised work in both sessions and be especially selective in the negatively marked Session II. Use official SSC notices, syllabus material, answer keys, and prior papers where available; recheck the new notification for any changes before the exam.
bullets: Schedule separate timed practice for mathematics/reasoning and for general awareness/English.
Maintain an error log for arithmetic methods, reasoning patterns, grammar errors, and guessed Session II answers.
For Havaldar applicants, pair written-test preparation with regular walking and a review of the official PET/PST standards.

sections.heading: What selection can lead to
paragraphs: Successful candidates may be selected for MTS posts in central-government ministries, departments, offices, constitutional bodies, statutory bodies, and tribunals. The 2025 notice stated that selected MTS candidates could be posted in different States or Union Territories and should be willing to serve anywhere in India, subject to user-department requirements.

Selection is conditional rather than automatic upon taking or passing the CBE. SSC processes merit and allocates candidates against reported vacancies and stated preferences, while the relevant user department or organisation conducts document verification after the final result. Candidates must substantiate educational, category, age-relaxation, and other claims with the required originals.

For the 2025 recruitment, MTS was classified at Pay Level 1. Exact take-home pay, allowances, vacancy counts, posting location, duties, and joining conditions are variable and should be confirmed from the recruitment notice, allocation result, and appointing department at the time of selection.
bullets: MTS offers a direct Class-10-entry pathway to eligible central-government Group C support roles.

Candidates can continue education separately, including pursuing a polytechnic diploma if eligible under the admitting institution’s rules; SSC MTS itself is an employment examination, not a diploma pathway.
Havaldar outcomes are limited to the CBIC/CBN posts included in the relevant notice and require clearing the additional physical stages.

title: State Forest Service Examination
description: A state-level competitive recruitment examination for Forest Range Officer and other state forest service posts.

quick_facts.label: What this node represents
quick_facts.value: “State Forest Service Examination” is best treated as an umbrella for state-administered forest-recruitment examinations, not one all-India examination: Uttarakhand’s 2025 notice uses “Assistant Conservator of Forest, Logging Officer and Forest Range Officer Combined Examination,” while Telangana has separately notified Forest Range Officer recruitment.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry post
quick_facts.value: A principal direct-recruitment outcome is Forest Range Officer / Forest Range Officer Grade-I; Rajasthan’s service rules provide for 50% direct recruitment and 50% promotion for Forest Range Officer Grade-I.

quick_facts.label: Forestry degree relevance
quick_facts.value: A B.Sc. (Hons.) Forestry is directly relevant to eligibility examples: Rajasthan’s rules name a bachelor’s degree in Forestry, and Telangana’s Forest Range Officer notice lists Forestry among acceptable subjects.

quick_facts.label: Controlling document
quick_facts.value: The particular state commission’s current advertisement is controlling for vacancies, dates, age limits, reservation, fees, physical standards, syllabus, and the selection stages; candidates should not transfer details from another state’s notice.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
paragraphs: This node covers competitive state recruitment routes into state forest departments, especially Range-level posts such as Forest Range Officer (FRO). It should not be confused with the Union Public Service Commission’s Indian Forest Service examination: the responsible recruiting authority, examination title, post mix, and rules are determined by the relevant State Public Service Commission or state recruiting body. For example, Uttarakhand combined ACF, Logging Officer, and FRO posts in one 2025 examination, whereas Telangana issued a Forest Range Officer recruitment notification.

A Range Forest Officer is a field-management role within the forest-department structure. Maharashtra’s Forest Department describes forest divisions as being divided into range units headed by a Range Forest Officer; Rajasthan’s forest records also show operational responsibilities involving protection, patrol/monitoring, and departmental management at range level.
bullets: Use the examination to seek appointment in the state named in the notification; it is not a transferable national qualification.
Read the advertised post name carefully: a notice may recruit FRO alone or combine it with Assistant Conservator of Forests, Logging Officer, or other forest-service posts.

sections.heading: Eligibility: degree, age, and physical fitness
paragraphs: A forestry honours degree is a strong academic route, but eligibility remains state- and notification-specific. Rajasthan’s Forest Subordinate Service Rules list a bachelor’s degree in Forestry among qualifications for direct recruitment to Forest Range Officer Grade-I; the same rules also accept specified science subjects, Agriculture, and Engineering. Telangana’s FRO notice similarly includes Forestry among a wider list of accepted disciplines.

Do not assume that academic eligibility alone is sufficient. State notices can set an age window, category-based relaxations, physical measurements, endurance/walking tests, and medical-fitness requirements. In the Telangana notice located for this research, the stated age range and physical standards were specific to that recruitment cycle, so they are historical examples rather than current universal requirements.
bullets: Before applying, match your degree title and subjects against the exact notice—not merely this node or another state’s rules.
Check the notice’s cut-off date for age and qualification, domicile/language requirements where applicable, reservation documentation, and physical/medical standards.
Obtain prescribed certificates only in the format and from the authority named in the advertisement.

sections.heading: Selection format varies by state
paragraphs: There is no single standard pattern. Uttarakhand’s Assistant Conservator of Forest, Logging Officer and Forest Range Officer Combined Examination–2025 illustrates a multi-stage design: a preliminary objective paper, a written main examination with compulsory and optional papers, and an interview. Its preliminary paper was General Studies and General Aptitude; its mains scheme included General Hindi, General English, General Knowledge, two optional subjects, and an interview.

Other state notices may organize selection differently and may separately assess physical standards or fitness. Treat a state’s current notification, syllabus, and instructions as the authoritative pattern for that cycle.
bullets: Download the official syllabus and scheme before planning optional-subject preparation.
Confirm whether the preliminary stage is screening-only or counted in final merit, and whether any paper has a minimum qualifying mark.
Check the notice for document verification, physical measurement/endurance testing, medical examination, and interview requirements.

sections.heading: Application process
paragraphs: Apply only through the recruiting commission’s official process during the window in its current advertisement. The UKPSC candidate portal, for example, separately maintains recruitment notifications, admit cards, answer keys, results, syllabi, previous question papers, and an examination calendar—useful checkpoints through the recruitment lifecycle.

Because deadlines, application fees, correction windows, upload specifications, and required certificates are cycle-specific, they should be treated as dated notice information rather than standing facts. Preserve the submitted form, payment/fee record where applicable, photo-ID details, and every notice issued after submission.
bullets: Locate the current advertisement on the relevant state commission’s official recruitment-notifications page.
Read the eligibility and instructions before paying or submitting the form.
Monitor the same official portal for correction notices, admit-card release, answer keys, objections, document verification, physical tests, and results.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Build preparation from the official scheme rather than from generic “forest service” coaching material. The Uttarakhand 2025 combined examination example required general studies/aptitude at preliminary stage and language, general knowledge, and optional-subject performance in mains; that structure supports a plan combining general competitive-exam skills with disciplined revision of the notified forestry/science optional subjects.

Use official previous question papers and syllabus pages when the commission provides them. UKPSC places both syllabus and old question papers in its Candidate Corner, which makes them more reliable starting points than unofficial reconstructed patterns.
bullets: Create a topic-by-topic checklist from the current official syllabus and map each topic to past official papers where available.
For B.Sc. Forestry graduates, revise core degree material only to the extent it matches the notified optional subjects and syllabus.
Practise timed objective tests, descriptive answers where mains papers require them, and the commission’s stated language-paper requirements.
Prepare physical fitness progressively if the notification requires a walking/endurance test; follow the notified standards and medical instructions rather than informal advice.

sections.heading: Career outcomes after selection
paragraphs: Successful candidates may enter a state forest department in the post named in the recruitment notice, commonly Forest Range Officer or Forest Range Officer Grade-I. This is a state-government career path and service conditions are governed by the respective state’s service rules and appointment orders. Rajasthan’s rules explicitly provide both direct-recruitment and promotional channels for FRO Grade-I, demonstrating that direct recruits join a cadre that also has an internal promotion route.

Range-level work is operational and field-facing: official forest-department material describes ranges as units headed by a Range Forest Officer, while forest codes and conservation plans show range-level responsibilities involving inspection, protection, patrol/monitoring, reporting, and supervision. Exact duties, postings, training, progression, and pay are state- and cadre-specific; salary should be verified from the applicable, dated notification or appointment/service rules.
bullets: Potential appointment title: Forest Range Officer / Forest Range Officer Grade-I, subject to the particular state notice.
Potential work setting: a forest range within a state forest department, with field and administrative responsibilities.
Post-selection requirements may include departmental or in-service training; Rajasthan’s department identifies refresher/orientation training for Range Officers among its HRD activities.
