title: State ITI Vocational Instructor Recruitment Examination
description: A state-level recruitment examination or selection process for appointment as a vocational instructor in a government ITI.

quick_facts.label: Jurisdiction
quick_facts.value: This is not one uniform all-India recruitment examination: government ITIs are administered day to day by State Governments or Union Territory Administrations, which issue their own recruitment rules and notifications.

quick_facts.label: Role targeted
quick_facts.value: The process is used to select trade-specific vocational instructors for government ITIs—for example, Electrician, Fitter, COPA/ICTSM, Mechanic Motor Vehicle, or Sewing Technology—rather than a general teaching post.

quick_facts.label: Core qualification pattern
quick_facts.value: Eligibility is normally tied to the notified trade. Official rules can accept relevant engineering degrees, diplomas/advanced diplomas, or NTC/NAC/STC trade credentials, usually paired with specified relevant experience; exact alternatives differ by State/UT and trade.

quick_facts.label: Instructor-training credential
quick_facts.value: CITS/NCIC is an important instructor-training credential in the ITI system. DGT’s CITS programme trains candidates in trade skills and training methodology, while recruitment notifications determine whether NCIC/CITS is essential, preferred, or required after appointment.

quick_facts.label: Selection method
quick_facts.value: There is no guaranteed common paper pattern. DGT model guidance contemplates a State-level teacher-eligibility test for skills, competencies and aptitude, while individual rules can prescribe other elements such as practical tests, document verification, merit lists, or interviews.

sections.heading: What this recruitment examination is for
paragraphs: “State ITI Vocational Instructor Recruitment Examination” is a useful umbrella name for State- or UT-run selection processes that fill vocational-instructor posts in government Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs). It is not a centrally administered national examination with one permanent syllabus or calendar: DGT sets national policy, standards, instructor training and trade-testing functions, but State Governments and UT Administrations control day-to-day ITI administration.

The selected person teaches and supervises training in a specific vocational trade. Official recruitment rules illustrate the trade-specific nature of the post by listing separate instructor positions and qualifications for areas such as Electrician, Mechanic Motor Vehicle, Electronics Mechanic, ICT System Maintenance, Carpentry, Plumber, COPA and Sewing Technology.
bullets: Treat the State/UT recruitment notification—not coaching material or a generic exam page—as the controlling document for post name, trade, vacancies, reservation, age rules, eligibility, selection stages and appointment conditions.
Do not confuse this recruitment process with CITS admission. CITS is instructor preparation/certification; a State ITI recruitment process is for public employment.

sections.heading: Eligibility: assess it trade by trade
paragraphs: Applicants should match their qualification and experience to the exact trade named in the advertisement. A representative official rule for vocational instructors permits alternative routes: a relevant B.Voc/engineering degree with one year of relevant experience, a relevant three-year diploma or DGT advanced diploma with two years of experience, or an NTC/NAC/STC in the relevant trade with three years of relevant experience. The acceptable disciplines and any additional requirements vary by trade.

CITS leading to the National Craft Instructor Certificate (NCIC) is central to the vocational-instructor ecosystem. DGT describes CITS as training in both technical skills and training methodology; its 2026–27 admission notice identifies NTC, NAC, diploma and degree holders as eligible entrants. However, an applicant must follow the recruitment notice for whether NCIC/CITS is mandatory at application, merely desirable, or to be acquired under service rules.
bullets: Verify the exact trade mapping—for example, Electrical qualifications for Electrician versus Automobile/Mechanical qualifications for Mechanic Motor Vehicle.
Count only experience that the notification recognizes, and preserve employer certificates showing dates, trade/role and nature of duties.

Check additional trade-specific conditions. Official rules may require credentials such as a valid LMV driving licence for a Mechanic Motor Vehicle instructor or shorthand/typing standards for Stenographer & Secretarial Assistant.
Check domicile, age, category/reservation, language, medical fitness and document-format requirements only from the current State/UT notice.

sections.heading: Selection format and assessment
paragraphs: The format is notification-dependent. DGT’s model career-progression guidance proposes a State-level teacher-eligibility test, conducted by the State recruiting agency, to assess prospective ITI trainers’ skills, competencies and aptitude; the model states that such a score would be valid for two years. This is guidance for States, not proof that every current recruitment uses an identical test.

Selection may also be practical or trade-demonstration based. For example, Ladakh recruitment rules provide for selection by a practical test for a promotion channel to vocational instructor. Therefore candidates should not assume that a written test alone decides recruitment, or that a practical test, interview, or teaching demonstration will necessarily appear in every State.
bullets: Read the notification and syllabus for the weighting and qualifying rules for written, practical, teaching-skill, interview and document-verification stages.
If a written examination is prescribed, prepare both the notified trade domain and any stated pedagogy, aptitude, language, general-awareness or computer components.
If a practical/skill test is prescribed, expect assessment against the actual tools, safety practices, fault-finding, procedures and outputs relevant to the notified trade.

sections.heading: How to apply safely
paragraphs: Apply only through the official portal or instructions named in the relevant State/UT recruiting-agency or skill-development/technical-education department notification. Since ITIs are administered by States and UTs, application dates, fees, correction windows, documents and the mode of application can change with each recruitment cycle.

Before submitting, create a trade-wise eligibility file: educational certificates and marksheets, NTC/NAC/STC or diploma/degree evidence, NCIC/CITS certificate if held or required, experience certificates, identity and category certificates, photographs/signature, and any trade-specific licence. Official recruitment advertisements commonly require candidates to upload proof of the advertised qualifications and experience.
bullets: Download and save the advertisement, instructions, submitted form, fee receipt and final confirmation page.
Use the post and trade code exactly as published; applying under a similar-sounding trade can make a candidate ineligible.
Recheck the cut-off date for age, qualification and experience before final submission.
Watch the official notice board for admit cards, corrigenda, answer keys, skill-test notices, document-verification lists and final results.

sections.heading: Preparation strategy
paragraphs: Start with the current notification’s syllabus and selection scheme, then build preparation around the exact trade. For vocational-instructor work, high-value preparation combines trade theory, hands-on procedures, workshop safety, tools and measurement, troubleshooting, quality practices and the ability to explain and demonstrate a task to trainees.

Add teaching-method preparation where the selection rules or job requirements call for it. DGT describes CITS as combining trade technology, engineering/vocational calculation and science, and training methodology/teaching practice. These areas provide a sound framework for developing the instructional capability expected of an ITI instructor, even though they do not replace the notified recruitment syllabus.
bullets: Revise the current curriculum and occupational standards for the relevant ITI trade, not a generic “ITI instructor” question bank.
Practise teaching one workshop task: state the objective, demonstrate safely, let a trainee perform it, observe errors, assess the output and give feedback.
Prepare concise explanations of safety, PPE, workshop discipline, tool selection, measurement and common trade faults.
Maintain originals and clear scans of all credentials early; document scrutiny can be decisive even after an examination or skill test.

sections.heading: What selection can lead to
paragraphs: A successful candidate may be appointed as a trade-specific vocational instructor in a government ITI, subject to the vacancy, merit/selection list, verification and appointment conditions in the State/UT process. The role supports practical vocational training and the transfer of hands-on skills to ITI trainees.

Terms after selection remain jurisdiction-specific. For example, official Ladakh rules show distinct service conditions and a CITS/NCIC-linked progression provision for its vocational-instructor cadre; this should not be treated as a salary or progression promise for other States or UTs. Always rely on the applicable recruitment rules and appointment order.
bullets: Appointment is not confirmed merely by clearing one stage; candidates may still need to pass document verification, medical/character checks and other stated conditions.
CITS/NCIC can strengthen long-term instructor readiness and may be a mandatory qualification or service requirement depending on the applicable rules.

title: State-level Junior Engineer Exam
description: Competitive examinations conducted by various state government bodies to recruit Junior Engineers for state departments and public sector units.

quick_facts.label: Scope
quick_facts.value: This is an umbrella label, not one all-India examination: state recruiting authorities issue their own post-specific notifications, eligibility rules, vacancies, selection stages, and schedules. For example, TNPSC includes Junior Engineer and other diploma-level technical posts in its Combined Technical Services Examination.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry qualification
quick_facts.value: A relevant engineering diploma is commonly required, but the exact branch is post-specific. In TNPSC's 2024 Junior Engineer (Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare) example, the stipulated qualification was a Diploma in Civil Engineering; related technical posts accepted other specified diploma branches or credentials.

quick_facts.label: Selection is notification-led
quick_facts.value: Candidates should not treat application admission as confirmation of eligibility or appointment. TNPSC states that admission is provisional and can be rejected after scrutiny; its process included written examination, certificate verification and, where applicable, counselling.

quick_facts.label: Schedule context
quick_facts.value: Schedules are variable and should be checked against the issuing state's latest notification. TNPSC's 2026 annual planner listed its Diploma/ITI-level Combined Technical Services notification for 7 July 2026 and examination commencement for 20 September 2026, while explicitly describing the planner as tentative and subject to change.

sections.heading: What a state-level Junior Engineer exam is for
paragraphs: State-level Junior Engineer examinations are competitive recruitment processes through which a state public service commission, staff-selection body, department, board, or state undertaking fills technical posts. They are often advertised under a broader technical-services examination rather than under one nationally standardised “State JE Exam” title.

The destination is a state technical post such as Junior Engineer, or a closely related diploma-level role in departments and public bodies. In a TNPSC example, a Junior Engineer post was added for the Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department; the same recruitment also covered technical roles connected with public works, highways, housing, water and urban-development organisations.
bullets: Read the exact notification as the controlling document for the department, engineering discipline, service conditions, reservations, medical standards, vacancy count, and selection method.
Do not assume that a Junior Engineer notification in one state establishes eligibility, syllabus, language requirements, pay level, or dates in another state.

sections.heading: Eligibility: match the post, branch and date cut-off
paragraphs: The central screening task is to match the candidate's qualification to the advertised post. In TNPSC's 2024 Junior Engineer example, a Diploma in Civil Engineering was required. The same addendum demonstrates why candidates must read the individual post table: other technical posts named Civil or Electrical Engineering diplomas, and some posts permitted alternate trade qualifications.

Age, community/reservation status, disability suitability, physical or vision standards, domicile or language requirements, and any experience requirement are state- and post-specific. In the cited TNPSC notification, age and medical/vision conditions were set separately for the Junior Engineer and related posts; these details are not safely transferable to other state recruiters.
bullets: Use the qualification held on the notification's stated cut-off date, not an assumed future qualification.
Confirm that the diploma branch and awarding institution meet the wording in the post table.
Keep originals and valid supporting documents ready for category, disability, age, qualification, experience, and other claims made in the application.

sections.heading: Exam format and selection stages
paragraphs: There is no single format across states. A representative official TNPSC Diploma/ITI-level technical-services notice used a single-stage written examination followed by onscreen certificate verification, physical certificate verification, and counselling where applicable. Its final ranking was based on written-examination marks, subject to applicable reservation rules.

That notification used two compulsory papers: Paper I included a language eligibility component, general studies, and aptitude/mental ability; Paper II was a diploma/ITI-level subject paper aligned to the technical discipline. Paper I was objective/OMR in that notice, while Paper II was computer-based. This is an example, not a universal JE pattern.
bullets: Obtain the current syllabus and scheme from the issuing authority's official recruitment page.
Check whether every paper is compulsory, whether a language paper is qualifying, the test mode, duration, scoring, minimum marks, and the discipline-specific subject-paper code.
Plan for document scrutiny and counselling after the written examination where the notification provides for them.

sections.heading: How to apply safely
paragraphs: Apply only through the official recruiting authority's portal during the published window. In TNPSC's 2024 process, candidates first used One Time Registration and then submitted the examination application online; they had to select the post and the prescribed subject paper corresponding to their qualification. The authority cautioned that a candidate is responsible for claims made in the form.

Deadlines, corrections, fee categories, uploading rules, and examination-centre choices are variable. Treat dates and fees in a particular notification as dated context only, and preserve the submitted application, payment acknowledgement, uploaded-document copies, and later hall-ticket or verification notices.
bullets: Create or update the authority's candidate profile before the last day rather than waiting for the final hours.
Enter the exact name, date of birth, diploma details, category, and post/discipline options supported by documents.
Use any correction window only to fix genuine errors; after its closure, changes may not be allowed.
Monitor the official dashboard for examination date, hall ticket, answer key, result, verification, counselling, and final-selection notices.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Build preparation from the latest official notification and syllabus for the target state and discipline. For a diploma-level technical-services model such as TNPSC's, preparation needs both the core engineering subject paper and the non-technical Paper I components; the cited scheme also makes clear that missing either compulsory paper prevents selection.

Practise in the stated test mode. Where the notice uses objective OMR and CBT papers, timed objective-question practice, error review, and familiarisation with the applicable mode are more relevant than relying on generic JE coaching material. Check the notification for language of question papers and any language-eligibility component before allocating study time.
bullets: Make a topic checklist directly from the official discipline syllabus and revise diploma fundamentals first.
Use official prior question papers, answer keys, and scheme documents when the recruiting authority publishes them.
Practise general studies, quantitative aptitude, reasoning, and required language components only in the weightage and format specified for the target notification.
Reserve time for document readiness; a high written score alone may not survive verification if eligibility claims are unsupported.

sections.heading: What selection can lead to
paragraphs: Successful candidates may enter a Junior Engineer role in a state department or state-linked organisation, but appointment depends on the notified vacancy, rank or merit position, reservation rules, successful verification, medical or other post conditions, and counselling where used. TNPSC's notice explicitly says that appearing in the written exam, being admitted to verification, or even inclusion in a selection list does not by itself create a right to appointment until the applicable conditions are satisfied.

Vacancy numbers, departments, and pay classifications are recruitment-specific and can be revised by addendum. For instance, TNPSC's 2025 addendum added a Junior Engineer post and revised the total vacancies in that technical-services recruitment. Candidates should therefore use the latest notice and corrigenda rather than old vacancy or salary discussions when comparing opportunities.
bullets: Possible next steps include state-government Junior Engineer service, technical roles in state public bodies, and later higher technical qualifications or promotions according to the employer's rules.
Keep checking for corrigenda, revised vacancy tables, document-verification lists, counselling memos, and final selection publications until the recruitment is formally concluded.

title: State Police Constable Recruitment Exam
description: State-level recruitment examinations for the post of Constable in various state police forces.

quick_facts.label: What this node covers
quick_facts.value: This is not one all-India examination. It is a family of state or state-police recruitment processes used to select Police Constables; the recruiting authority, vacancies, eligibility rules, test sequence, and timetable are set in the relevant state notification. Rajasthan Police describes constable as an entry level and notes that districts have separate recruitment, while current notices are also issued through bodies such as Haryana Staff Selection Commission and Bihar’s Central Selection Board of Constable.

quick_facts.label: Typical minimum education
quick_facts.value: The required qualification is notification-specific. For example, Goa’s 2026 Police Constable advertisement requires a Secondary School Certificate examination or equivalent for male and female constable posts; applicants must check the education requirement in the particular state and post advertisement rather than assume a national standard.

quick_facts.label: Physical standards matter
quick_facts.value: Physical measurement and/or efficiency testing is a core feature in many state constable selections. Goa’s 2026 notice specifies sex-specific height and physical-event requirements, and Rajasthan Police lists written, physical/medical examination, and physical-efficiency testing among constable recruitment stages.

quick_facts.label: Written-test pattern
quick_facts.value: There is no universal paper pattern. In one Himachal Pradesh Police constable recruitment notice, the written test was an 80-mark, 60-minute objective paper covering English, Hindi, general awareness, mathematics and science, and reasoning aptitude; another state’s notification may use a different pattern or selection order.

quick_facts.label: Where to track recruitment
quick_facts.value: Candidates should use the official recruiting authority’s notification and recruitment portal for applications, admit cards, test notices, answer keys, results, and document-verification instructions. Official examples include HSSC’s public-notice page, CSBC Bihar’s notifications page, and Mumbai Police’s recruitment page.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
paragraphs: State Police Constable Recruitment Exams are state-level hiring processes for entry-level constable posts in state police organisations. They should not be confused with the SSC Constable (GD) examination for Central Armed Police Forces: Rajasthan Police identifies Police Constable as a state-police entry level, whereas the Government of India’s SSC GD notice concerns CAPFs, SSF and Assam Rifles.
source_urls
bullets: Recruitment may be organised centrally by a state selection commission/board or through police headquarters, districts, or city police units.

The title “constable” can cover different advertised roles or units—for example general-duty, railway-police, driver, bandsman, armed, prison, or other state-specific posts—so the post code and notification must be read closely.

sections.heading: Eligibility: use the notification for the exact rules
paragraphs: Eligibility varies materially by state, category, cadre, and recruitment year. The official Goa Staff Selection Commission advertisement for Police Constable (Male/Female), for example, specifies secondary-school education or equivalent, a stated maximum age, physical standards/events, and knowledge of Konkani. These requirements are evidence of state-specific rules, not a nationwide template.

Applicants should verify the notification’s cut-off date and provisions on age, educational qualification, domicile or local-language requirements where applicable, reservation/category certificates, physical standards, medical fitness, and documents. Do not rely on coaching-site summaries or a previous recruitment cycle when deciding eligibility.
bullets: Check whether the advertised role is general-duty or a specialist post, since driver and bandsman recruitment can have additional tests or requirements.

Keep original and valid supporting certificates ready; Delhi Police’s constable notice, for example, states that required eligibility documents are collected and verified with originals during the physical-endurance/measurement and document-verification stage.

sections.heading: Selection format
paragraphs: A common selection architecture combines a written knowledge test with physical measurement and physical-efficiency/endurance testing, followed by document scrutiny and any required medical examination. The sequence is not fixed nationally: Rajasthan Police lists written, physical/medical, and physical-efficiency stages, while the cited Himachal Pradesh notice places an objective written examination before scrutiny of eligibility documents and certificate marks.

Written-test content also differs by recruitment. The cited Himachal Pradesh example used five areas—English, Hindi, general awareness, mathematics and science, and reasoning aptitude—and prescribed qualifying marks by category. Candidates should treat the syllabus, scoring, negative-marking rule, qualifying threshold, and whether a stage is qualifying or merit-bearing as notification-specific.
bullets: Physical stages may include height/chest measurement where applicable and timed running, jumping, or other events; exact benchmarks can differ by sex, category, geography, and state.

Specialist roles may add a relevant skill test. Mumbai Police’s recruitment page, for instance, publishes separate Bandsman skill-test notices alongside physical-test, written-test, answer-key, and result notices.

sections.heading: Application process
paragraphs: Apply only through the method, portal, and dates named in the current official advertisement. A practical workflow is: locate the state recruiting authority’s notice; read the eligibility, vacancy, reservation, fee, and document instructions; register and submit the form; preserve the acknowledgement; then monitor the same official site for correction windows, admit cards, test schedules, answer keys, results, and verification instructions.

Deadlines and fees are variable, dated recruitment-cycle terms and should never be carried over from an earlier advertisement. Official 2026 HSSC public notices demonstrate that physical-test schedules may be issued, postponed, or rescheduled; official portals are therefore the authoritative place to monitor changes.
bullets: Use the application details exactly as supported by your certificates; discrepancies can surface during document verification.
Download and retain notices, submitted-form copies, fee receipts where applicable, and admit cards.
Treat unofficial social-media claims with caution: CSBC Bihar has published official notices addressing fake-news issues connected with constable recruitment.

sections.heading: Preparation strategy
paragraphs: Prepare from the official syllabus and physical-test table in the advertisement, then work backwards from the stages that are eliminatory or merit-bearing. For the written component, use timed practice in the stated subjects; the Himachal Pradesh notice is a useful illustration of why candidates should cover language, general awareness, quantitative/science material, and reasoning only when those areas actually appear in their notification.

Build physical preparation around the exact notified event, distance, time, jump, measurement, and attempt rules. Goa’s official 2026 Police Constable notice, for example, specifies different physical standards and running/jump events for male and female applicants, showing why generic fitness advice cannot substitute for the applicable recruitment notice.
bullets: Practice completing objective questions under the notified duration and understand the stated marking rules before test day.
Use progressive, safe conditioning and verify your readiness against the official benchmarks; do not wait until after a written-test result to start physical preparation.
Organise certificates early and compare every document against the notification’s wording before document verification.

sections.heading: Outcomes after selection
paragraphs: Successful completion of the applicable selection process can lead to appointment as a Police Constable in the recruiting state force or advertised unit, subject to final merit, verification, medical or other stipulated conditions, and issuance of appointment orders. Recruitment portals commonly publish physical-test results, written-examination results or marks, answer-key/objection notices, and appointment-related updates in separate stages.

The result of a particular constable examination is not transferable as a general qualification for another state’s recruitment: each recruitment authority conducts selection against its own advertised vacancies and conditions. Candidates seeking a police career should separately track every state or unit in which they are eligible to apply.
bullets: Final selection should be confirmed only through the official result, merit/selection list, and appointment communications.
Salary, posting, probation, training, and service conditions are recruitment- and state-specific; consult the current advertisement and appointment terms for dated, authoritative details.

title: State Police Sub-Inspector Recruitment Exam
description: A competitive examination conducted by various state police recruitment boards to select candidates for the post of Sub-Inspector.

quick_facts.label: What this node covers
quick_facts.value: State Police Sub-Inspector recruitment is not a single all-India examination. It is a family of state-specific direct-recruitment processes run through the relevant state police recruitment board; for example, West Bengal Police Recruitment Board (WBPRB) and Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment & Promotion Board (UPPRPB) publish separate SI recruitment notices and results.

quick_facts.label: Typical educational threshold
quick_facts.value: A bachelor’s degree is a common eligibility benchmark, but candidates must rely on the notice for their state and cycle. WBPRB’s 2024 SI recruitment required a bachelor’s degree in any discipline from a recognised university or equivalent.

quick_facts.label: Selection is multi-stage
quick_facts.value: Written examination alone is generally not the complete selection process. In the WBPRB 2024 SI cycle, the route was preliminary examination, physical measurement test (PMT), physical efficiency test (PET), final combined competitive examination, and personality test, followed by character verification and medical examination for provisionally selected candidates.

quick_facts.label: State-specific conditions matter
quick_facts.value: Age limits, category relaxations, local-language requirements, physical standards, vacancies, fees, and the sequence of tests can differ by state and notification. For example, the WBPRB 2024 notice set an age band of 20–30 years as of its stated cut-off date and required Bengali language ability subject to a hill-area exception.

quick_facts.label: Current-cycle context
quick_facts.value: As of the review date, official boards should be checked directly rather than relying on old calendars: UPPRPB’s notice board records publication of the final selection result for its SI Civil Police and equivalent direct recruitment 2025 on 14 July 2026, while WBPRB’s SI 2024 recruitment page lists its final combined competitive-examination notices from February 2026.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
paragraphs: This node represents the competitive recruitment route into the rank of Sub-Inspector in a state police force. There is no single national “State Police SI Exam”: recruitment is announced, administered, and scheduled separately by state-level police recruitment authorities, and a drive may cover more than one SI stream or equivalent post. WBPRB, for instance, ran a combined process for Sub-Inspector posts in its Unarmed and Armed Branches; UPPRPB separately publishes notices for direct recruitment to Sub-Inspector Civil Police and equivalent posts.
source_urls
bullets: Treat the specific state board’s notification as the controlling document for eligibility, vacancies, exam scheme, reservation, physical criteria, fees, and dates.
Do not assume that a notification from one state establishes a rule for another state.

sections.heading: Eligibility: verify the notification for the target state
paragraphs: A bachelor’s degree is a frequent entry requirement for direct SI recruitment, but the exact qualification date and recognition rules are notification-specific. In WBPRB’s 2024 process, applicants needed a bachelor’s degree in any discipline from a recognised university or equivalent, and had to possess the stated qualifications by the online-application deadline.

Age, citizenship, language, reservation documentation, and physical standards must likewise be checked against the live notification. As a dated example only, WBPRB’s 2024 notice required Indian citizenship; an age of 20–30 years on 1 January 2024 with stated relaxations; and Bengali speaking, reading, and writing ability, subject to the published exception for permanent residents of the Darjeeling and Kalimpong hill subdivisions.
source_urls
bullets: Confirm the cut-off date for degree completion and age before applying.
Check whether the state requires a local-language qualification or provides a specified exemption.
Read physical-measurement tables carefully: standards can vary by branch, gender/category, and state.
Keep category, EWS, domicile, identity, educational, and—where applicable—employer NOC documents ready in the form and validity period stipulated by the recruiting board.

sections.heading: Exam and selection format
paragraphs: The format varies by state. A concrete official example is WBPRB’s 2024 SI process: a 200-mark preliminary OMR/MCQ screening examination in General Studies, logical and analytical reasoning, and arithmetic; PMT and PET for candidates clearing the screening stage; a 200-mark final written examination with three conventional-question papers; and a 30-mark personality test. WBPRB stated that preliminary marks were not counted toward final merit and that incorrect preliminary answers attracted one-fourth negative marking.

Physical testing is a qualifying gateway, not merely an administrative formality. In that WBPRB cycle, the notice prescribed PMT standards and a timed run for PET; successful candidates then progressed to the final written stage. The board’s recruitment page also documents the actual sequence of preliminary result, PMT/PET, and final examination notices for that cycle.
source_urls
bullets: Build preparation around the notification’s stated scheme, not a generic coaching template.
Expect written aptitude/general-studies testing plus physical measurement and efficiency assessments in many state SI recruitments.
Check whether the final written stage is objective, descriptive/conventional, or mixed; language papers and interview/personality-test stages are state-dependent.

sections.heading: Application process
paragraphs: Apply only through the portal and within the window named in the relevant state notification. In the WBPRB 2024 example, applications were online only; candidates chose their preferred SI branch while applying, uploaded a recent photograph and signature, and paid the notification-specific fee through approved online payment methods. That cycle’s application period and fee amounts are historical examples, not current universal deadlines or charges.

Before final submission, verify every field and save the application record and payment proof. WBPRB’s notice warned that later corrections could be restricted and that candidates advancing to later stages had to produce originals and supporting reservation/qualification documents. State boards also issue later notices for admit cards, answer keys, physical-test calls, results, and final selection, so applicants should monitor the official recruitment page after applying.
source_urls
bullets: Register through the official state recruitment-board portal linked in the notification.
Upload documents and photographs exactly to the prescribed specifications; retain the submitted application and transaction record.
Download admit cards only from official links, and check official notices for changes to venue, schedule, document verification, or physical-test instructions.
Treat application dates and fees as cycle-specific; confirm them from the current notification before payment.

sections.heading: Preparation strategy
paragraphs: Start with the syllabus and marking rules from the target state’s current notification. WBPRB’s published 2024 scheme illustrates the breadth candidates may need to cover: General Studies/general knowledge, logical and analytical reasoning, arithmetic at the specified school-level standard, English, and a selected regional-language paper at the final stage. Its preliminary stage was time-limited and used negative marking, so timed accuracy practice was important for that particular cycle.

Prepare physical fitness in parallel with written study. The WBPRB example used a qualifying run test after physical measurement, and its stated minimum run distances/times differed by candidate category. Candidates should train only for the standards in their own notice and schedule recovery, injury prevention, and mock test work well before the physical-test call letter.
source_urls
bullets: Map every topic, paper, duration, and negative-marking rule from the official syllabus into a weekly plan.
Use timed practice for arithmetic, reasoning, and general-studies questions; review errors rather than only increasing test volume.
Practise report writing, translation, grammar, and précis if the notification contains descriptive English or regional-language papers.
Measure baseline running capacity early and train progressively toward the notification’s PET requirement; also check PMT standards before committing to the process.

sections.heading: Outcome: appointment as a State Police Sub-Inspector
paragraphs: Candidates who clear all prescribed stages and place high enough in the state-specific merit process may be provisionally selected for appointment as a Sub-Inspector in the advertised branch or stream. In WBPRB’s 2024 model, final merit was based on final written-examination marks plus personality-test marks; candidates also had to meet the personality-test minimum, after which character-antecedent verification and medical examination applied to provisionally selected candidates.

Selection does not mean that every procedural requirement has ended. The WBPRB notice states that the appointing authority depends on the branch/post and that medical fitness, document verification, and character verification remain material conditions. The exact service terms, pay level, probation, training, posting, and branch allocation must be taken from the state’s applicable rules and appointment communication rather than inferred from another state’s recruitment.
source_urls
bullets: The direct career outcome is entry into the state police force as a Sub-Inspector, subject to the advertised branch and appointment process.
Final results, vacancies, and appointment timing are variable; follow the official board’s result notices and subsequent department instructions.

useful_links.label: West Bengal Police Recruitment Board — SI 2024 recruitment page
WBPRB SI 2024 information to applicants (official PDF)
Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment & Promotion Board — notices

title: State PSC Civil Services (various states)
description: State PSC Civil Services (various states) — govt recruitment exam (general), conducted by State Public Service Commissions.

quick_facts.label: What this node covers
quick_facts.value: “State PSC Civil Services” is an umbrella label for state-level competitive recruitment examinations conducted by State Public Service Commissions; it is not one single all-India examination.

quick_facts.label: Constitutional basis
quick_facts.value: Article 315 provides for a Public Service Commission for each State (and permits Joint State Public Service Commissions); Article 320 assigns State Commissions the duty to conduct examinations for appointments to state services.

quick_facts.label: Typical eligibility baseline
quick_facts.value: A recognised bachelor’s degree is a common baseline for general state civil-service posts, but age limits, reservations, domicile or language conditions, physical standards, and post-specific qualifications vary by state and notification. For example, TNPSC Group I’s 2025 notice set a minimum age of 21 and prescribed a recognised degree for several posts.

quick_facts.label: Typical selection route
quick_facts.value: A common pattern is a preliminary screening test followed by a main written examination and interview; Bihar PSC describes recruitment using a main written examination and interview of candidates successful in the prescribed preliminary test, while TNPSC Group I expressly uses preliminary, main, and interview stages.

quick_facts.label: Fees and dates
quick_facts.value: Application dates, vacancies, examination centres, and fees are notification-specific. As dated context only, TNPSC Group I’s 2025 notification listed a ₹100 preliminary fee and ₹200 main fee for candidates not claiming an applicable exemption; these figures must not be treated as current for another state or cycle.

sections.heading: Purpose and institutional role
paragraphs: State PSC Civil Services examinations are the principal competitive-recruitment route for many state civil-service and allied state-government posts. They are conducted by the relevant State Public Service Commission rather than by one national examining body. The Constitution establishes a State Public Service Commission for each State, allows Joint State Public Service Commissions, and assigns State Commissions responsibility for examinations for appointments to state services.

Because this is a cross-state category, the examination name, service groups, vacancy list, reservation rules, language requirements, post preferences, and appointment process must be read from the particular State PSC’s current advertisement. A current West Bengal PSC indicative advertisement, for example, describes its WBCS examination as recruitment to the West Bengal Civil Service (Executive) cadre and certain other services and posts, with detailed conditions to be issued separately.
bullets: Use the official website of the target State PSC as the authoritative source for the live notification, corrigenda, schedule, syllabus, admit-card instructions, results, and document-verification requirements.
Do not assume that eligibility or examination stages from one state transfer unchanged to another state.

sections.heading: Eligibility: check the specific notification
paragraphs: For general civil-service streams, a recognised undergraduate degree is commonly required. In the TNPSC Combined Civil Services Examination–I (Group I Services) notification dated April 1, 2025, a degree from specified recognised Indian universities or institutions was required for posts including Deputy Collector, Deputy Superintendent of Police, Assistant Commissioner (Commercial Taxes), Assistant Director of Rural Development, District Employment Officer, and Assistant Commissioner of Labour.

Age and post conditions are not uniform. The same TNPSC notice required candidates to be at least 21 years old as of July 1, 2025, set different upper-age limits by post and category, and specified differing eligibility for persons with benchmark disabilities. That notice is an illustration of notification-specific rules, not a nationwide State PSC rule.
bullets: Before applying, verify the notification’s cut-off date for age and education, permitted categories and concessions, citizenship or domicile provisions where applicable, language requirements, and medical or physical standards for the chosen post.

Check whether a post has additional or preferential qualifications. In the TNPSC 2025 example, the Commercial Taxes post listed preferences involving commerce, law, and taxation qualifications, while some other posts listed relevant preferred disciplines or experience.
Treat admission to an examination as provisional until document verification and all prescribed conditions are met.

sections.heading: Examination format and selection stages
paragraphs: A widely used State PSC civil-services structure is: preliminary examination, main written examination, and interview/personality test. Bihar PSC states that direct recruitment may be based on a main written examination and interview of candidates successful in the preliminary test. TNPSC Group I’s 2025 notice also describes these three successive stages and identifies preliminary marks as screening marks that do not count toward final merit in that recruitment.

The detailed design is state-specific. TNPSC’s published Group I scheme, for example, shows an objective preliminary paper covering General Studies and Aptitude and Mental Ability, followed by descriptive main papers and an interview. It also includes a Tamil eligibility paper in the main examination, demonstrating why candidates must prepare against the syllabus of their selected State PSC rather than a generic template.
bullets: Preliminary stage: commonly an objective screening examination; qualifying and cut-off rules vary.
Main stage: commonly written papers, often descriptive for senior civil-service streams; subjects, language papers, and marking rules vary.

Final stage: an interview may be used for some services; TNPSC describes its interview as assessing suitability through factors such as personality, bearing, aptitude, and general or technical knowledge.
Merit, reservation, certificate verification, medical examination, and post allocation are governed by the applicable state rules and advertisement.

sections.heading: Application process
paragraphs: Apply only through the target State PSC’s official portal and within the dates in its live notification. Online processes commonly require profile or one-time registration, submission of an examination-specific application, fee payment where applicable, and later uploading or producing supporting documents. For example, TNPSC’s 2025 Group I notice required One Time Registration followed by the online application and gave a limited post-deadline correction window.

Keep a copy of the final submitted application, fee receipt if paid, and documents supporting every claim made in the form. TNPSC’s notice warns that previewing an application is not the same as final submission, and that failure to pay a required fee in time may lead to rejection. Procedures and payment modes differ across State PSCs.
bullets: Read the complete notification and any corrigenda before selecting a service or post preference.
Create or update the required candidate profile or one-time registration, if the State PSC uses one.
Enter educational, category, age-concession, disability, and other claims exactly as supported by documents.
Submit before the deadline, pay any applicable fee through the specified channel, and download the submitted application.
Monitor the official portal for correction windows, admit cards, examination-centre instructions, answer keys, results, document verification, and interview notices.

sections.heading: Preparation approach
paragraphs: Start with the latest official notification, scheme, and syllabus for the selected State PSC and cycle. Build a topic checklist from the prelim and main syllabi separately, because an objective screening examination and descriptive main papers demand different practice. TNPSC’s official Group I scheme illustrates this split: its preliminary paper is objective, while its main General Studies papers are descriptive.

Give deliberate attention to state-specific content and language requirements. State PSC schemes can include state history, geography, administration, public-policy context, or a state-language eligibility component; TNPSC Group I includes a Tamil eligibility test and sets General Studies papers in the main examination. Practise timed objective papers for prelims, timed answer writing for mains, and a concise account of academic background, current issues, and service motivation for any interview stage.
bullets: Download the official syllabus, prior question papers where published, and official answer keys from the State PSC site.
Map every syllabus unit to study material and revise through objective-question practice for prelims and structured answer writing for mains.
Track official notices rather than relying on coaching schedules for dates, syllabus changes, or eligibility interpretation.
Prepare documents early: degree evidence, date-of-birth evidence, category or concession certificates, and any post-specific evidence should match the notification requirements.

sections.heading: Career outcomes
paragraphs: Success can lead to appointment in state civil services and allied departmental posts, with the precise posts determined by the state, examination group, vacancies, rank, reservation rules, preferences, verification, and medical or physical eligibility where prescribed. The TNPSC Group I 2025 notice, for example, included Deputy Collector, Deputy Superintendent of Police, Assistant Commissioner (Commercial Taxes), Assistant Director of Rural Development, District Employment Officer, and Assistant Commissioner of Labour.

The roles linked to this node—such as revenue, police, taxation, labour, rural-development, and employment-department careers—therefore represent possible state-government outcomes, not guaranteed placements from every State PSC examination. Candidates should use the current vacancy and service list to determine which outcomes are actually available in their target cycle.
bullets: Administrative and revenue-track posts may be offered under state civil-service cadres.
Police-service posts may have additional physical or medical eligibility conditions.
Tax, labour, rural-development, and employment roles may be included as allied services or departmental posts in particular state notifications.
Appointment remains subject to the applicable selection list, verification, and service rules; appearing for or qualifying an examination does not itself confer a right to appointment.

title: State TET (various states)
description: State TET (various states) — eligibility exam (teaching), conducted by State education boards.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: “State TET” is a family of state or Union Territory teacher-eligibility tests conducted by the appropriate state authority under the national TET framework; it is not one single all-India examination.

quick_facts.label: Teaching levels
quick_facts.value: The national framework distinguishes Paper I for prospective teachers of Classes I–V and Paper II for Classes VI–VIII. A state’s notification may use its own category names and add state-specific school-level categories.

quick_facts.label: Eligibility baseline
quick_facts.value: For elementary teaching, NCTE’s minimum-qualification notification combines an approved academic/teacher-education route with passing TET; the exact acceptable route and conditions must be checked in the relevant state notification.

quick_facts.label: Passing is not appointment
quick_facts.value: A TET pass is an eligibility criterion, not an automatic right to recruitment or employment. Candidates must separately satisfy the applicable recruitment advertisement, document verification, reservation, subject, language, and other service-rule requirements.

quick_facts.label: State-specific logistics
quick_facts.value: Application dates, fee, media/languages, exam date, paper pattern, qualifying concessions, certificate handling, and recognition rules vary by state and cycle. For example, Maharashtra’s official June 2026 portal lists separate Paper I/Paper II fees and a postponement notice, illustrating why the current notification must be checked rather than relying on a generic TET timetable.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
paragraphs: State TETs are eligibility examinations for elementary-school teaching. Under the NCTE framework, the appropriate government conducts TET for teacher appointment eligibility in Classes I–VIII; the state test normally serves that state’s government, local-authority, and relevant school recruitment ecosystem. The precise applicability of a certificate across employers or states is governed by the applicable state rules and recruitment notice.

Passing State TET should be treated as one step in a teacher-employment pathway rather than as a job offer. The national guidance says that school managements may give weight to TET scores in recruitment, but qualifying TET alone does not create a right to recruitment or employment.
bullets: Use State TET when targeting elementary-teacher roles covered by the particular state’s recruitment rules.
Use the current state notification—not coaching-site summaries—to confirm whether a state TET, CTET, or another accepted certificate is valid for the vacancy.
For private-school roles, employer requirements can differ, although TET may be required or preferred where the applicable rules make it relevant.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: Eligibility is state- and paper-specific. NCTE’s published minimum-qualification framework for Classes I–V includes routes such as Senior Secondary plus a recognised elementary-teacher-education qualification, B.El.Ed., special-education routes, or graduation plus D.El.Ed.; for Classes VI–VIII it includes routes such as graduation plus D.El.Ed. or B.Ed., alongside other specified teacher-education routes. These national provisions have amendments and state-level implementation details, so candidates should match their qualification, marks, category, language and training status to the live state notice.

A current state implementation can be more operationally specific. For example, Maharashtra’s official MAHATET FAQ distinguishes Paper I (Standards 1–5) from Paper II (Standards 6–8) and lists different educational/professional qualification combinations for each. This is an example, not a substitute for another state’s notification.
bullets: Choose Paper I for the primary level, Paper II for the upper-primary level, or both only where your qualifications and target roles support both.
Confirm recognition/status of D.El.Ed., B.Ed., B.El.Ed., special-education, or equivalent credentials before applying.
Check category-related concessions, age conditions if any, domicile/language requirements, and rules for candidates whose teacher-education course is ongoing in the specific notification.

sections.heading: Exam format
paragraphs: The NCTE TET guideline sets a two-paper elementary structure: Paper I for Classes I–V and Paper II for Classes VI–VIII. Its baseline structure uses objective multiple-choice questions, with child development and pedagogy, language, and mathematics/environmental studies in Paper I; Paper II includes child development and pedagogy, languages, and either mathematics/science or social studies. States may operationalise this framework through their own syllabus, language media, categories, timings and instructions.

The guideline describes 150 multiple-choice questions and a 90-minute duration for each paper, but candidates should treat those as framework-level reference points. The current state prospectus/admit-card instructions control the actual pattern, duration, accessibility accommodations, language options and permitted materials for that cycle.
bullets: Download the state’s latest syllabus and paper-wise scheme before beginning preparation.
Prepare for the pedagogy component as well as content knowledge; it is part of both elementary-level papers in the national framework.
Use only the official current-year paper pattern when planning time allocation.

sections.heading: Application process
paragraphs: The typical process is online: read the notification and eligibility rules, create a registration/login, complete the application, upload or enter the required information, pay the applicable fee, submit, and preserve the confirmation/printout. Maharashtra’s official FAQ documents this sequence for MAHATET, while Kerala’s K-TET portal directs applicants to read the notification, prospectus, general information and application guidelines before submission.

Dates and fees are cycle-specific. As a dated illustration only, Maharashtra’s June 2026 portal listed an online application window ending on April 24, 2026 and displayed separate fees for one paper versus both papers; its homepage also displayed a notice that the June 2026 examination had been postponed. Candidates must rely on the live portal for revised dates and should not infer a nationwide schedule from this example.
bullets: Apply only through the designated official state examination portal.
Save the submitted form, payment receipt, application number and login credentials.
Check the portal again for correction windows, admit-card availability, centre details, answer-key objections, result and certificate/document-verification instructions.

sections.heading: Preparation
paragraphs: Begin with the official paper-wise syllabus and model questions for the state and category selected. Kerala’s K-TET portal publishes category-specific syllabi and model-question links, and the MAHATET portal provides an official syllabus, question sets and answer keys. These materials are more reliable than assuming that another state’s topic distribution, terminology or language medium will apply.

Build preparation around the prescribed school-level content plus pedagogy: child development, inclusive learning, assessment, language pedagogy, and subject pedagogy. Then practise timed multiple-choice papers and use official answer keys or model questions to identify recurring weak areas. Recheck the notification shortly before the examination for changes to instructions or schedule.
bullets: Map every official syllabus unit to a study plan before buying materials or joining coaching.
Practise in the language medium selected for the examination whenever official materials are available.
Review official previous question sets, model questions and answer keys; do not treat unofficial answer keys as final.

sections.heading: Outcomes after qualifying
paragraphs: A qualifying State TET result can establish the TET component of eligibility for relevant elementary-teaching recruitment in that state, subject to the certificate’s applicable recognition and the vacancy rules. It can support progression toward primary or upper-primary teaching roles in state-government, local-authority, aided, or private-school settings where the relevant employer and rules accept it.

It does not replace the rest of recruitment. A candidate may still need to meet the post’s academic and professional qualifications, category and document requirements, language/subject conditions, selection-test or merit rules, and employer-specific conditions. The NCTE guidance expressly characterises TET as only one eligibility criterion for appointment.
bullets: Track teacher-recruitment notices separately after qualifying; the TET result itself is not a recruitment application.
Keep the certificate/result, qualification records, identity documents and category certificates ready for verification.
Before applying outside the issuing state, confirm acceptance of that State TET in the specific employer’s notification.

title: TISSNET
description: TISSNET — pg entrance exam (management), conducted by TISS.

quick_facts.label: Current status
quick_facts.value: TISSNET is a legacy TISS entrance-exam label, not the active postgraduate admission test for the 2026–27 cycle. TISS’s current admissions materials use CUET-PG for eligible programmes, CAT 2025 for three named Mumbai programmes, and a separate Non-CUET route for specified blended-learning programmes.

quick_facts.label: Institution
quick_facts.value: Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS), a deemed-to-be university under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956, administers its own programme admissions after the applicable entrance route.

quick_facts.label: 2026 CUET-PG selection basis
quick_facts.value: For the PG programmes covered by the CUET route, TISS states that CUET-PG 2026 score carries 100% weightage; it states there is no Extempore Reflection Test, group discussion, or online personal interview for those programmes.

quick_facts.label: Management-related exceptions in 2026
quick_facts.value: For 2026–27, TISS uses CAT 2025 scores—not TISSNET—for MA Human Resource Management & Labour Relations, MA Organisation Development, Change and Leadership, and Master of Hospital Administration at the Mumbai campus.

quick_facts.label: 2026 application timing
quick_facts.value: The published 2026 CUET-PG TISS-registration window was May 22 to June 11, 2026 (5:00 pm); this is past and dates, portals, and programme availability can change in later cycles.

sections.heading: What TISSNET means now
paragraphs: TISSNET historically referred to TISS’s own postgraduate entrance examination. For a current applicant, it should not be treated as an exam to register for in the 2026–27 cycle. TISS’s official 2026 PG materials state that admissions to its master’s programmes are based on CUET-PG 2026 scores except for three programmes using CAT 2025, while two specified blended-learning education programmes are presented under a Non-CUET route.

The node description is therefore only partly current: TISSNET was not limited to management admissions, and it is no longer the operative route for the current TISS PG cycle. Applicants should identify the exact TISS programme first and then follow its stated CUET-PG, CAT-PG, or Non-CUET procedure.
bullets: Use the official TISS admissions site rather than legacy TISSNET preparation pages or old notification PDFs.
For 2026–27, CAT applies to MA HRM & LR, MA ODCL, and MHA at Mumbai; eligible other listed master’s programmes use CUET-PG, subject to the programme’s published conditions.

sections.heading: Eligibility: check the programme and entrance route
paragraphs: There is no single current “TISSNET eligibility” rule to apply across TISS. TISS publishes programme-specific eligibility criteria and corresponding CUET-PG test-paper codes in its PG admissions materials. A candidate must meet the requirements of the particular programme as well as take the applicable entrance examination.

For the 2026 cycle, candidates for the three CAT-PG programmes needed CAT 2025, while applicants to eligible CUET-PG programmes were assessed through their CUET-PG 2026 score. TISS advises applicants to use its programme list and admission brochure for the precise requirements.
bullets: Confirm the degree/subject prerequisites for the target programme before applying.
Confirm the prescribed CUET-PG paper code where the programme is on the CUET route.
Do not assume that eligibility, testing route, or selection stages from a pre-2024 TISSNET notice remain valid.

sections.heading: Current assessment format
paragraphs: TISSNET has no current 2026 examination format because it is not the active TISS PG entrance route. For CUET-route TISS programmes, the relevant exam format is CUET-PG as conducted by the National Testing Agency; the TISS admission decision is based on CUET-PG 2026 score at 100% weightage for the programmes covered by TISS’s CUET selection criteria.

For the three CAT-PG programmes, applicants use CAT 2025 for the entrance-score component and should follow the TISS programme-specific selection process and calendar rather than any historical TISSNET pattern.
bullets: CUET-PG route: prepare according to the NTA CUET-PG paper applicable to the intended TISS programme.
CAT-PG route: prepare for CAT and monitor TISS’s separate selection and assessment notices.
Do not rely on old TISSNET sections, question patterns, or cut-offs as a current admission format.

sections.heading: How the 2026 process worked
paragraphs: For the CUET-PG route, the published 2026 calendar shows two distinct steps: registration for CUET-PG through the NTA process, followed by TISS’s own online application/registration and fee payment after the CUET result process. TISS then published merit lists and conducted document verification at the respective campuses.

The listed 2026 TISS CUET-PG application window ran from May 22, 2026 to June 11, 2026 at 5:00 pm. These dates are historical as of July 19, 2026, and TISS labels its schedule as tentative and subject to change. A future-cycle applicant should wait for the official calendar and follow the route assigned to the chosen programme.
bullets: 1. Choose a TISS programme and verify its entrance route and eligibility.
2. Take the required entrance examination: CUET-PG, CAT, or the specified Non-CUET assessment.
3. Complete the separate TISS programme application when its portal opens, if required for that route.
4. Monitor official merit-list, acceptance, fee-payment, and original-document-verification notices.

sections.heading: Preparation strategy for a former TISSNET aspirant
paragraphs: Replace a TISSNET-centric study plan with preparation for the current route. For a CUET-PG-eligible TISS programme, first locate the prescribed test-paper code and study the NTA syllabus and format for that paper. For the three CAT-PG programmes, prepare for CAT and then follow TISS’s programme-specific shortlist and assessment instructions.

TISS also notes that it receives CUET scores from multiple subject papers and uses a normalisation approach to make results comparable; where a candidate has taken multiple subjects, its 2026 brochure says the best-performing score is considered for the merit list. This makes selecting appropriate, permitted CUET subject papers and carefully checking TISS’s current rules important.
bullets: Start with the official TISS programme list, eligibility criteria, and required test-paper code—not a generic TISSNET syllabus.
Use the official NTA CUET-PG information for CUET preparation and the official CAT materials for CAT-route programmes.
Re-check TISS notices before every application or admission milestone because procedures and dates are cycle-specific.

sections.heading: What successful applicants receive
paragraphs: The entrance route is an admissions mechanism, not a qualification by itself. Successful applicants are offered places in TISS postgraduate programmes subject to merit-list position, the applicable reservation and priority rules, payment and acceptance steps, and document verification.

For CUET-route programmes in 2026, TISS states that reservation and priority rules are applied for final seat allocation through the merit list or waitlist. The institute’s PG programme page lists postgraduate offerings across its campuses; available programmes and their credit structures are subject to the applicable admission cycle and academic framework.
bullets: A qualifying CUET-PG or CAT score does not itself guarantee a TISS offer.
Complete acceptance, fees, and original-document verification within the dates stated in the relevant merit-list notice.
Review the specific TISS programme page for curriculum and campus details rather than inferring them from the former TISSNET exam label.

title: TOEFL iBT
description: TOEFL iBT — abroad exam (general), conducted by ETS.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: Educational Testing Service (ETS) administers the TOEFL iBT.

quick_facts.label: Purpose
quick_facts.value: An academic-English assessment covering Reading, Listening, Writing and Speaking, intended to help applicants and institutions assess readiness for English-medium academic communication.

quick_facts.label: Test delivery
quick_facts.value: Available on computer at an authorized test center and, where offered and suitable, as the TOEFL iBT Home Edition monitored by a live human proctor.

quick_facts.label: Current score reporting scale
quick_facts.value: For tests taken on or after January 21, 2026, ETS reports four section scores and an overall score on a 1–6 scale in half-point increments; a comparable 0–120 overall-score estimate is included during the two-year transition after January 2026.

quick_facts.label: Score validity
quick_facts.value: TOEFL iBT scores are valid for two years from the test date.

quick_facts.label: India fee context
quick_facts.value: ETS India's fee page displays a TOEFL iBT registration fee of ₹15,254. This is variable context: ETS states that fees and service charges can change, so applicants should verify the live India fee page before paying.

sections.heading: What TOEFL iBT is for
paragraphs: TOEFL iBT is an ETS English-language test designed around academic communication. ETS states that it measures Reading, Listening, Speaking and Writing as they are used in classrooms, using academic content and integrated tasks. For an Indian applicant, it is generally relevant when a chosen overseas university, programme, scholarship body or other recipient asks for TOEFL iBT evidence; confirm acceptance and the required score directly with every recipient rather than relying on a general acceptance list.

As of ETS’s current score-reporting policy, institutions may express requirements using either the newer 1–6 scale or a legacy 0–120 scale during the transition. An official report for a test taken on or after January 21, 2026 includes the 1–6 results and a comparable 0–120 overall-score estimate, but each institution decides which scores and score-reporting arrangements it accepts.
bullets: Use the test only after checking the destination programme’s English-language requirement, minimum section and overall scores, accepted test modes, and application deadline.
Do not treat an ETS destination-search listing as final confirmation: ETS says its results are a guide and directs applicants to verify with institutions.

sections.heading: Identity and accommodation requirements for test takers in India
paragraphs: For testing in India, ETS lists a passport bearing the candidate’s name, photograph and signature as the acceptable primary identification document for a person testing within their country of citizenship. The name and date of birth entered at registration must exactly match the identification used on test day; ETS warns that a mismatch can prevent testing and result in loss of the test fee.
Candidates who need disability- or health-related testing accommodations should begin early. ETS states that qualifying accommodations must be approved before registration.
bullets: Check the India-specific ID page before booking, especially if citizenship, test location or passport details differ from the usual case.
For Home Edition, separately review ETS’s technical, room, identity-verification and proctoring requirements before choosing that delivery mode.

sections.heading: Format, timing and scoring
paragraphs: For TOEFL iBT tests from January 21, 2026 onward, ETS describes an adaptive test with four sections: Reading, Listening, Writing and Speaking. The published task types include Complete the Words, Read in Daily Life and an academic passage in Reading; response, conversation, announcement and academic-talk tasks in Listening; sentence-building, email and academic-discussion tasks in Writing; and listen-and-repeat plus interview tasks in Speaking.

ETS gives an approximate base time of 30 minutes for Reading, 29 minutes for Listening, 23 minutes for Writing and 8 minutes for Speaking. Directions are additional, and ETS advises allowing about two hours in total; because the test adapts, time and item counts may vary.

The current report gives a score for each of the four skills and an overall score on the 1–6 scale in half-point increments. The overall score is the average of the four section scores, rounded to the nearest half band. ETS also provides a comparable 0–120 overall estimate during the transition period beginning January 2026.
bullets: Test center delivery is computer-based at an authorized center.
Home Edition delivery is computer-based at home with live human proctoring; confirm that the intended university accepts this mode before registering.

sections.heading: Registration and score-sending workflow
paragraphs: Create an ETS account, choose an available test appointment and register online or by phone. Enter the name and date of birth exactly as shown on the ID document that will be presented on test day. ETS recommends choosing a test date two to three months before the earliest admissions deadline and registering roughly four months before the desired test date; this is planning guidance, not an admissions deadline.

For applicants in India, ETS’s currently displayed registration fee is ₹15,254. ETS also lists separate, variable charges for late registration, rescheduling, score review and additional score reports. Recheck the official India page at the point of booking, because fees and policies can change.

The test fee includes up to four official score reports for recipients selected by the applicable cutoff. Official scores for tests taken on or after January 21, 2026 are posted to the ETS account approximately three days after the test; recipient delivery time depends on the recipient’s delivery method. Build this processing time and the university’s own application deadline into the plan.
bullets: Before payment: verify the programme’s deadline, its required overall and section scores, whether it accepts Home Edition, and its institutional score-recipient details.
Before test day: ensure the passport and ETS-account details match exactly.
After testing: download the ETS score report when available and confirm with the university that official scores were received if its application system requires this.

sections.heading: How to prepare effectively
paragraphs: Base preparation on the format that applies to the planned test date. For the post–January 21, 2026 version, practise the published task families across all four skills and become comfortable with the adaptive computer-based experience. ETS offers official preparation materials, including free interactive sample questions and free full-length practice tests, alongside paid options.

Use timed practice to identify a skill-level constraint, then practise targeted academic reading, listening, writing and speaking tasks. Before relying on a score target, compare the programme’s required section and overall scores with the current ETS score-report format; universities can update their admissions pages at different times.
bullets: Take at least one official full-length practice test under realistic timing conditions.
Practise the exact current Writing and Speaking task types rather than studying only older TOEFL formats.
Use official materials to learn the interface and score-report scale; use other resources only as supplementary practice.

sections.heading: Scores, reporting and next steps
paragraphs: ETS posts official TOEFL iBT scores for tests taken on or after January 21, 2026 approximately three days after the test date, and the scores remain valid for two years. The test fee includes up to four official score reports; additional reports can be ordered through the ETS account for a fee. Delivery to a designated institution varies by delivery channel, so an applicant should not equate ETS score availability with completion of the university’s application review.

There is no universal “good” TOEFL score. ETS states that the relevant score is the score needed by the institution being applied to, and institutions set their own requirements. Applicants should therefore use the score report to meet a specifically verified recipient requirement, not as a standalone admission guarantee.
bullets: Keep a PDF copy of the report, but follow the recipient’s instructions on official electronic delivery.
Scores older than two years cannot be reported or verified by ETS.
If retesting is needed, ETS’s bulletin says there is no overall limit on attempts, but a test taker cannot take the test more than once in a three-day period.
