title: TS EAMCET (TG EAPCET)
description: TS EAMCET (TG EAPCET) — ug entrance exam (engineering), conducted by JNTU Hyderabad / TSCHE.

quick_facts.label: Current name and legacy name
quick_facts.value: The Telangana Engineering, Agriculture and Pharmacy Common Entrance Test is officially styled TG EAPCET; “TS EAMCET” remains a widely used legacy name for the examination.

quick_facts.label: Conducting arrangement
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, JNT University Hyderabad conducted TG EAPCET on behalf of the Telangana Council of Higher Education (TGCHE).

quick_facts.label: Engineering-paper structure (2026)
quick_facts.value: The Engineering paper has 160 objective questions—80 Mathematics, 40 Physics and 40 Chemistry—for 160 marks, with one mark per correct response and no negative marking.

quick_facts.label: Mode and duration (2026)
quick_facts.value: The Engineering test is a computer-based test of three hours; 2026 sessions were scheduled from 9:00 AM–12:00 noon and 3:00 PM–6:00 PM.

quick_facts.label: Engineering-stream qualification route
quick_facts.value: For engineering courses, the 2026 notification permits candidates who have passed or are appearing in the final year of Intermediate (10+2) with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, or a recognized equivalent; course-specific conditions also apply at admission.

quick_facts.label: Admission use
quick_facts.value: A TG EAPCET rank is used in Telangana’s centralized admissions process for eligible candidates; admission also depends on counseling eligibility, verification, options exercised, reservation/local-status rules, seat availability and allotment.

sections.heading: What TG EAPCET is for
paragraphs: TG EAPCET is Telangana’s undergraduate entrance examination for Engineering, Agriculture and Pharmacy professional-course pathways. In the engineering context, its rank is used for admissions to first-year B.E./B.Tech. and specified related programmes offered by Telangana universities and private unaided affiliated professional colleges, subject to the applicable admission rules and each course’s requirements.

The exam itself is distinct from admission: writing or qualifying in TG EAPCET does not by itself create a right to a seat. The subsequent admissions authority verifies eligibility and allocates seats through counseling and web-option processing.
bullets: Use the official exam portal for examination notices, application access, hall-ticket/result services, syllabus and mock-test materials.
Use the TGCHE/NIC TG EAPCET admissions portal for counseling-stage instructions, certificate verification, web options and allotment information.

sections.heading: Eligibility: separate exam eligibility from seat-admission eligibility
paragraphs: For the 2026 examination, applicants had to be Indian nationals, Persons of Indian Origin (PIO), or Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card holders, and meet Telangana local/non-local-status requirements. The precise application and admission rules can change by cycle, so candidates should treat the current official notification and counseling notification as controlling documents.

For the Engineering stream, the core academic route is passing or appearing in the final year of Intermediate (10+2) with Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, or a recognized equivalent. The detailed notification also sets course-specific conditions—for example, different subject, marks, age or qualification requirements may apply to particular programmes. A candidate eligible to sit the test must still meet the separate requirements for counseling and the allotted course.
bullets: Check the current cycle’s notification before paying the fee or choosing a stream.
Keep original and scanned qualifying-exam, identity, study/local-status, category/EWS and special-category documents ready where applicable; counseling verification is consequential.
Do not infer eligibility for every programme merely from an EAPCET rank: the admissions notification and the institution/course rules apply additionally.

sections.heading: Engineering test format
paragraphs: In the 2026 Engineering instruction booklet, TG EAPCET used a three-hour computer-based test with 160 multiple-choice questions: Mathematics 80, Physics 40 and Chemistry 40. Each correct answer carried one mark, and the booklet specified no negative marking.

The 2026 test was held in multiple sessions. The official process describes normalization to account for session-level variation before ranks are prepared; candidates should therefore focus on maximizing their own correct responses rather than treating another shift’s perceived difficulty as a direct score comparison.
bullets: Total: 160 questions / 160 marks.
Subject weight: Mathematics 50%; Physics 25%; Chemistry 25%.
Question languages for the Engineering paper are English–Telugu or English–Urdu, as specified in the instruction booklet.

sections.heading: Application and admissions workflow
paragraphs: The recurring workflow is: read the official notification and stream-specific instruction booklet; submit the online application and fee through the official EAPCET portal within the notified window; use any notified correction facility; download the hall ticket; take the test; then use the rank/result in the separate TGCHE admissions process if eligible. Dates, fee amounts, correction rules and acceptable payment methods are cycle-specific and should never be carried forward from an earlier year.

For the 2026 cycle, the examination application period and testing dates have already passed. Candidates planning a future attempt should monitor the official EAPCET portal for the next notification rather than relying on third-party calendars. Candidates participating in admissions should follow the TGCHE/NIC portal’s live counseling instructions, including certificate verification and option-entry requirements.
bullets: Enter names, qualifying-exam details, category and local-status information exactly as supported by documents.
Save the payment reference, application number, submitted application PDF and hall ticket.
At counseling, upload or present only the documents specified in the live admissions notification; incomplete or incorrect documents can affect eligibility or allotment.

sections.heading: Preparation approach for the Engineering stream
paragraphs: Build preparation around the officially prescribed Engineering syllabus and the actual paper structure: Mathematics accounts for half of the questions, while Physics and Chemistry account for one quarter each. Study the Intermediate-level concepts in the official syllabus first, then use timed practice to convert knowledge into three-hour computer-based-test execution.

Use the official online mock test and official/authorized question-paper and answer-key materials when they are published for the relevant cycle. Practice full 160-question sessions under the same time limit, then review errors by topic, calculation mistake, concept gap and time-management issue. Because there is no negative marking in the 2026 scheme, a test-day attempt strategy should be based on informed answers and sufficient time to read every remaining question, rather than leaving answers blank solely due to a penalty concern.
bullets: Create a topic checklist from the official syllabus, not from a coaching-provider prediction list.
Take full-length CBT-style mocks regularly and review them more carefully than you take them.
Prioritize accuracy in familiar questions before spending disproportionate time on one difficult problem.

sections.heading: What a TG EAPCET result can lead to
paragraphs: The principal outcome is a normalized TG EAPCET rank that can support participation in Telangana undergraduate professional-course admissions, provided the candidate meets the counseling and course eligibility conditions. For engineering applicants, choices normally involve both programme/branch and college; the outcome is determined by the candidate’s rank, verified eligibility, applicable reservation and local/unreserved rules, preferences, seats available and the counseling allotment process.

A rank is also recognized in some JNTUH-specific opportunities alongside other admission routes. For example, JNTUH’s 2026 international integrated-programme notifications specified seat allocation using JEE Main and TG EAPCET ranks. This is programme-specific, not a general guarantee of admission or employment.

Neither an EAPCET score nor an allotment is a salary, placement, ranking or career-outcome guarantee. Those outcomes vary materially by institution, branch, student performance, internships, labor-market conditions and the year of graduation.
bullets: After results, compare eligible colleges and branches using official intake, fee and accreditation information for the applicable year.
Rank preferences broadly enough during web-option entry to reduce the risk of receiving no allotment.
Read the allotment, reporting and fee-payment instructions for the current counseling phase carefully; missing a deadline can affect the allotment.

title: UCEED
description: UCEED — ug entrance exam (design), conducted by IIT Bombay.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: UCEED (Undergraduate Common Entrance Examination for Design) is the entrance examination used for B.Des admission at the 2026 participating institutes; IIT Bombay is the organizing institute for UCEED 2026.

quick_facts.label: 2026 participating B.Des institutes
quick_facts.value: The joint UCEED 2026 B.Des process covers IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, IIT Guwahati, IIT Hyderabad, IIT Indore, IIT Roorkee and IIITDM Jabalpur.

quick_facts.label: Exam eligibility versus admission eligibility
quick_facts.value: For UCEED 2026, students from Science, Commerce and Arts & Humanities could appear for the exam if they met the age, attempt and qualifying-exam rules. B.Des eligibility then differed by institute: PCM students could apply to all seven participating institutes, while candidates from other streams were limited to IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, IIT Hyderabad and IIT Indore; IIITDM Jabalpur also accepted PCM/Biology for its stated requirement.

quick_facts.label: 2026 paper format
quick_facts.value: UCEED 2026 was a single English-language, three-hour, 300-mark paper. Part A was a two-hour computer-based test with NAT, MSQ and MCQ sections (200 marks); Part B was one hour and had subjective sketching and design-aptitude questions (100 marks).

quick_facts.label: Score and admission
quick_facts.value: A UCEED 2026 score was valid only for admissions in academic year 2026–27. Obtaining a rank did not guarantee admission: qualified candidates needed to submit the separate common B.Des application and participate in joint seat allocation.

quick_facts.label: 2026 cycle status
quick_facts.value: The UCEED 2026 examination was held on January 18, 2026; results were declared on March 6, 2026. The official schedule states that score-card downloads remain available through July 31, 2026. These dates are specific to the 2026 cycle and should not be treated as future-cycle deadlines.

sections.heading: What UCEED is for
paragraphs: UCEED is the national undergraduate design entrance examination organized by IIT Bombay for the 2026 cycle. Its central role is admission to B.Des programmes at the seven participating institutes through a common application and joint seat-allocation process administered by the UCEED Office, IIT Bombay.

A UCEED rank is an examination outcome, not an automatic seat offer. Candidates who qualify must separately apply for B.Des admission, state their institute preferences, provide supporting documents and then take part in seat allocation. The official UCEED site also lists result-sharing institutes, but those institutions set their own programme, application and admission rules rather than joining the IIT Bombay joint allocation process.
bullets: For the 2026–27 joint B.Des process, the participating institutes were IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, IIT Guwahati, IIT Hyderabad, IIT Indore, IIT Roorkee and IIITDM Jabalpur.
Treat the score as valid for the corresponding admission year only; the 2026 score applied to academic year 2026–27.

sections.heading: Eligibility: examine the institute-specific rules, not only the exam rule
paragraphs: In the 2026 cycle, an applicant had to satisfy all three exam conditions: the applicable date-of-birth limit, no more than two attempts in consecutive years, and the stated Class XII/equivalent timing requirement. Students from every school stream—Science, Commerce and Arts & Humanities—could appear for UCEED 2026 if they met those conditions.

That broad examination eligibility did not mean eligibility for every B.Des seat. For 2026 B.Des admission, a candidate needed a UCEED rank and passage of all five qualifying-examination subjects in 2025 or 2026. PCM at Class XII enabled applications to all seven participating institutes; candidates from other streams could apply to IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, IIT Hyderabad and IIT Indore. IIT Guwahati and IIT Roorkee required PCM, while IIITDM Jabalpur listed Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics/Biology.
bullets: The node’s PCM parent is especially relevant for access to IIT Guwahati, IIT Roorkee and, with the stated subject combination, IIITDM Jabalpur.

A three-year diploma could be acceptable for appearing in UCEED 2026, but the official brochure cautioned that participating-institute admission rules might not consider diploma holders; verify the admission rule for the target institute and year.
Age limits, qualifying-year windows and accepted credentials are cycle-specific; use the next official information brochure before applying.

sections.heading: Exam format and the abilities assessed
paragraphs: The 2026 UCEED paper had two compulsory parts within a total of three hours. Part A was a two-hour computer-based component worth 200 marks: 14 numerical-answer questions, 15 multiple-select questions and 28 multiple-choice questions. Part B was a one-hour, 100-mark subjective component: one sketching question and one design-aptitude question, answered in the supplied booklet while the prompts were displayed on screen.

The published syllabus indicates that Part A assesses visualization and spatial reasoning, practical and scientific knowledge, observation and design sensitivity, environment and society, analytical and logical reasoning, English comprehension and creativity. Part B assesses drawing—such as proportion, perspective and shading—and the ability to respond to design problems with ingenuity and empathy.
bullets: For 2026, Part A included negative marking for incorrect MSQs and MCQs; numerical-answer questions had no negative marking.
Part B is mandatory and subjectively evaluated, so preparation should cover both timed computer-based reasoning and hand-drawn visual communication.

sections.heading: Two-stage process: UCEED registration, then B.Des admission application
paragraphs: The examination registration and B.Des admission application are separate activities. For the 2026 examination, registration was online through the UCEED portal; candidates were responsible for accurate category and qualifying-exam information and for uploading valid documents. The registration fee was non-refundable and non-transferable.

After qualifying in UCEED 2026, applicants for the seven participating B.Des programmes used a common application through the IIT Bombay Admissions Portal. They entered personal details and ordered institute preferences, then submitted the form after paying the processing fee and uploading the required documents, including the score card and Class XII/equivalent records. The 2026 B.Des application window ran from March 14 to April 10, 2026, and is now closed; do not infer future deadlines from it.
bullets: Documents stated for the 2026 B.Des application included a photograph, signature, UCEED score card, qualifying-examination mark sheet, and—where applicable—category, PwD and OCI/PIO documentation.
For a future cycle, monitor the official UCEED site for its registration dates, current brochure, portal instructions and any revised schedule.

sections.heading: Preparation approach grounded in the official syllabus
paragraphs: Build preparation around the official topic list rather than assuming UCEED is solely a drawing test. Practice spatial transformations, observation of everyday products and settings, analytical reasoning, scientific principles in daily objects, design-aware reading of social and environmental contexts, English comprehension, and creative interpretation of symbols and analogies. Separately develop sketching fundamentals and concise, practical design responses for Part B.

Use official past papers and answer keys to learn the question styles and timing. IIT Bombay provides past UCEED papers and keys from 2015 through 2025, and the official FAQ says that it does not recommend particular textbooks; it directs candidates to the syllabus and previous papers.
bullets: Simulate the 2026-style time split: two hours for Part A and one hour for Part B.
For Part B, practise proportion, composition, perspective, line quality and shading, then review whether your solution responds empathetically and practically to the given situation.
Use the official sample interface to become comfortable with the computer-test workflow; it is designed for a desktop browser.

sections.heading: What a UCEED result can lead to
paragraphs: For the 2026 cycle, a qualified UCEED candidate could seek B.Des admission through the common process at the seven participating institutes, subject to institute-specific academic-stream eligibility, rank, stated preferences, document verification and the seat-allocation rules. The participating-institute route is specifically a B.Des route; UCEED itself does not convert a rank into a guaranteed offer.

UCEED may also be useful when applying to institutes identified by IIT Bombay as result-sharing institutes, but these are not part of the joint IIT Bombay B.Des allocation. Applicants should check the target institution’s own programme title, eligibility, fee, portfolio or interview requirements, application dates and decision process. This matters particularly for outcomes such as B.F.A., because the official UCEED joint process described here is for B.Des programmes, while other degree routes depend on the individual institution.
bullets: In the 2026 process, eligible B.Des applicants could preference IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, IIT Guwahati, IIT Hyderabad, IIT Indore, IIT Roorkee and IIITDM Jabalpur in the common application.
Fees are variable and institute-specific: the UCEED 2026 brochure states that 2026–27 programme fee structures would be published by the respective institutes closer to admission.

title: UGC-NET
description: UGC-NET — eligibility exam (general), conducted by NTA. Assistant Professor eligibility + JRF.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: The National Testing Agency (NTA) conducts UGC-NET on behalf of the University Grants Commission (UGC).

quick_facts.label: What it determines
quick_facts.value: UGC-NET determines eligibility in three result categories: JRF and Assistant Professor; Assistant Professor and Ph.D. admission; or Ph.D. admission only.

quick_facts.label: Exam mode
quick_facts.value: The June 2025 cycle was conducted as a computer-based test (CBT). Candidates should confirm the mode in the bulletin for their own cycle.

quick_facts.label: Test structure
quick_facts.value: In the June 2025 bulletin, the test had 50 Paper I MCQs (100 marks) and 100 subject-specific Paper II MCQs (200 marks), completed in one 180-minute session without a break.

quick_facts.label: Core qualification route
quick_facts.value: For the June 2025 cycle, a UGC-recognized master's degree or equivalent with at least 55% for General/Unreserved/General-EWS candidates, or 50% for OBC-NCL, SC, ST, PwD and third-gender candidates, was the standard eligibility route.

quick_facts.label: JRF age rule
quick_facts.value: For the June 2025 cycle, JRF applicants had to be no more than 30 years old on June 1, 2025; Assistant Professor and Ph.D.-admission categories had no upper age limit. Age cut-offs and relaxations are cycle-specific.

sections.heading: What UGC-NET is for
paragraphs: UGC-NET is India’s national eligibility test for Indian nationals seeking one of three outcomes in universities and colleges: Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) with Assistant Professor eligibility, Assistant Professor eligibility with Ph.D. admission, or Ph.D. admission only. The qualifying category matters: the “Ph.D. only” outcome does not confer JRF or Assistant Professor eligibility, while the Assistant Professor-and-Ph.D. category does not confer JRF.

The test is an eligibility credential, not an appointment offer. A candidate who qualifies for Assistant Professor remains subject to the recruitment rules of the relevant university, college, or state government. JRF-qualified candidates may pursue research subject to securing placement under the applicable institution’s process; the June 2025 bulletin states that the JRF offer is valid for three years from issue of the JRF award letter.
bullets: For Category 2 and Category 3 UGC-NET Ph.D. admissions, the June 2025 rules provided 70% weight to NET marks and 30% to the university/HEI interview or viva voce; those NET marks were valid for Ph.D. admission for one year from the result date.
Applicants should treat these as cycle-specific rules and read the information bulletin published for the session in which they apply.

sections.heading: Eligibility: main routes and important limits
paragraphs: The standard June 2025 eligibility route was a master’s degree or equivalent from a UGC-recognized institution: at least 55% marks without rounding for General/Unreserved/General-EWS candidates, and at least 50% without rounding for OBC-NCL, SC, ST, PwD, and third-gender candidates. Candidates awaiting final master’s results could apply provisionally, but had to meet the required marks and complete the qualification within the stated period after the NET result.

The June 2025 bulletin also allowed a four-year/eight-semester bachelor’s degree route with at least 75% aggregate, with a 5% relaxation for specified categories. This route could lead to JRF and Ph.D. admission, but not Assistant Professor eligibility. Candidates are advised to choose their postgraduate subject; if it is not listed among NET subjects, they may choose a related subject.
bullets: JRF had a cycle-specific upper-age limit of 30 years as of June 1, 2025. The bulletin provided specified relaxations, including up to five years for women and OBC-NCL/SC/ST/PwD/third-gender candidates, and three years for an LL.M.; total relaxation on the listed grounds could not exceed five years.
There was no upper age limit for the Assistant Professor or Ph.D.-admission categories in the June 2025 cycle.

Eligibility is self-declared at application and remains provisional; NTA states that it does not verify eligibility documents during online registration, and the relevant institution verifies qualifications and category documents later.

sections.heading: Exam format and scoring
paragraphs: The June 2025 UGC-NET scheme used CBT and two compulsory objective, multiple-choice sections in one uninterrupted three-hour session. Paper I had 50 questions for 100 marks and assessed teaching/research aptitude, reasoning, reading comprehension, divergent thinking, and general awareness. Paper II had 100 questions for 200 marks and assessed knowledge in the subject selected by the candidate.

Each question carried two marks, with two marks for a correct response and no negative marking for an incorrect response. Unanswered questions received no marks. Except for language papers, the June 2025 question paper was offered in English and Hindi; the medium selected in the application could not later be changed, and the English version governed if there was a translation ambiguity.
bullets: Total questions: 150; total marks: 300.
The published syllabus for each NET subject is linked through the UGC-NET bulletin; Paper II preparation should be tied to the official syllabus for the selected subject.
In multi-shift subjects, NTA may use its stated normalization procedure and report percentile/NTA Score alongside marks as applicable.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Applications are submitted online through the official UGC-NET/NTA portal when a cycle opens. In the June 2025 process, candidates registered using their own email address and mobile number, completed the form, uploaded a photograph and signature, paid the fee online, and saved the confirmation page. The application was treated as successful only after successful fee receipt.

Before applying, prepare identity and education details, the NET and postgraduate subject codes, category/PwD/EWS documents where applicable, and preferred examination cities. In June 2025, applicants selected four city preferences; NTA aimed to allot a city in the listed order but could allot another city for administrative reasons. Admit cards were downloaded from the website rather than sent by post.
bullets: Cycle-specific fee context: June 2025 charged ₹1,150 for General/Unreserved, ₹600 for General-EWS/OBC-NCL, and ₹325 for SC/ST/PwD/third-gender candidates, plus applicable payment-gateway charges and GST. Fees, dates, categories, and correction-window rules can change, so do not rely on these figures for a future session.
Only one application form was permitted in the June 2025 instructions; applications in other modes were not accepted.
Use only the current official bulletin and portal for deadlines, uploads, accepted IDs, fee payment, correction windows, city choices, and admit-card instructions.

sections.heading: Preparation approach grounded in the official scheme
paragraphs: Build a two-track plan because both papers contribute to aggregate performance. Use the official subject syllabus to map Paper II topics and study the Paper I capabilities named in the bulletin: teaching/research aptitude, reasoning, reading comprehension, divergent thinking, and general awareness. Allocate timed practice to the full 150-question, 180-minute CBT format rather than treating Paper I and Paper II as separate exam sittings.

Practice in a computer-based environment. The June 2025 bulletin directed candidates to NTA’s mock-test facility and also explains that candidates may later receive a limited opportunity to view recorded responses and challenge provisional answer keys for a prescribed fee. After each practice set, review weak syllabus units, accuracy, and pacing; since there was no negative marking in the cited cycle, formulate an attempt strategy only after confirming the current cycle’s marking rules.
bullets: Download and use the official syllabus for the exact Paper II subject selected in the application.
Take full-length timed mocks and rehearse on-screen navigation, marked-for-review use, and final submission.
Check the current official bulletin before relying on the 2025 medium, marking, or answer-key-challenge rules.

sections.heading: Results, cut-offs, and what qualifying means
paragraphs: UGC-NET qualification is competitive and subject/category-specific, not a simple fixed pass mark. Under the June 2025 result methodology, candidates first had to appear in both papers and achieve at least 40% aggregate for General/General-EWS or 35% aggregate for reserved categories. The number qualified for Assistant Professor eligibility was then set at 6% of candidates who appeared in both papers on the master’s-degree/equivalent basis, with category and subject allocation used to derive cut-offs.

NTA published June 2025 results in three outcome categories: JRF and Assistant Professor, Assistant Professor and Ph.D. admission, and Ph.D. only. The official June 2025 results release reported 5,269 candidates in the first category, 54,885 in the second, and 128,179 in the Ph.D.-only category. These counts describe that completed cycle, not a prediction of later cut-offs or selection chances.
bullets: Use the official subject/category cut-off document for the relevant completed cycle; required scores vary by subject, category, and cycle.
The final answer key is used to compile the result; NTA’s June 2025 bulletin did not provide for re-evaluation or re-checking after the result.
Download and preserve the scorecard/certificate from the official candidate portal, then separately meet the recruiting institution’s Assistant Professor or Ph.D. admission requirements.

title: UPSC CAPF (AC)
description: UPSC CAPF (AC) — govt recruitment exam (defence), conducted by UPSC.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body and purpose
quick_facts.value: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) conducts the CAPF (ACs) examination for recruitment of Assistant Commandants (Group A) in BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP and SSB.

quick_facts.label: 2026 examination date
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, UPSC notified the written examination for 19 July 2026. The notification states that the date may be changed at the Commission’s discretion.

quick_facts.label: Educational qualification
quick_facts.value: A bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification is required. Candidates awaiting the qualifying result in 2026 could sit the written examination, but must produce proof of passing if called to the physical stages, within the stipulated time.

quick_facts.label: Age and nationality in the 2026 notice
quick_facts.value: For 2026, candidates had to be 20–24 years old on 1 August 2026 (born from 2 August 2001 through 1 August 2006, inclusive as specified). The notice provides upper-age relaxations for eligible categories and requires Indian citizenship except where Central Government consent applies to subjects of Nepal or Bhutan.

quick_facts.label: Written examination
quick_facts.value: The written stage has Paper I: General Ability and Intelligence (250 marks, objective, English/Hindi) and Paper II: General Studies, Essay and Comprehension (200 marks). Paper I carries one-third negative marking for a wrong objective response.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: Candidates progress from the written examination to Physical Standards Tests/Physical Efficiency Tests, then an UPSC Interview/Personality Test worth 150 marks, followed by medical standards testing. Final merit is based on written-examination and interview/personality-test marks, subject to medical fitness.

quick_facts.label: 2026 fee context
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, the examination fee was ₹200 for candidates not exempted; female and SC/ST candidates were exempt, while OBC/EWS candidates were required to pay the full prescribed fee. Fees and exemptions can change in later notifications.

sections.heading: What UPSC CAPF (AC) is for
paragraphs: UPSC CAPF (AC) is the competitive recruitment examination for entry as an Assistant Commandant, a Group A officer post, in five Central Armed Police Forces: the Border Security Force (BSF), Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) and Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB). It is a recruitment route into these forces rather than a general academic entrance examination.

In the 2026 notification, UPSC listed 349 tentative vacancies across the five forces: BSF 108, CRPF 106, CISF 70, SSB 53 and ITBP 12. Those figures were expressly tentative and liable to alteration; they should not be treated as a forecast for a future cycle.
bullets: Applicants indicate force preferences in the online application. Allocation is made using final merit position and those preferences.
Both male and female candidates are eligible for appointment under the 2026 notice.

sections.heading: Eligibility: check the notification for the relevant year
paragraphs: The 2026 notice required a bachelor’s degree from a qualifying Indian university or an equivalent qualification. Candidates whose qualifying result was pending, or who planned to take the qualifying examination in 2026, could be admitted provisionally to the written examination, but had to provide acceptable evidence of passing if they qualified for the physical stages.

For that cycle, the ordinary age range was 20 to under 25 on 1 August 2026. Eligible SC/ST candidates could receive up to five years’ upper-age relaxation; eligible OBC candidates up to three years; and specified civilian Central Government servants and ex-servicemen up to five years, subject to the notification’s conditions. These cut-off dates and relaxations must be rechecked in each annual notice.

Physical and medical fitness are mandatory. The 2026 standards included minimum height, weight, eyesight and other medical requirements, alongside specified physical-efficiency events. Candidates should read the full physical and medical appendix before applying, rather than relying only on a summary.
bullets: 2026 minimum physical standards included: men—165 cm height, 81 cm unexpanded chest with 5 cm minimum expansion, and 50 kg weight; women—157 cm height and 46 kg weight, with weight also assessed against height-and-age tables.
NCC ‘B’ or ‘C’ certification was described as desirable and considered only at the interview/personality-test stage; it was not stated as a basic eligibility requirement.
A candidate already finally selected through an earlier CAPF (AC) examination for a participating force is not eligible to reappear for subsequent CAPF (AC) recruitment examinations.

sections.heading: Exam format and selection process
paragraphs: The written examination is held in two papers on the same day. In 2026, Paper I, General Ability and Intelligence, was a 250-mark objective paper set in English and Hindi; Paper II, General Studies, Essay and Comprehension, was worth 200 marks. The essay could be written in Hindi or English, but précis, comprehension and other language-skills components were in English only.

Paper I is screened first: Paper II is evaluated only for candidates who meet the Paper I minimum qualifying mark set by UPSC. In the objective paper, a wrong answer attracts a deduction of one-third of the marks assigned to that question; a blank response has no penalty.

Written-qualified candidates are called for Physical Standards Tests (PST) and Physical Efficiency Tests (PET). Candidates passing those stages are called for the 150-mark Interview/Personality Test. Medical standards testing follows for candidates who have appeared at the interview. The final merit list uses written and interview/personality-test marks, but appointment also requires meeting medical standards.
bullets: 2026 PET benchmarks: 100 m in 16 seconds for men and 18 seconds for women; 800 m in 3:45 for men and 4:45 for women; long jump of 3.5 m for men and 3.0 m for women, each with three chances.
The men’s 2026 PET also included a 7.26 kg shot put of 4.5 m, with three chances.

The notification’s detailed syllabus covers reasoning and quantitative/data interpretation, science, current affairs, polity and economy, Indian history, and Indian/world geography; Paper II includes an 80-mark essay component and 120 marks of English comprehension, précis and language skills.

sections.heading: Application process and 2026-cycle context
paragraphs: Applications are submitted online through UPSC’s online application portal. The 2026 process used a Universal Registration Number (URN), a Common Application Form and an examination-specific module; candidates had to provide supporting information and documents for claims such as date of birth, category and educational qualification. UPSC warned that required information or documents not provided as required could result in cancellation of candidature.

The 2026 application window ran from 20 February 2026 to 12 March 2026 at 18:00. That deadline has passed and is included only as dated context. Prospective applicants should use UPSC’s examination-notification archive and online portal for the next applicable cycle, rather than assuming that dates, documents, fees or procedures will repeat.

For 2026, applicants were required to give a government-issued photo-ID detail, upload a photograph and signature, and complete a live-photo capture in the common form. Once submitted, the examination-specific application could not be withdrawn or altered; the URN profile had a separate one-time edit facility whose changes did not alter an already submitted application.
bullets: Choose examination centre and force preferences carefully: centre availability may be capacity-limited, while force allocation uses merit and stated preferences.
Keep the URN, application number, application copy, active email address and photo-ID details available for later communication and stages.
An e-Admit Card is made available for download from UPSC’s portal; it is not sent by post or email.

sections.heading: Preparation priorities aligned to the official scheme
paragraphs: Build preparation around the notified syllabus rather than generic civil-services material alone. For Paper I, allocate recurring practice to reasoning, quantitative aptitude and data interpretation, general science, current affairs, polity/economy, history and geography. For Paper II, prepare timed essays on the listed themes—modern Indian history and freedom struggle, geography, polity/economy, security and human rights—and practise English-only comprehension, précis, counterarguments and grammar.

Treat physical preparation as a parallel requirement from the outset. A candidate must clear the physical standards and PET after the written result to reach the interview stage; therefore, a written-only study plan leaves a material selection risk. Train specifically for the notified sprint, 800 m and long-jump requirements, and, where applicable, shot put, while checking the complete medical standards early.

Use full-length, timed practice for both papers. In Paper I, accuracy matters because the 2026 notice applied one-third negative marking to each wrong objective answer. In Paper II, practise the permitted language rule: essays may be Hindi or English, but précis, comprehension and language-skills responses must be in English.
bullets: Download and work from UPSC’s official notification for the current syllabus, paper rules and physical/medical standards.
Use official UPSC previous-question-paper resources where available to become familiar with UPSC paper presentation and exam-day instructions.
Before committing substantial preparation time, assess eligibility, physical standards and medical requirements against the current notice.

sections.heading: What selection leads to
paragraphs: Successful candidates are recruited as Assistant Commandants in one of the five participating CAPFs—BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP or SSB. This is an officer-entry outcome, with the specific force determined through final merit and the candidate’s submitted force preferences, not simply by qualifying the written examination.

For the 2026 cycle, final selection was based on the combined written-examination and interview/personality-test marks. Passing the written stage or receiving an interview call was not by itself an appointment guarantee: candidates also had to clear PST/PET and satisfy the prescribed medical standards.

The notification did not establish a universal salary figure in the cited examination summary. Candidates seeking compensation, posting, training or service-condition information should consult the appointment documentation and the relevant force/MHA materials applicable at the time of selection.
bullets: Participating outcomes: Assistant Commandant in BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP or SSB.
Force allocation reflects merit rank and force preference.
Candidates found medically unfit after medical standards testing are not appointed under the 2026 scheme.

title: UPSC CDS
description: UPSC CDS — govt recruitment exam (defence), conducted by UPSC.

quick_facts.label: Conducting authority
quick_facts.value: Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) conducts the Combined Defence Services Examination (CDS).

quick_facts.label: Purpose
quick_facts.value: CDS is the competitive entry route for specified officer-training courses at the Indian Military Academy (IMA), Indian Naval Academy (INA), Air Force Academy (AFA), and Officers’ Training Academy (OTA).

quick_facts.label: Latest notified sitting
quick_facts.value: For CDS (II) 2026, UPSC notified the examination for 13 September 2026. The notice listed 451 tentative vacancies across IMA, INA, AFA, OTA (Men), and OTA (Women); dates and vacancies may change at UPSC/Services HQ discretion.

quick_facts.label: Minimum qualification
quick_facts.value: IMA and OTA require a recognised university degree or equivalent. INA requires an engineering degree, or a B.Sc. with Physics plus Physics and Mathematics at 10+2 level. AFA requires a degree with Physics and Mathematics at 10+2 level, or a Bachelor of Engineering.

quick_facts.label: Written-exam structure
quick_facts.value: IMA, INA and AFA candidates write English, General Knowledge and Elementary Mathematics (two hours and 100 marks each). OTA candidates write English and General Knowledge only (two hours and 100 marks each).

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: Selection comprises the UPSC written examination followed, for written-qualified candidates, by a Services Selection Board (SSB) intelligence and personality assessment and the prescribed medical standards.

quick_facts.label: Application fee context
quick_facts.value: In the CDS (II) 2026 notice, the examination fee was ₹200 for applicants other than women and SC/ST candidates; women and SC/ST candidates were exempt, while OBC/EWS candidates were not exempt. Fees and exemption rules should be checked in the relevant notification.

sections.heading: What UPSC CDS is for
paragraphs: UPSC CDS is a government competitive examination used to select candidates for officer training in the Armed Forces. The CDS (II) 2026 notice covers entry to IMA, INA, AFA, and OTA; final admission is based on the written examination, SSB selection process, medical fitness, service preferences, merit and available vacancies.

For the 2026 CDS (II) cycle, UPSC listed tentative vacancies for courses beginning in July or October 2027. These vacancy figures are not guarantees: the official notice states that Services Headquarters may change them during selection.
bullets: IMA, INA and AFA are regular-commission pathways described in the notification; OTA is for Short Service Commission courses.

Candidates must state eligible service/course preferences in the examination-specific application module; candidates are considered only for the preferences they exercise, subject to the rules in the notice.

sections.heading: Eligibility: degree, age, nationality and fitness
paragraphs: Eligibility is course-specific and must be verified against the notification for the particular CDS cycle. In CDS (II) 2026, IMA and INA were for unmarried men aged 19–24; AFA was generally for candidates aged 20–24, with a higher upper limit for holders of a valid current DGCA commercial pilot licence; OTA (Men) was for unmarried men aged 19–25; and OTA (Women) was for unmarried women, eligible issueless widows and eligible issueless divorcees aged 19–25. The notice specifies exact eligible dates of birth rather than relying solely on an age calculation.

The notice permits final-year/semester degree candidates to apply, but they must furnish the required evidence of passing by the stipulated deadline. Candidates must also meet the prescribed physical and medical standards; an e-admit card or provisional admission does not itself confirm final eligibility.

Nationality rules include Indian citizens, subjects of Nepal, and specified persons of Indian origin intending permanent settlement in India, with a Government of India eligibility certificate required in applicable cases.
bullets: Degree requirement: recognised degree/equivalent for IMA and OTA.
INA: engineering degree, or B.Sc. with Physics as core/elective plus Physics and Mathematics at 10+2.
AFA: degree with Physics and Mathematics at 10+2, or Bachelor of Engineering.
Women candidates in the CDS (II) 2026 notice were considered for OTA’s Short Service Commission course only.

sections.heading: Exam and SSB format
paragraphs: The written examination uses objective-type papers. For IMA, INA and AFA, the papers are English, General Knowledge and Elementary Mathematics, each for two hours and 100 marks. For OTA, the papers are English and General Knowledge, each for two hours and 100 marks. General Knowledge and Elementary Mathematics papers are bilingual in Hindi and English; the Elementary Mathematics standard is matriculation level, while the other papers are approximately graduate level.

UPSC applies negative marking to the objective papers: one-third of the marks assigned to a question is deducted for a wrong answer, while an unanswered question has no penalty. Calculators are not permitted.

Candidates who clear the written stage may be called for SSB. The SSB process has Stage I—Officer Intelligence Rating tests and Picture Perception & Description Test—and Stage II, comprising interview, group-testing tasks, psychology tests and conference. Stage II is conducted over four days according to the UPSC notice.
bullets: Maximum written marks are 300 for IMA, INA and AFA, and 200 for OTA; the interview maximum is equal to the corresponding written-exam total.
The 2026 official previous-question-paper archive provides CDS English, General Knowledge and Elementary Mathematics papers.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Applications are submitted online through UPSC’s application portal. For CDS (II) 2026, the process used four modules: account creation, Universal Registration Number (URN), Common Application Form (CAF), and the examination-specific module. Applicants submit identity, date-of-birth and education details, documents, service preferences, fee information where applicable, and an examination-centre choice.

For CDS (II) 2026, the notice specified 9 June 2026 at 6:00 p.m. as the application deadline, so that application window is closed as of 19 July 2026. Candidates should rely on the next UPSC notification and calendar rather than assuming a future CDS deadline, because UPSC states that examination dates may be altered.

UPSC required an acceptable government photo ID in the URN profile and instructed applicants to upload a photograph, capture a live photograph for the CAF, and upload a clear signature. The CDS (II) 2026 notice states that submitted examination applications could not be withdrawn or corrected; a separate one-time URN-profile update facility does not revise an application already submitted.
bullets: Use the official UPSC portal only; do not rely on third-party application services.
Keep both the URN and the exam-specific application number for future correspondence.
Apply early in a future cycle if a particular test city matters: allotment can be subject to centre capacity and first-apply-first-allot rules.

sections.heading: Preparation approach using official materials
paragraphs: Start with the current official notification: it defines the applicable eligibility, syllabus, paper structure, marking rules, medical requirements and course preferences. Build a paper-specific plan: English and General Knowledge for all relevant courses, with Elementary Mathematics additionally required for IMA, INA and AFA.

Use UPSC’s official previous-question-paper archive for timed practice in the actual subjects. Practise accuracy as well as speed because the objective papers carry a one-third-mark penalty for wrong answers. For SSB, preparation should focus on understanding the selection stages and presenting authentic, consistent evidence of officer-like qualities rather than treating it as a written-test extension.

Physical and medical readiness should begin early. The official notice makes medical fitness a condition of selection and links candidates to the applicable armed-forces medical standards; candidates with a health concern should consult the standards and a qualified clinician rather than self-assessing eligibility.
bullets: Read the full notification and appendices before choosing course preferences.
Use official papers to diagnose weak areas and to simulate two-hour papers.
Do not bring calculators or prohibited electronic items to the written exam.

sections.heading: What follows after selection
paragraphs: A written-exam result alone does not confer appointment. Candidates must clear SSB, satisfy medical standards, meet documentary eligibility requirements, rank sufficiently in the relevant merit process and be accommodated within vacancies. Successful candidates join the academy/course allocated under the applicable rules.

The CDS (II) 2026 notice describes IMA training as about 18 months, after which successful medically fit officer cadets are granted Permanent Commission as Lieutenants. The other courses have their own service and training terms in the notification.

Pay information is variable and should be treated as dated policy context, not a salary promise. In the CDS (II) 2026 notice, the starting Level-10 pay range for a Lieutenant was listed as ₹56,100–₹177,500 per month, and the fixed cadet-training stipend was listed as ₹56,100 per month; the same notice explicitly says pay, allowances and rules may be revised from time to time.
bullets: The 2026 notice lists 451 tentative vacancies for CDS (II), distributed across IMA, INA, AFA and OTA courses; the Services may revise vacancies.
During academy training, Government bears specified training costs, while candidates are expected to meet their own pocket expenses under the terms stated for the relevant academy.

title: UPSC Civil Services Examination
description: UPSC Civil Services Examination — govt recruitment exam (general), conducted by UPSC. IAS/IPS/IFS and allied services.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body and purpose
quick_facts.value: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) conducts the Civil Services Examination (CSE) to select candidates for the IAS, IFS, IPS and a range of other Group A and Group B civil services/posts.

quick_facts.label: 2026 eligibility baseline
quick_facts.value: For CSE 2026, applicants needed a graduate degree or equivalent qualification and had to be 21–31 years old as of 1 August 2026 (that is, born from 2 August 1994 through 1 August 2005), subject to specified relaxations.

quick_facts.label: Examination structure
quick_facts.value: CSE has a Preliminary objective examination that screens candidates for the Main examination, followed by Main written papers and the Interview/Personality Test; final ranking uses Main written and interview marks, not Preliminary marks.

quick_facts.label: Attempts
quick_facts.value: Under the 2026 rules, the general limit was six attempts; the notice provided category-based relaxations, including nine attempts for OBC candidates and unlimited attempts for SC/ST candidates, subject to eligibility and the applicable rules.

quick_facts.label: Next scheduled cycle
quick_facts.value: UPSC's calendar dated 20 May 2026 schedules CSE Preliminary 2027 notification for 13 January 2027, application deadline for 2 February 2027, Preliminary examination for 23 May 2027, and Main examination for 20 August 2027. UPSC states that calendar dates are liable to alteration.

sections.heading: What the UPSC Civil Services Examination is for
paragraphs: The UPSC Civil Services Examination is the Union government’s competitive selection route for multiple civil services. The 2026 notice lists the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Foreign Service (IFS), Indian Police Service (IPS), Indian Revenue Service (Customs and Indirect Taxes and Income Tax), and numerous other Group A and Group B services/posts.

Selection is not a guarantee of one particular service: UPSC determines final rank from the Main written examination and Interview/Personality Test, then allocates services with reference to rank and the candidate’s submitted preferences.
bullets: The 2026 notice estimated approximately 933 vacancies, including 33 vacancies reserved for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities; this was an estimate and UPSC stated that the final vacancy count could change.

IAS, IFS and IPS require Indian citizenship. The 2026 notice permits certain other nationality categories for other services, subject in relevant cases to a Government of India eligibility certificate.

sections.heading: Eligibility: degree, age, nationality and attempts
paragraphs: A qualifying graduate degree from a university established or incorporated under the specified Indian laws, or an equivalent qualification, was the baseline educational requirement in CSE 2026. Candidates awaiting qualifying-examination results could sit the written examination, but those reaching the Interview/Personality Test had to produce proof that they had passed within the prescribed timeframe.

For CSE 2026, the ordinary age rule was at least 21 and under 32 on 1 August 2026. The upper limit had specified relaxations—for example, up to five years for SC/ST candidates, up to three years for eligible OBC candidates, and up to ten years for eligible PwBD candidates. Applicants must use the notice for their own cycle because eligibility rules and reference dates can change.
bullets: In 2026, a candidate who actually appeared in at least one Preliminary paper was treated as having made an attempt.

The 2026 attempt limits were six for general candidates, nine for OBC candidates, unlimited for SC/ST candidates, and category-specific PwBD provisions; applicable age and rule restrictions still apply.
For IAS, IFS and IPS, the candidate must be an Indian citizen; the notification sets out separate nationality provisions for other services.

sections.heading: Examination format and scoring
paragraphs: The Preliminary examination comprises two compulsory, two-hour objective (multiple-choice) papers worth 200 marks each. General Studies Paper II is qualifying at 33%; Preliminary is a screening stage, so its marks do not count toward final merit. The notice also prescribes negative marking for wrong answers in objective papers.

The Main examination has nine conventional essay-type written papers. Two are qualifying papers—an Indian-language paper and English—and seven papers count for merit: Essay, four General Studies papers, and two papers in one optional subject. The written merit total is 1,750 marks; the Personality Test carries 275 marks, making a 2,025-mark total for final ranking.
bullets: Preliminary: two compulsory 200-mark papers; both are objective and two hours long.
Main: qualifying Indian-language and English papers are each 300 marks; their marks do not count toward merit, though candidates must meet the qualifying standard.
Main merit papers: Essay; GS I, II, III and IV; Optional Subject Papers I and II—250 marks each.
Interview/Personality Test: 275 marks, with no minimum qualifying marks stated in the 2026 notice.

sections.heading: Application process and cycle planning
paragraphs: Candidates apply online through UPSC’s application portal. In the 2026 process, applicants completed account creation, Universal Registration, a Common Application Form, and an examination-specific module; the Commission required supporting information and documents for claims such as date of birth and educational qualification. UPSC advised applicants to prepare documents before applying.

Candidates who qualified Preliminary had to return to the portal during a 10-day post-result window to update or reconfirm details and submit the form for admission to Main. Candidates qualifying the Main written stage similarly had a 15-day window to provide or update required information and documents for the Personality Test.

For forward planning only, UPSC’s 2027 calendar schedules the CSE Preliminary notification on 13 January 2027, applications closing on 2 February 2027, Preliminary on 23 May 2027, and Main from 20 August 2027. The calendar expressly warns that dates may change; candidates should rely on the notification issued for their own cycle.
bullets: CSE 2026 fees were ₹100 for the Preliminary stage and a further ₹200 for candidates admitted to Main, with women, SC, ST and PwBD candidates exempt under the stated conditions. These were 2026 fees and may change in a later notification.
In CSE 2026, UPSC required online applications only; the notification stated that applications could not be withdrawn or altered after submission.

Keep the application number and Universal Registration Number, and download the e-admit card from the UPSC portal when issued; no postal or email delivery of admit cards was provided in the 2026 notice.

sections.heading: Preparation approach grounded in the official scheme
paragraphs: Start with the official notification’s syllabus and paper structure, because it specifies the subjects, marks, qualifying requirements and examination rules. Build preparation around both stages: objective General Studies and qualifying CSAT-style Paper II for Preliminary, then answer-writing practice for Essay, General Studies, the selected optional subject, qualifying language papers and the Personality Test.

Use UPSC’s official previous-question-paper archive to practise against real papers. It includes the 2026 Preliminary General Studies Paper I and Paper II, allowing candidates to rehearse the objective format, timing and question style. Treat previous cut-offs only as historical context rather than a target or prediction: UPSC’s 2025 general-category Preliminary cut-off was 92.66 in GS Paper I, while the exact standard varies by year and category.
bullets: Plan separately for the 33% qualifying threshold in Preliminary General Studies Paper II; failing to meet it prevents qualification regardless of Paper I performance.
Practise negative-marking discipline for Preliminary, since the 2026 rules deduct one-third of the marks assigned to a question for an incorrect answer.

For Main, practise sustained written responses across Essay, four General Studies papers and two optional-subject papers; the official scheme makes these, together with the interview, decisive for final rank.

sections.heading: What selection can lead to
paragraphs: Candidates recommended through CSE may be allocated to IAS, IFS, IPS, IRS or other listed central civil services/posts. Allocation depends on final rank and the candidate’s preferences, rather than simply clearing a single cut-off.

The examination also leads to allied Group A and Group B administrative, financial, audit, information, railway-management, territorial civil-service and police-service roles listed in the notification. A policy-analyst career can be a related professional direction, but it is not itself a service allocation named in the CSE notice.

As one historical benchmark only, UPSC reported for CSE 2025 that the last recommended general-category candidate had a final score of 963 out of the applicable final total; cut-offs differ by category and cycle and should not be interpreted as a future threshold.
bullets: Examples of services named for CSE 2026 include Indian Audit and Accounts Service, Indian Civil Accounts Service, Indian Corporate Law Service, Indian Information Service, Indian Postal Service, Indian Railway Management Service, Indian Trade Service and Armed Forces Headquarters Civil Service.
Final ranking is based on Main written and Personality Test marks; Preliminary marks are not included in that ranking.
Service and cadre allocation is administered under the applicable government rules and depends on eligibility, medical/physical standards where relevant, rank, vacancies and preferences.

title: UPSC Engineering Services Examination (ESE/IES)
description: UPSC Engineering Services Examination (ESE/IES) — govt recruitment exam (engineering), conducted by UPSC.

quick_facts.label: Conducting body
quick_facts.value: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) conducts the Engineering Services Examination (ESE) for recruitment to notified Central Government engineering services and posts.

quick_facts.label: Engineering disciplines
quick_facts.value: The examination is organised in four categories: Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, and Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: Under the published examination plan, selection comprises Preliminary/Stage-I objective papers, Main/Stage-II conventional written papers, and a Personality Test.

quick_facts.label: 2026 cycle context
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 preliminary cycle, UPSC’s archive records notification on September 26, 2025, the preliminary examination on February 8, 2026, and an application deadline of October 16, 2025 at 18:00. Dates and deadlines vary by cycle.

quick_facts.label: Official preparation materials
quick_facts.value: UPSC publishes ESE previous-year preliminary and main question papers, including discipline-specific papers, on its Previous Year Question Papers page.

sections.heading: What ESE/IES is for
paragraphs: UPSC Engineering Services Examination (ESE), often referred to as IES, is a competitive recruitment examination for engineering services and posts of the Central Government. The notified services are grouped by Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, and Electronics & Telecommunication engineering categories; the exact services and vacancies are set afresh in each annual notice.

The services listed in the 2025 notice illustrate the range of possible outcomes: Central Engineering Service, Border Roads Engineering Service, Indian Defence Service of Engineers, Central Water Engineering Service, Indian Naval Armament Service, Indian Telecommunication Service, and Indian Radio Regulatory Service, among others. Candidates are ultimately allotted based on merit, stated preferences, available vacancies, and medical fitness.
bullets: Treat the annual UPSC notification—not coaching material or an older notice—as the authoritative source for the year’s participating services, vacancies, discipline mapping, reservations, and physical/medical requirements.
A candidate applies in one engineering category for that examination cycle; choosing the appropriate discipline is therefore a central application decision.

sections.heading: Eligibility: core requirements to check
paragraphs: Eligibility is cycle-specific. In the 2025 notice, the standard age band was 21 to 30 years as of January 1, 2025, with specified relaxations, including certain provisions for eligible Government servants and reserved categories. Applicants should calculate eligibility against the cut-off date and relaxation rules in the notice for their own cycle rather than relying on a previous year’s dates.

The standard educational route is an engineering degree from an eligible Indian university or institution. UPSC’s 2025 notice also listed certain professional and foreign qualifications, including Sections A and B of the Institution of Engineers (India) examinations, subject to the notice’s stated conditions. Some electronics-related posts permit designated M.Sc. qualifications. Final document verification and service-specific medical/physical fitness requirements remain material to appointment.
bullets: Nationality conditions in the published notice include Indian citizens and specified other categories, some of whom require a Government of India eligibility certificate before appointment.

Candidates who are awaiting the qualifying result may be allowed to apply provisionally under the notice’s rules, but must furnish proof of passing within UPSC’s prescribed window if called for the Personality Test.
Read the current notice carefully if using AMIE or another professional qualification, because recognition and service-specific conditions can matter.

sections.heading: Examination format and scoring
paragraphs: The published ESE scheme has three stages. Preliminary/Stage-I contains two objective multiple-choice papers worth 500 marks in total: General Studies and Engineering Aptitude (200 marks) and a discipline-specific paper (300 marks). Wrong answers in the objective papers attract a deduction of one-third of the marks assigned to the question; unanswered questions carry no negative mark.

Main/Stage-II consists of two conventional, discipline-specific papers of three hours each, worth 300 marks each (600 marks total). Stage-III is a 200-mark Personality Test. The published plan states that marks from all three stages determine final ranking; allocation also takes account of rank, service preferences, vacancies, and medical fitness. Conventional papers are to be answered in English.
bullets: The relevant discipline-specific paper is Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, or Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering.
UPSC sets qualifying standards and shortlists candidates from Preliminary to Main and from the written stages to the Personality Test; do not assume a fixed cut-off.
The Personality Test assesses qualities including leadership, initiative, intellectual curiosity, practical application, and integrity.

sections.heading: Applying through UPSC
paragraphs: UPSC requires online application through its application portal. In the cited notice, candidates first completed One Time Registration (OTR), then submitted the examination application and supporting information/documents for claims such as date of birth, category, and educational qualification. Admission is provisional until UPSC verifies eligibility against original documents at the appropriate stage.

Fees, exemptions, correction windows, photograph requirements, payment modes, and application closing times are cycle-dependent. As dated context only, the 2025 notice specified a ₹200 examination fee for candidates other than women and SC/ST/PwBD candidates, who were exempt subject to the stated rules. Applicants should use the current-year notification and portal instructions before paying or submitting.
bullets: Register or sign in through UPSC’s online application portal, then select the ESE cycle when applications are open.
Keep reliable proof for age, qualification, category and any claimed relaxation or fee exemption; the notice requires supporting information and later original-document verification.
Download the e-admission certificate from UPSC when issued; UPSC does not send it by post under the cited notice.

sections.heading: Preparation approach grounded in official materials
paragraphs: Begin with the current notification’s examination plan and syllabus, then organise preparation around both components of Preliminary: General Studies and Engineering Aptitude, plus the chosen discipline paper. Because Main is conventional/descriptive and carries 600 marks, preparation should include structured written solutions and timed three-hour practice—not only objective-question practice.

Use UPSC’s own previous-year question-paper archive to inspect the actual paper types and recurring disciplinary coverage. The archive currently includes 2026 preliminary papers for General Studies and Engineering Aptitude plus each engineering discipline, as well as 2026 main papers across the four disciplines. Match timed practice to the official marks, durations, and negative-marking rules in the notification.
bullets: Build separate practice routines for Preliminary MCQs and Main descriptive answers.
Practise the 200-mark General Studies and Engineering Aptitude paper alongside the 300-mark discipline paper; neither should be treated as optional.

For the Personality Test, prepare to explain engineering fundamentals, work or project experience, public-service motivation, and professional judgement; UPSC identifies leadership, initiative, practical application and integrity as assessment areas.

sections.heading: What qualifying can lead to
paragraphs: A successful candidate is recommended and allotted to a notified engineering service or post rather than receiving a generic engineering credential. Potential appointments depend on the discipline category, year-specific vacancy position, candidate rank, preferences, reservation rules, service eligibility, and medical fitness. The precise list can change from one ESE notice to another.

Examples from the cited 2025 notice include civil-side positions in Central Engineering Service, Border Roads Engineering Service and Central Water Engineering Service; defence and naval engineering roles across several disciplines; and electronics/telecom roles in Indian Telecommunication Service and Indian Radio Regulatory Service. This makes ESE a pathway into technical public-service careers, but not a guarantee of any particular named post.
bullets: Final rank is based on Preliminary, Main and Personality Test marks under the published scheme.
Service preferences matter, but allocation is constrained by rank, vacancies, applicable rules, and fitness requirements.
Candidates finally recommended by UPSC are required to undergo medical examination under the cited notice.
