title: Administrative Assistant B (DRDO)
description: A higher-grade DRDO administrative cadre post reached through departmental promotion, handling more complex establishment, records, and office administration work.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: A February 2024 Gazette recruitment rule names Administrative Assistant ‘B’ as a Level 4 post in the Central Pay Matrix (₹25,500–81,100 basic-pay range). This is pay-matrix context, not a guaranteed take-home salary: allowances, location, deductions, and future government revisions can change actual pay.

sections.heading: How the post is reached
paragraphs: Administrative Assistant ‘B’ is best understood as an internal DRDO administrative-cadre progression point, not the usual public entry post. In the 2011 statutory schedule, 75% of vacancies were to be filled by promotion from Administrative Assistant ‘A’ with eight years’ regular service in the relevant DPC-II group; the remaining 25% were through a Limited Departmental Competitive Examination (LDCE) route for eligible Group ‘C’ personnel with the stated educational and service conditions.

The route has been amended over time. In September 2013, DRDO’s amendment changed the designation of the post from a selection to a non-selection post and replaced “selection” with “seniority” in the recruitment method; it also retained a five-year eligibility concession for certain people already holding Administrative Assistant ‘A’ on the notification date. Accordingly, an employee should rely on the recruitment rules, departmental orders, seniority position, vacancy year, and DPC/LDCE notice actually applicable when promotion is considered rather than assuming that the original eight-year condition applies unchanged.

For an external candidate, the practical starting point has historically been Administrative Assistant ‘A’. For example, DRDO’s CEPTAM-09 Admin & Allied notice required 12th-class completion plus a computer typing test—35 words per minute in English or 30 words per minute in Hindi—for Administrative Assistant ‘A’. That notice is dated 2019 and is evidence of a prior entry route, not a current recruitment notification.
bullets: Join DRDO through an officially advertised eligible feeder or Admin & Allied role.
Build regular service, satisfactory service record, and eligibility under the then-applicable departmental rules.
Monitor DRDO/CEPTAM notices and internal establishment communications for promotion, DPC, or LDCE instructions.

sections.heading: Skills that support progression
paragraphs: The statutory rules do not publish a detailed duty statement for Administrative Assistant ‘B’. However, the documented feeder and entry pathway makes strong written communication, accurate computer-based typing, records discipline, familiarity with government-office procedures, and careful handling of service and establishment documentation relevant foundations. The historical Administrative Assistant ‘A’ notice specifically assessed computer typing in English or Hindi, while DRDO’s HR function identifies establishment-policy compliance, recruitment, compensation, performance assessment, and training among its responsibilities.

For promotion readiness, employees should develop capability in interpreting applicable orders, maintaining accurate files and registers, drafting clear official communications, protecting sensitive official information, and working reliably through prescribed administrative processes. These are career-development priorities inferred from DRDO’s administrative and HR operating context; precise duties can vary by laboratory, establishment, and assignment.
bullets: Computer typing and document preparation in the applicable language stream.
Accuracy in records, correspondence, and establishment documentation.
Working knowledge of applicable government and DRDO administrative procedures.
Professional communication, confidentiality, and process compliance.

sections.heading: Work setting and posting
paragraphs: Administrative Assistant ‘B’ belongs to DRDO’s administrative structure, which supports a defence research organisation operating laboratories, establishments, and units across India. DRDO states that its HR cluster handles such areas as recruitment, compensation, training, performance assessment, establishment-policy formulation, and compliance with Government of India guidelines.

A historical CEPTAM Admin & Allied recruitment notice stated that DRDO had more than 60 laboratories, establishments, and units across the country; it also stated that selected personnel could be posted anywhere in India, including field or remote locations, according to organisational requirements. Because that notice was issued in 2019, it should be read as service-condition context rather than a current posting guarantee.
bullets: Work may be in a DRDO laboratory, establishment, unit, or headquarters-linked administrative environment.
Posting and transfer are organisational decisions and may involve locations across India.
The work is governed by central-government service rules and DRDO establishment processes.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: For current pay-scale context, a February 2024 official Gazette rule lists Administrative Assistant ‘B’ at Pay Matrix Level 4, ₹25,500–81,100. This is the basic-pay matrix range, not an all-inclusive monthly salary or an assurance of a particular salary on promotion.

A DRDO Admin & Allied notice explains that central-government compensation may also include applicable dearness allowance, house-rent allowance, transport allowance, medical facilities, leave travel concession, and other benefits under Government of India rules; it also stated that recruits were covered by the National Pension System unless otherwise provided. That notice concerns 2019 recruitment and its benefits language is therefore contextual and subject to subsequent rules, posting location, and individual eligibility.
bullets: Reference basic-pay range: Level 4, ₹25,500–81,100, as identified in a February 2024 Gazette rule.
Take-home pay varies with allowances, city/posting category, pension contributions, tax, and government revisions.
Confirm current pay fixation and allowances with the relevant DRDO establishment office when promoted.

title: Administrative Assistant (DRDO)
description: A clerical role within DRDO responsible for general administrative duties, record keeping, and office management, often filled through the CEPTAM Admin & Allied cadre.

quick_facts.label: Recruiting authority and cadre
quick_facts.value: DRDO identifies CEPTAM as the recruiting body for its Admin & Allied cadre, which includes Group B and Group C recruitment; Administrative Assistant ‘A’ has been advertised under the Admin & Allied cadre.

quick_facts.label: Selection context
quick_facts.value: The historical CEPTAM-09 notice used a Tier-I computer-based test followed, where applicable, by Tier-II tests; passing the typing test was mandatory for Administrative Assistant ‘A’. DRDO states that CEPTAM handles advertising, application scrutiny, tests and appointment-related selection processes for Admin & Allied recruitment.

quick_facts.label: Current recruitment-checking context
quick_facts.value: DRDO’s CEPTAM-11 page, published for STA-B and Technician-A posts, is not an Administrative Assistant ‘A’ notification. Prospective applicants should monitor DRDO’s vacancies and CEPTAM notices for a future Admin & Allied advertisement rather than assume a standing annual intake.

sections.heading: Primary entry route: CEPTAM Admin & Allied recruitment
paragraphs: The normal external route is to wait for a DRDO CEPTAM Admin & Allied advertisement that specifically lists Administrative Assistant ‘A’ vacancies, then apply online through the official process and meet the post-code-specific requirements. DRDO says CEPTAM administers Admin & Allied recruitment, including advertising, scrutiny, written/CBT examinations, trade tests and selection processes.

For preparation planning, the most concrete official benchmark is the CEPTAM-09/Admin & Allied notification: it required 12th pass or equivalent plus a qualifying computer typing test—English at 35 wpm or Hindi at 30 wpm. That notice also made clear that a typing-test pass was essential. Vacancy numbers, language-wise posts, age limits, reservation, examination design and dates can change in later notifications, so the live advertisement prevails.

There has also historically been a limited internal-promotion channel into Administrative Assistant ‘A’. The 2014 amendment to the recruitment rules described 85% direct recruitment and 15% promotion, split between a departmental examination route and selection from eligible Group C staff. This is historical rules context; it should not be treated as confirmation of the currently applicable quota or eligibility without checking the latest DRDO rules and notification.
bullets: Complete Class 12 or an accepted equivalent qualification.
Build accurate, timed computer typing in the language—English or Hindi—specified in the recruitment notice.
Apply only when the official CEPTAM advertisement lists the relevant Administrative Assistant ‘A’ post code.
Treat the notice’s post-specific eligibility, test scheme and dates as controlling documents.

sections.heading: Skills demonstrated by the official entry standards
paragraphs: The clearest role-specific skills evidenced by official recruitment material are computer-based typing accuracy and speed, together with the ability to meet a formal recruitment examination process. CEPTAM-09 set separate English- and Hindi-typing standards for Administrative Assistant ‘A’, and required candidates for the post to pass the typing test.

Because the qualification benchmark in that notice was 12th pass or equivalent rather than a degree or specialist diploma, a Certificate in Computer Applications or a commerce background can be useful preparation but is not, by itself, established as a universal mandatory requirement for the post. Candidates should avoid assuming that an optional course substitutes for the notified typing and examination requirements.
bullets: Computer typing: practice the language and speed named in the notice.
Accuracy under a timed 10-minute typing test.
Basic comfort with computer-based recruitment tests and online applications.
Careful reading of post-code-specific eligibility and instructions.

sections.heading: Workplace and posting conditions
paragraphs: Administrative Assistant ‘A’ is part of DRDO’s Admin & Allied cadre, supporting an organisation that conducts defence research, design, development, testing and evaluation. The 2019 Admin & Allied notice listed Administrative Assistant ‘A’ vacancies across multiple DRDO posting stations and stated that selected candidates could be required to serve anywhere in India, including field or remote locations, according to organisational requirements.

That notice also stated that selected candidates would be subject to Central Government rules, appointed on probation, and normally required to serve at least five years at the first place of posting, subject to DRDO’s transfer provisions. These conditions are historical notification context and should be rechecked against the terms of any future appointment notice.
bullets: Potential placement in DRDO laboratories, establishments or units rather than a single fixed city.
Mobility may be a condition of appointment.
Employment conditions are governed by the relevant Central Government and DRDO rules.

useful_links.label: DRDO: How can I join DRDO?

title: Assistant Commandant in Border Security Force
description: A Group A Assistant Commandant officer in the Border Security Force, recruited through UPSC CAPF (AC) examination.

quick_facts.label: Role and service
quick_facts.value: Assistant Commandant is an officer rank in the Border Security Force (BSF), a Central Armed Police Force under the Ministry of Home Affairs; UPSC recruits Assistant Commandants as Group A officers through the CAPF (ACs) examination.

quick_facts.label: 2026 examination context
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 CAPF (ACs) cycle, UPSC scheduled the written examination for July 19, 2026. The notification listed 108 tentative BSF vacancies and expressly stated that vacancy numbers could change.

quick_facts.label: Baseline eligibility in the 2026 notice
quick_facts.value: The 2026 notice required a bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification. Both men and women were eligible; the standard age band was 20–25 years as of August 1, 2026, subject to specified relaxations.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: The notified route comprises a two-paper written examination, Physical Standards/Physical Efficiency Tests, an UPSC Interview/Personality Test worth 150 marks, and medical standards testing. Final merit is based on the written examination and interview/personality-test marks, subject to medical fitness.

quick_facts.label: Rank position
quick_facts.value: BSF rules classify Assistant Commandant as an officer rank. The listed officer hierarchy above it proceeds through Deputy Commandant, Second-in-Command, Commandant, Deputy Inspector-General, Inspector-General and senior ranks.

sections.heading: Operational purpose and responsibilities
paragraphs: The statutory tasks assigned to the BSF are to foster security among border-area residents; prevent trans-border crime and unauthorized entry into or exit from India; and prevent smuggling and other illegal activity. An Assistant Commandant serves as a Group A officer within this operational and command environment, rather than in a purely desk-based civil post.

The Force’s wider mission also encompasses continuous border vigilance, cooperation with border populations, internal-security duties when tasked, assistance to civil administration in disaster management, and defensive and rear-area-security operations during conventional war. Exact duties, authority and deployment will depend on the officer’s unit, location and assignment.
bullets: Border-security and anti-smuggling operations.
Work with border communities and coordinate in a security environment.
Potential internal-security, disaster-management, defensive or rear-area-security assignments when tasked.

sections.heading: Primary entry route: UPSC CAPF (ACs) examination
paragraphs: For the canonical direct-entry route, apply through the Union Public Service Commission’s Central Armed Police Forces (Assistant Commandants) examination and state force preferences as required in the application process. The examination recruits Group A Assistant Commandants for BSF and the other participating CAPFs; selection and subsequent appointment remain subject to the notified rules, documentary verification, physical standards and medical fitness.

In the 2026 notification, the written examination had Paper I, General Ability and Intelligence (250 marks), and Paper II, General Studies, Essay and Comprehension (200 marks). Candidates qualifying the written stage were called for physical standards and efficiency testing; those qualifying those tests were considered for the UPSC interview/personality test, followed by medical standards testing.

Entry rules are cycle-specific. For example, the 2026 application deadline was March 12, 2026, and the examination fee was ₹200 for candidates not exempted; women and SC/ST candidates were exempt under that notice. Future notifications can alter dates, vacancies, fees, standards and procedures.
bullets: Hold the degree/equivalent qualification and satisfy nationality, age, physical and medical rules in the relevant UPSC notice.
Prepare for both objective aptitude/general-knowledge assessment and descriptive writing in English/Hindi as prescribed.
Meet the Physical Efficiency Test standards and clear the interview and medical stages.

sections.heading: Capabilities to develop
paragraphs: The examination and operational role indicate a need for analytical reasoning, quantitative ability, general awareness, clear written communication, composure and physical conditioning. UPSC’s 2026 syllabus assessed general mental ability, general science, current events, Indian polity and economy, history, geography, essay writing, précis writing and English comprehension.

Physical readiness is an entry requirement, not simply an advantage. In the 2026 cycle, the Physical Efficiency Test included a 100-metre race, 800-metre race and long jump for all candidates, plus shot put for men; the required timings and distances differed by sex. Candidates also had to satisfy prescribed physical and medical standards.
bullets: Logical reasoning and numerical problem-solving.
Writing, comprehension and concise communication.
Sustained fitness, speed and endurance.
Judgment and disciplined conduct in a border-security setting.

sections.heading: Workplace and deployment context
paragraphs: BSF is the designated border-guarding force for the India–Pakistan and India–Bangladesh borders under the Government’s “one border, one border guarding force” approach. Its work therefore has a field-oriented border-management context that can involve border outposts, surveillance, patrolling, intelligence-linked coordination and response to illegal cross-border activity.

The Ministry of Home Affairs describes border management as combining manpower, sensors, networks, intelligence and command-and-control solutions. This means the workplace can combine outdoor operational duty with leadership, reporting, coordination and use of surveillance or communications systems; the precise mix varies by posting and assignment.
bullets: Potential postings on India–Pakistan or India–Bangladesh border sectors.
Operational settings can include border outposts and areas requiring patrol and surveillance.
Assignments may require coordination with civil administration and other security or intelligence stakeholders.

sections.heading: Rank progression context
paragraphs: The BSF Rules place Assistant Commandant within the officer cadre, with Deputy Commandant immediately above it in the listed hierarchy, followed by Second-in-Command and Commandant before the deputy inspector-general and inspector-general levels. This establishes the rank structure, but it should not be read as a guarantee of promotion: advancement is governed by applicable service rules, vacancies, performance and other conditions.

Assistant Commandants who are already appointed in a participating CAPF are not eligible to sit again for the UPSC CAPF (ACs) examination for recruitment as Assistant Commandants, according to the 2026 UPSC notice.
bullets: Assistant Commandant.
Deputy Commandant.
Second-in-Command.
Commandant and higher officer ranks.

title: Assistant Commandant in Central Industrial Security Force
description: A Group A Assistant Commandant officer in the Central Industrial Security Force, recruited through UPSC CAPF (AC) examination.

quick_facts.label: Position and cadre context
quick_facts.value: Assistant Commandant is a Group A, Gazetted, Non-Ministerial rank in CISF; a CISF Assistant Commandant/Fire vacancy notice identifies the corresponding revised pay level as Level 10 under the 7th CPC.

quick_facts.label: Primary external entry route
quick_facts.value: For the executive Assistant Commandant route, UPSC conducts the Central Armed Police Forces (ACs) Examination and allocates successful candidates across CAPFs, including CISF, subject to the notification, merit, medical fitness, vacancies and force preferences.

quick_facts.label: Education baseline
quick_facts.value: The UPSC CAPF (AC) 2025 notice required a bachelor's degree or an equivalent qualification; candidates awaiting qualifying results could be provisionally admitted subject to producing passing proof at the prescribed stage. Eligibility must be checked against the notification for the candidate's own examination year.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: The UPSC CAPF (AC) process includes a written examination, Physical Standards/Physical Efficiency Tests, an Interview/Personality Test, and medical standards testing. Final merit is based on written-examination and interview/personality-test marks, while medical fitness remains mandatory for appointment.

quick_facts.label: 2026 examination timing
quick_facts.value: UPSC’s examination-notification archive lists CAPF (AC) Examination 2026 as notified on February 20, 2026, with the written examination scheduled for July 19, 2026; the application deadline listed there was March 12, 2026 at 18:00. These are cycle-specific dates, not a standing annual timetable.

sections.heading: What a CISF Assistant Commandant does
paragraphs: An Assistant Commandant is a supervisory operational officer. Under the CISF Rules, the officer assists the Commandant, may perform the Commandant’s functions when required, assists a Deputy Commandant where applicable, and is responsible for the efficiency, discipline and morale of personnel under the officer as well as security of the undertaking or duties entrusted to the officer.

CISF’s security charter gives the operational setting for that responsibility: access control, perimeter security, protection of designated critical installations, prevention and control of crime, escorting vital consignments, personnel protection and counter-terror quick-response duties. The exact portfolio varies by posting and unit.
bullets: Lead, deploy and maintain discipline among personnel under command.
Support unit security management and take delegated command responsibilities.
Apply security procedures at critical infrastructure and public-facing protected sites.

sections.heading: Entering through UPSC CAPF (AC)
paragraphs: The canonical external route is the UPSC Central Armed Police Forces (Assistant Commandants) Examination. In the 2025 notice, both men and women were eligible; the notice set the ordinary age band at 20–25 years on its specified cut-off date, with listed category and service relaxations. It also required Indian citizenship subject to stated exceptions for subjects of Nepal or Bhutan, and a bachelor’s degree or equivalent. Requirements can change, so applicants should rely on the notice for their own cycle.

The written stage has two papers: General Ability and Intelligence (250 marks) and General Studies, Essay and Comprehension (200 marks). Candidates who qualify the written examination proceed to PST/PET; the 2025 PET included timed 100-metre and 800-metre runs, long jump, and—only for men—shot put. Candidates qualifying the physical stages are called for the UPSC Interview/Personality Test, worth 150 marks, followed by medical standards testing.

There is also an internal path into the AC (Executive) grade: the Ministry of Home Affairs stated in 2022 that 50% of AC (Executive) posts were filled through promotion, including LDCE. That is a route for eligible serving CISF personnel and is distinct from the UPSC CAPF (AC) external-entry route.
bullets: Track UPSC’s notification and apply through the official UPSC application portal specified for that cycle.
Prepare simultaneously for the written papers, physical standards/efficiency requirements, interview and medical fitness.
Treat age limits, physical standards, vacancies, preferences, fees and deadlines as notification-specific.

sections.heading: Skills that match the role and examination
paragraphs: The role calls for command judgement, personnel leadership, discipline, security awareness and the ability to operate within formal procedures, because the CISF Rules assign Assistant Commandants responsibility for personnel efficiency, morale and undertaking security. The selection syllabus also tests logical reasoning, quantitative aptitude, data interpretation, general science, current affairs, essay writing and English-language comprehension—useful indicators of the academic and communication preparation expected of applicants.

Physical readiness is not merely desirable: candidates must clear prescribed PST/PET and medical standards before appointment. Applicants should therefore build structured endurance, speed, basic power and injury-conscious conditioning alongside written-exam preparation.
bullets: Team leadership, calm decision-making and accountability.
Security assessment, access-control awareness and incident response.
Clear written communication for essays, reports and operational coordination.
Quantitative reasoning, general awareness and disciplined physical preparation.

sections.heading: Posting environment
paragraphs: CISF protects a broad range of critical infrastructure rather than operating in a single office environment. Its official description identifies deployments at nuclear and space establishments, airports, seaports, power plants, government buildings, heritage sites, the Delhi Metro, prisons and Parliament-related security duties. Consequently, an Assistant Commandant may work in field units, transport hubs, industrial or strategic installations, headquarters-linked assignments or training environments, depending on organisational need.

This is a nationally deployable uniformed service. CISF states that it is present across almost all states and runs reserve battalions and training institutions; applicants should therefore expect location, shift pattern, operational exposure and unit duties to vary materially by posting.
bullets: Potentially public-facing work at airports, metro systems and protected public sites.
Potentially high-security work at strategic, industrial, energy and infrastructure installations.
Transferable postings and operational command responsibilities rather than a fixed-location career.

sections.heading: Career progression context
paragraphs: Assistant Commandant is an officer rank within the CISF executive structure. Official CISF promotion orders document promotion from Assistant Commandant (Executive) to Deputy Commandant (Executive), demonstrating a higher officer grade beyond AC. Actual advancement depends on applicable recruitment/promotion rules, seniority, eligibility, performance, vacancies, prescribed training and other service conditions; it should not be treated as automatic.

For context on entry into the AC grade from within the force, the Ministry of Home Affairs stated that half of AC (Executive) posts were filled by promotion, including through LDCE, and that eligibility for promotion from Inspector included regular service, medical category, prescribed training and duty-battalion service. Those historical details describe the internal feeder route, not guaranteed promotion conditions for every future cycle.
bullets: A documented next officer rank is Deputy Commandant (Executive).
Promotional prospects are governed by service rules and organisational vacancies, not only time served.
Serving personnel may access AC (Executive) through promotion/LDCE under the applicable rules.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: A CISF notice for Assistant Commandant/Fire describes the post as revised Pay Level 10, with the 7th CPC matrix range of ₹56,100–₹1,77,500. This is pay-matrix context rather than a promise of take-home pay: gross and net pay vary with admissible allowances, duty location, accommodation, deductions, service status and future government revisions. The cited notice concerned AC/Fire on deputation, but it is official evidence for the Group A Assistant Commandant Level 10 pay context.

Candidates should verify the appointment offer, current pay orders and applicable CISF/MHA instructions for the precise compensation package at joining. Do not infer a fixed monthly in-hand salary solely from the Level 10 range.
bullets: Official cited pay context: revised Pay Level 10, ₹56,100–₹1,77,500.
Allowances and deductions are variable and can change with policy and posting.
Confirm the applicable appointment terms and current government orders before making financial decisions.

title: Assistant Commandant in Central Reserve Police Force
description: A Group A Assistant Commandant officer in the Central Reserve Police Force, recruited through UPSC CAPF (AC) examination.

quick_facts.label: Position and cadre
quick_facts.value: Assistant Commandant is the entry Group A officer post recruited through the UPSC Central Armed Police Forces (Assistant Commandants) examination; CRPF is one of the participating forces. Force allocation is based on the examination process and candidates submit force preferences.

quick_facts.label: Education requirement
quick_facts.value: In the 2025 UPSC CAPF (AC) notice, the minimum qualification was a bachelor’s degree from a recognized university or an equivalent qualification. Requirements should be checked against the notice for the applicable examination year.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: The 2025 process comprised a written examination, Physical Standards/Physical Efficiency Tests, an UPSC Interview/Personality Test, and Medical Standards Tests; final merit was based on written-examination and interview marks, subject to medical fitness.

quick_facts.label: Physical eligibility context
quick_facts.value: For the 2025 examination, UPSC prescribed minimum physical standards and PET events, including timed 100 m and 800 m races, long jump, and—for men—shot put. The governing notice for a future cycle may change these standards.

quick_facts.label: Promotion path
quick_facts.value: CRPF lists the gazetted-officer progression as Assistant Commandant → Deputy Commandant → Second-in-Command → Commandant → DIGP → IGP, with stated qualifying-service thresholds at each stage.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: Assistant Commandant is referenced by the Ministry of Home Affairs as Pay Matrix Level 10. The Seventh Central Pay Commission’s Level 10 entry-pay example is ₹56,100 basic pay; actual monthly earnings depend on prevailing allowances, posting, deductions, and pay rules.

sections.heading: Operational and administrative command
paragraphs: An Assistant Commandant is a gazetted CRPF officer expected to lead a service company during internal-security duties, plan, brief, and conduct company-level operations, command and supervise deployments, and train personnel for operational readiness. CRPF’s Assistant Commandant Promotion Course describes these as responsibilities inherent to the rank.

The role also carries substantial people-management and administration work: maintaining discipline, efficiency, morale and records; supervising and motivating subordinates; and carrying out gazetted-officer duties in a battalion or other institution. These responsibilities make the post a frontline leadership role rather than solely an examination-qualified desk post.
bullets: Lead and supervise company-level operations and deployments.
Train personnel and maintain operational preparedness.
Manage discipline, administration, documentation, efficiency, and morale within the command.

sections.heading: Primary entry route: UPSC CAPF (AC) examination
paragraphs: The standard direct-entry route is the UPSC Central Armed Police Forces (Assistant Commandants) examination. In the 2025 notice, UPSC recruited Group A Assistant Commandants for BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP and SSB; applicants stated their force preferences as part of the process. Appointment to CRPF therefore follows success in the common examination and subsequent allocation, rather than a separate CRPF-only Assistant Commandant examination.

For the 2025 cycle, both male and female candidates were eligible. UPSC required a bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification and set the ordinary age band at 20 to 25 years as on August 1, 2025, with specified relaxations. Those dates and conditions are historical, cycle-specific context—not a substitute for the next UPSC notification.

The assessed pathway included written papers, PST/PET for candidates qualifying the written stage, an Interview/Personality Test, and Medical Standards Tests. Candidates should treat the official UPSC notice for their own cycle as controlling for applications, eligibility, test standards, vacancies, fee, dates, and force-allocation preferences.
bullets: Earn a recognized bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification.
Apply to the annual UPSC CAPF (AC) examination when the official notice opens.
Qualify the written examination, PST/PET, interview/personality test, and medical examination.
Indicate CRPF among force preferences; final appointment depends on merit, eligibility, vacancies, and allocation rules.

sections.heading: Capabilities developed and assessed for the role
paragraphs: CRPF’s officer-training material identifies the practical capabilities expected at Assistant Commandant level: planning and briefing operations, conducting company-level tasks, command and deployment supervision, and training personnel. This supports preparation that combines physical readiness with tactical judgment, clear communication, and the ability to lead under demanding conditions.

The same official course material emphasizes administration, discipline, morale, document maintenance, and supervision of subordinate ranks. Accordingly, prospective officers benefit from organization, sound written communication, integrity, situational awareness, and the ability to motivate teams as well as operational fitness.
bullets: Operational planning, briefing, and execution.
Team leadership, supervision, discipline, and morale-building.
Physical endurance and readiness for prescribed PST/PET and medical standards.
Administrative control, record keeping, and professional written communication.

sections.heading: Where Assistant Commandants may serve
paragraphs: CRPF is a large nationwide force with general-duty, VIP-security, women, Rapid Action Force, CoBRA, signal, and special-duty units, alongside headquarters, group centres, training institutions, and hospitals. The organization’s published structure indicates that postings can span operational units and institutional or administrative establishments.

Assistant Commandants can also hold training-institution responsibilities. CRPF training pages show officers of Assistant Commandant/Deputy Commandant rank commanding faculties and serving as assistant principals or faculty officers. The exact posting, duties, accommodation, and hardship exposure vary by unit, location, operational requirement, and career stage.
bullets: Operational battalions and specialized formations, including RAF and CoBRA.
Headquarters, group centres, and other administrative establishments.
Training institutions, where Assistant Commandants may perform instructional or leadership roles.

sections.heading: Career progression in CRPF’s gazetted officer cadre
paragraphs: CRPF publishes a defined promotional avenue for cadre officers after joining as Assistant Commandant. The next rank is Deputy Commandant, for which CRPF states five years as Assistant Commandant as the qualifying service. Further published thresholds are five years as Deputy Commandant, with 10 total years of Group A service, for Second-in-Command; five years as Second-in-Command, with 15 Group A years, for Commandant; three years as Commandant, with 20 Group A years, for DIGP; and three years as DIG, with 24 Group A years, for IGP.

These are qualifying-service benchmarks published by CRPF, not guarantees of promotion. Actual advancement remains subject to the applicable service rules, vacancies, performance and other conditions.
bullets: Assistant Commandant → Deputy Commandant: 5 years as Assistant Commandant.
Deputy Commandant → Second-in-Command: 5 years as Deputy Commandant and 10 total Group A years.
Second-in-Command → Commandant: 5 years as Second-in-Command and 15 Group A years.
Commandant → DIGP → IGP: CRPF publishes additional qualifying-service thresholds.

sections.heading: Compensation: pay-matrix context, not a fixed take-home figure
paragraphs: The Ministry of Home Affairs has identified Assistant Commandant as Level 10 in the central pay matrix in a CAPF-related vacancy document. The Seventh Central Pay Commission’s published entry-pay example for direct recruitment at Level 10 is ₹56,100 basic pay. This is useful as a base-pay reference, but not as a promise of a particular in-hand salary.

Monthly compensation can differ materially with current dearness allowance, house-rent or government-accommodation arrangements, eligible risk/hardship or field-related allowances, deductions, location, and assignment. CRPF’s welfare material, for example, records separate risk/hardship provisions for eligible operational deployments and a CoBRA-related allowance for eligible personnel, illustrating why total compensation is posting-dependent.
bullets: Base-pay reference: Level 10, with the Seventh CPC’s stated direct-entry example of ₹56,100 basic pay.
Allowances and take-home pay are variable and should be confirmed from current government orders and the appointment/posting terms.
Operational or specialized assignments may have different eligible allowances.

title: Assistant Commandant in Indo-Tibetan Border Police
description: A Group A Assistant Commandant officer in the Indo-Tibetan Border Police, recruited through UPSC CAPF (AC) examination.

quick_facts.label: Position and cadre
quick_facts.value: Assistant Commandant (General Duty) in ITBP is classified in the published recruitment rules as a General Central Service, Group ‘A’, Gazetted, non-ministerial post.

quick_facts.label: Primary external entry route
quick_facts.value: For the general-duty post, the rules provide for 50% of vacancies to be filled by direct recruitment through the all-India competitive examination conducted by UPSC; the UPSC CAPF (ACs) process allocates a force based on merit position and the candidate’s stated force preferences.

quick_facts.label: Education requirement
quick_facts.value: The published ITBP General Duty Group A recruitment rules require a bachelor’s degree from a recognised university or an equivalent qualification. The UPSC CAPF (ACs) 2025 notice likewise required a bachelor’s degree.

quick_facts.label: Selection process
quick_facts.value: In the UPSC CAPF (ACs) 2025 cycle, selection comprised a written examination, physical standards/physical efficiency tests, interview/personality test, and medical standards tests. Final merit was based on the written examination and interview/personality-test marks, subject to medical fitness.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: The 2018 ITBP General Duty Group A recruitment rules list Assistant Commandant at Pay Matrix Level 10, ₹56,100–₹1,77,500. This is the published basic-pay matrix range, not a guaranteed take-home amount; applicable allowances and future pay-policy changes can alter total remuneration.

quick_facts.label: Service environment
quick_facts.value: ITBP is a border-guarding force trained for high-altitude mountainous terrain. MHA’s ITBP profile states that some border outposts are at heights up to 18,750 feet, where temperatures can fall to minus 40°C.

sections.heading: Responsibilities and operational role
paragraphs: An Assistant Commandant is an officer rank in the ITBP statutory rank structure. The ITBP Act specifically provides that an Assistant Commandant commanding a company, detachment or outpost has defined authority to proceed against personnel charged with offences and to award specified minor punishments, subject to the Act. In practice, this places command, discipline, supervision and accountable decision-making at the centre of the role.

ITBP’s published role includes constant border vigilance, border management, protection of border check posts and populations, counter-insurgency and internal-security duties, protection of vital installations and vulnerable points, disaster management, civic action, and a wartime role with the Army. An Assistant Commandant’s exact assignment depends on posting and formation, but these force-level duties frame the operational work that officers may lead or support.
bullets: Command and supervise a company, detachment or outpost when assigned.
Maintain discipline, readiness, reporting and lawful exercise of delegated command powers.
Lead or support border-management, security, internal-security and disaster-response tasks according to deployment.

sections.heading: Entry through UPSC CAPF (ACs)
paragraphs: For an applicant seeking this canonical General Duty officer role from outside ITBP, the relevant route is the UPSC Central Armed Police Forces (Assistant Commandants) Examination. The ITBP General Duty recruitment rules prescribe direct recruitment through the UPSC all-India competitive examination for 50% of vacancies, while the UPSC notice states that service/force allocation is determined by merit position and candidates’ force preferences. Selecting ITBP as a preference therefore does not itself guarantee ITBP allocation.

Eligibility and dates must be checked in the notice for the particular examination year. As a dated example, the 2025 UPSC CAPF (ACs) notice set the general age band at 20–25 years on August 1, 2025, required a bachelor’s degree, and allowed both male and female candidates to be appointed. The same notice set out category and service-related age relaxations; applicants should use the live UPSC notice rather than relying on a previous cycle.

The 2025 selection scheme used two written papers: General Ability and Intelligence (250 marks) and General Studies, Essay and Comprehension (200 marks). Written-qualified candidates proceeded to physical standards and physical-efficiency testing, then interview/personality testing and medical standards testing. The interview carried 150 marks; final merit was drawn from the written examination and interview, with appointment dependent on satisfying medical standards.
bullets: Earn a recognised bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification.
Apply in the relevant annual UPSC CAPF (ACs) notification and indicate force preferences carefully.
Prepare for the written papers, physical standards/efficiency requirements, interview and medical examination.
Treat age limits, vacancy numbers, application dates, standards and force-allocation rules as cycle-specific.

sections.heading: Skills to build
paragraphs: The examination and the force’s operational environment point to a blend of academic, communication, physical and leadership capabilities. UPSC’s written syllabus tests reasoning, quantitative ability, data interpretation, general science, current affairs, essay writing and English-language comprehension/communication. The physical tests and medical requirements mean candidates also need sustained conditioning and careful attention to fitness.

The role’s command and high-altitude border-security context make calm judgement, team leadership, situational awareness, discipline, clear written and spoken communication, and resilience especially relevant. These are role-aligned capabilities inferred from the statutory command responsibilities of Assistant Commandants and ITBP’s published duties; they are not a separate exhaustive eligibility checklist.
bullets: Logical reasoning, quantitative aptitude, general awareness and clear analytical writing.
Hindi/English examination readiness, including English precis, comprehension and communication components specified by UPSC.
Running, speed, jumping, strength and injury-aware physical conditioning for the prescribed tests.
Leadership, operational judgement, discipline and communication for command assignments.
Resilience and adaptability for remote, high-altitude and security-sensitive deployments.

sections.heading: Workplace and deployment context
paragraphs: ITBP is assigned border-guarding responsibilities on the India–China border and is specially trained to operate in high-altitude mountain terrain. Its work can include border outposts, units and operational deployments rather than a conventional office-only environment. MHA describes ITBP tasks that also extend to internal security, counter-insurgency, vital-installation and VIP security, disaster management, civic action and other duties.

The published recruitment rules identify Assistant Commandant as a Group A gazetted general-duty post, and the ITBP Act places the rank within the force’s officer structure. Posting, field exposure, command appointment and day-to-day work will vary materially by unit, location, operational requirements and career stage.
bullets: Potential field and border-outpost service in remote, mountainous areas.
Operational work may involve irregular hours, demanding weather and mobility constraints.
Assignments may also arise in security, internal-security, disaster-management or administrative/training contexts.

sections.heading: Career progression
paragraphs: The statutory officer hierarchy lists Assistant Commandant below Deputy Commandant, Second-in-Command and Commandant, followed by senior ranks including Deputy Inspector-General, Inspector-General, Additional Director-General and Director-General. Advancement is governed by the applicable recruitment rules, service record, vacancy, eligibility conditions and prescribed training rather than being automatic.

Under the published 2018 General Duty Group A recruitment rules, promotion from Assistant Commandant to Deputy Commandant requires five years of regular service in Level 10, including two years’ experience as Company Commander of a service company in a service battalion, plus successful completion of the prescribed pre-promotional training course; the rules specify an exception to that company-commander condition for officers in the central sports team. The same rules list Deputy Commandant at Level 11, Second-in-Command at Level 12 and Commandant at Level 13. Requirements can be amended, so serving personnel should consult current ITBP/MHA orders.
bullets: Entry rank: Assistant Commandant (General Duty), Level 10.
Next published rank: Deputy Commandant (General Duty), Level 11.
Subsequent published ranks include Second-in-Command (Level 12) and Commandant (Level 13).
Promotion is conditional on qualifying service, required experience where applicable, prescribed training and selection processes.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: The ITBP General Duty Group A recruitment rules published in 2018 place Assistant Commandant at Level 10 of the Central Government pay matrix: ₹56,100–₹1,77,500. This describes the basic pay range in that rule, not a single monthly in-hand salary.

Total compensation is variable. It can depend on basic-pay stage, admissible central-government and force allowances, place of posting, deductions, pension arrangements and changes to government policy. ITBP recruitment material for another Group A Assistant Commandant cadre describes Level 10 pay plus admissible ITBP/MHA allowances and coverage under the government’s contributory pension arrangement; applicants should confirm the terms in the notification and appointment conditions applicable to their own recruitment cycle and cadre.
bullets: Published basic-pay context: Level 10, ₹56,100–₹1,77,500.
Do not treat online ‘in-hand salary’ estimates as official or universal.
Confirm current allowances, deductions and pension terms from the relevant official notification and appointment documents.

title: Assistant Commandant in Sashastra Seema Bal

quick_facts.label: Role and service
quick_facts.value: Assistant Commandant is an officer rank in Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), which is one of the Central Armed Police Forces under the Ministry of Home Affairs. The SSB Rules list Assistant Commandant within the officer ranks.

quick_facts.label: Primary entry route
quick_facts.value: The principal open competitive route is the UPSC Central Armed Police Forces (Assistant Commandants) Examination. Candidates state force preferences in the application; allocation is based on merit position and those preferences.

quick_facts.label: 2026 SSB vacancies and examination date
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 CAPF (AC) cycle, UPSC notified 53 tentative SSB vacancies out of 349 total CAPF Assistant Commandant vacancies, and scheduled the written examination for July 19, 2026. UPSC states that vacancy numbers and the examination date are liable to change.

quick_facts.label: Baseline eligibility in the 2026 cycle
quick_facts.value: The 2026 notice required a bachelor’s degree (or an accepted equivalent), age 20–24 as of August 1, 2026, and compliance with prescribed physical and medical standards. Both men and women were eligible; specified age relaxations applied to eligible categories.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: The Ministry of Home Affairs’ 2026 CAPF (AC) examination rules place Assistant Commandant in Level 10, junior scale, of the pay matrix: ₹56,100–₹177,500 basic-pay range. sections.heading: What the role contributes to
paragraphs: SSB is tasked in its area of responsibility with safeguarding assigned borders, promoting a sense of security among border communities, preventing trans-border crime, smuggling and other illegal activity, preventing unauthorised entry or exit, carrying out civic-action programmes, and undertaking other duties assigned by the Central Government. An Assistant Commandant is an officer in this force structure and may be placed in command or other assigned roles supporting these functions.

The work is therefore operational as well as managerial: officers can be responsible for command, discipline, administration, morale, training and welfare of personnel under their assignment. The precise mix depends on the unit, location and orders rather than being fixed for every Assistant Commandant posting.
bullets: Border-security and anti-smuggling work in the assigned area of responsibility.
Leadership, discipline, administration, training and welfare responsibilities when personnel or a task are placed under the officer’s command.
Participation in civic-action and other duties lawfully assigned to the force.

sections.heading: Entering through UPSC CAPF (AC)
paragraphs: For the canonical route, apply to UPSC’s CAPF (AC) examination when the notification is open and include SSB in the force-preference order. In the 2026 notice, allocation was to be made using the final merit position and the preferences submitted with the application; selecting SSB is therefore not a separate SSB written examination under this route.

The 2026 selection sequence was: a two-paper written examination; Physical Standards Test and Physical Efficiency Test for written-qualified candidates; UPSC Interview/Personality Test for candidates qualifying PST/PET; and medical standards testing. Final merit is based on written-examination and interview/personality-test marks, while appointment also requires meeting medical standards.

The 2026 application deadline was March 12, 2026 and the examination was scheduled for July 19, 2026. Those dates, the fee, vacancy numbers, physical standards and eligibility conditions are cycle-specific, so prospective candidates should use the next UPSC notice rather than assume they will recur unchanged.
bullets: Written papers in 2026: General Ability and Intelligence (250 marks), followed by General Studies, Essay and Comprehension (200 marks).
2026 PET benchmarks included a 100-metre race, 800-metre race and long jump for all candidates; shot put applied to men in that notice.
NCC ‘B’ or ‘C’ certification was desirable in the 2026 notice and considered at interview/personality-test stage, not a mandatory baseline qualification.

sections.heading: Capabilities to build
paragraphs: The UPSC selection design indicates the capabilities an aspirant should develop: logical reasoning, numerical ability and data interpretation; scientific and current-affairs awareness; knowledge of Indian polity, economy, history and geography; clear essay writing; English comprehension and communication; and the fitness required to meet PST/PET and medical standards.

For service readiness, the force’s statutory tasks and command provisions make physical resilience, sound judgement, disciplined leadership, communication, ethical conduct, administration and the ability to work with border communities especially relevant. These are role-aligned capabilities, not a substitute for the formal UPSC eligibility and medical requirements.
bullets: Prepare both objective aptitude/general-awareness material and descriptive essay, précis and comprehension work.
Train specifically for the current notification’s test events and standards rather than relying on informal fitness advice.
Develop leadership and record-keeping habits alongside exam preparation, because force duties include command, discipline, administration, training and welfare.

sections.heading: Posting and working environment
paragraphs: SSB is the border-guarding force assigned to the Indo-Nepal and Indo-Bhutan borders. Its charter also includes preventing cross-border crime and unauthorised movement, as well as civic-action work. Accordingly, an Assistant Commandant can expect assignments connected with border-area units and their operational, administrative or training requirements; the specific station and duties are determined by service needs.

The SSB Rules provide that officers and members of the regular force are liable for continuous service for the term set out in their appointment or applicable rules. They also provide that members may be required to perform duties connected with the force’s task, administration, discipline, training and welfare, as well as other duties assigned under law or by superior order.
bullets: Border-area and unit-based work is central to SSB’s mandate.
Assignments can combine field operations with personnel administration, training and community-facing civic action.
Location, operational tempo and duties vary with the area of responsibility and orders.

sections.heading: Officer hierarchy and early career development
paragraphs: The SSB Rules place Assistant Commandant as an officer rank below Deputy Commandant, Second-in-Command, Commandant, Deputy Inspector-General, Inspector-General, Additional Director-General and Director-General. This establishes the officer hierarchy, but it should not be read as a guarantee of promotion on a particular timetable.

For officers recruited through CAPF (AC), the 2026 Ministry of Home Affairs rules set Assistant Commandant at Level 10 and list the succeeding CAPF scales through Inspector General. The rules also provide for professional training during probation and state that promotion is available only when the eligibility conditions in the relevant recruitment rules are met. Progression therefore depends on applicable rules, training, performance, vacancies and service requirements.
bullets: Entry rank: Assistant Commandant (Level 10 in the 2026 CAPF rules).
Next listed CAPF officer rank: Deputy Commandant (Level 11 in the 2026 rules).
Professional training and any required departmental examinations form part of the probationary development framework.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: As notified in the Ministry of Home Affairs’ 2026 CAPF (AC) examination rules, Assistant Commandant is in Pay Matrix Level 10 (junior scale), ₹56,100–₹177,500. The range is the published basic-pay matrix range, not a single monthly in-hand salary.

Actual monthly remuneration can differ by place and nature of posting because allowances, deductions and entitlements are governed by the rules in force and individual service circumstances. Candidates should therefore treat the stated scale as dated 2026 compensation context and verify current government orders before making financial comparisons.
bullets: Published 2026 basic-pay matrix: Level 10, ₹56,100–₹177,500.
Do not equate the pay-matrix range with take-home salary.
Allowances and deductions are variable and should be confirmed from current official orders.

title: Assistant Commissioner in State Labour Department
description: A state labour administration officer who enforces labour laws and supports industrial relations, worker welfare, and dispute resolution.

quick_facts.label: Role scope
quick_facts.value: An Assistant Commissioner of Labour is a state labour-administration post. Exact statutory powers, reporting structure, title, and territorial assignment vary by state; Maharashtra, for example, lists Assistant Commissioners within offices headed by Deputy Commissioners of Labour.

quick_facts.label: Core public-service purpose
quick_facts.value: The work commonly combines labour-law enforcement, industrial-relations administration, worker-welfare activity, and prevention or settlement of industrial disputes. State labour departments describe these as central departmental functions.

quick_facts.label: Usual entry channel
quick_facts.value: A common route is appointment through a State Public Service Commission civil-services or Group-I/combined-services recruitment. Telangana’s Group-I notification, for example, included Assistant Commissioner of Labour (Labour Service) as a notified post.

quick_facts.label: Education context
quick_facts.value: Eligibility is notification-specific. In one Telangana Group-I recruitment, a recognised bachelor’s degree in Arts, Commerce, Science, or Engineering was required for Assistant Commissioner of Labour, with preference for a postgraduate qualification in social work focused on labour welfare/personnel management/industrial labour relations.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: Pay is state- and notification-specific. As dated examples rather than a national salary promise: Telangana’s 2024 Group-I notice showed ₹54,220–₹1,33,630 for the post, while a Maharashtra Labour Department promotion order described Assistant Commissioner of Labour, Group A at Pay Matrix Level S-18 (₹49,100–₹1,55,800).

sections.heading: What the role does
paragraphs: The post supports the state’s labour-administration system rather than a single private employer. Departmental functions include safeguarding workers’ welfare, safety and health; promoting industrial peace; and dealing with employer–worker disputes such as strikes and lockouts. The precise powers delegated to an Assistant Commissioner depend on the state’s labour laws, departmental orders, and posting.

Industrial-relations work can include conciliation or mediation: the statutory industrial-disputes framework provides machinery for investigation and settlement of disputes, including conciliation officers, labour courts, and tribunals. In the comparable central labour-administration structure, Assistant Labour Commissioners are identified as conciliation officers and inspectors, illustrating the combination of dispute-resolution and enforcement functions that state labour systems may allocate through their own rules.

Casework may therefore involve receiving or processing complaints and claims, conducting or supervising inspections where authorised, engaging employers and unions, maintaining statutory records, and preparing reports or proceedings. These tasks are role-contextual rather than a universal checklist; candidates should verify the applicable state service rules and the specific recruitment notification.
bullets: Promote harmonious industrial relations and seek to prevent escalation of disputes.
Apply and administer labour-law provisions within the officer’s assigned jurisdiction and delegated authority.
Support worker welfare, workplace safety and health, and compliance activity.
Handle conciliation-related and quasi-judicial/administrative work only where the relevant state law or delegation confers that authority.

sections.heading: How to enter
paragraphs: The primary route is to watch the relevant State Public Service Commission (PSC) and state government recruitment portals for civil-services, Group-I, combined-services, or Labour Service notifications that expressly include this post. The title is not recruited on a single all-India calendar, and vacancies are intermittent.

Applicants must follow the notice for the concerned state because the examination stages, age limits, reservation rules, domicile or language requirements, medical standards, documents, and qualifications may differ. Telangana’s Group-I recruitment provides a useful example: it listed Assistant Commissioner of Labour in the Labour Service and specified a recognised bachelor’s degree, while giving preference to certain postgraduate labour-welfare or industrial-relations qualifications.

A practical preparation path is: earn the degree required by the target notification; study the PSC syllabus and examination scheme; build a working command of labour legislation, industrial relations, public administration, and state-specific rules; and apply only through the official recruitment process. A master’s degree or diploma in labour welfare, personnel management, social work, or industrial relations may be useful where a notification gives it preference, but it is not a universal requirement.
bullets: Track the official PSC and state Labour Department websites for the target state.
Treat the advertisement—not coaching material or old notifications—as the controlling source for eligibility and dates.
Prepare for the general civil-services components as well as labour, social-welfare, industrial-relations, and state-law content where the syllabus requires them.
Check whether the advertised role is direct recruitment, a service-allocation post, or a promotion-related vacancy.

sections.heading: Skills that fit the work
paragraphs: The role calls for careful legal and procedural reasoning, because labour departments administer statutory schemes and industrial-disputes processes. The ability to read rules closely, document facts, write clear orders or reports, and distinguish an administrative complaint from a matter requiring conciliation or adjudication is important.

Conciliation and labour-relations functions also make communication, impartial listening, negotiation, and conflict de-escalation central practical skills. Official labour-administration sources describe conciliation, mediation, prevention of disputes, enforcement, and worker welfare as core functions; the skills listed here are the practical capabilities directly implied by those functions.

Field-readiness matters as well: officers may operate through territorial offices and engage with workers, unions, employers, and other public authorities. Professional conduct, record management, comfort with inspections or hearings where assigned, and ability to work in relevant state/local languages can be especially valuable, subject to the state’s rules.
bullets: Labour-law literacy and procedural accuracy.
Conciliation, negotiation, and neutral stakeholder communication.
Fact-finding, inspection or compliance documentation where authorised.
Clear drafting, file management, and evidence-based reporting.
Public-service ethics, discretion, and ability to manage contentious interactions.

sections.heading: Workplace and posting pattern
paragraphs: This is ordinarily a government field-and-office role, not solely a secretariat desk position. Maharashtra’s Labour Department publishes offices in which Assistant Commissioners serve alongside Deputy Commissioners and Government Labour Officers, showing a territorial labour-administration setup. Actual posting can be district, regional, divisional, multi-zone, headquarters, or another unit specified by the state.

The work environment can mix office files and hearings with employer/worker meetings, complaint handling, coordination with other agencies, and visits or inspections when the officer’s statutory designation and assignment require them. Central labour field offices similarly combine enforcement, dispute prevention and settlement, and worker-welfare responsibilities; this is relevant contextual evidence, while the authority of a state officer remains governed by that state’s framework.
bullets: Expect postings outside the state capital as well as headquarters assignments.
Expect interaction with employers, workers, trade unions, advocates, other departments, and labour adjudicatory bodies.
Expect a mixture of administrative, legal-process, stakeholder-facing, and—where authorised—field compliance work.

sections.heading: Career progression context
paragraphs: Progression is governed by the service rules of the appointing state and should not be assumed to be identical across India. Departmental organisation can include Assistant Commissioners working below Deputy Commissioners or other senior labour-commissioner posts; Maharashtra’s published office roster is one current example of such a hierarchy.

Promotion can be a route into the Assistant Commissioner grade in some state systems. Maharashtra has published an order concerning temporary promotion to Assistant Commissioner of Labour, Group A, but that order alone does not establish a universal feeder cadre or promotion timetable. Candidates should consult the applicable state service rules, seniority lists, and departmental promotion orders.
bullets: Possible advancement depends on state cadre rules, vacancies, service record, departmental examinations where applicable, and promotion policy.
Do not infer a guaranteed promotion ladder or time scale from another state’s Labour Department structure.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: There is no single India-wide salary for this state-government post. Basic pay depends on the state pay matrix or scale, grade/cadre classification, and the recruitment or service order in force; take-home pay also varies with allowances, deductions, posting, and later pay revisions.

For dated official context only, Telangana’s 2024 Group-I notification listed Assistant Commissioner of Labour at ₹54,220–₹1,33,630, while a Maharashtra Labour Department order described the Group A post at Pay Matrix Level S-18, ₹49,100–₹1,55,800. These are state-specific historical reference points, not current or portable salary offers.
bullets: Verify the current advertisement and state pay-revision orders before making any compensation comparison.
Compare basic pay, grade/pay level, allowances, probation terms, pension coverage, and posting conditions—not just the headline range.

title: Assistant Commissioner of State Tax
description: A state tax administration officer who administers GST and other state tax laws, assessments, audits, and enforcement.

quick_facts.label: Role in the tax department hierarchy
quick_facts.value: In Maharashtra’s official GST department hierarchy, Assistant Commissioner of State Tax is placed below Deputy Commissioner of State Tax and above State Tax Officer.

quick_facts.label: Statutory status under state GST
quick_facts.value: The Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 expressly lists Assistant Commissioners of State Tax as a class of officer; jurisdiction and duties are subject to the Act and to assignments, conditions, and limitations set by the Commissioner.

quick_facts.label: Laws administered
quick_facts.value: The exact portfolio is state-specific. Maharashtra’s GST department identifies MGST, CGST, IGST, MVAT, CST, profession-tax, and Chit Fund laws among the important laws it administers.

quick_facts.label: Recruitment context
quick_facts.value: A principal direct-entry route is selection through the relevant State Public Service Commission’s gazetted civil-services examination when the state’s notification includes this or an equivalent state-tax post. Vacancy count, eligibility, stages, reservations, and dates must be checked in the applicable notification.

quick_facts.label: State variation in title and assignment
quick_facts.value: The same level of work may be titled differently across states. For example, Karnataka uses Assistant Commissioner of Commercial Taxes and assigns the rank to local GST-office and enforcement-and-vigilance functional wings.

sections.heading: What the role does
paragraphs: An Assistant Commissioner of State Tax is a mid-level state tax-administration officer. The role operates within a statutory chain of authority: Maharashtra’s MGST law recognizes Assistant Commissioners as State Tax officers, provides for officers’ jurisdiction over the state or assigned local areas, and allows them to exercise statutory powers and discharge duties subject to the Commissioner’s conditions and limitations.

In practice, the work is defined by the officer’s posting, territorial jurisdiction, and delegated powers. It can include administering GST and legacy/state taxes; handling taxpayer-facing statutory proceedings and orders; supervising subordinate tax staff; and, in specialist postings, undertaking investigation, vigilance, enforcement, or audit-related work. Maharashtra has published delegated-power material for Assistant Commissioners in investigation, while Karnataka’s service rules place comparable Assistant Commissioners in local GST offices and enforcement-and-vigilance wings.

The role is not identical in every state: legislation, departmental nomenclature, delegated powers, and case allocation determine the actual remit. Candidates should therefore treat a State PSC advertisement and the state tax department’s current orders as controlling documents, rather than assuming a uniform national job description.
bullets: Apply state tax statutes, rules, notifications, and departmental instructions within the officer’s assigned jurisdiction or function.
Make or supervise legally reasoned administrative decisions and maintain defensible records for review or appeal.
Coordinate with State Tax Officers and other departmental staff, while working within delegated authority and procedural safeguards.
Serve in field, enforcement, investigation, audit, or office-based tax-administration assignments depending on the state and posting.

sections.heading: How entry typically works
paragraphs: For a prospective entrant, the core route is the state’s civil-services recruitment process conducted by its State Public Service Commission, provided that the Assistant Commissioner of State Tax—or an equivalent commercial-tax/GST designation—is included among the notified services. Maharashtra, for example, publishes a Maharashtra Civil Services Gazetted Group A and Group B examination scheme and separate recruitment advertisements through MPSC.

This is a notification-led career path, not a single standing national intake. The authoritative notice for the relevant recruitment cycle sets the post list, number of vacancies, educational qualification, age limits, domicile or language conditions where applicable, examination pattern, application fee, reservation provisions, document requirements, and selection process. These items can change between cycles.

A second career pathway may exist through departmental advancement from subordinate state-tax cadres, but the proportion of direct recruitment versus promotion and the qualifying service rules are state-specific. It should not be assumed from the title alone.
bullets: Monitor the relevant State PSC’s civil-services/gazetted recruitment notices, not only general job aggregators.
Read the post-specific eligibility clauses and service-allocation provisions before applying.
Prepare for the particular State PSC’s notified preliminary and main examination pattern; selection stages may be revised.
After selection, expect appointment, verification, training, posting, and probation to be governed by the state’s service rules and departmental orders.

sections.heading: Skills that matter
paragraphs: Because the role involves exercising statutory authority within assigned limits, the most important professional capabilities are careful legal reading, evidence-based reasoning, accurate drafting, procedural discipline, and sound judgment. These are practical inferences from the statutory framework: state-tax officers may exercise powers and discharge duties under the GST law, while delegated powers can be conditioned or restricted by the Commissioner.

Tax and commercial literacy are highly useful, particularly GST concepts, taxpayer registration and return systems, input-tax-credit issues, invoices and business records, and the relationship between state GST and other state-administered tax laws. The department’s published portfolio shows that the work can extend beyond GST to VAT/CST and profession-tax administration.

Clear written communication is essential. Orders, notices, internal notes, and responses must accurately connect facts, legal provisions, evidence, and conclusions; officers also need the interpersonal composure to deal fairly with taxpayers, representatives, colleagues, and other public authorities.
bullets: Statutory interpretation and administrative-law awareness.
Quantitative and document-analysis skills for returns, invoices, accounts, and transaction records.
Precise drafting, recordkeeping, and case-management discipline.
Digital confidence with tax portals and data-backed workflows.
Integrity, impartiality, confidentiality, and the ability to explain procedure clearly.

sections.heading: Workplace and postings
paragraphs: This is principally a state-government office and field-administration role. Postings can be territorial—attached to a local jurisdiction—or functional, such as enforcement, vigilance, investigation, audit, head-office work, or a specialized taxpayer unit. Official Karnataka functional categories, for example, assign comparable Assistant Commissioners to local GST offices and to enforcement-and-vigilance divisions.

In Maharashtra, published departmental material shows Assistant Commissioners in nodal/divisional offices and separately identifies Assistant Commissioner of State Tax (Investigation) and vigilance posts. This indicates a mix of desk-based statutory work, supervision, taxpayer interaction, inspections or enquiries where authorized, and coordination across departmental units.

Location, transfer liability, field exposure, travel, caseload, and working hours vary materially by state, city or district, wing, and enforcement cycle. Applicants should view the appointing state’s service conditions and current department structure for the most reliable posting picture.
bullets: Potential settings include GST/tax offices, divisional or nodal offices, headquarters, and enforcement or investigation units.
The assignment may be territorial, taxpayer-segment based, or functional.
The role involves both administrative documentation and external-facing statutory work.

sections.heading: Career progression context
paragraphs: Departmental hierarchy provides the basic progression context, although it does not itself guarantee promotion. Maharashtra lists the sequence as State Tax Officer, Assistant Commissioner of State Tax, Deputy Commissioner, Joint Commissioner, Additional Commissioner, Special Commissioner, and Commissioner of State Tax. Actual advancement depends on the relevant state’s service rules, seniority, performance requirements, vacancy position, selection processes, and departmental decisions.

Career breadth can develop through changes in function as well as rank. Official examples show Assistant Commissioner-level work in local GST administration, enforcement and vigilance, and investigation. Such assignments can build experience in assessment and adjudication-related administration, compliance, enforcement, taxpayer services, and departmental management.

Do not treat a hierarchy chart as a fixed timetable. Promotion eligibility, inter-cadre movement, posting policy, and pay progression must be verified against the current rules and government orders of the specific state.
bullets: Maharashtra’s published hierarchy places the role between State Tax Officer and Deputy Commissioner of State Tax.
Functional exposure may span local GST administration, enforcement, vigilance, investigation, and related specialist work.
Promotion and transfer rules are state- and cadre-specific.
