title: Assistant Divisional Engineer in Indian Railways
description: An entry-level Group A engineering officer in the Indian Railway Management Service responsible for railway infrastructure, operations, or maintenance in the allotted discipline.

quick_facts.label: Role designation and status
quick_facts.value: Assistant Divisional Engineer (ADEN/ADE) is a railway engineering designation. Railway Board’s legacy IRSE draft places Assistant Divisional Engineer in the Group A Junior Time Scale; however, current zonal-railway material also uses ADEN/Assistant Executive Engineer for a Group B Civil Engineering promotion post. The designation alone therefore does not always establish an officer’s recruitment group or route.

quick_facts.label: Primary upstream examination
quick_facts.value: For the direct Group A engineering route described by this node, UPSC’s Engineering Services Examination (ESE) is the relevant competitive examination. UPSC listed the 2026 ESE Preliminary examination on 8 February 2026 and the 2026 ESE Main examination as active.

quick_facts.label: Engineering disciplines
quick_facts.value: UPSC ESE is organized around Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, and Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering. A 2025 UPSC addendum specifically inserted IRMS Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, Signal & Telecommunication, and Stores engineering posts among participating services/posts; candidates should check the notice for their own examination year because services and vacancies can change.

quick_facts.label: Probation after IRMS appointment
quick_facts.value: Railway Board terms for IRMS candidates recommended through the 2022 Civil Services Examination specify a two-year probation period and mandatory foundation training; these terms are appointment-batch-specific context, not a substitute for the terms issued with a future appointment.

sections.heading: What an Assistant Divisional Engineer does
paragraphs: In a divisional civil-engineering setting, the job is closely connected to the safe upkeep and delivery of railway infrastructure. A Western Railway divisional description identifies engineering work as safe maintenance of track and bridges, along with quarters, service buildings, roads, drainage and water supply; it also includes preparing plans and estimates and executing sanctioned civil works.

An ADEN can head a subdivision within a railway division. The precise portfolio, discipline, reporting relationships and whether the incumbent is a Group A or Group B officer depend on the railway, cadre arrangement and posting order.
bullets: Inspect and maintain infrastructure within the allotted jurisdiction, with safety as the central operational outcome.
Plan estimates and implement approved engineering works.
Coordinate field execution and administration across a subdivision or divisional engineering organization.

sections.heading: Entry route and eligibility
paragraphs: The direct officer route associated with this node is selection through UPSC’s Engineering Services Examination, followed by allocation to a participating service/post according to examination rank and the candidate’s stated preferences. UPSC’s ESE notice describes a three-stage process: Preliminary (objective), Main (conventional engineering papers), and Personality Test.

For the 2025 ESE notice, the minimum educational qualification included an engineering degree from a qualifying Indian university or institution, with specified alternative engineering qualifications. UPSC’s rules and the relevant annual notice control the final eligibility, age, medical and service-allocation conditions.

Do not conflate this direct Group A route with the separate internal route: South Central Railway material records ADEN/AXEN as a Group B Civil Engineering post filled through a selection quota. That is a promotion pathway for eligible railway employees, rather than entry through ESE as a new Group A officer.
bullets: Prepare in the applicable ESE discipline: Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, or Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering.
Meet the education, age, nationality, medical-fitness and other conditions in the notification for the particular ESE year.
Rank sufficiently high and submit service/post preferences; allotment is merit- and preference-based, subject to the notified vacancies and rules.

sections.heading: Skills to build
paragraphs: Strong engineering fundamentals in the allotted discipline are essential. UPSC tests general studies and engineering aptitude alongside discipline-specific Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, or Electronics & Telecommunication papers, at a standard approximately equivalent to an Indian engineering degree examination.

The role also calls for practical execution and public-service skills. UPSC says its Personality Test assesses leadership, initiative, intellectual curiosity, tact, social qualities, mental and physical energy, practical application and integrity; these are especially relevant to officers overseeing safety-critical assets, works and field teams.
bullets: Discipline-specific design, maintenance and troubleshooting knowledge.
Engineering aptitude, quantitative analysis, drawing/plan interpretation and clear technical writing.
Safety judgement, work planning, contractor or staff coordination, leadership and integrity.
Ability to apply engineering knowledge in field conditions and communicate across operations, maintenance and administrative teams.

sections.heading: Workplace and posting context
paragraphs: The workplace is not limited to an office. Divisional engineering work covers infrastructure distributed across a railway division, and an ADEN may lead a subdivision; this implies a mix of divisional-office coordination, site inspections and field supervision.

Postings and scope are variable: the legacy Group A engineering cadre schedule lists Assistant Divisional Engineer alongside Assistant Engineer roles at headquarters, workshops, railway electrification and RDSO. Current assignment must be confirmed from the individual posting order and applicable IRMS arrangements.
bullets: Railway division and subdivision offices.
Track, bridge, station, colony, road, drainage, water-supply and work-site locations in the assigned jurisdiction.
Potential engineering assignments outside a division, such as headquarters, workshops, railway electrification or RDSO, depending on the cadre and posting.

sections.heading: Career progression context
paragraphs: The legacy IRSE Group A schedule documents a technical-management ladder from Junior Time Scale roles including Assistant Divisional Engineer, to Senior Time Scale roles including Divisional Engineer, and then to Senior Divisional Engineer/Deputy Chief Engineer and higher engineering-management posts. It is useful context for the historical engineering-cadre structure, but it is a draft document predating the unified IRMS framework and should not be treated as a guarantee of present-day promotion timing or titles.

Promotion is governed by applicable service rules, eligibility, vacancies, selection processes and government orders. Candidates should rely on the rules and instructions current when they join rather than on historical grade-pay schedules.
bullets: Entry/JTS context: Assistant Divisional Engineer or related assistant-engineer roles.
Senior-scale context: Divisional Engineer or Executive Engineer roles.
Senior management context: Senior Divisional Engineer, Deputy Chief Engineer, Chief Engineer and related headquarters, construction, RDSO or Railway Board assignments.

title: Assistant Drugs Controller
description: A supervisory drug-control authority who oversees licensing, inspections, and enforcement work under a state or central drugs-control administration.

quick_facts.label: Central-government designation
quick_facts.value: In CDSCO usage, ADC(I) means Assistant Drugs Controller (India).

quick_facts.label: Central service classification
quick_facts.value: Under the 2024 CDSCO Medical Device Vertical recruitment rules, Assistant Drugs Controller (India) is a General Central Service, Group A, Gazetted, Non-Ministerial post.

quick_facts.label: Illustrative central recruitment mix
quick_facts.value: For the Medical Device Vertical, the 2024 rules prescribe 50% direct recruitment and 50% promotion, with deputation (including short-term contract) if promotion cannot fill vacancies.

quick_facts.label: Drug Inspector feeder route
quick_facts.value: In that Medical Device Vertical cadre, Drugs Inspectors in Pay Level 8 may be promoted to ADC(I) after eight years of regular service and the prescribed mandatory training.

quick_facts.label: Illustrative central pay context
quick_facts.value: The 2024 Medical Device Vertical rules place ADC(I) at Pay Level 11, ₹67,700–₹2,08,700 in the pay matrix. This is a dated basic-pay-scale reference; actual monthly remuneration varies with applicable allowances, posting, deductions, and later pay-rule changes.

quick_facts.label: Typical central postings
quick_facts.value: CDSCO identifies ADC(I) officers in zonal and port offices, including offices serving customs/import-export functions.

sections.heading: What an Assistant Drugs Controller does
paragraphs: The role is supervisory and regulatory rather than solely inspection-based. In a CDSCO sub-zonal disclosure, an ADC(I) is described as ensuring uniform implementation of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 with the State Licensing Authority; monitoring Drugs Inspectors and other staff; overseeing court cases and statutory reports; allocating and reviewing licence/certificate applications; and arranging or conducting manufacturing-site inspections before regulatory action.

At CDSCO port offices, the work can focus on import and export control: supervising scrutiny of Bills of Entry, checking regulatory compliance of drugs, medical devices, IVDs and cosmetics, arranging risk-based physical verification, issuing or supporting no-objection clearances, coordinating with Customs, and preventing release of consignments not permitted by the competent authority. The exact mix depends on the office and jurisdiction.
bullets: Supervise inspection, application-review, enforcement, reporting, and case-management work.
Apply the Drugs and Cosmetics Act and associated rules within the authority delegated to the office.
Coordinate with state licensing authorities, Customs, laboratories, applicants, and other investigating agencies where relevant.

sections.heading: Entry routes and eligibility context
paragraphs: Routes are cadre- and notification-specific. The central CDSCO Medical Device Vertical rules notified in 2024 provide a useful official example: direct recruits may qualify with a relevant master's degree plus four years' experience, or a relevant bachelor's degree plus six years' experience, in manufacturing, testing, regulation, or design of medical devices. The listed disciplines include pharmacy/pharmaceutical sciences, life sciences, chemistry, microbiology, medicine with clinical pharmacology, and several engineering fields.

The same rules establish an internal route from Drugs Inspector (Medical Devices): eight years of regular service in Level 8 plus prescribed mandatory training. They also permit deputation from qualifying government, public-sector, university, research, statutory, or autonomous-organisation officers. Candidates should treat these as rules for that specific central vertical—not as a universal eligibility rule for every state Assistant Drugs Controller post—and use the relevant recruitment notification as controlling.
bullets: Build an eligible academic foundation in the discipline specified in the target cadre's notification.
Gain documented experience in regulated manufacturing, testing, inspection, regulatory review, or the relevant technical domain.
For the internal central Medical Device Vertical route, progress through the Drugs Inspector cadre and complete required service and training.

sections.heading: Skills to develop
paragraphs: The official duties and recruitment rules point to a blend of technical-regulatory and supervisory capability. Candidates need enough scientific and product knowledge to evaluate manufacturing, testing, quality, safety, and compliance questions, together with working command of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act framework and the regulations applicable to the office's portfolio.

The role also calls for inspection planning and review, evidence-based documentation, clear regulatory correspondence, report writing, case and file management, and coordination with field inspectors and external agencies. For port postings, practical familiarity with import/export documentation and Customs coordination is particularly relevant.
bullets: Technical evaluation of drug, cosmetic, medical-device, or laboratory/manufacturing records, according to the assigned cadre.
Statutory interpretation and compliance assessment.
Inspection oversight, risk-based verification, documentation, and defensible reporting.
People supervision and inter-agency communication.

sections.heading: Where the work happens
paragraphs: Assistant Drugs Controller posts can be based in central CDSCO zonal, sub-zonal, and port offices. CDSCO's official directory lists ADC(I) positions alongside Deputy Drugs Controllers in regional/zonal offices, while its port-office directory lists ADC(I) offices at locations such as Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, and Chennai.

Work therefore combines office-based regulatory review and administration with field-facing activity: inspections of applicant facilities, oversight of inspectorate work, meetings with state authorities or Customs, verification of consignments, and handling of reports, court matters, RTI matters, or stakeholder communications as assigned.
bullets: Central zonal and sub-zonal regulatory offices.
Airport and seaport offices dealing with regulated imports and exports.
State drug-control administrations, where the title, hierarchy, recruitment rules, and delegated work may differ.

sections.heading: Progression from Drug Inspector
paragraphs: For the CDSCO Medical Device Vertical, the formal progression route is Drugs Inspector (Medical Devices) to Assistant Drugs Controller (India), subject to eight years of regular service in the feeder grade and mandatory training. The next higher central position is Deputy Drugs Controller (India): the 2025 recruitment rules for that post specify promotion from ADC(I) in Level 11 after five years' regular service and prescribed training.

This gives the node's parent-child relationship practical meaning: Drug Inspector experience supplies the inspection and enforcement foundation, while ADC(I) adds supervisory, coordination, and broader regulatory-accountability responsibilities. Actual movement, vacancies, seniority, training, and eligibility are governed by the applicable cadre rules and recruitment orders.
bullets: Drug Inspector → Assistant Drugs Controller (India): official Medical Device Vertical example requires eight years' regular service and training.
Assistant Drugs Controller (India) → Deputy Drugs Controller (India): the 2025 CDSCO rule specifies five years' regular service in Level 11 and prescribed training.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: For the central Medical Device Vertical, the 2024 recruitment rules specify Pay Level 11, ₹67,700–₹2,08,700, for ADC(I). This is the pay-matrix level and range stated in those rules, rather than a promise of take-home salary. Actual remuneration at any point depends on the applicable pay rules, dearness allowance, house-rent or transport allowances, location, deductions, and the employee's pay-stage placement.

Compensation for similarly titled state-government posts can differ because state cadres use their own recruitment rules and pay structures. Applicants should verify the salary, allowances, vacancy count, selection method, age limits, and application dates in the live official advertisement for the particular employer and cadre.
bullets: Use Pay Level 11 only as a dated central Medical Device Vertical reference.
Confirm current total pay and conditions from the issuing authority's recruitment notice and applicable pay orders.

title: Assistant Engineer (Central Government)
description: A supervisory engineering post in central government departments, commonly reached by promotion from Junior Engineer or through higher engineering-service recruitment.

quick_facts.label: Typical status and pay level
quick_facts.value: This is not a single, uniform all-India cadre: the employing department’s Recruitment Rules control its classification and method of appointment. For example, the Central Water Commission’s Farakka Barrage Project describes Assistant Engineer (Civil) as a General Central Service Group ‘B’, Gazetted, Non-Ministerial post in Pay Matrix Level 7 (basic-pay range ₹44,900–₹1,42,400 under the 7th CPC matrix).

quick_facts.label: Core role
quick_facts.value: In a Central Water Commission Assistant Engineer example, the officer heads a sub-division; supervises and executes work against approved designs, drawings and estimates; records/checks measurements; oversees maintenance; and submits progress and other reports to the divisional officer or higher authorities.

quick_facts.label: Main route from Junior Engineer
quick_facts.value: Promotion from Junior Engineer is a real central-government pathway, but eligibility and selection process differ by department. CPWD has conducted a Limited Departmental Competitive Online Examination for promotion from Junior Engineer (Civil/Electrical) to Assistant Engineer (Civil/Electrical), while the Department of Posts recorded promotions from Junior Engineer (Civil) to Assistant Engineer (Civil) in June 2026.

quick_facts.label: Qualification and service requirements
quick_facts.value: Department-specific rules can distinguish degree and diploma holders. A 2024 Delhi Milk Scheme notice for deputation to Assistant Engineer (Civil) required a Junior Engineer/equivalent with three years’ service for degree holders or seven years for diploma holders; other organizations may prescribe different conditions.

quick_facts.label: Career context
quick_facts.value: Assistant Engineer can be a feeder level for Executive Engineer or comparable posts. A 2025 Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology recruitment-rule notification lists nine years’ regular Level-7 Assistant Engineer service as one route for consideration to Executive Engineer (Civil), alongside other conditions.

sections.heading: What an Assistant Engineer does
paragraphs: An Assistant Engineer is commonly the supervisory link between Junior Engineers and the divisional engineering officer. In the Central Water Commission’s Farakka Barrage Project description, the Assistant Engineer heads a sub-division and is responsible for supervising and executing works in line with approved designs, drawings, estimates, norms and standards.

The same official description assigns measurement and quality-control-adjacent records work: taking measurements, checking work measured by Junior Engineers, examining standard measurement books, maintaining buildings/structures/areas/equipment, and furnishing progress and other reports to senior officers. The exact technical discipline and asset base—civil works, electrical systems, water infrastructure, estates or another function—depend on the department and sanctioned post.
bullets: Plan, supervise and document execution of assigned works.
Apply approved drawings, estimates, specifications and departmental standards.
Review Junior Engineer measurements and maintain prescribed measurement records.
Monitor maintenance work and prepare progress reports for the divisional hierarchy.

sections.heading: Entry routes from Junior Engineer and related routes
paragraphs: For this node, promotion from Junior Engineer is the principal route. The selection mechanism is department-specific: CPWD has used a Limited Departmental Competitive Online Examination for Junior Engineer-to-Assistant Engineer promotions, while other central organizations use promotion, deputation, or a composite method prescribed in their own Recruitment Rules.

Service and education thresholds are not portable from one department to another. For example, Delhi Milk Scheme’s 2024 Assistant Engineer (Civil) deputation notice recognized Junior Engineer/equivalent service of three years for degree holders and seven years for diploma holders. The Central Water Commission’s Farakka Barrage Project deputation description instead specified a civil-engineering degree and five years of regular Level-6 service for the stated route. Candidates should therefore read the recruitment rules, vacancy circular and promotion/LDCE notice for their own cadre rather than rely on a generic cutoff.

A distinct higher engineering-service route exists through UPSC’s Engineering Services Examination, but its advertised services commonly use titles such as Assistant Executive Engineer and Group A engineering-service appointments. It should not be treated as an automatic direct-entry route to every department’s Group B Assistant Engineer post.
bullets: Build regular service and a satisfactory record in the Junior Engineer feeder grade.
Check whether the department uses seniority-cum-fitness, a Departmental Promotion Committee, an LDCE, deputation, or a combination.
Verify the prescribed engineering discipline, degree/diploma treatment, qualifying service, vigilance clearance and any departmental examination requirements in the applicable notice.
For higher central engineering-service recruitment, track UPSC Engineering Services Examination notifications and the services/posts listed for that examination.

sections.heading: Skills to develop
paragraphs: The work description supports a practical skill profile centered on engineering execution and public-works controls: interpreting designs, drawings and estimates; site supervision; measurement and record verification; maintenance planning; and concise reporting to divisional authorities.

Because the Assistant Engineer checks work measured by Junior Engineers and ensures work conforms to approved standards, progression from Junior Engineer should include demonstrable accuracy in measurement books, estimates, drawings/specifications, work-progress monitoring and coordination with contractors, field staff and senior officers.
bullets: Engineering drawing, estimate and specification interpretation.
Site supervision, measurement, inspection and maintenance monitoring.
Measurement-book discipline, technical documentation and progress reporting.
Team oversight and clear coordination across Junior Engineers, contractors and divisional officers.

sections.heading: Where the role is performed
paragraphs: The post combines office-based engineering administration with field or asset-site work. The Central Water Commission example places the Assistant Engineer at sub-division level and explicitly covers execution, measurements, maintenance and reports—work that normally requires both site inspections and departmental-office documentation.

Location and working environment depend on the employer. Central-government Assistant Engineer roles may sit in project organizations, works/estate units, barrage or water-infrastructure offices, maintenance wings or other engineering establishments; postings and transfer liability should be confirmed from the relevant cadre rules and vacancy notice.
bullets: Sub-divisional or project engineering office.
Construction, maintenance and inspection sites.
Coordination with Junior Engineers and reporting through the divisional chain.

sections.heading: Progression after Assistant Engineer
paragraphs: Assistant Engineer experience can support movement into Executive Engineer or equivalent management roles where the department’s rules provide for it. In a 2025 MeitY notification, Executive Engineer (Civil) at Level 11 could be filled by promotion/deputation from a Level-7 Assistant Engineer (Civil) with nine years’ regular service, subject to the specified degree and construction/maintenance experience requirements.

This is an example, not a universal timetable. Promotion depends on the cadre’s recruitment rules, available vacancies, qualifying service, prescribed qualifications, selection process and other service conditions. Assistant Engineers should follow their department’s current seniority, DPC, promotion and recruitment-rule notices.
bullets: Develop progressively broader responsibility for design review, estimates, contracts, supervision and maintenance.
Maintain the engineering degree/experience profile required by the next promotional post where applicable.
Track cadre-specific eligibility rather than assuming a single central-government promotion schedule.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: As of the cited recruitment and vacancy documents, several central-government Assistant Engineer (Civil) posts are placed at 7th CPC Pay Matrix Level 7, whose basic-pay range is ₹44,900–₹1,42,400. This is a pay-matrix range, not a guaranteed take-home salary: monthly gross and net pay vary with admissible allowances, city/posting, deductions, deputation terms and future government pay revisions.

Classification also varies. The Central Water Commission example identifies a Group B Gazetted, Non-Ministerial post, and a MeitY recruitment-rule notification likewise lists Assistant Engineer (Civil) as Group B Gazetted, Non-Ministerial at Level 7. Candidates should use the specific advertisement or recruitment rules for the exact post to confirm pay level and status.
bullets: Treat ₹44,900–₹1,42,400 as cited Level-7 basic-pay context, not an in-hand-pay promise.
Confirm allowances, deductions, posting-related entitlements and deputation options in the department’s current notice.
Recheck pay details when applying because rules and allowances can change.

title: Assistant Engineer (State Government)
description: A state government engineering officer who designs, manages, and oversees public works projects and supervises Junior Engineers.

quick_facts.label: Role in the works hierarchy
quick_facts.value: In a Public Works Department example, an Assistant Engineer leads a task-force group in which Junior Engineers and other field staff work under the AE’s control.

quick_facts.label: Common direct-entry qualification
quick_facts.value: A bachelor’s degree in the relevant engineering discipline is a common direct-recruitment requirement. For example, Sikkim PSC’s Assistant Engineer (Civil) recruitment required a Civil Engineering degree from a recognised university.

quick_facts.label: Recruitment channel
quick_facts.value: State Public Service Commissions and state departments run selection processes for AE posts; Andhra Pradesh PSC published a selection notification for Assistant Engineer posts in various engineering subordinate services on 17 July 2026.

quick_facts.label: Technical scope
quick_facts.value: Official departmental role information associates engineering-office work with estimates, tenders, agreements, work execution and supervision, payments, budgets, and divisional correspondence; the exact allocation depends on the department and state.

quick_facts.label: Career movement
quick_facts.value: Promotion beyond AE is possible in state engineering services. West Bengal PWD issued an order promoting Assistant Engineers (Civil) to Executive Engineer in its engineering service.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: There is no single all-India AE pay scale. As a dated example, Goa’s 2026 advertisement for an Assistant Engineer in its Environment and Climate Change Department listed Pay Matrix Level 7; candidates must use the applicable state notification for current pay, allowances, and service conditions.

sections.heading: What an Assistant Engineer does
paragraphs: An Assistant Engineer is a supervisory engineering officer in a state department or state engineering service. Day-to-day responsibilities commonly combine technical and administrative control: preparing or checking estimates, handling tender and agreement work, supervising execution, monitoring payments and budgets, maintaining official correspondence, and coordinating field delivery. The precise powers—such as technical sanction, measurement, bill checking, or contract administration—are set by the concerned state’s departmental rules and delegation orders.

AEs also operate as a layer of field supervision. Puducherry PWD’s crisis-management arrangement places Junior Engineers, overseers, mechanics, and other field personnel under an Assistant Engineer-led task-force group, illustrating the role’s responsibility for directing staff and restoring public services during urgent works.
bullets: Translate approved public-works plans into estimates, procurement, work orders, and field execution.
Check technical and administrative documentation connected with works, agreements, payments, budgets, and records.
Supervise Junior Engineers and field staff, while reporting through the departmental engineering hierarchy.
Coordinate site responses and restoration work where the department assigns the AE operational control.

sections.heading: Entry routes and eligibility
paragraphs: Direct recruitment is commonly made through a State Public Service Commission or a state recruiting authority, but notifications are state-, department-, discipline-, category-, and vacancy-specific. Sikkim PSC’s direct recruitment notice for Assistant Engineer (Civil) required a Civil Engineering degree from a recognised university. Other AE streams can require the corresponding discipline, such as electrical, mechanical, environmental, or other specialised engineering qualifications.

Applicants should treat the current official notification as controlling. It sets the exact educational requirement, domicile or language conditions where applicable, age limits and relaxations, reservation rules, examination scheme, document verification, and appointment conditions. Andhra Pradesh PSC’s July 2026 publication of a selection notification for AE posts is an example of an official commission-led recruitment process.

Internal appointment or movement routes also vary. Goa’s 2026 deputation advertisement, for example, sought eligible officials in an equivalent or feeder pay level with specified service and a relevant Civil Engineering degree. This should not be read as a nationwide promotion rule.
bullets: Complete an engineering degree in the discipline specified by the recruiting state or department.
Apply through the official PSC or departmental recruitment notice and follow its examination and selection process.
For serving government employees, examine the applicable service rules and notification for promotion, transfer, or deputation eligibility rather than assuming a uniform route from Junior Engineer.

sections.heading: Skills that the role calls for
paragraphs: The work described in official departmental material makes technical design-and-estimation literacy, tender and agreement administration, construction/work supervision, budget awareness, and accurate technical correspondence central practical skills for an AE. Because the officer coordinates Junior Engineers and other field staff in departmental arrangements, supervision, task allocation, communication, and incident response are also important.

The specific technical toolkit depends on the posting. A civil AE in a roads, buildings, water-supply, irrigation, or rural-works office will use the standards, drawings, measurements, specifications, contracts, and quality-control processes relevant to that department; electrical and mechanical AE roles have parallel discipline-specific requirements.
bullets: Engineering estimation, drawings, specifications, and work planning.
Tender, agreement, payment, and budget documentation.
Site supervision, issue escalation, and coordination of field personnel.
Clear written communication and recordkeeping for divisional and departmental processes.

sections.heading: Where the job is performed
paragraphs: Assistant Engineers work in state-government engineering organisations rather than in one uniform national employer. Typical settings include Public Works, roads and highways, buildings, water supply, irrigation, rural works, municipal engineering, environment, and electricity-related departments or entities, depending on the state and engineering discipline.

The job normally combines office-based technical and administrative work with field supervision. In the Puducherry PWD example, AEs lead division-level task forces and coordinate Junior Engineers and other field personnel for emergency works. Departmental documents from Odisha likewise connect engineering-office functions with execution, supervision, estimates, tenders, agreements, payments, and budgets.
bullets: Division, subdivision, circle, project, or departmental office postings.
Construction, maintenance, utility, or public-infrastructure sites.
A mix of desk-based approvals and documentation with inspections and field coordination.

sections.heading: Progression after Assistant Engineer
paragraphs: Progression nomenclature differs across states and departments, but AE is commonly part of a wider engineering-service hierarchy. Official West Bengal PWD documentation records promotion of Assistant Engineers (Civil) to Executive Engineer, while Assam’s Irrigation Department records promotion from Assistant Engineer to Assistant Executive Engineer (Civil). These examples show why candidates should consult the service rules of their own cadre rather than assume one fixed national sequence.

The node’s connection to Junior Engineer reflects a common supervisory relationship: Puducherry PWD places Junior Engineers under an AE-led task force. However, whether a particular Junior Engineer can be promoted into AE, the qualifying service required, the quota between direct recruits and promotees, and seniority treatment are state-service-rule questions.
bullets: Build technical, supervisory, and departmental-process experience in the assigned engineering stream.
Track seniority, departmental examinations or training where prescribed, and vacancy-based promotion procedures.
Verify the applicable state service rules for the next designation, which may be Assistant Executive Engineer, Executive Engineer, or another state-specific equivalent.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: Compensation is set by the appointing state, department or service, pay-matrix level, appointment mode, and applicable allowance rules; it should not be represented as one nationwide AE salary. For a time-specific reference, Goa’s advertisement with an application window from 8 May 2026 to 22 June 2026 listed an Assistant Engineer post at Pay Matrix Level 7. That example is not a general benchmark for every state-government AE post.

Before applying, use the live official recruitment notice and the relevant state pay rules to confirm basic pay, probation or training pay where applicable, dearness allowance, house-rent allowance, location-related benefits, deductions, pension or NPS coverage, and contractual versus regular appointment status.
bullets: Compare only official notifications issued for the exact employer, discipline, and recruitment cycle.
Treat published pay levels and allowances as dated and variable across states.
Check whether the advertised post is regular, contractual, deputation-based, or another appointment type before comparing compensation.

title: Assistant Executive Engineer in Border Roads Engineering Service
description: A Group A engineering officer in the Border Roads Engineering Service responsible for strategically important road and infrastructure projects.

quick_facts.label: Service and entry post
quick_facts.value: Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) is the entry appointment in the Border Roads Engineering Service (BRES), Group ‘A’. In the 2026 Engineering Services Examination (ESE), UPSC listed AEE (Civil) in BRES under Civil Engineering and AEE (Electrical and Mechanical) in BRES for Mechanical Engineering posts.

quick_facts.label: Recruiting route
quick_facts.value: The direct entry route is UPSC’s Engineering Services Examination, with service allocation based on examination merit, candidate preferences, vacancies and medical fitness.

quick_facts.label: Initial appointment and training
quick_facts.value: Selected BRES officers are appointed as AEE on a two-year probation, report to GREF Centre, Pune for induction training as specified in the appointment letter, and may have to pass departmental physical and written tests and the Young Officers course.

quick_facts.label: Service liability
quick_facts.value: An officer is liable to serve anywhere in India or outside it, including field areas in peace and war; BRES officers in BRO are also subject to specified Army Act, 1950 and Army Rules, 1954 provisions for discipline because BRO is a uniformed force.

quick_facts.label: Pay-level context
quick_facts.value: The Engineering Services Examination Rules notified on September 26, 2025 place both AEE (Civil) and AEE (E&M) in BRES at Pay Matrix Level 10. Actual monthly pay is variable because applicable allowances depend on posting and prevailing government rules.

sections.heading: Role and responsibilities
paragraphs: The rules state that the Director General Border Roads (DGBR) specifies duties for posts across the establishments under DGBR, rather than publishing one fixed duty list for every AEE posting. In practice, the role sits within BRO’s strategic-infrastructure mission: the organisation constructs and maintains roads, bridges, tunnels, airfields and other infrastructure in difficult terrain to support the armed forces and border-area connectivity.

BRO’s official description makes clear why this is a field-oriented engineering service: its projects operate across border and remote regions, and it identifies work in high Himalayas, the North-East, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and other demanding locations. An AEE should therefore expect technical responsibility to be shaped by the assigned Civil or Electrical-and-Mechanical establishment, project and location rather than by a single uniform desk-job description.
bullets: Work scope is assigned by DGBR for the establishment concerned.
The service’s engineering context includes strategic roads and associated infrastructure such as bridges, tunnels and airfields.
Assignments can combine project-site conditions with the discipline and conduct requirements of a uniformed organisation.

sections.heading: How to enter through UPSC ESE
paragraphs: The standard direct route is the UPSC Engineering Services Examination. For the 2026 cycle, UPSC listed AEE (Civil) in BRES in the Civil Engineering category and AEE (Electrical and Mechanical) in BRES in the Mechanical Engineering category. Final service allocation is not automatic on passing: it depends on final merit, the candidate’s stated service preferences, available vacancies and medical fitness.

For the 2026 examination, UPSC required a recognised engineering degree or one of the alternative professional engineering qualifications specified in its notice. The selection structure was Preliminary/Stage I objective papers, Main/Stage II conventional engineering papers and a Personality Test. The 2026 preliminary application deadline of October 16, 2025 and examination date of February 8, 2026 are past; applicants should treat future eligibility, vacancies, dates and post availability as cycle-specific and verify them in the next UPSC notice.
bullets: Choose the relevant ESE discipline: Civil for AEE (Civil), or Mechanical for the listed AEE (Electrical and Mechanical) BRES posts.
Meet the notification’s nationality, age, education, medical-fitness and other conditions for that specific cycle.
Rank highly, state BRES appropriately in service preferences, and complete the post-selection medical and appointment process.

sections.heading: Skills and attributes to build
paragraphs: A prospective officer needs strong command of the relevant engineering discipline. UPSC’s ESE scheme tests General Studies and Engineering Aptitude alongside discipline-specific Civil or Mechanical engineering papers, with the technical-paper standard approximately at an Indian engineering-degree level.

The selection process also explicitly assesses leadership, initiative, intellectual curiosity, tact, social qualities, mental and physical energy, practical application and integrity. Those attributes are especially relevant to a service with induction training, departmental physical and written tests, and postings that can include field areas in war and peace.
bullets: Civil or Mechanical engineering fundamentals aligned to the applicable ESE paper.
Engineering analysis, numerical reasoning and practical problem-solving.
Leadership, initiative, communication and professional integrity.
Physical and mental readiness for the prescribed training and demanding field-service context.

sections.heading: Workplace and service conditions
paragraphs: BRES is part of the Border Roads Organisation ecosystem. BRO describes itself as a strategic construction organisation that supports the operational readiness and logistics of security forces while delivering connectivity infrastructure. Its official account says it works through projects across 11 states, three Union Territories and Bhutan, with work in some of India’s most challenging terrain.

The employment setting is not limited to a conventional office location. The governing ESE rules make selected BRES officers liable for service in any part of India or outside, including field areas in war and peace, and provide for discipline-related application of specified Army Act and Army Rules provisions. The precise establishment, location and duties are determined by DGBR.
bullets: Possible work environments include project and field establishments as well as organisational headquarters functions.
Remote, high-altitude and otherwise difficult-terrain conditions are a central feature of BRO’s operating context.
Postings and allowances should be evaluated case by case because they depend on the assigned area and applicable rules.

sections.heading: Career progression
paragraphs: The 2025-notified ESE rules describe a defined BRES Group ‘A’ ladder. In the Civil cadre, the progression named is AEE, Executive Engineer, Superintending Engineer, Chief Engineer and Additional DGBR. In the Electrical-and-Mechanical cadre, the named ladder is AEE, Executive Engineer, Superintending Engineer and Chief Engineer.

Promotion is conditional rather than time-guaranteed: the rules say officers may progress after meeting prescribed conditions, and promotion remains subject to vacancies in the higher grade. This means career timelines can vary by cadre strength, eligibility, performance-related requirements and vacancy availability.
bullets: Civil: AEE → Executive Engineer → Superintending Engineer → Chief Engineer → Additional DGBR.
E&M: AEE → Executive Engineer → Superintending Engineer → Chief Engineer.
Two-year probation includes induction and departmental training requirements before regular career development continues.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: As of the Engineering Services Examination Rules notified on September 26, 2025, the entry AEE post in both the Civil and E&M BRES cadres is at Pay Matrix Level 10. This is a pay-level reference, not a guarantee of a particular in-hand monthly amount.

The same rules state that officers posted in specified areas may receive special compensatory allowance and special duty allowance at prescribed rates, as well as free rations or an allowance in lieu of rations; HRA and other Central Government allowances may also apply, along with outfit allowance. Amounts, eligibility and take-home pay are variable and should be checked against the rules and orders in force for the eventual posting date and location.
bullets: Entry pay context: Pay Matrix Level 10 under the September 26, 2025 ESE rules.
Posting-linked benefits may include special compensatory and special duty allowances, rations or ration allowance, HRA and outfit allowance.
Do not rely on a static online salary figure: allowances and government pay rules can change.

title: Assistant Executive Engineer in Central Engineering Service
description: A Group A engineering officer in the Central Engineering Service, commonly posted in central public works and infrastructure organisations.

quick_facts.label: Service and cadre context
quick_facts.value: Central Engineering Service (CES) is listed as a Group A Civil Engineering service in the UPSC Engineering Services Examination (ESE) 2026 notice; that notice identifies the Central Public Works Department (CPWD) as the department for CES Group A.

quick_facts.label: Usual entry grade
quick_facts.value: CPWD’s published manual states that initial recruitment to its Group A engineering services in the civil, electrical and mechanical streams is made at the Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) level through a UPSC competitive examination.

quick_facts.label: Primary entry route
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, UPSC included Central Engineering Service among the Civil Engineering Group A services recruited through the Engineering Services Examination; final allocation depends on examination rank, stated service preferences, vacancies and medical fitness.

quick_facts.label: Educational baseline
quick_facts.value: The ESE 2026 notice requires an eligible engineering qualification, including a degree in Engineering from specified recognised Indian institutions or other listed equivalent routes; the CES vacancy is in the Civil Engineering category.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
paragraphs: In CPWD’s operating model, an Assistant Executive Engineer may lead a sub-divisional field unit for supervision and execution of works against approved designs, drawings and estimates. The role is tied to delivery targets, quality, economy and maintenance of buildings, structures, areas and equipment under charge.

The published CPWD manual also assigns the Assistant Engineer/Assistant Executive Engineer responsibility for work and stores accounts, maintaining stores records and periodically inspecting assets for condition and safety. Exact delegated powers and the mix of construction, maintenance and office work can vary by posting and discipline.
bullets: Supervise execution of public works to approved technical documents and departmental standards.
Coordinate and oversee Junior Engineers working in the sub-division.
Maintain work/stores accounts and inspect assets under charge, including safety-related condition checks.

sections.heading: Entry through UPSC Engineering Services Examination
paragraphs: The principal route is selection through UPSC’s Engineering Services Examination (ESE/IES), followed by service allocation. In the ESE 2026 notice, Central Engineering Service appears under the Civil Engineering Group A services. Candidates are allocated according to final merit, their service preferences, available vacancies and medical fitness.

For the 2026 examination cycle, UPSC specified a three-stage process: Preliminary (objective papers), Main (two conventional engineering papers), and a Personality Test. The 2026 notice set the general age band at 21 to under 30 years on January 1, 2026, with specified relaxations; eligibility, vacancies, age cut-offs and application dates are cycle-specific and must be checked in the applicable notice.
bullets: Obtain an eligible engineering qualification; CES is offered in ESE’s Civil Engineering category.
Apply for the relevant ESE cycle and clear Preliminary, Main and Personality Test stages.
Rank high enough for CES after submitting service preferences; allocation is not guaranteed merely by qualifying the examination.

sections.heading: Skills and capabilities
paragraphs: Core capability is civil-engineering judgement applied to drawings, estimates, construction supervision, maintenance and inspection. Because the CPWD field role also covers quality, economy, work accounts and stores accounts, officers need organised documentation, cost awareness, contractor- and site-facing coordination, and attention to safety.

UPSC’s ESE framework also explicitly tests or assesses engineering aptitude, standards and quality practices, project-management basics, information-and-communication-technology tools, engineering ethics, and leadership, initiative, practical application and integrity. These are useful preparation priorities as well as relevant professional capabilities for an AEE.
bullets: Civil engineering design, construction and maintenance fundamentals.
Reading and applying drawings, estimates, specifications and standards.
Project, quality, cost, accounts and stores-record discipline.
Leadership, communication, judgement, integrity and practical problem-solving.

sections.heading: Workplace and posting environment
paragraphs: CES Group A is administered in the CPWD context. CPWD reports that it has organised Group A services including Central Engineering Service (Civil), under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. Its field structure includes regions, zones, circles, divisions and sub-divisions; divisions are headed by Executive Engineers and sub-divisions by Assistant Engineers. An AEE assignment can therefore combine field-site supervision with sub-divisional administrative and technical work.

Posting location, project type and field exposure depend on the cadre-controlling department and the specific assignment. The UPSC ESE 2026 notice identifies CPWD as the department associated with CES Group A.
bullets: Potential setting: CPWD field formations and their project or maintenance assignments.
Work commonly spans office documentation, site inspection, execution monitoring and coordination with engineers, contractors and client departments.
The service is national in character; do not assume a particular city or project portfolio before allocation and posting orders.

title: Assistant Executive Engineer in Central Water Engineering Service
description: A Group A engineer in the Central Water Engineering Service working on national water-resources, irrigation, flood-control, and hydrology projects.

quick_facts.label: Service and entry grade
quick_facts.value: CWES is a Central Government Group A engineering service. A September 19, 2024 Ministry of Jal Shakti appointment offer for ESE-2023 allocatees describes the entry appointment as Assistant Director/Assistant Executive Engineer in the Junior Time Scale (JTS) of Central Water Engineering (Group A) Service.

quick_facts.label: Primary recruitment route
quick_facts.value: Direct recruits are allocated to CWES through the UPSC Engineering Services Examination (ESE); CWES appears under both the Civil Engineering and Mechanical Engineering categories in UPSC’s ESE notice.

quick_facts.label: Professional remit
quick_facts.value: The Central Water Commission’s functional domains include appraisal of water-resources projects, civil and structural design, hydrology, flood forecasting and observations, river management, project monitoring, and survey and investigation work.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: A Ministry of Jal Shakti appointment offer dated September 19, 2024 states that JTS Assistant Director/Assistant Executive Engineer appointees would have pay fixed at Pay Matrix Level 10, ₹56,100–₹1,77,500 per month, plus admissible Central Government allowances. This is dated appointment context, not a guarantee of current take-home pay.

quick_facts.label: Initial service conditions
quick_facts.value: The same 2024 offer specifies a two-year probation from assumption of charge in JTS, subject to extension if necessary, and an all-India service liability.

sections.heading: Engineering work across national water-resources functions
paragraphs: An Assistant Executive Engineer in CWES enters the Central Water Commission (CWC) at Junior Time Scale and can be deployed within the organisation’s water-resources functions. CWC identifies these functions as appraisal of preliminary and detailed project reports for major inter-state proposals; basin planning; civil and structural design, consultancy and appraisal; hydrological appraisal; flood monitoring and forecasting; river-management data work; surveys and investigations for DPRs; and monitoring of water-resources projects.

At the project-appraisal end of this work, CWC examines irrigation and multipurpose proposals through a multidisciplinary process that covers such matters as water availability, engineering design, construction materials and soil investigations, costs and benefits, and inter-state issues. This makes the role a public-sector engineering and technical-advisory career rather than a single-site construction-only post.
bullets: Support technical examination, design, appraisal, monitoring, data, or field-investigation work according to the directorate or regional posting.
Contribute to water-resources projects involving irrigation, flood management, multipurpose schemes, dams, hydrology, river systems, and related infrastructure.
Work with state governments and other central technical agencies in CWC’s coordination and appraisal processes.

sections.heading: Entry through the UPSC Engineering Services Examination
paragraphs: The normal direct-recruitment route is the UPSC Engineering Services Examination (ESE/IES), followed by allocation to CWES based on examination rank and the candidate’s service preferences. UPSC’s ESE notice lists Central Water Engineering (Group A) Service within both Civil Engineering and Mechanical Engineering service categories; the relevant annual notification and vacancy position control a particular recruitment cycle.

For the ESE notice used as a reference, UPSC requires an eligible engineering qualification, including an engineering degree from a qualifying Indian institution or other specified recognised qualifications. The selection structure is Preliminary (objective) examination, Main (conventional engineering papers), and a Personality Test. Candidates who are finally recommended must also undergo the prescribed medical examination. Eligibility, discipline coverage, age rules, reservation, vacancies, and dates should always be checked in the current UPSC notification rather than inferred from an earlier cycle.
bullets: Build eligibility around an engineering qualification recognised under the applicable UPSC ESE rules.
Choose the applicable Civil or Mechanical Engineering discipline and place CWES appropriately in service preferences when the applicable ESE process permits preferences.
Prepare for all three ESE stages: Preliminary, Main, and Personality Test; final allocation depends on merit rank and preferences.

sections.heading: Technical breadth for water-resources engineering
paragraphs: CWC’s own National Water Academy courseware indicates the technical areas relevant to its water-resources work: preparation of detailed project reports, construction-material surveys, environmental aspects of DPRs, hydrological aspects, project monitoring using geospatial web services, appraisal of irrigation/flood-management/multipurpose projects, cost estimation, economic evaluation, and water-resources information systems.

Accordingly, useful capabilities include sound civil or mechanical engineering fundamentals, hydrology and water-resources literacy, technical drawing/design or hydro-mechanical understanding as applicable, quantitative analysis, careful review of project documentation, and the ability to communicate technical findings in a multi-agency government setting. These are role-relevant competencies inferred from CWC’s published functions and training topics, not a separate statutory skills checklist.
bullets: Hydrology, flood and irrigation-project concepts.
DPR review, project appraisal, cost and economic evaluation.
Engineering design, surveys/investigations, data interpretation, and technical documentation.
Coordination with multidisciplinary teams, state agencies, and Central Government bodies.

sections.heading: Central Government postings with headquarters, regional, and field-facing work
paragraphs: CWES officers work in the Central Water Commission and may be associated with headquarters, regional, basin, project-appraisal, design, monitoring, hydrology, or information-system functions. CWC’s published functional structure includes both central technical functions and regional-office activity, while its headquarters contact location is Sewa Bhawan, R.K. Puram, New Delhi.

The 2024 CWES appointment offer carries liability to serve anywhere in India or outside India, as well as in specified defence-related service or posts under the stated conditions. In practice, location and day-to-day work therefore vary substantially with cadre posting and assignment: desk-based appraisal/design/data roles can sit alongside site visits, hydrological observation, project monitoring, and coordination with state project authorities.
bullets: Potential postings include New Delhi headquarters and CWC regional or basin organisations.
Assignments may combine technical-office work with project, monitoring, survey, or field coordination.
Posting mobility is an explicit condition of appointment.

sections.heading: Progression from Junior Time Scale through senior technical and management grades
paragraphs: The entry appointment is in Junior Time Scale. A CWC publication describing CWES career progression states that, under the recruitment rules prevalent at the time of publication, officers were expected to complete at least four years at JTS and nine years at Senior Time Scale before promotion to Junior Administrative Grade. It also describes early-career work as developing competencies through policy and planning, basin studies, hydrological observation, design, and construction-related engagements.

Actual promotions, grade designations, vacancy availability, performance requirements, training, and applicable service rules can change. Candidates should treat the published time periods as historical service-framework context and verify the current CWES rules and departmental orders after joining.
bullets: Entry: Assistant Director/Assistant Executive Engineer, Junior Time Scale.
Later progression is governed by CWES recruitment/service rules and departmental promotion processes.
Early postings can develop breadth across planning, basin studies, hydrology, design, and construction-related functions.

sections.heading: Level 10 basic-pay framework; allowances and net pay vary
paragraphs: For dated, official context, the Ministry of Jal Shakti’s September 19, 2024 offer to ESE-2023 CWES appointees fixed entry JTS pay at Level 10 of the Central Government pay matrix: ₹56,100–₹1,77,500 per month, with allowances admissible to Central Government officers of that grade. The offer also states that appointees are covered by the Defined Contribution Pension Scheme and the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme, subject to the applicable rules.

This figure is the basic-pay matrix range stated in that offer—not a current monthly in-hand salary estimate. Dearness allowance, house-rent allowance, transport allowance, deductions, place of posting, and subsequent Central Government pay decisions can materially change gross and take-home amounts. Use the current Department of Expenditure orders and the appointment terms applicable to the relevant batch for an up-to-date calculation.
bullets: Official dated entry-pay reference: Level 10, ₹56,100–₹1,77,500 basic-pay matrix range in the September 19, 2024 CWES offer.
Allowances are governed by Central Government rules and can vary over time and by posting.
The appointment offer refers to the Defined Contribution Pension Scheme and Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme.

title: Assistant Executive Engineer in Indian Defence Service of Engineers
description: A Group A engineering officer in the Indian Defence Service of Engineers responsible for military works and infrastructure under the Ministry of Defence.

quick_facts.label: Cadre and employing organisation
quick_facts.value: Indian Defence Service of Engineers (IDSE) is a Group A service within Military Engineer Services (MES), under the Ministry of Defence; UPSC’s Engineering Services notice lists IDSE Group A under MES.

quick_facts.label: Engineering streams
quick_facts.value: UPSC has listed IDSE appointments through the Engineering Services Examination in Civil, Mechanical and Electrical Engineering categories.

quick_facts.label: Core selection route
quick_facts.value: The usual direct-entry route is UPSC’s Engineering Services Examination (ESE), followed by allocation according to final merit, candidate preferences, vacancies and medical fitness.

quick_facts.label: Entry pay context
quick_facts.value: The ESE 2026 Rules’ service particulars list Assistant Executive Engineer in the IDSE cadre at 7th CPC Pay Level 10, with basic-pay range ₹56,100–₹1,77,500. This is basic-pay context from the notified rules, not a guaranteed in-hand salary.

quick_facts.label: Probation and induction
quick_facts.value: The ESE 2026 Rules state that selected IDSE/MES officers are appointed on two years’ probation and require a mandatory 40-week induction training course during probation.

sections.heading: Responsibilities in defence infrastructure delivery
paragraphs: An Assistant Executive Engineer in IDSE works within the MES ecosystem that provides rear-line engineering support to the Army, Navy, Air Force, Coast Guard and associated defence organisations. The work covers the delivery and upkeep of defence infrastructure rather than combat-engineering duties.

MES’s documented infrastructure remit includes residential and office buildings, hospitals, roads, runways, docks and harbours, including projects in border areas. Its work also involves facilities and asset maintenance; the organisation uses contractors and consultants for works and services, so project supervision, coordination, contract administration and technical oversight are central practical dimensions of the role.

The role also operates in a public-infrastructure context where safety, sustainability and modern project-management methods matter. In an address to MES probationers, the President of India specifically highlighted renewable energy, green-building practices, energy conservation and use of modern project-management tools as relevant to MES officers’ work.
bullets: Plan, supervise and help deliver construction, maintenance and infrastructure-service work for defence establishments.
Coordinate with contractors, consultants, technical staff and defence users in accordance with MES procedures.
Support the lifecycle maintenance and serviceability of facilities and assets, potentially in remote or difficult terrain.
Apply discipline-specific engineering knowledge in civil, mechanical or electrical works, depending on the allotted IDSE stream.

sections.heading: Entry through UPSC Engineering Services Examination
paragraphs: The direct route is the UPSC Engineering Services Examination (ESE/IES). In the UPSC notice, IDSE is included among the Group A services/posts available in Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering and Electrical Engineering categories. Selection for a particular service is not automatic merely by writing ESE: final allocation depends on examination rank, the candidate’s service preference, available vacancies and medical fitness.

The ESE selection structure described by UPSC has three stages: an objective Preliminary examination, discipline-specific conventional Main examination papers, and a Personality Test. Marks from all three stages determine final ranking. UPSC’s stated assessment for the Personality Test includes leadership, initiative, intellectual curiosity, practical application, social qualities, mental and physical energy, and integrity.

For the referenced ESE notice, accepted educational routes include an engineering degree from an eligible Indian institution, with certain specified professional/recognised equivalent qualifications also accepted. Candidates should always use the notice for their own examination year because eligibility, vacancies, dates, medical standards and service particulars can change.
After selection, the ESE 2026 Rules state that IDSE/MES entrants undergo two years’ probation, including a mandatory 40-week induction course; departmental and language tests may also be required.
bullets: Choose the applicable ESE engineering category: Civil, Mechanical or Electrical for IDSE opportunities listed in the notice.
Meet the educational, age, nationality, medical and other conditions in the ESE notice for the relevant year.
Clear Preliminary, Main and Personality Test, then state service preferences when UPSC calls for them.
Complete probation and prescribed induction/training requirements after appointment.

sections.heading: Skills and professional capabilities
paragraphs: The role calls for strong applied engineering capability in the allotted discipline—civil, mechanical or electrical—because IDSE officers are recruited through discipline-specific ESE categories and MES delivers both construction and maintenance work across a broad range of defence facilities.

Project execution and contract-management capability are particularly relevant. MES states that it engages contractors and consultants to provide works and services, while its official arbitration platform exists to monitor disputes arising from works and supply contracts. This makes careful documentation, specification interpretation, vendor coordination, quality oversight and risk management practically important.

Leadership, initiative, integrity, practical application, communication and adaptability are also directly aligned with UPSC’s stated Personality Test criteria. Officers should be prepared for multidisciplinary infrastructure work, evolving construction technologies and sustainability expectations.
bullets: Discipline-specific design, construction, maintenance and troubleshooting knowledge.
Project planning, estimation, execution monitoring, quality and safety management.
Contractor/consultant coordination and clear technical documentation.
Leadership, integrity, practical judgment and communication.
Awareness of sustainable construction, energy conservation and digital/project-management tools.

sections.heading: Workplace and posting context
paragraphs: MES is a nationwide defence-infrastructure organisation. Its official material describes construction and maintenance work for the Army, Air Force, Navy, Coast Guard and other government agencies, including projects such as buildings, hospitals, roads, runways, docks and harbours across the country and in border areas.

Accordingly, an IDSE Assistant Executive Engineer can expect a mix of office-based planning, procurement/contract and coordination activity with field/site responsibilities. The ESE 2026 Rules also place selected IDSE/MES personnel under the Civilian in Defence Service (Field Liability) Rules and require medical examination under the applicable standards.
This is a civilian Group A engineering role in a defence organisation. It should not be confused with a commissioned combat-engineering appointment in the Indian Armed Forces.
bullets: Potential postings span defence establishments and MES project locations across India, including border-area infrastructure.
Work commonly combines technical administration, site inspection/supervision, stakeholder coordination and asset-maintenance responsibilities.
Field-liability and medical requirements apply as specified in the relevant rules and appointment process.

sections.heading: Indicative IDSE cadre progression
paragraphs: The ESE 2026 Rules list the following IDSE pay-grade sequence: Assistant Executive Engineer (Level 10), Executive Engineer (Level 11), Executive Engineer (NFSG, Level 12), Superintending Engineer (Level 13), Chief Engineer (Level 14), and Additional Director General and Director General (both Level 15 in the listed particulars). This identifies the cadre’s grade structure, not an assured time-bound promotion schedule.

Actual advancement depends on the applicable service rules, vacancies, performance, eligibility, seniority and government promotion procedures. Candidates should not treat the grade sequence as a promise of promotion by a particular date.
bullets: Assistant Executive Engineer — Level 10 entry grade.
Executive Engineer and Executive Engineer (NFSG) — Levels 11 and 12.
Superintending Engineer and Chief Engineer — Levels 13 and 14.
Additional Director General and Director General — Level 15 in the ESE 2026 service particulars.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: For the ESE 2026 service particulars published in the Gazette, the IDSE Assistant Executive Engineer basic-pay range is ₹56,100–₹1,77,500 at 7th CPC Level 10. This is a pay-matrix range rather than a statement of monthly take-home pay.

The same rules note that dearness allowance for newly recruited Group A MES probationers is governed by Ministry of Defence directives. Total compensation can therefore vary with basic-pay cell, dearness allowance, posting-related entitlements, deductions and changes to central-government pay or allowance rules. Prospective candidates should consult the ESE notice and appointment documents applicable to their own recruitment year.
bullets: Notified ESE 2026 entry basic-pay context: Level 10, ₹56,100–₹1,77,500.
In-hand pay is variable and should not be inferred from the basic-pay range alone.
Allowances and conditions may change through government orders and posting circumstances.
