title: Assistant Loco Pilot (Indian Railways)
description: An entry-level position in the Indian Railways responsible for assisting the train driver (loco pilot) in train operations.

quick_facts.label: Recruiting authority and current notice
quick_facts.value: Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) is recruited through Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs). CEN 01/2026 was the current cited recruitment notice; its online application window ran from 15 May 2026 to 14 June 2026, so those dates are past as of this review.

quick_facts.label: Qualification routes
quick_facts.value: For CEN 01/2026, the minimum technical qualification was Matriculation/SSLC plus an eligible NCVT/SCVT ITI trade, or Course Completed Act Apprenticeship in those trades, or a three-year diploma (or accepted degree) in Mechanical, Electrical, Electronics, Automobile Engineering, or a permitted combination of those disciplines.

quick_facts.label: Medical standard
quick_facts.value: The CEN 01/2026 post parameter specified the stringent A-1 medical standard. The notice states unaided 6/6 distant vision in each eye, specified near-vision and colour/binocular/field/night/mesopic-vision tests; it also states that LASIK or other refractive-error corrective surgery is not eligible for ALP under that notice.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: The CEN 01/2026 process comprises CBT-1, CBT-2, Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT), document verification, and medical examination. CBT-1 is a screening stage and its marks do not count toward the final panel.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: For CEN 01/2026, ALP was listed at 7th CPC Pay Level 2 with initial basic pay of ₹19,900. This is recruitment-notice basic-pay context, not a statement of take-home pay; actual earnings and allowances vary with applicable rules and assignment.

sections.heading: What an Assistant Loco Pilot does
paragraphs: An ALP is part of the locomotive crew and supports the Loco Pilot in safety-critical train operation. Indian Railways’ safe-working material directs the ALP to check required registers and locomotive condition when taking charge, assist with locomotive preparation, verify safety equipment, and review the locomotive logbook.

During a run, the ALP calls out and points out signal aspects, speed restrictions and warning boards; keeps watch ahead, on adjacent lines and overhead equipment; and looks back for abnormalities in the train. General Rules material also requires ALPs to maintain a good lookout when not otherwise engaged, pay immediate attention to signals, and assist the Loco Pilot in exchanging signals. The Loco Pilot retains responsibility for observing and complying with signals.
bullets: Pre-departure and handover work: inspect visible locomotive equipment and safety items, consult records/logbooks, and communicate the condition of the locomotive/train at crew change.
In-motion safety support: signal calling, restriction-board awareness, observation for obstructions or abnormalities, and frequent rearward observation where possible.
Operational discipline: work under the lawful directions of the Loco Pilot while carrying out assigned crew duties.

sections.heading: Entering through RRB ALP recruitment
paragraphs: The principal external entry route is an ALP recruitment notice issued by the RRBs. In CEN 01/2026, applicants needed the prescribed technical qualification by the application closing date; candidates awaiting final results were not eligible. Candidates could submit one online application to one RRB and then state preferences among the eligible zonal railways/posts within that RRB.

The 2026 notice recognised several education pathways: Matriculation/SSLC plus a listed NCVT/SCVT ITI trade; Matriculation/SSLC plus Course Completed Act Apprenticeship in a listed trade; or Matriculation/SSLC plus a three-year diploma in Mechanical, Electrical, Electronics or Automobile Engineering (including allowed combinations). An engineering degree in those disciplines was accepted in lieu of the diploma.

The selection sequence in CEN 01/2026 was CBT-1, CBT-2, CBAT, document verification and medical examination. Passing the A-1 medical standard is essential: the notice says candidates found medically unsuitable for ALP will not receive an alternative appointment under that recruitment.
bullets: Check the exact CEN and any corrigenda for the recruitment cycle being applied to; vacancies and terms can change.

Treat medical eligibility as an early decision point, not merely a final formality: the cited 2026 notice imposed unaided-vision and other A-1 requirements and excluded refractive corrective surgery for ALP.
Complete prescribed initial training after selection; the CEN states that selected ALPs undergo training where prescribed and receive a stipend during that training period.

sections.heading: Skills and readiness developed for the role
paragraphs: The operating duties point to a combination of technical locomotive familiarity, sustained situational awareness, careful adherence to safety rules, and precise crew communication. Signal identification and call-outs, speed-restriction awareness, observation of the train and track environment, and systematic pre-departure checks are not optional soft skills: they are embedded in the safe-working instructions for ALPs.

Route knowledge is also operationally important. The General Rules material says locomotive crew must acquaint themselves with the working system, signal locations and local conditions for a section; it describes road-learning trips before working a section, including additional requirements for automatic-signalling territory and ghat sections.
bullets: Technical checking: understand locomotive condition, braking and visible mechanical/electrical equipment sufficiently to assist preparation and report defects.
Safety vigilance: continuously observe signals, restrictions, the route, the adjacent line and the train’s condition.
Clear communication: accurately call signals and indicators, exchange information during handover, and coordinate with the Loco Pilot.
Concentration and rule compliance: maintain alertness across running duties and apply the prescribed operating procedure consistently.

sections.heading: Work setting and posting context
paragraphs: ALPs work in the locomotive crew environment: locomotives, sheds, yards/pooling points and train-running sections. The safety-training material covers duties while taking charge, taking a locomotive out of a shed, checks at yards/pooling points, and duties while on the run—indicating a field-based operational role rather than a desk-based job.

Posting is tied closely to the railway/production unit selected through the recruitment process. CEN 01/2026 says a newly appointed railway servant is ordinarily employed throughout service on the zonal railway or production unit of first appointment, although the competent authority may transfer staff where service needs require it. It also cautions that a transfer request to another railway is ordinarily not registered until at least five to ten years of service are completed.
bullets: Expect safety-critical work on locomotives and across running, yard and shed contexts.
Choose the RRB and railway-zone preferences carefully because the cited recruitment notice links first appointment to that railway/production unit.
Work can require route learning and familiarity with local signalling and operating conditions before a crew member works a section.

sections.heading: Progression from ALP
paragraphs: ALP is part of the loco running cadre and can lead toward Loco Pilot roles through departmental progression, subject to the applicable railway rules, vacancies, suitability requirements, training and prescribed experience. An official Northeast Frontier Railway avenue-of-chart document shows ALP in the cadre path and lists Loco Pilot (Goods), Loco Pilot (Passenger) and Loco Pilot (Mail) among subsequent running-cadre roles.

That document notes that promotion to the relevant Level-6 posts involves seniority-cum-suitability with the prescribed benchmark, footplate experience, aptitude testing where prescribed, and pre-promotional training/written testing. It also describes a contingency route in which eligible ALPs with two years of service and 60,000 km footplate experience may be considered for Loco Pilot (Goods), subject to conditions and General Manager approval if the normal eligible staff are unavailable. This should not be read as a guaranteed or universal promotion timeline.
bullets: Near-term development can include gaining footplate experience, completing prescribed training, and meeting departmental suitability/aptitude requirements.

A commonly identified operational progression destination is Loco Pilot (Goods), followed in the avenue-of-chart by passenger/mail loco-pilot roles; the actual sequence is governed by the applicable railway’s rules and vacancies.
Technical education such as an eligible engineering diploma may support broader career options, but it does not by itself replace departmental promotion conditions for running-cadre advancement.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: In the CEN 01/2026 recruitment notice, Assistant Loco Pilot was placed in 7th CPC Pay Level 2 with initial pay of ₹19,900. This is a dated basic-pay figure from that notice, not a complete salary estimate or a guarantee for future recruitment cycles.

Candidates should distinguish basic pay from total monthly compensation. The cited notice does not state a universal take-home amount, and vacancies themselves are described as provisional and subject to increase, decrease or cancellation based on railway-administration requirements. For current pay and allowance treatment, rely on the latest applicable Railway Board orders and the specific appointment terms.
bullets: Dated reference point: ₹19,900 initial basic pay at Pay Level 2 in CEN 01/2026.
Avoid treating recruitment-cycle pay figures as permanent salary quotes; check the CEN and appointment documents applicable to the specific cycle and railway.
During prescribed initial training, the 2026 notice states that only a stipend is paid.

title: Assistant Section Officer in Central Secretariat Service (CSS)
description: A Group B non-gazetted post in various central government ministries, responsible for administrative and policy-related work.

quick_facts.label: Service and status
quick_facts.value: Assistant Section Officer (ASO) in the Central Secretariat Service is listed by the Staff Selection Commission (SSC) as a Group B post; SSC’s departmental ASO notice expressly describes the CSS ASO grade as Group B, non-gazetted.

quick_facts.label: Principal open-market entry route
quick_facts.value: The principal external recruitment route is the SSC Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination. DoPT’s CSS recruitment information states that direct induction into CSS is at the Assistant level through SSC’s graduate-level examination.

quick_facts.label: Education requirement for CGL route
quick_facts.value: In SSC’s CGL notice with qualifications assessed as of August 1, 2026, ASO CSS falls within “all other posts,” for which the essential qualification is a bachelor’s degree from a recognized university or equivalent.

quick_facts.label: Departmental route context
quick_facts.value: For the Assistant Section Officer/Assistant Grade LDCE recruitment year 2025, SSC stated that a CSS candidate had to be an Upper Division Grade officer in the Central Secretariat Clerical Service with at least six years of approved service as of July 1, 2025. This is an internal, cycle-specific route rather than an open application route.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: The CSS ASO grade is Pay Level 7. SSC’s CGL notice lists the Level 7 pay range as ₹44,900–₹1,42,400; actual monthly take-home pay varies with the applicable pay-matrix stage, allowances, deductions, posting, and rules in force.

quick_facts.label: Career ladder
quick_facts.value: DoPT identifies the CSS grade sequence as Assistant Section Officer, Section Officer, Grade I (Under Secretary), Selection Grade (Deputy Secretary), and Senior Selection Grade (Director). Advancement is governed by applicable service rules, vacancies, eligibility, and selection processes; it is not automatic merely by completing a stated number of years.

sections.heading: What an ASO in CSS does
paragraphs: The role is a secretariat administrative post centered on handling official cases and communications. The Institute of Secretariat Training & Management (ISTM), a DoPT institute, runs a course specifically for CSS ASOs and Section Officers whose objectives include applying a functional approach to noting and drafting effective official communications. SSC’s departmental ASO examination syllabus likewise tests the Central Secretariat Manual of Office Procedure, Allocation and Transaction of Business Rules, parliamentary procedures, and noting and drafting.

In practice, this points to work such as examining and putting up files, preparing notes and drafts, processing correspondence and proposals under office procedure, and supporting the Section Officer and higher officers with documented administrative decision-making. The precise portfolio depends on the ministry, department, section, and subject allocation.
bullets: Prepare clear file notes and draft official communications.
Apply Central Secretariat office procedure and government business rules to cases.
Track and process section work involving interdepartmental correspondence, parliamentary matters, and administrative proposals.
Maintain strong written communication and file-handling discipline in a rules-based environment.

sections.heading: How to enter the CSS ASO grade
paragraphs: For graduates entering from outside central government service, the route is SSC CGL. SSC’s CGL notice lists ASO, Central Secretariat Service under Pay Level 7 and a 20–30 age band for that notice; it also specifies a bachelor’s degree for posts in the general “all other posts” category. The same notice sets higher qualifying standards in the Computer Knowledge Test and Data Entry Speed Test for ASO CSS than for posts without prescribed computer proficiency. Candidates should always use the notice for the specific CGL cycle because vacancies, dates, age cut-offs, relaxations, and selection procedures can change.

There is also a limited departmental competitive examination (LDCE) route for eligible serving staff. In the SSC notice for the ASO/Assistant Grade LDCE recruitment year 2025, CSS eligibility was confined to officers in the Upper Division Grade of the Central Secretariat Clerical Service who had completed at least six years of approved service as of July 1, 2025. That notice used a computer-based examination plus evaluation of service records (APARs), so it should not be treated as a route available to fresh graduates.
bullets: External route: apply through the relevant SSC CGL notification, meet that cycle’s eligibility rules, and give CSS ASO the appropriate post preference where available.
Internal route: eligible CSCS Upper Division Grade staff may compete through the notified ASO/Assistant Grade LDCE, subject to the cycle’s service and other conditions.
Check the official notice rather than relying on coaching-site summaries: SSC post lists, vacancies, age rules, and cut-offs are cycle-specific.

sections.heading: Skills to build
paragraphs: Written analytical communication is central: ISTM’s ASO-focused noting-and-drafting training expects participants to apply a functional approach to noting and to produce appropriate, effective communications for a given situation. Knowledge of the Central Secretariat Manual of Office Procedure, government business rules, parliamentary procedures, and service rules is also directly reflected in SSC’s departmental ASO syllabus.

Digital competence matters at entry. In its CGL notice, SSC names ASO CSS among posts for which higher qualifying standards are set in the Computer Knowledge Test and Data Entry Speed Test. Prospective candidates should therefore build accurate keyboarding, office-software, document-formatting, and information-handling habits alongside examination preparation.
bullets: Concise note writing, drafting, and comprehension in official English/Hindi contexts.
Careful reading of rules, instructions, precedents, and case records.
Computer knowledge and accurate data entry.
Organization, confidentiality, version control, and deadline management.

sections.heading: Work setting and employer structure
paragraphs: ASOs belong to the Central Secretariat Service, whose cadre-controlling authority is DoPT. DoPT’s CSS material describes CSS cadre management across ministries and departments, and notes that ASO and Section Officer grade administration is partly centralized: functions including promotion DPCs, deputation clearances, resignations, voluntary retirement, and disciplinary matters for these grades are handled by the relevant ministries or departments (cadre units), while specified cadre functions are handled centrally by DoPT.

This is therefore primarily office-based central-government secretariat work, with the operational subject matter varying by the ministry or department to which the officer is posted. The current ISTM training calendar also provides a 10-week foundational training programme for direct-recruit CSS ASOs, indicating a structured induction component for new recruits.
bullets: Employer framework: Government of India, CSS, with DoPT as cadre-controlling authority.
Day-to-day administrative home: the ministry or department/cadre unit of posting.
Work content: section-based secretariat administration rather than a single specialized technical discipline.
Induction: direct-recruit ASOs are scheduled for CSS foundational training through ISTM.

sections.heading: Progression within CSS
paragraphs: DoPT’s CSS annual-report material places ASO at the entry grade of a defined service ladder: Assistant Section Officer; Section Officer; Grade I (Under Secretary); Selection Grade (Deputy Secretary); and Senior Selection Grade (Director). It lists Section Officer as Group B gazetted and the Under Secretary grade and above as Group A gazetted in the reported structure.

Progression to Section Officer is a formal personnel process, not a guaranteed time-bound outcome. For example, DoPT’s 2022 order included CSS ASOs in a Section Officers’ select list only after they were found fit by Departmental Promotion Committees and clear from the vigilance angle. Timelines can differ materially by cadre unit, vacancy position, seniority/eligibility conditions, and the rules applicable to a particular select-list year.
bullets: Entry: Assistant Section Officer — Group B, non-gazetted, Level 7.

Next grade: Section Officer — reported by DoPT as Group B gazetted, Level 8, with a reported non-functional Level 10 after four years of approved service for eligible Section Officers under the applicable arrangements.
Senior grades in the reported CSS hierarchy: Under Secretary, Deputy Secretary, and Director.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: As reflected in SSC notices available in 2026, the CSS ASO post is in Pay Level 7, whose stated pay-matrix range is ₹44,900 to ₹1,42,400. This is the basic-pay range associated with the level, not a promise of a fixed monthly in-hand amount. Basic pay depends on the officer’s matrix cell and progression; total pay and take-home amount vary with allowances, deductions, posting location, and government orders applicable at the time of appointment.

For comparison within the reported CSS hierarchy, DoPT lists ASO at Level 7 and Section Officer at Level 8, with a cited non-functional Level 10 arrangement after four years of approved service for Section Officers. These figures and structures should be treated as dated official context rather than an individual compensation estimate.
bullets: Dated official context: Level 7 basic-pay range ₹44,900–₹1,42,400 in SSC notices available in 2026.
Do not equate the basic-pay range with take-home pay; allowances and deductions are variable.
Verify the appointment letter and current central-government pay and allowance orders for the applicable posting and date.

title: Assistant Sub-Inspector in CAPFs
description: A supervisory non-gazetted rank in the Central Armed Police Forces, typically reached by promotion from Head Constable through seniority and departmental selection.

quick_facts.label: Rank and status
quick_facts.value: In the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) General Duty cadre, Assistant Sub-Inspector (General Duty) is classified as a General Central Service Group ‘C’, non-gazetted, non-ministerial post. This is a concrete force-and-cadre example; ASI posts also exist in specialised and ministerial cadres, so the exact rule set depends on the force and cadre.

quick_facts.label: Usual feeder rank in the ITBP GD example
quick_facts.value: ITBP’s 2022 General Duty recruitment rules provide for promotion to ASI (GD) from Head Constable (GD) with five years’ regular service in Pay Level 4 and successful completion of the prescribed pre-promotional training course; the rule provides deputation only if promotion fails.

quick_facts.label: Medical standard in the ITBP GD example
quick_facts.value: The same ITBP rules require medical category SHAPE-I for appointment and promotion under those rules, including promotion to ASI (GD).

quick_facts.label: Pay-matrix context
quick_facts.value: The ITBP 2022 rules place ASI (GD) at Pay Level 5, with the then-stated matrix range of ₹29,200–₹92,300. This is a dated basic-pay-matrix reference, not a current take-home-pay estimate; applicable allowances and deductions depend on current government orders, posting, and individual circumstances.

quick_facts.label: CAPF context
quick_facts.value: The Ministry of Home Affairs lists Assam Rifles, BSF, CISF, CRPF, ITBP, NSG and SSB on its Central Armed Police Forces page. A rank title alone does not identify one uniform employer, posting pattern, or ASI specialty across those organisations.

sections.heading: How the Head Constable-to-ASI route works
paragraphs: For the General Duty path documented in ITBP’s 2022 recruitment rules, ASI is not an open direct-recruit entry point: the rule records direct-recruit age and education fields as “not applicable” and specifies promotion, failing which deputation. The feeder cadre is Head Constable (General Duty).

The ITBP example should be treated as a force-specific benchmark rather than a universal CAPF rule. ASI is used in multiple functional cadres—such as General Duty, ministerial/stenographic, engineering and medical/technical roles—and each cadre’s notified recruitment rules or recruitment notice controls eligibility, selection, training and vacancy filling.
bullets: ITBP GD benchmark: five years’ regular service as Head Constable (GD) in Pay Level 4.
Completion of the prescribed pre-promotional training course is required in that ITBP rule.
Promotion is considered by a Group ‘C’ Departmental Promotion Committee comprising a Deputy Inspector-General, Commandant, and Deputy/Assistant Commandant in the ITBP rule.
Candidates should check the current recruitment rules, force orders and departmental notices for their own force and cadre before treating any service-length or course requirement as applicable.

sections.heading: Documented readiness requirements
paragraphs: The clearest formally documented requirements for the ITBP General Duty promotion route are continued medical fitness at SHAPE-I and successful completion of prescribed pre-promotional training. The published rule does not provide a generic, cross-CAPF competency checklist for every ASI specialty, so applicants should rely on the course requirements and cadre-specific rules issued by their force rather than assuming one common syllabus.
bullets: Maintain the medical category required by the applicable recruitment rules; ITBP’s GD rule specifies SHAPE-I.
Complete the notified pre-promotional course for the relevant cadre.
Keep service, training and eligibility records current for departmental promotion consideration.

sections.heading: Employer and posting context
paragraphs: ASI is a rank used within a multi-force central security system rather than a single workplace. MHA’s Police II Division handles policy, personnel, operational deployment and financial matters for CAPFs, while MHA separately identifies the constituent forces. Therefore, day-to-day work and location depend on the appointing force, cadre, unit and deployment—not on the ASI title alone.

For example, an ITBP ASI (GD) is governed by the ITBP General Duty cadre rules, whereas technical or medical ASI vacancies are notified against their own specialised designations. Candidates should read the force-specific notification to establish whether the role is General Duty, ministerial, engineering, medical or another specialist stream.
bullets: Potential employer context includes BSF, CISF, CRPF, ITBP and SSB, with MHA also listing Assam Rifles and NSG on its CAPF page.
Operational deployment is centrally administered at the MHA level but individual posting details are force and unit specific.
A vacancy title should be read together with its cadre label and recruitment rules before drawing conclusions about work setting or duties.

sections.heading: Rank progression context
paragraphs: The MHA’s May 29, 2025 honorary-rank scheme presents the rank sequence Head Constable → Assistant Sub-Inspector → Sub-Inspector for CAPFs. It is useful confirmation of the rank relationship represented by this node.

That scheme is not a regular-promotion rule: it grants an honorary higher rank on the day of retirement, subject to stated conditions, and expressly provides no financial or pension benefit. Regular advancement must instead be assessed under the applicable force and cadre recruitment rules, including service, training, medical and departmental-selection requirements.
bullets: Immediate feeder relationship represented here: Head Constable to Assistant Sub-Inspector.
Next rank in the MHA honorary-rank sequence: Sub-Inspector.
Do not treat honorary rank at retirement as substantive promotion, pay progression, pension enhancement or a substitute for departmental promotion.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: For a dated, official benchmark, ITBP’s General Duty recruitment rules notified in 2022 specify Pay Level 5 (₹29,200–₹92,300) for ASI (GD), compared with Pay Level 4 for Head Constable (GD). This establishes the published basic-pay-matrix placement for that cadre at that time.

It should not be converted into a universal or current monthly-salary claim. MHA maintains CAPF policy material covering matters such as risk and hardship allowance and other welfare or service measures; actual pay received can vary by the force, cadre, posting, current allowance orders, leave status, tax and other deductions. Verify the current pay and allowance orders through the employing force.
bullets: Use ₹29,200–₹92,300 only as the basic matrix range stated in the 2022 ITBP ASI (GD) rule.
The rule’s stated Head Constable (GD) feeder level is Pay Level 4, ₹25,500–₹81,100.
Check current force orders for any posting-linked or risk/hardship allowances before estimating compensation.

title: Assistant Town Planner
description: An entry-level government position responsible for assisting in the planning and regulation of urban and rural development projects within a municipality or state.

quick_facts.label: Typical employer setting
quick_facts.value: Assistant Town Planner posts occur in state Town & Country Planning departments, local-self-government planning wings, and planning/development authorities; the exact statutory powers depend on the state or authority.

quick_facts.label: B.Plan relevance
quick_facts.value: A Bachelor of Planning can be a direct-entry qualification where the applicable service rules accept a Bachelor Degree in Planning; eligibility must be checked against the particular state/UT recruitment notification.

quick_facts.label: Recruitment routes
quick_facts.value: Recruitment can be through direct recruitment, promotion/transfer, or deputation depending on the service rules. For example, Odisha specifies direct recruitment or deputation, while a Kerala notification documents a departmental-quota route.

quick_facts.label: Core work
quick_facts.value: Official planning-authority disclosures associate the role with master/development-plan work, development control under zoning regulations, technical advice, and—in some authorities—building-plan or planning-proposal processing.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: Pay is state- and rules-specific. A Manipur Town Planning Department disclosure updated in April 2025 listed Assistant Town Planner at Pay Level 9 with pay band ₹43,300, while a Kerala departmental-quota notice dated December 31, 2024 listed ₹55,200–₹1,15,300.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
paragraphs: The role supports statutory planning and regulated development rather than simply producing layouts. In an Odisha planning-unit disclosure, services connected with an Assistant Town Planner include preparing and implementing master-plan schemes, enforcing development control through zoning regulations, advising revenue authorities on land-use conversion within the master-plan area, and giving technical advice to other agencies.

A broader state department example from Himachal Pradesh includes preparation of development, sectoral and village plans; planning infrastructure; assisting people and government agencies with planning permission; and approving planning proposals or issuing related no-objection certificates. The exact signing, approval, and enforcement authority is determined by the employing department’s legislation, delegation, and post level.
bullets: Prepare, scrutinize, or contribute technical inputs to master, development, sectoral, or area plans.
Assess proposals against land-use plans, zoning regulations, development-control rules, and applicable planning permissions.
Coordinate technical inputs with revenue, engineering, architecture, and other public agencies; some establishments also require site visits and public-facing correspondence.
Support statutory processes such as citizen consultation, objections and suggestions on plans, and processing files upward for departmental approval.

sections.heading: Entry routes after B.Plan
paragraphs: A B.Plan is a relevant immediate route, but it is not a nationwide automatic eligibility rule. Odisha’s Municipal Planning Service rules specify direct recruitment to Assistant Town Planner for an Associate Member of the Institute of Town Planners, India, a Bachelor Degree in Planning, or a postgraduate planning degree from a recognised university; the same rules also require basic computer knowledge.

Other jurisdictions set different combinations of acceptable qualifications. For example, Kerala’s December 31, 2024 Assistant Town Planner departmental-quota notification accepted degrees in Planning/Town and Country Planning/Regional Planning/City Planning/Urban Planning or equivalent, and also listed Civil Engineering, Architecture, and Physical Planning degrees. Candidates should therefore treat the vacancy notification and the applicable recruitment rules—not a generic job title—as definitive.

Recruitment may be conducted through a State Public Service Commission or other notified state/UT process. Read the advertisement for reservation category, age and domicile requirements, qualification-equivalence rules, experience requirements, examination/interview stages, and document-verification instructions.
bullets: Complete a recognised B.Plan and retain degree, marksheets, identity, category/domicile, and other eligibility documents required by the recruiting authority.
Track official state PSC, Town & Country Planning, Urban Development, Local Self Government, and development-authority recruitment pages.
Match the degree title and recognition status exactly to the advertisement; where equivalence is claimed, obtain the evidence requested by the recruiter.
Do not assume that every ATP post is open recruitment: some are departmental quota, promotion, transfer, or deputation posts.

sections.heading: Skills to build
paragraphs: Planning-rule literacy is central: official descriptions connect the work with master plans, zoning and land-use conformity, development control, planning permissions, and statutory planning acts or municipal bye-laws. A candidate should be able to interpret a plan and translate its provisions into a clear technical note or proposal assessment.

Basic computer knowledge is an explicit eligibility requirement in Odisha’s direct-recruitment rule. Departmental workflows also show Assistant Town Planners working with Associate Town Planners, engineers, draughtsmen, research staff, and administrative sections, then processing matters upward for approval; this makes accurate documentation, coordination, and clear written communication practically important.
bullets: Land-use, zoning, development-control, and master-plan interpretation.
Computer-based drafting, mapping, data handling, and orderly digital file/document preparation.
Technical note writing, proposal scrutiny, and record-based justification of recommendations.
Coordination with engineering, architecture, revenue, legal, and administrative colleagues; respectful communication with applicants and the public.

sections.heading: Workplace and operating context
paragraphs: The post can be based at a state directorate, divisional or sub-divisional town-planning office, local-government planning wing, or a development/planning authority. Himachal Pradesh’s departmental structure lists Assistant Town Planners at headquarters and divisional/sub-divisional field offices, alongside planning officers, engineers, draughtsmen, survey staff, and administrative personnel.

The work mixes desk-based technical scrutiny with field and stakeholder activity. In Manipur’s Town Planning Department, Assistant Town Planners support the wing handling master plans, land-use-conformity checks, and state flagship schemes; files move upward through planning leadership for approval, with technical support from draughtsmen and other staff. Public consultation can also form part of master-plan preparation.
bullets: Desk work: maps, plans, regulations, application files, technical correspondence, and digital records.
Interdisciplinary work: planners, engineers, architects, draughtsmen, surveyors, revenue officials, and administrators.
Field/public work: site-related inputs where assigned, coordination with agencies, and planning consultations or responses to applicants.

sections.heading: Progression
paragraphs: Career ladders are controlled by state service rules. Odisha’s Municipal Planning Service rules place Assistant Town Planner below Associate City Planner and specify at least seven years of Assistant Town Planner service for promotion to that post. Rajasthan’s Town Planning Rules similarly show Assistant Town Planner as the feeder post for Deputy Town Planner, with five years’ experience specified for that promotion in the published rule table.

Progression is therefore usually based on the sanctioned hierarchy, qualifying service, departmental rules, vacancy position, and any required selection process—not solely on years worked. Because titles differ across states, candidates should read the current rules for the department they intend to join.
bullets: Potential next roles may include Associate City Planner, Deputy Town Planner, or comparable state-specific planning posts.
Build a record of statutory-plan work, development-control scrutiny, technical coordination, and compliant file processing.
Check the governing recruitment/promotion rules for minimum service, departmental examinations, and vacancy-based promotion conditions.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: There is no single India-wide Assistant Town Planner salary. Pay is fixed by the employing state/UT or authority’s pay rules and can differ materially by cadre and recruitment channel. As dated reference points, Manipur’s Town Planning Department disclosure, updated April 2025, lists Assistant Town Planner at Pay Level 9 and ₹43,300; Kerala PSC’s December 31, 2024 departmental-quota notification lists a scale of ₹55,200–₹1,15,300.

These are published pay references, not a portable salary promise or an estimate of take-home pay. Before applying, use the specific current advertisement and applicable pay-revision/allowance orders to confirm basic pay, level or scale, allowances, probation terms, and whether the vacancy is regular, contractual, departmental quota, or deputation.
bullets: Treat compensation figures as dated, employer-specific context.
Verify the current notification’s pay level/scale and the state’s applicable allowance and pay-revision rules.
Distinguish basic pay or pay band from gross and take-home monthly remuneration.

title: Auditor in Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)
description: A Group C post responsible for auditing the accounts of central and state government departments and public sector undertakings.

quick_facts.label: Recruiting examination and post classification
quick_facts.value: The Staff Selection Commission’s CGL notice lists “Auditor — Offices under C&AG” as a Group C post at Pay Level 5, with an age band of 18–27 years in that notice.

quick_facts.label: Education requirement
quick_facts.value: For Auditor and other CGL posts not assigned a separate qualification, the cited SSC notice requires a bachelor’s degree from a recognised university or equivalent. Eligibility conditions and cut-off dates must be checked in the relevant annual notice.

quick_facts.label: Audit remit
quick_facts.value: The CAG’s audit mandate covers Union, State and relevant Union Territory government receipts, expenditure and transactions; its mandate also extends, under applicable law, to government companies, corporations, bodies and authorities.

quick_facts.label: Internal advancement examination
quick_facts.value: An Auditor in an Audit Office is among the categories eligible for the departmental Subordinate Audit/Accounts Service (SAS) Examination after at least three years of continuous service in the specified field office and successful completion of probation; SAS is conducted for appointment to Assistant Audit/Accounts Officer, a Group B gazetted post.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: The SSC notice cited above shows Pay Level 5 as ₹29,200–₹92,300 in the pay matrix. This is dated pay-matrix/basic-pay context, not a promise of take-home salary; appointment terms, location and then-applicable government orders determine actual remuneration.

sections.heading: What an Auditor in CAG does
paragraphs: An Auditor works within the Indian Audit and Accounts Department’s audit function. The CAG regulations define audit as examination of accounts, transactions and records in carrying out the CAG’s constitutional and statutory duties; an “auditor” is an officer authorised to conduct audit. The work therefore centres on examining documentary and financial evidence against applicable rules, accounting principles and audit objectives, under the direction and procedures of the relevant audit office.

The subject matter can include government receipts and expenditure, government transactions, and—in the circumstances prescribed by law—government companies, statutory corporations, bodies and authorities. CAG auditing standards apply to financial, compliance and performance audits, so the precise assignments depend on the office and audit plan rather than being limited to one kind of account.
bullets: Examine records, accounts, transactions and supporting information made available for audit.
Apply CAG auditing standards and professional judgement while performing assigned audit work.
Help document and communicate audit observations through the audit-office process; CAG audit reports are ultimately placed before the appropriate legislature.

sections.heading: Primary entry route: SSC CGL
paragraphs: The normal external entry route represented by this node is the Staff Selection Commission’s Combined Graduate Level Examination (SSC CGL). The SSC notice lists Auditor in Offices under C&AG as a Group C, Pay Level 5 post. Candidates are allotted posts based on merit and the post preferences they submit; a post preference should be made only after checking the annual notice’s requirements.

In the cited SSC CGL notice, Auditor falls under the general qualification rule for “all other posts”: a bachelor’s degree from a recognised university or equivalent. The same notice describes a Tier I computer-based examination used for shortlisting and Tier II Paper I for posts other than the specialised JSO, Statistical Investigator, AAO and AAO-related papers. Examination structure, vacancies, eligibility dates, age relaxations and cut-offs can change from cycle to cycle, so candidates should use the active SSC notification rather than relying solely on this summary.
bullets: Complete a recognised bachelor’s degree or equivalent by the eligibility date in the applicable SSC CGL notice.
Apply for SSC CGL and include Auditor, Offices under C&AG in post preferences when the Commission requests preferences.
Qualify the examination stages and complete document verification and departmental appointment formalities if allotted the post.

sections.heading: Skills that fit the role
paragraphs: Useful preparation combines accounting and public-finance literacy with careful evidence handling. CAG regulations require audits to follow auditing standards, state that auditors must apply their own judgement to varied audit situations, and emphasise access to relevant data, information and documents. Those requirements make accuracy, structured analysis, ethical independence and clear written documentation particularly relevant skills.

Candidates can build practical readiness by strengthening numerical reasoning; reading of government rules and financial records; spreadsheet and computer proficiency; concise drafting; and the ability to ask focused questions about records and explanations. These are role-relevant capabilities inferred from the CAG’s stated audit standards and audit process, not additional SSC eligibility conditions.
bullets: Accounting, transaction and document analysis.
Understanding of audit evidence, internal controls, compliance and public-sector rules.
Professional judgement, attention to detail and independence from the auditable entity.
Clear written communication and comfort working with digital records and data.

sections.heading: Where and how the work is carried out
paragraphs: The post is in Offices under the C&AG within the Indian Audit and Accounts Department. CAG regulations describe an audit office as an office responsible for audit and recognise that audit may require access to accounts, books, papers and other documents relevant to auditable transactions. Accordingly, work may combine audit-office record analysis with audit activity involving the offices or entities being audited.

The particular state, audit office and subject area are allocation-dependent. CAG recruitment notices show that selected CGL candidates are allocated to a State/office, so applicants should treat the eventual place of posting and office allocation as part of the employment decision rather than assuming a single national headquarters location.
bullets: Audit-office work involving review and documentation of records.
Interaction with auditable government departments or entities for information and records within the CAG audit framework.
State/office allocation following selection, subject to the recruitment process for that cycle.

sections.heading: Progression and the SAS pathway
paragraphs: The departmental SAS Examination is an important formal progression route for eligible staff. The CAG states that SAS is conducted for the post of Assistant Audit/Accounts Officer, a Group B gazetted post. Its published eligibility list includes Auditors in Audit Offices who have completed at least three years of continuous service in one or more specified capacities in the relevant field office and successfully completed probation.

This should not be read as an automatic promotion guarantee: eligibility to sit SAS, qualifying the examination, vacancies, service rules and departmental decisions govern progression. The CAG states that SAS has a preliminary examination conducted by field offices and a computer-based main examination conducted by headquarters.
bullets: Entry role: Auditor, Pay Level 5, in an Audit Office.
Published intermediate category: Senior Auditor, Pay Level 6, appears in the SAS eligibility framework.
Potential examination-based route: SAS for Assistant Audit Officer, Group B gazetted, subject to the governing conditions.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: As a dated reference point, the SSC CGL notice available for the 2026 eligibility cycle lists Auditor in Offices under C&AG at Pay Level 5, with the pay-matrix range ₹29,200–₹92,300. This is the published level and basic-pay range, rather than a single starting salary or take-home figure.

Actual monthly pay can vary with the stage in the pay matrix and applicable government allowances and deductions. Applicants should verify the appointment offer, current pay rules and the applicable SSC notice at the time of selection.
bullets: Post shown in the cited SSC notice: Group C Auditor, Offices under C&AG.
Published pay context in that notice: Pay Level 5, ₹29,200–₹92,300.
Do not use the matrix range as a take-home-pay estimate.

title: Ayurvedic Medical Officer
description: A government-sector AYUSH physician who provides Ayurvedic outpatient care and public-health services in state hospitals, dispensaries, or health centres.

quick_facts.label: Core role
quick_facts.value: An Ayurvedic Medical Officer is a government-employed Ayurveda physician role centred on patient treatment and community-facing public-health work; official Odisha departmental material lists treatment of patients, health camps and health-awareness programmes among Ayurvedic/Unani Medical Officers’ duties.

quick_facts.label: Usual qualifying degree
quick_facts.value: BAMS is the foundational qualification route. NCISM’s 2022 BAMS regulations specify a five-and-a-half-year programme comprising three 18-month professional phases and a 12-month compulsory rotatory internship.

quick_facts.label: Registration
quick_facts.value: Registration is commonly required in recruitment: a Goa State Health Society notice for an AYUSH Doctor required a recognised Ayurveda degree and registration with the Goa board/central council of Indian medicine.

sections.heading: What an Ayurvedic Medical Officer does
paragraphs: The role combines Ayurvedic clinical service with public-health delivery. An official Odisha RTI manual assigns Ayurvedic/Unani Medical Officers responsibility for treating patients and conducting health camps and health-awareness programmes. In practice, the precise clinical scope, reporting requirements, medicine-management work and outreach duties are set by the employing state department and the specific facility.

Government AYUSH services also involve service delivery beyond an individual dispensary. Ministry of Ayush material describes National AYUSH Mission support for access to AYUSH services and for hospital/dispensary infrastructure, while state governments remain responsible for public-health service delivery and workforce deployment.
bullets: Provide Ayurveda-based outpatient clinical care within the post’s authorised service setting.
Participate in health camps and public-health awareness activities where assigned.
Work within state or UT administrative, reporting and facility procedures; the exact assignment can vary by posting.

sections.heading: Entry route after BAMS
paragraphs: The standard route begins with completing BAMS, including its compulsory rotatory internship. NCISM’s BAMS regulations set the programme duration at five years and six months, including a 12-month internship.

Candidates then need to meet the eligibility terms of a particular employer’s vacancy. These commonly include a recognised Ayurveda degree and professional registration; for example, Goa’s State Health Society required BAMS and a registration certificate for an AYUSH Doctor post. Recruitment may be through a state public service commission or through a state/district AYUSH or health society on a contractual basis. A 2026 HPPSC advertisement illustrates the commission route for an Ayurvedic Medical Officer post, while Goa’s 2026 National AYUSH Mission notice illustrates a fixed-term contractual engagement.
bullets: Complete BAMS and the compulsory internship.
Obtain the registration required by the relevant state or recruiting authority.
Track official state PSC, AYUSH department, health department, NHM and State AYUSH Society notices.
Check each notification for domicile, age, category, language, experience, examination and document-verification conditions; these are vacancy-specific.

sections.heading: Skills that fit the post
paragraphs: The clearest job-specific skills are those directly reflected in government duty descriptions: clinical patient management, communication for health-awareness work, and the ability to organise or participate in outreach camps. Because the role is delivered through a public facility, candidates should also be prepared for administrative instructions and reporting associated with their assigned dispensary or health programme.

Some vacancies add locally relevant capabilities. For example, a 2026 Goa National AYUSH Mission Medical Officer (Ayurveda) vacancy identified clinical Panchakarma or Ayurvedic-clinic/government-hospital experience as essential for that particular post, with computer knowledge and travel across the state listed as desirable or required conditions. These are examples, not universal eligibility rules.
bullets: Ayurvedic clinical assessment and patient communication.
Community-health communication and camp delivery.
Facility documentation, coordination and compliance with departmental instructions.
Adaptability to the specific programme or clinical focus named in the recruitment notice.

sections.heading: Where the role is performed
paragraphs: Workplaces include government Ayurvedic dispensaries and hospitals, primary-health-centre-linked services, AYUSH Health and Wellness Centres, and integrated AYUSH hospitals. The Ministry of Ayush states that the National AYUSH Mission includes provisions for contractual manpower in upgraded standalone government AYUSH hospitals, AYUSH Health and Wellness Centres, and 10-, 30- and 50-bedded integrated AYUSH hospitals.

Posting conditions can include rural or district-level service and mobility. For example, the Goa State AYUSH Society’s January 2026 Medical Officer (Ayurveda) notice placed the role at IPHB/PHC Chimbel and stated that the appointee would have to travel extensively within the state.
bullets: Government dispensaries and AYUSH hospitals.
PHC-linked and wellness-centre service points.
Integrated AYUSH facilities under state or National AYUSH Mission implementation.
Community outreach locations for camps and awareness programmes.

sections.heading: Compensation context: highly appointment-specific
paragraphs: Compensation should be read from the individual notification rather than treated as a national salary benchmark. As dated examples, HPPSC advertised an Ayurvedic Medical Officer (Job Trainee) role in February 2026 at ₹29,500 per month, while the Goa State AYUSH Society advertised a one-year National AYUSH Mission Medical Officer (Ayurveda) contract in January 2026 at ₹40,000 per month, described as ₹25,000 fixed plus ₹15,000 performance-linked incentive.

These figures are not directly comparable or predictive: the HP post was a state job-trainee appointment, whereas the Goa post was a specified fixed-term NAM contract with role-specific clinical-experience requirements. Pay, allowances, tenure, pension/benefits and progression depend on the state’s service rules and the vacancy’s employment terms.
bullets: Verify the appointment type first: regular service, job trainee, contractual/NAM or another engagement category.
Use the latest official advertisement for the stated monthly pay, allowances, tenure and benefits.
Do not extrapolate a single state’s advertised figure to all Ayurvedic Medical Officer jobs.

title: Block Development Officer in State Rural Development Department
description: A state officer who plans, implements, and monitors rural-development and local-government programmes for a development block.

quick_facts.label: Role at block level
quick_facts.value: A Block Development Officer (BDO) heads the Block Office and coordinates rural-development work with technical, field, and ministerial staff; the exact administrative set-up is state-specific.

quick_facts.label: Core remit
quick_facts.value: Typical official functions include preparing block plans and schemes, coordinating line departments, guiding and supervising village panchayats, monitoring programmes, and overseeing the use of grants and funds.

quick_facts.label: Public-administration responsibilities
quick_facts.value: In some states, the BDO is also the Panchayat Samiti’s executive officer, supervisory authority over block staff, drawing and disbursing officer, and may hold additional statutory or election-related responsibilities.

quick_facts.label: Entry pattern
quick_facts.value: Recruitment is not uniform across India. An Assam notification appointed BDOs following the Assam Public Service Commission’s Combined Competitive Examination 2024, while Goa Public Service Commission advertised direct BDO recruitment in 2026.

quick_facts.label: Education example
quick_facts.value: For Goa PSC’s 2026 BDO advertisement, a degree in any discipline and knowledge of Konkani were essential; Sociology or Social Work and Marathi were listed as desirable. Applicants must always follow the notification for their particular state and recruitment cycle.

quick_facts.label: Compensation context
quick_facts.value: Pay is state- and rules-dependent. In 2026, Goa PSC listed BDO at revised pay-matrix Level 7, while an Assam appointment notification listed Pay Band 4, ₹30,000–₹1,10,000 with ₹12,700 grade pay, plus admissible allowances.

sections.heading: What a Block Development Officer does
paragraphs: The BDO is a block-level rural-development and local-government administrator. Official Goa guidance describes the role as the block’s coordinating agency: formulating an integrated working plan, guiding and supervising village panchayats, coordinating departmental schemes, preparing schemes and estimates for sanction, and ensuring grants released to panchayats are properly used.

In practice, the post combines programme delivery, administration, public finance, field oversight, and local-government support. Odisha block-office disclosures describe BDOs as executive officers who implement and monitor block schemes, exercise supervisory and administrative control over staff, inspect Gram Panchayat offices and field works, and, in listed cases, act as drawing and disbursing officers and programme officers.

The portfolio can also expand during emergencies or statutory assignments. West Bengal’s disaster-management guidance assigns the head of block administration duties such as monitoring block disaster operations, maintaining accounts, assessing reconstruction-fund needs, preparing and revising annual block disaster-management plans, and reporting to higher authorities.
bullets: Translate state and district rural-development priorities into block plans, projects, estimates, implementation schedules, and monitoring activity.
Coordinate Panchayats, technical personnel, field staff, line departments, community organisations, and district-level authorities.
Supervise implementation of development, anti-poverty, welfare, infrastructure, sanitation, housing, livelihoods, and employment programmes assigned to the block.
Monitor panchayat administration and fund use; maintain records, reports, inspections, and—in posts where delegated—financial and statutory functions.
Respond to field conditions and public needs, including disaster-preparedness or relief responsibilities where assigned by the state.

sections.heading: Entry routes and eligibility
paragraphs: There is no single all-India BDO examination or universally identical eligibility rule. The route is determined by the state’s service rules and vacancy notification. A documented civil-services route is Assam: its Panchayat and Rural Development Department appointed eight BDOs in March 2026 on the recommendation of the Assam Public Service Commission under the Combined Competitive Examination 2024.

States may also recruit BDOs through a state public service commission advertisement for the particular post. Goa PSC’s May 2026 advertisement for three BDO posts required a degree in any branch from a recognised university or equivalent and knowledge of Konkani; it listed Sociology or Social Work and Marathi as desirable. That is a state-specific example, not a national rule.

Internal promotion can be another route in some services. Uttarakhand’s PSC records include promotion from Assistant Block Development Officer to BDO in the Rural Development Department, illustrating why candidates should check both direct-recruitment notices and departmental-service rules in their target state.
bullets: Track the relevant State PSC and Rural Development/Panchayati Raj department, rather than relying on a generic national eligibility checklist.
For civil-service allocation routes, prepare for the state combined competitive examination and verify whether BDO is included among posts for that recruitment year.
For direct-post advertisements, verify degree requirements, domicile or language requirements, age limits, reservation provisions, selection stages, and document rules in the original notification.
If already employed in a state rural-development service, review applicable promotion channels and departmental eligibility provisions.

sections.heading: Skills that fit the role
paragraphs: The role’s official functions point to a mixed administrative and field-facing skill set. Because BDOs plan schemes, coordinate multiple departments, supervise panchayats and staff, and monitor works and funds, strong written communication, planning, coordination, record management, and basic public-finance control are especially relevant.

Practical effectiveness also depends on community engagement and local-government literacy. Meghalaya’s Community and Rural Development Department states that BDOs are responsible for securing people’s participation and sustaining public enthusiasm in block programmes; Goa’s charter includes support to panchayats and strengthening village-level organisations among BDO functions.
bullets: Programme planning, work planning, estimation awareness, monitoring, and evidence-based reporting.
Coordination and stakeholder management across Panchayats, engineers, extension personnel, district administration, and line departments.
Clear drafting and communication for orders, meeting records, reports, beneficiary-facing processes, and compliance follow-up.
Financial diligence: grant utilisation oversight, bill and record scrutiny where responsibilities are delegated, and attention to auditability.
Field engagement, problem solving, and the ability to work constructively with elected local representatives and rural communities.

sections.heading: Workplace and operating environment
paragraphs: A BDO normally works from a development-block office within the state’s rural-development or Panchayati Raj system, while spending substantial time coordinating and inspecting work across the block. Meghalaya’s official organisational description identifies the BDO as head of the Block Office, supported by officers, technical staff, and ministerial staff responsible for executing development works.

The position is therefore neither solely desk-based nor solely field-based. Official block-level descriptions place the BDO between district administration and village institutions, with responsibility for coordinating programme implementation, supervising Panchayat activity, and working with agriculture, veterinary, engineering, accounts, extension, and field personnel.
bullets: Primary base: the Block Office or Panchayat Samiti/Block administration office.
Regular counterparts: village panchayats, district rural-development agencies, technical staff, field staff, line departments, and community groups.
Work pattern: office administration and documentation combined with field visits, inspections, review meetings, scheme monitoring, and public interaction.
Additional assignments may arise from state laws, elections, programme guidelines, or disaster-management arrangements.

sections.heading: Career progression context
paragraphs: Career progression is governed by the relevant state cadre and service rules, so a BDO should not assume a common national promotion ladder. Official Uttarakhand PSC material records promotions from Assistant Block Development Officer to BDO, showing that BDO can be a promotional destination in one state service; other states may fill the post through civil-service allocation, direct PSC recruitment, or a mix of methods.

For career planning, the reliable source is the service rules, recruitment notification, and departmental promotion orders for the target state. These documents determine cadre structure, qualifying service, departmental examinations or training, seniority, probation, and the posts available after BDO.
bullets: Check the state’s Rural Development/Panchayati Raj service rules for the applicable cadre hierarchy.
Distinguish between direct-entry BDO posts, civil-service allocations, and by-transfer or promotional posts.
Treat any claimed next post, pay progression, or timeline as state- and rule-specific until verified in the current notification or service rules.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: BDO pay cannot be stated as a single India-wide salary. It changes with the employing state, cadre, pay-revision framework, allowances, and whether the post is filled through a state civil service, direct recruitment, or promotion.

As dated examples rather than universal benchmarks: Goa PSC’s advertisement uploaded on May 8, 2026 placed BDO at revised pay-matrix Level 7. Assam’s March 4, 2026 appointment notification for BDOs selected through its Combined Competitive Examination stated a Pay Band 4 scale of ₹30,000–₹1,10,000 with ₹12,700 grade pay per month, plus allowances admissible under government rules. Candidates should use the live notification and current state pay orders for any decision involving compensation.
bullets: Compare the exact pay level or pay band shown in the current official vacancy notice.
Check whether dearness allowance, house-rent allowance, travel entitlement, pension or national-pension coverage, probation conditions, and location-related provisions apply.
Do not compare figures across states without accounting for different pay structures and allowance rules.

title: Chief Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor in Indian Railways
description: A railway commercial supervisory employee recruited through graduate-level RRB NTPC posts to oversee ticketing, passenger services and commercial operations.

quick_facts.label: Recruiting route
quick_facts.value: This is a graduate-level Non-Technical Popular Categories (NTPC) post recruited by Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs) through centralized employment notices; the relevant recent notice was CEN 05/2024.

quick_facts.label: Education eligibility
quick_facts.value: In CEN 05/2024, the minimum educational qualification for the graduate NTPC posts, including Chief Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor, was a university degree or equivalent. Eligibility must always be checked against the specific new notification.

quick_facts.label: Pay level
quick_facts.value: CEN 05/2024 listed Chief Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor at Level 6 of the 7th CPC Pay Matrix, with initial pay of ₹35,400. This is notification-specific basic-pay context, not a guarantee of current take-home pay.

quick_facts.label: Medical standard
quick_facts.value: The CEN 05/2024 post table specified medical standard B-2 for Chief Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor; candidates must satisfy the applicable Railway medical examination requirements.

quick_facts.label: Recent recruitment context
quick_facts.value: CEN 05/2024 notified 1,736 Chief Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor vacancies across RRBs. The CEN page subsequently posted document-verification and medical-examination scheduling in May 2026, so applicants should use their own RRB's official notices rather than assume a fresh application window is open.

sections.heading: What the role covers
paragraphs: A Chief Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor works in Indian Railways' commercial function. At department level, commercial work spans the sale and marketing of railway transport, passenger-facing service, correct collection, accounting and remittance of traffic receipts, fares and rates, refunds and compensation claims, passenger amenities, ticket checking, and reserved and unreserved ticketing systems. The exact local allocation of supervisory work can vary by railway, division, station, and operational need.

The role's operational knowledge base is broad: a 2025 Railway selection syllabus for Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor includes ticketing and reservation/refund rules, cash remittance and e-balance-sheet processes, ticket-checking procedures and irregular-travel handling, passenger amenities and grievance channels, and relevant goods and parcel commercial rules. This supports a role profile combining frontline passenger-service oversight, revenue/ticketing control, rule compliance, and coordination with commercial staff.
bullets: Supervise or support ticketing, ticket-checking, passenger-service, and commercial-receipt processes within the assigned commercial unit.
Apply published commercial rules on reservations, refunds, concessions, luggage, irregular travel, and related passenger transactions.
Maintain accurate handling, accounting, and remittance of commercial receipts in accordance with Railway procedures.
Respond to passenger-service issues and coordinate with the wider commercial organisation on amenities, complaints, and service delivery.

sections.heading: Entry through RRB NTPC (graduate)
paragraphs: The principal external entry route evidenced by the recent recruitment cycle is RRB NTPC Graduate. CEN 05/2024 listed Chief Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor as a Level-6 graduate post and required a university degree or equivalent. For that notice, the normal age band was 18–33 as of January 1, 2025; a one-time three-year relaxation made the applicable age band 18–36. Age limits, reservations, relaxations, vacancies, fees, and dates can change in later CENs.

The CEN describes a recruitment process involving computer-based tests, document verification, and medical examination. The official CEN 05/2024 page shows that candidates for this cycle progressed to document verification and medical examination in 2026. Candidates should rely only on the RRB and RRB Apply channels named in the live notification.
bullets: Complete the educational, nationality, age, reservation, and medical eligibility conditions in the applicable CEN.
Apply online to one selected RRB when a relevant NTPC Graduate CEN is open.
Prepare for the notified computer-based-test stages; complete document verification and the Railway medical examination if shortlisted.
Do not treat the 2024 vacancy count or its dates as a standing recruitment schedule.

sections.heading: Knowledge and skills to develop
paragraphs: The official CCTS selection syllabus points to the practical capabilities needed after appointment or for advancement in the commercial stream: command of ticketing, reservation, refund, concession, luggage, parcel and freight rules; careful handling of revenue and cash-remittance procedures; ticket-checking and irregular-travel procedures; use of railway digital systems; and awareness of passenger amenities, RailMadad, the 139 helpline, and grievance processes.

Because the commercial department handles both public service and receipt accountability, strong communication, rule interpretation, numerical accuracy, record discipline, customer handling, and calm decision-making in busy passenger environments are especially relevant. These are role-relevant capabilities inferred from the department's stated functions and the published syllabus, rather than separate formal eligibility criteria.
bullets: Ticketing, reservation, fare, refund, concession, luggage, parcel, and ticket-checking rules.
Cash/receipt accountability, remittance procedures, and accurate commercial records.
Passenger communication, complaint handling, and service recovery.
Working knowledge of UTS, mobile ticketing, reservation-related systems, handheld devices, and railway grievance/service applications.
Ability to apply rules consistently while coordinating with ticket-checking and other commercial personnel.

sections.heading: Where and how the work is performed
paragraphs: The post sits in the commercial department of Indian Railways, whose work covers stations and onboard passenger services as well as ticket sales, goods booking, passenger claims, and other commercial activity. Consequently, assignments may be in a railway zone or division and can involve station-based, passenger-service, ticket-checking, or commercial-office work depending on the posting and local organisation.

The work is public-facing and operational rather than limited to a desk: commercial functions include passenger amenities, ticket checking, reserved and unreserved ticketing, claims, fares, and revenue collection. Posting location, rosters, and precise duties are determined by the employing railway administration.
bullets: Potential settings include stations, divisional commercial offices, ticketing/reservation environments, and passenger-service or ticket-checking operations.
The role requires coordination across the commercial organisation and interaction with travelling passengers.
Work patterns and location are posting-dependent; candidates should not assume a particular city, office-only role, or fixed schedule.

sections.heading: Career development context
paragraphs: Career development is within the Railway commercial department, which has responsibilities extending across passenger services, ticketing, claims, fares, freight-related commercial work, and commercial revenue. Published Railway material also shows Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor as a Level-6 selection post and identifies higher commercial levels in departmental restructuring discussions; however, an individual's promotion path depends on applicable Railway Board rules, seniority, eligibility, vacancies, selection processes, and the cadre structure of the particular railway or division.

A sound development path is therefore to build demonstrable proficiency in commercial rules, revenue control, passenger-service systems, and supervisory administration, and to monitor official departmental-selection and personnel notices of the employing railway. Exact promotional designations or timelines should not be assumed from general career websites.
bullets: Develop breadth across passenger, ticketing, ticket-checking, revenue, parcel, and goods-commercial procedures.
Track official personnel and departmental-selection notices in the assigned railway or division.
Promotion opportunities and criteria are cadre- and rule-dependent rather than automatic.

sections.heading: Pay and compensation context
paragraphs: For dated context, CEN 05/2024 placed Chief Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor in Pay Level 6 under the 7th CPC and stated initial pay of ₹35,400. This is the starting basic-pay figure published for that recruitment notice—not an estimate of monthly in-hand pay.

Actual earnings can differ because applicable allowances, deductions, place of posting, and government orders affect pay. Candidates should verify the pay level and all current service/allowance conditions in the CEN and appointment terms applicable to their own recruitment cycle.
bullets: CEN 05/2024 context: 7th CPC Pay Level 6; initial basic pay ₹35,400.
Do not equate initial basic pay with take-home salary.
Check the live official CEN and appointment documentation for the current position.
