title: Civil Judge-cum-Judicial Magistrate in State Judicial Service
description: A combined entry-level state judicial post that exercises civil judge and judicial magistrate responsibilities where the state recruitment rules provide for it.

quick_facts.label: What this title means
quick_facts.value: This is a state-specific, combined entry-level judicial-service designation rather than one uniform all-India cadre title. Rajasthan officially lists “Civil Judge and Judicial Magistrate” among its district courts, while Uttar Pradesh rules treat a Civil Judge (Junior Division) as including a Judicial Magistrate First Class and related postings.

quick_facts.label: Core legal basis for the combined role
quick_facts.value: Under section 9 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the High Court may confer the powers of a Judicial Magistrate of the first or second class on a member of a State Judicial Service who is functioning as a judge in a civil court.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry mechanism
quick_facts.value: Entry is ordinarily through the relevant state judicial-services competitive recruitment process, but the authority, eligibility conditions, examination pattern, vacancies, and dates are state- and notification-specific. For example, Uttar Pradesh’s rules provide for direct recruitment to Civil Judge (Junior Division) through a competitive examination conducted by the state commission, subject to vacancies.

quick_facts.label: Education and language example
quick_facts.value: Candidates must follow the governing state notification. As an illustration only, the Uttar Pradesh rules require an LL.B. from a recognised university or specified advocate/barrister status, plus thorough knowledge of Hindi in Devanagari; these conditions should not be assumed to apply unchanged in another state.

quick_facts.label: Institutional setting
quick_facts.value: Judicial Magistrates’ courts are established district-wise by the State Government after consultation with the High Court, and their presiding officers are appointed by the High Court. Judicial Magistrates other than the Chief Judicial Magistrate are, subject to the Sessions Judge’s general control, subordinate to the Chief Judicial Magistrate.

sections.heading: Responsibilities: civil-court judging combined with criminal-magisterial powers
paragraphs: The combined title reflects a state judicial officer who may function as a judge in a civil court and also be invested with Judicial Magistrate powers. Section 9 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) expressly permits the High Court to confer first- or second-class Judicial Magistrate powers on a State Judicial Service member functioning as a civil-court judge. The exact allocation of civil and criminal work depends on the state’s cadre rules, posting order, local jurisdiction, and the business distribution made by the competent judicial authority.

In the criminal-magisterial capacity, a first-class Magistrate has the sentencing authority specified by BNSS section 23: imprisonment up to three years, a fine up to ₹50,000, both, or community service, subject to the statute and the facts of the case. The officer must therefore conduct proceedings, assess material placed before the court, issue reasoned judicial orders, and work within the jurisdiction and powers assigned by law.
The role is judicial, not executive-magisterial. BNSS separately identifies Judicial Magistrates and Executive Magistrates as distinct classes of criminal courts/officers.
bullets: Apply procedural and substantive law to matters assigned to the court.
Conduct hearings and make judicial orders in the civil and criminal jurisdiction lawfully conferred.
Maintain a clear record of proceedings and reasons, particularly where evidence or an accused’s examination must be recorded under the BNSS.
Operate within local jurisdiction and the administrative distribution of work under the district judiciary.

sections.heading: Entry route: state judicial-services recruitment
paragraphs: The practical route is the state-wise Judicial Services Examination (often called PCS-J or Civil Judge recruitment), followed by appointment under the applicable state judicial-service rules. Recruitment is not nationally standardised: candidates should use the relevant High Court, state public service commission, or recruiting authority’s current advertisement as the controlling document for vacancies, age, reservation, language requirements, examination scheme, fees, and deadlines.

Uttar Pradesh provides a useful official illustration of the route: direct recruitment to Civil Judge (Junior Division) is through a competitive examination conducted by the Commission; its rules describe a written examination in legal and allied subjects including procedure, language testing, and an interview. The same rules require appointed officers to undergo training during probation. These details demonstrate the structure of one state’s process, not a universal eligibility checklist.

For an applicant considering a state that uses the literal combined designation, Rajasthan’s High Court has used “Civil Judge and Judicial Magistrate” as the post label in its recruitment materials. Applicants should still rely on the latest recruitment notice rather than historical instructions or another state’s rules.
bullets: Complete a recognised legal qualification required by the recruiting state.
Track the current state judicial-services notification issued by the competent authority.
Prepare for state-prescribed written papers, language requirements where applicable, and interview/personality assessment where prescribed.
After selection, complete the probationary and judicial-training requirements specified by the state or High Court.

sections.heading: Skills signalled by the recruitment and judicial work
paragraphs: The role requires strong legal analysis and procedural command. Uttar Pradesh’s official rules, for example, test legal and allied subjects including procedure, and use an interview to assess merit, ability, character, personality, physique, and general suitability. Because a combined post may involve both civil-court work and magisterial functions, candidates need to read statutes carefully, distinguish jurisdictional limits, analyse facts and evidence, and write legally sustainable reasons.

Language and communication capability are also material but state-specific. Uttar Pradesh’s rules require thorough knowledge of Hindi in Devanagari and test Hindi, English, and Urdu in its competitive examination. Other states may prescribe different official-language requirements, so the current notification governs.

Professional integrity, independence, impartiality, careful case management, and the ability to communicate respectfully in court are essential practical capabilities for a judicial office, consistent with the statutory responsibility to ensure expeditious and proper disposal of cases in courts subordinate to the High Court.
bullets: Legal research, statutory interpretation, and command of civil and criminal procedure.
Structured judicial writing: concise orders, clear reasons, and accurate recording of proceedings.
Evidence and fact analysis, including identifying the limits of the court’s jurisdiction and powers.
Courtroom communication, listening, fairness, composure, and disciplined case management.
State-prescribed language proficiency.

sections.heading: Workplace and reporting context
paragraphs: The usual workplace is the subordinate judiciary/district-court system in the recruiting state, rather than a ministry or a police organisation. BNSS provides that the State Government establishes courts of Judicial Magistrates in districts after consultation with the High Court, while the High Court appoints their presiding officers. A posting may therefore be tied to a district, sub-division, or other local jurisdiction fixed under law.

The judicial hierarchy matters to daily work. BNSS places the Chief Judicial Magistrate under the Sessions Judge, and other Judicial Magistrates under the Chief Judicial Magistrate, subject to the Sessions Judge’s general control. The Chief Judicial Magistrate may also make rules or special orders for business distribution among subordinate magistrates. This means an officer’s criminal docket and territorial scope are determined by lawful assignment, not solely by the title of the post.

In a state using a combined civil-judge/judicial-magistrate structure, the officer may be assigned civil-court and criminal-magisterial functions at different times or in different postings. Uttar Pradesh’s recent High Court notifications illustrate that officers can be posted between Civil Judge (Junior Division), Additional Civil Judge (Junior Division), and Judicial Magistrate First Class assignments.
bullets: District and subordinate courts within the state judicial system.
Courtroom hearings, chambers-based judgment/order writing, case-record review, and administrative judicial work.
Posting, local jurisdiction, and case allocation determined by the High Court and district judicial hierarchy.
Potential movement among equivalent or related junior-division civil and magisterial assignments, according to state rules and posting orders.

sections.heading: Progression: promotion within the state judicial service
paragraphs: Career progression is controlled by the relevant state judicial-service rules and High Court decisions; it is not a single national ladder. In Uttar Pradesh, the rules identify Civil Judge (Junior Division) and Civil Judge (Senior Division) as service cadres and provide that promotion to Civil Judge (Senior Division) is made by the High Court from Civil Judge (Junior Division) officers, based on seniority-cum-merit after a selection process.

UP’s rules also show that training and performance remain relevant after entry: every newly appointed Civil Judge (Junior Division) undergoes training during probation, the normal probation period is two years, and confirmation takes account of satisfactory prescribed training and work and conduct. Other states can use different cadre names, promotion criteria, training institutions, or timelines.

At the magisterial side, BNSS provides for High Court appointment of a first-class Judicial Magistrate as Chief Judicial Magistrate and allows appointment as Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate. Whether and when an individual officer reaches those assignments depends on the applicable service rules, seniority, merit, vacancy position, and High Court orders.
bullets: Entry/junior cadre: Civil Judge (Junior Division) or the state’s equivalent combined designation.
State-specific postings may include Civil Judge, Additional Civil Judge, or Judicial Magistrate First Class functions.
Illustrative UP promotion: Civil Judge (Junior Division) to Civil Judge (Senior Division), through High Court selection on seniority-cum-merit.
Higher magisterial leadership assignments can include Chief Judicial Magistrate or Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate where appointed by the High Court.

title: Civil Judge (Junior Division) in State Judicial Service
description: An entry-level state judicial officer who adjudicates civil matters in subordinate courts after qualifying the state Judicial Services Examination.

quick_facts.label: Service position
quick_facts.value: A Civil Judge (Junior Division) is an entry-level post in a State’s judicial service—i.e., a civil judicial post below District Judge. The exact cadre name, jurisdiction, and whether the officer is also assigned Judicial Magistrate functions depend on the State’s rules and posting orders.

quick_facts.label: Constitutional appointment framework
quick_facts.value: For judicial-service appointments other than District Judges, Article 234 provides for appointment by the State Governor under rules made after consultation with the State Public Service Commission and the relevant High Court; Article 235 places control over subordinate courts and officers below District Judge with the High Court.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry credential
quick_facts.value: A law degree is a core eligibility requirement in State-specific recruitment rules. For example, the Punjab Civil Service (Judicial Branch) rules applicable through the Punjab and Haryana High Court require an LL.B. from a university established by law and approved/recognised by the Bar Council of India, along with basic computer-application knowledge.

quick_facts.label: Selection route
quick_facts.value: Entry is ordinarily through the relevant State Judicial Services / PCS-J recruitment process, rather than one national examination. The governing State rules and recruitment notice determine the examination stages, syllabus, eligibility, reservation, vacancies, and timetable.

quick_facts.label: Training and departmental requirements
quick_facts.value: Requirements after selection are State-specific. As one current official example, Haryana’s rules require every Civil Judge (Junior Division) to undergo at least one year of training and require selected candidates to pass a departmental examination within two years of joining, subject to the High Court’s stated powers regarding exemption or extension.

sections.heading: What the role does
paragraphs: A Civil Judge (Junior Division) presides over civil matters assigned within the court’s territorial and pecuniary jurisdiction, applies procedural and substantive law, records and evaluates material placed before the court, and delivers judicial orders, judgments, and decrees. The Code of Civil Procedure provides that civil suits are instituted in the lowest-grade court competent to try them, while jurisdiction remains subject to statutory limits; consequently, the exact civil docket is determined by the applicable State law and local allocation of work.

In some State cadres, an entry-level judicial officer may also be required to work as a Judicial Magistrate or in both civil-judge and judicial-magistrate capacities. This is not a uniform national job allocation: for example, Haryana’s rules expressly permit this arrangement, and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita permits a High Court to confer Judicial Magistrate powers on a member of the State judicial service functioning as a civil-court judge.
bullets: Conduct proceedings fairly and independently, including managing hearings and issuing reasoned judicial decisions within assigned jurisdiction.
Apply civil procedure and the relevant substantive laws; jurisdiction and case types vary by State, court establishment, and posting.
Where empowered and posted accordingly, perform Judicial Magistrate functions in addition to civil-court work.

sections.heading: How entry into the cadre works
paragraphs: The canonical route is qualifying the Judicial Services Examination conducted under the particular State’s constitutional and service-rule framework. Article 234 makes this a State appointment process undertaken under rules made by the Governor after consultation with the State Public Service Commission and the High Court; it should therefore not be treated as a single, nationwide PCS-J syllabus or calendar.

Applicants should read the applicable State notification and rules in the recruitment year. A representative official rule set for the Punjab/Haryana judicial branch requires an LL.B. recognised by the Bar Council of India and basic computer knowledge. Its published examination syllabus includes civil-law papers, criminal-law material, English composition, a State-language paper, and viva voce; other States can prescribe materially different papers, language requirements, age limits, eligibility conditions, and stages.

Selection does not itself end professional formation. For example, Haryana’s current rules provide for a minimum one-year training period for each Civil Judge (Junior Division), and a departmental examination requirement after joining. Newly appointed Civil Judges in Uttar Pradesh have also been formally directed for induction and field training, illustrating the practical importance of post-appointment training.
bullets: Obtain the law qualification and meet the eligibility conditions in the relevant State’s live notification.
Prepare for the State-prescribed written examination and interview/viva voce, where applicable.
After appointment, complete induction/field training and any departmental tests required by that State’s rules.

sections.heading: Capabilities the examination and office demand
paragraphs: The role calls for strong legal analysis, disciplined legal writing, evidence-based reasoning, procedural accuracy, impartial decision-making, and clear communication. These are grounded in the subject areas and assessment methods used in judicial-service selection: the published Punjab/Haryana syllabus covers civil procedure and civil law, criminal law and procedure, evidence, legal-language/essay writing, and a viva voce intended to assess candidates’ personal qualities.

Digital competence is increasingly relevant to daily court functioning. One State rule set expressly requires basic computer-application knowledge for appointment, while the Department of Justice describes the eCourts programme as using technology to make processes in district and subordinate courts more efficient and to provide a unified, paperless interface under Phase III.
bullets: Command of civil procedure, evidence, substantive civil law, and—where the cadre requires it—criminal law and procedure.
Clear, precise judgment and order writing, including legal reasoning under time and record-management constraints.
Professional integrity, fairness, composure, and oral communication suitable for hearings and judicial decision-making.
Basic digital literacy and ability to work in technology-enabled court processes.

sections.heading: Court setting and institutional accountability
paragraphs: Civil Judges (Junior Division) work in the district and subordinate judiciary of a State, with postings and service administration shaped by the relevant High Court and State Government. Constitutionally, High Courts exercise control over district courts and subordinate courts, including posting and promotion of judicial-service officers below the District Judge level; the Department of Justice likewise states that administrative and disciplinary control over the subordinate judiciary rests with the concerned High Court and State Government.

The workplace is increasingly technology-enabled through eCourts infrastructure and process reform. The Department of Justice describes eCourts as a joint effort with the Supreme Court’s eCommittee and High Courts to improve judicial processes across district and subordinate courts.
bullets: Posting may be anywhere within the State judicial-service establishment, subject to the applicable service rules and High Court administration.
The officer works within an independent judicial institution, not as an advocate for either party or as an executive-department decision-maker.
Court operations may include digital case-management and other eCourts-enabled processes.

sections.heading: Career progression
paragraphs: The usual internal progression is from Civil Judge (Junior Division) to Civil Judge (Senior Division) or equivalent posts, followed by possible movement into the higher judicial service and District Judge-level roles under the applicable State rules. The exact service-length thresholds, selection criteria, quotas, and nomenclature vary across States and can be amended.

For example, an Allahabad High Court publication on the Uttar Pradesh Judicial Service Rules states that promotion to Civil Judge (Senior Division) is made from Civil Judges (Junior Division), using seniority-cum-merit. A Calcutta High Court notification similarly records promotion to the Civil Judge (Senior Division)/Chief Judicial Magistrate cadre from eligible Civil Judge (Junior Division)/Judicial Magistrate officers after six years’ continuous service in that specific 2021 process. These are examples, not a national minimum-service rule.

At the next level, higher judicial service rules can provide a mix of promotion, limited competitive examination, and direct recruitment from the Bar. The current Haryana Superior Judicial Service Rules, updated through March 27, 2026, illustrate that State-specific structure; candidates should verify the live rules of their own State.
bullets: Entry cadre: Civil Judge (Junior Division), with State-specific equivalent/combined designations possible.
Common internal next step: Civil Judge (Senior Division) or equivalent, subject to service rules and selection.
Longer-term advancement can lead to higher judicial service and District Judge-level appointments, through routes fixed by State rules.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: There is no single all-India salary figure for Civil Judges (Junior Division). Pay, allowances, pension-related terms, and revisions are governed by the relevant State’s pay rules and service conditions, and may differ by cadre, appointment date, location, and subsequent pay-revision orders. Compensation figures should therefore be checked against the current State government notification or High Court/State pay record rather than inferred from another State’s recruitment advertisement.

As a dated illustration only—not a nationwide salary benchmark—the Punjab and Haryana High Court’s Haryana gradation list published in 2026 displays ₹77,840 alongside several serving Civil Judge (Junior Division)/JMIC entries. The document does not establish that this figure is an identical current entitlement for every Civil Judge or for officers in other States.
bullets: Treat salary and allowances as State-specific and date-sensitive.
Verify the applicable pay matrix, dearness allowance, house-rent allowance, deductions, and probation/service conditions in the live State order.
Do not compare offers across States using a single quoted ‘PCS-J salary’ figure without checking the governing pay notification.

title: Commercial cum Ticket Clerk in Indian Railways
description: A railway ticketing and passenger-services clerk recruited through undergraduate-level RRB NTPC posts.

quick_facts.label: Recruitment category
quick_facts.value: Commercial Cum Ticket Clerk (CCTC) is an RRB Non-Technical Popular Categories (NTPC) undergraduate post, listed at Pay Level 3 in the 7th Central Pay Commission pay matrix.

quick_facts.label: Minimum education
quick_facts.value: In CEN 06/2024, the prescribed qualification was 12th (+2 stage) or equivalent with at least 50% aggregate marks; the 50% condition was waived for SC/ST/PwBD/ex-servicemen candidates and candidates holding qualifications higher than 12th.

quick_facts.label: Selection route
quick_facts.value: For CCTC, CEN 06/2024 specified two computer-based tests, followed by document verification and a Railway medical examination; unlike clerical-typist posts, it did not specify a typing-skill test for CCTC.

quick_facts.label: Medical standard
quick_facts.value: The CCTC post was notified with medical standard B2 in CEN 06/2024. Candidates must meet the applicable Railway medical-fitness requirements for the notified post.

quick_facts.label: Entry basic pay context
quick_facts.value: The CEN 06/2024 notification stated an initial basic pay of ₹21,700 for CCTC at Pay Level 3. This is a dated basic-pay figure; actual monthly gross and take-home pay vary with applicable allowances, place of posting, deductions, and later pay revisions.

quick_facts.label: Training
quick_facts.value: Indian Railways' published initial/promotion module for Commercial-cum-Ticket Clerks is 60 working days (360 hours), covering coaching and goods work, accounts, safety, IT, soft skills, field training, and examination.

sections.heading: What the role covers
paragraphs: A Commercial Cum Ticket Clerk works within Indian Railways' Commercial Department, whose functions include selling railway services, passenger amenities, ticketing, collection and accounting of traffic receipts, and passenger-facing service. At the post level, this points to frontline commercial and passenger-service work rather than train operation or engineering.

The published CCTC training curriculum includes coaching theory and practical work, goods theory and practical work, accounts, safety management, information technology, and field training. Accordingly, the role requires staff to apply ticketing and commercial procedures, use the relevant systems, handle records and money accurately where assigned, and provide courteous, rule-based assistance to passengers.
bullets: Work may involve ticketing and related passenger-commercial services under local Railway rules and the assigned office or station.
The precise mix of counter, station, ticket-checking-support, accounts, or other commercial duties is determined by the Railway administration and posting.

sections.heading: How to enter through RRB NTPC
paragraphs: The external-entry route is an RRB Centralised Employment Notice (CEN) for NTPC undergraduate posts when CCTC vacancies are notified. The candidate applies online to one chosen RRB and must satisfy the post parameters in that particular CEN, including education, age, nationality, medical standard, reservation documentation where applicable, and other conditions.

The CEN 06/2024 pattern for CCTC was first-stage CBT, second-stage CBT, document verification, and medical examination. Appointment is not made by the RRB itself: the CEN states that RRBs recommend empanelled candidates, while the relevant Railway Administration offers appointment after the prescribed checks.

Existing Railway staff may also enter the grade through departmental selection where a Railway administration notifies such a quota; for example, South Central Railway published a CCTC Level-3 selection under an LDCE quota. This is a separate internal route, not a substitute for an open RRB notification.
bullets: Use only the official RRB websites and the relevant detailed CEN for live eligibility, vacancy, fee, dates, category-wise conditions, and examination instructions.
Do not assume that dates, vacancy totals, age relaxations, or the selection timetable from CEN 06/2024 apply to a future recruitment cycle.

sections.heading: Skills developed and used
paragraphs: The formal training modules indicate the core capability areas: passenger/coaching commercial knowledge, goods-commercial knowledge, accounts, safety, information technology, ethical leadership and soft skills, and supervised field practice. These support accurate, customer-facing work in a safety-conscious public-service setting.

Practical strengths for aspirants include clear communication with a diverse travelling public, numerical and record-keeping accuracy, comfort with computerised ticketing and office systems, calm handling of queues or service issues, and disciplined compliance with fares, concessions, accounting, and safety procedures.
bullets: Computer familiarity matters: the initial course includes an information-technology module, and Indian Railways' commercial functions use passenger systems such as PRS and UTS.
A typing test was not prescribed for CCTC in CEN 06/2024, but computer use and accurate data entry remain relevant operational skills.

sections.heading: Posting and work environment
paragraphs: CCTC vacancies are notified for Indian Railways' zonal railways and production units, so candidates should be prepared for assignment within the Railway/RRB allocation reflected in the recruitment notice and appointment process. The broader Commercial Department provides ticketing, passenger services, claims and commercial functions across the railway system.

In practice, the work is public-facing and may be stationed at railway offices, booking or ticketing locations, and other commercial establishments. Official staff records show CCTC and Senior Commercial Cum Ticket Clerk personnel posted under ticket-checking staff at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, illustrating that actual workplace assignment can vary within the commercial organisation.
bullets: Expect rule-driven work, public interaction, use of commercial systems, and local supervisory arrangements.
Posting location, duties, shift arrangements, and transfer liability must be checked in the applicable CEN, Railway rules, and appointment terms rather than assumed from the job title.

sections.heading: Progression and professional development
paragraphs: Indian Railways' published Commercial training framework separately provides for CCTC initial/promotion training and for Senior Commercial Cum Ticket Clerk initial training. This documents a departmental development path into senior commercial-clerk work, although promotion is not automatic and depends on the applicable service rules, eligibility, vacancies, selection process, and Railway administration.

A Senior Commercial Cum Ticket Clerk has also been notified as a distinct higher-level NTPC graduate post at Pay Level 5 in Railway recruitment material. Candidates should treat this as evidence of a related senior role, not as a guarantee that every CCTC will progress through the same route or timeline.
bullets: Use departmental notifications and current Railway establishment rules for promotion eligibility and quotas.
The published refresher module for Commercial-cum-Ticket Clerks is mandatory every two years for the covered lower-grade combined cadre, supporting continuing operational learning.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: CEN 06/2024 placed CCTC at Level 3 of the 7th CPC pay matrix with an initial basic pay of ₹21,700. This should be read as the notification's entry basic-pay context, rather than as a current in-hand salary promise.

Actual earnings can differ materially by date and posting because central-government pay components and deductions may change, and because house-rent, dearness, transport and other allowances depend on the applicable rules and circumstances. Candidates should verify current pay and allowances from their appointment documents and official Railway/Central Government orders.
bullets: Use basic pay, not unverified online “in-hand salary” estimates, for a reliable comparison of the notified post.
The notified CEN's age, vacancy, fee, and pay details are recruitment-cycle-specific and may be revised through corrigenda or future CENs.

title: Community Health Officer
description: A healthcare professional under the National Health Mission (NHM) who leads a team at a Health and Wellness Centre, providing primary healthcare services to the community.

quick_facts.label: Role in the public-health system
quick_facts.value: A Community Health Officer (CHO) is the mid-level provider who leads the primary-health-care team at a Health and Wellness Centre–Sub Health Centre (HWC-SHC), working with multipurpose workers and ASHAs to deliver comprehensive primary health care.

quick_facts.label: Core qualification pattern
quick_facts.value: Eligibility is set through state/UT NHM recruitment notices. Recent official examples use GNM, B.Sc. Nursing or Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing plus valid state nursing/midwifery registration; states may recruit candidates into a Certificate in Community Health / Community Health Nursing training route before posting.

quick_facts.label: Clinical scope
quick_facts.value: CHOs provide care according to approved care pathways and standard treatment guidelines, coordinate chronic-disease case management initiated by medical officers or specialists, and may dispense medicines within the applicable Schedule K provision and standing orders.

quick_facts.label: Employment model
quick_facts.value: CHO/MLHP engagement is commonly implemented through state NHM arrangements rather than one uniform national cadre. Terms such as contract status, age limits, training bonds, assessment method and incentives are determined by the recruiting state or district notice.

quick_facts.label: Work setting
quick_facts.value: The usual base is an Ayushman Arogya Mandir / Health and Wellness Centre at sub-health-centre level, linked to a PHC that acts as a first referral point for conditions requiring escalation.

sections.heading: Responsibilities and service remit
paragraphs: At an HWC-SHC, the CHO combines clinical and public-health leadership. The Indian Public Health Standards assign CHOs functions including household listing and empanelment, clinical care under defined pathways, coordination of chronic-care case management, timely data use and reporting, local planning based on morbidity and mortality patterns, and engagement with community platforms and local government bodies.

The role is not limited to clinic consultations. The HWC model is intended to provide preventive, promotive, curative, rehabilitative and palliative care, including early identification, counselling, adherence support, follow-up, referral and health promotion. A CHO must therefore work within referral and treatment protocols and coordinate with the PHC medical officer and the frontline team rather than practise as an independent physician.
bullets: Maintain an empanelled household/population record and use service data for planning and reporting.
Provide the specified primary-care services and coordinate referrals, follow-up and chronic-disease care.
Lead and support the HWC team of frontline workers, including ASHAs and multipurpose workers.
Mobilise community action with VHSNCs, Mahila Arogya Samitis, self-help groups and PRI/ULB stakeholders.
Address health promotion and social/environmental determinants such as sanitation, water and behavioural risks through intersectoral coordination.

sections.heading: How entry typically works
paragraphs: There is no single India-wide CHO application form or permanently fixed eligibility rule. Recruitment is run by state or district NHM bodies, so applicants should treat the current official notification for the relevant state as controlling. Official NHM examples show a nursing route based on GNM, B.Sc. Nursing or Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing, valid state nursing/midwifery registration, selection assessment and community-health training before HWC posting.

For example, a Uttar Pradesh NHM CHO-CCHN recruitment notice specified GNM-RNRM, B.Sc. Nursing or Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing and registration with the UP Nurses & Midwives Council; it also described training followed by posting at an SC-HWC. Assam’s NHM CCH notice similarly described a six-month full-time theory-and-practical programme and listed B.Sc. Nursing/Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing or GNM with relevant registration among eligibility routes. These are examples, not universal rules.
bullets: Complete a recognised nursing qualification that meets the particular state notice, commonly GNM, B.Sc. Nursing or Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing.
Keep registration with the required State Nurses and Midwives/Nursing Council valid.
Apply through the relevant state or district NHM recruitment portal and complete the stated examination, document verification and other selection steps.
Where specified, complete the Certificate in Community Health / Community Health Nursing training and meet any posting, service-bond or local-placement conditions.

sections.heading: Skills that the role calls for
paragraphs: The official service model makes community-health nursing knowledge central: the CHO needs to assess common health needs, follow clinical pathways and standard treatment guidelines, recognise cases requiring referral, support long-term treatment adherence and use telehealth or referral coordination where available.

The role also requires operational public-health skills: maintaining population and service records, interpreting local health patterns, reporting accurately, planning with measurable targets, communicating with households and community institutions, and leading a mixed frontline team. Recruitment syllabi reinforce this breadth by covering community health, epidemiology, maternal and child health, immunisation, communicable and non-communicable diseases, emergencies, pharmacology, communication and computer-based skills.
bullets: Community assessment, screening, counselling, follow-up and safe referral.
Clinical-protocol adherence and awareness of the limits of delegated medicine dispensing.
Maternal, child, adolescent, communicable-disease and NCD programme knowledge.
Data recording, digital reporting, basic analysis and use of local population data.
Team leadership, respectful communication and community mobilisation.

sections.heading: Where and with whom CHOs work
paragraphs: CHOs are principally posted in primary-care facilities transformed as Health and Wellness Centres, now presented by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare as Ayushman Arogya Mandirs. At the sub-health-centre level, the CHO leads a team that includes male and female multipurpose workers and ASHAs.

The role is community-facing and facility-based. Services extend across households and community platforms, the HWC itself, and referral facilities. PHCs linked to a cluster of HWCs serve as the first referral point for many conditions; the PHC medical officer is responsible for ensuring delivery of comprehensive primary-health-care services across the linked HWCs.
bullets: Base facility: HWC-SHC / Ayushman Arogya Mandir, with rural or urban deployment depending on the state programme.
Frontline collaborators: ASHAs and multipurpose health workers.
Clinical and referral collaborators: PHC medical officers, staff nurses, pharmacists, laboratory personnel and higher referral facilities.
Community collaborators: local self-help groups, VHSNC/MAS platforms and Panchayati Raj or urban local-body institutions.

sections.heading: Progression and adjacent pathways
paragraphs: CHO is a service role, not a nationally standardised automatic promotion ladder. Progression depends on state NHM staffing rules, recruitment processes, experience and further qualifications. For nurses seeking deeper clinical, teaching, management or public-health preparation, an M.Sc. Nursing is one formal higher-education option: Indian Nursing Council eligibility information requires RN/RM (or equivalent) registration, a qualifying B.Sc./Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing degree with the stipulated marks, and the stated work-experience condition.

Other adjacent options include applying for Nursing Officer recruitment through AIIMS NORCET when the applicable notice’s requirements are met, pursuing recognised public-health-nursing qualifications, or moving into supervisory/public-health posts when a specific employer’s vacancy criteria permit it. The INC lists a Post Basic Diploma in Public Health Nursing and maintains information on recognised higher nursing qualifications; AIIMS NORCET notices set their own eligibility and selection conditions.
bullets: M.Sc. Nursing: a higher nursing qualification route subject to INC eligibility and institution admission rules.
AIIMS NORCET / Nursing Officer: a separate competitive recruitment route, not a CHO promotion.
Public-health nursing: recognised post-basic public-health nursing study may strengthen fit for public-health roles.
Nursing supervision or programme management: possible only where the recruiting employer’s experience, registration and qualification criteria are met.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: There is no reliable national CHO salary figure because NHM engagement and pay are administered through state and district notices, and may combine a fixed monthly amount with a performance-linked component. Applicants should rely on the pay clause in the live advertisement for their state, not on national averages or coaching-site estimates.

As dated illustrations only: a UP NHM CHO-CCHN notice stated a training stipend of ₹10,000 per month and, on posting, up to ₹35,500 per month consisting of ₹20,500 salary plus up to ₹15,000 performance-based incentive. A Kozhikode NHM notice dated December 30, 2025 listed a Mid Level Service Provider rate of ₹20,500 per month during training and ₹20,500 plus ₹1,000 fixed travelling allowance after successful training. Neither example establishes current pay elsewhere in India.
bullets: Check whether the post is contractual, its duration and renewal terms.
Separate fixed remuneration from performance incentives, travel allowance, training stipend and deductions.
Review any service bond, minimum-service obligation, posting-location condition and training-cost support before accepting an offer.
Confirm the current figure only from the recruiting NHM/state/district notice.

title: Constable (General Duty) in CAPFs
description: An entry-level security role in India's Central Armed Police Forces (e.g., BSF, CISF, CRPF), secured through the SSC GD exam.

quick_facts.label: Primary recruitment route
quick_facts.value: The usual entry route is SSC’s Constable (GD) examination, which recruits for Constable (GD) posts in CAPFs; the SSC GD 2026 notice also included SSF and Rifleman (GD) in Assam Rifles.

quick_facts.label: Education requirement
quick_facts.value: For the SSC GD 2026 cycle, applicants had to have passed Matriculation/10th Class from a recognized board or university by January 1, 2026. Eligibility dates and conditions can change in later notices.

quick_facts.label: Age context
quick_facts.value: For SSC GD 2026, the prescribed age was 18–23 years as of January 1, 2026, with category-based upper-age relaxations set out in the notice. Candidates should use the age date in the cycle they apply for.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: The SSC GD 2026 process comprised a computer-based examination, Physical Efficiency Test, Physical Standard Test, medical examination, and document verification.

quick_facts.label: Force allocation
quick_facts.value: In the SSC GD 2026 notice, candidates had to state preferences across BSF, CISF, CRPF, SSB, ITBP, Assam Rifles, and SSF; final allocation was based on merit, preferences, vacancies, and qualifying the physical and medical stages.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: The SSC GD 2026 notice specified Pay Level 3, ₹21,700–₹69,100, for the advertised posts. This is a pay-level range rather than a take-home-pay guarantee; allowances and deductions depend on applicable rules and posting circumstances.

sections.heading: Responsibilities and operational purpose
paragraphs: Constable (GD) work varies substantially by force and posting. CRPF describes duties that include crowd and riot control, counter-insurgency and left-wing-extremism operations, election-security arrangements, protection of vital installations and VIPs, disaster rescue and relief, and support during wartime. A constable may contribute to such duties as part of a disciplined unit under the force’s command structure.

CISF illustrates a different deployment profile: its published duty charter includes access control, perimeter security, protection of designated critical installations, crime prevention and control, escort of important consignments, personnel security, and counter-terror quick-response duties. Therefore, candidates should not assume that all CAPF postings resemble either a conventional local-police beat or a single static-security role.
bullets: Expect force-specific assignments, collective operational work, strict adherence to lawful orders, and readiness for relocation.
The actual nature of duty depends on the force allotted, unit, location, security environment, and operational requirement.

sections.heading: Entry through SSC GD
paragraphs: For this node, the principal entry route is the Staff Selection Commission’s Constable (GD) recruitment. In the SSC GD 2026 notice, applications were online and the recruitment sequence was CBE, PET/PST, medical examination, and document verification. The CAPFs conduct the physical, medical, and document-verification stages under the recruitment arrangement described in the notice.

The 2026 CBE was an objective paper of 80 questions and 160 marks, covering General Intelligence and Reasoning, General Knowledge and General Awareness, Elementary Mathematics, and English/Hindi. The notice stated that final selection and force allocation used normalized CBE merit, NCC bonus marks where applicable, force preference, and satisfaction of physical, medical, and other stated conditions.

Entry requirements are cycle-specific. For example, SSC GD 2026 required a recognized Matriculation/10th pass by January 1, 2026 and set the standard age band at 18–23 years on that date. Always read the current SSC notice rather than relying on an earlier cycle’s dates, vacancies, standards, or relaxations.
bullets: Monitor SSC notices for the live application window, vacancy distribution, domicile provisions, physical standards, medical standards, and category relaxations.
Enter force preferences carefully: the 2026 notice stated that all listed force preferences were essential and that preferences could not be changed after application completion.

PET/PST readiness is essential. In the 2026 notice, the standard race benchmark outside Ladakh was 5 km in 24 minutes for male candidates and 1.6 km in 8½ minutes for female candidates; prescribed standards may change in future notices.

sections.heading: Skills to build for selection and service
paragraphs: For SSC GD selection preparation, build foundational reasoning, general awareness, elementary mathematics, and basic English or Hindi comprehension, because these were the four CBE components in the SSC GD 2026 scheme. The same notice described questions as being at Matriculation level and applied negative marking for wrong answers.

Physical conditioning is equally important. The SSC GD 2026 PET required candidates to complete a timed race, while PST included measurement of height, weight, and chest where applicable. A sustainable running programme, mobility work, injury prevention, recovery habits, and familiarity with the current official standards are more useful than last-minute training.

For service, the official roles described by CRPF and CISF point to the value of discipline, situational awareness, teamwork, clear communication, alertness at security posts, ability to follow procedures, and composure during public-order, emergency, or high-security duties.
bullets: Prepare from SSC’s official notice and mock-test resources, not solely from coaching material.
Train progressively for the notified PET benchmark and obtain appropriate medical advice before intense physical training.
Develop Hindi/English comprehension and numeracy alongside physical fitness; the written test remains decisive for merit under the cited scheme.

sections.heading: Workplace and deployment reality
paragraphs: This is an all-India public-security career rather than a job tied to one city. CRPF describes itself as having a nationwide presence and lists duties across public-order, election, internal-security, protection, and disaster-response contexts. CISF reports deployments at critical infrastructure and public-facing sites such as airports, ports, power facilities, government buildings, metro systems, and other strategic establishments.

Work settings can therefore range from field units and camps to transport hubs and guarded installations. Posting, schedules, accommodation arrangements, risk exposure, and the balance between static and mobile duty are determined by the allotted force and operational need, not by the SSC exam alone.
bullets: Be prepared for transfers and service away from one’s home district or state.

Compare force missions before expressing SSC preferences; CISF’s infrastructure-security emphasis and CRPF’s broad internal-security/public-order role illustrate why the day-to-day environment can differ.

sections.heading: Progression after appointment
paragraphs: Promotion structures are force- and cadre-specific. CRPF’s published career-prospects page describes a General Duty progression from Constable to Head Constable, then Head Constable to Sub-Inspector, and Sub-Inspector to Inspector. For the CRPF Constable-to-Head-Constable route shown there, the published conditions include a minimum of eight years of service from enlistment, completion of prescribed Junior Cadre and Section Commander courses, a satisfactory service record, and no specified recent adverse reports or major punishments.

CRPF also publishes a Head Constable Promotional Course designed to prepare senior constables awaiting promotion to perform as effective section second-in-command operationally and administratively. This supports Head Constable as a meaningful next career node, but promotion is not automatic: vacancies, qualifying courses, service record, medical fitness, and force rules matter.
bullets: Treat Head Constable as a common immediate progression target, not an assured time-bound outcome.
Maintain fitness, conduct, course readiness, and a strong service record throughout the constable stage.
For officer-level progression, assess both internal promotional rules and separate competitive routes such as UPSC CAPF (AC), which have distinct eligibility and selection requirements.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: As dated recruitment context, SSC’s Constable (GD) 2026 notice listed Pay Level 3 at ₹21,700–₹69,100 for all posts covered by that notice. This figure should be read as the notified pay-level range, not as a universal monthly in-hand amount.

A candidate’s actual monthly pay can differ from the pay-level figure because government compensation is administered through applicable pay, allowance, posting, tax, pension/NPS, and other deduction rules. Applicants should use the appointment offer and the current force and central-government rules for a posting-specific estimate rather than treating an old SSC notification as a permanent salary quote.
bullets: Use the current SSC notification to verify the pay level for the recruitment cycle.
Do not compare postings solely on the basic pay range: force allocation and place of posting can affect the applicable compensation context.

title: Data Entry Operator (DEO)
description: A clerical post responsible for entering, updating, and maintaining data in computer systems for various government organizations, such as the C&AG.

quick_facts.label: Primary entry examination
quick_facts.value: For central-government DEO and DEO Grade ‘A’ vacancies covered by SSC, the usual open-recruitment route is the Combined Higher Secondary (10+2) Level Examination (CHSL).

quick_facts.label: Minimum education for most CHSL DEO posts
quick_facts.value: The SSC CHSL 2025 notice required a pass in Class 12 (or equivalent) from a recognised board or university for DEO/DEO Grade ‘A’ posts, except for specified departments that require Science with Mathematics in Class 12.

quick_facts.label: Skill-test benchmark
quick_facts.value: In the SSC CHSL 2025 scheme, the mandatory DEO skill test used a 15-minute computer data-entry test: 8,000 key depressions per hour for most DEO posts and 15,000 key depressions per hour for the specified higher-speed posts.

quick_facts.label: C&AG cadre levels
quick_facts.value: C&AG office disclosures list DEO Grade ‘A’ as Group C, non-gazetted, Pay Level 4, and DEO Grade ‘B’ as Group C, non-gazetted, Pay Level 5.

quick_facts.label: C&AG Grade A to Grade B progression
quick_facts.value: Under the C&AG DEO recruitment rules, DEO Grade ‘A’ staff can be considered for Grade ‘B’ promotion after five years’ regular service in Grade A and completion of prescribed two-week relevant training.

sections.heading: Responsibilities: accurate electronic records and department-specific data work
paragraphs: A government DEO’s work is primarily computer-based record handling. The exact dataset and software differ by office, but an official Fisheries Survey of India DEO duty list illustrates the scope: compiling incoming data, entering and validating records, preserving source sheets, preparing periodic reports, monitoring email-based reporting, and entering operational or expenditure details for reports.

In practice, this makes accuracy, validation, record traceability and timely reporting central to the role—not merely fast typing. Some government offices also assign DEOs e-service workflows and reconciliations; for example, an Odisha RTI disclosure describes online entry, reconciliation of fees and charges, and generation of books and certificates in an e-registration system.
bullets: Enter, compile and update departmental data in the assigned computer system.
Check and validate entries against source documents and retain required records.
Produce recurring reports, registers, statements or system-generated outputs.
Undertake related data-processing duties assigned by the employing office; the mix is department-specific.

sections.heading: Entry route: SSC CHSL, Class 12 eligibility and a qualifying data-entry test
paragraphs: For the central-government DEO posts represented by this node, SSC CHSL is the principal direct-recruitment pathway. The C&AG’s establishment material states that direct recruitment to DEO Grade ‘A’ is made from candidates sponsored by the Staff Selection Commission, while the SSC CHSL notice explicitly includes DEO and DEO Grade ‘A’ posts.

For the 2025 CHSL notice, most DEO/DEO Grade ‘A’ candidates needed Class 12 or equivalent. DEO/DEO Grade ‘A’ posts in the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Ministry of Culture and SSC required Class 12 Science with Mathematics. The same notice accepted qualifications from recognised institutions, including specified Open and Distance Learning qualifications under its recognition conditions.

The SSC’s 2025 selection scheme placed DEO candidates in Tier II, which included Mathematics, Reasoning and General Intelligence, English, General Awareness, a Computer Knowledge Test, and the mandatory Skill Test. The relevant notification should always be checked for the particular CHSL cycle because age dates, vacancies, departments, standards and eligibility wording can change.
bullets: Complete Class 12 or an accepted equivalent qualification; verify whether a selected DEO preference has the Science-with-Mathematics requirement.
Apply through the SSC CHSL notification for the applicable recruitment cycle and express post preferences as instructed.
Prepare for the Tier II academic modules, Computer Knowledge Test and compulsory DEO Skill Test.

A Certificate in Computer Applications, undergraduate degree or recognised distance-learning degree can strengthen computer or subject knowledge, but SSC’s cited baseline eligibility for most DEO posts is Class 12—not a bachelor’s degree.

sections.heading: Skills to build: speed with accuracy, computer fluency and data control
paragraphs: The SSC DEO Skill Test directly measures accurate computer entry at a prescribed key-depression rate, so keyboard fluency and sustained accuracy are essential. SSC’s Tier II scheme also includes a Computer Knowledge Test, while official DEO duty descriptions show the need to compile, validate, preserve and report on data.

Useful preparation therefore combines timed data-entry practice with practical competence in the office software and data systems used by the recruiting department. Candidates should treat the speed target as an examination standard rather than as a complete description of on-the-job competence: routine work also calls for careful checking, organised digital records and confidentiality-conscious handling of official information.
bullets: Fast, accurate keyboard data entry and error checking.
Computer knowledge tested through SSC CHSL, plus comfort with office data systems.
Data validation, document organisation and preservation of source records.
Ability to compile periodic reports and follow office procedures precisely.

sections.heading: Workplace: office-based central-government service, with department-specific assignments
paragraphs: DEO work is generally desk- and system-based, but the employer determines the records, applications and operational context. Within the Indian Audit and Accounts Department, C&AG materials identify DEO Grade ‘A’, Grade ‘B’ and Grade ‘D’ cadres in Audit and Accounts & Entitlement offices, and C&AG office disclosures show Grade A and Grade B as Group C, non-gazetted EDP posts.

Candidates should not assume a local posting. The SSC CHSL 2025 notice stated that its posts carry All India Service Liability, meaning a selected candidate may be required to serve anywhere in India. Actual posting, transfer and day-to-day responsibilities depend on the user ministry, department or office receiving the vacancy.
bullets: Predominantly computer-based office work handling the employer’s records and reporting systems.
Potential placement in different central-government ministries, departments or C&AG/IA&AD offices.
Location and exact workflow depend on the allotted user department; SSC notified All India Service Liability for the covered CHSL posts.

sections.heading: Progression: DEO Grade A to Grade B, plus departmental examination eligibility
paragraphs: In the C&AG/IA&AD EDP cadre, a defined progression exists from DEO Grade ‘A’ to DEO Grade ‘B’. The recruitment rules and C&AG establishment manual state that Grade A staff with five years of regular service and completion of prescribed two-week relevant training are eligible for promotion to Grade B. C&AG training material also refers to departmental examination and training arrangements for Grade A officials progressing to Grade B.

A separate longer-term opportunity may arise through departmental examinations where service rules permit. C&AG’s examination FAQ says that DEO Grade A, B and D staff in Audit/A&E offices who have completed probation and at least three years’ continuous service in specified capacities may be eligible to appear for the relevant departmental examination. This is eligibility to sit an examination, not an automatic promotion or a guarantee of a particular post.
bullets: Join as DEO/DEO Grade A through the notified recruitment route.
Complete probation, departmental training and required service milestones.
For the C&AG cadre, seek consideration for DEO Grade B after the prescribed five years in Grade A and relevant training.
Review the current departmental examination and promotion rules of the employing office before planning a move.

sections.heading: Compensation context: central pay levels rather than a single fixed take-home salary
paragraphs: Compensation varies by post, location, allowances and prevailing government orders. As dated context, SSC’s CHSL 2025 notice listed DEO posts at Pay Level 4 (₹25,500–₹81,100) and Pay Level 5 (₹29,200–₹92,300), while DEO Grade ‘A’ was listed at Pay Level 4 (₹25,500–₹81,100). C&AG office RTI disclosures likewise identify DEO Grade A with Level 4 and Grade B with Level 5.

These are pay-matrix basic-pay ranges, not promised in-hand salary figures. The eventual pay depends on the offered post, pay fixation and applicable allowances and deductions; applicants should use the notice for their own recruitment cycle and the appointing department’s current rules.
bullets: DEO Grade A: commonly shown in official SSC/C&AG material at Pay Level 4.
DEO Grade B in the C&AG EDP cadre: commonly shown at Pay Level 5.
Treat 2025 SSC amounts as historical recruitment-notice context; confirm pay and allowances in the current appointment documentation.

title: Data Entry Operator Grade B
description: A higher-level government data-entry post with greater responsibility for data processing, validation, records management, and supervision of junior operators.

quick_facts.label: Role scope
quick_facts.value: “Data Entry Operator Grade B” is not a single uniform India-wide job specification: central-government cadres and individual employers use the title with different recruitment methods, qualification requirements and pay levels. Candidates should rely on the recruitment rules and advertisement for the specific department and post code.

quick_facts.label: Central SSC EDP-cadre status
quick_facts.value: Under the Electronic Data Processing Cadre (Group C post) Recruitment Rules, 2024 for the Staff Selection Commission, DEO Grade B is a General Central Service, Group C, non-gazetted and non-ministerial post at Pay Matrix Level 5 (basic-pay range ₹29,200–₹92,300).

quick_facts.label: One documented internal route
quick_facts.value: In the SSC Electronic Data Processing cadre, DEO Grade B is filled by promotion from DEO Grade A after five years of regular Level-4 service and four weeks of relevant training; if promotion cannot fill the post, the rules provide for deputation.

quick_facts.label: Recent recruitment context
quick_facts.value: SSC’s 2025 Selection Post Phase XIII notice included a DEO Grade B vacancy at the Central Leprosy Teaching and Research Institute, Directorate General of Health Services, with an age band of 18–30, graduation-and-above qualification category, and Pay Level 6—illustrating that department-specific advertised posts can differ from the SSC EDP-cadre rules.

sections.heading: What the work involves
paragraphs: The evidence supports a records-and-systems support role rather than a universally defined supervisory position. In a June 2024 LBSNAA vacancy for DEO Grade B, the stated responsibilities were entering information into computer databases for record keeping, collecting data for entry, organising files, maintaining records of computer equipment (including printers and UPS units), and completing other related duties assigned by the employer.

A candidate should therefore expect accuracy-sensitive data handling, file and record organisation, and basic stewardship of office IT assets. The supplied “higher-level” description may apply in some offices, but official material located for this guide does not establish supervision of junior operators as a universal Grade-B duty; the exact job description is employer- and cadre-specific.
bullets: Enter, organise and maintain official data and digital records.
Collect and prepare source material before entry, then keep files orderly and retrievable.
Maintain administrative records relating to assigned computer peripherals and power-backup equipment.
Read the vacancy circular or recruitment rules for the particular ministry, department, institute and post code before assuming specialised, validation or supervisory duties.

sections.heading: Entry routes and eligibility: identify the employing cadre first
paragraphs: There is no one universal entrance examination or qualification rule attached to the title. For the SSC Electronic Data Processing cadre governed by the 2024 rules, DEO Grade B is not a direct-recruit post: the prescribed method is promotion, failing which deputation. The promotion feeder is DEO Grade A at Level 4 with five years of regular service and successful completion of four weeks’ relevant training.

For deputation in that SSC cadre, the rules require Central Government officers holding an analogous post, or officers with five years of regular Level-4 service, plus 12th-standard Science with Mathematics and a computer speed test of at least 15,000 key depressions per hour. These are cadre-specific conditions—not a claim about every post carrying the Grade-B title.

Other employers may use different routes. For example, LBSNAA’s 2024 vacancy was through deputation and required a recognised university degree and at least 8,000 key depressions per hour. Separately, SSC’s 2025 Selection Post notice listed a Grade-B vacancy at the Central Leprosy Teaching and Research Institute as a graduation-and-above, 18–30, Level-6 position. Always apply the notice for the exact post, not a generic online eligibility summary.
bullets: For serving SSC EDP-cadre DEO Grade A staff: monitor departmental promotion eligibility, service records and prescribed training.
For deputation opportunities: verify parent-cadre status, analogous/feeder-grade service, qualification, typing-speed and tenure conditions in the vacancy circular.
For direct/open-market vacancies where advertised: track the responsible recruiting body—often SSC Selection Posts or the relevant employer—and use its named post code, region and advertisement.
Treat all age, educational, speed-test, vacancy and reservation conditions as advertisement-specific and time-bound.

sections.heading: Skills worth building
paragraphs: Fast, accurate computer data entry is an explicitly tested or required capability in multiple official Grade-B sources. The SSC EDP-cadre rules specify a computer speed test of at least 15,000 key depressions per hour for the deputation route, while LBSNAA’s 2024 deputation vacancy specified at least 8,000 key depressions per hour. The difference reinforces that candidates must prepare for the standard in the relevant notice.

Beyond speed, the documented duties make careful data handling, file organisation, records discipline and familiarity with routine office hardware practical priorities. A strong candidate should be able to preserve accuracy while working from source documents and follow departmental processes for official records and equipment.
bullets: Keyboard fluency and accuracy under the applicable computer speed-test standard.
Data-quality discipline: careful transcription, checking source material and maintaining orderly records.
Digital file organisation and basic office database/spreadsheet workflows.
Routine awareness of office computer, printer and UPS record-keeping requirements.
Ability to follow employer-specific confidentiality, retention and administrative procedures.

sections.heading: Where Grade-B posts can sit
paragraphs: The title appears in varied public-sector settings. LBSNAA advertised a Grade-B post at its civil-services training academy in Mussoorie, while SSC’s 2025 Selection Post notice listed a Grade-B post at the Central Leprosy Teaching and Research Institute under the Directorate General of Health Services. This range means the day-to-day data domain can be training/administration, health or another department-specific function.

The SSC EDP-cadre rules classify their Grade-B role as General Central Service, Group C, non-gazetted and non-ministerial. That classification should not automatically be transferred to every state-government, autonomous-body, project or other central-department post using the same title.
bullets: Potential settings include central training institutions, health-service institutes and other government offices.
Work is generally office- and computer-based, but the information systems, records and operational context depend on the employer.
Confirm the service classification, place of posting, transfer liability and reporting structure in the individual notice or recruitment rules.

sections.heading: Career progression
paragraphs: A documented progression route exists within the SSC Electronic Data Processing cadre: DEO Grade A at Level 4 can be considered for promotion to DEO Grade B after five years of regular service and successful completion of four weeks of relevant training. The Grade-B post is expressly described as non-selection in those rules, and promotion is the first prescribed filling method.

This is a concrete cadre route, not a universal hierarchy for every role labelled DEO Grade B. In other organisations, Grade B may be filled by deputation, direct/open recruitment, or an employer-specific promotion arrangement. Examine the applicable recruitment rules and vacancy notice to understand whether there is a higher post, departmental examination, training requirement or transfer route.
bullets: Build a clean record of regular service, relevant training and assessed performance where departmental promotion applies.
Maintain documentation needed for deputation: service particulars, vigilance/disciplinary clearance where requested, educational records and speed-test evidence if stipulated.
Do not infer a guaranteed next designation solely from the “Grade B” label; career ladders are cadre-specific.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: Pay must be read against the governing cadre and the dated advertisement. In the SSC Electronic Data Processing Cadre Recruitment Rules, 2024, DEO Grade B is Pay Matrix Level 5, with the stated basic-pay range of ₹29,200–₹92,300. LBSNAA’s June 2024 deputation circular likewise identified its Grade-B post as Level 5 and stated that dearness allowance, house-rent allowance and other allowances would be admissible under Central Government orders from time to time.

However, SSC’s 2025 Selection Post Phase XIII notice listed the Central Leprosy Teaching and Research Institute Grade-B vacancy at Level 6. Thus, ₹29,200–₹92,300 is useful 2024 Level-5 basic-pay context for the SSC EDP cadre; it is not a reliable universal salary figure for every Grade-B vacancy. Take-home pay depends on the notified level, city-based allowances, deductions, service conditions and rules in force at appointment.
bullets: Use the pay level and basic-pay range printed in the specific recruitment rules or advertisement.
Separate basic pay from allowances and net take-home pay.
Treat compensation figures as dated context: the cited Level-5 range is from 2024 rules, while the cited Level-6 example is from an SSC 2025 vacancy notice.

title: Dental Hygienist in Indian Railways
description: A Railway dental-services professional who assists with oral-health assessment, preventive dental care, and dental clinic procedures.

quick_facts.label: Role scope
quick_facts.value: A dental hygienist is a non-dentist, non-medical-practitioner professional who scales, cleans or polishes teeth and gives dental-hygiene instruction; the Dental Hygienists Course Regulations state that the hygienist works under a registered dental surgeon’s supervision.

quick_facts.label: Railway recruitment channel
quick_facts.value: The post has been notified through Railway Recruitment Boards’ centralized paramedical recruitment process. In CEN 04/2024, Dental Hygienist was one of the paramedical posts notified.

quick_facts.label: Eligibility in the 2024 RRB notice
quick_facts.value: CEN 04/2024 required a science degree with Biology, a two-year Dental Hygiene diploma/certificate from a Dental Council of India-recognized institute, Dental Council of India registration as a dental hygienist, and two years’ hygienist experience. The notice allowed discretionary relaxation of the experience requirement for SC/ST candidates where sufficient eligible candidates were not available.

quick_facts.label: 2024 pay and medical standard
quick_facts.value: For the 2024 notification only, the post was Pay Level 6 under the 7th CPC, with initial pay of ₹35,400 and medical standard C2. Pay, allowances, medical standards, age rules and vacancies must be checked in the specific future CEN.

quick_facts.label: 2024 vacancy context
quick_facts.value: CEN 04/2024 notified three Dental Hygienist vacancies across all RRBs, with an age range of 18–36 years as on January 1, 2025. This was a recruitment-specific figure, not a forecast of future vacancies.

sections.heading: What the role involves
paragraphs: The statutory training framework defines dental-hygiene work around preventive oral care: scaling, cleaning and polishing teeth, along with giving dental-hygiene instruction. It places the hygienist under the supervision of a registered dental surgeon, so this is an allied dental-services role rather than an independent dentist role.

The prescribed course content supports practical work in oral prophylaxis, plaque and calculus management, brushing and flossing instruction, tooth polishing, topical fluoride application, dental-health education, community/public-health dentistry and preventive dentistry. In a Railway dental-service setting, the exact duty allocation will depend on the employing Railway administration and supervising dental surgeon.
bullets: Provide preventive oral-hygiene procedures within the authorized/supervised scope.
Educate patients on oral hygiene and preventive practices.
Support dental-clinic and oral-health-prevention work using training in dental hygiene, prophylaxis and dental public health.

sections.heading: Entry route through RRB paramedical recruitment
paragraphs: The practical route is to first obtain the requisite dental-hygiene education and professional registration, then apply when an RRB centralized paramedical notification includes Dental Hygienist vacancies. The most recent notice located for this role, CEN 04/2024, specified a Biology-based science degree, a two-year Dental Hygiene diploma/certificate from a DCI-recognized institute, registration as a dental hygienist, and two years of relevant experience.

The underlying Dental Council regulations prescribe a two-academic-year Dental Hygienist Diploma and set the course-entry baseline at 10+2/intermediate with Physics, Chemistry and Biology. Candidates should distinguish this educational admission requirement from the more demanding qualification criteria that an individual RRB recruitment notice may prescribe.

For CEN 04/2024, the recruitment sequence evidenced on the official RRB page included a computer-based test, shortlisting for document verification, and medical examination. Recruitment notices, eligibility cut-off dates, examination arrangements and selection stages can change, so applicants should use the detailed CEN published for the cycle in which they apply.
bullets: Complete 10+2 with Physics, Chemistry and Biology for admission to the regulated diploma pathway.
Complete the two-year Dental Hygienist Diploma/recognized equivalent and secure the registration required by the applicable RRB notice.
Monitor official RRB notices for the post, submit one application as instructed, and complete CBT, document verification and medical examination when called.

sections.heading: Skills developed and assessed
paragraphs: The regulated curriculum emphasizes both clinical preventive-care competence and patient education. Its listed study areas include dental anatomy, physiology and histology, pathology and microbiology, dental radiology, nutrition, dental hygiene and oral prophylaxis, community/public-health dentistry, preventive dentistry, ethics and jurisprudence, dental materials, and basic computer knowledge.

Accordingly, candidates benefit from careful clinical technique, infection-control and instrument-handling discipline, clear communication for oral-hygiene instruction, accurate record-oriented work, and the ability to work as part of a dental team under a registered dental surgeon.
bullets: Oral prophylaxis, scaling-related knowledge and polishing techniques.
Patient education on plaque control, brushing, flossing and preventive oral care.
Understanding of preventive dentistry, community dental health, ethics and clinical teamwork.
Basic computer knowledge and conscientious clinical documentation practices.

sections.heading: Railway employment setting
paragraphs: This is a Railway paramedical post recruited through RRBs. In the 2024 recruitment notice it carried medical standard C2, and candidates could indicate preferences for eligible Railway Zones and posts within the RRB selected; the notice also stated that RRB-wise and Railway-wise vacancies were provisional. Therefore, location and the particular Railway administration are determined by the notification, preferences, merit and available vacancies—not by a universally fixed posting location.

The professional dental-hygiene regulations envisage clinical training with dental chairs, ultrasonic scalers, hand instruments and sterilization facilities, and require the hygienist to work under a registered dental surgeon. Those requirements provide useful context for the clinical and supervised nature of the work, but an individual Railway facility’s equipment and daily workflow can vary.
bullets: Government Railway health-service/paramedical employment after RRB selection and allocation.
A supervised dental-care environment rather than independent dental practice.
Potential placement depends on the RRB notice, zone preferences, merit and vacancy availability.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: Compensation should be read from the applicable recruitment notice rather than treated as a permanent salary promise. In CEN 04/2024, Dental Hygienist was listed at 7th CPC Pay Level 6 with initial pay of ₹35,400. The notification’s figures were tied to that 2024 recruitment and do not by themselves establish current take-home pay or future pay terms.

Actual earnings can vary with the applicable central-government pay rules, admissible allowances, place of posting, deductions and any changes made in later notifications or pay-policy decisions. Verify the detailed CEN and appointment terms before making financial decisions.
bullets: 2024 notice context: Pay Level 6, initial pay ₹35,400.
Do not equate initial basic pay with take-home salary.
Treat vacancies, age limits, allowances and compensation as recruitment-cycle-specific.
