title: Inspector of Income Tax in CBDT
description: A Group C post responsible for assessing, verifying, and processing income tax records and conducting raids.

quick_facts.label: Current classification
quick_facts.value: Inspector of Income Tax in the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) is listed as a Group B post in the SSC Combined Graduate Level Examination (CGLE) 2026 notice. This corrects the supplied node description’s “Group C” label; SSC also issued a 2025 corrigendum changing this post’s classification from Group C to Group B.

quick_facts.label: Main entry route
quick_facts.value: The principal direct-recruitment route is SSC’s Combined Graduate Level Examination, followed by post/department preference and final allotment under the applicable SSC notice.

quick_facts.label: Education and age context
quick_facts.value: For CGLE 2026, the post was listed with an 18–30 age limit. SSC’s general qualification for posts not assigned a special qualification was a bachelor’s degree from a recognised university or equivalent; candidates should always check the notice for their own examination year and applicable relaxations.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: The CGLE 2026 notice placed the post at Pay Level 7, with the stated pay-matrix range of ₹44,900–₹1,42,400. This is basic-pay matrix context, not a guaranteed in-hand salary: allowances, deductions, place of posting and future pay revisions can change the amount received.

quick_facts.label: Geographic allocation
quick_facts.value: CBDT has previously sought region preferences from selected Income Tax Inspectors and stated that regional allocation is made on merit-cum-preference. The 2023 preference form covered 18 regions, illustrating that postings can be across India rather than confined to one city.

sections.heading: What the role does
paragraphs: An Income Tax Inspector works within the Income Tax Department under CBDT, the direct-tax board overseen by the Department of Revenue. The work involves applying tax law and handling records and information connected with direct-tax administration; exact duties depend on the charge, supervising officers and assignment.

The shorthand claim that every Inspector “conducts raids” is too broad. An Inspector can exercise specified survey-related powers when authorised: inspecting books and documents available at the survey location, checking or verifying cash, stock or valuables, and marking or copying records. Search-and-seizure operations are a separate, legally controlled enforcement function; an Inspector’s involvement, if assigned, should not be confused with an independent power to initiate or lead every search operation.
bullets: Review and verify documentary, financial and business information within assigned tax-administration work.
Conduct or assist with authorised survey and information-gathering activity, following the statutory limits and directions of the competent authority.
Maintain accuracy, confidentiality, evidence discipline and procedural compliance when handling taxpayer records.

sections.heading: How to enter through SSC CGL
paragraphs: For external candidates, the practical route is to apply for the applicable SSC Combined Graduate Level Examination and place Inspector of Income Tax/CBDT appropriately in the post-preference exercise. SSC’s CGLE 2026 notice identifies the post, CBDT, the Group B classification and the 18–30 age band; it also says final allotment depends on Tier-II performance and the candidate’s post preferences.

For CGLE 2026, Tier I was a computer-based objective examination covering General Intelligence and Reasoning, General Awareness, Quantitative Aptitude and English Comprehension. Candidates shortlisted from Tier I take Tier II; SSC states that final merit for ordinary posts is based on Tier-II Paper-I scoring, subject to qualifying the prescribed components. Examination structures, age dates, vacancy numbers, category relaxations and deadlines are cycle-specific, so the live SSC notice—not a coaching summary—should control an application.
bullets: Hold the bachelor’s qualification required under the relevant SSC notice.
Meet the post-specific age and other eligibility conditions for that cycle, including any applicable category or service relaxation.
Prepare for both computer-based tiers and submit post preferences carefully: SSC treats the selected preference as final and irreversible for allotment purposes.
After selection, complete department-side formalities, including regional preference/allocation where called for by CBDT.

sections.heading: Skills worth building
paragraphs: The role rewards careful legal and numerical work more than generic clerical speed. CBDT’s 2024 departmental Inspector paper is explicitly titled “Income Tax Law and Computation” and tests direct-tax provisions, indicating the importance of learning statutory concepts, computation logic and the disciplined interpretation of records after appointment.

For the entrance route, SSC’s CGLE structure makes quantitative aptitude, reasoning, general awareness and English comprehension directly relevant. The Tier-II scheme also includes a qualifying computer-knowledge component and data-entry speed test, so routine digital accuracy remains useful even though the Inspector post is distinct from Tax Assistant posts.
bullets: Read tax provisions and official instructions closely; distinguish survey, assessment, search and other procedures.
Perform accurate numerical checks and tax-related computations.
Analyse records, spot inconsistencies and document findings clearly.
Use computer systems carefully and protect confidential taxpayer information.
Communicate professionally in written English/Hindi as required by departmental work.

sections.heading: Workplace and posting reality
paragraphs: The service is part of CBDT’s Income Tax Department within the Department of Revenue. It combines office-based handling of tax information and records with possible authorised field activity, such as survey-related verification. The balance is not uniform across postings and should not be assumed to be either entirely desk-based or entirely field-based.

Location is a material career consideration. In CBDT’s 2023 allocation process for CGLE-2021 Inspector selectees, candidates ranked preferences among 18 departmental regions; CBDT stated that a region/state would be allotted on merit-cum-preference if a candidate did not submit preferences. That document is a historical example, not a promise that future regions, transfer policies or allocation rules will be identical.
bullets: Employer framework: Central Board of Direct Taxes, Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.
Likely settings: Income Tax Department offices and, where officially authorised, taxpayer business premises for statutory survey/information work.
Posting can be in different CBDT regions across India; regional allocation and later movement depend on the rules and administrative requirements in force.

sections.heading: Progression
paragraphs: Progression to Income Tax Officer (ITO) is evidenced in departmental promotion orders. For example, a July 1, 2024 order of the Principal Chief Commissioner of Income Tax for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana records promotion of an Inspector of Income Tax to Income Tax Officer, a Group B Gazetted post in Pay Level 8. Progression is therefore possible, but timing is not automatic: it is contingent on the applicable recruitment/service rules, eligibility, seniority, vacancies, departmental promotion committee action and administrative decisions.

A CBDT draft recruitment-rules document also described the Inspector cadre as having both promotion and direct-recruitment channels, with two-thirds of vacancies proposed for promotion and one-third for direct recruitment. Because the document is expressly a draft, it is useful historical context rather than a substitute for current notified rules.
bullets: Typical next recognised promotion point evidenced by departmental orders: Income Tax Officer (ITO).
Do not rely on fixed “years to promotion” claims; vacancy position and departmental rules can materially alter progression.
Track current CBDT, Department of Personnel and Training, and regional-office orders for the rules actually applicable to a serving employee.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: As stated in SSC’s CGLE 2026 notice, Inspector of Income Tax is in Pay Level 7, whose listed matrix range is ₹44,900–₹1,42,400. The ₹44,900 figure is the entry basic pay in the Level 7 matrix, not a complete monthly salary figure.

Actual monthly gross and take-home pay vary. They depend on the employee’s matrix cell, dearness allowance and other admissible allowances, city/posting classification, pension and tax deductions, and any future changes to Central Government pay or allowance rules. Use the appointment offer, current Department of Expenditure orders and payroll office calculations for a current personal estimate.
bullets: Dated official context used here: CGLE 2026 lists Pay Level 7 at ₹44,900–₹1,42,400.
Avoid treating online “in-hand salary” estimates as universal; they usually omit location and deduction differences.
Promotion to ITO can move an employee to Pay Level 8, as shown in the cited 2024 departmental promotion order.

title: Judge Advocate General (JAG) Entry Scheme
description: A recruitment scheme for law graduates to join the Indian Army's legal branch as commissioned officers.

quick_facts.label: What the scheme is
quick_facts.value: The JAG Entry Scheme is an Indian Army Short Service Commission (Non-Technical) entry for law graduates into the Judge Advocate General Branch; successful trainees are commissioned as Lieutenants.

quick_facts.label: Current recruitment context
quick_facts.value: For the 125th JAG Course, scheduled to commence in April 2027, the Indian Army notification reports 10 combined vacancies for unmarried male and female law graduates. Vacancy numbers, course dates and application windows are notification-specific and can change in later intakes.

quick_facts.label: Core academic eligibility
quick_facts.value: The current 125th-course notification requires at least 55% aggregate in a three-year LL.B. after graduation or a five-year integrated LL.B.; the degree institution must be recognised by the Bar Council of India and the applicant must be eligible to register as an advocate with a State Bar Council/Bar Council of India.

quick_facts.label: CLAT PG requirement
quick_facts.value: For the 125th course, CLAT PG 2026 is mandatory, including for LL.M.-qualified or LL.M.-appearing candidates; the score is used for shortlisting and must be verified at the Selection Centre before SSB.

quick_facts.label: Selection and training
quick_facts.value: The notified route is online application, shortlisting using CLAT PG score, SSB interview, medical examination, merit and pre-commission training at Officers Training Academy (OTA), Chennai. The preceding 124th-course notification specifies 49 weeks of OTA training, illustrating that training details should be checked against the intake-specific notification.

quick_facts.label: Legal function
quick_facts.value: Under the Army Rules, a judge-advocate represents the Judge-Advocate General at a court-martial, advises on legal questions and procedural defects, sums up evidence and its legal bearing, and must remain impartial.

sections.heading: What a JAG officer does
paragraphs: A JAG officer is a commissioned Army legal officer, not a civilian legal adviser. The statutory court-martial role includes representing the Judge-Advocate General, giving legal opinions to the prosecutor and accused on questions relating to the charge or trial, identifying irregularities in charges or the constitution of the court, advising the court and convening officer, and summing up the evidence and its legal bearing before deliberation.

The role requires procedural fairness as well as legal analysis. The Army Rules state that a judge-advocate shares responsibility for ensuring that an accused person is not disadvantaged by their position or inability to examine or cross-examine witnesses, and requires the judge-advocate to maintain an entirely impartial position. Court-martial proceedings must also be recorded accurately.

The Army Act provides that every general court-martial, and potentially district or summary general courts-martial, may be attended by a judge-advocate from the Judge Advocate General’s Department or another officer approved by the Judge Advocate General.
bullets: Advise on military-law questions arising from charges and trials.
Identify procedural or legal defects and advise the court and convening authority.
Assist in safeguarding fairness for the accused while maintaining impartiality.
Record or ensure accurate recording of court-martial proceedings where acting as judge-advocate.

sections.heading: Entry route from law school
paragraphs: The direct route represented by this node is the Indian Army’s intake-specific JAG Entry Scheme notification. Applicants apply online through Join Indian Army when the relevant JAG Short Service Commission course is open. The 125th-course notification, for an April 2027 course, states that the entry is open to unmarried male and unmarried female law graduates and that applications are made online.

Applicants should treat eligibility as intake-specific. For the 125th course, the stated age band is 21–27 years as of January 1, 2027; it requires a minimum 55% aggregate LL.B., eligibility for advocate registration, a Bar Council of India-recognised college or university, and CLAT PG 2026. An LL.M. does not replace the specified CLAT PG requirement for that notification.

The notified selection sequence is application and CLAT PG-based shortlisting, SSB selection, medical examination, merit list and issue of joining instructions. Passing SSB alone does not guarantee joining: final selection remains subject to merit, medical fitness, eligibility and the notified number of vacancies.
bullets: Complete an eligible three-year LL.B. or five-year integrated LL.B. and retain degree/marks documentation.
Take the CLAT PG examination specified by the relevant Army JAG notification.
Apply through the Join Indian Army officer-entry portal during the published window.
If shortlisted, complete SSB, medical examination and document/CLAT-score verification.
Join OTA, Chennai only if placed on final merit within the available vacancies.

sections.heading: Skills indicated by the legal role
paragraphs: The Army Rules make strong legal reasoning and military-procedure knowledge central to the role: a judge-advocate must advise on questions of law, evaluate legal and procedural irregularities, explain the legal bearing of evidence and guide the court on points of law. The Rules also emphasise knowledge of general legal principles, rules of evidence and courts-martial practice and procedure.

Equally important are careful written-record practices, impartial judgement and the ability to support fair proceedings. These are role requirements grounded in the governing Rules rather than a separate employability checklist.
bullets: Legal research, statutory interpretation and evidence analysis.
Knowledge of courts-martial practice, procedure and military law.
Clear, impartial legal advice under formal process requirements.
Accurate drafting and record-management discipline.
Professional judgement when dealing with procedural fairness.

sections.heading: Work setting and training environment
paragraphs: JAG officers serve as Army officers in the Judge Advocate General Branch. Their formal legal work can involve courts-martial and related military-justice processes, where the Army Rules prescribe advisory, procedural and record-related functions for a judge-advocate.

Selected JAG candidates undergo pre-commission training at Officers Training Academy, Chennai. The 124th JAG-course notification specified a 49-week course and stated that successful cadets receive a Post Graduate Diploma in Defence Management and Strategic Studies from the University of Madras; candidates should verify the duration and award in the notification for their own intake.
bullets: Military legal and justice settings, including court-martial-related duties.
Officer pre-commission training at OTA, Chennai.
Service conditions, medical standards and postings are governed by Army policies and the applicable recruitment notification.

sections.heading: Commission, tenure and progression
paragraphs: On successful completion of training, the JAG-entry candidate is commissioned as a Lieutenant. The 124th-course notice lists time-based promotion milestones of Captain after two years of reckonable commissioned service, Major after six years and Lieutenant Colonel after 13 years; selection-based progression beyond this is subject to the applicable service rules and conditions.

JAG entry is a Short Service Commission route. The 124th-course notification describes an initial 10-year tenure that may be extended by four years. It also says eligible and suitable officers may be considered for Permanent Commission in their 10th year under policies in force at that time; this is consideration, not an automatic entitlement. Terms can be amended, so applicants should rely on the notification and policy applicable to their own course.
bullets: Commissioned rank on passing out: Lieutenant.
Published time-based milestones in the 124th-course notice: Captain at 2 years, Major at 6 years and Lieutenant Colonel at 13 years of reckonable commissioned service.

Short Service Commission terms in that notice: 10 years initially, potentially extendable to 14 years; consideration for Permanent Commission may arise in the 10th year subject to eligibility, suitability and policy.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: Compensation is government pay-matrix based and should be treated as dated, variable context rather than a guaranteed take-home amount. The 124th-course notification lists a cadet stipend of ₹56,100 per month during OTA training. On commissioning, it lists Lieutenant pay at Level 10, ₹56,100–₹177,500, and fixed Military Service Pay of ₹15,500 per month for ranks from Lieutenant through Brigadier.

The same notice describes additional allowances as conditional on the applicable rules, rank and posting area. It also presents an approximate annual CTC figure; that estimate is not a salary guarantee because allowances, deductions, posting and government pay revisions can change actual compensation.
bullets: Training stipend stated in the 2026 124th-course notice: ₹56,100 per month.
Lieutenant pay matrix stated in that notice: Level 10, ₹56,100–₹177,500.
Military Service Pay stated in that notice: ₹15,500 per month for Lieutenant to Brigadier.
Allowances and total compensation vary by entitlement, location, rank and rules in force.

title: Judicial Magistrate First Class in State Judicial Service
description: An entry-level judicial magistrate in the state subordinate judiciary handling criminal cases and related magisterial functions.

quick_facts.label: Role in the criminal-court structure
quick_facts.value: A Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) presides over a Court of Judicial Magistrate established for a district or local area. Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), the State Government establishes such courts after consulting the High Court, and the High Court appoints their presiding officers.

quick_facts.label: Statutory sentencing ceiling
quick_facts.value: Under BNSS section 23, a Court of Magistrate of the First Class may impose imprisonment up to three years, a fine up to ₹50,000, both, or community service, subject to the court's jurisdiction and the applicable offence provisions.

quick_facts.label: Entry pathway
quick_facts.value: The usual entry route is the relevant State Judicial Service / Civil Judge (Junior Division) competitive recruitment process, often called PCS-J. Requirements, age limits, languages, reservations, examination scheme, and the precise designation are set state by state rather than through one national JMFC examination.

quick_facts.label: Baseline qualification example
quick_facts.value: A law degree is the central educational requirement in state rules and notices. For example, Haryana's rules require an LL.B. from a university established by law and approved/recognised by the Bar Council of India, while the Sikkim Judicial Service notice required a law degree from a university established by law in India.

quick_facts.label: Designation and posting
quick_facts.value: The entry cadre may be labelled Civil Judge (Junior Division), Civil Judge-cum-Judicial Magistrate, or another state-specific equivalent. A judicial-service member can be assigned civil work, judicial-magisterial work, or both, depending on the state and posting.

sections.heading: Core judicial-magisterial responsibilities
paragraphs: A JMFC is a judicial officer in the subordinate criminal judiciary. The officer conducts criminal proceedings allocated to the court, decides matters within the court's territorial and subject-matter jurisdiction, issues judicial orders, and tries offences that the applicable criminal law and its schedules make triable by that court.

The BNSS provides the operational framework: Courts of Judicial Magistrates are constituted in districts; their presiding officers are appointed by the High Court; and the Chief Judicial Magistrate may define local areas within which magistrates exercise their powers. The statutory sentencing power of an JMFC is limited to imprisonment up to three years, fine up to ₹50,000, both, or community service. These are ceilings, not a description of every case an individual court will receive.

A JMFC is distinct from an Executive Magistrate. This node concerns the judicial branch: adjudication in criminal courts under the High Court-led subordinate judiciary, rather than executive or revenue administration.
bullets: Conduct hearings and criminal trials or other proceedings assigned by law and by roster.
Assess evidence and legal submissions, record reasons, and issue reasoned judicial orders.
Exercise only the jurisdiction and powers conferred by statute, notification, and High Court allocation.
Work within the supervisory structure of the Chief Judicial Magistrate and the High Court.

sections.heading: How entry through PCS-J / State Judicial Service works
paragraphs: There is no single all-India JMFC recruitment examination. Article 234 of the Constitution provides the constitutional framework for appointments to a state's judicial service other than district judges: appointments are made by the Governor in accordance with state rules, after consultation with the State Public Service Commission and the High Court. In practice, the responsible recruiting body and process vary by state; a High Court, State Public Service Commission, or state-authorised process may publish the recruitment notice.

Candidates normally target an entry judicial post such as Civil Judge (Junior Division) or Civil Judge-cum-Judicial Magistrate through the state-specific judicial-services examination. An LL.B. is the core qualification, but applicants must treat the live notification and governing state rules as controlling: age range, domicile or local-language requirements, computer knowledge, category relaxations, character/medical requirements, number of vacancies, and examination stages can differ.

For illustration only, Haryana's published rules set age and LL.B./basic-computer requirements for Civil Judge (Junior Division), while a Sikkim Judicial Service notice for Civil Judge-cum-Judicial Magistrate (Grade III) required Indian citizenship, a law degree, an upper-age condition, state-language communication ability, and computer knowledge tested at viva voce. These examples should not be treated as universal eligibility rules.
bullets: Complete a qualifying LL.B. from an institution acceptable under the applicable state rules or notification.
Monitor the relevant High Court and/or State Public Service Commission recruitment portal for a live Civil Judge / Judicial Service notice.
Prepare for the stated selection stages, which commonly include a screening or preliminary examination, written main examination, and viva voce, where prescribed.
After selection, complete appointment formalities, posting, probation, and the state judicial academy's induction programme where applicable.

sections.heading: Capabilities the role demands
paragraphs: The role requires strong command of criminal procedure and the ability to apply statutory limits on jurisdiction, sentencing, and case handling. Because the officer must decide proceedings through judicial orders, disciplined legal analysis, careful evaluation of the record, clear legal writing, and procedural fairness are central professional capabilities.

Digital-court capability is increasingly relevant. Haryana's entry rules expressly include basic computer-application knowledge, and the Madhya Pradesh State Judicial Academy schedules ICT and e-Courts induction programming for newly recruited Civil Judges. Training calendars also include criminal rules and court-rules programmes for serving civil judges, illustrating the continuing professional-development demands of the job.
bullets: Criminal-law and criminal-procedure analysis.
Reasoned judgment and order writing.
Evidence assessment, hearing management, and procedural accuracy.
Impartiality, judicial temperament, confidentiality, and professional ethics.
Working competence with court technology and electronic records.

sections.heading: Where and under whom the officer works
paragraphs: The workplace is ordinarily a district-level subordinate court or a court serving a defined local area. The BNSS contemplates Courts of Judicial Magistrates in every district and permits the establishment of special JMFC courts for particular cases or classes of cases. Exact court location, subject allocation, and local jurisdiction are determined through the statutory and High Court administrative framework.

The High Court appoints the presiding officers of Courts of Judicial Magistrates and may appoint a JMFC as Chief Judicial Magistrate or Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate. At entry, officers may first undergo institutional and field induction training before or alongside independent judicial assignments; for example, a Madhya Pradesh High Court posting order required newly appointed Civil Judges (Junior Division) to undergo both forms of induction training.
bullets: District and subordinate criminal courts, with postings transferable under the relevant state service rules.
Potential assignment to a combined civil-judge and judicial-magistrate role where the state cadre so provides.
Administrative supervision through the Chief Judicial Magistrate structure and the High Court.
Judicial-academy induction and continuing education as prescribed by the state.

sections.heading: Career progression is state-service specific
paragraphs: Progression is governed by the particular state's judicial-service rules and High Court administration; it is not automatic merely from holding an JMFC posting. The BNSS expressly allows the High Court to appoint a JMFC as Chief Judicial Magistrate, Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, or—in a sub-division—Sub-divisional Judicial Magistrate, subject to the statutory framework and High Court directions.

A common broad pathway in state subordinate judiciaries is movement from an entry Civil Judge (Junior Division)/judicial-magistrate role to senior civil-judge or chief-judicial-magistrate responsibilities and, subject to the relevant rules and selection methods, to the higher judicial service. Haryana's published higher judicial-service rules, for example, identify Civil Judges (Senior Division), Chief Judicial Magistrates, and Additional Civil Judges (Senior Division) as the feeder group for specified promotional routes. Titles, quotas, qualifying service, examinations, and seniority rules differ by state.
bullets: Entry judicial-service posting: Civil Judge (Junior Division), Judicial Magistrate, or a combined equivalent.
Possible higher magisterial responsibilities: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Chief Judicial Magistrate, or Sub-divisional Judicial Magistrate, where appointed by the High Court.
Potential advancement into senior civil-judge and higher judicial-service cadres under state rules.

sections.heading: Compensation context: state pay matrices, not a single national salary
paragraphs: There is no single nationwide JMFC salary. Pay, allowances, probation terms, and revisions are determined by the relevant state government and judicial-service rules, so candidates should rely on the current recruitment advertisement, appointment order, and pay-revision notifications for their state.

As a dated illustration rather than a current universal rate, a Madhya Pradesh High Court posting order dated December 5, 2023 recorded newly appointed Civil Judges (Junior Division), Entry Level, on a temporary basis in the ₹77,840–₹136,520 Level J-1 scale. A Sikkim Judicial Service recruitment notice for Civil Judge-cum-Judicial Magistrate (Grade III) likewise advertised Pay Matrix J-1 at ₹77,840 plus admissible allowances. Actual take-home pay varies with state rules, allowances, deductions, posting, and later pay revisions.
bullets: Check the live state notification for the applicable pay level and allowances.
Do not use historic pay scales or another state's pay matrix as a guaranteed salary estimate.
Account for probationary status, location-linked allowances, and statutory deductions when comparing compensation.

title: Junior Account Assistant cum Typist in Indian Railways
description: A railway accounts clerical employee recruited through graduate-level RRB NTPC posts to maintain accounts and financial records.

quick_facts.label: Recruiting route
quick_facts.value: Junior Account Assistant cum Typist (JAACT) is a graduate-level Non-Technical Popular Categories post recruited through Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs), as illustrated by Centralised Employment Notice (CEN) 05/2024.

quick_facts.label: Minimum qualification
quick_facts.value: In CEN 05/2024, the post required a degree from a recognised university or equivalent, plus typing proficiency in English or Hindi on computer.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages
quick_facts.value: The cited RRB NTPC graduate notice specified two computer-based tests, followed for JAACT candidates by a Typing Skill Test; document verification and medical examination apply before appointment.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: CEN 05/2024 listed JAACT at Pay Level 5 of the 7th CPC pay matrix, with initial basic pay of ₹29,200. This is a dated recruitment-notice figure, not a guaranteed current gross or take-home salary.

quick_facts.label: Medical standard
quick_facts.value: The CEN 05/2024 post-parameter table listed medical standard C-2 for JAACT; candidates must meet the medical requirements in the applicable notice.

sections.heading: What the role supports
paragraphs: JAACT is an Accounts Department clerical role. Indian Railways’ Accounts Code describes railway accounts-office work as spanning booking and compilation, budget, cash and pay, compensation claims, engineering accounts, and other financial functions. In that environment, a junior accounts assistant can be expected to support the accurate recording, compilation, checking, retrieval, and typed processing of financial papers and records under local allocation of work; the exact desk duties vary by railway, division, production unit, and accounts branch.

The control environment is consequential: Railway accounts procedures require internal checks over cash and pay work, vouchers, receipts, payments, and related records. This makes careful data handling, document control, arithmetic accuracy, and adherence to prescribed procedures central to the work rather than merely administrative extras.
bullets: Maintain and process accounts-office records, statements, vouchers, bills, and correspondence as assigned.
Assist with compilation and checking work connected with railway receipts, expenditure, payroll/cash-and-pay, budget, or other accounts branches.
Type and prepare official material on computer, while following applicable financial-code, office-procedure, and internal-check requirements.

sections.heading: Entry through RRB NTPC
paragraphs: The principal open-market route is an RRB NTPC graduate-level notification that includes JAACT vacancies. In CEN 05/2024, applicants needed a recognised university degree or equivalent and computer typing proficiency in English or Hindi. Eligibility, age limits, reservation, medical standards, vacancy distribution, and application dates are notification-specific and must be checked in the live CEN for the relevant recruitment cycle.

For the CEN 05/2024 process, the RRB prescribed CBT 1 and CBT 2, then a qualifying Typing Skill Test for JAACT, followed by document verification and medical examination. The notice states that typing-test marks are not added to merit; candidates need 30 words per minute in English or 25 words per minute in Hindi on a computer without editing tools or spell-check facilities.

Indian Railway Establishment Manual material also records an internal departmental path into the historical Junior Accounts Assistant grade from Accounts Clerk roles. That route is governed by departmental quotas, service conditions, examinations, and current railway instructions, so it should not be treated as a substitute for the RRB direct-recruitment route.
bullets: Monitor official RRB websites for a current NTPC graduate CEN and its RRB-wise vacancy table.
Confirm degree status, age and category eligibility, C-2 medical standard, and required documents against that specific notification.
Prepare for both CBT stages and practise computer typing in the permitted English or Hindi mode.
Treat departmental promotion as an internal-service route subject to extant railway rules, not as an external application pathway.

sections.heading: Skills to build
paragraphs: The post’s formal recruitment requirements make computer typing and dependable digital work essential. RRB’s CEN 05/2024 required English/Hindi computer typing proficiency and used a qualifying typing test for this post. Candidates should therefore build sustained speed with accuracy, comfort working on a standard desktop keyboard, and the ability to produce clean official text without relying on spell-check or editing tools during the test.

The work context also rewards practical accounting discipline: numerical accuracy, reconciliation-minded checking, orderly handling of vouchers and files, spreadsheet and office-software fluency, confidentiality, and the ability to apply written rules. These are role-relevant capabilities inferred from the documented accounts-office functions and internal-control requirements, rather than a separate published JAACT competency framework.
bullets: English or Hindi computer typing, with accuracy as well as speed.
Numeracy, basic accounting concepts, and careful checking of entries and supporting documents.
Spreadsheets, word processing, structured digital records, and file management.
Reading and applying financial/administrative procedures; attention to audit trails and confidentiality.

sections.heading: Where the job is based
paragraphs: The CEN 05/2024 notice advertised JAACT vacancies in Zonal Railways and Production Units of Indian Railways. Actual posting depends on the RRB, notified railway/unit, vacancy allocation, medical fitness, and administrative requirements; applicants should not assume a preferred city or home-state posting.

The usual setting is an accounts office or related railway administrative unit. Railway Accounts Code material identifies accounts-office divisions including budget, booking and compilation, cash and pay, compensation claims, and engineering accounts, indicating that the role may sit in different finance-and-records workflows rather than in one uniform desk assignment.
bullets: Potential employers/locations: Zonal Railways and Production Units notified through the selected RRB.
Typical setting: office-based accounts, finance, cash-and-pay, budget, compilation, or related administrative work.
Posting and branch allocation are variable and governed by the recruitment notice and railway administration.

sections.heading: Career development context
paragraphs: The Indian Railway Establishment Manual sets out an accounts-cadre progression framework in which Junior Accounts Assistants could progress to Accounts Assistant after three years of service and passing the Appendix II examination; it also describes further channels involving Section Officer (Accounts), Inspector of Stores Accounts, and Travelling Inspector of Accounts, subject to qualifying examinations and the applicable rules. The cited manual uses legacy pay-scale terminology, so it is useful for understanding the broad cadre pathway but not for predicting current pay levels, vacancies, timelines, or promotion entitlement.

Progression in practice depends on the sanctioned cadre, seniority, fitness/selection process where applicable, qualifying departmental examinations, and extant Railway Board instructions. A new JAACT should confirm the current divisional or zonal Accounts Department promotion rules after joining.
bullets: Build mastery of railway accounts procedures and departmental examinations required for the assigned cadre path.
Track current seniority, eligibility, selection, and training rules through the employing railway rather than relying on historical pay-scale references.

Possible higher accounts functions described in the manual include Accounts Assistant and, for qualified staff, Section Officer (Accounts), Inspector of Stores Accounts, or Travelling Inspector of Accounts.

sections.heading: Pay and compensation context
paragraphs: For dated context, the official CEN 05/2024 indicative notice placed JAACT in Level 5 under the 7th CPC pay matrix and stated an initial basic pay of ₹29,200. That number is basic pay at the time and terms of that notice, not an all-inclusive monthly salary.

Actual gross pay and take-home pay vary with the prevailing dearness allowance, house-rent allowance where admissible, transport and other eligible allowances, place of posting, deductions, and changes to government pay rules. Candidates should use the current appointment offer, railway payroll guidance, and applicable government orders for a current figure.
bullets: Dated official notice context: Pay Level 5, initial basic pay ₹29,200 under CEN 05/2024.
Do not equate initial basic pay with take-home pay.
Allowance and deduction outcomes are posting- and rule-dependent and can change over time.

title: Junior Clerk cum Typist in Indian Railways
description: A railway junior clerical employee recruited through undergraduate-level RRB NTPC posts for records, correspondence and typing duties.

quick_facts.label: Recruitment channel
quick_facts.value: Junior Clerk Cum Typist is an RRB Non-Technical Popular Categories (NTPC) undergraduate-level post. The RRB Bhubaneswar official notification index lists it under the newer CEN 07/2025 NTPC (Undergraduate) recruitment, while the detailed CEN 06/2024 notice identifies it as an NTPC undergraduate post.

quick_facts.label: Minimum qualification (dated notice context)
quick_facts.value: In CEN 06/2024, the requirement was 12th (+2 stage) or equivalent with at least 50% aggregate marks; the 50% threshold did not apply to SC/ST, PwBD, ex-servicemen, or candidates with qualifications higher than 12th. Computer typing proficiency in English or Hindi was essential. Applicants must use the eligibility terms in the specific current CEN.

quick_facts.label: Selection stages (dated notice context)
quick_facts.value: CEN 06/2024 used first-stage CBT, second-stage CBT, a qualifying typing skill test for this post, document verification, and medical examination. Appointment is offered by the relevant Railway Administration after selection and required checks.

quick_facts.label: Typing benchmark (dated notice context)
quick_facts.value: CEN 06/2024 specified 30 words per minute in English or 25 words per minute in Hindi on a personal computer, without editing tools or spell-check facilities. The typing test was qualifying; its marks were not added to merit.

quick_facts.label: Pay level and medical category (dated notice context)
quick_facts.value: CEN 06/2024 placed Junior Clerk Cum Typist at 7th CPC Pay Level 2, with an initial basic pay of ₹19,900 and medical standard C2. Basic pay, allowances, vacancies, age limits, and medical provisions can change by notification and applicable rules.

sections.heading: Entry through RRB NTPC undergraduate recruitment
paragraphs: The normal external entry route is an RRB NTPC undergraduate Centralised Employment Notice (CEN). Candidates apply online to one chosen RRB for vacancies notified for that recruitment cycle, rank the posts and Railway/Production Unit preferences for which they are eligible, and proceed through the prescribed selection stages.

The detailed CEN 06/2024 route illustrates the process: first-stage CBT is used to shortlist for second-stage CBT; for Junior Clerk Cum Typist, second-stage CBT performance is used to shortlist candidates for the typing skill test. Candidates then undergo document verification and a Railway medical fitness examination. RRBs recommend empanelled candidates, but the respective Railway Administration makes the appointment offer.

Because post parameters, age cut-offs, vacancies, fee arrangements, dates, and relaxation provisions are notification-specific, candidates should treat an active RRB CEN—not older notices or coaching sites—as the controlling document. The RRB Bhubaneswar index shows Junior Clerk Cum Typist in CEN 07/2025 NTPC (Undergraduate), demonstrating that recruitment is issued in cycles.

sections.heading: Skills demonstrated in recruitment
paragraphs: The clearest role-specific skill formally tested for this post is computer typing. Under CEN 06/2024, candidates for Junior Clerk Cum Typist had to meet a qualifying benchmark of 30 WPM in English or 25 WPM in Hindi on a personal computer without editing tools or spell-check. Hindi test-takers could use Kruti Dev or Mangal fonts.

The CBT syllabus in the same notice covered mathematics, general intelligence and reasoning, general awareness, and basics of computers and computer applications. This makes accurate keyboarding, basic computer familiarity, numerical comfort, reasoning, and careful reading practical preparation priorities. These are examination requirements rather than a complete employer-issued description of daily duties.

sections.heading: Employer and posting context
paragraphs: This is a Ministry of Railways/Indian Railways clerical recruitment category. In CEN 06/2024, RRBs invited applications for NTPC undergraduate posts in various Zonal Railways and Production Units, and the vacancy annexures allocated Junior Clerk Cum Typist positions across named railways and units. A candidate's final organisation and location therefore depend on the vacancies, preferences, merit, medical fitness, and allotment in the applicable recruitment cycle.

The post is listed with medical standard C2 in the 2024 detailed notice. Candidates should not assume a particular zone, production unit, city, or vacancy count from a previous CEN; these elements vary by cycle.

title: Junior Engineer (Central Government)
description: A Group-B non-gazetted technical post in various ministries, departments and organisations of the Government of India, recruited through the SSC JE exam.

quick_facts.label: Recruiting examination
quick_facts.value: The Staff Selection Commission (SSC) conducts the Junior Engineer (Civil, Mechanical & Electrical) Examination to recruit junior engineers for various Government of India departments and organisations.

quick_facts.label: Post classification and pay level
quick_facts.value: For the SSC JE 2024 recruitment, the advertised posts were Group ‘B’ (Non-Gazetted), Non-Ministerial posts at 7th CPC Pay Level 6, with the published pay-matrix range of ₹35,400–₹1,12,400. Classification, vacancies and terms should be verified against the notice for the relevant examination year and organisation.

quick_facts.label: Disciplines
quick_facts.value: The SSC JE examination covers Civil, Mechanical and Electrical engineering streams; the actual posts and organisations available depend on the recruitment notice and candidate preference/allocation process.

quick_facts.label: Selection structure
quick_facts.value: In SSC JE 2025, candidates were shortlisted from Paper I to Paper II, and the first-round allocation used performance in both papers together with the online post/organisation preferences submitted by candidates.

quick_facts.label: A documented departmental pathway
quick_facts.value: CPWD’s published manual describes a departmental examination route to Junior Engineer (Civil/Electrical) for eligible regular or work-charged staff with a relevant diploma or higher qualification; this is distinct from open SSC JE recruitment and is department-specific.

sections.heading: What a Central Government Junior Engineer does
paragraphs: Responsibilities vary by allotted organisation and engineering stream. In CPWD—a major central engineering employer—Junior Engineers are field officers responsible for maintenance and construction work at section level and report to the sub-divisional officer.

CPWD describes work that includes collecting and compiling engineering data, preparing estimates and drawings, supervising works, checking quality and conformity with designs/specifications, recording measurements, and maintaining official records and registers. These duties are a useful concrete example of the technical, documentation and site-supervision character of many public-works JE roles, rather than a universal job description for every SSC JE allocation.
bullets: Oversee assigned construction, maintenance or engineering-service work.
Prepare or support estimates, drawings, measurements and work records.
Monitor quality, specifications and execution at site.
Coordinate within the engineering reporting structure, typically under an Assistant Engineer or Sub-Divisional Officer in the CPWD example.

sections.heading: Primary entry route: SSC JE
paragraphs: The normal open-recruitment route for this node is the SSC Junior Engineer (Civil, Mechanical & Electrical) Examination. SSC describes it as a competitive examination for recruiting junior engineers in government departments and organisations.

Applicants should use the SSC notice issued for the specific examination cycle—not coaching summaries—to confirm eligible engineering discipline, qualification, age limits, vacancies, medical or physical conditions where applicable, application dates and organisation-wise posts. SSC’s 2025 process also required candidates who reached the relevant stage to submit an online option-cum-preference for posts and organisations.

A separate, internal route may exist in individual organisations. For example, CPWD publishes departmental examinations for eligible staff for appointment to Junior Engineer; that is not a substitute for SSC JE open recruitment and its eligibility is governed by CPWD rules.
bullets: Complete SSC One-Time Registration and apply through the SSC portal when the relevant JE notice is live.
Hold the exact diploma, degree or other technical qualification specified for the chosen post/organisation in that year’s SSC notice.
Prepare for both examination papers; in the 2025 cycle, performance in Paper I and Paper II informed allocation.
Submit post/organisation preferences when SSC opens the option-cum-preference window.

sections.heading: Skills developed and used
paragraphs: The CPWD description of JE work indicates that the role requires applied engineering judgement as well as disciplined public-works documentation. Core capabilities include interpreting drawings and specifications, estimating, measurement recording, quality oversight, maintaining registers and compiling engineering data.

Because the role combines technical execution with documented accountability, candidates benefit from clear written communication, accuracy in calculations and records, familiarity with the applicable engineering discipline, and the ability to work between office documentation and field supervision.
bullets: Discipline-specific civil, mechanical or electrical engineering fundamentals.
Estimation, drawings, measurements and technical record-keeping.
Quality control and checking conformance with approved designs and specifications.
Field supervision, data collection and coordination with the engineering chain of command.

sections.heading: Workplace and posting context
paragraphs: SSC JE is not one single employer-specific job: SSC recruits for junior-engineer posts across government departments and organisations. The eventual workplace, technical portfolio and conditions therefore depend on the organisation and post for which the candidate is allocated.

The CPWD example shows a mixed office-and-field role: JEs are deployed in maintenance and construction, manage work at section level and directly oversee works. CPWD’s published office listings also show JE posts distributed across regional and sub-divisional structures, illustrating the potential for geographically dispersed postings.
bullets: Expect the organisation and location to be determined through the vacancy and allocation process.
Construction and maintenance assignments may require regular site oversight in addition to office-based estimating, records and coordination.
Some organisations or posts can have additional medical or physical standards; SSC specifically flags separate standards for Border Roads Organisation JE posts.

sections.heading: Progression after appointment
paragraphs: Career progression is organisation-specific. In CPWD, Junior Engineer is described as a direct-entry post and feeder grade for Assistant Engineer. CPWD also publishes limited departmental competitive examinations and results for promotion from JE (Civil/Electrical) to Assistant Engineer (Civil/Electrical).

Accordingly, an appointed JE should treat promotion rules, qualifying service, departmental examinations, seniority and vacancy position as employer-specific matters. Higher qualifications or external examinations may support longer-term career choices, but they do not by themselves guarantee promotion within a central-government cadre.
bullets: Build verified technical, site-supervision and record-management experience in the allotted organisation.
Track the employer’s recruitment rules, seniority instructions and departmental-examination notices.
Where available, pursue the JE-to-AE promotional channel under the applicable departmental rules.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: As dated context rather than a current guaranteed offer: the Government’s SSC JE 2024 announcement placed the advertised JE posts at 7th CPC Pay Level 6, ₹35,400–₹1,12,400 in the pay matrix. This is the basic pay-matrix level, not a universal in-hand monthly salary.

Actual monthly remuneration can vary with applicable allowances, place of posting, deductions and the recruitment notice or service conditions of the allotted organisation. Candidates should therefore use the current SSC notice and appointment terms for a specific-cycle estimate rather than relying on an older salary figure.
bullets: Published 2024 pay-matrix context: Pay Level 6, ₹35,400–₹1,12,400.
Do not equate the pay-matrix range with take-home pay.
Verify current pay, allowances and conditions in the relevant SSC notification and employer appointment documents.

title: Junior Engineer (Indian Railways)
description: A technical role in the Indian Railways responsible for assisting in the planning, execution, and maintenance of various engineering projects and systems.

quick_facts.label: Recruiting body and route
quick_facts.value: Indian Railways recruits Junior Engineer categories through Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs) under Centralised Employment Notices; the applicable post, railway/unit, allocation and vacancy position are notification-specific.

quick_facts.label: Entry qualification
quick_facts.value: For the 2024 RRB JE notice, qualifications were discipline- and post-specific, generally requiring a three-year engineering diploma or an accepted engineering degree/technology qualification in the relevant discipline; civil, electrical, mechanical and signal/telecom JE posts had different approved disciplines.

quick_facts.label: Selection process
quick_facts.value: The 2024 RRB JE process comprised CBT-I, CBT-II, document verification and a railway medical examination. Requirements and schedules can change in a future notification.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: In CEN 03/2024, JE was listed at Level 6 of the 7th CPC Pay Matrix with initial basic pay of ₹35,400 plus admissible allowances. This is dated recruitment-notice context rather than a guarantee of current take-home pay.

quick_facts.label: Promotion context
quick_facts.value: Senior Section Engineer (SSE) is an evidenced progression destination in some railway cadres: an official Southern Railway order records promotion from JE/Signal in Level 6 to SSE/Signal in Level 7. Cadre rules, vacancies and selection conditions vary by department and railway.

sections.heading: What a Junior Engineer does
paragraphs: A Junior Engineer’s work is technical and department-specific rather than a single uniform job. In engineering-maintenance assignments, the role can combine inspection, maintenance, execution of approved works, records and safety-related reporting. For example, the Indian Railway Maintenance Manual assigns JE/Works responsibility for inspection and maintenance of service buildings, staff quarters, roads, water supply, drainage and sewerage systems, as well as execution of works.

For permanent-way assignments, the official manual describes JE/SSE responsibilities including safe track inspection and maintenance, identifying and rectifying defects, completing specified works to approved plans and specifications, and maintaining inspection information. The safety-critical nature of the assignment means that the exact duties depend strongly on the JE’s branch and posting.
bullets: Civil/P-Way and bridge work may involve field inspection, asset maintenance, special works and safety observations.
Works assignments may cover railway buildings, staff housing, roads, water supply and drainage assets.
Electrical, mechanical, signal and telecom assignments are separately notified categories and require the corresponding technical discipline.

sections.heading: How to enter through RRB JE
paragraphs: The main external route is to apply when an RRB publishes a JE Centralised Employment Notice, choose only posts for which the candidate has the specified technical qualification, and complete the prescribed selection stages. In CEN 03/2024, candidates applied online to one RRB and the process consisted of CBT-I, CBT-II, document verification and medical examination; candidates also had to meet the post’s medical standard.

A three-year diploma is a common threshold, but it is not a blanket qualification for every JE post. The 2024 notice mapped particular engineering disciplines to particular JE categories and stated that B.E./B.Tech could be accepted in lieu of the relevant three-year diploma. Candidates should therefore use the detailed post-parameter table in the live notification—not coaching-site summaries—to check discipline, age, medical and reservation requirements.

There are also internal railway advancement routes into some JE cadres. Railway Board training material explicitly describes JE/Works induction after LDCE promotion from the Works category, while zonal railway material records departmental/LDCE selections for particular JE posts. Those routes are for eligible serving employees and are not a substitute for the open RRB recruitment route.
bullets: Obtain the relevant diploma or degree in the discipline named for the intended JE category.
Monitor official RRB websites for a live notice and apply only through the official application process.
Prepare for two computer-based tests, then retain original qualification and category documents for verification.
Meet the medical standard assigned to the selected category; standards differ among posts.

sections.heading: Skills to develop
paragraphs: A prospective JE needs sound fundamentals in the relevant engineering branch and the ability to apply procedures in a regulated railway setting. The RRB’s CBT-II syllabus for the 2024 notice included technical subjects such as basic civil engineering, electrical engineering, electronics, computers, environment and pollution prevention, and engineering drawing-related knowledge, alongside general abilities tested in CBT-I.

Operationally, inspection discipline, technical documentation, interpreting plans/specifications, quality awareness and safety-focused judgment are important. Railway induction material for P-Way trainees specifically includes inspection formats, Track Management System entries, maintenance activity, work-site protection near running lines, quality control and field exposure. Some drawing roles additionally receive computer and AutoCAD training.
bullets: Relevant branch engineering: civil, mechanical, electrical, electronics, signal/telecom or another discipline specified in the notice.
Inspection, fault observation, measurement and maintenance planning.
Reading drawings, using technical records and producing clear reports.
Safety-rule adherence and careful coordination during field work.
Digital skills appropriate to the assignment, including Track Management System workflows or CAD exposure where applicable.

sections.heading: Where and how the work is performed
paragraphs: Junior Engineers can be assigned across zonal railways, production units and technical departments. The 2024 RRB post table included JE categories in Engineering, Electrical, Mechanical, Signal & Telecommunications, production units, workshops, R&D, track machines, diesel sheds, carriage and wagon, and telecom/signal functions. The eventual post and railway/unit are allocated under the recruitment notice’s preference, merit, reservation and vacancy provisions.

The environment can therefore range from offices and drawing/design work to workshops, depots, stations, railway colonies, track sections, bridges and other field locations. For field engineering roles, official induction programmes include both institute instruction and open-line/construction field exposure, including work-site protection near running lines.
bullets: Posting location and branch are not fully interchangeable: they are tied to the category and unit notified by the RRB.
Field roles may require inspections and work around operating railway infrastructure.
Induction and refresher training are part of the structured railway technical-work environment.

sections.heading: Progression and professional development
paragraphs: Progression is cadre- and department-dependent. An official Southern Railway promotion order documents JEs in Signal & Telecommunications being promoted from Level 6 to Senior Section Engineer/Signal in Level 7, subject to the applicable selection and service conditions. Railway Board training modules also provide promotion training for SSE/P-Way from JE and for SSE/Track Machines from JE/Track Machines, confirming that JE-to-SSE progression exists in those streams.

Career development also includes structured induction and periodic refresher training. For example, the Railway Board’s engineering training programme specifies one-year JE induction programmes in several engineering streams and refresher courses for JE/SSE categories. Departmental promotion examinations or LDCE may be relevant to eligible serving employees in particular cadres; their quotas and eligibility cannot be generalized across all JE branches.
bullets: Build branch-specific expertise through induction, field attachment and refresher training.
Track the promotion rules and selection notices of the employing railway and department.
Senior Section Engineer is a common next supervisory technical role in several, but not necessarily all, JE cadres.
Professional credentials or further study may strengthen technical capability, but they do not replace the formal railway recruitment or promotion rules.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: The most reliable pay reference is the specific RRB notice under which appointment is made. CEN 03/2024 listed Junior Engineer in Pay Level 6 of the 7th CPC Pay Matrix with initial basic pay of ₹35,400 and stated that other allowances would be admissible at the time. This is basic-pay context from a 2024 notice, not an estimate of in-hand salary.

Actual monthly pay can vary with the applicable allowances, place of posting, deductions and subsequent government orders. Candidates should check the current recruitment notification and the applicable Railway/central-government pay and allowance orders before making financial decisions.
bullets: CEN 03/2024 reference: Level 6, initial basic pay ₹35,400.
Allowances were described as admissible at the time and should be verified against current orders.
Do not treat advertised basic pay as take-home pay.

title: Junior Engineer (State Government)
description: A role in a state government department (e.g., PWD, Irrigation) focusing on project execution, supervision, and maintenance tasks.

quick_facts.label: Typical appointment status
quick_facts.value: State-government JE is commonly a technical, non-gazetted post, but its group/classification differs by state and department. Maharashtra PWD’s 2023 rules classify JE (Civil) as Group B, Non-Gazetted; Puducherry PWD’s notified rules likewise list the post as Group B, non-gazetted and non-ministerial.

quick_facts.label: Core work
quick_facts.value: The role is field-facing project execution: preparing engineering data, site plans and estimates; supervising work against approved drawings and specifications; recording measurements; preparing bills; maintaining works/material records; and submitting reports or returns to superiors.

quick_facts.label: Direct-entry qualification
quick_facts.value: A diploma or degree in the relevant engineering branch is a common eligibility pattern, but the exact branch, recognition requirement, experience, age limits, domicile/language conditions and reservations must be checked in the specific state advertisement. For example, Maharashtra PWD specifies a diploma, degree or higher qualification in Civil Engineering; Puducherry PWD specifies a Civil Engineering diploma or bachelor’s degree.

quick_facts.label: Recruitment routes
quick_facts.value: Recruitment can include a competitive examination/direct nomination route and departmental promotion. Maharashtra PWD’s 2023 JE (Civil) rules provide both promotion and nomination through a competitive examination, in a stated 60:40 promotion-to-nomination ratio for that cadre; this is an example, not an all-India rule.

quick_facts.label: Mobility and posting
quick_facts.value: JE work may involve office, section and construction-site duties, and service rules can make an appointee transferable across the state. Maharashtra’s PWD JE (Civil) rules explicitly make appointees liable for transfer anywhere in Maharashtra.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: Pay is state- and cadre-specific rather than nationally uniform. As dated official examples, Puducherry PWD’s JE (Civil) rules list Level 6, ₹35,400–₹1,12,400, while a November 2025 West Bengal PWD appointment notification lists JE (Civil) in WBS ROPA 2019 Pay Matrix Level 12 with admissible allowances.

sections.heading: Responsibilities: execute public works with technical and record-keeping accountability
paragraphs: A state-government Junior Engineer generally serves as the section-level technical executor for public infrastructure and assets. Official departmental job descriptions show responsibility for gathering engineering data; producing site plans, rough drawings and estimates; laying out and supervising works undertaken by contractors or departmental labour; and ensuring work conforms to approved specifications, drawings, standards and samples.

The role also carries documentation and measurement responsibilities. Typical functions include recording work measurements, preparing measurement abstracts and bills, verifying bills, keeping material/tool and prescribed works registers, and sending progress reports and returns to senior engineering officers. In practice, the exact financial powers and approval authority remain defined by the relevant state’s PWD/irrigation/municipal rules and delegation orders.
bullets: Supervise construction, repair and maintenance work in an allotted section or project area.
Check workmanship and quality against approved drawings, specifications and standards.
Prepare or support estimates, drawings, site plans, quantities, measurement records and work bills.
Maintain technical, stock/material, testing and site-order records; escalate deviations, delays and site issues.
Coordinate with contractors, departmental labour, field staff and senior engineers.

sections.heading: Entry routes: state-specific competitive recruitment and internal promotion
paragraphs: The main external route is to apply against a state department, state recruitment board or public service commission notification and qualify the stated selection process. State JE posts are not governed by one universal national eligibility rule: the recruiting authority sets the discipline, qualification, age, category relaxations, language/computer requirements, examination scheme, document verification and other conditions in the advertisement.

Engineering diploma holders and degree holders can both be eligible in many Civil JE cadres. Maharashtra PWD’s 2023 rules, for instance, require at least a diploma or degree in Civil Engineering for nomination through the competitive-examination route. Puducherry PWD’s JE (Civil) rules similarly accept a Civil Engineering diploma or bachelor’s degree. Electrical and mechanical JE vacancies must be read separately because their required branch and technical syllabus may differ.

Internal progression can also be an entry route into the JE grade. In the Maharashtra PWD example, a Civil Engineering Assistant with at least seven years of regular continuous service and the prescribed professional examination may be considered for promotion; the same rules state that appointment is through promotion and nomination in a 60:40 ratio. These conditions are cadre-specific and should not be generalized to another state.
bullets: Match the engineering branch named in the notification—commonly Civil, Electrical or Mechanical.
Use only the official notification to confirm recognition of the diploma/degree, age cut-off date, reservation rules and selection stages.
For serving employees, check the departmental recruitment/promotion rules, seniority requirements and mandatory professional or language examinations.
Do not treat SSC JE, RRB JE or another state’s JE examination as appointment to a state-government JE post; they are separate recruitment channels and employers.

sections.heading: Skills: applied engineering, site control and accurate public-works records
paragraphs: The work calls for practical command of the relevant engineering discipline and the ability to interpret drawings, specifications, estimates and site conditions. Because the JE is responsible for supervision, measurements, bills and registers, accuracy in quantity measurement, documentation and compliance is as important as technical knowledge.

Public-works practice also requires quality awareness, contractor and labour coordination, reporting discipline and comfort with field inspections. For electrical JE work, official PWD guidance additionally emphasizes defect rectification, safe maintenance, periodic testing and recording test readings.
bullets: Engineering drawing and specification reading; surveying, estimation and quantity/measurement work.
Construction or maintenance supervision, inspection and quality-control awareness.
Measurement-book, bill, material/stock and site-record accuracy.
Clear reporting and coordination with contractors, field staff and Assistant/Executive Engineers.
For electrical/mechanical cadres: applicable safety, maintenance and testing practices.

sections.heading: Workplace: a mix of field sections, project sites and engineering offices
paragraphs: A JE is typically attached to a department or local engineering unit responsible for public assets—for example, public works, roads/buildings, irrigation, water supply, municipal works, electrical installations or mechanical services. The job combines on-site inspection and supervision with office-based estimating, records, bills and reporting.

Location stability should not be assumed. In Maharashtra PWD’s JE (Civil) rules, the appointee is liable for transfer anywhere in the state. Actual posting, transfer policy, site exposure, travel needs and emergency/maintenance duties vary by department, cadre and state.
bullets: Potential work settings: road/building works, irrigation or water assets, public facilities, electrical installations, workshops or local-body infrastructure.
Regular interaction with contractors, departmental labour, suppliers, residents/users and senior engineering staff is common.
Field visits are integral where work execution, measurements, inspections or maintenance are assigned.

sections.heading: Progression: departmental examinations, seniority/eligibility processes and Assistant Engineer opportunities
paragraphs: Career progression is governed by the state’s service and promotion rules, vacancies, seniority, qualifying service, performance/fitness and any mandatory examinations. A common engineering ladder includes eligibility for promotion to Assistant Engineer, but the time requirement and whether a degree, diploma, departmental examination or other condition is required differ among cadres.

Official evidence shows this pathway operates in state departments: Himachal Pradesh PWD publishes promotion material for JE to Assistant Engineer, and Uttarakhand’s public-service materials list promotion from Junior/Additional Assistant Engineer to Assistant Engineer in PWD and other engineering departments. Maharashtra’s JE rules also make passing prescribed professional, computer-operation and language examinations consequential for increments or promotion where applicable.
bullets: Build a reliable record in execution, measurement, quality, documentation and departmental procedures.
Track service-rule changes and departmental examination requirements from the employing department.
Check whether the target Assistant Engineer cadre differentiates between diploma and degree holders or prescribes a minimum regular-service period.
Promotion is not automatic: it depends on applicable rules, vacancies and formal selection/promotion processes.

sections.heading: Compensation context: pay matrices and allowances vary by state and cadre
paragraphs: There is no single India-wide state-government JE salary. The applicable basic pay comes from the recruiting state’s pay matrix and the particular departmental/cadre notification; admissible allowances and take-home pay depend on that state’s current pay rules, posting location, deductions and employment terms.

For dated comparison only, Puducherry PWD’s notified JE (Civil) recruitment rules show Pay Matrix Level 6, ₹35,400–₹1,12,400. A West Bengal PWD appointment notification dated November 25, 2025 places JE (Civil) in WBS ROPA 2019 Pay Matrix Level 12 and states that other allowances are admissible. These examples demonstrate variation and are not a salary forecast for a different state or future recruitment.
bullets: Verify basic pay, pay level, allowances, probation, pension/NPS coverage and contractual-versus-regular status in the specific advertisement and appointment rules.
Treat old grade-pay figures and coaching-site salary claims cautiously; use the current state notification and pay-revision orders.
Compare posts within the same state only after checking their cadre classification and current pay-matrix entry.
