title: Station Master in Indian Railways
description: A railway operations officer recruited through RRB NTPC who manages station operations, train movements and passenger safety.

quick_facts.label: Recruiting route
quick_facts.value: Station Master is recruited through Railway Recruitment Board (RRB) Non-Technical Popular Categories (NTPC) graduate-level recruitment when the post is notified.

quick_facts.label: Core role
quick_facts.value: The Station Master is in overall charge of the station, with responsibility for safe, rule-compliant station working and the efficient discharge of duties by staff under their direction.

quick_facts.label: Qualification context
quick_facts.value: A university degree or equivalent has been the prescribed educational qualification for direct recruitment to the Station Master/Assistant Station Master stream; candidates must always use the detailed CEN for the particular recruitment cycle as the controlling eligibility notice.

quick_facts.label: Selection context
quick_facts.value: In CEN 05/2024, the Station Master selection stream included CBT-I, CBT-II, a Computer-Based Aptitude Test (CBAT), followed by document verification and medical examination for shortlisted candidates.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: As a dated example, CEN 05/2024 listed Station Master at 7th CPC Pay Level 6 with initial basic pay of ₹35,400. Basic pay is not take-home pay; allowances, deductions, posting, and applicable government orders affect actual earnings.

sections.heading: What a Station Master does
paragraphs: A Station Master is the station’s operational lead. Indian Railways’ Operating Manual assigns responsibility for ensuring that station work follows current rules, procedures and instructions; supervising staff; supporting safe and courteous passenger service; maintaining operating and safety literature, records, and accident documentation; and attending accidents and relief work when required.

For train operations, the role requires safe coordination with control and adherence to General and Subsidiary Rules and Station Working Rules. The manual states that the Station Master on duty is responsible for ensuring the applicable rules are observed before giving “Line Clear,” and remains responsible for safe execution of crossings and precedence arrangements.
bullets: Supervise station staff and the safe, efficient operation of the station.
Monitor points, signals, track circuits and essential safety equipment as prescribed.
Maintain operational registers, records, notices and safety documentation.
Coordinate with control and respond to incidents, disruptions and emergency situations.
Oversee public-facing station conditions and escalate or address operational deficiencies.

sections.heading: Entry through RRB NTPC
paragraphs: The principal external entry route is an RRB NTPC graduate recruitment notice that includes Station Master vacancies. The detailed Centralised Employment Notice (CEN), not coaching material or an earlier notification, controls the eligibility, category-wise vacancies, age limits, medical standard, examination rules and application dates for that cycle.

The 2024 graduate NTPC cycle is a useful illustration rather than a permanent rule: its Station Master pathway used CBT-I, CBT-II and CBAT, with document verification and medical examination for provisionally shortlisted candidates. RRB Chandigarh’s recruitment pages subsequently listed CEN 06/2025 as a newer graduate NTPC cycle, demonstrating why applicants should check the active official notice rather than rely on a prior cycle.
bullets: Watch official RRB websites for a graduate NTPC CEN that actually includes Station Master vacancies.
Check the cycle-specific degree/equivalence requirement, age cut-off, reservation conditions and medical standards in the detailed CEN.
Prepare for the CBT stages and, where specified for Station Master, CBAT.
Treat document verification and medical examination as mandatory later stages for shortlisted candidates; shortlisting does not itself guarantee appointment.

sections.heading: Skills the role demands
paragraphs: The role demands disciplined rule application, safety-focused judgement and calm operational communication. This follows directly from duties involving line-clear procedure, train regulation, checking of signalling-related equipment, coordination with control, maintenance of records, and emergency response.

It also requires supervisory and public-service capability: the Operating Manual makes the Station Master responsible for staff performance, passenger safety and security, handling public complaints, station upkeep and communication of current operating instructions to staff.
bullets: Safety and procedural discipline when working with train movements and station rules.
Situational awareness and decision-making under time pressure or service disruption.
Clear communication with control, train-working staff and passengers.
Accurate recordkeeping, reporting and use of operating documentation.
Staff supervision, customer-service judgement and incident coordination.

sections.heading: Workplace and working pattern
paragraphs: Station Masters work in the operating environment of railway stations and station limits, rather than in a conventional desk-only setting. The job interfaces with platforms, yards, cabins, goods sheds, level crossings and station equipment, depending on the station’s facilities and local Station Working Rules.

The work is roster-based operational work. Indian Railways’ manual requires Station Working Rules to specify train-working staff available in each shift and their duties, and it describes coordination between the Station Master and the section controller for train movements. Posting conditions and local duties can therefore differ considerably between stations and railway zones.
bullets: Possible work areas include the Station Master’s office, platforms, station yard, cabins and other facilities under station charge.
Work is organised through shifts and operational rosters.
The role involves coordination across operating, signalling, engineering, commercial, security and medical/relief functions during normal operations or incidents.
Local technology and procedures vary: Station Working Rules specify the relevant signalling, interlocking and communications arrangements.

sections.heading: Progression and development
paragraphs: Promotion opportunities depend on Indian Railways establishment rules, seniority/selection processes, eligibility and vacancies in the relevant railway administration. The Indian Railway Establishment Manual records that Station Superintendent posts in Level 7 are filled by promotion through selection from the Station Master feeder grade.

There may also be opportunities to compete for higher operating-management posts through departmental channels. For example, South Central Railway has published notices for selection to Group B Assistant Operations Manager/Assistant Traffic Manager posts in Level 8. This should be understood as an available departmental progression context, not a guaranteed automatic career ladder for every Station Master.
bullets: Potential advancement can include supervisory station roles such as Station Superintendent, subject to the applicable promotion process.
Departmental selection and competitive routes may provide access to higher operating-management roles.
Initial and refresher learning are important because station staff must remain current with operating rules, safety instructions and competency requirements.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: Compensation should be read from the applicable recruitment notice and current government pay orders, rather than from informal salary estimates. In the CEN 05/2024 notification, Station Master was listed at 7th CPC Pay Level 6 with an initial basic pay of ₹35,400.

That ₹35,400 figure is dated to the 2024 notification and is basic pay, not a universal monthly in-hand amount. Actual remuneration can vary with admissible allowances, place of posting, duty-related entitlements, deductions and later revisions to government pay or allowance rules.
bullets: Dated reference point: CEN 05/2024 listed ₹35,400 as initial basic pay at Pay Level 6.
Do not equate initial basic pay with take-home pay.
Confirm the current CEN and Railway Board/government orders for the terms applicable at appointment.

title: Stenographer (Government)
description: A government role responsible for transcribing spoken words by typing them into a steno machine, providing secretarial and clerical support.

quick_facts.label: Role scope
quick_facts.value: At the central-government level, the SSC Stenographer Grade ‘C’ and ‘D’ examination recruits stenographers for government ministries and departments.

quick_facts.label: Selection administration in DRDO
quick_facts.value: CEPTAM handles recruitment activities including vacancy advertising, application scrutiny, computer-based tests, trade tests and selection committees, then recommends final select lists to appointing authorities.

quick_facts.label: Promotion context
quick_facts.value: A 2025 SSC limited departmental examination notice provided routes from Stenographer Grade ‘D’ to Grade ‘C’/Personal Assistant-type roles in specified central secretariat and allied stenographer services, subject to cadre-specific service eligibility.

sections.heading: What a government stenographer does
paragraphs: The core work is to capture spoken dictation in shorthand and produce an accurate computer transcription under time limits. DRDO’s published skill-test instructions require candidates to take dictated material, review shorthand notes, transcribe on an allotted computer, and complete comparison and correction within the prescribed period—activities that closely reflect the accuracy- and deadline-sensitive work of the role.

In central-secretariat settings, stenographer services are intended to assist senior and top-level officers. In practice, this places stenographic work alongside confidential secretarial support, preparation of typed material and office coordination; the exact distribution of duties depends on the employing ministry, department, laboratory or cadre rules.
bullets: Take shorthand dictation and transcribe it accurately on a computer.
Review, compare and correct transcribed material within prescribed time limits.
Provide secretarial support to officers; assignment mix varies by organisation and posting.

sections.heading: Entry routes and eligibility
paragraphs: A broad central-government route is the SSC Stenographer Grade ‘C’ and ‘D’ examination, which the Staff Selection Commission describes as recruitment for stenographers in government ministries and departments. Candidates should use the live notice for the relevant examination cycle because eligibility, vacancies, age limits, language options, testing arrangements and department allocations can change.

For the DRDO-linked route represented by this node, CEPTAM has historically recruited Stenographer Grade-II in its Admin & Allied cadre. The CEPTAM-09 notice required a recognised 12th-class qualification, placed the post at an 18–27 age band subject to applicable relaxations, and used a computer-based Tier I followed by a mandatory qualifying dictation-and-transcription test. Treat these as an example from that advertisement, not as standing eligibility for a future DRDO vacancy.

CEPTAM is DRDO’s recruitment body, but a CEPTAM notification must actually include a stenographer post before it can be used as an entry route. For example, the currently listed CEPTAM-11 advertisement concerns STA-B and Technician-A positions, so applicants should not assume that every CEPTAM cycle recruits stenographers.
bullets: Monitor SSC notices for Grade ‘C’ and Grade ‘D’ direct-recruitment cycles.
Monitor DRDO/CEPTAM vacancy notices specifically for Admin & Allied stenographer openings.
Confirm the exact notification’s educational qualification, age cut-off, language, test format, vacancy count and posting conditions before applying.

sections.heading: Skills to develop
paragraphs: The defining technical skill is rapid, accurate shorthand-to-computer transcription. DRDO’s published Stenographer Grade-II norm—80 words per minute dictation for 10 minutes followed by 50 minutes of English transcription—makes clear that speed alone is insufficient: candidates must also read shorthand notes reliably, type efficiently, and correct errors under pressure.

Computer literacy is also material to progression. The SSC’s 2025 limited departmental examination notice states that Stenographer Grade ‘D’ officials seeking promotion to Personal Assistant must transcribe shorthand notes on computers. Strong English usage, careful listening, proofreading, document formatting and discretion are therefore practical complements to shorthand and typing ability.
bullets: English shorthand dictation and transcription practice.
Fast, accurate computer typing and proofreading.
Listening concentration, grammar and punctuation control.
Computer-based document production and confidential office handling.

sections.heading: Workplace and posting conditions
paragraphs: Central-government stenographers can be allocated to different ministries, departments and offices through SSC selection, with final placement linked to the applicable recruitment process and candidate preferences where the notice provides for them.

For DRDO’s Admin & Allied recruitment, the CEPTAM-09 notice stated that selected candidates could be appointed anywhere within the Union of India, including field or remote locations, according to organisational requirements. The same notice listed multiple possible stations and stated a minimum five-year period at the first posting, while allowing public-interest transfers. These are dated DRDO-notice conditions and may differ in a later recruitment cycle.
bullets: Office-based work is typical, supporting officers and organisational units.
Central-government postings may vary by allocated department or office.
DRDO postings can be geographically mobile and organisation-driven.

sections.heading: Progression pathways
paragraphs: Progression is cadre-specific rather than automatic. The SSC’s 2025 Grade ‘C’ Stenographers Limited Departmental Competitive Examination covered several services, including the Central Secretariat Stenographers Service, Indian Foreign Service Branch (B), Armed Forces Headquarters, Railway Board Secretariat, Election Commission and Central Vigilance Commission stenographer services.

In the Central Secretariat Stenographers Service example, regularly appointed Grade ‘D’ stenographers could seek promotion through the limited departmental examination after meeting the notice’s approved-service conditions; the 2025 notice generally specified six years, with a stated proviso for certain competitively appointed officials. Other named cadres applied different qualifying-service requirements. A move toward Personal Assistant is therefore possible, but depends on the employee’s service/cadre rules, length of approved service, examination and vacancies.
bullets: Build a record of accurate transcription, computer proficiency and reliable secretarial work.
Track the departmental/limited competitive examinations applicable to the specific cadre.
Check cadre-specific service-length rules and training requirements rather than relying on a single promotion timeline.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: Compensation differs by employer, grade, city and the applicable government orders. As a concrete but dated DRDO example, the CEPTAM-09 Admin & Allied advertisement listed Stenographer Grade-II at 7th CPC Pay Level 4 with a basic-pay range of ₹25,500–81,100. It also described eligibility for allowances and facilities under Government of India rules, including dearness allowance, house-rent allowance, transport allowance and medical facilities, and stated National Pension System coverage unless otherwise provided by rules.

This should not be read as a current take-home-pay estimate or as a pay guarantee for all government stenographer posts. Candidates should use the pay level, allowances, pension terms, city classification and conditions stated in the particular appointment advertisement and current Department of Expenditure orders.
bullets: Use the vacancy notice’s pay level and pay matrix as the starting point.
Treat basic pay, allowances and take-home pay as distinct figures.
Verify current allowance and pension rules at the time of application or appointment.

title: Store Assistant B (DRDO)
description: A higher-grade DRDO stores position involving greater responsibility for receipt, accounting, preservation and issue of defence materials.

quick_facts.label: Service classification
quick_facts.value: Store Assistant ‘B’ is governed with Store Assistant ‘A’ under DRDO’s Group ‘C’ recruitment rules; the principal rules were published on 15 September 2022 and amended in 2023.

quick_facts.label: Pay level
quick_facts.value: The post is referenced in current DRDO recruitment rules as Pay Matrix Level 4, ₹25,500–81,100 basic pay. This is the matrix range, not a guaranteed take-home salary.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry basis
quick_facts.value: The Seventh Central Pay Commission’s DRDO cadre table identifies Store Assistant ‘B’ entry as promotion and Limited Departmental Competitive Examination, rather than a general educational-entry post.

quick_facts.label: Identified onward progression
quick_facts.value: Under the 2023 rules for Senior Store Assistant, Store Assistant ‘B’ personnel at Level 4 may be considered for promotion after 10 years of regular service in grade and completion of two to four weeks of relevant training.

sections.heading: How this grade is normally reached
paragraphs: Store Assistant ‘B’ should be understood as a departmental career grade, not assumed to be an open, direct-recruitment role. The official Seventh Central Pay Commission report lists its entry mode in the DRDO cadre as “Promotion and Limited Departmental Competitive Examination.” The applicable DRDO Group ‘C’ rules for Store Assistant ‘A’ and ‘B’ were issued in 2022 and amended in 2023; applicants and serving staff should use the current DRDO vacancy notice and departmental instructions for the precise eligibility, vacancy quota, examination, and seniority conditions in force at the time.

The related Store Assistant ‘A’ cadre is the practical feeder context: the 2023 amendment provides for a five-percent non-selection promotion channel into Store Assistant ‘A’ from eligible Level-1 Group ‘C’ staff with three years’ regular service and Class 12 qualification. That provision does not itself establish eligibility for Store Assistant ‘B’; it illustrates why candidates should distinguish the A-grade entry route from the B-grade internal advancement route.
bullets: Monitor DRDO’s official vacancies portal and the relevant departmental circulars rather than relying on coaching-site summaries.

For serving staff, verify regular-service counting, departmental-examination requirements, training, vacancy year, and any reservation or seniority provisions in the notice applicable to the particular promotion process.

sections.heading: DRDO work setting
paragraphs: A Store Assistant ‘B’ works within the Ministry of Defence’s DRDO environment. DRDO describes itself as a network of around 41 laboratories and five DRDO Young Scientist Laboratories, spanning fields including aeronautics, armaments, electronics, combat vehicles, missiles, naval systems, life sciences, materials, computing, training, information systems and agriculture. Consequently, the operational setting can vary substantially by laboratory or establishment and the materials, documentation, and support requirements of its programme.
bullets: Expect a government defence-research establishment setting rather than a single uniform workplace.
The particular laboratory or establishment determines the local work processes and the types of stores supported.

sections.heading: Progression beyond Store Assistant ‘B’
paragraphs: The clearest rule-based next step identified in the current store-cadre rules is Senior Store Assistant, a Level-6 post. The 2023 Recruitment Rules provide that 40% of Senior Store Assistant vacancies are filled by promotion, failing which by deputation. The feeder provision expressly includes Store Assistant ‘B’ at Level 4 with 10 years’ regular service in the grade and successful completion of two to four weeks of relevant training from CEPTAM or another recognised training institute.

The same rules also show that Senior Store Assistant is a mixed-recruitment post: 60% direct recruitment and 40% promotion, failing which deputation. Promotion depends on the rule conditions and vacancies; completing the service period or training does not by itself guarantee appointment.
bullets: Build and retain documented regular service in the grade.
Complete the prescribed relevant training when made available or required.
Check the applicable promotion notice, since vacancy distribution and procedural requirements can change through later rules or notifications.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: As of this review, the cited recruitment rules place Store Assistant ‘B’ at Level 4 in the Central Government pay matrix, whose stated range is ₹25,500–81,100. This is basic pay determined by the appropriate matrix cell and pay-fixation rules, not an all-inclusive monthly salary figure.

Actual gross and take-home pay are variable. They depend on the employee’s matrix cell, applicable dearness allowance, house-rent allowance or government accommodation, transport allowance, location, deductions, tax, and other service-specific entitlements. For that reason, a single “in-hand salary” figure should not be treated as canonical for this node.
bullets: Use ₹25,500 as the Level-4 entry cell in the cited pay matrix, not as a universal net-pay figure.
Recheck Department of Expenditure orders and the individual appointment or pay-fixation order for current allowance rates and entitlement.

title: Store Assistant (DRDO)
description: A role within DRDO responsible for managing inventory, procurement, and distribution of materials and equipment required for research and other activities.

quick_facts.label: Recruiting channel
quick_facts.value: DRDO identifies CEPTAM as the recruitment channel for its DRTC, Administrative and Allied Group B and Group C cadres; Store Assistant A is governed as a Group C post.

quick_facts.label: Internal promotion provision
quick_facts.value: The 2023 amendment to the Store Assistant A/B recruitment rules provides that 5% of Store Assistant A vacancies may be filled by non-selection promotion from eligible Level-1 Group C employees with three years' regular service and a recognized-board Class 12 pass; the rules also refer to qualifying in a departmental examination.

sections.heading: What the stores function covers
paragraphs: DRDO’s published job description for a Stores Officer—not a post-specific duty statement for Store Assistant A—defines the stores function as supervising stores, ledger and bill work; managing receipt, verification, documentation, stacking/binning, preservation and issue of stores; coordinating audit matters; and total inventory management. This is useful operational context for understanding a Store Assistant role, but it should not be read as an exhaustive or binding job description for every Store Assistant A posting.
source_urls
bullets: Likely work is records- and process-oriented: receiving and documenting material, maintaining store records, supporting issue/distribution processes, and working within inventory-control and audit procedures.
Exact allocation of duties, security requirements, software, material categories and laboratory/establishment posting should be confirmed from the appointment or vacancy notice.

sections.heading: How to enter through CEPTAM
paragraphs: For direct recruitment, follow the Store Assistant A-specific CEPTAM advertisement when it is issued. DRDO states that CEPTAM recruits for its Administrative and Allied Group B and Group C cadres. The last Store Assistant A-specific official Admin & Allied advertisement located for this guide is CEPTAM-10 (2022); it is evidence of the previous route, not confirmation that a Store Assistant vacancy is currently open.
source_urls
bullets: Previous official CEPTAM-10 context: Store Assistant A was offered in English-typing and Hindi-typing variants; the published essential education context was a Class 12 pass from a recognized board or equivalent.
Previous official CEPTAM-10 context: Tier I was a CBT, followed for Store Assistant A by a qualifying typing test for shortlisted candidates.

Internal route: the 2023 recruitment-rule amendment provides a limited promotion channel into Store Assistant A for qualifying Level-1 Group C employees with the stipulated service and Class 12 qualification.

Do not assume that a Certificate in Computer Applications or a stores/inventory certificate is mandatory: the cited CEPTAM-10 requirement was Class 12 plus the prescribed typing test. Such certificates may still be useful preparation, but a future notification controls eligibility.

sections.heading: Skills to prepare
paragraphs: Typing is the clearest role-specific skill evidenced by the official CEPTAM-10 process: passing the typing test was essential for Store Assistant A. The stores-function description published by DRDO also supports preparation in accurate documentation, ledger/record work, verification, inventory handling and audit-conscious processes.
source_urls
bullets: Computer typing in the language option specified in the notification.
Accuracy in data entry, document handling and maintaining records.
Basic inventory and material-handling concepts: receipt, verification, storage/binning, preservation and issue.
Careful adherence to procedures, because stores work interfaces with bills, vouchers, ledgers and audit.

sections.heading: Progression and departmental route
paragraphs: The official 2023 amendment confirms a departmental-examination-linked promotion provision into Store Assistant A: 5% of vacancies may be filled through non-selection promotion from qualifying Level-1 Group C employees who have completed three years of regular service and hold a Class 12 pass. Employees who qualify in excess of vacancies may be considered for later vacancies before employees qualifying at a later examination, as provided in the rule.
source_urls
bullets: This rule supports a documented internal entry/progression route into Store Assistant A.

Although the recruitment rules cover Store Assistant A and Store Assistant B, the amendment cited here does not, by itself, establish the eligibility, timing or mechanism for promotion from Store Assistant A to Store Assistant B. Verify the then-current recruitment rules and departmental orders before treating Store Assistant B as an assured next step.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: In CEPTAM-10/Admin & Allied recruitment (2022), Store Assistant A was listed at 7th CPC Pay Level 2: ₹19,900–₹63,200 in the pay matrix, with other benefits and allowances under then-applicable Government of India rules. Basic pay, allowances, deductions and take-home compensation can vary with the appointment date, posting location, pay cell, government orders and future recruitment terms.
source_urls
bullets: Use the pay level and matrix range as historical official context rather than a current salary quote.
Before applying, check the Store Assistant-specific official advertisement and appointment terms for the applicable pay level, allowances, age limits, vacancies and test standards.

title: Sub Inspector in Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)
description: A Group B post responsible for investigating corruption, economic offenses, and other major crimes at a national level.

quick_facts.label: Entry examination
quick_facts.value: Direct recruitment to Sub-Inspector (CBI) is listed through the Staff Selection Commission’s Combined Graduate Level (SSC CGL) examination; applicants must include the post in their SSC preference options to be considered.

quick_facts.label: Post status
quick_facts.value: The SSC CGL 2025 notice lists Sub Inspector, Central Bureau of Investigation as a Group B post in Pay Level 7.

quick_facts.label: Education requirement
quick_facts.value: For this post, the applicable SSC CGL requirement is a bachelor’s degree from a recognized university or equivalent; the notice’s special subject requirements apply only to specified other posts.

quick_facts.label: Age context
quick_facts.value: In the SSC CGL 2025 notice, the CBI Sub-Inspector post carried a 20–30 year age band as of August 1, 2026, subject to the notice’s category-specific relaxations. Age rules can change with a future notification.

quick_facts.label: Post-specific medical standards
quick_facts.value: The cited SSC notice prescribes minimum height, chest (for men), and vision standards for CBI Sub-Inspector candidates; physical and medical checks are conducted by the user department after final selection.

sections.heading: What the role is connected to
paragraphs: A CBI Sub-Inspector is an investigative-law-enforcement entry post within the Central Bureau of Investigation. CBI’s published institutional profile describes a multi-disciplinary central police agency with Anti-Corruption, Economic Offences, Special Crimes, Prosecution, Administration, Policy & Coordination, and forensic functions. In practical terms, the role should be understood as supporting investigations and casework within that wider remit rather than as a general administrative post.

The exact case assignment, powers exercised, and day-to-day mix of fieldwork, records, evidence handling, coordination, and court-related work depend on the unit and investigation. Applicants should avoid assuming a guaranteed specialization merely from selecting the post in SSC CGL.
bullets: Potential investigative domains include corruption-related matters, economic offences, and special-crime work because these are named CBI functional divisions.
The Bureau’s published profile states that it investigates and prosecutes offences across India, so the work context can extend beyond a single local jurisdiction.

sections.heading: Primary entry route: SSC CGL
paragraphs: The canonical direct-entry route is SSC CGL. In the SSC CGL 2025 notice, CBI Sub-Inspector appears under Pay Level 7 with a 20–30 age limit and falls under the general bachelor’s-degree qualification applicable to “all other posts.” These are notification-specific conditions, not permanent guarantees for later cycles.

Selection in that notice used a computer-based Tier I screening examination followed by Tier II. Tier I tested reasoning, general awareness, quantitative aptitude, and English comprehension. Tier II Paper I included mathematical abilities, reasoning and general intelligence, English language and comprehension, general awareness, computer knowledge, and a data-entry speed test. SSC stated that final merit for the relevant posts would be based on Tier II performance, with post preferences submitted online.

Candidates considering CBI Sub-Inspector must assess the physical and medical requirements before indicating the post preference. The notice says that the department conducts those checks after final selection and warns that a candidate who fails them may not then be considered for another post or department.
bullets: Qualification reference: bachelor’s degree from a recognized university or equivalent.
2025-notice age reference: 20–30 years on August 1, 2026; verify the age date and relaxations in the notification actually being applied for.

CBI SI standards in the cited notice: men—165 cm height and 76 cm chest with expansion; women—150 cm height; height relaxation of 5 cm for hillsmen and tribals; specified distant and near vision benchmarks apply.
Post preference matters: SSC stated that candidates who do not indicate a post/department preference are not considered for it.

sections.heading: Skills to build
paragraphs: The SSC CGL examination design makes quantitative reasoning, logical reasoning, English comprehension, general awareness, computer knowledge, and accurate data entry directly relevant preparation skills. These are selection skills; they do not by themselves replace professional investigation training.

For career readiness, it is reasonable to develop careful written communication, document organization, numerical literacy, ethical judgment, and comfort with digital evidence and financial/cybercrime concepts. This is an inference from CBI’s anti-corruption, economic-offences, special-crime, and forensic remit, and from the CBI Academy’s published training coverage in investigation of financial and cyber-enabled crime.
bullets: Prepare SSC CGL foundations: mathematics, reasoning, English, general awareness, computer knowledge, and timed data entry.
Build investigation-adjacent capabilities: precise note-taking and report writing, file and evidence discipline, and basic financial and digital literacy.
Maintain the fitness and vision standards required for the specific CBI SI post notification.

sections.heading: Work setting and training context
paragraphs: CBI is a central-government investigating agency under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, with functions spanning anti-corruption, economic offences, special crimes, prosecution, coordination, administration, and forensic support. Therefore, a Sub-Inspector’s working environment may combine office-based case preparation and coordination with investigation-related duties, depending on the posting and unit.

The CBI Academy in Ghaziabad is identified by the Government of India’s Capacity Building Commission as a central training institution serving CBI officers and serving police officers at Sub-Inspector level and above. Its inclusion indicates an institutional training environment relevant to the profession, though specific induction curriculum and duration should be confirmed from appointment instructions rather than assumed in advance.
bullets: Employer context: Central Bureau of Investigation, under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions.
Functional context: anti-corruption, economic-offences, special-crimes, prosecution, policy/coordination, administration, and forensic functions.
Training-institution context: CBI Academy, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh.

sections.heading: Pay context
paragraphs: Salary should be treated as dated, rule-based context rather than a take-home-pay promise. The SSC CGL 2025 notice placed CBI Sub-Inspector in Pay Level 7 and showed the Level 7 pay-matrix range as ₹44,900–₹1,42,400. Actual monthly pay varies with admissible allowances, place of posting, deductions, and any later government pay revisions.

The same SSC material classified the role as Group B; a 2025 SSC tentative-vacancy document further described the CBI SI listing as Group B (Non-Gazetted). Vacancy counts and compensation components vary by recruitment cycle and should be checked in the live SSC notice and relevant government orders.
bullets: Dated basic-pay context from SSC CGL 2025: Pay Level 7, ₹44,900–₹1,42,400.
Do not equate the pay-matrix range with in-hand salary; allowances and deductions are variable.
The 2025 tentative-vacancy document listed 93 CBI SI vacancies as of July 31, 2025; this is historical context only and not a forecast of future vacancies.

title: Sub-Inspector in State Police
description: A state police officer appointed as a Sub-Inspector through a state police recruitment board, responsible for investigation, law and order, and station-level duties.

quick_facts.label: Core role
quick_facts.value: A State Police Sub-Inspector (SI) is a field-level police officer whose work can include crime prevention, investigation and detection, maintenance of law and order, and—in some police stations—acting as Station House Officer (SHO).

quick_facts.label: Appointment route
quick_facts.value: Direct recruitment is conducted through the relevant State’s notified recruiting authority rather than through one all-India State-Police SI examination; for example, Rajasthan identifies its Public Service Commission as the recruiter for Police SI, while Madhya Pradesh lists a dedicated Subedar and Sub-Inspector recruitment test.

quick_facts.label: Typical selection components
quick_facts.value: The exact process is notification-specific, but recent official SI recruitment material shows written examination stages and physical tests. Bihar’s SI recruitment notices show preliminary and mains written examinations followed by PET/document-verification activity; Goa’s 2025 notice specifies physical standards and physical-efficiency tests.

quick_facts.label: Entry eligibility is state-specific
quick_facts.value: A recognized degree is a common requirement in official examples, but age limits, local-language or driving requirements, reservation rules, medical standards and physical benchmarks vary by State and by notification. Goa’s 2025 Police SI notice, for example, required a recognized degree or specified diploma, computer knowledge, a light-vehicle licence and Konkani knowledge.

quick_facts.label: Initial training
quick_facts.value: Appointees ordinarily complete prescribed basic police training after recruitment; Goa’s 2025 Police SI advertisement expressly states that recruited candidates must undergo and pass the basic course at a Police Training College or Police Training Academy.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: Pay is set by the relevant State/UT and recruitment rules, not by a single national SI salary scale. As a dated example only, Goa Staff Selection Commission’s 2025 Police SI advertisement listed Pay Level 6; candidates should rely on the pay level and allowances stated in the applicable vacancy notice.

sections.heading: Responsibilities and authority in station-level policing
paragraphs: The work is operational, investigative and supervisory. Haryana Police’s statutory disclosure describes police functions as prevention, investigation and detection of crime and maintenance of law and order. It lists FIR/NCR registration, case investigation, arrest, recovery of stolen property, filing/challaning cases and prosecution-related work among police functions.

A Sub-Inspector may be the officer in charge of a police station, subject to the State’s posting structure. Haryana Police states that a police-station in-charge may be an Inspector or Sub-Inspector, and identifies SIs as able to act as SHOs. The National Career Service occupational profile additionally describes SI work as controlling station staff, allocating duties, supervising patrols and responding to local intelligence and problems.
bullets: Maintain public order and support crime prevention in the assigned jurisdiction.
Investigate cognizable cases and manage case-related fieldwork, records and court/prosecution processes as required.
Direct and deploy subordinate station staff; monitor patrol and duty arrangements.
Where posted as SHO, carry station-level administrative, operational and statutory responsibilities.

sections.heading: How to enter through State SI recruitment
paragraphs: The standard external route is to apply against a State Police SI vacancy issued by the State police recruitment board, staff selection commission, public service commission, or another authority named in that State’s rules. The recruiting body is not uniform: Rajasthan Police identifies the Rajasthan Public Service Commission for SI recruitment, while the Madhya Pradesh Employees Selection Board lists a separate Subedar and Sub-Inspector Recruitment Test for Police Headquarters/Home (Police).

Read the individual notification as the controlling document. Official examples show that eligibility and tests can differ materially. Goa’s 2025 Police SI notice specified education, computer knowledge, physical standards, a physical-efficiency test, driving licence and language knowledge, followed by basic training. Bihar Police Subordinate Services Commission notices for its SI recruitment show preliminary and mains written-exam milestones and later PET/document-verification activity.
bullets: Track the official recruitment authority for the intended State; do not assume another State’s schedule, syllabus or eligibility applies.
Confirm nationality/domicile, category/reservation, age, educational qualification, language, licence, medical and physical requirements in the live notification.
Prepare for the notified written examination stages and for qualifying physical measurement/efficiency, document-verification, medical and other prescribed stages.
Complete academy or police-training-college training after appointment when required.

sections.heading: Skills developed and used
paragraphs: The role calls for a combination of investigative judgement, legal and procedural discipline, physical readiness, communication and team supervision. This is an evidence-based inference from official task descriptions: police disclosures assign SIs investigation, arrest/recovery and SHO work, while the National Career Service profile includes staff control, duty allocation, patrol supervision, intelligence handling and engagement with local problems.

Candidates should develop both written-exam capability and practical professional habits: accurate report and case-record preparation, respectful public interaction, situational judgement, evidence-aware investigation, command of local procedures, and the stamina to meet the specific physical standards prescribed in the relevant notification.
bullets: Investigation and case-management discipline.
Clear written communication and accurate official documentation.
Public-facing communication, conflict management and local-area awareness.
Supervision, task allocation and patrol/deployment management.
Physical fitness appropriate to the notified PET and operational duties.

sections.heading: Workplace and posting context
paragraphs: An SI commonly works from a police station or police post while also performing field duties in the station jurisdiction. Haryana Police states that stations are manned by SIs, ASIs, head constables and constables, and that station-level work includes law-and-order duties and investigation. Its disclosure also recognises an SI as a possible SHO.

The job therefore mixes desk-based statutory work—such as registration, records, case progression and coordination—with unpredictable field deployments for investigation, patrol supervision, public-order situations and urgent complaints. The particular unit, shift pattern, armed/unarmed role, specialist assignment and transfer conditions depend on the State police organisation and posting order.
bullets: Police stations and police posts.
Crime scenes, patrol areas and other locations within the assigned jurisdiction.
Court/prosecution and inter-agency coordination connected with cases.
Potential deployment in specialised functions such as traffic, intelligence, security or investigations, where the State organisation assigns such work.

sections.heading: Career progression
paragraphs: Career progression is governed by the applicable State police service rules, seniority, vacancies, performance and departmental selection processes. The National Career Service’s occupational profile presents a broad indicative progression from constable through head constable and ASI to SI, then Inspector and higher ranks. It should not be read as a guaranteed or identical promotion ladder in every State.

For an officer already appointed as SI, Inspector is the usual next rank shown in that national occupational profile. Candidates and serving personnel should check their own State’s police service rules and departmental orders for promotion quotas, qualifying service, examinations and specialised postings.
bullets: Indicative upward movement from SI: Inspector and then higher supervisory ranks, subject to State rules.
Specialisation or postings may include investigation, traffic, intelligence, security, enforcement or anti-corruption-related functions.
Promotion conditions and timelines are variable; official State service rules are decisive.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: There is no single all-India pay figure for a State Police SI. Compensation is determined by the appointing State/UT, the notified pay level, prevailing pay rules and eligible allowances. As a concrete but non-transferable example, Goa Staff Selection Commission’s Advertisement No. 1 of 2025 listed Police Sub-Inspector at Level 6.

Use the vacancy notification and the current State government pay/allowance orders to assess actual compensation. Pay level alone does not establish take-home pay: postings, admissible allowances, deductions and subsequent pay revisions can change the amount.
bullets: Treat any salary figure from a coaching or job-listing site as non-authoritative unless it matches the official advertisement.
Check the live notification for pay level or scale, probation terms and any stated allowances.
Verify current State orders for allowances and implementation of pay revisions before making financial decisions.

title: Tax Assistant in CBDT
description: An entry-level Group C clerical post in the Central Board of Direct Taxes responsible for record maintenance and assisting senior officers in tax administration.

quick_facts.label: Recruiting examination
quick_facts.value: Tax Assistant (CBDT) is listed among the Group C posts filled through the Staff Selection Commission’s Combined Graduate Level Examination (SSC CGL).

quick_facts.label: Employer and cadre
quick_facts.value: The post is in the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.

quick_facts.label: Classification and age band
quick_facts.value: In the SSC CGL notice uploaded on May 21, 2026, Tax Assistant in CBDT is shown as a Group C post with an 18–27 age limit, subject to the notice’s eligibility date and applicable relaxations.

quick_facts.label: Education requirement
quick_facts.value: Tax Assistant falls under SSC CGL’s “all other posts” qualification: a bachelor’s degree from a recognized university or equivalent, with the qualification required by the notice’s specified cut-off date.

quick_facts.label: Pay-level context
quick_facts.value: The May 2026 SSC CGL notice places Tax Assistant (CBDT) at Pay Level 4, with the published basic-pay range of ₹25,500–₹81,100. This is a pay-matrix range, not a promise of a particular in-hand salary.

quick_facts.label: Skill-test requirement
quick_facts.value: SSC CGL Tier II includes a qualifying Data Entry Speed Test (DEST). SSC specifies a higher DEST standard for Tax Assistant in CBDT; the test is described as approximately 2,000 key depressions in 15 minutes.

sections.heading: Entry route: SSC CGL selection and post preference
paragraphs: The direct entry route is SSC CGL. The Commission’s 2026 notice lists Tax Assistant in CBDT as a likely Group C post and states that final allotment is based on merit-cum-preference of posts submitted by candidates. A candidate therefore needs to be eligible for SSC CGL, take the applicable computer-based tiers, and rank sufficiently for the CBDT Tax Assistant preference against vacancies reported for that cycle.

For this post, the general degree requirement in the cited notice is a bachelor’s degree or equivalent from a recognized institution. The same notice describes Tier I and Tier II as the examination structure. In Tier II Paper I, candidates must separately qualify its sections; the qualifying DEST is specifically relevant to Tax Assistant in CBDT and has a higher qualifying standard than for many other posts. Applicants should treat each future SSC CGL notice as controlling, because vacancy numbers, dates, cut-off date for age/qualification, and implementation details can change by recruitment year.
bullets: Obtain the required bachelor’s degree or equivalent by the cut-off date in the relevant SSC CGL notice.
Apply through SSC’s online process and complete the CGL computer-based examination stages.
Give Tax Assistant—CBDT an informed post preference when SSC calls for preferences.
Prepare for the higher-standard DEST as well as the objective portions of Tier II.

sections.heading: Skills signalled by the selection process
paragraphs: The official examination pattern makes keyboard accuracy, data entry, and baseline computer familiarity especially material for this role. Tier II Paper I contains Mathematical Abilities, Reasoning and General Intelligence, English Language and Comprehension, General Awareness, a Computer Knowledge Test, and DEST. The Commission makes DEST qualifying for all posts and identifies Tax Assistant in CBDT as one of the posts for which a higher DEST standard applies.

Practical preparation should therefore emphasize sustained accurate typing, careful handling of numeric and text data, basic computer concepts, clear written English, and disciplined checking of entries. These are evidence-based preparation priorities from the SSC selection design; they should not be read as a complete departmental job description.
bullets: Accurate keyboarding and data entry under a timed test.
Computer knowledge appropriate to SSC CGL Tier II.
Quantitative reasoning, English comprehension, general awareness, and logical reasoning.
Attention to detail when entering and checking text and numeric information.

sections.heading: Departmental setting and postings
paragraphs: A CBDT Tax Assistant is employed within the Income Tax Department’s direct-tax administration structure under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance. The SSC notice identifies the cadre as CBDT rather than CBIC, which is a separate board and a separately listed Tax Assistant post.

Posting and personnel administration are managed within departmental regions and offices. For example, the Income Tax Department’s Kolkata regional site publishes Tax Assistant confirmation, seniority, transfer/posting, and promotion orders. This demonstrates that the cadre is administered through departmental establishments; a candidate should not assume a particular city or office from the SSC post title alone.
bullets: Employer: CBDT, Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.
Cadre: Group C Tax Assistant, distinct from Tax Assistant in CBIC.
Location and posting administration depend on departmental allocation and personnel orders.

sections.heading: Progression: departmental, vacancy-dependent
paragraphs: Career movement is governed by applicable recruitment rules, seniority, eligibility conditions, departmental processes, and vacancies rather than by an automatic time schedule. Departmental records from the Income Tax Department’s Kolkata region separately show Tax Assistant and Senior Tax Assistant seniority and promotion actions, as well as promotion actions for Income Tax Inspectors and Income Tax Officers.

A Central Administrative Tribunal matter concerning Income Tax Department employees describes individuals initially appointed as Tax Assistants after SSC CGL, later promoted to Senior Tax Assistant, and then promoted as Income Tax Inspectors after passing the departmental examination. This is evidence of a documented route, not a guarantee of timing or of promotion for every appointee. Candidates should check the rules and orders applicable to their own region and year of service.
bullets: Tax Assistant and Senior Tax Assistant are distinct departmental grades reflected in regional seniority and promotion records.
Progression to Income Tax Inspector has occurred through departmental promotion processes.
Promotion pace is variable and should not be inferred from any single region’s orders or individual case.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: As of the SSC CGL notice uploaded on May 21, 2026, Tax Assistant in CBDT is shown at Pay Level 4: ₹25,500–₹81,100 in the published pay matrix. That figure is useful as a basic-pay context for the post, but it is not an annual package or take-home-pay estimate.

Actual monthly receipts can differ from the Level 4 basic figure because government pay is processed under applicable pay, allowance, tax, deduction, posting, and service rules. For an application decision, use the relevant year’s SSC notice for the pay level and consult appointment/pay documents for the terms that apply after allocation.
bullets: Dated reference point: SSC notice uploaded May 21, 2026.
Published level: Pay Level 4.
Published basic-pay range: ₹25,500–₹81,100.
Do not treat the range as a fixed in-hand salary.

title: Technical Officer A (DRDO)
description: An entry-level Technical Officer post in DRDO’s technical cadre, typically reached by eligible Senior Technical Assistants through departmental assessment and promotion.

quick_facts.label: Cadre position and status
quick_facts.value: Technical Officer ‘A’ (TO-A) is a Category-B grade in DRDO’s Defence Research Technical Cadre (DRTC). It is classified as Group ‘B’, Gazetted, Non-Ministerial.

quick_facts.label: Usual entry route
quick_facts.value: Under the current DRTC rules, new direct recruitment is confined to the lowest grades of the two categories; in Category-B, that lowest grade is Senior Technical Assistant ‘B’ (STA-B). The rules place promotion from STA-B to TO-A within the cadre’s merit-based Limited Flexible Complementing Scheme.

quick_facts.label: Promotion eligibility
quick_facts.value: For consideration from STA-B to TO-A, the Third Schedule specifies six years of regular service in STA-B. Eligibility is ordinarily determined as of 1 July of the assessment year, subject to the rule’s stated relaxations in limited circumstances.

quick_facts.label: Assessment and selection
quick_facts.value: Promotion is merit-based and assessed through the Central Assessment Board. For the STA-B-to-TO-A step, the rules cap promotions at 50% of eligible employees in an annual assessment; eligibility alone therefore does not guarantee promotion.

quick_facts.label: Pay-level context
quick_facts.value: The Gazette-notified 2024 DRTC schedule places TO-A at 7th CPC Pay Matrix Level 7, with a stated range of ₹44,900–₹1,42,400. This is a dated basic-pay-matrix context; actual monthly remuneration varies with applicable government allowances, location, deductions, and future pay-rule revisions.

quick_facts.label: Next grade
quick_facts.value: The normal next DRTC Category-B grade is Technical Officer ‘B’ (TO-B), a Group ‘A’, Gazetted, Non-Ministerial Level 10 post. The current schedule specifies six years’ regular service for consideration from TO-A to TO-B, with up to 40% of eligible employees promotable in an annual assessment on overall merit.

sections.heading: Role and responsibilities
paragraphs: Technical Officer ‘A’ is a promoted technical-cadre grade rather than a separately advertised entry-level direct-recruitment post. The DRTC rules do not prescribe a single uniform job description for every TO-A. They state that, on promotion, an employee may be required to continue performing the duties performed before promotion or to perform other duties assigned by the appointing authority.

DRDO’s organisational work provides the operating context: it formulates and executes scientific research, design, development, testing and evaluation programmes for defence systems, subsystems, devices and products. A TO-A’s particular technical duties will consequently depend on the laboratory or establishment, discipline, functional requirement and assignment rather than the grade title alone.
bullets: Expect role-specific technical work and duties assigned by the relevant DRDO laboratory or establishment.
Do not assume that promotion necessarily means an immediate change of technical specialty or day-to-day work; the rules expressly allow continuation of prior duties.
The post is part of the civilian Defence Research Technical Cadre, not the separate DRDO scientist service (DRDS).

sections.heading: How the post is reached
paragraphs: For the canonical route, an employee joins or serves in the Category-B feeder grade of Senior Technical Assistant ‘B’ and is considered for promotion to TO-A through the DRTC’s merit-based Limited Flexible Complementing Scheme. Current rules make employees eligible for assessment after the stipulated regular-service period; for STA-B to TO-A, that period is six years.

The rules distinguish eligibility from selection. An Eligibility Screening Committee recommends eligible personnel for Central Assessment, and the Central Assessment Board assesses suitability for TO-A. In each annual assessment, no more than 50% of eligible STA-B employees may be promoted to TO-A, with promotions based on overall merit.

The current rules provide for direct recruitment only to the lowest grade of Category-B, STA-B—not to TO-A. Applicants seeking to enter DRDO from outside should therefore monitor CEPTAM recruitment for STA-B and read the specific advertisement in force for qualifications, disciplines, age limits, vacancies and selection procedure.
bullets: Feeder grade: Senior Technical Assistant ‘B’ (STA-B).
Minimum regular service for consideration: six years in STA-B under the 2024 schedule.
Selection mechanism: eligibility screening followed by Central Assessment; promotion is merit-based and subject to the annual promotion percentage.
External entry context: CEPTAM handles DRDO’s direct recruitment of Senior Technical Assistants and Technicians.

sections.heading: Capabilities relevant to progression
paragraphs: The formal promotion framework emphasizes sustained, meritorious performance within the technical cadre: candidates must first satisfy the required regular-service condition, pass eligibility screening and be assessed by the Central Assessment Board. Accordingly, maintaining a documented record of effective technical work, reliability and readiness for formal assessment is central to the progression route.

Specialisation is role-dependent. The DRTC rules allow the appointing authority to choose specialisations for lowest-grade recruitment according to functional requirements, while DRDO’s mission spans research, design, development, testing and evaluation. The technical knowledge most useful to a prospective TO-A is therefore the knowledge relevant to the employee’s assigned discipline and laboratory.
bullets: Discipline-specific technical competence aligned to the employing laboratory or establishment.
Sustained performance that can support merit-based assessment and progression.
Ability to undertake assigned duties, including continuation of prior work or new duties after promotion.

sections.heading: Workplace context
paragraphs: TO-A is a civilian DRTC position in DRDO. Work is performed within DRDO laboratories and establishments supporting defence research and development activities; the exact setting depends on the posting, technical discipline and organisational requirement.

The promotion architecture itself reflects an organisation-wide cadre: TO-A assessments are handled through a Central Assessment Board chaired by the Chairperson of CEPTAM or a nominee, with departmental members and a laboratory or establishment representative. This indicates that career assessment is centrally governed even though day-to-day work is tied to an assigned laboratory or establishment.
bullets: Employer: Defence Research and Development Organisation, Ministry of Defence, Government of India.
Work setting: DRDO laboratory or establishment; duties are assignment-specific.
Career assessment: central assessment involving CEPTAM and the relevant laboratory or establishment.

sections.heading: Career progression
paragraphs: The Category-B DRTC sequence shown in the current rules is STA-B (Level 6) → TO-A (Level 7) → TO-B (Level 10) → TO-C (Level 11) → TO-D (Level 12). Each move is governed by the merit-based Limited Flexible Complementing Scheme, not by automatic seniority progression.

For the next move after TO-A, the Third Schedule specifies six years of regular service for consideration to TO-B. At an annual assessment, up to 40% of eligible TO-A employees may be promoted to TO-B, based on overall merit. Assessments are to be held once each year, with recommendations ordinarily implemented from 1 July of the relevant year unless the board makes a specific recommendation on the effective date.
bullets: TO-A → TO-B: six years’ regular service required for consideration under the current schedule.
TO-A → TO-B: annual promotion ceiling of 40% of eligible employees, with selection on overall merit.
TO-B is a Group ‘A’, Gazetted, Non-Ministerial Level 10 grade.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: As notified in the 2024 DRTC Recruitment Rules, TO-A is in Pay Matrix Level 7, ₹44,900–₹1,42,400. This is the published pay-matrix range rather than a guaranteed take-home salary or a current vacancy offer.

For comparison within the same route, STA-B is listed at Level 6, ₹35,400–₹1,12,400, while TO-B is listed at Level 10, ₹56,100–₹1,77,500. Allowances and net pay should be checked against the applicable Government of India rules and the specific posting at the time of appointment or promotion.
bullets: TO-A: Level 7, ₹44,900–₹1,42,400 in the 2024 notified schedule.
STA-B feeder grade: Level 6, ₹35,400–₹1,12,400.
TO-B next grade: Level 10, ₹56,100–₹1,77,500.
Pay ranges and allowances are variable over time and should not be treated as a current in-hand-pay estimate.

title: Technician B (DRDO)
description: A higher technical-cadre position in DRDO reached by promotion from Technician A through the applicable departmental assessment and service requirements.

quick_facts.label: Cadre position
quick_facts.value: Technician ‘B’ is a Category-A Defence Research Technical Cadre post at Pay Level 4, classified as Group ‘C’, Non-Gazetted and Non-Ministerial under the 2024 DRDO Technical Cadre Recruitment Rules.

quick_facts.label: Promotion gateway
quick_facts.value: The prescribed progression into Technician ‘B’ is from Technician ‘A’. A Technician ‘A’ needs five years of regular service for consideration, and up to 75% of eligible employees may be promoted in an annual assessment, on overall merit.

quick_facts.label: Assessment timing and authority
quick_facts.value: Eligible employees are assessed annually; ordinarily, the qualifying service is measured as of 1 July of the assessment year. Promotions through Technical Assistant ‘B’ in Category-A are assessed by a Local Assessment Board.

quick_facts.label: External-entry context
quick_facts.value: The rules provide direct recruitment and Departmental Competitive Examination routes only for the lowest Category-A grade, Technician ‘A’, rather than for Technician ‘B’. DRDO states that CEPTAM manages recruitment for DRTC technical posts.

quick_facts.label: Pay-matrix context
quick_facts.value: The 2024 rules list Technician ‘B’ at Level 4, ₹25,500–₹81,100 in the pay matrix. This is basic-pay range context from the rules, not a current take-home-pay guarantee; allowances and applicable government orders can vary.

sections.heading: Role and duties after promotion
paragraphs: The recruitment rules do not publish a separate, universal duty list for Technician ‘B’. Instead, they provide that a person promoted from one grade to another can be required to continue the duties performed before promotion, or to undertake other duties assigned by the appointing authority. In practice, the precise technical work therefore depends on the DRDO laboratory or establishment, trade/discipline, and assigned project or support function.
source_urls
bullets: A Technician ‘B’ is part of the Category-A Defence Research Technical Cadre, above Technician ‘A’ and below Technician ‘C’.
The appointing authority may retain the employee on substantially the same work after promotion or assign different duties.

sections.heading: How this position is reached
paragraphs: Technician ‘B’ is principally an internal career-progression grade, not the normal external entry point. Under the 2024 rules, direct recruitment is confined to the lowest grades of Category-A and Category-B; for Category-A, that entry grade is Technician ‘A’. The rules also allow a Departmental Competitive Examination route to the lowest Category-A grade for qualifying departmental employees with at least three years of regular DRDO service, subject to the prescribed qualifications.
source_urls
bullets: Enter the Category-A technical stream as Technician ‘A’ through the applicable DRDO/CEPTAM recruitment process, or, where notified, through the Departmental Competitive Examination route to Technician ‘A’.

For Technician ‘A’ external entry, the rules specify Class X/equivalent plus the relevant ITI certificate, qualifying institutional certificate, National Trade Certificate, or National Apprenticeship Certificate, as applicable.
Serve as Technician ‘A’ for the required regular-service period and become eligible for the annual promotion assessment under the Limited Flexible Complementing Scheme.

sections.heading: Promotion rules and onward progression
paragraphs: Promotion from Technician ‘A’ to Technician ‘B’ is governed by DRDO’s merit-based Limited Flexible Complementing Scheme. The Eligibility Screening Committee identifies eligible personnel under approved norms, and the applicable Assessment Board considers promotion. Five years of regular service in Technician ‘A’ is the stated minimum for consideration; the rules cap promotions at 75% of eligible Technician ‘A’ employees in an annual assessment and require selection on overall merit.

The next listed Category-A grade is Technician ‘C’. A Technician ‘B’ requires five years of regular service to be considered for Technician ‘C’; the annual promotion percentage at that step is up to 65% of eligible employees. The subsequent listed path is Technical Assistant ‘B’, Technical Officer, and then Technical Officer ‘B’. These are eligibility and assessment rules, not assurances that an individual promotion will be granted.
source_urls
bullets: Annual assessments are ordinarily implemented from 1 July of the year to which the Assessment Board pertains, unless the Board specifies otherwise.
Unauthorised absence and extraordinary leave on personal grounds do not count toward qualifying service; the rules include limited relaxation provisions in specified circumstances.
For promotions up to Technical Assistant ‘B’ in Category-A, assessment is by a Local Assessment Board.

sections.heading: Pay context
paragraphs: As set out in the Ministry of Defence’s 2024 DRDO Technical Cadre Recruitment Rules, Technician ‘B’ carries Pay Level 4 in the central pay matrix, ₹25,500–₹81,100. This should be read as the rule-based basic-pay matrix for the grade, published in September 2024. Actual monthly gross and take-home pay may differ by pay-cell placement, dearness allowance, house-rent or government-accommodation status, transport and other admissible allowances, deductions, location, and later revisions to central-government compensation rules.

title: Technician (DRDO)
description: A Group 'C' Non-Gazetted, Non-Ministerial technical role in the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) responsible for operating and maintaining laboratory equipment and assisting in technical tasks.

quick_facts.label: Current official post title
quick_facts.value: The current CEPTAM recruitment designation is Technician-A (Tech-A), not “Technician B.” It is part of the Defence Research & Development Organisation Technical Cadre (DRTC).

quick_facts.label: Service classification
quick_facts.value: Technician-A is a Group ‘C’, Non-Gazetted, Non-Ministerial post.

quick_facts.label: Core entry qualification
quick_facts.value: In CEPTAM-11, applicants needed Class 10/equivalent plus a certificate from a recognised ITI in the applicable trade. Where an ITI does not award that trade certificate, a recognised minimum one-year certificate, National Trade Certificate (NTC), or National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) may qualify, subject to the notification’s terms.

quick_facts.label: Recruitment route
quick_facts.value: CEPTAM conducts recruitment for DRDO’s technical cadre. For Technician-A in CEPTAM-11, selection comprised Tier-I CBT screening, Tier-II subject-specific CBT, and a mandatory qualifying trade test, except where the advertisement provides a trade-test exemption for eligible recent DRDO apprentices.

quick_facts.label: Pay context
quick_facts.value: For the CEPTAM-11 cycle, Technician-A carried 7th CPC Pay Matrix Level 2: ₹19,900–₹63,200 basic pay, with allowances and benefits governed by then-extant Government of India rules. This is dated recruitment context, not a guaranteed take-home salary.

quick_facts.label: Posting and mobility
quick_facts.value: CEPTAM-11 identified postings across DRDO locations and stated all-India service liability. Selected candidates could be posted anywhere in India, including field or remote locations, and the notification stated a minimum five-year tenure at the first posting station, subject to its terms and public-interest transfers.

sections.heading: What a DRDO Technician-A does
paragraphs: Technician-A is a trade-based technical-cadre role rather than one uniform job assignment. The CEPTAM-11 recruitment listed trade streams including electrician, electronics, fitter, machinist, CNC operator, draughtsman (mechanical), COPA, carpenter, welder, surveyor, optical worker and others. In practice, the technical work is therefore tied to the trade for which a candidate is recruited and the needs of the nominated DRDO laboratory, establishment or unit.

DRDO describes its work as research and development of defence systems, technologies, infrastructure and related activities for the armed services. A Technician-A should therefore expect practical, trade-specific technical support in that research-and-development environment, rather than a general clerical role.
bullets: Apply only for a trade whose stated qualification exactly matches the notification.
Treat the post code and named trade as central to the work profile and examination preparation.
Read the specific recruitment advertisement for the applicable cycle because listed trades, vacancies and posting stations can change.

sections.heading: Entry route through CEPTAM
paragraphs: The principal entry route is an open CEPTAM direct-recruitment notification for Technician-A. In the CEPTAM-11 cycle, the normal age band was 18–28 years as of January 1, 2026, with category-specific relaxations under Government of India rules. Eligibility, age cut-off, trade list, fee and documentation must be checked afresh for each notification.

For CEPTAM-11, candidates took Tier-I in computer-based-test format for screening; it covered general science, English, quantitative aptitude/general mathematics, and general intelligence and reasoning. Tier-II included a subject-specific test for the post code, followed by an ITI-level practical trade test that was qualifying in nature. Tier-II and trade-test scheduling and selection mechanics are notification-specific.

Applicants should not assume a polytechnic diploma is the standard prerequisite for this post. Technician-A is primarily an ITI/trade-certificate route; the CEPTAM-11 advertisement did state that diploma or bachelor’s-degree holders could be eligible only if they also fulfilled the prescribed Technician-A educational requirement, while certain higher qualifications were excluded for that cycle.
bullets: Complete Class 10 or its recognised equivalent.
Obtain the required ITI certificate in the advertised trade; use the NTC/NAC or one-year-certificate alternative only where the notification permits it.
Monitor DRDO’s official CEPTAM vacancy page and submit applications only through the official process.
Prepare both CBT fundamentals and hands-on ITI-level trade competence.

sections.heading: Skills to build
paragraphs: The official examination pattern gives a practical skills map for aspirants: foundational general science, English, quantitative aptitude/general mathematics, reasoning, and strong command of the particular ITI trade. Tier-II is subject-specific, and the trade test is designed to assess practical skills in the related trade at ITI level under the syllabus specified by the Directorate General of Training (DGT).

Beyond test preparation, candidates benefit from disciplined trade practice: interpreting task requirements, using the trade’s tools and methods safely, and working accurately enough to meet a qualifying practical assessment. This is an inference from the notification’s ITI-level trade-test requirement, rather than a substitute for a laboratory-specific job description.
bullets: Trade theory and hands-on ITI practical work.
General science, basic mathematics, English and reasoning for Tier-I.
Accuracy and timed CBT practice; CEPTAM-11 used negative marking in Tier-I and the subject-specific part of Tier-II.
Document readiness: educational certificates, identity/age proof and applicable reservation or relaxation records.

sections.heading: Workplace, posting and service conditions
paragraphs: Technician-A recruits are nominated to DRDO laboratories, establishments or units. CEPTAM-11 listed stations such as Ahilyanagar, Ambernath, Balasore, Bengaluru, Chandigarh, Chennai, Dehradun, Delhi, Haldwani, Hyderabad, Jodhpur, Kanpur, Kochi, Mysuru, Nashik, Pune and Visakhapatnam; the actual station depends on the notified trade, vacancies and organisational requirement.

The CEPTAM-11 service conditions stated that recruits would initially serve a two-year probation and could be required to serve anywhere in India, including field or remote locations. It also stated that DRDO could post candidates anywhere in India and that first-posting transfer requests would ordinarily not be entertained for five years, while transfers in public interest remained possible.
bullets: Expect a laboratory, establishment or unit assignment—not necessarily a posting in the applicant’s home state.
Treat location preferences as preferences, not a guarantee of allotment.
Review the current notice carefully because stations, vacancy counts and service terms can be revised by recruitment cycle.

sections.heading: Career progression
paragraphs: CEPTAM-11 states that DRTC posts are covered by the merit-based Limited Flexible Complementing Scheme (LFCS) for promotion to the next higher grade. That establishes an internal promotion framework, but the advertisement does not provide a universal time-to-promotion or assure promotion for every individual.

A Technician-A who wants to move into a different entry-grade technical post should distinguish internal progression from fresh direct recruitment. For example, Senior Technical Assistant-B (STA-B) is separately advertised as a Group ‘B’, Non-Gazetted, Non-Ministerial role with different degree/diploma-based qualification requirements and selection rules.
bullets: Use the applicable DRTC/LFCS rules and departmental guidance for promotion details.
Do not treat a diploma alone as an automatic conversion or promotion to STA-B.
Track official CEPTAM notices for vacancies and eligibility conditions relevant to any future direct-recruitment application.

sections.heading: Compensation and application-cost context
paragraphs: As published for CEPTAM-11, Technician-A was in Pay Matrix Level 2, ₹19,900–₹63,200 basic pay under the 7th Central Pay Commission. The notice also referred to dearness allowance, house-rent allowance, transport allowance, children education allowance, leave travel concession, medical facilities, CSD facility and other benefits under extant government rules; pension coverage was stated as NPS/UPS according to the rules then in force. Allowances, pension coverage, deductions, city classification and resulting in-hand pay are variable and should not be inferred from the basic-pay range alone.

For the CEPTAM-11 application cycle, General/OBC/EWS/MSP Technician-A applicants paid ₹600 upfront: ₹100 non-refundable application fee plus ₹500 refundable fee, while women, SC, ST, PwBD and eligible ex-servicemen paid ₹500 refundable fee. The ₹500 refundable component was payable back only to candidates who appeared in Tier-I. These are historical, cycle-specific figures; future fees and refund terms can change.
bullets: Use the notified pay level as basic-pay context, not an estimate of monthly take-home pay.
Check the current notice for current allowances, pension rules, fee categories and refund rules.
Vacancy totals and compensation-related conditions are subject to the relevant notification and Government of India rules.
