title: Monitoring and Evaluation Officer
description: A professional who tracks programme indicators, evaluates outcomes, and reports evidence for public-health interventions.

quick_facts.label: Core purpose
quick_facts.value: Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Officers establish or support results frameworks, define and track indicators, assess programme progress and outcomes, analyse data, and prepare evidence-based reports for managers, government counterparts, donors, and partners.

quick_facts.label: Relevant education routes
quick_facts.value: For Indian public-health and development programmes, published employer requirements have included master's-level study in public health, health management, community/social development, development economics, management, and other social sciences. This makes the node’s MPH and MSW parent qualifications relevant routes, though each vacancy sets its own eligibility criteria.

quick_facts.label: Experience expectation
quick_facts.value: Requirements vary sharply by seniority: a WHO India National Professional Officer (M&E) notice required two years of relevant public-health-programme experience, while an earlier India-based UNDP RBSK M&E Officer vacancy required at least 10 years of relevant post-master's experience.

quick_facts.label: Indian employment contexts
quick_facts.value: The role appears in government-linked health systems and development programmes: examples include WHO India support to national health programmes, the UNDP-supported RBSK unit in New Delhi, and National Health Mission recruitment/appointment activity for District Monitoring and Evaluation Officers in Madhya Pradesh.

sections.heading: What a Monitoring and Evaluation Officer does
paragraphs: In public-health interventions, the role turns programme plans into measurable evidence. Typical work includes helping design monitoring and evaluation plans; developing logframes, indicator matrices, data-collection formats and supportive-supervision tools; setting baselines and targets; and checking whether implementation is progressing against agreed indicators.

The officer also validates and analyses incoming programme data, synthesises results in tables, graphs, presentations and periodic reports, and identifies achievements, gaps, bottlenecks, lessons and corrective actions. The work commonly involves coordinating with implementing teams, government authorities, technical partners and information-system specialists so that reporting processes and data standards are consistent.

Evaluation duties can extend beyond routine reporting: WHO's published role description includes support for mid-term evaluation methodology and consolidation of evaluation reports, while the UNDP India RBSK role included operationalising an integrated M&E system and supplying analysed information to the programme unit and the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
bullets: Design or maintain results frameworks, logframes, indicator definitions, baselines, targets and reporting matrices.
Develop or improve data-collection, monitoring and supportive-supervision tools.
Clean, validate, analyse and interpret programme data; communicate findings through reports, dashboards, tables, graphs and presentations.
Support periodic reviews and evaluations, document lessons learned, and recommend action when delivery is off track.
Coordinate reporting and data use with programme teams, government counterparts, implementing partners and donors.

sections.heading: Entry routes from MPH and MSW
paragraphs: An MPH is a direct route where the position is embedded in health programmes, because employers may specifically seek public-health education and experience with health-programme monitoring. WHO India's published M&E role listed a university degree in medicine or public health as essential and postgraduate study in preventive/social medicine, community medicine, public health or business administration as desirable.

An MSW can be a relevant route particularly for community, social-development and implementation-facing programmes. An India-based UNDP M&E Officer vacancy accepted master's qualifications in community/social development and other social sciences alongside public health and health management. Candidates from either route become more competitive by gaining supervised experience in field implementation, routine data systems, surveys, research, reporting or programme coordination.

There is no single statutory Indian licence or one nationally uniform qualification for this job title evident from these employer sources. Applicants should therefore read each recruitment notice for its subject, experience, language, software and location requirements.
bullets: MPH route: build exposure to epidemiology, biostatistics, health information systems, programme management, evaluation methods and public-health field placements.
MSW route: build exposure to community development, research methods, participatory monitoring, implementation management, safeguarding and outcome reporting.
For either route: seek internships or entry-level work involving data quality checks, surveys, dashboard/report preparation, HMIS/MIS work, programme reviews or partner coordination.
Document demonstrable outputs such as indicator trackers, analysis plans, data-collection tools, evaluation protocols, reports or presentations.

sections.heading: Skills employers look for
paragraphs: The role combines quantitative and programme-management capability. Published India-focused role descriptions call for analysis of programme data, development of monitoring frameworks and indicators, use of Excel or statistical software, data collection, report writing, and presentation of findings. The WHO India notice also emphasised rigorous analysis, clear and influential presentation, computer skills, coordination and collaboration.

Practical M&E competency includes understanding results-based management: distinguishing activities, outputs and outcomes; defining usable indicators; specifying data sources and collection frequency; checking data quality; and using findings to improve implementation. Communication matters because officers must make technical evidence intelligible to programme managers, government counterparts, field teams and partners.

For public-health and social programmes, professional practice also requires sensitivity to equity, inclusion, confidentiality and ethical data handling. These requirements are especially important when data concern communities, children, patients or other vulnerable populations.
bullets: Indicator, logframe and results-framework design.
Quantitative and qualitative data collection, cleaning, validation, analysis and interpretation.
Excel and, where required, statistical, database, GIS, HMIS or other information-system tools.
Survey and evaluation protocol/tool development; baseline, midline and endline work.
Clear technical writing, report production, data visualisation and presentation.
Stakeholder coordination, training or capacity building, and practical problem solving.
Ethical, confidential and inclusive handling of programme data.

sections.heading: Where the work is done
paragraphs: In India, M&E Officers can work within public-health programme units, state or district health systems, government-supported missions, UN and multilateral technical-assistance offices, NGOs, research or implementation partners, and donor-funded projects. Work is often a mix of office-based analysis and reporting with coordination across national, state, district and community levels.

The work can involve liaising with government and non-government institutions, field offices and partner organisations; reviewing data received from multiple implementation sites; and supporting monitoring visits, training or review meetings. The exact balance between desk analysis and travel depends on the programme, geography and contract.
bullets: National, state, district or facility-linked public-health programmes.
Government missions and health-system implementation units.
UN, multilateral and donor-supported technical-assistance projects.
Non-governmental organisations and research/implementation partners delivering health or social interventions.

sections.heading: Career progression
paragraphs: Career development is employer- and programme-dependent rather than governed by one universal Indian ladder. An early-career practitioner may begin with data collection, reporting, research assistance or district-level monitoring responsibilities, then move toward independent framework design, evaluation management, technical assistance, capacity building and coordination across multiple geographies or partners.

Senior posts may require substantial prior M&E-system experience. For example, the historical UNDP RBSK India vacancy sought experience establishing M&E frameworks and managing health-project M&E systems at state or national level, while WHO India described work supporting comprehensive M&E planning, evaluation methodology and country-office performance assessment. Possible onward titles therefore include M&E Specialist, MERL Officer/Manager, Programme Manager, Research or Health-Information-System Specialist, or technical adviser, but titles and thresholds vary by organisation.
bullets: Build from routine data and reporting tasks toward framework design, evaluation planning and data-use leadership.
Gain experience across field implementation, HMIS/MIS, surveys, evaluation and multi-stakeholder coordination.
Develop a portfolio showing tools, analyses, reports and evidence of improvements made from findings.
Treat job titles as variable: assess the actual scope, grade, contract type and experience requirements in each vacancy.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: Pay is highly variable by employer, grade, location, funding source, contract type and seniority; historical vacancy figures should not be treated as a current market salary benchmark. For dated context, WHO India's 30 June 2023 National Professional Officer (M&E) notice stated an annual base salary starting at INR 2,626,256, subject to applicable mandatory deductions. A much earlier UNDP India RBSK posting, with a 10-year post-master's experience requirement, listed INR 127,175 per month taxable.

Before comparing offers, check whether the stated amount is monthly or annual; gross or net; employee, consultant or service-contract compensation; and whether pension, insurance, travel or other benefits are included. Verify the live recruitment notice because historical figures, grades and contract conditions may no longer apply.
bullets: Use current vacancy notices, not old listings, for compensation decisions.
Compare role scope and experience threshold alongside salary; both cited examples were senior or specialised posts.
Check deductions, benefits, contract duration and whether remuneration is taxable before evaluating an offer.

title: Motion Graphics Designer
description: A designer who creates animated graphics, titles, explainer videos, and visual effects for digital media.

quick_facts.label: Common deliverables
quick_facts.value: Employer briefs include motion graphics for corporate and explainer videos, websites, marketing demonstrations, product walkthroughs and social-media content.

quick_facts.label: Entry evidence
quick_facts.value: A demonstrable portfolio can be central to selection: a 2025 public-sector vacancy specifically required a strong motion-graphics portfolio alongside video-editing ability.

quick_facts.label: Education routes
quick_facts.value: Relevant formal-study routes include design, animation, visual effects and media technology. For example, NID's 2026–27 B.Des. includes Animation Film Design and Graphic Design specialisations; individual employers may set different qualification and experience requirements.

quick_facts.label: Typical software and production knowledge
quick_facts.value: Current Indian role specifications commonly ask for tools such as Adobe After Effects, Photoshop and Premiere Pro, plus knowledge of timing, continuity, special effects, 3D and compositing.

sections.heading: What a Motion Graphics Designer does
paragraphs: Motion graphics design extends graphic-design practice into time-based media. In a Government of India National Instructional Media Institute role description, the work includes using computer programs to create 2D and 3D animation and contributing across conceptualisation, scripting, storyboarding, animation and editing; keyframing and typography may also be part of the work.

In Indian employer briefs, the role is commonly tied to communication goals: translating ideas into visual stories, producing branded video assets, and working with creative or cross-functional teams. Deliverables can range from explainers and campaigns to product walkthroughs, social content and interface motion.
bullets: Interpret a creative brief and select an appropriate visual treatment, pacing and animation approach.
Develop storyboards, layouts, typography, transitions and animated assets.
Animate, composite and edit video while maintaining brand standards and delivery requirements.
Coordinate feedback and hand-offs with creative teams, video editors, 3D artists, developers or product teams, depending on the workplace.

sections.heading: Entry routes in India
paragraphs: There is no single nationally mandated qualification shown by the sources for this job title. Recruitment requirements vary by employer and seniority. A 2025 C-DIT (Government of Kerala) Motion Graphics Designer notification accepted either a degree in Design, Animation, Visual Effects, Media Technology or a related field with two years’ production-house experience, or Class 12 plus a related diploma with five years’ experience. This illustrates that qualifications and demonstrated experience are assessed together in at least some formal recruitment processes.

A structured higher-education route can build foundations in visual storytelling and animation. NID’s 2026–27 B.Des. admissions handbook lists Animation Film Design and Graphic Design in its Communication Design faculty, and its Animation Film Design teaching includes a motion-graphics workshop alongside storyboarding, time-and-image and sound-design learning. Independent practice, project work and a portfolio remain important complements to formal study.
bullets: After Class 12: pursue a relevant degree or diploma in design, animation, visual effects, media technology, film/video or a closely related discipline; check the current admission and eligibility rules of each institution.
Build a portfolio with brief-led work: title sequences, animated brand assets, explainers, social-video assets, UI motion or short narrative pieces.
Seek internships, junior roles, freelance briefs or campus productions to learn feedback cycles, file organisation and production deadlines.
Read each vacancy closely: requirements can differ substantially across agencies, production houses, technology companies, broadcasters and public-sector contracts.

sections.heading: Skills to develop
paragraphs: The core is a blend of design judgment and animation craft. The NIMI description highlights 2D/3D animation, typography, layout, colour theory, creative thinking and interpersonal communication. The C-DIT specification additionally calls for a strong portfolio, video-editing ability, timing and continuity, special effects, 3D and compositing.

Tool requirements should be treated as vacancy-specific rather than universal. Adobe After Effects, Photoshop and Premiere Pro appear in the C-DIT recruitment specification; a current Publicis Groupe India listing also names animation/compositing tools and adjacent tools such as Illustrator, Animate, Figma and InDesign. A candidate should prioritise understanding animation principles and visual communication over merely collecting software badges.
bullets: Design fundamentals: layout, typography, colour, hierarchy and brand consistency.
Motion fundamentals: timing, keyframes, transitions, continuity, pacing and storytelling.
Production: storyboarding, asset preparation, animation, compositing, rendering and video editing.
Technical fluency: learn the software and file formats required by the target workplace; build a portfolio that shows the process as well as finished work.
Collaboration: interpret briefs, present creative choices, manage revisions and meet delivery timelines.

sections.heading: Where the work is done
paragraphs: The role can sit in production houses, advertising and brand-content teams, animation studios, broadcasters, digital-product organisations and e-learning or gaming-related organisations. NID identifies production houses, TV channels, independent animation studios, digital gaming studios, UI/UX organisations and e-learning companies as employment settings for Animation Film Design graduates. Current employer listings also show work connected with digital campaigns, XR applications, product demonstrations, marketing and social content.

Work arrangements vary. A recent Bengaluru role was advertised as hybrid or remote, while other vacancies are location-based and team-oriented. Candidates should therefore confirm the employer’s current location, remote-work, equipment, working-hours and employment-status terms before applying.
bullets: Creative agencies and in-house marketing teams: advertising, campaign and social-media assets.
Production, animation and post-production studios: titles, explainers, VFX-adjacent work and video content.
Technology and product teams: interface animation, product demonstrations and interactive/XR visual assets.
Education and media organisations: e-learning, broadcast and public-information content.

sections.heading: Career development
paragraphs: Career development commonly comes through deeper capability in animation, visual storytelling and production responsibility, rather than through a single prescribed ladder. NID reports employment outcomes for Animation Film Design graduates across animator, character designer, storyboard artist, designer, producer, consultant and creative-director work, as well as independent studios. This suggests that a motion-graphics practitioner may broaden into adjacent animation, design-direction, production or independent-practice paths as their portfolio and experience develop.

A practical progression strategy is to move from clearly scoped assets to ownership of larger sequences or campaigns, while choosing a specialism that matches target employers—for example 2D brand motion, 3D/compositing, character animation, product/UI motion or video post-production. These are career options, not guaranteed promotions; titles and responsibilities are employer-specific.
bullets: Early career: strengthen execution, revision discipline and a concise portfolio of finished motion pieces.
Developing practitioner: take ownership of storyboards, visual systems, longer edits, compositing or a chosen technical specialism.
Broader options: animation, storyboarding, character design, production, creative direction, consulting, freelance work or studio entrepreneurship.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: Compensation is highly variable by city, employer, employment type, portfolio, software/production specialism and experience; a single posted figure should not be treated as an India-wide salary benchmark. As a dated public-sector example, C-DIT’s 2025 notification advertised one Motion Graphics Designer role on a one-year, performance-extendable contract at ₹34,190–₹37,800 per month consolidated, with stated qualification and experience criteria. The amount and terms applied to that specific notification only and may no longer be available.

When comparing offers, consider the full arrangement: fixed versus freelance/contract engagement, expected working hours, remote or on-site requirements, ownership and reuse rights for work, equipment/software provision, benefits and the scope of revisions or delivery responsibility.
bullets: Use dated vacancy notices as examples of individual offers, not as current market-wide pay data.
Compare annual fixed pay or consolidated monthly pay with benefits, contract duration, location costs and the work scope.
Keep a portfolio and documented project outcomes: employers may assess demonstrated craft and production experience alongside formal qualifications.

title: MRI Technologist
description: A radiography professional specialising in magnetic resonance imaging procedures, MRI safety protocols, and scanner operation.

quick_facts.label: Indian professional classification
quick_facts.value: MRI work sits within the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP) category of “Radiology and Imaging Technologist,” which explicitly includes Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) alongside diagnostic radiography, CT, mammography and sonography.

quick_facts.label: Common education route
quick_facts.value: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) model curriculum identifies two entry pathways in Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology (MRIT): a 2.5-year diploma including six months of clinical training, and a four-year bachelor’s programme including one year of clinical training/internship.

quick_facts.label: Bachelor’s entry background
quick_facts.value: For its model B.Sc. MRIT route, MoHFW specifies 10+2/equivalent with Physics, Chemistry and Biology, while noting that institutional selection and admission rules apply.

quick_facts.label: Scope and supervision
quick_facts.value: Under the NCAHP Act’s listed description, medical imaging and therapeutic equipment professionals operate imaging equipment to produce images for diagnosis and treatment and work under the supervision of a radiologist or other medical professional.

quick_facts.label: MRI-specific preparation
quick_facts.value: The MoHFW MRIT curriculum includes MRI instrumentation, pulse sequences, whole-body protocols, artefact management, MRI safety and MRI quality assurance.

sections.heading: What an MRI Technologist does
paragraphs: An MRI Technologist is a radiography/imaging professional focused on safely acquiring diagnostic MRI examinations. In the broader statutory classification, MRI is named as a radiology and imaging technologist specialism; the role operates imaging equipment to create body-structure images that support diagnosis and treatment, within a radiologist-led or other appropriate medical-professional supervision structure.

The MoHFW model curriculum describes graduate-level MRIT capability as independently undertaking MRI procedures, operating imaging equipment, processing and technically evaluating images, providing empathetic patient care, documenting orders, maintaining equipment, and identifying and managing emergencies. In practice, this means screening and preparing patients, selecting and executing approved scan protocols, monitoring the patient during the examination, checking image quality, and escalating clinical or safety concerns rather than independently interpreting the diagnostic findings.
bullets: Perform MRI examinations and obtain technically adequate images using approved protocols.
Apply MRI safety screening, safe access control, equipment checks and quality-assurance processes.
Prepare, position and communicate with patients; maintain dignity, comfort and observation during the scan.
Document workflow and orders, manage images in digital systems, and coordinate with radiologists, nurses and other imaging-team members.
Recognise emergencies or unsafe conditions and follow local escalation procedures.

sections.heading: Education and entry routes in India
paragraphs: The most directly relevant formal preparation is Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology, which may be titled B.Sc. MRIT, BMRIT, Medical Imaging Technology, Radiography, or a closely related institutional title. MoHFW’s model pathway distinguishes a diploma-level Junior MRIT route from a bachelor’s-level MRIT route; it recommends 2.5 years including clinical training for the diploma and four years including a one-year clinical internship for the bachelor’s programme.

For the model B.Sc. MRIT route, MoHFW lists 10+2/equivalent with Physics, Chemistry and Biology as the standard academic background, and also describes admission criteria and selection as institution-specific. Applicants should therefore verify the current prospectus of each university or teaching hospital—particularly its recognised qualification, clinical placement arrangements, entrance/merit process, age rules, fee and reservation policies—before applying.

MRI is normally a modality specialism built on radiography/imaging education and supervised clinical exposure, rather than a separate statutory profession in the NCAHP list. Candidates should seek programmes and placements that demonstrably cover MRI physics, protocols, safety, image quality and patient care.
bullets: After Class 12 science: pursue a recognised bachelor’s programme in MRIT, medical imaging technology or radiography with substantial clinical training.
Alternative entry: a diploma in MRIT/radiography may lead to junior/assistant-level imaging work; progression requirements vary by employer and state.
Build MRI competence through supervised rotations or posts in an MRI service; do not assume that a general radiography qualification alone proves MRI readiness.
Check the awarding university/institution, hospital affiliation and the current employer requirements rather than relying only on a course title.

sections.heading: Core skills for MRI practice
paragraphs: MRI practice requires a combination of cross-sectional anatomy, MRI physics and scanner operation with careful patient-facing work. The MoHFW curriculum specifically covers magnets and coils, RF shielding, pulse sequences, flow phenomena, whole-body protocols, artefacts, MRI safety and MRI quality assurance; its graduate outcomes also include image-quality evaluation, emergency management, digital/computer skills and professional communication.

Safety is central because MRI uses a powerful magnetic environment. A capable technologist follows local MRI-zone/access controls and screening processes, identifies contraindication or implant concerns for escalation, and ensures that people and equipment entering the scanner area are appropriate for the environment. These operational safeguards complement—not replace—the facility’s radiologist, MRI safety and manufacturer protocols.
bullets: MRI physics, sequence selection and scanner-console workflow.
Cross-sectional anatomy, positioning and protocol-based image acquisition.
MRI safety screening, access control, incident recognition and escalation.
Image-quality assessment, artefact recognition and quality assurance.
Calm, clear patient communication, including support for anxious, unwell or mobility-limited patients.
Clinical documentation, digital image-management/PACS workflow, teamwork and emergency response.

sections.heading: Where the role is performed
paragraphs: MRI Technologists work in hospital radiology/imaging departments and dedicated diagnostic imaging centres. MoHFW’s diploma curriculum describes medical-imaging work across hospital departments, patient bedside settings, operating rooms, emergency settings and private imaging clinics/centres; MRI roles are primarily based in controlled MRI suites but coordinate with those wider clinical services.

The work is team-based. MRI services may include plain and contrast-enhanced MRI, MR angiography and MR spectroscopy, as illustrated by the radiodiagnosis service at VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital. Staffing and shift arrangements differ by institution; emergency and inpatient imaging can require scheduled, extended-hour or on-call coverage.
bullets: Government and private hospitals with radiology departments.
Diagnostic imaging centres and multi-specialty clinics.
Teaching hospitals and academic imaging services.
Equipment-industry clinical applications, technical-support or training roles after relevant experience.

sections.heading: Career progression and specialisation
paragraphs: MoHFW presents a proposed—not universally implemented—MRIT progression map. It places diploma holders at Junior MRIT level and B.Sc. MRIT graduates at MRIT level, with later senior technologist and technical-officer levels linked to experience and, at higher levels, postgraduate qualifications. The handbook explicitly cautions that implementation may vary with the existing system and regulations, so employer grade structures should be checked case by case.

Progression can remain clinical—developing deeper MRI, CT, interventional, quality or safety expertise—or move toward education, research, departmental management, PACS/informatics, equipment applications or industry roles. The model curriculum lists applications specialist, radiological safety officer, quality-control technologist, PACS manager, diagnostic manager, teaching/research and industry posts as possible directions. The same handbook states that diagnostic interpretation and final clinical decision-making remain with the radiologist/physician.
bullets: Junior MRIT/radiographer or imaging technologist to MRI-focused MRIT roles.
Senior MRI/MRIT technologist, technical officer or modality lead, subject to employer requirements and experience.
M.Sc. MRIT or related postgraduate study for advanced practice, academic and leadership pathways.
Applications specialist, PACS/informatics, quality, safety, education, research or imaging-industry roles.

title: Nursery Manager
description: A professional who manages commercial plant nurseries, including propagation, plant health, inventory, and sales operations.

quick_facts.label: Official occupational classification
quick_facts.value: India’s National Classification of Occupations (NCO 2015) lists “Manager, Nursery” under code 1311.0900 in the Agricultural and Forestry Production Managers group.

quick_facts.label: Plant-nursery scope
quick_facts.value: For this role, “nursery” means a commercial horticultural plant nursery producing trees, shrubs, flowers, ornamental plants or vegetables for trade or retail customers.

quick_facts.label: Relevant higher-education foundations
quick_facts.value: ICAR’s undergraduate curricula include plant propagation and nursery management, pest and disease management, soil fertility and nutrient management, economics and marketing in horticulture; forestry curricula include tree seed and nursery technology, forest health and protection, forest economics and marketing, and forest business management.

quick_facts.label: Skills-training context
quick_facts.value: As listed by the Agriculture Skill Council of India on July 18, 2026, relevant NSQF-aligned qualifications include Plant Nursery Associate (Level 3), Gardener cum Nursery Raiser (Level 4), and Professional Gardening and Nursery Management (Level 4.5). Qualification availability and validity dates can change.

sections.heading: What a Nursery Manager does
paragraphs: A Nursery Manager plans what plant material to raise and in what quantities, taking account of demand, growing conditions and technical requirements such as germination, plant growth habits, soils, nutrients and disease control. The role also includes selecting inputs such as seed, nutrients and plant-protection materials.

The manager monitors crop and work quality; directs nursery workers undertaking sowing, raising, plant-growth and disease-control activities, and transplanting, potting or cutting plants for sale. Commercial responsibilities extend to records, accounts, marketing and, where applicable, purchasing stock for resale and selling related garden inputs.
bullets: Plan production mix and volumes for commercial plant sales.
Manage propagation, crop health, growing media, nutrition and plant handling.
Supervise workers and inspect nursery crops, soil and work quality.
Maintain operational, inventory, accounting and marketing records.

sections.heading: Entry routes in India
paragraphs: A strong formal route is B.Sc. (Hons.) Horticulture. ICAR’s model undergraduate curriculum includes practical-credit courses in plant propagation and nursery management for fruit, plantation, vegetable, flower and medicinal crops, alongside protected cultivation, pest and disease management, nutrient management, economics and marketing, and an experiential-learning or internship component.

B.Sc. (Hons.) Forestry is also a relevant route, particularly for tree, forest or plantation nurseries: the ICAR curriculum includes Tree Seed and Nursery Technology, Forest Health and Protection, Forest Economics and Marketing, Forest Business Management, and a commercial tree-seedling-production elective.

A work-based route can begin with a nursery-raising or plant-nursery associate qualification and supervised nursery experience, then build toward broader nursery-management capability. ASCI lists occupational standards in these areas; candidates should verify the current qualification version, approved training provider and validity before enrolling.

The graph parent “Nursery Teacher” should not be treated as a like-for-like preparation route for this plant role. This is an inference from the official NCO definition, which explicitly concerns horticultural plants and commercial nursery operations rather than early-years education.
bullets: B.Sc. (Hons.) Horticulture: best-aligned for fruit, vegetable, floriculture, ornamental and protected-cultivation nurseries.
B.Sc. (Hons.) Forestry: especially relevant for tree-seedling, agroforestry, plantation and forest nurseries.
NSQF-aligned training plus hands-on nursery work: a practical pathway into junior nursery operations before management responsibility.

sections.heading: Core skills to develop
paragraphs: Technical capability should cover propagation, plant germination and growth, soils and growing media, nutrient management, irrigation, pest and disease management, and crop inspection. These capabilities follow directly from the NCO responsibilities and are reinforced by ICAR horticulture and forestry curriculum content.

Management capability matters equally: a manager needs to schedule and supervise nursery work, procure inputs, maintain production and business records, interpret market needs, and support sales and marketing. Communication and practical worker supervision are therefore central, not optional, skills.
bullets: Plant propagation and nursery production practices.
Plant-health observation, pest and disease management, and hygiene.
Soil, media, nutrition and irrigation management.
Quality control for planting material and crop handling.
Labour supervision, procurement, inventory and record keeping.
Demand awareness, marketing and customer-facing sales operations.

sections.heading: Workplace and operating context
paragraphs: The work is based in commercial horticultural nurseries serving trade or retail buyers. Depending on the crop and business model, production may occur in controlled environments such as hothouses or greenhouses, or in field conditions under natural weather.

The role combines plant-production oversight with operational work: inspecting crops and work areas, supervising nursery staff, managing inputs and records, and coordinating marketing activities. The balance between production, retail and administrative work will vary by nursery type and scale.
bullets: Field nursery beds and outdoor growing areas.
Protected structures such as greenhouses or hothouses.
Propagation, potting and plant-handling areas.
Stock, input, record-keeping and customer-sales operations.

title: Nursery Teacher
description: An educator specializing in early childhood education, working with children in pre-primary, nursery, or kindergarten settings.

quick_facts.label: Role focus
quick_facts.value: A nursery teacher works in the pre-school/nursery stage, which NCTE’s 2014 minimum-qualification framework identifies for children aged 4–6 years.

quick_facts.label: Core educational approach
quick_facts.value: The national framework for the Foundational Stage emphasizes developmentally appropriate, play-based learning for young children rather than a textbook- or rote-centred approach.

quick_facts.label: Qualification rule
quick_facts.value: There is no single India-wide hiring checklist that can safely be assumed for every nursery post: CBSE-affiliated schools must follow applicable NCTE minimum-qualification regulations and the recruitment rules of the appropriate government, with the applicable NCTE provisions prevailing where relevant.

quick_facts.label: Formal ECCE study option
quick_facts.value: IGNOU’s Diploma in Early Childhood Care and Education (DECE) is open to 10+2-qualified learners and is designed for work with children from birth to six in settings including preschools, nursery schools, kindergartens, crèches and day-care centres.

sections.heading: What a Nursery Teacher Does
paragraphs: The role is to create a safe, stimulating early-learning environment and facilitate children’s holistic development through age-appropriate experiences. The National Curriculum Framework for the Foundational Stage positions early childhood care and education as an integrated developmental stage, while CBSE’s teacher expectations call for learning that moves away from rote methods and supports overall development.
source: https://www.education.gov.in/sites/upload_files/mhrd/files/NCF_for_Foundational_Stage_20_October_2022.pdf
source: https://www.cbse.gov.in/cbsenew/cbse-exp-teacher.html
bullets: Plan and facilitate play-based, activity-based learning experiences suited to young children’s developmental level. Source: https://www.education.gov.in/sites/upload_files/mhrd/files/NCF_for_Foundational_Stage_20_October_2022.pdf

Observe children’s participation and development, maintain teaching/pedagogical records where required by the school, and adapt classroom support. Source: https://www.cbse.gov.in/cbsenew/cbse-exp-teacher.html

Contribute to a nurturing classroom culture that supports children’s personality, wellbeing and all-round development rather than narrow academic drill. Source: https://www.cbse.gov.in/cbsenew/cbse-exp-teacher.html

sections.heading: Entry Routes and Qualification Checks
paragraphs: For pre-school/nursery teaching, NCTE’s 2014 framework listed Senior Secondary qualification plus an approved early-childhood/nursery teacher-education route as the principal professional route, and also included B.Ed. in the listed alternatives. However, candidates should not treat an old national table as a universal job guarantee: the hiring school, state or UT recruitment rules, recognition conditions and current NCTE requirements must be checked for the particular vacancy.
source: https://ncte.gov.in/website/PDF/AnnualReport/2013-14.pdf
source: https://www.cbse.gov.in/cbsenew/staff.html
bullets: A directly relevant pathway is early-childhood education training. NCTE’s norms describe a pre-school teacher-education programme intended to prepare teachers for children aged 4–6; the published norm states Class X/equivalent as its programme-entry eligibility, subject to the applicable state admission policy. Source: https://ncte.gov.in/Website/NCTEACT10.aspx/Hindi/nmm/AcademicDivision.aspx

A practical post-10+2 option is IGNOU’s DECE, whose published admission eligibility is 10+2 and whose target settings include nursery schools and pre-primary classes. It is a programme option, not a substitute for checking an employer’s stated eligibility. Source: https://www.ignou.ac.in/schools/programme/DECE

D.El.Ed. is a useful elementary-teacher-education background and can support movement toward elementary teaching, but candidates should verify the exact qualification required for a nursery vacancy rather than assuming any teaching diploma is automatically accepted. CBSE directs affiliated schools to applicable NCTE rules and appropriate-government recruitment rules. Source: https://www.cbse.gov.in/cbsenew/staff.html

Before enrolling in a course or accepting an offer, verify the institution/course recognition where relevant, the school’s board affiliation, and the current state/UT or employer recruitment notice. Source: https://saras.cbse.gov.in/SARAS/Affiliation%20Bye-Laws/Affiliation-Bye-Laws-English.pdf

sections.heading: Skills to Build
paragraphs: The strongest preparation combines knowledge of child development with the ability to design playful, inclusive and responsive learning experiences. This follows the Foundational Stage framework’s developmental orientation and CBSE’s expectation that teachers enrich the curriculum for overall development.
source: https://www.education.gov.in/sites/upload_files/mhrd/files/NCF_for_Foundational_Stage_20_October_2022.pdf
source: https://www.cbse.gov.in/cbsenew/cbse-exp-teacher.html
bullets: Early-childhood observation and responsive support: notice children’s participation, needs and emerging capabilities, then adjust activities accordingly. Source: https://www.education.gov.in/sites/upload_files/mhrd/files/NCF_for_Foundational_Stage_20_October_2022.pdf

Play-based pedagogy and activity design: select stories, conversation, movement, art, play and exploration that make learning meaningful for young children. Source: https://www.education.gov.in/sites/upload_files/mhrd/files/NCF_for_Foundational_Stage_20_October_2022.pdf
Record-keeping and reflective practice: maintain a teacher diary/record of teaching process and pedagogical activities where required. Source: https://www.cbse.gov.in/cbsenew/cbse-exp-teacher.html

Ongoing professional learning: CBSE directs teachers to DIKSHA for training courses, teaching-learning resources and assessment practices; individual schools may set additional training expectations. Source: https://www.cbse.gov.in/cbsenew/cbse-exp-teacher.html

sections.heading: Where the Role Is Found
paragraphs: Nursery teachers commonly work in early-childhood settings such as preschools, nursery schools, pre-primary sections, kindergartens, crèches, balwadis and some anganwadi-linked contexts. Actual job titles, staff structure, hours, pay and required credentials vary substantially by provider and by state or UT.
source: https://www.ignou.ac.in/schools/programme/DECE
source: https://www.education.gov.in/sites/upload_files/mhrd/files/NCF_for_Foundational_Stage_20_October_2022.pdf
bullets: In CBSE-affiliated school settings, the institution is expected to have trained and qualified teaching staff and to arrange annual teacher training; the school’s applicable qualification rules still govern recruitment. Source: https://www.cbse.gov.in/cbse.html

The work may involve both education and care-oriented routines because ECCE spans developmental needs in the early years; the exact division of duties depends on the setting and employer. Source: https://www.ignou.ac.in/schools/programme/DECE

sections.heading: Possible Progression
paragraphs: With experience and further study, a nursery teacher may progress into pre-primary coordination, centre management, curriculum/content development, training or entrepreneurship. These are career directions rather than automatic promotions; employers determine experience, degree and recognition requirements for each post.
source: https://www.ignou.ac.in/schools/programme/PGDPPED
source: https://www.ignou.ac.in/schools/programme/PGDECFE
bullets: Pre-primary School Coordinator or Head: IGNOU’s postgraduate diploma in pre-primary education identifies managing daily operations, staff and curriculum implementation in pre-primary institutions as a potential outcome. Source: https://www.ignou.ac.in/schools/programme/PGDPPED

Educational Content Developer or curriculum-focused work: IGNOU’s PGDECFE identifies curriculum developers among relevant professionals and covers planning curriculum and play-/experience-based pedagogy. Source: https://www.ignou.ac.in/schools/programme/PGDECFE

Playschool entrepreneurship or Nursery Manager responsibilities: IGNOU’s DECE states that its learning is useful to people wishing to establish ECCE centres, and its stated settings include preschools and nursery schools. Local business, safety, registration and staffing obligations require separate verification. Source: https://www.ignou.ac.in/schools/programme/DECE

Primary School Teacher (Private) is a distinct move: check the school’s current recruitment notice because CBSE-affiliated schools apply NCTE and appropriate-government qualification rules, rather than treating nursery experience alone as sufficient. Source: https://www.cbse.gov.in/cbsenew/staff.html

title: Nursing Supervisor
description: A senior clinical nurse who supervises ward operations, allocates staff, and ensures nursing-care standards.

quick_facts.label: Core function
quick_facts.value: Nursing Supervisors coordinate and supervise nursing-service delivery: this commonly includes staffing/roster oversight, adherence to patient-care procedures, and safety controls within hospital nursing administration.

quick_facts.label: Professional foundation
quick_facts.value: The usual foundation is a recognised nursing qualification and State Nursing Registration Council registration; INC materials define RN & RM as a person completing recognised B.Sc. Nursing or GNM and registered with an SNRC.

quick_facts.label: Typical entry pattern
quick_facts.value: This is commonly a senior, experience-based role rather than an entry-level nursing post. For example, Ladakh rules provide for promotion to Assistant Matron/Sister/Nursing Supervisor from Senior Nurse after five years of substantive service.

quick_facts.label: Example employer requirement
quick_facts.value: A Tata Memorial Centre Nursing Supervisor advertisement required GNM plus an oncology diploma, or B.Sc./Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing; eligibility for INC/State Nursing Council registration; and six years of clinical experience in a 100-bed hospital. Requirements are employer- and specialty-specific.

quick_facts.label: Public-sector pay context
quick_facts.value: Pay is employer and cadre specific. In Ladakh's notified rules, Assistant Matron/Sister/Nursing Supervisor is shown at Level 6E, ₹35,900–₹113,200; this is an example of a government pay structure, not an India-wide salary benchmark.

sections.heading: What a Nursing Supervisor does
paragraphs: A Nursing Supervisor is a senior clinical-nursing operations role. The work centres on organising nursing personnel and maintaining safe, consistent patient care across a ward, unit, or assigned service. Central-government hospital administration guidance addresses equitable nursing duty rosters, leave and absence arrangements, written nursing instructions/SOPs, and supervision of safety controls for hazards such as fire, oxygen or therapy-gas equipment, and electrical appliances.

The supervisory remit is both clinical and managerial: the INC nursing-management curriculum explicitly includes planning, supervision and management of the nursing workforce, nursing-service organisation, inter-agency coordination, and quality nursing services. Day-to-day duties therefore depend on the hospital and specialty, but typically combine staff deployment, escalation of operational problems, monitoring practice against local procedures, documentation/communication, and support to nurses delivering bedside care.
bullets: Prepare or oversee duty deployment and ensure appropriate coverage across shifts, leave, holidays and night duty.
Support compliance with local nursing procedures and safety measures, escalating risks that affect patient care or ward operations.
Coordinate with nursing leadership, clinicians and other hospital departments when staffing, patient flow, equipment or safety issues require action.
Guide and supervise nursing personnel rather than functioning solely as an independently assigned bedside nurse.

sections.heading: Entry routes in India
paragraphs: The route normally begins with a recognised professional nursing programme, such as GNM or B.Sc. Nursing, followed by registration with the relevant State Nursing Registration Council. INC's regulatory material describes RN & RM status in terms of a recognised B.Sc. Nursing or GNM qualification and SNRC registration. Candidates should verify that both their programme and registration meet the requirements of the specific recruiting employer and state.

Advancement to Nursing Supervisor is commonly through clinical-service experience and promotion from staff/senior-nurse grades. The exact feeder grade and qualifying service vary by jurisdiction and organisation. As a current public-service example, Ladakh's rules place Nursing Supervisor with Assistant Matron/Sister and provide promotion from Senior Nurse after five years of substantive service. A specialist employer may instead recruit against its own criteria: Tata Memorial Centre's cited advertisement sought recognised nursing credentials, registration eligibility and six years' clinical experience in a 100-bed hospital.
bullets: Complete an INC-recognised nursing qualification pathway relevant to the intended employer, commonly GNM or B.Sc. Nursing.
Obtain and maintain registration with the applicable State Nursing Registration Council.
Build substantial clinical experience, often in hospital nursing and sometimes in a relevant specialty.
Apply through internal promotion processes or employer recruitment notices; read the notified service, qualification, specialty and registration conditions for that vacancy.

sections.heading: Skills to develop
paragraphs: The role requires a blend of clinical credibility and nursing-administration capability. INC's nursing-management curriculum identifies planning, supervision and management of the nursing workforce; organisation of health and nursing services; coordination with other agencies; and quality nursing services as learning outcomes. Hospital nursing-administration guidance also makes roster management, SOP communication and safety oversight operationally relevant.

Accordingly, strong candidates need clear handover and escalation communication, fair staff allocation, situational judgement, documentation discipline, familiarity with local clinical and safety procedures, and the ability to mentor staff while keeping patient care central.
bullets: Workforce planning, shift allocation and handover management.
Clinical governance, patient-safety awareness and adherence to local SOPs.
Calm escalation, interdisciplinary coordination and clear written and verbal communication.
Coaching, supervision and performance support for nursing staff.
Accurate records and practical use of hospital reporting systems.

sections.heading: Where the role is found
paragraphs: Nursing Supervisors work principally in hospitals and hospital-linked specialty services, where nursing staff must be organised over continuous shifts. Government hospital guidance on nursing administration addresses hospital rosters, leave, unit placement and equipment safety, while Tata Memorial Centre's recruitment example situates the post in an oncology-hospital context and requires prior experience in a 100-bed hospital.

The precise title and reporting line are not nationally uniform. Comparable senior nursing titles may include Ward Sister, Sister, Assistant Matron, Assistant Nursing Superintendent, Deputy Nursing Superintendent, Matron or Nursing Superintendent, depending on the employer's cadre rules.
bullets: General wards and inpatient units.
Specialty services such as oncology, critical care, paediatrics or peri-operative areas, subject to employer criteria.
Government hospitals, autonomous institutions and private or charitable hospital employers, each with distinct recruitment rules and grades.

sections.heading: Career progression
paragraphs: Progression is governed by the employing organisation's service rules, seniority and eligibility conditions rather than a single national ladder. In the Ladakh example, Senior Nurse can progress to Assistant Matron/Sister/Nursing Supervisor after five years of substantive service, and an employee in that supervisor grouping can progress to Matron after at least three years of substantive service. This illustrates a possible administrative pathway, not a universal rule.

At central government research-hospital level, Department of Health Research recruitment rules published for comment showed a Nursing Supervisor post filled 100% by promotion from eligible Staff Nurses with two years of regular Level-7 service, and a Deputy Nursing Superintendent post promoted from eligible Nursing Supervisors with two years of regular Level-8 service. Candidates should use the rules and vacancy notice of their own cadre as the controlling source.
bullets: Staff Nurse or Nursing Officer → Senior Nurse or equivalent clinical senior grade.
Senior Nurse → Nursing Supervisor/Sister/Assistant Matron, where service rules provide for this.
Nursing Supervisor → Matron, Assistant/Deputy Nursing Superintendent or other nursing-administration roles, subject to cadre rules and vacancies.
Specialty experience and additional recognised education may strengthen eligibility where employers specify them.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: There is no single India-wide Nursing Supervisor salary. Compensation differs by government cadre, state or Union Territory, employer, appointment type, location, allowances, specialty and years of service. In the Ladakh Health and Medical (Subordinate) Service rules available in 2025, the combined Assistant Matron/Sister/Nursing Supervisor designation is listed at Level 6E, ₹35,900–₹113,200. This is a pay-matrix range for that service, not take-home pay or a general market rate.

For a dated non-pay-matrix comparison, a Tata Memorial Centre advertisement published in 2022 listed a fixed monthly ₹30,000 for one Nursing Supervisor opening at HBCH&RC Muzaffarpur, alongside specified qualification and experience conditions. It should be treated only as historical vacancy context; candidates should rely on the live advertisement, appointment terms and applicable allowances when assessing an offer.
bullets: Check whether the vacancy is permanent, contractual, deputation-based or outsourced before comparing pay.
For government positions, identify the notified pay level, starting basic pay, allowances and promotion grade.
For non-government or project roles, confirm fixed versus consolidated pay, shift allowance, accommodation, insurance and contract duration.

title: Nursing Tutor
description: A nursing educator who teaches and supervises student nurses in nursing colleges and clinical settings.

quick_facts.label: Core role
quick_facts.value: A Nursing Tutor (also termed a Sister Tutor or, in some services, Tutor/Clinical Instructor) organizes and delivers nursing teaching, plans students’ practical and ward experience, and provides clinical teaching and supervision.

quick_facts.label: Qualification context
quick_facts.value: For an Indian Nursing Council (INC) College of Nursing tutor post, M.Sc. Nursing is stated as preferable; B.Sc. Nursing or Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing with one year of experience is also listed. Requirements differ by programme and recruiting employer.

quick_facts.label: Registration context
quick_facts.value: INC minimum-requirement guidance says nursing teachers must hold a basic university/equivalent qualification recognized under the INC Act and be registered under the applicable State Nursing Registration Act.

quick_facts.label: M.Sc. Nursing route
quick_facts.value: INC lists M.Sc. Nursing admission prerequisites including registration as a nurse and midwife/equivalent with a State Nursing Registration Council, a B.Sc./B.Sc. (Hons.)/Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing qualification with at least 55% aggregate marks, and one year of relevant work experience under the applicable basic or post-basic route.

quick_facts.label: Teaching and clinical workload
quick_facts.value: INC guidance states that nursing teachers other than the Principal and Vice-Principal should spend at least four hours daily in the clinical area for clinical teaching and/or supervision of care.

sections.heading: Teaching, student support, and clinical supervision
paragraphs: The role combines classroom teaching with supervised practice. The College of Nursing at VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital describes the Sister Tutor as responsible to the Principal for organizing and conducting the teaching programme. Listed work includes planning orientation and teaching programmes, preparing classes and demonstrations, teaching nursing subjects, arranging practical experience and ward assignments, guiding students’ study and use of the library, and giving individual attention where needed.

INC’s college standards also place nursing faculty in clinical teaching: except for the Principal and Vice-Principal, teachers should spend at least four hours each day in the clinical area for teaching and/or supervision of care. This makes safe clinical instruction, learner feedback, coordination with clinical areas, and record-ready academic planning central to the role.
bullets: Plan lessons, orientations, demonstrations, practical placements, ward teaching, and student schedules.
Teach nursing subjects and support students with assignments, study methods, reference use, and individual learning needs.
Supervise or teach in clinical areas and coordinate practical learning with hospitals or other practice settings.
Work under the academic leadership of the Principal/Vice-Principal and within the institution’s INC-related faculty standards.

sections.heading: Entry routes from M.Sc. Nursing and other nursing qualifications
paragraphs: For the canonical M.Sc. Nursing pathway, INC’s published eligibility criteria for M.Sc. Nursing require State Nursing Registration Council registration as a nurse and midwife or equivalent, an eligible B.Sc. Nursing-family degree with at least 55% aggregate marks, and one year of work experience as specified for the basic or post-basic route.

An M.Sc. Nursing is advantageous but is not a universal minimum for every role called “Tutor.” INC’s College of Nursing minimum requirements describe M.Sc. Nursing as preferable for a tutor; they also permit B.Sc. Nursing or Post Basic B.Sc. Nursing with one year of experience. By contrast, a 2023 NEIGRIHMS draft recruitment-rule document proposed M.Sc. Nursing from a recognized institution/university as the essential direct-recruitment qualification. Candidates should therefore read the current notification of the specific college, university, hospital, state service commission, or central institution before applying.

For GNM teaching faculty, INC guidance separately lists tutor eligibility that can include M.Sc. Nursing, B.Sc. Nursing (Basic/Post Basic), or Diploma in Nursing Education and Administration, with two years of professional experience. This programme-specific distinction is important when comparing vacancies.
bullets: Complete an INC-recognized nursing qualification and maintain the registration required by the relevant State Nursing Registration Act.
For the M.Sc. Nursing route, meet the applicable INC academic, registration, and experience prerequisites for admission.
Build clinical and/or teaching experience, since experience requirements differ across college standards, programme regulations, and employer recruitment rules.
Check the vacancy’s exact designation: “Nursing Tutor,” “Sister Tutor,” and “Tutor/Clinical Instructor” may have different recruitment rules.

sections.heading: Skills evidenced by the work
paragraphs: The formal duty descriptions point to a practical skill mix: lesson and placement planning, classroom and demonstration teaching, assessment-oriented course planning, learner guidance, use of educational materials and references, and clinical supervision. Because tutors work across academic and care settings, they also need clear communication and coordination with academic leaders and clinical teams.

Applicants should be able to show both nursing competence and educational practice rather than treating the role as classroom-only work. INC’s expectation of daily clinical teaching/supervision for most nursing teachers reinforces the importance of current clinical judgment and the ability to connect theory to safe patient care.
bullets: Instructional planning and delivery, including demonstrations and orientation.
Clinical teaching, supervision of care, and coordination of practical or ward assignments.
Student mentoring, feedback, individual academic support, and guidance on study resources.
Communication and collaboration with the Principal/Vice-Principal, nursing faculty, and clinical-service teams.

sections.heading: Where Nursing Tutors work
paragraphs: The core workplace is a School or College of Nursing, with regular work extending into affiliated hospital wards and other clinical learning areas. VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital’s official description situates the Sister Tutor in the College/School of Nursing while assigning responsibility for students’ practical experience and ward teaching. INC standards similarly require substantial clinical-area teaching or supervision for most nursing teachers.

Public-sector nursing education services may use related designations. Maharashtra’s State Nursing Cell lists “Nursing Officers/Tutors/Clinical Instructors” among its public-health nursing cadres, while NEIGRIHMS uses the designation “Tutor/Clinical Instructor” in its recruitment-rule material.
bullets: Nursing colleges and schools.
Teaching hospitals and affiliated clinical wards.
Government health-service nursing-training establishments.
Institutions that use related titles such as Sister Tutor or Tutor/Clinical Instructor.

sections.heading: Academic progression
paragraphs: In INC College of Nursing minimum requirements, the teaching hierarchy above Tutor includes Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Professor, Vice-Principal-cum-Professor, and Principal-cum-Professor. The listed experience thresholds increase at each stage: Assistant Professor requires M.Sc. Nursing with three years of teaching experience; Associate Professor requires a total of eight years’ experience including five years’ teaching experience; and Professor requires 12 years’ experience with 10 years’ teaching experience after M.Sc. Nursing. These are regulatory staffing standards, not an automatic promotion entitlement.

An M.Sc. Nursing therefore supports progression into higher academic posts, but candidates should verify the applicable university statutes, state recruitment rules, and employer-specific selection criteria for each vacancy.
bullets: Tutor → Assistant Professor, subject to the stated M.Sc. Nursing and experience requirements.
Assistant Professor → Associate Professor → Professor, with progressively higher total and teaching-experience thresholds in INC college standards.
Senior academic leadership roles include Vice-Principal-cum-Professor and Principal-cum-Professor.

sections.heading: Compensation context: employer and state rules matter
paragraphs: Pay is highly employer-, state-, cadre-, and appointment-rule-specific, so it should not be treated as a national salary benchmark. For dated public-sector context, a Kerala Directorate of Health Services appointment order dated September 7, 2024 appointed Nursing Tutors in the pay scale of ₹50,200–₹105,300. A NEIGRIHMS document concerning amended draft recruitment rules dated 2023 proposed Level 10 of the pay matrix for Tutor; it is a draft-rule reference rather than evidence of a universal pay entitlement.

Applicants should use the pay level or scale printed in the live recruitment notification and confirm whether the post is permanent, temporary, contractual, or governed by a particular state or central pay framework.
bullets: Example only: Kerala Health Services appointment order dated September 7, 2024 — ₹50,200–₹105,300 for Nursing Tutor appointments covered by that order.
Example only: NEIGRIHMS 2023 amended draft rules proposed Pay Matrix Level 10 for Tutor.
Do not extrapolate either example to private colleges, other states, or later recruitment cycles.

title: Nutritionist
description: A professional who provides nutrition education, diet guidance, and wellness support in hospitals, wellness organisations, food companies, or community programmes.

quick_facts.label: Role focus
quick_facts.value: A nutritionist translates nutrition science into practical food, meal and behaviour guidance; in clinical settings, this can include individualised dietary counselling for patients and families alongside the treating medical team.

quick_facts.label: Relevant undergraduate foundation
quick_facts.value: B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science is an ICAR-recognised degree nomenclature. ICAR’s minimum requirements identify Food Science and Nutrition and Food Policy and Public Health Nutrition as departments within the programme structure.

quick_facts.label: Typical advanced study
quick_facts.value: For hospital dietetics roles, postgraduate qualifications in Food and Nutrition, Dietetics/Food Service Management, Nutritional Sciences and related fields are commonly represented in the AIIMS New Delhi dietetics cadre.

quick_facts.label: Work settings evidenced in public sources
quick_facts.value: Nutrition professionals are used in hospital clinical departments and can contribute to community nutrition work, including nutrition surveys, nutrition education and intervention programmes.

quick_facts.label: Evidence base for Indian dietary advice
quick_facts.value: ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition is the nodal agency for recommending nutrient requirements and recommended dietary allowances for Indians; these recommendations are revised as food habits, activity patterns and health profiles change.

sections.heading: What a nutritionist does
paragraphs: The work centres on assessing dietary needs and turning nutrition evidence into feasible, person-specific guidance. In clinical care, a nutritionist/dietician may counsel patients and families, plan a nutritionally balanced diet appropriate to the condition, explain safe and restricted foods, and reinforce adherence over time. ICMR’s celiac-disease guidance specifically calls for a dietician who can give individual patient-specific, balanced diet advice and practical counselling for home, school/work, travel and restaurants.

In community-facing work, nutrition responsibilities can extend beyond one-to-one counselling to nutrition surveys, education and intervention programmes. UGC community-engagement guidance gives examples of nutrition surveys for mothers and children and nutrition education; higher-education nutrition research material also identifies community nutrition, food-consumption studies, malnutrition and intervention programmes as relevant areas.
bullets: Conduct dietary assessment and provide practical food and meal guidance tailored to the person or target group.
Communicate clearly with clients, families and, where relevant, the wider healthcare team; provide written food guidance when needed.
Support nutrition education, surveys and community interventions, with attention to local food practices and feasibility.

Use current Indian nutrient-requirement and dietary guidance as an evidence base, while working within the remit of the employing organisation and referring clinical diagnosis and medical treatment decisions to appropriately qualified clinicians.

sections.heading: Entry route from B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science
paragraphs: B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science is a relevant undergraduate starting point because ICAR’s programme standards place Food Science and Nutrition and Food Policy and Public Health Nutrition within the discipline. For ICAR undergraduate admissions, the 2025 CUET (ICAR-UG) bulletin listed B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science among agriculture-and-allied programmes and required Class 12 study in at least three of Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture/Inter-Agriculture for the general eligibility route described there.

After the degree, a student can build a nutrition-focused profile through supervised practical exposure and, where the target role requires it, postgraduate study in Food and Nutrition, Dietetics/Food Service Management, Nutritional Sciences or a closely related specialism. AIIMS New Delhi’s dietetics cadre records these types of postgraduate qualifications among its dietetics personnel, illustrating the qualifications represented in a major public hospital setting. Individual employer recruitment rules—not a single generic title—should be checked before applying.
bullets: Complete the B.Sc. (Hons.) Community Science programme and choose food, nutrition, dietetics and public-health-nutrition coursework or projects where available.
Seek field, food-service, hospital or community-nutrition experience that develops assessment, counselling and programme-delivery skills.
Consider a relevant master’s degree for roles that specify postgraduate education or for progression towards specialist hospital dietetics work.
Read the exact vacancy notice for eligibility, experience, registration/certification requirements and job scope; requirements differ by employer and state.

sections.heading: Skills to develop
paragraphs: A strong nutritionist combines food-and-nutrition knowledge with evidence appraisal, quantitative reasoning and communication. UGC’s undergraduate learning-outcomes framework identifies scientific reasoning, data interpretation and information/digital literacy as core graduate capabilities. In nutrition practice, these capabilities support reading dietary evidence, assessing intake information, interpreting measurements within one’s role and explaining recommendations in accessible language.

Practical competence should also cover menu and meal planning, food-safety awareness, culturally appropriate counselling and documentation. Home-science research material describes work across diet and disease, food-service management and dietetics, dietary-counselling software, culinary skills, food adulteration, community nutrition, food-consumption patterns and nutrition interventions.
bullets: Nutrition science, meal planning and food-service fundamentals.
Dietary assessment, basic data handling and evidence appraisal.
Clear, empathetic counselling and health education for individuals, families and communities.
Cultural and economic adaptation of food advice to local diets and food access.
Digital information literacy and accurate record/document preparation.

sections.heading: Where nutritionists may work
paragraphs: Hospital employment is a major pathway: AIIMS New Delhi’s published dietetics cadre shows dietetics personnel working across its hospital, gastroenterology and human nutrition, endocrinology and metabolism, paediatrics, cancer and surgical services. ICMR clinical guidance also describes the role of a nutritionist/dietician in counselling patients and families as part of disease management.

Community and public-health-oriented work is another route. UGC materials describe nutrition surveys and nutrition education for mothers and children as examples of community engagement, while home-science nutrition research covers community nutrition, food-consumption patterns and intervention programmes. The mix of clinical, community, food-service and research work varies substantially by employer.
bullets: Hospitals and speciality clinical departments.
Community nutrition, health-promotion and education programmes.
Food service, institutional catering and wellness settings.
Research, nutrition surveys and programme implementation roles.

sections.heading: Career progression
paragraphs: Progression depends on sector, experience, qualifications and the employer’s cadre rules. A public-hospital example is AIIMS New Delhi, whose dietetics cadre lists Assistant Dietician, Dietician, Senior Dietician and Chief Dietician levels. The cadre also shows postgraduate Food and Nutrition and related qualifications across these levels, although this is an institutional example rather than a nationwide promotion rule.

Professional development can move toward clinical specialisation, food-service management, public-health/community nutrition, research or supervisory leadership. Students should treat titles and eligibility as employer-specific and use current recruitment notices to determine the required qualifications and experience.
bullets: Early roles may focus on supervised counselling, menu planning, food-service support, surveys or programme delivery.
With relevant experience and further study, pathways may broaden into specialist clinical dietetics, community/public-health nutrition, research or management.
Public-sector career ladders are governed by the recruiting institution’s rules; private-sector titles and progression structures vary.
