title: Urban Planner
description: A professional who develops plans and programs for the use of land, helping create communities, accommodate population growth, and revitalize physical facilities in towns and cities.

quick_facts.label: Core purpose
quick_facts.value: Urban planners translate evidence on land, people, infrastructure and regulation into plans and development controls for cities, towns and regions; public planning departments may prepare development, sectoral and village plans, frame rules, advise on permissions and coordinate planned development.

quick_facts.label: Direct undergraduate route
quick_facts.value: B.Planning is a four-year, eight-semester undergraduate programme under ITPI course-approval guidance. SPA Delhi describes its B.Plan as training students to prepare layout, zonal, master, regional and functional plans.

quick_facts.label: Architecture-to-planning route
quick_facts.value: A bachelor’s degree in Architecture is an accepted prior qualification for entry to a Master’s planning programme under ITPI’s course-approval guidance; the exact eligibility and entrance process are set by the admitting institution.

quick_facts.label: Recruitment is post-specific
quick_facts.value: Eligibility is not uniform across employers. For example, Ladakh’s 2024 Assistant Town Planner rules accept a postgraduate planning degree, or a B.Planning/B.Tech in Planning with three years’ planning experience, for direct recruitment.

quick_facts.label: Professional settings
quick_facts.value: Planning careers span government and semi-government organisations, private/self-employed practice, teaching, and research-and-development organisations, as reflected in ITPI’s membership experience categories.

sections.heading: What an Urban Planner does
paragraphs: In the Indian public-sector context, urban-planning work commonly combines spatial planning, development management and public-interest outcomes. A state Town and Country Planning department lists preparation of development and sectoral plans; planning essential urban infrastructure; making efficient use of urban land; improving habitat and environmental conditions; and coordinating with government and development authorities among its functions.

At local planning-authority level, the role can also involve implementing master-plan schemes, applying zoning regulations, providing technical advice to agencies, supporting land-use conversion decisions, and reviewing or sanctioning building-plan proposals where statutory powers are assigned. The precise authority held by an individual planner depends on the applicable state or UT law, service rules and delegation of powers.
bullets: Prepare, analyse and communicate master, regional, zonal, layout or sectoral plans.
Use land-use, population, infrastructure and site information to diagnose problems and develop policy or plan proposals.
Work with development-control rules, zoning and planning-permission processes in roles that carry those responsibilities.
Coordinate with engineers, architects, revenue and local-government teams, agencies and communities.

sections.heading: Entry routes from B.Arch and B.Plan
paragraphs: The clearest undergraduate route is B.Plan. ITPI’s guidance specifies B.Planning as a four-year/eight-semester programme, and SPA Delhi’s programme illustrates the interdisciplinary preparation expected in planning: physical, social, economic and political analysis; studios and field exercises; internships; plan preparation; and independent research.

B.Arch is a relevant adjacent route rather than an automatic substitute for every planner vacancy. ITPI identifies Architecture as an eligible bachelor’s background for Master’s planning admission. An architecture graduate seeking urban-planning roles can therefore commonly strengthen the route through an M.Plan or a closely specified planning qualification, then check each recruitment notice carefully.

Government vacancies may use titles such as Planning Assistant, Assistant Town Planner, Town Planner or planning officer, but qualification, experience, age, examination and selection rules vary by employer. In Ladakh’s 2024 Assistant Town Planner rules, direct recruitment specifies either a postgraduate degree in listed planning fields or B.Planning/B.Tech in Planning plus three years of planning experience.
bullets: B.Plan → internship/project portfolio → entry-level planning, GIS, research or development-management roles; verify each employer’s criteria.
B.Arch → M.Plan or another employer-accepted planning specialisation → planning roles whose notification accepts that qualification.
For public jobs, rely on the current official recruitment notification rather than assuming one state or UT’s eligibility applies nationally.

sections.heading: Skills to build
paragraphs: A strong planning skill set blends spatial, analytical and communication capabilities. SPA Delhi’s B.Plan curriculum identifies data collection, analysis and interpretation, mapping, GIS-based mapping and analysis, drafting, policy analysis, report writing, teamwork, problem solving, visual communication and verbal communication as learning outcomes or core training areas.

Planning also requires the ability to relate land-use decisions to housing, transport, infrastructure, environmental conditions, governance, finance and social equity. This interdisciplinary perspective matters because plans must be evidence-based but also workable within legal, institutional and community constraints.
bullets: Spatial analysis: mapping, GIS, remote-sensing awareness, site and land-use survey methods.
Quantitative and research skills: data collection, statistics, demographic and economic analysis, interpretation and reporting.
Planning practice: development plans, regulations, land allocation, policy formulation and implementation awareness.
Communication and collaboration: drawings and visualisation, concise written reports, stakeholder engagement, teamwork and professional judgement.

sections.heading: Where the work happens
paragraphs: Urban planners can work in public planning departments and planning authorities, including state, divisional, sub-divisional and town-planning offices. These teams may include town and country planners, assistant town planners, planning officers, engineers, draftspeople, surveyors, legal staff and research staff, so the work is inherently multidisciplinary.

The field also extends beyond government employment. ITPI’s membership framework explicitly recognises professional experience in government/private or semi-government sectors, self-employed professional practice, teaching, and research-and-development organisations. Day-to-day work can therefore mix office-based analysis and drafting with site visits, surveys, coordination meetings and public-facing planning processes.
bullets: State/UT town and country planning departments and urban-planning departments.
Local or special planning authorities and development authorities.
Private planning, urban-design, infrastructure or real-estate consultancies.
Universities and research organisations working on urban and regional development.

sections.heading: Career progression
paragraphs: Progression depends on the employer’s cadre structure and service rules. One public-department example shows a hierarchy from Planning Officer through Assistant Town Planner and Town & Country Planner to State Town Planner and Director. In Ladakh’s 2024 rules, an Assistant Town Planner post may be filled partly by promotion from Planning Assistant after specified regular service, as well as by direct recruitment or deputation.

Over time, planners can deepen subject expertise—such as land-use planning, transport, housing, infrastructure, environment or regional planning—or move toward project leadership, statutory planning, policy, consultancy, teaching or research. ITPI’s fellow-membership framework also recognises substantial professional experience across government, private practice, teaching and research, illustrating the range of senior career settings.
bullets: Early career: planning assistant, junior planner, GIS/research or project-support roles.
Mid career: assistant town planner, planning officer, specialist planner or project lead, subject to employer criteria.
Senior career: town/country planner, senior consultant, team leader, academic or research leadership roles.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: Compensation varies substantially by employer, location, contract type, seniority, qualifications and whether the role is public-sector, consultancy, academic or self-employed practice. As a dated public-sector example—not a national salary benchmark—Ladakh’s Assistant Town Planner Recruitment Rules, 2024 list Pay Level 8A, with a pay-matrix range of ₹50,700–₹160,600. Applicants should use the live vacancy notice and applicable pay rules for a current figure.
bullets: Treat published public pay levels as role-, jurisdiction- and date-specific.
Do not extrapolate a government pay matrix to private-consultancy, research or self-employed planning work.

title: Veterinarian
description: A licensed veterinary professional who diagnoses, treats and prevents diseases in companion animals, livestock and other animals.

quick_facts.label: Professional status
quick_facts.value: Veterinary practice in India is regulated through the Indian Veterinary Council Act, 1984; the Veterinary Council of India (VCI) regulates veterinary education and practice and maintains the Indian Veterinary Practitioners’ Register.

quick_facts.label: Core qualifying degree
quick_facts.value: The standard entry qualification is B.V.Sc. & A.H. (Bachelor of Veterinary Science and Animal Husbandry), a 5.5-year programme that includes a compulsory one-year internship.

quick_facts.label: Admission context
quick_facts.value: For the 2025–26 academic session, VCI used the qualified NEET (UG) 2025 merit list for its 15% All India Quota seats in recognised veterinary colleges. Admission procedures, seat matrices and counselling schedules are academic-year-specific.

quick_facts.label: Registration
quick_facts.value: VCI’s direct-registration guidance requires, among other documents, a degree from a VCI-recognised university and a State Veterinary Council certificate.

quick_facts.label: Practice rights
quick_facts.value: Under the Act, a person enrolled on the Indian Veterinary Practitioners’ Register may practise as a veterinary practitioner; registered practitioners also have statutory roles in government veterinary posts, veterinary health certification and expert evidence on veterinary medicine, subject to the Act’s conditions and restrictions.

sections.heading: What veterinarians do
paragraphs: A veterinarian applies modern scientific veterinary medicine, including veterinary surgery and obstetrics, to animal-health work. In regulated practice, registered practitioners may practise veterinary medicine, sign or authenticate veterinary health certificates where the law requires a duly qualified veterinary practitioner, and provide expert evidence on veterinary-medicine matters in court.

Veterinarians also supervise certain minor veterinary services when a State Government permits a qualified veterinary supervisor, stockman or stock assistant to deliver them under a registered practitioner’s supervision and direction. This gives the role a clinical, public-service and legal-certification dimension beyond treating individual animals.
bullets: Assess animal-health problems and provide veterinary medical, surgical or obstetric care within professional competence.
Issue veterinary health certificates when legally required and act as an expert on veterinary-medicine matters where appropriate.
Supervise authorised delivery of minor veterinary services, such as preliminary aid, vaccination, castration and wound dressing, where applicable State arrangements permit this.

sections.heading: Entry route in India
paragraphs: The canonical route is B.V.Sc. & A.H. from a recognised veterinary institution. The VCI’s 2025–26 counselling bulletin describes the degree as 5.5 years including a compulsory one-year internship.

For admissions following the VCI-MSVE framework, applicants typically need Class XII/equivalent science preparation including English, Physics, Chemistry and Biology or Biotechnology. An official ICAR–IVRI admissions page also specifies qualifying NEET (UG) in the admission year for its regular/open and payment-seat route. Exact eligibility, category provisions, cut-offs, domicile rules, quotas, college recognition and counselling processes must be checked in the current year’s VCI, university and State notices.

After graduation, registration is a practical professional step: VCI’s direct-registration page asks for a degree from a VCI-recognised university and a State Veterinary Council certificate. Students should verify that both the intended college and qualification are recognised before enrolling.
bullets: Complete Class XII/equivalent with the required science and English subjects.
Qualify NEET (UG) where required for the applicable admission route and year.
Join a recognised B.V.Sc. & A.H. programme and complete the compulsory rotating internship.
Obtain registration through the applicable State Veterinary Council and, where relevant, VCI registration processes.

sections.heading: Skills developed and needed
paragraphs: The education route combines biomedical and clinical capability with livestock and animal-husbandry knowledge. The legal definition of veterinary medicine expressly includes all branches of modern scientific veterinary medicine, including surgery and obstetrics; the B.V.Sc. & A.H. route also includes a compulsory internship, making supervised practical work central to preparation.

Strong professional practice also requires careful documentation, ethical judgement and communication. The VCI is empowered to specify standards of professional conduct, etiquette and a code of ethics, while statutory veterinary roles can involve certificates, official responsibilities and expert evidence.
bullets: Clinical reasoning and practical animal examination; safe application of medical, surgical and obstetric knowledge.
Animal-health prevention and basic population-health awareness, including vaccination-related work.
Animal husbandry and livestock-production understanding alongside companion-animal clinical knowledge.
Clear communication with animal owners, farmers, colleagues and public authorities.
Accurate records, certification judgement, professional ethics and awareness of scope-of-practice requirements.

sections.heading: Where veterinarians work
paragraphs: A registered veterinarian may practise veterinary medicine and can hold veterinary physician, surgeon or similar offices in government or institutions maintained by local or other authorities, subject to the Act. This supports careers in clinical practice and in public animal-health and animal-husbandry services.

Research and academic settings are another pathway. ICAR’s Animal Science Division reports species-specific research farms and laboratories working across animal genetics, nutrition, physiology, reproduction, animal health and animal-products technology; its institutional ecosystem includes veterinary and animal-science universities. These settings can employ or train veterinary professionals in research, teaching, diagnostics, extension and specialised animal-health work.
bullets: Private veterinary practice and animal-health clinics.
Government veterinary offices and institutions maintained by local or other authorities.
Livestock, dairy, poultry and other farm-linked animal-health services.
Veterinary colleges, universities and teaching hospitals.
ICAR and related research environments, including animal farms and animal-health laboratories.

sections.heading: Progression and specialisation
paragraphs: Following B.V.Sc. & A.H. and registration, veterinarians can build clinical experience, move into public service or private practice, or pursue postgraduate study. VCI’s published draft postgraduate regulations describe B.V.Sc. & A.H. from a recognised veterinary college as the qualifying degree for the competitive postgraduate entrance route; because that document is labelled a draft, applicants should confirm the rules in the final notification for their admission year.

Recognised university and ICAR listings show postgraduate pathways across areas such as veterinary medicine, surgery and radiology, pathology, microbiology, parasitology, pharmacology and toxicology, animal reproduction, veterinary public health and epidemiology, animal nutrition, animal genetics and breeding, livestock production and management, livestock-products technology, poultry science and veterinary extension. Progression can therefore lead toward advanced clinical work, teaching, research, diagnostics, public health, livestock systems or specialist technical roles.
bullets: Early career: internship completion, registration and supervised or independent professional practice within the legal framework.
Postgraduate study: M.V.Sc. in a veterinary or animal-science discipline, subject to the applicable current admissions rules.
Research and academic route: Ph.D. and roles in veterinary colleges, ICAR institutes or related animal-science organisations.
Professional advancement: clinical, public-health, diagnostic, livestock-production, research, teaching or administrative specialisation.

title: Visual Merchandiser
description: A professional responsible for designing and creating attractive visual displays in retail outlets to attract customers and promote products.

quick_facts.label: Sector and qualification level
quick_facts.value: India’s National Qualifications Register lists Visual Merchandiser as a Retail-sector certificate qualification at NCrF/NSQF level 4.5 (NQR code QG-4.5-OR-02430-2024-V2-RASCI).

quick_facts.label: Core purpose
quick_facts.value: The role implements visual-merchandising concepts, themes and plots in stores under head-office, store and brand guidelines, with the aim of strengthening store visibility and supporting sales.

quick_facts.label: Recognised entry benchmark
quick_facts.value: For the current NQR short-term qualification, listed entry combinations include a three-year diploma after Class 10 plus one year of relevant experience; Class 12 plus 1.5 years; or Class 10 plus 4.5 years of relevant experience.

quick_facts.label: Training format
quick_facts.value: The NQR qualification specifies blended delivery: 327 hours for the classroom/offline route (including 60 mandatory OJT hours) or 213 hours online; actual provider delivery can differ within applicable rules.

quick_facts.label: Formal study option
quick_facts.value: NIFT Mumbai lists a six-month Continuing Education programme in Visual Merchandising for 2026–27, with 10+2 eligibility stated for its CE and diploma courses; availability and admissions are provider- and cycle-specific.

sections.heading: What a Visual Merchandiser does
paragraphs: A visual merchandiser translates a store or brand brief into window and in-store displays designed to bring attention to products and support purchase decisions. The national qualification describes the work as implementing visual-merchandising concepts and elements, then executing themes and plots according to business needs.

The job combines design execution with commercial and operational work: interpreting customer and category trends, using space, lighting, props and accessories, creating or maintaining displays, ensuring compliance with store, vendor and statutory requirements, and collecting data on the impact of promotions and events. Displays must be kept consistent with brand and store guidelines rather than treated only as decorative installations.
bullets: Develop display themes, plots, floor/layout concepts and focal points from brand or marketing briefs.
Select and group merchandise, signage, props, fixtures and lighting to create intended visual effects.
Implement, inspect, maintain and improve window and in-store displays while observing safety, policy and regulatory requirements.
Review sales/category and promotion information to assess display performance, and coordinate with internal teams, brands, vendors and other stakeholders.

sections.heading: Entry routes in India
paragraphs: A practical entry route is to build experience in retail-store operations, marketing or category-related work and then pursue a role-specific skills credential. The NQR’s April 2024 qualification file is explicit that its entry routes combine school/diploma attainment with relevant work experience; it should not be read as a universal hiring rule for every retailer.

A design-led higher-education route can also be relevant. NIFT identifies Visual Merchandiser among positions offered to its Fashion Communication graduates; the programme covers graphic design, space design, fashion media and fashion thinking, alongside industry exposure and projects. For focused upskilling, NIFT Mumbai’s 2026–27 continuing-education listing includes a six-month Visual Merchandising programme, subject to that centre’s admissions process and schedule.
bullets: Skills-certification route: meet the applicable NQR educational-and-experience combination, complete training and assessment, and develop demonstrable retail-display work.
Design-education route: pursue a related fashion, communication, space/interior or design programme and assemble a portfolio of display, styling, spatial-design and brand-communication work.
Retail-experience route: gain exposure to store operations, merchandising, sales data, stock/display upkeep or category execution, then move toward visual-merchandising responsibilities.

sections.heading: Skills to build
paragraphs: The national qualification combines visual-design capability with retail analysis and execution. It specifically identifies layout-design techniques and drawing conventions; display dressing for different merchandise; the use of light, colour, texture, shape and dimension; store and brand procedures; analysis of promotional impact; and maintenance of visual-merchandising elements.

Candidates should also be able to turn business requirements into practical plans: identify target customers and sales patterns, organise information and communicate findings, work across stakeholders, make justified adjustments to displays, and take responsibility for quality and safety. Training infrastructure specified for the qualification includes planograms, mannequins, point-of-sale displays, signage, cameras, computer equipment and Photoshop/Illustrator/2D/3D-design software, indicating useful hands-on and digital capabilities.
bullets: Visual composition: colour, lighting, scale, texture, shape, focal points, styling and merchandise grouping.
Spatial and technical execution: planograms, layout interpretation, display installation, signage, props, fixtures and safe use of tools/equipment.
Commercial judgement: customer segments, category sales patterns, seasonality, product offers, promotion effectiveness and store profitability.
Digital and communication capability: presentation of ideas, data collection and analysis, stakeholder coordination, and design-software familiarity.

sections.heading: Where the work happens
paragraphs: This is principally an on-site retail role, since displays are implemented and maintained in selling spaces. The NSDC/RASCI Visual Merchandiser standard identifies department stores, supermarkets, specialty stores, fresh-food stores and quick-service food stores as retail-operation settings for the role; work can cover both in-store and window displays.

The role requires coordination beyond the shop floor. The qualification includes liaison with internal and external stakeholders, and the NQR industry-validation list includes organisations associated with fashion retail, department stores, jewellery, consumer electronics, grocery and other retail formats. Store visits, display changeovers and campaign/event deadlines are therefore integral possibilities, although exact schedules and travel demands depend on employer, store network and seniority.
bullets: Department, specialty, supermarket, grocery/fresh-food and quick-service retail environments.
Fashion/lifestyle, jewellery, consumer-electronics and multi-format retail businesses.
Collaboration with store operations, marketing, category teams, brand teams, suppliers and display/fixture vendors.

sections.heading: Progression context
paragraphs: The current NQR qualification names Marketing Manager as the progression path after attaining the Visual Merchandiser qualification. This is a qualification-framework indication, not a guaranteed promotion sequence: employers may use titles such as senior visual merchandiser, visual-merchandising lead, store/brand visual specialist, category or marketing roles differently.

Progression is strengthened by demonstrating that displays deliver commercial outcomes as well as visual quality: analysing promotional results, improving underperforming categories, maintaining brand compliance, managing implementation resources and coordinating stakeholders. The NQR framework also characterises the role as one that can complete complex routine tasks with responsibility for output quality and supervise routine work of others.
bullets: Build evidence of display concepts, before/after execution, planograms, campaign roll-outs and measured promotion/category outcomes.
Develop leadership through vendor coordination, standards audits, briefing store teams and maintaining multi-store consistency.
Broaden toward retail marketing, category-related work, store visual leadership or marketing-management responsibilities, subject to employer structures and experience.

title: Vocational Instructor (Private Institute)
description: An instructor teaching trade-specific skills at privately-owned Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), vocational colleges, or corporate training centers.

quick_facts.label: Core function
quick_facts.value: Delivers competency-based, trade-specific vocational instruction, combining practical skill transfer with training methodology so learners can meet defined vocational outcomes.

quick_facts.label: Key preparation route
quick_facts.value: CITS is DGT’s principal instructor-training route. DGT states that eligible entrants hold an NTC, NAC, diploma or degree; successful CITS trainees receive the National Craft Instructor Certificate (NCIC). Trade-specific eligibility must be checked in the current admission material.

quick_facts.label: Private-ITI context
quick_facts.value: Private ITIs can operate within the DGT/NCVET affiliation ecosystem. DGT’s affiliation page publishes admission and affiliation actions for both government and private ITIs.

quick_facts.label: Standards orientation
quick_facts.value: Training is expected to align with NSQF-approved qualifications and defined learning outcomes; NSQF is an outcome- and competency-based framework covering vocational education, training, skilling and relevant experience.

quick_facts.label: Experience-based recognition route
quick_facts.value: For eligible in-service ITI instructors without NCIC, DGT’s CITS Recognition of Prior Learning route sets conditions including a relevant CTS/diploma/degree base qualification and at least three years of teaching experience; private-ITI candidates must meet the documentation and sponsorship/evidence requirements in the guideline.

sections.heading: What the role involves
paragraphs: A vocational instructor translates a trade curriculum into competency-based teaching: preparing training content for the relevant job role, delivering theory and hands-on practice, using suitable training and assessment methods, and supporting learners’ industry and job-market readiness. In a private institute, the precise timetable, trade portfolio, learner mix and administrative duties are set by the employer, but the instructional work should remain tied to the qualification outcomes being delivered.

CITS materials describe the instructor purpose as transferring hands-on skills and training skilled manpower for industry. NCVET also identifies training implementation, subject-matter preparation, current-practice application, learning strategies, assessment modes, industry connections and overall training-process management as trainer responsibilities.
bullets: Plan sessions around the approved occupational/qualification outcomes and practical tasks.
Demonstrate trade procedures, supervise workshop or laboratory practice, and give corrective feedback.
Use assessments and training records consistent with the institute’s programme and applicable qualification requirements.
Build employability awareness through industry-relevant practice, communication and workplace-readiness support.

sections.heading: Entry routes and credentials
paragraphs: A common route is first to build trade competence through an ITI/CTS qualification (NTC or NAC), a relevant diploma, or a relevant degree, then undertake CITS in the appropriate trade. DGT describes CITS as combining technical skill with training methodology and lists NTC, NAC, diploma and degree holders as eligible categories; exact prerequisites differ by CITS trade and admission cycle.

A B.Voc or another relevant degree can be a useful higher-education foundation where it matches the technical trade and the institute’s hiring requirements, but it is not a universal substitute for trade-specific eligibility. Candidates should compare their qualification against the current CITS trade entry criteria and the private institute’s vacancy notice.

An experienced instructor may instead be eligible for DGT’s CITS RPL process. The published guideline requires, among other conditions, a relevant CTS/diploma/degree qualification and at least three years of teaching experience; it also specifies evidence requirements for experience claimed at private ITIs.
bullets: Develop demonstrable competence in the trade you intend to teach.
Add formal vocational pedagogy through CITS or another applicable NCVET-recognized Training of Trainers route.
For each vacancy, verify the institute’s affiliation status, the trade being taught, required experience, and whether NCIC/CITS is specified.
Treat entrance tests, intake dates, course availability and certificate-validity rules as cycle-specific; confirm them from current DGT/NSTI notices before applying.

sections.heading: Skills to develop
paragraphs: The role needs both domain skills and platform skills. NCVET defines domain skills as sector-, subsector- or job-role-specific capability, and platform skills as transferable training skills, including vocational pedagogy. Its trainer guidance also points to learner-needs analysis, content development and delivery, appropriate methodology, communication, assessment, blended learning and impact assessment.

For trade instruction, safety-conscious practical demonstration, observation of performance, clear feedback and the ability to adapt explanations to learners with different prior preparation are especially important. These capabilities support the competency-based, outcome-focused design of NSQF-aligned training.
bullets: Current technical competence in the assigned trade and familiarity with industry practice.
Vocational pedagogy: lesson design, demonstrations, practice sequencing and learner support.
Assessment literacy: interpreting outcomes, observing performance and applying the required assessment strategy.
Communication, group facilitation, inclusivity and workplace-readiness coaching.
Digital and blended-training capability where the programme or employer uses it.

sections.heading: Where and how the work is done
paragraphs: The most direct setting is a private ITI or other private vocational-training provider delivering a defined trade. DGT’s current affiliation material explicitly covers NCVET-affiliated government and private ITIs, while its CITS guidance describes the national ITI and skill ecosystem as a major destination for trained instructors.

The work commonly spans classroom instruction and supervised practical learning in workshops, laboratories or simulated work areas. Where an ITI participates in DGT’s Dual System of Training, instructors may also coordinate learning that combines ITI-based theory with industry-based practical exposure; DGT says eligible government and private affiliated ITIs can run the scheme in their relevant affiliated trades.
bullets: Private ITIs affiliated within the national vocational-training system.
Private skill-development providers delivering short- or long-term programmes.
Industry-linked training arrangements, including ITI–industry dual-training models where applicable.
Corporate or industry training roles may be a related transition for instructors who can train workers and coordinate technical learning.

sections.heading: Progression options
paragraphs: With stronger instructional experience and recognised trainer preparation, a private vocational instructor can broaden into senior instruction, master-trainer work, curriculum or written instructional-material development, training coordination, corporate technical training, or assessment-related work. DGT’s CITS prospectus identifies instructor work in ITIs, certified delivery under skill-development schemes, industry training coordination and preparation of Written Instructional Materials as outcomes of CITS; NCVET separately describes Trainer and Master Trainer pathways through recognised Training of Trainers and Master Trainer programmes.

Assessment is a distinct progression direction rather than an automatic extension of teaching. NCVET publishes separate Training of Assessors guidelines, so a candidate seeking assessor work should check the current qualification, awarding-body and assessment-agency requirements.
bullets: Senior vocational instructor or lead trainer for a trade area.
Master Trainer after suitable recognised preparation and demonstrated training capability.
Corporate technical trainer or industry training coordinator.
Curriculum, learning-material or instructional-design work.
Skill assessor, subject to the applicable assessor-training and engagement requirements.
Vocational training centre entrepreneurship, subject to affiliation, infrastructure, staffing and local regulatory requirements.

title: Wealth Manager
description: Financial adviser who develops and manages investment, retirement and wealth plans for high-net-worth clients.

quick_facts.label: Role scope
quick_facts.value: A Wealth Manager typically combines client financial planning with investment and portfolio advice. In India, advice on securities, investment strategies, or portfolio allocation can fall within SEBI’s investment-adviser framework, so the precise responsibilities depend on the employer, products, and regulatory role.

quick_facts.label: Regulated-advisory certification
quick_facts.value: For an individual SEBI-registered investment adviser, or the principal officer of a non-individual registered investment adviser, NISM states that both NISM-Series-X-A (Investment Adviser Level 1) and NISM-Series-X-B (Investment Adviser Level 2) are required to meet the certification requirements under the SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013.

quick_facts.label: CFA pathway relevance
quick_facts.value: The CFA Program comprises three exam levels and covers investment tools, asset valuation, portfolio management, wealth planning, ethics, and—at Level III—a Private Wealth pathway. It is relevant preparation for wealth-management work, but it is not itself a substitute for Indian regulatory registration or product-specific permissions.

quick_facts.label: Mutual-fund distribution is distinct
quick_facts.value: Where the job includes selling or distributing mutual-fund products, AMFI states that the relevant route includes NISM Series V-A certification and AMFI registration (ARN); employees engaged in sale or distribution require the relevant certification and EUIN. This is distinct from acting as a SEBI investment adviser.

sections.heading: What a Wealth Manager does
paragraphs: The role is client-centred and usually starts with understanding objectives, financial position, cash flows, liabilities, risk exposure, time horizon, and constraints. NISM’s investment-adviser curriculum explicitly covers goal setting, budgeting and cash-flow management, insurance, debt, investment planning and asset allocation, tax planning, and retirement planning.

For wealthy clients, portfolio work extends beyond selecting investments: CFA Institute’s private-wealth material describes comprehensive plans that consider goals, human capital, taxation, liquidity, assets, liabilities, and risk exposures. In a regulated advisory setting, recommendations and client interactions must also follow applicable SEBI requirements and the registered firm’s compliance processes.
bullets: Develop and review goal-based financial and retirement plans.
Assess risk, construct or monitor portfolios, and explain investment trade-offs.
Coordinate planning considerations such as liquidity, insurance, debt, taxes, and succession-related objectives where within the professional’s mandate.
Maintain client documentation, suitability processes, disclosures, and escalation practices required by the relevant employer and regulatory model.

sections.heading: Entry routes from BFIA and the CFA Program
paragraphs: A BFIA-oriented undergraduate route can build a useful foundation in finance and investment analysis. The CFA Program is a complementary professional pathway: candidates progress through Levels I, II, and III, with content that moves from investment foundations to analysis, portfolio management, and wealth planning. CFA Institute identifies Wealth Manager as one of the career paths associated with the Program.

For a role that actually provides regulated investment advice in India, academic study and the CFA exams should be separated from regulatory eligibility. NISM states that individual registered investment advisers, principal officers of non-individual registered advisers, and associated persons providing investment advice must meet the applicable Investment Adviser Level 1 and Level 2 certification requirements. A candidate should confirm the intended employer’s business model—advisory, distribution, banking, brokerage, or another regulated activity—before selecting required certifications.
bullets: Build finance, accounting, markets, statistics, communication, and spreadsheet-analysis capability through undergraduate study and internships.
Use the CFA Program to deepen investment analysis, ethics, portfolio management, and private-wealth knowledge.

For SEBI-regulated investment-advice responsibilities, complete the applicable NISM Investment Adviser certifications and work through the registration/compliance route required for the individual or firm.
For mutual-fund distribution responsibilities, check the separate NISM Series V-A and AMFI ARN/EUIN requirements.

sections.heading: Core skills to develop
paragraphs: The strongest technical base combines personal-finance diagnosis with investment analysis. NISM’s Level 1 objectives include evaluating a client’s financial position, debt and loans, financial products across equity, debt, derivatives and managed portfolios, portfolio construction, performance monitoring, regulation, ethics, and grievance redressal.

The CFA curriculum adds asset valuation, portfolio management, ethical and professional standards, asset allocation, portfolio construction, performance measurement, derivatives and risk management, and a Private Wealth pathway. These subjects support the analytical side of the role; clear client communication and the ability to translate risk and trade-offs into understandable choices remain essential in practice.
bullets: Client discovery, goal prioritisation, and risk profiling.
Asset allocation, portfolio construction, monitoring, and performance evaluation.
Knowledge of equity, fixed income, mutual funds, alternatives, derivatives, insurance, and retirement-planning concepts.
Ethics, regulatory awareness, documentation discipline, and client communication.
Quantitative analysis and practical use of spreadsheets and financial data.

sections.heading: Where the role may sit
paragraphs: Wealth-management work can be performed within financial-services organisations, including wealth-management firms, banks, brokerages, and investment-management businesses. CFA Institute lists wealth management among the employers and career settings associated with CFA charterholders, while AMFI notes that mutual-fund distributors can be individuals or non-individual entities such as banks, broking houses, and online distribution channels.

The job title alone does not determine what a professional may recommend, sell, or execute. In India, the practical scope is shaped by whether the firm is operating as a SEBI-registered investment adviser, a distributor, or another regulated intermediary, along with the individual’s assigned role and applicable certifications.
bullets: Private-wealth and wealth-management teams at banks or investment firms.
Brokerage and distribution organisations serving retail or affluent clients.
SEBI-registered investment-advisory firms and related client-advisory teams.
Independent practice only after meeting the applicable registration, certification, and compliance requirements.

sections.heading: Career development
paragraphs: An early-career route can begin with analyst, client-service, relationship, investment-support, distribution, or advisory-support work, then broaden toward client ownership and more complex planning as technical competence, product permissions, and compliance responsibilities grow. This is a role-development pattern rather than a guaranteed promotion ladder; employers structure titles and client segments differently.

The CFA Program is designed around increasingly advanced exam levels, and its Level III curriculum includes a Private Wealth pathway. CFA Institute also identifies Wealth Manager among the career paths linked to the credential. For regulated advice, continued eligibility depends on maintaining the certifications and registrations applicable to the actual advisory activity.
bullets: Build supervised experience in client onboarding, research, portfolio reporting, and review preparation.
Develop depth in a client segment or planning area, such as retirement, investments, or private wealth.
Take on larger and more complex client relationships only within employer authorisation and the applicable regulatory framework.
Maintain current NISM certification or other applicable accreditation when performing regulated advisory work.

title: Web Developer
description: A programmer who creates and maintains websites and web applications, working on either the front-end, back-end, or both (full-stack).

quick_facts.label: Role scope
quick_facts.value: A Web Developer designs and writes code for web-based applications, websites and portals, maintains them, handles their technical aspects, and helps establish coding standards.

quick_facts.label: Sector
quick_facts.value: India’s National Career Service classifies Web Developer within the IT-ITeS sector and lists related titles including Web Content Management Developer, Web Application Developer and Web Services Developer.

quick_facts.label: Academic routes
quick_facts.value: BCA is a recognised bachelor’s degree entered after 10+2, while MCA is a recognised master’s degree entered after a bachelor’s degree. Programme curricula, admissions and durations can differ by institution and applicable regulations.

quick_facts.label: NIMCET route
quick_facts.value: For the 2026–27 cycle, NIMCET is the national-level entrance test used for MCA admission at the participating 11 NITs and 2 IIITs; applicants should rely on the applicable year’s official brochure and eligibility rules.

quick_facts.label: Core technical capabilities
quick_facts.value: The National Career Service profile identifies web technologies, databases, responsive design, version control, database design, client-server/internet architecture, object-oriented programming and browser compatibility as relevant competencies.

quick_facts.label: Indicative pay context
quick_facts.value: The NCS Web Developer profile, last updated on 9 August 2016, reported indicative monthly earnings of ₹8,000–₹12,500 for new entrants and ₹20,000–₹45,000 for experienced candidates. These are historical reference figures, not a current salary benchmark.

sections.heading: What a Web Developer does
paragraphs: Web development covers building and maintaining web-facing software. In the National Career Service occupational profile, the role includes designing and coding websites, portals and web applications; maintaining those systems; handling technical aspects; and designing, communicating and maintaining coding standards.

In practice, the role can be front-end focused, back-end focused or full-stack. A front-end emphasis concerns the browser-facing interface and responsive behaviour; a back-end emphasis concerns server-side services, APIs, data storage and application logic; full-stack work combines both. The precise split depends on the employer, product and team structure.
bullets: Translate requirements, designs or wireframes into working web pages or application features.
Write, test, debug and maintain code; address browser/device compatibility and responsiveness.
Integrate interfaces with back-end services, APIs and databases where the role requires it.
Use version control and follow team coding standards, review practices and delivery processes.
Improve reliability, maintainability and performance over the life of a website or web application.

sections.heading: Entry routes in the Indian education system
paragraphs: A common academic route is BCA followed by entry-level web-development work, portfolio building and internships. UGC’s degree specification lists BCA as a bachelor’s degree with 10+2 as the minimum entry qualification, so it is an identifiable undergraduate parent route for this node.

MCA can deepen computing preparation before or after initial work experience. It is a postgraduate route after a bachelor’s degree; however, applicants must check the eligibility, curriculum, duration and admission rules of each institution rather than assuming one uniform national pattern.

NIMCET is an admission examination, not a web-development certification or a job. In the 2026 cycle, it is used for MCA admissions at the participating NITs and IIITs. Its schedules, participating institutes, eligibility and counselling rules are cycle-specific, so candidates should use the official year-specific information brochure.

A skills-first route is also possible: learn the relevant technologies, build deployable projects, obtain practical experience through internships or client work, and demonstrate work through a portfolio and code samples. The NCS profile notes that web-designing/development internship or work experience is generally relevant for the occupation.
bullets: After 10+2: pursue a BCA or another relevant computing programme, while building practical web projects.
After a bachelor’s degree: pursue MCA where it fits career goals; NIMCET is one route to MCA at its participating institutes.
Alongside either route: develop a portfolio, use version control, practise debugging and responsive development, and seek internship or junior developer opportunities.
GATE may be relevant for some postgraduate admissions or recruitment pathways, but qualifying it does not itself guarantee admission, scholarship or employment.

sections.heading: Skills to develop
paragraphs: A Web Developer needs both implementation skills and delivery discipline. The NCS profile specifically names HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, responsive web design, PHP and .NET examples, along with DBMS/MySQL, database architecture, version control, client-server and internet architecture, XML schemas, object-oriented programming and browser-specific compatibility work. Tool choices change over time, but these underlying capability areas remain useful for evaluating a learning plan.

The role also requires communication and collaboration: understanding requirements, estimating work, incorporating client or stakeholder feedback, and working independently or in teams are all reflected in the NCS profile.
bullets: Front end: semantic HTML, CSS, JavaScript, responsive layouts and cross-browser testing.
Back end and data: server-side programming concepts, APIs, authentication concepts, database modelling and SQL/DBMS fundamentals.
Engineering workflow: version control, readable code, debugging, testing habits, documentation and deployment awareness.
Product delivery: requirement interpretation, estimation, feedback incorporation and clear communication with designers, project managers and clients.
Portfolio evidence: completed projects that show responsive interfaces, data/API integration, maintainable source code and problem-solving decisions.

sections.heading: Work setting and collaboration
paragraphs: The NCS occupational profile describes Web Developer as primarily a desk-based role and notes that work-from-home may be available. It also indicates that work hours, shift arrangements and overtime vary by organisation. These are role-level indicators rather than guarantees for any employer or employment contract.

Web developers commonly collaborate with design, content and project functions. An NCS-listed website-developer vacancy describes working with UI/UX designers, content creators and project managers, as well as integrating with back-end services, APIs and databases. That vacancy is an example of employer expectations, not a universal requirement.
bullets: Typical environments include IT services firms, software product companies, digital agencies, internal enterprise technology teams and independent client work.
Work may be office-based, hybrid or remote depending on the employer and assignment.
Expect coordination with UI/UX, QA, content, product and delivery stakeholders; team size and on-call or release expectations vary.

sections.heading: Progression and adjacent paths
paragraphs: The NCS profile presents an indicative progression from Engineer Trainee to Web Developer, Senior Web Developer, Web Solution Developer, Delivery Lead, Offering/Domain Lead and Head of Company/CEO. It also identifies project management as a possible occupational move. Actual titles and promotion criteria vary substantially by employer.

The node’s listed children should be read as possible next steps rather than a compulsory ladder. Examples include progressing toward senior software engineering, freelancing, product or design-adjacent work, an MCA, or entrepreneurship. CAT and GATE are examinations that may support particular education or career choices; they are not job titles or automatic promotions.
bullets: Deepen technical scope: senior developer or senior software-engineering roles.
Broaden delivery scope: technical lead, solution development, delivery leadership or project/product-facing work.
Change working model: freelance web development or founding a technology venture.
Continue education: MCA through institution-specific admissions; NIMCET is a route for participating NIT/IIIT MCA programmes.
Use entrance examinations purposefully: GATE can support selected postgraduate or PSU-related opportunities, but does not guarantee admission or a job.

sections.heading: Compensation context
paragraphs: Salary depends on location, employer type, skill depth, prior experience, work arrangement, technology stack and the ability to demonstrate production-quality work. No single figure should be treated as a current market rate across India.

For dated historical context only, the National Career Service Web Developer profile—last updated on 9 August 2016—listed indicative earnings of ₹8,000–₹12,500 per month for new entrants and ₹20,000–₹45,000 per month for candidates with experience, while explicitly stating that the figures were indicative and subject to change. These figures should not be used to set a 2026 salary expectation; candidates should compare current, location-specific offers and the complete compensation terms.
bullets: Assess an offer using fixed pay, variable pay, benefits, work location, probation terms, notice period, learning support and expected hours—not base pay alone.
For freelance work, assess compensation against scope, revision limits, maintenance obligations, payment milestones and tax/compliance responsibilities.
Treat salary data from old occupational profiles as historical context, not a live benchmark.

title: Class 10 (Secondary School)
description: Completion of secondary school (Class 10) under CBSE, ICSE, or a state board — the first major branching point in the Indian education system.

quick_facts.label: CBSE Class X scheme (2026–27)
quick_facts.value: CBSE lists two languages, Mathematics or Mathematics Advanced, Science or Science Advanced, Social Science, academic electives, and school-based internal-assessment subjects in its Class X curriculum; subject availability remains school-specific.

quick_facts.label: Technical-training option
quick_facts.value: DGT’s Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) is delivered through ITIs. Entry requirements are trade-specific: many listed technical trades require Class 10 with Science and Mathematics, while some trades require only Class 10 or Class 8.

quick_facts.label: Examples of Class-10-level government recruitment eligibility
quick_facts.value: The SSC GD Constable Examination 2026 required Matriculation/Class 10 from a recognised board by the notified cut-off. The SSC MTS and Havaldar 2025 notice likewise set Matriculation or equivalent as the essential educational qualification; each recruitment has its own age, physical, medical, domicile and other conditions.

quick_facts.label: Agniveer example
quick_facts.value: The Indian Navy’s Agniveer (MR) eligibility material specifies Matriculation with at least 50% aggregate marks for that entry; recruitment batches, vacancies, age limits, physical standards and other conditions must be checked in the current service notification.

sections.heading: What Class 10 covers
paragraphs: Class 10 is a board-assessed secondary-school milestone, but its precise subject package depends on the board and school. In CBSE’s 2026–27 Class X scheme, the core structure includes languages, Mathematics or Mathematics Advanced, Science or Science Advanced, and Social Science, alongside electives and internal-assessment areas. CBSE also lists Class X skill subjects such as Information Technology, Security, Automotive and Artificial Intelligence.

ICSE uses a different grouping structure. Its Year 2026 syllabus groups English, a second language, and History/Civics/Geography in Group I; offers Mathematics, Science, Economics and Commercial Studies among Group II choices; and provides Group III options including Computer Applications, Commercial Applications, Art, Physical Education and vocational subjects. State-board subject and assessment rules should be checked directly with the relevant state board and school.
bullets: Keep the Class 10 marksheet, passing certificate, school-leaving/transfer certificate, identity documents and category certificates (where applicable) ready for Class XI, ITI, diploma and recruitment applications.

For CBSE learners, distinguish Mathematics from Mathematics Advanced and Science from Science Advanced when choosing and preparing for Class X, because the Board publishes them separately in the current curriculum.
A skill or additional subject can be useful evidence of interest, but it does not replace a later course’s stated eligibility requirements.

sections.heading: Choosing the next step after Class 10
paragraphs: The familiar labels Arts/Humanities, Commerce, Science PCM, Science PCB and PCMB are practical ways schools organise Class XI–XII subject combinations; they are not a single all-India CBSE subject scheme. CBSE’s current senior-secondary curriculum instead publishes a broad menu that includes Accountancy, Business Studies, Economics, History, Political Science, Psychology, Sociology, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Computer Science and others. Before choosing a stream, confirm the exact Class XI combination that the intended school actually offers.

Start with future prerequisite flexibility rather than a stream label alone. In particular, many DGT technical ITI trades list Class 10 Science and Mathematics (or a related vocational subject) as entry requirements, while other trades have different thresholds. A student considering technical pathways should therefore preserve and strengthen Mathematics and Science where possible, then verify the specific trade or programme criteria before applying.

Admissions, cut-offs, fees, counselling dates and reservation rules are local and time-sensitive. For example, Assam’s 2026–27 state-polytechnic process used an online registration and counselling schedule, while its published rules require HSLC/equivalent with Mathematics and Science as compulsory subjects and specified minimum marks for that state system. This is an example of why applicants must use the current brochure of their own state admission authority rather than treating another state’s criteria as universal.
bullets: Compare the actual Class XI timetable, laboratory access, teacher availability and subject combinations at each candidate school.
If considering a diploma or technical ITI route, check whether Class 10 Mathematics and Science are mandatory for the specific branch or trade.
Use official current-year notices for any recruitment route; education eligibility is only one part of selection.

Do not assume that Class 10 board marks alone guarantee admission: schools, state diploma authorities and recruiters may apply additional eligibility, merit, entrance-test, physical or document-verification requirements.

sections.heading: Routes opened after Class 10
paragraphs: Senior secondary (Classes XI–XII) is the main academic continuation route. Students may build an arts/humanities-, commerce- or science-oriented subject combination from the subjects their school and board offer. CBSE’s current senior-secondary list supports combinations involving humanities and social-science subjects, business and accountancy subjects, and Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics and Biology, subject to school availability and the Board’s combination rules.

Polytechnic diploma admission is a direct post-Class-10 technical route administered through state-level systems. The details are not nationally uniform: for illustration, the Assam Directorate of Technical Education ran a separate 2026–27 state-polytechnic registration/counselling process and publishes its own eligibility rules. Applicants should use their home state’s current diploma admission brochure, not past dates or another state’s schedule.

ITI is a skills-first route under DGT’s CTS network. DGT lists 169 NSQF-compliant trades and identifies trade-specific duration and entry qualifications. Examples include one-year and two-year technical trades that require Class 10 with Science and Mathematics, alongside trades whose entry qualification is simply Class 10 or Class 8.

Class 10 can also meet the education threshold for selected uniformed-service and central-government recruitment notices, but it is not an automatic job route. The SSC GD 2026 notice required Class 10 and also prescribed computer-based examination, physical standards/efficiency tests, medical examination and document verification. Indian Navy Agniveer (MR) is an example of a service entry using Matriculation-based eligibility, but its official calendar warns that detailed conditions are subject to the notification for each entry and batch. SSC MTS notices similarly need to be checked cycle by cycle.
bullets: Class XI–XII: Arts/Humanities, Commerce, PCM, PCB and PCMB-style pathways, where offered by the school.
Polytechnic Diploma (Engineering): consult the current state technical-education authority’s brochure, eligibility rules and counselling schedule.
ITI: select a CTS trade by its stated entry qualification, duration, NSQF level and local institute availability.
SSC GD Constable or SSC MTS: apply only when a live SSC notice confirms the qualification, age, vacancy, deadline and selection process.
Agniveer: check the current Army, Navy or Air Force notification for the particular category; Class 10 eligibility applies only to specified entries, not all Agniveer categories.
