title: Arts & Humanities Stream (11th & 12th)
description: Senior-secondary humanities stream (History, Political Science, Psychology, Languages, etc.) leading toward BA, law, design, civil services, media and social sciences.

quick_facts.label: What this stream means
quick_facts.value: Arts & Humanities is a common school-level label for a Class XI–XII subject combination centred on humanities and social-science electives; it is not a single nationally fixed course or a restriction to only humanities subjects.

quick_facts.label: Typical CBSE subject options
quick_facts.value: For senior secondary, CBSE lists languages plus electives including Economics, Fine Arts, Geography, History, Home Science, Legal Studies, Political Science, Psychology and Sociology. The exact subjects a student can take depend on the school’s approved offerings and timetable.

quick_facts.label: Law-route compatibility
quick_facts.value: For CLAT 2026 UG, candidates need a 10+2/equivalent qualification with at least 45% marks (40% for SC/ST/PwD); the published eligibility does not prescribe a particular school stream.

quick_facts.label: Design-route compatibility
quick_facts.value: NIFT’s 2026 B.Des eligibility accepts a recognised 10+2 qualification or specified equivalents; unlike B.F.Tech, the B.Des eligibility text does not require Mathematics, Physics or a specified stream.

quick_facts.label: Teacher-education route
quick_facts.value: NCTE’s D.El.Ed. regulatory material describes D.El.Ed. as a two-academic-year elementary-teacher-education programme; admission eligibility and procedures are also governed by the applicable NCTE and State Government rules, so candidates should verify the current state notification and institutional recognition.

sections.heading: Subjects and how the stream is structured
paragraphs: Arts & Humanities in Classes XI and XII should be understood as a flexible subject basket rather than a uniform national package. In the CBSE senior-secondary curriculum, students study language subject(s) and may combine electives such as History, Political Science, Psychology, Sociology, Geography, Economics, Fine Arts, Home Science and Legal Studies. A school may not offer every subject that appears in the board curriculum, so the actual decision is made from the combinations that the school can timetable and register.

A sound combination starts with the learner’s interests and intended next step. For example, History, Political Science, Sociology, Psychology, Economics, Geography, languages and Legal Studies can support different undergraduate choices, but they do not themselves guarantee admission to a particular course. Retain Mathematics or Applied Mathematics only if it is both available and useful for the courses under consideration; individual universities and programmes set their own eligibility and subject requirements.
bullets: Check the school’s Class XI subject-combination sheet before choosing: availability, subject clashes, minimum enrolment rules and whether a sixth/additional subject is permitted can matter.
Use the current board syllabus—not coaching material alone—to understand the academic content and assessment for each shortlisted subject.

Keep a record of the Class XII subjects you will actually appear in. CUET-UG 2026 permits candidates to choose up to five test subjects, but programme-specific subject mapping is determined by the receiving university or institution.
Do not treat “Arts” as excluding creative, language, social-science, legal-studies, economics or selected quantitative options; the permitted mix is board- and school-specific.

sections.heading: How to decide whether Arts & Humanities is the right Class XI choice
paragraphs: Choose the stream because its subjects fit the student’s strengths, sustained interests and realistic post-Class-XII options—not because it is assumed to be easier or because a particular career is presumed to require it. The decision is most useful when made after comparing the school’s actual subject menu with the formal entrance and programme eligibility rules for a few possible destinations.

This stream preserves direct routes into broad undergraduate study, law and many design programmes. For instance, CLAT’s published UG eligibility is based on 10+2 marks rather than a specified stream, and NIFT’s B.Des rules accept recognised 10+2 qualifications without imposing Mathematics; however, NIFT’s B.F.Tech route does require Mathematics. This illustrates why students should check the precise programme, not rely on a broad statement that a field is “open to Arts students.”
bullets: Shortlist at least three possible routes—for example BA/social sciences, law, design, management or teacher education—then check each official admission notice before finalising subjects.

If considering BBA, BA, a university LLB route or CUET-UG, inspect the target university’s current programme bulletin for minimum marks, accepted tests and required Class XII subjects; these vary by institution and admission cycle.
If considering NIFT, distinguish B.Des from B.F.Tech: their Class XII subject requirements differ.

If considering government recruitment or defence examinations after Class XII, read the notification for the particular post and year. SSC and UPSC notices set post- and examination-specific educational, age, physical and other conditions; a Class XII stream label alone does not establish eligibility.
For D.El.Ed., verify both the provider’s recognition and the current state admission process rather than assuming that every diploma provider or format is valid for the intended purpose.

sections.heading: Routes available after Class XII
paragraphs: A humanities-oriented Class XII combination can lead directly to BA and related undergraduate programmes in the humanities, social sciences, languages and interdisciplinary fields; admissions may be through a university’s own process or CUET-UG where the university uses it. For 2026, NTA described CUET-UG as allowing candidates to choose up to five subjects, but candidates must still match their test choices and Class XII record to the requirements published by each target university.

Law is a major route: CLAT provides admission-test access to participating National Law Universities’ UG programmes, subject to the Consortium’s eligibility and admission rules. Design is another route: NIFT’s B.Des admission framework accepts recognised Class XII qualifications from any stream, subject to the entrance/admission process and the current prospectus. D.El.Ed. is a separate regulated teacher-education route, with state-level admission procedures and recognition requirements.

BBA, direct university LLB programmes, BA programmes, government recruitment examinations such as SSC CHSL, and UPSC NDA & NA are possible node children, but they are not interchangeable pathways. Each has a separate notification, eligibility standard, selection process and timetable. Students should therefore use official notices in their Class XII year rather than assuming that an earlier year’s rules or dates will apply.
bullets: BA: compare the university’s offered disciplines, subject eligibility, entrance route and admission policy.
BBA: check whether the target institution uses board marks, CUET-UG, its own test or another examination; rules vary by university.
LLB/CLAT: for CLAT 2026 UG, the published minimum is 45% in 10+2/equivalent, or 40% for SC/ST/PwD candidates; follow the current cycle’s rules.
B.Des/NIFT Entrance Exam: NIFT’s B.Des eligibility is compatible with a recognised 10+2 qualification, while B.F.Tech has Mathematics requirements—select the programme deliberately.
D.El.Ed.: use NCTE resources and the relevant state authority to confirm recognised institutions and the year-specific admission process.
SSC CHSL and UPSC NDA & NA: monitor SSC and UPSC official notices for the exact year because recruitment/examination conditions and dates are notice-specific.

title: Commerce Stream (11th & 12th)
description: Senior-secondary commerce stream (Accountancy, Business Studies, Economics) leading toward B.Com, CA/CS/CMA, management, finance and law.

quick_facts.label: What the stream comprises
quick_facts.value: In CBSE’s 2026–27 senior-secondary curriculum, Accountancy, Business Studies and Economics are listed as separate academic electives for Classes XI–XII; schools determine the actual subject combinations they offer.

quick_facts.label: Subject planning matters for admissions
quick_facts.value: For CUET (UG) 2026, candidates could choose up to five test subjects, but NTA directs them to choose according to the eligibility requirements of their intended university programme. Students should therefore check programme-level requirements before finalising Class XI subjects.

quick_facts.label: Professional-course entry can begin during school
quick_facts.value: ICAI permits provisional registration for CA Foundation after Class X; a candidate must have appeared in the Class XII examination and complete the prescribed study period before taking the Foundation examination.

quick_facts.label: Commerce is not a restriction to one career family
quick_facts.value: After or while completing Class XII, eligible students can pursue routes including CA Foundation, CSEET for CS, CMA Foundation, ACET, CLAT and NCHM JEE; each body sets its own current eligibility and examination rules.

sections.heading: What students typically study in Commerce in Classes XI–XII
paragraphs: Commerce is a senior-secondary subject pathway rather than a single nationally uniform course. In the CBSE 2026–27 scheme, Accountancy, Business Studies and Economics appear as separate academic electives for Classes XI–XII. A school may also offer choices such as Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, Entrepreneurship, Informatics Practices, Computer Science, Legal Studies, languages and skill subjects; availability and permitted combinations must be confirmed with the particular school and board.

The core subjects develop complementary foundations: Accountancy focuses on recording, classifying and interpreting financial transactions; Business Studies addresses business organisation and management; and Economics provides frameworks for understanding economic activity. Students who anticipate quantitatively intensive study should consider whether Mathematics or Applied Mathematics is available and appropriate: ICAI’s current CA Foundation quantitative-aptitude material includes business mathematics, logical reasoning and statistics, while ACET preparation references mathematics at the 10+2 level.
bullets: Confirm the school’s offered combination before admission; a label such as “Commerce with Maths” is a local subject combination, not a universal national qualification.
Retain English and any subjects required by target universities or entrance tests. For CUET-UG, NTA advises selecting test subjects with the desired university programme’s eligibility in mind.
Use Class XI–XII to build numerical fluency, reading and writing ability, spreadsheet/data skills, and familiarity with financial statements and business concepts.

sections.heading: How to decide whether Commerce is a good fit
paragraphs: Commerce can suit students interested in how organisations earn, spend, report, regulate and finance activity, and those who are comfortable developing accuracy with numbers as well as communication and analytical skills. It should not be chosen on the assumption that it automatically preserves eligibility for every undergraduate programme: admission requirements are set programme by programme and university by university.

Check intended pathways early. The CUET-UG 2026 bulletin explicitly says candidates should choose subjects based on the eligibility criteria for their desired university programme. This makes it sensible to shortlist possible degrees—such as B.Com, BBA, BCA, economics, law or hospitality—and then verify the Class XII and entrance-test subjects required by each target institution before locking in electives.

Students considering professional routes should distinguish eligibility from preparation. CA Foundation registration can begin provisionally after Class X, CSEET is open to candidates who have passed or are appearing in Senior Secondary (10+2), and CMA Foundation admission can begin after Class X although Class XII is needed to sit the Foundation examination. These routes are open beyond Commerce, but Commerce subjects can provide relevant conceptual preparation.
bullets: Choose Accountancy if you are prepared for systematic practice with rules, entries, statements and error checking.
Choose Mathematics or Applied Mathematics after checking target-course requirements and your willingness to practise quantitative work; do not rely on assumptions based solely on a course title.
Compare the latest official eligibility, subject, age, registration and fee rules before applying. Such rules and dates can change between examination cycles.
Keep a realistic workload: combining board preparation with CA, CS, CMA or other entrance preparation requires a study plan that protects Class XII performance.

sections.heading: Routes after Class XII
paragraphs: Undergraduate study is the broadest route. B.Com, BBA and BCA are common next steps, but their admission criteria are institution-specific. CUET-UG is used for undergraduate admissions by central and participating universities; its 2026 bulletin states that candidates may choose up to five subjects and must align choices with the eligibility conditions of the intended university programme.

The accounting and corporate-profession routes can be started alongside or after school. ICAI allows provisional CA Foundation registration after Class X, with eligibility to sit after appearing in Class XII and completing the required study period. ICSI’s restructured CSEET, effective from the June 2026 session, accepts Indian nationals who have passed or are appearing in Senior Secondary (10+2). ICMAI allows Foundation-course admission after Class X, while a 10+2 pass is required before appearing in the CMA Foundation examination.

Commerce can also lead to law, actuarial science and hospitality. For CLAT 2026 undergraduate eligibility, candidates needed a 10+2 qualification with the stated minimum marks, with appearing candidates eligible subject to later proof of passing. ACET is available to candidates who have appeared in or passed 10+2, and the Institute of Actuaries of India identifies numeracy and mathematics interest as relevant preparation. For NCHMCT’s B.Sc. Hospitality and Hotel Administration, the published minimum qualification is 10+2 with English as a subject; admissions use NCHM JEE and centralised counselling.
bullets: B.Com/BBA/BCA and related undergraduate programmes: verify the institution’s Class XII subjects, entrance-test combination, marks and admission process before applying.
CA Foundation: suitable for a structured chartered-accountancy pathway; review ICAI’s current examination calendar, registration cut-offs and syllabus.
CSEET and CS Executive: suitable for corporate-law, governance and compliance interests; the revised CSEET framework applies from the June 2026 session.
CMA Foundation: suitable for cost and management-accounting interests; confirm current ICMAI admission and examination rules.
CLAT: a route toward five-year integrated law programmes at participating National Law Universities and other institutions using CLAT scores; eligibility and participating institutions vary by cycle.
ACET: an actuarial entry route for students drawn to probability, statistics, finance and quantitative modelling.
NCHM JEE: a hospitality-management route requiring 10+2 with English for the NCHMCT B.Sc. HHA programme.

useful_links.label: Institute of Actuaries of India: ACET
NCHMCT B.Sc. Hospitality and Hotel Administration admission

title: Science Stream — PCB (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
description: Senior-secondary science stream with Physics, Chemistry and Biology; the standard route toward medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, nursing and life sciences.

quick_facts.label: CBSE subject structure
quick_facts.value: In CBSE’s 2025–26 Senior Secondary curriculum, Physics (042), Chemistry (043), and Biology (044) are separate Academic Electives; each is assessed as 70 marks theory plus 30 marks practical. “PCB” commonly denotes taking these three subjects together, alongside the board’s required language and other selected subjects.

quick_facts.label: Medical-entry foundation
quick_facts.value: For NEET-UG eligibility under the Graduate Medical Education Regulations, 2023, candidates need 10+2/equivalent with Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English. Thus PCB aligns directly with the core school-subject requirement for undergraduate medical admissions, subject to the applicable year’s examination bulletin and admission rules.

quick_facts.label: Nursing and pharmacy fit
quick_facts.value: PCB is directly accepted for B.Sc. Nursing and pharmacy pathways: the Indian Nursing Council specifies 10+2 Science (PCB) and English for B.Sc. Nursing, while Pharmacy Council of India rules permit 10+2 science with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics or Biology for B.Pharm.

quick_facts.label: Agriculture and science-research options
quick_facts.value: PCB can support agriculture/allied-science applications through CUET (ICAR-UG): the 2026 bulletin permits candidates with at least three core subjects among Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture. It can also support IISER applications through IAT; the 2026 brochure accepts eligible Class XII/equivalent candidates, while particular programmes may impose additional Mathematics requirements.

sections.heading: What the PCB stream studies
paragraphs: PCB is a senior-secondary subject combination centred on Physics, Chemistry and Biology. In the CBSE 2025–26 framework, these are distinct Academic Electives—Physics 042, Chemistry 043 and Biology 044—and each includes substantial practical assessment (30 of 100 marks). A student’s complete Class XI–XII package also normally includes a language and may include other electives or skill subjects according to the board and school’s scheme of studies.

Biology is especially relevant to students considering health, life-science, environmental, agricultural or biotechnology-oriented study: CBSE describes its Biology curriculum as connecting biological concepts with health, environment, industry and agriculture, while developing observation, experimentation, documentation and quantitative reasoning. Physics and Chemistry remain important rather than merely supporting subjects: they are part of the prescribed combination for medical eligibility and are foundational in pharmacy and many science degrees.
bullets: Physics: mechanics, electricity, optics, modern physics and laboratory/investigatory work, subject to the applicable board syllabus.
Chemistry: physical, organic and inorganic chemistry, with practical laboratory work under the applicable board syllabus.
Biology: plant and animal biology, human biology, genetics/evolution, ecology and practical/investigatory work under the applicable board syllabus.

The exact compulsory, optional and assessment arrangements vary across boards, schools and academic years; students should check their own board’s current curriculum and school subject-offering list before finalising selections.

sections.heading: How to decide whether PCB is the right combination
paragraphs: Choose PCB when sustained interest in biology and laboratory-based science is paired with readiness to continue studying Physics and Chemistry seriously. It is a particularly direct fit for undergraduate medicine, dentistry, nursing, pharmacy, physiotherapy, life sciences and many agriculture/allied-science programmes, but it is not a single universal eligibility credential: each course, institution and entrance examination sets its own subject, marks, age, category and counselling conditions.

The most consequential decision is whether to retain Mathematics as an additional subject where the school permits it. PCB alone supports many health and life-science routes, but some programmes or branches elsewhere require Mathematics. For example, the 2026 IISER admission brochure identifies programmes with a Class XII Mathematics requirement, and the ICAR 2026 bulletin requires applicants to take examination subjects consistent with those studied at Class XII. Take this decision based on plausible degree targets, workload capacity and the current prospectuses of intended institutions—not on a generic assumption that all science programmes accept the same combination.

Do not treat entry tests, eligibility and counselling as interchangeable. NEET-UG is the relevant national examination route for undergraduate medical admissions, whereas the Medical Counselling Committee administers All India counselling processes for participating MBBS, BDS and B.Sc. Nursing seats. Nursing, pharmacy, agricultural and research-science routes can use different regulators, admission authorities and examinations. Rules and dates should be checked again in the admission year.
bullets: For MBBS/BDS: verify the applicable NEET-UG information bulletin, NMC eligibility rules and counselling authority requirements.
For B.Sc. Nursing: verify the Indian Nursing Council baseline criteria and the individual university/state entrance or counselling rules.

For B.Pharm/D.Pharm: verify that the programme and institution are approved as applicable under Pharmacy Council of India requirements; PCB is accepted, although Pharmacy rules also allow Mathematics as the alternative third science subject.
For B.Sc., agriculture and research programmes: read each university’s programme-specific eligibility and required test-subject combination before applying.
Do not rely on historical cut-offs, fees, seat counts or deadlines; these are admission-cycle-specific and can change.

sections.heading: Routes available after Class XII PCB
paragraphs: PCB provides a strong route into regulated health programmes. The National Medical Commission’s 2023 regulations identify Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English at 10+2/equivalent as the school-subject basis for appearing in NEET-UG. MCC’s undergraduate counselling system covers participating MBBS, BDS and B.Sc. Nursing seats; students must separately meet the applicable examination, rank, eligibility, documentation and counselling requirements.

It also supports professional and scientific alternatives beyond medicine. The Indian Nursing Council’s stated B.Sc. Nursing baseline is 10+2 Science (PCB) with English and a 45% aggregate requirement; the Pharmacy Council of India permits B.Pharm entry with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics or Biology. These are regulatory baselines, not a guarantee of admission at an individual college.

For agriculture and allied sciences, the ICAR 2026 CUET (ICAR-UG) bulletin allows Class XII candidates who studied at least three core subjects among Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture/Inter-Agriculture, with programme- and university-specific conditions still applying. For basic-science and interdisciplinary research pathways, IAT is the IISER admission route; its 2026 brochure makes Class XII/equivalent qualification central, but identifies additional subject conditions for certain programmes. Conventional B.Sc. admissions likewise depend on the individual university’s published eligibility and selection method.
bullets: MBBS and BDS: NEET-UG qualification followed by the relevant counselling process; confirm the current-year bulletin and seat/counselling rules.
B.Sc. Nursing: PCB-and-English foundation; admissions may involve NEET or institution/state-specific processes depending on the programme and year.
B.Pharm and D.Pharm: PCB is acceptable under PCI rules; confirm programme approval and the institution’s current admissions procedure.
BPT and paramedical programmes: often PCB-aligned, but verify the individual university, state authority and profession-specific admission rules.
B.Sc. life sciences, biotechnology, microbiology, zoology, botany, biochemistry and related fields: university-specific admissions, potentially through CUET-UG or another institutional process.
Agriculture and allied sciences: CUET (ICAR-UG) can be relevant where the applicant’s Class XII subjects and the target university’s programme conditions match.
IISER/basic-science pathways: IAT-based admission; check programme-level subject requirements, particularly where Mathematics is stipulated.

useful_links.label: NMC clarification citing Graduate Medical Education Regulations, 2023 NEET-UG subject eligibility
Medical Counselling Committee — UG Medical Counselling
Pharmacy Council of India — B.Pharm regulations and syllabus

title: Science Stream — PCM (Physics, Chemistry, Maths)
description: Senior-secondary science stream with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics; the standard route toward engineering, architecture, defence and quantitative fields.

quick_facts.label: What PCM means
quick_facts.value: PCM is the Class XI–XII subject combination of Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics. In CBSE’s 2026–27 senior-secondary curriculum, all three are listed as separate academic electives; students also take a language and may have other school/board-prescribed subjects and internal-assessment components.

quick_facts.label: Engineering and IIT route
quick_facts.value: PCM is directly relevant to engineering admissions: for JEE (Advanced) 2026, candidates must have appeared in Class XII with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics as compulsory subjects; JEE (Main) is the qualifying route for Indian candidates seeking JEE (Advanced), subject to the published criteria.

quick_facts.label: Architecture route
quick_facts.value: For first-year B.Arch admission under the Council of Architecture’s stated 2026 criteria, Physics and Mathematics are compulsory at 10+2, alongside one permitted third subject that includes Chemistry. NATA is an aptitude-test qualifier, not by itself a guarantee of admission.

quick_facts.label: Not an exclusive route to every field
quick_facts.value: PCM keeps mathematics-dependent options open, but it is not required for every listed entrance route: CLAT UG accepts qualifying 10+2 candidates meeting its marks requirement, while UCEED permits candidates from all streams for the examination, although participating B.Des institutes can set programme-specific subject conditions.

sections.heading: What students study in the PCM stream
paragraphs: Science—PCM is normally undertaken in Classes XI and XII after Class 10. It centres on Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, but the exact subject package, language requirement, additional elective, practical work and assessment scheme depend on the board and school. For example, CBSE’s 2026–27 senior-secondary curriculum places Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics among academic electives and separately lists languages and internal-assessment subjects.

The academic profile is strongly quantitative and includes conceptual study, problem-solving and experimental work. In CBSE’s Class XI Physics curriculum, the syllabus begins with measurement and moves through mechanics, gravitation, properties of matter, thermodynamics, kinetic theory, oscillations and waves; CBSE describes the subject as developing experimental, observational, investigatory, decision-making and problem-solving skills. The corresponding Mathematics curriculum includes sets and functions, algebra, coordinate geometry, calculus, statistics and probability.
bullets: Confirm whether the school offers Mathematics (rather than only Applied Mathematics), Physics and Chemistry together, and obtain its exact Class XI subject-combination rules before enrolment.
Treat laboratory attendance, practical records and board-specific assessment requirements as part of the stream, not as optional extras.
Check the current syllabus issued by the student’s own board; the CBSE examples describe CBSE, not a universal national syllabus.

sections.heading: How to decide whether PCM is a good fit
paragraphs: PCM is an especially practical choice when a student wants to preserve eligibility for programmes that expressly require Mathematics with Physics and Chemistry. For the 2026 cycle, JEE (Advanced) requires Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics as compulsory Class XII subjects; BITS Pilani’s B.E. and M.Sc. eligibility requires Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics among five Class XII subjects; and VIT’s published PCM route is eligible for all of its B.Tech programmes. These are programme-specific rules, not a universal guarantee of admission.

Architecture is another reason to retain Mathematics. The Council of Architecture’s 2026 B.Arch criteria require Physics and Mathematics at 10+2 plus an approved third subject, and specify that qualifying NATA alone does not create a right to admission. Conversely, students should not select PCM solely because it is perceived as the only route to higher education: CLAT and UCEED illustrate routes whose examination eligibility is not universally PCM-only.

A sound choice therefore combines genuine readiness for sustained mathematics and science study with a shortlist of intended courses and entrance routes. Before finalising subjects, compare the currently published eligibility rules for each target institution or examination, since requirements, thresholds, attempts, age rules, reservations and counselling procedures can change by admission cycle.
bullets: Choose PCM if you are willing to practise mathematical problem-solving regularly and to complete theory and practical work in Physics and Chemistry.

If engineering is a target, map Class XII subjects early against JEE (Main), JEE (Advanced), BITSAT, state examinations and target-university rules rather than assuming that one examination covers every college.
If B.Arch is a target, retain Mathematics and review the Council of Architecture rules plus the relevant state/institution admission process.
Keep a separate list of deadlines and eligibility rules for each exam; do not infer eligibility from the name of a stream alone.

sections.heading: Routes available after Class XII PCM
paragraphs: Engineering and quantitative undergraduate routes are the most direct continuation. JEE (Main) has B.E./B.Tech and B.Arch/B.Planning papers; candidates meeting the relevant JEE (Main) criteria may progress to JEE (Advanced), whose 2026 Indian-national eligibility requires a top-2,50,000 position in the JEE (Main) B.E./B.Tech paper and Class XII PCM. Other major routes include BITSAT for BITS first-degree programmes, VITEEE for VIT B.Tech admissions, and WBJEE for undergraduate engineering, technology, pharmacy and architecture admissions in West Bengal. Eligibility, marks thresholds, examination patterns and counselling rules are cycle-specific.

For B.Arch, students can use NATA or the JEE route where accepted by the competent admission authority, while also satisfying the Council of Architecture’s Class XII subject and marks requirements. PCM is also relevant to some defence technical opportunities: the Indian Navy’s published Agniveer SSR eligibility requires 10+2 Mathematics and Physics, subject to its stated marks, fitness and recruitment conditions.

PCM does not prevent movement to broader options. B.Sc and BCA admission requirements are set by the admitting university or college; CUET-UG and institution-level admission criteria should be checked course by course. It can also coexist with applications to law, design and overseas admissions, but these routes have independent entrance, subject, score and institutional requirements rather than a single PCM-based rule.
bullets: B.Tech / engineering: JEE Main, JEE Advanced, BITSAT, VITEEE, WBJEE and institution-specific admissions.
B.Arch / architecture: NATA or the applicable JEE route, followed by the competent authority’s admission process.
B.Sc and BCA: verify the target university’s current programme-level subject eligibility and its accepted admission route, including CUET-UG where applicable.

Defence: review the live recruitment notice for the particular service and entry; PCM may meet academic requirements for some technical entries, but does not replace physical, medical, age or other selection criteria.
Law, design and overseas routes: PCM students may apply where their individual qualifying and test rules are met; CLAT and UCEED eligibility demonstrate that these are not inherently PCM-exclusive.

title: Science Stream — PCMB (Physics, Chemistry, Maths, Biology)
description: Senior-secondary science stream keeping both Mathematics and Biology, preserving eligibility for both engineering and medical entrance exams.

quick_facts.label: What PCMB means
quick_facts.value: PCMB is the senior-secondary science combination that includes Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics and Biology. In the CBSE 2026–27 senior-secondary curriculum, these are listed as separate academic electives (Mathematics 041, Physics 042, Chemistry 043 and Biology 044); the exact subject package and availability are determined by the student’s board and school.

quick_facts.label: Why students choose it
quick_facts.value: Keeping Mathematics and Biology preserves the Class XII subject base used by major engineering and medical routes: IIT admission through JEE (Advanced) requires Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, while NEET’s qualifying-examination codes require Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English, including practical work in the science subjects.

quick_facts.label: Medical entrance fit
quick_facts.value: For NEET-UG 2026, the test itself covers Physics, Chemistry, and Biology (Botany and Zoology). PCMB includes all of those academic areas, but students must also check the applicable English and practical-work requirements in the current NEET information bulletin.

quick_facts.label: Engineering entrance fit
quick_facts.value: For admission to IITs in the 2026 cycle, JEE (Advanced) specifies Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics as compulsory Class XII subjects. Biology is not a substitute for Mathematics for this route, so retaining Mathematics is the key PCMB advantage for engineering options.

quick_facts.label: Agriculture and science routes
quick_facts.value: PCMB also aligns well with interdisciplinary science and agriculture options. CUET (ICAR-UG) 2026 accepts applicants with at least three core subjects from Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture/Inter-Agriculture, subject to programme- and university-specific conditions.

sections.heading: Subjects and academic structure
paragraphs: PCMB combines four full senior-secondary science disciplines: Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics and Biology. It is a subject combination rather than a single nationally uniform course label. For example, CBSE’s 2026–27 Senior Secondary Curriculum lists Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics and Physics individually under academic electives, alongside language and other possible subjects. A student should therefore confirm the school’s actual Class XI–XII scheme of studies, timetable, laboratory access and whether it permits all four subjects together before selecting it.

Physics, Chemistry and Biology involve practical and laboratory-oriented learning in addition to theory. Mathematics adds a separate, substantial problem-solving syllabus. The combined package is consequently broad: it is well suited to students who genuinely wish to retain both quantitative/engineering and life-science/health possibilities, but it requires consistent time allocation across four major subjects rather than early specialization in only PCM or PCB.
bullets: Confirm the board, school and subject codes shown on the eventual Class XII marksheet.
Keep an appropriate language subject: it is relevant to board requirements and is explicitly referenced in NEET qualifying-examination codes and in JEE (Advanced) Class XII aggregate calculations.
Check that the school can support practical instruction and assessment for Physics, Chemistry and Biology.

sections.heading: When PCMB is a good choice
paragraphs: Choose PCMB when keeping both medical/biological and mathematics-dependent pathways open is a real priority—not merely because it seems broadly prestigious. Its clearest structural benefit is eligibility resilience: the 2026 JEE (Advanced) rules require Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics for IIT admission, while the NEET-UG qualifying codes require Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English and include practical tests in the science subjects. PCMB supplies the two distinct subject sets, subject to all other exam, age, marks, category, university and counselling rules.

The trade-off is academic load. NEET-UG 2026 tests Physics, Chemistry and Biology, with Biology accounting for 90 of 180 questions; engineering entrances emphasize Mathematics alongside Physics and Chemistry. Students aiming for both types of examination should plan deliberately for the different question styles and syllabi, protect board-exam performance, and periodically decide whether dual preparation remains sustainable. Entrance rules change by cycle, so the current official bulletin—not a coaching claim or an older eligibility summary—should be checked before applications are made.

Before enrolling, compare the school’s teaching quality and lab facilities with the student’s interests, strengths and intended routes. PCMB is not required for every science, law, architecture, diploma or general university option; taking the extra subject is most valuable where the retained flexibility is likely to be used.
bullets: Use Mathematics if engineering, quantitative science, architecture-related routes or mathematics-required university programmes remain possible.
Use Biology if NEET-linked health professions, biological sciences, agriculture, biotechnology or life-science programmes remain possible.
Do not assume that taking an entrance test guarantees admission: programme and institution eligibility can impose additional conditions.

For CUET-UG, select test subjects based on the specific university and programme requirements; NTA’s university guidance says applicants must verify the required language, domain subjects and/or General Test with the respective university.

sections.heading: Routes kept open after Class XII
paragraphs: Engineering and technology: PCMB retains the Mathematics requirement that is central to JEE-based engineering routes. For IIT admission in the 2026 cycle, JEE (Advanced) requires Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics as compulsory Class XII subjects and applies additional conditions, including Class XII performance criteria and examination eligibility rules. JEE Main, NATA, institute-specific admissions and diploma options have their own current rules, so students should verify each target route separately.

Medicine and allied health: PCMB retains Biology alongside Physics and Chemistry for NEET-linked routes. The NEET-UG 2026 bulletin describes its use for MBBS, BDS, BAMS, BUMS, BSMS and BHMS admissions under the relevant regulatory framework; the exact course, seat, counselling authority and eligibility criteria vary. A PCMB marksheet does not remove the need to meet NEET’s current qualifying-examination, age, score and counselling conditions.

Basic science, agriculture and multidisciplinary degrees: PCMB supports applications where either Mathematics or Biology may be required or advantageous. IISER Admissions 2026 describes IISERs as institutions established to integrate and promote interdisciplinary science education and research. CUET (ICAR-UG) 2026 accepts at least three core subjects from Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture/Inter-Agriculture for listed agriculture and allied programmes, while also warning that individual admitting universities may impose special conditions. CUET-UG 2026 offers separate Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics and Physics domain subjects, but the required test-subject combination is programme-specific.

Other immediate routes remain possible but are not dependent on the PCMB label alone: CUET-UG can lead to many university programmes; CLAT and some law programmes primarily require meeting their own admission rules; Polytechnic diplomas, NDA/NA and architecture routes each publish distinct subject and examination requirements. Check the relevant official notification for the intended admission year before treating any route as available.
bullets: JEE Main / JEE Advanced: engineering and technology pathways; Mathematics is essential for many target programmes.
NEET-UG: undergraduate medical, dental and specified AYUSH routes; Biology/Biotechnology is essential under the qualifying-examination rules.
IISER Aptitude Test: science and research-oriented undergraduate programmes; review that cycle’s IISER eligibility and programme details.
ICAR route: agriculture, fisheries, horticulture, forestry, food, dairy, agricultural engineering and related programmes, subject to the participating university’s rules.
CUET-UG: broad university route; select domains and language/aptitude components only after checking the chosen university’s programme page.

title: BARC Orientation Course for Engineering Graduates and Science Postgraduates
description: A one-year BARC Orientation Course for selected OCES candidates that prepares them for Scientific Officer appointments in the Department of Atomic Energy.

quick_facts.label: Provider and purpose
quick_facts.value: BARC Training Schools run OCES as a Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) recruitment-and-training route for Scientific Officer appointments following successful completion.

quick_facts.label: Duration and 2026 locations
quick_facts.value: OCES is a one-year programme. The OCES-2026 brochure states that the 2026–27 course is to be conducted at BARC Training Schools in Mumbai or Hyderabad; its tentative commencement date was July 31, 2026.

quick_facts.label: Training financial support (2026 intake)
quick_facts.value: For OCES-2026, Trainee Scientific Officers are stated to receive a stipend of ₹74,000 per month during the one-year training period plus a one-time ₹30,000 book allowance. These amounts are intake-specific and may change in later notices.

quick_facts.label: Completion outcome
quick_facts.value: For OCES-2026, a Trainee Scientific Officer must score at least 35% in each subject and 50% overall to pass; successful trainees are posted as Scientific Officer “C” in a DAE unit, with DAE retaining placement discretion including possible placement in AERB.

sections.heading: Who can apply
paragraphs: Eligibility is discipline-specific. For the 2026 cycle, engineering applicants needed an eligible B.E., B.Tech., B.Sc. (Engineering), or five-year integrated M.Tech. in one of the notified disciplines—mechanical, chemical, metallurgical, electrical, electronics, computer science, instrumentation, or civil engineering—with at least 60% aggregate marks or 6.0/10 CGPA (or equivalent). Science routes covered specified postgraduate qualifications in physics, chemistry, biosciences, geology, and geophysics, with subject prerequisites that differ by discipline.

All qualifying and pre-qualifying degrees must be regular, full-time, on-campus qualifications; correspondence, distance, research-mode, and part-time degrees are not eligible under the 2026 brochure. Applicants must be Indian citizens. For that intake, the minimum age was 18 as of August 1, 2026; maximum ages and relaxations varied by category, so applicants should use the next official brochure rather than rely on the 2026 limits.

GATE was an optional screening channel rather than the only route: eligible candidates could use the BARC online examination, a valid applicable GATE score, or both, subject to the rules for their chosen discipline.
bullets: Check the notified eligible degree title—not merely a related field—against the applicable discipline table.
For a GATE-based screening application in 2026, accepted scores were GATE 2024, 2025, or 2026 in the prescribed paper.
Government, PSU, and aided-institute employees needed a No Objection Certificate at the selection interview.

sections.heading: Length, format, and location
paragraphs: OCES is structured as one year of full-time training. BARC describes the course work as three trimesters of classroom teaching, practical training, and project work, with continuous evaluation through examinations and assignments.

The 2026–27 brochure identified Mumbai and Hyderabad as the OCES training-school locations for that cycle. Location and discipline allocations are programme-specific, so a future intake may not replicate the same options.
bullets: One-year orientation course.
Three trimesters in BARC’s general course description.
For OCES-2026, the brochure listed tentative commencement on July 31, 2026.

sections.heading: What trainees study and do
paragraphs: The programme is intended to develop R&D knowledge and skills in nuclear science and technology. BARC’s general OCES description includes foundation, core, advanced, and elective courses, mini-projects, practical training, and project work.

Training is discipline-oriented. For example, the 2026 Mumbai options covered engineering design, development, operation, and maintenance of nuclear reactors, plus research in frontier basic and engineering sciences; the Hyderabad geology option focused on uranium and other atomic-mineral exploration techniques and related R&D. The precise scheme depends on the screening discipline and training-school allocation.
bullets: Foundation, core, advanced, and elective coursework.
Practical work, mini-projects, and project work.
Continuous assessment through examinations and assignments.

sections.heading: Selection and application process
paragraphs: OCES selection is a two-stage process: screening followed by a selection interview. In the 2026 cycle, screening could be through BARC’s computer-based online examination and/or an applicable GATE score; final selection was based on the selection interview, subject to medical fitness.

Applications are online through the BARC OCES/DGFS portal, and an applicant may choose only one OCES screening discipline. The 2026 schedule listed a January 21, 2026 application deadline, online tests on March 14–15, 2026, interviews from May 12 to June 12, 2026, and final OCES selections in late June. Those dates are past as of July 19, 2026 and were explicitly tentative; prospective applicants should monitor the official portal for the next intake rather than infer a recurring deadline.
bullets: Choose at least one screening option: BARC online examination, eligible GATE score, or both where permitted.
Shortlisted candidates attend selection interviews; for the 2026 cycle, most disciplines were interviewed in Mumbai, while geology and geophysics interviews were in Hyderabad.
A pre-employment medical test is required before joining.

sections.heading: Application cost, stipend, and service commitment
paragraphs: OCES is a paid training programme rather than a conventional fee-paying course. For OCES-2026, BARC specified a ₹74,000 monthly stipend and a one-time ₹30,000 book allowance. Boarding and lodging in a DAE hostel were mandatory during the OCES training period. The brochure does not present these as permanent terms, so applicants should verify financial provisions in the notice for their own intake.

For the 2026 recruitment cycle, the non-refundable application fee was ₹500 plus applicable bank charges for specified male General, OBC (non-creamy layer), Dependent-1984, and Kashmir-domicile applicants. Women, transgender applicants, SC/ST applicants, eligible dependents of defence personnel killed in action, and persons with benchmark disability as specified in the brochure were exempt. Fee rules can change by cycle.

Selected OCES-2026 candidates were required to sign an agreement and personal indemnity bond to serve DAE for at least three years after training. The bond amount consisted of stipend and the one-time book allowance actually paid; no third-party surety was required.
bullets: 2026 monthly stipend: ₹74,000.
2026 one-time book allowance: ₹30,000.
2026 application fee where applicable: ₹500 plus bank charges.
Service commitment for OCES-2026: at least three years after training.

sections.heading: After OCES
paragraphs: A trainee who meets the 2026 passing standard is appointed as a Scientific Officer “C.” Allocation to a DAE unit is based on DAE programme needs and the trainee’s OCES performance; DAE may also place candidates in AERB or its regional offices. The 2026 brochure listed potential DAE destinations including BARC, IGCAR, RRCAT, VECC, HWB, NFC, BRIT, NPCIL, BHAVINI, UCIL, AMD, and DCSEM, with postings potentially at facilities elsewhere in India.

For OCES-2026, engineering trainees who completed the training and met a minimum performance criterion could enrol for an HBNI M.Tech.; other trainees could enrol for an HBNI Post-Graduate Diploma if their academic performance exceeded the specified threshold. BARC also describes OCES course work as recognized for HBNI postgraduate diploma and as course work toward certain HBNI higher degrees.

The 2026 brochure stated that appointment as Scientific Officer “C” is at Level 10, ₹56,100 in the Seventh Central Pay Commission pay matrix, with two or three performance-linked increments for OCES trainees. This is a dated 2026 pay context, not a guarantee of future compensation.
bullets: Scientific Officer “C” appointment after successful completion.
DAE determines unit and location according to organisational needs and trainee performance.
Potential HBNI M.Tech. or Post-Graduate Diploma pathway, subject to the stated performance conditions.

title: CA Articleship Practical Training
description: Mandatory supervised practical training under a practising Chartered Accountant or eligible organisation for CA students who have passed CA Intermediate.

quick_facts.label: Entry point under the current ICAI scheme
quick_facts.value: A student may commence practical training only after passing both groups of CA Intermediate and successfully completing the four-week Integrated Course on Information Technology and Soft Skills (ICITSS).

quick_facts.label: Standard duration
quick_facts.value: Practical training under ICAI’s New Scheme of Education and Training is two years. Students who had already commenced a three-year articleship under the old scheme continue under that prior arrangement.

quick_facts.label: Leave entitlement
quick_facts.value: Under the New Scheme, an articled assistant is entitled to 12 days of leave in each year of practical training; leave beyond that entitlement is excess leave to be served.

quick_facts.label: Digital training record
quick_facts.value: For students commencing practical training on or after January 1, 2026, ICAI requires use of the E-Diary to record attendance and work performed, with periodic review by the principal.

quick_facts.label: Industrial-training alternative
quick_facts.value: During the second year/last part of the two-year practical-training period, an eligible articled assistant may undertake industrial training for 9–12 months through an ICAI-approved arrangement. ICAI’s January 2026 announcement states that eligibility requires at least 12 months of practical training and Intermediate passed.

sections.heading: Who can begin CA articleship?
paragraphs: For students following ICAI’s New Scheme of Education and Training, passing CA Intermediate alone is not sufficient: the student must have passed both Intermediate groups and completed the four-week ICITSS before commencing practical training. ICITSS combines the Orientation Course and Information Technology Training.

This makes articleship the supervised work-based stage after Intermediate rather than a route that can ordinarily begin alongside Intermediate study. Students should confirm their course-scheme status in ICAI’s Self Service Portal (SSP), because candidates who began under earlier schemes can remain subject to transition arrangements.
bullets: The prerequisite is both groups of CA Intermediate passed.
ICITSS must be completed before the training start date.
Students who commenced three-year training under the old scheme continue that three-year commitment rather than automatically moving to two years.

sections.heading: Length, leave, and working-time framework
paragraphs: The New Scheme prescribes two years of practical training. ICAI’s articleship guidance allows 12 days of leave in each training year; excess leave must be made good, so it can extend the effective completion date.

ICAI’s working-hours directions specify 35 hours a week excluding lunch. Work beyond normal hours is intended only for exceptional circumstances, and aggregate hours may not exceed 45 in a week; compensatory leave applies where weekly hours exceed 35. These directions also restrict attendance at college or another institution during training work hours.
bullets: New Scheme duration: 2 years.
Leave: 12 days in each year; excess leave must be served.
Normal training workload: 35 hours per week excluding lunch; the exceptional maximum is 45 hours per week.
The normal office hours for articled assistants are not to begin after 11:00 a.m. or end before 5:00 p.m.

sections.heading: What practical training covers
paragraphs: Articleship is supervised on-the-job professional training rather than a standalone classroom syllabus. ICAI’s E-Diary framework requires trainees beginning from January 1, 2026 to digitally record attendance and tasks, while principals review the entries. ICAI describes the system as a mechanism for skill mapping, training-quality consistency, and monitoring.

The work exposure is shaped by the principal or approved training setting. ICAI specifically identifies auditing, taxation, and consultancy among the areas whose hours and tasks can be tracked through the E-Diary. A student should therefore assess a prospective principal or organisation for the breadth of assignments and supervision offered, rather than assuming every articleship provides identical exposure.
bullets: Record daily attendance and work performed in the E-Diary if commencing on or after January 1, 2026.
Submit task records fortnightly for principal review and approval.
Expect work-based exposure that may include audit, tax, and consultancy, depending on the training placement.

sections.heading: How articleship is registered
paragraphs: In practice, the student first secures a training placement with a principal and executes the articleship deed. ICAI’s articleship-forms FAQ states that the deed must be executed on stamp paper dated within 30 days of commencement; failure to execute Form 102 on stamp paper makes the articles training invalid.

Registration is handled through the SSP workflow. ICAI says physical copies of Forms 102, 103, or 104 need not be posted to the regional office; after member approval, the student submits the form through SSP for regional-office approval. Delayed filing is possible with a condonation request, prescribed fee, and supporting records such as attendance, work diary, and bank evidence of stipend payment.
bullets: Execute the deed, including Form 102, on appropriate stamp paper within 30 days of starting.
Submit the applicable registration form through ICAI SSP after member approval; do not rely on postal submission alone.
Keep copies and evidence of the deed, attendance, work diary, and monthly stipend credits.
If pursuing another course or occupation alongside articleship, obtain ICAI permission through Form 112 as applicable.

sections.heading: Stipend and filing-cost context
paragraphs: Articleship is paid training, but the applicable stipend rules should be checked at the time of joining. ICAI’s New Scheme FAQ, last updated September 27, 2024, described proposed two-year-scheme monthly minimums of ₹5,000/₹6,000 in cities or towns with population of 20 lakh or more, ₹4,000/₹5,000 for locations from 5 lakh to below 20 lakh, and ₹3,000/₹4,000 for locations below 5 lakh, for the first and second year respectively. Crucially, ICAI labelled these figures as recommendations subject to amendment of Regulation 48, so they should not be treated as confirmed current 2026 rates without checking the then-current regulation or SSP guidance.

For industrial training, ICAI’s January 2026 announcement states a minimum monthly stipend of ₹15,000, with the amount otherwise mutually agreed between the industrial trainee and the member imparting training. Administrative charges can also arise if registration forms are late: ICAI’s articleship FAQ lists dated condonation-fee bands from ₹500 to ₹10,000 depending on delay length. These amounts and procedures can change, so applicants should verify them before submission.
bullets: Do not assume a proposed or historical stipend table is the current statutory minimum.
Industrial-training stipend: ICAI stated a minimum of ₹15,000 per month in its January 12, 2026 announcement.
Late registration can trigger variable condonation fees; submit forms promptly through SSP.

sections.heading: Options after and during practical training
paragraphs: The principal next pathway is CA Final. Under ICAI’s New Scheme FAQ, a student may appear for the Final Examination after registering for Final, completing practical training six months before the first day of the examination month, completing Advanced ICITSS, and qualifying all four applicable Self-Paced Online Modules.

An alternative within the training period is industrial training. ICAI’s current January 2026 announcement permits an articled assistant who has completed at least 12 months of practical training to undertake 9–12 months of industrial training, subject to the required notice to the principal and an approved training arrangement. ICAI treats completed industrial training as service under articles when the prescribed completion certificate is furnished.
bullets: Progress to CA Final after satisfying Final registration, practical-training, Advanced ICITSS, and self-paced-module requirements.
Consider 9–12 months of industrial training after at least 12 months of practical training, if an approved placement is available.
Complete and submit the relevant training-completion documentation through ICAI’s processes.

title: Craft Instructor Training Scheme (CITS)
description: A one-year program to train ITI graduates as certified instructors for ITIs and other vocational training centers.

quick_facts.label: Administering authority
quick_facts.value: CITS is conducted under the Directorate General of Training (DGT), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India.

quick_facts.label: Purpose
quick_facts.value: The scheme prepares instructor trainees to transfer hands-on skills and train semi-skilled and skilled manpower for industry.

quick_facts.label: Duration
quick_facts.value: The DGT course catalogue lists CITS as a one-year, two-semester programme; the assessment pattern is annual.

quick_facts.label: Entry routes
quick_facts.value: The principal entry routes are relevant NTC, NAC, diploma, or degree qualifications, but the precise eligible qualification is trade-specific in DGT’s course catalogue.

quick_facts.label: Credential
quick_facts.value: The 2025–26 DGT prospectus states that successful CITS completers receive the National Craft Instructor Certificate (NCIC), recognized by NCVET.

quick_facts.label: 2026–27 admission route and timing
quick_facts.value: DGT’s 2026–27 notice specifies admission through the computer-based All India Common Entrance Test (AICET). Its published schedule marked registration as 18 April–10 May 2026 and the AICET as 31 May 2026; these dates have passed as of 18 July 2026. The schedule labels later counselling and session milestones as tentative.

sections.heading: Who can pursue CITS?
paragraphs: CITS is designed for people who already have trade or technical preparation and want to become vocational trainers. DGT identifies NTC, NAC, diploma, and degree holders as eligible categories; the current course catalogue makes clear that the exact qualification must match the selected CITS trade.

For example, entry conditions can differ materially between trades: some accept an NTC/NAC in the named or related trade, while others specify relevant engineering degrees or three-year diplomas. Applicants should therefore use the entry-qualification column and syllabus for the particular trade rather than relying only on the broad eligibility summary.
bullets: Check that the prior ITI/NTC, apprenticeship/NAC, diploma, degree, or other route is explicitly accepted for the chosen trade.

The 2025–26 official prospectus also stated that SCVT candidates were eligible, CoE candidates were not eligible, and appearing NTC/NAC/diploma/degree candidates could receive provisional admission subject to the applicable order; applicants should verify whether those provisions are retained in the current admission material.
The 2025–26 prospectus specified a minimum age of 16 on the first day of the academic session and no upper age limit, except where a syllabus specifies otherwise.

sections.heading: Programme length and delivery
paragraphs: CITS is a one-year, two-semester programme in DGT’s course catalogue. The 2025–26 DGT prospectus describes an annual examination system and gives a programme workload of 1,200 hours, plus mandatory 150 hours of on-the-job training (OJT) or group project and an optional 240-hour component.

Training is delivered through National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs) and DGT-affiliated Institutes for Training of Trainers (IToTs). Institute availability and the set of trades offered should be checked against DGT’s current institute and course lists before applying.
bullets: Course length: one year (two semesters).
Assessment framework: annual examination.
Practical exposure: the 2025–26 prospectus specifies mandatory OJT/group project work.

sections.heading: What is studied
paragraphs: CITS combines trade expertise with the ability to teach that trade. DGT describes comprehensive preparation in skills and training methodology, while NSTI programme descriptions identify Trade Technology, Engineering Technology, and Training Methodology as core components.

The trade component is not identical for all learners: DGT publishes separate syllabus documents and entry requirements for individual trades. The catalogue includes both engineering and non-engineering offerings, and each listed course is shown as a one-year, two-semester programme with its applicable NSQF level.
bullets: Trade Technology: basic and advanced trade practice and theory.
Engineering Technology: commonly includes workshop calculation/science and engineering drawing, where applicable.
Training Methodology / Principles of Teaching: teaching practice and principles of teaching.
Mandatory OJT or group project is included in the 2025–26 programme structure.

sections.heading: Admission process and 2026–27 position
paragraphs: DGT uses the All India Common Entrance Test (AICET) followed by centralized counselling for CITS admission at NSTIs and IToTs. The 2025–26 prospectus says the online test assesses the relevant CTS trade syllabus (75% of questions) and logical, numerical, and reasoning aptitude (25%).

For 2026–27, DGT’s admission notice set online applications for 18 April through 10 May 2026 and the computer-based AICET for 31 May 2026. DGT’s tentative schedule put third-round choice filling on 15–18 July 2026, with the result scheduled for 20 July, spot/walk-in admissions on 3–5 August, physical admissions on 10–14 August, and session commencement on 17 August 2026. These remaining milestones are explicitly tentative and should be rechecked on the official portal.
bullets: Application and AICET: use the official NIMI online-admission portal when the admission window is open.
Allocation: centralized counselling uses merit and candidates’ preferences; the 2025–26 prospectus stated that direct/walk-in admission outside the AICET merit list was not permitted.
For 2026–27, the application deadline of 10 May 2026 and AICET date of 31 May 2026 are already past as of 18 July 2026.

sections.heading: Fees: dated and institute-dependent
paragraphs: Fees must be treated as year- and institute-specific. The latest detailed DGT prospectus located for 2025–26 listed annual NSTI charges of ₹2,420 for an individual general-category candidate and ₹920 for an individual SC/ST/PH/EWS candidate; the listed total for a government-sponsored candidate was ₹570. These figures should not be assumed to be the 2026–27 fees.

That same 2025–26 prospectus listed the AICET examination fee as ₹500 for general candidates and ₹300 for SC/ST/PH/EWS/women candidates. It also states that state-government and private IToT fee structures are set by their respective bodies, so applicants need to confirm the amount with the allotted institute or its nodal officer.
bullets: 2025–26 NSTI annual-fee context only: ₹2,420 for an individual general-category candidate; ₹920 for an individual SC/ST/PH/EWS candidate.
2025–26 AICET-fee context only: ₹500 general; ₹300 SC/ST/PH/EWS/women.
Private and state IToT fees can differ from NSTI fees.

sections.heading: What CITS can lead to
paragraphs: CITS is a trainer-preparation credential rather than an automatic appointment to a government post. According to DGT’s 2025–26 prospectus, successful trainees can work as instructors in ITIs, certified instructors in short- and long-term skill-development schemes, industry training coordinators, and developers of written instructional materials and e-learning content.

Accordingly, the direct next step is typically to seek vocational-instructor or training-coordinator opportunities in government ITIs, private training institutes, industry training departments, or skill-development programmes. Actual eligibility for a particular government ITI or PSU role remains governed by that employer’s recruitment notice, including its trade, experience, reservation, and examination requirements.
bullets: Vocational Instructor — government ITI, subject to the recruiting authority’s rules.
Vocational Instructor — private institute or short-/long-term skill programme.
Industry training coordinator or workplace skills trainer.
Vocational instructional-materials or e-learning-content development.

useful_links.label: DGT CITS course catalogue, syllabi and trade-specific entry qualifications

title: DAE Graduate Fellowship Scheme Fellowship
description: A Department of Atomic Energy fellowship for selected DGFS candidates to pursue sponsored postgraduate study before joining the DAE as a Scientific Officer.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: DGFS-2026 is a two-year DAE-sponsored M.Tech. route for engineering graduates who are selected through the BARC Training Schools process and independently obtain admission in an approved DGFS institute and specialization; fellows retain DAE employment while studying.

quick_facts.label: 2026 study locations
quick_facts.value: For the 2026 cycle, the brochure identifies IIT Bombay and IIT Madras as the DGFS institutes; the permitted M.Tech. specializations are controlled by the annual Table 3 listing.

quick_facts.label: Study funding (2026 cycle)
quick_facts.value: The 2026 brochure states that fellows receive ₹74,000 per month for two years, reimbursement of M.Tech. tuition, and a ₹60,000-per-year contingency grant for two years; it also describes project-equipment funding of up to ₹4,00,000 under the BRNS Fast Track Project scheme, subject to actual payment.

quick_facts.label: Service commitment
quick_facts.value: Selected DGFS-2026 candidates must execute an agreement and personal indemnity bond to serve DAE for at least three years after training. The bond includes the relevant stipend, tuition, contingency, and applicable project funding; no third-party surety is required.

quick_facts.label: Post-fellowship outcome
quick_facts.value: After the M.Tech. and the required four-month Orientation Course for DGFS Fellows (OCDF), successful fellows are appointed as Scientific Officer 'C' in a Group A DAE post. The 2026 placement route is BARC for IIT Bombay fellows and IGCAR for IIT Madras fellows, with BARC placement potentially at facilities elsewhere in India.

sections.heading: Who can be considered for DGFS
paragraphs: DGFS is not a separate open M.Tech. scholarship application. In the 2026 cycle, an applicant first had to meet the OCES/DGFS engineering eligibility rules, be selected for OCES through the BARC Training Schools selection process, and independently secure admission in the same academic year to an approved M.Tech. specialization at a DGFS institute.

The 2026 brochure lists the eligible engineering screening disciplines as mechanical, chemical, metallurgical, electrical, electronics, computer science, instrumentation, and civil engineering. For these routes, the qualifying degree is B.E., B.Tech., B.Sc. (Engineering), or a five-year integrated M.Tech. in the applicable discipline, with at least 60% aggregate marks or a 6.0/10 CGPA (or equivalent). Eligibility, age limits, admissible degree names, and institute-specialization combinations are cycle-specific and should be checked in the next official brochure rather than inferred from 2026 rules.
bullets: For GATE-based screening in 2026, a valid GATE 2024, 2025, or 2026 score in the applicable GATE paper was accepted.
The 2026 recruitment notice was for Indian nationals; its maximum age reference date was August 1, 2026, with category-specific relaxations.
Admission to IIT Bombay or IIT Madras is the candidate's responsibility; selection by DAE does not substitute for the institute's M.Tech. admission requirements.

sections.heading: Length and sequence
paragraphs: DGFS-2026 is a two-year M.Tech. fellowship. The first year is institute course work. After completing that course work, the fellow undertakes DAE-assigned project work. Following successful completion of the M.Tech., the fellow must complete a four-month OCDF at the BARC Training School in Mumbai before appointment.
The orientation course follows the degree rather than replacing any part of it, so applicants should plan for the two-year postgraduate programme plus the post-degree OCDF requirement.
bullets: M.Tech.: two years.
DAE-linked project work: after one year of institute course work.
OCDF: four months after the M.Tech. and before joining the assigned DAE unit.

sections.heading: Academic work and DAE project
paragraphs: The degree curriculum is the approved M.Tech. programme at the relevant DGFS institute and specialization. The distinctive DGFS component is the project: DAE assigns it, and it is jointly supervised by a DAE guide and an institute guide, aligning the research with DAE programme requirements and the fellow's specialization.

The 2026 brochure also says fellows must participate in teaching apprenticeship (TA) work during the M.Tech. where required under the DGFS institute's terms and conditions. OCDF is a separate four-month orientation at BARC Training School, Mumbai.
bullets: Institute-led M.Tech. course work in an approved specialization.
DAE-assigned project with joint DAE and institute supervision.
Teaching apprenticeship where prescribed by the institute.
Four-month OCDF after the degree.

sections.heading: Selection and conversion into DGFS
paragraphs: For the 2026 recruitment cycle, OCES/DGFS selection used two stages: screening followed by a selection interview. Screening could be through the BARC computer-based online examination or through an eligible GATE score; the final selection decision was based solely on interview performance, subject to medical fitness.

Candidates who excel in the OCES selection interview may be offered the DGFS route only if they independently obtain qualifying M.Tech. admission at an approved DGFS institute and specialization in that academic year. Thus, applicants must manage both the BARC selection route and the separate postgraduate institute admission route.
bullets: Screening: BARC online examination or valid GATE score, as allowed for the annual cycle.
Selection: BARC Training Schools interview after shortlisting.
DGFS condition: selection for OCES plus independent admission to the listed M.Tech. option.
Medical fitness is required before stipend release in the 2026 cycle.

sections.heading: Funding, housing, and financial obligations
paragraphs: For DGFS-2026, DAE states a stipend of ₹74,000 per month during the two-year fellowship and reimbursement of M.Tech. tuition fees. It additionally specifies a ₹60,000 annual contingency grant for each of the two years for project-related expenses and possible BRNS Fast Track Project support of up to ₹4,00,000 for necessary project equipment or consumables, based on actual amounts paid. These are 2026-cycle terms and may be revised in future notices.

Hostel boarding and lodging at the DGFS institute is mandatory during the M.Tech. The brochure does not state that every personal expense is covered, so candidates should confirm hostel, mess, insurance, travel, and institute-specific charges directly with the allotted institute.

The funding is tied to a service obligation: the personal indemnity bond requires at least three years of DAE service after training. Its eventual amount depends on the support actually paid, including tuition and relevant project support.
bullets: 2026 monthly stipend: ₹74,000 for two years.
2026 tuition treatment: M.Tech. tuition reimbursed.
2026 contingency support: ₹60,000 per year for two years.
Mandatory institute-hostel residence during the M.Tech.
Minimum post-training service commitment: three years.

sections.heading: Career path after DGFS
paragraphs: A fellow who successfully completes the M.Tech. proceeds to the four-month OCDF and then joins DAE as Scientific Officer 'C'. For the 2026 scheme, IIT Bombay fellows are allocated to BARC and IIT Madras fellows to IGCAR; BARC may post an officer at any of its facilities in India. Allocation is made at the beginning of the M.Tech. programme based on DAE programme needs and selection-interview merit.

The official 2026 material describes the appointment as a Group A gazetted Government of India post. BARC's career page lists the Scientific Officer 'C' entry level as Level 10, basic pay ₹56,100 under the 7th Central Pay Commission matrix; actual monthly pay depends on increments, allowances, location, and prevailing government orders, so it should be treated as variable rather than a guaranteed take-home amount.
bullets: Complete M.Tech. and OCDF successfully.
Join as Scientific Officer 'C' in DAE.
2026 location pathway: BARC after IIT Bombay, or IGCAR after IIT Madras.
Further academic development may be available during a DAE career, including Ph.D. opportunities through HBNI as described in DAE recruitment material.
