title: ICMAI Practical Training
description: Mandatory supervised practical training under ICMAI rules, undertaken after CMA Intermediate registration to gain cost and management accounting experience.

sections.heading: Duration and timing
paragraphs: The required practical-training period is 15 months, undertaken on a full-time basis. It can begin from Intermediate registration, rather than waiting until Intermediate examination results or Final enrolment.

For Final-examination timing, the ICMAI prospectus states that 15 months must be completed before appearing in both or the remaining CMA Final group(s). The Scheme also describes interim Form T-5 certification cut-offs: August 31 for a December examination and February 28/29 for a June examination, each showing at least 10 months of training as of that cut-off. Students should confirm the applicable examination-term notification because ICMAI may revise cut-offs or procedures.
bullets: If the principal or employer changes, the student must inform ICMAI within 30 days using a new Form T-1 or T-4, as applicable; qualifying periods with different employers can accumulate under the published rules.
The published FAQ says no more than three principal/employer changes are allowed during a 15-month training period, and excess leave must be made up through an equivalent additional training period.

sections.heading: How to arrange and register the training
paragraphs: After Intermediate registration, the student may approach a recognized organization or a Practising Cost Accountant directly. ICMAI maintains practical-training resources, including lists of organizations, registered PCMAs and training opportunities, to support the search.

Once the student joins, ICMAI requires intimation within 30 days. For training with a PCMA or firm of PCMAs, the applicable engagement intimation is Form T-1 (with UDIN); for a company or organization, it is Form T-4. On completing the training, the student submits Form T-5. ICMAI states that practical-training forms are submitted online, not as offline hard copies.
bullets: Form T-1: intimation of engagement with a PCMA or firm of PCMAs.
Form T-4: intimation of engagement with a company or organization.
Form T-5: certificate of training imparted, submitted for the Final-examination requirement.
Form T-3: application route for practical-training exemption based on qualifying experience.

sections.heading: Fees and stipend context
paragraphs: Fee information can change. ICMAI’s CMA Prospectus 2025 lists a ₹2,500 practical-training registration fee when registering through Form T-1 or T-4, a ₹1,000 fee for notifying a change of principal/employer, and a ₹4,500 fee for a practical-training exemption application through Form T-3. Students should verify the amount in the live ICMAI training portal or current notification before paying.

Stipend is employer-paid rather than a course fee. In ICMAI’s July 19, 2024 circular, the minimum recommended monthly stipend for a student pursuing CMA Intermediate and training with a corporate/organization other than a PCMA or PCMA firm was ₹20,000 in Category X cities, ₹18,000 in Category Y cities, and ₹15,000 in Category Z locations for year 1; the circular states this structure applied from August 1, 2024. This is dated guidance and can be revised.
bullets: Published 2025 prospectus fee: ₹2,500 to register practical training through Form T-1/T-4.
Published 2025 prospectus fee: ₹4,500 for a Form T-3 exemption application.
Published July 2024 corporate/organization stipend guidance for CMA Intermediate year 1: ₹15,000–₹20,000 per month depending on city/town category; the circular excludes PCMAs/firms of PCMAs.

title: ICSI Long-Term Practical Training
description: Mandatory practical training under ICSI, ordinarily undertaken after passing CS Executive as part of qualification for Associate Company Secretary membership.

quick_facts.label: What it is
quick_facts.value: ICSI’s Long-Term Practical Training is the 21-month practical-training component prescribed under Regulation 46BB of the Company Secretaries Regulations, 1982.

quick_facts.label: Entry point
quick_facts.value: An Executive Programme pass student may start only after completing the one-month Executive Development Programme (15 days online e-EDP plus 15 days classroom EDP).

quick_facts.label: Where it may be undertaken
quick_facts.value: Training may be undertaken with an ICSI-eligible practising Company Secretary, company, or other eligible entity; the regulations describe it as whole-time training during normal working hours.

quick_facts.label: Trainee stipend
quick_facts.value: The ICSI training guidelines state that a practising Company Secretary or company engaging a trainee must pay at least ₹5,000 per month, subject to change by the Council; payment is to be through banking channels.

quick_facts.label: Membership relevance
quick_facts.value: An applicant for Associate Membership must provide documentary proof satisfactory to ICSI that the required practical training was completed or that an exemption was granted.

sections.heading: Who can begin the training
paragraphs: Under ICSI’s current published training guidelines, the standard route is for a student who has passed the CS Executive Programme and completed the full one-month EDP: 15 days of online e-EDP followed by 15 days of classroom EDP. The 21-month training can then be pursued under an eligible practising Company Secretary (PCS), company, or other entity recognised under Regulation 46BB and ICSI’s trainer criteria.

The regulations also permit ICSI to grant full, partial, conditional, or no exemption from EDP and practical training where a student claims equivalent practical knowledge and skills; this is an individual ICSI determination rather than an automatic alternative route.
bullets: The normal prerequisite is: CS Executive pass + 30 days of EDP.
Training is workplace-based and must be with an eligible/registered trainer or entity.
Students seeking an exemption should use ICSI’s applicable exemption process and criteria rather than assume prior employment automatically qualifies.

sections.heading: Duration and training conditions
paragraphs: The prescribed long-term practical-training period is 21 months. ICSI characterises the regulatory requirement as whole-time practical training during normal working hours. Its guidelines provide that working hours are set by trainee–trainer mutual consent, generally between 8:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m., with a minimum of eight hours a day, subject to applicable state or Union Territory law.

The trainer must file quarterly progress reports online, and the trainee must prepare and submit a project report based on the practical training through ICSI’s Stimulate portal. The first two months are a probation period; a transfer within that period requires 14 days’ notice and an NOC, while later transfers are ordinarily limited to specified exceptional cases.
bullets: Required period: 21 months.
Quarterly reports: filed by the trainer through ICSI’s online process.
Project report: prepared under the trainer’s guidance and submitted through Stimulate.

Registration timing: ICSI says training should preferably be registered before it begins; registration remains possible within 30 days of commencement, while a delay beyond 30 days is not treated as valid training.

sections.heading: Practical learning areas
paragraphs: This is not a classroom course with a single fixed paper syllabus. ICSI specifies indicative core workplace areas so that the training develops practical capability relevant to company-secretarial work. The actual work exposure will depend on the registered trainer or organisation, but ICSI’s list covers legal, governance, compliance, finance, regulatory, and technology-related responsibilities.
bullets: Legal and management work.
Corporate law, including insolvency; securities law; direct and indirect tax; economic and business laws; and labour laws.
Governance, ESG and CSR; audit; financial management; corporate funding; arbitration and mediation.
Artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and appearances/proceedings before regulators such as MCA, NCLT, ED, and RBI.

sections.heading: How to register the training
paragraphs: There is no separate entrance examination for this training stage in the published process. After finding an eligible trainer, a trainee under a PCS executes ICSI’s prescribed long-term-training contract; a trainee joining a company or other entity obtains a letter of training. The application to register training must include evidence of passing the Executive Programme and the one-month EDP completion certificate.

ICSI provides the prescribed 21-month contract format, training forms, NOC format, project-report format, and training-completion certificate format on its training pages. Students should use the current versions in the ICSI portal and should register the arrangement before starting wherever possible.
bullets: PCS route: execute the prescribed contract, in duplicate, on the required stamp paper/franking/e-stamp basis.
Company or other-entity route: obtain a letter of training from the trainer.
Attach Executive pass proof and the 30-day EDP completion certificate.
Register before commencement where possible, or no later than 30 days after commencement under the published guideline.

sections.heading: Costs and stipend context
paragraphs: ICSI’s published long-term-training guideline does not present a standalone trainee tuition fee for the 21-month placement in the relevant section. Instead, it requires a PCS or company engaging the trainee to pay a minimum monthly stipend of ₹5,000, with the amount subject to revision by the ICSI Council. This is a minimum stipend obligation, not a guarantee of a particular employer’s total compensation.

Students should separately budget for the prerequisite EDP. In the currently posted guidelines, the 15-day online EDP fee is ₹2,000 and the 15-day classroom EDP fee is ₹8,000 inclusive of listed refreshments, lunch, and ₹300 of study material; ICSI states these fees may be prescribed or changed from time to time. Confirm the fee shown in the current Stimulate registration flow before paying.
bullets: Minimum published stipend for a PCS/company trainee: ₹5,000 per month, subject to future Council revision.
Published prerequisite EDP fees: ₹2,000 online plus ₹8,000 classroom, subject to change.
Potential personal expenses such as relocation, commuting, accommodation, stamp/e-stamp costs, and exam preparation depend on the trainee and training location.

sections.heading: What follows long-term practical training
paragraphs: The usual qualification pathway continues with the CS Professional Programme and ICSI’s Corporate Leadership Development Programme (CLDP). Under the published guidelines, a student who has passed the Professional Programme and completed the 30-day EDP plus 21 months of practical training becomes eligible for CLDP Phase I; completing Phase I is required before CLDP Phase II. The regulations provide for CLDP of not less than 30 days and not more than 60 days after passing the Professional Programme.

For Associate Company Secretary (ACS) membership, the student must apply to ICSI in the prescribed form and submit documentary proof satisfactory to the Institute that the required practical training was completed or exempted. ICSI’s forms page also provides a document list for Form-A for ACS and a training-completion certificate format.
bullets: Pass the CS Professional Programme, if not already passed while completing training.
Complete the applicable CLDP sequence after satisfying its eligibility requirements.
Apply for ACS membership with ICSI and include the required training evidence.

title: ITI (Industrial Training Institute)
description: Government-recognized vocational trade training (1-2 years) after Class 10 in trades like electrician, fitter, welder, COPA; leads to apprenticeships and skilled-trade employment.

quick_facts.label: What ITI training is
quick_facts.value: Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) deliver Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) vocational courses through government and private institutes; DGT sets national standards and certification arrangements, while States/UTs administer institutes and admissions.

quick_facts.label: Entry requirement
quick_facts.value: Eligibility is trade-specific. Many engineering trades, including Fitter, require Class 10 with Science and Mathematics (or an equivalent/vocational subject in the sector), while some CTS trades accept Class 8 or Class 10 without that subject combination.

quick_facts.label: Course length
quick_facts.value: CTS trade durations currently include 6 months (600 hours), one year (1,200 hours), and two years (2,400 hours); the exact duration depends on the selected trade.

quick_facts.label: Certification
quick_facts.value: After completing a CTS trade and passing the All India Trade Test (AITT), a trainee receives a National Trade Certificate (NTC). A National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) is a later, separate outcome after completing trade apprenticeship training and passing the apprenticeship AITT.

quick_facts.label: Trade choice
quick_facts.value: DGT’s CTS catalogue lists 169 NSQF-compliant trades across engineering, non-engineering and Divyang categories. Examples include Electrician, Fitter, Welder and Computer Operator & Programming Assistant (COPA), but availability varies by institute and State/UT.

sections.heading: Who can enter an ITI course?
paragraphs: ITI is not a single course with one national entry rule: CTS eligibility is set trade by trade. For many technical trades, Class 10 with Science and Mathematics is required; for example, DGT lists this requirement for Fitter. Other trades have Class 8 or general Class 10 entry requirements. Applicants should therefore check the exact DGT trade entry requirement and their State/UT admission notice rather than relying only on the broad label “ITI after Class 10.”

Admission is administered by the relevant State Government or Union Territory administration. State/UT notices can additionally specify age, domicile, reservation, document-verification and counselling conditions.
bullets: For a Class 10 student seeking an engineering trade, confirm whether Science and Mathematics are compulsory for that trade.
Choose an NCVT-affiliated CTS unit and verify that the institute is offering the trade in the intended admission session.
Treat trade-specific eligibility and the State/UT prospectus as controlling documents for admission.

sections.heading: How long does ITI take?
paragraphs: The familiar one- or two-year ITI route is the main pathway for many trades, but CTS also includes six-month courses. DGT’s current course catalogue identifies courses as 600-hour, 1,200-hour or 2,400-hour programmes, corresponding to six months, one year and two years respectively.

For restructured one-year CTS courses, DGT specifies 1,200 learning hours plus 150 hours of mandatory on-the-job training or group project work. Two-year courses are listed at 2,400 hours; practical structure can vary by trade and institute.
bullets: Six months: 600 hours.
One year: 1,200 hours, plus mandatory OJT/group-project provision in the restructured curriculum.
Two years: 2,400 hours.

sections.heading: What students learn
paragraphs: CTS training is trade-led and combines hands-on trade practical work with trade theory and employability skills. The detailed learning outcomes, tools, safety content and assessment components are published in DGT’s individual trade curricula; these should be reviewed before selecting a trade because an Electrician, Fitter, Welder and COPA programme lead to materially different work skills.

The CTS framework has been aligned to NSQF levels. DGT also provides for on-the-job training/project work within the restructured curriculum. Some affiliated ITIs may offer the Dual System of Training, in which industry exposure is integrated into the CTS course; this is not automatically available at every ITI or in every trade.
bullets: Trade practical and trade theory are the core of the programme.
Employability skills form a common curriculum component.
Course content, NSQF level, duration and minimum qualification can be checked in DGT’s CTS course catalogue.
Dual System of Training can provide structured industry exposure where the ITI and an industry partner offer it.

sections.heading: How admission works
paragraphs: There is no single all-India ITI admission process for all institutes. DGT states that national policy, training standards, examinations and certification are central responsibilities, while day-to-day ITI administration—including admissions—rests with the respective State/UT. Applicants should use the relevant State/UT vocational-training or skill-development admission portal and the institute’s official notice for the current session.

Before applying, verify the specific institute and unit, the selected trade’s entry qualification and duration, seat availability, whether the unit is affiliated, and the current State/UT counselling or merit procedure. Session dates, application fees, reservation rules and document requirements are variable and should not be assumed from another State.
bullets: Start with the State/UT ITI admission authority, not an unofficial aggregator.
Cross-check the trade in DGT’s CTS catalogue.
Use NCVT MIS/DGT-linked resources to verify the course and institute information where available.

sections.heading: What comes after ITI?
paragraphs: The immediate formal outcome of CTS is the National Trade Certificate, not the NAC: trainees who pass the CTS All India Trade Test receive an NTC. The NTC is recognized for recruitment to relevant posts and services in Central/State government and private establishments, but every employer or recruitment examination sets its own trade, age, physical, category and other eligibility conditions.

A common progression is trade apprenticeship. Under the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme information published by MSDE, apprenticeship for ITI pass-outs in designated trades ordinarily lasts one year. On completion of apprenticeship training, candidates may take the apprenticeship AITT; passing it leads to the National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC).

An ITI/NTC can also support progression toward instructor training. DGT’s Craft Instructor Training Scheme (CITS) lists NTC or NAC as eligible qualifications for relevant CITS trades, alongside diploma/degree routes where applicable. CITS is therefore a trade-specific pathway toward becoming a vocational instructor, not an automatic next step for every ITI graduate.

Employment and self-employment are also intended CTS outcomes. For progression to Polytechnic Diploma, Armed Forces recruitment, RRB ALP, DRDO CEPTAM or other technical recruitment, candidates must check the live official notification: an ITI/NTC alone does not establish eligibility across all posts, and accepted trades and requirements vary by recruiting body and year.
bullets: Pass CTS AITT → National Trade Certificate (NTC).
Undertake a registered trade apprenticeship → pass apprenticeship AITT → National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC).
Apply for trade-relevant technician, production, maintenance, service or self-employment opportunities.
Consider CITS where the candidate holds the required trade-relevant NTC/NAC and meets that course’s conditions.
Check separate, current official notifications for diploma admission and government recruitment pathways.

title: Para Regiment Probation
description: A demanding volunteer selection and probation process for serving Indian Army personnel seeking transfer to the Parachute Regiment or its special-forces stream.

quick_facts.label: Training context
quick_facts.value: Official Ministry of Defence accounting guidance describes a probationary attachment to airborne forces for personnel serving in Parachute units and formations; it is linked to subsequent attendance at a Basic Parachute Course and parachute-duty qualification.

quick_facts.label: Documented minimum probation attachment
quick_facts.value: For the parachute-pay rules cited in the official guidance, the relevant probationary attachment is one month. This should not be treated as a published duration for every Para Regiment or Para (Special Forces) selection pathway, because the public source does not set out a complete selection syllabus or universal probation length.

quick_facts.label: Institutional destination
quick_facts.value: The Ministry of Defence publicly identifies both conventional Parachute Regiment battalions and Parachute Regiment (Special Forces) battalions, confirming that the Regiment includes a special-forces stream.

quick_facts.label: Public-information limitation
quick_facts.value: The official sources located describe probationary attachment, parachute-course qualification, duty status and allowances, but do not publish a public civilian application form, a complete probation test battery, a pass rate, or universal age/service thresholds for transfer volunteers.

sections.heading: Eligibility: a serving-personnel pathway, not a civilian course
paragraphs: This node should be understood as an internal Indian Army pathway for serving personnel rather than a standalone civilian education programme. The official material publicly available refers to personnel serving in Parachute units and airborne formations, their probationary attachment, parachute-course qualification and parachute duties; it does not publish a general public enrolment route for the process.

The public record is insufficient to state a universal age limit, minimum prior service, medical standard, vacancy rule, or a guaranteed right for every Sepoy to volunteer. Those details should therefore be obtained through the soldier’s chain of command and current unit/Army orders rather than inferred from unofficial online claims.
bullets: A candidate must already be within the service system relevant to the posting or attachment; this is not presented in the cited government material as direct civilian recruitment.
Probationary attachment is associated with a parachute formation/airborne-force context and with the Basic Parachute Course.

Eligibility, attachment and any waiver are administratively controlled; the officer guidance specifically refers to waivers by administrative authorities where the prescribed probation period was not completed.

sections.heading: Duration: what official public sources establish
paragraphs: The clearest official, publicly accessible duration is a one-month probationary attachment used in the rules governing parachute allowance. For personnel serving in Parachute units and airborne formations, the guidance ties eligibility for parachute pay after Basic Parachute Course qualification to one month from the start of probationary attachment, subject to the stated timing rules.

That one-month figure is a documented administrative/pay condition. It is not adequate evidence for claiming that all Para Regiment or Para (Special Forces) volunteer selection and continuation training lasts exactly one month; the detailed operational selection timeline is not published in the official sources reviewed.
bullets: Published qualification-related probationary attachment: one month.
The source links the attachment with the Basic Parachute Course and applies timing conditions when the gap before the course exceeds three months.
For continuation of Para pay, JCOs/other ranks are required to attend a yearly parachute refresher course that includes at least two jumps, subject to listed exemptions.

sections.heading: Training content supported by public sources
paragraphs: The public government documentation supports a narrow but important training sequence: probationary attachment in an airborne setting, a Basic Parachute Course, qualification as a parachutist, and continuing refresher activity. It does not publish the physical tests, field exercises, navigation tasks, weapons standards, sleep-deprivation regime, or selection scoring often described in unofficial accounts.

After qualification, continued parachute-duty status is connected to refresher training. The cited manual specifies a refresher course in each training year, including a minimum of two jumps, for continuation of Para pay for JCOs and other ranks, with provisions for operational jumps and limited exemptions.
bullets: Probationary attachment to airborne forces or a parachute formation.
Basic Parachute Course.
Qualification for parachute duties and subsequent parachute descents where required by normal duties.
Annual refresher requirement for the applicable pay entitlement: a parachute refresher course including at least two jumps.

sections.heading: Admission and administrative control
paragraphs: There is no verified public admissions portal or civilian application deadline for this node. The available official sources instead show an internal administrative process: allowances are authorised through Part II Orders, the relevant appointment must be authorised in the unit/formation establishment, and commander or administrative-authority decisions can be relevant where a course is not completed or probationary attachment is waived.

For a serving Sepoy, the practical route is consequently unit-led: raise the intention through the chain of command and rely on current Army instructions for vacancies, medical categorisation, approvals, attachment and reporting. This is an operational inference from the internal-order structure in the official material, not a claim that every request must be accepted.
bullets: No publicly verified civilian application form or published annual deadline was found in the official sources reviewed.
Part II Orders are the documented authority used for the relevant Para allowance administration.
The official guidance requires the person to be employed on parachute duties and to hold an appointment authorised by the relevant establishment for the allowance context.

sections.heading: What follows successful parachute qualification
paragraphs: The publicly documented immediate progression is qualification at the Basic Parachute Course and employment on parachute duties in an authorised appointment. Personnel who remain in the applicable parachute-duty framework may continue to receive parachute pay while they meet the refresher requirements and remain medically fit for jumping, under the rules cited.

The Regiment also contains identified Parachute Regiment (Special Forces) battalions. However, the official sources reviewed do not establish that completing the one-month probationary attachment or Basic Parachute Course automatically transfers a soldier into a Para (Special Forces) battalion. Such posting or selection should be treated as subject to separate, current Army authority and requirements.
bullets: Basic Parachute Course qualification and parachute-duty employment are the verified immediate outcomes in the official guidance.
Ongoing refresher participation is relevant to continued Para pay in the cited rules.
Parachute Regiment (Special Forces) battalions exist, but no automatic progression rule from basic parachute qualification to that stream is publicly substantiated here.
